EDCS-00380260.translation: Of Titus Attius Paetus of Concordiensis.
EDCS-00380260.summary: This is likely a funerary or ownership inscription referring to Titus Attius Paetus of Concordiensis.

EDCS-00380263.translation: In the fourth year before the Ides of February, he rests here, Felicissimus, who lived four years. He rests in peace with God.
EDCS-00380263.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the death of Felicissimus, who lived for four years.

EDCS-00380264.translation: To Gaius Licinius Pilomusus, freedman of Gaius, a Gaulish merchant. Gaius Licinius Andero, his freedman, made this for himself and his patron, a space of 16 square feet.
EDCS-00380264.summary: A funerary monument or marker set up by a freedman for himself and his patron, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-00380265.translation: To Fortune. Felix, made this for the Emperors, for many years.
EDCS-00380265.summary: A dedication to the goddess Fortuna, likely set up by an individual named Felix, possibly in relation to the reigning emperors, the specific context and date are unclear.

EDCS-00380269.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to be part of a funerary monument, likely recording a person's name and parentage, no date is inferable.

EDCS-00380278.summary: This is likely a funerary or ownership inscription referring to Gaius Titius Hermerotis.

EDCS-00380279.summary: This is likely a funerary or ownership inscription referring to Marcus Albius Rufus.

EDCS-00380280.summary: This is likely a funerary or ownership inscription referring to Lucius Elpidius Theodorus.

EDCS-00380281.summary: This is likely a funerary or ownership inscription referring to Valeria Magna Epidiana.

EDCS-00380283.translation: Flora made this for herself and Prisca.
EDCS-00380283.summary: A funerary or commemorative inscription, likely set up by Flora for herself and another individual named Prisca, date is not inferable.

EDCS-00380284.translation: Publius Tullius, son of Publius, 10 feet in front, 10 feet behind.
EDCS-00380284.summary: A boundary marker or funerary inscription indicating dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period, the exact purpose requires more context.

EDCS-00380286.translation: Publius Turillius, son of Publius, while alive, for himself and...
EDCS-00380286.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication or funerary inscription made by Publius Turillius.

EDCS-01300002.translation: Aulus Barbius Parnax, freedman of Aulus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Belenus.
EDCS-01300002.summary: A votive inscription dedicating fulfillment of a vow to the Celtic deity Belenus, set up by a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300003.translation: Lucius Curtius, son of Numerius, willingly and deservedly gave this offering to Holy Belenus.
EDCS-01300003.summary: A votive inscription offering a gift to the deity Belenus, set up by Lucius Curtius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300004.translation: Lucius Pinnius Sopilus, freedman of Lucius, for the Bonae Deae (?). At the place of exercise.
EDCS-01300004.summary: A dedication to a female deity (possibly Bonae Deae) associated with a place of exercise, set up by a freedman, date is not inferable.

EDCS-01300006.translation: Caius Albius Andies gives an altar to Hercules. Caius Dindius, freedman of Titus, Mogio, gives an altar to Hercules.
EDCS-01300006.summary: This inscription records two altars dedicated to Hercules, one by Caius Albius Andies and the other by Caius Dindius, a freedman.

EDCS-01300007.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication to a personified concept or a deity related to the mind, date and context are unknown.

EDCS-01300010.translation: Spurius Erugios gave a gift to Temavus willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01300010.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the deity Temavus by Spurius Erugios.

EDCS-01300015.translation: Vibius, son of Kaeso, son of Gavillius, censors.
EDCS-01300015.summary: This inscription likely refers to Vibius, son of Kaeso, son of Gavillius, who held the office of censor.

EDCS-01300018.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely mentioning a magistrate, P(ublius) Sa[---], who held the office of IIIIvir (iure dicundo).

EDCS-01300019.translation: Petronia, daughter of Caius, Caius Aufidius, son of Caius, scribe and librarian, quaestorius of the decuriae, V Titus, son of Caius, quaestor, Marcus, son of Caius.
EDCS-01300019.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including officials like a scribe, librarian, and quaestor, likely related to a public or collegial body.

EDCS-01300023.translation: Lucius Catius; Quintus Verus, son of Quintus; Balbus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-01300023.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely listing several individuals, possibly related to property ownership or inheritance, date is not inferable.

EDCS-01300025.translation: Place of Titus Plasius. Place of Titus Pum[---], [---] of Lucius Ves[---].
EDCS-01300025.summary: This inscription appears to list locations or properties associated with individuals named Titus Plasius, Titus Pum[---], and Lucius Ves[---].

EDCS-01300026.translation: XXII [places?]. [---]a. XXI places of Publius Porcius(?). XXII places of Caius Valerius. Places of Publius Al[---] Antius. Of Rutedia Alfena Procla, the first and second places. XX places of Caius Cluvius(?). Places of Caius Pomponius. XIX places of Titus Val[---]. Places of Caius Al[---] Cominius.
EDCS-01300026.summary: This inscription seems to be a list of places or properties, possibly rentals or subdivisions, associated with various individuals, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01300028.translation: Of Marcus Maxsuma. Of Cervonia. Titus Ros[---]. Two places of Eburia Maxsuma. [[Of Titus Ros]].
EDCS-01300028.summary: This inscription records two places belonging to Eburia Maxsuma, with mentions of Marcus Maxsuma, Cervonia, and Titus Ros, possibly relating to property ownership.

EDCS-01300029.translation: Sextus Magius, son of Caius, from the Fabia tribe, from Patavium, centurion of the second legion.
EDCS-01300029.summary: This is a funerary or official inscription identifying Sextus Magius, a centurion of the second legion, noting his tribal affiliation and origin.

EDCS-01300030.translation: Lucius Vibius, son of Marcus, a rope-maker.
EDCS-01300030.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Vibius, son of Marcus, by his profession as a clavarius (rope-maker).

EDCS-01300031.translation: Ofellenus Colonus, son of Publius, while alive, made this for himself and his family, freedmen and freedwomen, for a space of sixteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-01300031.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Ofellenus Colonus for himself and his household, specifying the size of the plot.

EDCS-01300032.translation: [---]arbius(?), freedman of Aulus [---]. [---] a [ferrarius?], freedman of Aulus Bit[---].
EDCS-01300032.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely identifies two freedmen, possibly associated with a craftsman like a ferrarius (ironworker), and mentions their patron Aulus.

EDCS-01300033.translation: [---] gladiator. Titus Licinius, son of Marcus, Secunda, not obedient.
EDCS-01300033.summary: This inscription mentions a gladiator and identifies Titus Licinius, son of Marcus, along with a woman named Secunda, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-01300034.translation: Trosia Hilara, freedwoman of Publius Hermon, a wool-worker and street vendor, while alive, made this space of sixteen square feet for her freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01300034.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Trosia Hilara, a freedwoman and vendor, for herself and her freed slaves, indicating the size of the allocated space.

EDCS-01300037.translation: Lucius Aiacius Dama, a Jewish porter and freedman of Publius, while alive, made this for himself.
EDCS-01300037.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Aiacius Dama, identified as a Jewish porter and freedman.

EDCS-01300038.text_edition: \n Paelignus Philocles tibeicen sic vivus fecit Albia Lucumonis liberta H Paeligna Cai liberta Clara\n
EDCS-01300038.translation: Paelignus Philocles, a piper, made this tombstone for himself alive. Albia Clara, freedwoman of Lucumo Paelignus, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-01300038.summary: This is a tombstone inscription (dis Manibus) set up by the piper Paelignus Philocles for himself during his lifetime, with additional dedications by two freedwomen.

EDCS-01300040.translation: A private boundary marker in a private place, belonging to Tertius, son of Magius, son of Mansuetus.
EDCS-01300040.summary: This inscription marks a private boundary in a private location and identifies its owner.

EDCS-01300042.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its content, but it likely records a name and potentially an origin or affiliation.

EDCS-01300045.summary: This is a dedication to the god Aesculapius, with the inscription being incomplete.

EDCS-01300046.translation: To Aesculapius, sacred to Augustus. Marcus Terentius, freedman of Publius [---].
EDCS-01300046.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aesculapius, sacred to Augustus, made by Marcus Terentius, freedman of Publius, and is incomplete.

EDCS-01300047.text_edition: \n Aesontio sacrum Lucius Barbius Montanus primus pilus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300047.translation: Sacred to Aesontius. Lucius Barbius Montanus, first centurion, gladly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-01300047.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Lucius Barbius Montanus, a first centurion, to the deity Aesontius.

EDCS-01300048.translation: Flavia Charite to the eternal god.
EDCS-01300048.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Flavia Charite to an eternal god.

EDCS-01300049.translation: To the eternal god, for a vow undertaken and obtained. Hyginus, freedman of Gaius Atilius V[---], fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01300049.summary: This inscription records Hyginus fulfilling a vow to the eternal god, likely on behalf of his master.

EDCS-01300050.translation: To the eternal god for the health of Lucius Statius Candidianus. Lucius Statius Fortunatianus and Novia Candida gladly paid their vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-01300050.summary: This inscription records Lucius Statius Fortunatianus and Novia Candida paying a vow to the eternal god for the health of Lucius Statius Candidianus.

EDCS-01300051.text_edition: \n Hilarus Syriaci Augusti liberti tabularii servus accipe Phoebe precor Tirynthia munera pro me haec tibi quae potui fortia dona dedi hic orbem domuit tu pacem Phoebe dedisti utraque res votis annuat ista meis\n
EDCS-01300051.translation: Hilarus, slave of Syriacus, procurator of the imperial records office, accept these offerings, Phoebus, I pray, these strong gifts which I have given to you; I subdued the world, you, Phoebus, gave peace; may both these things grant my wishes.
EDCS-01300051.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Hilarus, a slave of an imperial official, to Apollo (Phoebus), likely commemorating his master's achievements and seeking personal favor.

EDCS-01300052.text_edition: \n Athictus Ursionis Caesaris verna Didieni Puri Belino votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300052.translation: Athictus, Ver(na) of Ursio, Caesar's slave, paid his vow to Belenus, son of Didius Purus, gladly and as was deserved.
EDCS-01300052.summary: This inscription records Athictus, a slave of Ursio, paying a vow to the deity Belenus.

EDCS-01300053.translation: To Belenus. Gaius Aulius, freedman of Gaius [---], Hypatus(?).
EDCS-01300053.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicating something to Belenus by Gaius Aulius Hypatus, a freedman.

EDCS-01300054.translation: To the Good Goddess. Lucius Aurelius Pisinus, freedman of the emperor, gave a gift.
EDCS-01300054.summary: This inscription records Lucius Aurelius Pisinus, an imperial freedman, making a dedication to the Bona Dea (Good Goddess).

EDCS-01300055.translation: To Belenus. Lucius Cantius Spendusae, freedman, Ionicus, gladly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-01300055.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cantius Spendusae, an Ionic freedman, paying a vow to Belenus.

EDCS-01300056.text_edition: \n Deo Beleno Marcus Flavius Florianus vir egregius a ducenariis quod princeps legionis vovit \n
EDCS-01300056.translation: To the god Belenus. Marcus Flavius Florianus, an excellent man, from the ducenarii, for having vowed when he was the commander of the legion, [paid his vow].
EDCS-01300056.summary: This inscription records Marcus Flavius Florianus, a high-ranking military officer, paying a vow to the god Belenus.

EDCS-01300057.translation: To Titus Gavius Aquila, for Belenos.
EDCS-01300057.summary: This is a dedication to the god Belenos by Titus Gavius Aquila.

EDCS-01300058.translation: To Belenos, Quintus Prestius Verecundus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300058.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Belenos by Quintus Prestius Verecundus.

EDCS-01300059.translation: Lucius Safnius Communis, freedman of Lucius, for Lepidus the slave, willingly and deservedly paid his vow, sacred to Belenos.
EDCS-01300059.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Safnius Communis for his slave Lepidus, dedicated to Belenos.

EDCS-01300060.translation: To Belenos, Titus Thorius Felix willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300060.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Belenos by Titus Thorius Felix.

EDCS-01300061.translation: Titus Tudisius Fuscus, freedman of Titus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Belenos.
EDCS-01300061.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Belenos by Titus Tudisius Fuscus, a freedman.

EDCS-01300065.translation: Aesennia Eupistis gave this gift to Belenos Augustus.
EDCS-01300065.summary: This inscription records a gift given to the imperialized god Belenos by Aesennia Eupistis.

EDCS-01300066.summary: This is a partial inscription dedicating something to Belenos Augustus by Gaius Annius [---]mius.

EDCS-01300067.translation: To Belenos Augustus, Publius Artiscius Cornelianus [---].
EDCS-01300067.summary: This is a partial inscription dedicating something to Belenos Augustus by Publius Artiscius Cornelianus.

EDCS-01300068.translation: To the god Belenos Augustus, Lucius Calpurnius Parthenopaeus, IIIIvir of Aquileia, paid his vow; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01300068.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Lucius Calpurnius Parthenopaeus, a magistrate of Aquileia, to Belenos Augustus, with the site granted by the local council.

EDCS-01300069.translation: Sacred to Belenos Augustus, Quintus Calventius Pollentinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300069.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Belenos Augustus by Quintus Calventius Pollentinus.

EDCS-01300070.translation: To Belinus Augustus. Marcus Carminius Trophimus, freedman of Marcus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300070.summary: An altar dedicated to the god Belinus Augustus by Marcus Carminius Trophimus, a freedman, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300072.translation: Sacred to Belinus Augustus. Marcus Licinius [paid his vow].
EDCS-01300072.summary: An inscription fragment dedicated to Belinus Augustus, likely recording a vow paid by Marcus Licinius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300073.translation: To the god Belinus Augustus. Lucilius Marcellinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300073.summary: An altar dedicated to the god Belinus Augustus by Lucilius Marcellinus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300074.translation: To Belinus Augustus. Sextus Mutilius Abascantus paid his vow.
EDCS-01300074.summary: An inscription dedicated to Belinus Augustus by Sextus Mutilius Abascantus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300075.text_edition: \n Belino Augusto Publicius Placidus negotiator Romaniensis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300075.translation: To Belinus Augustus. Publicius Placidus, a merchant from Rians, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300075.summary: An inscription dedicated to Belinus Augustus by Publicius Placidus, a merchant from Rians (Rigomagus), dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300076.text_edition: \n August-- sacrum Lucius Trebius Verecundus Altinas votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300076.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Lucius Trebius Verecundus from Altina willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300076.summary: An inscription dedicated to Augustus by Lucius Trebius Verecundus from Altina, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300077.text_edition: \n Beleno Defensori Augusto sacrum Titus Plot Titi filius Felix et Plot3 \n
EDCS-01300077.translation: Sacred to Belinus the Defender Augustus. Titus Plotus Felix, son of Titus Plotus, and Plotus [paid their vow].
EDCS-01300077.summary: A dedication to Belinus the Defender Augustus by Titus Plotus Felix and possibly another individual named Plotus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300078.translation: To Belinus the Holy [paid his vow].
EDCS-01300078.summary: A fragmentary inscription dedicated to Belinus the Holy, likely recording a vow, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300079.translation: Decimus Lurius, son of Decimus, of the Voltinia tribe, to Belinus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow. To the Nymphs.
EDCS-01300079.summary: A dedication to Belinus and the Nymphs by Decimus Lurius, a citizen of the Voltinia tribe, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300085.translation: [Some name] and [some name] gave [this] to Concordia.
EDCS-01300085.summary: A dedication to the goddess Concordia by at least two individuals, whose names are partially lost, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300090.text_edition: \n Numini praestantissimo et Dianae Augustae Marcus Appius Helpidianus periculo liberatus pro salute sua et suorum votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300090.translation: Marcus Appius Helpidianus, having been freed from danger, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the most excellent divine power and Diana Augusta for his own safety and that of his family.
EDCS-01300090.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Appius Helpidianus to the divine power and Diana Augusta, dedicating a vow for his safety and that of his family.

EDCS-01300091.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Magnus domo Ephesius decurio coloniae Aquileiensium \n
EDCS-01300091.translation: Tiberius Claudius Magnus, from Ephesus, a decurion of the colony of Aquileia.
EDCS-01300091.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Claudius Magnus, identified as a decurion from Ephesus serving in the colony of Aquileia.

EDCS-01300095.text_edition: \n Fonti sacrum Poblicius Statutus votum solvit\n
EDCS-01300095.translation: Poblicius Statutus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Spring.
EDCS-01300095.summary: This is a votive inscription by Poblicius Statutus to a Spring.

EDCS-01300096.text_edition: \n Quintus Titacius Maxsumus sic Fonti votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300096.translation: Quintus Titacius Maximus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Spring.
EDCS-01300096.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Titacius Maximus to the Spring.

EDCS-01300097.translation: Caius F. S., a money-changer, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vows to the divine power.
EDCS-01300097.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius F. S., a money-changer, to the divine power.

EDCS-01300099.translation: The devotees of the Genius of Aquileia [offered this to] the magistrates Titus Flavius Hermetes [[6]].
EDCS-01300099.summary: This inscription records an offering by the devotees of the Genius of Aquileia to their magistrates, including Titus Flavius Hermetes.

EDCS-01300100.translation: Titus Caser[nius] [dedicated this] to Sotira[e] Hecat[ae].
EDCS-01300100.summary: This inscription records Titus Caser[nius] dedicating something to Sotira and Hecata.

EDCS-01300101.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a dedication to Sotira and Hecata.

EDCS-01300103.translation: Cl]arus Faustus, freedman of Titus Saufeius Titus, [and] Ianus Princeps Hostilius, son of Marcus, [dedicated].
EDCS-01300103.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication to Janus by Clarus Faustus and Ianus Princeps Hostilius.

EDCS-01300104.text_edition: \n Isidi sacrum Tiberius Veturius Fuscus vestiarius tenuarius IIIIIIvir beneficio ordinis\n
EDCS-01300104.translation: Tiberius Veturius Fuscus, a vestiarius (seller of women's clothing) and tenuarius (possibly a type of official), [dedicated this] sacred offering to Isis, as a benefit from the board of six officials (IIIIIIvir).
EDCS-01300104.summary: This is a sacred dedication to Isis by Tiberius Veturius Fuscus, an official involved in selling women's clothing, acknowledging a benefit from the board of six officials.

EDCS-01300107.text_edition: \n Isidi Reginae ex visu Titus Flavius Castus\n
EDCS-01300107.translation: To Queen Isis, from a vision. Titus Flavius Castus.
EDCS-01300107.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription from Titus Flavius Castus to Queen Isis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300110.translation: To Jupiter. Marcus Freminus Priscus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01300110.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a votive offering to Jupiter by Marcus Freminus Priscus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300111.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. From the cultivators of Aquileia, Martial is dedicated.
EDCS-01300111.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter by the cultivators of Aquileia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300112.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. Varia Phyllis, from a vision.
EDCS-01300112.summary: An ex-voto inscription from Varia Phyllis to Jupiter, prompted by a vision, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300113.translation: Sacred to Jupiter (?). To the Defender, by order from a vision. Mercurius placed [this].
EDCS-01300113.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter (or a related deity) and the 'Defender', set up by Mercurius after receiving divine instruction, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300114.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Publius Aurelius Severinus, veteran, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01300114.summary: A votive inscription from Publius Aurelius Severinus, a veteran, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300117.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, the Eternal. [---] Soteri(c)ius, VIvir of Aquileia, [by order?] of the Divinity, placed [this] for the Divinity. [---]
EDCS-01300117.summary: An inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Aeternus, possibly by Soteri(c)ius, a VIvir of Aquileia, who acted on divine inspiration, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300118.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, the Dolichrene, the Heliopolitan. Lucianus, vicarius of the station of Atratum, belonging to Eutyches, the steward of our Emperor, while the vow of good [men] remains, [set this up?] with [---]
EDCS-01300118.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, both Dolichrene and Heliopolitan, by Lucianus, a vicarius of a postal station, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300119.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest the Liberator. Rutilius Severus willingly placed this altar for Eternal Aquileia (?).
EDCS-01300119.summary: An inscription recording Rutilius Severus placing an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Liberator, possibly for the benefit of Aquileia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300120.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Victori Conservatori Defensorique compos voti suscepti Hermes \n
EDCS-01300120.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest the Victorious Protector and Defender. Hermes, having fulfilled a vow made, [placed this].
EDCS-01300120.summary: This inscription records Hermes fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Victor and Protector, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300121.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et numini domini nostri Imperatoris Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti et genio splendidissimae coloniae Aquileiae Eutyches Augusti nostri servus vilicus vectigalis Illyrici praepositus quinquagesimae stationes utrasque empori ex commodis suis ampliavit et restituit\n
EDCS-01300121.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to the divine numen of our lord Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, and to the genius of the most splendid colony of Aquileia, Eutyches, steward of our Augustus and supervisor of the Illyrian customs tax, who was in charge of both stations of the emporium, enlarged and restored them from his own funds.
EDCS-01300121.summary: This inscription records the restoration and enlargement of two customs stations at the emporium by Eutyches, a steward and tax supervisor, likely during the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-01300122.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Minervae Marti Protectori Victori pro salute et victoria dddominorum nnnostrorum Impperatorum Caesarum Marci Clodi Pupieni et Decimi Caeli Calvini Balbini Augggustorum et Marci Antoni Gordiani nobilissimi Caesaris ex voto Flavius Servilianus a militiis et Flavius Adiutor praefectus cohortis I Ulpiae Galatarum praepositi militum agentium in protensione Aquileiae\n
EDCS-01300122.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno, Minerva, Mars the Protector and Victor, for the health and victory of our lords Emperors Caesar Marcus Clodius Pupienus and Decimus Caelus Calvinus Balbinus Augusti, and of Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, the most noble, Flavius Servilianus, holder of military office, and Flavius Adiutor, prefect of the I Ulpia Galatarum cohort, having charge of the soldiers serving in the defense of Aquileia, fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01300122.summary: This inscription records a vow made by military officials, Flavius Servilianus and Flavius Adiutor, for the well-being and victory of the emperors Pupienus, Balbinus, and Gordian, likely around 238 AD.

EDCS-01300123.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Sancto Silvano Olympus actor Aeli Sperati |(centurionis) ex vetustate restituit libens merito\n
EDCS-01300123.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Holy Silvanus, Olympus, agent of Aelius Speratus (a centurion), restored this out of devotion and due respect from its ancient state.
EDCS-01300123.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something (likely a building or monument) by Olympus, an agent of Aelius Speratus, to Jupiter and Silvanus.

EDCS-01300128.text_edition: \n Magnae Deum Matri sacrum Lucius Decidius Eucarpus IIIIIIvir \n
EDCS-01300128.translation: Sacred to the Great Mother of the Gods, by Lucius Decidius Eucarpus, one of the IIIIvir.
EDCS-01300128.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Magna Mater by Lucius Decidius Eucarpus, a member of the college of IIIIvir.

EDCS-01300134.translation: Lucius Satonius Liberalis fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-01300134.summary: This inscription records a votive offering fulfilled by Lucius Satonius Liberalis to Mercury.

EDCS-01300137.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicated to Minerva Augusta.

EDCS-01300139.translation: In the consulship of Cilo II and Libo, to the Unconquered Invincible God Mithras, Titus Aelius Verecundus and Marcus Aurelius [...]
EDCS-01300139.summary: This inscription, dated by the consuls Cilo and Libo (likely 207 AD), records a dedication to the god Mithras by Titus Aelius Verecundus and Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-01300140.translation: To the Unconquered Invincible God Mithras, Lucius Septimius Cassianus, standard-bearer of the IV Hispana Legion, serving in the lustrum of Publius Porcius Faustus, primipilaris, gladly and deservedly placed his vow.
EDCS-01300140.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Lucius Septimius Cassianus, a standard-bearer in the IV Hispana Legion, to Mithras, likely during the late 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-01300143.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicated to Nemesis.

EDCS-01300144.translation: To Nemesis Augusta, Acutius, servant of the state, [...]icio [...]
EDCS-01300144.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicated to Nemesis Augusta by Acutius, a public servant.

EDCS-01300147.text_edition: \n Neptuno Augusto sacrum Lucius Titius Felix IIIIIIvir dedit\n
EDCS-01300147.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus; Lucius Titius Felix, a member of the college of six, dedicated it.
EDCS-01300147.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Neptune Augustus by Lucius Titius Felix, a Six-Man, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01300149.translation: Calpurnia Zosime fulfilled her vow to Serapis and Isis.
EDCS-01300149.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Calpurnia Zosime to the gods Serapis and Isis, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300151.translation: Sacred to Silvanus; Marcus Iulius Festus willingly dedicated it, as deserved.
EDCS-01300151.summary: This inscription records a willing dedication to Silvanus by Marcus Iulius Festus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300152.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus; Titus Campanius Cerialis fulfilled his vow willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-01300152.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Titus Campanius Cerialis to Silvanus Augustus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300153.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus, in honor of Quintus Claudius...
EDCS-01300153.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus in honor of Quintus Claudius, with the dedicant's name missing, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300155.translation: Sacred to Hope Augustus; Gaius Aelius Cupitus fulfilled his vow willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-01300155.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Gaius Aelius Cupitus to Hope Augustus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300157.text_edition: \n Terrae Matri Caius Baebius Cai filius Palatina Antiochianus equo publico decurio Aquileiae et Caius Baebius Antiochus IIIIIIvir Aquileiae ius IIII liberorum consecutus ex voto\n
EDCS-01300157.translation: To Mother Earth, Gaius Baebius Antiochianus, son of Gaius Baebius, a decurion of Aquileia with public horse status, and Gaius Baebius Antiochus, a Six-Man of Aquileia who attained the rights of having six children, according to a vow.
EDCS-01300157.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Gaius Baebius Antiochianus and Gaius Baebius Antiochus to Terra Mater (Mother Earth) in Aquileia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300161.translation: ...Aebutia Gratilliana fulfilled her vow willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-01300161.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Aebutia Gratilliana, with the deity unspecified and the beginning missing, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300162.translation: ...of Aquileia, the freedman Encolpus, freedman of Verus the younger, for his children Vera and Severianus.
EDCS-01300162.summary: This inscription records the freedman Encolpus, freedman of Verus the younger, dedicating something for his children Vera and Severianus in Aquileia, with the recipient and purpose missing, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300164.translation: Attius Primus willingly and deservedly paid his sacred vow.
EDCS-01300164.summary: This is a dedication recording Attius Primus fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-01300166.translation: ...for restored health, Tiberius Claudius Celadus, son of Publius Aristoclis, fulfilled his vow willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-01300166.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Claudius Celadus fulfilling a vow for restored health, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01300167.translation: To the sacred grove. In memory of his patron, Manius Coelius Phoebus, Manius Coelius Trophimus gave this offering.
EDCS-01300167.summary: This inscription records a votive offering dedicated by Manius Coelius Trophimus in memory of his patron, Manius Coelius Phoebus, likely a private dedication.

EDCS-01300168.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Demetrius, fulfilling a vow, possibly on a small altar or monument.

EDCS-01300169.translation: The birthday of Eventus, on the 18th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01300169.summary: This inscription records the birthday of Eventus, likely an anniversary marker or personal memorial.

EDCS-01300170.translation: Flavinae [?], daughter of [?], of the family of [?], set this up.
EDCS-01300170.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Flavinae, with incomplete dedicatory information indicating a familial relationship.

EDCS-01300171.translation: Florus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300171.summary: This inscription records a personal vow fulfilled by Florus, likely on a religious monument.

EDCS-01300175.translation: Lucius Patronius Severus, freedman of Lucius, a member of the college of IIIIvir, at Aquileia.
EDCS-01300175.summary: This inscription records the name and office (IIIIvir) of Lucius Patronius Severus, a freedman at Aquileia, likely on a public or honorary monument.

EDCS-01300176.translation: Philippus(?) and Nestoris(?) gave and dedicated this offering.
EDCS-01300176.summary: This inscription records a joint dedication of an offering by Philippus and Nestoris, with the names possibly being patron and freedman or a married couple.

EDCS-01300177.summary: This fragmentary inscription possibly records the name of a patron and a freedwoman, with incomplete details.

EDCS-01300178.translation: Plenius Atimetus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01300178.summary: This inscription records a personal vow fulfilled by Plenius Atimetus, likely on a religious monument.

EDCS-01300179.translation: Lucius Publilius(?) Eumelus and Septueia Meletine willingly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-01300179.summary: This inscription records a joint vow fulfilled by Lucius Publilius Eumelus and Septueia Meletine, possibly a couple or business partners.

EDCS-01300182.summary: This inscription is a fragment likely naming Lucius Titius, possibly part of a larger dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-01300183.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment recording a statement made by Titius Profuturus, a father, possibly related to a vow or order.

EDCS-01300184.translation: Ge and Fla, freedmen of Trofimus, gave this gift.
EDCS-01300184.summary: This inscription records a gift given by two freedmen, Ge and Fla, to their patron Trofimus.

EDCS-01300186.translation: [...] to Augustus(?) [...] Caius Volu[...], fulfilled [his] vow
EDCS-01300186.summary: This fragment indicates that Caius Volu[...], possibly in honor of Augustus, fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-01300195.translation: [...] Quintus [---]ontius fulfilled [his] vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01300195.summary: This inscription records Quintus [---]ontius fulfilling a vow, likely on a monument.

EDCS-01300204.translation: [To Antoniae], mother of Germanicus, mother of Germanicus Caesar
EDCS-01300204.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Antoniae, identifying her as the mother of Germanicus Caesar.

EDCS-01300221.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quinto alumno Saturninus Augusti nostri adiutor tabularii rationis patrimonii\n
EDCS-01300221.translation: To the departed spirits. Saturninus, tutor of our Augustus and assistant in the records office of the imperial patrimony [made this].
EDCS-01300221.summary: This is an epitaph for Saturninus, who held administrative positions related to the imperial treasury, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01300222.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titus Aelius Verecundus, freedman of the emperor, in charge of petitions, to his most excellent wife Magia Philete.
EDCS-01300222.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Magia Philete, dedicated by her husband Titus Aelius Verecundus, a high-ranking imperial freedman.

EDCS-01300223.translation: Celer Merypianus, freedman of the emperor, an accountant in the imperial treasury, to himself and to Chrysis, freedwoman of the emperor, his fellow-dweller.
EDCS-01300223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Celer Merypianus and Chrysis, who were fellow-dwellers and imperial freedmen with financial responsibilities.

EDCS-01300224.translation: To Tropianus, slave of Basso, Caesar's Augustan freedman. Gratus, his deputy, [made this monument] 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01300224.summary: This is a funerary monument for Tropianus, a slave of an imperial freedman, established by his deputy Gratus, likely from the 1st-2nd century AD.

EDCS-01300225.translation: Ulpia Narde made this for Hermerotes, slave of the Caesars, her well-deserving husband, in a purchased place of 8 feet in front and 15 feet of land.
EDCS-01300225.summary: This is a funerary monument for Hermerotes, a slave of the emperors, erected by his wife Ulpia Narde, specifying the dimensions of the purchased plot, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01300226.translation: To Secundus, slave of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus. Symphorianus, Tyrannus Felix, Valens, deputies, [made this].
EDCS-01300226.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Secundus, a slave of Emperor Claudius, erected by his deputies Symphorianus, Tyrannus Felix, and Valens, dating to the mid-1st century AD.

EDCS-01300227.translation: [To...]a[e] Veri[...], his most dutiful wife. Lucius Ammius Pollio, patron of the colony(?) of Aquileia(?), elected into the ranks of the imperial judges in Rome, having fulfilled municipal offices, curator of works and calendar, [made this] with his son Marcus Ammius Pollio.
EDCS-01300227.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Ammius Pollio and his son Marcus for his wife, detailing Pollio's distinguished career in Rome and local administration, possibly in Aquileia, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01300228.summary: This inscription records the name of Quintus Baienus Blassianus, likely from a funerary monument or a dedication, possibly in the late Roman period.

EDCS-01300229.text_edition: \n Rutiliae Marci Clementis Prisci filiae Priscae Sabinianae Caeserni Macedonis\n
EDCS-01300229.translation: To Prisca Sabiniana, daughter of Rutilia, wife of Marcius Clement, son of Priscus, and descendant of Caesernus Macedo.
EDCS-01300229.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Prisca Sabiniana, identifying her parentage and marital connections, possibly from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300230.text_edition: \n Tito Caesernio Statio Quinctio Macedoni Quinctiano consuli sodali Augustali curatori viae Appiae et alimentorum legato legionis X geminae piae fidelis comiti divi Hadriani per Orientem et Illyricum praetori inter cives et peregrinos tribuno plebis candidato comiti per Siciliam Africam Mauretaniam quaestori candidato tribuno laticlavio legionis XXX Ulpiae victricis triumviro aere auro argento flando feriundo patrono coloniae flamini decurioni Lucius Cervonius Hieronymus cliens\n
EDCS-01300230.translation: To Titus Caesernius Statius Quintius Macedo Quintianus, consul, Augustal sodalis, curator of the Appian Way and of the alimentary scheme, legate of the Tenth Legion Gemina Pia Fidelis, companion of the deified Hadrian in the East and Illyricum, praetor for citizens and foreigners, tribune of the plebs (candidate), companion through Sicily, Africa, and Mauretania, quaestor (candidate), laticlavian tribune of the Thirtieth Legion Ulpia Victrix, triumvir for minting bronze, gold, and silver, patron of the colony, and flamen; Lucius Cervonius Hieronymus, his client.
EDCS-01300230.summary: This is an extensive senatorial career inscription for Titus Caesernius Statius Quintius Macedo Quintianus, detailing his numerous high-ranking political and military offices, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300234.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Tiberi filio Palatina Rufo Statio Macedoni Xviro stlitibus iudicandis tribuno militum decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-01300234.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Rufus Statius Macedo, son of Tiberius, of the Palatine tribe, Xvir for settling lawsuits, military tribune, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01300234.summary: This inscription honors Tiberius Claudius Rufus Statius Macedo, detailing his civic and military roles, including being a member of the Xvirate and a military tribune, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300235.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Tiberi filio Palatina Secundino Lucio Statio Macedoni primo pilo legionis IIII Flaviae felicis tribuno cohortis I vigilum tribuno cohortis XI urbanae tribuno cohortis IX praetoriae primo pilo iterum praefecto legionis II Traianae fortis procuratori Augusti XX hereditatium procuratori provinciarum Lugudunensis et Aquitaniae a rationibus Augusti praefecto nnae flamini divi Vespasiani Publius Cassidius Fortunatus IIIIIIvir et Augustalis amico locus datus decreto decurionum procuratori provinciarum Lugdunensis et Aquitaniae a rationibus Augusti praefecto annonae Lucius Saufeius Iulianus amico optimo\n
EDCS-01300235.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Secundinus, son of Tiberius, of the Palatine tribe, to Lucius Statius Macedo, first-rank centurion of the Fourth Legion Flavia Felix, tribune of the First Cohort of Vigiles, tribune of the Eleventh Urban Cohort, tribune of the Ninth Praetorian Cohort, first-rank centurion again, prefect of the Second Legion Traiana Fortis, procurator of Augustus for inheritance taxes (XX hereditatium), procurator of the provinces of Lugudunensis and Aquitania, a rationibus (administrator of finances) of Augustus, prefect of the grain supply; Publius Cassidius Fortunatus, IIIIvir and Augustalis, friend, given a place by decree of the decurions; to Lucius Saufeius Iulianus, procurator of the provinces of Lugudunensis and Aquitania, a rationibus Augusti, prefect of the grain supply, his most excellent friend.
EDCS-01300235.summary: This is a dedication honoring Tiberius Claudius Secundinus and Lucius Statius Macedo for their extensive military and administrative careers, with the inscription itself commissioned by Publius Cassidius Fortunatus and Lucius Saufeius Iulianus, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300237.text_edition: \n Caio Oetio Luci filio Oufentina Rixae tribuno militum praefecto equitum procuratori Tiberi Claudi Caesaris Augusti Caius Oetius Rixa Gellianus sua pecunia\n
EDCS-01300237.translation: To Gaius Oetius Rixa Gellianus, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe, military tribune, prefect of the cavalry, procurator of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus, at his own expense.
EDCS-01300237.summary: This inscription is a dedication made at his own expense by Gaius Oetius Rixa Gellianus, detailing his military and procuratorial appointments, likely from the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-01300238.text_edition: \n Caius Quinctius Cai filius Velina Certus Poblicius Marcellus consul augur legatus divi Hadriani provinciarum Syriae et Germaniae superioris ornamentis triumphalibus\n
EDCS-01300238.translation: To Gaius Quinctius Certus Poblicius Marcellus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, consul, augur, legate of the deified Hadrian in the provinces of Syria and Upper Germany, with triumphal decorations.
EDCS-01300238.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Quinctius Certus Poblicius Marcellus, listing his high offices including consul, augur, and legate, and noting he received triumphal decorations, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300248.translation: Titus Vettidius Lemnus, freedman of Procula, IIIIvir Augustalis, clerk to a consul, clerk to a praetor twice, made this himself while alive for himself and his family: Vettidia Hellas, freedwoman of Titus, daughter; Vettidia Tertia, freedwoman of Titus, wife; Vinisia Festa, granddaughter of the latter; Lucius Vinisius Lycambas, freedman of Lucius, IIIIvir of Tergeste, clerk to a consul. Herennia Avita, daughter of Publius, patroness of the cult of the Genius of Aquileia, gave this for preservation while alive. // Herennia Avita, daughter of Publius, patroness of the cult of the Genius of Aquileia, gave this for preservation while alive.
EDCS-01300248.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and a dedication for the cult of the Genius of Aquileia, commissioned by Titus Vettidius Lemnus and Herennia Avita, detailing family members and civic roles, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300250.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Cai filio Fabia Agathopo flamini patrono coloniae IIIIviro iure dicundo quinquennali ordo Augustalium et IIIIIIvirorum ob honorifica merita eius et in exhibendis populo voluptatibus largum nitorem\n
EDCS-01300250.translation: To Gaius Julius Agathopus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, flamen, patron of the colony, IIIIvir for dispensing justice, quinquennalis, for his honorary merits and for the abundant splendor in his public entertainments, the ordo of the Augustales and the IIIIviri.
EDCS-01300250.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Julius Agathopus for his public service and generosity, commissioned by the local elite (Augustales and IIIIviri), likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01300252.translation: To Lucius Rufius Honoratus(?), who lived 3 years, 3 months, and [X] days; Lucius Rufius [and] Rufia Septimina, parents, to their sweetest son. Lucius Rufius, IIIIvir for dispensing justice, and Rufia Septimina.
EDCS-01300252.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Lucius Rufius Honoratus(?), with his parents identified and Lucius Rufius noted as a IIIIvir, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300253.translation: The dimensions of the plot of Gaius Titus Rufus, son of Gaius, one of the four magistrates with aedilician power: 24 feet in front, 16 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01300253.summary: An inscription recording the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to a magistrate, likely for a tomb or building, with dimensions of 24 feet (frontage) and 16 feet (depth).

EDCS-01300254.translation: To Venerius Io, of the guild of craftsmen of Aquileia, the four magistrates with the power of judging, [---]mos, most distinguished.
EDCS-01300254.summary: A dedication from the guild of craftsmen of Aquileia to a magistrate, likely honored for his distinguished service.

EDCS-01300263.translation: [---] who held the office of aedile, patron of the guild of fabric workers, Donatus, who held the office of aedile twice and was an Augustalis, [---] Pyrrhus, his freedman.
EDCS-01300263.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the career of an individual named Donatus, who held multiple public and guild offices.

EDCS-01300265.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely refers to a high-ranking official, possibly a prefect of justice.

EDCS-01300266.summary: This is a simple inscription likely from a tombstone or monument, identifying Gaius Lucilius, son of Gaius.

EDCS-01300268.translation: Aius Iuna, Arruntius Cassianus, and others, according to custom, were present for the repayment, as they decreed regarding what was repaid and what would be repaid in the future. Our colleague, [---]m, and [---]tii, and [---]veri, by their patriotism and industry.
EDCS-01300268.summary: A record of a collegium's decision regarding the repayment of funds, possibly for a public project or inheritance, highlighting the contributions of its members.

EDCS-01300269.translation: Made by L. libertus Philus, freedwoman of the colonist Publius Petronius Sulla, Publius Petronius Primus, Persaea, and Puscula.
EDCS-01300269.summary: An inscription detailing the makers of a monument, including freedmen and freedwomen, possibly related to the Petronii family.

EDCS-01300273.translation: [---] Stephen(?), actor of the sums(?) of the municipality of Aquileia.
EDCS-01300273.summary: This fragmentary inscription identifies an official named Stephen, likely an accountant or administrator for the municipality of Aquileia.

EDCS-01300274.text_edition: \n Lucio Appuleio Maximiano decurioni Aquileiae heredes faciundum curaverunt\n
EDCS-01300274.translation: Lucius Appuleius Maximianus, decurion of Aquileia, his heirs had this made.
EDCS-01300274.summary: A funerary inscription stating that the heirs of Lucius Appuleius Maximianus, a decurion of Aquileia, commissioned his monument.

EDCS-01300275.translation: The site of the monument of Titus Calpurnius Flaccus, a decurion, 16 feet in front, 24 feet in the rear.
EDCS-01300275.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land for the monument of Titus Calpurnius Flaccus, a decurion.

EDCS-01300276.text_edition: \n Petillia Quinti filia Modesta uxor Caius Mutillius Cai filius decurio Aquileiensis sibi et uxori fecit\n
EDCS-01300276.translation: Petillia Modesta, daughter of Quintus, wife of Gaius Mutillius, son of Gaius, decurion of Aquileia, made this for himself and his wife.
EDCS-01300276.summary: A funerary inscription for a married couple, Petillia Modesta and Gaius Mutillius, a decurion of Aquileia.

EDCS-01300279.translation: Habilis the public official made this for himself and for Prima.
EDCS-01300279.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that Habilis, a public official, commissioned this monument for himself and Prima.

EDCS-01300281.translation: To the departed spirits. Aemilia Fuscula to her most excellent husband, Quintus Aquilius Primus Palatina, who had held all the offices in his homeland, and was flamen Augusti of the province of Narbonensis.
EDCS-01300281.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her husband, a prominent figure who held local offices and served as a provincial flamen.

EDCS-01300282.translation: Lucius Poblicius Anteros, freedman of Lucius; Publius Postumius Felix, freedman of Publius; Publius Oppius Atticus, freedman of Publius; Capito, slave of Iulius Nason; Urbanus, son of Titus Helvius, slave; Primus, slave of Titus Voconius, willingly gave as magistrates.
EDCS-01300282.summary: An inscription listing several individuals, including freedmen and slaves, who served as magistrates and made a dedication.

EDCS-01300284.translation: The location of the monument of Tiberius Claudius Germanus and Iulia Procina: 42 feet in front, 32 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01300284.summary: An inscription marking the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Tiberius Claudius Germanus and Iulia Procina, likely for a tomb.

EDCS-01300286.translation: Tiberius Claudius Germanus and Iulia Procne, freedwoman of Quintus, made this while alive for their son Tiberius Claudius Proculus, aged 27 years, and for his mother Iulia, and for Marcus [---]vius Adjutorius, a VIvir.
EDCS-01300286.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by parents for their deceased son and for other family members and an associate, possibly indicating a familial burial plot or a shared monument.

EDCS-01300287.translation: For Quintus Albius Auctus, freedman of Quintus, a VIvir, and for Maia Severa, aged about 22 years. Maia (?) made this while alive.
EDCS-01300287.summary: This funerary inscription records the names and ages of Quintus Albius Auctus, a freedman and VIvir, and Maia Severa, with Maia (?) identified as the dedicator.

EDCS-01300288.translation: To the memory of Albius Vitalis, a VIvir. Gaius Vennonius Primus, his friend.
EDCS-01300288.summary: This inscription is a memorial dedicated by a friend to Albius Vitalis, who held the civic office of VIvir.

EDCS-01300289.translation: [---]DIO G[---] for Annius Primigenius (?), son and freedman, a VIvir, and for Annia PE[---], freedwoman of Lucius (LL), and for Annius N[---], and for Annius F[---], and for Lucius Aterius N[---], for his freedmen and freedwomen, ordered to be made by will. In front, 21 feet.
EDCS-01300289.summary: This inscription, likely part of a funerary monument, details the beneficiaries of a will, including a freedman who was a VIvir, and specifies the dimensions of the front of the property.

EDCS-01300290.translation: Lucius Apponius Diomedes, freedman, and Lucius Apponius Quadratus, freedman, Temanti's freedman, and Apponia Aletia, Diomedes' freedwoman, and Lucius Apponius Tem[---], Diomedes' freedman, ordered these to be made as sexvirs.
EDCS-01300290.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument for Lucius Apponius Diomedes and other members of his family, including freedmen, by family members, who also held the position of sexvir.

EDCS-01300291.text_edition: \n Tito Caesernio Titi liberto Alypo IIIIIIviro Augustali Ionicus libertus IIIIIIvir\n
EDCS-01300291.translation: Ionicus, freedman and also a member of the Augustales, erected this for Titus Caesernius Alypus, freedman and member of the Augustales.
EDCS-01300291.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Ionicus, a freedman and Augustalis, for Titus Caesernius Alypus, also a freedman and Augustalis.

EDCS-01300292.translation: Sextus Caesernius Cedrus, a sexvir, and Caesernia Prima, freedwoman of Sextus, erected this in honor of their patron Sextus Caesernius Libanus, alive, and for their friends, alive: Caesernia Iridis, daughter of Caesernia, alive; Caesernia Iucunda, alive; Lucius Plancius Antas, friend, alive; Sextus Caesernius Diodotus, fellow freedman, alive; Caesernia Venusta, freedwoman, alive; and for their freedmen and freedwomen, living.
EDCS-01300292.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the erection of a tomb by Sextus Caesernius Cedrus and his wife for their patron, friends, and freedmen, indicating familial and social connections within a community.

EDCS-01300294.translation: Aulus Fabius Liccaeus, freedman of Aulus, a VIvir.
EDCS-01300294.summary: This inscription records the name and civic position of Aulus Fabius Liccaeus, a freedman who was a VIvir.

EDCS-01300296.translation: Sixteenth decurial official, Eutychia, most unfortunate.
EDCS-01300296.summary: This inscription mentions Eutychia, who held the rank of a sixteenth decurial official, and is inscribed with a lament of her misfortune.

EDCS-01300297.translation: Lucius Gavius Licinus, freedman, a sexvir.
EDCS-01300297.summary: This inscription records the name and position of Lucius Gavius Licinus, a freedman who was a sexvir.

EDCS-01300298.translation: To Fabricia Severina, aged 16 years and 10 months. Hermes, a member of the Augustales and of the sexvirs, and his wife Sentia Severa, parents, have given this place. From the Statii.
EDCS-01300298.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fabricia Severina, erected by her parents, who were prominent members of local religious and civic organizations (Augustales and sexvirs).

EDCS-01300299.translation: Gaius Julius Primigenius, decemvir, and Valeria Syrtis, freedwoman of a woman, made this alive for themselves and for Gaius Julius Alexas, Valeria Optata, Valeria Salvia, Valerius Vitulus, and Statia Nymphe.
EDCS-01300299.summary: A dedication made by Gaius Julius Primigenius and Valeria Syrtis for themselves and five other individuals, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-01300300.translation: Lucius Junius Abscantus placed this for the 16-year-old Agelastus and Manlia Spectata, while alive.
EDCS-01300300.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Junius Abscantus for Agelastus and Manlia Spectata, dating to the time of their lives.

EDCS-01300302.translation: Gaius Paccius Calamus, son of a freedman of Gaius, decemvir.
EDCS-01300302.summary: An inscription recording the name and office of Gaius Paccius Calamus, a decemvir.

EDCS-01300303.translation: To Gaius Pomponius Modestus, sixteenth decurial official, Gaius Pomponius Chresimus.
EDCS-01300303.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Pomponius Chresimus to Gaius Pomponius Modestus, who was a sixteenth decurial official.

EDCS-01300304.summary: A fragmented inscription honoring Lucius Titius, who held the office of decemvir.

EDCS-01300305.translation: Gaius Vennonius Harpastus, freedman of Gaius, a decemvir, made this alive for Domitia Longina, daughter of Sextus, his wife.
EDCS-01300305.summary: A funerary monument made by Gaius Vennonius Harpastus for his wife Domitia Longina.

EDCS-01300307.translation: To Apseudetus, freedman and sixteenth decurial official, his slaves having died: [one] of XX years, Apseudetus [one] of XX years, Vano [one] of XXV years.
EDCS-01300307.summary: This inscription records the ages of Apseudetus (a freedman and sixteenth decurial official) and two slaves, Vano and another named Apseudetus, noting the death of the slaves.

EDCS-01300311.translation: [---] son of Lucius [---] [---] [---] decemvir [---] [---] to Iulia Donace, freedwoman of Sextus, here [---]
EDCS-01300311.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription for Iulia Donace, a freedwoman, mentioning a decemvir.

EDCS-01300322.translation: Of Lucius Decidius // Of Publius Metellus // [Location? ---] number LIIII, location I, wedge [---]
EDCS-01300322.summary: An inscription that appears to record seating arrangements or plot assignments within a public venue, possibly a theater or amphitheater.

EDCS-01300329.translation: Lucius Pescennius Triptolemus erected the Aquila and brought in the water.
EDCS-01300329.summary: An inscription recording Lucius Pescennius Triptolemus's act of erecting a standard (Aquila) and installing a water supply.

EDCS-01300336.translation: Lucius Avillius Utilis, decurion of the guild of artisans, for himself and his wife Salaria Modesta.
EDCS-01300336.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Avillius Utilis, a decurion in the guild of artisans, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-01300337.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Caedicius Paris, who gave himself to the guild of artisans while alive, one thousand denarii, and of Marcus Antonius Menander. Marcus Antonius Alcimus and Caedicia Quinta made this for the deserving, while alive, and for themselves. // Marcus Antonius Alcimus for Gaius Caedicius Paternus, his friend.
EDCS-01300337.summary: A funerary monument with multiple dedications and inscriptions, including a donation to a guild and a dedication to a friend.

EDCS-01300339.translation: Gentil[ius?], Fid[ius?], Gaius Vibius Ap[tus?], Vibia Po[lia?], Vultilia P[--].
EDCS-01300339.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing names, likely from a tomb or funerary monument.

EDCS-01300341.translation: Consecrated to the spirits of the departed by the sacred guild of Mars. Gaius Licinius Onesimus, Licinia Clymene, Gaius Titius Peregrinus son of Gaius, Barbia Amanda freedwoman of Lucius son of Lucius, Goppia Tertia daughter of Sextus, Gaius Caesonius Aprilis, Fortunatus, Publius Mutilius Aprio, Gaius Marcinius Eupras, Gaius Helvius Synecdemus, Lucius Allius Omuncio, Gaius Baebius Clario, Marcus Calidius Marcellus, Fortunatus, Aulus Barbius Zmaragdus the doctor. Whoever was a debtor colleague, if he dies and is buried in a tomb, or if he leaves alive and enters this place, shall not be buried.
EDCS-01300341.summary: This inscription records the burial arrangements and membership of a guild of Mars, likely from the Roman Imperial period, specifying exclusion for debtor colleagues.

EDCS-01300342.translation: Place granted by decree of the decurions. Montanius(?) Secundus, Primigenius, Babia, freedwoman of Lucius, Callitiche, Sextus Tesitanus Phoebus, Valens, Gaius Julius Chius, Gavia Clymene, Titus Caesernius Ursio, Lucius Metonius Ampliatus, Gaius Vettius Linus, son of Lucius, Gaius Levissatius Sabinus, Thiasus, freedman of Tiberius Claudius Cypaerus, Lucius Plotus Restitutus, Aulus Gavius Primigenius, Arvenius Primigenius, Arvenia Vitalis, Petronius Celadus, Blandonia Tertulla, Blandonius Narcissus, Titia Tertia, Plotia Procne, Corinthius Longinus, Fabius Caritho, Atimetus, Julius Felix Lucanus, Epicomus, son of Dapnius.
EDCS-01300342.summary: This inscription lists a large number of individuals, possibly landowners or residents, to whom a specific place was granted by a decree of the decurions.

EDCS-01300344.translation: Site of the monument. Genutus Salvius. In the front, 80 feet; in the rear, 120 feet. Four epitaphs. Marcus T. C. dedicated.
EDCS-01300344.summary: This inscription specifies land dimensions and the number of epitaphs for a monument site, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300345.translation: By permission of the guild. Titania Charis, freedwoman of Gaius, made this for herself while alive, and for her most devoted husband, Sextus Teius Ianuarius; for Quintus Catabronius Martialis, freedman of a woman; for Titania Secundina; for Menander; for Persicus.
EDCS-01300345.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Titania Charis for herself and family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300346.translation: Marcus Vibius [--], Manlia [--], Gaius Mamilius Lucifer, Lucius Cornelius Aprio, Publius Varius [Aug]ctus, Marcus Acellius [Feli]x(?), Sextus Eppius [He]rmes, Claudia Prepusa, Tosia Gemela, Caesia Secunda, Babuleia Hyllis, Caesernia Hal[lis(?)] [--].
EDCS-01300346.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing numerous personal names, likely from a tomb or funerary monument of the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300347.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to mention a group (possibly firemen or textile workers) and a person named Victor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300354.translation: Eures, freedman of Lucius Junius Gratus, aged 22 years [--].
EDCS-01300354.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the name and age of Eures, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300355.translation: Consecrated to the spirits of the departed. For Dionysius, the assistant. Processus, the steward.
EDCS-01300355.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Dionysius, an assistant, by his steward Processus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300357.translation: [--] of Mansuetus, freedman, Primigenius, an engraver and silversmith, and for Pullia Merope [--].
EDCS-01300357.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions an engraver and silversmith named Primigenius and Pullia Merope, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300358.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Lucius Herennius Mani filius faber aciarius Manio Herennio Cai filio patri Coeliae Cai filiae Quartae matri Caio Herennio Mani filio fratri Publio Herennio Mani filio fratri Herenniae Mani filiae Tertullae sorori Caeciliae Quinti libertae Primae coniugi Herenniae Primigeniae libertae Herenniae Calliste libertae Lucio Fabricio Verecundo Fabriciae Luci libertae Venustae Iulio Pancarpo amicis Aulo Petronio Laeto Vitrico Asiniae Fuscae coniugi carissimae nnorum XXXI mensium VII dierum X Lucius Herennius Luci filius Vitalis libertis libertabusque\n
EDCS-01300358.translation: Lucius Herennius Vitalis, son of Lucius, freedman, made this while alive for his father Manius Herennius, son of Caius, a smith; for his mother Coelia Quartis, daughter of Caius; for his brother Caius Herennius; for his brother Publius Herennius; for his sister Herennia Tertulla; for his wife Caecilia Prima, freedwoman of Quintus; for Herennia Calliste, freedwoman; for Lucius Fabricius Verecundus; for Venusta, freedwoman of Lucius Fabricius; for Julius Pancarpus; for his friends Aulus Petronius Laetus and Vitricus; for Asinia Fusca, his dearest wife, aged 31 years, 7 months, and 10 days. Lucius Herennius Vitalis, son of Lucius, for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01300358.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription by Lucius Herennius Vitalis for his family, wife, friends, and freedpersons, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300359.translation: Publius Cattius Salvius, son of Publius, made this monument while alive for himself and all his relatives, and for his wife Ofelia Tertia, daughter of Caius. Cattia Festa, daughter of Publius, and Publius Cattius Gratus, son of Publius, and Caius Cattius Tertius, son of Publius, and for their freedmen and freedwomen. The monument's space measures 16 feet in every direction. Naval craftsman.
EDCS-01300359.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Publius Cattius Salvius, a naval craftsman, for himself, his family, and his freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-01300362.translation: Lucius Cantius Fructus, freedman of Lucius, a merchant, lies here. Lucius Cantius Apollonius, freedman of Verus.
EDCS-01300362.summary: A tombstone recording two individuals, Lucius Cantius Fructus and Lucius Cantius Apollonius, both identified as merchants or freedmen, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300364.translation: Fructus, freedman of Crispus, a merchant, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his partner Minicia Potita, freedwoman of Caius; and for his mother Hilara, freedwoman of Crispus; and for his sister Crispia Vitali; and for his sister Crispia Procula; and for his household slave Caius Minicius Decembrius; and for his mother Helpidia, freedwoman of Caius. Placidus, freedman and also heir, saw to its construction.
EDCS-01300364.summary: A funerary monument established by will by Fructus, a merchant and freedman of Crispus, for himself, his partner, family members, a household slave, and his mother, with his freedman heir overseeing its construction.

EDCS-01300365.translation: Lucius Valerius Primus, a merchant, dealer in pearls, from Rome.
EDCS-01300365.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Valerius Primus as a pearl merchant from Rome.

EDCS-01300366.translation: To Aptas, freedwoman of Galgestia, the wet-nurse, from Tertulla.
EDCS-01300366.summary: A dedication to a wet-nurse, Aptas, by Tertulla, likely a personal token of affection or gratitude.

EDCS-01300368.translation: To Diogenes the teacher from Nebridius.
EDCS-01300368.summary: A dedication to Diogenes, identified as a teacher, by Nebridius, possibly a student or patron.

EDCS-01300371.translation: ] Varius, freedman of Lucius [Mi]a, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and Publius? [...] Aric[...] Exa[...], freedman of Quintus, an ointment maker, and for his freedmen [...]. Onome. The monument's space is 16 feet in front and [...] feet in the ground.
EDCS-01300371.summary: A funerary monument inscription where Varius, a freedman and likely an ointment maker, makes provisions for himself, other individuals, and his freedmen, with burial plot dimensions specified.

EDCS-01300372.translation: Arkaia Tertia, daughter of Caius, wife. Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, mother. Lucius Alfius Statius, son of Lucius, alive, for himself and his family, freedmen, and freedwomen. Statia Alfia, daughter of Lucius, sister. Secunda Caesia, daughter of Marcus, sister. Galla Caesia, daughter of Marcus, sister. The plot measures 16 feet in front and 20 feet in the ground; this monument will not bind the heir.
EDCS-01300372.summary: A family tomb with a specified plot size, indicating it is not inheritable, mentioning various family members including wives, mothers, sisters, and the primary builder Lucius Alfius Statius.

EDCS-01300375.summary: This fragment of an inscription likely records a transaction involving Tyrian goods measured by weight.

EDCS-01300376.translation: [...] of my loved ones, for their freedmen and freedwomen. In front 8 feet, in the ground 4 feet. This monument will not bind the heir.
EDCS-01300376.summary: A funerary inscription with dimensions for the plot, stating it is for freedmen and freedwomen and is not inheritable.

EDCS-01300385.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aelius [...]
EDCS-01300385.summary: A funerary inscription beginning with a dedication to the gods of the underworld, mentioning the name Aelius, with the text incomplete.

EDCS-01300387.translation: To Caius Aelius Silenus, son of Caius [...]
EDCS-01300387.summary: An incomplete dedication to Caius Aelius Silenus, son of Caius, possibly a funerary or honorific inscription.

EDCS-01300388.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Aelius V[---] made this for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-01300388.summary: A funerary dedication for the maker and their descendants, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01300390.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription, possibly recording the name of a son and a father, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300391.translation: To the departed spirits. Aelia Suabis [dedicated this] to her most sweet son, Sempronius Mercurius.
EDCS-01300391.summary: A funerary dedication from a mother to her son, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300392.translation: To Titus(?) Aemilius(?) [---], son of Titus(?) [---]
EDCS-01300392.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely recording a patronymic and filiation, possibly funerary, from the imperial period.

EDCS-01300393.translation: [---]a, daughter, to her most sweet son [---]
EDCS-01300393.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication from a mother to her son, from the imperial period.

EDCS-01300394.translation: To Publius Aethrius Rufus, son of Caius, [for his] father, and to Lollia Posilla, daughter of Quintus, [for her] mother, Caius Aethrius Hister, son of Publius, made this while alive. // The dimensions of the monument: 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01300394.summary: A dedication made by a son, Caius Aethrius Hister, for his deceased parents and brother, also specifying the dimensions of the monument, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300397.translation: To the departed spirits. To Agilioni [---]
EDCS-01300397.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription, likely a dedication to an individual named Agilioni, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300398.translation: Lucius Aius, son of Lucius Aius, son of Lucius Aius, son of Aius Priscus, sister (?) we carry.
EDCS-01300398.summary: This inscription repeats the patronymic of Lucius Aius multiple times, possibly for emphasis or legal clarity, and mentions a sister.

EDCS-01300399.summary: This inscription, though fragmentary, mentions Marcus Aius and the word 'adversus', suggesting a legal or confrontational context.

EDCS-01300401.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription beginning with the name Quintus Aius.

EDCS-01300403.translation: Caius Albius Lucanus, son of Caius, made this while alive for himself and for Plenia Tertulla, daughter of Titus, his wife, and for Caius Albius Iucundus, his father, and for Naevia Polla, daughter of Lucius, his mother. [---] Cn. Caepario Maximo [---]
EDCS-01300403.summary: A funerary dedication made by Caius Albius Lucanus for himself, his wife, his parents, and possibly another individual, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300404.translation: To the departed spirits. Albia Optata made this for Gnaeus Albius Optatus.
EDCS-01300404.summary: A funerary dedication from a daughter to her father, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300407.translation: Alcimus, son of Ieronis, [made this] for Marcia Dioclis, daughter of Marcia. Domitius, son of Alcimus, made this while alive.
EDCS-01300407.summary: An inscription recording the erection of a monument by Alcimus for Marcia, and also by Domitius, son of Alcimus, likely a father-son relationship, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-01300408.summary: This inscription records the name Alexander(?), possibly as a dedication or as part of a larger text.

EDCS-01300409.translation: Plotia Pothina, freedwoman of Plotia, made this for herself and her own, and for Plotia Prima, daughter of Quintus, her patroness. Also for Lucius Alfius Iucundus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-01300409.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Plotia Pothina for herself, her family, and her patroness, and also mentioning Lucius Alfius Iucundus.

EDCS-01300410.translation: Lucius Allius Auctus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, his wife, his freedmen and freedwomen, and for his patroness Barbia Nicini, freedwoman of Aulus, wife of the freedman. Also for Allia Fausta, freedwoman of Lucius, and Postumia Augis, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-01300410.summary: This is a funerary epitaph established by Lucius Allius Auctus for himself and his family, including his patroness.

EDCS-01300414.summary: This inscription records the maker of a monument, Amaranthus, a freedman.

EDCS-01300416.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or epitaph for a person named Firminus, possibly associated with the Amnii family.

EDCS-01300417.translation: For Publius Ampius Marinus and Ampia Amanda, freedwoman of Publius. Marcus Licinius Marcellus [granted] the burial place, extending sixteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-01300417.summary: This inscription records a grant of burial space by Marcus Licinius Marcellus for Publius Ampius Marinus and Ampia Amanda.

EDCS-01300420.translation: Annea Helpis gave the place, an unhappy mother.
EDCS-01300420.summary: This inscription records Annea Helpis granting a burial place, with a note of her grief.

EDCS-01300421.translation: Of Titus Annius Secundus, freedman of Titus, and of Eppia Secunda, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-01300421.summary: This inscription records the names of Titus Annius Secundus, a freedman, and Eppia Secunda, likely related to him, possibly as a spouse or family member.

EDCS-01300424.translation: To the departed spirits. Hail Antestia Marciane, to be remembered forever, who lived 12 years, 1 month, and 25 days. Marcus Antistius Marcianus and Vergilia Fortunata, parents, for their sweetest daughter.
EDCS-01300424.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antestia Marciane, set up by her parents, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-01300426.summary: This is a dedication to Tito Antonio VENRI.

EDCS-01300427.summary: This inscription simply records the name Antonia Firmina, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-01300428.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Plotia Callinice placed this for her dearest husband, Antonius Castus, who lived 36 years and 5 months, with whom she lived 11 years and 5 months.
EDCS-01300428.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonius Castus, set up by his wife Plotia Callinice, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300432.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Apinius Servandus and Calidia Felicula, while alive, made this for themselves, and for Gaius Calidius Servandus, and for Apinia Trophime, his freedwoman, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument will not follow an heir. The burial plot is 40 feet in front and [---] feet in the rear.
EDCS-01300432.summary: This is a funerary epitaph established by Marcus Apinius Servandus and Calidia Felicula for themselves and others, specifying burial plot dimensions and stipulating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-01300433.translation: To Aponia Eutychis, who lived 3 years, 11 months, and 20 days. Aponius Eutyches [dedicated this] to his dearest daughter.
EDCS-01300433.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Aponia Eutychis, set up by her father.

EDCS-01300434.translation: Marcus Apronius Terminalis made this for himself and for his sister Apronia Ingenua while he was alive.
EDCS-01300434.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Apronius Terminalis, who dedicated it to himself and his sister, likely indicating he died before her or wished to be buried with her.

EDCS-01300441.translation: Publius Aquileiensis Secundus made this for himself and for his wife Aspania Venusta, for Venustus his son, for Aspania Euprosyne his daughter, for Eutycia his freedwoman, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, while he was alive.
EDCS-01300441.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aquileiensis Secundus, who dedicated it for himself, his wife, children, and extended household, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01300442.translation: Aratria Galla, daughter of Gaius, [dedicated this] to Decumanus. [---]
EDCS-01300442.summary: A fragmentary inscription that likely records a dedication to a person named Decumanus by Aratria Galla, daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-01300443.translation: Caius Dio, freedman of a woman, made this for himself and for his wife Ammiadis, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-01300443.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Dio, a freedman, who dedicated it for himself and his wife while alive, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300444.translation: Clarus and Corinthus made this for their mother Aria Iucunda while she was alive.
EDCS-01300444.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aria Iucunda, dedicated by her sons Clarus and Corinthus while she was alive.

EDCS-01300445.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Statia Severa and Arrenius Alexander [dedicated this] to their most dutiful son, Arrenius Alexander, who lived 3 years, 5 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-01300445.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child named Arrenius Alexander, dedicated by his parents.

EDCS-01300449.summary: A fragmentary epitaph indicating that someone named Artillus placed this monument for himself.

EDCS-01300451.translation: To Marcus Artor [---] freedman of Hyginus. [---] to Artoria Teretis, freedwoman of Firmus. Flavonia Cerialis, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-01300451.summary: A complex funerary inscription that mentions multiple individuals and dedications, including Marcus Arto[--] and Artoria Teretis, with Flavonia Cerialis as the likely primary dedicator.

EDCS-01300454.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ascle, a freedman, who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-01300458.text_edition: \n Lucio Atilio Luci liberto Saturnino nnum XL domo Flavia Scarbantia interfecto a latronibus inrtusis sic Atilius Tertius frater et Statius Onesimus amico locus gratuitum datum ab Clodia Tertia\n
EDCS-01300458.translation: Lucius Atilius Saturninus, freedman of Lucius, aged 40, from Flavia, was killed by bandits in [---]. Thus, his brother Atilius Tertius and his friend Statius Onesimus [dedicated this]. The place was given free of charge by Clodia Tertia.
EDCS-01300458.summary: A funerary inscription recording the violent death of Lucius Atilius Saturninus and dedicated by his brother and friend, with the land provided by Clodia Tertia.

EDCS-01300460.text_edition: \n Attiariae Ianuariae quae vixit annos XXI menses Quintus Attiarius Septiminus sorori dulcissimae\n
EDCS-01300460.translation: To Attiaria Ianuaria, who lived 21 years, 5 months. From her brother, Quintus Attiarius Septiminus, to his sweetest sister.
EDCS-01300460.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Attiaria Ianuaria and dedicated by her brother, Quintus Attiarius Septiminus.

EDCS-01300462.translation: Marcus Attius Facundus, freedman of a woman, made this while alive for himself and his family, and for Attia Gemellina, daughter of Spurius, aged 20 years.
EDCS-01300462.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Attius Facundus for himself, his family, and Attia Gemellina, possibly his wife or daughter.

EDCS-01300463.translation: Gaius Aufidius Hilario, freedman of Gaius. Aufidia, freedwoman of Gaius. [---]
EDCS-01300463.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Gaius Aufidius Hilario and Aufidia, possibly his wife, both freedpeople.

EDCS-01300465.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Avillius PVD.

EDCS-01300466.translation: To his most innocent and most unfortunate sister. [---]tinus Avitus [---]
EDCS-01300466.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to an unnamed sister by Avitus, possibly named [---]tinus Avitus.

EDCS-01300467.translation: To Gaius Aulus Vitalis, freedman of Titus. To Aria Iucunda, freedwoman of Aria. Common space. This monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-01300467.summary: A funerary monument likely recording two individuals, Gaius Aulus Vitalis and Aria Iucunda, and stating that the property is not inheritable.
