EDCS-01300468.translation: Marcus Aurelius M[---], who [---]. To Severia Vet[---]. Aur[elius?] Pon[---]
EDCS-01300468.summary: A highly fragmented inscription that may be funerary or dedicatory, mentioning Marcus Aurelius and Severia.

EDCS-01300469.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Aurelius Magnus to Aphrodite, his most dutiful mother, aged 27 years.
EDCS-01300469.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Aphrodite by her son Marcus Aurelius Magnus.

EDCS-01300471.translation: [---]rae who lived [about X] years, 5 months [---] and with me [---]. For 10 years and 1 day without any quarrel. Aurelius Achillaeus made this for his [well-deserving wife].
EDCS-01300471.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by Aurelius Achillaeus to his wife, praising their harmonious long-term relationship.

EDCS-01300473.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Aurelius Avitus, aged [about X] years. R[---] RA[---]
EDCS-01300473.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Aurelius Avitus, mentioning his age.

EDCS-01300474.summary: This inscription records Aurelius H, possibly a dedication or a statement of presence, by an individual who is alive.

EDCS-01300477.translation: For Aurelia Chresteni, 7 years and 8 months old, Marcus Aurelius Ma [---] and Vibia Mariane placed this for their dearest daughter.
EDCS-01300477.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelia Chresteni, set up by her parents Marcus Aurelius Ma[---] and Vibia Mariane.

EDCS-01300478.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aurelia Eutychiane to Crescentinus, her most unfortunate pupil.
EDCS-01300478.summary: A funerary inscription from Aurelia Eutychiane dedicating the monument to her pupil, Crescentinus.

EDCS-01300479.translation: Titus Aurelius Laetus, the father, and Aurelia Flac, the mother, made this for their dearest daughter, Polydiana, [aged] 5 years and [---] days.
EDCS-01300479.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Polydiana, set up by her parents Titus Aurelius Laetus and Aurelia Flac.

EDCS-01300480.translation: Lucius Baebius Barba, son of Lucius, of the Herennia tribe, and Quincta, his wife.
EDCS-01300480.summary: This funerary epitaph identifies Lucius Baebius Barba and his wife Quincta.

EDCS-01300481.translation: To the dearest Baebius, son of [---], who lived 5 years and [---] months, and to the excellent husband Baebius [---].
EDCS-01300481.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication to a son named Baebius and a husband, also named Baebius.

EDCS-01300482.translation: Bones of Baebius Lucius, freedman. M[---]
EDCS-01300482.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Baebius Lucius, a freedman.

EDCS-01300483.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Lucius M Pu Bar.

EDCS-01300484.translation: Barbia Procula, daughter of Spurius, of the Barbia tribe, wife, made this while alive for Provinciae, her freedwoman. Monument: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the land area, for freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-01300484.summary: This funerary epitaph, set up by Barbia Procula for her freedwoman and for their descendants, includes property measurements for the monument.

EDCS-01300486.translation: To Lucius Barbius Marcion, patron, Lucius Barbius Philotimus made this while alive for himself, his relatives, freedmen, and freedwomen. Monument: 16 square feet in all directions.
EDCS-01300486.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication by Lucius Barbius Philotimus to his patron, Lucius Barbius Marcion, and specifies the monument's size.

EDCS-01300487.translation: Marcus Barbius Dromo for himself and his relatives, and for Albidia Nobili, his wife.
EDCS-01300487.summary: This funerary epitaph records Marcus Barbius Dromo dedicating a monument for himself, his family, and his wife.

EDCS-01300488.translation: To Marcus Barbius Dromon, Marcus Barbius Receptus made this while alive for Barbia Prima, freedwoman of Marcus, his mother, for Barbia Grata, freedwoman of Marcus, his sister, and for Allia Secunda, his wife.
EDCS-01300488.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication by Marcus Barbius Receptus to his mother, two sisters, and his wife, all deceased relatives.

EDCS-01300489.translation: The site of Marcus Barbius Dromon: 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the land area.
EDCS-01300489.summary: This inscription marks the plot of land belonging to Marcus Barbius Dromon and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-01300490.translation: Tiberius Barbius Liberalis, freedman of Verio, and Tedia Procula, daughter of Spurius, made this while alive for themselves and [---].
EDCS-01300490.summary: This funerary epitaph records Tiberius Barbius Liberalis and Tedia Procula setting up a monument for themselves and possibly others.

EDCS-01300494.translation: To Billienus, son of Marcus, Met[---]
EDCS-01300494.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication or epitaph for Billienus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-01300495.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Billienia Marcellina, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300497.translation: To the Divine Shades. Obaesathus made this for Bonanus Amaresemus, his father, who lived 50 years, the best.
EDCS-01300497.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication by Obaesathus to his deceased father, Bonanus Amaresemus.

EDCS-01300498.translation: Lucius Bovius Lucrio, freedman of Lucius, and Barbia Maxuma, daughter of Titus, made this while alive for themselves, their relatives, freedmen, and freedwomen. Area: 16 square feet.
EDCS-01300498.summary: This funerary epitaph records Lucius Bovius Lucrio and Barbia Maxuma establishing a monument for their family and dependents, with specific area measurements.

EDCS-01300502.translation: If, as you pass by, you wish to know who lies here, Aquileia was my mother and Synforus my father. I was suddenly snatched away, having lived for nine years. After my death, my father placed this monument for me, to be a solace for his dear child.
EDCS-01300502.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of a young boy named Cacurius, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-01300503.summary: This epitaph records Caecilius Dio as the dedicator, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300505.translation: The remains of Gaius Caecina Alximus.
EDCS-01300505.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely an epitaph for Gaius Caecina Alximus.

EDCS-01300506.translation: Lucius Caenius, son of Lucius, of the Stellatina tribe.
EDCS-01300506.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Lucius Caenius, son of Lucius, and his tribal affiliation, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01300508.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Calidiae Barbiae Calidius Candidianus quae vixit annos XXXV coniugi dulcissimae\n
EDCS-01300508.translation: To the departed spirits. Calidius Candidianus for his most sweet wife Calidia Barba, who lived for 35 years.
EDCS-01300508.summary: A funerary dedication to Calidia Barba by her husband, noting her age at death.

EDCS-01300509.translation: To the spirits. Callicla, freedwoman of Tyche.
EDCS-01300509.summary: A funerary dedication to Callicla, identified as a freedwoman.

EDCS-01300510.translation: [Perhaps to Calvina] Calendina, the most dutiful alumna [for her foster mother].
EDCS-01300510.summary: A funerary inscription for Calendina, likely dedicated by her foster mother, Titia, indicating a relationship of care and duty.

EDCS-01300512.translation: To the departed spirits. Campe[---], who lived for 10 [---] days, and [---] who lived for 1 year, 10 months [---]. From their parents.
EDCS-01300512.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription recording the ages at death of at least two individuals, dedicated by their parents.

EDCS-01300514.summary: This inscription records Titus Canius Diphilus dedicating something for an unspecified individual, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300517.translation: For Lucius Cantius Fuscus and Cantia Europa.
EDCS-01300517.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Cantius Fuscus and Cantia Europa, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300518.translation: Lucius Cantius, son of [---], of the Velina tribe, Sec[---]
EDCS-01300518.summary: An incomplete inscription that appears to be the beginning of a personal name and tribal affiliation, likely for a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-01300519.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Cascius Honoratus, dutiful, lived for 25 years. Gaius L. F. made this.
EDCS-01300519.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Cascius Honoratus, recording his age at death and indicating it was erected by C. L. F.

EDCS-01300520.translation: To Lucius Cassius Severus, Cassia Secunda [erected this] for her dearest husband.
EDCS-01300520.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Cassia Secunda for her husband Lucius Cassius Severus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01300521.translation: To the departed spirits. For Cassia Hilaritas, who lived [---]
EDCS-01300521.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Cassia Hilaritas, noting her name and implying her death.

EDCS-01300522.translation: To Cassianus from the region of [his] grandfather, [as] husband.
EDCS-01300522.summary: This inscription likely records a funerary dedication for Cassianus, possibly a husband, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300523.translation: Lucius Cattius, son of Gaius, made this while alive for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, slaves, and slave women. A plot of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01300523.summary: A funerary inscription where Lucius Cattius, son of Gaius, sets aside burial space for himself and his household, including freedpeople and slaves.

EDCS-01300524.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to a woman named Celerina by her husband.

EDCS-01300525.translation: I removed [it] so that it may be permitted with Cerell erected.
EDCS-01300525.summary: This inscription records a puzzling removal of an object, with Cerell as the dedicator, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300527.translation: Deuter, freedman of Cestronia (a woman), and Tabanus, freedman of Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Hippia, and Sextus, freedman of Sextus Erbonius.
EDCS-01300527.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph listing several freedmen, likely belonging to patrons named Cestronia and Sextus Erbonius.

EDCS-01300529.summary: This inscription records Chreste as a 'guardian' who erected something, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01300530.translation: Erected while alive for himself, his freedmen, and freedwomen, Gaius V. Caminati and Quintus Claudius.
EDCS-01300530.summary: This is a self-funded funerary inscription by Gaius V. Caminati and Quintus Claudius, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01300531.translation: To Tiberius Claudius [---]. Claudia Ven[---], freedwoman of Tiberius, made this while alive for herself and her father and her son Iphilus (?) and Domitia [---].
EDCS-01300531.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by a freedwoman named Claudia Ven[---] for herself and her family members, possibly dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-01300532.translation: Claudia Secunda placed this for her deserving husband Claudius.
EDCS-01300532.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Claudia Secunda to her husband Claudius.

EDCS-01300533.translation: To the departed spirits. For Claudia Secunda, his incomparable wife. Lucius Manlius Encolpus, and himself while alive, and for their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01300533.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Lucius Manlius Encolpus to his wife Claudia Secunda and also provides for his freedmen and freedwomen and himself.

EDCS-01300535.translation: He made this for his son Claudius.
EDCS-01300535.summary: A funerary monument made by an unnamed father for his son Claudius.

EDCS-01300541.translation: The bones of Clodia, freedwoman of Decimus, Optata.
EDCS-01300541.summary: A funerary inscription for Clodia, freedwoman of Decimus, named Optata.

EDCS-01300544.translation: Julius Valens and Iulia Severina, parents, placed this for their most dutiful daughter Cocceia Valentina, who lived for 3 years, 3 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-01300544.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Cocceia Valentina, set up by her parents.

EDCS-01300547.translation: The same [placed this] for his wife Lucius Coelius Firmus.
EDCS-01300547.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Coelius Firmus, placed by an unnamed individual (likely his wife based on context).

EDCS-01300548.translation: Lucius Coelius Tergestinus made this for his Urbana, while alive; bones here.
EDCS-01300548.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Coelius Tergestinus for his wife Urbana during his lifetime.

EDCS-01300549.summary: An incomplete inscription, likely funerary, mentioning Quintus Coelius.

EDCS-01300551.translation: Coelius [placed this] for Coelius Phoebus and Arulena Priscilla. Coelius M.
EDCS-01300551.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Coelius M. to Coelius Phoebus and Arulena Priscilla.

EDCS-01300552.translation: For Lucius Cominius Minervius, aged 9 years, his most devoted mother Cominia gave this place.
EDCS-01300552.summary: A funerary inscription where Cominia, mother of Lucius Cominius Minervius (aged 9), dedicated a burial plot.

EDCS-01300554.translation: Corinthia Paulina, heir, arranged for this monument to be made. To Corinthia Elpis, her most dutiful mother, and to Corinthius Salutaris, her brother. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-01300554.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Corinthia Paulina to her mother and brother, and includes a clause that the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-01300558.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age of Cornelius Aq at death.

EDCS-01300563.summary: A very brief funerary epitaph for a girl named Cybele.

EDCS-01300565.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For his most dutiful son, who lived 28 years and 5 months, the most unfortunate mother Lucius Decimius Serena, and his brother Lucius Decimius Charito, and his father Marcus Considienus Maximianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-01300565.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Decimius Sereno, dedicated by his mother, father, and brother, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-01300569.translation: To the departed spirits and eternal peace. For Marcus Domitius Ingenuus. Marcus Trosius Ingenuus, to his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-01300569.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Marcus Trosius Ingenuus to his brother Marcus Domitius Ingenuus.

EDCS-01300572.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gorgia Maxima, for her most devoted son Mari Egnatius Sabinus, who lived 7 years, 2 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-01300572.summary: A funerary dedication for a young boy, Mari Egnatius Sabinus, by his mother, Gorgia Maxima.

EDCS-01300574.translation: Marcus Ennius Marcellus, son of Titus, and Patronia Fusca, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive for their freedmen and freedwomen and slaves, male and female, in common ownership. The monument's location is 16 feet in front and 16 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01300574.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and plot marker created by a couple, Marcus Ennius Marcellus and Patronia Fusca, for themselves and their dependants, with specific dimensions for the burial plot.

EDCS-01300575.translation: Sextus Erbonius Surus, freedman of Sextus, Erbonia Cirrata, freedwoman of Sextus, and Erbonia Tertia, freedwoman of [a woman], made this while alive for themselves and their own, and their freedmen and freedwomen, and [---]. 16 square feet.
EDCS-01300575.summary: This funerary epitaph is for several individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, and also marks a burial plot of 16 square feet.

EDCS-01300580.translation: Eutycelus, living, made for himself and for Celer Aquilius, [son of] M. P.
EDCS-01300580.summary: A funerary dedication made by Eutycelus for himself and Celer Aquilius.

EDCS-01300584.translation: for Eutychius and his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01300584.summary: Part of a funerary dedication specifying beneficiaries, likely for Eutychius.

EDCS-01300585.summary: An inscription fragment that appears to be part of a dedication or ownership mark, potentially identifying Caius, son of Fabius.

EDCS-01300586.translation: Gaius Fabius Glaucus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-01300586.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name of Gaius Fabius Glaucus.

EDCS-01300587.translation: Fabia Clara, freedwoman of Lucius, and Fabia Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, and Fabia Arbuscula, freedwoman of the woman, and Lucius Fabius Urbanus, freedman of the woman, and Lucius Fabius Mansuetus, freedman of the woman, made [this] while alive, those listed above. The area is 16 square feet in every direction.
EDCS-01300587.summary: A funerary monument erected by several members of the Fabii family, likely related, indicating a family burial plot of 16 square feet.

EDCS-01300588.summary: A dedication fragment likely for a wife named Fabi Cornelia.

EDCS-01300589.translation: The bones of Lucius Fabricius Valens.
EDCS-01300589.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Fabricius Valens.

EDCS-01300591.translation: Faltonia Rufa, freedwoman of Publius, made [this] while alive for her husband Gaius Octavius Faustus, freedman of Gaius, for herself and her freedmen and freedwomen. The area is 16 square feet.
EDCS-01300591.summary: A funerary monument erected by Faltonia Rufa for herself and her family, indicating a burial plot of 16 square feet.

EDCS-01300592.translation: The bones are here of Fania Glycaera.
EDCS-01300592.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fania Glycaera.

EDCS-01300593.translation: Farsuleia Marcellina [dedicated this] to her parents and to her brother Marcus Farsuleius.
EDCS-01300593.summary: A funerary dedication by Farsuleia Marcellina for her parents and brother, Marcus Farsuleius.

EDCS-01300596.translation: Aia Nereis, freedwoman of Felix, made [this] while alive for herself and her [family].
EDCS-01300596.summary: A funerary monument likely erected by Aia Nereis for herself and her dependents.

EDCS-01300598.translation: C. Aelius Felix, son, to his most devoted mother.
EDCS-01300598.summary: A funerary dedication from C. Aelius Felix to his mother.

EDCS-01300600.translation: Figila [made this] for herself and IO.
EDCS-01300600.summary: A funerary dedication by Figila for herself and IO.

EDCS-01300605.translation: The bones of Marcus Flavius Primus.
EDCS-01300605.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Flavius Primus.

EDCS-01300606.translation: To Titus Flavius Demetrius, freedman of Montanus.
EDCS-01300606.summary: A dedication to Titus Flavius Demetrius, a freedman.

EDCS-01300607.translation: Flavia Marcella to her most beloved husband Iustinus Victorinus, who lived [X] years, 9 months. She arranged for the title to be restored. To the divine shades.
EDCS-01300607.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iustinus Victorinus, erected by his wife Flavia Marcella, who also arranged for its restoration.

EDCS-01300611.translation: Sever and his brothers [dedicated this] to Fortunata.
EDCS-01300611.summary: A dedication by Sever and his brothers to Fortunata.

EDCS-01300614.summary: An inscription identifying Fuscus as the freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-01300616.translation: Gavillia Surisca, freedwoman of Aulus, patroness; Aulus Gavillius Optatus, freedman of the woman; Pomponia Fausta, freedwoman of the woman, made [this] while alive for herself and her spouse. The area is 16 square feet.
EDCS-01300616.summary: A funerary monument erected by Gavillia Surisca and Pomponia Fausta for themselves and their spouses, indicating a burial plot of 16 square feet.

EDCS-01300617.translation: Quintus Gavius Secundus, son of Quintus, and Vettidia Amoena, while alive, made this for themselves and for their freedman Communis, and for the freedman Optatus.
EDCS-01300617.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Gavius Secundus and Vettidia Amoena for themselves and their freedmen, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-01300618.translation: Geroninus of Rome, born in the city, who
EDCS-01300618.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or a personal statement, possibly part of a larger text.

EDCS-01300619.translation: The bones of Caius Heiulius Gatis.
EDCS-01300619.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking the burial place of Caius Heiulius Gatis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300622.translation: To Marcus Helvius Servandus, a deserving husband, Numeria Secundina [erected this].
EDCS-01300622.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Numeria Secundina to her deserving husband, Marcus Helvius Servandus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300623.translation: The bones of Marcus Herennius Amaranthus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-01300623.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating the burial of Marcus Herennius Amaranthus, son of Marcus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300626.summary: This is a dedication from an unknown person to her husband, Hermadius.

EDCS-01300629.translation: Lucius Hostilius Surus made this for himself and for his son Lucius Hostilius Laudicenus, and for his wife Decia Venustas. In the front 16 feet, in depth 20 feet.
EDCS-01300629.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Hostilius Surus dedicating a plot of land for himself, his son, and his wife, specifying the dimensions of the plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300631.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Ianinius Diadumenus, son of [---].
EDCS-01300631.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Marcus Ianinius Diadumenus, son of [---], likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300636.summary: This epitaph records the age and status of a freedwoman named Iucunda.

EDCS-01300641.translation: To the Divine Shades. Publius Cat Ith, to his friend Gaius Iu
EDCS-01300641.summary: This is a dedication to the 'Divine Shades' (Dis Manibus), an epitaph for a friend named Gaius Iu.

EDCS-01300642.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Paulina made this for herself and for her son Gaius Iulius Onesimus, a worthy husband to Gaius Iulius Aeltho, aged 42, and her son, with 12 feet of space in all directions.
EDCS-01300642.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Valeria Paulina for her husband Gaius Iulius Aeltho and son Gaius Iulius Onesimus, specifying burial plot dimensions.

EDCS-01300643.translation: Gaius Julius Agathopus lived 23 years, to his incomparable wife
EDCS-01300643.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Gaius Julius Agathopus to his wife, providing his age at death.

EDCS-01300644.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Caius Iulius Boio, identified as a friend, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300645.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating that Caius Iulius Flavus is buried here, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300646.translation: Iulia Soteris, his mother, while alive, made this for Caius Iulius Passer, aged 11.
EDCS-01300646.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Iulia Soteris for her son Caius Iulius Passer, who died at the age of 11, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01300647.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Urbicus, alive, made this for himself and for his dearest wife Valeria Dubitata. Monument space in front 8 feet, in depth [---].
EDCS-01300647.summary: This funerary monument, likely from the Roman Imperial period, was erected by Caius Iulius Urbicus for himself and his wife, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-01300648.translation: Marcus Julius Melius, son of Gaius, [---]
EDCS-01300648.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Marcus Julius Melius.

EDCS-01300649.translation: To the divine shades. Julia Cantilia set up this for her well-deserving patron, Sextus Julius Fortunatus.
EDCS-01300649.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Julia Cantilia for her patron, Sextus Julius Fortunatus.

EDCS-01300650.translation: to Julius Victor, 3 months and 2 days
EDCS-01300650.summary: This is a funerary dedication or record of lifespan for Julius Victor, specifying a duration of 3 months and 2 days.

EDCS-01300651.translation: Julius Zosimus erected this in his lifetime for himself
EDCS-01300651.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Julius Zosimus for himself during his own lifetime.

EDCS-01300654.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iulia for herself during her lifetime.

EDCS-01300655.translation: To the divine shades. For Julia Felicitas, daughter, who lived 15 years, and for Tuticius Trophimus, her son-in-law. [---]
EDCS-01300655.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Julia Felicitas and her son-in-law Tuticius Trophimus.

EDCS-01300657.translation: To the divine shades. For Julia Sperata, aged 22. Julia Secunda, her most dutiful sister-in-law, has granted this plot, given by Petronius Antoninus.
EDCS-01300657.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julia Sperata, with the plot granted by her sister-in-law and given by Petronius Antoninus.

EDCS-01300658.translation: Cannutia Primigenia, freedwoman of Tiberius, made this for her sister Julia Veneria, freedwoman of Gaius, while she was alive.
EDCS-01300658.summary: This is an epitaph set up by Cannutia Primigenia for her sister Julia Veneria.

EDCS-01300659.translation: to Julia, his excellent wife, 15 feet in front
EDCS-01300659.summary: This funerary dedication is from an unnamed person to his wife Julia, possibly indicating the dimensions of the burial space.

EDCS-01300661.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Julius, who lived 105 years.
EDCS-01300661.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Julius, who lived to be 105 years old.

EDCS-01300662.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be part of a funerary monument or an epitaph, mentioning 'Julius Lucius'.

EDCS-01300663.translation: to Eivn Fundania, daughter of Ep, aged 25 years.
EDCS-01300663.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fundania, daughter of Ep, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-01300666.translation: Barbia Ursina [set this up] for her son Iuventus Iunianus, aged 3 months and 3 days.
EDCS-01300666.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young child, Iuventus Iunianus, set up by his mother Barbia Ursina.

EDCS-01300668.translation: Laberia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, made this while alive for herself, and for Lucius Laberius Salvius, son of Marcus, her brother, and for Caius Firmus, son of Lucius, and for Lucius Firmus, son of Titus, her son, and for Marcus Laberius, her father, and for Sauconia Tertia, daughter of Andetis, her mother.
EDCS-01300668.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Laberia Secunda for herself and several family members, including her brother, son, father, and mother.

EDCS-01300669.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a freedwoman named Laeta.

EDCS-01300670.translation: To Lucius Lastorius, from Annaea Rufa, his wife.
EDCS-01300670.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Lastorius by his wife, Annaea Rufa.

EDCS-01300673.translation: Gaius Lorentius Eutyches, freedman of Gaius, [dedicated this] to his willing patron, and Lucius Epidius Epagathus, for [his] freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-01300673.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Lorentius Eutyches to his patron and by Lucius Epidius Epagathus for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.

EDCS-01300674.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Lurentia Nices, freedwoman of Caius, most holy. Caius Eutyches, his freedman, made this.
EDCS-01300674.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Caius Eutyches to Lurentia Nices, his freedwoman, described as 'most holy'.

EDCS-01300675.translation: Lucius Lucilius Primus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, and for his wife, and for Licilius Archelaus, his fellow freedman, and for himself, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, in front 16 feet, in depth 32 feet, undivided.
EDCS-01300675.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Lucilius Primus for himself and his family, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-01300676.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Caius Lucretius Primigenius. Caius Lucretius Pr[---] for his pupil.
EDCS-01300676.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring Caius Lucretius Primigenius, with the dedicator being Caius Lucretius Pr[---] for his pupil.

EDCS-01300679.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a name and dedication, possibly an epitaph.

EDCS-01400003.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or a name.

EDCS-01400004.translation: [---] to his wife, for Quintus Maelius Phariaticus, the son. [---]
EDCS-01400004.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a wife and a son named Quintus Maelius Phariaticus.

EDCS-01400005.translation: The remains of Maia, Quintus' freedwoman, daughter of [3], [3] years old; her mother made this (monument) while alive.
EDCS-01400005.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maia, a freedwoman, set up by her mother.

EDCS-01400006.translation: For Lucius Mamilius Epaphra, and for Lucius Mamilius Firmo, aged 20, and for Mamilia Chrysogone, and for Lucius Mamilius Trophimus, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; this monument will not follow its heir. The size of the monument is 16 feet in front and 32 feet in the depth of the field.
EDCS-01400006.summary: This funerary monument, likely a family tomb, was established by Lucius Mamilius Epaphra for himself, his son, other family members, and descendants, with specified dimensions and a clause about inheritance.

EDCS-01400007.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Lucius Mamilius Florus.

EDCS-01400008.translation: AN, made this while alive for himself and, undivided, Marcus Saec Fur Quinto Ammio Er Marcus Ser...
EDCS-01400008.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication made by 'AN' for himself and Marcus Saec Fur Quinto Ammio Er Marcus Ser, with an indication of shared property.

EDCS-01400009.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; for Marcia, daughter of Caius, freedwoman, Ut[...]
EDCS-01400009.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the underworld gods for Marcia, daughter of Caius and a freedwoman.

EDCS-01400010.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Marius Hecataeus, freedman of Gaius, to his most devoted wife, Maria Lacaena, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-01400010.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Maria Lacaena, set up by her husband Gaius Marius Hecataeus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-01400012.translation: [...] for Africanus; his mother set (this up). Caius Matius Rufus, of two brothers [...]
EDCS-01400012.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription for 'Africanus', set up by his mother, and also mentions Caius Matius Rufus.

EDCS-01400016.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mercator.

EDCS-01400017.translation: For Caius Mercusenius Saturninus; Lucius Iulius Blastus, his paternal uncle, with the permission of the patronesses [...]
EDCS-01400017.summary: This funerary inscription records the setting up of a monument for Caius Mercusenius Saturninus by his paternal uncle, Lucius Iulius Blastus, with the permission of the patronesses.

EDCS-01400020.translation: To Claudius Mettius Marcianus, who lived one year and eleven months; Claudius Mettius Evaristus, for his most beloved son.
EDCS-01400020.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudius Mettius Marcianus, set up by his father, Claudius Mettius Evaristus.

EDCS-01400021.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; for Mettia Elpis; Mettia Thaumaste, daughter [...]
EDCS-01400021.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Mettia Elpis by her daughter, Mettia Thaumaste.

EDCS-01400022.translation: For Lucius Homullius, freedman of Lucius, [3]; for Lucius Mevius, son of Lucius Saturninus; for both [3] // Lucius Mev[3] // he gave the same (number of) feet [...]
EDCS-01400022.summary: This inscription likely records a land grant or dedication, possibly for funerary use, involving Lucius Homullius and Lucius Mevius, with specified dimensions.

EDCS-01400025.translation: To his freedman Gaius, to his spouse. Unfortunate.
EDCS-01400025.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman named Gaius, set up by his spouse, with an expression of grief, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-01400026.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the short life of a girl named Moniania Primilla.

EDCS-01400027.summary: This is a simple name inscription, possibly a tombstone or a label, for Quintus Mucius Bassus.

EDCS-01400028.translation: Gaius Mulvius Proculus, son of Titus.
EDCS-01400028.summary: This is a funerary epitaph fragment, identifying Gaius Mulvius Proculus, son of Titus.

EDCS-01400029.translation: Munatia Secundina lends to Aulia Sperata and Gaius Fruticius Genialis.
EDCS-01400029.summary: This inscription records a loan or rental agreement made by Munatia Secundina to Aulia Sperata and Gaius Fruticius Genialis.

EDCS-01400030.translation: To Lucius, freedman of Gaius, 1 year and some months old.
EDCS-01400030.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Lucius, who died at the age of 1 year and some months.

EDCS-01400031.translation: Gaius Mutillius Crispus, son of Gaius, father; Satria, daughter of Sextus, mother; Gaius Mutillius Crispus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-01400031.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a family, identifying the parents and their son, Gaius Mutillius Crispus.

EDCS-01400032.translation: To Naevia Braeciana, Naevius Iulianus, for one who deserved well.
EDCS-01400032.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Naevia Braeciana, set up by Naevius Iulianus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-01400033.translation: Nedymus, slave of Maecia Secunda, aged 26, is laid here.
EDCS-01400033.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Nedymus, a 26-year-old slave belonging to Maecia Secunda.

EDCS-01400035.summary: This is a funerary dedication fragment to a woman named Nonienia Saturnina.

EDCS-01400036.summary: This inscription appears to be a name and possibly a cognomen, perhaps an epitaph for Lucius Numisius Faustus Tertius.

EDCS-01400037.summary: This inscription records the name of Titus, a freedman of Appuleius Nymphius, likely a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-01400041.translation: Gnaeus Octavius Cladus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-01400041.summary: This is an epitaph or dedication for Gnaeus Octavius Cladus, freedman of Gaius, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-01400042.summary: This is a funerary epitaph fragment for Octavia, freedwoman of Gaius, and possibly Pomponius.

EDCS-01400044.translation: Onesimus, slave of Claudia Praxia, a most distinguished lady, erected this while alive for himself and for Aphrodisia, his fellow slave.
EDCS-01400044.summary: This funerary epitaph records a slave named Onesimus, belonging to Claudia Praxia, who erected a tomb for himself and his fellow slave Aphrodisia.

EDCS-01400045.translation: who lived, Gaius Onesimus, with whom she lived.
EDCS-01400045.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to be part of a funerary dedication for a woman, mentioning Gaius Onesimus as her partner.

EDCS-01400047.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marciania Ursula to Victor, her most dutiful freedman.
EDCS-01400047.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication by Marciania Ursula to her freedman Opitionius Victor.

EDCS-01400049.translation: Quintus Otronius Diphilus ordered this to be made for himself and for Otronia Clara, Quintus Otronius Aptos, Quintus Otronius Princeps, freedman, Otronia Hilara, freedwoman, Quintus Otronius Festivus, freedman of Aptos, and Helvia Faustus. Monument plot in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400049.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and plot description for Quintus Otronius Diphilus and his family and freedmen, including a detailed measurement of the burial plot.

EDCS-01400051.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Paezusa, a young woman, is laid here. Phillis, her mother, made this at her own expense.
EDCS-01400051.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Paezusa, a young woman, with the monument erected by her mother, Phillis.

EDCS-01400053.translation: Papia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, made this for herself while alive, and for her son Publius Petronius Sabinus, son of Claudia Marcella (daughter of Marcus), and for her sister's son Gaius Aurellius Marcellinus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-01400053.summary: A funerary monument made by Papia Secunda for herself and her relatives, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-01400055.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Paulo, my foster-son. Sentius, with the permission of Caecilius.
EDCS-01400055.summary: A funerary dedication by Sentius for his foster-son Paulo, with permission from Caecilius, probably from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01400057.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Pedenia Rufina. Sextus Pedienus Rufus and [Aelia] Romana, her parents.
EDCS-01400057.summary: A funerary dedication for Pedenia Rufina by her parents, Sextus Pedienus Rufus and Aelia Romana, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01400059.translation: Laudenus, son of Pelas, aged 29 years.
EDCS-01400059.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young man named Laudenus who died at the age of 29.

EDCS-01400060.translation: Op, the most unhappy, placed this for her husband Peregrinus, born of Macis, aged 35 years, to his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-01400060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Peregrinus, erected by his wife Op, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400061.translation: ... [You] treated everyone as a guest. May you fare well. I wish you were among the living. And for Gaius Petronius Gratus, my son, who lies here. He lived for 3 years and 6 months. The dimensions of the monument: 18 feet in front, 18 feet in depth.
EDCS-01400061.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Petronius Gratus, with a farewell wish to an unknown person, possibly a parent, and providing burial plot dimensions, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01400064.summary: This is a dedication or a tombstone where Gaius Valerius honors Petronius, the date is not specified.

EDCS-01400065.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Petronius Fortunatus, with no specific date or context provided.

EDCS-01400069.translation: ... by the authority of Hermerotis and Pylades, freedmen.
EDCS-01400069.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning the authority of two freedmen, Hermerotis and Pylades, the context of which is unclear.

EDCS-01400070.summary: This inscription expresses the grief of Placidus for Petronius, likely a tombstone or memorial, date unknown.

EDCS-01400071.translation: Plaetoria Nice, freedwoman, aged 25, lies here.
EDCS-01400071.summary: A simple tombstone for Plaetoria Nice, a freedwoman, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01400072.translation: Gaius Plenius Chilo, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, and for his brother Lucius Plenius, son of Lucius, and for freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01400072.summary: A funerary monument erected by Gaius Plenius Chilo for himself and his brother Lucius Plenius, as well as for his freedmen and freedwomen, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-01400080.translation: Burial place. Pontia Amatla made this for herself and her family while alive.
EDCS-01400080.summary: A funerary inscription indicating a burial plot made by Pontia Amatla for herself and her family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01400081.translation: Quintus Pontienus ... for his father Daphnus, for his mother, and for his brother Licoreus, for his sister ...
EDCS-01400081.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication by Quintus Pontienus for his deceased family members, including parents, brother, and sister, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01400085.translation: ...iano(?) from Napocen(?) He lived for 37 years and served for 17 years. Titus Postumius Tiadcus, to his tent-mate.
EDCS-01400085.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Postumius Tiadcus for his deceased tent-mate, who served in the army and lived to 37, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400086.translation: To Postumia, daughter of Publius, from the To[wnship?]
EDCS-01400086.summary: This incomplete inscription appears to record the name of a woman, possibly related to a land division or boundary marker.

EDCS-01400089.translation: Primus, Gaius Valerius, son of Primus.
EDCS-01400089.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely identifying a person named Primus, son of Gaius Valerius Primus, date uncertain.

EDCS-01400091.translation: And you... The location of the monument in front is 32 feet, in the field 16 feet // and for you
EDCS-01400091.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to indicate land measurements for a monument, possibly a tomb, with an address to the deceased or a future visitor.

EDCS-01400092.translation: He made this for himself, his family, and for Primigenius, son of...rio, son of Titus, a freedman.
EDCS-01400092.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that someone erected a monument for themselves, their family, and a freedman named Primigenius.

EDCS-01400093.summary: This epitaph records the death of Primigenius at the age of 19.

EDCS-01400096.summary: This inscription records Pyrallis, a freedwoman, setting up something for herself, likely a funerary monument, date unknown.

EDCS-01400097.translation: Quarta Aquilia erected this in memory of her contubernalis (partner/companion) and sons, aged 30.
EDCS-01400097.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Quarta Aquilia commemorating her partner and sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400099.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication identifying Raia Venusta, a freedwoman.

EDCS-01400100.translation: freedwoman of Rapideia; Hermeus, freedwoman of Luxia Mae; to Lucius Allius Cinna, freedman of Lucius. Square location 16 feet.
EDCS-01400100.summary: This inscription lists several freedwomen and a freedman, likely as part of a shared burial plot or property division, with dimensions provided.

EDCS-01400102.translation: Restituta, daughter of Lucius Vettius, aged 7 years.
EDCS-01400102.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Restituta, the daughter of Lucius Vettius, who died at the age of 7.

EDCS-01400106.translation: Publius Rufrius... to Claudia, freedwoman of Caius... with whom he lived
EDCS-01400106.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or funerary text, mentioning a man, Publius Rufrius, and a woman, Claudia, with whom he had lived.

EDCS-01400107.summary: This is a funerary dedication from an unknown individual to their cousin Rufus.

EDCS-01400109.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Rupilia Tertulla.

EDCS-01400111.summary: This inscription records two freedmen, one of whom was freed by Sextus and the other by Aulus.

EDCS-01400112.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Sabina as the daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-01400114.summary: This inscription names Calpurnia Sabiniana, possibly indicating approval or a status.

EDCS-01400115.summary: This inscription names Sabinus, with a possible indication of his role or status as a supporter.

EDCS-01400116.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Sabinus as the son of Marcus.

EDCS-01400117.translation: Publius Salavius Rufinus lived 3 years, 5 months.
EDCS-01400117.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of a child, Publius Salavius Rufinus.

EDCS-01400118.summary: This inscription indicates that a decision or action was made by the arbitration of Salvius.

EDCS-01400119.translation: Publius Salvius Philodamus, freedman of Publius, and Publius Salvius Liccaeus, freedman of Publius, made this while alive for themselves and for Salvia, freedwoman of Mummius, and for their kin, and for their freedmen and freedwomen. Monument location 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01400119.summary: This funerary inscription records a man, Publius Salvius Philodamus, and his associate Publius Salvius Liccaeus, erecting a monument for themselves, their relatives, and their freedpersons, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-01400121.summary: This is a dedication to Threptas, likely a person from Sardinia.

EDCS-01400123.translation: Lucius Satrius Speratus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and for Hygino, freedman, and for Philetus, freedman.
EDCS-01400123.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Satrius Speratus, a freedman, erecting a monument for himself and two freedmen, Hygino and Philetus.

EDCS-01400127.translation: Secunda Pontia, daughter of Lucius, erected this for herself, obedient to her family, and her husband. Aulus Geminius and Tertia, her sister, [also contributed].
EDCS-01400127.summary: This funerary inscription records Secunda Pontia, her husband, and her sister Tertia and brother Aulus Geminius, who set up the monument for her and herself.

EDCS-01400128.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Secundinus as a brother.

EDCS-01400133.translation: The bones of Marcus Serionius Hermes.
EDCS-01400133.summary: This inscription records the burial place for Marcus Serionius Hermes.

EDCS-01400135.summary: This inscription records the burial place for Septimia Grapta.

EDCS-01400137.translation: Gaius Servilius Veneto, son of Gaius, and his wife Rauconia, daughter of Marcus, made (this tomb) for themselves and their descendants, freedmen and freedwomen. A square space of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01400137.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman and his wife for themselves and their descendants, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400139.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment for a woman named Severa, likely part of a longer epitaph indicating her lifespan.

EDCS-01400140.translation: Severinus, for himself and his family
EDCS-01400140.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment, possibly part of a dedication made by Severinus for his household.

EDCS-01400141.translation: for 17 years, to mother and brother Sever...
EDCS-01400141.summary: This funerary inscription fragment mentions a duration of 17 years and is dedicated to a mother and brother, with the brother's name likely starting with Sever.

EDCS-01400142.translation: To the departed spirits. For the well-deserving mother, [bereaved children] made (this).
EDCS-01400142.summary: A funerary dedication from children to their well-deserving mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400146.translation: Menela, aged... Silvanus Saturninus, while alive, made [this] for himself and for Caius, his freedwoman wife, and for the freedman of the woman
EDCS-01400146.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment where Silvanus Saturninus, while alive, dedicated the monument to himself, his freedwoman wife, and a freedman.

EDCS-01400148.translation: to Soteris, who lived 19 years and 1 month, her father placed [this]
EDCS-01400148.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Soteris, who lived 19 years and 1 month, and was set up by her father.

EDCS-01400149.translation: To the departed spirits. Helius (set this up) for his well-deserving daughter Sperata, from the Augustan colony.
EDCS-01400149.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Helius for his daughter Sperata, from the Roman colony of Augusta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400150.translation: Livi Au[re]lia, while alive, made [this] for herself and for Fusca, her freedwoman, and for Livia Sperata, her wife, and for her freedmen and freedwomen
EDCS-01400150.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Livia Aurelia for herself, her freedwoman Fusca, her wife Livia Sperata, and their freed dependents.

EDCS-01400154.translation: to Lucius Statius Firmus, son of Lucius
EDCS-01400154.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment, likely a dedication to Lucius Statius Firmus.

EDCS-01400155.translation: Publius Statius Nammus, freedman of Publius / Statia Hilara, freedwoman of Publius / Statia Fausta, freedwoman of Publius / Publius Statius Rufio, freedman of Publius, ordered [this] to be made / area measuring 16 feet in every direction
EDCS-01400155.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the ordering of a tomb by Publius Statius Rufio for himself and other freedmen and freedwomen of Publius Statius, with specified dimensions for the burial plot.

EDCS-01400156.translation: To Gaius Statius Faustus, freedman of Paratus.
EDCS-01400156.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedman named Gaius Statius Faustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400157.translation: For Statia Iuventiana, aged 2 years, 3 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-01400157.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a young child named Statia Iuventiana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400159.translation: The bones of Successus, aged 14 years.
EDCS-01400159.summary: This inscription records the burial place of Successus, who died at the age of 14.

EDCS-01400161.translation: Suria. Gaius and Lucius [set this up]
EDCS-01400161.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment, likely recording the names of Suria and the dedicators Gaius and Lucius.

EDCS-01400163.translation: The bones of Successus, his friend, and of Iucunda, his daughter, aged 5 years, and of Sperata, his partner.
EDCS-01400163.summary: This inscription records the burial place of Successus, his daughter Iucunda, and his partner Sperata.

EDCS-01400164.translation: to Aulus Terentius Abascantus, his freedman
EDCS-01400164.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment, likely a dedication to Aulus Terentius Abascantus, who was the freedman of the person setting it up.

EDCS-01400165.translation: Valeria Fortunata, the mother, made (this) while alive for her son Quintus Terentius Valerianus, aged 5 years, 7 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-01400165.summary: This funerary monument was set up by a mother for her young son, Quintus Terentius Valerianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01400166.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a dedication or epitaph naming Titus Terentius Moderatus.

EDCS-01400168.translation: Of Grata, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-01400168.summary: This inscription names Grata, a freedwoman, and is likely part of a tombstone or funerary monument.

EDCS-01400172.summary: This inscription is a simple name, possibly a funerary epitaph or a dedication.

EDCS-01400173.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Lucius Titius Acceptus. Marcus, son of Lucius, [made this].
EDCS-01400173.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Titius Acceptus by Marcus, his son.

EDCS-01400174.translation: Lucius Titius Epaneitus made this monument for himself and his wife Mansueta while alive; it will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-01400174.summary: A funerary monument set up by Lucius Titius Epaneitus for himself and his wife Mansueta, with specific inheritance instructions.

EDCS-01400175.translation: Publius Titius Primigenius, son of Publius, son of Iovinus.
EDCS-01400175.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Publius Titius Primigenius, possibly for a tombstone or a legal document.

EDCS-01400176.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Titia Ursa, [his] most dutiful wife, Claudius Papias [made this].
EDCS-01400176.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by Claudius Papias to his devoted wife, Titia Ursa.

EDCS-01400179.translation: Tritus, freedman of Publius, made this for himself and his wife.
EDCS-01400179.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by a freedman named Tritus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-01400181.summary: A simple naming inscription, possibly an epitaph or a dedication, identifying Trosia Caesia.

EDCS-01400183.translation: Marcus Tullius Anteros granted this burial place for himself and his friends listed below: to Titia Melpomene, freedwoman of a woman [Tullia?], companion of Anteros; to Titus Betutius Karus, freedman of Titus; to Festai, freedwoman of Titus; to Titus Kanicus Thallus, freedman of Titus; to Proculus, son of Titus Kanicus; to Petronia Procila, daughter of Lucius; to Rufonia Sabina; to Gaius Poppius Corinthus; to Antiponia Tryphera, freedwoman of Gaius; to Barbia Iada, freedwoman of a woman [Camuria?]; to Liberalis, companion of Camuria; to Verecunda; to Quintus Julius Liberalis, son of Quintus; to Marcus Tullius Asticus, freedman of Marcus; to Nymphe, freedwoman of a woman [Mulius?]; to Hygiae, freedwoman of a woman [Mamilia?]. To Quintus Acilius [son of Quintus?]; to Pontia; to Quintus Acilius [?]; to Gaius Barbius [?]; to Aspania [?]; Sereni[?], freedwoman of Lucius Vesidius.
EDCS-01400183.summary: A detailed funerary inscription recording the allocation of burial plots by Marcus Tullius Anteros to himself, his companion, and numerous friends, freedmen, and freedwomen, with extensive genealogical information.

EDCS-01400184.translation: Marcus Turpillius Omation, freedman of Marcus, and Tertia Attia, daughter of Caius, [allocated] 12 square feet of space.
EDCS-01400184.summary: This inscription records the allocation of burial space for Marcus Turpillius Omation and Tertia Attia.

EDCS-01400187.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of a young girl named Urania at the age of four.

EDCS-01400190.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Ursio Helpidiano, son of Eracla.
EDCS-01400190.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Ursio Helpidiano, son of Eracla.

EDCS-01400191.translation: [...]. Valentina made this while alive for herself and for Gnaeus Vibius Quinctilius, her husband, for herself and her family.
EDCS-01400191.summary: A funerary monument set up by Valentina for herself and her husband Gnaeus Vibius Quinctilius, indicating it is for their household.

EDCS-01400193.translation: To his patron and to his friend Lucius Valerius B.
EDCS-01400193.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a patron and a friend, likely on a public or private monument.

EDCS-01400194.text_edition: \n Marcus Valerius Marci filius Burdo Valeriae Inventae coniugi pientissimae et Valeriis Secundo Valeriano Invento collibertis vivis et sibi\n
EDCS-01400194.translation: Marcus Valerius Burdo, son of Marcus Valerius, [dedicated this] to Valeria Inventa, his most dutiful wife, and to his living co-freedmen Valerius Secundus and Valerianus Inventus, and to himself.
EDCS-01400194.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Marcus Valerius Burdo for his wife Valeria Inventa and his co-freedmen, also including himself.

EDCS-01400195.translation: Valeria Marta set this up for her father, Marcus Valerius Apollonius.
EDCS-01400195.summary: A funerary dedication by a daughter for her father.

EDCS-01400196.translation: Quintus Valerius Gallicanus, son of Quintus, made this while alive for his sister Valeria Romula, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-01400196.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument built by Quintus Valerius Gallicanus for his sister Valeria Romula.

EDCS-01400197.translation: To Valerius Vale Martina, [her] husband, here, against [his] vow.
EDCS-01400197.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication, possibly indicating a dedication made against a vow, for Valerius Vale Martina.

EDCS-01400198.summary: This inscription is part of a dedication, indicating that Valeria Cale was involved in setting up a monument or object.

EDCS-01400199.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Pelagia, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-01400202.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning several individuals, possibly including a woman named Veneteia.

EDCS-01400203.translation: For Venustus, a most exceptional slave. Gaius Iulius Trophimus [dedicated this].
EDCS-01400203.summary: A dedication by Gaius Iulius Trophimus for his highly valued slave, Venustus.

EDCS-01400204.translation: To Vera, daughter, aged 32; her father, still living.
EDCS-01400204.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Vera, set up by her father.

EDCS-01400205.summary: A funerary epitaph for Verecundus Aquilo, likely recording the location of his remains.

EDCS-01400206.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy named Vestalis.

EDCS-01400207.translation: To the departed spirits of Publius Vetticius Vitalis.
EDCS-01400207.summary: A standard dedication to the departed spirits for Publius Vetticius Vitalis.

EDCS-01400208.translation: To the departed spirits of Gaius Vettidius Soterichus. [Erected by] fellow freedmen.
EDCS-01400208.summary: A funerary dedication by fellow freedmen for Gaius Vettidius Soterichus.

EDCS-01400209.text_edition: \n Titus Vettidius Cladus et Octavia Cnaei liberta Italia vivi fecerunt sibi et suis libertis libertabusque Ampliatus anniculus et dierum VII hic situs est et Caio Dindio Zenonis liberto Ianuario amico locus monumenti quoquo versus pedes XXII\n
EDCS-01400209.translation: Titus Vettidius Cladus and Octavia, freedwoman of Gnaeus, his wife, made this monument while alive for themselves and their [family], and their freedmen and freedwomen. Ampliatus, one year old and seven days, is buried here, and also Gaius Dindius Ianuarius, freedman of Zenon, a friend. The monument plot measures twenty-two feet in every direction.
EDCS-01400209.summary: A funerary monument set up by Titus Vettidius Cladus and his wife Octavia for themselves, their descendants, freedmen, and friends, including detailed plot dimensions and the burial of an infant.

EDCS-01400889.summary: This inscription marks the burial site of Suavis, a slave of Gnaeus Octavius, and specifies dimensions.

EDCS-01400890.translation: A plot belonging to Octavia Epicharis, for herself and her freedmen and freedwomen, measuring 60 feet in frontage and 30 feet in depth.
EDCS-01400890.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot intended for Octavia Epicharis and her freed dependents.

EDCS-01400898.translation: Monument site for Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus, measuring 16 feet in frontage and 32 feet in depth.
EDCS-01400898.summary: This inscription marks the burial site of Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-01400899.translation: [...] 32 feet in depth belonging to Caius Peccius Secundinus.
EDCS-01400899.summary: This inscription records the depth of a burial plot belonging to Caius Peccius Secundinus, with the frontage lost.

EDCS-01400900.translation: Monument site for Peticia Amphinomi, measuring 20 feet in frontage and 50 feet in depth.
EDCS-01400900.summary: This inscription marks the burial site of Peticia Amphinomi and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-01400901.translation: Monument site for Caius Petronius Amphion, measuring 16 feet in frontage and 32 feet in depth.
EDCS-01400901.summary: This inscription marks the burial site of Caius Petronius Amphion and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-01400902.translation: Plot belonging to Publius Petronius Receptus, [dimensions lost].
EDCS-01400902.summary: This inscription records that a plot belonged to Publius Petronius Receptus, with the dimensions now lost.

EDCS-01400903.translation: Plot of Publius Petronius Tertius: in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400903.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Publius Petronius Tertius.

EDCS-01400904.translation: The place of the monument of Gaius Pinnius Provincialis in front 20 feet.
EDCS-01400904.summary: This inscription indicates the location and size of a monument belonging to Gaius Pinnius Provincialis.

EDCS-01400905.translation: Plot of monument for Marcus Plinius Priscus: in front 24 feet, in the field 16 feet.
EDCS-01400905.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Marcus Plinius Priscus.

EDCS-01400906.translation: Plot of monument for Plotia Anthidus: in front 35 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400906.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Plotia Anthidus.

EDCS-01400908.translation: Plot of monument for Marcus Poppaeus Speratus.
EDCS-01400908.summary: This inscription indicates a plot of land belonging to Marcus Poppaeus Speratus.

EDCS-01400910.translation: Burial plot in all directions 70 feet; burial plot in all directions 70 feet. Lucia Prima, daughter of Gaius, while alive, for herself and her patron, for herself and her family.
EDCS-01400910.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot purchased by Lucia Prima for herself, her patron, and her family.

EDCS-01400911.translation: Plot of monument for Primigenius: in front 4 feet, in the field 8 feet.
EDCS-01400911.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot likely belonging to Primigenius.

EDCS-01400912.translation: Plot of monument for Quintus Cornelius Primi(ge)nius. In front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet, and for Teniedia Restituta, freedwoman of a woman, and for her freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01400912.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot for Quintus Cornelius Primigenius and his freedpeople, including Teniedia Restituta.

EDCS-01400913.translation: Plot of monument for Prolibus Athictus of Faventina: in front 20 feet, in the field 64 feet.
EDCS-01400913.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Prolibus Athictus of Faventina.

EDCS-01400916.translation: Plot for [---] Rufus Bromus: in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet. 16 feet. 32 feet.
EDCS-01400916.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Rufus Bromus.

EDCS-01400917.translation: For Rumor and Gresia Paula: in front [feet...].
EDCS-01400917.summary: This inscription appears to record the dimensions of a burial plot for Rumor and Gresia Paula.

EDCS-01400921.translation: Location of monument: of Salvius Varius Saturninus, in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400921.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Salvius Varius Saturninus.

EDCS-01400922.translation: Location of monument: of Vibius Sempronius, in front 16 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-01400922.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Vibius Sempronius.

EDCS-01400923.translation: Sextia, daughter of Lucius, Maxuma, 16 square feet.
EDCS-01400923.summary: This inscription records the area of 16 square feet, likely a burial plot, belonging to Sextia Maxuma.

EDCS-01400924.translation: Location of monument: of Quintus Siculus Florus, 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01400924.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Quintus Siculus Florus.

EDCS-01400925.translation: Location of monument: of Lucius Silicius Celer, son of Lucius, and Publius Avillius, son of Publius, in front 20 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400925.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot shared by Lucius Silicius Celer and Publius Avillius.

EDCS-01400926.translation: Location of monument: of Quintus Sossidius, in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400926.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Quintus Sossidius.

EDCS-01400927.translation: Location of monument: of Lucius Spurius Pulcher, in front 25 feet, in the field 45 feet. Location of monument: of Lucius Spurius Pulcher, in front 25 feet, in the field 45 feet.
EDCS-01400927.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Spurius Pulcher, possibly with a redundant entry.

EDCS-01400928.translation: Location of monument: of Caius Statius Heuretus and Marcus Servius Cladus, in front 30 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400928.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Statius Heuretus and Marcus Servius Cladus.

EDCS-01400929.translation: Statinia Phaenusa, freedwoman of Marcus, 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01400929.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Statinia Phaenusa.

EDCS-01400930.translation: Location of the Statii, of Secundus Bassus Optatus, in front 48 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01400930.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Secundus Bassus Optatus of the Statii family.

EDCS-01400935.translation: Plot of monument for Terentia Casta: 28 feet in front, 40 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01400935.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot designated for Terentia Casta.

EDCS-01400937.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Tettiena Phila.

EDCS-01400938.translation: Plot of monument for Gaius Titus Primus, son of Gaius, and Titia Ampiata, freedwoman of Gaius: 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01400938.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot for Gaius Titus Primus and Titia Ampiata.

EDCS-01400939.translation: Plot of monument for Marcus Trosius Liberalis: 32 feet in front, 64 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01400939.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot for Marcus Trosius Liberalis.

EDCS-01400940.translation: Plot of monument for Gaius Truttedius Fructus and Lucius Pontius Auctus: 16 feet in front, 40 feet in the ground. [plot of monument for Gaius Truttedius Fructus and Lucius Pontius Auctus: 16 feet in front, 40 feet in the ground.] [plot of monument for Gaius Truttedius Fructus and Lucius Pontius]
EDCS-01400940.summary: This is a repetitive inscription detailing the dimensions of a burial plot for Gaius Truttedius Fructus and Lucius Pontius Auctus, with significant portions repeated or restored.

EDCS-01400948.translation: Plot of monument for [---] Valerius Partisus and Sextus Petilius Verus.
EDCS-01400948.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a burial plot intended for Valerius Partisus and Sextus Petilius Verus.

EDCS-01400950.translation: Plot of Lucius Valerius Auctus: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01400950.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot for Lucius Valerius Auctus.

EDCS-01400951.translation: For Lucius Valerius Primus, son of Marcus: plot of monument, 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01400951.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot for Lucius Valerius Primus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-01400952.translation: Plot of monument for Valeria Agapema: 16 feet in front, 30 feet in the ground.
EDCS-01400952.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot for Valeria Agapema.

EDCS-01400954.translation: Marcus Velaeus Senecio, son of Gaius, bought a plot of 16 square feet in all directions.
EDCS-01400954.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a square burial plot of 16 square feet by Marcus Velaeus Senecio.

EDCS-01400955.translation: The place of the monument of Quintus Veratius Bassus, son of Gaius, 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01400955.summary: This is a boundary marker defining a plot of land measuring 16 feet on all sides, belonging to Quintus Veratius Bassus.

EDCS-01400956.translation: The place of the monument of Marcus Vettius Speratus, 16 feet in the front and 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-01400956.summary: This inscription marks a plot of land belonging to Marcus Vettius Speratus, with dimensions of 16 feet (frontage) by 40 feet (depth).

EDCS-01400957.translation: The place of the monument of Vettia Iucunda, freedwoman of Titus, for herself and her family, and for her freedman Nicomedes, and his freedmen and freedwomen, 16 feet in the front and 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-01400957.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot for Vettia Iucunda, her family, and her freedman Nicomedes and his descendants, with dimensions of 16x16 feet.

EDCS-01400958.translation: Of Gaius Vettitius [3] ... [3] feet in the front, [3] feet in the field.
EDCS-01400958.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely marking a plot of land belonging to Gaius Vettitius, with partial dimensions recorded.

EDCS-01400959.translation: The place of Lucius Vibius Liberalis, 16 feet in the front and 36 feet in the field.
EDCS-01400959.summary: This inscription marks a plot of land belonging to Lucius Vibius Liberalis, measuring 16 feet in frontage and 36 feet in depth.

EDCS-01400960.translation: The place of Lucius Viburius N[, 16 square feet.
EDCS-01400960.summary: This inscription records a plot of 16 square feet belonging to Lucius Viburius N.

EDCS-01400961.translation: The place of the monument of Quintus Vittorius, 30 feet in the front and 24 feet in the field.
EDCS-01400961.summary: This inscription marks a plot of land belonging to Quintus Vittorius, measuring 30 feet in frontage and 24 feet in depth.

EDCS-01400962.translation: The place of the monument of Lucius Volunsius Ibycus and Domitia Pherusa, and of Lucius Volunsius Sporus, 20 feet in the front and 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01400962.summary: This inscription designates a plot of land for Lucius Volunsius Ibycus, Domitia Pherusa, and Lucius Volunsius Sporus, with dimensions of 20x32 feet.

EDCS-01401102.translation: Gaius Carminius Celer served for 23 years in the I Adiutrix Legion, in the 1st cohort, under centurion Helios Donatus. Quintus Oppius Celer set this up. The place of the monument, 16 feet in the front and 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-01401102.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Carminius Celer, a soldier who served 23 years in the I Adiutrix Legion, erected by Quintus Oppius Celer, and it also marks a plot of land.

EDCS-01401103.translation: Lucius Vibius Valens, veteran of the I Italica Legion, made (this) for himself and Vibius Fe[3], Vibius T[3], and Caius? Vibius [
EDCS-01401103.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vibius Valens, a veteran of the I Italica Legion, who made it for himself and possibly other family members.

EDCS-01401104.translation: Titus Gallius Euphrosinus, a soldier of the II Italica legion, who lived for [some number of] years, for his most innocent daughter.
EDCS-01401104.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Gallius Euphrosinus, a soldier of the II Italica legion, dedicated to his daughter.

EDCS-01401106.text_edition: \n Quintus Etuvius Sexti filius Voltinia Capreolus domo Vienna miles legionis IIII Scythicae nnos IIII eques nnos X centurio nnos XXI praefectus cohortis II Thracum in Germania nnos V vixit nnos LX testamento fieri iussit arbitratu libertorum idemque heredum vivi fecerunt patrono et sibi Ilus IIIIIIvir Epigonus Secundus Illyricus Heracla\n
EDCS-01401106.translation: Quintus Etuvius Capreolus, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vienna, a soldier of the Fourth Scythian Legion for 4 years, an equestrian for 10 years, a centurion for 21 years, prefect of the Second Thracian Cohort in Germany for 5 years, lived 60 years. He ordered this to be made by his will, under the supervision of his freedmen, who are also his heirs. While still alive, they made this for their patron and for themselves: Ilus, quinquennalis, Epigonus, Secundus, Illyricus, Heracla.
EDCS-01401106.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Quintus Etuvius Capreolus, detailing his military career and life span, and commissioned by his freedmen/heirs.

EDCS-01401108.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Thrasybulus, com(mentariensis) of the consular governor, of the 7th Claudian Legion in the province of Upper Moesia, lived 42 years, with 20 years of service. [Made by] Demetrius, his ward.
EDCS-01401108.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Marcus Aurelius Thrasybulus, likely a veteran or officer, detailing his age and service, and dedicated by his ward.

EDCS-01401109.translation: To Gnaeus Acilius Relatus, a soldier of the VIII legion, discharged, to his son Gnaeus Acilius Saturninus, aged 5 years, and to Caesiana Procula, daughter of Spurii.
EDCS-01401109.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gnaeus Acilius Relatus, a discharged soldier, and includes his young son and wife, Caesiana Procula.

EDCS-01401110.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Albius Rufus, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion. Ampia Itala Prima [his wife] and [he] made this while alive for their mother Abudia Prima and for their mother Ampia Itala Aucta.
EDCS-01401110.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Titus Albius Rufus, a soldier, and his mother(s), made by him and his wife while alive.

EDCS-01401111.text_edition: \n Quinto Cerrinio Cai filio Camilia Cordo militi legionis VIII Augustae patrono Quintus Cerrinius Quinti libertus Corinthus vivus fecit Iuliae Sexti libertae Donacini sic contubernali\n
EDCS-01401111.translation: To Quintus Cerrinius Corinthus, freedman of Quintus Cerrinius, son of Quintus, of the Camilia tribe, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, and his patron. Corinthus made this while alive for Iulia Donacina, freedwoman of Sextus, his fellow soldier.
EDCS-01401111.summary: This is a tomb inscription commissioned by Quintus Cerrinius Corinthus, a freedman and soldier, for his fellow soldier and patron, Iulia Donacina.

EDCS-01401112.text_edition: \n Marcus Miledius Marci filius Pollia miles legionis VIII Augustae domo Mutina testamento fieri iussit arbitratu Marci Petroni Marci liberti Dromonis Marcus Miledius Datus libertus locus monumenti quoquov(ersus) pedes quadratos XVI\n
EDCS-01401112.translation: Marcus Miledius Datus, freedman of Marcus Miledius, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, from Mutina. He ordered this to be made by his will, under the supervision of Marcus Petronius Dromon, freedman of Marcus. A monument for Marcus Miledius Datus, freedman, with 16 square feet of space.
EDCS-01401112.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Marcus Miledius Datus, a soldier, commissioned by his patron through his will and specifying the monument's dimensions.

EDCS-01401113.text_edition: \n Caius Varius Auli filius Scaptia Priscus veteranus legionis VIII Augustae Marcus Cornelius Marci filius Veturia Rufus Marcus Cornelius Marci libertus Clarus IIIIIIvir Valeria Cai liberta Pergamis Caius Varius Cai filius Velina Priscus annorum XXII miles cohortis VIII praetoriae stipendiorum VI Marcus Cornelius Rufi libertus Mansuetus VIvir\n
EDCS-01401113.translation: Gaius Varius Priscus, son of Aulus, of the Scaptia tribe, a veteran of the Eighth Augustan Legion. Marcus Cornelius Rufus, son of Marcus, of the Veturia tribe. Marcus Cornelius Clarus, freedman of Marcus. Valeria Pergamis, freedwoman of Gaius. Gaius Varius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, 22 years old, soldier of the Eighth Praetorian Cohort, with 6 years of service. Marcus Cornelius Mansuetus, freedman of Rufus, duovir.
EDCS-01401113.summary: This inscription records several individuals, including a veteran and a soldier, and seems to be a funerary monument possibly for Gaius Varius Priscus, with titles held by others.

EDCS-01401114.translation: Quintus Vettius Vemens, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe, centurion of the Eighth Augustan Legion, with 39 years of service. Made this while alive for Primio and Servanda, his freedmen, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-01401114.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Quintus Vettius Vemens, a centurion, for himself and his freedmen and their descendants.

EDCS-01401119.text_edition: \n Betutia Sexti liberta Fusca viva fecit sibi et Sexto Betutio Sexti filio Voltinia Vianna sic patrono signifero legionis VIIII veterano et Sexto Betutio Sexti liberto Secundo conliberto et Marco Salvio Primo amico\n
EDCS-01401119.translation: Betutia Fusca, freedwoman of Sextus, made this while alive for herself, and for her patron Sextus Betutius Vianna, standard-bearer of the Ninth Legion, and for his fellow soldier Sextus Betutius Secundus, freedman of Sextus, and for her friend Marcus Salvius Primus.
EDCS-01401119.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by Betutia Fusca, a freedwoman, for herself, her patron, his fellow soldier, and her friend.

EDCS-01401125.translation: Titus Statius Marrax, son of Publius, of the Sergia tribe, primus pilus of the Thirteenth Gemina Legion, honored with torques, armbands, phalerae, a pure hasta, and five golden crowns.
EDCS-01401125.summary: This inscription honors Titus Statius Marrax, a high-ranking officer (primus pilus), for his military decorations and achievements.

EDCS-01401126.translation: [Publius] Carfenus, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, from Mutina, a veteran of the Fifteenth Apollinaris Legion. [He] made this while alive for himself and for Publius Carfenus Murranus, freedman of Publius; for Trosia Melete, his wife; for [F]uria, freedwoman of Rufus; for [Fortu]nata(?). Monument space: 10 feet in front, 18 feet in depth.
EDCS-01401126.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Publius Carfenus, a veteran, made by himself while alive for his family and freedmen, and specifying the plot dimensions.

EDCS-01401127.translation: Quintus Dellius Super, son of Quintus, of the Pollia tribe, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, and his son Quintus Dellius Clemens, and his wife Dellia Falerna, and his freedman Albanus, and his freedwoman Pusilla, and you.
EDCS-01401127.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Dellius Super, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, listing his family members and possibly a final address to a reader.

EDCS-01401128.translation: Quintus Fuficius placed this monument for his brother, Publius Fuficius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, aged 53, with 33 years of service; the monument covers 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01401128.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Fuficius, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, erected by his brother, indicating his age and years of service, and the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-01401129.translation: For Quintus Laberius of the XV Apollinaris legion, for his freedmen and freedwomen: 20 feet in front, 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01401129.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot dedicated by Quintus Laberius, a soldier of the XV Apollinaris legion, for his freedmen and freedwomen, with specified dimensions for the land.

EDCS-01401130.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01401130.text_edition: \n Lucius Pellartius Cai Lemonia Celer Iulius Montanus stipendiorum XLIII missus ex evocato et armidoctor legionis XV Apollinaris ab Imperatore Domitiano Caesare Augusto et accepit pro commodis HS XXXtriginta milia quod ante illum nemo alius accebit sic ex hac militie sic item bello Iudaeico sic donis donatum sic et corona aurea ab divo Tito tulit annos secum LXXIII hoc sepulcrum cum suo titulo donavit et filiabus Lucius Pellartius Anthus cui et aditus datur locus monumenti in fronte pedes LV in agro pedes XLV\n
EDCS-01401130.translation: Lucius Pellartius, son of Cai, of the Lemonia tribe, Celer Julius Montanus, a veteran with 43 years of service, discharged as an evocatus and armor-bearer of the XV Apollinaris legion by Emperor Domitian Caesar Augustus, received 30,000 sesterces for his service, a sum previously unprecedented, and thus released from military service and decorated in the Jewish War, and he received a golden crown from the deified Titus. He lived 73 years. Lucius Pellartius Anthus, to whom access is also granted, donated this tomb with its epitaph, and [donated the land to] his daughters. The tomb occupies 55 feet in front and 45 feet in the field.
