EDCS-01401130.summary: This is a lengthy tombstone inscription for Lucius Pellartius, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, detailing his long service, awards, significant financial compensation, and his age at death, with provisions made for his daughters and heir.

EDCS-01401132.text_edition: \n Lucio Iulio Pansae cohortis I |(centurio) Brittonum veteranae ex testamento ipsius faciendum curavit Caius Iulius Proculus heres\n
EDCS-01401132.translation: Caius Julius Proculus, the heir, saw to the construction of this monument for Lucius Julius Pansa, a centurion of the I Cohort of Britons, a veteran, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-01401132.summary: This inscription records a tomb built by Caius Julius Proculus, the heir, for Lucius Julius Pansa, a veteran centurion.

EDCS-01401133.text_edition: \n Publio Acutio Publi filio Martiali veterano ex centyrione sic cohortis primae Germanorum Publius Acutius Lucretianus patri\n
EDCS-01401133.translation: Publius Acutius Lucretianus [erected this] for his father, Publius Acutius Martialis, a veteran ex-centurion of the First Cohort of Germans.
EDCS-01401133.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Acutius Martialis, a veteran ex-centurion of the First Cohort of Germans, erected by his son.

EDCS-01401134.text_edition: \n Crispinus eques imaginifer cohortis I Pannoniorum vivus fecit Dasio filio suo nnorum XIII\n
EDCS-01401134.translation: Crispinus, a cavalryman and standard-bearer of the I Cohort of Pannonians, made this alive for his son Dasios, aged 13.
EDCS-01401134.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Crispinus, a standard-bearer in the I Cohort of Pannonians, for his young son Dasios.

EDCS-01401135.translation: Of the I Cohort of [---]norum, of the Claudii, Minervius [---], 20 [feet?].
EDCS-01401135.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to belong to a tomb or monument for a soldier of the I Cohort of [---]norum and possibly his family, with an unclear measurement at the end.

EDCS-01401137.translation: To Primitivos and Hermes, well-deserving, for their patron, the cornicularius (horn-blower) of Tribune Petronius's century, a soldier of cohort [---], with 15 years of service.
EDCS-01401137.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a cornicularius, a non-commissioned officer, who served in the cohort [---] and had 15 years of service, erected by fellow soldiers or beneficiaries.

EDCS-01401138.text_edition: \n Locus monumenti Liccai ISsesquiplicarius et Acuti IIduplicarius equitum alae Aravacorum II in fronte pedes XVI in agro pedes XXXII\n
EDCS-01401138.translation: The monument's location belongs to Liccai, an ISsesquiplicarius (soldier receiving 1.5 times pay), and Acuti, an IIduplicarius (soldier receiving double pay), of the cavalry ala Aravacorum II: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01401138.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot dimensions for two cavalry soldiers, an Isesquiplicarius and an Iidùplicarius of the Ala II Aravacorum, indicating the size of their allocated space.

EDCS-01401139.translation: To the departed spirits. For Marcus Iulius Sabinus, son of Tiberius, cavalry subprefect of the Ala Scubulorum, former magistrate (IIvir) with power of jurisdiction, quinquennial censor. His wards, the children of Iulius Diomedes, Sabinus and Sabina, erected this.
EDCS-01401139.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Iulius Sabinus, a military officer and magistrate, erected by his wards.

EDCS-01401140.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Cai filio Fabia Capitoni subpraefecto equitum in fronte pedes XII in agro pedes XII mater posuit\n
EDCS-01401140.translation: His mother erected this for Gaius Iulius Capito, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, cavalry prefect, twelve feet in the front and twelve feet in the land.
EDCS-01401140.summary: This is a funerary monument for Gaius Iulius Capito, a cavalry prefect, erected by his mother.

EDCS-01401141.text_edition: \n Daza Panentis filius annos vixit XXX militavit XVI III Corcodilo fecit Plusia liberta patrono suo et sibi in fronte pedes IV\n
EDCS-01401141.translation: Daza, son of Panentis, lived 30 years, served 16 years. Corcodilus made this for Plusia, his freedwoman, and for himself, four feet in the front.
EDCS-01401141.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Daza, son of Panentis, detailing his lifespan and military service, and also for his freedwoman Plusia, made by Corcodilus.

EDCS-01401142.text_edition: \n Liccaeus Verzonis filius |(centurio) testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-01401142.translation: Liccaeus, son of Verzo, a centurion, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-01401142.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that a centurion named Liccaeus wished for this monument to be erected after his death.

EDCS-01401143.text_edition: \n Cleo Lucceius trierarchus Didymo Lucceio fratri |(centurioni) sibi et suis locus monumenti quoquo versus pedes XVI\n
EDCS-01401143.translation: Cleo for his brother Didymus Lucceius, a centurion, for himself and his family, a plot of 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01401143.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Didymus Lucceius, a centurion, and his family, erected by his brother Cleo.

EDCS-01401144.text_edition: \n Marcus Mevius Praxiai sic filius Telephus |(centurio) classicus locus quadratus pedes XVI\n
EDCS-01401144.translation: Marcus Mevius Telephus, son of Praxias, a regular centurion, a square plot of 16 feet.
EDCS-01401144.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Mevius Telephus, a centurion, specifying the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-01401145.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aurelius Sabinus, a soldier of the first praetorian cohort, served for 12 years. Ampelus set this up for his brother, centurion of Ionysus.
EDCS-01401145.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Ampelus for his brother, Aurelius Sabinus, a soldier in the praetorian guard who served for 12 years.

EDCS-01401147.translation: Of Lucius Decimus Aper, of the 3rd Praetorian cohort, from Bononia, a trumpeter. He lived 28 years, served 9 years. His brother [erected this] in consolation.
EDCS-01401147.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Decimus Aper, a trumpeter in the Praetorian Guard, erected by his brother.

EDCS-01401148.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Sentio Vitali equiti cohortis V praetoriae Arrius Secundus evocatus amico bene merenti\n
EDCS-01401148.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Sentius Vitalis, a cavalryman of the 5th Praetorian cohort. Arrius Secundus, an evocatus, [erected this for] his well-deserving friend.
EDCS-01401148.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Sentius Vitalis, a cavalryman in the Praetorian Guard, erected by his friend.

EDCS-01401149.translation: Publius Maenelius Stablus, son of Statius, of the Pollia tribe, from Mutina, a soldier of the 6th Praetorian cohort, is buried here.
EDCS-01401149.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius Maenelius Stablus, a soldier of the 6th Praetorian cohort from Mutina.

EDCS-01401151.translation: Lucius Caelus, son of Quintus, of the Scaptia tribe, from Faesulae, a soldier of the 8th Praetorian cohort, lived 3X years, served [X] years.
EDCS-01401151.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caelus, a soldier in the 8th Praetorian cohort, detailing his age and service length.

EDCS-01401152.translation: Marcus Glitius, son of Marcus, of the Lemonia tribe, from Bononia, a soldier of the 8th Praetorian cohort, lived 30 years, served 8 years.
EDCS-01401152.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Glitius, a soldier of the Praetorian guard, who died at the age of 30 after 8 years of service.

EDCS-01401153.translation: To the horseman Nervae, of the 8th Praetorian cohort, 30 years of age, [with X] years of service.
EDCS-01401153.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Nervae, a horseman in the Praetorian guard, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-01401157.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et in perpetuo securitatem Licinius Fulgentius ex numero Stablesianorum natus in Norico Ragandone qui vixit annos L menses VI dies III qui perit in aqua Aquileiae die V Idus Iulias facta memoria de suo per Avitum exarchum filium Aduirmium\n
EDCS-01401157.translation: To the departed spirits and for eternal security, Licinius Fulgentius, from the rank of Stablesiani, born in Noricum at Ragandone, who lived 50 years, 6 months, and 3 days, and who perished in the water at Aquileia on the 5th day before the Ides of July; memorial established at his own expense by Avitus, exarch, his son.
EDCS-01401157.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Licinius Fulgentius, a man from Noricum who died in Aquileia, with the memorial established by his son.

EDCS-01401159.translation: To Tiberius Julius Viator, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe, subprefect of the 3rd Lusitanian cohort, II vir for administering justice, prefect of the mounted Ubian cohort; and to his wife Erbonia Grata, daughter of Sextus. Caius Julius Linus, freedman of Augustus, [erected this] for his son and daughter-in-law.
EDCS-01401159.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Caius Julius Linus to his son and daughter-in-law, who held significant military and civic positions.

EDCS-01401160.translation: To the departed spirits. To Marcus Aurelius Eumelus, his messmate and son of Marcus Aurelius Eumelus, a grain dealer, who lived 30 years, 10 days. Tettia Aeliana, his most devoted daughter, made this in the absence of his father, her husband.
EDCS-01401160.summary: This tombstone, set up by Tettia Aeliana for her deceased son and husband, honors Marcus Aurelius Eumelus, a soldier and son of a grain dealer.

EDCS-01401162.translation: Aur(elius) Niger [---], standard-bearer of the [---] legion, was honored/dedicated [---]
EDCS-01401162.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Aurelius Niger, a standard-bearer of a Roman legion.

EDCS-01401163.translation: Gaius Statius, [a veteran] of legion [X], made this himself while alive, for Gaius Statius [his son?].
EDCS-01401163.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Statius, a veteran of an unnamed legion, for himself and possibly his son.

EDCS-01401164.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Antonius Valens, son of a veteran, originally from Fabia in Vercitum, erected this monument for myself and my wife Flavia Crescentina. I have included this monument in my house, where I have lived for many years, as I ordained in my will, that it may not be sold or foreclosed by my freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, from which its income is to be given to my 25th century, the Maroniana of the college of craftsmen, 35; to the Parentalia, 22 and a half, as you are to provide for me and my wife. However, my century is to receive the wine we accept from Marcianus in the Vicus Provinicalis on the 4th day before the Ides of May, so that you may pour libations at my tomb for me and my wife, and feast yourselves. If you do not, the 25th century of Apollinaris will provide for me.
EDCS-01401164.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription detailing the wishes of Marcus Antonius Valens for his tomb and the management of his estate, including provisions for freedmen, descendants, and collegia.

EDCS-01401165.translation: Aurelius Mestrianus has died, having served [X] years.
EDCS-01401165.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Mestrianus, recording his death and years of service.

EDCS-01401167.text_edition: \n Lucius Viennius Luci Aniensis Verus Foro Iuli m[iles legionis VIIII ------\n
EDCS-01401167.translation: Lucius Viennius Verus, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Forum Iulii, a soldier of the 9th legion...
EDCS-01401167.summary: This inscription begins the record of Lucius Viennius Verus, a soldier of the 9th legion from Forum Iulii.

EDCS-01401177.translation: To our Lord Flavius Jovian, triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the state, to our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, perpetual, pious, happy, always Augusti.
EDCS-01401177.summary: This is an imperial dedication to the emperors Jovian, Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-01401178.translation: To our Lord Flavius Jovian, triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-01401178.summary: This is an imperial dedication to Emperor Jovian, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-01401179.translation: To the Emperors, Caesars, our Lords Valentinian and Valens, always Augusti, an insignia born from the happy empire of theirs.
EDCS-01401179.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors Valentinian and Valens, celebrating their rule.

EDCS-01401180.translation: To our lord Valerius Licinianus Licinius, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Emperor.
EDCS-01401180.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Valerius Licinianus Licinius, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-01401181.translation: Nine miles. To Magnentius, Invincible Prince, Victor and Triumphant Emperor, our lord, liberator of the world, restorer of liberty, and protector of soldiers and provinces.
EDCS-01401181.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to the emperor Magnentius, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-01401182.translation: Lucius Novius Culicio sold the Mattonianum estate to Claudia Semne at the 7th milestone on the road leading [to ...].
EDCS-01401182.summary: This is a legal record of a property sale by Lucius Novius Culicio to Claudia Semne, specifying the location by milestone and road.

EDCS-01500001.text_edition: \n Hic requiescit in pace s Farius qui etlis tribunus Minerviorum tribunus primorum militum Moesiacorum regionis Montanae vixit annos LXX depo[situs ------\n
EDCS-01500001.translation: Here lies in peace Farius, who was also a tribune of the Minervii, a tribune of the first soldiers of the Moesian region Montana, lived 70 years, buried [---]
EDCS-01500001.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Farius, a military officer, and mentions his rank and place of service.

EDCS-01500003.translation: Sabinus departed from this world at fifty years of age, from among the protectors.
EDCS-01500003.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the death of Sabinus, a former member of the protectors, at the age of fifty.

EDCS-01500004.text_edition: \n Flavius Posidonius veteranus ex numeromerum qui sibi fecit hunc locum uxori hunc locum uxore suae\n
EDCS-01500004.translation: Flavius Posidonius, a veteran from the numerus, who made this place for himself and for his wife.
EDCS-01500004.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Flavius Posidonius, a veteran, for himself and his wife, indicating the creation of a burial plot.

EDCS-01500008.text_edition: \n Aurelius Fortunatus veteranus legio<n=R>um XI Claudiae coniugi merenti posuit quae vixit mecum annis sic XVIIII et mensis VI et dies V Nonarum VI dignae animae tuae posuit non gratulor quod ante tempus me decipisti sic et natos tuos nutricatos Libersio alomnus sic tecum pace \n
EDCS-01500008.translation: Aurelius Fortunatus, a veteran of the Legio XI Claudia, placed this for his deserving wife who lived with me for 19 years, 6 months, and 5 days. To your worthy soul, I do not rejoice that you deceived me ahead of time. So too your children, raised by Libersius, the foster father. So may you be in peace.
EDCS-01500008.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Aurelius Fortunatus, a veteran of Legio XI Claudia, to his deceased wife, detailing their years together and expressing grief.

EDCS-01500011.translation: Here lies Urbicus, the charioteer, who was called Romulus, who lived 23 years, 5 months, 10 days; died on the Ides of October.
EDCS-01500011.summary: This is a tomb inscription for a charioteer named Urbicus, also known as Romulus, who died on October 15th.

EDCS-01500012.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01500012.translation: Here rests Iovinus the silversmith, who bought a place while alive for himself, buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of February by the faithful.
EDCS-01500012.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Iovinus, a silversmith, who had purchased his burial plot during his lifetime, and notes the date of his interment.

EDCS-01500014.translation: To the good memory of Maxsimius Satriniani, scholaris, lived 22 years, 10 months.
EDCS-01500014.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Maxsimius, a scholaris, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-01500015.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01500015.translation: To the departed spirits. Vincentius, well-deserving, they made [this] against a vow.
EDCS-01500015.summary: This votive dedication is made to the Manes for Vincentius, who is described as 'well-deserving'.

EDCS-01500017.text_edition: \n Accepit requiem post septuaginta non minus annos nulli numquam nocuit sinceriter semper amavit amicos thalamo suscepit Stratonicenem coniugem iunctam o prava genesis primum sic qui sic tulisti maritum nihil pulchrius fuerat quam coniugem in ante misisset iuncta quem possedit XXXV vel amplius annos ut lacrimae minimae sic per genitoris vitam fuissent si scire vis lector qui pausat capita versorum require defunctus in pace XVII Kalendas Novembres Nepotiano et Facundo conssulibus\n
EDCS-01500017.translation: He received rest after no less than seventy years. He never harmed anyone. He always loved friends sincerely. He welcomed Stratonicene, his joined wife, into his chamber. Perhaps fate decreed it. There was nothing more beautiful than a wife sent before. Whom he possessed as his wife for 35 years or more. As tears are small, so might life have been through the parent. If you wish to know, reader, who rests here, seek the end of the verses. Died in peace on the 17th day before the Kalends of November, when Nepotianus and Facundus were consuls.
EDCS-01500017.summary: This lengthy epitaph commemorates a deceased individual, praising their virtues, their marriage of over 35 years, and recording their death date in the consulship of Nepotianus and Facundus.

EDCS-01500018.translation: Here lies Secundinus, who lived 45 years, 8 months, 3 days; laid to rest in peace on the 4th day before the Ides of July, when Tatianus and Symmachus, most distinguished men, were consuls.
EDCS-01500018.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Secundinus, who died on July 12th during the consulship of Tatianus and Symmachus (likely 391 CE).

EDCS-01500019.translation: 3 months, who lies with her brother Ursulus and was laid to rest on the Nones of December, during the 6th consulship of our lord Honorius Augustus, with Benignus and Honorata. Parents made (this) against their vow.
EDCS-01500019.summary: This funerary inscription records a person laid to rest on December 7th, during the reign of Honorius, with parents placing the monument against their wishes.

EDCS-01500020.translation: To good memory Abra, who lived about 75 years; Maxentia, who lived about 40 years; to good memory Maximina, who lived about 4 years. Departed in faithful peace, laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01500020.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Abra, Maxentia, and Maximina, who were laid to rest on October 20th.

EDCS-01500037.translation: Aurelius Helianus of Nicomedia, here placed.
EDCS-01500037.summary: A simple epitaph identifying Aurelius Helianus of Nicomedia as being buried at this location.

EDCS-01500038.text_edition: \n Aurelius Iulianus qui vixit in saeculo nnos XXXI menses IIII dies III Aurelia Dionilla soror carissima fratri dulcissimo corpus curavit neofitus sic discessit\n
EDCS-01500038.translation: Aurelius Iulianus, who lived 31 years, 4 months, and 3 days. Aurelia Dionilla, dearest sister, cared for her sweetest brother's body. He departed as a neophyte.
EDCS-01500038.summary: This epitaph records the death of Aurelius Iulianus at the age of 31 and mentions that his sister, Aurelia Dionilla, arranged for his burial.

EDCS-01500041.translation: Aurelius Ursinianus, who lived 86 years, 5 months, 20 days, with his dearest wife Iulia Valeria, with whom he lived 24 years, made (this monument) for themselves while alive in peace.
EDCS-01500041.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Aurelius Ursinianus and his wife Iulia Valeria for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-01500042.summary: This is a simple tomb inscription indicating that Aurelius V is buried here.

EDCS-01500045.text_edition: \n Aurelia Isevera eam nnorum XVIII agnovisse virum eam vixisse nnos XXXV cum carum virginium suum Rufinianum de matre nati fili XIIII dolorem ex eo patri dimisit duos orfanos sibi similantes et se moriens petuit sic carum virginium suum corpus tradere e<i=N>dem sepulchro eam paussavisse sic Kalendis Martiis \n
EDCS-01500045.translation: Aurelia Isevera, having recognized a husband at the age of 18, having lived 35 years with her dear virgin Rufinianus, the son of her mother, left him twelve children. And dying, she requested that her dear virgin husband's body be placed in the same tomb. She rested on the Kalends of March.
EDCS-01500045.summary: This epitaph records the death of Aurelia Isevera, who lived 35 years and had 12 children with her husband Rufinianus, and her wish to be buried in the same tomb as him.

EDCS-01500047.translation: Aurelia Nigella placed this for her deserving husband Urso, who lived with me for 5 years. Receive your innocent son Ursicinus, who lived for 3 years and 1 month. Spiritus vester in bonum.
EDCS-01500047.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Aurelia Nigella for her husband Urso and son Ursicinus, and dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500048.translation: Aurelia Quiriacae erected this monument to her sweetest husband Flavius Salvius, who lived 46 years, 8 months, 15 days.
EDCS-01500048.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by Aurelia Quiriacae for her husband Flavius Salvius.

EDCS-01500052.translation: In this place lies Pullicla, named Benedicta.
EDCS-01500052.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pullicla Benedicta, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500055.translation: To good memory: Honoratus, [a] good father, [placed this] for his parents against [their] wishes.
EDCS-01500055.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for parents, set up by their son Honoratus, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500058.translation: For the well-deserving Caricus, who lived approximately 60 years, buried on the 9th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-01500058.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial date and approximate age of Caricus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500059.translation: Catus has been laid to rest.
EDCS-01500059.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Catus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500069.translation: For the well-deserving Didati, who lived approximately 60 years, buried on the 3rd day before the Nones of November.
EDCS-01500069.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial date and approximate age of Didati, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500072.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a financial transaction or debt settlement, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500074.translation: Flavius Eubeus, who lived for three years, rests in peace.
EDCS-01500074.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Eubeus, recording his short life, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500087.translation: Flavius Castus [erected this] for Silvanus, who lived [well], deserving.
EDCS-01500087.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Flavius Castus to Silvanus, recognizing his merit, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500090.translation: To good memory: Pompeia [placed this] for her dearest son, Flavius Felix, who lived 4 months and 30 days.
EDCS-01500090.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Pompeia to her son Flavius Felix, noting his very young age, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500091.translation: Flavius M[--]lius set up [this for] his dearest wife Valentina, however...
EDCS-01500091.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman imperial period, was erected by Flavius M[--]lius for his wife Valentina.

EDCS-01500092.translation: Flavius Victor placed this for his most worthy wife Satria Severa, who lived with me for 32 years, [3] days, and 2 hours, who rested.
EDCS-01500092.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Flavius Victor for his wife Satria Severa, recording the duration of their marriage, and dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500095.translation: Caianus, who lived for six years and two months and five days, and Lupicinus, who lived for five years and twenty-two days. Aurelius Lupus, father, placed this for his dearest sons, alive.
EDCS-01500095.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Aurelius Lupus for his sons Caianus and Lupicinus, providing their ages and likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500096.translation: To Modesta, a worthy woman, a citizen of Gallisana, well deserving.
EDCS-01500096.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Modesta, a deserving female citizen of Gallisana, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500099.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the name Ger and his lifespan, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500103.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01500103.translation: For Honesimus, of all innocence and praiseworthy discipline, who lived with me for 8 years. Casta placed this for her husband against her vow.
EDCS-01500103.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Casta for her husband Honesimus, noting his virtuous character and the duration of their marriage, and dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500105.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01500105.translation: Innox Ienuarianus, who lived for 6 years, 2 months, and 15 days. His parents made this against their vow.
EDCS-01500105.summary: This funerary epitaph records the ages of Innox Ienuarianus at death and was made by his parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500107.translation: The well-deserving Inginianus, who lived for 51 years, 7 months, and 5 days, buried on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of [Month]. He departed in peace.
EDCS-01500107.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and burial date of Inginianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500112.translation: and Iulia, around [age?] years old, laid to rest on the Kalends.
EDCS-01500112.summary: This inscription likely records the burial of Iulia, mentioning her age and date of burial.

EDCS-01500115.translation: and the memory of Iustus L, who left his parents, who lived.
EDCS-01500115.summary: This inscription commemorates Iustus L, referencing his parents and lifespan.

EDCS-01500117.translation: Largius, faithful son, departed in peace, who lived 29 years, 6 months, 6 days, on the III Idus of October. His parents placed him here contrary to his wishes.
EDCS-01500117.summary: This epitaph records the death of Largius, detailing his age at death and burial date, and noting his parents' action.

EDCS-01500121.text_edition: \n Valentina octavo die Mercuri recesset sic\n
EDCS-01500121.translation: Valentina departed on the eighth day of Mercury.
EDCS-01500121.summary: This inscription records the death of Valentina on a specific day, likely a funerary marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500122.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Liberius, identifying him as faithful, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500123.translation: Macarius rests here for a good memory, with his wife.
EDCS-01500123.summary: This inscription is a memorial for Macarius and his wife, intended to be remembered well.

EDCS-01500124.translation: In the name of Jesus Christ. Here rests Mamula, wife of Iustinus, who accepted her husband, aged 14 years. She lived 52 years, she rested in peace.
EDCS-01500124.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Mamula, recording her age at death and her marriage, likely dating to the Christian period.

EDCS-01500127.translation: In good memory. Mascolianus, who lived 40 years and 6 months.
EDCS-01500127.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mascolianus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500129.translation: Mauricius, laid to rest in peace on the 4th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-01500129.summary: This inscription records the burial of Mauricius on a specific date in August.

EDCS-01500134.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus bene merita Muccianilla qui sic vixit annos XL menses V dies X maritus meus doliens fecet sic recesinset sic in pace fedelis sic Deposita XX Calendas Nobembres sic\n
EDCS-01500134.translation: To the departed spirits. Muccianilla, who lived 40 years, 5 months, and 10 days. Her husband, grieving, made this. She departed thus, a faithful one, in peace. Interred the 20th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01500134.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Muccianilla and the grief of her husband who erected the monument, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500137.translation: To the well-deserving Orta, who lived about two years, 3 months, and 7 days. She departed in peace, a faithful one, interred the day before the Kalends of August. Her parents, grieving, made this against their wishes, and her grandmother also, when she departed with her granddaughter.
EDCS-01500137.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short lifespan of Orta and the grief of her parents and grandmother who erected the monument, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500138.text_edition: \n Pardo Lucifera filio merenti qui bixit sic annis cinque sic\n
EDCS-01500138.translation: To Pardo Lucifera, a deserving son, who lived for five years.
EDCS-01500138.summary: This funerary epitaph honors a son named Pardo Lucifera, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500140.summary: This inscription is a simple naming of Domnula Peregrina, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-01500145.translation: In this holy place rests Pisinio, who lived 1 year, 10 months, and 2 days, laid to rest on the 11th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01500145.summary: This inscription records the burial of Pisinio in a holy place, detailing his age at death and burial date.

EDCS-01500149.text_edition: \n Bene meritae Primitivae qui sic vixit annos XLV menses VII dies XV virginius suos sic dolies contra votum posuit recessit in paca sic fidelis Nonis Octobris sic\n
EDCS-01500149.translation: To the well-deserving Primitiva, who lived 45 years, 7 months, and 15 days. Her husband, grieving, placed this against his wishes. She departed in peace, a faithful one, on the Ides of October.
EDCS-01500149.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Primitiva and the grief of her husband who erected the monument, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500152.translation: To good memory. For the innocent Proculina, who lived 6 years, 5 months, and 9 days. She departed in peace, a faithful one, interred the day before the Ides of June.
EDCS-01500152.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of the young Proculina and her burial date, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500153.translation: Purpuria rested in peace, aged 4 years.
EDCS-01500153.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short lifespan of Purpuria and her peaceful repose, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500157.translation: Laid to rest in this pool, he rests in peace in the name of Christ the Savior, who lived approximately until the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01500157.summary: This inscription records a burial in a 'pool' (perhaps a baptistery or a tomb complex), mentioning Christ and an approximate date of death.

EDCS-01500159.summary: This inscription is a simple statement of Secundina's peaceful rest, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-01500160.translation: For a good memory of Secundus, who lived 80 years, [and] months, departed on the ninth day before the Kalends of December, faithful in peace.
EDCS-01500160.summary: This epitaph commemorates Secundus, detailing his age at death and burial date, and affirming his faithful peaceful rest.

EDCS-01500167.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Soricinus and a vow, possibly related to a religious dedication or a funerary marker.

EDCS-01500170.translation: Died from life on the 13th day before the Kalends of Statia; she lived [for some period].
EDCS-01500170.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of an individual, specifying the date and the duration of life.

EDCS-01500171.translation: His most devoted sons placed this for their most deserving and pious parents, who lived in their care for 30 years, Sura and Vitalio.
EDCS-01500171.summary: This funerary monument was erected by sons for their parents, Sura and Vitalio, commemorating their piety and the duration of their lives together.

EDCS-01500173.translation: The mother made this for her daughter, Iovina, who lived well, for 6 years, 6 months, 16 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-01500173.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of a young girl named Iovina, erected by her grieving mother, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500177.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01500177.translation: To the departed spirits. For the innocent Ursa, who lived about 15 years. Her mother, grieving, placed this against her wishes on the 6th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-01500177.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Ursa and the grief of her mother who erected the monument, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01500180.translation: For the well-deserving Ursus, who lived [for some period].
EDCS-01500180.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Ursus, acknowledging his well-deserving nature and recording his lifespan.

EDCS-01500187.translation: To Valentiniana of good memory, who deserved well, who lived for [3] years and with her husband for [3] years, and departed on the Kalends of March [in peace?], the faithful parents [---] erected.
EDCS-01500187.summary: This epitaph commemorates Valentiniana, detailing her lifespan and marital duration, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-01500188.translation: Here rests the innocent Venerosa, who lived 56 years and 10 months, buried on the day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01500188.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Venerosa, providing her age at death and the date of her burial.

EDCS-01500190.translation: For the Manes of Victoria, their most sweet daughter, well-deserving, who lived one year and 53 days and 2 night hours; Felicissimus and Felicissima, her parents, made this.
EDCS-01500190.summary: This funerary dedication was made by parents, Felicissimus and Felicissima, for their daughter Victoria, noting her short life.

EDCS-01500197.text_edition: \n Apollini Beleno Publius Aemilius Eutyches conductor VIII et XX ripae fluminis Danuvi pecunia sua votum solvit\n
EDCS-01500197.translation: To Apollo Belenus, Publius Aemilius Eutyches, overseer of the 8th and 20th sections of the bank of the river Danube, paid his vow with his own money.
EDCS-01500197.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid by Publius Aemilius Eutyches, an overseer of the Danube riverbank, to the god Apollo Belenus.

EDCS-01500199.translation: To Vulcanus Augustus, Gaius Iulius Lampsacus and Iulia Heo(?) Hec[---] willingly paid what was due.
EDCS-01500199.summary: This inscription records a voluntary vow paid to Vulcanus Augustus by Gaius Iulius Lampsacus and Iulia Heo(?), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500201.translation: The place was given by Abas, slave of the colonists of Aquileia, to his friend, the official of Hercules, as a place.
EDCS-01500201.summary: This inscription records the allocation of a plot of land by Abas, a slave of the Aquileian colonists, to an official of Hercules.

EDCS-01500202.translation: Decuria I [---] / Gaius Volusius Sa[---] / Timinia [---] / [---] / Domitius [---] / Domitia [---] / Gaius Babullius [---] / Babullia [---]
EDCS-01500202.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to list names, possibly related to a civic or religious group, with some restored names.

EDCS-01500204.translation: [---] to Marcus Novius [---], formerly prefect of a legion, deceased [---].
EDCS-01500204.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to Marcus Novius, identified as a former legionary prefect, possibly an epitaph.

EDCS-01500206.translation: Valeria Eutychia made this for Lucius Valerius Agathias, her most devoted VIvir of Aquileia, while alive, and for Lucius Valerius Agathocles and Valerius Gratus, grandsons, and Valeria Mnesitheia, daughter, and Gaius Lucretius Sabinus, son, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-01500206.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Valeria Eutychia for her husband Lucius Valerius Agathias, a VIvir of Aquileia, and other family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500207.translation: [---] of Aquileia, for 11 months and 12 days [---]stus, VIvir [---] Eutychia [---] the most unhappy parents.
EDCS-01500207.summary: This fragmented epitaph mentions a period of 11 months and 12 days and refers to parents, possibly related to Eutychia and a VIvir.

EDCS-01500208.text_edition: \n Publio Aemilio Severiano filio Publius Aemilius Eutyches pater piiss[im ------\n
EDCS-01500208.translation: Publius Aemilius Eutyches, the most devoted father, for Publius Aemilius Severianus, his son [---].
EDCS-01500208.summary: This is a dedication made by a father, Publius Aemilius Eutyches, to his son, Publius Aemilius Severianus, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-01500209.translation: To the Manes of Publius Annius Caeneus. Titus Cilnius Caeneus and Annia Eucarpia, [dedicate this here].
EDCS-01500209.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to Publius Annius Caeneus by Titus Cilnius Caeneus and Annia Eucarpia.

EDCS-01500210.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, mentioning the name Aphrodisius, possibly a person's name or a deity's.

EDCS-01500211.translation: [---] Aphrodisius and [his] freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-01500211.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning Aphrodisius and his extended household, likely a dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-01500212.translation: To the Divine Shades. Baburius Antius erected this for himself and for Petronia Augeni, his incomparable wife, who lived with me for 46 years.
EDCS-01500212.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Baburius Antius for himself and his wife Petronia Augeni, recording their years of marriage, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500214.translation: The space for the monument of Gaius Calvus Messor: 15 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-01500214.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot or monument for Gaius Calvus Messor.

EDCS-01500216.summary: This inscription appears to be a name fragment, likely from a funerary monument.

EDCS-01500218.translation: To Flavia Victorina, who deserved well.
EDCS-01500218.summary: This is a dedication to Flavia Victorina, likely for her deserving conduct, possibly on a tomb.

EDCS-01500219.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Fulvia Venusta created this monument for herself.

EDCS-01500220.translation: To Iulius Cotillus, who lived 80 years, erected for himself while alive, and to Iulius Antonius, his son, and Iulius Pl[---]ophitus.
EDCS-01500220.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulius Cotillus and his son, erected by Cotillus himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-01500222.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Licinio Baburio Philocalo Marcus Licinius Philocalus et Baburia Clementiane filio piissimo\n
EDCS-01500222.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Licinius Philocalus and Baburia Clementiane to their most dutiful son, Marcus Licinius Baburius Philocalus.
EDCS-01500222.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents to their pious son, Marcus Licinius Baburius Philocalus.

EDCS-01500224.translation: Valeria Tertia to her most dutiful husband, Lucius Magius Lamyros; she made this while alive.
EDCS-01500224.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife to her dutiful husband, Lucius Magius Lamyros, made by the wife during her lifetime.

EDCS-01500225.translation: To Gaius Mercusenus Suasor, freedman, made for himself while alive; to his son, Gaius Mercusenus Florus, and to Celadus, freedman, son of the freedwoman Appuleia.
EDCS-01500225.summary: This inscription records multiple individuals, likely family members and freedmen, with funerary dedications, including a self-funded tomb by Gaius Mercusenus Suasor.

EDCS-01500227.translation: Site of the monument of Aulus Petronius Alexander and Marcus Licinius Prudentis Massa, 31 feet in front, 75 feet in the field. Site of the monument of Marcus Licinius Prudentis Massa and Aulus Petronius Alexander, 31 feet in front, 75 feet in the field.
EDCS-01500227.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions and ownership of a burial plot, with duplicate entries for the same individuals and measurements.

EDCS-01500228.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Philagrypnos, noting his age at death.

EDCS-01500230.translation: To Valerius M[---], freedman of Gaius, and [---]ria Spele[---].
EDCS-01500230.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary funerary dedication to two individuals, one of whom is identified as a freedman.

EDCS-01500231.translation: To Lucius Statius Hermadion; Statius Hermais, his daughter, and Vibia Stativa [dedicated this].
EDCS-01500231.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Statius Hermadion by his daughter and another woman, likely a family member.

EDCS-01500251.translation: To Utio, freedman of Lucius, and to Maxima.
EDCS-01500251.summary: This is a dedication to two individuals, Utio and Maxima, likely by their patrons or family members.

EDCS-01500255.translation: Helias, bishop of Aquileia, servant of Jesus Christ, by the grace and aid of God, fulfilled his vow as founder of the church of Saint Euphemia.
EDCS-01500255.summary: This inscription records Bishop Helias of Aquileia fulfilling his vow as the founder of the church of Saint Euphemia, likely dating to his episcopacy.

EDCS-01500256.translation: Stephanus, Gregory, priest, and Antonius made (this).
EDCS-01500256.summary: This is a dedication or commission of a work by Stephanus, Gregorius (priest), and Antonius.

EDCS-01500257.translation: Stephanus, the shipowner, fulfilled his vow with his people.
EDCS-01500257.summary: This inscription records Stephanus, a shipowner, fulfilling a vow with his associates or crew.

EDCS-01500259.translation: Sesinius, the chamberlain, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01500259.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sesinius, identified as a chamberlain.

EDCS-01500262.translation: Here rests in the peace of Christ, Marcianus, bishop of holy memory, who lived in the episcopacy for 44 years and traveled abroad for the cause of the faith for 40 years; he was laid to rest in this tomb on the 8th day before the Kalends of May, in the eleventh indiction.
EDCS-01500262.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcianus, a bishop, detailing his years of service, travels, and date of death, likely from the 4th or 5th century based on the indiction.

EDCS-01500263.translation: Helias, bishop, servant of Jesus Christ, made (this) serving you, holy church of Aquileia.
EDCS-01500263.summary: This inscription records Bishop Helias of Aquileia dedicating something to the church he serves.

EDCS-01500264.translation: Dominicus, the notary, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01500264.summary: This is a votive inscription by Dominicus, identified as a notary.

EDCS-01500267.translation: Iustinus, the notary, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01500267.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iustinus, identified as a notary.

EDCS-01500268.translation: Laurentius, the deacon, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01500268.summary: This is a votive inscription by Laurentius, identified as a deacon.

EDCS-01500269.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lautus, likely a freedman given the commonality of the name and the context of vows.

EDCS-01500270.translation: Petrus the notary fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01500270.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Petrus, identified as a notary, indicating his religious commitment.

EDCS-01500273.translation: To my dearest wife Aurelia, who lived 3 years, 8 months, and with me in marriage 1 year, 8 months, and days.
EDCS-01500273.summary: This epitaph commemorates Aurelia, detailing her lifespan and the duration of her marriage.

EDCS-01500277.translation: Here lies the infant Nonnea, 3 years and 6 months old, buried on a Tuesday.
EDCS-01500277.summary: This epitaph records the burial of an infant named Nonnea, specifying her age and the day of burial.

EDCS-01500278.translation: For the most excellent, kind, and innocent Cervonius, and for Quartina Theodora, a most chaste woman, who always sought with prayers from their children the gift of fate for both, so that a single house might hold their resting bodies. This was accomplished by the pious will of their two children, obeying the commands of their parents. For thus their merits demanded and their deeds, whose life was renowned and deeds most well-known. Oh modesty, oh goodness, always fitting to be loved, worthy honor bestowed upon the worthy. Learn from fear, thus children should always be to their parents. Here, the brothers Marcellus and Marcellinus against their own desire establish a tomb.
EDCS-01500278.summary: This lengthy epitaph, likely from the late antique period, records the construction of a tomb by two brothers, Marcellus and Marcellinus, in honor of their parents, Cervonius and Quartina Theodora, praising their virtues and the filial piety that led to the tomb's creation.

EDCS-01500279.translation: To our lady, daughter, daughter Ursa, Sabbatius and Candida placed [this] for their innocent daughter, who lived 5 years and 9 days, their most innocent daughter, in peace. [Also for] son Luentius, who lived 8 years, 2 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-01500279.summary: This epitaph records the memorial placed by Sabbatius and Candida for their two children, Ursa and Luentius, detailing their ages at death.

EDCS-01500283.translation: It happened to me, a terrible wound, only son. I raised him flourishing, my sweetest son, who lived 12 years, 6 months, and 8 days. Victorinus the father, against [his] vow.
EDCS-01500283.summary: This epitaph laments the death of a son and records his age, erected by his grieving father, Victorinus.

EDCS-01500285.translation: Agapitus and Daimia made [this] with their family.
EDCS-01500285.summary: This inscription records a dedication or construction made by Agapitus and Daimia along with their household.

EDCS-01500286.translation: Hilarus and Tus and Afrodisia made [this] with all their family, 100 feet.
EDCS-01500286.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication made by Hilarus, Tus, and Afrodisia with their families, measuring 100 feet.

EDCS-01500288.translation: Paulinus and Marcellina with all their family, 1500 feet.
EDCS-01500288.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication made by Paulinus and Marcellina with their families, measuring 1500 feet.

EDCS-01500291.translation: Lucius Albius Buccio, son of Lucius, and his wife Albia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-01500291.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman and his wife, indicating they paid for it during their lifetime.

EDCS-01500292.translation: Gaius Appuleius Philomusus, freedman of Tappo, while alive.
EDCS-01500292.summary: This inscription records Gaius Appuleius Philomusus, a freedman, who likely set up his own monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-01500293.translation: Gaius Appuleius Philomusus, freedman of Tappo, while alive. He made [this monument] for himself and his family, and for Barbaia Prima, freedwoman of Gaius, his fellow freedwoman, and for Marcus Trosius Hilarus, freedman of Marcus. The plot is 16 feet in front and 16 feet in depth.
EDCS-01500293.summary: This is a funerary monument for Gaius Appuleius Philomusus and his relatives/fellow freedmen, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-01500294.translation: Tiberius Barbius, son of Tiberius, freedman.
EDCS-01500294.summary: This is a personal name, likely an epitaph or a dedication by Tiberius Barbius, a freedman.

EDCS-01500297.translation: Clodia Medula Prima, daughter of Lucius, while alive, made [this monument] for herself and her freedmen and freedwomen, and for Vettia Tryphera, freedwoman of Marcus, and for Bellonius. The plot is 16 square feet.
EDCS-01500297.summary: This funerary inscription records Clodia Medula Prima dedicating a plot for herself, her dependents, and others, specifying the plot size.

EDCS-01500298.translation: Lucius Cluvius Nicephor, son of Lucius, [set up this] plot. It is 30 feet in front and 31 feet in depth.
EDCS-01500298.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Lucius Cluvius Nicephor, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01500299.translation: Sextus Cominius Atetmus, son of Sextus, freedman.
EDCS-01500299.summary: This is a personal name, likely an epitaph or a dedication by Sextus Cominius Atetmus, a freedman.

EDCS-01500301.translation: Cuspius Timo, freedman of Lucius, while alive, and Tertia Cuspi [set up this] plot, 16 square feet. [Plot] 16 square feet. [Plot] 16 square feet. [Plot, 16 square feet].
EDCS-01500301.summary: This inscription records Cuspius Timo and Tertia Cuspi setting up multiple burial plots, each measuring 16 square feet.

EDCS-01500302.translation: Titus Decidius [son of Titus?], served without fault, what he had through his patron perished.
EDCS-01500302.summary: This inscription seems to be a epitaph lamenting the loss of someone's property or legacy after their death.

EDCS-01500303.translation: Lucius Fabius Statius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Fabius Restatus, freedman of Lucius. The father, while alive, made [this monument] for himself and his freedmen, for Lucius Philomusus, and for Lucius Hilarus, freedman of Lucius. The plot is 16 square feet.
EDCS-01500303.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Fabius Statius and his freedman setting up a monument and plot for themselves and other freedmen.

EDCS-01500305.translation: Pamphila, Feronia, Caius Ferionius, freedman of Caius, and Teucer, freedman of Caius, made [this plot] while alive. The plot is 16 feet wide and 16 feet deep.
EDCS-01500305.summary: This inscription records four individuals, likely freedmen and their patron or family members, jointly establishing a burial plot.

EDCS-01500306.translation: Marcus Lucius, freedman of Marcus, and Lucia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, and Marcus Labeo, son of Marcus, while alive made this. Iulia Secunda, daughter of Iulius, his wife, while alive made this for herself, her descendants, and her freedmen and freedwomen. Area of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01500306.summary: This funerary epitaph records the makers of a tomb for themselves and their freedmen, likely dating to the 1st century BCE or 1st century CE.

EDCS-01500307.translation: Sextus Lusius Liccaeus, freedman of Sextus.
EDCS-01500307.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying an individual and their status, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500311.translation: Aulus Antiochus, freedman of Aulus, while alive made this for himself and his family. Maia Hilara, freedwoman of Aulus.
EDCS-01500311.summary: This epitaph records a man and woman, likely a couple, who erected a monument for themselves, probably dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500313.translation: For Lucius Minatius Damaes, freedman of Lucius Publius. Liccaeus, son, for himself and his family, and for his fellow freedwoman Fausta. Area of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01500313.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording a man dedicating a plot for himself, his family, and a fellow freedwoman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500314.translation: Marcus Octavius Asclepa, son of Marcus, freedman.
EDCS-01500314.summary: This is a personal name, likely an epitaph or a dedication by Marcus Octavius Asclepa, a freedman.

EDCS-01500317.translation: Quintus Ovidius, son of Caius, greetings.
EDCS-01500317.summary: This inscription records a greeting to Quintus Ovidius, son of Caius, possibly on a tombstone or a marker.

EDCS-01500318.translation: Caius Ovidius, son of Caius; Caius, Lucius Quintus, Titus, sons of Caius.
EDCS-01500318.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely family members, with Caius Ovidius being the primary subject and the others his sons or relatives.

EDCS-01500319.summary: This is a brief greeting possibly from or to someone associated with the place name Pacaene.

EDCS-01500320.translation: Titus Paccius Rufus, son of Titus, and Titus Paccius, son of Quintus, while alive. Therefore, the labor of the bricks has stood; these bricks have endured.
EDCS-01500320.summary: This epitaph commemorates two individuals, Titus Paccius Rufus and Titus Paccius, and celebrates the enduring quality of the brickwork of their monument, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500321.translation: Marcus Tertius, son of Marcus. Tertia [Petice]dia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-01500321.summary: This fragmented epitaph records two individuals, likely father and daughter, whose monument is partially lost, possibly dating to the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01500322.summary: This very fragmented epitaph records a freedman and his patron, with minimal information available, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500323.translation: Publius Petronius Persa, son of Lucius.
EDCS-01500323.summary: This is a personal name, likely an epitaph or a dedication by Publius Petronius Persa, son of Lucius.

EDCS-01500324.summary: This is a highly fragmented inscription, possibly a funerary epitaph, with only a few letters and a possible name preserved.

EDCS-01500325.translation: Lucius Pinarius Natta, the father. Lucius Pinarius Natta, the son. Cailia Antiopa, freedwoman of Caius, the most obedient wife.
EDCS-01500325.summary: This funerary epitaph records a father and son, with an inscription for the wife of the father, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500326.translation: Caius Popilius Ter, son of Caius, freedman.
EDCS-01500326.summary: This is a personal name, likely an epitaph or a dedication by Caius Popilius Ter, a freedman.

EDCS-01500328.translation: Publius Hilarus, freedman of Ario, while alive made this for Ario and his freedmen and freedwomen. Titus Firmius Primigenius.
EDCS-01500328.summary: This epitaph records a freedman dedicating a monument for his patron and the patron's freedmen, possibly dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500331.translation: Lucius Samiarius, son of Ovius; Lucius, son of Lucius; Marcus, son of Lucius; Caius, son of Lucius; Quintus, son of Lucius; Sextus, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made.
EDCS-01500331.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Samiarius and his five sons (Lucius, Marcus, Caius, Quintus, and Sextus) commissioned the creation of a monument or work.

EDCS-01500332.summary: This inscription begins with the name Caius Titellius, son of Marcus, and indicates that further information is missing or illegible.

EDCS-01500334.translation: Marcus Varc, Titus Vettius, Cnaeus Glitius, Lucius Ma...
EDCS-01500334.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several Roman personal names.

EDCS-01500335.translation: Varia Hermiona, freedwoman of a woman, [daughter?] of Marcus, freedman...
EDCS-01500335.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription concerning Varia Hermiona, identified as a freedwoman, and possibly related to a freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-01500336.translation: Lucius Vibius Philodamus, freedman of Lucius, and Vibia Asia, freedwoman of Lucius, and Lucius Vibius Anderorus, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Paetus, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Vibius [3]rorus, freedman of Lucius, made [this].
EDCS-01500336.summary: This funerary monument was erected by freedmen for their patron and other freedmen, likely in the first or second century CE.

EDCS-01500341.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins with a praenomen and gentilician name, followed by a filiation.

EDCS-01500360.translation: Domnabus, willingly and deservedly, paid his vow with a cheerful spirit from chastity.
EDCS-01500360.summary: This is a dedication from an individual named Domnabus who fulfilled a vow, possibly related to a deity of chastity, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500361.translation: [...] and I commit to your fidelity and to your heirs, so that they may be kept safe, [...] as they are [...], under the consulship of G(aius) Gallus Quintus Carminius [3] and [3] Martias.
EDCS-01500361.summary: This fragment appears to be part of a legal document or testament, likely from the Roman Imperial period, referencing heirs and consuls.

EDCS-01500362.translation: Lucius Vibius was elected by the jurors and, as praefectus iure dicundo, was honored with a hasta pura (ceremonial spear).
EDCS-01500362.summary: This inscription records Lucius Vibius, who was elected by jurors and honored with a hasta pura while serving as praefectus iure dicundo, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01500363.translation: Marcus Antistius Euporus made [this]. Boreas, Desolinus, Eurus, Auster, Africus, Favonius, Aquilo, Septentrio.
EDCS-01500363.summary: This inscription records the creation of something by Marcus Antistius Euporus, followed by a list of names, possibly personifications of winds, likely a funerary monument from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500364.translation: Aratria Galla, daughter of Caius, by her will, provided for the paving of the decumanus from the forum(?) to the sea(?) gate with stone(?).
EDCS-01500364.summary: This funerary epitaph records a woman, Aratria Galla, who bequeathed funds for the paving of a public road, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01500366.translation: [...]nia to Lucia Ci[3]niae, to Gaius T[...]
EDCS-01500366.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to record a dedication or a familial relationship, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01500370.translation: colleagues and fellow citizens made [this] for him from their own funds. May the Manes grant you happy places and grant us [deep places]. May you [always] be remembered with us. Born in the castle of Dardanos, died in Aquileia.
EDCS-01500370.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an individual who died in Aquileia, likely from the Roman Imperial period, mentioning colleagues, citizens, and the underworld.

EDCS-01500374.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly referring to someone or something related to Augustus, originating from Africa.

EDCS-01500379.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a name or title, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500385.translation: Place of the monument: Belonging to Fructus, freedman of Crispus. In the front 16 feet, in the land 50 feet.
EDCS-01500385.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, specifying its dimensions and ownership by Fructus, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01500389.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01500389.text_edition: \n Locus publice Cai filius Palatina Iulius Festus IIvir quinquennalis Campanorum praefectus cohortis I Asturum praefectus alae III Asturum piae fidelis civium Romanorum subpraefectus vigilum advocatus fisci procurator divi Hadriani\n
EDCS-01500389.translation: Public place of Lucius Julius Festus, son of Caius, of the Palatina tribe, twice quinquennial duovir, prefect of the first cohort of Asturians, prefect of the third ala of Asturians, pious and faithful citizen of the Romans, subprefect of the vigiles, advocate of the imperial treasury, procurator of the divine Hadrian.
EDCS-01500389.summary: This is a detailed funerary epitaph and career summary for Lucius Julius Festus, a Roman official who served in various military and administrative roles, likely from the Hadrianic period (mid-2nd century CE).

EDCS-01500391.translation: Publius Occius Dunomarus, freedman of Publius, and Publius Occius Anchialus, freedman of Publius, made this [tomb] while alive for themselves and their families; a square plot of 16 feet.
EDCS-01500391.summary: This funerary monument was erected by two freedmen, Publius Occius Dunomarus and Publius Occius Anchialus, for themselves and their families.

EDCS-01500392.translation: Gaius Octavius Tertius, freedman of Gaius, made [this] while alive for [his wife?] Secunda, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-01500392.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Gaius Octavius Tertius, a freedman, for his wife Secunda.

EDCS-01500394.translation: The plot of the monument for Ummidia Phoebe: 16 feet in front and 70 feet in depth.
EDCS-01500394.summary: This records the dimensions of a plot of land intended for a monument, likely funerary, belonging to Ummidia Phoebe.

EDCS-01500395.translation: The site of the monument of Ummidia Phoebe: 16 feet in front, 70 feet in the field.
EDCS-01500395.summary: This inscription defines the land boundaries for the monument of Ummidia Phoebe, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01500396.translation: [The patron] ordered [this] to be made for himself, his patron, and his freedmen [and freedwomen?].
EDCS-01500396.summary: This inscription likely records the commissioning of a monument by a patron for himself and his dependents.

EDCS-01600001.translation: To Dis Pater and Aecura. Marcus Aurelius Gaurus, a veteran, has paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600001.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the deities Dis Pater and Aecura by Marcus Aurelius Gaurus, a veteran.

EDCS-01600003.translation: Egirus, slave of Marcus B. M., paid his vow willingly and deservedly to Aesculapius.
EDCS-01600003.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Aesculapius by Egirus, a slave.

EDCS-01600005.summary: This is a dedication to Aesculapius Augustus, with the name of the dedicator partially preserved.

EDCS-01600007.translation: Sacred to the Augusti Aesculapius and Hygieia. Gaius Statius Moschus, a magistrate of the guild of fabric workers in Aquileia, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600007.summary: This votive inscription was dedicated to Aesculapius and Hygieia by Gaius Statius Moschus, a prominent member of the guild of fabric workers in Aquileia.

EDCS-01600010.translation: To Belenus Augustus. Lucius Annius Fidelis.
EDCS-01600010.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Belenus Augustus by Lucius Annius Fidelis.

EDCS-01600011.translation: Achillaeus, father of Belenus, [erected this] for Apthonetus, his brother, and for Theodorus, his son.
EDCS-01600011.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Achillaeus for his deceased brother Apthonetus and his son Theodorus.

EDCS-01600012.translation: Gaius Aquileiensis Diadumenus paid his vow to Belenus.
EDCS-01600012.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Aquileiensis Diadumenus to the god Belenus.

EDCS-01600013.text_edition: \n Apollini Beleno Caius Aquileiensis Felix quod vilicus summarum vovit solvit\n
EDCS-01600013.translation: Gaius Aquileiensis Felix, as supervisor, paid his vow to Apollo Belenus.
EDCS-01600013.summary: This votive inscription by Gaius Aquileiensis Felix, identified as a supervisor, is dedicated to Apollo Belenus.

EDCS-01600014.translation: Phoebus, freedman, with joy and deservedly paid his vow for Aulus Aquillius Valens, son of Gaius, designated as a four-man magistrate with judicial powers, to Belenus Augustus.
EDCS-01600014.summary: This is a votive inscription by the freedman Phoebus for Aulus Aquillius Valens, a designated magistrate, dedicated to Belenus Augustus.

EDCS-01600015.translation: Publius C. paid his vow to Belenus with joy and good will.
EDCS-01600015.summary: This is a partial votive inscription by Publius C. to Belenus.

EDCS-01600016.text_edition: \n Belino Sextus Caesernius Faustus IIIIIIvir votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-01600016.translation: Sextus Caesernius Faustus, a six-man magistrate, paid his vow to Belenus with joy and deservedly.
EDCS-01600016.summary: This votive inscription by Sextus Caesernius Faustus, a six-man magistrate, is dedicated to Belenus.

EDCS-01600017.text_edition: \n Apollini Beleno Augusto Tiberius Claudius Aristio et Cornelia Eutychiane coniunx sic cum filis Claudiis Constante Ferociano Eutychiane Aristione ex voto posuerunt signum Cupidinis locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-01600017.translation: Tiberius Claudius Aristio and his wife Cornelia Eutychiane, along with their children Claudius Constans Ferocianus, Eutychiane, and Aristio, set up this statue of Cupid in fulfillment of a vow to Apollo Belenus Augustus; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600017.summary: This inscription records the setting up of a statue of Cupid by Tiberius Claudius Aristio and his family to Apollo Belenus Augustus, with the site granted by the decurions.

EDCS-01600018.translation: Lucius Cornelius Secundinus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, an evocatus of our emperor Augustus, joyfully set up this gift in Aquileia, which he vowed while in the city, and had brought to Aquileia; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600018.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cornelius Secundinus, an evocatus, setting up a vowed gift in Aquileia, with the site granted by the decurions.

EDCS-01600019.translation: Marcus Hostilius Auctus, a five-man magistrate, sacred to the Good Goddess.
EDCS-01600019.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Hostilius Auctus, a five-man magistrate, to the Good Goddess.

EDCS-01600020.translation: Gaius Julius Agathopus, a six-man magistrate in Aquileia, [dedicated this] in memory of the Iulii Marcellus and Marcella, and in honor of the Iuliae, daughters of Charites and Marcella, and of their younger grandson Licinius Macronis; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600020.summary: This inscription by Gaius Julius Agathopus honors members of the Iulii family and Licinius Macronis, with the site granted by the decurions.

EDCS-01600021.translation: Lucius Junius Successus paid his vow to Belenus Augustus from the Altinas estate with joy and deservedly.
EDCS-01600021.summary: This votive inscription by Lucius Junius Successus is dedicated to Belenus Augustus.

EDCS-01600022.translation: Beleno; Mansuetus Verus of Lauriacenses and Lavinenses and Vibiania Iantulla fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600022.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Mansuetus Verus and Vibiania Iantulla to the deity Beleno.

EDCS-01600023.translation: Titus Marius Aptus of Vercellae and Asiaticus presented a vow to Beleno, fulfilling it willingly and gladly, and took care of its erection.
EDCS-01600023.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Titus Marius Aptus and Asiaticus to Beleno, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600024.text_edition: \n Apollini Beleno Augusto sacrum Caius Petilius Venustus tribunus praetorianus votum solvit\n
EDCS-01600024.translation: Sacred to Apollo Belenus Augustus, Gaius Petilius Venustus, a praetorian tribune, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600024.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Gaius Petilius Venustus, a praetorian tribune, to Apollo Belenus Augustus.

EDCS-01600025.translation: Diocles, freedman, gave this gift to Apollo Belenus Augustus in honor of Gaius Pettius Philtatus, son of Gaius, of the Palatina tribe, public equestrian, prefect with aedilician power, prefect and patron of the guilds of builders and clothiers; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600025.summary: This inscription records a gift by the freedman Diocles to Apollo Belenus Augustus, honoring the prominent local official Gaius Pettius Philtatus, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600026.translation: Sacred to Belenus, Publius Trosius Cinna, son of Gaius.
EDCS-01600026.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to Belenus by Publius Trosius Cinna.

EDCS-01600027.translation: Sacred to Belenus, Lucius Vettonius Secundus, freedman of Lucius, a municipal priest.
EDCS-01600027.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering to Belenus by Lucius Vettonius Secundus, a freedman and a member of the municipal college of priests.

EDCS-01600028.translation: Titus Vibius Abascantus, a municipal priest of Aquileia, gave this gift to Belenus Augustus.
EDCS-01600028.summary: This inscription records a gift to Belenus Augustus by Titus Vibius Abascantus, a municipal priest from Aquileia.

EDCS-01600029.translation: To Apollo Belenus Augustus, Gaius Volusius...
EDCS-01600029.summary: This is a partial inscription dedicating something to Apollo Belenus Augustus by Gaius Volusius.

EDCS-01600030.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication to a fountain associated with Belenus.

EDCS-01600031.translation: Sacred to the Fountain of Belenus (?), Titus Kanius Ianuarius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600031.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Titus Kanius Ianuarius to a fountain associated with Belenus.

EDCS-01600032.translation: Sacred to the Good August Goddess.
EDCS-01600032.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Good August Goddess, with the beginning of the text being lost.

EDCS-01600033.translation: Aninia Magna, daughter of Marcus, Seia Ionis, and Cornelia Ephyre, priestesses of the Good Goddess, restored the portico and the small shrine of Fonionis.
EDCS-01600033.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a portico and a small shrine by three priestesses of the Good Goddess, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600034.text_edition: \n Fonioni sacrum Seia Ionis magistra dono dedit\n
EDCS-01600034.translation: Seia Ionis, priestess, dedicated this to Fonionis.
EDCS-01600034.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fonionis by Seia Ionis, who held the office of priestess, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600035.translation: Petrusia Proba, priestess of the Good Goddess, daughter of Galgestus Hermerotes, dedicated this.
EDCS-01600035.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Good Goddess by Petrusia Proba, a priestess and freedwoman, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600036.translation: To the August Good Goddess [?], Castrensis, Feronia Libani, freedwoman, [---], Tiberius Claudius Stephanus, freedman [---].
EDCS-01600036.summary: This inscription is a damaged dedication to the August Good Goddess, naming two individuals, likely freedpeople, one of whom is Feronia Libani.

EDCS-01600037.translation: Sacred to the August Good Goddess Ceres, a temple was made by T[y]che, freedman of [3]ystis, at his own expense. Faustus Barbonius, aedile, presented the gift.
EDCS-01600037.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple to the August Good Goddess Ceres, financed by a freedman and presented by a local magistrate (IIIIvir).

EDCS-01600038.translation: To the Good Pagan Goddess. Rufria Festa, daughter of Caius, and Caecilia Scylace, freedwoman of Quintus, priestesses, dedicated at their own expense.
EDCS-01600038.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Good Pagan Goddess by two priestesses who funded the monument themselves, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600039.translation: Decidia Paula, daughter of Lucius, and Peregrina, freedwoman of Lucius, ministers of the Good Goddess, built the temple with their own money.
EDCS-01600039.summary: This inscription records that Decidia Paula and Peregrina, ministers of the Bona Dea, funded the construction of a temple, likely in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01600040.translation: To Cautes. Quintus Baienus Proculus, father. To Cautopates. Quintus Baienus Proculus, father.
EDCS-01600040.summary: This inscription is a double dedication to the twin deities Cautes and Cautopates, made by Quintus Baienus Proculus, identified as 'father', likely a high-ranking local official.

EDCS-01600041.translation: Sacred to Sol. Quintus Baienus Proculus, father, by his own name.
EDCS-01600041.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the sun god Sol by Quintus Baienus Proculus, identified as 'father', likely a high-ranking local official, perhaps indicating a personal vow.

EDCS-01600042.translation: To Cautopates, sacred to Augustus. Callistus O[---].
EDCS-01600042.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cautopates and Augustus, begun by Callistus, with the rest of the text missing.

EDCS-01600043.text_edition: \n Atte Papa Theudas Theudatis filius dono dedit libens merito\n
EDCS-01600043.translation: Atte Papa Theudas, son of Theudates, gave this gift willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600043.summary: This inscription records a personal dedication made by Atte Papa Theudas to an unspecified deity.

EDCS-01600044.translation: Sacred to the gods and goddesses, from a vow, by Victor, the temple attendant.
EDCS-01600044.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the gods and goddesses by Victor, a temple attendant.

EDCS-01600045.translation: Sacred to Isis and Augusta, Gaius Curiatius Callistus fulfilled his vow; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600045.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Isis and Augusta by Gaius Curiatius Callistus, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600046.translation: To the Eternal God, for the health of Lucius Comatius Dionysus, Clodia Chrysa fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600046.summary: This is a votive inscription to the Eternal God, dedicated by Clodia Chrysa for the health of Lucius Comatius Dionysus.

EDCS-01600047.translation: To the Eternal God, Marcus Valerius Philippus and his wife Iulia Iuliana.
EDCS-01600047.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Eternal God by Marcus Valerius Philippus and his wife Iulia Iuliana.

EDCS-01600048.translation: Sacred to Augusta Diana, Flavius Severus with his workers restored this.
EDCS-01600048.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a sanctuary to Diana Augusta by Flavius Severus and his workers.

EDCS-01600049.translation: To Augusta Diana, in honor of Lucius Vibius Lucullus, most indulgent patron, Epagathus, his freedman, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600049.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Epagathus, a freedman, to Diana Augusta in honor of his patron, Lucius Vibius Lucullus.

EDCS-01600051.translation: Sacred to Domnabus. Sextus Baebius Bai filius, a veteran and clothier from the fleet, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01600051.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Sextus Baebius Bai filius, a veteran and clothier from the fleet, to the deity Domnabus, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600052.translation: To the Divine and Barbarian Fates, Postumia Callirhoe, freedwoman of Publius, fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600052.summary: This inscription is a votive offering to the Fates by Postumia Callirhoe, a freedwoman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600053.translation: Titus Kanius Ianuaris, gratuitous priest, dedicated this altar(?) in memory of his son Mineius Priscus, and gave a gift in the 40th year.
EDCS-01600053.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar by Titus Kanius Ianuaris in memory of his son Mineius Priscus, also noting his priestly office and the year of dedication.

EDCS-01600054.translation: Varia Venus fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly to Fortuna.
EDCS-01600054.summary: This is a votive inscription to Fortuna by Varia Venus.

EDCS-01600055.translation: To Fortuna Virunsiensis, Octavia Quinta, freedwoman, willingly and gladly set this up by decree.
EDCS-01600055.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Virunsiensis, set up by Octavia Quinta.

EDCS-01600056.translation: Sacred to Isis. Lucius Magius Phileas, a VIvir (member of the college of six officials), from Aquileia, for the health of his son Grattianus and Grattia [---].
EDCS-01600056.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Isis, made by Lucius Magius Phileas for the health of his children.

EDCS-01600057.translation: Sacred to the Iunones. Sextus Licinius Verecundus.
EDCS-01600057.summary: This is a dedication to the Iunones, made by Sextus Licinius Verecundus.

EDCS-01600058.text_edition: \n Iunonibus sacrum Marcus Magius Marci libertus Amaranthus IIIIIIvir et Magia Marci filia Vera Magia Marci liberta Ilias aedem signa Ill porticum cum maceris et culina et locum in quo ea sunt votum solverunt loco privato\n
EDCS-01600058.translation: Sacred to the Iunones. Marcus Magius Amaranthus, freedman of Marcus, and Magia Vera, daughter of Marcus, and Magia Ilias, freedwoman of Marcus, paid their vow, dedicating the temple, statues, the portico with its walls and kitchen, and the site on which they stand, a private property.
EDCS-01600058.summary: This is a vow paid by Marcus Magius Amaranthus, Magia Vera, and Magia Ilias to the Iunones, dedicating a temple and associated structures.

EDCS-01600059.translation: Sacred to the Iunones. Marcus Mogetius Hospes paid his vow.
EDCS-01600059.summary: This is a dedication to the Iunones, with Marcus Mogetius Hospes paying a vow.

EDCS-01600060.translation: To Iuppiter Dianus. Gaius Herrenius Candidus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-01600060.summary: This is a dedication to Iuppiter Dianus, with Gaius Herreius Candidus paying a vow.

EDCS-01600061.translation: To Iuppiter Optimus Maximus. The college of veterans set this up under the governor Titus. Amantius wrote [it?], Sculptor.
EDCS-01600061.summary: This is a dedication to Iuppiter Optimus Maximus, set up by the college of veterans during the governorship of Titus.

EDCS-01600062.translation: To Iuppiter Optimus Maximus. Aurelius Cassianus, a 'barbaricarius' (dealer in foreign goods or perhaps a tax collector of foreign goods), decurion of the colony of Forum Iulii (Cividale del Friuli), from the region of Cyrrhus, [dedicated this].
EDCS-01600062.summary: This is a dedication to Iuppiter Optimus Maximus by Aurelius Cassianus, a decurion from Forum Iulii with connections to Cyrrhus.

EDCS-01600063.text_edition: \n Iovi Optumo Maximo Lucius Cantius Verus sacerdos\n
EDCS-01600063.translation: To Iuppiter Optimus Maximus. Lucius Cantius Verus, priest.
EDCS-01600063.summary: This is a dedication to Iuppiter Optimus Maximus by the priest Lucius Cantius Verus.

EDCS-01600064.translation: Sacred to Iuppiter Optimus Maximus. Petronia Laodicia.
EDCS-01600064.summary: This is a dedication to Iuppiter Optimus Maximus by Petronia Laodicia.

EDCS-01600065.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Marcus Ulpius Potentianus, in gratitude for his health and that of his family, willingly and deservedly pays his vow.
EDCS-01600065.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter by Marcus Ulpius Potentianus for his and his family's health.
