EDCS-01600067.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the Preserver, and to the goddess Ambisagra(?), Primus willingly and gladly [dedicated this].
EDCS-01600067.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter and the goddess Ambisagra by Primus.

EDCS-01600068.translation: Sextus Fabius Stephanus, freedman of Sextus Fabius, and Sextus Fabius Laetus, freedman of Stephanus, dedicated this sacred offering to the Lares from their own money.
EDCS-01600068.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred offering to the Lares by two freedmen, Sextus Fabius Stephanus and Sextus Fabius Laetus, funded by themselves.

EDCS-01600069.translation: Sacred to the Lares. The magistrates are dedicating [this]. Lucius Licinius [son?] of [---]tavius, Gnaeus Licinius [son?] of [---]tavius, freedman of Lucius [---]tilius Sinna, Epagatus, slave of Fabius [Lucius?], T(h)raex(?), slave of the partners, the porter, Diphilus, slave of Vibius Marcus [---].
EDCS-01600069.summary: This is a dedication to the Lares by magistrates, listing several individuals, likely including slaves and freedmen involved in the dedication, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600070.translation: Sacred to Liber and Libera. Publius Gavius Astectus, a member of the college of VI viri, erected this by order.
EDCS-01600070.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred space to Liber and Libera by Publius Gavius Astectus, a member of the VI viri, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600071.text_edition: \n Lunae Marti Fruticiae Thymeles rogatu Marcus Statinius Dorus\n
EDCS-01600071.translation: Marcus Statinius Dorus, at the request of Luna, Mars, Fruticia, and Thymeles.
EDCS-01600071.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Marcus Statinius Dorus at the request of several individuals or deities.

EDCS-01600072.translation: Leontius erected an altar to the god Mars and Mercury.
EDCS-01600072.summary: This is an altar erected by Leontius to the gods Mars and Mercury.

EDCS-01600074.text_edition: \n Magnae Deum Matri Cereriae votum solvit Fruticia Thymele Marci Statini Dori\n
EDCS-01600074.translation: Fruticia Thymele, wife of Marcus Statinius Dorus, paid her vow to the Great Mother of the Gods, Cereria.
EDCS-01600074.summary: This is a votive inscription by Fruticia Thymele, wife of Marcus Statinius Dorus, to the goddess Cereria.

EDCS-01600078.translation: Sacred to Minerva Augusta. Lucius Fabius Quelianus [dedicated this] in accordance with his vow; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600078.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Augusta by Lucius Fabius Quelianus, with the land for the shrine granted by the town council.

EDCS-01600079.translation: Marcus Valerius Venustus and Mulcedatia Tais, for the gentile kin of the Artorians, the bath attendants, gave this altar as a gift to Minerva Augusta.
EDCS-01600079.summary: This inscription records the gift of an altar to Minerva Augusta by Marcus Valerius Venustus and Mulcedatia Tais, dedicated to their gentile kin and bath attendants.

EDCS-01600080.translation: Sacred to Minerva Augusta. [Ma]xima, freedwoman of [---]eteia, daughter of Quintus, [dedicated this].
EDCS-01600080.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Augusta by Maxima, a freedwoman.

EDCS-01600081.translation: To the Unconquered Sun, Diocletian and Maximian, Augusti.
EDCS-01600081.summary: A dedication to the Unconquered Sun by the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-01600082.translation: To the Unconquered God, by Lucius Aebutius Eutychus, freedman of Primus.
EDCS-01600082.summary: A dedication to the Unconquered God by Lucius Aebutius Eutychus, a freedman, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600083.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Invicto Mithrae Publius Aelius Mercurialis Quintus Tessignius Maximianus patres prosedente Tito Aurelio Victore votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-01600083.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras, Publius Aelius Mercurialis and Quintus Tessignius Maximianus, as fathers, having Titus Aurelius Victor presiding, fulfilled their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600083.summary: A dedication to Mithras by two men identified as 'fathers' (likely within a mystery cult context), fulfilling a vow, possibly dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600084.translation: To the Unconquered Sun Mithras, Gaius Calidius Agathopus, a six-man official of Aquileia, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600084.summary: A votive inscription to Sol Invictus Mithras by Gaius Calidius Agathopus, a local official in Aquileia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600085.translation: Sacred to the Unconquered Sun God, Feronius Censor, standard-bearer, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600085.summary: A dedication to the Unconquered Sun by Feronius Censor, a standard-bearer, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600086.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras, Flavius Exuperatus, serving in the lustrum of Flavius Sabinus, primipilus, and Aelius Severus, serving in the lustrum of Aurelius Flavius, princeps, standard-bearer of the III Pia Fidelis Legion, and Valerius Valens, standard-bearer of the XIII Gemina Legion, serving in the lustrum of Aurelius Zenon, primipilus, fulfilled their vows willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600086.summary: A complex votive inscription to Mithras by multiple individuals, including military personnel and those involved in administrative 'lustra', likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-01600088.translation: For the health of Tiberius Claudius Macronis, contractor for the Norican iron mines, Velox, his slave, the overseer, made a cave with all its furnishings.
EDCS-01600088.summary: A dedication for the health of an iron mine contractor, commissioned by his slave overseer, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600089.translation: For his own health and that of his family, Septimius Marcianus, optio of the II Adjutrix Pia Fidelis Legion, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600089.summary: A votive inscription for health by Septimius Marcianus, a military officer, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600091.translation: Sacred to Nemesis Augusta, by Gaius Turranius Sozomenus, six-man official, by vision.
EDCS-01600091.summary: A dedication to the goddess Nemesis Augusta by Gaius Turranius Sozomenus, a local official, made in response to a divine vision, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600092.translation: Leuce Anspaniae, freedwoman, Occusia Venusta, as magistra, give to the goddess Obsequens.
EDCS-01600092.summary: An inscription recording a gift to the goddess Obsequens by two women, one identified as a freedwoman and the other as a 'magistra', likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01600094.text_edition: \n Silvano sacrum Caius Petronius Andronicus ex viso\n
EDCS-01600094.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Gaius Petronius Andronicus, from a vision.
EDCS-01600094.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus by Gaius Petronius Andronicus, prompted by a vision, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600095.translation: Calybe to the Silvani. Freely and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-01600095.summary: This inscription records Calybe fulfilling a vow to the Silvani, likely a votive offering, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600096.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. Marcus Aulius Primus.
EDCS-01600096.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus by Marcus Aulius Primus, likely a personal dedication from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600097.translation: To Silvanus Augustus, sacred. Lucius Coelius Septumus, six-time magistrate of Aquileia, six-time magistrate of Este, on behalf of Firminus, Firmina, and their children, gave this offering.
EDCS-01600097.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus by Lucius Coelius Septumus, who held high civic offices in Aquileia and Este, offering it on behalf of his family, likely from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600098.translation: To Silvanus Augustus, sacred. Eleutherus, bailiff of Gaius Antonius Rufus, public collector of taxes, gave this offering.
EDCS-01600098.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus by Eleutherus, a bailiff and tax collector for Gaius Antonius Rufus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600099.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. In memory of Quintus Etuvius Hedychrus, six-time magistrate of Aquileia. Quintus Etuvius Eros, freedman, six-time magistrate of Aquileia, gave this offering.
EDCS-01600099.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus, made by the freedman Quintus Etuvius Eros in memory of his patron Quintus Etuvius Hedychrus, both of whom were prominent officials in Aquileia, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600100.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. In memory of Publius Mutilius Laurentinus, his son, and Publius Mutilius Glyco, his spouse, gave this offering.
EDCS-01600100.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus, made in memory of Publius Mutilius Laurentinus and his spouse Publius Mutilius Glyco, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600101.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. Gaius Opeterius Agathemrus. Freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600101.summary: This inscription records Gaius Opeterius Agathemrus fulfilling a vow to Silvanus Augustus, likely a personal dedication from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600102.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. In memory of Rufus Anthus, six-time magistrate. Thallus, freedman, gave this offering.
EDCS-01600102.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Augustus, made by the freedman Thallus in memory of his patron Rufus Anthus, who was a six-time magistrate, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600103.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. Lucius Spurius Celer gave this offering in memory of Gaius Avilius Florus, son of Gaius, veteran of the 5th Praetorian cohort.
EDCS-01600103.summary: This inscription records Lucius Spurius Celer dedicating an offering to Silvanus Augustus in memory of Gaius Avilius Florus, a veteran of the Praetorian Guard, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600104.translation: To Silvanus Augustus. Gaius Statius Eutychus Manianus, freedman of Gaius and Lucius, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600104.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Silvanus Augustus by a freedman, Gaius Statius Eutychus Manianus.

EDCS-01600105.text_edition: \n Silvano Augusto sacrum in honorem Luci Stati Onesimi IIIIIIviri et in memoriam Cai Stati Primigeni Augustalis decreto decurionum Luci Stati Hermetis Lucius Statius Encolpus IIIIIIvir\n
EDCS-01600105.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus, in honor of Lucius Statius Onesimus, one of the six high priests, and in memory of Gaius Statius Primigenius, an Augustalis, by decree of the decurions, Lucius Statius Encolpus, one of the six high priests.
EDCS-01600105.summary: This inscription honors and memorializes officials named Lucius Statius Onesimus and Gaius Statius Primigenius, dedicated by Lucius Statius Encolpus, likely by order of the town council.

EDCS-01600106.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus, in memory of Lucius T. Fruendus, patron, one of the six high priests and an Augustalis.
EDCS-01600106.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Silvanus Augustus in memory of Lucius T. Fruendus, who held prominent civic and religious positions.

EDCS-01600107.translation: To Silvanus Augustus, in honor of Lucius Titus Ismarus and in memory of Lucius Titus Epagathus, son of Hermetis, and of Lucius Titus Epagathus the elder. Lucius Titius Onesimus, freedman of Ismarus, one of the six high priests of Aquileia, gave this gift.
EDCS-01600107.summary: This inscription honors and memorializes members of the Titus family, dedicated by Lucius Titius Onesimus, a freedman and high priest of Aquileia.

EDCS-01600108.translation: To Silvanus Augustus, in honor of Marcus Trosius Daphnus, one of the six high priests, and of his freedman Marcus Trosius Cissus. Marcus Trosius Modestus gave this gift.
EDCS-01600108.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Trosius Daphnus and his freedman Cissus, with the gift presented by Marcus Trosius Modestus.

EDCS-01600109.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus, in honor and goodwill of Publius Tullius Ty[...], freedman of Publius.
EDCS-01600109.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Silvanus Augustus in honor of Publius Tullius Ty[...], a freedman.

EDCS-01600110.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus, in honor of Lucius Valerius Nymphodotus, one of the six priests and an Augustalis by decree of the decurions, and of Gaius Statius Primigenius, and in memory of Gaius Statius Heuretes, one of the six priests and an Augustalis by decree of the decurions. Alypus, freedman.
EDCS-01600110.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Valerius Nymphodotus and Gaius Statius Primigenius, and memorializes Gaius Statius Heuretes, all holding significant civic roles, dedicated by the freedman Alypus.

EDCS-01600111.translation: In honor of Lucius Valerius Nymphodotus and Gaius Statius Primigenius, and in memory of Gaius Statius Heuretes. Eupor, freedman.
EDCS-01600111.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Valerius Nymphodotus and Gaius Statius Primigenius, and memorializes Gaius Statius Heuretes, dedicated by the freedman Eupor.

EDCS-01600112.translation: Sacred to Hope Augustus. Lucius Cornelius Potitus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01600112.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Hope Augustus by Lucius Cornelius Potitus.

EDCS-01600113.text_edition: \n Veneri Augustae Popillia Luci filia Marcellina Attia mater ornamenta eius exornavit\n
EDCS-01600113.translation: Popillia Marcellina, daughter of Lucius, wife of Attius, adorned her ornaments for Venus Augusta.
EDCS-01600113.summary: This inscription records Popillia Marcellina dedicating ornaments to Venus Augusta.

EDCS-01600114.translation: To Venus Augusta. Vetilia Potens, daughter of Lucius, set this up in memory of her daughter Calvia Bassilia.
EDCS-01600114.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Vetilia Potens for her daughter, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600115.translation: Sacred to the divine Venus. Gaius Vettius Gavolus, son of Caius, [set this up].
EDCS-01600115.summary: This is a dedication to the divine Venus by Gaius Vettius Gavolus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600117.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Titus Flavius Italicus gave and dedicated this gift.
EDCS-01600117.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Titus Flavius Italicus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600118.translation: The aediles, Caius Lucretius Vibi filius and Lucius Horatius Luci filius, arranged for the sacred rites concerning the gifts to be performed.
EDCS-01600118.summary: This inscription records the arrangement for sacred rites concerning gifts by the aediles Caius Lucretius and Lucius Horatius, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600119.translation: For his own safety and that of his family, Quintus V...
EDCS-01600119.summary: This is a votive inscription, possibly a dedication or a record of a vow, for the well-being of Quintus V... and his relatives, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600121.translation: [...], Florus, having been warned by a vision.
EDCS-01600121.summary: This inscription records Florus, who received some divine revelation or warning, possibly related to a religious or votive context, from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600124.translation: [...], sacred. Acilia Galatea Plate, freedwoman of Publius, [dedicated?] this Cist[...]
EDCS-01600124.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred object, possibly a chest (cista), by Acilia Galatea Plate, a freedwoman, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600125.translation: Iulia, daughter of Sextus, [priestess?] of the Good Goddess, gave/dedicated the gift.
EDCS-01600125.summary: This is a dedication, possibly by a priestess (magistra?), of a gift to the Bona Dea by Iulia, daughter of Sextus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600126.translation: To the Gods [?]. Quintus Cervius Isthmus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow. Quintus Cervius Romanus [also?] fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600126.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of vows by Quintus Cervius Isthmus and Quintus Cervius Romanus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600127.translation: Herennius Trophimianus on his own behalf and
EDCS-01600127.summary: This inscription fragment appears to record a dedication or dedication by Herennius Trophimianus, possibly on behalf of himself and others, with the rest of the inscription missing.

EDCS-01600128.translation: Aurelianus Marianus, veteran of the Thirteenth Gemina Legion, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600128.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aurelianus Marianus, a veteran of Legio XIII Gemina, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600129.translation: [...], sons of Marcellus, having attained their vows, their parents Sextius Calliparthenus and Revidia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, made their vows.
EDCS-01600129.summary: This inscription records Sextius Calliparthenus and Revidia Marcella fulfilling vows on behalf of their sons, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600139.translation: To Gaius Appuleius Tappo, son of Gaius, pontifex. Sepstinia, his wife.
EDCS-01600139.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Appuleius Tappo, a pontifex, by his wife Sepstinia.

EDCS-01600140.text_edition: \n Caius Appuleius Marci filius Tappo praetor aedilis tribunus plebis quaestor iudex quaesitionis rerum capitalium\n
EDCS-01600140.translation: Gaius Appuleius Tappo, son of Marcus, was praetor, aedile, tribune of the plebs, quaestor, judge in capital cases.
EDCS-01600140.summary: This inscription lists the career of Gaius Appuleius Tappo, a Roman magistrate.

EDCS-01600141.translation: to Gaius Aurelius Cotta, son of Marcus, proconsul
EDCS-01600141.summary: This inscription fragment records a dedication to Gaius Aurelius Cotta, son of Marcus, who held the office of proconsul.

EDCS-01600144.text_edition: \n Titus Caesernius Macedo Quinctianus consul collegio fabrorum dono dedit\n
EDCS-01600144.translation: Titus Caesernius Macedo Quinctianus gave this as a gift to the guild of artisans.
EDCS-01600144.summary: This records a gift from Titus Caesernius Macedo Quinctianus to the collegium fabrorum (guild of artisans).

EDCS-01600145.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Tiberi filio Palatina Secundino Lucio Statio Macedoni primo pilo legionis IIII Flaviae felicis tribuno cohortis primae vigilum tribuno cohortis XI urbanae tribuno cohortis VIIII praetoriae primo pilo iterum praefecto legionis II Traianae fortis procuratori XX hereditatium procuratori provinciae Lugdunensis et Aquitanicae a rationibus Augusti praefecto annonae Lucius Saufeius Iulianus amico optimo\n
EDCS-01600145.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Secundinus, son of Tiberius, of the Palatina tribe, also known as Lucius Statilius Macedo, primus pilus of the IV Scythica legion, tribune of the first cohort of vigiles, tribune of the eleventh urban cohort, tribune of the ninth praetorian cohort, primus pilus for a second time, prefect of the II Traiana Fortis legion, procurator of the XX hereditatium, procurator of the province of Lugdunensis and Aquitanica, imperial financial officer, prefect of the grain supply. Lucius Saufeius Iulianus to his best friend.
EDCS-01600145.summary: This is a dedication to Tiberius Claudius Secundinus by his friend Lucius Saufeius Iulianus, listing his extensive military and administrative career, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600146.translation: To Naico, slave and unctor. From Fabianus, the consular.
EDCS-01600146.summary: This is a dedication to a slave named Naico, an unctor (perhaps a masseur or groom), by Fabianus, who held a consular position.

EDCS-01600147.translation: To Phoebianus, slave and doctor. From Fabianus, the consular.
EDCS-01600147.summary: This is a dedication to a slave named Phoebianus, who was a doctor, by Fabianus, who held a consular position.

EDCS-01600148.translation: To Trophimus, freedman. From Fabianus, the consular.
EDCS-01600148.summary: This is a dedication to Trophimus, a freedman, by Fabianus, who held a consular position.

EDCS-01600149.translation: Of Marcus Licinius Petilius, of most distinguished memory, an incomparable father. Aelia Licinia Petilia, his daughter.
EDCS-01600149.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Licinius Petilius, praised as an incomparable father, by his daughter Aelia Licinia Petilia.

EDCS-01600150.translation: Gaius Lucilius, son of Gaius, one of the moneyers of the mint
EDCS-01600150.summary: This inscription fragment identifies Gaius Lucilius, son of Gaius, as having held the position of a triumvir capitalis, a judicial and financial official.

EDCS-01600151.translation: Lucius Manlius Acidinus, son of Lucius, triumvir for the establishment of the colony of Aquileia
EDCS-01600151.summary: This inscription fragment identifies Lucius Manlius Acidinus, son of Lucius, as a triumvir responsible for establishing the colony of Aquileia.

EDCS-01600153.inscription_type: senatus consulta, tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-01600153.text_edition: \n Caio Minicio Cai filio Velina ltalo llllviro iure dicundo praefecto cohortis V Gallorum equitatae praefecto cohortis I Breucorum equitatae civium Romanorum praefecto cohortis II Varcianorum equitatae tribuno militum legionis VI victricis praefecto equitum alae I singularium civium Romanorum donis donato a divo Vespasiano corona aurea hasta pura procuratori provinciae Hellesponti procuratori provinciae Asiae quam mandatu principis vice defuncti proconsulis rexit procuratori provinciarum Luguduniensis et Aquitanicae item Lactorae praefecto annonae praefecto Aegypti flamini divi Claudi decreto decurionum Publius Tullius Maximus? et --- Mamula IIIIviri iure dicundo III Kalendas Iunias senatum consuluerunt scribendo adfuerunt Proculus Caius Appuleius Celer Aulus Iunius G Sextus Cossutius Secundus quod verba facta sunt in honorem Cai Minici Itali honestissimum virum quidquid consequi gratiae aut potentiae per summos honores equestris dignitatis potuerit it sic omne ad augendam et ornandam patriam suam convertisse nec ullo se feliciorem credere officio quam ut pro ea laboret quid de ea re fieri placeret de ea re ita censuerunt cum Caius Minicius Italus vir honestissimus hunc praecipuum virtutum suarum finem duxerit et multis patriae fortunam loci sui amplificaverit et super cetera omnibus sit notum sacratissimum principem Traianum Augustum decrevisse rogatu eius ut incolae quibus fere censemur muneribus nobiscum fungantur et ut pleniorem indulgentiam maximi imperatoris potuerimus obtigisse placere huic ordini adque e re publica videri statuam aeream cum basi marmorea poni decretumque nostrum basi inscribi quo testatius sit pro meritis beneficiisque tanti viri solvendo nos aliter non esse nisi ut de eo publice gloriemur censuerunt Tiberio Iulio Candido II Caio Antio Quadrato II consulibus\n
EDCS-01600153.translation: On the 3rd day before the Kalends of June, under the consulship of Tiberius Iulius Candidus and Gaius Antius Quadratus. The four magistrates for dispensing justice consulted the senate, and were present for the recording: Proculus, Gaius Appuleius Celer, Aulus Iunius G., Sextus Cossutius Secundus. Regarding the words spoken in honor of Gaius Minicius Italus, a most honorable man, that whatever praise or influence he could attain through the highest offices of equestrian rank, he has directed all of it towards increasing and adorning his fatherland, and believes no duty more fortunate than to labor for it. What it seemed fitting should be done in this matter, they have thus decided: Since Gaius Minicius Italus, a most honorable man, has made this the ultimate goal of his virtues and has increased the prosperity of his fatherland through many means, and it is known to all besides that the most sacred emperor Trajan Augustus, at his request, decreed that the inhabitants, by whom we are considered to be bound by duties, should also perform duties with us, and that we might obtain the fullest favor of the greatest emperor, it seems pleasing to this order and beneficial to the state, that a bronze statue with a marble base be erected, and that our decree be inscribed on the base, so that it may be more evident how we are not able to repay his merits and favors other than by publicly glorifying him.
EDCS-01600153.summary: This decree from the town council honors Gaius Minicius Italus for his public service and achievements, leading to the erection of a bronze statue, likely in the early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600154.translation: To Quintus Mutillius Sura Accianus Nepos, one of the twelve men judging lawsuits.
EDCS-01600154.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Mutillius Sura Accianus Nepos, who served as a decemvir stlitibus iudicandis (one of the twelve men judging lawsuits).

EDCS-01600155.text_edition: \n Aulo Platorio Auli filio Sergia Nepoti Aponio Italico Maniliano Caio Licinio Pollioni consuli auguri legato Augusti pro praetore provinciae Britanniae legato pro praetore provinciae Germaniae inferioris legato pro praetore provinciae Thraciae legato legionis l adiutricis quaestori provinciae Macedoniae curatori viarum Cassiae Clodiae Ciminiae novae Traianae candidato divi Traiani tribuno militum legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis praetori tribuno plebis lIlviro capitali patrono decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-01600155.translation: To Aulus Platorius Nepos, son of Aulus, of the Sergia tribe, son of Apponius Italicus Manlianus, consul, augur, legate of the Emperor Augustus with praetorian power in the province of Britain, legate with praetorian power in the province of Lower Germany, legate with praetorian power in the province of Thrace, legate of the legion I Adiutrix, quaestor of the province of Macedonia, curator of the Cassian, Claudian, Ciminian, and new Trajanic roads, candidate of divine Trajan, military tribune of the legion XXII Primigenia, pious and faithful, praetor, tribune of the plebs, aedile, patron, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-01600155.summary: This inscription is a dedicatory inscription honouring Aulus Platorius Nepos, listing his extensive career and official positions in the Roman Empire, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600156.translation: Syntrophus, slave of Sisenna, steward of Taurus the pontiff.
EDCS-01600156.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Syntrophus, a steward, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600161.translation: [...], Quartio, duovir, assessor of the consul, and his wife, Salvia, freedwoman of Aratria, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-01600161.summary: This inscription records the death of Quartio, a duovir and assessor to the consul, and his wife Salvia, likely from a Roman municipal context.

EDCS-01600163.translation: Adiutor, son of Laucus, citizen of the Menapii, soldier of the 1st cohort of Pannonians, in the century of Bassus, served for 11 years, aged 32 years, is buried here.
EDCS-01600163.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Adiutor, a soldier from the Menapii tribe serving in the 1st Cohort of Pannonians, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600164.translation: Gaius Albucius, son of Gaius, from the Falernian region, from Intimilio, soldier of the 8th praetorian cohort, served for 17 years, lived for 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-01600164.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Albucius, a soldier of the 8th Praetorian Cohort, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600166.translation: To Marcus Antonius, son of Marcus, a veteran of the 1st Adiutrix legion. Titus Flavius Vettianus, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, [erected this] as a former duovir of Aquileia.
EDCS-01600166.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Titus Flavius Vettianus, a former duovir of Aquileia, for Marcus Antonius, a veteran of the 1st Adiutrix legion.

EDCS-01600167.translation: To Lucius Arrius Macro, a veteran centurion, served for 36 years, inscribed on bronze by divine Vespasian. Arria Trophime, freedwoman of Lucius, to her patron, erected this while alive, for herself and her family; and for Gaius Varius Arrianus, aged 15, deceived by a friend.
EDCS-01600167.summary: This monument was erected by Arria Trophime, a freedwoman, for her patron Lucius Arrius Macro, a veteran centurion, and also for her family, likely dating to the Flavian period.

EDCS-01600168.translation: Camaronia Plecusa dedicated this tomb while alive to her relative Speia, and to Marcus Auctorius Trophimus, her husband, an excellent man, well deserving; and to Theophilus, son of the [---] Julius, her husband, an excellent man, well deserving; and to Tedia Hedonene, her friend. She granted the place for burial if anyone should bury [---] here. Marcus Aufustius Actiacus, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, to his wife Valeria Charis, freedwoman of Gaius; to their daughter Chrysida, aged 20, killed; to Lucius Albius Sabinus, freedman of Lucius, his comrade. Camaronia Plecusa and Stacte, freedwoman of Quintus, to their mother.
EDCS-01600168.summary: This is a complex funerary monument with multiple dedications and burials, recording the wishes of Camaronia Plecusa and the family of Marcus Aufustius Actiacus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600169.translation: Marcus Aunicius Messallinus, son of Marcus, of the Publilia tribe, a veteran of the 15th Apollinaris legion, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his daughter Fortunata.
EDCS-01600169.summary: This is a funerary inscription by will for Marcus Aunicius Messallinus, a veteran of the 15th Apollinaris legion, and his daughter Fortunata.

EDCS-01600170.translation: To the divine spirits. Aurelius Maximianus placed this for his most dear brother Aurelius Clarianus, a soldier of the 1st Adiutrix legion, born in the region of Lower Moesia, in the vicus [---]dianus, aged 38 years.
EDCS-01600170.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Aurelius Maximianus for his brother Aurelius Clarianus, a soldier of the 1st Adiutrix legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600171.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelius Dizo, a soldier of the eleventh Claudian Legion, lived 27 years, served 5 years. Died in Mauretania. His fellow soldiers and comrades erected this monument at their own expense for a deserving man.
EDCS-01600171.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Dizo, a soldier of the Legio XI Claudia, who died in Mauretania.

EDCS-01600172.translation: Aurelius Domitianus, a subordinate officer (beneficiarius) of the first Adjututrix Legion, lived 40 years, served 20 years, and received his discharge.
EDCS-01600172.summary: This inscription records the service and discharge of Aurelius Domitianus, a soldier of the Legio I Adjutrix.

EDCS-01600173.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelius Flavinus, a subaltern officer (optio) of the eleventh Claudian Legion, 40 years of age, who served 14 years as a soldier and 10 years as an optio, erected this monument at his own expense, with his fellow citizens present, at a cost of 10,000 denarii.
EDCS-01600173.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Flavinus, an optio in the Legio XI Claudia, who erected his own monument.

EDCS-01600174.translation: Aurelius Iustinus, an equestrian soldier in the eleventh Claudia Legion, approved at age 17, served as a distinguished soldier for 7 years and as an equestrian for 4 years, served in the first cohort of spearmen (hastati) in the posterior section; his own inscription cost 101 denarii.
EDCS-01600174.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Iustinus, an equestrian soldier of the Legio XI Claudia, detailing his service and the cost of his tombstone.

EDCS-01600175.translation: To the departed spirits. Valentinus, a cousin, erected this for Aurelius [---], a soldier of the thirteenth Gemina Legion.
EDCS-01600175.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius [---], a soldier of the Legio XIII Gemina, erected by his cousin.

EDCS-01600176.translation: Aurelius Moca served in the Claudian cohort as a soldier for 8 years, became a tribune's subordinate officer (beneficiarius) for 3 years, and was then transferred to the Augusta Legion, becoming a standard-bearer (signifer) for 12 years. Born in Dardania, in the village of Zatidis, he gave his name to military service for 23 years, lived 55 years. Aurelius Maximianus, his nephew, erected this for his deserving uncle.
EDCS-01600176.summary: This funerary epitaph records the military career and origin of Aurelius Moca, who served in various units and was eventually honored by his nephew.

EDCS-01600178.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelius Sudlcentius, a soldier of the eleventh Claudia Legion.
EDCS-01600178.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Sudlcentius, a soldier of the Legio XI Claudia.

EDCS-01600179.translation: To the departed spirits. For Quintus Caecilius Maximus, son of Quintus, of the Maecia tribe, a soldier of the VII Praetorian Cohort, a singular soldier of the tribune.
EDCS-01600179.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Caecilius Maximus, a soldier in the VII Praetorian Cohort.

EDCS-01600180.translation: Marcus Caesius Priscus, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe, a veteran of the Eighth Augusta Legion, made this while alive for himself and his family, for Carconia Prisca, daughter of Marcus, his companion in the barracks, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, except for Primus, Tyrannus, and Sintychus.
EDCS-01600180.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Marcus Caesius Priscus, a veteran of the Legio VIII Augusta, for himself, his wife, and his freedmen.

EDCS-01600181.text_edition: \n Aulo Caesilio Auli filio Velina Acastino primo pilo IIIIviro iure dicundo quinquennali rei publicae suae amantissimo municipes et incolae in solacium amissi optimi et rarissimi civis locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-01600181.translation: The townsfolk and inhabitants, in consolation for the loss of their most excellent and rare citizen, have granted this space by decree of the decurions, for Aulus Caesilius Acastinus, son of Aulus, of the Velina tribe, a first-rank centurion (primo pilo), a quinquennial magistrate (iure dicundo quinquennali) for his state, most devoted to his public service.
EDCS-01600181.summary: This is a public dedication of a burial plot in honor of Aulus Caesilius Acastinus, a distinguished local magistrate and former centurion, by the citizens of his town.

EDCS-01600182.translation: Marcus Calventius, son of Titus, of the Lemonia tribe, from Bononia, soldier of the 8th Praetorian cohort, served for 7 years, lived for 28 years.
EDCS-01600182.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Calventius, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, detailing his military service and age at death.

EDCS-01600183.translation: Lucius Cassius, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, from Parma, soldier of the 12th cohort, lived for 26 years, served for 6 years, is buried here.
EDCS-01600183.summary: This tombstone inscription records the life details of Lucius Cassius, a soldier, including his age, service length, and place of burial.

EDCS-01600184.translation: Titus Cassius Firmus, son of Titus, a centurion of the 9th Spanish legion, and a quaestor with judicial authority.
EDCS-01600184.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Cassius Firmus, a centurion of a Roman legion, and records his civic office.

EDCS-01600185.translation: Catalus, son of Callaeus, of Sequanian origin, an officer (eques) in the ala Scubulorum, served as a sesquiplicarius for 22 years, is buried here.
EDCS-01600185.summary: This tombstone commemorates Catalus, a foreign cavalryman serving in a Roman auxiliary unit, detailing his rank and service length.

EDCS-01600186.translation: Tiberius Claudius Astylus, son of the veteran Tiberius Claudius Epaphroditianus of the 7th Claudian Pia Fidelis legion, a tool-maker for the guild of builders, made this for himself and his wife Julia Dionysias, who deserved well of him, while still alive.
EDCS-01600186.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Tiberius Claudius Astylus, a builder and son of a legionary veteran, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-01600187.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Corneli Successus, son of Caius, soldier of the 12th Urban cohort, aged 17 years and 5 months. Caius Cusionius Dionysius and Statia Cale, to their grandson, as a comfort, from Lucius Gavilius Secundinus and Statia Danae, his parents.
EDCS-01600187.summary: This tombstone is dedicated to Caius Corneli Successus, a young soldier, by his grandparents, to offer solace after the loss of his parents.

EDCS-01600188.text_edition: \n Lucio Decimio Scavae Dercelonis filio missicius ex classe Monus\n
EDCS-01600188.translation: To Lucius Decimius Scava, son of Dercelo, discharged from the fleet.
EDCS-01600188.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Decimius Scava, who was discharged from naval service.

EDCS-01600189.translation: Caius Fabius, son of Caius, of the Publilia tribe, from Verona, soldier of the 9th Spanish legion, is buried here.
EDCS-01600189.summary: This tombstone marks the burial place of Caius Fabius, a soldier in the 9th Spanish legion.

EDCS-01600190.translation: Caius Firmidius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Aemilia tribe, from Suessa Aurunca, soldier of the 6th Praetorian cohort, served for 7 years. Lucius Pompilius Celer, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, his fellow soldier, erected this marker at his own expense.
EDCS-01600190.summary: This tombstone, erected by a fellow soldier, records the details of Caius Firmidius Rufus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, including his service length.

EDCS-01600191.translation: Lucius Flaminius Hister, son of Lucius, augur, military tribune. Titia, daughter of Publius, his wife. Babullia, daughter of Titus, his mother. Quintus Flaminius Hister, son of Lucius, military tribune. Sextus Flaminius Hister, son of Lucius, military tribune.
EDCS-01600191.summary: This inscription lists members of the Flaminius family, including a man with multiple family members who held the prestigious position of military tribune.

EDCS-01600192.translation: To the departed spirits. Flavius Augustalis, centurion of the First Italian Legion in Moesia, served for 20 years, 6 months, and 12 days, 4 hours. He lived 41 years, 7 months, and 15 days, 4 hours. He had a wife, Castorina, for 8 years, 3 months, and 6 days, 4 hours, and a son, Stercorius, who lived 3 years, 7 months, and 10 days, 6 hours. His father survived him by 47 days. Castorina placed this tablet for her dearest husband.
EDCS-01600192.summary: A tombstone for Flavius Augustalis, a centurion, and his family, detailing his military service, lifespan, and family relationships.

EDCS-01600193.translation: To Lucius Gailonius Fidelis, freedman of Lucius Gailonius Corinthus. To Lucius Gailonius Iustinus, son of Lucius, soldier of the II Adiutrix and II Augusta legions. To Lucius Iustus, son of Lucius, brother. To Gailonia Prima, freedwoman.
EDCS-01600193.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating multiple members of the Gailonius family, including freedmen and soldiers.

EDCS-01600194.translation: Quintus GAVIUS Aquila, son of Quintus, decurion, military tribune elected by the people. Hortia Secunda, daughter of Caius, his wife. Gavia, daughter of Quintus, his daughter.
EDCS-01600194.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Gavius Aquila, a decurion and elected military tribune, and members of his family.

EDCS-01600195.translation: Marcus Gellius, son of Marcus, veteran of the XV Legion, ordered this to be made for himself and for Ceia Grata, freedwoman of Titus, his wife, in his will.
EDCS-01600195.summary: A tombstone commissioned by Marcus Gellius, a veteran, for himself and his wife Ceia Grata.

EDCS-01600196.translation: Sextus Hostilius Mansuetus, son of Sextus, of the Promontina tribe, a cavalryman of the 9th Praetorian Cohort, century of Pudentis, lived 28 years, served 10 years. He lies here.
EDCS-01600196.summary: A tombstone for Sextus Hostilius Mansuetus, a cavalryman in the Praetorian Guard, detailing his age and service length.

EDCS-01600197.translation: To the departed spirits. For Iulius Optatus, veteran of the 10th Gemina Legion. Iulia Vitalis... [his wife?]... placed this for [her most pious husband?].
EDCS-01600197.summary: A tombstone for Iulius Optatus, a veteran of the 10th Gemina Legion, with a dedication by his wife.

EDCS-01600198.translation: Caius Hispanus, son of Lucius, soldier of the VII Gemina Felix Legion, from Palentina, is 20 years old. He lies here.
EDCS-01600198.summary: A tombstone for Caius Hispanus, a soldier of the VII Gemina Felix Legion, stating his age and origin.

EDCS-01600199.translation: Marcus Licinius Celer, son of Marcus, of the Palatina tribe, on the public equestrian roll, in memory of Lucius [---], son of Lucius, of the Palatina tribe, Gi[---], military tribune, [---] of historians [?], his friend [---].
EDCS-01600199.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Lucius [---], a military tribune and possibly a historian, with a dedication by his friend Marcus Licinius Celer.

EDCS-01600200.translation: Caius Mamilius Rufus, son of Caius, an official (IIIIvir), military tribune. Caius Mamilius Cresimus, alive, made this for his patron and himself, and for Mamilia Philostrata, his sister, and for [his] freedmen and freedwomen. 16 square feet.
EDCS-01600200.summary: A tombstone commissioned by Caius Mamilius Cresimus for his patron, himself, his sister, and his freed dependents, likely in a columbarium.

EDCS-01600201.translation: Here lies Iustus, a judge, an advocate of equity, whom Sassina begot. Now Aquileia holds him. He commanded a century of the 7th Praetorian Cohort, faithful, not of a barbarian legion. Caius Manlius Valerianus, called by that name, placed this for his brother Sentilius because he deserved it.
EDCS-01600201.summary: A tombstone for Iustus, a judge and advocate, with a dedication by his brother Caius Manlius Valerianus, mentioning his service in the Praetorian Guard.

EDCS-01600202.translation: Gaius Mettius, son of Marcus, of the tribe Tromentina, soldier of the 2nd Praetorian Cohort, lived for 30 years, served for 10 years.
EDCS-01600202.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Mettius, a soldier of the Praetorian Guard, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600203.translation: Marcus Munatius Etruscus Florentinus, son of Marcus, of the tribe Scaptia, lived for 18 years. Quintus Munatius, a soldier of the 7th Praetorian Cohort, erected this for his brother.
EDCS-01600203.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Munatius, a young boy, and his brother Quintus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600205.translation: Lucius Pomponius Silvanus, soldier of the 11th Legion, lies here.
EDCS-01600205.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Pomponius Silvanus, a soldier of the 11th Legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600207.translation: To the divine shades. For Publicia Corinthia, Gaius Bassius Corinthianus, centurion of the 13th Urban Cohort, for his most dutiful mother. The burial plot was given by Tullius Posidonius.
EDCS-01600207.summary: A funerary dedication for Publicia Corinthia, set up by her son Gaius Bassius Corinthianus, a centurion of an urban cohort, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-01600208.text_edition: \n Caio Quintilio Cai filio Romilia Prisco primo pilo tribuno cohortis I vigilum tribuno cohortis Xll urbanae tribuno cohortis VI praetoriae donis militaribus donato IIII Marcus Valerius Chrysanthus IIIIIIvir Aquileiae bene merenti locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-01600208.translation: To Gaius Quintilius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the tribe Romilia, primipilaris, tribune of the 1st Cohort of Vigiles, tribune of the 12th Urban Cohort, tribune of the 6th Praetorian Cohort, honored with military decorations four times. Marcus Valerius Chrysanthus, a quinquennial duovir of Aquileia, worthy of remembrance, was granted this burial plot by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600208.summary: A funerary monument for Gaius Quintilius Priscus, a high-ranking officer with service in the Vigiles, urban, and Praetorian cohorts, who received multiple military honors, with a plot granted by the local council of Aquileia.

EDCS-01600209.translation: Gaius Rufrenus, son of Gaius, of the tribe Pollia, from Fano, for Fortuna. Soldier of the 7th Praetorian Cohort, served for 8 years.
EDCS-01600209.summary: A dedication to the goddess Fortuna and a tombstone for Gaius Rufrenus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600210.translation: Lucius Rutius Sabinus, son of Lucius, of the tribe Sergia, from Hispania, soldier of the 10th Gemina Legion, in the century of Seranus, aged 50 years, 26 years of service, lies here. His heir erected this according to his will. The monument plot is 10 feet in front and 10 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600210.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Rutius Sabinus, a veteran soldier of the 10th Legion who served for 26 years, with a plot of specific dimensions designated in his will.

EDCS-01600211.translation: Lucius Pomponius Silvanus, soldier of the 11th Legion, lies here.
EDCS-01600211.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Pomponius Silvanus, a soldier of the 11th Legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600213.translation: Lucius Titius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Voturia, veteran of the 8th Augusta Legion, with 25 years of service, provision measurer, made this monument for himself while alive, and for his freedwoman concubine Titia Fusca, for his son Vitalis, for his daughter Ingenua, for Veneria the beloved, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their children born and to be born. Quintus Titius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Voturia, veteran of the 8th Augusta Legion, standard-bearer, with 25 years of service, ordered this to be made by his will, for himself and for his wife Pacilia Severa, freedwoman of Titus, for his son Quintus Titius Severus, and for Venusta, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their children born and to be born. The monument plot is 16 feet in front and 32 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600213.summary: A large family tomb monument for two veterans of the 8th Augusta Legion, Lucius Titius and Quintus Titius, detailing their military service, family members, and designated plot sizes, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-01600215.text_edition: \n merui post classicus miles ad latus Augusti annos septem decemque \n
EDCS-01600215.translation: I served for seventeen years as a miles classicus at the side of Augustus.
EDCS-01600215.summary: A personal inscription from a soldier who served 17 years in the imperial service, likely during the reign of Augustus.

EDCS-01600216.translation: Lucius Valerius, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Vercelli, soldier of the 20th legion, 30 years old, 9 years in service, lies here.
EDCS-01600216.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Valerius, a soldier of the 20th legion, indicating his age and years of service.

EDCS-01600217.translation: Valerius Aulucentius of the 11th Claudian legion served as a common soldier for 14 years and as a centurion for 3 years; he lived for 40 years and 5 months. His brother made this memorial.
EDCS-01600217.summary: This is a memorial set up by a brother for Valerius Aulucentius, a soldier and then centurion of the 11th Claudian legion, recording his lifespan and military career.

EDCS-01600218.translation: To Lucius Valerius Calinus, quartermaster of the 7th Gemina legion...
EDCS-01600218.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Valerius Calinus, who served as a quartermaster in the 7th Gemina legion; the inscription is incomplete.

EDCS-01600219.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valerius Longinianus lived for 45 years, served as optio of the 11th Claudian legion for 15 years, and as a regular centurion for 6 years. Born in Lower Moesia, in the fort of Abritanum.
EDCS-01600219.summary: This tombstone commemorates Valerius Longinianus, an optio and centurion of the 11th Claudian legion, detailing his age, service length, and place of origin.

EDCS-01600220.translation: Lucius Valerius Longinus, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, from Savaria, veteran of the 13th urban cohort, made this while alive for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-01600220.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument set up by Lucius Valerius Longinus, a veteran of the 13th urban cohort, for himself and his freedmen and their descendants.

EDCS-01600221.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valerius Quintus, a cadet of the cavalry of the 11th Claudian legion, a citizen...
EDCS-01600221.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Valerius Quintus, a cavalry cadet of the 11th Claudian legion, indicating he was a Roman citizen.

EDCS-01600222.translation: Valeria Rufilla, the mother, placed this monument for her most beloved son, Valerius Victor, a cavalryman who lived 27 years.
EDCS-01600222.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Valeria Rufilla for her son, Valerius Victor, a cavalryman, recording his age at death.

EDCS-01600223.translation: Valeria Eutychia, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive for herself and for her patron Lucius Valerius Tironus, who served for 30 years, and for her husband Gaius Valerius Priscus, who served for 27 years, and for her freedman Hermetus, and for their descendants.
EDCS-01600223.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Valeria Eutychia for herself, her patron, her husband, and her freedman, detailing their military service lengths.

EDCS-01600224.translation: Quintus Vettidius, son of Quintus, of the Beria tribe, soldier of the 9th legion, 8 years of service. Marcus Petronius and Marcus Attius, his heirs, placed this.
EDCS-01600224.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Vettidius, a soldier of the 9th legion, with his heirs Marcus Petronius and Marcus Attius listed as the dedicator.

EDCS-01600225.translation: Quintus Vetuleius, son of Marcus, soldier of the 20th legion, Pollia tribe, 17 years of service.
EDCS-01600225.summary: This tombstone records Quintus Vetuleius, a soldier of the 20th legion, indicating his tribe and length of service.

EDCS-01600226.translation: Lucius Vibius, elected juror, a prefect appointed by the sword, donated a pure spear.
EDCS-01600226.summary: This inscription likely records a military honor or a legal appointment granted to Lucius Vibius, possibly in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01600227.translation: To Lucía Vitellia, also called Senecilla, daughter of Lucius Vitellius Maternus, centurion of the 10th Gemina legion. Sempronius Stella, centurion of the 10th Gemina legion, placed this for his most devoted and chaste wife.
EDCS-01600227.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a soldier to his wife, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, given the mention of the 10th Gemina legion.

EDCS-01600228.translation: Ulpia Martia, who lived 41 years, and Aurelius Aper, who lived 10 years, and Aurelius Abentius, who lived 8 years. Aurelius Silvanus, soldier of the 13th Gemina legion, placed this for his most beloved wife and children.
EDCS-01600228.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a soldier for his wife and children, dating from the period when the 13th Gemina legion was active, likely the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600229.translation: Marcus Vocusius Crescens, freedman of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and for Vocusia Veneria, his excellent wife, and for his son Petronius Vocusianus, a soldier of the 3rd Praetorian cohort, aged 18 years, 3 months, and 18 days. If anyone sells, buys, or reclaims this chest, he shall pay 20,000 sesterces to the public treasury of Aquileia as a penalty, and the informer shall receive a quarter.
EDCS-01600229.summary: This is a funerary monument and a legal warning from Aquileia, dating to the Imperial period, by a freedman for his family, specifying penalties for tampering with the tomb.

EDCS-01600230.translation: To ... son of Gaius ... Julius, standard-bearer of the 2nd Thracian cohort. To ... husband. To ... son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe, Proculus, prefect appointed by the sword, his son. Procula, living, made this for her ... DIA FAUSTA, her friend. ...
EDCS-01600230.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE, dedicating the monument to multiple individuals, including a standard-bearer and a prefect, and possibly a friend.

EDCS-01600238.inscription_type: leges, senatus consulta, tituli honorarii, tituli operum
EDCS-01600238.text_edition: \n Kalendis Novembribus Lucius Nonius Rufinus Pomponianus Quintus Vesonius Fuscus praefecti iure dicundo scribendo adfuerunt Caius Lucretius Helvianus Marcus Trebius Proculus Lucius Cammius Maximus senatus consultum cum prona voluntate honestissimo animo ultro Calvius Pollio IIIIvir iure dicundo in proximum annum professus sit quo facto haesitationi publicae in partem moram ademerit placere ei quo magis etiam ceteri ad bene faciendum in re publica provocentur statuam equestrem auratam in foro nostro poni censuerunt primus censuit Caius Lucretius Helvianus\n
EDCS-01600238.translation: On the Kalends of November, Lucius Nonius Rufinus Pomponianus and Quintus Vesonius Fuscus, prefects appointed by the sword, were present at the writing. Caius Lucretius Helvianus, Marcus Trebius Proculus, Lucius Cammius Maximus, [having decreed] with willing and noble spirit, voluntarily, that Calvius Pollio, as a four-man official for justice in the next year, having registered, and by this action having removed public hesitation and delay, it seemed fitting to them that even more others be encouraged to act well in the state, they decreed that a gilded equestrian statue be erected in our forum. Caius Lucretius Helvianus proposed this first.
EDCS-01600238.summary: This decree from Aquileia, dated by its mention of officials and a senatorial action, records the decision to erect a gilded equestrian statue to honor Calvius Pollio for his public service, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600239.translation: ...ius Iulianus ... Aruntius Cassianus. Because words were spoken in the council of Aquileia according to the custom of public affection, [they are] ready to return lawful rewards to the deserving from their wealth, so that both present recognition is given to them and hope for a similar gift in the future, with the matter having been handled thus, they have decreed thus. With our colleague Aius Pomps..., a most honorable man, and by the modesty of his character and the industry of his life, he has deserved the public... through many previous acts of generosity to our fatherland... Public...
EDCS-01600239.summary: This is a fragmented senatorial decree from Aquileia, likely from the Imperial period, praising a colleague and expressing a desire to reward deserving individuals, but the specific details of the reward and the recipient are largely lost.

EDCS-01600240.translation: Publius Accius Athictus, freedman of Publius, a six-time magistrate, made this while alive for himself and for Accia Horrea, freedwoman of Publius, his dearest wife.
EDCS-01600240.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Aquileia, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period, set up by a prominent freedman for himself and his wife.

EDCS-01600241.translation: To Quintus Acellius Acanthus, freedman of Quintus, who made this while alive for his brother Quintus Acellius Severus, freedman of Quintus; and for Quintus Acellius Modestus, freedman of Quintus, a six-time magistrate and fellow freedman; and for Quintus Acellius Amandus, freedman of Quintus, a six-time magistrate and fellow freedman; and for Acellia Donata, freedwoman of Quintus, his wife; and for Quintus Acellius Principus, freedman of Quintus, a fellow freedman.
EDCS-01600241.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Aquileia, likely from the early Imperial period, set up by a freedman for himself, his brother, his wife, and several fellow freedmen who held the position of IIIIvir.

EDCS-01600242.translation: To Lucius Acestius Saturninus, freedman of Lucius, a six-time magistrate. Statinia Thymele, his wife, made this.
EDCS-01600242.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Aquileia, likely from the early Imperial period, dedicated by a wife to her husband, who was a freedman and a six-time magistrate.

EDCS-01600243.translation: Marcus Alfius Colonus, son of Marcus, a quinquennial duumvir, commissioned this; Lucius Servilius Frater, son of Lucius, also commissioned this.
EDCS-01600243.summary: This inscription records a public work commissioned by two men, Marcus Alfius Colonus and Lucius Servilius Frater, who held the office of quinquennial duumvir.

EDCS-01600244.translation: [...]tius Alsus, a quinquennial duumvir, for his wife Sabina, daughter of Lucius, and for his freedman [...]tio Herma, freedman [...]io Hermaisco, freedman [...]tio Phileto, and freedman [...]io Agili, and the freedmen of both.
EDCS-01600244.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication by a man named Alsus for his wife and several freedmen, likely on a tomb or a funerary monument.

EDCS-01600245.translation: Gaius Annius, son of Titus, from Interamna, gives from his own money to the municipality of Aquileia
EDCS-01600245.summary: This inscription records a donation made by Gaius Annius, son of Titus, from Interamna, to the municipality of Aquileia from his personal funds.

EDCS-01600246.translation: In this work, the state expended 5,000 sesterces from its own funds, and Marcus Antistius Nereus bequeathed 5,000 sesterces by his will.
EDCS-01600246.summary: This inscription records the funding of a public work, with part of the expense covered by the state and part by a bequest from Marcus Antistius Nereus.

EDCS-01600247.translation: Mevia Iucunda erected this for her patron Lucius Apinus Potitus, a sexennial duumvir, for her husband Gaius Afidius Adiutor, son of Gaius and freedman, and for herself, while alive.
EDCS-01600247.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Mevia Iucunda for her husband, her patron Lucius Apinus Potitus (a sexennial duumvir), and herself.

EDCS-01600248.translation: Titus Apollonius, son of Gaius, Publius Babrinius, son of Marcus, duumvirs
EDCS-01600248.summary: This inscription fragment names Titus Apollonius, son of Gaius, and Publius Babrinius, son of Marcus, as holding the office of duumvirs.

EDCS-01600250.translation: Sextus Attius, Raia, daughter of Marcus, Sextus Attius, son of Sextus, Publius, son of Sextus, all of the Velina tribe, were decurions.
EDCS-01600250.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely related, who were decurions and possibly members of the Velina tribe, probably related to local governance or a collegium.

EDCS-01600251.translation: For Publius Barbilius Primigenius, a sexennial duumvir of Aquileia, his freedmen Chresimus and Donata [erected this] for their most dutiful father.
EDCS-01600251.summary: This inscription is a dedication by two freedmen, Chresimus and Donata, to their father, Publius Barbilius Primigenius, a distinguished official in Aquileia.

EDCS-01600252.translation: To Lucius Caecilius Proccessus, son of Lucius, of the Aelia tribe, a decurion and Roman knight, who lived for 26 years.
EDCS-01600252.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Caecilius Proccessus, a young man who held the rank of decurion and Roman knight and died at the age of 26.

EDCS-01600253.translation: Publius Caesius Romilia, son of Publius, aedile of Sora, a tax collector in Rome, [by the arbitration] of Arrius Paedatis and his freedman Hilarius Me[...].
EDCS-01600253.summary: This inscription concerns Publius Caesius Romilia, an aedile of Sora and a tax collector in Rome, whose activities or dispute were arbitrated by Arrius Paedatis and his freedman.

EDCS-01600254.text_edition: \n Lucius Calius Marci filius Claudia Cremona Concordia decurio quaestor operis publicis in Bithynia fuit Calio Marci filio Claudia Cremona Malliolo fratri et in operis publicis in Asia et \n
EDCS-01600254.translation: Lucius Calius Marci filius Claudia Cremona Concordia, a decurion and quaestor of public works in Bithynia, [also] for his brother Calius Marci filius Claudia Cremona Malliolus, and in public works in Asia.
EDCS-01600254.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Calius Concordia, who served as a decurion and quaestor for public works in Bithynia, and also mentions his brother Malliolus and public works in Asia.

EDCS-01600255.translation: To Titus Canius Adrastus, son of Titus, a freedman, a sexennial duumvir, [and] patron.
EDCS-01600255.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Canius Adrastus, a freedman who held the prestigious office of sexennial duumvir and was also honored as a patron.

EDCS-01600256.translation: Cervonia Tyche made this while alive for herself, and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants; if anyone wishes to sell or buy or inscribe this chest or this monument, then they must give 20,000 sesterces to the public treasury of the people of Aquileia as a penalty.
EDCS-01600256.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription by Cervonia Tyche, who dedicates it to herself and her descendants, and imposes a penalty for its sale or unauthorized alteration, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600257.translation: Tiberius Claudius Asianus, one of the six priests of Aquileia, to Tutilia Medama
EDCS-01600257.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Tiberius Claudius Asianus, a member of the college of six priests in Aquileia, to Tutilia Medama.

EDCS-01600258.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Cornelius Crescens, member of the college of six, for himself and for Cornelia Thalussa, his most excellent wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, this monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-01600258.summary: A funerary monument set up by Cornelius Crescens for himself, his wife, and freedpersons, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE, stating that the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-01600259.translation: Sacred to the gods of the underworld. To Valeria Saturnini, freedwoman, Aristoclia, freedwoman of Marcus Cornelia, Hermione, his most excellent wife. Lucius Valerius Arista, member of the college of three, made this while alive.
EDCS-01600259.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Valerius Arista for his wife Hermione and her freedwoman Aristoclia, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600260.translation: Decia Galla, daughter of Quintus, mother. Decia, daughter of Quintus, sister. Quintus Decius Flaccus, son of Quintus, member of the college of four.
EDCS-01600260.summary: A tomb inscription honoring Decia Galla and her family, identifying Quintus Decius Flaccus as a member of the college of four, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600261.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Hermes, freedman of Gnaeus, member of the college of six, made this while alive for himself and for Domitia Iusta, daughter of Gnaeus, and for Pompeia Celsina, his most chaste wife, and for Epaphra and Hermes, his most faithful freedmen.
EDCS-01600261.summary: A funerary monument erected by Gnaeus Domitius Hermes for himself, his wife, daughter, and freedpersons, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600263.translation: Lucius Fabius Epagatus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive, and for his freedmen: Lucius Fabius Diphilus, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Fabius Heraclida, freedman of Lucius, alive.
EDCS-01600263.summary: A funerary monument set up by Lucius Fabius Epagatus for himself and two freedmen, identifying them as members of the college of six, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600264.translation: Titus Flavius Crescens, freedman of Augustus, member of the college of six, made this while alive for himself and for Julia Nomas, his dearest wife, and for Cassidia Marcella, daughter, and for Flavia Procilla, daughter.
EDCS-01600264.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Titus Flavius Crescens, a freedman of Augustus, for himself, his wife, and two daughters, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600266.translation: [...] Fruticius, son of Marcus, member of the college of four in judgment, quinquennial; member of the college of four in judgment.
EDCS-01600266.summary: An inscription honoring Fruticius, son of Marcus, who held the office of member of the college of four in judgment twice, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600267.translation: Of Lucius Fundanius Rufus, decurion of Aquileia. Fundania Athenais, pupil and heir.
EDCS-01600267.summary: A dedication by Fundania Athenais, pupil and heir, to Lucius Fundanius Rufus, a decurion of Aquileia, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600268.translation: [...] Hilara, freedwoman of Caius. [...]bullius, freedman of Caius. [...]conlibertus. [...]lius, freedman of Caius. [...] member of the college of six. [...] Tertius, freedman of Marcus. [...] his own. [...] Tertia. [...]cundae, freedwoman, alive.
EDCS-01600268.summary: A complex funerary inscription listing several individuals, including freedmen and a member of the college of six, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600269.translation: Sacred to the gods of the underworld. From the Feroniensian Watermen. [...] Ianuarius. [...] Opellia(?). To Lucius Mineius Heleno. [...]ia. To Facilinus, servant(?). To Quintus F. Adius(?), Ieniscus. [...]simia. To Honiada. [...] Kanius. To Varia Phil[...], wife. And to Kania Procilla [...]. To the sons of Docilius the Elder(?).
EDCS-01600269.summary: A funerary inscription possibly related to a guild of watermen, mentioning several individuals including freedpersons and family members, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600270.translation: To Lucius Luccius Lucullus, son of Lucius, a four-time magistrate with judicial powers, from Belun.
EDCS-01600270.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Luccius Lucullus, a magistrate, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-01600271.translation: Marcus Lucius Dromo, freedman of Marcus, a six-time magistrate.
EDCS-01600271.summary: This is an epitaph for Marcus Lucius Dromo, a freedman and a six-time magistrate.

EDCS-01600272.translation: Caius Lucius Maniacus, son of Caius, and Vettia Figuli, daughter of Marcus. Caius Lucius Maniacus, son of Caius, and Caius Lucius Maniacus, son of Caius, four-time magistrates with judicial powers, by the favor of the people. Caius Lucius, son of Caius, made this.
EDCS-01600272.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Caius Lucius Maniacus and Vettia Figuli, possibly commemorating their service as magistrates, with a statement of construction by Caius Lucius.

EDCS-01600273.translation: Aulus Lucretius Attalus, son of Gaius, son of Gaius; Gaius Lucretius Secundus, son of Aulus, son of Gaius; Secunda Petronia, daughter of Gaius, daughter of Gaius; Aulus Lucretius, son of Aulus, son of Gaius; duumvir.
EDCS-01600273.summary: This inscription lists members of the Lucretius family, including Aulus Lucretius Attalus and Gaius Lucretius Secundus, along with Petronia, and identifies one of them as a duumvir, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01600274.translation: Lucius Marius Proculus, son of Lucius. Lucius Marius Felix, freedman of Lucius, a six-time magistrate, an insulator, made this for himself and for his wife Cornelia Procula, daughter of Spurius, and for his daughter Maria Marulla, daughter of Lucius, and for his freedwoman wife Maria, freedwoman of Lucius, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01600274.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Marius Felix, a six-time magistrate, for himself and his family, including his wife, daughter, and freedpersons.

EDCS-01600276.translation: Gnaeus Octavius Cornicula, son of Caius, a four-time magistrate, made this while alive.
EDCS-01600276.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Gnaeus Octavius Cornicula, a four-time magistrate, erected his own tomb.

EDCS-01600277.text_edition: \n Cnaeo Octavio Cnaei filio Palatina Vitali Cnaeus Octavius Zosimus et Titia Agrippina parentes locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-01600277.translation: To Gnaeus Octavius Vitalis, son of Gnaeus, of the Palatina tribe. Gnaeus Octavius Zosimus and Titia Agrippina, parents, gave this plot by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600277.summary: This inscription records the allocation of burial space to Gnaeus Octavius Vitalis by his parents, Gnaeus Octavius Zosimus and Titia Agrippina, following a decree by local councillors.

EDCS-01600278.translation: Caius Petronius, son of Titus, a four-time magistrate, gave this place for his freedmen, freedwomen, and the freedmen and freedwomen of his freedmen. Caius Petronius Hermia, son of Caius. Petronia Argentilla, freedwoman of Caius. Caius Petronius Liccaeus, son of Caius. Caius Petronius Nicephor, son of Caius. Caius Petronius Philogenes, son of Caius.
EDCS-01600278.summary: This inscription records Caius Petronius, a four-time magistrate, dedicating a burial plot for his extended family of freedpersons and also lists several individuals, likely freedmen or their descendants, with the name Caius Petronius.

EDCS-01600279.translation: Manius Petronius, son of Manius, a decurion. Graiena, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-01600279.summary: This inscription appears to be a tombstone or memorial for Manius Petronius, a decurion, and Graiena.

EDCS-01600280.translation: Marcus Petronius Scaenarius, son of Marcus. Marcus Petronius Romanus, freedman of Marcus, a six-time magistrate.
EDCS-01600280.summary: This inscription is an epitaph for Marcus Petronius Scaenarius and his freedman Marcus Petronius Romanus, who was a six-time magistrate.

EDCS-01600281.text_edition: \n Petroniae Cai filiae Bassillae Caius Petronius Felix IIIIIIvir et Augustalis et Petronia \n
EDCS-01600281.translation: To Petronia Bassilla, daughter of Caius. Caius Petronius Felix, a six-time magistrate and Augustalis, and Petronia.
EDCS-01600281.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Petronia Bassilla, likely by Caius Petronius Felix, who held multiple civic and religious offices, and Petronia.

EDCS-01600283.translation: Quintus Pontienus Amycus, quinquennial official, made this himself and for his wife Iuventia Anthi, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and for his freedwoman Iuventia. The monument's location: 10 feet in front, 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600283.summary: A funerary monument erected by Quintus Pontienus Amycus, a quinquennial official, for himself and his family, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600284.translation: To Statinia Strategis, his mother. Caius Plenius Strato, quinquennial official, made this himself.
EDCS-01600284.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Caius Plenius Strato, a quinquennial official, to his mother Statinia Strategis, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600285.translation: Lucius Suedius Iucundus, quinquennial official, [lists 21 other individuals].
EDCS-01600285.summary: A list of 22 members of the quinquennial college (IIIIvir) in a Roman colony, likely commemorative or honorary, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600286.translation: Terentia Casta made this herself and for her husband [Lucius?] Granius Apollonius, quinquennial official, in Aquileia. Also for her husband Quintus Hortensius Euenus, for Lucius Granius Primigenius, for Lucius Granius Crescens, and for Grania Secunda.
EDCS-01600286.summary: A funerary monument erected by Terentia Casta for herself and multiple family members, including two husbands, one of whom was a quinquennial official in Aquileia, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600287.translation: Lucius Titius, son of Marcus, quinquennial official with jurisdiction, holding the office for the fifth year.
EDCS-01600287.summary: An inscription identifying Lucius Titius, son of Marcus, as a quinquennial official with judicial powers, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600288.translation: [Trophimus], an Augustalis, [decorated] with the honours of a decurion of the colony of Claudia Savaria.
EDCS-01600288.summary: An inscription honoring Trophimus, an Augustalis, who was awarded decurional honors in the colony of Claudia Savaria, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600289.translation: Gaius Turanius, son of Gaius, of Aquileia, a place was given by decree of the decurions for ten merits; Gaius Turanius, son of Lucius
EDCS-01600289.summary: This inscription records that a place was granted by decree of the town council to Gaius Turanius, son of Gaius, a citizen of Aquileia, due to his ten merits, with a reference to Gaius Turanius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-01600290.translation: To Gaius Valerius Eusebetus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, a quinquennial IIII vir iure dicundo, patron of Septimia Aurelia Augusta, and a IIII vir patron of the guild of wool-workers and wood-carvers of Aquileia, on account of his remarkable generosity and liberality towards them, a place was granted by unanimous vote at the expense of the guild of artisans, as their most worthy patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01600290.summary: This is a funerary monument honoring Gaius Valerius Eusebetus, a prominent citizen and patron of several guilds in Aquileia, who was granted a place of honor by the town council.

EDCS-01600291.translation: Lucius Vallius Auctus, son of Lucius, quinquennial official, to his wife Fructuosa Martialis, freedwoman, his cherished wife, aged 15.
EDCS-01600291.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fructuosa Martialis, wife of Lucius Vallius Auctus (a quinquennial official), dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600292.translation: To Caius Varius Zosimus, freedman of Caius, patron and quinquennial official. Tychius, freedman and vigintivir, made this place of rest for his body himself, and for his dearest wife Varia Graeca, and for his daughter Varia Successa, and for Eutycius.
EDCS-01600292.summary: A funerary monument erected by Tychius, a vigintivir, for his patron Zosimus (a quinquennial official) and his own family, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600293.translation: [Verus], aedile, quinquennial official, pontifex, gave this gift with his daughter Priscilla.
EDCS-01600293.summary: An inscription recording Verus, who held the offices of aedile, quinquennial official, and pontifex, and dedicated a gift with his daughter, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600294.translation: Titus Vibius Ruso, son of Titus, quinquennial official with jurisdiction, quinquennial official for the fifth year. Titus Vibius Ruso, augur. Caeparia, daughter of Gnaeus.
EDCS-01600294.summary: An inscription identifying Titus Vibius Ruso who held multiple magistracies including augur and quinquennial official, along with a female relative, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600295.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Arsio, who held the civic office of decurion.

EDCS-01600303.translation: To Aurelia Felicitas, of the Bennas tribe, who lived 23 years. Julius Gemellus, to his dearest wife.
EDCS-01600303.summary: This is a tombstone for Aurelia Felicitas, erected by her husband Julius Gemellus, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-01600304.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Cassius Longinus, an expert of the law, a good man. Titus Flavius Valerianus, his heir.
EDCS-01600304.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Cassius Longinus, an accomplished jurist, by his heir Titus Flavius Valerianus.

EDCS-01600305.translation: Gnaeus Coponius was taken from life by fate; born in Tibur, he died in Aquileia; his brother wished to honor the deceased with a tomb.
EDCS-01600305.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Gnaeus Coponius in Aquileia, who was originally from Tibur, and erected by his brother.

EDCS-01600306.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Lauto, the rhetorician.
EDCS-01600306.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Cornelius Lauto, a teacher of rhetoric, likely set up by a student or admirer.

EDCS-01600307.translation: Marcus Fabius, son of Lucius, from Atesta, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-01600307.summary: This is an incomplete funerary or commemorative inscription for Marcus Fabius, indicating his origin and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-01600308.translation: Lucius Firmius, son of Titus, the craftsman.
EDCS-01600308.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Lucius Firmius as a craftsman and son of Titus.

EDCS-01600309.translation: Gaudentius Priscianus, deceased in Syria. Aurelius OOETG erected this for his most devoted brother.
EDCS-01600309.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaudentius Priscianus, who died in Syria, erected by his loving brother Aurelius.

EDCS-01600310.translation: Quintus Gavius Fortunatus, the Cypriot, made this for himself while alive, and for Gavia Agra, his patroness.
EDCS-01600310.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Gavius Fortunatus, a man from Cyprus, for himself and his patroness Gavia Agra.

EDCS-01600312.translation: Hermophilus, a household slave and steward.
EDCS-01600312.summary: This is an identification of Hermophilus, a slave who served as a steward.

EDCS-01600313.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning Hyginus, identified as a trustworthy agent, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory text.

EDCS-01600314.translation: Aulus Mulvius Iucundus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, a baker, erected this while alive for himself, and for his patron, and for his own freedmen and freedwomen, and for Aulus Mulvius Bassus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Iuvenes, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Priamus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Pudens, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Firmus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Modestus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Faustus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius, and for Aulus Mulvius Chrisellus, freedman of Aulus Mulvius.
EDCS-01600314.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Aulus Mulvius Iucundus, a freedman baker, for himself, his patron, and a large number of his own freedmen and other individuals named Aulus Mulvius.

EDCS-01600315.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Passerus, the retiarius. His wife Aelia, well-deserving.
EDCS-01600315.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Passerus, a net-fighter (retiarius), set up by his devoted wife Aelia.

EDCS-01600316.translation: To Patroclus, of the highest [qualities], Ulpius Priscus [erected this] for a soul deserving [of honor].
EDCS-01600316.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Ulpius Priscus to Patroclus, honoring his esteemed qualities.

EDCS-01600317.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Philagrypnos, a freedman of Augustus from the province of Africa, who lived 22 years, 8 months, and 25 days. Heliodorus, an anointer at the office of Africa, made this for him, well-deserving.
EDCS-01600317.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Philagrypnos, a young freedman of Augustus who worked as an anointer, erected by Heliodorus.
