EDCS-01600318.translation: Gaius Plos, merchant; Publius Plosu Petronius.
EDCS-01600318.summary: This inscription possibly records the names of two individuals, Gaius Plos, a merchant, and Publius Plosu Petronius, likely a funerary or commemorative notice.

EDCS-01600319.translation: The bones of Publius Postumius Felix, the lintio.
EDCS-01600319.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Postumius Felix, identified by his profession (lintio).

EDCS-01600320.translation: To Lucius Gallonius Primigenius, freedman of Corinthus, a incense seller. Euthichus, freedman.
EDCS-01600320.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Gallonius Primigenius, a freedman incense seller, by Euthichus, also a freedman.

EDCS-01600321.translation: To Publicius, Terentia, Terentius Iulius, to No [?], Terentia acting as procurator. Annianus Terentius.
EDCS-01600321.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication or funerary text involving several individuals named Terentius and Terentia, with one acting as a procurator.

EDCS-01600322.translation: To Marcus Pullius Castus, freedman of Marcus; to Marcus Pullius Fuscus, freedman of Marcus, a purple-dyer; Pullia Prima, freedwoman of Marcus; Marcus Flavius Ianuarius; Marcus Pullius Hormus, freedman of Marcus, a purple-dyer.
EDCS-01600322.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including freedmen and a purple-dyer, likely related to a business or family, with no specific date indicated.

EDCS-01600323.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Viatrix, to her excellent and deserving husband Romulus Bizegonis filius Hemesenus.
EDCS-01600323.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Viatrix for her husband Romulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600324.translation: Sextus Samiarius Andronicus, freedman of Sextus, a baker, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-01600324.summary: A baker named Sextus Samiarius Andronicus dedicated a tomb for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-01600325.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Secundius Genialis, from Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium, a merchant, an excellent patron. Marcus Secundius Eutychus, his freedman, as heir in part of the estate, made this monument at his own expense.
EDCS-01600325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Secundius Genialis, a merchant from Cologne, erected by his freedman and heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600327.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions an 'actor' (a legal or administrative official) and is too incomplete to provide further context or date.

EDCS-01600328.translation: Private boundary stone. In private ground. To Terentius Heracla.
EDCS-01600328.summary: This is a boundary marker designating private property and naming Terentius Heracla, likely of the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600330.translation: List of names, likely belonging to a funerary or collegial context, some with freedman and patron relationships indicated.
EDCS-01600330.summary: This inscription is a long list of Roman names, possibly members of a collegium or a family burial group, with some familial and social relationships indicated.

EDCS-01600331.translation: Space of Lucius Abundius Crispus. For Septumia Veneria. In the front, 20 feet; in the field, 32 feet.
EDCS-01600331.summary: This inscription allocates a plot of land measuring 20 by 32 feet for Septumia Veneria, belonging to Lucius Abundius Crispus, likely a property record from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600332.translation: Lucius Accius, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-01600332.summary: Lucius Accius, son of Marcus, commissioned this monument to be created after his death through his will.

EDCS-01600333.translation: Lucius Aebutius Trophimianus, who lived 6 years, 4 months, and who was ill for 1 year, 4 months. Aebutius Corint[h]us and Trophima, parents, to their most sweet son.
EDCS-01600333.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Aebutius Trophimianus, recording his age at death and a period of illness, set up by his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600334.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Publius Aelius Domitianus, son of Publius, who lived 5 years and 13 days. Publius Aelius Sabinus, to his innocent and most sweet son.
EDCS-01600334.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Domitianus, recording his age at death, set up by his father Publius Aelius Sabinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600335.translation: Aelia Balbina, to her most beloved wife, who lived 23 years. Lucius Allius [---]nus, evocatus.
EDCS-01600335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Balbina, recording her age at death, set up by her husband Lucius Allius [---]nus, an evocatus (a type of soldier), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600336.translation: To Aelia Sosolia, their most sweet daughter. Minucius Sosus and Aelia Primitiva, parents.
EDCS-01600336.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Sosolia, set up by her parents Minucius Sosus and Aelia Primitiva, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600337.translation: The location of the monument of Lucius Aemilius Paullus: in front 16 feet, in the field 22 feet.
EDCS-01600337.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Aemilius Paullus.

EDCS-01600339.translation: Lucius Aius Tiro, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and his family, under the supervision of Lucius Aius Primigenius, freedman of Lucius, and Aia Vitalina, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Lucius Aius Severus, son of Lucius, and Stentilius, son of Lucius Aius.
EDCS-01600339.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Lucius Aius Tiro via his will, specifying beneficiaries and the supervisor of its construction.

EDCS-01600340.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly naming a person named Urbanus.

EDCS-01600341.translation: The location of Lucius Albius: 16 square feet.
EDCS-01600341.summary: This inscription records the size of a plot belonging to Lucius Albius, likely for burial.

EDCS-01600342.translation: Titus Alphius Ariston made this for himself, his family, and his freedmen and freedwomen: a square plot of 16 feet.
EDCS-01600342.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Titus Alphius Ariston for himself and his household, defining a burial plot.

EDCS-01600343.translation: The location of the monument of Lucius Alli Trophimus: in front 48 feet, in the field 29 feet.
EDCS-01600343.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Alli Trophimus.

EDCS-01600344.translation: Allia Quieta made this while alive for herself and for her husband Lucius Aurelius Fortunatus...
EDCS-01600344.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Allia Quieta for herself and her deceased husband, Lucius Aurelius Fortunatus.

EDCS-01600345.translation: Amphion, Drusianus, freedman of Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus, made this while alive for himself and for Prima Aphrodisia, his companion, for six years.
EDCS-01600345.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Amphion Drusianus, a freedman of Emperor Augustus, for himself and his partner, indicating the duration of their relationship.

EDCS-01600347.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records dimensions of a plot and possibly names of freedmen, perhaps related to burials.

EDCS-01600348.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits of Ampulena Secundina, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-01600348.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Ampulena Secundina.

EDCS-01600349.translation: I, Anicia Glucera, freedwoman of Publius, existed; I spoke enough about my life, pleasing my good husband who brought me from the lowest rank to the highest honor. I bequeathed an altar to the underworld gods in my will.
EDCS-01600349.summary: Anicia Glucera, a freedwoman, dedicates an altar to the underworld gods in her will, reflecting on her life and her husband's elevated status.

EDCS-01600350.translation: Helena, freedwoman of Annava, for herself and for Marcus Poblicius Cruscillus, freedman of a woman; the plot of the monument is 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01600350.summary: Helena, a freedwoman, dedicates a burial plot of 16 square feet for herself and Marcus Poblicius Cruscillus.

EDCS-01600351.translation: To the divine spirits of Antistia Felicula. Antistia Syntyche, freedwoman, made this for her most devoted patroness and for her daughter Antistia Felicula, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument will not pass to an heir; the plot of the monument is 25 feet in front and 20 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600351.summary: Antistia Syntyche, a freedwoman, dedicates a monument for her patroness Antistia Felicula, her daughter, and future descendants, stipulating it is not inheritable and defining the plot size.

EDCS-01600352.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Plotia Callinice placed this for her sweetest husband, Antoni Castus, who lived 32 years and 5 months, with whom she lived 11 years and 5 months.
EDCS-01600352.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Plotia Callinice for her husband Antoni Castus, detailing their ages and years together.

EDCS-01600353.translation: To Marcus Antonius Euthetus Gemella, son of Marcus, from his wife.
EDCS-01600353.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Antonius Euthetus, dedicated by his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600354.translation: Apollonius, [---] of the household of Servius Hilarius, and Servia(?) Aucta, freedwoman of Manius, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-01600354.summary: A funerary epitaph for Apollonius and Servia Aucta, made by them during their lifetime, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600355.translation: Marcus Aponius Faustus, patron; Peticia Prima; Marcus Apponius Optatus, freedman of Marcus, ordered this to be made for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01600355.summary: Marcus Aponius Faustus, a patron, and his freedman Marcus Apponius Optatus commissioned a monument for themselves and their freed dependents.

EDCS-01600356.translation: To Apponia Proposis, freedwoman of Lucius, from her heirs.
EDCS-01600356.summary: A funerary dedication to Apponia Proposis, freedwoman of Lucius, by her heirs, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600357.translation: Sextus Appuleius Cato, freedman of Sextus; Sextus Suavis, freedman of Sextus; Sextus Firmus, freedman of Sextus.
EDCS-01600357.summary: A list of three men, all freedmen of a Sextus Appuleius, likely recording individuals associated with a family or estate, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600358.translation: To Marcus Appuleius Primigenius, freedman; to Marcus Appuleius Communis, freedman; to Marcus Appuleius Eron, freedman.
EDCS-01600358.summary: A funerary dedication to three freedmen of a Marcus Appuleius, likely commemorating their lives or deaths, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600359.translation: [---] Appuleius Synhistor [dedicated this] to his most devoted colleague.
EDCS-01600359.summary: A dedication fragment, possibly funerary, from a colleague named Appuleius Synhistor to a 'most devoted colleague', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600360.translation: Aptus, son of Sextus Cossutius, aged 12 years.
EDCS-01600360.summary: A child's epitaph for Aptus, son of Sextus Cossutius, who died at age 12, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600362.translation: [---] to the most devoted son, servant of our Caesar, and to Lucius Aquileiensis Agathio, and to Helios, the colonists.
EDCS-01600362.summary: A fragmentary dedication to a deceased 'son' and servant of the emperor, as well as to Lucius Aquileiensis Agathio and Helios, identified as colonists, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600363.translation: Titus Aquileiensis Stratonicus for himself and for his most devoted son, Numisius Tiberinus Basileus, who lived 36 years, 5 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-01600363.summary: A funerary epitaph for Numisius Tiberinus Basileus, dedicated by his father Titus Aquileiensis Stratonicus, providing his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600364.translation: To the spirits of the departed: to Aquileiensis Calendi(nae?), aged 22 years and 6 months; to Aquileiensis Daramon; from his mother.
EDCS-01600364.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to two individuals, Aquileiensis Calendi(nae?) and Aquileiensis Daramon, by Daramon's mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600365.translation: Burial place (16 feet in every direction).
EDCS-01600365.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of 16 Roman feet in each direction, likely in Aquileia.

EDCS-01600366.translation: and for Ve Ianuaria, wife, with whom he lived for 17 years and 6 months, and for Ursa Aquileiensis, her excellent sister.
EDCS-01600366.summary: This inscription fragment records dedications to a wife, Ve Ianuaria, and her sister, Ursa Aquileiensis.

EDCS-01600367.translation: To Ursula, from Claudius Mettius Evaristus, her son-in-law.
EDCS-01600367.summary: This is a dedication to Ursula from her son-in-law, Claudius Mettius Evaristus, likely in Aquileia.

EDCS-01600368.translation: To the divine spirits of Palatina, freedwoman of Quintus Aquilius. Si N
EDCS-01600368.summary: A dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' (divine spirits) of Palatina, a freedwoman belonging to Quintus Aquilius, with an incomplete name following.

EDCS-01600369.translation: In Aquileia, for Octavia, daughter of Aquilus, who lived 5 years, and for her siblings Mercurialis and Irene, and for Octavia Primitiva and Aquila Felix, who lived [3].
EDCS-01600369.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Octavia, daughter of Aquilus, who died at age 5, along with her siblings and possibly others, in Aquileia.

EDCS-01600370.translation: Gaius Aratrius, son of Caius; Lucius, son of Caius, from Aquino; Beria, daughter of Mani; Lucius Aratrius, son of Caius; Lucius, son of Caius [
EDCS-01600370.summary: This inscription lists several names and patronymics, possibly related to a family or property, and appears to be incomplete from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01600371.translation: ] of Caius Arat[--], freedman of Caius Rufus, for himself and his family.
EDCS-01600371.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication or funerary marker by a freedman of Caius Rufus for himself and his family.

EDCS-01600372.translation: Lucius Aratrius Surio, to his excellent wife Aratria Elpis.
EDCS-01600372.summary: This is a dedication from Lucius Aratrius Surio to his wife, Aratria Elpis, likely in Aquileia.

EDCS-01600373.translation: Arria Amarillis, freedwoman of Caius, made this while alive for herself and for Lucius Caettennius Tertullus.
EDCS-01600373.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Arria Amarillis, a freedwoman of Caius, for herself and Lucius Caettennius Tertullus.

EDCS-01600374.translation: Barbius Gratus dedicated the first, second, and third place for one sestertius.
EDCS-01600374.summary: This is a dedication by Barbius Gratus for three locations, possibly related to a public space or funerary context, for a nominal sum.

EDCS-01600375.translation: ] to Arria Galena(?), to Caius Arrius Epopta(?), to Marcus Aulus Avitus(?), to Caius Arrius Fortis(?), to Caius Arrius Primigenius(?).
EDCS-01600375.summary: This fragmented inscription lists several names, possibly recipients of dedications or deceased individuals, with tentative restorations of names and relationships.

EDCS-01600376.translation: Burial place for Arria Nicopoles; 16 feet in the front, 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600376.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Arria Nicopoles, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600377.translation: Quintus Aspasius Apollonides made this living for Hygia, his freedwoman Valeria.
EDCS-01600377.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quintus Aspasius Apollonides for his freedwoman and possibly wife, Hygia.

EDCS-01600378.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that lists several Greek names, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory text.

EDCS-01600379.translation: Titus Atilius Primus, son of Gaius, and Pompeia Rufa, daughter of Marcus, and Iulia Callisti, freedwoman of Archeni[a], made (this) while alive.
EDCS-01600379.summary: A funerary monument set up by Titus Atilius Primus, Pompeia Rufa, and Iulia Callisti, possibly a family group or patrons and freedwoman, dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-01600380.translation: To Atilia Onesimenus, with whom I lived for 15 years, my dearest wife. Gaius Iulius Epictetus, who also, by fate, placed (this) while alive, and for himself: if anyone after two bodies are placed here opens this tomb or displaces (them) and places another body, he shall pay 100,000 sesterces to the treasury.
EDCS-01600380.summary: A funerary inscription for Atilia Onesimenus, set up by her husband Gaius Iulius Epictetus, who also reserved a space for himself and imposed a heavy penalty for violating the burial arrangements.

EDCS-01600381.translation: To Statilia Zosime, his Anatolian wife.
EDCS-01600381.summary: This is a dedication from an unknown person to his wife, Statilia Zosime, of Anatolian origin.

EDCS-01600382.translation: To Attia Optata, freedwoman of a woman, and to Marcus Servilius [---].
EDCS-01600382.summary: An incomplete funerary dedication to Attia Optata and Marcus Servilius.

EDCS-01600383.translation: [---] Venustus and Attia Sabina made (this) for themselves while alive.
EDCS-01600383.summary: A funerary monument set up by Venustus and Attia Sabina for themselves, indicating a couple.

EDCS-01600385.translation: Auctianus, son of Marcus, of the Tromentina tribe, dedicated this.
EDCS-01600385.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Auctianus, identifying his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-01600386.translation: DA [dedicated this] to Candida Avertinia Severina, his most rare and incomparable friend.
EDCS-01600386.summary: This inscription is a dedication from an unknown person (initials DA) to their exceptionally esteemed friend, Candida Avertinia Severina.

EDCS-01600387.translation: Publius Aufidius Epaphra, son of Publius, freedman, made (this) for himself and his family while alive. For Iulia [3]iata, daughter of Gaius, freedwoman. For Casta, daughter, aged 21 years. For Castus, son. For Proba, daughter. For freedmen and freedwomen. The monument's space, facing in every direction, 16 feet.
EDCS-01600387.summary: A funerary monument erected by the freedman Publius Aufidius Epaphra for himself, his family, and his freedmen, detailing burial spaces and dimensions.

EDCS-01600388.translation: For Quintus Avilius Phanetis, freedman [---]. The monument's space: 30 feet in front, 70 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600388.summary: A funerary monument marking the dimensions of a burial plot for Quintus Avilius Phanetis, a freedman.

EDCS-01600391.translation: To the departed spirits and eternal rest. Aurelius Ap[{{fill}}]lo, his most unfortunate son, who lived 19 years. Aurelius Maximinus and Apla, parents, bereaved of their only son.
EDCS-01600391.summary: A funerary dedication from parents Aurelius Maximinus and Apla to their son Aurelius Aplillus, who died young.

EDCS-01600392.summary: An incomplete inscription possibly related to a funerary monument or dedication.

EDCS-01600393.translation: To the departed spirits. I, Ianuaris, his wife, made (this) for Aurelius Hilarus, well deserving, my husband.
EDCS-01600393.summary: A funerary dedication from Ianuaris to her husband Aurelius Hilarus, honoring his good character.

EDCS-01600394.translation: Aurelius Hylas, son of Hylatis, lived 5 years and 7 months. His mother Iulia placed (this).
EDCS-01600394.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child, Aurelius Hylas, set up by his mother Iulia.

EDCS-01600395.translation: To the departed spirits. Irene set this up for her most beloved husband, Aurelius Karnuntinus.
EDCS-01600395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Irene for her husband, Aurelius Karnuntinus.

EDCS-01600397.translation: To the safety of Aurelia, most chaste woman, with whom I lived for 30 years. Taurus and Taurinus dedicated this to their most chaste freedwoman Avia, wife.
EDCS-01600397.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Taurus and Taurinus to their wife and freedwoman Avia, commemorating their 30 years together and her chastity.

EDCS-01600398.translation: Caetronia Saturnina made this living for herself and for her daughter Tullia, daughter of Aulus Prisca.
EDCS-01600398.summary: This funerary monument was made by Caetronia Saturnina for herself and her daughter Tullia Prisca.

EDCS-01600399.translation: To Aurelia Patern, who lived 18 years, Mennius Centullius Paulinus [dedicated this] to his most innocent wife.
EDCS-01600399.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Mennius Centullius Paulinus to his wife Aurelia Patern, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-01600400.translation: To the departed spirits. Autei Helen made this living for himself and his family. The monument occupies 16 feet in front and 30 feet in the area.
EDCS-01600400.summary: This funerary inscription by Autei Helen specifies the dimensions of the plot dedicated for himself and his family.

EDCS-01600401.translation: Babullia Aucta, Babullia Iucunda, and Babullia Grata made this for their patron.
EDCS-01600401.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated to a patron by three freedwomen: Babullia Aucta, Babullia Iucunda, and Babullia Grata.

EDCS-01600402.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Badusius Paulinus set this up for his most beloved son, T. Badusius Sabinianus, who lived 5 years and 10 months. The monument occupies 45 front feet and 50 field feet.
EDCS-01600402.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy, T. Badusius Sabinianus, indicating the dimensions of the funerary plot.

EDCS-01600403.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription or marker bearing the name Tiberius Barbius Ingenuus.

EDCS-01600404.translation: The monument occupies the property of Lucius Barbius Mercator and Gavillia Nigella, 10 front feet and 30 field feet.
EDCS-01600404.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Lucius Barbius Mercator and Gavillia Nigella.

EDCS-01600405.translation: Barbia Maxuma, daughter of Mani, made this while alive for herself, and for Gaius Barbins Niger, son of Lucius, and for Gaius Barbins Tertius, son of Caius.
EDCS-01600405.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Barbia Maxuma for herself and relatives.

EDCS-01600407.translation: A plot was given to Quintus Blassius Agathopus and his wife Manlia Fusca, and to their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, by Gaius Clodius Ilironius.
EDCS-01600407.summary: This inscription records the granting of burial space by Gaius Clodius Ilironius to Quintus Blassius Agathopus, his wife, and their descendants.

EDCS-01600408.translation: The monument occupies the property of Lucius Brussius Baianus [---].
EDCS-01600408.summary: This inscription records the ownership or dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Lucius Brussius Baianus.

EDCS-01600409.translation: Gaius Burredius Grapo, freedman of Gaius; Burredia Parra, freedwoman of Gaius; Gaius Burredius Bursa, freedman of Gaius; Burredia Fausta, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-01600409.summary: This inscription lists four individuals, likely family members, who are freedmen and freedwomen of Gaius Burredius.

EDCS-01600410.translation: Caemia Eyphrosyne placed this while alive for herself.
EDCS-01600410.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Caemia Eyphrosyne for herself.

EDCS-01600411.summary: This is a tombstone for Caesernia Epinis.

EDCS-01600413.translation: Sextus Philargurus, freedman of Sextus, made this for himself and his freedmen while alive. The monument occupies 16 front feet and 33 field feet.
EDCS-01600413.summary: This is a funerary monument self-dedicated by Sextus Philargurus, a freedman, for himself and his own freedmen, also specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-01600414.translation: Publius Flavius Successus for his well-deserving wife, Caesernia Hypatia, freedwoman.
EDCS-01600414.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Publius Flavius Successus for his wife, Caesernia Hypatia.

EDCS-01600415.translation: The property of Quintus Caesilius Bathyllus, 20 front feet and 72 field feet.
EDCS-01600415.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property belonging to Quintus Caesilius Bathyllus.

EDCS-01600416.translation: The freedwoman of Quintus, Cinnamis, placed the bones of her beloved Dindiae Lauridi, aged 24, here.
EDCS-01600416.summary: This inscription records the burial of Dindiae Lauridi, aged 24, by her freedwoman Cinnamis.

EDCS-01600417.translation: The monument occupies the property of Lucius Caestranius Primigenius, 20 front feet and 50 field feet.
EDCS-01600417.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Lucius Caestranius Primigenius.

EDCS-01600418.translation: Sextus Caesernius made this for his brothers Sexto Caesernio Communi, Titus Pomponius Gemellus Caeserninus, and his sister Caestrania Rustica, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-01600418.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Sextus Caesernius for his siblings.

EDCS-01600419.translation: Caetronia Saturnina made this, while alive, for herself and Tullia A[--].
EDCS-01600419.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Caetronia Saturnina for herself and another individual, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600420.translation: Marcus, son of Gaius, son of Marcus, [in width?] 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01600420.summary: This inscription likely marks the boundaries of a plot of land belonging to Marcus, son of Gaius.

EDCS-01600421.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caldinia Heliopolitana, while alive, made this for herself, and for Caldinia Egnoidi and Castra Profutura, for her dearest son Aelius Floridus, for her most faithful husband Aelius Floridus, and for her son-in-law Valerius Competalus, and for Prima Artemisia, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. The monument measures 90 feet in front and 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600421.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for multiple family members, including Caldinia Heliopolitana, her husband, son, daughter-in-law, and others, with details about the size of the burial plot, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600422.translation: Cale, aged 4 years and 11 months. Gaius Valerius Agathonicus for his dearest adopted daughter.
EDCS-01600422.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Cale, set up by Gaius Valerius Agathonicus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600423.translation: Gaius Callidius Priscianus for his parents, Gaius Callidius Hermetus and Annaea Priscina, and for his freedwoman Callidia Ursula. The monument measures 70 feet in front.
EDCS-01600423.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Callidius Priscianus for his parents and his freedwoman, including the dimensions of the burial plot, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600424.translation: To Canidiae Marcellinae, his grandmother, Aelius Constans [has set this up] in the 21st year of his life.
EDCS-01600424.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Aelius Constans to his grandmother Canidiae Marcellinae.

EDCS-01600425.translation: Lucius Cantius Verus, most dutiful son, made this for his father Lucius Cantius, while alive.
EDCS-01600425.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Cantius Verus for his father, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600426.summary: This is a simple burial marker for Capella.

EDCS-01600427.translation: For Carfania Dice, most dutiful mother. Gaius Carfanius Iustus, her son, made this for her, while alive, for himself, and for Gnaeus Domitius Apollonius, and for their descendants and his own.
EDCS-01600427.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Carfanius Iustus for his mother Carfania Dice, and also for himself and Gnaeus Domitius Apollonius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600428.translation: Marcurius Crinianus made this while alive for his wife Cassia, [wife] of Titus. [He set this up?]
EDCS-01600428.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcurius Crinianus for his wife Cassia.

EDCS-01600429.translation: The plot of Quintus Cassius, 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the field, and of Lucius Rutilius Mercator.
EDCS-01600429.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Quintus Cassius and Lucius Rutilius Mercator.

EDCS-01600430.translation: Quintus Cassius Donatus, son of Quintus Cassius Philomusus, made this, while alive.
EDCS-01600430.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cassius Donatus, erected by his father, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600431.translation: The bones of Catia, freedwoman of Quintus, to Compsinis.
EDCS-01600431.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Catia, a freedwoman, likely indicating her burial place.

EDCS-01600432.translation: Tituria Tuenda, while alive, made this for her husband Quintus Cervius Treptus, freedman of Quintus, and for herself, and for Quintus Cervius Pudentus, son of Quintus, and for [her] daughter Verecunda.
EDCS-01600432.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Tituria Tuenda for her husband, herself, and her children, including a son and a daughter.

EDCS-01600433.translation: Zele, freedwoman, made this, while alive, for Gaius Cervonius Hyacinthus, freedman of Gaius, and for herself.
EDCS-01600433.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Zele for herself and for Gaius Cervonius Hyacinthus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600434.translation: To Titus Cetevius, son of Ceth.
EDCS-01600434.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary or honorary, to Titus Cetevius.

EDCS-01600435.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Chariton.
EDCS-01600435.summary: This is a funerary epitaph simply dedicating a grave to Chariton, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600436.translation: [Octavia?] for her freedman Octavius Cladus, freedman of Gnaeus, and for Octavia, freedwoman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-01600436.summary: This is a funerary inscription that appears to record a dedication by Octavia for her freedman Cladus and another freedwoman named Octavia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600437.translation: Tiberius Claudius N, while alive, made this for himself and A.
EDCS-01600437.summary: This inscription records a pre-arranged burial plot or monument made by Tiberius Claudius N for himself and another individual, A.

EDCS-01600438.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Obsequentius by Claudius Aelianus, possibly a dedication or memorial.

EDCS-01600439.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Tiberius Claudius Apollonius, while alive, made this for himself, for Claudia Apra, his patroness, and for Claudia Fusca, his freedwoman and dearest wife.
EDCS-01600439.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Tiberius Claudius Apollonius for himself, his patroness, and his freedwoman and wife.

EDCS-01600440.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely names Tiberius Claudius Aristio.

EDCS-01600441.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Tiberius Claudius Primanus, as a living man, made this for his most excellent parent Tiberius Claudius Blastus, and for his parent Menecrates' daughter Zmyrna, and for Menophilus, and for their ancestors, freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. The space for the monument in front is 20 feet, in the field 3 feet. This monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-01600441.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Tiberius Claudius Primanus for his parents and other relatives, specifying the dimensions of the plot and that it is not inheritable.

EDCS-01600442.translation: To Quintus Claudius Herclianus, Claudia Mycale [his] dearest wife.
EDCS-01600442.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, from Claudia Mycale to her husband Quintus Claudius Herclianus.

EDCS-01600443.translation: Who lived 2 years, 8 months, and days. Quintus Claudius Marcellus, the father, placed this for his dearest daughter.
EDCS-01600443.summary: This inscription commemorates a young daughter who died at a very early age, erected by her father, Quintus Claudius Marcellus.

EDCS-01600444.translation: Of Quintus Claudius Primigenius, his brother.
EDCS-01600444.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment or label, possibly related to a tomb, indicating it belongs to or refers to Quintus Claudius Primigenius, the brother of the deceased or donor.

EDCS-01600445.translation: Hercles and Hercles, son [of the deceased], made this, while alive, for Claudia Agele, wife of Pettius Hercoles, most holy and most dutiful, and for themselves.
EDCS-01600445.summary: This is a funerary monument established by Hercles and his son for Claudia Agele, the wife of Pettius Hercles, and for themselves.

EDCS-01600446.translation: For Claudia Caesaris Secunda, her husband...
EDCS-01600446.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or memorial to Claudia Caesaris Secunda by her husband.

EDCS-01600448.translation: Caius Clodius Diastus ordered to be made.
EDCS-01600448.summary: This inscription records an order by Caius Clodius Diastus for something to be made, possibly a funerary monument.

EDCS-01600449.translation: Lucius Cluvius Ingenuus, freedman of Lucius, made this for himself and his family. Rullia Galla, daughter of Spurius, [grants] 40 square feet.
EDCS-01600449.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a funerary plot by Lucius Cluvius Ingenuus and Rullia Galla.

EDCS-01600451.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Cocceius Philetus for his wife Cocceia Pompeia.
EDCS-01600451.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Cocceius Philetus for his wife Cocceia Pompeia.

EDCS-01600452.translation: To Lucius Cominius Patrobius, who lived 19 years, 7 months, and 15 days. Cominia Euhodia, his mother, [erected this] for her most devoted son.
EDCS-01600452.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Cominius Patrobius, set up by his mother.

EDCS-01600453.translation: To Lucius Cominius Minervius, aged 9. Cominia, his most devoted mother, [grants] the plot.
EDCS-01600453.summary: This funerary epitaph records the allocation of a plot for Lucius Cominius Minervius by his mother.

EDCS-01600454.translation: Gaius Julius Ma[---], son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, soldier of the 5th Praetorian cohort, for his mother Cominia [---], for his father [---]nio, for his maternal aunt Cominia Secunda, for his maternal aunt Cominia Quincta, for himself, his family, his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01600454.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier of the Praetorian Guard and his family, detailing the recipients of the memorial.

EDCS-01600455.translation: For Lucius Cornelius Epigonus, his freedman, for Plectinus and Eclectus, the beloved.
EDCS-01600455.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a freedman, Lucius Cornelius Epigonus, for his beloved freedmen or pets named Flaccus and Didymus.

EDCS-01600456.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Secundus, for his mother Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, wife of Verecunda Pullia.
EDCS-01600456.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Cornelius Secundus' mother.

EDCS-01600457.translation: Zelus, freedman, saw to the making for Cornelia, daughter of Publius, Atticilla.
EDCS-01600457.summary: This inscription records that Zelus, a freedman, arranged for the construction of a monument for Cornelia Atticilla.

EDCS-01600458.translation: To Cornelia Prima, daughter of Lucius; Marcus Cornelius Marcita; and Lucius Cornelius Noster.
EDCS-01600458.summary: This inscription names three individuals, likely members of the same family, possibly on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-01600459.translation: Gaius Cossutius, son of Marcus, and Titus, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made.
EDCS-01600459.summary: This inscription records a commission by two brothers, Gaius and Titus Cossutius, for a monument.

EDCS-01600460.translation: Space for the monument of Gnaeus Cossutius Er Otis, in front 16 feet, in the field 16 feet.
EDCS-01600460.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Gnaeus Cossutius Er Otis.

EDCS-01600461.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To the parents Cteto, Barbia Procilla, and Barbia Zmaragdis, and Epictetus, while alive, erected this.
EDCS-01600461.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to parents by their children, likely erected in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600462.translation: Lucius Curius Nepos, freedman of Lucius, and Stratonica, freedwoman of [---], mother, and Curia Napolis, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-01600462.summary: This funerary monument was erected by several individuals, likely members of a family and their freedpeople, during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600463.translation: The place of the monument for Sextus Curienus Faustus and Cassia Macrina, daughter of Spurius. In the front 26 feet, in the field 20 feet to the ditch.
EDCS-01600463.summary: This is a property boundary marker for a burial plot, indicating the dimensions and location of the monument, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600464.translation: Daphno, aged 7. Domitius Agathopus, father, made this.
EDCS-01600464.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Daphno, erected by her father, Domitius Agathopus, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600465.translation: Titus Decidius Auctus, freedman of [Titus], made this for himself and his freedmen while alive. The place of the monument: in the front 17 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600465.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription for a freedman, Titus Decidius Auctus, who prepared it for himself and his own freedpeople, indicating dimensions of the plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600466.translation: The place for Caius Decidius Rufus (?) and Caesernia Salvia. In the front [X] feet.
EDCS-01600466.summary: This is a boundary marker inscription for a burial plot, indicating the names of the owners and the frontal dimension, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600467.translation: For Caius Decidius Urbanus. In the front 32 feet, in the field 40 feet.
EDCS-01600467.summary: This is a boundary marker inscription for a burial plot belonging to Caius Decidius Urbanus, specifying the dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600468.text_edition: \n Tito Desticio Titi filio Claudia Severo primo pilo legionis X g[eminae ------\n
EDCS-01600468.translation: To Titus Desticcius Severus, son of Titus, first-rank centurion of the Legio X Gemina, [---]
EDCS-01600468.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription for a high-ranking military officer, Titus Desticcius Severus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600469.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Dindius Onesimus, freedman of Iusta, made this for himself and for his son Liberalis, and for his wife Dindia Asia, while alive. Eutychus and Atimetus, his sons, saw to its construction.
EDCS-01600469.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman, Lucius Dindius Onesimus, dedicated to himself, his son, and wife, and was commissioned by his other sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600470.translation: Diphilus. He lived without avarice. He lived until [---] came. Farewell.
EDCS-01600470.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph, possibly for a freedman named Diphilus, highlighting his virtuous life, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600471.translation: Hermes, freedman of Gnaeus Domitius, in his youth, made this for himself and for his deceased wife Domitia Hygeia and for his mother Claudia Prima.
EDCS-01600471.summary: A funerary monument erected by Hermes for himself, his wife, and his mother.

EDCS-01600472.translation: The plot and monument, donated by Gnaeus Domitius Hermes, shall not pass to an heir.
EDCS-01600472.summary: This inscription records the donation of a funerary plot and monument by Gnaeus Domitius Hermes, with a stipulation against inheritance.

EDCS-01600473.translation: To Domitia Iusta, from Gnaeus Domitius Hermes.
EDCS-01600473.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Domitia Iusta by Gnaeus Domitius Hermes.

EDCS-01600474.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Sextus Donnius Dorus, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-01600475.translation: To the shades of Helvius Firminus. Helvius Respektos for his most dutiful father.
EDCS-01600475.summary: A funerary dedication by Helvius Respektos to his father, Helvius Firminus.

EDCS-01600476.translation: Quintus Etuvius Felix, freedman of Quintus, and Cassia Nice, and Lucius Ovius Privatianus, while alive, made this for themselves and for Marcus Claudius Nicostratus and Ovia Primula, their well-deserving friends; this monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-01600476.summary: A funerary monument jointly erected by three individuals for themselves and their friends, specifying it is not inheritable.

EDCS-01600477.translation: For Euvagrius, a most sweet infant, who lived 8 years, 2 months, 20 days. Urbana, unhappy mother, had this made contrary to a vow.
EDCS-01600477.summary: A funerary epitaph for an infant named Euvagrius, erected by his grieving mother.

EDCS-01600478.summary: This inscription identifies Euhodus, a freedman of Picens, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-01600480.translation: Lucius Fabius Flaccus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-01600480.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Fabius Flaccus.

EDCS-01600481.translation: Lucius Fabius Philotimus, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Fabius Epagatus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-01600481.summary: A funerary inscription possibly for two individuals named Lucius Fabius, both freedmen.

EDCS-01600482.translation: Lucius Fadius Salvius made this while alive for his patron and himself.
EDCS-01600482.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Lucius Fadius Salvius erected a monument for his patron and himself.

EDCS-01600483.translation: Fabius, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made for Alexe and F[---].
EDCS-01600483.summary: This funerary inscription records that Fabius, son of Lucius, commissioned a monument for Alexe and another person.

EDCS-01600484.translation: For Idia Fausta. For Prisca, freedwoman of Lucius. Prepo, freedman of a woman, made this while alive. For Orinnini, wife of [---], freedwoman of a woman. For Optata, mother of [---], freedwoman of Sextus. For Phoebini, freedwoman of a woman. For Urbana, freedwoman of a woman. For Faustus [---]
EDCS-01600484.summary: A funerary monument erected by Prepo for his wife Orinnini, his mother Optata, and other relatives, with some names lost.

EDCS-01600485.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins with the name Lucius Fidiclanius.

EDCS-01600486.translation: In front 16 feet, in the field 20 feet, a private place.
EDCS-01600486.summary: An inscription recording the dimensions and location of a private burial plot.

EDCS-01600488.translation: To the shades of Flaminus Aelianus, who lived 4 years, 7 months, 4 days. Aelia Trophime, mother, for her most sweet son. Hail, Flaminus Aelianus!
EDCS-01600488.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy named Flaminus Aelianus, erected by his mother.

EDCS-01600489.translation: Flaminia, his concubine, set this up for Galerius.
EDCS-01600489.summary: This inscription records that Flaminia, the concubine of Galerius, erected a monument for him.

EDCS-01600491.translation: To Quintus Flavius Aprilis, for his most dear wife Apinia Chreste.
EDCS-01600491.summary: A funerary dedication by Quintus Flavius Aprilis to his beloved wife Apinia Chreste.

EDCS-01600492.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavius Atticus for his dearest wife Flavia Caesiae.
EDCS-01600492.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavius Atticus to his wife Flavia Caesiae.

EDCS-01600493.translation: Flavia Edonei, freedwoman of Marcus, to her son Crescentius.
EDCS-01600493.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavia Edonei to her son Crescentius.

EDCS-01600494.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavia Eutychiane for her husband Aurelius Phoenix, in token of remembrance.
EDCS-01600494.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavia Eutychiane to her husband Aurelius Phoenix.

EDCS-01600495.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Julius Melus for Flavia Sabina his wife and Sabinus his son.
EDCS-01600495.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Julius Melus for his wife Flavia Sabina and son Sabinus.

EDCS-01600497.translation: Aurelius Vincentinus for Aurelia Iuventia, his most virtuous wife, with whom he lived for 21 years, 9 months, and 11 days, without any complaint.
EDCS-01600497.summary: A funerary dedication by Aurelius Vincentinus to his wife Aurelia Iuventia, specifying the length of their marriage.

EDCS-01600498.translation: Site of the monument of Lucius Occusius Festus, freedman of Quintus Fruticius Primi, on the front 32 feet.
EDCS-01600498.summary: A property boundary marker indicating the dimensions of a burial plot owned by Lucius Occusius Festus.

EDCS-01600499.translation: Quintus Appuleius Hyginus for his mother-in-law Fufidia Malchis.
EDCS-01600499.summary: A funerary dedication by Quintus Appuleius Hyginus to his mother-in-law Fufidia Malchis.

EDCS-01600500.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Fullonia Paulla, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-01600501.translation: Site of the monument, on the front 60 feet, in the field 50 feet, of Caius Fulvius Agatho.
EDCS-01600501.summary: A property marker indicating the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Fulvius Agatho.

EDCS-01600502.summary: This inscription records the age of Fundania as 25 years.

EDCS-01600503.summary: The name Fundania Pantia, possibly a funerary dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-01600504.translation: Caius Gabius Senecio, son of Caius Gabius, for his father Caius Gabius, son of Caius.
EDCS-01600504.summary: A funerary dedication by Caius Gabius Senecio to his father Caius Gabius.

EDCS-01600505.translation: Site of the monument of Caius Galerius Hilarus: on the front 16 feet, in the field 40 feet.
EDCS-01600505.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Galerius Hilarus.

EDCS-01600506.translation: Publius Gavius, son of Publius, freedman...
EDCS-01600506.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely belonging to a tomb marker, identifying a freedman named Publius Gavius.

EDCS-01600507.translation: Quintus, son of Quintus. Cestius, son of Caius. Vibius An[---].
EDCS-01600507.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several individuals, likely related to property or inheritance.

EDCS-01600508.translation: Site of Lucius Gavius Celer, son of Lucius: 20 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01600508.summary: This inscription designates the boundaries of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Gavius Celer.

EDCS-01600509.translation: Quintus Gavius Inventus, son of Quintus, freedman, made (this) for himself and for all his freeborn and freedmen and their descendants, living: on the front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600509.summary: This is an epitaph for a tomb built by Quintus Gavius Inventus for himself and his family, including dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-01600510.translation: Site of the monument of Quintus Gavius Victor: ...
EDCS-01600510.summary: This inscription marks the location of a monument belonging to Quintus Gavius Victor, but is incomplete.

EDCS-01600511.translation: Titus Gavius Urbanus, son of Titus, freedman, made (this) for himself and for his and for the freedwoman Iadi, wife of Voltilia, and for the freedwoman Peticia Chelido, daughter of Lucius, and for the freedwoman Voltilia Paulla, daughter of Publius, and for their freedmen and freedwomen: site of the monument, 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01600511.summary: This epitaph records a tomb built by Titus Gavius Urbanus for himself, his wife, and their freedpersons, also specifying the plot size.

EDCS-01600512.translation: Gavia Arche, living, made (this) for herself and for her family, and for her brother Quintus Gavius Cerialis, son of Quintus, freedman, and for her daughter Corinthia, and for her daughter Gavia Iucunda, and for her mother Macedonius, and for her father.
EDCS-01600512.summary: This is an epitaph for Gavia Arche, who built a tomb for herself, her brother, her daughters, and her parents.

EDCS-01600513.translation: Lucius Gavillius Carpus, freedman of a woman, son of Lucius. Lucius Gavillius Philemo, freedman of Lucius, alive. Lucius Helenus, freedman of Lucius, alive. Lucius Lepidus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-01600513.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the relationship and status of several freedmen, likely belonging to the same family or household.

EDCS-01600514.translation: Gnaeus Gavillius, son of Gnaeus, son of Ganea.
EDCS-01600514.summary: This inscription records the full name and filiation of Gnaeus Gavillius.

EDCS-01600515.translation: Place of Lucius Gemini, son of Lucius, 16 square feet [---] ossa Piit.
EDCS-01600515.summary: This inscription appears to record the size of a burial plot, possibly measuring 16 square feet, with a lacuna for the verb.

EDCS-01600516.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Germanus, while alive, set this up for his deserving father Rufinianus, who lived 35 years, and Am Cu
EDCS-01600516.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Germanus for his father Rufinianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600517.translation: ...lliae / ... Glaphyre / on the front 16 feet / in the field 70 feet.
EDCS-01600517.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely marks the dimensions of a burial plot, possibly for a person named Glaphyre.

EDCS-01600518.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly an epitaph or dedication, to Quintus Graenius Eucharistos.

EDCS-01600519.translation: ...aisiaca... / of Caius, freedwoman Grata / and Helpidius, freedman / on the front 20 feet / in the field 30 feet
EDCS-01600519.summary: This fragmentary inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot and names at least two individuals, a freedwoman Grata and a freedman Helpidius.

EDCS-01600520.translation: The place of the monument of Lucius Grattius Montanus, in front 18 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600520.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Lucius Grattius Montanus.

EDCS-01600521.text_edition: \n Velina Gratus Clemens danus pater f\n
EDCS-01600521.translation: Velina Gratus Clemens, the father of Danus.
EDCS-01600521.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented dedication or statement of familial relation, possibly related to a funerary context.

EDCS-01600522.translation: The place of the monument of Publius Graxi, son of Publius Capreolus, in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600522.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Publius Graxi Capreolus.

EDCS-01600523.translation: The place of Quintus Helvius Clarus, 16 square feet.
EDCS-01600523.summary: This inscription records the area of a plot of land belonging to Quintus Helvius Clarus.

EDCS-01600524.translation: [...]. Helvius Fortunatus willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-01600524.summary: This is a votive inscription where Helvius Fortunatus fulfilled a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-01600525.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a woman named Helvia Galla, likely a tombstone or a dedication, from the Roman period.

EDCS-01600526.translation: The burial plot of Marcus Herennius Blastus, 10 feet in front
EDCS-01600526.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Marcus Herennius Blastus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600527.translation: [...]onius made this for himself and for his excellent father Hymenaeus
EDCS-01600527.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by an individual for themselves and their father, Hymenaeus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600528.translation: To Ialysos, his wife, and to Nemesis, freedwoman of Gaius Aquileius Suavius, and to Gaius Frenius Secundus Gramme
EDCS-01600528.summary: This is a dedication to multiple individuals, likely a family tomb inscription, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600529.translation: Igubia, who lived 23 years, 3 months, 15 days. Ammonius placed this living for his most beloved companion, who lived with me 4 years, 2 months.
EDCS-01600529.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Igubia, set up by her partner Ammonius, detailing her age and the duration of their relationship.

EDCS-01600530.translation: Gaius Iulius Agathopus, freedman of the freedman of the divine Augustus, made this for himself and Fusca, freedwoman, and Iulia Sperata, his wife, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01600530.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Iulius Agathopus for himself, his wife, and their freedmen, dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-01600531.translation: To Sextus Julius Antonianus, from Iulia Decia Felicissima, his most dutiful sister
EDCS-01600531.summary: This is a dedication set up by Iulia Decia Felicissima in honor of her brother Sextus Julius Antonianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600532.translation: The place of the monument of Caius Iulius Auctus, in front 32 feet, in the field 72 feet.
EDCS-01600532.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Caius Iulius Auctus.

EDCS-01600533.translation: To the departed spirits. Sextus Iulius Hamillus made [...] in front.
EDCS-01600533.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription dedicated to Sextus Iulius Hamillus.

EDCS-01600534.translation: For Iulia Amanda, freedwoman of Gaius Julius, daughter of Gaius Julius Hilarion, his fellow freedman. For Secundus, freedman. For Iulia Cinura, freedwoman, daughter of Aucta, aged 35.
EDCS-01600534.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, possibly a funerary monument or a record of familial and social connections, including freedmen and their relations.

EDCS-01600536.translation: Space of the monument of Decimus Julius Venustus, 16 feet.
EDCS-01600536.summary: This inscription marks the funerary plot of Decimus Julius Venustus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600537.translation: Of [name] of 23 years. Julius Verecundus, father.
EDCS-01600537.summary: This inscription likely records the death of a young person, identified as the child of Julius Verecundus.

EDCS-01600538.translation: Space in all directions, 16 feet, of Gaius Julius Vitulus.
EDCS-01600538.summary: This inscription marks the funerary plot of Gaius Julius Vitulus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600539.translation: Iulia Agape erected this eternal home for her obedient husband
EDCS-01600539.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Iulia Agape for her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600540.translation: Iulia Barachus made this for herself while alive
EDCS-01600540.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Iulia Barachus provided for her own burial plot during her lifetime, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600541.translation: To the departed spirits of [name] and Julia Donata.
EDCS-01600541.summary: This is a funerary dedication to at least two individuals, one of whom is partially restored and the other is Julia Donata.

EDCS-01600542.translation: To Aria, most beloved, from Allius Iulianus [TAVCIE]
EDCS-01600542.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aria by Allius Iulianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600543.translation: Lucius Iunius Primus, son of Lucius Iunius, set this up while alive for his father Voseius, his mother, and his wife Soleia, daughter of Titus, and for all his own family. The plot is 16.5 feet in front and 50 feet in the field
EDCS-01600543.summary: This is a funerary monument self-funded by Lucius Iunius Primus for his family, including specific dimensions for the plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600544.translation: Space of the monument of Aulus Junius Charito, 57 feet in front, 60 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600544.summary: This inscription marks the funerary plot of Aulus Junius Charito, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600545.translation: Gaius Iumius Fabius made this in his lifetime for himself and his wife Vibbia Secunda.
EDCS-01600545.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Gaius Iumius Fabius for himself and his wife, likely of the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600546.translation: Lucius Iustius Senilis, father, [erected this] for Lucius Iustius Ponticus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-01600546.summary: A funerary monument erected by a father for his son, possibly from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01600547.translation: Space of the monument of Iuventia, freedwoman of Sextus, Flora, 16 feet in front, 20 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600547.summary: This inscription marks the funerary plot of Iuventia, freedwoman of Sextus, also known as Flora, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600548.translation: To Titus Kanius Monimianus, son of Titus, aged 28 years. Kania Laeta, most dutiful mother.
EDCS-01600548.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Kania Laeta for her son Titus Kanius Monimianus, who died at age 28.

EDCS-01600549.translation: Titus Caunius Priscus, son, and Caunia Ianuaria, daughter, [made this] for their most devoted parents, Titus Caunius Melior, freedman of Titus, and Restituta, freedwoman of Titus, and for their most excellent friend Titus Caunius Cupito, fellow freedman, and Titus Caunius Quernio, fellow freedman.
EDCS-01600549.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by children for their deceased parents and friends, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600550.translation: [text illegible] made for himself and his family: for Lucius Licinius Placidus, son, aged 18 years; for Licinia Tychis, his mother; for Magia Repentina, a slave woman, aged 16 years. Space of the monument, 22 feet in front, 60 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600550.summary: This inscription marks a funerary plot and lists several individuals for whom it was intended, including a father, his son, his mother, and a slave woman.

EDCS-01600551.translation: Numisia Antonina for her most beloved husband Marcus Licinius Trophimus.
EDCS-01600551.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife for her husband, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600552.translation: Licinia for her husband Publius Aelius Licinius, with whom she lived.
EDCS-01600552.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife for her husband, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600553.translation: Aulus Livius Gem and Iulia Iusta, most unhappy parents, [erected this for] Aulus Livius Iustus, aged 1 year and 3 months.
EDCS-01600553.summary: A funerary monument erected by grieving parents for their infant son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600554.translation: Space of the monument of Marcus Livius Maritimus, 16 feet in front, 26 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600554.summary: This inscription marks the funerary plot of Marcus Livius Maritimus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600555.translation: To the departed spirits of Laurentia Iucunda, [name illegible].
EDCS-01600555.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Laurentia Iucunda and at least one other individual whose name is lost.

EDCS-01600556.translation: Lucius Lucilius, son of Caius, priest(?) quaestor(?).
EDCS-01600556.summary: This is a funerary inscription or epitaph for Lucius Lucilius, identifying his name and possible offices.

EDCS-01600557.translation: The place of the monument of Quintus Lucilius Florus and Caius Tettidius Primus, 21 feet in front and 22 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600557.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot allocated to Quintus Lucilius Florus and Caius Tettidius Primus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600558.translation: To Publius Lucretius Eutactus, Theotimus, son of Niiane, Cyrus, his assistant, remembering [who gave] half [the plot].
EDCS-01600558.summary: This is a dedication for a burial plot, potentially part of a larger funerary monument, given by Theotimus (son of Niiane) and Cyrus to Publius Lucretius Eutactus.

EDCS-01600559.summary: A funerary monument or dedication for Gaius Lucretius Exoratus, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600560.translation: Gaius Lucretius Firmus, son of Gaius Lucretius Paramon, made this in his lifetime for himself and his brothers Marcus Lucretius Paramon, Gaius Lucretius Philippus, Quintus Lucretius Paramon, his sister Lucretia Severa, his uncle Gaius Lucretius Firmus, Mummia ProVinciana, Gaius Vibius Provincialus, and Vergina Iucunda.
EDCS-01600560.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Gaius Lucretius Firmus for himself and numerous relatives and associates, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-01600561.translation: Gaius Lucretius Isidorus, freedman of Gaius, and Lucretia Surisca, freedwoman of Gaius, [erected this] in their lifetime.
EDCS-01600561.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by a freedman and freedwoman for themselves, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600562.translation: Gaius Lucretius Surus, freedman of Gaius, and Vergilia Nice, freedwoman of Gaius, for themselves and their husband, while alive, [erected this].
EDCS-01600562.summary: This funerary inscription records the allocation of a burial plot by Gaius Lucretius Surus and Vergilia Nice for themselves and their spouse.

EDCS-01600564.translation: Lucius Titius Caristus, fellow freedman, and for himself, in his lifetime, [erected this] to the Divine Manes of Lucretia Verissima.
EDCS-01600564.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Lucius Titius Caristus for his deceased fellow freedwoman and for himself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600565.translation: Place, 26 square feet in all directions, of Luculus.
EDCS-01600565.summary: This inscription denotes a burial plot measuring 26 square feet belonging to someone named Luculus.

EDCS-01600566.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Lydē.

EDCS-01600567.translation: Place, 16 feet in front and 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600567.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot with dimensions of 16 feet in the front and 40 feet in the field, likely associated with the name Macri.

EDCS-01600568.translation: Publius Magius Notus, freedman of the woman Publius, daughter of Publius; Statius, freedman of Publius Minius, son of Publius, for themselves and their relatives, freedmen and freedwomen, a place of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01600568.summary: This inscription allocates a burial plot of 16 square feet to several individuals and their extended families, including freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-01600569.translation: The place of the monument of Magia Iliadis, 55 feet in front, 45 feet in the field, 60 feet at the rear, for freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01600569.summary: This inscription marks the location of a monument for Magia Iliadis and designates space for her freedmen and freedwomen, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-01600570.translation: Marcus Mammius Niger, son of Marcus, and Gaius Chilo, son of Marcus, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-01600570.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Mammius Niger and Gaius Chilo, indicating they erected the monument for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-01600571.translation: To Gaius Manlius Restutus, from his dearest sons, to their most dutiful father.
EDCS-01600571.summary: This is a funerary dedication from sons to their father, Gaius Manlius Restutus.

EDCS-01600572.translation: To Gaius Marius, son of Lucius, to his father; to Aletia, freedwoman of Seius, his mother; to Prima, sister, daughter of Maria and Caius; to Secunda, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-01600572.summary: This funerary inscription records the familial relationships of Gaius Marius, Aletia, Prima, and Secunda.

EDCS-01600573.translation: Of Titus Marcius Atticus, 16 feet in front and 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600573.summary: This inscription indicates the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Titus Marcius Atticus.

EDCS-01600574.translation: Martha, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive for herself, and for Tio Polla, and their freedmen and freedwomen. Frontitius [dedicated it to] Untigonus.
EDCS-01600574.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by the freedwoman Martha for herself and others, with a dedication possibly to Untigonus by Frontitius.

EDCS-01600575.translation: To Mascellonia, freedwoman of Apra, most rare; Marcus Mascellionius Belliger, patron, [dedicated this].
EDCS-01600575.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a patron to his deceased freedwoman, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600576.translation: Menander, freedman of Gaius Ummidius Quadratus, is buried here.
EDCS-01600576.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Menander, a freedman of Gaius Ummidius Quadratus, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600577.translation: To Secunda, daughter of Caius, his concubine; to Marcus Messius Niger, son of Marcus; to Paulla, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-01600577.summary: This inscription records dedications to Secunda, Marcus Messius Niger, and Paulla.

EDCS-01600578.translation: Mestria, freedwoman of Mulieris, and Per[---], and Marcus Vipsanius [---], and Gaius Eiuleius Eu[---] Hellas S[---]
EDCS-01600578.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription possibly recording multiple individuals, including freedwomen and men, with incomplete names and relationships, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600579.translation: The burial place for Lucius Mevius Primus, son of Lucius, of the Stellatina tribe, for himself and his family.
EDCS-01600579.summary: This is a funerary land grant inscription specifying the dimensions of a burial plot for Lucius Mevius Primus and his family, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600580.translation: Gaius Minatius Africanus, son of Gaius, and Marcus Minatius, son of Gaius, made [this].
EDCS-01600580.summary: This is an inscription recording the construction of a monument by two brothers, Gaius Minatius Africanus and Marcus Minatius, sons of Gaius, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-01600581.translation: The burial place [for] Minicia Leucinis, daughter of Lucius (?), [---] and Lucius P() Sti[---], [---] and Lucius P() At[---], in front [---]
EDCS-01600581.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording a burial plot for Minicia Leucinis and other individuals, with incomplete dimensions and names, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600582.translation: To Minicia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, aged fifteen. Aemilia Procula, daughter of Titus, her mother, made [this].
EDCS-01600582.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Minicia Secunda, a fifteen-year-old girl, dedicated by her mother Aemilia Procula, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600583.translation: To Modestus, of the Princeps, of Tiberius Caesar.
EDCS-01600583.summary: This is a dedication to Modestus, an individual associated with Tiberius Caesar, possibly a personal attendant or official, dating to the reign of Tiberius (14-37 CE).

EDCS-01600584.translation: The bones of Corinthus, freedman of Titus Mollicius, son of Titus.
EDCS-01600584.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying the remains of Corinthus, freedman of Titus Mollicius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600585.translation: Monument (?) for Vedia [---], Theodota, daughter of Vedi Lucilius, front XX, land L.
EDCS-01600585.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription that likely records a burial monument for Vedia and Theodota, with specified dimensions for the plot, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600586.translation: To Monianis Hygia, her most dutiful mother, Monianis Fortunata erected this while alive.
EDCS-01600586.summary: A dedication by a daughter to her mother, likely from a tomb monument, with the dedicant's name possibly linked to the mother's.

EDCS-01600587.translation: Publius Mulvius, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe, [erected this] to Atilia Secunda, daughter of Quintus; to Lucius Mulvius Primus, son of Lucius; to Statio Mulvius Stabilion, son of Publius; to Gaius Mulvius, brother of Publius; for himself and his family.
EDCS-01600587.summary: A family funerary monument commemorating multiple individuals, including the dedicator, his brother, and other relatives, with a tribal affiliation indicated.

EDCS-01600588.summary: An incomplete inscription that likely records a name, possibly of foreign origin, with the beginning of a stone or monument mentioned.

EDCS-01600589.translation: Burial place of the Mutillii, of Theodorus and Damion, 20 feet in front, 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600589.summary: A property marker for a burial plot, indicating dimensions of land allocated for a tomb, likely of the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600591.translation: Burial place of the slave of Naevius Eutychides, in all directions 16 feet.
EDCS-01600591.summary: A boundary marker for a burial plot belonging to a slave, specifying the dimensions of the area.

EDCS-01600592.translation: Nereis, thirteen years old, is buried here.
EDCS-01600592.summary: This is a tombstone marking the burial place of Nereis, who died at the age of thirteen.

EDCS-01600593.translation: Nomonicus, freedman of Nereus, and Ingenuus, son of Titus.
EDCS-01600593.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Nomonicus and Ingenuus, possibly related to a burial.

EDCS-01600594.translation: Lucius Neriatius, son of Publius, of the Lemonia tribe, 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01600594.summary: A property marker, likely for a tomb, belonging to Lucius Neriatius, indicating the dimensions of his plot and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-01600595.translation: Gaius Nevissatius Sabinus made this while alive for himself, and for Geminia Paulina, his wife, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-01600595.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Nevissatius Sabinus for himself, his wife, and their descendants and freedpersons.

EDCS-01600596.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Nicolaia and Prototyche.

EDCS-01600598.translation: To Nymphio, son, aged 3 years. Nymphodotus, slave of the freedman of the divine Augustus.
EDCS-01600598.summary: A tomb inscription for a young child, dedicated by a slave who was formerly owned by an imperial freedman.

EDCS-01600599.translation: Gaius Octavius Diophantus, freedman of Caius, [served as a] sexvir.
EDCS-01600599.summary: This inscription records the name and position of Gaius Octavius Diophantus, a freedman who served as a sexvir.

EDCS-01600600.translation: Burial place of the family of Gnaeus Octavius Rufus, 32 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01600600.summary: A boundary marker for a family tomb belonging to Gnaeus Octavius Rufus, specifying the area's dimensions.

EDCS-01600601.translation: The memorial plot of Octavia Pelagia and Lucius Octavius Callistus; in front 32 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600601.summary: This is a property boundary marker for the burial plot of Octavia Pelagia and Lucius Octavius Callistus.

EDCS-01600602.translation: Octavia Procina, freedwoman of Gaius, ordered [this] to be made by the arrangement of Cupita, beloved [companion] of Melaena, beloved [companion] of Gaius Octavius Helenus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-01600602.summary: A funerary commission for several individuals, including freedwomen and beloved companions, orchestrated by another freedwoman.

EDCS-01600603.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Onesimus Iustus, my most unfortunate grandson, who lived for 3 years, 4 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-01600603.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a grandson named Onesimus Iustus.

EDCS-01600604.translation: Selicia Optata, freedwoman of Quintus, [and Quintus] Selicius Liccaeus, freedman of Quintus, [and Quintus] Selicius Malchio, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-01600604.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for members of the Selicia family, including freedmen, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600605.translation: For the deceased slaves of Pactumeius Iucundus: Natalis, aged 21, and Proculus, aged 15.
EDCS-01600605.summary: This inscription lists two deceased slaves, Natalis and Proculus, belonging to Pactumeius Iucundus.

EDCS-01600606.translation: Ground of the monument of Maximi and Kaninia Ianuaria. In the front, 16 feet; in the field, 45 feet.
EDCS-01600606.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land intended for a monument, belonging to Maximi and Kaninia Ianuaria, probably from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600607.translation: Ground of Persias Meroes. [In the front] 10 feet.
EDCS-01600607.summary: This is a boundary marker indicating the size of a plot of land belonging to Persias Meroes, with measurements for the front portion.

EDCS-01600608.translation: Peticia Doris, freedwoman of Lucius, made [this] for herself while alive and for her son Doro, who is buried here, aged 5 years.
EDCS-01600608.summary: This epitaph records that Peticia Doris, a freedwoman, dedicated a tomb for herself and her young son Doro.

EDCS-01600609.translation: To Cerialis, freedman of Petilius Tiro. From Petilia Cybele, fellow freedwoman and partner.
EDCS-01600609.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a freedwoman, Petilia Cybele, to her deceased partner, Cerialis.

EDCS-01600610.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lusidiena Pieris made [this] for her most dutiful daughter Petilia Iusta, aged 17 years, 3 months, and 10 days, and also for her son Titus Lusidienus Secundus, aged 21 years.
EDCS-01600610.summary: This funerary dedication was set up by a mother, Lusidiena Pieris, for her deceased daughter and son, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600611.translation: To Marcus Petronius Epitynchanus, [my] husband, and to Marcus Petronius Agilis, [my] son, aged 7 years and 2 months. Iulia Helpis made [this] for them and for herself while alive.
EDCS-01600611.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Iulia Helpis for her deceased husband and young son, and also for herself.

EDCS-01600612.translation: Caius Petronius Hilarus, freedman of Caius. Caius Petronius Pauper, son of Caius.
EDCS-01600612.summary: This is a simple epitaph listing two individuals, likely father and son, Caius Petronius Hilarus and Caius Petronius Pauper, with the former identified as a freedman.

EDCS-01600613.translation: Plot of land of L. Petronius Institutus. In the front, 16 feet; [in the] field, 32 feet.
EDCS-01600613.summary: This inscription designates a plot of land belonging to L. Petronius Institutus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-01600614.translation: To Gaius Petronius Secundus, patron. From Dasius, freedman, Vitalis, freedman, and Sperata, freedwoman.
EDCS-01600614.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Petronius Secundus, a patron, and is set up by his freedmen and freedwoman.

EDCS-01600615.translation: To Lucius Petronius, dearest son, aged 11 months and 29 days. Petronius Vettianus and Magia Daphnis, parents, erected this.
EDCS-01600615.summary: A funerary monument set up by parents for their young son, Lucius Petronius.

EDCS-01600616.translation: To Petronia of Aquileia. From Marcus Iulius Soter, incomparable wife.
EDCS-01600616.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Marcus Iulius Soter to his wife, Petronia.

EDCS-01600617.translation: [Plot] of Philomitus Communis. The plot is 16 feet in front and 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600617.summary: This marks a plot of land belonging to Philomitus Communis, detailing its front and field dimensions.

EDCS-01600618.translation: [Erected by?] Caius Plenius Hyacinthus for Caius Plenius Fortunatus, his freedman, aged 30 years, [his] excellent freedman, and for Plenia Ursula, his sister, aged 20 years.
EDCS-01600618.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated by Caius Plenius Hyacinthus to his freedman and his sister, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600619.translation: Lucius Plotius Quadratus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and [---].
EDCS-01600619.summary: This epitaph records Lucius Plotius Quadratus, a freedman, who erected a monument for himself and possibly others.

EDCS-01600620.translation: Plotia Hippolyte made this while alive for herself.
EDCS-01600620.summary: This epitaph records Plotia Hippolyte, who erected a monument for herself.

EDCS-01600621.translation: For Procula Rufina, who lived 7 years and 7 months. Marcus Pomponius Proculus and Mutilia Rufina, to their dearest daughter.
EDCS-01600621.summary: A funerary inscription set up by parents for their young daughter, Procula Rufina.

EDCS-01600622.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely honoring Publius Popilius.

EDCS-01600623.translation: Publius Postumius Optatus, son of Publius, made this while alive for himself and for Julia Severa, dearest wife, and for Publius Postumius Ampliatus, father, and for Calvia Severa, mother, and for Postumius Severus, brother.
EDCS-01600623.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Publius Postumius Optatus for himself and his family members.

EDCS-01600624.translation: [---] to Secunda, daughter of Gaius, from the Horti; may it be permitted for Publius Postumius Priamus, freedman of Publius, and Aulus Terpolius Nico, freedman of Aulus, to be buried for themselves, their freedmen and freedwomen, with a space in front of 16 feet and a depth of 16 feet.
EDCS-01600624.summary: This funerary inscription from an unspecified location records the burial rights for Publius Postumius Priamus and Aulus Terpolius Nico, their families, and freedmen, possibly within a plot belonging to Secunda.

EDCS-01600625.translation: [---] Pothi; in front 16 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600625.summary: This inscription fragment likely records the dimensions of a burial plot associated with a person named Pothi.

EDCS-01600626.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly listing names, possibly funerary or dedicatory.

EDCS-01600627.summary: This inscription records that Protesilaus and Laodomia were the makers of the monument.

EDCS-01600630.translation: Burial place of Publicius Fidelis and Barbia Phoebadis; in front 16 feet.
EDCS-01600630.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot for Publicius Fidelis and Barbia Phoebadis.

EDCS-01600631.translation: Burial place of Gaius Pullius Blastus; in all directions 32 feet.
EDCS-01600631.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot for Gaius Pullius Blastus, with dimensions given in all directions.

EDCS-01600632.translation: Burial place of Lucius Pupius Lucullus; in front 36 feet, in the field 100 feet, facing the field 56 feet.
EDCS-01600632.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot for Lucius Pupius Lucullus, detailing its dimensions along the front, in the field, and its depth.

EDCS-01600633.text_edition: \n Caio Quinctio Cai filio Velina Certo Poblicio Marcello Minicius Noster\n
EDCS-01600633.translation: To Gaius Quinctius Certus Poblicius Marcellus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, Minicius Noster [dedicated this].
