EDCS-01600633.summary: This dedication records Minicius Noster honoring Gaius Quinctius Certus Poblicius Marcellus.

EDCS-01600634.translation: Titus Regius Niger, son of Marcus, [made this] while alive for his dearest wife Regiae Mhuccae.
EDCS-01600634.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Titus Regius Niger for his wife, dating to when he was alive.

EDCS-01600635.translation: Titus Rufellius Demetrius, freedman of Titus, and Rufellia Secunda, freedwoman of Titus, made this while alive; Titus Rufellius Acastus, freedman of Titus; Titus Rufellius Achiba, freedman of Titus; Rufellia Silenio, freedwoman of Titus; Rufellia Dotilla, freedwoman of Titus; Titus Veius Philostratus, freedman of Titus; in front 16 feet, in the field 16 feet.
EDCS-01600635.summary: This epitaph records the construction of a monument by Titus Rufellius Demetrius and Rufellia Secunda for themselves and other family members and freedmen, likely including Titus Rufellius Acastus, Titus Rufellius Achiba, Rufellia Silenio, Rufellia Dotilla, and Titus Veius Philostratus.

EDCS-01600637.translation: For Publius Rufrius Callistus, 23 years old, Publius Rufrius Hermaiscus and Rufria Saturnina, his parents, made this while alive for their most dutiful son and for themselves and their descendants.
EDCS-01600637.summary: This funerary monument was erected by parents for their son and for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-01600638.translation: Sabia Optata, freedwoman of Plaetor, made this while alive for herself and her family, and for her husband Andis, son of Gaius, and for her daughter Aufidia Lyrica, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-01600638.summary: This epitaph records Sabia Optata, a freedwoman, who erected a monument for herself, her husband Andis, and her daughter Aufidia Lyrica.

EDCS-01600639.translation: To the divine shades. Felix erected this for his most excellent and most devoted wife, Sabina.
EDCS-01600639.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600640.translation: Lucius Safinius, son of Lucius, Sabelio...
EDCS-01600640.summary: The beginning of a funerary epitaph or a dedicatory inscription, with missing text.

EDCS-01600641.translation: Salonia Ingenua, daughter of Titus, made this while alive for herself and for her freedman Titus Salonio Germano, for freedmen and freedwomen, and for Quintus Licovius Philocomus, for Licovia Teletini, for Quintus Licovius Diadumenus. The space for the monument is 16 feet in front and 20 feet in the field; this monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-01600641.summary: A funerary monument inscription detailing ownership and dimensions, including provisions for freedmen and a restriction on inheritance, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600642.translation: Posilla, daughter of Titus, while alive, made this for Marcus Salvius Rufus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-01600642.summary: This funerary inscription records Posilla dedicating a monument to her husband, Marcus Salvius Rufus, while she was alive.

EDCS-01600643.translation: For Sammio Sabinus, who lived 10 years, Sammio Cycnus placed this for his most innocent foster-son.
EDCS-01600643.summary: This inscription records Sammio Cycnus dedicating a monument to his foster-son, Sammio Sabinus.

EDCS-01600644.translation: Sardia Artemisia made this while alive for herself and for her most excellent husband, Lucius Cantio Proculus, and for her sweetest daughter, Cassia Secundina. [Text illegible]...
EDCS-01600644.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a woman for herself, her husband, and her daughter, with some damaged or illegible text, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600645.translation: Saturninus made this for his most devoted wife Lamyra, and for himself.
EDCS-01600645.summary: This funerary inscription records Saturninus dedicating a monument to his wife and himself.

EDCS-01600646.summary: This inscription records Titus Saufeius dedicating a monument to himself.

EDCS-01600647.translation: Publius Saufeius Sabda added 9 feet in front and 32 feet in the field, for himself and his family.
EDCS-01600647.summary: This inscription details land dimensions added by Publius Saufeius Sabda for himself and his family.

EDCS-01600648.translation: Space belonging to Caius Seius, son of Caius, Terti; 16 feet in front and 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600648.summary: An inscription marking the dimensions of a plot of land, possibly for a tomb or other structure, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600649.translation: Lucius Septimius Firmus, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made. Septimia Gemina, daughter of Lucius, his sister, and Blassia Paulla, his wife, made it according to the will. The space for the monument is 16 square feet.
EDCS-01600649.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a monument by a sister and wife based on a will, with specific dimensions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600650.translation: Septimius Heraclida placed this for his aunt Aurelia Panthia.
EDCS-01600650.summary: This inscription records Septimius Heraclida dedicating a monument to his aunt, Aurelia Panthia.

EDCS-01600652.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for his wife Servandus.
EDCS-01600652.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Departed) for the wife of Servandus.

EDCS-01600653.translation: Space for the monument of Marcus Servius Firminus...
EDCS-01600653.summary: The beginning of an inscription that marks a plot of land for a monument, with missing text, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600654.translation: Space belonging to Manius Servius Hilarus.
EDCS-01600654.summary: An inscription identifying a plot of land, likely for a tomb, belonging to Manius Servius Hilarus, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600655.translation: Servia Secunda made this for Manius Servius Primigenius, and for herself and her family.
EDCS-01600655.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a mother for her son and herself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600656.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caecilia Plusias, while alive, made this for herself and for Trebia Maxima, for Servia Cervola and Primitivus, her beloved ward, who died at thirteen years of age.
EDCS-01600656.summary: A funerary dedication by Caecilia Plusias for herself, her relative Trebia Maxima, and her deceased ward Servia Cervola and Primitivus.

EDCS-01600657.translation: Marcus Sexstius Chryseros, freedman of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and his family, and he granted the space.
EDCS-01600657.summary: An inscription by a freedman who established a burial space for himself and his family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600658.translation: Lucius Sextilius Crescens, freedman of Lucius, ordered this to be made by his will for his freedmen and freedwomen. Monumental space: 16 feet in front.
EDCS-01600658.summary: This inscription records a funerary commission by a freedman for his freedmen and freedwomen, also noting the dimensions of the funerary plot.

EDCS-01600659.translation: To Siphara, foster-daughter, who lived 20 years, 5 months, and 7 days. Aurelia Paula placed this.
EDCS-01600659.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Siphara, noting her age and dedicating her with the term 'alumnae', placed by Aurelia Paula.

EDCS-01600660.translation: To the departed spirits. To Soterides, fellow freedwoman. Glycer[a], most pious.
EDCS-01600660.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Soterides, a fellow freedwoman, by Glycer[a].

EDCS-01600661.translation: Lucius Publius Spedies, son of Salvius, be well.
EDCS-01600661.summary: A dedication or greeting from Lucius Publius Spedies to Salvius.

EDCS-01600662.translation: Spendon, alive, made this for himself and ado, Imphe, Myso his brother, Momo his father, Hne his mother, [for] his daughter 14. Agoge and Iunio the freedman [for his freedmen and freedwomen].
EDCS-01600662.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Spendon for himself and his family members, including his freedman.

EDCS-01600663.translation: Tertia, daughter of Statius. Publius Publi f. Statius Lucullus, Publi f. Tertius [with them]. 16 square feet.
EDCS-01600663.summary: This inscription lists several family members, likely related to a funerary monument, and specifies the area of land.

EDCS-01600664.translation: Monumental space: of Caius Statius Priscus. 16 feet in front.
EDCS-01600664.summary: This inscription denotes the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Statius Priscus.

EDCS-01600665.translation: Marcus Statius Surio and Aemilius Flaccus set this up for Aelia Suria, their dearest wife, and for their most dutiful mother.
EDCS-01600665.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Statius Surio and Aemilius Flaccus for their wife and mother, respectively.

EDCS-01600666.translation: Aurelia Chreste for Statia Chreste, her most unfortunate ward.
EDCS-01600666.summary: A funerary dedication by Aurelia Chreste for her ward Statia Chreste.

EDCS-01600667.translation: Monumental space: of Statia Lydes. 20 feet in front, 50 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600667.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Statia Lydes.

EDCS-01600668.translation: to Statia Sabina, his wife, seventeen years of age.
EDCS-01600668.summary: A funerary inscription fragment recording the name and age of Statia Sabina, wife of an unnamed man.

EDCS-01600669.translation: Monumental space: of Caius Stertinius Zosimus and Titus Varronius Mercurius [[and Varronia Mercussena]]. Mercurius and Mercussena, alive, built the wall with their own money. 20 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-01600669.summary: This inscription records a construction project, likely a funerary enclosure, financed by Caius Stertinius Zosimus and Titus Varronius Mercurius, and includes dimensions.

EDCS-01600670.translation: Stratonice lived 27 years, 8 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-01600670.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Stratonice, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-01600671.translation: Suria, freedwoman of the woman, made this while alive.
EDCS-01600671.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Suria, a freedwoman, during her lifetime.

EDCS-01600672.summary: A dedication to Caius Suro, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-01600673.translation: To the departed spirits. Epa[---]phroditus and Victor, sons, to their most dutiful mother, Surtia Tycheni, who deserved well of them.
EDCS-01600673.summary: This is a tombstone set up by sons for their deceased mother, Surtia Tycheni, indicating a familial memorial.

EDCS-01600674.translation: Lucius Tariolenus Hilarus, freedman of Lucius, (erected this) for Lucius Tariolenus Liccaeus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-01600674.summary: This funerary epitaph records a freedman, Hilarus, setting up a monument for another freedman, Liccaeus, likely a former master or fellow freedman.

EDCS-01600675.translation: Fausta, freedwoman of Lucius Tariolenus; Doris, freedwoman of Lucius Tariolenus; Lucius Tariolenus Princeps; Appulleia N[---
EDCS-01600675.summary: A funerary or ownership inscription listing several individuals connected to the gens Tariolena and Appulleia.

EDCS-01600677.translation: Site of the monument of Caius Terentius Aoedimus. In front sixteen feet, in the field [three] feet.
EDCS-01600677.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Terentius Aoedimus, indicating the allocated space for his monument.

EDCS-01600678.translation: The burial place of Marcus Terentius Lalus, freedman of Publius Municius Hierax.
EDCS-01600678.summary: A funerary inscription identifying a burial plot belonging to Marcus Terentius Lalus, freedman of Publius Municius Hierax.

EDCS-01600679.translation: Terentius Nico set this up for his most sweet wife, Clara Sabiniana.
EDCS-01600679.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Terentius Nico to his wife, Clara Sabiniana.

EDCS-01600680.translation: To the departed spirits. For Aulus Terentius Paccianus, who lived sixteen years and thirty-five days. Terentia Statia to her dearest son. Terentia Statia to her most dutiful sister.
EDCS-01600680.summary: This is a tombstone for a young boy, Aulus Terentius Paccianus, set up by his mother and possibly his sister, indicating a tragic early death.

EDCS-01600681.translation: To Terentia Maxima, daughter of Tettius, and to [her] mother-in-law, Luscia Clementia.
EDCS-01600681.summary: A funerary dedication to Terentia Maxima and her mother-in-law Luscia Clementia.

EDCS-01600682.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tertia, wife, and Primigenia, daughter, aged twenty-four years. Crescentius, father, for the well-deserving.
EDCS-01600682.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by a father, Crescentius, to his deceased wife, Tertia, and daughter, Primigenia, highlighting a familial loss.

EDCS-01600683.summary: This is a simple ossuary inscription for Tertia Cania, indicating the relocation or consolidation of her remains.

EDCS-01600684.translation: Tertulla made this for her husband, and for Rufus, her father, Tertia, her mother, Ephebus, her freedman, Lasciva, her freedwoman, the beloved Phoebus, the beloved Naida, aged 18.
EDCS-01600684.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Tertulla to her husband, parents, freedmen, and beloved slaves, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600686.translation: Lucius Tettienus. Lucius Tettienus who lived for...
EDCS-01600686.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription for Lucius Tettienus, recording his name and the beginning of his lifespan.

EDCS-01600687.translation: To Thallo, from his fellow slave Caius, from his own means.
EDCS-01600687.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a fellow slave, Caius, for Thallo.

EDCS-01600688.translation: To the departed spirits. Threptus, sixteen years.
EDCS-01600688.summary: This is a tombstone for a young individual named Threptus, who died at the age of sixteen.

EDCS-01600689.translation: Lucius Titius Graptus, freedman of Lucius, and Barba Paulina, being alive, made (this) for themselves and for their cherished son Primitivus, aged seven years, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, Daphnus and Graphice. Site of the monument: in front sixteen feet, in the field twenty feet. This monument shall not follow the heir.
EDCS-01600689.summary: This is a tombstone and burial plot marker created by a living couple, Lucius Titius Graptus and Barba Paulina, for themselves, their son, and their freed dependents, with a clause preventing its alienation.

EDCS-01600690.translation: Site of Marcus Titius Laetus. In front twenty feet, in the field thirty feet.
EDCS-01600690.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot allocated to Marcus Titius Laetus.

EDCS-01600691.translation: Titus Titius, son of Titus, ordered this to be made.
EDCS-01600691.summary: This inscription records the commission of a monument by Titus Titius.

EDCS-01600692.translation: For Lucius Titius Pudentus and Asellia Glycera.
EDCS-01600692.summary: This is a dedication for Lucius Titius Pudentus and Asellia Glycera, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-01600693.translation: The site of the monument of Titia Lales: in front 122 feet, in the field 60 feet.
EDCS-01600693.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot or monument for Titia Lales.

EDCS-01600694.translation: For Caius Titurnius Senecio, freedman of Caius. Iucundus, freedman, being alive, made (this) and for himself, and for Pyllis, fellow freedwoman, and for Restitutus, son, aged four years, and for Quadratus, fellow freedman, and for Crescentius, fellow freedman, and for freedmen and freedwomen. Site of the monument: in front twenty and a half feet, in the field thirty-two feet.
EDCS-01600694.summary: This is a tombstone and burial plot marker created by a living freedman, Iucundus, for himself, his fellow freedpersons, his young son, and other freed dependents, detailing the plot dimensions.

EDCS-01600695.translation: Marcus Trebius Victor [dedicated this] to his incomparable wife Variana of Vescantia, who lived with me for 2 years, 11 months, 5 days.
EDCS-01600695.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Trebius Victor for his wife Variana, recording their married life together.

EDCS-01600696.translation: Trebia Fortunata made [this for] Aphrodisius, her beloved, aged 6.
EDCS-01600696.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Aphrodisius, set up by Trebia Fortunata, likely his mother or guardian.

EDCS-01600697.translation: Grata Plotia, freedwoman of Gnaeus, made [this] for her father, Lucius Treblanus Acastus, freedman of Lucius. The plot is 20 feet across the front and 20 feet deep.
EDCS-01600697.summary: This is a funerary monument for Lucius Treblanus Acastus, erected by his freedwoman and daughter, Grata Plotia.

EDCS-01600698.translation: Caius Trosius Asbestus, freedman of Trosia, [made this] for his wife Trosia Nymphinis, and for his son Flaccus, aged 22. The plot is 17 feet across the front and 32 feet deep.
EDCS-01600698.summary: This is a funerary monument for Trosia Nymphinis and her son Flaccus, erected by her husband and their father, Caius Trosius Asbestus.

EDCS-01600699.translation: A plot for Marcus Trosius Celadus, for himself and his family. 20 feet across the front and 32 feet deep.
EDCS-01600699.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot measuring 20 feet by 32 feet, intended for Marcus Trosius Celadus and his relatives.

EDCS-01600700.translation: To the divine shades of Trosia.
EDCS-01600700.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Trosia, invoking the 'Dis Manibus' (shades of the departed).

EDCS-01600702.translation: A plot for Gnaeus Tullius Lepidus, freedman of Gnaeus, 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01600702.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot of 16 Roman feet on each side for Gnaeus Tullius Lepidus, freedman of Gnaeus.

EDCS-01600703.translation: Tullius Orpheus placed [this] for his most worthy friend, Cyrius, a colleague, and [his wife?].
EDCS-01600703.summary: This inscription records that Tullius Orpheus erected a monument for his esteemed friend and colleague, Cyrius, and possibly Cyrius's wife.

EDCS-01600705.translation: A burial plot for Lucius Turpilius Abascantus. 16 feet across the front and 20 feet deep.
EDCS-01600705.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot measuring 16 feet by 20 feet for Lucius Turpilius Abascantus.

EDCS-01600706.translation: The site of Lucius Turpilius Cilo: in front 15 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-01600706.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot or monument belonging to Lucius Turpilius Cilo.

EDCS-01600707.translation: To the divine shades of Tutilia Medama, wife of Alexandrinus.
EDCS-01600707.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Tutilia Medama, the wife of Alexandrinus, invoking the 'Dis Manibus' (shades of the departed).

EDCS-01600709.translation: Vabia Logas, freedwoman of Lucius, made this tomb for herself while alive, and for her sister Naida, freedwoman of Lucius, and for their son Gaius Aspianus Scarus Primigenius, aged 12.
EDCS-01600709.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vabia Logas, her sister, and her son, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01600710.translation: Vaccia Prima, freedwoman of Publius, ordered this to be made for Vaccia Silenionis, freedwoman of Vaccia, under the supervision of Lucius Laberius, son of Titus, and Titus Laberius, son of Titus.
EDCS-01600710.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Vaccia Prima for Vaccia Silenionis, with the work overseen by two individuals named Lucius Laberius and Titus Laberius.

EDCS-01600711.translation: For Lucius Valerius Chresimus, aged 5 [?]. Valeria I[...]
EDCS-01600711.summary: This is a partial funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Chresimus, who died at the age of 5, with a portion for Valeria I...

EDCS-01600712.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely referring to a man named Valerius Metus, son of Verus, possibly a tombstone or a dedication, date uncertain.

EDCS-01600713.translation: The space of the monument of Lucius Valerius Secundus, thirty feet in front.
EDCS-01600713.summary: This inscription defines the funerary plot size for Lucius Valerius Secundus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01600714.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Valerius Turnius is buried here.
EDCS-01600714.summary: This is a standard funerary epitaph for Valerius Turnius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600715.translation: Sextus Valerius Valerianus made [this] while alive for himself, and for Valeria Secunda, daughter of Sextus, his mother and patroness, and for his wife Cossutia I...?ieni, most excellent, and for his closest friends, Caius Cornelius Aviticianus, Cornelia Fortunata, and Caius Urvinus Abascantus, and [...]ius Clarus [...]
EDCS-01600715.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Sextus Valerius Valerianus for himself, his mother Valeria Secunda, his wife Cossutia ?, and several friends, including Cornelius Aviticianus and Urvinus Abascantus.

EDCS-01600716.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Valeria Messilles, who lived 30 years and 56 days, and Iulius Gorgonius, who lived with me 18 years and 56 days, for his most faithful wife.
EDCS-01600716.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Messilles, set up by her husband Iulius Gorgonius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600717.translation: To Gaius Varenus Privatus, aged 24. From Clodia Moschis, his most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-01600717.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young man named Gaius Varenus Privatus, set up by his daughter.

EDCS-01600718.translation: For Varia Calena and Gaius Arcius Titychus.
EDCS-01600718.summary: This is a dedication or a funerary marker for two individuals, Varia Calena and Gaius Arcius Titychus.

EDCS-01600719.translation: Varia Callituche made this for Lucius Titius Semno, her tent-mate, and for Quintus Caelius Pyramus, her son, while alive.
EDCS-01600719.summary: This funerary epitaph records Varia Callituche's dedication to her partner and son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600720.translation: Publius Veiedius, son of Caius; Gaius Postumius, son of Caius; Marcus Allius, son of Publius; Lucius Capenius, son of Lucius; Quintus Geminius, son of Publius; quaestors.
EDCS-01600720.summary: This inscription lists the names and parentage of five individuals who held the office of quaestor, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600721.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or epitaph, with the name Venantius, date uncertain.

EDCS-01600722.translation: Gaius Venonius Repertius, freedman, the wealthy one, and Petronia Adaucta placed this while alive for themselves, and for Histro, a freedman, and their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-01600722.summary: This funerary monument inscription records Gaius Venonius Repertius and Petronia Adaucta establishing a burial plot for themselves and their dependents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600723.translation: Here alone, Murus succeeds his heirs from his own property. Venucius Severinus.
EDCS-01600723.summary: This inscription appears to be a legal or property record related to inheritance or succession, involving Murus and Venucius Severinus, date uncertain.

EDCS-01600724.translation: To Vergilia, freedwoman of Gaius, and Iunius Primus, son of Lucius, his father. To Aelia(?) ..., mother. To Procula, daughter of Lucius. To his sister, alive. Iunius Maxumus, son of Lucius, made (this) alive for himself and all his family.
EDCS-01600724.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Iunius Maxumus for his father, mother, and sister, as well as for himself and his household.

EDCS-01600725.translation: [... Vettius, son of Lucius, ...] of them, [...] and their freedmen. [...] plot of monument, 25 feet [...].
EDCS-01600725.summary: This fragment seems to indicate a funerary plot, possibly for Vettius and his freedmen, with measurements for the monument's area.

EDCS-01600726.translation: Lucius Vettius Acastus, freedman of Lucius. Tullia Secunda, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-01600726.summary: This inscription records the names of Lucius Vettius Acastus and Tullia Secunda, likely a married couple or related individuals.

EDCS-01600727.translation: To Vettia Sabina, freedwoman of Lucius, aged 26, Caius Titurnius Verus set this up for his mother.
EDCS-01600727.summary: A funerary monument set up by Caius Titurnius Verus for his freedwoman mother, Vettia Sabina.

EDCS-01600728.translation: Vettia Saluta, freedwoman of Sextus. Sextus Vettius Astragalus and Sextus Vettius Dama made (this) alive for their patroness, Vettia Prima, freedwoman of the woman. Vettia Sophe, freedwoman of the woman. Vettia Aucta, freedwoman of the woman. Vettia Polis, freedwoman of the woman. For their freedmen and freedwomen. Plot of monument: in front 25 feet, in depth 32 feet.
EDCS-01600728.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Sextus Vettius Astragalus and Sextus Vettius Dama for their patroness Vettia Prima and other freedwomen, including themselves and their freedmen.

EDCS-01600729.translation: To Aulus Vectiarius Martialis, his best friend, Lucius Epidius Diadumenus Statianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-01600729.summary: A dedication by Lucius Epidius Diadumenus Statianus to his friend Aulus Vectiarius Martialis.

EDCS-01600730.translation: Iucundus, Quintus Licovius, Caius Vettienus Tyrannus, Publius Valerius Celer, Cupitus, Auli Caeserni, Acastus, Pudens, son of Quinti Licovi Albani.
EDCS-01600730.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, possibly patrons and clients or members of a collegium.

EDCS-01600734.translation: Marcus Vibius Stativus, son of Marcus, made (this) alive for himself and his family, and for Caesilia [...].
EDCS-01600734.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Vibius Stativus for himself, his family, and Caesilia.

EDCS-01600735.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Vibius Anatus, his incomparable wife, Alexander, son of Titus, set this up.
EDCS-01600735.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Alexander for his wife Vibia Anatus.

EDCS-01600736.translation: To Vibia Aquilinia, his best mother, Terentia Vibiana, daughter of Titus, made this while alive, and for herself.
EDCS-01600736.summary: A funerary monument set up by Terentia Vibiana for her mother Vibia Aquilinia, also intended for herself.

EDCS-01600737.translation: To Viburia, freedwoman of Lucius, named Cecrop, aged [---].
EDCS-01600737.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for Viburia, a freedwoman, with her age partially preserved.

EDCS-01600738.translation: Lucius Vinisius Alexander, freedman of Titus Lucius, made (this) alive for himself and his family, and for Vinisia Prima, freedwoman of Titus Lucius, and for his beloved freedwoman Iulia Methe, daughter of Gaius, and for his son, Lucius Vinusius Florus, freedman, and for his freedwoman Vinisia Corinna. Plot of monument: 20 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01600738.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Vinisius Alexander for his family, beloved freedwoman, son, and other freedpeople, specifying the plot size.

EDCS-01600739.translation: Plot of monument of Sextus Vinisius Prospectus: in front 20 1/2 feet, in depth 70 feet.
EDCS-01600739.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Sextus Vinisius Prospectus.

EDCS-01600740.translation: To Viola. Primitivos for his wife. And to Primitiva, their household slave daughter.
EDCS-01600740.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Primitivos to his wife Viola and their daughter Primitiva, who was a slave born in the household.

EDCS-01600741.translation: Visena, daughter of Lucius, the living Tertia, made this for herself and for Gaius Septimius Nicomachus, freedman of Gaius, and for Visena Procula, freedwoman of a woman, and for Visena Cupita, freedwoman of a woman, and for Visena Potestas, freedwoman of a woman, and for Lucius Varius Chresimus, freedman of a woman, and for her freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01600741.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Visena Tertia for herself and her extended family, including freedmen and freedwomen, likely in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600742.translation: To Vitalis, aged 27, son of Decimus Publicius Macco, his fellow slave Pudens gave this.
EDCS-01600742.summary: A funerary dedication by a fellow slave, Pudens, for Vitalis, also a slave.

EDCS-01600743.translation: The place of the monument for Ummidia Phoebe, 16 feet in front and 70 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600743.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Ummidia Phoebe.

EDCS-01600744.translation: Titus Voltilius Celer, alive, made this for himself and for his wife Mamilia Thoin, freedwoman of Gaius, and for his son Titus Voltilius Priscus, and for his daughter Voltilia Celerina, and for his brother Titus Voltilius Optatus.
EDCS-01600744.summary: This is a funerary monument established by Titus Voltilius Celer for himself and his immediate family, including his wife, son, daughter, and brother, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-01600745.translation: [This was set up] for himself and for Voltilia, freedwoman of Quintus, of April [born?].
EDCS-01600745.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication for two individuals, one possibly named Voltilia.

EDCS-01600746.translation: To the divine shades. Of Marcus Utius Sabinus, a most innocent youth, who lived 20 years. His clients.
EDCS-01600746.summary: This tombstone honors Marcus Utius Sabinus, a young man who died at age 20, and was set up by his clients, probably in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01600803.translation: [---] son of Quintus, ordered by his will to be set up for himself.
EDCS-01600803.summary: A fragmentary inscription indicating a person, son of Quintus, who arranged for a monument for himself in his will.

EDCS-01600804.translation: Of Caius Julius F. [dimensions for the front part of the plot]. Of K. F. Prima, freedwoman?, 16 feet in front and 70 feet in depth.
EDCS-01600804.summary: This inscription denotes the dimensions of two burial plots, one for Caius Julius F. and another for Prima, possibly a freedwoman.

EDCS-01600813.translation: [---] who lived [---], Apitonius [set this up] for the most devoted [---].
EDCS-01600813.summary: A fragmentary epitaph mentioning Apitonius and a recipient described as 'most devoted'.

EDCS-01600816.translation: To Lucius, freedman; to Lucius, aged 17; to Acatia Stochadis, freedwoman of Lucius, wife of Lucius, freedman; to [---]
EDCS-01600816.summary: This is a funerary inscription for members of a family, likely freedpeople, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600818.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, by Caius Catius.
EDCS-01600818.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Caius Catius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600830.summary: This is a funerary epitaph or a formal statement of kinship, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600832.summary: This inscription records the name and title of Urbicus, a prefect, possibly indicating an official or funerary context from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600839.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600844.translation: The place of the monument for Anarius.
EDCS-01600844.summary: This inscription simply marks the burial location intended for Anarius.

EDCS-01600846.summary: This is a heavily damaged inscription fragment that likely refers to a pious individual.

EDCS-01600847.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely an epitaph or a record of parentage, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600848.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription dedicated to the divine shades, with illegible names.

EDCS-01600853.translation: [---]doi orae, son of Meanus, from Glucene, son of Surdus Canti.
EDCS-01600853.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a person's name and parentage, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600854.translation: Pi, freedwoman, wife of the deceased, made this place for the monument, 16 feet in all directions.
EDCS-01600854.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription by a freedwoman for her deceased husband, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600856.translation: He feared what was behind him. Decima S.
EDCS-01600856.summary: This is a fragmentary and somewhat cryptic inscription, possibly of a funerary nature, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600858.translation: Communis, alive, made this for himself and his family, and for his freedmen and freedwomen. The place of the monument in all directions is 16 feet.
EDCS-01600858.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Communis erected it for himself and his household, including freedpersons, and defines the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-01600859.translation: Parecorius Apollinaris, consular of Venetia and Istria, most distinguished man, made the fountain in honor of the holy apostles.
EDCS-01600859.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a fountain by Parecorius Apollinaris, a high-ranking official, in honor of the apostles, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-01600860.translation: Amara and Antonina, with their daughters Haelia and Mellita, fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600860.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Amara and Antonina with their daughters, likely a private dedication.

EDCS-01600861.translation: Concordius and Nitiana, with their family, made it, 25 feet.
EDCS-01600861.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication of 25 feet by Concordius and Nitiana with their family.

EDCS-01600862.translation: Dominicus the bootmaker, with his wife Severa, made it, 15 feet.
EDCS-01600862.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication of 15 feet by Dominicus the bootmaker and his wife Severa.

EDCS-01600863.translation: Dominicus the scribe, with his family, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600863.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Dominicus, a scribe, with his family.

EDCS-01600864.translation: Gazeus the deacon, with his mother Bona, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600864.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Gazeus, a deacon, and his mother Bona.

EDCS-01600865.translation: Guderit, with his family, made it, 25 feet.
EDCS-01600865.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication of 25 feet by Guderit with his family.

EDCS-01600866.translation: Iohannes the lector, with his mother Agneta, made it, 25 feet.
EDCS-01600866.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication of 25 feet by Iohannes the lector and his mother Agneta.

EDCS-01600867.translation: Iohannis the soldier from the cohort of Cadis, with his wife Severina, made it, 25 feet.
EDCS-01600867.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication of 25 feet by Iohannis, a soldier from the Cadis cohort, and his wife Severina.

EDCS-01600868.translation: Iohannes the soldier from the equestrian cohort of Persoiustinianus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600868.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Iohannes, a soldier from the equestrian cohort of Persoiustinianus.

EDCS-01600869.translation: Laurentius, a most illustrious man of the palace, fulfilled his vow with his family and made a gift of 200 feet.
EDCS-01600869.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled and a gift of 200 feet made by Laurentius, a high-ranking imperial official, with his family.

EDCS-01600870.translation: Laurentius, a soldier from the Tarvisian cohort, and son of a lord, made this [monument] 25 feet [in size].
EDCS-01600870.summary: This inscription records a military man, Laurentius, and his father, who commissioned a monument of 25 feet.

EDCS-01600871.translation: Laurentius, a deacon and servant of Christ, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600871.summary: This inscription records a deacon named Laurentius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01600872.translation: Lautus, an actuary of the holy church of Aquileia, with his family, fulfilled his vow. Lucinus, Romana, Lucianus, and Luciana, servants of Christ, made this [monument] 100 feet [in size].
EDCS-01600872.summary: This inscription records an actuary of the church of Aquileia, Lautus, and four other individuals, servants of Christ, fulfilling vows and commissioning a monument of 100 feet.

EDCS-01600873.translation: Marcus and Bibulus, with their brothers, fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600873.summary: This inscription records Marcus, Bibulus, and their brothers fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01600875.translation: Maximus, a shipowner, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600875.summary: This inscription records a shipowner named Maximus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01600876.translation: Murgio, a lector, and Bona, with their children, made this [monument] 10 feet [in size].
EDCS-01600876.summary: This inscription records Murgio, a lector, and Bona, with their children, who commissioned a monument of 10 feet.

EDCS-01600877.translation: The servants of the holy martyr Euphemia, Nonnus and Eusebia, Petrus and Iohannes, made this [monument] 100 feet [in size] according to their vow for their health and that of all their family.
EDCS-01600877.summary: This inscription records four individuals, servants of Saint Euphemia, who commissioned a 100-foot monument for their well-being and that of their families.

EDCS-01600878.translation: Paulus, a notary, and Diugenia, with their family, fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600878.summary: This inscription records Paulus, a notary, and Diugenia, with their family, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01600879.translation: Petrus, a notary, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600879.summary: This inscription records a notary named Petrus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01600880.translation: Petrus, a notary, with his family, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01600880.summary: This inscription records Petrus, a notary, with his family, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01600881.translation: Probina and her son Thomas the scribe fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600881.summary: This inscription records Probina and her son fulfilling a vow, likely of late Roman or early Byzantine date.

EDCS-01600883.summary: This inscription identifies Terentius as a 'duplicarius nauclerus', possibly a second-in-command of a ship's crew, from the Roman period.

EDCS-01600885.translation: Tertius fulfilled his vow in the name of the Lord.
EDCS-01600885.summary: Tertius fulfilled a vow in the name of the Lord, indicating a Christian dedication from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-01600886.translation: Valerianus and his daughter Valeria, with Decentiana, fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600886.summary: This inscription records Valerianus and his daughter Valeria, along with Decentiana, fulfilling a vow, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-01600887.translation: And Valeriana fulfilled her vow with Eugenia.
EDCS-01600887.summary: This inscription states that Valeriana and Eugenia fulfilled a vow, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-01600888.translation: Victorinus the reader, his son, fulfilled his vow with Antoninus and his family.
EDCS-01600888.summary: Victorinus, identified as a 'lector' (reader), fulfilled a vow with his son Antoninus and their family, suggesting a Christian context from the late Roman or early Byzantine era.

EDCS-01600889.translation: Vitales and Valerianus made [this] with their families, 40 feet.
EDCS-01600889.summary: This inscription records Vitales and Valerianus, with their families, making something that measures 40 feet, possibly indicating a construction or dedication, from the Roman period.

EDCS-01600890.translation: Ursus and Aureliana fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-01600890.summary: This inscription records Ursus and Aureliana fulfilling a vow, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-01600892.translation: Giving thanks to God and the Holy Euphemia, for my entire household I made [this] before the 4th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01600892.summary: This bilingual inscription (Greek and Latin) records a thanksgiving to God and St. Euphemia for the donor's household, made before November 1st, likely in the 4th century CE or later.

EDCS-01600900.translation: Gregorius, a priest, faithful, holy, and gentle, worthy whom the people desired to be their own; worthy, thus, to share in sacred rites with twin leaders; to rule with faithful counsel. He lies in his own tomb, whose name is Amantius. A prescient cause for future merit gave him; he presided over twenty-two peoples for years. If he had not departed, that praise would have been less. He was laid to rest on the 8th day before the Ides of April, in the 11th indiction. Ambrosius the deacon was laid to rest on the Kalends of December, when Marinianus and Asclepiodotus were consuls, most excellent men, in the 7th indiction.
EDCS-01600900.summary: This epitaph commemorates two individuals: Amantius, a priest who presided over twenty-two communities, and Ambrosius, a deacon, providing details of their lives, deaths, and consular dates in the 4th century CE.

EDCS-01600902.translation: Parents for their most innocent daughter Amantia, who lived more or less 7 years and 5 months, laid to rest the day before the Nones of July, in peace.
EDCS-01600902.summary: This tombstone, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE, was erected by parents for their daughter Amantia, who died at a young age.

EDCS-01600903.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the memory of Antoninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600905.translation: In good memory of Aurelius Fortunius, who lived 40 years, 5 months, 20 days, who lived 10 years, 5 months with his partner. To Flora Florentina, his incomparable wife, together with the college [...]
EDCS-01600905.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Fortunius and his wife Flora Florentina, set up by a college (possibly a trade association), dating likely to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600906.translation: To Aurelius Iustinus, faithful, who lived for 1 year, 6 months, and 8 days, and
EDCS-01600906.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Aurelius Iustinus, likely a child, with his lifespan provided.

EDCS-01600907.translation: To the good memory of Aurelius Primitivus, his wife Valer… Tom, his most precious spouse.
EDCS-01600907.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Aurelius Primitivus and his wife, with the dedicant likely being Valericus Tom.

EDCS-01600908.translation: Aurelius and Prima made this for their most sweet daughter Aurelia Anima, who lived in peace for 4 years, 6 months, and 24 days.
EDCS-01600908.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their daughter Aurelia Anima, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-01600910.translation: Aurelius Flavianus, a Syris citizen, while alive, dedicated this to Aurelia Angulata and Aurelia Firmina, his wives.
EDCS-01600910.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aurelius Flavianus for his two wives, Aurelia Angulata and Aurelia Firmina, indicating he was alive at the time of dedication.

EDCS-01600911.translation: Aurelia Eustochia lived for 2 years, 10 months, and 18 days. Her father handed her body over for burial. She was born on Friday at the 11th hour and died on Friday at the 2nd hour. Marcus Iovinus lived for 12 years, 4 months, and 6 days. He rests.
EDCS-01600911.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Aurelia Eustochia and Marcus Iovinus, likely siblings, with details of their birth and death times and days.

EDCS-01600913.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01600913.translation: To Aurelia Maria, an innocent, most holy virgin girl, proceeding to the righteous Elysian Fields in peace, who lived sixteen years, five months, seventeen days, betrothed to Aurelius Damas for twenty-five days. Aurelius Ienisireus, a veteran, and Sextilia, most unhappy parents, to their most sweet and loving daughter, contrary to their vow. Who while they lived had great sorrow. Holy martyrs, hold Maria in mind.
EDCS-01600913.summary: This is a touching funerary epitaph for a young betrothed girl, Aurelia Maria, set up by her grieving parents, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-01600914.translation: Here rests Auta in peace, who lived for 2 years, 11 months, and 27 days. She departed.
EDCS-01600914.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Auta, recording her lifespan and that she rests in peace.

EDCS-01600915.translation: Flavius Iucundus and his mother Eutalia, full of sorrow, made this monument for their well-deserving daughter Bonipedia, in peace, who lived for 9 years, 3 months, and 15 days. She was laid to rest on the 6th day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-01600915.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Flavius Iucundus and his mother Eutalia for their daughter Bonipedia, recording her lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-01600916.translation: In this monument, the pious Bonosus [...], greatly [...], his life [...]
EDCS-01600916.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription for someone named Bonosus, indicating a pious sentiment and lament for the deceased, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-01600918.translation: Caesius Carinianus, against his will, erected this for his most sweet wife Caesiae Benigna, who lived for 37 years, 9 months, and 15 days, and for his daughter Caesiae Donata, also called Severa, who lived as a virgin for 15 years, 3 months, and 2 days.
EDCS-01600918.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caesius Carinianus for his wife Caesiae Benigna and daughter Caesiae Donata (Severa), providing their ages and noting the father's grief.

EDCS-01600919.translation: Caramantus, having lived a worthy life with his partner, prepared this vow for themselves, who were equally deserving.
EDCS-01600919.summary: This is a funerary epitaph likely indicating a shared tomb or monument prepared by Caramantus and his partner, highlighting their mutual deservingness.

EDCS-01600920.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01600920.translation: To the departed spirits. To Constantius, innocent, most sweet, well-deserving, who lived fifteen months and fifteen days, against the vow. With grieving hearts, they set this up.
EDCS-01600920.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Constantius, set up by grieving relatives, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-01600921.translation: Crescentina, Ianuarius, Flavius Aquilinus made this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-01600921.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Crescentina, Ianuarius, and Flavius Aquilinus commissioned this monument for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-01600922.translation: Daccus, who lived more or less twenty years, lived faithfully in peace.
EDCS-01600922.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating a certain Daccus who lived for approximately twenty years and was faithful.

EDCS-01600923.translation: The son of Dizones, the prefect, named Diogenianus, who lived two years, seven months, and fourteen days, was buried on the twelfth day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01600923.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and burial date of Diogenianus, son of the prefect Dizones, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-01600924.translation: To Varius Florentius for his wife Zonysati, who lived twenty-three years, six months, and eighteen days, with whom I lived two years, six months, and eight days; she died on the sixth day before the Ides of June, in peace.
EDCS-01600924.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Varius Florentius for his deceased wife Zonysati, detailing their ages and lengths of marriage.

EDCS-01600926.translation: Eutychius made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-01600926.summary: This is a self-made funerary epitaph (a 'pro memoria' inscription) for Eutychius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600927.translation: Sorb, father, mother [set this up] against the will [of the deceased], for his daughter Firm, who lived 3 years, 10 months.
EDCS-01600927.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a daughter named Firm, set up by her parents against their wishes, indicating her short lifespan.

EDCS-01600928.translation: To Firmus, for his wife, with whom he lived twenty-five years and four months.
EDCS-01600928.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a wife, set up by her husband Firmus, noting their marital duration.

EDCS-01600929.translation: To the well-deserving Flavius Aparenta, who lived more or less ninety-nine years, laid to rest from the tribunes, gave up his soul on the Ides of December.
EDCS-01600929.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Aparenta, mentioning his long life and a deposition, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-01600930.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01600930.translation: To the well-deserving Flavius [name illegible], who lived about 70 years, laid to rest [...]. A virgin and son(s?) made this against their vow.
EDCS-01600930.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph for Flavius [name illegible], set up by a virgin and son(s?), likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-01600932.translation: Flavius Antiochus, his wife arranged to have made for her husband, who lived thirty-six years, in peace.
EDCS-01600932.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Antiochus, set up by his wife, who lived thirty-six years.

EDCS-01600934.translation: To Flavia Valentinina, most chaste, who lived with her husband chastity and loyalty and great affection, for whom her husband set this up as well-deserving, on the ninth day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-01600934.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife Flavia Valentinina, praising her chastity, loyalty, and affection.

EDCS-01600935.translation: To the good memory of Flavius Victorinus, a most excellent man, count, and Perellia Romana, of Italian origin, citizens of Aquileia. Flavius Victorinus, Romana, and Celsus made this for their most sweet fathers. The bodies were laid to rest on the 3rd day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-01600935.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Victorinus and Perellia Romana, set up by their children, indicating their citizenship in Aquileia and a burial date, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-01600937.translation: Crescens, her husband, for his most sweet wife Florentia, who lived twenty-three years, in peace.
EDCS-01600937.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Crescens for his beloved wife Florentia, who lived twenty-three years.

EDCS-01600938.translation: To Furiae Firminae Gaudentiae, incomparable wife, who lived twenty-six years, six days, [and] hours; to the most beloved virgin, who lived with me nine years, months, [and] days; died in October. Her husband, Virginius, made this in peace.
EDCS-01600938.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Virginius for his wife Furiae Firminae Gaudentiae, detailing her age and the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-01600939.translation: When, at the very beginning of his age, Geminius had attained the age of nearly 40 years, one month, and 15 days, born from the city of Tusurita in the province of Africa, born from Restutus, created from mother Maiora, fortunate in God, buried on the eighth day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-01600939.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Geminius from Tusurita, Africa, detailing his age at death and his parentage.

EDCS-01600940.translation: Here lies a woman who lived 28 years, named Donata.
EDCS-01600940.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of a woman named Donata who died at 28 years old.

EDCS-01600941.translation: Germanio, well-deserving, who lived 30 years and 3 months and 7 days, departed faithfully in peace on the seventh day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-01600941.summary: A funerary epitaph for Germanio, who died after living 30 years, 3 months, and 7 days, dated to the 7th day before the Kalends of April (April 25th).

EDCS-01600943.translation: Gerontia, you earned a sign of future chastity and a light of wisdom with exceptional character, a glory to all; snatched from your parents suddenly in your flourishing youth, you brought so much to us pitiable ones after eleven years and twenty-three days. Stercorius and Dizaneti, who against their vows placed these inscriptions and this memorial.
EDCS-01600943.summary: A complex funerary epitaph commemorating Gerontia, praising her virtues and lamenting her early death, set up by Stercorius and Dizaneti.

EDCS-01600944.translation: Getulicus lived 75 years, 7 days, and 5 hours. Simplicia and her son made this for her husband.
EDCS-01600944.summary: A funerary epitaph for Getulicus, who lived 75 years, 7 days, and 5 hours, set up by his wife Simplicia and son.

EDCS-01600945.summary: A dedication or epitaph for someone named Hilarus.

EDCS-01600946.translation: In good deeds for Honoratus and [---] whose [---] departed on the Kalends of May.
EDCS-01600946.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph mentioning Honoratus, dated to the Kalends of May (May 1st).

EDCS-01600947.translation: Well-deserving Pri[---]icius who lived 3 years, 5 months, 10 days; well-deserving Honorius who lived more or less 6 years and 7 months; well-deserving Maria who lived more or less 11 years and 9 months and 7 days. Parents placed this against their vows.
EDCS-01600947.summary: A funerary epitaph for three children, Pri[---]icius, Honorius, and Maria, set up by their parents.

EDCS-01600948.translation: Ianuarius set up this tablet for his dear wife, well-deserving, who lived in God 70 years, 5 months, 7 days.
EDCS-01600948.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Ianuarius for his wife, mentioning her piety ('in deo') and lifespan, likely late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-01600950.translation: Here rests the boy John, who lived for 4 years, 2 months, and 13 days, buried on the 13th day before the Kalends of August, in peace.
EDCS-01600950.summary: A funerary inscription for a boy named John, recording his age and date of burial, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-01600953.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01600953.translation: His wet nurses made this for Julia Gaudentia, their sweetest daughter, who lived for 4 years, 10 months, and 12 days; she died separated from life contrary to their vows.
EDCS-01600953.summary: A tombstone erected by wet nurses for their daughter Julia Gaudentia, detailing her age and lamenting her premature death.

EDCS-01600955.translation: This seat shall cover Leontia, well-deserving, to whom such a tomb, the holy neighborhood of the blessed, grants worthy rest. She lived with her husband Simplicio for 18 years, and was 32 years old, daughter of the most distinguished Valentinianus and Vetranissa.
EDCS-01600955.summary: A funerary epitaph for Leontia, who lived 32 years and was married for 18 years to Simplicio, daughter of Valentinianus and Vetranissa.

EDCS-01600956.summary: A name inscription, likely for a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-01600957.translation: To Macrobios the palatine eunuch, a centenarian of good memory. Flavius Firminus, a vir ducenarius, placed this inscription for the well-deserving one, who lived 70 years, 9 months, and 20 days. Flavius Caritosus and Romanus, freedmen, placed this against their vows, departed from the world, faithfully laid to rest on the third day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01600957.summary: A funerary epitaph for Macrobios, a palatine eunuch and centenarian, set up by Flavius Firminus and his freedmen Flavius Caritosus and Romanus, dated to the 3rd day before the Kalends of September (August 30th).

EDCS-01600958.translation: [...] II days [...] in his [...] faithful [...] for his daughter Marciana, who lived for 3 years, 5 months, and 20 days, she rested on the 7th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01600958.summary: A funerary inscription for Marciana, providing her age and date of repose, with significant portions lost to damage.

EDCS-01600959.translation: To the good memory of Marina, who lived thirteen years and eleven days, buried on the Kalends of September. Faithful.
EDCS-01600959.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Marina, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-01600960.translation: To the good memory of Tiodora, mother, who fulfilled her vow for her dearest son Marinianus, who lived about eight years, and departed in peace.
EDCS-01600960.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother, Tiodora, for her son Marinianus, fulfilling a vow and recording his age at death.

EDCS-01600962.translation: I, Flavia Leonta, placed this table for my well-deserving pupils Martinus and his wife Senea, on the fourth day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01600962.summary: This inscription records Flavia Leonta setting up a table for her deserving pupils, Martinus and Senea, likely in a public or educational context, with a date in late October.

EDCS-01600963.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01600963.translation: Maximus and Masclina set up this monument for their daughter Maxentia, an innocent soul, who lived for 3 years, 6 months, and 13 days, and is accepted into the holy spirit; her parents set this up out of grief for their impious daughter.
EDCS-01600963.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maxentia, set up by her parents, noting her age and acceptance into the spiritual realm, with a complex and somewhat contradictory sentiment.

EDCS-01600965.translation: For our dearest son Maximo, who lived about twenty-six years, four months, and three days, buried on the fifth day before the Ides of September, well-deserving, in peace.
EDCS-01600965.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph from parents for their beloved son Maximo, detailing his age and date of burial in mid-September.

EDCS-01600966.translation: To the good memory of Megetiolo, who lived five years, ten months, and eighteen days. Flavius Megetius and Petronia, parents, fulfilled their vow for their dearest son, and placed this tombstone. Buried in peace on the third day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-01600966.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from parents, Flavius Megetius and Petronia, for their son Megetiolo, recording his age, their vow, and his burial date in late July.

EDCS-01600968.translation: I, Babbius, [placed this] for Nonnita, my wife, who lived with me for six years and seven days.
EDCS-01600968.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband, Babbius, for his wife Nonnita, recording the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-01600969.translation: Felix Pascasius lived for five years, in peace.
EDCS-01600969.summary: This inscription is a simple funerary epitaph for a child named Felix Pascasius, stating his age at death.

EDCS-01600970.translation: He made this for his Paulinus. The principals were increased by the affection and pious love for Olympia, who was joined in maidenhood to Proba, with chastity. She brightly endured her twentieth year. If anyone has undeservedly acquired [...] with divine will, she received heavenly hospitality. [...] Olympia willingly gave [...] the future [...] holy, whom God [...] forever [...] the name [...] she proceeded faithfully [...] with eloquence, Blanda [...] she had [...] on the Kalends of November, winter [...] she found earthly [...] memorial in peace triumphed (?) [...] with whom decreed [...] Olympia [...]
EDCS-01600970.summary: This is a fragmented and complex epitaph, likely for a woman named Olympia, celebrating her virtues and her reception into heaven, possibly commissioned by someone named Paulinus.

EDCS-01600971.translation: For the dearest son Peculiaris, who lived seven years. [---] placed this tombstone on the ninth day before the Ides of May.
EDCS-01600971.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for a son named Peculiaris, recording his age and the date of burial in early May, with the dedicant missing.

EDCS-01600973.translation: Petronia Urnia, who died on the 4th Ides of May, who lived beyond her maidenhood for 5 years and six months.
EDCS-01600973.summary: A funerary inscription for Petronia Urnia, stating her date of death and her age at death, implying she was a maiden.

EDCS-01600975.translation: In this holy place rests Pisinio, who lived one year, ten months, and two days. Buried on the eleventh day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01600975.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Pisinio in a sacred location, detailing his age and date of burial in late August.

EDCS-01600976.translation: Here rests Pista of good memory, from the group of the Misaci, who lived approximately 40 years, buried in peace on the 7th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01600976.summary: A funerary inscription for Pista, a member of the 'Misaci', providing her approximate age and date of burial.

EDCS-01600977.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph recording the name and age at death of Praetor.

EDCS-01600978.translation: To the good memory of Quiricetus, who lived 30 years, 2 months, and 15 days, returned to peace.
EDCS-01600978.summary: This epitaph commemorates Quiricetus, recording his lifespan and peaceful repose.

EDCS-01600980.translation: Here lies Restutus, a faithful official, who came from Africa to see this city; this unwelcome land wished to have his body. Longing to return to where he was born, it was more cruel that he would not see any of his own family, and he had found more than enough of his own parents, and was no longer a stranger, as it happened, but from them, since no one can resist where fate calls. The fellowship of Florentines made this [monument] contrary to his wishes.
EDCS-01600980.summary: This epitaph records the death of Restutus, an African who died far from home, with a lament about his fate and the creation of his memorial by the Florentine fellowship.

EDCS-01600981.translation: To the good memory of the memorable and ever-watchful provider, Revocatus. Marcellinus, his son, erected this contrary to his wishes. He lived 75 years.
EDCS-01600981.summary: This epitaph commemorates Revocatus, erected by his son Marcellinus, and states his age at death.

EDCS-01600982.translation: [...] for the future, for his well-deserving wife Sabiniana, who followed me through all the provinces. With whom I spent [...] years and Aquileia received me [...] and I created sons.
EDCS-01600982.summary: A funerary inscription from a husband for his wife Sabiniana, praising her companionship and mentioning their life together and children.

EDCS-01600983.translation: For their sweetest lord, their nephew Sabinus. Istercoria, their sweetest aunt, whose misfortune they lament, who lived for 15 years.
EDCS-01600983.summary: An epitaph for a nephew named Sabinus, erected by his aunt and other relatives, noting his age and the grief his death caused.

EDCS-01600984.translation: Good-memorious Severus departed on the Kalends of August, on a Thursday. He lived 5 years, 7 months, and 22 days. His parents made this for him, most unhappily.
EDCS-01600984.summary: This epitaph records the death of Severus, who died at a young age, and was made by his grieving parents.

EDCS-01600985.translation: To good memory, to [my] loyal daughter, who lived 35 years, Silvina placed this. [Erected] in peace.
EDCS-01600985.summary: This epitaph commemorates a faithful daughter who lived 35 years, erected by Silvina.

EDCS-01600986.translation: This memorial was made during his lifetime by Recius Simplicius, known and beloved by all, for himself and his faithful wife Cressiana, who lived 93 years. Laid to rest in peace on the Kalends of August.
EDCS-01600986.summary: This epitaph records a self-made memorial for Recius Simplicius and his wife Cressiana, noting their long lives and peaceful repose.

EDCS-01600987.translation: Solida, who lived with her husband, a chaste and beautiful woman, full of modesty, here lies, oppressed by final, evil fates. The same night gave her marriage and death. When she was twenty-four years old, she had given worthy solace to her dear husband, but the empty marriage bed departed to the west, since fate turns all things. For her merits, Valerian, grieving, prepared this beautiful seat of marble for her in common peace. Deposited on the 4th day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-01600987.summary: This epitaph laments the death of Solida at age 24, detailing her virtues and her husband Valerian's grief in commissioning a marble tomb.

EDCS-01600989.translation: The character and praiseworthy life of this man are here celebrated. Valentinian made an eternal home for himself and for his most sweet wife Athenodora. Valentinian himself said to the reader: 'If you have riches, enjoy them; if you cannot give, what are you doing?' A superior man who knows not how to live.
EDCS-01600989.summary: This epitaph records a memorial built by Valentinian for himself and his wife Athenodora, accompanied by a philosophical reflection on wealth and life.

EDCS-01600990.translation: To the Divine Shades, to the well-deserving Valentino, who lived more or less 13 years, 5 months, and 7 days. Laid to rest on the day before the Nones of December, returned to peace, a faithful one. His grieving parents made this contrary to their wishes.
EDCS-01600990.summary: This epitaph commemorates Valentino, who died at about 13 years of age, and was erected by his grieving parents.

EDCS-01600991.translation: To my son Balerius, who lived 18 years, 5 months, and who departed as a Christian. His mother Simplicia placed this contrary to her wishes. And to a girl named Malisa, may she rest in peace.
EDCS-01600991.summary: This epitaph records a memorial for a Christian son named Balerius and a girl named Malisa, erected by his mother Simplicia.

EDCS-01600992.translation: Of good memory, Victorina, who lived approximately 29 years, 5 months, and 6 days, with her husband, who lived for 1 year, 2 months, and 29 days, the husband made this contrary to the deceit; she was buried the day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-01600992.summary: A funerary inscription for Victorina and her husband, detailing their ages and dates of death, with a note that the husband's monument was made unexpectedly.

EDCS-01600993.translation: For Victuturus, who lived 3 years and 3 months, his parents made this [monument] contrary to their vow.
EDCS-01600993.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Victuturus, set up by his parents, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01600994.translation: To good memory, Vegetantius, having deserved well, lived eighty-one years more or less, who departed on the fifth day before the Kalends of January, rests in faithful peace.
EDCS-01600994.summary: This inscription is a memorial epitaph for Vegetantius, noting his age at death and date of departure, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-01600996.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph, possibly for a deity or a person named Mesi Urbica, identified as faithful.

EDCS-01600998.translation: The destined day arrived not by desire but by fate in youth, when he rejoiced in his merits which he had once sought through labor; then, abandoned, it is sweet within the conjugal bond, and after a short and cruel time, harsh fate joined their bodies; they lie together not in bed but in a tomb, nor did they leave behind offspring to remember them, which indeed has not happened now for the first time in ages; he was always a dear friend to all his own. Here, with the dignity of a centurion, he had deserved among chosen men; his tent-mates set this up against their wishes; perhaps whoever hears this will grieve, but thus fate bore itself.
EDCS-01600998.summary: This is a complex epitaph for a couple, mourning their untimely deaths and the absence of children, and mentioning the deceased's distinguished military service (centurion) and the grief of his comrades, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-01600999.translation: To the innocent spirit, whom the Lord chose, [he/she] rests in peace, faithful, ten days before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-01600999.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph commemorating the resting of an innocent spirit, dated to August 23rd, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-01601001.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its meaning or context, but it likely relates to a person's life span.

EDCS-01601006.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-01601006.translation: Here rests Gerotia Innocentia, who lived for about 4 years, placed in a dolium on the seventh day before the Kalends of September; she made the dolium for her parents.
EDCS-01601006.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Gerotia Innocentia, noting her age and burial date.

EDCS-01601008.translation: For Bulo Suerus, my sweetest son, contrary to [our] vow.
EDCS-01601008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a son named Bulo Suerus, set up by his parents, indicating they had made a vow related to him.

EDCS-01601009.translation: To Bona, sweetest companion, her husband made [this] against [his] will, against [his] vow.
EDCS-01601009.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife Bona, expressing his grief and the circumstances of its creation.

EDCS-01601010.summary: This inscription is heavily damaged and fragmented, making its interpretation impossible.

EDCS-01601012.summary: This fragment likely refers to the lifespan of a person, possibly a child, and appears to be part of a funerary inscription.

EDCS-01601014.translation: Faithful in peace. Died in February. Here rests Felicissima, who lived for 4 years, returned in peace, faithful.
EDCS-01601014.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicissima, a young child who died in February and is described as faithful.

EDCS-01601019.translation: Undina... to Vericundus, six years, twenty... who was faithful, whom the saints...
EDCS-01601019.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for someone named Vericundus, indicating his age and faithfulness, possibly with Christian connotations.

EDCS-01601024.translation: most... assistant of the decurions, a citizen... by the will of [the gods?]...
EDCS-01601024.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that likely records a dedication or honorific title for an individual who served as an assistant to decurions, suggesting a civic or administrative role.

EDCS-01601025.translation: Marcus Ventus, as if for his wife, Curinus, the sweetest.
EDCS-01601025.summary: An epitaph for Ventus, likely a husband, with a personal dedication.

EDCS-01601026.translation: To the well-deserving. [Name] lived for about [duration]. Faithful. [She/He] rested.
EDCS-01601026.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely for a deceased individual named by the missing text, who was considered well-deserving and faithful.

EDCS-01601035.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius. Ampia Sabina [restored name]...
EDCS-01601035.summary: This is a dedication to the god Aesculapius, possibly by Ampia Sabina, likely from a Roman shrine or temple.

EDCS-01601036.text_edition: \n Aesculapio et Hygiae pro salute liberorum suorum et Antoniae Callistes coniugis Caius Turranius Onesimus votum solvit\n
EDCS-01601036.translation: To Aesculapius and Hygieia, for the health of their children and of their wife Antonia Calliste, Gaius Turranius Onesimus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01601036.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Turranius Onesimus to Aesculapius and Hygieia, seeking health for his children and wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601037.translation: To the Eternal God, the Hearer, Antonius Valens, prompted by a dream, for his health and that of all his people and the neighborhood.
EDCS-01601037.summary: This is a dedication to a solar or un-named supreme deity by Antonius Valens, prompted by a dream, for the well-being of himself, his family, and the community, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-01601038.translation: To Eternal Luna, offered a vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01601038.summary: This is a votive inscription to the goddess Luna, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601039.translation: To Anubis, the August. Lutatia Tyche offered a vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01601039.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Anubis by Lutatia Tyche, likely from the Roman Imperial period, possibly in Egypt or a Roman cult center.

EDCS-01601040.translation: To Ise and Serapis the god. Marcus Iuventius, the magistracy of the district, [dedicates].
EDCS-01601040.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the gods Ise and Serapis by Marcus Iuventius, identified as a magistracy of the district, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601041.text_edition: \n Apollini Beleno Aquileiensis ntus IIIIIIvir Aquileiae coactor argentarius dono dedit\n
EDCS-01601041.translation: To Apollo Belenus of Aquileia, the Six-Men college of Aquileia, a tax collector of silver, dedicated this gift.
EDCS-01601041.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Apollo Belenus by Gaius Valerius Thallus, a member of the IIIIvirate and a silver tax collector in Aquileia, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601043.translation: Appaedia Mansueta, freedwoman of Sextus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Goddess Diana.
EDCS-01601043.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the Goddess Diana by Appaedia Mansueta, a freedwoman, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601044.text_edition: \n Dianae Augustae sacrum Quintus Claudius Severinus IIIIIIvir Aquileiae voto suscepto remonente dea solvi\n
EDCS-01601044.translation: Sacred to Diana Augusta. Quintus Claudius Severinus, a Six-Man of Aquileia, having undertaken a vow, fulfilled it when the goddess urged him.
EDCS-01601044.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Diana Augusta by Quintus Claudius Severinus, a member of the IIIIvirate in Aquileia, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601045.translation: Tertia willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Fates.
EDCS-01601045.summary: A votive inscription by Tertia, dedicating a fulfillment of a vow to the Fates.

EDCS-01601046.translation: Sacred to Feronia. Titus Kanius Ianvarius, the priest, gave this gift.
EDCS-01601046.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Feronia by Titus Kanius Ianvarius, a priest, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601047.translation: To the Great Mother [of the gods?]. Sextus Vettius Secundus, a Six-Man, and his freedwoman Vettia Dorchas, [dedicate]. To Fortis Fortuna, Sextus Vettius Secundus, a Six-Man, and his freedwoman Vettia Dorchas, [dedicate].
EDCS-01601047.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Great Mother and to Fortuna by Sextus Vettius Secundus, a member of the IIIIvirate, and his freedwoman Vettia Dorchas, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601048.translation: Gaius Varius Anthiochus, freedman of Gaius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-01601048.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Hercules by Gaius Varius Anthiochus, a freedman, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601051.translation: To Isis Augusta. Lucius Iulius Senilis [dedicates].
EDCS-01601051.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Isis Augusta by Lucius Iulius Senilis, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601052.translation: Sacred to Isis Augusta. Gaius Minicius Trophimus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-01601052.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Isis Augusta by Gaius Minicius Trophimus, with the site granted by a decree of the local council, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601053.translation: To Isis Augusta, sacred. Lucius Rubrius Verna willingly [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-01601053.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Isis Augusta by Lucius Rubrius Verna, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-01601054.translation: Sacred to Isis Augusta; Titius Eupor [dedicates?].
EDCS-01601054.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Isis Augusta by Titius Eupor, likely on a monument.

EDCS-01601055.translation: To Isis Regina; Quintus Agrinius Glaucias, Augustalis, a statue(?).
EDCS-01601055.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a statue to Isis Regina by Quintus Agrinius Glaucias, an Augustalis.

EDCS-01601056.translation: Sacred to Isis Regina; Titus Fabius Pulcher, for the health of himself and of Rome, and of his wife.
EDCS-01601056.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Isis Regina by Titus Fabius Pulcher for the health of himself, Rome, and his wife.

EDCS-01601057.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, for the health of Aurelia Victoria.
EDCS-01601057.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus for the health of Aurelia Victoria.

EDCS-01601058.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Eternal; Aulus Barbius Maximianus.
EDCS-01601058.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Aeternus by Aulus Barbius Maximianus.

EDCS-01601060.translation: Sacred to the August Lares; the owner(?) Viatoris.
EDCS-01601060.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the August Lares by Viatoris, possibly a shopkeeper.

EDCS-01601062.translation: Titus Arius Celadus restored this sacred [monument] to Mars Gradivus.
EDCS-01601062.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a sacred monument to Mars Gradivus by Titus Arius Celadus.

EDCS-01601067.translation: To Nemesis Augusta, sacred; Septimius made his vow.
EDCS-01601067.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Nemesis Augusta made by Septimius.

EDCS-01601068.translation: Decidia Egloge gave an altar to the Parcae and a silver phial weighing 1.5 pounds to the Bona Dea.
EDCS-01601068.summary: This inscription records Decidia Egloge's offerings of an altar to the Parcae and a silver phial to the Bona Dea.

EDCS-01601069.translation: To Silvanus; Quintus Claudius Hermeros fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01601069.summary: This inscription records Quintus Claudius Hermeros fulfilling a vow to Silvanus.

EDCS-01601070.translation: To Silvanus Augustus, in honor of Lucius Annius Euporus, their patron, Lucius Annius...
EDCS-01601070.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus Augustus, possibly by a freedman honoring his patron Lucius Annius Euporus.

EDCS-01601072.translation: Cervia Musa of the Domnabus Tribus willingly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-01601072.summary: This is a votive inscription by Cervia Musa, a member of the Domnabus Tribus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-01601073.translation: Lucius Antonius Herma, by his strength, willingly and deservedly paid his vow. // Viribus, freedman of Festus Ursionius Augustus, [his] slave, restored an altar by vow.
EDCS-01601073.summary: This inscription records two dedications: Lucius Antonius Herma fulfilling a vow, and a slave of Festus Ursionius Augustus restoring an altar.

EDCS-01601074.translation: Sacred to the Augusti Viribus. Lucius Terentius Hermes, as a IIIIvir, made [it] to be...
