EDCS-01601074.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to the 'Augusti Viribus' by Lucius Terentius Hermes, who held the position of IIIIvir.

EDCS-01601075.text_edition: \n Minervae Victrici sacrum Augusto Augustae donum dat Publius Vettius Publi filius Decumanus decurio Aquileiae\n
EDCS-01601075.translation: Sacred to Minerva Victrix, Publius Vettius Decumanus, son of Publius, a decurion of Aquileia, offers this gift to Augustus and Augusta.
EDCS-01601075.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Victrix by Publius Vettius Decumanus, a decurion of Aquileia, and likely dates to the early Imperial period given the mention of Augustus and Augusta.

EDCS-01601076.translation: Heracla placed [this] for the Augusti Fontibus.
EDCS-01601076.summary: This is a dedication to the 'Augusti Fontibus' (divine springs associated with the emperors) by Heracla.

EDCS-01601077.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-01601077.text_edition: \n Lucius Domitius Epaphroditus is anno primo magisteri cum base et hasta pri isdem pridie Nonas lutabernas IX et cibaria\n
EDCS-01601077.translation: Lucius Domitius Epaphroditus, in his first year as magister, with a base and spear, on the ninth day before the Kalends of February, and provisions...
EDCS-01601077.summary: This inscription records expenses or activities related to Lucius Domitius Epaphroditus's tenure as magister, including provisions and a spear.

EDCS-01601078.translation: Lucius Safinius [---], Salvius Bassius, freedman of Salvius [---], Gaius Cassius Metrodorus(?), freedman of Gaius, Gnaeus Ceianius Communis(?), Titus Trebius Amoenus, freedman of Titus, Lucius Lucius Cimber, freedman of Lucius, Acastus, slave of Albida, son of Publius, Hilario, slave of Mulvus, son of Marcus, dedicated a roofed altar and a club.
EDCS-01601078.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including freedmen and slaves, who jointly dedicated a roofed altar and a club, possibly to a deity or as a funerary monument.

EDCS-01601079.translation: The ministers served: Publius Caesius Pollentinus, Publius Taurius Secundus, Marcus Servius Diadumenus, Sextus Nonius Felix, Vettia Libas, Tauria Primula.
EDCS-01601079.summary: This inscription lists the names of six individuals identified as 'ministers' who apparently performed a service, likely religious.

EDCS-01601080.translation: Heliodorius, happy with his companion, Salvius.
EDCS-01601080.summary: An epitaph for Heliodorius, mentioning his companion Salvius.

EDCS-01601081.translation: [---] Dindius Liberalis, Lucius Dindius, freedman of Iusta, Onesimus, willingly and deservedly paid their vows.
EDCS-01601081.summary: This votive inscription records Dindius Liberalis and Onesimus, freedman of Iusta, fulfilling their vows.

EDCS-01601082.translation: For the health of Quintus Marcus Marcianus, his son, he fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01601082.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made for the health of Quintus Marcus Marcianus.

EDCS-01601084.translation: For the health of Lucius Primitius, his freedman, his wife, and their children Moschana and Titianus, and all of theirs, he fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-01601084.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by a husband and father for his family.

EDCS-01601085.translation: Abascanthus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-01601085.summary: This is a votive inscription by Abascanthus.

EDCS-01601086.summary: This inscription records a dedication by three women named Cantia, Secundina, and Priscilla.

EDCS-01601087.translation: Rutenia Melite placed this by order of the goddess.
EDCS-01601087.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Rutenia Melite at the command of a goddess.

EDCS-01601088.summary: This inscription records a gift given by a person whose name is partially restored as Naso.

EDCS-01601096.translation: Marcus Aurelius, soldier of the Fourteenth Legion Gemina, [---]
EDCS-01601096.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the Fourteenth Legion Gemina.

EDCS-01601097.translation: To the divine shades. For Aurelius Aurelianus, Roman knight, his father-in-law. Aurelius Septiminus, tribune, [dedicated this to his] most dutiful father-in-law, who lived 22 years, and to Rosula, his niece, [aged] 3 years. // King Atilin [---] of the god's scourge.
EDCS-01601097.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated by a tribune to his father-in-law and niece, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-01601098.translation: Marcus Cato, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, from Cremona. Soldier of the VI Praetorian cohort. He served 18 years, lived 38 years. He was a beneficarius [adjunct] of a tribune.
EDCS-01601098.summary: This inscription details the career of Marcus Cato, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard.

EDCS-01601099.translation: To the divine shades. For Claudius Iustianus, ordinary centurion of the II Adiutrix Legion, stipend 12 [denarii]. Who lived 38 years. Aurelius Severianus, beneficarius of the office of the governor of Pannonia Inferior of the aforementioned legion, his second heir, placed this memorial to the well-deserving.
EDCS-01601099.summary: This tomb inscription commemorates Claudius Iustianus, a centurion of the II Adiutrix Legion, and was erected by his heir, Aurelius Severianus.

EDCS-01601101.translation: Titus Gallius Euphrosynus, soldier of the II Italica legion, [dedicated this to his] most innocent daughter, who lived [about 3] years.
EDCS-01601101.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a soldier's daughter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601102.translation: Julius, a supernumerary centurion of the XI Claudia legion, with 24 years of service, about 40 years old, accepted as a recruit at 16, later advanced by learning horsemanship, was made a decurio and appointed magister equitum, and is laid here.
EDCS-01601102.summary: This inscription records the career progression of a soldier named Julius from recruit to magister equitum in the XI Claudia legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601103.translation: Titus Paccius Priscus, son of Titus, son of Marcus, a quattuorvir and prefect of artisans, made [this for] Trosia Charis, daughter of Marcus, his wife.
EDCS-01601103.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Paccius Priscus for his wife Trosia Charis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601104.translation: Marcus Annaus, son of Quintus, a quinquennial duovir, awarded the contract and approved the reconstruction of the gate, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-01601104.summary: A public inscription recording Marcus Annaus's responsibility for a gate reconstruction, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-01601107.translation: Lucius Sallustius Urbino, of the Stellatina tribe, soldier of the 7th praetorian cohort.
EDCS-01601107.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Sallustius Urbino, a soldier in the praetorian guard, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601109.translation: To the departed spirits. For the freedmen Lucius Occusius Festus and Quintus Fruticus Primus, on the front 30 feet, in the field 30 feet.
EDCS-01601109.summary: This is a funerary dedication for two freedmen, likely from the Roman Imperial period, specifying the dimensions of their burial plot.

EDCS-01601112.translation: Marcus Annaeus, son of Quintus, quinquennial official, commissioned the rebuilding of the gate by resolution of the senate and approved it himself.
EDCS-01601112.summary: This inscription records a public works project commissioned by Marcus Annaeus, a quinquennial official, for the rebuilding of a gate.

EDCS-01601115.translation: To Lucius Gavius Alquinus, son of Lucius, prefect of the justice of Aquileia.
EDCS-01601115.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Lucius Gavius Alquinus, who served as a judicial prefect in Aquileia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601116.summary: A simple epitaph or dedication by Gaius Lucilius, son of Gaius.

EDCS-01601117.translation: Moschatis Eutychetes, having performed the priesthood, having passed from this age and having entered the twenty-first year, for whom the benefit of the air [was provided] when the elderly Sarca died, leaving the part of the light, Flavius Eutyches, following the priesthood, made this tomb.
EDCS-01601117.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Flavius Eutyches for Moschatis Eutychetes, who held a priesthood, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601118.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Titius Onesimus the elder, a decurio, [dedicated this] for his friend Lucius Naevius Allius, while he was alive, and for Naevia Severina. And Lucius Naevius Iustinus, a decurio, [dedicated this] for his parents.
EDCS-01601118.summary: This funerary inscription records dedications by two decurions for friends and parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601120.translation: [---]llaeus, of his son Petronianus, for his indulgence, the order appointed him priest in his place.
EDCS-01601120.summary: A fragmentary inscription concerning the appointment of a priest, likely in memory of Petronianus or his son.

EDCS-01601121.text_edition: \n Titus Plausurnius Titi filius quaestor coiravit\n
EDCS-01601121.translation: Titus Plausurnius, son of Titus, quaestor, arranged this.
EDCS-01601121.summary: This is an inscription indicating that Titus Plausurnius, a quaestor, commissioned or arranged the construction, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601122.translation: Quintus Titius Faustus, a decurio, made [this] for himself and for his wife Culcina Procula, and for their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-01601122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Titius Faustus, a decurio, for himself, his wife, and their freedmen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601124.translation: Argus, freedman, made this while alive for himself and for Italia, freedwoman, his wife.
EDCS-01601124.summary: A funerary inscription by Argus for himself and his wife Italia.

EDCS-01601127.translation: Of Laberius, son of Quintus, one of the four magistrates.
EDCS-01601127.summary: This inscription records a man, Laberius, who was one of the four magistrates of a collegium or local administration, likely for a funerary monument.

EDCS-01601128.translation: Turranius Calavinus, designated for eternal remembrance, made this tomb while alive for himself and his friend, the fourth magistrate, Calavia, daughter of Quintus Cervola, and for his daughter Turrania Calaviana, and for their descendants and freedmen and freedwomen whose names are written above; let no one else bring burial remains into this monument; if anyone commits an offense, any person of the populace is authorized to prosecute. Location of the monument in front: 3 feet; in the field: 30 feet. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-01601128.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Turranius Calavinus for himself and his family, stipulating conditions for its use and prosecution of violators, with specific dimensions for its location.

EDCS-01601136.summary: This fragment mentions money and the name Publius Cassin, likely related to a financial transaction or dedication.

EDCS-01601138.translation: [...] of a dignified woman, bought [...]; [...]ama, a slave? [bought]...
EDCS-01601138.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to record the purchase of something or someone, possibly a slave woman, by a woman identified as 'ama'.

EDCS-01601140.translation: Quintus Aebutius Scitus, freedman of Quintus, a money changer, made this while alive for himself and for Petronia Celido, freedwoman of Lucius and Gnaeus, and for their freedmen and freedwomen. The site is a square of 12 feet; 16 feet into the field.
EDCS-01601140.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Quintus Aebutius Scitus, a money changer, for himself and his family, with specified dimensions for the burial plot.

EDCS-01601141.translation: To Epaphroditus, my guest-friend, from Ceremeta, from Cornelia Helpis.
EDCS-01601141.summary: This is a dedication from Cornelia Helpis to her guest-friend Epaphroditus.

EDCS-01601142.translation: Publius Julius Protus, freedman of Publius; Publius Raedo, freedman of Publius; Publius Dio, freedman of Publius, eye doctor; 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01601142.summary: This inscription records three individuals, likely a medical practitioner and his associates, along with the dimensions of their burial plot.

EDCS-01601143.translation: From Verona, Gaius Poblicius Datus made this while alive for himself and his freedmen and freedwomen. The site of the monument is [3] feet in every direction.
EDCS-01601143.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Poblicius Datus of Verona for himself and his descendants, with partial dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-01601144.translation: [...] to my most excellent wife, Marcus Abudius Vitalis, for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. The site of the monument is 40 feet in front and 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-01601144.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Abudius Vitalis to his wife, for himself, his family, and his freedmen, with specified dimensions for the monument's location.

EDCS-01601145.summary: A simple epitaph or dedication by Acastus, a freedman.

EDCS-01601146.translation: The site of the monument of Caius Aebutius, [...]
EDCS-01601146.summary: This is a fragment indicating the location of a monument belonging to Caius Aebutius.

EDCS-01601147.translation: To Mercury, Aelius Crescentius dedicated this to his well-deserving brother.
EDCS-01601147.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury by Aelius Crescentius for his brother.

EDCS-01601148.translation: He/she lived for 3 years, 5 months and... Also Aelia Val[---] most sweet[---]
EDCS-01601148.summary: A funerary inscription for a child, likely providing the age at death and mentioning family members, with significant lacunae.

EDCS-01601150.translation: Albia Tertia, daughter of Lucius. A square plot of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01601150.summary: A funerary marker indicating the size of a burial plot allocated to Albia Tertia.

EDCS-01601151.translation: Gaius Allius Mento, son of Gaius, and Arria mater, daughter of Titus, made this at their own expense.
EDCS-01601151.summary: A dedication for a construction or monument, funded by Gaius Allius Mento and Arria mater.

EDCS-01601153.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming Roman individuals, possibly from a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-01601154.translation: Antonia Heraclia set up this monument to her most dutiful father, Gaius Antonius Heracles.
EDCS-01601154.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Gaius Antonius Heracles by his daughter Antonia Heraclia.

EDCS-01601155.translation: [---] made [this for] Apollo, freedman of Titus [---], son of Lucius [---].
EDCS-01601155.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription possibly dedicating a monument to Apollo, a freedman.

EDCS-01601158.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Aquilinus, aged 6 years, his parents Gaius Petronius Amerimnus (freedman of Tertullina) and Petronia Savarina (freedwoman of Gaius) made this while alive. Also for Successus, beloved, aged 4 years. This monument shall not pass to their heirs, freedmen, freedwomen, or their descendants. 12 feet in front, 20.5 feet in depth.
EDCS-01601158.summary: A large funerary monument with a complex dedication, including provisions for heirs and specifying plot dimensions, for the deceased Aquilinus and Successus.

EDCS-01601161.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming Roman individuals, possibly from a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-01601162.translation: Aurelius Proclianus and Mucia Severina made this.
EDCS-01601162.summary: A simple dedication by Aurelius Proclianus and Mucia Severina, likely for a funerary monument or a public work.

EDCS-01601163.translation: Aurelia Quiriacae placed this monument for her most sweet husband Flavius Salvius, who lived for 46 years, 8 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-01601163.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aurelia Quiriacae for her husband Flavius Salvius.

EDCS-01601165.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming Roman individuals, possibly from a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-01601168.translation: [---] to my father Basilus, son of Marcus. Also to Salvia, freedwoman of Marcus [---] daughter of Pothina, freedwoman of Marcus [---] Clara, beloved [---], also to my son-in-law Niger, son of Lucius [---], and to my friend Silon, son of [---]. And to Suavis, freedman of a woman [---]. 16 feet in front, 31 feet in depth.
EDCS-01601168.summary: A multi-part funerary inscription commemorating several individuals including family members and friends, and specifying burial plot dimensions.

EDCS-01601169.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Gaius Caecilius Aquileiensis, aged 30 years, 4 months, and 17 days. Caecilius Pollion dedicated this to his deserving son-in-law.
EDCS-01601169.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Caecilius Aquileiensis, detailing his age at death and dedicated by his son-in-law.

EDCS-01601170.translation: Caius Caecilius Seneca, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe. Rustica, freedwoman of Caecilius [---]. To Caecilius [---].
EDCS-01601170.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription likely dedicating a monument to members of the Caecilius family.

EDCS-01601171.translation: Exsoche Caesernia: the space of the monument is 7 feet, in the field 3 feet.
EDCS-01601171.summary: This inscription seems to be a boundary marker indicating land measurements.

EDCS-01601172.translation: Aulus Caesilius Sophilus, son of Aulus, his freedman, his patron.
EDCS-01601172.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning a freedman and his patron.

EDCS-01601173.translation: Quintus Caetronius, son of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-01601173.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Caetronius, who commissioned his own tomb.

EDCS-01601174.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely referring to ownership or a dedication to someone named Camerinus.

EDCS-01601175.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tito Canio Restituto and Memmia Nicene, husband and wife, who lived together without any quarrel for twenty-three years and thirty days. Their sons erected this for their parents.
EDCS-01601175.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a married couple, Tito Canio Restituto and Memmia Nicene, set up by their sons.

EDCS-01601176.translation: Campanius Nicolaus for himself, from his own resources.
EDCS-01601176.summary: This inscription records Campanius Nicolaus setting up something at his own expense, possibly a public work or a funerary monument.

EDCS-01601177.translation: To Titus Cantenius Dama, son of Titus, freedman of Titus; and to Doxa, freedwoman of Titus. Titus Cantenius Acastus, son of Titus, freedman of Titus, made this while alive for himself, and for his freedmen Nysa, Narcissus, and his son [---]to.
EDCS-01601177.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Cantenius Dama and Doxa, set up by Titus Cantenius Acastus, who also dedicated space for his freedmen and a son.

EDCS-01601178.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Lucius Cantio Acutus. Lucius Cantius Chrestus, his patron, erected this monument for his deserving freedman.
EDCS-01601178.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring a freedman, Lucius Cantio Acutus, by his patron Lucius Cantius Chrestus.

EDCS-01601179.translation: To Carfenia Callyrhoe, his excellent wife. Marcus Poblicius Eupor.
EDCS-01601179.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Carfenia Callyrhoe, dedicated by her husband Marcus Poblicius Eupor.

EDCS-01601180.translation: Gaius Cassius Pulverinus, son of Lucius, made this in his lifetime.
EDCS-01601180.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, possibly for a tombstone, set up by Gaius Cassius Pulverinus during his own lifetime.

EDCS-01601181.translation: For Cassius Thalamus and Nymphadium ANHNS E L V, Cassius Ianuarius, son [of...]
EDCS-01601181.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Cassius Thalamus and Nymphadium by Cassius Ianuarius.

EDCS-01601182.translation: Gaius Castricius, son of Gaius. Fabia Celer.
EDCS-01601182.summary: This is likely a tombstone or funerary marker for Fabia Celer, possibly related to Gaius Castricius.

EDCS-01601214.translation: To Marcus Gavius Communis, his freedman; to Marcus Gavius Primus, his freedman; to Marcus Gavius Blandus, his freedman; to Marcus Gavius Lator, his freedman.

EDCS-01601230.translation: Licaea, daughter of Marcus, aged 56, beloved, deserving.

EDCS-01601231.translation: To Lucius Licinius Calvus, our patron.
EDCS-01601231.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Licinius Calvus, honored as a patron.

EDCS-01601234.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Lucius Lucilius, to his son.

EDCS-01601235.translation: Sacred. Gaius Lucretius Echio, Lucius Satonius Socialis (?), Gaius Iu[---].

EDCS-01601236.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Lucretia Eutychia for an unnamed person.

EDCS-01601237.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, possibly for Luxuria, mentioning an age of 7 and 30.

EDCS-01601239.summary: This funerary inscription records that someone made the monument while alive for himself and his sons.

EDCS-01601240.translation: The place of the monument is 16 feet in front and 16 feet in the field, for Mar(cus) Sec(undus?) and Anicia Faustina.
EDCS-01601240.summary: This is a boundary marker for a burial plot, indicating its dimensions and owners.

EDCS-01601241.translation: Gaius Martius Philota, freedman of Caius, ordered this to be made for Fuctoria, freedwoman of Faustus, for Fuctoria Flora, Faustus' mother, and for Fuctorius Philostratus, her paternal uncle.
EDCS-01601241.summary: This inscription records a commission by Gaius Martius Philota for a monument honoring several family members, including freedmen and a mother and uncle.

EDCS-01601243.translation: To Mercury and Memorius Chryseros, for well-deserved services.
EDCS-01601243.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mercury and an individual named Memorius Chryseros, likely for services rendered.

EDCS-01601244.translation: Naevia Placida, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be set up in her will.
EDCS-01601244.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Naevia Placida arranged for her monument through her will.

EDCS-01601245.translation: Gaius Novius Tappo, son of Lucius, and Titia Polla, daughter of Marcus, and Gaius Novius Tappo, son of Gaius, for their freedmen and freedwomen, a plot of 16 square feet.
EDCS-01601245.summary: This inscription records the allocation of a 16 square foot burial plot for a family and their freed dependents.

EDCS-01601247.translation: The place for Octavia Venusta, freedwoman of Gnaeus, 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-01601247.summary: This is a boundary marker for a burial plot belonging to Octavia Venusta, a freedwoman.

EDCS-01601250.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Publius Peducaeus Boletanus.

EDCS-01601251.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating the age of a person named Persicus, likely an adult with remaining months specified.

EDCS-01601252.translation: ... of 8 months and 8 days, and Petronia, for her son.
EDCS-01601252.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the age of a child (8 months and 8 days) and commemorates them on behalf of Petronia and her son.

EDCS-01601253.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated to a woman named Pettia, likely by her spouse.

EDCS-01601254.translation: Philargurus [?]: space of 6 square feet for him and his freedmen.
EDCS-01601254.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot, possibly for a freedman named Philargurus.

EDCS-01601255.translation: Cn(aeus) Plo[---], M[---], C(aius) Ploti[---], while living (?).
EDCS-01601255.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary marker, mentioning individuals with the cognomen Plot[---].

EDCS-01601258.summary: This is a fragment mentioning a person named Primigen and 'brother', likely part of a funerary dedication.

EDCS-01601259.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Primitivus, the slave. Valerius Eutychianus.
EDCS-01601259.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a slave named Primitivus by Valerius Eutychianus.

EDCS-01601260.translation: The place of the monument for Mar(cus) Publi[---] Marcel[---], 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-01601260.summary: This is a fragmentary boundary marker for a monument, indicating its dimensions in the field and belonging to individuals named Mar(cus) Publi[---] and Marcel[---].

EDCS-01601262.translation: Burial place of Titus Raienus Festus, son of Titus, and Talassa, freedwoman of Furinia Caius; she made this while alive.
EDCS-01601262.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot and names Titus Raienus Festus and Talassa, a freedwoman, as the deceased or owners.

EDCS-01601263.translation: Marcus Rennius Tertius, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his freedwomen Urbana, freedwoman of Marcus Rennius, and for all his own people.
EDCS-01601263.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Rennius Tertius's commission for his own tomb and that of his freedwoman and other dependents, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-01601264.translation: Burial place of Gaius Rufus Successus: 20 feet in front, [?] feet in the field.
EDCS-01601264.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Gaius Rufus Successus.

EDCS-01601265.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a burial plot designated for Rufellia.

EDCS-01601266.translation: Place for a monument for Publius Rufrius Hermas and Lucius Iulius Reciperatus; 32 feet in front and 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-01601266.summary: This inscription marks out a burial plot of 32 by 32 feet for Publius Rufrius Hermas and Lucius Iulius Reciperatus, probably from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-01601267.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Caius Rutenius Primus, who lived 22 years and 3 months. Lucretia Paulina, his mother.

EDCS-01601294.summary: This is a boundary inscription defining the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Titia Hilara.

EDCS-01601304.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Titus Vettidius Phindarus for himself and his wife, also specifying the dimensions of their plot.

EDCS-01601305.translation: Calliope, freedwoman of Titus, placed (this) for her mother Vettidia.
EDCS-01601305.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Calliope for her mother Vettidia.

EDCS-01601306.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Vibius Valentis.

EDCS-01601310.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Publius Virrius.

EDCS-01601311.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Ulpius Felix for his wife Ulpia Heuporia.

EDCS-01601324.translation: The location of the monument of Servus Naevius Eutychides.

EDCS-01601368.translation: C. Ulpius, son of Caius, and his daughter To(x)via, daughter of Caius, and his freedwoman wife, Cai liberta.

EDCS-01601377.summary: This inscription appears to allocate burial plots, possibly mentioning Quintus Rigius and Quintus Vettius.

EDCS-01601383.translation: [erected by?] Maternus(?), soldier of the First Legion Minervia, for his most devoted brother, erected while alive.
EDCS-01601383.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Maternus, a soldier, for his brother.

EDCS-01601385.translation: Us, freedman of Quintus. Elpus. Us, freedman of Titus Quintus. Atus, freedwoman of Quintus, alive. Bius, freedman of Titus, alive. Us, freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-01601387.summary: This inscription identifies Terentius by his military rank and occupation.

EDCS-01601388.summary: This fragment likely records the lifespan of a person named Agape.

EDCS-01601389.translation: Annia Maxima, faithful virgin, who lived 15 years, 8 months, and 26 days. Aurelius Maximianus and Restituta, parents, made (this) for their dearest daughter.
EDCS-01601389.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Annia Maxima, detailing her age and erected by her parents.

EDCS-01601390.translation: For Asellus, well-deserving, who lived two years, 4 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-01601390.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a dog named Asellus, detailing its age.

EDCS-01601392.translation: [erected by?] Aurelius Felicianus(?), most devoted(?), with
EDCS-01601392.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly a dedication by Aurelius Felicianus.

EDCS-01601393.translation: To the Divine Manes. Bononia, who lived with her Virginis for 3 years and 9 days, departed in peace.
EDCS-01601393.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bononia, who lived with Virginis and died at a young age.

EDCS-01601395.summary: This is a dedication to Lar, son of Faustus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-01601397.translation: To Flacius, his dearest son, who lived for two months. Quilacius Guri and Drelia Sev, his parents, set this up against their vows.
EDCS-01601397.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flacius, set up by his parents.

EDCS-01601398.translation: Flavius Satur lived for [number] years. Laid to rest on the 5th of February, faithfully rested in peace.
EDCS-01601398.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Satur, recording his death date and peaceful repose.

EDCS-01601400.translation: Iovinianus, a citizen of Aeсаnus from Apulia, rests here, buried on the 3rd day before the Nones of August.
EDCS-01601400.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iovinianus, specifying his origin and burial date.

EDCS-01601401.translation: Istric, 8 months of age, laid to rest.
EDCS-01601401.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Istric, noting the age at death.

EDCS-01601403.translation: To Bona, remembered. [Number] years, more or less, with her Virginus. Laid to rest on the third day before the Kalends of [Month].
EDCS-01601403.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Bona, mentioning a companion named Virginus and a burial date.

EDCS-01601404.translation: To the memory of Maxima, who lived blamelessly with her husband for seven years, six months, and twenty-five days, departed from this world. I, Flavius Leontius, most devoted, made this for my dearest wife against my vows.
EDCS-01601404.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maxima, erected by her devoted husband Flavius Leontius.

EDCS-01601405.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for my most devoted wife Nicella, who lived twenty-five years, more or less, five months, and eleven days. Laid to rest on the eighth day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-01601405.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Nicella, recording her lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-01601406.translation: To daughters of good memory, Pascasia and [who] lived for 2 years, 10 months, 18 days.
EDCS-01601406.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two daughters, one named Pascasia, who died at a young age.

EDCS-01601408.translation: Innocens Pientia rests here, who lived for 4 years, 3 months, 15 days.
EDCS-01601408.summary: A funerary inscription for a child named Pientia, indicating her lifespan.

EDCS-01601410.translation: To his dearest wife Sabbatia. Theodorus, with whom she was united for ten years. They lived thirty years in this world.
EDCS-01601410.summary: This funerary inscription records the marriage duration of Sabbatia and Theodorus, and their lifespan.

EDCS-01601412.translation: Here lies Savina, who lived thirty-five years. Laid to rest on the day before the Ides of [Month].
EDCS-01601412.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, lifespan, and burial date of Savina.

EDCS-01601414.translation: To the well-deserving son Tertio, who lived for 12 years and 29 days, he reposed in peace, faithfully deposited on the 4th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-01601414.summary: A funerary inscription for a son named Tertio, including his age and date of death, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-01601415.translation: To the good memory of Theodore, dearest husband, his wife Hilara set this up contrary to her wishes. He lived
EDCS-01601415.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Theodore, set up by his wife Hilara, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601416.translation: To the memory of Verecunda, who lived for 5 years, 3 months, departed on the 5th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-01601416.summary: A funerary inscription for a child named Verecunda, stating her age and date of death.

EDCS-01601419.translation: In this place was laid to rest Vitalis, having lived more or less 4 years. He rested on the 17th day before the Kalends of September, a Monday, having died in peace.
EDCS-01601419.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vitalis, recording his age and date of death, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-01601420.translation: He lived more or less 50 years, who lived with his wife Ursa for 10 years and 20 days. He made [this] for them both and for his wife contrary to his wishes.
EDCS-01601420.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph, likely mentioning a man who lived with his wife Ursa, with a statement of devotion, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601421.translation: To the good memory of Ursina, deserving well, who lived 30 years and 2 months.
EDCS-01601421.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ursina, recording her age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601424.translation: Father Tiberius Mesa, who lived with me for 25 years and [several] months, without any complaint.
EDCS-01601424.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Mesa, set up by his son, highlighting their relationship, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601433.translation: Palubailgl[o] with his partner for 26 years, 8 months, and 5 days, rested in peace, faithful, on the 11th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-01601433.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and peaceful rest of Palubailgl[o] and his partner, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-01601444.translation: Merita [na], who lived 5 months and 6 days, faithful in peace. The same.
EDCS-01601444.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Merita [na], recording her short life and peaceful passing, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-01601447.translation: To Mucianus, who lived 50 years, 4 months. His wife [set this up] for the same.
EDCS-01601447.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mucianus, set up by his wife, recording his age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601452.translation: Riicia, an upright, good wife always.
EDCS-01601452.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely a praise for Riicia, describing her virtues, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-01601456.translation: Urnia, who was laid to rest on the 4th Ides of May.
EDCS-01601456.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Urnia, recording her date of burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-02900282.translation: Aurilia Victorina made this for Flavius Amantius, dearest husband, who lived with me for 37 years, 2 months, 10 days, to her sweetest husband.
EDCS-02900282.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Aurelia Victorina for her husband Flavius Amantius, who lived with her for 37 years.

EDCS-02900284.translation: Hermeros, freedman of Manius Curius and a woman, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Fontus.
EDCS-02900284.summary: This is a votive inscription from a freedman to the god Fontus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000332.translation: Titus Annius, son of Titus, as triumvir, caused this temple to be built, dedicated it, drew up the laws, and co-opted the senate three times.
EDCS-03000332.summary: This inscription records the civic and religious benefactions of Titus Annius, a triumvir, who funded and established a temple, likely during the Roman Republic.

EDCS-03000335.translation: To Venus Caelestis, by order of the goddess.
EDCS-03000335.summary: A dedication to the goddess Venus Caelestis, possibly by an oracle or priestess.

EDCS-03000338.translation: Aurelius Verinus, centurion of the XIIII Gemina, set this up for Colenda, his wife, for her merits.
EDCS-03000338.summary: An epitaph set up by Aurelius Verinus, a centurion, for his wife Colenda.

EDCS-03000339.translation: Lucius Titius Apella, Titia Ven[---], freedwoman of Lucius, Lucius Titius Stabilio, freedman of Lucius, for them and their freedmen and freedwomen, a square plot of 16 feet.
EDCS-03000339.summary: An inscription detailing a burial plot and its dimensions, likely for a family and their freedpersons, mentioning Lucius Titius Apella and his freedmen.

EDCS-03000340.translation: [---], Vibia Lochias, freedwoman of Marcus, made while alive for her patron, and for Mutilia Euche, freedwoman of Publius, daughter, for Marcus Vibius Crocus, freedman of a woman, son, for Pyramus, son.
EDCS-03000340.summary: A dedication made by Vibia Lochias for her patron and for other family members, including her children.

EDCS-03000341.translation: Gaius Petronius, son of Sextus, ordered this to be made for himself and for Optata, freedwoman, for Iucunda, freedwoman, a place [---].
EDCS-03000341.summary: An inscription commissioned by Gaius Petronius for himself and his freedwomen, Optata and Iucunda, to mark a burial place.

EDCS-03000343.translation: Marcus Licinius Vitalis, a member of the college of six, and an Augustalis, paid his vow to Aesontius.
EDCS-03000343.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Licinius Vitalis, an Augustalis priest, dedicated to Aesontius, likely a local deity, and dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-03000344.translation: Marcus(?), son of Caius(?), Secundus(?), and his wife, [---].
EDCS-03000344.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment possibly commemorating Marcus Secundus and his wife, with incomplete names and filiation, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-03000346.translation: Sextus Caelius Apollonius, freedman of Sextus.
EDCS-03000346.summary: This is a dedication to Apollo by a freedman named Apollonius, son of Sextus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000347.translation: Sextus Marcius Das, freedman of Sextus, gives (this) to Hercules.
EDCS-03000347.summary: This is a dedication of an offering to Hercules by Sextus Marcius Das, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000348.translation: [---] 32 feet in the field, and Adeptus.
EDCS-03000348.summary: This inscription fragment seems to indicate land measurement (32 feet) and possibly refers to a person named Adeptus, perhaps related to a property boundary or burial plot from the Imperial period.

EDCS-03000350.translation: Site of the monument: 20 feet in front, 32 feet in the field. Belonging to Lucius Marcius Macer.
EDCS-03000350.summary: This inscription marks the location and dimensions (20x32 feet) of a monument belonging to Lucius Marcius Macer, likely a property marker or funerary dedication from the Imperial period.

EDCS-03000354.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletian.
EDCS-03000354.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicating something to the Roman Emperor Diocletian, dating to the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-03000356.translation: Sextus Veturius Telephus, freedman of Sextus and Quintus, made (this) for himself while alive, and for those who will be born of him, and for all who are born of Tommo, just as if they were freeborn.
EDCS-03000356.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman, Sextus Veturius Telephus, who established a burial plot for himself and his descendants, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000359.translation: Caius Valerius Secundinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the Eternal God.
EDCS-03000359.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Valerius Secundinus to the 'Eternal God', likely a syncretic deity, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-03000370.translation: Of Quintus Sulpicius, son of Sextus.
EDCS-03000370.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a name and filiation, likely from a tombstone or public monument, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-03300269.translation: Of Decimus Poblicius, son of Decimus.
EDCS-03300269.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a name and filiation, likely from a tombstone or public monument, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-03300273.translation: Of Lucius Titius Primus the Younger.
EDCS-03300273.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a name, likely from a tombstone or public monument, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-03300274.translation: Publius Rasius Pollio for himself, Gellia Cupita, and his family, 12 feet in front, 24 feet in the field. This is the place.
EDCS-03300274.summary: This is a property marker or funerary dedication by Publius Rasius Pollio for himself and his family, specifying dimensions (12x24 feet), dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-03300275.translation: Vibia Maxima, daughter of Spurius, made this while alive for herself, for her father Lucius Vibius, for her mother Voesia Tertia, and for her freedmen Lucius Vibius Ianuarius, Anicetus, Optatus, Tertius, and her freedwomen Phiale, Didon, and Ephesia, and for other freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-03300275.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Vibia Maxima for herself and numerous family members and freedpersons, including a freedman who was a IIIIvir, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-03300276.translation: Prima placed (this) for her fellow soldier Aeros, her handmaid, who lived with her.
EDCS-03300276.summary: This funerary inscription records a handmaid named Prima placing a monument for her companion Aeros, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03300277.translation: He gladly fulfilled his vow to Hercules, as was deserved.
EDCS-03300277.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Hercules.

EDCS-03300283.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying an individual by name and filiation.

EDCS-03300284.translation: Sacred to the August Diana. Sextus Cinisius Theomnustus(?), Caius Cincius Veitor, Quintus Pipponicus Tae[---], members of the college of six.
EDCS-03300284.summary: This is a dedication to 'August Diana' by several individuals, including members of the college of six (VIvir), dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-03300292.translation: Titus Plotius Diadumenus erected this for his patron Titus Plotius Hermes, and for his freedwoman Plotia Elate, and for his freedwoman Plotia Prosis, while alive; for his freedmen and freedwomen. In front 20 feet, behind 35 feet.
EDCS-03300292.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription by Titus Plotius Diadumenus, honoring his patron and freedpersons, and marking property boundaries.

EDCS-03300297.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying an individual as the slave of Gavi.

EDCS-03300298.translation: Lucius Sarius Surus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-03300298.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying an individual by name, filiation, and status as a freedman.

EDCS-03300302.translation: To Verecundus, the restorer. Primigenius, the fellow villager.
EDCS-03300302.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph, possibly a tombstone, for Verecundus the restorer, by Primigenius, a fellow villager.

EDCS-03300303.translation: Vivus made this: Gaius Audasius for Iason and his wife, 31 feet in front and [space] feet in the field.
EDCS-03300303.summary: This is a property marker or boundary stone, likely from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period, recording dimensions and a donor named Gaius Audasius.

EDCS-03300304.translation: Lucius Hostilius Fronto and Gaius Clodius Merga, *seviri*, whitewashed work.
EDCS-03300304.summary: This inscription records the work performed by Lucius Hostilius Fronto and Gaius Clodius Merga, who held the rank of *seviri*, likely related to a building project.

EDCS-03300307.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary or possessive, identifying Gaius Rutilius Critus.

EDCS-03600001.translation: To Titus Iestinius Augurinus, son of Titus, a quaestor of justice, curator of the treasury, prefect of the engineers.
EDCS-03600001.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph listing the career of Titus Iestinius Augurinus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700279.translation: Quintus Porcius Optatus, freedman of Quintus; Sextus Erbonius Adiutor, freedman of Sextus; Marcus Quinctilius Secundus, freedman of Marcus; Sextus Erbonius Princeps, freedman of Sextus; Sextus Erbonius Gallus, freedman of Sextus; Quintus Marius Myro, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-03700279.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing six individuals, all identified as freedmen with their patrons, possibly indicating a family or business association.

EDCS-03700280.translation: To Turpilia Tertia, daughter of Marcus, mother; to Gaius Acutius, son of Gaius, father.
EDCS-03700280.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph dedicated by children to their parents, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700282.translation: Magia Tertia, daughter of Quintus, for herself and for her husband Marcus Terentius Homunculus, son of Gaius, and for her daughter Terentia Tertullina, daughter of Marcus. To Lucius Mamilius Trophimus and Maxima, daughter of Lucius, [daughter] of Caetronia. To Lucius Ostorius Secundus. To Lucius Licinius Fortunatus and Primigenia, freedwoman of Lucius. To Lucius Quinctius Ianuarius and Aegloga, daughter of Aemilia. And to Gaius Maecenas Lillaeus. To Titus Olio Ianuarius and Aegloga, freedwoman of Gaius. To Gaius Julius Helicus and Nomada, freedwoman of Gaius. Lucius Mamilius Trophimus dedicated this place to his associates, in front 25 feet, to the rear 75 feet.
EDCS-03700282.summary: This is a funerary inscription specifying dimensions and dedicating a burial plot to associates, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700284.translation: Rectus placed [this] for his father Gaius Iunius and his mother Cluat ia.
EDCS-03700284.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a son for his parents, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700285.translation: [Sa]ufeius Pelops and [Ann]ava Secunda, daughter of Marcus, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-03700285.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that the monument was constructed by the individuals themselves during their lifetime, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700286.translation: For Drusus Caesar, son of Tiberius Augustus, grandson of the deified Augustus, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-03700286.summary: This inscription honors Drusus Caesar, son of Tiberius, and was erected by senatorial decree, likely dating to the early Roman Empire.

EDCS-03700287.translation: To the departed spirits. Gavinia Amanda lived 32 years. Gavinius Paris [placed this].
EDCS-03700287.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Gavinia Amanda, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700288.translation: Burial place of Manlius Moderatus, in front 22.5 feet, to the rear 30 feet.
EDCS-03700288.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot and specifies its dimensions, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700289.translation: To the departed spirits. Crescentina placed [this] for her well-deserving husband Marcellianus. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-03700289.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcellianus, dedicated by his wife, with a clause about the monument not being inherited, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700290.summary: This is an inscription recording that Aemilia Formiana created the object or monument.

EDCS-03700291.summary: This is an inscription recording that Lucius Septimius Secundinus created the object or monument.

EDCS-03700292.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with illegible names and titles, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-03700293.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Tiberius Caelsius Natus, son of Lucius, erected this for his most excellent wife, Julia Ephesia, while he was alive, for his sons Titus Fronton, son of Tiberius, and Lucius Eron, son of Tiberius.
EDCS-03700293.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband for his wife and sons, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-03700294.summary: This is a personal funerary epitaph for Cameria Secunda, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-03700295.translation: A burial place was given to Spedia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, 30 feet in front and 30 feet deep.
EDCS-03700295.summary: This inscription records the grant of a burial plot, measuring 30x30 feet, to Spedia Secunda, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-03700296.translation: To the Divine Spirits. A burial place was given to Quintus Pinnio, freedman of Quintus, by Camilia, 40 feet in front and 40 feet deep.
EDCS-03700296.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial plot of 40x40 feet to Quintus Pinnio, freedman of Quintus, by Camilia.

EDCS-03700298.translation: Caius Antonius Protemius, freedman of Caius, placed the bones of his daughter Protemilla here.
EDCS-03700298.summary: This inscription records Caius Antonius Protemius, freedman of Caius, placing the remains of his daughter.

EDCS-04200001.translation: Lucius Caesius Glaphirus, freedman of Lucius, made this for himself while alive and for Caesiah Grata, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04200001.summary: This is a funerary monument made during the lifetime of Lucius Caesius Glaphirus, freedman of Lucius, for himself and his freedwoman Caesiah Grata.

EDCS-04200003.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Gaius Laecanius Severus erected this for himself and for Cerdon, who deserved well, while he was alive. [Also for] Phonarius [and] Laecanius.
EDCS-04200003.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Laecanius Severus for himself and others, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200004.translation: Caius Furius Gemellus, son of Caius, a soldier of the 4th Praetorian Cohort, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04200004.summary: This funerary inscription records that Caius Furius Gemellus, a soldier of the 4th Praetorian Cohort, commissioned this monument in his will.

EDCS-04200005.translation: [...]tia, a freedwoman, ordered this to be made in her will for herself and for Pyracmon, freedman of Io, and for Rufus, and for Heuresis, and for Sphragis, and for Modesta, from the goods of Pyracmon...
EDCS-04200005.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription details provisions made in the will of a freedwoman named [...]tia for herself and several other individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, and beneficiaries from Pyracmon's estate.

EDCS-04200006.translation: Sacred to Asclepius Augustus. Iuventius Eutyches granted the site.
EDCS-04200006.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred site to Asclepius Augustus by Iuventius Eutyches.

EDCS-04200007.translation: Euangelus of the settlers of Pola fulfilled his vow to Boria willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04200007.summary: This inscription records that Euangelus, from the settlers of Pola, fulfilled a vow made to Boria.

EDCS-04200008.translation: Antonia Severina fulfilled her vow to Eiae Augusta willingly.
EDCS-04200008.summary: This inscription records Antonia Severina fulfilling a vow to Eiae Augusta.

EDCS-04200010.translation: By the command of Isis. Quintus Lutatius Iucundus.
EDCS-04200010.summary: A dedication to the goddess Isis by Quintus Lutatius Iucundus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200012.translation: Sacred to Jupiter the Protector. Diocles, freedman of Augustus, procurator.
EDCS-04200012.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Conservator by Diocles, a freedman and procurator of Augustus.

EDCS-04200013.translation: Caius Iulius Chrysogonus made this, having vowed it, to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04200013.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Caius Iulius Chrysogonus.

EDCS-04200014.translation: Caius Laecanius Ialysus to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04200014.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Caius Laecanius Ialysus.

EDCS-04200015.translation: Marcus Titius Maximus to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04200015.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Titius Maximus.

EDCS-04200017.translation: Sacred to Nemesis Augusta. Gaius Lecanius Vitalis, also called Serpullius, willingly dedicated this.
EDCS-04200017.summary: A votive dedication to the goddess Nemesis Augusta by Gaius Lecanius Vitalis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200020.translation: Titus Annius Philargyrus willingly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-04200020.summary: This inscription records Titus Annius Philargyrus willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04200021.translation: Titus Valeris Lycnos, freedman of Titus, gave this with a willing spirit.
EDCS-04200021.summary: This is a dedication by Titus Valeris Lycnos, freedman of Titus.

EDCS-04200022.translation: Vridve Artiod willingly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-04200022.summary: This inscription records Vridve Artiod willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04200023.text_edition: \n Neroni Caesari Germanici filio Tiberi Augusti nepoti divi Augusti pronepoti \n
EDCS-04200023.translation: To Nero Caesar, son of Germanicus, grandson of Tiberius Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Augustus.
EDCS-04200023.summary: A titulature inscription for Emperor Nero, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-04200024.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Drusi Germanici filio Neroni Germanico auguri sodali Augustali sodali Titio consuli\n
EDCS-04200024.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, augur, member of the college of Augustales, member of the college of Titii, consul.
EDCS-04200024.summary: A titulature inscription for Emperor Claudius, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-04200025.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Drusi filio Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate V imperatori VIII consuli III designato IIII patri patriae\n
EDCS-04200025.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the fifth time, emperor for the eighth time, consul for the third time, designated consul for the fourth time, father of his country.
EDCS-04200025.summary: A comprehensive titulature inscription for Emperor Claudius, detailing his honors and powers.

EDCS-04200026.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Vespasiano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate IIII imperatori X patri patriae consuli IIII designato V\n
EDCS-04200026.translation: To Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the fourth time, emperor for the tenth time, father of his country, consul for the fourth time, designated consul for the fifth time.
EDCS-04200026.summary: A titulature inscription for Emperor Vespasian, detailing his imperial honors and offices.

EDCS-04200027.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VI imperatori XI consuli II patri patriae Marcus Aurelius Menophilus ornatus iudicio eius equo publico sacerdos Tusculanus aedilis Polae cum Menophilo patre liberto Auggustorum nnostrorum ex procuratore indulgentissimo <principi> locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200027.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the sixth time, emperor for the eleventh time, consul for the second time, father of his country. Marcus Aurelius Menophilus, priest of Tusculum and aedile of Pola, honored by his judgment and the public equestrian order, with his freedman father, formerly a procurator of our emperors, the most indulgent prince, has been granted this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04200027.summary: An inscription recording the granting of a public space by decree of the decurions to Marcus Aurelius Menophilus, priest of Tusculum and aedile of Pola, in honor of Emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-04200028.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Britannico maximo pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XVI imperatori II consuli IIII patri patriae proconsuli divi Severi filio divi Marci Antonini nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani abnepoti divi Traiani et divi Nervae adnepoti magno imperatori decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200028.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the sixteenth time, emperor for the second time, consul for the fourth time, father of his country, proconsul, son of the deified Severus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan and the deified Nerva, the great emperor. By decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04200028.summary: A detailed titulature inscription for Emperor Caracalla, listing his imperial titles and lineage, decreed by the local decurions.

EDCS-04200029.text_edition: \n Ulpiae Severinae Augustae coniugi domini nostri Aureliani Invicti Augusti matri castrorum res publica Polensium\n
EDCS-04200029.translation: To Ulpia Severina, Augusta, wife of our lord Aurelian Invictus Augustus, mother of the camps, from the public community of the Polensians.
EDCS-04200029.summary: A dedication to Empress Ulpia Severina by the community of Polensians, likely dating to the reign of Aurelian (270-275 CE).

EDCS-04200031.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Valerio Liciniano Licinio Pio Felici Invicto Augusto res publica Polensium devota numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-04200031.translation: To Emperor Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, the public community of the Polensians, devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-04200031.summary: A dedication to Emperor Licinius by the community of Polensians, likely dating to his reign (308-324 CE).

EDCS-04200033.translation: Publius Aelius Peregrinus, son of King Rasparaganus of the Sarmatians, made (this) for himself and for Attia Procilla, daughter of Quintus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-04200033.summary: A private funerary monument erected by Publius Aelius Peregrinus, son of a Sarmatian king, for himself and his family, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200034.text_edition: \n Lucio Anneio Luci filio Domitio Proculo clarissimo puero pronepoti Antoni Felicis Antonia Clementiana avia locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200034.translation: A place was granted by decree of the decurions to Lucius Annaeus Domitius Proculus, son of Lucius, a most distinguished boy, great-grandson of Antonius Felix, by his grandmother Antonia Clementiana.
EDCS-04200034.summary: A public grant of burial space ('locus datus') to Lucius Annaeus Domitius Proculus, a boy of distinguished lineage, by his grandmother, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200035.text_edition: \n Sexto Palpellio Publi filio Velina Histro legato Tiberi Claudi Caesaris Augusti pro consule praetori tribuno plebis Xviro stlitibus iudicandis tribuno militum legionis XIIII geminae comiti Tiberi Caesaris Augusti dato ab divo Augusto Caius Precius Felix Neapolitanus memor benefici\n
EDCS-04200035.translation: To Sextus Palpellius Hestro, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, legate of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus, proconsul, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor of judicial disputes, tribune of the soldiers of the 14th Gemina legion, companion of Tiberius Caesar Augustus appointed by the deified Augustus; Caius Precius Felix of Neapolis, in remembrance of his benefaction.
EDCS-04200035.summary: A dedication to Sextus Palpellius Hestro by Caius Precius Felix of Neapolis, commemorating his benefactions, likely dating to the reign of Tiberius (14-37 CE).

EDCS-04200037.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Chryscomallus, freedman of Augustus, procurator, (erected this) for his excellent foster-son, Titus Aelius Callimorphus.
EDCS-04200037.summary: A funerary dedication for Titus Aelius Callimorphus by his foster-father and patron, Chryscomallus, an imperial freedman and procurator, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200038.translation: To the departed spirits. Chrysomallus, freedman of Augustus, procurator, [dedicated this] to his foster children.
EDCS-04200038.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Manes by Chrysomallus, a freedman and procurator of Augustus, for his foster children.

EDCS-04200039.translation: Chryscomallus, freedman of the Augusti, procurator.
EDCS-04200039.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning Chryscomallus, an imperial freedman and procurator, likely a continuation or fragment of another inscription, possibly from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200040.translation: Arogo to his father and dearest brothers, Erotus, freedman of Augustus in the archive office.
EDCS-04200040.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Arogo to his father and brothers, mentioning Erotus, a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-04200041.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Harmonia and Gymnas, daughters, (and) Flavia Prima, wife, (and) for themselves, while alive, made (this) for their most devoted father Euphemus, freedman of Augustus, a record-keeper, and for his faithful wife, and for Ianuarius, freedman of Augustus, a record-keeper from the imperial patrimony.
EDCS-04200041.summary: A funerary monument erected by the daughters and wife for Euphemus, an imperial freedman and record-keeper, and his wife, and another imperial freedman, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200042.translation: Symphorus and Scorpus, freedmen and heirs, made this for their deserving patron, a freedman of Augustus in the archive office.
EDCS-04200042.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the freedmen and heirs Symphorus and Scorpus to their deserving patron, who was an Augustan freedman.

EDCS-04200046.translation: To Aurelius Gutho, soldier of the II Italica legion, with 23 years of service. Terentius Lucianus, standard-bearer of the aforementioned legion, made (this) for his tent-mate.
EDCS-04200046.summary: A funerary monument erected by a standard-bearer for his deceased tent-mate, Aurelius Gutho, a soldier in the II Italica legion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200047.translation: Lucius Menacius Priscus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, with public equestrian rank, prefect of the artificers, aedile, duumvir, quinquennial duumvir, military tribune, flamen of the Augusti, patron of the colony, brought the Augustan aqueduct to the upper and lower parts of the colony at his own expense and dedicated it for its protection with 400,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04200047.summary: A dedication by Lucius Menacius Priscus, a prominent local official, for financing and dedicating a new aqueduct to the colony, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200048.translation: Sextus Palpelli[us] Hister, soldier of the IVth Flavian Legion, son of Sextus Palpellius Regulus, veteran of the VIIth Claudian Legion, formerly a beneficiarius consularis, made this.
EDCS-04200048.summary: A tombstone for a soldier named Sextus Palpellius Hister, set up by his father, a veteran of another legion.

EDCS-04200050.translation: Lucius Sergius son of Caius, aedile, duumvir. Salvia Postuma Sergi. Lucius Sergius Lepidus, son of Lucius, aedile, military tribune of the 29th Legion. Gnaeus Sergius, son of Caius, aedile, quinquennial duumvir. Salvia Postuma Sergi, from her own funds.
EDCS-04200050.summary: This inscription lists several members of the Sergi family and their public offices, including aediles, duumvirs, and a military tribune, with a note that the last named individual funded a project.

EDCS-04200051.translation: To the departed spirits. Octavi, son of Publius Aelius, of the Camilian tribe, aedile, twice duovir iuri dicundo of Pola.
EDCS-04200051.summary: An epitaph for Octavi, a local magistrate of Pola.

EDCS-04200053.translation: Marcus Aurelius Felix, quaestor of public funds, aedile, and duovir iuri dicundo quinquennalis of Cremona, having fulfilled all offices, set this up for himself and Aurelia Marciana Virginia, a primary woman, while alive. She lived 46 years and 14 days. To her who deserved well. In front 20 feet, in the field [XXII?] feet.
EDCS-04200053.summary: A funerary monument erected by Marcus Aurelius Felix, a prominent magistrate, for himself and his wife Aurelia Marciana Virginia, indicating her age and the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04200054.translation: Lucius Cassius Longinus, son of Gaius, and Lucius Calpurnius Piso, son of Lucius, duoviri quinquennales.
EDCS-04200054.summary: An inscription recording two individuals, Lucius Cassius Longinus and Lucius Calpurnius Piso, who held the office of duovir quinquennalis.

EDCS-04200055.translation: Gaius Helvius Iulianus to Julia Fortunata, his most chaste and incomparable wife, for whom this splendid order of Aquileians dedicated this.
EDCS-04200055.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Helvius Iulianus to his wife Iulia Fortunata, likely from Aquileia.

EDCS-04200057.translation: To Titus Orbasio Clementi, son of Lucius, decurion of Pola. To Titus Orbasio Paullo, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04200057.summary: This inscription records a dedication to two individuals named Titus Orbasio, sons of Lucius, one identified as a decurion of Pola.

EDCS-04200058.translation: Gaius Plaestinus, son of Gaius, of the Petillian family, made this for Quintus Petillius Crispus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, decurion.
EDCS-04200058.summary: A tombstone set up by Gaius Plaestinus for his brother Quintus Petillius Crispus, a decurion.

EDCS-04200059.translation: As quinquennial duumvir, by decree of the decurions, he undertook, cared for, and dedicated [this] to Memmia Prisca.
EDCS-04200059.summary: This records the commissioning and dedication of a project to Memmia Prisca by a quinquennial duumvir, acting on the decision of the town council.

EDCS-04200060.text_edition: \n Cnaeo Papirio Cnaei filio Velina Secundino IIviro IIiro quinquennali patrono et praefecto collegii fabrorum Polensium curatori rei publicae Flanatium Marcus Helvius Hermias amico dignissimo locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200060.translation: To Gnaeus Papirius Secundinus, son of Gnaeus, of the Velina tribe, duovir, quinquennial duovir, patron and prefect of the college of artisans of Pola, curator of the republic of Flanatium, Marcus Helvius Hermias, his most worthy friend, granted this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04200060.summary: A dedication of a public space to Gnaeus Papirius Secundinus, honoring his various civic and collegial roles in Pola and Flanatium.

EDCS-04200066.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Apuleia Zosime, freedwoman of Sextus, made this herself while alive by her will for herself and for Sextus Apuleius Apollonius, freedman of Sextus, Augustalis VIvir of Tergeste and Pola, her most devoted and deserving husband, and for her freedman Themesthocles, and for her freedwoman Apuleia Theseis, wife of Themesthocles.
EDCS-04200066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Apuleia Zosime, a freedwoman, for herself and her family, including her husband Sextus Apuleius Apollonius, an Augustalis VIvir in Tergeste and Pola.

EDCS-04200067.summary: This inscription simply names two individuals, Epagathus and Felix, identified as servants of the emperor.

EDCS-04200068.translation: To Iulia Chrisanthidi, aged 31 years, 3 months, and 29 days. Titus Lusidienus Nestor, Augustalis, to his incomparable wife of Pola, with whom he lived for 16 years and 4 months, well-deserving.
EDCS-04200068.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Chrisanthidi, detailing her age and the duration of her marriage to Titus Lusidienus Nestor, an Augustalis of Pola.

EDCS-04200069.translation: Modia Prugia, freedwoman of Lucius; Modia Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius; Lucius Modius Pamphilus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for themselves and their kin. They were sexviri.
EDCS-04200069.summary: A tombstone set up by three freedpeople, two women and one man, who were sexviri, for themselves and their relatives.

EDCS-04200070.translation: To Saturninus, aged 21 years. Lucius Satonius Trophimus, VIvir, at Aquileia.
EDCS-04200070.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Saturninus, aged 21, by Lucius Satonius Trophimus, a VIvir in Aquileia.

EDCS-04200072.translation: Lucius Selicius: 21 feet in front, 17 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200072.summary: This inscription records land measurements, specifically the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Lucius Selicius.

EDCS-04200073.translation: Quintus Sirtius Callistus, a living sexvir Augustalis, made this for himself and for Laecania Prisca, his excellent wife, and for all their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04200073.summary: A funerary monument erected by Quintus Sirtius Callistus, a living sexvir Augustalis, for himself, his wife, and their freed dependents.

EDCS-04200074.translation: Gaius Socconius, freedman of the woman Statius, sexvir, made this himself while alive for himself and for Socconia Phoebe, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04200074.summary: This is a tombstone inscription set up by Gaius Socconius, a freedman and sexvir, for himself and his freedwoman Socconia Phoebe.

EDCS-04200075.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vibius Augustalis, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-04200076.translation: of the six senior priests, Augustalis of Pola.
EDCS-04200076.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Augustalis of Pola as a member of the IIIIII viri (a college of priests).

EDCS-04200078.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Augustalis of Pola.

EDCS-04200080.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04200080.translation: The Dendrophori of Pola. Gaius Laecanius Theodorus, priest of the Great Mother Goddess of Ida, donated this place with burial rights. In front 42 feet, in the field 62 feet.
EDCS-04200080.summary: A dedication of a burial plot by Gaius Laecanius Theodorus, a priest of the cult of the Great Mother, for the use of the Dendrophori of Pola.

EDCS-04200081.translation: Gaius Turpilius Felix, while alive, made this for himself and for Betuvia Felicula, brought it for Gaius Pollentius Liberalis to the guild of dendrophori, and for Turpilius Vitalis, son of Apronius, for Etrusca, for Eulalus the First of Tralles, for his freedmen, for Gaius Settidius Donatus, for Lucius Annius Venustus, the good students.
EDCS-04200081.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Turpilius Felix for himself, his family, and members of the dendrophori guild, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200082.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Valerianus, freedwoman of Pollentia Processa, freedwoman of the colonists of Pola, the chief administrator, dedicated this to his most rare freedwoman.
EDCS-04200082.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Valerianus for his freedwoman, Pollentia Processa, who was also a freedwoman of the colonists of Pola, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200173.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Aulus Atius Caius, the physician, while alive, made this for himself and for Julia Prima, his incomparable wife.
EDCS-04200173.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Atius Caius, a physician, for himself and his wife, Julia Prima, indicating it was erected during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200174.translation: His sons Aurelius Soter and Aurelius Stephanus erected this for Aurelia Soteria, their most dutiful mother, who feared the Jewish religion.
EDCS-04200174.summary: A tombstone set up by two sons for their pious mother, Aurelia Soteria, noting her adherence to Judaism.

EDCS-04200175.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Publius Coesius Ortensianus, physician, aged 18, and for Milusus Primus, his student.
EDCS-04200175.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young physician, Publius Coesius Ortensianus, and his student, Milusus Primus.

EDCS-04200176.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Donata, his wife, and sons erected this for Fortunatus, actor of Iulius Fronto, a well-deserving man. The front is 20 feet, the depth 25 feet. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04200176.summary: A funerary monument erected by a wife and sons for Fortunatus, an actor, with property dimensions and a stipulation against inheritance.

EDCS-04200177.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Maximus, an administrator, [erected this] for Magnia Felicissima, his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-04200177.summary: A funerary dedication by Maximus, an administrator, to his wife Magnia Felicissima.

EDCS-04200178.translation: The depth is 16 feet, the front 12 feet. [---]ius, son of Dosa, from Syria Palaestina, erected this for himself and his family while alive in Neapolis. Marcia Casta, daughter of Marcus, exceedingly rare, lived 30 years.
EDCS-04200178.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcia Casta, who lived 30 years, erected by her husband [---]ius, possibly from Neapolis.

EDCS-04200179.translation: To Nothus, son of Lucius Selicius Gemini, a slave banker, aged 23, and to his son Quintus Sallustius Ianianus, freedman of Quintus, and to Hespero, slave of Gaius Orbus Quartus, her husband, Mutilia, freedwoman of Lucius, [dedicated this] to Nothis.
EDCS-04200179.summary: This is a complex funerary epitaph dedicated by Mutilia for her husband Nothus, their son Ianianus, and another individual Hespero, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200180.translation: To Marcus Petronius Amerimnus, freedman of Marcus, the sailor.
EDCS-04200180.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Petronius Amerimnus, a freedman and sailor.

EDCS-04200181.translation: The plot of land of Marcus Postumius, son of Lucius, from Veronensis, Publilia Postumi [dedicated this]; in front 12 feet, in the field 18 feet.
EDCS-04200181.summary: This inscription marks a plot of land measuring 12 feet in front and 18 feet in the field, belonging to Marcus Postumius and dedicated by Publilia Postumi.

EDCS-04200182.translation: Epidectus, administrator of the Emperor, [erected this] for Primigenius, son of Spendontis, his friend.
EDCS-04200182.summary: A dedication by Epidectus, an imperial administrator, to his friend Primigenius.

EDCS-04200183.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Primo, a 30-year-old smith.

EDCS-04200184.translation: Titia Eutychia erected this for herself and for her son Lucius Maesius Modestus, aged 18, and for her daughter Valeria Vera, aged 18, and for her dearly beloved husband Lucius Maesius Terentinus, a comb maker, while she was alive.
EDCS-04200184.summary: A family tomb erected by Titia Eutychia for herself, her husband Lucius Maesius Terentinus (a comb maker), and their two children, Lucius Maesius Modestus and Valeria Vera, both aged 18.

EDCS-04200185.translation: Lucius Verginius Pudens, a haruspex, and Iulia Luculla, daughter of Quintus, erected [this].
EDCS-04200185.summary: A dedication by Lucius Verginius Pudens, a haruspex (diviner of entrails), and his wife Iulia Luculla.

EDCS-04200188.translation: Aelius Priscilianus and Aelia Chreste erected this while alive for themselves.
EDCS-04200188.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a monument set up by Aelius Priscilianus and Aelia Chreste for their own future use.

EDCS-04200189.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Trophimus erected [this] for Aelia Artemisia, his most loving mother.
EDCS-04200189.summary: A funerary dedication by Trophimus for his mother, Aelia Artemisia.

EDCS-04200190.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulius Marcellinus erected this while alive for his deserving wife, Aelia Nymphidia.
EDCS-04200190.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Aelia Nymphidia by her husband, Iulius Marcellinus, who set it up during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200191.text_edition: \n Mater posuit tumulum Aelia Octavia filiae incomparabili Aepaphroditae sic quae vixit annos IIII menses X dies V horas V hic sita\n
EDCS-04200191.translation: Aelia Octavia placed this tomb for her incomparable daughter Aepaphrodita, who lived 4 years, 10 months, 5 days, and 5 hours, and lies here.
EDCS-04200191.summary: A tomb erected by Aelia Octavia for her young daughter Aepaphrodita, who died at the age of 4 years, 10 months, 5 days, and 5 hours.

EDCS-04200192.translation: To Aemilia Dionysia, dearest daughter, who lived 13 years, 3 months, and 16 days. Her father Dionysius erected this.
EDCS-04200192.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Aemilia Dionysia, commemorating her life and erected by her father.

EDCS-04200193.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Lucius Afranius.
EDCS-04200193.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Afranius.

EDCS-04200194.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Agathes, of Caesar, erected [this] while alive for his exceedingly rare wife, aged 35.
EDCS-04200194.summary: A funerary monument erected by Agathes, an imperial servant, for his wife, who died at 35.

EDCS-04200196.translation: Lucius Anneius Chrestus, freedman of Lucius, erected [this] for himself and Vibia Maxima while alive.
EDCS-04200196.summary: A dedication by Lucius Anneius Chrestus, a freedman, for himself and Vibia Maxima.

EDCS-04200197.translation: Lucius Annius Vitalis, son of Publius, to his own [family/property/etc.].
EDCS-04200197.summary: This inscription likely records a property boundary or dedication by Lucius Annius Vitalis.

EDCS-04200198.translation: Of Ianni [and] Euripides, 10 feet in the field, 11 feet in the front.
EDCS-04200198.summary: This is a boundary stone marking a property of 10 by 11 feet, possibly belonging to Ianni and Euripides.

EDCS-04200199.translation: To Annia Tertulla, daughter of Caius, mother most excellent.
EDCS-04200199.summary: This is an honorary inscription or tombstone dedicated to Annia Tertulla, described as an excellent mother.

EDCS-04200200.translation: Germanilla Antistia Donace, mother, erected this while alive.
EDCS-04200200.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Germanilla Antistia Donace for herself.

EDCS-04200201.translation: Marcus Antonius Stachus for himself and his family and Antonia Celia.
EDCS-04200201.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records an owner, Marcus Antonius Stachus, and mentions family members, possibly for a tomb or property.

EDCS-04200202.translation: Anusia Tertia, daughter of Publius, made this while alive for herself and for her son Titus Sornatius, son of Caius Sabinus, who was taken by fate in his earliest youth and imposed great grief upon me, his mother.
EDCS-04200202.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Anusia Tertia for herself and her son Titus Sornatius Sabinus, lamenting his early death.

EDCS-04200203.translation: To the departed spirits. What a father ought to do for his son, premature death prevented him from doing; so the father, Sextus Apuleius Probus, alive, made [this] for his son Sextus Apuleius, aged VI years.
EDCS-04200203.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Sextus Apuleius Probus for his son Sextus Apuleius, who died at age six, with the father regretting not being able to do more.
