EDCS-04200204.translation: Of Lucius Aquileiensis Trophimus: 20 feet in front, 25 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200204.summary: This inscription likely records land dimensions or measurements associated with Lucius Aquileiensis Trophimus.

EDCS-04200205.translation: To the Divine Shades. Asclepia, slave of Antistius, aged 14. Her parents erected this while alive.
EDCS-04200205.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Asclepia, a 14-year-old slave, erected by her parents.

EDCS-04200206.translation: To the departed spirits. Pompeius Marianus for his well-deserving wife Aufidia Marcellina and his son Pompeius Marcellinus, from his own means.
EDCS-04200206.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Pompeius Marianus and his son for his wife and their mother, Aufidia Marcellina.

EDCS-04200207.translation: Avidia Maximina, while alive, placed this eternal home for herself; if anyone places another body on top, let him pay 300,000 denarii to the treasury.
EDCS-04200207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with a penalty clause for improper burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200208.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aurelius E, while alive, placed this for himself.
EDCS-04200208.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius E, who dedicated it for himself during his lifetime, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200209.translation: Aurelius Agrippinus and Aurelia Victoria, his partner, from their savings, erected this eternal house for themselves while alive.
EDCS-04200209.summary: This is an inscription on a house built by Aurelius Agrippinus and Aurelia Victoria for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-04200210.translation: Marcus Aurelius Eutyches and Aurelia Rufena erected this resting place for themselves while alive, working with one mind and without any complaint.
EDCS-04200210.summary: This is an inscription on a tomb or dwelling erected by Marcus Aurelius Eutyches and Aurelia Rufena for themselves.

EDCS-04200211.translation: Aurelius Minervinus placed [this] for his well-deserving wife Vera, who lived 45 years.
EDCS-04200211.summary: This is a tombstone set up by Aurelius Minervinus for his wife Vera, recording her name and lifespan.

EDCS-04200212.translation: Aurelius Plocianus and Valeria Saturnia placed [this].
EDCS-04200212.summary: This is a simple dedication by Aurelius Plocianus and Valeria Saturnia, likely for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-04200213.translation: To the departed spirits. Aspasia, the freedwoman, made [this] while alive for Aurelius Timarchus.
EDCS-04200213.summary: This is a tombstone erected by the freedwoman Aspasia for Aurelius Timarchus.

EDCS-04200214.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelia Crescentina placed this, at her own expense and with due regard, for her husband Gaius Aurelius Epaphroditus, with whom she lived for 11 years.
EDCS-04200214.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband, dating likely to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200215.translation: To the departed spirits. Vibius Achilles made this for his unparalleled wife, Aurelia Ianuaria.
EDCS-04200215.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200216.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Aurelia Leucippe by her husband, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200217.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelia Soteria, full of devotion, placed this in memory of her piety towards her most dutiful and unparalleled foster-child, who lived 20 years, 10 months, and 2 days, her fidelity having been recognized.
EDCS-04200217.summary: A funerary epitaph erected by a foster-mother for her deceased foster-child, with details of her lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200218.translation: To Aurelia Stephana, the dutiful, who lived 19 years, 9 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-04200218.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life span of Aurelia Stephana, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200219.translation: To the departed spirits. Freedwoman Barbatia Anthemis for her well-deserving patron, Barbatio Hugino.
EDCS-04200219.summary: A funerary epitaph for a freedman erected by his freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200220.translation: Lucius Barbius Ephebus made this while alive for himself, his partner Statia Aufa, freedwoman of Marcus, and his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04200220.summary: A funerary epitaph for a man setting up a tomb for himself, his partner, and his freed dependents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200221.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Barbia Proba placed this for her husband, Lucius Barbio Rufus, who well deserved it.
EDCS-04200221.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Lucius Barbio Rufus, dedicated by his wife Barbia Proba, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200222.translation: Marcus Barbius Soter for his most dutiful daughter, Barbia Asclepidora.
EDCS-04200222.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a father for his daughter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200223.translation: Gaius Gaianus Basilides, an equestrian from Rome, and Aurelia Vibia Vibiana, a matron, the parents, made this for their most rare daughter, Gaia Basilia Crispine, a good matron, aged 17 years, 6 months, and 5 days, while they lived.
EDCS-04200223.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Gaia Basilia Crispine at a young age and was erected by her parents, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200224.translation: Gaius Billienus Philogenes, freedman of Gaius, [made this] while alive for himself and [Gaius] Laecanius, freedman of Gaius, [---]
EDCS-04200224.summary: A funerary epitaph initiated by a freedman for himself and another freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200225.translation: Octavius Marcarius [dedicated this] to Caecilia Prima, his wife, to Octavia Proclia, his daughter, and to Diana, his granddaughter.
EDCS-04200225.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Octavius Marcarius to his wife, daughter, and granddaughter, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200226.translation: Caelia Hilara, freedwoman of Caius, ordered this to be made by her will for herself and for Berulla, her freedwoman.
EDCS-04200226.summary: This funerary epitaph records a burial arrangement made by Caelia Hilara in her will for herself and her freedwoman, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200227.translation: Caesia Secunda, daughter of Caius, while alive, made this for herself and for her father Caio Caesio Maximo, her mother Sociae Maximae, her sister Caesiae Paullinae, her brother Caesio Sabino, and for Phaedimus, the beloved pet, according to her will.
EDCS-04200227.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Caesia Secunda for herself and her family members, including a pet, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200228.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Valeria placed this for her husband Callio Crispino, who well deserved it.
EDCS-04200228.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Callio Crispino, dedicated by his wife Valeria, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200229.translation: For Calvius Fidentinus, dearest husband, with whom I lived 30 years without fault. Septilia Priscilla, for her unparalleled husband.
EDCS-04200229.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife dedicated to her husband, recording their years of marriage, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200230.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Vinucia Primigenia [dedicates this] to her husband Marcus Caninius Verus.
EDCS-04200230.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife to her deceased husband.

EDCS-04200231.translation: Canuleia Clara and [she dedicates this] for herself.
EDCS-04200231.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Canuleia Clara for herself, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-04200232.translation: [She dedicates this] to Onesimus and to his wife Caonia Amanda.
EDCS-04200232.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a couple, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-04200233.translation: Capria Rutila, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made in her will, under the supervision of Flaminia Rutila, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04200233.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument or burial place established by a woman according to her will.

EDCS-04200234.translation: A burial plot of Publius Cassius Adiutor, and of his concubine Vibius Optata, and for themselves, sixteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-04200234.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot designated by Publius Cassius Adiutor for himself, his concubine, and others.

EDCS-04200235.translation: A burial plot of Publius Cassius Adiutor, and for themselves, sixteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-04200235.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot designated by Publius Cassius Adiutor for himself and potentially others.

EDCS-04200236.translation: Causorius and Causorius Malabanus, from their own peculium (private funds), saw to it that this monument was made for their tutors Causorius Felicissimus and Causoria Victoria.
EDCS-04200236.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by freedmen for their former masters (tutors), funded from their personal savings.

EDCS-04200237.translation: For Quintus Ceccedius Senecio, son of Quintus; for Quintus Ceccedius, son of Quintus, [---]; for Ceccedia Adventa, daughter of Quintus, according to the will.
EDCS-04200237.summary: A funerary epitaph listing multiple individuals, including one provision made by will, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200238.translation: To Claudius Maximus, son of Caius, [as] son-in-law.
EDCS-04200238.summary: This is likely a funerary dedication or memorial for a son-in-law.

EDCS-04200239.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Claudius Cervo, freedman of Ion [or his freedman].
EDCS-04200239.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a freedman named Claudius Cervo.

EDCS-04200240.translation: Lucius Cornelius, son of Gnaeus; Laecania Maxima, wife of Spurius. For his wife, who performed her duty to him alone in marriage, such that he grieved for her never but death.
EDCS-04200240.summary: A funerary epitaph by a husband mourning his deceased wife, emphasizing her unique devotion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200241.translation: Cornelius Calvus, a freedman, made [this] for himself while alive, and for Cornelia Ostila, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04200241.summary: This is a funerary monument established by a freedman for himself and his wife, who was also a freedwoman.

EDCS-04200242.summary: This inscription is a personal name, likely identifying a tombstone or a dedication made by Gaius Decius Augustalis.

EDCS-04200243.translation: Donatus, freedman of the emperor, and Annia Primitiva, while alive, set up this seat for themselves as the fruit of their labor.
EDCS-04200243.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument, a seat set up by a freedman and Annia Primitiva for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-04200244.translation: They set [it up] for their servant and for Felicio, her sister, aged 15.
EDCS-04200244.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument dedicated to a servant and her sister, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-04200245.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Euphrosyne, aged 32 years, 2 months, and 2 days, and [her daughter] aged 8 years, 10 months, her most devoted wife and daughter, whose death, after many miserable days, also claimed her mother.
EDCS-04200245.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Euphrosyne and her daughter, recording their ages and the tragic circumstances of their deaths, which implies a date in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200246.translation: Gaius Fannius Psalmus, while alive, made [this] for himself, for Fannia Noe, freedwoman of Gaius, his Juno, and for Fannia Prisca, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04200246.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument constructed by Gaius Fannius Psalmus for himself and his freedwomen, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200247.translation: Eutychus and Fortunata, while alive, set up this seat for themselves.
EDCS-04200247.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument, a seat set up by Eutychus and Fortunata for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-04200248.translation: To Felicitas, aged 19 years and 11 months. Cycnus [set this up] for Minerva Polensis, his most excellent wife.
EDCS-04200248.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph set up by Cycnus for his wife, Minerva Polensis, recording her age, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200249.translation: Quintus Fictorius Tertius, freedman of Quintus, for himself, for his mother Galgestia Auge, and for all his [family], in front 12 feet, in the field 16 feet.
EDCS-04200249.summary: This inscription records a funerary plot and its dimensions, dedicated by Quintus Fictorius Tertius for himself, his mother, and his family.

EDCS-04200250.translation: Titus Galgestes Martialis ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04200250.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating a burial monument was commissioned by Titus Galgestes Martialis through his will.

EDCS-04200251.translation: Lucius Gavilius Donicus and Iunia Claudia.
EDCS-04200251.summary: This inscription contains two personal names, Lucius Gavilius Donicus and Iunia Claudia, possibly indicating a joint dedication or tomb.

EDCS-04200252.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Gellius Primitius made this while alive for his parent, Quintus Gellius Spendophorus.
EDCS-04200252.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Quintus Gellius Primitius for his parent, Quintus Gellius Spendophorus, indicating it was built during the parent's lifetime.

EDCS-04200253.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Geminius Thallus made this while alive for his daughter, Gemina Hygia, aged 13, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200253.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Geminius Thallus for his deceased daughter Gemina Hygia, who died at 13, and also for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200254.summary: This inscription is a bilingual greeting in Greek and Latin to Glycera, likely a personal dedication or marker.

EDCS-04200255.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Gracinus Exsuperatus, most excellent and most dutiful; his sister Mecenia Secundina [dedicated this].
EDCS-04200255.summary: A funerary dedication to Gracinus Exsuperatus by his sister.

EDCS-04200256.translation: To Hectice, my blameless wife; Eutyches made this tomb for Minerva and himself while alive.
EDCS-04200256.summary: A funerary dedication for Hectice, made by her husband Eutyches.

EDCS-04200257.translation: To Hedytera, dearest, and to her son of 21 years.
EDCS-04200257.summary: A dedication to Hedytera and her son.

EDCS-04200259.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Marcus Helvius Crescentis; Marcus Helvius Hermias, his freedman, made this while alive.
EDCS-04200259.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcus Helvius Crescentis, made by his freedman.

EDCS-04200260.translation: [---] cresty, Heurema, who was alive, made [this].
EDCS-04200260.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription, likely set up by Heurema for herself.

EDCS-04200261.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Host[---].

EDCS-04200262.translation: Hostilia Calliste, his sister, made this while alive for Titus Hostilius Callistus, freedman of Titus, aged 27.
EDCS-04200262.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Hostilia Calliste for her brother, Titus Hostilius Callistus, who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-04200264.translation: Iliona, freedwoman of [---], made this while alive for herself and her family.
EDCS-04200264.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iliona, a freedwoman, for herself and her family.

EDCS-04200265.translation: The monument of Iulius Hermeros: 20.5 feet in front, 40.5 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200265.summary: An inscription defining the dimensions of a plot of land for a monument belonging to Iulius Hermeros.

EDCS-04200266.translation: Iulia Matrona erected this for Aurelius Aquilinus, her partner, with whom she lived for 22 years without any complaint, a deserving recipient.
EDCS-04200266.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iulia Matrona for her partner Aurelius Aquilinus, commemorating their 22 years of harmonious life together.

EDCS-04200267.summary: A dedication to Chrestus by Laecania.

EDCS-04200268.translation: To Gaius Laecanius Simonis, freedman Catagraphus, I made this for myself and my family: for Laecania Prophas, my wife, and Laecania Ephyre, my daughter and freedwoman, and Grapte, my daughter, and Tryphaena, my daughter, and Rhodope, my daughter, and Heus, my son, and Hedynoe, my daughter; to Tryphaena, my mother, and Diogenes, my brother, and my dearest friends who wish to come here; let them come on their own day and rest.
EDCS-04200268.summary: A lengthy funerary epitaph for Gaius Laecanius Simonis, his family, friends, and freedmen, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200269.translation: To Gaius Laecanius Horeus; Licinia Nephele of her own accord.
EDCS-04200269.summary: A dedication to Gaius Laecanius Horeus by Licinia Nephele.

EDCS-04200270.translation: Laecania Clementia, mother, made [this] for Laecania Phronoe.
EDCS-04200270.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Laecania Clementia for her daughter, Laecania Phronoe.

EDCS-04200271.translation: To Publius Laecanius Rufus, my son.
EDCS-04200271.summary: A dedication to Publius Laecanius Rufus, likely by a parent.

EDCS-04200272.summary: This is a personal name, likely appearing as a dedicator or the subject of an inscription.

EDCS-04200273.translation: Laetania Attice, freedwoman of Gaius, wife of Gaius Vibius Fuscus, a freedman, is buried here.
EDCS-04200273.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Laetania Attice, a freedwoman and wife of a freedman.

EDCS-04200276.translation: Peticius Ingenuus, while alive, made this for himself and for his freedwoman Laecania Servanda, and for his son Lucius Peticius Maximus, and for his mother Laecania Secunda, and for his sister Septimia Faustae. For Felici, a recruit (?), 11 feet in front, 11 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04200276.summary: This is a tomb inscription detailing the burials of multiple family members and a freedwoman, commissioned by Peticius Ingenuus while alive, with specific plot dimensions.

EDCS-04200277.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gaius Laecanius Agathocles made this for Gaius Laecanius Valens, who deserved well.
EDCS-04200277.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Gaius Laecanius Agathocles for Gaius Laecanius Valens, indicating a familial or patronal relationship.

EDCS-04200278.translation: To the Divine Shades. I was formerly a servant girl of Laelia Onesime.
EDCS-04200278.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for a former servant girl dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-04200279.translation: Marcus Liburnius Anchialus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04200279.summary: This is a personal name, identifying Marcus Liburnius Anchialus as a freedman.

EDCS-04200280.translation: Marcus Lurius Zosimus, freedman, made this for his patron Marcus Lurius Hyalisus, his freedwoman Luria Spe, and his son Marcus Lurius Zosimus.
EDCS-04200280.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Lurius Zosimus dedicating a monument to his patron, freedwoman, and son.

EDCS-04200281.translation: Manilia Paula set up this eternal home from her own savings for herself and for Aelius Paulinus, her partner.
EDCS-04200281.summary: This is an epitaph where Manilia Paula dedicated a burial structure from her savings for herself and her partner, Aelius Paulinus.

EDCS-04200283.translation: Lucius Marcius Pamphilus Firmilius Primus, freedman of Sabinus.
EDCS-04200283.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Marcius Pamphilus Firmilius Primus, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-04200284.translation: To the departed spirits. Maximo, my son, 17 years old. He made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-04200284.summary: This funerary epitaph records a father's dedication to his son Maximo, who died at 17 years old.

EDCS-04200286.translation: To Melaina, daughter of Veturia Vene.
EDCS-04200286.summary: This inscription records the name Melaina, daughter of Veturia Vene, possibly as a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-04200287.summary: This is an incomplete personal name, likely Quintus Mucius Pylades, appearing on a monument.

EDCS-04200288.translation: Lucius made this for his son, Nephele, freedwoman of Antistia, who deserved very well of him.
EDCS-04200288.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius dedicating a monument to his son Nephele, who was a freedwoman of Antistia.

EDCS-04200289.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Obellia Maxima.

EDCS-04200290.translation: To the departed spirits. To Oclatia Chreste. Oclatius Hiaeronimus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-04200290.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Oclatia Chreste, dedicated by Oclatius Hiaeronimus.

EDCS-04200291.translation: and for Gaius Octavius Castus, son of Gaius, son and [---
EDCS-04200291.summary: This inscription appears to be part of a larger dedication, naming Gaius Octavius Castus and his father.

EDCS-04200292.translation: Publius Oppius Vulsor and his wife Iuliana, working with one spirit, placed this monument for us with one spirit.
EDCS-04200292.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Publius Oppius Vulsor and his wife Iuliana for themselves.

EDCS-04200293.translation: To the spirits of Rufilla, wife of Caius Caeparius Alcatus, Nothus Tiberius Erucius Nostimus [dedicated this] to his wife, aged 18.
EDCS-04200293.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Nothus Tiberius Erucius Nostimus to his wife Rufilla, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-04200294.translation: To Libanius, my comrade; to Palpellius Trophimus, mother; to Salvius, brother; to Chrysidis, sister; to Valens, brother; to Mutillia Tertia, sister.
EDCS-04200294.summary: This inscription lists several family members and comrades, likely as part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-04200295.translation: Lucius Papirius Maximus made this while alive for his most dutiful mother Papiria Rhodos and for Titus Flavius Narcissus.
EDCS-04200295.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Papirius Maximus for his mother Papiria Rhodos and Titus Flavius Narcissus.

EDCS-04200296.translation: Papiria Prima, while alive, placed this for herself for the departed spirits.
EDCS-04200296.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Papiria Prima for herself.

EDCS-04200297.translation: To Papiria Rufina, freedwoman of Gaius. Papirius Probus, her husband, [made this].
EDCS-04200297.summary: This funerary epitaph records Papirius Probus dedicating a monument to his wife, Papiria Rufina.

EDCS-04200298.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from a tomb, for Marcus Pollentius, possibly dedicated by a Pollentia.

EDCS-04200299.translation: To the departed spirits. To Publius Pollentius Geminus, 2 years and 9 months and 28 days old. Pollentius Processus and Rufia Hilaritas, his parents, set this up.
EDCS-04200299.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication of a monument by parents, Pollentius Processus and Rufia Hilaritas, to their young son, Publius Pollentius Geminus.

EDCS-04200301.translation: Pompullienus, son of Quintus Secundus, ordered by his will that this be made for himself and for his freedwoman concubine Optata.
EDCS-04200301.summary: This is a funerary inscription, indicated to be set up by will, for Pompullienus and his concubine Optata.

EDCS-04200305.translation: Processus, 22 years old. This monument will not be followed by an heir. In front 30 feet, in the field 41 feet.
EDCS-04200305.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a tomb and states that it is not to be inherited, likely concerning a burial plot for Processus.

EDCS-04200306.translation: To [my] dutiful daughter. Publicius Myrinus made this.
EDCS-04200306.summary: This funerary epitaph records Publicius Myrinus dedicating a monument to his dutiful daughter.

EDCS-04200308.translation: To the departed spirits. For Salaminus, slave of Augustus, for himself and his children Eufrosinus and Gemellina, and for Calliopena, his wife. Silvinus, slave of Augustus, took care that an altar be placed for them.
EDCS-04200308.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Silvinus, slave of Augustus, to his family including Salaminus, his children, and wife Calliopena.

EDCS-04200309.translation: To the departed spirits of Caius Saturnius Hermias, from Caius Settidius Zosimus, his friend.
EDCS-04200309.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Caius Settidius Zosimus to his friend Caius Saturnius Hermias.

EDCS-04200311.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Sempronius Polycletus, Publius Antistius Proculus, the son, made this for Laecania Danae.
EDCS-04200311.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Publius Antistius Proculus for Lucius Sempronius Polycletus and Laecania Danae.

EDCS-04200312.translation: Sergia Flavia Lusiana set up this complete monument for me and for Quintus Flavius Lusianus, my dearest grandson by my son, who was my brother's most loving husband.
EDCS-04200312.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Sergia Flavia Lusiana for herself and her grandson Quintus Flavius Lusianus, also commemorating her late husband.

EDCS-04200313.translation: To the departed spirits of Caius Servilius Didimus, freedman of Caius, and of his son Caius Servilius Frequens.
EDCS-04200313.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Caius Servilius Didimus and his son Caius Servilius Frequens.

EDCS-04200314.translation: Gaius Servilius Propolus, while alive, made this for himself and for his wife Cominia Iustina. In front 15 feet, in the field 13+ feet. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04200314.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and boundary marker set up by Gaius Servilius Propolus for himself and his wife, likely in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04200315.translation: To Servillia Methe, for herself and for her husband Gaius Ussius Mansuetus, and for her daughter Servillia Libas, and for her freedwoman Phyllis.
EDCS-04200315.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Servillia Methe to herself and her family members, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-04200316.translation: To the freedman of Gaius Settidius Firmus, Ianuarius. (Text is fragmentary and difficult to fully interpret).
EDCS-04200316.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to record an individual named Ianuarius, a freedman of Gaius Settidius Firmus, with unclear further details, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200317.translation: For Eusebia, 12 years old. Settidia Agrypne, to her most devoted daughter.
EDCS-04200317.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eusebia, a young girl, set up by her mother Settidia Agrypne, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200318.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aelia Creste set up this altar to her dearest friend, Callityche.
EDCS-04200318.summary: This is a funerary altar dedicated by Aelia Creste to her beloved friend Callityche, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200319.translation: To Settidia Heliad, Settidius Helias (dedicates this).
EDCS-04200319.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Settidius Helias to Settidia Heliad, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200320.translation: Stipia, mother, made this for her son Pupinia Statio.
EDCS-04200320.summary: This funerary inscription records a mother, Stipia, dedicating a monument to her son, Pupinia Statio, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04200321.translation: The place of the monument of Thias, freedman of Publius Sulpicius, is twelve feet in front; for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200321.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of twelve feet for Thias, freedman of Publius Sulpicius, and his family, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04200322.translation: To Cinnamus, freedman of Theseus, freedman of the deified Augustus, and fellow freedman.
EDCS-04200322.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Cinnamus to another freedman, also named Theseus, who was a freedman of the deified Augustus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200323.translation: Theseus, slave of our emperor, and Ianuaria, his wife, made (this) while alive for his most devoted sister.
EDCS-04200323.summary: This funerary inscription records Theseus, a slave of the emperor, and his wife Ianuaria, dedicating a monument to his sister, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200324.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication to an individual named Theseus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200325.translation: To Threptus, aged 5 years, 11 months, and 0 days. Vibius Threptus and Vibiae Eucariae. (This monument) was made by Eucaria, his sister, alive. Farewell.
EDCS-04200325.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a child named Threptus, and the monument was erected by his sister Eucaria, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04200326.translation: To Toria Agrippina, from her husband Nigidius Capito, for a short time.
EDCS-04200326.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Nigidius Capito to his wife Toria Agrippina, indicating a brief marriage, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200327.translation: Gaius Turpilius Chryseros, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-04200327.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Gaius Turpilius Chryseros, a freedman.

EDCS-04200329.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His mother Histria set this up for her son Valentino, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-04200329.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Histria for her son Valentino, who died at age 16, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200330.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The slave of Minerva Polensis, while alive, made this for his wife Valentiana.
EDCS-04200330.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a slave dedicated to his wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200331.translation: Quintus Valerius Tertius, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-04200331.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Quintus Valerius Tertius, a freedman.

EDCS-04200332.translation: To the spirits and to the Genius of Publius Vatrius Severus.
EDCS-04200332.summary: This is a dedication to the spirits of the departed and the Genius of Publius Vatrius Severus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200333.translation: Gaius Vectius Pedo, son of Gaius, 14 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200333.summary: This inscription likely records land dimensions associated with Gaius Vectius Pedo.

EDCS-04200334.translation: For him, Lucius Vettius, Epaphra of Pollentia, himself and his family; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04200334.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Lucius Vettius, Epaphra of Pollentia, and their family.

EDCS-04200335.translation: Gaius Vibius Dioclis and his daughter Vibius Myrsine, 24 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200335.summary: This inscription likely records land dimensions associated with Gaius Vibius Dioclis and his daughter Vibius Myrsine.

EDCS-04200336.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Vibius Lupus, aged 16 years and 15 days. Lucius Vibius Polensis and Mindia Lupa, his most unhappy parents, erected this while alive.
EDCS-04200336.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vibius Lupus, erected by his parents.

EDCS-04200337.translation: Vibius Protocetus erected this while alive, who lived...
EDCS-04200337.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Vibius Protocetus erected his own monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200338.translation: Gaius Vibius Tertius, from the entrance.
EDCS-04200338.summary: This inscription likely identifies Gaius Vibius Tertius and potentially his position or role.

EDCS-04200341.translation: Lucius Heraclius Pasocres erected this for Vibius Athenaidis, who deserved well.
EDCS-04200341.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Heraclius Pasocres honoring Vibius Athenaidis.

EDCS-04200342.translation: Hetoeme, freedwoman of Vibia. Lucius Clodius Maximus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04200342.summary: This inscription names Hetoeme, a freedwoman of Vibia, and Lucius Clodius Maximus.

EDCS-04200343.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Publius Antonius Hilarus to his most dutiful mother, Vibiae Trofimeni.
EDCS-04200343.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Publius Antonius Hilarus for his mother.

EDCS-04200344.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Settidius Securus to his deserving wife, Vicuria Onesimeni.
EDCS-04200344.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caius Settidius Securus for his wife.

EDCS-04200346.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Ulpius Varceius made this, while alive, for his dearest brother, Marcus Ulpio Quadrato Provinciali, and for himself.
EDCS-04200346.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Ulpius Varceius for his brother and himself.

EDCS-04200347.translation: A memorial for Zosimus, incomparable husband, who lived 22 years, 7 months, 7 days, to those who deserved well.
EDCS-04200347.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Zosimus, husband, with details of his life and a dedication to those deserving.

EDCS-04200351.translation: [...]elius, son of Caius, made this while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200351.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Elius, son of Caius, erected the monument for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200352.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Luci, a freedwoman belonging to Deci.

EDCS-04200355.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For [---]menetus, son of [---]ectus. [---]ilius Eu-
EDCS-04200355.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200356.summary: This inscription appears to record dedications to Clarae and her freedman.

EDCS-04200357.translation: Lucius Annius [---]lo, freedman of Lucius, while alive, made this for her husband. In front 12 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-04200357.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and boundary marker set up by Lucius Annius' freedman for her husband, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200360.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Marcello, my wife.
EDCS-04200360.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Marcello, wife of the dedicator.

EDCS-04200366.summary: This inscription records the name Cutlanus, a freedman of Numerius, followed by another name or part of a name.

EDCS-04200369.translation: [...]mus, freedman of Vibus, [son?], 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200369.summary: This inscription records the name of a freedman and specifies land dimensions, likely related to a property boundary or burial plot.

EDCS-04200370.summary: This inscription records that Lucius and Macer were the makers of this monument.

EDCS-04200390.translation: Thomas the tribune dedicated [this] in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04200390.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Thomas, a tribune, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04200394.translation: A sanctuary to Fortuna, begun by Gaius Vibius Varus the father, Quintus Caesius Macrinus completed and dedicated it.
EDCS-04200394.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a sanctuary to Fortuna, noting completion and dedication by Quintus Caesius Macrinus after it was begun by his father, Gaius Vibius Varus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200395.translation: A sanctuary to Histria, begun by Gaius Vibius Varus the father, Quintus Caesius Macrinus completed and dedicated it.
EDCS-04200395.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a sanctuary to Histria, noting completion and dedication by Quintus Caesius Macrinus after it was begun by his father, Gaius Vibius Varus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200397.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Laevinia, daughter of Gaius, Sabina.
EDCS-04200397.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Laevinia, daughter of Gaius, named Sabina.

EDCS-04200398.translation: Quintus Sergius and Sextia R[---], most unhappy parents, set this up for their son, as was permissible for parents to do for their children who died prematurely.
EDCS-04200398.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by grieving parents for their deceased son.

EDCS-04200399.translation: Titus Annius Gallio, freedman of Titus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04200399.summary: This inscription records Titus Annius Gallio, a freedman, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04200400.translation: Titus Fabius erected this for his brother Gaius Fabius, a veteran of the Eleventh Legion, with twenty-eight years of service.
EDCS-04200400.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a brother for his deceased sibling, a veteran of the Eleventh Legion.

EDCS-04200401.translation: Sons made [this] for Gaius Vibius Salvius, freedman of Gaius, and for Salvia, his freedwoman fellow-slave.
EDCS-04200401.summary: This inscription records sons dedicating a monument to their freedman father and his fellow freedwoman.

EDCS-04200402.translation: Annia Tertia, daughter of Titus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04200402.summary: This inscription records Annia Tertia, daughter of Titus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04200403.translation: Publius Caledius, son of Gaius, and Mussia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, while alive, made [this] for themselves and their family: Gaius Caledius, father; Publia Gnoia, mother; the fathers of Secunda, Lucius Mussius, Gaius, Titus, Marcus Mussius; their mothers Clausia and their brothers.
EDCS-04200403.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a couple, Publius Caledius and Mussia Secunda, who built a tomb for themselves and their extended family, including parents and siblings, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200404.translation: Marcus Hostilius Crestus made [this] for himself while alive.
EDCS-04200404.summary: This inscription records Marcus Hostilius Crestus commissioning his own monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200406.translation: Laelia Maxima, daughter of Gaius, aged 100.
EDCS-04200406.summary: A funerary epitaph for Laelia Maxima, recording her name, parentage, and age.

EDCS-04200407.summary: A funerary epitaph for Opiaus Reviarius, recording his name and age.

EDCS-04200408.translation: Valeria Tertia, daughter of Publius, mother of Lucius [---] Proqu[---], aged 17, [set this up].
EDCS-04200408.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Tertia, recording her parentage and her relationship to a deceased youth.

EDCS-04200409.translation: Lucius Vibius Canalius, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe, aged 50.
EDCS-04200409.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Vibius Canalius, recording his name, parentage, tribal affiliation, and age.

EDCS-04200410.translation: Titus Avilius Proculus ordered this to be made for himself and for Iulia Ianuar(ia).
EDCS-04200410.summary: A funerary epitaph commissioned by Titus Avilius Proculus for himself and Iulia Ianuar(ia).

EDCS-04200411.translation: Gaius Valerius Priscus, a cloth merchant from Aquileia, dedicated this.
EDCS-04200411.summary: An epitaph for Gaius Valerius Priscus, identified as a cloth merchant from Aquileia.

EDCS-04200412.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Publius Veturis Silvestris. His father made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200412.summary: This is a funerary inscription where a father dedicated a monument to his son, Publius Veturis Silvestris, and for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200413.translation: Sacred to the Genius of Liber Augustus. Lucius Salonius Severus [dedicated this].
EDCS-04200413.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Salonius Severus to the Genius of Liber Augustus.

EDCS-04200414.translation: Carminia Prisca, daughter of Lucius, from Histria, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04200414.summary: A votive inscription by Carminia Prisca, likely dedicated to a deity, from the Roman province of Histria.

EDCS-04200415.translation: Titus Abudius Verus dedicated this to Neptune and the August Deities after his term as sub-prefect of the Ravenna fleet, having restored the temple, constructed buildings, improved his house, on an area granted to him by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04200415.summary: A dedication to Neptune and the August Deities by Titus Abudius Verus, commemorating his accomplishments after his naval command and detailing the civic honors he received.

EDCS-04200418.text_edition: \n Caio Praecellio Gai filio Papiria Augurino Vettio Festo Crispiniano Vibio Vero Cassiano clarissimo iuveni triumviro capitali tribuno legionis VII gaeminae sic patrono splendidissimae coloniae Aquileiensium et Parentinorum Opiterginorum Hemonensium ordo et pleps sic Parentinorum aere collato locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200418.translation: To Gaius Praecellius Augurinus Vettius Festus Crispinianus Vibius Verus Cassianus, son of Gaius, a most distinguished youth, vigintivir of the mint, tribune of the Seventh Gemina legion, and patron of the most splendid colonies of Aquileia, Parentium, and Opitergium, the order and people of Parentium, by pooling their money, granted this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04200418.summary: A dedication of a public space to a distinguished young man, Gaius Praecellius Augurinus Vettius Festus Crispinianus Vibius Verus Cassianus, by the community of Parentium, recognizing his patron status.

EDCS-04200420.translation: Veturia made this monument for her husband Marcus Lucius Maximus, and for her son Publius and Gaius, and for her grandson Aurelius Titinius Veturia, a most rare one; he will not follow an heir. In front 20 feet, in the field [unknown number] feet.
EDCS-04200420.summary: A funerary monument erected by Veturia for her husband and grandson, specifying burial plot dimensions and prohibiting an heir from inheriting.

EDCS-04200422.text_edition: \n Lucio Cantio Luci filio Lemonia Septimino equo publico flamini patrono coloniae luliae Parentinorum curiali veteri Parentii omnibus honoribus municipalibus functo praefecto et patrono collegii fabrum plebs aere conlato dono dedit\n
EDCS-04200422.translation: To Lucius Cantius, son of Lucius, of the Lemonia tribe, Septiminus, who, as an eques publicus, served as flamen and patron of the colony of Parentium, and as a former town councillor of Parentium, having held all municipal offices, and as prefect and patron of the guild of smiths, the plebs, by means of a collection of money, dedicated this.
EDCS-04200422.summary: A public monument erected by the plebs of Parentium to honor Lucius Cantius, a local official and patron of the guild of smiths.

EDCS-04200423.summary: A simple funerary inscription identifying Gratus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04200424.translation: Cnaeus Flavius Eros, a magistrate of the Augustales (a college of priests serving the imperial cult), made this for Cnaeus Flavius Secundus, also a magistrate of the Augustales.
EDCS-04200424.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Cnaeus Flavius Eros to Cnaeus Flavius Secundus, both members of the Augustales college.

EDCS-04200425.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Vero, son of Sextus Fulcinius, of the Velina tribe, a decurion, aged 14 years and 37 days. The most dutiful town council, by its decree, ordered a public funeral for him and for the state [provided] three pounds of incense; all unanimously voted that the public notice be displayed. Also, the college of craftsmen had the honor of sending incense, who left behind his miserable, aged parents in mourning. His parents, while alive, erected this for their most dutiful son and for themselves.
EDCS-04200425.summary: A funerary inscription for Vero, a young decurion, detailing the public honors and funeral arrangements decreed by the town council and a craftsmen's guild, and stating that his parents erected it while alive.

EDCS-04200427.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Sempronius Succesinus, the Roman knight. Marcus Sempronius [likely the father or relative].
EDCS-04200427.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Sempronius Succesinus, a Roman knight, with a partial mention of another Marcus Sempronius.

EDCS-04200428.translation: Tychius, freedman of Gaius Servilius Pansa, a magistrate of the Augustales, made this for himself and his family. Servilia ordered it to be made in her will.
EDCS-04200428.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Tychius, a freedman and Augustalis magistrate, for his family, as stipulated in Servilia's will.

EDCS-04200431.translation: To the divine spirits. Iunius Aprio made this for his most holy wife Aelia Fortunata, and for himself and his descendants, while alive.
EDCS-04200431.summary: A tombstone set up by Iunius Aprio for his wife Aelia Fortunata and himself, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200432.summary: A simple funerary inscription identifying Marcus Balbius, son of Publius.

EDCS-04200433.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Caledius Satius, freedman of Gaius, [son?] io Calc Dressiu nis. Titus Caledius Maximus, his heir, [had this made] for Basso Ser.
EDCS-04200433.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Caledius Satius and Titus Caledius Maximus, mentioning an heir and likely a relative named Basso.

EDCS-04200434.translation: [...], freedman of Flavius, Cladus. In front 90 feet.
EDCS-04200434.summary: A funerary inscription mentioning Cladus, a freedman of Flavius, and specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-04200436.translation: To his wife, Episidia, daughter of Lucius, called Tertia.
EDCS-04200436.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a wife.

EDCS-04200437.translation: Caius Fabius Clarus made this while alive; 12 feet in front, [and] --- feet in the field.
EDCS-04200437.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land, likely funerary, made by Caius Fabius Clarus.

EDCS-04200440.translation: Lucius Ta Genialis to Cornelia Ia, his wife; 30 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200440.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land, likely funerary, dedicated by Lucius Ta Genialis to his wife.

EDCS-04200441.summary: This is a fragmentary personal identification, likely part of a longer inscription.

EDCS-04200442.translation: To Matidiania, daughter of Caius, most beloved. O...
EDCS-04200442.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication to Matidiania.

EDCS-04200443.translation: Publius Modius Celer for himself and for Modia Cybele, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04200443.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to a freedwoman by Publius Modius Celer.

EDCS-04200444.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, Sabina, daughter of Aulus, brothers.
EDCS-04200444.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication to Sabina by her brothers.

EDCS-04200445.translation: Titus Pomponius Maximus, son of Titus; Publius Pomponius Constans, son of Titus; Pomponius Celer, son of Titus, made this.
EDCS-04200445.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by three brothers, sons of Titus Pomponius.

EDCS-04200446.translation: Myrtis, freedwoman of a woman, made this while alive for herself, and for her most beloved husband Lucius Titidius Olympos, and for her son Lucius Titidius Maximus.
EDCS-04200446.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Myrtis for herself, her husband, and her son.

EDCS-04200447.translation: Tussidia Storge made this while alive for herself.
EDCS-04200447.summary: This is a self-dedication made by Tussidia Storge.

EDCS-04200448.translation: Volginia Secunda, daughter of Publius, (a dedication or tombstone).
EDCS-04200448.summary: An incomplete funerary or dedicatory inscription for Volginia Secunda, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-04200449.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Priscinus [made this] for his most unfortunate [daughter/wife/relative] who lived for 14 years.
EDCS-04200449.summary: A funerary epitaph for a deceased female who lived to be 14 years old, erected by Priscinus. The exact relationship is not specified but implies a mourning family member. The inscription is likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200453.translation: Fausta, a distinguished woman, made 90 feet with her dependants; Claudia, a devout woman, with her granddaughter Honoria, made 90 feet for her vow; Basilia, a devout woman, made 90 feet with her dependants.
EDCS-04200453.summary: This inscription records three women, Fausta, Claudia, and Basilia, each dedicating a section of 90 feet, possibly for a building project or public work, with Claudia fulfilling a vow. The mention of 'religiosa femina' suggests a religious context, and the inscription likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200454.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Crescens, assistant clerk, and Aurelia Sabina, devoted parents, made [this] for their son Marcus Aurelius Amandus, aged 4 years.
EDCS-04200454.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy, Marcus Aurelius Amandus, erected by his grieving parents, Crescens and Aurelia Sabina, who held the position of 'adiutor tabulariorum'. The inscription is from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200456.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Parthenopeo Augusti dispensatori vernae Festa coniuncx sic et Mercurialis vir eius bene merenti fecerunt\n
EDCS-04200456.translation: To the divine spirits. His wife Festa, and his husband Mercurialis, made this for Parthenopoeus, a freedman steward of Augustus, who deserved well.
EDCS-04200456.summary: A tombstone erected by Festa and Mercurialis for Parthenopoeus, an imperial freedman steward, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200457.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Ianuarius, assistant clerk of our Emperor, arranged for the making [of this monument] for Ianuaria, his most devoted mother.
EDCS-04200457.summary: A funerary epitaph commissioned by Ianuarius, an assistant clerk to the Emperor, for his devoted mother, Ianuaria. The inscription indicates a Roman Imperial date due to the mention of the Emperor and the official's title.

EDCS-04200458.translation: [... for] the most innocent and most holy treasurer of our Caesar, well deserving.
EDCS-04200458.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be part of a dedication or funerary monument for an official ('dispensator') serving the Emperor ('Caesar'). The description 'innocentissimo et sanctissimo bene merenti' suggests a person of high moral standing and merit, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200459.translation: To the divine spirits. Dorcas made this for Donatus, her husband.
EDCS-04200459.summary: A tombstone made by Dorcas for her husband Donatus, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200460.translation: Aurelia Suefia made this tomb for her most loving and dearest husband Flavius Ursicinus, a centurion of the imperial stable, for him.
EDCS-04200460.summary: A tombstone commissioned by Aurelia Suefia for her husband Flavius Ursicinus, a centurion of the imperial stable, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-04200461.translation: Of Gaius Tocernius Maximianus, soldier of the II Italica legion, with 5 years of service, scribe to the consular governor, aged 23 years, 8 months, and 6 days. His father, Gaius Tocernius Hermeros, (erected this) for his dearest son.
EDCS-04200461.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Tocernius Maximianus, a young soldier and scribe, erected by his father, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-04200463.translation: Manis Plotus, son of Manis, of the Pupinia tribe, having the power of an aedile, made this for himself and for his wife Voluntilia Prisca, daughter of Marcus, while alive.
EDCS-04200463.summary: A tombstone erected by Manis Plotus for himself and his wife Voluntilia Prisca, possibly from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04200464.translation: Voluntilia Paulla, alive, made this for Publius Valerius Tiron, son of Publius, son of Publius, of the Pupinia tribe, a husband of a duovir, and for her son Publius Valerius, son of Publius, of the Pupinia tribe.
EDCS-04200464.summary: A tombstone erected by Voluntilia Paulla for her husband Publius Valerius, a duovir, and their son Publius Valerius Tiron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200465.translation: Lucius Calpurnius Cupitus made this for himself, and for his son Lucius Calpurnius Dexter, aged 18 years, and for his wife Calpurnia Procula, daughter of Spurius.
EDCS-04200465.summary: A tombstone commissioned by Lucius Calpurnius Cupitus for himself, his son Lucius Calpurnius Dexter, and his wife Calpurnia Procula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200467.translation: Gaius Clepius Senecio, son of Titus, of the Pupinia tribe, made this (monument) for himself while alive, and for his father Titus Clepius Tommus, and for his mother Clepia Menda, daughter of Spurius, and for his wife Coelia Secunda, daughter of Spurius, and for his niece Tertia, daughter of Quirquis. And for any of my kin who shall be named Clepius, I grant this place for burial, and likewise a place for the bones.
EDCS-04200467.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Clepius Senecio for himself and various relatives, specifying burial rights.

EDCS-04200468.translation: To the departed spirits. Dionysius had this made for his most innocent grandson Paramytho, 10 years, 11 days old.
EDCS-04200468.summary: A funerary dedication for a young child, Dionysius, by his grandfather, specifying the child's age.

EDCS-04200469.translation: Titus Cornelius Felix is buried here. Maecia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, placed (this).
EDCS-04200469.summary: A tombstone indicating the burial of Titus Cornelius Felix and identifying Maecia Tertia as the person who placed it.

EDCS-04200470.translation: Gaius Plotius, son of Manius, of the Pupinia tribe. The monument's area is 50 feet in front and 50 feet in the field.
EDCS-04200470.summary: An inscription specifying the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Gaius Plotius.

EDCS-04200471.translation: Sextus Pompeius Verus made this while alive for his wife Grania Serena and his daughter Pompeia Vera.
EDCS-04200471.summary: A funerary monument erected by Sextus Pompeius Verus for his wife and daughter during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200472.translation: Marcus Pomponius Theudatus, son of Titus Siccus, while alive, and his wife, while alive.
EDCS-04200472.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Pomponius Theudatus and his wife for themselves.

EDCS-04200473.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning several names, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory text.

EDCS-04200478.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Titus Blaesius Rusticus, aged 13 years, 5 months, and days, his most unfortunate parents, Blaesia Ane and Primigenius, [made this].
EDCS-04200478.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Blaesius Rusticus, who died at the age of 13 years, 5 months, and some days, erected by his grieving parents. The inscription is likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200479.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Cornelia Secundina, aged 40 years, and Cominius Optatus, her parents. Optatatus Junior made [this] for his father while he was alive, out of devotion.
EDCS-04200479.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelia Secundina and Cominius Optatus, likely parents of the dedicator Optatatus Junior, who erected the monument for his father while he was still alive. The inscription records a gesture of filial piety and dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200480.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph naming Cornelia Erotis, likely a deceased individual. The inscription is likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200481.translation: Gratus, his uncle, made [this] for Ascae [or Asca]...
EDCS-04200481.summary: This fragmented inscription records Gratus dedicating something, possibly a monument or gift, to 'Ascae' or 'Asca' using the term 'avunculus' (maternal uncle), indicating a familial relationship. The inscription likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200482.summary: This inscription identifies Entellus and Helena as colonists, likely marking property or a tomb, and dates to the Roman period.

EDCS-04200483.summary: A dedication or memorial inscription addressed to Vibius Polybius, with the text being incomplete.

EDCS-04200484.translation: Lucius Vinisius, son of Lucius, a veteran of the Ninth Legion Triumphalis, to his wife Vinusia Tertulla, daughter of Publius, and to his daughter [named] Vinusia Tertulla, aged 10.
EDCS-04200484.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Lucius Vinisius, a veteran of the Ninth Legion, and his wife and daughter.

EDCS-04200485.translation: Titus Ammaeus Priscus, son of Lucius, made this monument while alive for himself and for his wife Salluvia Secunda, daughter of Sextus. The monument's space is 15 feet in front and 16 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04200485.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Ammaeus Priscus for himself and his wife, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04200486.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Petronius Florentinus made this while alive for his excellent wife, Cosconia Sabina, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04200486.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Caius Petronius Florentinus to his wife, Cosconia Sabina.

EDCS-04200487.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Petronius Florentinus made this for his most dutiful son, Caius Petronius Florinus, aged 12.
EDCS-04200487.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Caius Petronius Florentinus to his son, Caius Petronius Florinus.

EDCS-04200488.translation: Metra Leuca, freedwoman of Publius, made this while alive for herself, and for Publius Metrus Felix, son of Publius, freedman, and for Publius Metrus Acastus, fellow freedman of Publius. The monument's space is 25 feet in front and 25 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04200488.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Metra Leuca, a freedwoman, for herself and two freedmen, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04200489.translation: Caius Sabennus Maximus, son of Caius, made this while alive for his wife Voltilia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, and for his mother Leucina Orfa, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200489.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Caius Sabennus Maximus for his wife, mother, and himself.

EDCS-04200491.translation: Publius Postumius Mato, freedman of Publius, and Postumia Cirrata, freedwoman of Publius, are living.
EDCS-04200491.summary: This inscription indicates that Publius Postumius Mato and Postumia Cirrata, both freedmen, are alive.

EDCS-04200492.translation: Favonia made this while alive for herself and (perhaps) her daughter Septimia Maxima, aged 20.
EDCS-04200492.summary: A funerary monument erected by Favonia for herself and possibly her deceased daughter.

EDCS-04200493.translation: Caius Flavius, freedman of Caius, is buried here.
EDCS-04200493.summary: This is a simple burial marker for Caius Flavius, a freedman.

EDCS-04200495.translation: While Florentia and our Lucilla Plautiana prospered, Silvina, a slavewoman, gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04200495.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Silvina, a slavewoman, for the well-being of her mistresses Florentia and Lucilla Plautiana.

EDCS-04200496.translation: Titus Statilius Taurus, son of Sisenna, made this while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200496.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Statilius Taurus for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200497.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a woman named Fasaca, providing her parentage and age.

EDCS-04200498.translation: To Maxsuma, his mother, and Valeria Tertia, his wife, Publius Posurnius [dedicated this].
EDCS-04200498.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Publius Posurnius to his mother and wife.

EDCS-04200499.translation: To Juno Feronia. Baria Secunda, daughter of Lucius, gave this temple, statue, and portico from her own funds.
EDCS-04200499.summary: A religious dedication of a temple, statue, and portico to Juno Feronia, funded by Baria Secunda.

EDCS-04200500.translation: Calpurnius, son of [3], of the Pupinia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04200500.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by will by a man named Calpurnius.

EDCS-04200503.translation: He lived 33 years, 10 months, and 6 days. Minicius Valerianus set this up for the deserving person.
EDCS-04200503.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and funerary monument of an unnamed individual, set up by Minicius Valerianus.

EDCS-04200504.translation: Lucius? Cornvinus, son of Caius, Tommus, while alive...
EDCS-04200504.summary: This inscription records an incomplete dedication or epitaph for Lucius? Cornvinus Tommus, set up by himself while alive.

EDCS-04200505.translation: To Lucius Mariarius, father, son of Sextus; to Vaxsonia, mother, daughter of Lucius, Voltiomna; to Sextus Mariarius, brother, son of Lucius; to Mariaria, sister, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04200505.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated to multiple family members: Lucius Mariarius, Vaxsonia Voltiomna, Sextus Mariarius, and Mariaria.

EDCS-04200506.translation: Gaius Valerius Gallus, son of Gaius // Lucius Valerius Cofius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04200506.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Gaius Valerius Gallus and Lucius Valerius Cofius, likely brothers, with their filiations.

EDCS-04200507.translation: To Lucius Flavius Maximus, son of Quintus, and Prisca, daughter of Velsonis Poccia. Marcus Flavius Maximus, son of Lucius, for his parents.
EDCS-04200507.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Flavius Maximus to his parents, Lucius Flavius Maximus and Prisca.

EDCS-04200508.translation: To Julia Secunda?, daughter of [ ], 21 years, 6 months old. Lucius Julius Chrestus and Flaemica Paullina, parents, made [this] while alive, and Tiberius Claudius Maritalis, husband, made [this] while alive, and for himself.
EDCS-04200508.summary: This is a funerary monument for Julia Secunda, set up by her parents and her husband, Tiberius Claudius Maritalis.

EDCS-04200509.translation: To Sestia Ursa, freedwoman of Severus. Sestia Spendusa made [this] for her mother.
EDCS-04200509.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument dedicated by Sestia Spendusa to her mother, Sestia Ursa.

EDCS-04200510.translation: To Volginia Marcella, freedwoman of Lucius; Lucius Aufidius Romulus; Titus Popillius Longus, son of Gaius; Lucius Aufidius Montanus.
EDCS-04200510.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, possibly indicating a dedication or a property transfer, with complex familial and freedman relationships.

EDCS-04200511.translation: To Silvanus Augustus. Gaius Aquilius Celer willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04200511.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Gaius Aquilius Celer to the god Silvanus Augustus.

EDCS-04200512.translation: Gaius Commius, son of Lucius; Commia Maxima; Acutia Tertia.
EDCS-04200512.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a family or a group, with no explicit dedication or relationship stated.

EDCS-04200514.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Oppius Severianus fulfilled [his] vow.
EDCS-04200514.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Oppius Severianus to Jupiter.

EDCS-04200515.translation: To Augusta Salus, for the safety of the people of Piquentum, Lucius Ventinaris Lucumo, having added a yoke, gladly and willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04200515.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the goddess Salus by Lucius Ventinaris Lucumo for the protection of the Piquentini.

EDCS-04200516.translation: To Silvanus, he fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04200516.summary: This is a simple votive inscription dedicating a monument to the god Silvanus.

EDCS-04200517.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Gallius Silvester, a soldier of the 2nd Praetorian cohort, ordered this to be made for himself and his parents for 4,000 sesterces by his will.
EDCS-04200517.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Gallius Silvester, a Praetorian guardsman, who arranged for his own and his parents' burial at his expense.

EDCS-04200518.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedwoman named Quinta.

EDCS-04200519.translation: To Marcus Agornicus, son of Caius, from Tabina(?).
EDCS-04200519.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph, likely to Marcus Agornicus, mentioning a place of origin.

EDCS-04200520.translation: For Gaius Boicus Avitus, 18 years old. Gaius Boicus Silvester and Lotticina Marcellina made this monument for themselves and while alive.
EDCS-04200520.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Boicus Silvester and Lotticina Marcellina for their son Gaius Boicus Avitus, and also for themselves.

EDCS-04200521.summary: This appears to be a fragmented funerary epitaph for Bouiada Liera.

EDCS-04200522.translation: Cassia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, 80 years old.
EDCS-04200522.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cassia Secunda, recording her name, parentage, and age.

EDCS-04200523.translation: Maximus, son, erected this monument while alive for his parents, Lucius Clangoco Adventus and his freedwoman Priscilla Maxima, and for Bouiada Maxima.
EDCS-04200523.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Maximus for his parents and another individual, Bouiada Maxima.

EDCS-04200524.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph to Lucius Fervallocus Pudentius.

EDCS-04200525.translation: Publius Flaminius Macer and Volginia Quincta, daughter of Lucius, lie here.
EDCS-04200525.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial place of Publius Flaminius Macer and Volginia Quincta.

EDCS-04200526.translation: To Gavillius, son of Caius, aged 20.
EDCS-04200526.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gavillius, son of Caius, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-04200527.translation: Graecinia Procula, daughter of Publius, aged 23.
EDCS-04200527.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Graecinia Procula, daughter of Publius, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-04200529.translation: Caius Labienus Potens restored the memorial of his father at his own expense.
EDCS-04200529.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a father's memorial by his son, Caius Labienus Potens.

EDCS-04200530.translation: Laepoca, daughter of Dommius [and] Laepoca, daughter of Metellus, Tuia [daughter of Metellus?].
EDCS-04200530.summary: This funerary inscription lists several individuals, likely family members, including two women named Laepoca and one named Tuia.

EDCS-04200531.translation: Gaius Laepocus Rufus, while alive, made this for himself and for his wife, Caesia Marcellina, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04200531.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Laepocus Rufus for himself and his wife, Caesia Marcellina.

EDCS-04200532.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription beginning with a dedication to Lucius Licinius.

EDCS-04200533.translation: To Lucius Mamilius Magaplinus, daughter of Spurius, [and] to Gemoni the wife of Capito, [her] resting place.
EDCS-04200533.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial places of Lucius Mamilius Magaplinus and his wife, Gemoni.

EDCS-04200534.translation: Megaplina Maximilla, while alive, made this for herself and for her daughter, Gemoni Marcella.
EDCS-04200534.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Megaplina Maximilla for herself and her daughter, Gemoni Marcella.

EDCS-04200535.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning an individual ending in '-aplina' and another name fragment.

EDCS-04200536.translation: Years XV. Years XII. Years II. Years III. Messius Laevicus, freedman of Lamber, aged 40. Years XIX. Ternila Laevica, freedwoman of Regilia, aged 32. Years XIV. Ovia Laevica, daughter of Domator, aged 67. Years XXXXV. Marcella Laepoca, daughter of [---], aged 30. Years XLII. Laevicus Hospolis, son of Lucius, aged 13. Years XXXIII. Sabina Laevica, daughter of Mercius, aged 56. Son, aged 25. Years XI. Gaius, son of [---]. Years VIII. Marxius Pletoris, son of [---]. Years III. Marxius Salus.
EDCS-04200536.summary: This funerary inscription lists the names and ages of several individuals, likely family members, and their relationship to each other, possibly from a tomb.

EDCS-04200537.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Mocolica.

EDCS-04200539.translation: Caius Patalicus, son of Tertius, aged 57. His brother Marcus placed this.
EDCS-04200539.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Caius Patalicus and indicates that his brother Marcus erected the monument.

EDCS-04200540.translation: Valens [placed this] for his parents, for himself, and for his wife Laepoca Tertulla, for Gaius Petronius, son of Lucius, and for Nevica Prisca.
EDCS-04200540.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Valens for his parents, himself, his wife, and two other individuals, Gaius Petronius and Nevica Prisca.

EDCS-04200541.translation: Hospita Petronia, daughter of Publius, aged 80.
EDCS-04200541.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Hospita Petronia.

EDCS-04200542.translation: Pletoronia Polla erected [this] for her most devoted parents, Lucius Pletoronius Luponi and Balbica Petala, and for her sister Balbica Phronime.
EDCS-04200542.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Pletoronia Polla for her parents and sister.

EDCS-04200543.translation: Lucius Sexticus, son of Lucius, aged 60. Ixiionia Caesuella, aged 60. His son(?) placed this.
EDCS-04200543.summary: This funerary inscription records the names and ages of Lucius Sexticus and Ixiionia Caesuella, with the monument placed by a son.

EDCS-04200545.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Tedia Marcella.

EDCS-04200546.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Tedia Prima is buried here.

EDCS-04200547.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Titacia Marcella.

EDCS-04200549.translation: Virtia Maxima made (this) for her father, Gaius Virtius Severus, while alive.
EDCS-04200549.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Virtia Maxima for her father, Gaius Virtius Severus.

EDCS-04200550.translation: For Volginia Tertia, daughter of Volsonius. Lucius Volginius Genialis (set this up) for his patroness, in memory. In front 15 feet, in the field 12 feet.
EDCS-04200550.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Volginius Genialis for his patroness, Volginia Tertia, with boundary measurements.

EDCS-04200551.translation: Voltilia Prisca, daughter of Caius, aged 20 years.
EDCS-04200551.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Voltilia Prisca, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-04200553.translation: To [Ab]alicus Maximus and Voranica Marcella, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04200553.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Abilicus Maximus and Voranica Marcella, indicating their parentage.

EDCS-04200560.translation: Ursus the priest adorned this small room for the holy church in the time of our lord Justinian, with Frugiferus as bishop, in the indiction after the consulship of Basilius.
EDCS-04200560.summary: This inscription records the embellishment of a church room by a priest named Ursus during the reign of Emperor Justinian and Bishop Frugiferus, dated by indiction and consulship.

EDCS-04200561.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Crescens made (this) for his stepson Anthimus, secretary of our Emperor, while alive, and for himself and his dearest wife, Flavia Felicitas.
EDCS-04200561.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Flavius Crescens for his stepson Anthimus and his wife Flavia Felicitas, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04200562.translation: To the departed spirits. Calpurnia Primigenia made (this) for her husband Lucius Plexinas Etruscus, and for herself.
EDCS-04200562.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Calpurnia Primigenia for her husband Lucius Plexinas Etruscus and for herself.

EDCS-04200563.text_edition: \n V vivus fecit sibi et Taricae Luci filiae Proculae\n
EDCS-04200563.translation: Made for himself and for Tarica Procula, daughter of Lucius, while alive.
EDCS-04200563.summary: This funerary monument was set up by an individual for himself and for Tarica Procula.

EDCS-04200564.translation: To Lucius Arius, son of Lucius, a praetorian soldier, aged 3[--]; To Gaius Arius, son of Lucius, [---].
EDCS-04200564.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two individuals, Lucius Arius, a soldier, and Gaius Arius, providing their parentage and some age details.

EDCS-04200565.translation: Quintus Ragonius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for Lucius Ragonius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, his brother, and for Lucius Ragonius, son of Lucius, nephew of his brother.
EDCS-04200565.summary: This funerary inscription specifies that Quintus Ragonius commissioned a tomb for himself, his brother Lucius, and his brother's nephew, Lucius, as stated in his will.

EDCS-04200566.translation: Publius Trosius, son of Gaius, of the Porcia tribe; Naevia Quarta, daughter of Publius, of the Fabia tribe; Trosia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, alive.
EDCS-04200566.summary: This inscription lists three individuals with their parentage, tribal affiliations, and marital status (Trosia Tertia is noted as alive), likely related to family or property.

EDCS-04200567.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Papius Marcellinus, a veteran of the First Italian Legion, made (this) for himself while alive, and for his wife Mu[---] Secundina, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-04200567.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Lucius Papius Marcellinus, a veteran of the First Italian Legion, for himself, his wife, and their descendants.

EDCS-04200568.translation: To Eucaerus, freedman of Titus Caesernius Macedo, aged 22, his father Helix made this.
EDCS-04200568.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Helix for his son Eucaerus, who was a freedman of Titus Caesernius Macedo and died at the age of 22.

EDCS-04200569.translation: Marcus Surinus, son of Marcus, of the Pupinia tribe.
EDCS-04200569.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of an individual, Marcus Surinus.

EDCS-04200570.text_edition: \n Isidi sacrum ex monitu eius dono dedit Lucius Valerius Memor VIvir Augustalis locus datus publice\n
EDCS-04200570.translation: A sacred offering to Isis, given by Lucius Valerius Memor, VIvir Augustalis, at her instruction; the site was granted publicly.
EDCS-04200570.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Isis by Lucius Valerius Memor, a member of the vigintivirate, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04200571.translation: Quintus Appuleius Epagathus, having made a vow, willingly and deservedly fulfilled (it) to Silvanus Augustus.
EDCS-04200571.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Silvanus Augustus by Quintus Appuleius Epagathus.

EDCS-04200572.translation: Gaius Titius, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vienna, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion.
EDCS-04200572.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Titius, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, noting his origin and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04200574.translation: Forensis, of the Pupinia tribe, aged 23 years, chosen by the vote of the jurymen.
EDCS-04200574.summary: This inscription records the age and selection by jury of an individual named Forensis.

EDCS-04200575.translation: Lucius Publicius Syntropus, chief gallus, made (this) for himself and his family while alive; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04200575.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Publicius Syntropus, a chief gallus, for himself and his family, with a clause preventing it from passing to an heir.

EDCS-04200576.translation: Sextus Brinniarius Certus, having fulfilled his vow with money from his own resources, made this portico, 100 feet long.
EDCS-04200576.summary: This inscription records Sextus Brinniarius Certus's construction of a 100-foot-long portico as a votive offering.

EDCS-04200577.translation: Location of the monument: in front 16 feet, in the field 22 feet.
EDCS-04200577.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land intended for a monument.

EDCS-04200579.translation: To the divine shades. To Publius Aelius Victor, aged 8 years, 3 months. Most devoted parents.
EDCS-04200579.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Publius Aelius Victor, erected by his parents.

EDCS-04200580.translation: To the divine shades. To Publius Aelius Victor, aged 6 years, 8 months, 4 days. Publius Aelius Quartus(?) and Salvius Nicostratus, sons of Lucius, his most devoted parents.
EDCS-04200580.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a boy named Publius Aelius Victor, erected by his parents, Publius Aelius Quartus(?) and Salvius Nicostratus, likely indicating a familial relationship.

EDCS-04200581.translation: To the divine shades. For Baburia Plotia. Taronius Plotianus and Iuliana [erected this] to their most devoted mother.
EDCS-04200581.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Baburia Plotia, dedicated by her children, Taronius Plotianus and Iuliana.

EDCS-04200582.translation: Gaius Calpurnius Alexander (?), freedman of Gaius Calpurnius Frugi, son of Sabinnaeus, made this for his father from his own peculium.
EDCS-04200582.summary: This inscription records a freedman, Alexander (?), making a dedication for his father, Gaius Calpurnius Frugi.

EDCS-04200583.translation: Quintus Cervius Fidelis, son of Quintus, son of his freedman, made [this] for himself while alive.
EDCS-04200583.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Quintus Cervius Fidelis for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200584.translation: Gaius Cornelius, son of Lucius, made [this] for himself and his family while alive. For Lucius Cornelius Firmus, son of Lucius, father. For Paplinia Polla, daughter of Lucius, mother. For Lucius Cornelius Firmus, son of Gaius, brother. For Cornelia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, wife. For Raeconia Tertulla, daughter of Publius, wife, while alive. For Lucius Cornelius Favor, son of Gaius, alive. For Gaius Cornelius Augurinus, son of Gaius, alive. For Cornelia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, known as Augurina, alive.
EDCS-04200584.summary: This is a large funerary monument commissioned by Gaius Cornelius for himself and his extended family, including parents, siblings, wives, and children, many of whom are noted as being alive at the time of dedication.

EDCS-04200585.translation: To the divine shades. For Celotis. Naevola, mother.
EDCS-04200585.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Celotis, dedicated by Naevola, identified as the mother.

EDCS-04200586.translation: Lucius Herennius [---], Pupinia [---], made [this] for himself while alive. And Lucius [---] Priscus.
