EDCS-04200586.summary: This incomplete inscription records a man, Lucius Herennius, commissioning a monument for himself while alive, with a possible mention of another individual, Lucius Priscus.

EDCS-04200587.translation: Gaius Lorentius Tesifon placed this for himself while alive.
EDCS-04200587.summary: This inscription records Gaius Lorentius Tesifon dedicating a monument for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200588.translation: Magaplina Tertia, freedwoman of Magaplina [?], aged [?]; [?]; Magaplina Raeci, daughter of Magaplina, aged 50 years [?]; [?] daughter, aged 10 years [?]; [?] made [this] for [her] daughter Maxima, aged [?]; Magaplinus [?]; freedman of Marcella; Magaplinus [?]; freedman of Marcella; Magaplina V [?]; [?] daughter of Tib[---]
EDCS-04200588.summary: This fragmented inscription lists several individuals, likely family members, including a freedwoman and daughters, with some ages provided. It appears to be a funerary monument.

EDCS-04200589.translation: For Lucio Pa[?] Sellius Plautius, worthy of well-deserved honor, [she/he] placed [this].
EDCS-04200589.summary: This inscription records a dedication for Lucio Pa[?] Sellius Plautius, possibly by a wife or other relative.

EDCS-04200590.translation: Publius Sardius Prudens, son of Publius, his freedman, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-04200590.summary: This inscription records Publius Sardius Prudens commissioning a monument for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200591.translation: To Tullia Septimina, most innocent soul, who lived 6 years, 9 months, 8 days. Tullia Privata, [her] most unhappy mother.
EDCS-04200591.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Tullia Septimina, erected by her grieving mother, Tullia Privata.

EDCS-04200599.translation: Marcus So[--], son of Manius, made this while alive for himself and for Manius So[--]aeius and for Paulla, daughter of [--].
EDCS-04200599.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus, son of Manius, for himself and other family members.

EDCS-04200602.text_edition: \n Dianae sacrum Caius Valerius Trophimus VIvir Augustalis testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-04200602.translation: Sacred to Diana. Gaius Valerius Trophimus, one of the six priests of the imperial cult, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04200602.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana, commissioned by a local magistrate in his will.

EDCS-04200603.translation: To the gods and goddesses, and to the household gods, Titus Veturius Eudaemon placed this for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200603.summary: This inscription records Titus Veturius Eudaemon dedicating a shrine or offering to the household gods for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200604.translation: Lucius Mutilius Bassus, freedman of Magnus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules. Bassus arranged for it to be made. Lucius [Mutilius] Bassus, freedman of Magnus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04200604.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Hercules by a freedman.

EDCS-04200608.translation: To the Great Mother of the Gods, Quintus Publicius Charito, priest, and Gaius Publicius Hermes, temple attendant, and Secunda, cymbal player.
EDCS-04200608.summary: This is a dedication to the Great Mother of the Gods, made by a priest, a temple attendant, and a musician.

EDCS-04200609.translation: To the Great Mother of the Gods, in memory of Usia Tertullina, daughter of Lucius, priestess of the divine mothers, her mother. Sextus Appuleius Marcellus dedicated this offering.
EDCS-04200609.summary: This is a dedication to the Great Mother of the Gods, set up in memory of a priestess by her son.

EDCS-04200610.translation: Publius Cassius Eros, freedman of Publius, willingly fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04200610.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Minerva by a freedman.

EDCS-04200611.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto sacrum Lucius Arnius Luci filius Pupinia Bassus miles legionis XV Apollinaris miles cohortis I praetoriae cohortis II civium Romanorum legionis XIIII geminae legionis II Augustae legionis VI victricis testamento fieri iussit locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200611.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Lucius Arnius Bassus, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe, soldier of the 15th Apollinaris Legion, soldier of the 1st Praetorian Cohort, soldier of the 2nd Cohort of Roman Citizens, soldier of the 14th Gemina Legion, soldier of the 2nd Augusta Legion, soldier of the 6th Victrix Legion, ordered this to be made in his will. The site was granted by decree of the town council.
EDCS-04200611.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury Augustus, commissioned in his will by a soldier who served in multiple legions and cohorts, with land granted by the town council.

EDCS-04200612.translation: By the response of the presiding priests, Prospolois, for Gaius Lucanus Severus, for his son Lucius Lucanus.
EDCS-04200612.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Prospolois, acting on the advice of priests, for Gaius Lucanus Severus and his son Lucius Lucanus.

EDCS-04200613.summary: This is a dedication to Silvanus Castrensis, likely on an altar or shrine.

EDCS-04200616.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Augusta.

EDCS-04200620.text_edition: \n Caio Calpetano Rantio Quirinali Valerio Publi filio Pomptina Festo IIIIviro viarum curandarum tribuno militum legionis VI victricis quaestori seviro equitum Romanorum tribuno plebis praetori sodali Augustali legato pro praetore exercitus Africae consuli donato ab imperatore hastis puris IIII vexillis IIII coronis IIII vallari murali classica aurea curatori alvei Tiberis et riparum pontifici legato Augusti pro praetore provinciae Pannoniae et provinciae Hispaniae patrono plebs urbana\n
EDCS-04200620.translation: To Gaius Calpetanus Rantius Quirinalis Valerius Festus, son of Publius, of the Pomptina tribe, who served as aedile for the upkeep of the roads, military tribune of the 6th Victrix Legion, quaestor, Severus of the Roman Equites, tribune of the plebs, praetor, sodalis Augustalis, legate pro praetore of the army of Africa, consul, honored by the emperor with four spears, four standards, four golden crowns, and a rampart crown, curator of the Tiber River's channel and banks, pontifex, legate of Augustus pro praetore of the province of Pannonia and the province of Hispania, patron. The urban plebs.
EDCS-04200620.summary: This is a lengthy inscription honoring Gaius Calpetanus Festus, detailing his extensive career in military, judicial, and administrative positions, and listing the honors bestowed upon him by the urban plebs and the emperor.

EDCS-04200621.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-04200621.text_edition: \n Lucio Fabio Luci ffilio Pupinia Severo quaestori urbano decuriones et plebs Tergestinorum Quod Aspanius Lentulus et s Nepos II viri iure dicundo verba fecerunt Lucium Fabium Severum clarissimum virum multa iam pridem in rem publicam nostram beneficia contulisse ut qui a prima statim aetate id egerit uti in adiuvanda patria sua et dignitate et eloquentia cresceret nam ita multas et magnificas causas publicas aput sic optimum principem Antoninum Augustum Pium adservisse egisse vicisse sine ullo quidem aerari nostri inpendio ut quamvis admodum adulescens senilibus tamen et perfectis operibus ac factis patriam suam nosque insuper sibi universos obstinxerit nunc vero tam grandi beneficio tam salubri ingenio tam perpetua utilitate rem publicam nostram adfecisse ut omnia praecedentia facta sua quamquam immensa et eximia sint facile superarit nam in hoc quoque mirabilem esse clarissimi viri virtutem quod cotidie in bene faciendo et in patria sua tuenda ipse se vincat et idcirco quamvis pro mensura beneficiorum eius impares in referenda gratia simus interim tamen pro tempore vel facultate ut adiuvet saepe facturus remunderandam esse clarissimi viri benivolentiam non ut illum proniorem habeamus aliut enim vir ita natus non potest facere sed ut nos iudicantibus gratos praebeamus et dignos tali decore talique praesidio quid fieri placeret de ea re ita censuerunt primo censente Calpurnio Certo cum Fabius Severus vir amplissimus atque clarissimus tanta pietate tantaque adfectione rem publicam nostram amplexus sit itaque pro minimis maximisque commodis eius excubet atque omnem praestantiam suam exerat ut manifestum sit id eum agere ut non modo nobis sed proximis quoque civitatibus declaratum velit esse non ali quam patriae suae natum et civilia studia quae in eo quamvis admodum invene iam sint peracta atque perfecta ac senatoriam dignitatem hac maxime ex causa concupivisse uti patriam suam cum ornatam tum ab omnibus iniuriis tutam defensamque praestaret interim aput sic iudices a Caesare datos interim aput sic ipsum imperatorem causis publicis patrocinando quas cum iustitia divini principis tum sua eximia ac prudentissima oration<e> semper nobis cum victoria firmiores remisit ex proximo vero ut manifestatur caelestibus litteris Antonini Augusti Pii tam feliciter desiderium publicum aput sic eum sit prosecutus impetrando uti Carni Catalique attributi a divo Augusto rei publicae nostrae pro ut qui meruissent vita atque censu per aedilitatis gradum in curiam nostram admitterentur ac per hoc civitatem Romanam apiserentur <quo> et aerarium nostrum ditavit et curiam complevit et universam rem publicam nostram cum fomentis ampliavit admittendo ad honorum communionem et usurpationem Romanae civitatis et optimum et locupletissimum quemque ut scilicet qui olim erant tantum in reditu pecuniario nunc et in illo ipso <et> duplici quidem per honorariae numerationem repperiantur et sint cum quibus munera decurionatus iam ut paucis onerosa honeste de pleno compartiamur ad cuius rei gratiam habendam ut in saecula permansuro eiusmodi beneficio oportuerat quidem si fieri posset ac si verecundia clarissimi viri permitteret universos nos ire et gratias ei iuxta optimum principem agere sed quoniam certum est nobis onerosum ei futurum tale nostrum officium illut sic certe proxime fieri oporteto statuam ei auratam equestrem primo quoque tempore in celeberrima fori nostri parte poni et in basi eius hanc nostram consensionem atque hoc decretum inscribi uti ad posteros nostros tam voltus amplissimi viri quam facta permaneant petique a <Fa>bio Vero egregio viro patre Severi uti quando quidem et commentum hoc ipsius sit providentiae qua rem publicam nostram infatigabili cura gubernat et in hoc plus publici benefici quod talem et nobis et imperio civem procreavit atque formavit cuius opera studioque et ornatiores et tutiores in dies nos magis magisque sentiamus uti patiatur se in hanc rem ad filium suum legari mandarique sibi uti gratias publice clarissimo viro mandatu nostro agat et gaudium universorum singulorumque ac voluntatem ut magister talium rerum in notitiam eius perferat censuerunt\n
EDCS-04200621.translation: To Lucius Fabius Severus, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe. The town councilors and the plebs of Tergeste, because Aspanius Lentulus and Nepos, the two magistrates with judicial authority, spoke words concerning Lucius Fabius Severus, most illustrious man, who for a long time has bestowed many benefits upon our republic, for he has always striven from his earliest age to grow in both dignity and eloquence in aiding his fatherland, for he has so served, pleaded, and won many public cases before the most excellent emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, as to always achieve victory with his exceptional and most prudent oratory, and with no expense to our treasury, so that although very young, he nevertheless bound his fatherland and us all to himself with elderly and perfect deeds and actions; but now he has favored our republic with so great a benefit, so wholesome a genius, so perpetual an advantage, that he easily surpasses all his preceding deeds, however immense and extraordinary. For in this too, the virtue of this most illustrious man is wonderful, that he daily surpasses himself in doing good and in defending his fatherland, and therefore, although we are unequal in repaying him in proportion to his benefits, in the meantime, according to the time or opportunity, we must render a reward for his benevolence, not so that we may have him more favorably disposed (for a man born such cannot do otherwise), but so that we may show ourselves grateful and worthy of such honor and such protection to those who judge. It was decreed thus: first, Calpurnius Certus proposes that since Fabius Severus, a most distinguished and illustrious man, has embraced our republic with such piety and affection, and watches over its smallest and greatest advantages, and exerts all his excellence, it is clear that he acts so that he wishes it to be declared not only to us but also to neighboring cities that he was born for his fatherland alone, and that he pursued and perfected civil studies, which were already present in him at a very young age, and desired the senatorial dignity for this reason above all, namely to provide his fatherland with adornment and protection from all injustices. In the meantime, before the judges appointed by Caesar, and before the emperor himself, by pleading public cases, which, together with the justice of the divine emperor, and his own exceptional and most prudent oratory, he has always brought us victory with greater certainty. And most recently, as is made clear by the heavenly letters of Antoninus Augustus Pius, he has so happily followed up on the public desire before him by obtaining that the Carni and Catali, attributed to our republic by the divine Augustus, be admitted to our town council based on their life and census, through the grade of aedileship, and thereby receive Roman citizenship, which has enriched our treasury, filled our council, and expanded our entire republic with subsidies, by admitting the worthy and wealthiest to the communion of honors and the use of Roman citizenship, so that indeed those who formerly were only in financial return are now found and exist in both, and indeed double, through the payment of honorary fees, and with whom we may honestly share the burdens of the aedileship, which has now become onerous for a few, from a full share. In order to show gratitude for this deed, as it should last for all ages, it would indeed have been fitting, if possible and if the modesty of this illustrious man permitted, for all of us to go and thank him together, according to the most excellent emperor. But since it is certain that such an undertaking would be burdensome to him, it is certainly most fitting that we do the following: that a gilded equestrian statue be erected to him in the most frequented part of our forum as soon as possible, and that this our consensus and decree be inscribed on its base, so that both the countenance of this most distinguished man and his deeds may endure for posterity. And that we ask Fabius Verus, an excellent man and father of Severus, since this plan is also his providence by which he governs our republic with tireless care, and in this he has conferred a greater public benefit by producing and shaping such a citizen for us and for the empire, whose work and zeal make us feel daily more adorned and safer, that he permit himself to be appointed to this task concerning his son, and that he be commanded to publicly convey our thanks to this most illustrious man and to bring to his notice the joy and will of all and each of us, as master of such matters. It was decreed.
EDCS-04200621.summary: This is a lengthy decree by the town council and plebs of Tergeste honoring Lucius Fabius Severus, detailing his extensive public service, legal victories, and benefits bestowed upon the city, including the granting of Roman citizenship to certain groups, and decreeing the erection of a statue and the inscription of this decree.

EDCS-04200622.translation: Publius Palpellius Clodius, son of Publius, of the Maecia tribe, from Quirinalis, first spear of the 20th Legion, military tribune of the 7th Claudian Legion, procurator of the Emperor, prefect of the fleet, dedicated [this].
EDCS-04200622.summary: This inscription details the extensive military and administrative career of Publius Palpellius Clodius, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200623.translation: Quintus Petronius Modestus, son of Gaius, of the Pupinia tribe, first-class soldier twice over of the XII Fulminata and I Adjutrix legions, tribune of the V cohort of the Vigiles, tribune of the XII urban cohort, tribune of the V Praetorian cohort, procurator of the divine Nero and Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus for the provinces of Hispania Citerior, Asturia, and Callaecia, priest of the divine Claudius; he himself dedicated it.
EDCS-04200623.summary: This is a military career inscription for Quintus Petronius Modestus, detailing his service and appointments, and indicating he dedicated the monument.

EDCS-04200626.translation: To the spirits of Lucius Satrius Silvinus, procurator of supreme revenues (?), for his dearest wife Caesidia Amabilis. He made (this).
EDCS-04200626.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a procurator for his beloved wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200628.translation: To Tiberius Attius Hilarus, son of Tiberius, of the Pupinia tribe, decurion emeritus of the I Flavia Fidelis cavalry ala. Antistia Ilias, his wife, made (this) for him while she was alive, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-04200628.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a wife for her deceased husband, a former decurion, and their freedmen and descendants.

EDCS-04200629.text_edition: \n Quinto Baieno Publi filio Pupinia Blassiano praefecto cohortis II Asturum tribuno legionis VII Claudiae piae fidelis \n
EDCS-04200629.translation: To Quintus Baienus Blassiannus, son of Publius, of the Pupinia tribe, prefect of the II Cohort of Asturians, tribune of the VII Claudia Pia Fidelis Legion.
EDCS-04200629.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Baienus Blassiannus, recording his military career as a prefect and tribune, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200630.translation: Publius Clodius Chrestus, while alive, made (this) for himself and his family: for Publius Clodius Quirinalis, soldier of the XV Apollinaris Legion, and for his wife Blassia Placidia, daughter of Lucius, and for Cominius Verus, soldier of the XIII Gemina Legion, and for his friend Aulus Tullius Chrysanthus.
EDCS-04200630.summary: This is a family funerary dedication made by Publius Clodius Chrestus for himself, his wife, and other family members and a friend, indicating service in various legions.

EDCS-04200631.translation: To the spirits of Titus Domitius Gracilis, of the Ditio tribe, who lived for 50 years, served for 13 years, (and was) four times a Pado(?). His heirs, Lucius Plaetorius Bassus and Lucius Murranius Super, set this up for him, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-04200631.summary: This funerary inscription records the age, military service duration, and achievements of Titus Domitius Gracilis, with his heirs setting up the monument.

EDCS-04200633.text_edition: \n Luci Seugoni Agrippini evokati Augusti nostri cohortis VIIII praetoriae piae vindicis Severianae Sextilia Maximilla heres itemque uxor coniugi rarissimo Speranti\n
EDCS-04200633.translation: Sextilia Maximilla, heir and also wife, (made this) for her very dear husband Lucius Seugonius Agrippinus, evocatus of our Augustus, of the IX Praetorian cohort, pia vindicis Severianae.
EDCS-04200633.summary: This monument was erected by a wife for her husband, Lucius Seugonius Agrippinus, who served as an evocatus in the Praetorian Guard during the Severan period.

EDCS-04200634.translation: Marcus Surinus Marcellus, son of Marcus. Aedile, prefect in judicial matters, duovir, pontifex, prefect of craftsmen, quinquennial. By decree of the decurions. Marcus Surinus Marcellus, son of Marcus, his son.
EDCS-04200634.summary: This inscription records the public career of Marcus Surinus Marcellus and mentions his son also named Marcus Surinus Marcellus, likely from a Roman town council in the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200635.text_edition: \n Lucio Vario Papirio Papiriano IIviro iure dicundo IIviro iure dicundo quinquennali praefecto fabrum Romae et Tergeste flamini Hadrianali pontifici auguri collegium fabrum patrono merenti\n
EDCS-04200635.translation: To Lucius Varius Papirius Papirianus, for his merits: duovir iure dicundo, quinquennial duovir, prefect of the guild of fabric workers in Rome and Trieste, flamen Hadrianalis, pontiff, augur, patron of the guild of fabric workers.
EDCS-04200635.summary: This honorary inscription celebrates Lucius Varius Papirius Papirianus for his various civic and religious roles, including leadership in the guild of fabric workers.

EDCS-04200636.text_edition: \n ------ donis donato] ob bellum Parthicum torquibus armillis phaleris corona Lucius Varius Papirius Papirianus pater IIvir iure dicundo IIvir iure dicundo quinqennalis Tergeste praefectus fabrum Romae et Tergeste\n
EDCS-04200636.translation: Lucius Varius Papirius Papirianus, father, duovir iure dicundo, quinquennial duovir, prefect of the guild of fabric workers in Rome and Trieste, (received) donations for the Parthian war: torques, armbands, phalerae, and a crown.
EDCS-04200636.summary: This inscription details military honors received by Lucius Varius Papirius Papirianus for his service in the Parthian War, likely commissioned by his father.

EDCS-04200637.translation: Titus Vidius Fortunatus, soldier of the 5th Alaudae Legion, served for 26 years. Camula his wife made [this].
EDCS-04200637.summary: This funerary inscription records the service of Titus Vidius Fortunatus in the 5th Alaudae Legion and was erected by his wife, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200639.translation: Lucius Apisius, son of Titus, of the Pupinia tribe, duovir. Apisia [his wife/daughter?] [erected this].
EDCS-04200639.summary: This inscription likely refers to Lucius Apisius, a duovir, and an individual named Apisia, possibly his wife or daughter, possibly from a municipal context.

EDCS-04200641.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning an individual named Sextus Ca[---] who held the office of aedile, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-04200642.translation: Sextus Caesius Cinnamus, freedman of Sextus, Augustalis, sixth-member of the duoviri, is laid here. For you and yours.
EDCS-04200642.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Caesius Cinnamus, an Augustalis and a member of the local elite, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200643.translation: Manius Cassidius, son of Marcus, a decurion, ordered [this] to be made. Attia Secunda, his wife.
EDCS-04200643.summary: This inscription records that Manius Cassidius, a decurion, commissioned a monument or work, which was then completed or associated with his wife, Attia Secunda.

EDCS-04200644.text_edition: \n Caio Getacio Pupinia Severiano aedili lIviro iure dicundo Tergeste Caius Getacius Severianus pater\n
EDCS-04200644.translation: To Gaius Getacius Severianus, father, for his son Gaius Getacius Severianus, who served as aedile and duovir with the power of jurisdiction in Tergeste.
EDCS-04200644.summary: A father dedicates this monument to his son, a local magistrate in Tergeste.

EDCS-04200645.translation: Titus Marcius Secundus, Augustalis duovir. Marcia Quarta, freedwoman of Titus, his wife.
EDCS-04200645.summary: This inscription records Titus Marcius Secundus, who held the municipal office of Augustalis duovir, and his wife Marcia Quarta, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04200646.translation: [---] Publius Me[---] Pollio [---], decurion of Pola [---]
EDCS-04200646.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Publius Me[---] Pollio, who was a decurion in the town of Pola.

EDCS-04200648.text_edition: \n Mamiliae ex pecunia honoraria adiecta in pensa sua Spinther aedilis\n
EDCS-04200648.translation: Spinther, aedile, from the honorarium fund, added to his own expenses.
EDCS-04200648.summary: An aedile records the use of honorarium funds for public works or expenses.

EDCS-04200649.translation: [...], IIIIIIvir, and [...], freedman of Lucius, Teucer, and [...], freedwoman of Lucius, Ammia, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-04200649.summary: This inscription records the makers of a monument, including a member of the IIIIIIvirate, who completed the work during their lifetime.

EDCS-04200652.translation: Lucius Alfius Isochrysus, freedman of Lucius, a doctor, and Lucius Alfius Eudemus, freedman of Isochrysus, made (this) while alive for themselves, and for their patron, and for Alfia Attica, freedwoman of Lucius, his wife, and for their family. A good man and you.
EDCS-04200652.summary: A doctor and his freedman establish a tomb for themselves and their family, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200653.translation: Constantius, munerarius (organizer of games), gave a magnificent gift to his gladiators because of their favor, to Decoratus the retiarius, who killed Caeruleum and fell, having been killed; the game's rudis (teacher/master) extinguished both, protecting both. Decoratus the secutor, in 9 fights, left first grief to his wife Valeria.
EDCS-04200653.summary: This epitaph commemorates a gladiator named Decoratus who died in a match, funded by the games organizer Constantius, and details his combat record and family.

EDCS-04200654.translation: Lucius Mussius Salvius, son of Salvius, of the Pollia tribe, born in Fano, age 20, lies here. His brother, Publius Mussius Salvius, son of Salvius, (lies here).
EDCS-04200654.summary: An epitaph for Lucius Mussius Salvius, who died at age 20, erected by his brother Publius.

EDCS-04200655.translation: Publius Aelius Felix, freedman of Augustus, made (this) while alive for himself, and for his dearest wife Caesernia Saturnina, and for his most dutiful son Aelius Firminus, age 1.
EDCS-04200655.summary: A tomb was erected by Publius Aelius Felix, a freedman of Augustus, for his family, including a child who died at age one.

EDCS-04200656.translation: Quintus Atedius Scaevola, alive, made (this). Quintus Pos[...]. [...] in front [...] feet [...] in the field [...] feet.
EDCS-04200656.summary: Partially preserved funerary inscription indicating the dimensions of a plot of land purchased by Quintus Atedius Scaevola.

EDCS-04200657.translation: For Alfia Chila, freedwoman of a woman, mother. Felix, her son, made (this) while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200657.summary: A son erected a tomb for his mother, Alfia Chila, and for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200658.translation: To Alfia Hetaera, freedwoman of Marcus, patroness. Felix, her freedman.
EDCS-04200658.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a freedman, Felix, to his patroness Alfia Hetaera, who was herself a freedwoman.

EDCS-04200659.translation: Publius Allius, son of Quintus; Publius Allius Severus, son of Publius.
EDCS-04200659.summary: This inscription lists names, likely father and son, potentially on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-04200660.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Annalis. Publius Aelius Firmus (dedicated this) for his friend, and Baebia Quinta for her husband.
EDCS-04200660.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by a friend and a wife to the deceased Annalis.

EDCS-04200661.translation: Apuleia Saturnina; Marcosena Successa, daughter of Agate Cheraunia; Crocale.
EDCS-04200661.summary: This inscription lists several female names, possibly related to each other or forming a group associated with a monument.

EDCS-04200662.translation: Paraclovi[us?] ordered [this to] be made in his will for his wife Tertia, aged 65.
EDCS-04200662.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband's posthumous dedication for his wife, commissioned in his will.

EDCS-04200663.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Arrius Maximianus made this, while alive, for his most devoted son, Lucius Arrius Maximianus.
EDCS-04200663.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father for his son, Lucius Arrius Maximianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200664.summary: This inscription contains incomplete names and possibly titles, suggesting a fragmented record of individuals.

EDCS-04200667.translation: Aulus Barbius Epinicus; Aulus Barbius Epaphroditus; Quintus Petronius Parthenius; Sextus Cossutius Euschemus; Lucius Gallius Felix; Lucius Usius Lascivos; Lucius Lopsius Clymenus; Lucius Lopsius Aprio; Lucius Publicius Iustus; Pontiena Peregrin(a); Publicia Primigenia.
EDCS-04200667.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely members of a collegium or a funerary association, with some names separated by a 'll' suggesting a division or change.

EDCS-04200668.translation: [E]ucharid[in]us, son of Barbius Eu[charistus], with Secundus, his father.
EDCS-04200668.summary: This inscription likely records a familial relationship, possibly on a tomb, mentioning a father and son.

EDCS-04200669.text_edition: \n Lucio Barbio Luci filio Lucullo Lucio Barbio Luci liberto Addaeo patronis Lucio Barbio Spuri filio Rufo filio Lucio Barbio Luci liberto Fausto filio Barbia Luci liberta Philostrata sibi et suis fieri iussit Lucio Barbio Luci liberto Felici filio Tulliae Boi filiae Secundae Barbiae Luci libertae Optatae filiae\n
EDCS-04200669.translation: Lucius Barbius Lucullus, son of Lucius; Lucius Addaeus, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Rufus, son of Lucius; Lucius Faustus, freedman of Lucius; Philostrata, freedwoman of Lucius, ordered this to be made for themselves and their families; for Lucius Felix, son of Lucius; for Tullia Secunda, daughter of Boius; and for Baria Optata, freedwoman of Lucius, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04200669.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by members of the Barbius family and their freedmen, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04200670.translation: [...] for himself and for Caesia Luperca, freedwoman and wife, and for Caesia Successa, freedwoman, and for freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04200670.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by an individual for themselves, their freedwoman wife, and other freedpersons.

EDCS-04200671.translation: Calventius Felicianus [for his mother] Calventia Proclina.
EDCS-04200671.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, from a son to his mother.

EDCS-04200672.summary: This inscription contains fragmented names, possibly indicating individuals associated with a monument or dedication.

EDCS-04200673.translation: Lucius Cassius Phoebus, freedman of Longinus, lies here.
EDCS-04200673.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Lucius Cassius Phoebus, a freedman, indicating he is buried in this location.

EDCS-04200675.translation: [...]di [...] for his mother, Quintus Cervius Natalis.
EDCS-04200675.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Quintus Cervius Natalis for his mother.

EDCS-04200676.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking the burial place of Cervula Lentula.

EDCS-04200677.translation: Titus Salvius ordered by his will that Moilicus and Ligemia be [buried] for himself.
EDCS-04200677.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating a will commissioned burials for Moilicus and Ligemia.

EDCS-04200678.translation: To Quintus Clodius [---] Iucunda and Tullia [---] Iucunda.
EDCS-04200678.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Quintus Clodius and possibly others.

EDCS-04200679.translation: Lucius Clodius Servatus, freedman of Lucius, made this, while alive, for himself and his family: for his wife Clodia Amanda, freedwoman of Lucius; and for his son Lucius Clodius Amandus, aged 28.
EDCS-04200679.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Clodius Servatus for himself, his wife, and his son, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200680.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely names individuals, possibly for a funerary or dedicatory purpose.

EDCS-04200681.translation: [---] for his [family] and [---] of Crispina [---] [---] for [---]
EDCS-04200681.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be dedicatory or funerary in nature, mentioning 'Crispina'.

EDCS-04200682.translation: Publius Domitius Asbestus and Festa, parents, gave [this] for their son Cerialis, aged 20, at their own expense.
EDCS-04200682.summary: This is a funerary inscription by parents dedicating a tomb for their son Cerialis.

EDCS-04200683.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins with the name Publius Egnatius, possibly for funerary or dedicatory purposes.

EDCS-04200684.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that names Equasia and Marcus Cassius, likely for funerary or dedicatory purposes.

EDCS-04200685.translation: Flaccia Moschis, freedwoman of the woman [Flaccius?], lies here. The plot of the monument is in the field, 3 feet [wide?]; in the front [3 feet?].
EDCS-04200685.summary: This funerary epitaph for Flaccia Moschis also records the dimensions of her burial plot, suggesting it was a purchased or allocated space.

EDCS-04200686.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Flaminius Secundus.

EDCS-04200687.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that names individuals including Maia and Flaminia, likely for funerary or dedicatory purposes.

EDCS-04200688.translation: Flavius Ven[3] and Erbonia had this erected for themselves while alive.
EDCS-04200688.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Ven[3] and Erbonia, who dedicated their own monument.

EDCS-04200689.translation: To Gallia Clementiana, aged 10 years and 9 months. Caesidius Euphrosinus (dedicated this) to his dearest granddaughter.
EDCS-04200689.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Gallia Clementiana, dedicated by her grandfather Caesidius Euphrosinus.

EDCS-04200692.translation: By decision of Lucius Gavillius, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Gavillius, freedman of Lucius, [3]...
EDCS-04200692.summary: This inscription seems to record a property division or boundary marker, arbitrated by two freedmen of Lucius Gavillius.

EDCS-04200694.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their daughter, Getacia Servanda.

EDCS-04200696.translation: Hermes (dedicated this) to his daughter Iulia Agele, aged 9 years.
EDCS-04200696.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Agele, aged 9, dedicated by her father Hermes.

EDCS-04200697.translation: For Gaius Hostilius Frugio, son of Gaius; for Nepos, son of Gaius Hostilius, son of Gaius; for Lucius Nymphodotus, son of Lucius Mutillius; for Hostilia Provincia, freedwoman of Gaius, she made this, while alive.
EDCS-04200697.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Hostilia Provincia for her family members, including her father, brother, and a freedman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04200699.translation: ] Lartius (dedicated this) for himself [3] / Publius Lartius [3] / [3]cos[3] / [3]binia
EDCS-04200699.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely for Publius Lartius and possibly others named Lartius and Binia.

EDCS-04200700.translation: Gaius Lucanus, son of Sextus, of the Pupinia tribe; Cominia Aletia, freedwoman of Lucius; Cominia Fausta, freedwoman of Manius; Marcus Valerius, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe. (Dedicated this) alive to (people) alive.
EDCS-04200700.summary: This is an epitaph for Gaius Lucanus, Cominia Aletia, Cominia Fausta, and Marcus Valerius, who set up the monument for themselves while living.

EDCS-04200701.translation: Lucretia, freedwoman of Lucius, [3]... aged [3] years, 7 months [
EDCS-04200701.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Lucretia, aged approximately 7 years and some months.

EDCS-04200702.translation: Quintus Lurius Apollophanes, freedman of Quintus, lies here.
EDCS-04200702.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Lurius Apollophanes, a freedman.

EDCS-04200703.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a name on a tombstone or marker for Quintus Manlius.

EDCS-04200704.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Quintus Manlius Blastus, freedman of Quintus. Manlia Theocrite made this, while alive, for herself, for her most devoted husband, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-04200704.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by Manlia Theocrite for her husband Quintus Manlius Blastus, and also for future generations of their freedpeople.

EDCS-04200706.translation: Manlia Pia made this, while alive, for her parents, Quintus Manlius Hermetus and Manlia Epigone.
EDCS-04200706.summary: This funerary inscription records Manlia Pia dedicating a monument to her parents, Quintus Manlius Hermetus and Manlia Epigone.

EDCS-04200707.translation: Marcosena for Filo. Septimia Cercola, wife, made this, while alive.
EDCS-04200707.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by Septimia Cercola for her husband, Marcosena Filo.

EDCS-04200708.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a name or dedication for Publius Mercu[3].

EDCS-04200709.translation: Lucius Meter, son of Sextus, and Metra, freedwoman of Sextus, Caesulla.
EDCS-04200709.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming three individuals: Lucius Meter, Metra, and Caesulla, likely family members or freedpersons related to a Sextus.

EDCS-04200710.summary: A funerary inscription for Musae, who died at the age of 26.

EDCS-04200714.translation: To Paconia Bassilla, aged 4 years, 9 months, and 16 days. Caius Paconius Salutaris and Paconia Calliste, her parents, commissioned this.
EDCS-04200714.summary: A funerary inscription for Paconia Bassilla, commissioned by her parents, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200715.translation: By the authority of Lucius Patronius Dia, his freedman, Primus, ordered this to be made by his will; the monument extends 30 feet in all directions.
EDCS-04200715.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by a freedman, Primus, in accordance with the will of his patron Lucius Patronius Dia, likely from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-04200716.translation: For Planitia Sbanatea Mercusina, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04200716.summary: A funerary dedication for Planitia Sbanatea Mercusina, freedwoman of Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200717.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Plautius Marcellinus and Laelia Septimina (erected this) for their dearest son, (Lucius) Plautius Marcellinus, aged 7 years and 10 months.
EDCS-04200717.summary: This is a tombstone for a young child, Lucius Plautius Marcellinus, set up by his parents, Lucius Plautius Marcellinus and Laelia Septimina, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200719.translation: Quintus Publicius Felix, freedman of the people of Tergeste, and Sexta, daughter of Spurius, wife of Quintus Publicius Felix, (and) Ingenuus, freedman of Quintus Publicius Felix, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-04200719.summary: This is a funerary monument established by a freedman, Quintus Publicius Felix, and his wife Sexta, and also mentions another freedman, Ingenuus, likely as part of their household or patronage, probably from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200720.translation: For Restuta, slave of the Marii, aged 24 years, 7 months, and 10 days. Restutus, her son, and Epictetus, her husband, made (this) while alive, and for themselves.
EDCS-04200720.summary: This is a tombstone for Restuta, a slave belonging to the Marii family, erected by her son Restutus and husband Epictetus, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04200721.translation: To the departed spirits. For Salvia Severianena, who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 24 days, with whom I lived 7 years and 20 days, Lurius Phoebianus (erected this) for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-04200721.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Salvia Severianena, set up by her husband Lurius Phoebianus, detailing her age and the duration of their marriage, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200722.translation: To the departed spirits. Saufeia Threpte made (this) while alive; this monument will not follow her heir.
EDCS-04200722.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Saufeia Threpte for herself, with the stipulation that the monument would not pass to her heir, probably from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200723.translation: Lucius Sempronius Faustus ordered this to be made for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04200723.summary: A funerary commission by Lucius Sempronius Faustus for himself and his freed dependents, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200724.translation: Marcus Septimius Rufus, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Lucius Figilius Statio, son of Titus, his father, and for Lucius Figilius, son of Titus [...]
EDCS-04200724.summary: A funerary commission by Marcus Septimius Rufus for himself, his father, and another individual named Lucius Figilius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200725.translation: Publius Septimius, son of Publius, Roman knight and patron, granted everything to the people of Tergeste [...]
EDCS-04200725.summary: A dedication recording the generosity of Publius Septimius, a Roman knight and patron, towards the inhabitants of Tergeste, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200726.translation: Severa, buried by Dextris. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04200726.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Severa, mentioning her burial by someone named Dextris and dedicating the monument to the departed spirits.

EDCS-04200727.translation: Taurus Taurius Federatus, by name, from his own funds(?).
EDCS-04200727.summary: A dedication or commission by Taurus Taurius Federatus, possibly funded by himself, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04200728.translation: [To(?)] Tottia(?) / here she is laid / with probity / with piety / with obedience
EDCS-04200728.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph for a woman named Tottia, praising her virtues.

EDCS-04200730.summary: A fragment of an inscription, likely a funerary dedication, for Trosius, son of Sextus.

EDCS-04200731.translation: Publius Trosius Peregrinus made (this) while alive for himself and for Publius Trosius Severus, father, and Arria Quartilla, daughter of Gaius, mother, and Trosia Caesulla, freedwoman of Publius, sister, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument will not follow her heir. For Publius Trosius Communis, son of Publius.
EDCS-04200731.summary: This is a complex funerary monument, possibly a family tomb, established by Publius Trosius Peregrinus for himself and various relatives, including his father, mother, sister, and a freedman, also specifying that the monument will not pass to an heir, and also noting Publius Trosius Communis.

EDCS-04200732.translation: [...] for himself and for Aulus Tullius [...]ino [...]
EDCS-04200732.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a commission or dedication for two individuals, one named Aulus Tullius, possibly funerary.

EDCS-04200733.translation: To Gaius Valerius Sabinus, patron, to Gaius Valerius Sabinus, son, to Cerellia Clementa, wife.
EDCS-04200733.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Valerius Sabinus, his son, and his wife, likely from a family tomb.

EDCS-04200734.translation: Lucius Vibius Pollio, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe. Floria Hilara, freedwoman of Gaius, his wife, ordered (this) to be made. In front 20 feet, in the field 20 feet, from the road to the boundary.
EDCS-04200734.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of land, detailing its dimensions and location, and was commissioned by Floria Hilara for her husband Lucius Vibius Pollio.

EDCS-04200735.translation: Vibia Tertulla, daughter of Gaius, made this while alive for herself, and for her sons Lucius Afarius Niger and Gaius Afarius Celer, and for her partner Marcus Afranus Gratus, and for her freedmen and freedwomen, and for her husband Publius Satrius Saturninus and their son Lucius Satrius Valerianus. This monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-04200735.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vibia Tertulla and her family, including her partner and husband, indicating a private burial monument.

EDCS-04200736.translation: Gaius Voltidius Fusc[us], son of Gaius, ordered this to be made by his will, to Gaius Voltidius Gazaeus, his father, to Petronia, daughter of Quintus, his mother, to Titus Voltidius, son of Gaius, his brother, to Grata, freedwoman of Titus, his wife.
EDCS-04200736.summary: This funerary inscription, ordered by will, commemorates Gaius Voltidius Fusc[us]'s family members: father, mother, brother, and wife.

EDCS-04200737.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription with names that cannot be fully reconstructed.

EDCS-04200738.translation: Lucius Usius Philippus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, and for his son Lucius Usius Fidus, and for Lucius Usius Thaso, aged 5, and for Lucius Usius Venustus, his freedman, and for Tullia Cypare, freedwoman of Aulus, and for Attia Cogitata, freedwoman of Tiberius, and for Lucius Usius Evangellus, freedman of Lucius, and for Cossutia Tyche. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed.
EDCS-04200738.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Usius Philippus and members of his household, including family and freedmen, for a private burial.

EDCS-04200740.translation: Gavia Sabina ordered this to be made in her will for her mother [3]viae [3]erinae.
EDCS-04200740.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a mother, with the testator, Gavia Sabina, indicating a posthumous commission by will.

EDCS-04200786.translation: Here rests in peace Maurentius, a distinguished man, who lived for more or less 34 years, was buried on the 15 days before the Kalends of November, in the 5th indiction, after the consulship of our lord Justinian the Emperor.
EDCS-04200786.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of Maurentius, a high-ranking individual, specifying his age and the date of his interment during the reign of Justinian.

EDCS-04200787.translation: Rufinus, the custodian, had the pavement made as his vow in the 15th indiction year.
EDCS-04200787.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Rufinus, the custodian, who commissioned the creation of a pavement.

EDCS-04200790.translation: Lucius Rufellius Severus, a former centurion of the first rank, restored this straight road, which was originally laid out by the centurion Atius after a decision by Aulus Plautius, legate of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, and later transferred by the Rundicti into the territory of Gaius Laecanius Bassus, by order of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator.
EDCS-04200790.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription commemorating the restoration of a road by Lucius Rufellius Severus under imperial command during the reign of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus.

EDCS-04200794.translation: Lucius Fari[---] made this for himself and [---] Artimid[---] O[---]
EDCS-04200794.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely for Lucius Farius and others, indicating a private burial monument.

EDCS-04200795.translation: Agatho, freedman of Lucius, the messenger of the associates, and the slaves of the magistrates, made the columns from their own resources, a willing gift to Minerva, deserved.
EDCS-04200795.summary: This inscription records that Agatho, a freedman and messenger, along with slaves of the magistrates, voluntarily donated columns to Minerva.

EDCS-04200796.translation: Abennaeus, slave of Catus Marcius, made the wall, pinnacles, and entrance from his own resources and dedicated it to Minerva.
EDCS-04200796.summary: This inscription states that Abennaeus, a slave, used his own funds to build a wall, pinnacles, and an entrance dedicated to Minerva.

EDCS-04200797.translation: Octavia Sperata willingly fulfilled her vow to the Fates.
EDCS-04200797.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Fates by Octavia Sperata.

EDCS-04200798.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus, for the health of Aquilinus, steward of the emperors, and of Tiberius Julius Aquilinus. Iulia Stratonice fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04200798.summary: This is a votive dedication to Silvanus Augustus made by Iulia Stratonice for the health of imperial officials.

EDCS-04200799.translation: Sacconius Varro, tribune of the I Cohort of Dacians, willingly fulfilled his vow to Hope of the Emperors.
EDCS-04200799.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Hope of the Emperors by Sacconius Varro, a military officer.

EDCS-04200800.translation: Auconius Optatus, an equestrian of public standing and a decurion and duovir of Claudius Aguntum, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for the health of his son Titus Auconius Optatus, a Roman knight.
EDCS-04200800.summary: This is a votive dedication made by Auconius Optatus, a local magistrate, for the health of his son.

EDCS-04200803.translation: To Gaius Cornelius Lucullus, aged 30, and Cornelia Tertulla, aged 25, and Gaius Cornelius Proculus, aged 40, most dutiful sons, by Gaius Cornelius Firmus and Volsaria Paulla.
EDCS-04200803.summary: This tomb inscription honors three deceased children, dedicating the monument to them from their parents, Gaius Cornelius Firmus and Volsaria Paulla.

EDCS-04200806.translation: Artoria Prisca, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive for herself, and for Maxuma, daughter of Manius, her mother, and for her grandfather Manius Minucius, and for Lucius Livius, son of Caius.
EDCS-04200806.summary: This funerary monument, made by Artoria Prisca during her lifetime, is dedicated to herself and several family members: her mother, grandfather, and uncle.

EDCS-04200807.translation: Publius Publicius Ursio made this while alive for himself and his dearest wife Voltilia Saturnina, while I manage public lands, this was decided upon on this private plot of land.
EDCS-04200807.summary: This epitaph records that Publius Publicius Ursio commissioned his own tomb and that of his wife, Voltilia Saturnina, on his private land while he was still alive and managing public estates.

EDCS-04200812.translation: To Marcus, son of Marcus, brother Faustus the freedman, brother Meleager the freedman, brother Commodus the freedman, and brother Quintus, the road.
EDCS-04200812.summary: This dedication records a road given to Marcus, his freedmen brothers, and Quintus.

EDCS-04200813.translation: To Gaius Lucretius, son of Sextus, aged 9 years. Here lies Caelia Secunda, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04200813.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Lucretius, aged 9, and Caelia Secunda, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-04200818.translation: Lucius Octavius Callistus, a Six-man and Augustalis of Aquileia, willingly fulfilled his vow to Fortuna Augusta.
EDCS-04200818.summary: This is a votive dedication to Fortuna Augusta made by Lucius Octavius Callistus, a local religious and civic official.

EDCS-04200820.translation: Eros, freedman of (the woman) Velaia, son of Gaius Velaeus, gives the altar and the paved seating.
EDCS-04200820.summary: An altar and seating were dedicated by Eros, a freedman, who also held the position of sexvir.

EDCS-04200821.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Imperatoris Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti filio res publica Foroiuliensium\n
EDCS-04200821.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, from the community of Forojuliensium.
EDCS-04200821.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the community of Forojuliensium to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus.

EDCS-04200822.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Publico Licinio Gallieno Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli II patri patriae res publica Foroiuliensium devota numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-04200822.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power, consul for the second time, father of the fatherland, the community of Forojuliensium is devoted to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-04200822.summary: The community of Forojuliensium expresses its devotion to Emperor Gallienus.

EDCS-04200823.translation: Aurelia Gemellina set up (this monument) to her incomparable son, Caecilius Rufus, son of Quintus Caecilius Rufus, praefect, who lived for 10 years and 24 days.
EDCS-04200823.summary: A mother erected a tombstone for her son, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-04200824.translation: Quintus Caedius, son of Publius, of the Pupinia tribe, as a sexvir, made (this) while alive. His wife, Vinisia Maxuma, daughter of Quintus. His mother, Apusidia Secunda, daughter of Gaius. His brother, Gaius Caedius, son of Publius.
EDCS-04200824.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Quintus Caedius, his wife, mother, and brother, indicating his status as a sexvir.

EDCS-04200825.translation: To Publius Fabius Pudentus, son of Publius, of the Scaptia tribe, a quinquennalis and patron of the municipality, and to his son Publius Fabius Verecundus, a freedman and Augustalis. Publius Fabius Philetus, his freedman, a sexvir, made (this) while alive, for his wife Fabia Festa, freedwoman of Publius, for his son Adauctus, aged 20, for his son Felix, freedman of Publius, for his freedwoman Fabia Compse, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04200825.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Fabius Philetus, a sexvir, for his family members including his father, wife, and sons, and other freedpersons.

EDCS-04200826.translation: Titus Vettidius Valens, son of Titus, of the Scaptia tribe, a quinquennalis presiding over justice and a pontifex, ordered (this monument) to be made by his will for himself and for his son Titus Vettidius Potens, who was 20 years, 4 months, and 5 days old.
EDCS-04200826.summary: Titus Vettidius Valens, a quinquennalis and pontifex, established a monument for himself and his son who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-04200827.translation: Agathus, having attained the rights of children through divine majesty, a sexvir Augustalis of Aquileia, made (this) for himself.
EDCS-04200827.summary: Agathus, a sexvir Augustalis of Aquileia, erected a monument for himself.

EDCS-04200830.translation: Apilia Caelerina set up (this monument) for herself while alive.
EDCS-04200830.summary: Apilia Caelerina dedicated a monument to herself during her lifetime.

EDCS-04200831.translation: Gaius Arrius, son of Gaius, ordered (this monument) to be made for himself. Sextus Acilius, son of Gaius, his heir, made (it).
EDCS-04200831.summary: Gaius Arrius commissioned a tomb for himself, which his heir, Sextus Acilius, constructed.

EDCS-04200832.translation: To Marcus Aulus Mitiacus; by Aula Mitiaci, daughter; and by [---]us, son of Caius, son of T[---].
EDCS-04200832.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription likely recording the deceased and their relations, possibly from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200833.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Campilea Aphrodisia, aged 20 years and 10 months. [---]philos. The patron set this up.
EDCS-04200833.summary: A funerary epitaph for Campilea Aphrodisia, detailing her age and noting that her patron erected the monument, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200834.translation: Rustica ordered this to be made in her will. By Amerimnus, freedman of Flavidius, and To[---], freedwoman of Flavidia.
EDCS-04200834.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that the monument was commissioned by Rustica in her will, and erected by her freedmen Amerimnus and To[---], likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200835.translation: To Publius Graxius, son of Publius, father. Ti[---].
EDCS-04200835.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription honoring Publius Graxius, possibly indicating his role as a father, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200836.translation: Lucius Menaudonius Flaccus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04200836.summary: A simple funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Menaudonius Flaccus and his former master, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200837.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Revidia Marcella, a woman of unique chastity and modesty. Sextius Eros, because of her distinguished devotion towards his son, [set this up].
EDCS-04200837.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Sextius Eros to Revidia Marcella, praising her character and her devotion to his son, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200838.translation: Titus Suttius, son of Lucius, of the Scaptia tribe; Aiteia, daughter of Lucius; Posilia, wife. Made the monument in her will.
EDCS-04200838.summary: A funerary monument erected by Posilia in her will, commemorating herself and her husband Titus Suttius and his sister Aiteia, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04200840.summary: A very fragmentary inscription possibly recording freedmen, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200843.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04200843.translation: To well-deserving Augustus and Ursila, who lived Augustus for 4 years, 7 months, 12 days, and Ursilla for 4 years, [7] months, 15 days. The parents erected this against [their] hopes.
EDCS-04200843.summary: A funerary epitaph for two children, Augustus and Ursilla, detailing their ages and erected by their parents who buried them prematurely, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200844.summary: A fragment possibly identifying a person named Proculus from Milan, origin unknown, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04200845.translation: To the Divine Shades of Marcus Aurelius Hilarion, freedman of the Emperors.
EDCS-04200845.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades of a freedman of the emperors.

EDCS-04200847.translation: To Lucilia Politice, from Titus Virtius Homerus, her dearest wife.
EDCS-04200847.summary: This epitaph is dedicated by Titus Virtius Homerus to his beloved wife, Lucilia Politice.

EDCS-04200850.summary: This dedication is to Ollode, the wife of Saturninus.

EDCS-04200852.translation: Titus Fanius, son of Titus; Gaius Fanius Niger, son of Titus; Titus Fanius, son of Gaius; Tullia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, wife. They made (this tomb) for themselves and their family while alive.
EDCS-04200852.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the Fanius family, likely made by members while they were alive for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-04200853.translation: Lucius Tumbilicius, son of Aulus, from the Claudia tribe. A plot of land extending 30 feet in all directions.
EDCS-04200853.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, specifying its dimensions (30 feet in every direction) and belonging to Lucius Tumbilicius.

EDCS-04200855.translation: To my sweetest husband Albinus, the well-deserving, to good memory. Crescentina, the virgin, with whom he lived united for 30 years, and served in the military, and lived in the world 80 years, 4 months, and 8 days, as a standard-bearer veteran and protector. Crescentina, his wife, made this.
EDCS-04200855.summary: This epitaph honors Albinus, a veteran, and records his lifespan and marriage duration, erected by his wife Crescentina.

EDCS-04200856.translation: To Gaius Hostilius Rufus, son of Gaius. For himself and his family. The front length of the monument plot is 60 feet.
EDCS-04200856.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates a plot of land measuring 60 feet in width to Gaius Hostilius Rufus for himself and his family.

EDCS-04200857.translation: To Marcus Pacilius Marcello, my husband; to our son Marcus Pacilius Collino, son of Marcus (from the Claudia tribe); to our daughter Pacilia Marcella, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04200857.summary: This is a familial funerary inscription honoring a husband and two children, likely set up by a surviving spouse.

EDCS-04200860.translation: To Ionis, freedwoman of Sallustia Minnis. Callistus, deputy of Phoebus, Caesar Augustus's cashier, for his fellow soldier (contubernalis), aged 16.
EDCS-04200860.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Callistus to his deceased fellow soldier (contubernalis), Ionis, who was the freedwoman of Sallustia Minnis and died at age 16.

EDCS-04200861.translation: Titus Veratius, son of Titus (from the Claudia tribe), made (this) for himself and his family while alive. Valeria Quarta, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04200861.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Veratius, made by himself while alive for his family, and also mentioning Valeria Quarta.

EDCS-04200862.translation: Titus Veratius, son of Titus; Publius Veratius, son of Titus. [Set up by] Gemini.
EDCS-04200862.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Titus Veratius and Publius Veratius, sons of Titus, possibly brothers, with Gemini indicated as the dedicator.

EDCS-04200863.translation: Marcus Ennius Marcellus, son of Publius, made (this) for himself and for his son Marcus Ennius Maximus, aged 20; most devoted to him; and for his wife Maecilia Tertia, daughter of Gaius. He made (this) while alive.
EDCS-04200863.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Marcus Ennius Marcellus while alive for himself, his son Marcus Ennius Maximus (who died at age 20), and his wife Maecilia Tertia.

EDCS-04200864.translation: Publius Veidius Birro, son of Gaius. Pontia Tertia, daughter of Sextus, his wife. Gaius Veidius Maximus, son of Publius. Veidia Maxuma, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04200864.summary: This is a family tombstone for Publius Veidius Birro, his wife Pontia Tertia, and their children Gaius and Veidia.

EDCS-04200865.translation: To [---], son of Titus, Claudia, wife of [---], a man of the second rank.
EDCS-04200865.summary: This inscription mentions a man, his wife Claudia, and his rank within a group, possibly a collegium.

EDCS-04200866.translation: Gaius Egnatius, son of Titus, Veitor, made this while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200866.summary: This is a dedication made by Gaius Egnatius Veitor for himself and his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200867.translation: To Gaius Virginus Pulcher, son of Gaius, who lived 10 years, 2 months, and 6 days. Caius Virginius Marcellinus, son of Gaius, and Lollia Prisca, daughter of Lucius, the most unhappy parents, placed this for their sweetest and incomparable little son.
EDCS-04200867.summary: This epitaph is a memorial from extremely grieving parents to their young son who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-04200868.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Cautuspati.

EDCS-04200870.translation: To [---]. Aurelius Marcellus, Septimius Marcellinus, Septimius Speratus, Umbrius Iustinus, Bovius Rufinus, Musidius Valentinus, Frondius Frondianus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04200870.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely freedmen and others, who fulfilled a vow, possibly related to the cult of Hercules given the later context of similar inscriptions.

EDCS-04200871.text_edition: \n Caio Matio Cai filio Collina Sabinio Sullino Vatiniano Anicio Maximo Caesuleno Martiali Pisibano Lepido allecto inter quaestorios salio Palatino IIIviro monetali auro argento aere flando feriundo seviro equitum Romanorum flamini Iuliano patricio praetori candidato consuli curatori et patrono decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04200871.translation: To Gaius Matius Sabinius Sullinus Vatinianus Anicius Maximus Caesulenus Martialis Pisibanus Lepidus, son of Gaius, of the Collina tribe, who was appointed to the quaestorian rank, a Salian Palatine priest, a moneyer triumvir responsible for minting gold, silver, and bronze, a six-member equestrian leader, a Julian flamen, a patrician, a candidate for praetor, a curator, and patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04200871.summary: This is an honorific inscription, likely set up by a city council (decurions), celebrating the extensive career and high status of Gaius Matius Sabinius Sullinus Vatinianus Anicius Maximus Caesulenus Martialis Pisibanus Lepidus.

EDCS-04200872.translation: To Tiberius Magius Caecinianus, trierarch, and to his wife Alsiae Postumae: I was not, I am not, I do not care.
EDCS-04200872.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Magius Caecinianus, a trierarch, and his wife, with a philosophical statement about existence and indifference.

EDCS-04200874.summary: This is the beginning of an inscription recording the name and filiation of Titus Baebius, possibly a magistrate or a citizen.

EDCS-04200875.translation: Lucius Celerius Fronto, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, made this while alive for himself and his family, and for Clevia Maxima, daughter of Titus, his most dutiful wife.
EDCS-04200875.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Celerius Fronto for himself, his family, and his wife Clevia Maxima, indicating it was constructed during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200876.translation: Publius Arrius Dexter to Decia Avita, daughter of Publius, his most sacred mother.
EDCS-04200876.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Publius Arrius Dexter to his mother, Decia Avita, likely a funerary or honorific monument.

EDCS-04200877.translation: Marcus Fouscius Licnus, son of Caius, a traveler. Caius Fouscius Balbus, son of Caius, made this while alive for themselves and their families.
EDCS-04200877.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caius Fouscius Balbus for himself and his family, mentioning Marcus Fouscius Licnus, possibly a relative or fellow traveler.

EDCS-04200878.translation: To Iuventia Donata, his excellent wife, who lived 25 years and 3 months. Titius Iulius Iulianus.
EDCS-04200878.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Iuventia Donata, wife of Titius Iulius Iulianus, who died at the age of 25 years and 3 months.

EDCS-04200879.translation: Made by Sextus Lisinius Hilarus, freedman of Sextus Lisinius, for himself while alive. Also made by Sextus Lisinius Argentillus, freedman of Sextus Lisinius, while alive. Also made by Sextus Lisinius, freedman of Sextus Lisinius Dasmus.
EDCS-04200879.summary: This funerary inscription records several individuals, likely freedmen and their patrons from the Lisinii family, who set up their monuments during their lifetimes.

EDCS-04200880.translation: Lucius Lucretius made this while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200880.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Lucius Lucretius constructed the monument for himself and his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-04200881.translation: Here rests in peace Columba, a consecrated virgin of God, who lived in the Lord for about ninety years, laid to rest on the eighth day before the Ides of August, with Opilio, a most distinguished man, as consul, in the second indiction.
EDCS-04200881.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Columba, a consecrated virgin, providing her age, burial date, and the consul of the year, dating it to late antiquity.

EDCS-04200886.translation: The bones of Lucius Accius Libellus (?).
EDCS-04200886.summary: This is a very brief epitaph, likely on a burial marker or ossuary, identifying the remains as belonging to Lucius Acci Libell(i?).

EDCS-04200887.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Fulvius Arpetio made this while alive for himself and for Sextilia Tertia, his incomparable wife, deceased at 35 years of age.
EDCS-04200887.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, set up by Quintus Fulvius Arpetio for himself and his deceased wife Sextilia Tertia, who died at 35.

EDCS-04200888.translation: The above-mentioned men, Publius Erbonius Princeps, freedman of Publius, and Sextus Votticius Argentillus, freedman of Sextus, as magistrates of the district, restored the temple of Belinus with their own money and dedicated five gilded shields and two statues on the pediment.
EDCS-04200888.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the temple of Belinus and the dedication of votive offerings by two local magistrates, Publius Erbonius Princeps and Sextus Votticius Argentillus.

EDCS-04200889.translation: The magistrates of the district, Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Philogenes; Gavius, freedman of Philemon, Hilarius; Lucius Regontius, freedman of Lucius, Stephanus; Mulvius, freedman of Dition, Senecio; Lucius Gavius, freedman of Lucius, Gratus; Hilarus, slave of Vettius, freedman of Titus, Philoemon; Sextus Votticius, freedman of Argentilus, Amor; Titus Titius, freedman of Titus, Philoemon; Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Philogenes; Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Diphilus; Marcus Quinctilius, freedman of Marcus, Donatus, erected the temple of Hercules at their own expense.
EDCS-04200889.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple dedicated to Hercules by a group of district magistrates, many of whom are freedmen, likely dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04200890.translation: [...] Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Graptus, [...] the temple of Hercules.
EDCS-04200890.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the construction or repair of a temple dedicated to Hercules by Sextus Erbonius.

EDCS-04200891.translation: Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Tertius; Gaius Rotenius, freedman of Gaius, Severus; Gnaeus Cornelius, freedman of Gnaeus, Rufio; Quintus Porcius, freedman of Quintus, Optatus; Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Adiutor; Marcus Quinctilius, freedman of Marcus, Secundus; Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Princeps; Sextus Erbonius, freedman of Sextus, Gallio; Quintus Marius, freedman of Quintus, Myro; [...]
EDCS-04200891.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, primarily freedmen, likely associated with a specific collegium or vici, with their names and patrons.

EDCS-04200892.translation: Cato, son of Quintus. Tertius, son of Marcus. Priscus, son of Caius. Marcellus, son of Marcus. Aquilo, son of Lucius. Rufus, son of Caius. Castellus, son of Quintus. Niger, son of Tiberius. Priscus, son of Titus.
EDCS-04200892.summary: This inscription lists the names and patronymics of nine individuals, likely indicating their presence or ownership in a particular location or context, possibly a list of property owners or members of a group.

EDCS-04200896.translation: By the gracious will of our lord the Invictus Emperor Marcus Aurelius Alexander Augustus, the market hall was restored, under the care of Falerio Falerianus.
EDCS-04200896.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a market building (macellum) under the authority of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Alexander, with Falerio Falerianus overseeing the work, dating it to his reign (222-235 AD).

EDCS-04200898.translation: Marcus Iuventius Oclatus, son of Marcus, of the Claudia tribe, a veteran of the 8th Praetorian cohort, ordered this to be made for himself by his will.
EDCS-04200898.summary: A funerary monument for Marcus Iuventius Oclatus, a veteran of the Praetorian Guard, erected by his will.

EDCS-04200899.translation: Gaius Retinacius, son of Gaius, twice a civic officer, ordered this to be made by his will. Retinacia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, his wife. Retinacia Gaia, daughter of Lucius. Lucius Retinacius Crispus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04200899.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument erected by order of Gaius Retinacius, funded by his will, and also honors his wife and son, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04200900.translation: To the gods of the departed. Marcus Volumnius Urbanus, son of Marcus, of the Claudia tribe, decurion of the colony of Iulius Carnicus, IIvir iure dicundo, [dedicated this] to his well-deserving patron Marcus Volumnius Ardeatinus and to his most beloved wife, Iulia Iucunda.
EDCS-04200900.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Volumnius Urbanus, a local magistrate, to his patron and wife, likely from the colony of Iulius Carnicus.

EDCS-04200902.translation: [...] brought water [...] ano and Gaius Vitorio
EDCS-04200902.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the provision of water, possibly part of an aqueduct or fountain project, mentioning Gaius Vitorio.

EDCS-04200903.summary: This inscription records the name of a freedman and his patron, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-04200904.text_edition: \n Apiniae Marci filiae Tertiae ex testamento fieri iussit Marcus Apinius Fidelis libertus fecit\n
EDCS-04200904.translation: Marcus Apinius Fidelis, freedman, ordered this to be made for Apinia Tertia, daughter of Marcus, according to her will.
EDCS-04200904.summary: A funerary monument for Apinia Tertia, commissioned by her freedman Marcus Apinius Fidelis as per her will.

EDCS-04200906.translation: To Marcus Baebius Urbinianus, son of Marcus, son of Velina.
EDCS-04200906.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Baebius Urbinianus, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04200907.translation: Lucius Cominius Philostratus, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and his family. Lucius Cilo, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Raetus, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Princeps, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius. Cominia Urbana, freedwoman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Galata, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04200907.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Cominius Philostratus and several freedmen for themselves and their families, indicating a complex network of freed patronage.

EDCS-04200909.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a name and filiation.

EDCS-04200910.translation: Of Marcus Orbicius, freedman of Lucius Marcus Nicetonis, in the consular rank.
EDCS-04200910.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Orbicius, freedman of Nicetonis, and refers to a consular office.

EDCS-04200912.translation: Gaius Gentus, freedman of Gaius Papius.
EDCS-04200912.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a name and freedman status.

EDCS-04200913.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a name and freedman status.

EDCS-04200914.summary: This inscription likely indicates a burial place for Plonica.

EDCS-04200916.summary: This inscription appears to list names, possibly of individuals associated with a monument or funerary context.

EDCS-04200917.translation: Here rests in peace Ienuarius, bishop of this holy church, who ruled it for 10 years, buried on the day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of Faustus, most illustrious junior.
EDCS-04200917.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Ienuarius, a bishop, and mentions his tenure and the date of his burial.

EDCS-04200919.summary: This fragmented inscription contains partial names, likely from a funerary or commemorative context.

EDCS-04200921.translation: By the munificence of our lords Emperors Valentinian and Valens, this road, where people and animals travelled with danger, was opened, under the supervision of Apinus Programmatius, curator of the public affairs of the people of Iulian Carnorum, in the fourth consulship of our lords Valentinian and Valens.
EDCS-04200921.summary: This inscription records the opening of a dangerous road through imperial munificence, supervised by Apinus Programmatius, and dates to the fourth consulship of Valentinian and Valens.

EDCS-04200922.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Trivia, Quadrivia, and all the gods, he dedicated this solemn vow with a statue. Hermias, undertaker of eternal work, inscribed this immense title on the Alpine mountain with huge letters, so that often when travelers were in danger and the people were crossing at the bridge, it was not pleasing. For the curia and their quaestor Attius Braetianus, an honored man, showing a new road, Hermias, trusting greatly in his work and prepared for the task, united all to explain this road.
EDCS-04200922.summary: An inscription detailing the construction of a new road and bridge, commissioned by Hermias and approved by the curia and quaestor Attius Braetianus, likely in a mountainous region.

EDCS-04200923.text_edition: \n Respectus Titi Iuli Persei conductoris publici portorii vectigalis Illyrici servus vilicus stationis Glemoniensis ERIN PERON PERICLITAI TAMT ex TID\n
EDCS-04200923.translation: Respectus, slave of Titus Iulius Perseus, public contractor of the port duties and taxes of Illyricum, overseer of the Glemoniensis station, PERICLITAI TAMT from TID.
EDCS-04200923.summary: An inscription identifying Respectus, a slave and overseer for a tax collector in the Illyricum region, likely at the Glemoniensis station.

EDCS-04200924.translation: Lucius Virtius Albinus, son of Lucius, and Regia Ommonta, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive for themselves, their families, their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants; this monument will not be inherited by an heir.
EDCS-04200924.summary: A funerary monument erected by a couple, Lucius Virtius Albinus and Regia Ommonta, for themselves, their families, and freedmen, with a clause preventing it from passing to an heir.

EDCS-04200925.translation: Marcus Porcius Tertius, to Belenus Augustus, for Concord.
EDCS-04200925.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Belenus Augustus by Marcus Porcius Tertius, possibly for concord.

EDCS-04200926.text_edition: \n Fortunae Augustae sacrum Caius Opetrius Philetus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04200926.translation: Sacred to Imperial Fortune. Caius Opetrius Philetus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04200926.summary: A private dedication to Fortuna Augusta by Caius Opetrius Philetus.

EDCS-04200927.translation: Ixus, freedman, to the Genius of his master, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04200927.summary: A freedman named Ixus dedicates an offering to the Genius of his master.

EDCS-04200928.translation: [---] Laco, son of Caius, to Isis.
EDCS-04200928.summary: A dedication to the goddess Isis by Laco.

EDCS-04200929.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus, for the safety of the Emperor Commodus Augustus, Pius Felix, Valerius Maximus, centurion of the IV Flavia legion, and for his own, from a vision.
EDCS-04200929.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter Dolichenus by Valerius Maximus, a centurion, for the safety of Emperor Commodus and himself.

EDCS-04200933.text_edition: \n Caio Arrio Cai filio Quirina Antonino praefecto aerari Saturni iuridico per Italiam regionis Transpadanae primo fratri Arvali praetori cui primo iurisdictio pupillaris a sanctissimis imperatoribus mandata est aedili curuli ab actis senatus seviro equestrium turmarum tribuno laticlavio legionis IIII Scythicae IIIIviro viarum curandarum qui providentia maximorum imperatorum missus urgentis annonae difficulitates sic iuvit et consuluit securitati fundatis rei publicae opibus ordo Concordiensium patrono optimo ob innocentiam et labori sic\n
EDCS-04200933.translation: To Caius Arrius Antoninus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, praefect of the Saturnian treasury, juridical official for the region of Transpadana, first brother of the Arvales, praetor, to whom the guardianship of minors was first entrusted by the most holy emperors, curule aedile, official for the acta of the Senate, seviral for the equestrian turmae, broad-striped legionary tribune of the IV Scythica legion, quaestor for public works, who, by the foresight of the most powerful emperors, was sent to relieve difficulties of the grain supply and so aided and secured the Republic's resources, the order of Concordiensium [dedicates this] to their most excellent patron for his integrity and for his efforts.
