EDCS-04200933.summary: A dedication by the people of Concordium to Caius Arrius Antoninus, honoring his extensive public career and service to the grain supply.

EDCS-04200934.text_edition: \n Tito Desticio Titi filio Claudia Iubae clarissimo viro praetorio ordo Concor diensium patrono\n
EDCS-04200934.translation: To Titus Desticus Iuba, son of Titus, of the Claudia tribe, a most distinguished man, formerly praetorian, the order of Concordiensium [dedicates this] as patron.
EDCS-04200934.summary: The people of Concordium honor Titus Desticus Iuba, a distinguished former praetorian, as their patron.

EDCS-04200935.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Potentinus, slave, made [this] for Desticia Philenis, aged 30, freedwoman of Titus Desticus Iuba, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-04200935.summary: A tombstone set up by a slave for his deceased freedwoman, who was also the freedwoman of a distinguished man.

EDCS-04200937.text_edition: \n Tito Trebelleno Luci filio Claudia Rufo quaestori tribuno plebis legato Caesaris Augusti plebs\n
EDCS-04200937.translation: To Titus Trebellennus Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, legate of Caesar Augustus, the plebs [dedicates this].
EDCS-04200937.summary: The plebs honor Titus Trebellennus Rufus, who served as quaestor, tribune, and legate.

EDCS-04200939.translation: To Flavius Victor, a ducenarius and chief of the imperial stable, who lived 62 years and served under Augustus for 13 years. Aurelia Maura, his wife, [made this] for her most dear husband. What Verginius ought to have done for his daughter [now] Virginia has done. With whom she lived well for 35 years. She also made [this] for herself. If anyone wishes to be buried in this place, they will pay 600 folles of denarii into the public treasury.
EDCS-04200939.summary: A tombstone set up by a wife for her husband, a stable official, which also includes a provision for future burials and payment to the state.

EDCS-04200940.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aurelius Valerius, formerly standard-bearer of the V Macedonica legion, lived 60 years.
EDCS-04200940.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Aurelius Valerius, a former standard-bearer of the V Macedonica legion.

EDCS-04200941.translation: Gaius Baebius, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe. Publius Baebius, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe. Publius Baebius, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe, an equestrian of the 13th Twin Legion, adorned with armbands. Pedania Secunda, daughter of Lucius, his mother. Publius Baebius, son of Publius, his father, who held magistracies and served as a military tribune.
EDCS-04200941.summary: This funerary inscription honors members of the Baebius family, including a legionary veteran and his father, who achieved military rank, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200942.translation: Gaius Aquillius Mela, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, from the armamentaria department, ordered this to be made, having served twice as a quinquennial.
EDCS-04200942.summary: This inscription records a building project commissioned by Gaius Aquillius Mela, who held a quinquennial office, likely in the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200943.translation: To Marcus Armonius Astura, freedman of Marcus, his patron, a sevir of Forum Cornelii and a sexvir. Julia Concordia ordered this to be made by testament for Marcus Armonius, freedman of Marcus, named Auctus, and for Opponia, freedwoman of Gaius, named Tertia. Marcus Armonius Salvius, freedman of Marcus, a sexvir, ordered this to be made by testament.
EDCS-04200943.summary: This funerary inscription records the commission of tombs by freedmen and for freedmen, mentioning their patrons and civic offices, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200944.translation: Marcus Arrius, son of Gaius, a decurion.
EDCS-04200944.summary: This very brief inscription likely records the name and status of Marcus Arrius, a decurion, possibly a tombstone or a dedication of a public office, from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200945.translation: Aulus Bruttius Secundus, freedman of Aulus, a sextumvir, prefect of architects, gave the crepidines (steps or platforms) between the wall and the bridge for half and a third part.
EDCS-04200945.summary: This inscription records a donation of construction materials for a public work by Aulus Bruttius Secundus, who held significant civic and professional roles, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200946.translation: Aulus Bruttius Tarto, freedman of Aulus, a sextumvir, [provided] the crepidines between the two bridges.
EDCS-04200946.summary: This inscription records a donation of construction materials by Aulus Bruttius Tarto, identified as a sextumvir, likely for a public infrastructure project, from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200947.translation: [Commissioned] by testament to be made for the aedile, prefect of craftsmen. Quintus Decius Calvinus, son of Quintus, for his sister's son.
EDCS-04200947.summary: This funerary inscription indicates a testament commission for a deceased aedile and prefect of craftsmen, with the monument dedicated by his nephew, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200948.text_edition: \n Ennius Luci filius Runcho IIIIIIvir dedit\n
EDCS-04200948.translation: Ennius Runcho, son of Lucius, a quinquennial duovir, dedicated [this].
EDCS-04200948.summary: Ennius Runcho, a quinquennial duovir, dedicated this monument.

EDCS-04200949.translation: Gaius Fulvius, son of Spurius; Marcus Muttenus, son of Aulus; Lucius Iulius, son of Gaius; Lucius Trosius, son of Marcus; magistrates.
EDCS-04200949.summary: This inscription lists the names and patronymics of four individuals who held magistracies, likely in a local government context, from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200950.translation: Quintus Lancidinus, son of Quintus, Publius [---], as IIvir (two officials), by decree of the decurions, a crypt [---].
EDCS-04200950.summary: This inscription records a public work, a crypt, commissioned by a local official named Quintus Lancidinus.

EDCS-04200951.translation: Publius Minnius Salvius, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe, a former primipilus and honorary decurion, having received the IIviral ornaments, ordered by his testament that the roads around the temple of Minerva be paved with dressed stone.
EDCS-04200951.summary: This inscription records a testamentary bequest by Publius Minnius Salvius, a distinguished military veteran and local official, for the paving of roads around the temple of Minerva, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200952.translation: To Lucius Numisius, son of Gaius, aedile of Forum Cornelii. Gracconia, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04200952.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Numisius, an aedile of Forum Cornelii, likely set up by his wife or female relative, Gracconia, from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04200953.translation: Aulus Ritius Tertius Augustalis, freedman of Aulus, by his will ordered the road to be paved, on which 30,000 sesterces were spent.
EDCS-04200953.summary: This inscription records a posthumous benefaction by Aulus Ritius Tertius Augustalis, who funded the paving of a road.

EDCS-04200954.translation: For the memory of Publius Terentius Claudius, aedile and IIvir. Titus Vettius Gnesius gave 400,000 sesterces for the work and ornamentation, with the twentieth part deducted.
EDCS-04200954.summary: This inscription records a donation of 400,000 sesterces by Titus Vettius Gnesius for public works and decoration, likely during the period when Publius Terentius Claudius was aedile and IIvir.

EDCS-04200955.translation: Lucius Varius Myro, freedman of Lucius, Augustalis, made this monument in his lifetime for himself and for his mother Acilia Primigenia, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants; this monument will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-04200955.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Varius Myro, a freedman, for himself and his family, stipulating that it is not hereditary.

EDCS-04200958.translation: Ordered to be made by Concordia.
EDCS-04200958.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to record the dedication or commissioning of a monument or work by a person or deity named Concordia.

EDCS-04200962.translation: Attia Corinthis, freedwoman of Marcus, from Ancona.
EDCS-04200962.summary: This inscription identifies Attia Corinthis, a freedwoman from Ancona, likely as the subject of a dedication or marker.

EDCS-04200963.translation: Italia Metti Aulus made this in her lifetime for herself and for Lascivus, trainer of murmillones (a type of gladiator).
EDCS-04200963.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument made by Italia Metti Aulus for herself and her trainer of gladiators, Lascivus.

EDCS-04200964.translation: To Lucius Manlius Tutor, son of Manlius, from Noricum, of the Titenian tribe.
EDCS-04200964.summary: This is a dedication or memorial to Lucius Manlius Tutor, providing his filiation, origin (Noricum), and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04200965.translation: To Decimus Sempronius Hilarus, patron and physician.
EDCS-04200965.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Decimus Sempronius Hilarus, honoring him as both a patron and a physician.

EDCS-04200966.translation: Decimus Sempronius Iucundus, physician, from Ariminum [---].
EDCS-04200966.summary: This inscription identifies Decimus Sempronius Iucundus as a physician from Ariminum.

EDCS-04200967.summary: This inscription commemorates Anthusa, the companion-in-arms of Troilus, likely a soldier.

EDCS-04200968.translation: Marcus Antistius Statius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04200968.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Antistius Statius, a freedman of Marcus, possibly marking his tomb or a dedication.

EDCS-04200969.summary: This inscription records the death of a child named Atticus who lived for three years.

EDCS-04200970.translation: Marcus Avillius Herophilus, freedman of Marcus, and Fausta, a freedwoman, set this up.
EDCS-04200970.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Marcus Avillius Herophilus, a freedman of Marcus, and Fausta, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04200971.translation: Marcus Auruncius Alexander made this in his lifetime for Autronia Maxuma, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04200971.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Marcus Auruncius Alexander for Autronia Maxuma.

EDCS-04200972.translation: Lucius Barbius Abascantus made this in his lifetime for himself and for his freedwoman wife Zoe, and for his children Lucius Barbius Zoilus and Barhia Severilla, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-04200972.summary: This funerary monument was made by Lucius Barbius Abascantus for himself, his wife Zoe, their children, and their descendants and freedpersons.

EDCS-04200973.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription beginning with the genitive case, likely part of a dedication or ownership marker for Lucius Caesius Co...

EDCS-04200974.translation: Publius Cervonius Marinus, son of Publius, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his wife Cinciai Secundai, daughter of Sextus, and for his concubine Cilai.
EDCS-04200974.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Publius Cervonius Marinus commissioned his tomb by will for himself, his wife, and his concubine.

EDCS-04200975.translation: Lucius Cervonius Zosimus made this for himself and for his wife Cassia Pyrrha and his family; in front 12 feet, behind 26 feet.
EDCS-04200975.summary: This inscription marks a plot of land measuring 12 feet in the front and 26 feet in the back, made by Lucius Cervonius Zosimus for his family.

EDCS-04200976.translation: Caius Clavenius Faustus, son of Caius, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04200976.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Caius Clavenius Faustus for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-04200977.translation: To Quintus Decius Pothumenus, aged 5 years, 6 months, and 20 days, a most beloved son. Decii Helius and Chreste, his parents, made this.
EDCS-04200977.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Decius Pothumenus, a young child, set up by his parents, Decii Helius and Chreste.

EDCS-04200978.translation: Caius Deipius Philotimus, son of Publius.
EDCS-04200978.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Deipius Philotimus, son of Publius.

EDCS-04200979.translation: To Eroti, freedman of Caius. Elvia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, [and] Marcus Elvius Marcellus, son of Marcus, her brother. To Domitia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, their mother.
EDCS-04200979.summary: This funerary inscription honors Eroti, freedman of Caius, and remembers Elvia Secunda, Marcus Elvius Marcellus, and their mother Domitia Tertia.

EDCS-04200980.translation: Caius Ennius Enno, son of Caius, in front 20 feet, behind 20 feet.
EDCS-04200980.summary: This inscription indicates a plot of land, 20 feet by 20 feet, belonging to Caius Ennius Enno.

EDCS-04200981.translation: Burial place of Caius Ennius Thesmus, freedman of Caius, and Trebia Lepida, freedwoman of Publius, in front 30 feet, behind 25 feet.
EDCS-04200981.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot measuring 30 feet by 25 feet, belonging to Caius Ennius Thesmus and Trebia Lepida.

EDCS-04200982.translation: To Quintus Fabio Caemianus, a noble youth, who lived 17 years, 6 months, and 22 days; from his mother Turrania Sestia, to her dearest son.
EDCS-04200982.summary: This epitaph records the death of a young man named Quintus Fabio Caemianus, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-04200983.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gavia Auge, a freedwoman of Publius.

EDCS-04200984.translation: To Iulia Nigella, his beloved Thallusae, aged 19 years.
EDCS-04200984.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Iulia Nigella, aged 19, by her beloved Thallusae.

EDCS-04200985.translation: To the shades below. Gaius Laecinius Maximus made this for himself and his wife Vedia Restuta, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, while he was alive.
EDCS-04200985.summary: This is a funerary monument (likely a tomb) dedicated by Gaius Laecinius Maximus for himself, his wife, and his freedmen.

EDCS-04200986.translation: Lamirus made this for his son Sextus.
EDCS-04200986.summary: This funerary inscription records that Lamirus made the monument for his son Sextus.

EDCS-04200987.translation: [made] by Fausto, from Lancidena Rutila, his freedwoman, to Nigella, while he was alive.
EDCS-04200987.summary: This inscription records a tomb made by Fausto for Nigella, his freedwoman.

EDCS-04200988.translation: Burial place of Marcus Lurius Ianuarius, in front 16 feet, to the back 30 feet.
EDCS-04200988.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Marcus Lurius Ianuarius, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04200989.translation: Caius Mammius Sabinus, son of Caius, aged 81 [or perhaps 30?], [for] his wife, Caius Mammius Silon, son of Caius.
EDCS-04200989.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Mammius Sabinus and his wife, possibly also including Caius Mammius Silon.

EDCS-04200990.translation: To the shades below. [---]neteia Maxima, in front 19 feet, in the field 50 feet.
EDCS-04200990.summary: This inscription, part of a funerary monument, records the dimensions of a plot for Maxima.

EDCS-04200991.translation: Sextus Numisius Hilarus, freedman of Sextus. Cincia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, his wife. Numisia Prima, daughter of Sextus. Sextus Numisius Niger, son of Sextus.
EDCS-04200991.summary: This funerary inscription lists Sextus Numisius Hilarus, his wife Cincia Secunda, and their children Numisia Prima and Sextus Numisius Niger.

EDCS-04200992.translation: Hail Octavius Alexander, who lived 27 years.
EDCS-04200992.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a man named Octavius Alexander who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-04200994.translation: To Gaius Plotus Primus, father; to Plotia, mother; to Plotus, son; to Plotia Secunda, daughter.
EDCS-04200994.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating deceased family members: a father, mother, son, and daughter, all bearing the name Plotus or Plotia.

EDCS-04200995.translation: To the shades below. Greetings, Primitiva. And you, whoever you are. Cincia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, wife of Numisius Prima. Sextus Numisius Niger, son of Sextus.
EDCS-04200995.summary: This is a tombstone for Cincia Secunda and Numisia Prima, with an inscription addressing passersby.

EDCS-04200997.translation: Gaius Seppius, son of Gaius, [restored] Tiburtia Nice.
EDCS-04200997.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records the names of individuals, possibly related to a funerary monument, with Gaius Seppius and Tiburtia Nice mentioned.

EDCS-04200998.translation: [dedicated] to his dearest son, who lived 12 years and 6 months. Lucius Statius Victorinus and his wife Julia Helena, the most unhappy parents, [dedicated this] for themselves.
EDCS-04200998.summary: This epitaph records the death of a son and is dedicated by his parents, Lucius Statius Victorinus and Julia Helena.

EDCS-04200999.translation: To the shades below. For Suavia Auxiliaris, the vicarius (subordinate official?).
EDCS-04200999.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Suavia Auxiliaris.

EDCS-04201000.translation: Gaius Titius Terentianus erected this while alive for himself.
EDCS-04201000.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Titius Terentianus for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04201001.translation: Sextus Titinius Nestor, freedman of Sextus, [purchased a plot] in front 20 feet, inwards 20 feet.
EDCS-04201001.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot purchased by Sextus Titinius Nestor, a freedman, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04201002.translation: Truttidia Prima, freedwoman of Sextus, ordered this to be made by her will for herself and for her freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04201002.summary: This funerary inscription, set up by Truttidia Prima, a freedwoman, for herself and her freed dependents, indicates she used her will to arrange for its construction.

EDCS-04201003.translation: Burial place of Quintus Valerius Anthus and Seppia Thisbe, and of Seppia Chrysaspis, in front 15 feet, in the field 30 feet.
EDCS-04201003.summary: This inscription delineates a burial plot belonging to Quintus Valerius Anthus, Seppia Thisbe, and Seppia Chrysaspis.

EDCS-04201004.translation: To the departed spirits. Valerius Firminus, aged 39. Priest.
EDCS-04201004.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valerius Firminus, who died at age 39, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201005.translation: Burial place and monument. In front, 20 feet; to the rear, 30 feet. Of Lucius Vilonius Lucullus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04201005.summary: A funerary inscription defining the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Vilonius Lucullus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201006.text_edition: \n Lucretius Auli filius Claudia sibi et sueis sic\n
EDCS-04201006.translation: Lucretius, son of Aulus, of the Claudia tribe, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201006.summary: An inscription by Lucretius, son of Aulus, reserving a space for himself and his family, probably for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-04201007.translation: Here lies... Cale, for himself and Ameno.
EDCS-04201007.summary: A funerary inscription, possibly designating a burial space for Cale and Ameno, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201011.translation: to Gio, son of Lucius, brother of Florus, Fad [restored]
EDCS-04201011.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to be part of a dedication or epitaph, mentioning individuals named Gio, Lucius, and Florus.

EDCS-04201012.translation: Paius Verzonis, son of Marte, erected this while alive for himself, his freedmen and freedwomen, by testament; the galley Clupeo.
EDCS-04201012.summary: A funerary monument erected by Paius Verzonis for himself and his freedpersons, mentioning a galley named Clupeo, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201013.translation: To Firmia Eleuthera, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201013.summary: This is a dedication to Firmia Eleuthera, identified as a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-04201014.translation: Quintus Licovius Dida, freedman of Quintus; Licovia Sperata, freedwoman of Quintus; Licovia Venusta, freedwoman of the woman; Quintus Licovius Ianuarius, freedman of the woman, aged 24. Quintus Licovius Priscus erected this while alive for himself and his family, and for the families of his family. For his dearest wife, Licovia Rufina.
EDCS-04201014.summary: A funerary monument erected by Quintus Licovius Priscus and others for themselves, their families, and specifically for his wife Licovia Rufina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201015.translation: Naevius, son of Titus, Publ [restored] in front.
EDCS-04201015.summary: This fragmented inscription mentions Naevius, son of Titus, and may refer to an inscription or monument's front part.

EDCS-04201018.translation: Olympus Leonicus, for himself and the body of Ursa Iulia.
EDCS-04201018.summary: A funerary inscription by Olympus Leonicus for himself and for Ursa Iulia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201019.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Gaius Lucius Tertius fulfills his vow willingly and deservedly for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201019.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Gaius Lucius Tertius, fulfilling a vow for himself and his family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201020.translation: Quintus Carminius Phileros, freedman of Quintus, erected this altar to Virbius, fulfilling his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04201020.summary: A dedication of an altar to the god Virbius by Quintus Carminius Phileros, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201022.text_edition: \n filio pontifici maximo patri patriae tribunicia potestate consuli II optimo maximoque principi Opitergini\n
EDCS-04201022.translation: To the son, pontifex maximus, father of the fatherland, holder of tribunician power, twice consul, the best and greatest princeps, of Opitergium.
EDCS-04201022.summary: An honorific inscription, likely for an emperor or high-ranking official, listing his titles and origin from Opitergium, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201023.text_edition: \n Pio Felici Invicto Augusto ordo Opiterginorum\n
EDCS-04201023.translation: To the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, the town council of the Opiterginians.
EDCS-04201023.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Augustus by the town council of Opitergium, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-04201026.text_edition: \n Lucio Ragonio Luci filio Papiria Tuscenio Quintiano clarissimo iuveni \n
EDCS-04201026.translation: To Lucius Ragonius Tuscenius Quintianus, son of Lucius Ragonius, of the Papirian tribe, a most distinguished young man.
EDCS-04201026.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Ragonius Tuscenius Quintianus, identified as a young man of high standing.

EDCS-04201027.translation: Lucius Ragonius Quintianus ordered this to be made by will for Gaius Sempronius Cassianus, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, his friend's son.
EDCS-04201027.summary: This funerary inscription records that Lucius Ragonius Quintianus commissioned a monument by his will for Gaius Sempronius Cassianus, his friend's son.

EDCS-04201029.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04201029.translation: Flavius Victor, veteran, for himself and his incomparable wife Zosmeti, with whom he lived religiously and with all chastity for 25 years, made this [tomb] while alive, from his own property. Whoever wishes to open this tomb after our death must pay six hundred folles (600 denarii) to the treasury.
EDCS-04201029.summary: This is an epitaph and funerary inscription by a veteran named Flavius Victor for himself and his wife, specifying a penalty for unauthorized opening of the tomb.

EDCS-04201030.translation: Caesia Grata, freedwoman of Manius, living, made this for Manius Caesius Euno, a IIIIvir, and for herself.
EDCS-04201030.summary: This funerary inscription records that Caesia Grata, a freedwoman, made a monument while alive for Manius Caesius Euno, a member of the IIIIvirate, and for herself.

EDCS-04201031.translation: Prima, freedwoman of Manius Castricius, Augustalis. [To whom?] / [---]
EDCS-04201031.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription for Prima, a freedwoman and an Augustalis, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201032.translation: By decree of the Augustales of Opitergium, to Titus Ennius Plancus.
EDCS-04201032.summary: A dedication to Titus Ennius Plancus, likely a local official or benefactor, by the Augustales of Opitergium.

EDCS-04201033.translation: Marcus Fulvius Marcellinus, son of Marcus, a VIvir of Concord, and of Opitergium, for himself and for Renniae Lygis, freedwoman of a woman, his excellent wife, made [this tomb] while alive. In front [X] feet.
EDCS-04201033.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Fulvius Marcellinus for himself and his wife Renniae Lygis, specifying dimensions of the monument.

EDCS-04201034.text_edition: \n Marco Laetorio Marci filio Papiria Patercliano IIIIviro iure dicundo II allecto aerarii salio patrono collegii Marcus Laetorius Paterclianus numero collegi Opitergii salutem collegii vest m omnibus ex optimi collegia c quoque cons ris commodis e posteritatis ut honorem ta nme conferendo s quo amore me debui hoc vestrum m largitione licet modica remunerare fero vobis HS XX millia nummum cum usuris centesimi quorum reditus efficit annuos cuius summae po sportulis vestr die natalis mei i qui vero |(denari---) I ticentur uo am vita meum orem OI \n
EDCS-04201034.translation: Marcus Laetorius Paterclianus, son of Marcus, of the Papirian tribe, a IIvir iure dicundo, a member of the aerarii salii, patron of the college, to Marcus Laetorius Paterclianus, of the college, greetings. It is fitting that your college, by conferring this honor upon me out of love and respect, should also acknowledge my merits and my posterity. I offer you 20,000 sesterces with interest at one percent, whose annual income amounts to... [---] denarii.
EDCS-04201034.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Laetorius Paterclianus to his college, donating a significant sum of money for their benefit and to commemorate himself.

EDCS-04201035.translation: Titus Quinctius, son of Marcus, gave this to the people.
EDCS-04201035.summary: A dedication by Titus Quinctius, son of Marcus, to the community, possibly related to a public work or gift.

EDCS-04201036.translation: Lucius Sempronius Ursio, a *quattuorvir iure dicundo*, made this in his lifetime for his parents, Lucius Sempronius Maximus, a *quattuorvir iure dicundo*, and Celerina, daughter of Lucius, and for his wife Ursa, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04201036.summary: A funerary or commemorative monument erected during his lifetime by Lucius Sempronius Ursio for his parents and wife, all of whom held or were related to holders of the *quattuorvirate* office.

EDCS-04201037.translation: Manius, a *sexvir*, [son] of Manius the freedman, [and] Manius the freedman's freedwoman.
EDCS-04201037.summary: An inscription listing individuals, possibly part of a tomb or group monument, identifying Manius as a *sexvir* and mentioning his freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-04201038.translation: Lucius Sicinius Priamus, freedman of Lucius, a goldsmith. Titus Carminius Atreus, freedman of a woman, a merchant.
EDCS-04201038.summary: A dual inscription recording two freedmen, Lucius Sicinius Priamus the goldsmith and Titus Carminius Atreus the merchant, possibly on a shared tomb or workplace.

EDCS-04201039.translation: To Publius Aiacius, son of Publius.
EDCS-04201039.summary: A dedication or epitaph for Publius Aiacius, son of Publius.

EDCS-04201040.translation: Lucius Autronius Maximus, 30 feet in front.
EDCS-04201040.summary: An inscription indicating a measurement of 30 feet related to Lucius Autronius Maximus, possibly marking land or a structure.

EDCS-04201041.translation: Barbia Maxuma, daughter of Manius, for herself and for Gaius Barbius Niger, son of Lucius, and for Gaius Barbius Tertius, son of Gaius, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-04201041.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Barbia Maxuma for herself and two men, likely family members, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201042.translation: To Titus Caelsius Chilo, son of Lucius, a man.
EDCS-04201042.summary: An epitaph or dedication for Titus Caelsius Chilo, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04201043.translation: Titus Cannutius, son of Titus. In front 30 feet, in the rear 34 feet.
EDCS-04201043.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Titus Cannutius, son of Titus.

EDCS-04201044.summary: A simple inscription listing two names, Canutia Regilla and Canutia Sedata, possibly on a tomb or as owners of property.

EDCS-04201045.translation: Gaius Carminius Iunianus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04201045.summary: This is a simple dedication or identification of Gaius Carminius Iunianus, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04201046.translation: To Carminia Mina, daughter of Caius, and to Stacte, the nurse.
EDCS-04201046.summary: A dedication or epitaph honoring Carminia Mina, daughter of Caius, and her nurse Stacte.

EDCS-04201048.translation: To my father and to Catia Maxuma, daughter of Tiberius, my mother.
EDCS-04201048.summary: This is a dedication to parents, likely from an epitaph.

EDCS-04201049.translation: His sons made (this) for Tito Cervonio Secundino, a good father.
EDCS-04201049.summary: This epitaph records sons dedicating a monument to their father, Tito Cervonio Secundino.

EDCS-04201050.translation: Titus Crutonius Acer, son of Titus, called Aper.
EDCS-04201050.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Titus Crutonius Acer Aper and his filiation.

EDCS-04201052.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Lucius Furius, son of Gnaeus.

EDCS-04201053.translation: To the Shades Below. Greetings to me. Heraclus, my incomparable son, who lived 9 years, 11 months, and 13 days. A most devoted father placed [this] for his deserving son.
EDCS-04201053.summary: This is a poignant epitaph from a father to his young son, Heraclus, detailing his lifespan and expressing deep grief.

EDCS-04201054.translation: Quintus Herennius Modestus, son of Tiberius.
EDCS-04201054.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Quintus Herennius Modestus and his filiation.

EDCS-04201055.summary: This funerary inscription identifies Iulia Dynamis.

EDCS-04201056.translation: To Gaius Laelius Optatus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-04201056.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Laelius Optatus, a freedman.

EDCS-04201057.translation: Laetilia Secunda, daughter of Tiberius, ordered (this) to be made by her will.
EDCS-04201057.summary: This funerary inscription states that Laetilia Secunda had this monument erected by her will.

EDCS-04201058.translation: Marcus Laetorius Donatus, freedman of Marcus, (grants) a place for burial and a monument: 15 feet in front, 55 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04201058.summary: This inscription records the grant of burial space and a monument by Marcus Laetorius Donatus.

EDCS-04201059.translation: To the departed spirits. Turelia Tertia, daughter of Titus, to her daughter Laplesosia. Tubero, son of [3]ti, ordered [this].
EDCS-04201059.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Turelia Tertia to her deceased daughter Laplesosia, with Tubero as the orderer.

EDCS-04201060.translation: To my wife and to Messia Maxsuma, daughter of Primus.
EDCS-04201060.summary: This is a dedication to a wife and her daughter, likely from an epitaph.

EDCS-04201061.translation: To Gaius Numonius Varia and Ubbia.
EDCS-04201061.summary: This inscription names two individuals, likely part of a dedication or funerary context.

EDCS-04201062.translation: To Popillia Paetilla, daughter of Manius, and her daughter Carminia Semprulla, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-04201062.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Popillia Paetilla and her daughter Carminia Semprulla.

EDCS-04201063.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [3]a Probata to Fructus, her most dutiful husband, publicly [dedicated this] and to herself and her most brave husband, with a frontage of 8 feet and a depth of 40 feet in the land.
EDCS-04201063.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Probata to her husband Fructus, likely dating to the Imperial period, and specifies the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04201064.summary: This inscription records the name of a freedwoman, Loeme.

EDCS-04201065.translation: Gaius Raecius, son of Spurius, made this while alive for himself and for his excellent wife, Cannutia Maxima, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04201065.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Raecius for himself and his wife, Cannutia Maxima.

EDCS-04201066.translation: Caesia, freedwoman of Raecia, daughter of Tiberius, ordered this to be made while alive for her patron and herself.
EDCS-04201066.summary: This inscription records the commission of a monument by Caesia, freedwoman of Raecia, for her patron and herself.

EDCS-04201067.translation: Lucius Rattius, son of Sextus, made this for himself, his family, and his wife, while alive. For Sextus Rattius, son of Quintus, his father, and Cassia, daughter of Sextus, his mother.
EDCS-04201067.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Rattius for himself and his family, including his parents Sextus Rattius and Cassia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201068.translation: To Gaius Rubrius Capito, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, and to his freedmen Secundus Optatus Fuscus.
EDCS-04201068.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Rubrius Capito and his freedmen.

EDCS-04201069.translation: Sarenus Valerius and Sarena Maxima made this monument for their dearest son Valentinian, who lived 5 years and 30 days, snatched away by a premature death.
EDCS-04201069.summary: This funerary inscription records the monument erected by Sarenus Valerius and Sarena Maxima for their young son Valentinian, who died prematurely.

EDCS-04201070.translation: Satria Tigris, daughter of Gaius, for herself and for her son Marcellus.
EDCS-04201070.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Satria Tigris for herself and her son Marcellus.

EDCS-04201071.translation: Lucius Seius Faustus, son of Lucius, and Titus Seius Fronto, son of Lucius, (made this) while alive for themselves, and for their mother Pisentia Secunda, and for their sister Seia, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04201071.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by two brothers, Lucius Seius Faustus and Titus Seius Fronto, for themselves and their mother and sister.

EDCS-04201072.translation: To Gaius Seppius, son of Publius.
EDCS-04201072.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Seppius, son of Publius.

EDCS-04201073.translation: Gaius Sestius Rufio, son of Publius, for himself and Fau[...
EDCS-04201073.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Sestius Rufio dedicating a monument for himself and another individual whose name is lost.

EDCS-04201074.translation: Marcus Socellius Cleno ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his freedwoman, Pilinna, his mother.
EDCS-04201074.summary: A funerary dedication for a man, his freedwoman, and his mother, likely dating to the 1st century BCE or 1st century CE.

EDCS-04201075.translation: Manius Terentius, son of Voltietis, made this for himself and his wife.
EDCS-04201075.summary: A funerary dedication for a man and his wife, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201076.translation: To Tertulla, freedwoman of Caius, daughter of Manius, wife of Tuscillus, son of Manius.
EDCS-04201076.summary: A funerary dedication for a freedwoman, indicating familial relationships and social status, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201077.translation: For Tiberius Varius, son of Tiberius; Caius Varius, son of Tiberius; Titus Varius, son of Tiberius. Burial place in front 30 feet, depth 70 feet.
EDCS-04201077.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to the Varii family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201078.translation: To Qu... son of... he made.
EDCS-04201078.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning a dedication to a son of Qu... by an unnamed dedicator.

EDCS-04201089.translation: Publius Aelius Pollius placed this, having been advised, to Asclepius.
EDCS-04201089.summary: A dedication to the god Asclepius, indicating a personal vow or commission.

EDCS-04201090.translation: For the honor of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, Sextus Paeticus, son of Quintus, the Third, and Sextus Paeticus, son of Sextus, Firmus, gave a clock with seating for pagans and laborers.
EDCS-04201090.summary: A dedication of a public clock and seating to the emperor Nero, likely dating to his reign (54-68 CE).

EDCS-04201091.translation: To Aesculapius Augustus, Ityrius Secundinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04201091.summary: This is a votive inscription from Ityrius Secundinus to the god Aesculapius Augustus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201093.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Publius Hostilius Sertorianus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04201093.summary: This is a votive inscription from Publius Hostilius Sertorianus to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201094.translation: Publius Geminius Severus, son of Caius, willingly and deservedly paid his vow. Publius Geminius Severus, son of Caius, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04201094.summary: This is a votive inscription repeated by Publius Geminius Severus to an unspecified deity, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201095.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Armeniaco Medico Parthico maximo pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XXI imperatori IIII consuli III patri patriae divi Antonini filio divi Hadriani nepoti divi Traiani Parthici pronepoti divi Nervae abnepoti decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04201095.translation: By decree of the decurions to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus maximus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 21st time, imperator for the 4th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, son of the divine Antoninus, grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the divine Nerva.
EDCS-04201095.summary: This is a decree by the decurions honouring Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus with a full titulature, reflecting his titles and lineage, likely from the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201096.summary: An incomplete inscription that begins with a personal name, likely a dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-04201097.translation: Titus Curtius, son of Titus Pris, the prefect.
EDCS-04201097.summary: An inscription identifying a Roman official, Titus Curtius Pris, who held the office of prefect.

EDCS-04201098.translation: To Gaius Durenus Secundus, of Opitergium by birth, who had fulfilled all the offices, Praecellia Procula for her most excellent husband.
EDCS-04201098.summary: A funerary dedication from a wife to her husband who had a distinguished career in public service in his municipality.

EDCS-04201099.translation: Gaius Flavius Hostilius Papirius Sertorianus Laurens Lavinas, priest and Roman knight, made this living for himself and for his incomparable wife, Domitia, daughter of Titus Severa, and 'be ever mindful of the mountains, rejoice'.
EDCS-04201099.summary: A funerary dedication made by a prominent Roman citizen for himself and his wife, including a Greek epigram, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201100.translation: To Praecellia Maxima, to her dearest husband M. Iunius Maximus, duovir for administering justice, she made this (monument) while alive.
EDCS-04201100.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a wife for her husband, who held the office of duovir.

EDCS-04201101.translation: Iuventius Titus, a most distinguished man, made and gave this living for himself and his wife, Iuventia Marcelina, to the guild of artisans, to foster remembrance: five hundred denarii given to the aforesaid guild for harvests and vintage festivals.
EDCS-04201101.summary: A funerary dedication by a prominent man to his wife and a guild of artisans, including a financial endowment, likely dating to the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201102.translation: To Titus Sertorius Proculus, duovir for administering justice, prefect, quaestor, and flamen, who lived 30 years and 6 months, his parents made this monument for their excellent son.
EDCS-04201102.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by parents for their son, Titus Sertorius Proculus, who had held several civic and religious offices and died at the age of 30.

EDCS-04201103.translation: To Publius Turranius Pisto, quinquennial aedile, and to Aemilia Olila, daughter of Publius, his parents P. Turranius Placidus erected this (monument) for his excellent parents while alive.
EDCS-04201103.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Publius Turranius Placidus for his parents, one of whom, Publius Turranius Pisto, served as a quinquennial aedile.

EDCS-04201104.translation: To Aurelia Casta, Publius Gemellus placed [this] for his deserving wife.
EDCS-04201104.summary: A funerary monument set up by Publius Gemellus for his wife Aurelia Casta.

EDCS-04201105.translation: To the departed spirits: Capertia Valentina, to her husband C. M. Valerian[us]...
EDCS-04201105.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Capertia Valentina and her husband, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-04201106.translation: Bones of Ennia Marcella, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04201106.summary: A funerary inscription for Ennia Marcella, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-04201107.translation: To Flavia Severa, daughter of Caius, aged 3 years, 11 months, and 5 days, for their dearest daughter. Caius Flavius Hostilianus and Plaetoria Laeonica, daughter of Lucius, her parents, made [this].
EDCS-04201107.summary: A funerary epitaph for the young Flavia Severa, erected by her parents, Caius Flavius Hostilianus and Plaetoria Laeonica.

EDCS-04201108.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription mentioning Fonteia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04201109.translation: Quintus Fulvius, son of Publius, made (this) for himself and...
EDCS-04201109.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Quintus Fulvius, son of Publius, made a monument for himself and others.

EDCS-04201110.translation: Marcus Praecellius Vitulus, son of Quintus, of the Papirian tribe, made this while alive for himself and for Durenia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, his wife, and for his own family.
EDCS-04201110.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Praecellius Vitulus for himself, his wife Durenia Secunda, and his family.

EDCS-04201111.translation: A memorial for Publicius Asper, whom Quinctia Prima placed, for herself during her lifetime, along with her dear husband.
EDCS-04201111.summary: A funerary monument established by Quinctia Prima for her husband Publicius Asper and herself.

EDCS-04201112.translation: To the departed spirits: Quinctia Maxima made this for herself and for her husband Cusinius Severinus while alive.
EDCS-04201112.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quinctia Maxima for herself and her husband, Cusinius Severinus.

EDCS-04201113.translation: Titus Turranius Severinus made this while alive for his dearest wife, Blicia Constantina.
EDCS-04201113.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Titus Turranius Severinus for his wife, Blicia Constantina.

EDCS-04201114.translation: To Titus Volusius, son of Caius, Volusia P[...].
EDCS-04201114.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription mentioning Titus Volusius, son of Caius, and likely another individual.

EDCS-04201115.translation: For Tiberius Upsidius Gemini, son of Tiberius, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201115.summary: A funerary inscription for Tiberius Upsidius Gemini and his family.

EDCS-04201120.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04201120.text_edition: \n Fili posuerunt memoriam patri suo Saturniano Potio obito cum compare sua Valentina Volusia\n
EDCS-04201120.translation: Sons erected a memorial for their father Saturnianus Potio upon his death with his partner Valentina Volusia.
EDCS-04201120.summary: This inscription records sons setting up a memorial for their father, Saturnianus Potio, and his partner Valentina Volusia.

EDCS-04201121.translation: Hostilia Serena, daughter of Publius, [for] Ludrianus.
EDCS-04201121.summary: A funerary inscription likely indicating Hostilia Serena setting up a monument for Ludrianus.

EDCS-04201122.translation: To Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus, grandson of the deified (emperor), Augustus, consul-designate, prince of the youth.
EDCS-04201122.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus, likely on a public monument or altar, honoring his status as heir apparent.

EDCS-04201123.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Caio Messio Quinto Traiano Decio Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate III consuli II patri patriae proconsuli ordo Feltrinorum\n
EDCS-04201123.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Trajanus Decius Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, proconsul; the council of Feltrini.
EDCS-04201123.summary: A dedication by the council of Feltrini to Emperor Decius, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201124.translation: To Lucius Occlatius Tertius, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, father, and to Lucius Occlatius Florentinus, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, brother and soldier of the first praetorian cohort, who died at the age of 23 years; Lucius Occlatius Rocianus, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, a four-man official, prefect with jurisdiction, appointed to the treasury, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201124.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Occlatius Rocianus for his father and brother, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201125.translation: To Titus Caelio Montanus, grandfather, prefect with jurisdiction, appointed to the treasury, and to Lucius Caelio Montanus, father, prefect with jurisdiction, appointed to the treasury.
EDCS-04201125.summary: An epitaph honoring a grandfather and father, both named Montanus and holding judicial and treasury appointments, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201126.text_edition: \n Caio Firmio Cai filio Menenia Rufino equo publico Laurenti Lavinati decurioni flamini patrono collegiorum fabrum centonariorum dendrophororum Feltriae itemque Beruensium collegium fabrum Altinatium patrono\n
EDCS-04201126.translation: To Gaius Firmio Rufino, son of Gaius, of the Menenia tribe, a knight with public horse, decurion of Laurentum and Lavinium, flamen, patron of the guilds of fabric workers, carpet makers, and dendrophori of Feltria, and also patron of the guild of fabric workers of Beruensium of Altinum.
EDCS-04201126.summary: An inscription honoring Gaius Firmio Rufino for his distinguished public service and patronage of various guilds in Feltria and Altinum, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201127.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Veturio Nepos, to whom I bequeathed 1600 sesterces for them to perform funeral rites for me; to the Ciarinenses 1600 sesterces, likewise to the Herculanenses 400 sesterces, and to the women 400 sesterces, so that the Ciarinenses might perform his natalia with food and wine, the Herculanenses his parentalia, and the women might place roses; I made this for myself while alive.
EDCS-04201127.summary: A self-funded funerary dedication by Lucius Veturio Nepos, specifying bequests for religious observances by different groups, likely from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201128.translation: Caius Arrenus Marcellinus, most devoted brother.
EDCS-04201128.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Arrenus Marcellinus, described as a devoted brother.

EDCS-04201129.summary: A funerary inscription mentioning Publius Gellius Proculus and Gellius Manta, likely related.

EDCS-04201131.translation: To Lucius and to his wife Iucunda.
EDCS-04201131.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius and his wife Iucunda, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201133.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Petronia Maxuma, daughter of Caius, probably from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201134.translation: To the departed spirits. For Publicia Pia, my most holy mother, and for Publica Primula, my most dutiful sister. From Secundinus.
EDCS-04201134.summary: A funerary dedication by Secundinus to his mother and sister, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201135.translation: Gaius Illius Sanucius, son of Gaius, [dedicates] a burial plot, 30 feet in front and 21 feet in depth.
EDCS-04201135.summary: This is an inscription marking a burial plot of 30 by 21 feet, dedicated by Gaius Illius Sanucius, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201141.translation: Grania Bacchis gave this as a gift to Diana.
EDCS-04201141.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Grania Bacchis dedicating a gift to the goddess Diana, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201142.translation: Manius Fapius Dariins willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Juno Regina.
EDCS-04201142.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Manius Fapius Dariins paying a vow to Juno Regina, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201143.translation: For Tiberius Claudius Caesar. Marcus Salonius Superstes [erected this].
EDCS-04201143.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar, likely set up by Marcus Salonius Superstes, probably from the mid-1st century AD.

EDCS-04201145.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Vettonius Maximus Fabia, a veteran, having returned from military service, made this himself while alive, and in memory of himself and for the proper observance of burial rites, he gave 800 sesterces to the pagan populace of Misquilen(ses) for meals. From the income of this sum, they should place no less than 16 sesterces worth of roses and the remainder, whatever it may be, from the interest, for meals, both rosy and autumnal, to be placed every year, and he ordered the place to be used.
EDCS-04201145.summary: A self-funded funerary monument and endowment by Gaius Vettonius Maximus Fabia for the perpetual care of his burial and provision of meals and roses, likely from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201146.translation: Gaius Rapidius Rufus, son of Gaius, duovir with aedilician power, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Sempronia Tertia, wife of Gaius, daughter of Lucius, and for his son Gaius Rapidius Rufinus, son of Gaius, and for his grandson Gaius Rapidius, son of Gaius, and for his granddaughter Rapidia Maxima, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04201146.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Rapidius Rufus, his wife, son, and grandchildren, commissioned by Rufus himself in his will, likely from the late 1st century BC or early 1st century AD.

EDCS-04201149.translation: Titus Firmius Tarvisanus, son of Quintus, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201149.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Firmius Tarvisanus for himself and his relatives, the original text is incomplete, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201150.translation: Volacina erected this for her husband Volacinus, an architect, with whom she lived for 40 years without any discord, and for Volacinus Hillarius, deserving [of remembrance].
EDCS-04201150.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Volacinus, an architect, and his son Volacinus Hillarius, erected by his wife Volacina, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201151.translation: Arvenius Donatus, freedman of Nigella, made this for Arvenia Cutela, freedwoman of Nigella.
EDCS-04201151.summary: This is a funerary inscription erected by Arvenius Donatus for Arvenia Cutela, both freedpersons of Nigella, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201152.translation: Publius Braetius Fronto, son of Publius, made this for Cla...
EDCS-04201152.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription set up by Publius Braetius Fronto, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201153.translation: Braetia, 50 feet in front and 32 feet behind.
EDCS-04201153.summary: This inscription specifies boundary dimensions for a property named Braetia.

EDCS-04201154.translation: Coelia Libua, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for herself and (perhaps) her heirs, and this monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-04201154.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Coelia Libua erected her own tomb and stipulated that it should not pass to an heir.

EDCS-04201155.translation: To Gaius Messius Pat and his brother Gnaeus Sevius, Gaius Messius Th.
EDCS-04201155.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Gaius Messius Pat and Gnaeus Sevius by Gaius Messius Th.

EDCS-04201156.translation: To Gaius Publicius, son of Gaius, grandson of Titus, father; to Birria, daughter of Lucius, mother.
EDCS-04201156.summary: This epitaph honors the parents of the deceased, identifying them as father and mother.

EDCS-04201157.translation: Lucius Rapidius Iustus, son of Gaius, this tomb, in front 3 feet, behind 25 feet; for himself and his family, he made while alive.
EDCS-04201157.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Rapidius Iustus for himself and his family, specifying dimensions, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201158.translation: To the departed spirits. For Serena, who lived 1 year, 3 months, 17 days. Caepiacus Serenus and Crispina, parents, placed this for their most sweet daughter.
EDCS-04201158.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Serena, erected by her parents, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201160.translation: and to Valeria Tertulla, daughter of Publius, his wife; to Gaius Hostilius Saturninus, son of Gaius, his son; to Hostilia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, his sister.
EDCS-04201160.summary: This inscription lists family members being honored or memorialized, likely for a tomb.

EDCS-04201161.translation: To [---] Velleius, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, for himself and Marcus Velleius.
EDCS-04201161.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication by [---] Velleius, son of Titus, for himself and Marcus Velleius.

EDCS-04201162.translation: L. I. V., son of Titus, con[secrated] v[ow?].
EDCS-04201162.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly recording a dedication or votive offering by a person identified with the initials L. I. V.

EDCS-04201163.translation: To Martina, dear wife, who lived about 40 years, who came from Gaul through 50 stages to commemorate the memory of her sweetest husband. Rest well, my sweetest husband.
EDCS-04201163.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a husband, set up by his wife who traveled a great distance to honor his memory.

EDCS-04201164.translation: To Isis Regina, Lucius Publicius Eutyches, freedman of the municipality of Tarvisium.
EDCS-04201164.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Isis Regina by Lucius Publicius Eutyches, a freedman of Tarvisium.

EDCS-04201165.translation: To Father Liber, Publius Cassius Longinus, son of Quintus, of the Claudia tribe.
EDCS-04201165.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Father Liber by Publius Cassius Longinus.

EDCS-04201166.translation: To Cornelia Salonina, Augusta, wife of Gallienus.
EDCS-04201166.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cornelia Salonina, wife of the emperor Gallienus.

EDCS-04201167.text_edition: \n Lucio Ragonio Luci filio Papiria Urinatio Larcio Quintiano consuli sodali Hadrianali legato legionis XIIII geminae donis militaribus donato ab Imperatore C[ommodo] Antonino Augusto proconsuli provinciae Sardiniae iuridico per Apuliam praefecto frumenti dandi praetori aedili quaestori provinciae Africae seviro Chrysopaes Eutyches [] servi domino optimo\n
EDCS-04201167.translation: To Lucius Ragonius Ursinatio, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, consul, Hadrianic associate, legate of the Legio XIIII Geminae, honored with military gifts by the Emperor Commodus Antoninus Augustus, proconsul of the province of Sardinia, legal official for Apulia, prefect for the distribution of grain, praetor, quaestor of the province of Africa, seviri. Eutyches, slave of the best master, [erected this].
EDCS-04201167.summary: This is a laudatory inscription honoring Lucius Ragonius Ursinatio, detailing his many high-ranking military and administrative positions, and likely set up by his freedman and slave.

EDCS-04201168.translation: To Acilia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, from Titus Helvius Salinator, son of Titus, centurion of the Legio VII.
EDCS-04201168.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Acilia Secunda, with the dedicator identified as a centurion.

EDCS-04201169.translation: To Gaius Andenius Vilicius, son of Gaius, and to Secunda, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04201169.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to Gaius Andenius Vilicius and Secunda.

EDCS-04201170.text_edition: \n Sexto Ligustino Sexti filio fratri veterano legionis XV Apollinaris IIIIviro iure dicundo Ligustino Sexti filio fratri veterano legionis XV Apollinaris Ligustinae Sexti filiae Maxumae sorori\n
EDCS-04201170.translation: To Sextus Ligustinus, son of Sextus, brother, veteran of the Legio XV Apollinaris; to Ligustinus, son of Sextus, brother, veteran of the Legio XV Apollinaris; to Maxuma, daughter of Sextus, sister.
EDCS-04201170.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring multiple family members, including two veterans of the Legio XV Apollinaris, likely set up by a surviving relative.

EDCS-04201171.translation: The six men (elected officials) paved the road with flagstones from the crossroads to the wall, in honor.
EDCS-04201171.summary: This inscription records the paving of a road by a group of six elected officials (IIIIIIviri), likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201172.translation: He added that after his death, he wished the honor of the decurionate, for which he had judged him worthy, to be transferred to Marcus Saufeius Pudentes, son of Titus, his closest relative, so that Pris[cus] might have in that perpetual seat, having finally relinquished excessive infirmities, a splendid kinsman of public affection and his parent, who, having lost his only son, was severely afflicted by excessive grief, might perceive sublime solace through the intervention of the most benevolent decree. Octavia Serena, daughter of Tiberius, his most excellent wife; Marcus Saufeius Pudens and Titus Saufeius Severus, [erected this] for their son Montanus, son of Titus Saufeius, aged 3 years, and for Mulvia Severa, daughter of Titus, his most holy wife. The living made this monument; it will not pass to the heir. In front 34 feet, behind 35 feet.
EDCS-04201172.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by parents for their young son and his mother, who had previously lost their only son, indicating a complex family history and the transfer of honors.

EDCS-04201173.translation: Gaius Sevius Fuscus, son of Gaius, a IIIIvir.
EDCS-04201173.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Gaius Sevius Fuscus, who held the office of IIIIvir.

EDCS-04201174.translation: Lucius Titius Linus, freedman of Lucius, made this for his patron Lucius Titius Maximo, a VIvir, his most excellent patron.
EDCS-04201174.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a freedman for his patron, a VIvir.

EDCS-04201175.translation: [for] Calvius and Accia Secunda, his wife.
EDCS-04201175.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates the monument to Accia Secunda and her husband Calvius.

EDCS-04201176.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Ammia as the wife of an individual mentioned previously.

EDCS-04201177.translation: Sextus Cassius Eros, freedman of Sextus, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-04201177.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Sextus Cassius Eros for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04201178.translation: Publius Catius Tertius, freedman of Publius, and Petale, freedwoman.
EDCS-04201178.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Publius Catius Tertius, a freedman, and Petale, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201181.translation: To Faelia Catulla, freedwoman colleague, and to Faelia Vitalis, her best friend. Gaius Faelius Onesimus and Faelia Restituta, the living, made [this] for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-04201181.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by two individuals for their freedpersons and their descendants, indicating a familial or close relationship.

EDCS-04201183.translation: Flavia Prisca, daughter of Lucius, aged twenty-four.
EDCS-04201183.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Flavia Prisca.

EDCS-04201184.translation: Iulia Melaenis, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and for her daughter Disinia Prima and her mother Sequana, and for Abascantus, freedman of a woman, her mother.
EDCS-04201184.summary: This funerary inscription is set up by Iulia Melaenis for herself, her daughter, and her mother, and also for Abascantus, a freedman.

EDCS-04201185.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Marcus Navonius.

EDCS-04201186.translation: Place of burial for Publius Paetinus Heracla. In front 30 feet, behind 30 feet.
EDCS-04201186.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Publius Paetinus Heracla, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04201187.translation: [To] Lucius Pinn[ius]... Zabd[a]... to Lucius Pinn[ius]... Pri[...], his patron (?).
EDCS-04201187.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Lucius Pinn[ius] and Zabd[a], possibly as patron and freedwoman.

EDCS-04201188.translation: To Tertulla, freedwoman of Publius, belonging to Ragonia.
EDCS-04201188.summary: This is a funerary inscription honouring Tertulla, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201189.translation: Gaius Terentius Chilo, freedman of a woman, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-04201189.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman named Gaius Terentius Chilo for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04201190.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Suavia.

EDCS-04201191.translation: To Marcus Vilonius Antiochus, freedman of Marcus. [...]
EDCS-04201191.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Marcus Vilonius Antiochus, a freedman.

EDCS-04201192.translation: Ulpia Macedonia and her son Magn Semnus to their mother Ulpia Macedonia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201192.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Ulpia Macedonia and her son Magn Semnus for Ulpia Macedonia, the mother and wife.

EDCS-04201197.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription stating that the deceased's father erected the monument.

EDCS-04201198.text_edition: \n Lucius Aquillius Narcissus Augustalis Beleno votum solvit\n
EDCS-04201198.translation: Lucius Aquillius Narcissus, Augustalis, fulfilled a vow to Belenus.
EDCS-04201198.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Belenus by Lucius Aquillius Narcissus, an Augustalis.

EDCS-04201199.text_edition: \n Belino Augusto votum solvit Quintus Herennius Paulli libertus Polybius Augustalis\n
EDCS-04201199.translation: Quintus Herennius Polybius, freedman of Paullus, Augustalis, fulfilled a vow to Belenus Augustus.
EDCS-04201199.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Belenus Augustus by Quintus Herennius Polybius, an Augustalis and freedman.

EDCS-04201200.translation: Gaius Lucretius Rufus, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Belenus.
EDCS-04201200.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Lucretius Rufus fulfilling a vow to the god Belenus.

EDCS-04201202.translation: Gaius Egnatius Bassus willingly and deservedly [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-04201202.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Egnatius Bassus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04201210.translation: To Chaerontius, freedman of our Emperor, administrator of the accounts of the supply corps for the expeditions, from the two years II and III of the German campaigns.
EDCS-04201210.summary: This is a dedication to Chaerontius, an imperial administrator, likely related to military supply and possibly dating to specific consular years indicated by 'II et III Germ(anicarum)'.

EDCS-04201211.translation: To Parthenius, freedman of the Emperor, administrator of Illyricum.
EDCS-04201211.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Parthenius, a freedman of the Emperor and administrator of Illyricum.

EDCS-04201212.translation: To Gaius Aratrius, prefect of artisans, for the construction [of something?] and the basilica.
EDCS-04201212.summary: This dedication is to Gaius Aratrius, a prefect of artisans, likely commemorating his role in the construction of a basilica.

EDCS-04201213.translation: Marcus Furius Saturninus, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made by testament for his father Marcus Furius Verana, son of Statius; his wife Grattia Secunda, daughter of Marcus; and his mother Cervonia Prima, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201213.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Marcus Furius Saturninus for his father, wife, and mother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201214.translation: Marcus Julius Victor, soldier of the same legion, placed [this] for Lucius Gallus Soranus, soldier of the Legio IIII Flavia Felix, deserving man, who lived 40 years and 4 months.
EDCS-04201214.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier of the Legio IIII Flavia Felix, erected by a fellow soldier.

EDCS-04201215.translation: [---] Gaius Gavius Aquilo, son of Lucius, [---] a quaestor by lot, a magistrate with judicial authority, a duovir with curule authority, a military tribune, prefect of cavalry, [---] of the sums.
EDCS-04201215.summary: This inscription lists the various magistracies and military commands held by Gavius Aquilo, son of Lucius, including duovir, tribune, and prefect of cavalry.

EDCS-04201216.translation: To the Divine Spirits, the remains of Marcus Iulius Albanus, an evocatus.
EDCS-04201216.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Iulius Albanus, who served as an evocatus (a type of select soldier).

EDCS-04201217.translation: Gnaeus Numerius Frontus, son of Gnaeus, of the Voltinia tribe, a veteran of the horsemen of the Eighth Augustan Legion, a magistrate with judicial power, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, for his freedman Gnaeus Numerius Felix, a six-member priest, and for his freedmen Crescentius and Tuendus.
EDCS-04201217.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by a veteran and magistrate for himself and his freedmen, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201218.translation: To Manius Titius, son of Manius, of the Fabia tribe, a military tribune of the Eighth Legion.
EDCS-04201218.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Manius Titius, son of Manius, who served as a military tribune in the Eighth Legion.

EDCS-04201221.translation: Lucius Acilius Scaptia, son of Publius, a decurion, for himself and for Publius Acilius, son of Manius, his father, for Sextilia, daughter of Saenius, his mother, for Publius Acilius, son of Publius, his brother. In the front 120 feet, in the rear 120 feet.
EDCS-04201221.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Acilius for his family, specifying plot dimensions, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201222.translation: Quintus Acutius Diomedes, freedman of Quintus, a duovir.
EDCS-04201222.summary: This inscription records Quintus Acutius Diomedes, a freedman of Quintus, holding the office of duovir.

EDCS-04201223.translation: For the honor of Titus Firmius Proculus, duovir with curule authority, Titus Antonius Clementinus.
EDCS-04201223.summary: This inscription commemorates Titus Firmius Proculus, a duovir with curule authority, honoring him for his service.

EDCS-04201224.translation: To Marcus Barbius Maturus, son of Titus, duovir with judicial authority, [---]cretiis.
EDCS-04201224.summary: This dedication is to Marcus Barbius Maturus, son of Titus, who served as a duovir with judicial authority.

EDCS-04201225.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Cassius Herma, the priest, made this while alive for himself, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-04201225.summary: A funerary dedication by a priest for himself and his descendants, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201226.translation: Chryseros ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201226.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Chryseros commissioned the monument in his will.

EDCS-04201227.translation: To Cornelia Paulina, daughter of Gaius, who deserved exceptionally well of her family, publicly by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201227.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Cornelia Paulina, dedicated publicly by decree of the local council.

EDCS-04201228.translation: For Quintus Epidius Appelai, son of Quintus, a six-member priest, from Forum Cornelii. Tertius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04201228.summary: An inscription honoring a local magistrate and priest named Quintus Epidius Appelai, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201230.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lartia Secunda, daughter of Publius, our patroness, from Halenus, a fellow freedman, and for myself. Publius Lartius Homullus, a six-member priest, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201230.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a freedman to his patroness and for himself, commissioned by a local magistrate, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201231.translation: Lucius Ogius Patroclus, following his sense of duty, donated gardens with a building attached to this burial plot to the college of fullers, while alive, so that from their income might be provided roses and food for his patron and, eventually, for himself.
EDCS-04201231.summary: A donation of land and a building by Lucius Ogius Patroclus to a guild of fullers for the upkeep of his and his patron's burial, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201232.translation: To Plautia Tulla, publicly by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201232.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Plautia Tulla, dedicated publicly by decree of the local council.

EDCS-04201233.translation: with Lucius Postumius, augur and colleague, written in the archives
EDCS-04201233.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly related to official records concerning Lucius Postumius, an augur.

EDCS-04201234.summary: This is an inscription honoring Marcus Ruferius, who held the office of duovir.

EDCS-04201235.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sextus Valerius Alcides, a six-member official, made this while alive for himself and for Auceia Psyche, his wife, for Valerius Hermetes, for Calidius Hermetes, for Pontius Apollonarius(?), for his friends Soterichus and Gamice, and for Talia the beloved freedwoman. The monument space is 16 feet in front and 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-04201235.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Valerius Alcides, his wife, friends, and freedwoman, specifying plot dimensions, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201236.translation: To Publius Aelius Philetianus, the doctor. Aelius Irenaeus to his most pious father.
EDCS-04201236.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Philetianus, a doctor, dedicated by his son Irenaeus.

EDCS-04201237.translation: To the spirits of the departed, to Caecilius Cosmio, his freedman, the best, Caecilius Bassus, procurator.
EDCS-04201237.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Caecilius Bassus, a procurator, to his favored freedman Caecilius Cosmio.

EDCS-04201238.translation: Lucius Crassicius Hermia, a freedman of a woman, a veteran veterinarian, made this while alive for himself and for Abiria Maxima, freedwoman of Lucius, his wife, and for Eugenia, a freedwoman.
EDCS-04201238.summary: A funerary dedication by a veteran veterinarian for himself, his wife, and a freedwoman, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201239.translation: Publius Herennius Primus, freedman of Publius, a turarius.
EDCS-04201239.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Publius Herennius Primus, a freedman who worked as a turarius.

EDCS-04201240.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Plotia Felicitas, who lived 16 years. Marcus Ulpius Castresis, the pantomime, made this for his well-deserving.
EDCS-04201240.summary: A funerary monument by a pantomime actor for Plotia Felicitas, who died at age 16, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201242.translation: To the departed spirits. Abidia Crescentilla made this for her daughter Superva, who was 6 years old.
EDCS-04201242.summary: A funerary epitaph by a mother for her young daughter, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201243.translation: To the spirits of the departed, to Acellius Ianuarius, deceased at the age of 11 years, by Acellia Septimilla, to her unfortunate son.
EDCS-04201243.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Acellius Ianuarius, an 11-year-old boy, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-04201244.translation: To Blanda, freedwoman of Lucius Acutius.
EDCS-04201244.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Blanda, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201245.translation: For the spirits of Severilla, daughter of Acutius, [aged ---] years.
EDCS-04201245.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Severilla, daughter of Acutius, with missing age information.

EDCS-04201246.translation: To Aelia Rufina, his mother, by Lucius Aelius Tarquinus.
EDCS-04201246.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Aelius Tarquinus to his mother, Aelia Rufina.

EDCS-04201247.summary: This inscription appears to be a name, likely of an individual commemorated by this text, possibly on a tombstone or other dedicatory monument.

EDCS-04201248.translation: Ancharia Quincta, daughter of Tiberius, for herself and for her husband Titus Vettius, son of Caius.
EDCS-04201248.summary: This inscription records Ancharia Quincta dedicating a monument or space for herself and her husband, Titus Vettius.

EDCS-04201249.translation: Lucius Antonius Bassus placed this from his own means for his most devoted mother.
EDCS-04201249.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Lucius Antonius Bassus for his mother.

EDCS-04201250.translation: Vassa Apicula, freedwoman of Marcus, [is placed here for] Iulia, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04201250.summary: This inscription seems to indicate that Vassa Apicula, a freedwoman of Marcus, is being honored or placed in relation to Iulia, another freedwoman of Marcus.

EDCS-04201251.translation: Marcus Philocles, freedman of Marcus Apronius, made this for himself while alive, and for Sintia Caesia, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-04201251.summary: This is a self-dedication by Marcus Philocles, a freedman, for himself and Sintia Caesia, also a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201252.translation: In this place is laid Aquilina Vintina, a most unfortunate girl, who lived 8 years, 11 months, and 4 days. Her mother Lollia Uxesina placed this for her and for herself.
EDCS-04201252.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young girl, Aquilina Vintina, set up by her mother, Lollia Uxesina, who also included herself.

EDCS-04201253.translation: Lucius Aratrius, son of Lucius; Lucius Aratrius, freedman of Lucius; Diog, freedman of Lucius Aratrius; Arrius, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201253.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely members of a family or freedmen connected to a Lucius Aratrius.

EDCS-04201254.translation: Apollonius, his freedman, for Aria Serena, daughter of Quintus, and for himself.
EDCS-04201254.summary: This inscription records Apollonius, a freedman, dedicating something for Aria Serena and for himself.

EDCS-04201256.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Caius Atteius Symphorus placed this for his patron Caius Atteius Antiochus, and for himself, and for his descendants and their successors.
EDCS-04201256.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Caius Atteius Symphorus for his patron, Caius Atteius Antiochus, and for his own family and future descendants.

EDCS-04201257.summary: This inscription records Publius Attius Neptunalis setting up something for Hermetus.

EDCS-04201258.translation: To Attius Salvius, son of Gaius. --
EDCS-04201258.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication for Attius Salvius, son of Gaius.

EDCS-04201259.translation: Avillia, freedwoman of Aulus, for herself and for Aulus Avillius, son of Publius, and Octavius, son of Publius Avillius. --
EDCS-04201259.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication set up by Avillia, freedwoman of Aulus, for herself and for others, including Aulus Avillius and Octavius.

EDCS-04201260.translation: The bones of Gaius Ianuarius, son of Aulus and Sextus.
EDCS-04201260.summary: This inscription records the burial place of Gaius Ianuarius, son of Aulus and Sextus.

EDCS-04201261.translation: Gaius Aulius Restitutus, freedman of Gaius, for himself and for his wife Aquilia Peregrina, daughter of Publius, aged 25 years.
EDCS-04201261.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Gaius Aulius Restitutus, freedman of Gaius, for himself and his wife Aquilia Peregrina.

EDCS-04201262.translation: Aurelius Pontianus set this up for himself while alive.
EDCS-04201262.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Aurelius Pontianus for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04201263.translation: Aurelius Zosimus set this up for his most devoted granddaughter, Aurelia Valentina, who lived for 3 years, 5 months, and 2 days.
EDCS-04201263.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Aurelius Zosimus for his granddaughter Aurelia Valentina.

EDCS-04201264.translation: A burial place for Barbea Progenita and her brother Etuvenius. Barbea Zmaragdis and Quintus Etuvius, a living husband, made this.
EDCS-04201264.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot dedicated by Barbea Zmaragdis and Quintus Etuvius for Barbea Progenita and her brother Etuvenius.

EDCS-04201265.translation: Burial place of Tecinius Maximus and Caecilia Iusta, 55 feet in front and 55 feet in the back.
EDCS-04201265.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Tecinius Maximus and Caecilia Iusta.

EDCS-04201266.summary: This is a dedication by Caecina Charis.

EDCS-04201267.translation: To the guardian spirit of Publius Caelsius Terminalis.
EDCS-04201267.summary: This is a dedication to the genius (guardian spirit) of Publius Caelsius Terminalis.

EDCS-04201268.translation: For Lucius Cethegus Secundus, son of Lucius. Lucius Cethegus Priscus, freedman of Lucius, (erected this). Frontage 16 feet, depth 30 feet.
EDCS-04201268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and boundary marker for Lucius Cethegus Secundus, set up by his freedman Lucius Cethegus Priscus.

EDCS-04201269.translation: Antiochus set this up for his wife Charitinus, who lived for about 22 years, as a deserving wife.
EDCS-04201269.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Antiochus for his wife Charitinus.
