EDCS-04201270.translation: Gaius Clodius Fusculus, son of Gaius, aged 7 years.
EDCS-04201270.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Clodius Fusculus, a child.

EDCS-04201271.translation: To Marcus Cocceius, freedman of the emperor, Hos[3], to his best friend [3] and Titus Mestri[3] Hospitian
EDCS-04201271.summary: An epitaph for Marcus Cocceius, mentioning his freedman, and possibly another individual named Titus Mestrius Hospitian.

EDCS-04201272.translation: Hermes, freedman of Anthusa, arranged for the erection of this monument to Marcus Cocceius Nepos and Faleria Anthusa.
EDCS-04201272.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Hermes, a freedman, for Marcus Cocceius Nepos and Faleria Anthusa.

EDCS-04201273.translation: Titus Coelius Celer, son of Titus, aged 26.
EDCS-04201273.summary: An epitaph recording the name, parentage, and age of Titus Coelius Celer.

EDCS-04201274.summary: An epitaph for Combulius Tertius, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-04201275.translation: Cusonia Posilla, daughter of Marcus, made this for herself while alive, and for her mother Passena Enoclia, freedwoman of Ostius, and for Cusonia, her mother.
EDCS-04201275.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Cusonia Posilla for herself and her mother and other relatives.

EDCS-04201276.translation: Aulus Daphnis, freedman of Cnaeus, to his freedman Cnaeus Acastus. Cnaeus Daphnis, freedman of Cnaeus.
EDCS-04201276.summary: An epitaph recording the dedication by Aulus Daphnis, a freedman, to his own freedman Cnaeus Acastus.

EDCS-04201277.translation: Marcus Domitius Salvius, son of Marcus, placed this for his wife Postuma, most excellent and most chaste.
EDCS-04201277.summary: An epitaph set up by Marcus Domitius Salvius for his wife Postuma.

EDCS-04201278.translation: To his Galatea, from Manius Ennius Esychus, freedman of Manius.
EDCS-04201278.summary: An epitaph dedicated by Manius Ennius Esychus, a freedman, to his companion Galatea.

EDCS-04201279.translation: Ennia Veneria, freedwoman of Publius, (made this) for herself and for Titus Trosius Secundus, son of Titus, and for Titus Saufeius Magirus, freedman of Steipanus, while alive.
EDCS-04201279.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Ennia Veneria for herself and two other individuals.

EDCS-04201280.translation: To Lucius Fabricius, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04201280.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument to Lucius Fabricius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04201281.translation: Burial plot of Caius Fannius Successus, 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the back.
EDCS-04201281.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Fannius Successus.

EDCS-04201282.translation: To the most excellent Faustina, from Cae Cae
EDCS-04201282.summary: A dedication to Faustina, possibly a wife or other close relation, from someone also named Cae (repeated).

EDCS-04201283.translation: Arruntia Clementina made (this monument) for Flavia Ianuaria, who lived 25 years, 5 months, and 24 days, and for her daughter Antonia Crescentina, most beloved, and for her wife Vettius Clementina, most excellent.
EDCS-04201283.summary: This epitaph records the erection of a funerary monument by Arruntia Clementina for her daughter-in-law Flavia Ianuaria, and for her daughter and wife.

EDCS-04201284.translation: He ordered that (this monument) be made in his will for Fronton and for Murria Compsina, a freedwoman.
EDCS-04201284.summary: This inscription records a posthumous commission for a monument to Fronton and Murria Compsina, a freedwoman, as specified in a will.

EDCS-04201285.translation: To Garrulus Argutus, for his father, for Vaccia Venusta, his aunt, and for Vaccia Amabilis, his sister.
EDCS-04201285.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Garrulus Argutus to his father, aunt, and sister.

EDCS-04201286.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and for eternal security, Gelasius Threptus, for his most beloved father.
EDCS-04201286.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Gelasius Threptus to his father, invoking the Manes and eternal security.

EDCS-04201287.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Helvidius Florus, by Helvidia Prima, his daughter.
EDCS-04201287.summary: This epitaph records the dedication to the Manes of Helvidius Florus by his daughter, Helvidia Prima.

EDCS-04201288.translation: Lucius Herennius Aesopus, dear to his friends.
EDCS-04201288.summary: This epitaph commemorates Lucius Herennius Aesopus, noting his popularity among his friends.

EDCS-04201289.translation: Marcus' freedman Hilarius made (this monument) while alive for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04201289.summary: This inscription records Hilarius, a freedman of Marcus, erecting a monument during his lifetime for his own freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-04201290.translation: For Gaius Julius Quietus, son of Gaius, of the Trom(entina) tribe. Titia Quieta, mother, (made this) for her most dutiful son.
EDCS-04201290.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Quietus, set up by his devoted mother.

EDCS-04201291.translation: To Julia Afrodisia, mother most beloved, who lived 57 years, 5 months, and 23 days, made by Iula Vinia, deserving.
EDCS-04201291.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Iula Vinia to her deserving mother, Julia Afrodisia, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-04201292.translation: For Iulia Eutychia, aged 20 years and 55 days, by Hermes, an unhappy father, son of Lucius Noni Emporus, and for Marcus Cocceius Maritimus, his son-in-law.
EDCS-04201292.summary: This epitaph is set up by Hermes, the father of Iulia Eutychia, and Marcus Cocceius Maritimus, the son-in-law, commemorating Iulia Eutychia who died at 20 years and 55 days.

EDCS-04201293.translation: To Iulia Galatia, a good wife, who lived 35 years, by Filippus, for his deserving spouse.
EDCS-04201293.summary: This epitaph records Filippus dedicating a monument to his wife, Iulia Galatia, who died at 35 years of age.

EDCS-04201294.translation: Junius, son of Junius, of the Fabia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his wife, Pontia, daughter of Caius, of the Quinctia tribe.
EDCS-04201294.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph ordered by Junius for himself and his wife, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201295.translation: Marcus Marius Faustinus, son of Caius, while alive, for himself and for his brother Caius Marius.
EDCS-04201295.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Marius Faustinus and his brother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201296.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titus Mestrius Logismus, freedman of Titus, made this for himself and for his wife Mestria Sperata, while alive.
EDCS-04201296.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Mestrius Logismus and his wife, made by himself while alive.

EDCS-04201297.translation: Sextus Minucius Optatus ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his sister Minucia, freedwoman of a woman, and for Asconia, freedwoman of Lucius, Pus.
EDCS-04201297.summary: This funerary epitaph was commissioned by Sextus Minucius Optatus for himself, his sister, and Asconia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201298.translation: Publius Munatius Primus, freedman of a woman, made this while alive for himself and for his partner (contubernalis) Tucia Tertulla, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-04201298.summary: This funerary epitaph was made by Publius Munatius Primus for himself and his partner Tucia Tertulla, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201299.translation: Caius Murius, son of Caius, for himself and for Potia Secunda, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201299.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Murius and Potia Secunda, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201300.translation: For Lucius Nigidius Primio, freedman of a woman, and Nigidia Musa, freedwoman of a woman, and Nigidia Florenti, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius Nigidius Florus and Fabia Primula made this at their own expense.
EDCS-04201300.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument funded by Lucius Nigidius Florus and Fabia Primula for several freedpersons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201301.translation: For Novia Salvilla, freedwoman of a woman, and Abascantus, freedman.
EDCS-04201301.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Novia Salvilla and Abascantus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201302.translation: Burial place for Martha, daughter of Quintus, and freedwoman of a woman. Quintus Nunnius Campanus and Quintus Nunnius Donatus made this for their very dear fellow freedwoman.
EDCS-04201302.summary: This inscription records a burial plot provided by Quintus Nunnius Campanus and Quintus Nunnius Donatus for their fellow freedwoman Martha, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201303.translation: Cnaeus Octavius Cosmus made this while alive for himself and for Octavia Censorina and her children.
EDCS-04201303.summary: This funerary epitaph was made by Cnaeus Octavius Cosmus for himself, his wife Octavia Censorina, and their children, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201305.translation: Titius Severus, son of Caius, and Ostilia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, made this for themselves and their families while alive. The heirs placed this according to their will. In the front 5 feet, in the rear 20 feet.
EDCS-04201305.summary: This inscription records a family burial plot of specified dimensions, commissioned by Titius Severus and Ostilia Secunda, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201306.translation: Paescia Tertia, daughter of Caius, ordered this to be made in her will for herself and Sesrus.
EDCS-04201306.summary: This funerary inscription records a woman, Paescia Tertia, who commissioned her own tomb through her will, also for Sesrus.

EDCS-04201307.translation: Gaius Papirius Sodalis, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself and for his wife Elonia Murra, freedwoman of Lucius, while alive.
EDCS-04201307.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Papirius Sodalis and his wife, made by himself while alive.

EDCS-04201308.translation: To Percennia Sabina, who lived 19 years and 35 days. Marcus Percennius Mursensis for his most beloved daughter.
EDCS-04201308.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Marcus Percennius Mursensis to his daughter, Percennia Sabina, providing her age at death.

EDCS-04201309.summary: This inscription likely marks the ownership of a house belonging to Lucius Peticius Salvius.

EDCS-04201312.translation: Lucius Plotius Geminianus, Quintus Murtius Hermes, and Manius Terentius Varianus, friends among themselves, made this: they jointly purchased a plot of land measuring 60 feet in front and 60 feet in depth. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-04201312.summary: A funerary dedication by friends who jointly purchased a burial plot, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201313.translation: For Lucius Poblicius Gratus, 40 feet in frontage.
EDCS-04201313.summary: This inscription seems to record a land grant or property measurement for Lucius Poblicius Gratus, possibly related to a public building or plot.

EDCS-04201314.translation: Popilia, freedwoman of the woman, for her son.
EDCS-04201314.summary: This inscription records Popilia, a freedwoman, dedicating something for her son.

EDCS-04201315.summary: This very brief inscription likely identifies a person named Iccion as Roman, possibly on a monument or object.

EDCS-04201316.translation: To the departed spirits of Publius Rutilius Epaphroditus.
EDCS-04201316.summary: A funerary dedication to Publius Rutilius Epaphroditus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201317.translation: Her mother made this for Secunda Urtia Maxima, a slave of one and a half years.
EDCS-04201317.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a very young slave girl, Secunda Urtia Maxima, dedicated by her mother.

EDCS-04201318.translation: us, son of Marcus, Coliso and herself.
EDCS-04201318.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to record a dedication or identification involving a person named Coliso, son of Marcus, and possibly himself and another individual.

EDCS-04201319.translation: For Seia Philumina, freedwoman of Mani Publius. Phos, freedman.
EDCS-04201319.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Seia Philumina, a freedwoman, and mentions Phos, also a freedman.

EDCS-04201320.translation: Titus Senatius Firminus, son of Titus, [made this] for his brother Tiberius Senatius Maturus, son of Titus, measuring 26 feet in front and 38 feet in depth.
EDCS-04201320.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Senatius Firminus for his brother, specifying the dimensions of the plot, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201321.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Sextius as a freedman of Marcus, likely on a tombstone or property marker.

EDCS-04201323.translation: Lucius Statius Prudens made this for his fellow freedman Lucius Statius Faustus, son of Sabinus, and Natalinus, while he was alive.
EDCS-04201323.summary: A funerary dedication made by a patron for his freedman and another individual, commissioned during the patron's lifetime, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201324.translation: Terentia Hicete, freedwoman of Gaius, ordered this to be made in her will for herself, her mother, father, and sister.
EDCS-04201324.summary: A funerary monument commissioned in a will by Terentia Hicete for herself and her family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201325.translation: Tettenius Artemidorus erected this while alive for his dearest son Cassius Artemidorus, aged 22.
EDCS-04201325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by a father for his deceased son.

EDCS-04201326.translation: Gaius Titurnius Florus ordered this to be made for his patron, Gratus, freedman of Gaius Titurnius.
EDCS-04201326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by a freedman for his patron.

EDCS-04201327.translation: Marcus Trebius Fremmus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04201327.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying an individual by name and status.

EDCS-04201328.translation: Marcus Trebius for his incomparable wife, Veneria, freedwoman of Trebia Quinta.
EDCS-04201328.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his deceased wife.

EDCS-04201331.translation: For Publius Valerius Secundus, son of Publius, 15 feet in front and 40 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04201331.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land allocated to Publius Valerius Secundus.

EDCS-04201332.translation: Valgia Secundina, daughter of Spurius, lived 7 years and 11 months.
EDCS-04201332.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a young girl.

EDCS-04201333.translation: Veidius Aphrodisius, freedman of Publius, and (perhaps)anus, freedman of Gnaeus, for (?) Sima, freedwoman of a woman (named) Eone.
EDCS-04201333.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription possibly involving multiple individuals and dedications.

EDCS-04201334.translation: The plot of Lucius Vettius Priscus and Valeria Iucunda, 60 feet in front and 200 feet in the field.
EDCS-04201334.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Lucius Vettius Priscus and Valeria Iucunda.

EDCS-04201335.translation: For Vettius Verus, by Afinia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04201335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Afinia for Vettius Verus.

EDCS-04201336.translation: Lucius Vibius Secundus, son of Caius, and his wife, Seconda, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201336.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a husband and wife.

EDCS-04201337.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Upsidia Chomi.

EDCS-04201338.translation: Miscus, son of Marcus, son of Tullius, ordered this to be made in his will for Nai, wife of Lucius, daughter of Tullius.
EDCS-04201338.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the beneficiaries and the manner of its construction (by will).

EDCS-04201339.translation: [---] Cestius, son of Marcus, and for his family ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04201339.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Cestius, son of Marcus, bequeaths a burial plot for himself and his family.

EDCS-04201340.translation: Arbenia, the most sensible of women, always devoted to her husband.
EDCS-04201340.summary: This is a funerary inscription praising the deceased woman, Arbenia.

EDCS-04201347.translation: Ricus son of Gritus, Ipl, son of Torus, Nistla, grandmother, Iacle, Ti, Ius.
EDCS-04201347.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary dedication with several personal names.

EDCS-04201351.translation: Quirinus, son ofrus, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201351.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Quirinus, son of rus, constructed his own tomb.

EDCS-04201353.translation: --- Nem, to Dis Manibus, for Remula Matrona, most unhappy, against eleven.
EDCS-04201353.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely concerning the deceased Remula Matrona and possibly a dispute or time frame.

EDCS-04201358.translation: Aurelius Saturninus, the deacon, made this for himself and for Aurelia Veneria, his most beloved wife, from his own property. I ask and beg all the clergy and the entire brotherhood that no one of the family or any other person be placed in this burial.
EDCS-04201358.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription by a deacon, Aurelius Saturninus, reserving his burial plot for himself and his wife and prohibiting others from being interred there.

EDCS-04201359.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Publicia Felicissima, the wife of the dedicator.

EDCS-04201360.translation: Made by Caius Socceius Fidelis, freedman of Caius, while alive, for Caius Socceius Atticus, son of Caius, and for his wife Matura, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-04201360.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Caius Socceius Fidelis, a freedman, for his son and daughter-in-law.

EDCS-04201361.translation: Coattenus Lamirus, the goldsmith, made this for himself, for his wife Popilia Varsa, and for his two sons Venustus and Egdotus and Arceius Eutychus, during his lifetime.
EDCS-04201361.summary: A goldsmith named Coattenus Lamirus dedicated this tomb for himself and his family, likely in the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201362.translation: and ordered by will that it be made for Pollentia Iphis and all her freedmen and freedwomen, for 10,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04201362.summary: This text, likely a continuation of a funerary dedication, specifies a sum of money for the construction of a monument for Pollentia Iphis and her dependants.

EDCS-04201363.translation: Cominia Euvodia [placed this] for Ulpius Bassianus, who lived 4 years, 8 months, and 15 days, her unfortunate grandson.
EDCS-04201363.summary: A funerary dedication by a grandmother for her young grandson, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201364.translation: Burial place of Marcus Volumnius Tenax, son of Marcus. 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-04201364.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot of Marcus Volumnius Tenax, specifying its dimensions, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201367.translation: By decree of the decurions, a burial place was granted to Maelia, daughter of Quintus Marcellus. 40 feet in front, 40 feet inward.
EDCS-04201367.summary: This inscription records a public grant of burial land to Maelia, daughter of Quintus Marcellus, by the local town council (decurions).

EDCS-04201368.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Titius Severus, his son, who also gave to the association of sailors of the municipium of Atria 400,000 sesterces in his will, to provide roses and food for him every year.
EDCS-04201368.summary: A son dedicated this tomb to his father, Quintus Titius Sertorianus, also noting a significant bequest to the sailors' guild of Atria for annual offerings.

EDCS-04201369.translation: Aemilia Lexis, freedwoman of the woman, made this for Ismarus, a freedman, while she was alive.
EDCS-04201369.summary: A funerary dedication made by Aemilia Lexis for Ismarus, both freedpersons, commissioned during her lifetime, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201370.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication identifying Ancharia Deutera, a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-04201371.translation: Titus Attius Rufus, son of Titus.
EDCS-04201371.summary: This is a standard Roman parentelic name formula identifying Titus Attius Rufus, son of Titus.

EDCS-04201372.summary: This is a standard Roman parentelic name formula identifying Aurelia Maxsima, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-04201375.translation: To Caesias Tertulla, daughter of Manius.
EDCS-04201375.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Caesias Tertulla, daughter of Manius.

EDCS-04201376.translation: To Quintus Stephanus, freedman of Marcus, and Vitalis, freedman of Citronia, and Ianuaria, Talasus.
EDCS-04201376.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Quintus Stephanus, Vitalis, and Ianuaria, identifying their patrons and relationships.

EDCS-04201377.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calidia T. Titia.

EDCS-04201378.translation: Grata, freedwoman of the wife of Cameria.
EDCS-04201378.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Grata, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201379.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quarta, daughter of Lucius Cameria.

EDCS-04201380.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secunda Cammica, daughter of Sipon.

EDCS-04201381.translation: Lucius Carisius Faber, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04201381.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Carisius Faber, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04201383.translation: Quintus Clodius Aprilis, son of Titus.
EDCS-04201383.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Clodius Aprilis, son of Titus.

EDCS-04201384.translation: Lucius Coelius Concerio, son of Marcus, aged 90 years.
EDCS-04201384.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Coelius Concerio, aged 90.

EDCS-04201386.translation: Lucius Curtius Priscus, freedman of Lucius; Curtia Neuma, freedwoman of Lucius; Curtia Pyramis, freedwoman of the wife.
EDCS-04201386.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Curtius Priscus, Curtia Neuma, and Curtia Pyramis.

EDCS-04201388.summary: This is a funerary inscription where a son dedicated a monument to his father.

EDCS-04201391.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Prima, daughter of Lucius Firmia.

EDCS-04201392.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Fulvia.

EDCS-04201393.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Gaius Gavius Chrestus.

EDCS-04201394.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Grattia.

EDCS-04201395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedwoman named Sura.

EDCS-04201396.translation: Hylas of the municipality of Atriatium.
EDCS-04201396.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hylas, possibly from the municipality of Atriatium.

EDCS-04201397.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Lucius Laberius.

EDCS-04201398.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Lucius Laberius Cornic.

EDCS-04201399.translation: Lucius Lepidius, son of Lucius, veteran.
EDCS-04201399.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Lepidius, a veteran.

EDCS-04201401.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lochias, son of Lucius Pullus.

EDCS-04201402.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Lucius Luc.

EDCS-04201403.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcinia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-04201404.translation: [Someone] made this for his fellow slave and companion [---]imae, freedwoman of Lucius Maximus, measuring 12 feet in front and 30 feet in depth.
EDCS-04201404.summary: A funerary dedication for a female slave and companion, specifying the plot dimensions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201405.translation: Aser for himself and his wife Aurina and Modestus, by decree of the decurions of the Matria tribe.
EDCS-04201405.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument dedicated by Aser for himself and his family, authorized by local officials.

EDCS-04201408.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Oppia, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-04201409.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Petronius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04201410.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Poblicius Communis.

EDCS-04201411.translation: Lucius Pullius Secundus, son of Caius.
EDCS-04201411.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Pullius Secundus, son of Caius.

EDCS-04201412.summary: This is a funerary epitaph forennia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04201413.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Rubrius, son of Caius.

EDCS-04201414.translation: To Titus Rubrius, son of Caius.
EDCS-04201414.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Titus Rubrius, son of Caius.

EDCS-04201415.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Sabinius Apsens, who died at the age of two.

EDCS-04201416.translation: Titus Saufeius Saucio, son of Lucius, greetings.
EDCS-04201416.summary: This is a greeting formula found on a tombstone, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201417.summary: This inscription is a simple name and status identification, likely for a tombstone, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201418.summary: This inscription identifies a freedwoman by name and her former status, likely on a tombstone from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201419.translation: Quintus Teidius Hil, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-04201419.summary: This inscription provides a name and manumission status, likely for a tombstone, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201420.summary: This inscription identifies a freedwoman by name and her patron, likely on a tombstone from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201421.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Marcus Mustius Secundinus made this for his most dutiful wife, Terentia ؟Capitolina, while he was alive.
EDCS-04201421.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a husband for his wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201422.summary: This inscription is a simple genealogical identification, likely for a tombstone, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201423.translation: Tertia, daughter of Marcus Aniavius, aged 70 years.
EDCS-04201423.summary: This inscription records the name, parentage, and age of a woman, likely on a tombstone from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201424.translation: Marcus Titius Marcellus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04201424.summary: This inscription is a simple genealogical identification, likely for a tombstone, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201425.summary: This inscription is a simple name, likely for a tombstone, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201499.translation: To Braetia Quarta, daughter of Manius.
EDCS-04201499.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Braetia Quarta, daughter of Manius.

EDCS-04201500.translation: Rufus Cilo grants the water channel by precarium.
EDCS-04201500.summary: This inscription records a grant of a water channel by Rufus Cilo, likely concerning property or access rights.

EDCS-04201501.translation: Viclus, son of Caius, 4th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-04201501.summary: This fragment likely records a person's name and a date, possibly for a legal or administrative record.

EDCS-04201502.translation: Aulus Vettius Venetus, freedman of Aulus Vettius, and his wife, ordered this to be made for his mother, Vettia Hila[---], while alive.
EDCS-04201502.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aulus Vettius Venetus for his mother, Vettia Hila[---], indicating a familial relationship and a posthumous dedication.

EDCS-04201503.translation: Volumnia Venusta, freedwoman of Gaius, wife; Murranus, son; Thebanus, son; Volumnia Casia, freedwoman of Gaius, daughter; made this for herself and her family, while alive.
EDCS-04201503.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Volumnia Venusta and Volumnia Casia for their family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201504.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iucunda, a freedwoman of Titus Vetius.

EDCS-04201505.translation: Maxima for herself and for Curtia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, her daughter-in-law, and for Quintus Novellius Crescens, son of Quintus, her grandson, and for Sextus Novellius, son of Quintus, her grandson.
EDCS-04201505.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Maxima for herself, her daughter-in-law Curtia Secunda, and two grandsons, Quintus Novellius Crescens and Sextus Novellius.

EDCS-04201506.translation: To Marcus Sacconius Antonius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04201506.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Marcus Sacconius Antonius, freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-04201508.translation: Attia Pupa, daughter of Marcus, ordered this to be made by her will for herself, her husband Marcus Vecilius Marcellus, her daughter Vecilia Prisca, daughter of Marcus, and her son Marcus Vecilius Praesens, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04201508.summary: This funerary epitaph was commissioned in a will by Attia Pupa for herself, her husband, daughter, and son.

EDCS-04201509.translation: [Dedication] of Quintus Amplius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe.
EDCS-04201509.summary: A dedication mentioning Quintus Amplius and his tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201510.translation: Sextus Carfenus Tertius, son of Sextus, for himself and for his freedmen, Sextus Carfenus Modestus, and his freedwomen.
EDCS-04201510.summary: This funerary monument was established by Sextus Carfenus Tertius for himself, his freedmen, and his freedwomen.

EDCS-04201511.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Statius Speratus, son of a freedman, dedicated this to his son Quintus Statius, who lived for 1 year, 2 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-04201511.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a child, made by his father, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201512.translation: To the Divine Shades: to our dearest Antonia, who lived 308 years [?], and Posturus Con[---].
EDCS-04201512.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the Divine Shades, honoring Antonia and Posturus Con[---], with an unusual age given for Antonia.

EDCS-04201513.translation: Of Lucius Valerius Vitlus, son of Lucius, twenty feet in front and twenty feet in the field.
EDCS-04201513.summary: This inscription appears to record land boundaries or measurements associated with Lucius Valerius Vitlus.

EDCS-04201514.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that records the name of a woman, Pupa, daughter of Ancaria.

EDCS-04201515.translation: Of Quintus Baebius Cardilliacus, son of Gaius; Maria Tertia, his wife, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04201515.summary: This inscription records the names of a married couple, Quintus Baebius Cardilliacus and his wife Maria Tertia.

EDCS-04201516.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the god Apollo, with the dedicator possibly named C. Alfianus.

EDCS-04201517.translation: Sextus Aponius Severus, son of Sextus, of the Romilia tribe, [---]
EDCS-04201517.summary: This is the beginning of a funerary inscription for Sextus Aponius Severus, with his name, filiation, and tribe, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201518.translation: Marcus Pontius Exoratus, son of Marcus. This burial plot will not pass to an heir. In front 20 feet, in the land 20 feet. Laelia Iucunda, freedwoman of Gaius, made this.
EDCS-04201518.summary: This is a funerary dedication establishing a burial plot that is not to be inherited, with dimensions specified, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201519.translation: Of Marcus Cocceius Salvius, son of Marcus, freedman.
EDCS-04201519.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely marking a tomb or a dedication, identifying Marcus Cocceius Salvius and his status as a freedman, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201520.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Valeria Dubitata placed this for her most devoted son Gaius Vibius Firmus and for herself.
EDCS-04201520.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Gaius Vibius Firmus by his mother Valeria Dubitata, who also provided for herself.

EDCS-04201521.translation: To Fadiena Restituta. Titus Fadienus [dedicates this] to Volusius.
EDCS-04201521.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fadiena Restituta by Titus Fadienus, possibly related to Volusius.

EDCS-04201523.translation: To Fortune. Titus Pinnius Firmus, son of Titus, [dedicated this].
EDCS-04201523.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the goddess Fortuna by Titus Pinnius Firmus.

EDCS-04201524.translation: Gaius Titius Pelops, freedman of Gaius, placed this by order of Jupiter, seen in a vision.
EDCS-04201524.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Gaius Titius Pelops, a freedman, who claims divine instruction from Jupiter.

EDCS-04201526.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. Titus Trebius, son of Titus, dedicated this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04201526.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Titus Trebius, son of Titus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201528.translation: Quintus Licinius Ateste, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, veteran of the fifteenth Apollinaris legion, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-04201528.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Nymphs by Quintus Licinius Ateste, a veteran of the fifteenth legion, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201529.translation: Lucius Minucius Optatus, freedman of Lucius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Silvanus; he also paved [this area].
EDCS-04201529.summary: This is a votive dedication to Silvanus by Lucius Minucius Optatus, a freedman, who also performed paving work, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201530.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Titus Calventius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04201530.summary: This is a votive dedication to Silvanus by Titus Calventius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201531.translation: Gaius Lartius Felix, freedman of Gaius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Viri [Potentes?].
EDCS-04201531.summary: This is a votive dedication by Gaius Lartius Felix, a freedman, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201533.translation: Gaius Nunnius Sabatina, son of Gaius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Furias.
EDCS-04201533.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Gaius Nunnius Sabatina to a deity or person named Furias.

EDCS-04201534.translation: Pag Savio Beg [son of] Laagis, son of Lucius, [dedicated this] to Lucius Clodius Mummius, B [consul?], with 200,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04201534.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 200,000 sesterces by Pag Savio Beg to Lucius Clodius Mummius, possibly a magistrate.

EDCS-04201535.translation: [---] Castricius, the sponge-maker, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04201535.summary: This is a fragmentary votive dedication by Castricius, identified by his occupation as a sponge-maker, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201536.translation: The Cenomani restored [this monument/place]; they willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-04201536.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by the Cenomani, possibly a tribal group, with the phrase indicating a restoration.

EDCS-04201537.summary: This is a short dedication by Quintus Cludius, likely on a private monument or offering, dated to the 1st century CE.

EDCS-04201538.translation: Fausta Lartia willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04201538.summary: This is a votive inscription by Fausta Lartia, indicating she fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-04201539.translation: Gaius Petronius Primus, freedman of Gaius, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04201539.summary: A votive inscription by Gaius Petronius Primus, a freedman, expressing fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-04201542.translation: Sextus Atilius Saranus, son of Marcus, proconsul, by decree of the Senate, ordered the boundaries and borders to be established between the Atestini and the Veicetini.
EDCS-04201542.summary: This inscription records a senatorial decree, issued by the proconsul Sextus Atilius Saranus, to establish territorial boundaries between two peoples, dated to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201543.translation: Lucius Caecilius, son of Quintus, proconsul, ordered the boundaries and borders to be established between the Atestini and the Patavini by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-04201543.summary: This inscription records a senatorial decree, issued by the proconsul Lucius Caecilius, to establish territorial boundaries between the Atestini and Patavini, likely in the 1st century BCE or early 1st century CE.

EDCS-04201544.translation: By decree of the Senate, Lucius Caecilius, son of Quintus, proconsul, ordered the boundaries and borders to be established between the Patavini and the Atestini.
EDCS-04201544.summary: This inscription records a senatorial decree, issued by the proconsul Lucius Caecilius, to establish territorial boundaries between the Patavini and Atestini, likely in the 1st century BCE or early 1st century CE.

EDCS-04201546.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning a prefect of the first cohort, possibly part of a military honorific, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201547.translation: Caius Aebutius Rufus, son of Caius, standard-bearer of the 11th Legion.
EDCS-04201547.summary: This inscription identifies Caius Aebutius Rufus as a standard-bearer in the 11th Legion, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201548.translation: Quintus Aetrius Macer, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, soldier of the 10th Praetorian Cohort.
EDCS-04201548.summary: This inscription records Quintus Aetrius Macer as a soldier in the 10th Praetorian Cohort, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201549.translation: To the memory of [---], son of Caius Alli [---], of the 14th Legion [---], from Clodia, freedwoman of Caius, [---] of his wife.
EDCS-04201549.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier of the 14th Legion and his wife, with significant portions missing, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201551.translation: Titus Atidius Porcio, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, soldier of the 18th Legion.
EDCS-04201551.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Atidius Porcio as a soldier in the 18th Legion, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201552.translation: Auctus, belonging to Lucius Allienus, a veteran of the VI Legion, served him for 11 years. Thus, in recognition of his services, he set up this monument. He lived for 25 years, born in Sardinia. He is buried here and [named] his heir in his will.
EDCS-04201552.summary: This funerary inscription records the relationship between a freedman, Auctus, and his former master, a veteran of the VI Legion, detailing his service and burial arrangements.

EDCS-04201553.translation: Marcus Billienus Actiacus, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, was admitted to the colony as a decurion after a naval battle fought by the XI Legion. A frugal man.
EDCS-04201553.summary: This inscription commemorates Marcus Billienus Actiacus, detailing his military service with the XI Legion, his admission to a colony as a decurion, and his character.

EDCS-04201554.translation: Lucius Caltius, son of Sextus, of the Romilia tribe, standard-bearer of the 12th Legion.
EDCS-04201554.summary: This inscription records Lucius Caltius as a standard-bearer in the 12th Legion, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201555.translation: Quintus Coelius, son of Lucius, of the XI Actian Legion, standard-bearer.
EDCS-04201555.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Coelius, son of Lucius, as a standard-bearer in the XI Actian Legion.

EDCS-04201556.translation: Titus Ennius Secundus, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, tribune of soldiers, prefect for administering justice, curator of the treasury, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201556.summary: This funerary inscription honors Titus Ennius Secundus, who held various military and administrative posts, with the monument erected by his will.

EDCS-04201557.translation: Fannia Festa, freedwoman of Titus, for her patron Titus Fannius, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe, of the 1st Praetorian cohort, and for herself, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201557.summary: This is a dedication made by a freedwoman, Fannia Festa, for her patron and herself, indicating it was erected during their lifetimes.

EDCS-04201558.translation: To Marcus Gellius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, from cohort II. His brother, Manius Gellius.
EDCS-04201558.summary: A tombstone or dedication from a brother to Marcus Gellius, a soldier in cohort II.

EDCS-04201559.translation: Lucius Mestrius, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe, of the legion IX.
EDCS-04201559.summary: A tombstone or dedication for Lucius Mestrius, a soldier in the ninth legion.

EDCS-04201560.translation: Lucius Osidius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, of the V Legion.
EDCS-04201560.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Osidius, son of Lucius, as a member of the V Legion.

EDCS-04201561.translation: Prefect of the arsenal of C. Titus Priscus.
EDCS-04201561.summary: An inscription identifying a military officer, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04201562.translation: Gaius Rutilius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, of the V Legion.
EDCS-04201562.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Rutilius, son of Titus, as a member of the V Legion.

EDCS-04201563.translation: To Lucius Sincus Dracon, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe, a soldier of the V Praetorian Cohort, who lived 21 years, served 4 years. To Sincia, daughter of Quintus, [---]lae, his daughter, who lived 29 years. To Gaius Tiburtius Clemens, son of Marcus, brother. To Tiburtia Quarta, daughter of Marcus. For herself and her family.
EDCS-04201563.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Sincus Dracon and Sincia, likely his sister, and Tiburtia Quarta, likely her mother, who were all members of the Praetorian Guard or related to them.

EDCS-04201564.translation: Gaius Talponius, son of Publius, of the Romilia tribe, from the XI Legion.
EDCS-04201564.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Talponius, a soldier of the XI Legion.

EDCS-04201565.translation: His mother Ena and his sister Ena, daughter of Caius, Prisca, made this while alive for Severus, soldier of the Praetorian cohort XI, aged 23, for herself and her family.
EDCS-04201565.summary: A tombstone for Severus, a soldier in the Praetorian cohort XI, erected by his mother and sister.

EDCS-04201566.translation: To Gaius Titus Magnus, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe, standard-bearer of the V Urban Cohort.
EDCS-04201566.summary: This inscription records Gaius Titus Magnus, a standard-bearer of the V Urban Cohort, likely from the mid-1st to early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201567.translation: Marcus Tudicius Niger, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, from the V Urban Cohort, for himself and his wife Aphrodisias, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-04201567.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Tudicius Niger, a soldier in the V Urban Cohort, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04201568.translation: Lucius Valerius, son of Titus, of the legion XV, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201568.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Valerius, a soldier in the fifteenth legion, whose monument was erected according to his will.

EDCS-04201569.translation: To Manius Vettius Vitalis, son of Manius, of the Romilia tribe, for his father Manius Vettius, son of Manius, of the Romilia tribe, and for his brother Quintus Vettius Quintellus, son of Quintus. Manius Vettius Vitalis was discharged from the VII Praetorian Cohort. He ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04201569.summary: This tombstone was erected by Manius Vettius Vitalis, a discharged soldier of the VII Praetorian Cohort, in memory of his father and brother.

EDCS-04201570.translation: Caius Veturius, son of Aulus, of the V Urban Cohort, ordered this to be made in his will for his father Aulus Veturtius, and his mother Petronia Tannia, daughter of Aulus, and his wife Terentia Secunda, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04201570.summary: This inscription records a will-based funerary dedication by Caius Veturius, a soldier of the V Urban Cohort, for his parents and wife.

EDCS-04201571.translation: To Titus Vibius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, centurion of the V Legion.
EDCS-04201571.summary: This inscription records Titus Vibius, a centurion of the V Legion.

EDCS-04201573.translation: Albucia Chreste, for herself and for Publius Cornelius Eglogus, deserving husband, and Publius Cornelius Albucius, son, Augustalis official, and Albucia Syntyche, and Publius Cornelius Pamphilus, and their freedmen and freedwomen, and [---].
EDCS-04201573.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Albucia Chreste for herself, her husband, son, and other family members and freedmen.

EDCS-04201574.translation: Anneiaria Festa, daughter of Caius. Titus Carnius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe, decurion.
EDCS-04201574.summary: This inscription records Anneiaria Festa and Titus Carnius, a decurion of the Romilia tribe.

EDCS-04201575.translation: Titus Aretius Apiolus, freedman of Titus Aretius Proculus, of Titus, Caius, Lucius, a Sexvir, also Augustalis, for himself and for Aretia Modesta, his freedwoman, and Titus Aretius Proculus, son of Spurius Modesta, his freedwoman. He made this while alive; this burial place will not follow the heir.
EDCS-04201575.summary: This is a self-funded funerary dedication by Titus Aretius Apiolus, a Sexvir and Augustalis, for himself, his freedwoman wife, and their daughter.

EDCS-04201576.translation: Marcus Doius Clemens, son of Marcus (of the Romilia tribe), elected decurion, quaestor twice, and Augustalis priest, ordered this to be made by his will for 76,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04201576.summary: This funerary inscription records a posthumous dedication by Marcus Doius Clemens, detailing his career and the sum of money left for its erection.

EDCS-04201577.translation: Lucius Ducenius Atimetus, the Augustalis from Patavium, the companion, [set this up for] Pyrallis, his freedwoman, 11 feet in front and 11 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04201577.summary: This is a funerary marker for a freedwoman, Pyrallis, set up by her patron and a fellow Augustalis, Lucius Ducenius Atimetus.

EDCS-04201578.translation: Lucius Gra[---], freedman of Lucius Don[---], Mate[---], a member of the IIIIvirate [---], for himself and [for] Magia, his wife [---].
EDCS-04201578.summary: A dedication for a man and his wife, likely a tombstone, mentioning his status as a member of the IIIIvirate.

EDCS-04201579.translation: Lucius Luc[---], Phu[---], a member of the IIIIvirate.
EDCS-04201579.summary: An incomplete inscription mentioning a man named Lucius Luc[---] and his role as a member of the IIIIvirate.

EDCS-04201580.translation: To Titus Pullius Linus, freedman of Titus, member of the IIIIvirate, Augustalis [---] Alb[---] [---].
EDCS-04201580.summary: A dedication to Titus Pullius Linus, a freedman who held the positions of IIIIvir and Augustalis.

EDCS-04201581.translation: From public funds, Caius Rubenius, son of Caius, built a gladiatorial training school.
EDCS-04201581.summary: A public works inscription recording the construction of a gladiatorial school by Caius Rubenius.

EDCS-04201582.translation: Manius Rufrius Faustus, freedman of Manius, a physician, IIIIvir, Augustalis, for Volumnia Maxuma, wife of Titus, and for Murra, freedwoman of Volumnia.
EDCS-04201582.summary: A tombstone for Manius Rufrius Faustus, a physician and local official, and his wife Volumnia Maxuma, also mentioning a freedwoman named Murra.

EDCS-04201583.translation: To Lucius Sicinius Optatus, freedman of Lucius, a member of the college of six, from his will, the first plot, facing every direction, twenty feet.
EDCS-04201583.summary: This inscription records a burial plot bequeathed by Lucius Sicinius Optatus, a member of the college of six, from his will.

EDCS-04201584.translation: Lucius Titinius Abascantus, a Sexvir, made this while alive for himself and for Titinia Eutaxia, his excellent freedwoman, and for Lucius Titinius Treptus, and for Titinia Campania, freedwoman, and for Lucius Titinius Aeucaristus, freedman.
EDCS-04201584.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Titinius Abascantus, a Sexvir, for himself and several freedmen and freedwomen, as well as other family members.

EDCS-04201587.translation: [Son] of C(aius), A[---] paved the road in honor.
EDCS-04201587.summary: This fragmented inscription records the paving of a road as a public service or honor by an individual identified by his father's name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04201588.translation: quinquennial for the second time, Julian, priest [---], sexviral [---]
EDCS-04201588.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to an official with multiple roles, possibly in a municipal context.

EDCS-04201589.translation: To P(ublius) Acutius [---]amo, freedman of Publius, actor.
EDCS-04201589.summary: This is a dedication to an actor named Publius Acutius, possibly a freedman, with his name partially restored.

EDCS-04201590.translation: Lucius Allenius Vespa, son of Lucius (of the Romilia tribe), a comb-maker.
EDCS-04201590.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Allenius Vespa, identified by his name, patronymic, tribal affiliation, and profession as a comb-maker.

EDCS-04201591.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph identifying a fuller named Anterotis.

EDCS-04201592.translation: The bones of Lucius Domitius Tigranus of Padua.
EDCS-04201592.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Lucius Domitius Tigranus, a native of Padua.

EDCS-04201593.translation: To Quintus Clodius Fortuatus, son of Quintus, freedman of Quintus Clodius, and to Quintus Clodius Nymphus, freedman of Quintus, and to Clodia Primigenia, freedwoman of Quintus, the hunting retinue of Marcus Etti Baebianus, freedman of Marcus, to their well-deserving friends.
EDCS-04201593.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a hunting retinue to their friends, identifying several freedmen and freedwomen by name.

EDCS-04201594.translation: Sacred to the divine shades of Lucretia Placidia, freedwoman of Marcus, a seamstress.
EDCS-04201594.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucretia Placidia, a freedwoman who worked as a seamstress.

EDCS-04201595.translation: Burial plot of Lucius Octavius Servandus, a comb-maker, twenty-two feet in front, twenty-four feet in the rear.
EDCS-04201595.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Octavius Servandus, a comb-maker.

EDCS-04201596.translation: Marcus Valerius Bucinus; Lucius Optatus, cook.
EDCS-04201596.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Marcus Valerius Bucinus and Lucius Optatus, who was a cook.

EDCS-04201597.translation: Vibia Maxuma, freedwoman of Lucius, erected [this] for Marcius, the doctor.
EDCS-04201597.summary: This inscription records that Vibia Maxuma, a freedwoman, set up a monument for Marcius, a doctor.

EDCS-04201599.translation: through Quintus Critronius, the road is owed to Quintus Critronius, son of Quintus, and to Pomponius Silon, and to no one else.
EDCS-04201599.summary: This inscription seems to record a right of way or an easement granted to Quintus Critronius and Pomponius Silon, specifying its extent and exclusivity.

EDCS-04201600.translation: The right of passage is owed to the Enian property by Gaius Quintus Largis, son of Lucius, and Gaius Ollius Salvius.
EDCS-04201600.summary: This inscription records a grant of a private right of way concerning the Enian estate, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201602.translation: To the departed spirits: in front 23 feet, behind 26 feet; Lucius A. T. from his own resources.
EDCS-04201602.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a plot of land of specified dimensions to the departed, paid for by Lucius A. T., likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201603.translation: Burial place of Gaius Accius Boethus: in front 33 feet, in the field 24 feet.
EDCS-04201603.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Gaius Accius Boethus, with its dimensions specified, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201605.translation: To Marcus Acutius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe; to Gaius Acutius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-04201605.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or notice of ownership concerning two individuals, Marcus Acutius and Gaius Acutius, both of the Romilia tribe, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201606.translation: Burial place of Acutia Allages: in front 22 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-04201606.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Acutia Allages, with its dimensions provided, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201607.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription identifying Acutia Athenais.

EDCS-04201608.translation: Aelius Valentio [set this up for] his most dutiful mother, Aelia Urba, who died at the age of eighty.
EDCS-04201608.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aelia Urba at eighty years old and is dedicated by her son, Aelius Valentio.

EDCS-04201609.translation: Publius Alius Brevis, son of Publius.
EDCS-04201609.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple tombstone or dedication for Publius Alius Brevis, son of Publius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201610.summary: This inscription is likely a tombstone or dedication for Lucius Allidius, son of Lucius, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201611.translation: Caius Ancharius Picens, son of Caius, lived for 12 years; [here lie the] bones of Sempronia, daughter of Lucius, his mother.
EDCS-04201611.summary: This inscription records the death of a child, Caius Ancharius Picens, aged 12, and mentions the bones of his mother, Sempronia.

EDCS-04201612.translation: Titus Annaienus, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-04201612.summary: This inscription is likely a tombstone or dedication for Titus Annaienus, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201613.translation: Gaius Antonius, son of Sextus, of the Romilia tribe, made this for himself and for his wife, Deminconia Mania, daughter of Minus, while he was alive.
EDCS-04201613.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gaius Antonius for himself and his wife, Deminconia Mania, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201614.translation: To Antonius Verus, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201614.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Antonius Verus for himself and his family, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201615.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Tertia Apicia, daughter of Lucius, likely a tombstone or epitaph.

EDCS-04201616.translation: Quintus Appaeus Rufio, freedman of Quintus, dedicated this while alive to himself and to Prima, daughter of Quintus Appaeus.
EDCS-04201616.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Quintus Appaeus Rufio, a freedman, for himself and his daughter, Prima.

EDCS-04201618.translation: Caius Artorius, son of Caius, dedicated this to Montana, freedwoman of Quintus Appaeus.
EDCS-04201618.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Caius Artorius to Montana, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201620.translation: The bones of Aculla, freed daughter of Marcus Arrius Elegans, freedman of Marcus, to her mother.
EDCS-04201620.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the placement of bones for Aculla, daughter of a freedman, to her mother.

EDCS-04201621.translation: Publius Asinius Rufus of the Romilia tribe, son of Publius, set this up while alive for himself, and for Turpio, his freedman, and for Fausta, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04201621.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Asinius Rufus for himself and his freedman and freedwoman.

EDCS-04201622.translation: Titus Atilius, son of Caius, and his wife Montana, daughter of Lucius, Furia, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201622.summary: This inscription records a monument or tombstone made by Titus Atilius and his wife Montana Furia during their lifetime.

EDCS-04201625.translation: Augusta made this by her will.
EDCS-04201625.summary: This inscription states that Augusta commissioned this monument or action through her will.

EDCS-04201626.translation: Montana, freedwoman of Salius Avillius, by her will.
EDCS-04201626.summary: This inscription indicates that Montana, a freedwoman, made arrangements by her will.

EDCS-04201627.translation: Lucius Aurelius Eros, freedman of Lucius, and Celido, freedwoman, and Coelia Secunda, daughter of Quintus, placed this.
EDCS-04201627.summary: This funerary inscription records the placement of a monument by Lucius Aurelius Eros, Celido, and Coelia Secunda.

EDCS-04201628.translation: Titus Aurelius Felix, freedman of Titus, made this while alive for himself and for all his freedmen and his fellow freedmen and his fellow freedwoman Grata, 16 feet in front and 20 feet in the land; the monument will not follow an heir. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-04201628.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription by Titus Aurelius Felix, specifying dimensions and intended beneficiaries, to be independent of inheritance.

EDCS-04201629.translation: Aurelius Phileta, son of Publius, dedicated this to his sister.
EDCS-04201629.summary: This is a dedication by Aurelius Phileta to his sister, likely on a tomb or memorial, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201630.summary: This inscription likely names two individuals, Quintus Caecilius Memor and L. Emor, possibly on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-04201631.translation: Caeneus and his daughter Tertulla wish for this to be made for themselves in accordance with their will.
EDCS-04201631.summary: This funerary inscription records the wishes of Caeneus and his daughter Tertulla regarding their tomb, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201632.translation: To Gaius Cassius, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe, according to his will.
EDCS-04201632.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Cassius, fulfilling his testamentary wishes, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201633.translation: Publius Caesonius Cimo, freedman of Publius Lupe, made this while alive for himself and for Fullonia, daughter of Titus, Fren[--] and Publius Caes[--].
EDCS-04201633.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Publius Caesonius Cimo for himself and his family, indicating a date during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201634.translation: This is a burial place for Titus Caetronius Firminus, son of Titus, and Gavia, daughter of Caius; 25 feet in front and 25 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04201634.summary: This funerary inscription marks the burial plot of Titus Caetronius Firminus and Gavia, specifying dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201635.summary: This very brief inscription likely records the name of a person, Calpurnius Erulli, possibly on a tomb or property marker, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201636.translation: Vassidia Aquilina, daughter of Marcus, placed this for her mother Calpurnia Venaeria, freedwoman of the woman.
EDCS-04201636.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Vassidia Aquilina to her mother Calpurnia Venaeria, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201637.translation: Burial place of Marcus Canius Marcel; 15 feet in front and 20 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04201637.summary: This funerary inscription designates the burial plot of Marcus Canius Marcel, including its dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201638.translation: For Caninius Auctus, son of Publius, and Romilia, daughter of Publius, wife of Mellai.
EDCS-04201638.summary: This inscription records the names of Caninius Auctus and his wife Romilia, likely as a dedication or on a funerary monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201639.translation: Sacred to the deified spirits of Kaninia Secunda, daughter of Vibus.
EDCS-04201639.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the deified spirits of Kaninia Secunda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201640.translation: Of Publius Carminius Priscus, freedman of Publius, freedman of Princeps.
EDCS-04201640.summary: This inscription records the complex freedman status of Publius Carminius Priscus, indicating patronage, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201641.translation: Quintus Cartilius, son of Quintus, and Tertia, daughter of Titus Luxonius.
EDCS-04201641.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Quintus Cartilius and Tertia, likely on a tomb or as part of a family record, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201642.translation: For the burial place of the associates of Lucius Cassius Cambarus, son of Quintus, and Cassia Iucunda, daughter of Publius, freedwoman of Cotia Callas.
EDCS-04201642.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial place for associates of Lucius Cassius Cambarus and Cassia Iucunda, indicating a shared burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201643.summary: This inscription identifies Auge as a freedwoman of Marcus, likely on a tomb or as a personal marker, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201645.translation: Ae, Cai's freedwoman Musa, to her mother, to Gaius Catius Vitalis, son of Caius, her husband; Talonia Prima, daughter of Titus, made this for herself and her family while alive.
EDCS-04201645.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by a freedwoman to her mother and husband, likely on a tombstone, specifying it was built during her lifetime.

EDCS-04201646.translation: Titia Celido, freedwoman of Titus, daughter of Titus, ordered this to be made in her will for her husband Tito Catulatio Receptus, freedman of Titus, and for her mother.
EDCS-04201646.summary: This text records a testamentary dedication ordered by Titia Celido for her husband and mother, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-04201647.translation: Catulla Maxuma, daughter of Quintus, aged 17.
EDCS-04201647.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Catulla Maxuma, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-04201649.translation: Tuvvius Certus, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-04201649.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple naming formula, identifying Tuvvius Certus by his father and tribal affiliation, possibly from a tomb or marker.

EDCS-04201650.summary: This inscription is a brief identification of Cilo, son of Caius, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-04201651.translation: The tomb of Cinicia Lepida, freedwoman of Lucius, in front 17.5 feet, behind 24 feet.
EDCS-04201651.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Cinicia Lepida, specifying the dimensions of the tomb area.

EDCS-04201655.translation: Of Lucius Clodius Clar(us), freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201655.summary: This inscription names Lucius Clodius Clar(us), a freedman of Lucius, likely as the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-04201656.summary: This inscription records the name of Clodia Polla, daughter of Manius, probably from a tombstone.

EDCS-04201657.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Urbana, the wife of Clodius, likely on a tomb or a monument honoring her.

EDCS-04201658.translation: Titus Coelius Phoebus for himself and for his excellent wife Asconia Renata and for his family, Tirubeni(us) and Albina Muri(a).
EDCS-04201658.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Titus Coelius Phoebus for himself, his wife, and his family, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-04201659.translation: Prima Coelia, daughter of Mataronis, placed [this monument].
EDCS-04201659.summary: A funerary monument set up by Prima Coelia for herself or a relative.

EDCS-04201660.translation: Publius Coelius Aper, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe, and Epidia Secunda, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04201660.summary: This inscription records the names of Publius Coelius Aper and Epidia Secunda, possibly a married couple or individuals sharing a monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201661.translation: Gaius Coelius Severus, son of Publius.
EDCS-04201661.summary: A funerary or honorary inscription identifying Gaius Coelius Severus, son of Publius.

EDCS-04201662.translation: Marcus Cominius Deuter, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for Titus Cotius Quadratus, freedman of Titus, and for Marcus Cominius Repentinus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04201662.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Cominius Deuter for himself and two other freedmen, likely indicating familial or social ties, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201663.translation: To Cornelius, son of Lucius, father of Caninius Unda.
EDCS-04201663.summary: A dedication to Cornelius, son of Lucius, identified as the father of Caninius Unda.

EDCS-04201664.translation: Romilia Tertia, [daughter] of Titus Cornelius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04201664.summary: An inscription identifying Romilia Tertia, daughter of Titus Cornelius, son of Gaius.

EDCS-04201665.translation: Cornelia Venusta, freedwoman of Cornelia Acme, freedwoman of Marcus, placed [this monument].
EDCS-04201665.summary: A funerary monument set up by Cornelia Venusta, a freedwoman, for her patroness Cornelia Acme.

EDCS-04201666.translation: Burial place of Cornelia Lucius Lepida.
EDCS-04201666.summary: An inscription designating a burial plot for Cornelia Lucius Lepida.

EDCS-04201667.summary: A dedication or funerary inscription for Posilla, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04201668.translation: Marcus Crimilius Optatus, son of Lucius, and Geminia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, while alive, for themselves and [their] husband.
EDCS-04201668.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Crimilius Optatus and Geminia Secunda for themselves and one of their husbands.

EDCS-04201669.translation: Damale, slave of Tiberius Iunius, 20 years old, is buried here.
EDCS-04201669.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Damale, a slave who died at the age of 20, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201670.translation: Lucius Ennius, son of Lucius, [and] Romilia Enicenius [and] Rutilia C.
EDCS-04201670.summary: An inscription listing members of a family, likely on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-04201671.translation: Murranus, freedman, placed (this) for Gaius Ennius Hilarion, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-04201671.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Murranus to Gaius Ennius Hilarion, indicating a relationship between freedmen, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201672.translation: To Epictetus, aged 2 years, 8 months, 19 days. Gaius Valerius Eucarpus, [his] father, and Nice, [his] mother, [set this up, a] miserable [mother].
EDCS-04201672.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Epictetus, set up by his parents, Gaius Valerius Eucarpus and Nice.

EDCS-04201673.translation: To the divine spirits of Marcus Eppius Rufus, son of Marcus, who lived 12 years and 20 days. Marcus Eppius Ianuarius, freedman of the woman, and Cominia Procula, daughter of Lucius, his parents, [erected this].
EDCS-04201673.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy, erected by his parents, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201675.translation: Fuscus and Chia, parents, for Facundus, aged 10.
EDCS-04201675.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their young son, Facundus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201676.translation: To Felicia, freedwoman of Lucius, from Juvavia.
EDCS-04201676.summary: A dedication to a freedwoman, possibly indicating her origin or place of residence, date unknown.

EDCS-04201678.translation: Gaius Flavius, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe, fisherman.
EDCS-04201678.summary: An epitaph or identification for a fisherman named Gaius Flavius, likely Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201679.translation: Lucius Flavianus Adrastus, freedman of Manius.
EDCS-04201679.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Lucius Flavianus Adrastus, a freedman, likely on a tomb or funerary marker, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201680.translation: To Fonnia Venusta, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201680.summary: A dedication to a freedwoman, likely part of a funerary or honorific monument, date unknown.

EDCS-04201681.translation: To Sextus Gabius Euphemus and Asconia Merope and my descendants, in front 20 feet, back 20 feet.
EDCS-04201681.summary: A funerary dedication granting burial space for named individuals and their descendants, indicating dimensions of the plot, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201682.translation: Publius Gellius [erected this for] his brother.
EDCS-04201682.summary: A dedication by Publius Gellius for his brother, likely a funerary monument, date unknown.

EDCS-04201683.summary: A record indicating that the inscription's subject or endowment was established by the will of Gelotius, date unknown.

EDCS-04201684.translation: Graccellia Secunda, daughter of Publius, dedicated the place, 20 feet on all sides, to herself and hers, to Publius Gracellius, son of Lucius, her father, and Acellasia Maxima, daughter of Lucius, her mother, to Philetus for public use.
EDCS-04201684.summary: A dedication of land for public use and burial by Graccellia Secunda for herself, her parents, and Philetus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201685.translation: To Lucius Gracchanus Anicetus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201685.summary: A dedication to a freedman named Lucius Gracchanus Anicetus, likely part of a funerary monument, date unknown.

EDCS-04201686.translation: To the divine spirits of Grania Romana, freedwoman of Marcus. Marcus Granius Ursio erected [this] for her, who deserved exceedingly well of him.
EDCS-04201686.summary: A funerary epitaph erected by Marcus Granius Ursio for his freedwoman Grania Romana, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201687.translation: To Grania Secunda, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201687.summary: This is a dedication to Grania Secunda, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-04201688.translation: Grania, daughter of Mani, and her freedwoman give the place.
EDCS-04201688.summary: This inscription records Grania, daughter of Mani, and her freedwoman donating a place.

EDCS-04201689.translation: To Lucius Plasidienus, son of Hebenus.
EDCS-04201689.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Plasidienus, son of Hebenus.

EDCS-04201690.translation: Titus Heiuleius Hilarus, freedman of Titus, [dedicated this] for himself and for Pompeia Sura, freedwoman of Gnaeus, 14 feet in front and 15 feet behind.
EDCS-04201690.summary: A funerary inscription for Titus Heiuleius Hilarus and Pompeia Sura, indicating the dimensions of their plot.

EDCS-04201691.translation: To Hilarius, freedman of Publius, for the road of Iurius, son of Publius, and his freedman.
EDCS-04201691.summary: This is a dedication concerning a road, made for Hilarius, freedman of Publius, and his freedman.

EDCS-04201692.translation: To the departed spirits: Irene, who lived 18 years, 8 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-04201692.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Irene.

EDCS-04201693.translation: Gnaeus Lepidius, son of Marcus, 38 feet in front, 36 feet in the land.
EDCS-04201693.summary: This inscription records land dimensions measured by Gnaeus Lepidius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04201694.translation: Lucius Licinius, son of Marcus, 20 feet in front, [ ] feet in the land.
EDCS-04201694.summary: This inscription records land dimensions, with the rear measurement incomplete, for Lucius Licinius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04201695.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius, son of Caius.

EDCS-04201696.translation: Son of Romilia Ligus by will.
EDCS-04201696.summary: This inscription indicates a bequest or inheritance related to a son of Romilia Ligus.

EDCS-04201697.translation: Luccia Quarta, daughter of Caius, mother for herself and for her son Marcus Velitius.
EDCS-04201697.summary: This funerary inscription records Luccia Quarta making provisions for herself and her son Marcus Velitius.

EDCS-04201698.translation: To Numerius Lusius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-04201698.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Numerius Lusius, identifying his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04201699.translation: Primus, Dasius, and the freedman Dasius, freedmen of C. Macedonius Philargyrus, son of C. [son of] P(ublius)...
EDCS-04201699.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription possibly honoring freedmen associated with C. Macedonius Philargyrus.

EDCS-04201700.translation: [---], Manilius, son of Aulus, of the Collina tribe.
EDCS-04201700.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Manilius, his father, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04201701.translation: Marcus Marcius, son of [---], of the Romilia tribe, Marc[---]
EDCS-04201701.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Marcus Marcius, his father, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04201703.translation: Lucius Melminius Eutychus, while alive, made this for his dearest son Lucius Melminius Romilius Festus and for himself; a plot with surrounding space was given by Octavia Mai, 10 feet in front and 20 feet in depth in the field.
EDCS-04201703.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Melminius Eutychus for his son and himself, with details about the donated plot of land.

EDCS-04201704.summary: This is an inscription identifying Mulvia Maxsuma and her father.

EDCS-04201705.translation: Titus Muttinius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, Nael, while alive, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201705.summary: This funerary inscription, set up by Nael, states that Titus Muttinius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, ordered it to be made in his will.

EDCS-04201706.translation: Octavia Venusta, daughter of Titus, a freedwoman of Octavia Primula, while alive, made this for Titus Octavius Laetus, son of Titus.
EDCS-04201706.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Octavia Venusta for Titus Octavius Laetus.

EDCS-04201707.translation: Titus Livius, son of Gaius, placed [this] for Octavia Secunda, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04201707.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Titus Livius for Octavia Secunda.

EDCS-04201708.translation: Orbia Severa, daughter of Titus, while alive, made this for her father Titus Orbius, son of Lucius, and for her mother Coelia Prisca, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-04201708.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Orbia Severa for her parents, Titus Orbius and Coelia Prisca.

EDCS-04201711.translation: Lucius Petronicus Primus, freedman of Lucius, ordered [this] to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201711.summary: A funerary monument commissioned in the will of Lucius Petronicus Primus.

EDCS-04201712.translation: Petronia, daughter of Caius, wife of Marcus Cusonius.
EDCS-04201712.summary: This inscription identifies Petronia, daughter of Caius, and her husband Marcus Cusonius.

EDCS-04201714.translation: Gaius Plotius, son of Gaius, and Vettia Secunda, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04201714.summary: This inscription identifies two individuals, Gaius Plotius and Vettia Secunda, along with their fathers' names.

EDCS-04201715.translation: To Marcus Plotius, son of Titus, from the Romilia tribe, Marcello.
EDCS-04201715.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Plotius, identified by his tribal affiliation and gentilicium.

EDCS-04201717.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of an individual named Pollio.

EDCS-04201718.translation: Titus Pomponenus Gratus, freedman of a woman, [ordered this] to be made by will for Clodia Arche, freedwoman of C. [---].
EDCS-04201718.summary: A funerary epitaph commissioned by will for Clodia Arche by Titus Pomponenus Gratus.

EDCS-04201721.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph for Primigenia, freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-04201722.translation: Priscilla, daughter of [---]ari, freedwoman of Priscianus.
EDCS-04201722.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Priscilla, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201724.translation: Primus, freedman of Sextus Quosonius, the freedman Ancialis, set this up.
EDCS-04201724.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Primus, a freedman, honoring his patron.

EDCS-04201725.translation: Burial place: 15 feet in front, 20 feet in the field, of Lucius Rutilius.
EDCS-04201725.summary: This is a boundary marker or plot description for a burial space belonging to Lucius Rutilius.

EDCS-04201726.translation: Sextus Rutilius, son of Quintus, from the Romilia tribe, made this while alive for himself, for his father Quintus Rutilius, son of Lucius; for his mother Caltia, daughter of Caius; and for his wife Ingenua, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04201726.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Sextus Rutilius for himself and his family members, including parents and wife.

EDCS-04201727.translation: To Sabina, wife of Lucius Helvius Justus. Lucius Sempronius Chrestus and Prima, the father and mother, [erected this].
EDCS-04201727.summary: This funerary dedication is for Sabina, wife of Lucius Helvius Justus, and was set up by her parents.

EDCS-04201728.summary: A simple funerary epitaph for Sacidia Benigna, freedwoman of Publius.

EDCS-04201729.translation: For Quintus Salvius Simo. Pla, his wife, set this up for herself and for her patron; this place and monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-04201729.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Pla for her husband Quintus Salvius Simo and herself, stipulating it is not heritable.

EDCS-04201732.translation: Satria, freedwoman of Armis, ordered this to be made in her will.
EDCS-04201732.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Satria, a freedwoman, through her will.

EDCS-04201734.translation: Sempidiena, freedwoman of Publius, of Acumis, dutiful.
EDCS-04201734.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Sempidiena, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201735.translation: Secundus, freedman of Quintus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his wife Sabina, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201735.summary: This funerary monument records a self-funded burial by a freedman for himself and his wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201736.translation: Spica, daughter of Caius, in her third year and month.
EDCS-04201736.summary: This inscription likely records the name and age of a young child, possibly a funerary marker, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201737.translation: To Pica, mother of Septumius, from Adepris.
EDCS-04201737.summary: This votive or funerary inscription records a dedication to a mother named Pica by someone named Adepris, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201738.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Primus for Severa Ossa.

EDCS-04201739.summary: This very brief inscription possibly identifies a freedman named Severus, perhaps on a tomb or object, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201740.translation: Titus Sextius Eros, freedman of Titus, and Cila, freedwoman of the woman Coponia.
EDCS-04201740.summary: This inscription identifies two individuals, Titus Sextius Eros and Cila, both freedpersons, likely a funerary marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201742.translation: To the departed spirits, to eternal piety, Sotericiano, aged seven. Soterichus and [---] D[---]
EDCS-04201742.summary: A funerary inscription for a young boy named Sotericiano, dedicated by Soterichus and another person.

EDCS-04201743.summary: This inscription names Speratus, a freedman of Sextus, possibly as part of a funerary monument or ownership mark from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201744.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of a 15-year-old named Suavis, from the Roman Imperial period.
