EDCS-04201746.translation: Sulla and Urbana, freedman and freedwoman respectively of Vivi Abius, placed [this].
EDCS-04201746.summary: This funerary inscription records that Sulla and Urbana, freedpersons, erected a monument, likely for themselves or another, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201747.summary: This inscription names Quintus Sulpicius Martialis and another individual, likely a funerary or dedication context, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201749.translation: Bones of Lucius Talponius, son of Caius, aged 12 years, and of Lucius Talponius Firmu, grandson of Caius, aged 14 months.
EDCS-04201749.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages and familial relationships of two young boys, Lucius Talponius and Lucius Talponius Firmu, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201750.translation: Valeria Rhodine made this for Gaius Taurius Ursus, her deserving husband, and for herself while she was alive.
EDCS-04201750.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife to her husband and herself.

EDCS-04201752.translation: Lucius Manius Blattii, grandsons, gave this for Quintus Terentius, son of Lucius, and Rufa, daughter of Calventia Mani.
EDCS-04201752.summary: A dedication by grandsons for their grandparents.

EDCS-04201753.translation: For Manius Terentius Suetonius, from Manius Terentius Utycus, the most dutiful.
EDCS-04201753.summary: A dedication to a deserving individual.

EDCS-04201754.translation: Olia Graphe [dedicated this] to Terentia Chrysidis (or perhaps to Terentius Chrysidus).
EDCS-04201754.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription possibly dedicating a monument to Terentia Chrysidis by Olia Graphe.

EDCS-04201755.translation: Fronte 10 feet. Terentia Maxuma, daughter of Manius, (dedicated) a plot of 20 feet in the land, for burial space, for the other half.
EDCS-04201755.summary: A funerary plot demarcation specifying dimensions and ownership.

EDCS-04201756.translation: The bones of Tiburtia Secunda, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201756.summary: A simple ossuary inscription indicating the deceased.

EDCS-04201757.translation: Lucius Titurius Sura, son of Caius, placed this; Acutia Auga, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04201757.summary: A monument erected by a freedwoman for her patron.

EDCS-04201758.translation: For Publius Trottedius Sasa, freedman of Publius.

EDCS-04201759.translation: Elate, freedwoman of Publius, made this for herself and for her husband, Lucius Fonteius Salona, son of Lucius, while she was alive.
EDCS-04201759.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife to herself and her husband.

EDCS-04201760.translation: Romilia Marcella and Barbia Secunda, daughter of Manius, made this for Marcus Tudicius, son of Publius, and for themselves while they were alive.
EDCS-04201760.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by two women for a man and for themselves.

EDCS-04201761.translation: Gaius Tullius, son of Titus, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04201761.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by will.

EDCS-04201762.translation: Corinthus and Coriscus, freedmen of Gaius Tullius Secundus, set this up for their patron.
EDCS-04201762.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by freedmen for their patron.

EDCS-04201763.translation: For Gaius Turpilius Hilario, fifteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-04201763.summary: This inscription likely marks the burial space or property boundaries for Gaius Turpilius Hilario.

EDCS-04201765.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Gaius Valerius.
EDCS-04201765.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a grave to Gaius Valerius.

EDCS-04201766.translation: For Manius Valerius Pamphilus, freedman of Manius.
EDCS-04201766.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Manius Valerius Pamphilus, a freedman.

EDCS-04201767.translation: Tertia, daughter of Valeria, daughter of Tertius.
EDCS-04201767.summary: This is an ownership or familial inscription identifying Valeria Tertia.

EDCS-04201768.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription for Valgia Cupula.

EDCS-04201769.translation: To Gaius Varius Calvio, son of Gaius Varius, son of Gaius, and to his wife Livia Quarta, Gaius Varius Calvio, son of Gaius, son of Gaius, dedicates this for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201769.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Varius Calvio for himself, his wife, and family, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201770.translation: Varia Priscilla, daughter of Gaius, and if she is well.
EDCS-04201770.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication, possibly funerary, to Varia Priscilla, mentioning the Nautae (boatmen/sailors).

EDCS-04201771.translation: Lucius Vedius, son of Lucius, for himself and for his wife Satria Secunda, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04201771.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Vedius for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04201772.translation: Romilia, wife of Gaius Veienus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04201772.summary: This inscription identifies Romilia, the wife of Gaius Veienus.

EDCS-04201773.translation: Gaius Versinius, son of Gaius, twenty-seven years old.
EDCS-04201773.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Gaius Versinius, likely for funerary or identification purposes.

EDCS-04201774.translation: Vettia, daughter of Titus, for herself and for Titus Nerius Macro, Nerius Liberalis, and Petronia Men, daughter of Titus, erected this.
EDCS-04201774.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Vettia for herself and other family members, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201776.translation: Gaius Vibius, son of Caius, the shoemaker, for Veria.
EDCS-04201776.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Veria, set up by Gaius Vibius Sutor, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201777.translation: Titus Vibius Eros, on the front.
EDCS-04201777.summary: This inscription likely marks the front of a tomb or monument belonging to Titus Vibius Eros, dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201791.summary: This is a dedication to the god Anganius Temivaius, likely an indigenous deity, set up possibly by a local magistrate, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-04201827.translation: Fougonia, daughter of Fecitorei, [dedicated this] to Fucienia Iamsoius.
EDCS-04201827.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fougonia for Fucienia Iamsoius, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201829.translation: Adeptus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo.
EDCS-04201829.summary: A personal votive inscription by Adeptus to the god Apollo, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201830.translation: Gaius Acutius Maturus, son of Gaius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-04201830.summary: A personal votive inscription by Gaius Acutius Maturus to Apollo Augustus, likely from Apono, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201831.translation: Gaius Cassius Severus, former praetorian speculator, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-04201831.summary: A personal votive inscription by Gaius Cassius Severus, identifying his military and civil service, likely from Apono, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201832.text_edition: \n Aquis Aponi Caius Cluentius Caio filius Romulia sic Proculus Ateste aedilis IIvir quaestor aerarii bis pontifex votum solvit\n
EDCS-04201832.translation: Gaius Cluentius Proculus, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe, from Atesta, having served as aedile twice, duumvir, quaestor of the treasury twice, and pontifex, willingly fulfilled his vow to the Baths of Aponus.
EDCS-04201832.summary: This inscription records the civic and religious offices held by Gaius Cluentius Proculus before he fulfilled a vow to the Baths of Aponus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201833.translation: Nigellus, freedman of Macrinus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-04201833.summary: A personal votive inscription by Nigellus, a freedman, to Apollo Augustus, likely from Apono, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201834.translation: Quintus Magurius Ferox, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, who performed in exhibitions and with cithara players in the Veturian herd, also called the Junian herd, dedicated to the Baths of Apono eight EURAS (measures of land?) and twelve uncinorum (ropes?), totaling 259 units.
EDCS-04201834.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Magurius Ferox, possibly a performer or organizer of games, to the Baths of Apono, including land and other measures, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201835.translation: Marcus Terentius Secundus, freedman of Marcus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-04201835.summary: A personal votive inscription by Marcus Terentius Secundus, a freedman, to Apollo Augustus, likely from Apono, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201836.translation: Gaius Titius, son of Caius, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-04201836.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Titius fulfilling a vow to Apollo Augustus, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201837.translation: Gaius Trebius Firmus, son of Caius, along with a gift, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-04201837.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Trebius Firmus fulfilling a vow to Apollo Augustus, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201838.translation: Sacred to Fortuna. Publius Opsidius Rufus, son of Publius, a municipal official (IIIIvir), military tribune of the IV Scythica legion, and prefect of the engineers, dedicated this.
EDCS-04201838.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna by Publius Opsidius Rufus, who lists his military and civic offices, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201839.translation: Velleia Chreste, daughter of Publius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Fortuna.
EDCS-04201839.summary: A personal votive inscription by Velleia Chreste to the goddess Fortuna, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201840.translation: Veturia Gemella, daughter of Marcus, and Gaius Dorcatius Verus, gave and dedicated this gift to Fortuna Muliebris.
EDCS-04201840.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Muliebris by Veturia Gemella and Gaius Dorcatius Verus, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201841.translation: To the Genius of the Guild of Dendrophori. Manius Laelius Magnus, as VIvir, because of the quinquennal office, number 261.
EDCS-04201841.summary: This is a dedication by Manius Laelius Magnus to the Genius of the Dendrophori guild, likely commemorating his quinquennal office, dated by context to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201842.translation: To the Genius of the Masters and to the Lares of the public. Titus Poblicius Crescens gave two silver statues by will, for 2000 sesterces.
EDCS-04201842.summary: Titus Poblicius Crescens dedicated two silver statues to the household gods (Genius of the Masters and public Lares) via his will, indicating a date in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201843.text_edition: \n Isidi signum Harpocratis Caius Didius Acutianus dono dedit\n
EDCS-04201843.translation: Gaius Didius Acutianus gave a statue of Harpocrates to Isis as a gift.
EDCS-04201843.summary: This inscription records a votive gift of a statue of Harpocrates to the goddess Isis by Gaius Didius Acutianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201844.translation: To Isis Regina. Publius Postumius Hecateus and Publicia Felicitas. The place was granted by decree of the decurions, number 302.
EDCS-04201844.summary: This is a dedication to Isis Regina by Publius Postumius Hecateus and Publicia Felicitas, with the plot granted by local officials, suggesting a date in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201845.translation: Quintus Valerius Menander, son of Quintus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Juno.
EDCS-04201845.summary: Quintus Valerius Menander fulfilled a vow to Juno, indicating a personal religious dedication from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201846.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tampia, daughter of Lucius, likely dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201847.translation: Gaius Helvius Romanus, for himself and his family, willingly paid his vow to the Unconquered God.
EDCS-04201847.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Helvius Romanus fulfilling a vow to an "Unconquered God", possibly Sol Invictus or a local deity, likely dating from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-04201848.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Aelia Maxima placed [this] in memory of her son, Caius Lartius Taurinus. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201848.summary: Aelia Maxima dedicated this monument to Mercury Augustus in memory of her son, Caius Lartius Taurinus, with the site granted by local officials, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201851.translation: By order of Proserpina, Lucius Calventius Festus, freedman of Lucius, set up this altar, a sacred offering.
EDCS-04201851.summary: An altar dedicated to Proserpina by Lucius Calventius Festus, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-04201852.translation: Prima Minucia placed [this] for Venus Victrix, having been commanded by a vision.
EDCS-04201852.summary: Prima Minucia dedicated this offering to Venus Victrix after receiving a divine vision, a personal religious act from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201855.summary: A simple dedication by Publius Mulvius Cilo, possibly a funerary monument or a donation.

EDCS-04201856.translation: Sextus Pompeius, son of Sextus, gave (this).
EDCS-04201856.summary: A dedication by Sextus Pompeius, son of Sextus, likely for a funerary monument or a donation.

EDCS-04201857.translation: Manius Publicius Festus gave [this] as a gift.
EDCS-04201857.summary: Manius Publicius Festus made a dedication or gift, a simple votive inscription from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201860.translation: Marcus Agrippa, son of Lucius, consul [III?].
EDCS-04201860.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning Marcus Agrippa, son of Lucius, and his third consulship, dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201863.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi filio decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04201863.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201863.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla) and records that the honor was granted by decree of the decurions, dating it to his reign in the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201864.text_edition: \n Aeterno imperatori nostro maximo optimoque principi Aurelio Valerio Diocletiano Pio Felici Invicto Augusto Paetus Honoratus vir clarissimus corrector Italiae numini eius dicatissimus\n
EDCS-04201864.translation: To our eternal, greatest, and best emperor, Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, Paetus Honoratus, a most distinguished man, corrector of Italy, most devoted to his divine will.
EDCS-04201864.summary: An inscription dedicated to Emperor Diocletian by Paetus Honoratus, corrector of Italy, likely dating to his reign (late 3rd/early 4th century CE).

EDCS-04201865.text_edition: \n Piissimo ac fortissimo domino nostro Marco Aurelio Valerio Maximiano Pio Felici Invicto semper Augusto Isteius Tertullus vir clarissimus corrector Venetiae et Histriae numini eius semper devotus\n
EDCS-04201865.translation: To our most pious and bravest lord, our Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered, ever Augustus, Isteius Tertullus, a most distinguished man, corrector of Venetia and Istria, ever devoted to his divine will.
EDCS-04201865.summary: An inscription dedicated to Emperor Maximian by Isteius Tertullus, corrector of Venetia and Istria, likely dating to his reign (late 3rd/early 4th century CE).

EDCS-04201866.translation: To Marcus Arruntius Aquila, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, official for striking coinage, Caesar's quaestor, tribune of the plebs, praetor, consul, XVvir for sacred rites; for his son.
EDCS-04201866.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Arruntius Aquila, detailing his extensive political and religious career, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201867.translation: [...] Rufus, Quintus Asconius Gabinius Modestus, governor, prefect of Saturn's treasury, gave (this).
EDCS-04201867.summary: A dedication by Quintus Asconius Gabinius Modestus, listing his high offices as governor and prefect of the treasury, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04201869.translation: To Titus Mustius Hostilius Fabricius Medulla, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, admitted to the rank of military tribune by Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus, curator of the treasury, pontifex, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201869.summary: A funerary monument or dedication to Titus Mustius Hostilius Fabricius Medulla, who held various public offices including curator of the treasury and pontifex, likely dating to the reign of Nerva (96-98 CE).

EDCS-04201870.text_edition: \n Sexto Papinio Quinti filio Allenio tribuno militum quaestori legato Tiberi Caesaris Augusti tribuno plebis praetori legato Tiberi Caesaris Augusti pro praetore consuli XVviro sacris faciundis decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04201870.translation: To Sextus Papinius Allenius, son of Quintus, military tribune, quaestor, legate of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, tribune of the plebs, praetor, legate of Tiberius Caesar Augustus pro praetore, consul, member of the XV viri sacris faciundis, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201870.summary: An inscription honoring Sextus Papinius Allenius, who held numerous high-ranking political and religious offices, including consul, likely dating to the 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201875.translation: Manius Allenius Crassus Caesonius, son of Manius, of the Fabian tribe, military tribune, prefect of the Fabri, IIvir.
EDCS-04201875.summary: A tombstone or dedication for Manius Allenius Crassus Caesonius, who served as military tribune, prefect of the Fabri, and IIvir, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201876.translation: To Gaius Asconius Sardo, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, IIvir iure dicundo, prefect of the Fabri, for his brother and his mother Sardi, daughter of Marcus; and for himself, Asconia Augurini, daughter of Gaius, priestess of the deified Domitilla.
EDCS-04201876.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Asconia for her brother and mother, and also for herself, mentioning her family's public offices and her own role as priestess of deified Domitilla, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201877.translation: To Aurelius Iustinus Apronianus, veteran, his heirs Septimius Proculus and Valerius Proculus, with Faustinus and Julius, freedmen, supervised this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-04201877.summary: A funerary monument erected by the heirs and freedmen for Aurelius Iustinus Apronianus, a veteran, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04201881.translation: To Lucius Memmius Hebrenus, called idem, sailor of the fleet, of Sabinus's century, who lived for 30 years and served for 12 years; his heirs, Iarsa his brother, Paulus, and Q. Cusfilius, had this made through Lucius Coranus Ursulus, the fiduciary heir.
EDCS-04201881.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Memmius Hebrenus, a sailor, erected by his heirs and brother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201882.translation: To Titus Mutius Cracilius, son of Titus, prefect of the Fabri, IIvir iure dicundo, by public decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201882.summary: A public monument or dedication to Titus Mutius Cracilius, who held the offices of prefect of the Fabri and IIvir iure dicundo, by public decree of the decurions, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201883.translation: To Sextus Pompeius, son of Sextus, prefect iure dicundo, twice prefect of the Fabri, augur; for himself and for his wife Tullia Severa, daughter of Sextus, and for Severa his daughter, aged 20 years.
EDCS-04201883.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Sextus Pompeius for himself, his wife Tullia Severa, and his daughter Severa, detailing his public and religious offices, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04201884.translation: Gaius Remmius Rufus, son of Publius, was appointed by the divine Augustus as curator of the praetorian guard.
EDCS-04201884.summary: This inscription records the appointment of Gaius Remmius Rufus as curator of the praetorian guard under the divine Augustus, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04201885.translation: Fabius, a veteran of the Twentieth Legion, made this for himself and for his wife, Tullia Secunda, daughter of Quintus, daughter of Titus Saufeius.
EDCS-04201885.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Fabius, a veteran of Legio XX, for himself and his wife, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04201886.translation: The bones of Salvius Sempronius, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe, of the Eleventh Legion, who fought at Actium; Licinia, daughter of Lucius, made this.
EDCS-04201886.summary: This tombstone commemorates Salvius Sempronius, a soldier of Legio XI who participated in the Battle of Actium, and was set up by Licinia.

EDCS-04201888.translation: To Lucius Valerius Priscus Viennensis, prefect of the II cohort of the Third Thracian and of the Second Equitum, tribune of the Tenth Fretensis legion, prefect of the Flavian ala, prefect of engineers, a burial place was publicly granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04201888.summary: A funerary inscription detailing the distinguished military and engineering career of Lucius Valerius Priscus Viennensis, who was granted a burial plot by decree.

EDCS-04201890.translation: Caius Acilius Severus, freedman of Caius, and his wife Conc(ordia), by testament ordered this to be made for himself and for Acilia Secunda, freedwoman of Caius, his mother, and for Donata, freedwoman of Lucius and a woman.
EDCS-04201890.summary: A funerary inscription funded by testament, for the dedicator Caius Acilius Severus, his wife, his mother, and another woman named Donata.

EDCS-04201891.translation: Lucius Aelius Macer, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, a member of the board of six, made this for himself while alive, and for his partner Lucius Aelius Antigonus, freedman, and for his friend Publius Saltius Mysticus and Saltia Euthycia; this monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-04201891.summary: This epitaph, likely from the early imperial period, records Lucius Aelius Macer, a decurio, setting up a monument for himself, his freedman partner, and a friend, stipulating it is not heritable.

EDCS-04201892.translation: Caius Albarenius, son of Caius, Marcus Pomponius Pisander (?), son of Quintus, [3]onius, son of Lucius, Tullus, Caius Pomponius Scapula, son of Lucius, were appointed [or acted as] overseers for the construction of the bridge by decree of the decurions and approved it.
EDCS-04201892.summary: This inscription records officials, possibly surveyors or overseers, appointed by the decurions to contract and approve the construction of a bridge, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201893.translation: ... and prefect for administering justice. Agathangelus, freedman of Aulus, son of Aulus, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201893.summary: This fragmented inscription records Agathangelus, a freedman and formerly prefect for administering justice, setting up a monument for himself while alive, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201894.translation: Lucius Arrius, son of Titus, a sexvir, ordered this to be made by testament for Opitergus and his family.
EDCS-04201894.summary: This inscription states that Lucius Arrius, a member of the board of six, willed this monument to be built for Opitergus and his family, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201895.translation: [To the spirits of] Quintus Asconius Labeo, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, a pontiff; he lived 15 years.
EDCS-04201895.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription commemorates Quintus Asconius Labeo, a young pontiff of the Fabia tribe who died at the age of 15, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201896.text_edition: \n Caio Avilio filio Fabia Vindici praefecto iure dicundo viro Caedia Publi filia Sabina\n
EDCS-04201896.translation: To Caius Avilius Vindicus, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, prefect for administering justice, husband of Caedia Sabina, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04201896.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Caius Avilius Vindicus, a prefect for administering justice, and his wife Caedia Sabina, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201897.translation: Titus Aurelius Florentinus, of the Palatina tribe, decurio and quaestor of the guild of craftsmen.
EDCS-04201897.summary: This inscription records the titles of Titus Aurelius Florentinus, a decurio and quaestor of the guild of craftsmen, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04201898.translation: Quintus Braetius Salius, son of Manius, of the Fabian tribe, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201898.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Quintus Braetius Salius for himself and his family through his will.

EDCS-04201900.translation: Publius Caelius Liccaeus, freedman of Publius, a member of the college of IIIIvir, [dedicated this] for his concubine Iunia Faustae, freedwoman of Caius, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201900.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Caelius Liccaeus, a magistrate, and his concubine Iunia Faustae, commissioned for themselves and their families.

EDCS-04201902.translation: To Quintus Camerius Culleo, son of Quintus, pontiff.
EDCS-04201902.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Camerius Culleo, a pontiff, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-04201903.translation: The prefects consulted Lucius Canius Festus, Caius Aufidius Candidus, Caius Avilius Stabilis, son of Quintus, Decimus Cervius Stabilis, and the decurions on the VI Nones of May in the curia. Lucius Laelius Stulio, Quintus Satrius Asconius Pastor, Quintus Stenius Augurinus, Caius Curtius Strabo, and Caius Acilius Rufus were present for the writing. Because the prefects spoke regarding Lucius Perpetus Amiantus, the position of the pillar-makers outside the Roman gate was requested to be put up for auction for 160 [sestertii?] for three years without injustice.
EDCS-04201903.summary: This inscription records a decision made by prefects and decurions on May 2nd regarding the auction of a position for pillar-makers outside the Roman gate, dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04201905.translation: To Publius Cervonius Cervolus, son of Publius, prefect with judicial authority, a man worthy of Cassia [---].
EDCS-04201905.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Cervonius Cervolus, a prefect with judicial authority, likely on a monument honouring him.

EDCS-04201906.translation: Quintus Cervonius Simplex, son of Caius, prefect with judicial authority, [dedicated this] to his mother, Victoria, daughter of Caius. Cervonius.
EDCS-04201906.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Quintus Cervonius Simplex, a prefect, to his mother Victoria.

EDCS-04201907.translation: Publius Flavius Stabilis, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe, who was admitted as a decurion, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, for his son Publius Flavius Festus, also admitted as a decurion, and for his wife Ennia Tertia.
EDCS-04201907.summary: This funerary inscription was commissioned by Publius Flavius Stabilis for himself, his son, and his wife, indicating the father and son held the rank of decurion.

EDCS-04201908.text_edition: \n Quintus Gellius praefectus fabrum curator aerarii statuas I et in tui[tionem ------ O L NO fieri ERO \n
EDCS-04201908.translation: Quintus Gellius, prefect of the engineers, curator of the treasury, ordered statues and [something] for their protection.
EDCS-04201908.summary: This inscription records Quintus Gellius, a prefect of engineers and treasury curator, commissioning statues and their protection, likely a public commission.

EDCS-04201910.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio filio Fabia Marcellino IIIIvi[ro ------\n
EDCS-04201910.translation: To Caius Iulius Marcellinus, son of Caius, a member of the college of IIIIvir.
EDCS-04201910.summary: This is a dedication to Caius Iulius Marcellinus, a magistrate, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-04201911.translation: Marcus Iunius Sabinus, a IIIIvir with aedilic power under the Julian municipal law, patron of the guild of torchbearers, adorned the front of the temple with marble bulls and herms at his own expense and provided for its upkeep, at the cost of 2240 sesterces. Natalis 242.
EDCS-04201911.summary: This inscription records Marcus Iunius Sabinus, a magistrate and patron, who funded the decoration of a temple with marble sculptures and its maintenance, likely during the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04201912.translation: Halys, freedman of Titus Livius Quartus, of cordial disposition, from Patavium, made this while alive for himself and all his family.
EDCS-04201912.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by a freedman named Halys for himself and his family, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201913.translation: If anyone leaves fewer possessions, let the children seek them for themselves. Farewell, traveler, you are at the springs, a mile away. Quintus Marcius, son of Publius, of the Sergia tribe, Rex.
EDCS-04201913.summary: An epitaph for Quintus Marcius Rex, likely marking a roadside tomb or a place near springs, indicating proximity to a town or settlement.

EDCS-04201915.translation: To Publius Mulvius Frontonus(?), who served as praefect with judicial authority and as prefect of the artisans, Publius Allonius(?)...
EDCS-04201915.summary: This is the beginning of a dedication to Publius Mulvius Frontonus, who held significant administrative and military positions, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04201916.translation: Sextus Navinius Apollonius, freedman of Sextus, of cordial disposition, for himself and his family, with 36 feet in front and 20 feet in the back.
EDCS-04201916.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating the dimensions of a plot of land allocated by Sextus Navinius Apollonius for his family, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201917.translation: Marcus Petronius Primulus, a member of the college of six priests and Augustalis, made this while alive for himself, for his wife Petronia, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04201917.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Petronius Primulus, an Augustalis priest, and his family, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201919.translation: Lucius Terentius Acutus, Augustalis of cordial disposition, made this while alive for himself and his family, including his son Lucius Terentius Optatus (of cordial disposition), his freedwoman wife Terentia Saturnina, his freedman Lucanus, and his freedwoman Pudentia.
EDCS-04201919.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Terentius Acutus, an Augustalis, and his family, including his son and freedmen/freedwomen, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201920.translation: In the amount of 300... To Gaius Terentius Caetronianus, son of Titus, of the Fabian tribe, a magistrate with judicial authority, who lived 80 years, 2 months, and 2 days. His sons, Sabinianus and Lucius Valerianus, erected this to their excellent father.
EDCS-04201920.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by two sons for their father, Gaius Terentius Caetronianus, who was a magistrate, with details of his lifespan, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201921.translation: Titus Turranius Euanthus, freedman of Gaius, of cordial disposition, made this while alive for Titus Turranius Pantagathus and for his excellent freedman Gaius Turranius Eutyches.
EDCS-04201921.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by a freedman named Euanthus for himself and two other individuals, possibly relatives or patrons, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201922.translation: Marcus Varronius Stephanus, VIvir Augustalis of Concord.
EDCS-04201922.summary: A simple inscription identifying Marcus Varronius Stephanus as a member of the college of VIviri Augustales, a municipal priesthood, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04201923.translation: Gaius Vennonius Primus, freedman of Gaius, a member of the college of six priests; Petronia Marcella, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04201923.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vennonius Primus, a priest, and Petronia Marcella, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201928.translation: Lucius Crimilius Hila[---], Lucius Annius, freedman of Lucius [---], Crimilia, freedwoman of Lucius [---] Cri[---], Crimilia, freedwoman of Lucius Phile[---]. Ravenas Philenaa, Sarci() Nav Lemmo, CR Aureli.
EDCS-04201928.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to list several names, possibly related to funerary arrangements or family relations, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201929.translation: Of Timothy the Greek, freedman of Marcus Arrius Zethus, the chief attendant. VI made this. Of Doctor Bassanus.
EDCS-04201929.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription mentioning individuals with Greek names and roles like 'chief attendant' and 'doctor', dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04201930.translation: To Prutius Petronius Aelius, administrator, whom Livia Quarta, daughter of Titus, [left in her will].
EDCS-04201930.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication by Livia Quarta to her administrator, Prutius Petronius Aelius, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-04201932.translation: Plot 256. For Caius Sepullius Onesimus, workshop owner. Burial place of Marcus C. P. In width 21 feet, depth 36 feet.
EDCS-04201932.summary: This is a funerary land division record specifying the dimensions and owner of a burial plot.

EDCS-04201934.translation: Acilia Basio, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and for Titus Cartorius Scirtus, her husband.
EDCS-04201934.summary: This is an epitaph dedicating a burial place to Acilia Basio and her husband, Titus Cartorius Scirtus.

EDCS-04201935.translation: Titus Aebius, son of Caius, ordered this to be made by his will. In width 45 feet, depth 30 feet.
EDCS-04201935.summary: This inscription, likely on a tomb, records the dimensions of a plot dedicated by Titus Aebius in his will.

EDCS-04201936.translation: To Titus Aelius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-04201936.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Aelius, son of Quintus, identifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04201937.translation: Aelia Gnome, freedwoman of Publius, and Publius Aelius Narcissus, freedman of a woman, set this up while alive.
EDCS-04201937.summary: A funerary monument erected by Aelia Gnome and Publius Aelius Narcissus, likely a couple, who set it up during their lifetime.

EDCS-04201938.translation: Publius Aemilius Deodorus, freedman of Publius, for himself and his family. In width 10 feet, depth 12 feet.
EDCS-04201938.summary: This funerary inscription allocates a burial plot of specified dimensions for Publius Aemilius Deodorus and his family.

EDCS-04201939.translation: Ameryllis, freedwoman of Aletia, made this for herself and her family while alive.
EDCS-04201939.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for herself and her family.

EDCS-04201940.translation: [For] his wife, for Marcus Allius Festus, son of Marcus, for his son, for Hostilia Severa, freedwoman of Caius: 'I was not, I am not, I do not care'.
EDCS-04201940.summary: This epitaph dedicates a tomb to a wife, son, and freedwoman, concluding with a common funerary epigram expressing indifference to life and death.

EDCS-04201941.translation: Tiberius Annius Dardanus, freedman of Tiberius. // Tiberius Annius Dardanus, freedman of Tiberius.
EDCS-04201941.summary: This inscription, possibly on a tomb or marker, records the name of Tiberius Annius Dardanus, freedman of Tiberius, repeated on both sides.

EDCS-04201942.translation: Antonia, daughter of Caius, wife; Terentia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04201942.summary: This inscription lists two women, Antonia, wife and daughter of Caius, and Terentia, daughter of Publius, likely related to a funerary monument.

EDCS-04201943.translation: To the departed spirits. Aprilia Priscilla, while alive, placed this for her perpetual security. E. F. N.
EDCS-04201943.summary: This is a funerary epitaph placed by Aprilia Priscilla during her lifetime for her eternal security, likely invoking deities or concepts represented by E.F.N.

EDCS-04201944.translation: Gaius Apronius Thyrsus made this while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04201944.summary: This inscription records a private funerary monument made by Gaius Apronius Thyrsus for his family.

EDCS-04201945.translation: Titus Arbenius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201945.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Titus Arbenius through his will.

EDCS-04201946.translation: Asconia Sabina made this while alive for herself and her well-deserving husband, Marcus Valerius Celadus.
EDCS-04201946.summary: This inscription records a private funerary monument made by Asconia Sabina for herself and her husband.

EDCS-04201947.translation: Atilia... while alive... for Quintus Coelius... Atilia... the place in front... in the field...
EDCS-04201947.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record the allocation of funerary plots, possibly for Quintus Coelius and Atilia.

EDCS-04201948.translation: Publius Avilius, son of Publius, and Philodamus, and his wife Caesonia Aptae, made this while alive.
EDCS-04201948.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument made by Publius Avilius and Philodamus for themselves and their wives.

EDCS-04201949.translation: Made while alive by Manius Autonius, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe; 20 feet in front, 30 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04201949.summary: This inscription records a private funerary plot designated by Manius Autonius, indicating its dimensions.

EDCS-04201950.translation: To the divine shades. For Lucius Axios Charistus, friend, brother, comrade, who lived 21 years and 54 days, and also for his parents, Lucius Axios Crescens, and Axia Tyche, and for their descendants, by Marcus Calvisius Claudius Victor for his well-deserving friends.
EDCS-04201950.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lucius Axios Charistus, his parents, and descendants, set up by his friend Marcus Calvisius Claudius Victor.

EDCS-04201952.translation: Marcus Baebius Maturus, son of Quintus, placed this while alive for himself and his family: 38.5 feet in front and 50 feet behind.
EDCS-04201952.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary plot purchased by Marcus Baebius Maturus for his family.

EDCS-04201953.translation: Birrius, son of Voltiomnus, Sumbica, Ostiala, Birria Frema(?), Birria Quarta, Birria Tertia, daughter of Voltiomnus, ordered to be made by her will.
EDCS-04201953.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument that Birria Tertia ordered to be made by her will, likely for family members including Birrius and others named.

EDCS-04201954.translation: Caius Brigenius Clementis, son of Caius, and Coelia, wife of Euchinus, gave the place to Salvius Nigellus and Salvia Iucunda.
EDCS-04201954.summary: This inscription records the donation of a burial plot by Caius Brigenius Clementis and his wife Coelia Euchini to Salvius Nigellus and Salvia Iucunda.

EDCS-04201955.translation: Lucius Caedius Eros, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for his freedman Hilarius and his freedman Ac[---]...
EDCS-04201955.summary: This is a fragmented inscription for a funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Caedius Eros for himself and his freedmen.

EDCS-04201956.translation: Mutteia Hospita, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for herself and her family, and for Marcus Appuleius Scenon.
EDCS-04201956.summary: This is a funerary epigram recording a woman, Mutteia Hospita, who commissioned her own tomb and that of Marcus Appuleius Scenon.

EDCS-04201957.translation: This was made by Caius Cesidius Hermerotis and Cesidia Hora, his freedwoman and wife.
EDCS-04201957.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb commissioned by Caius Cesidius Hermerotis for himself, his freedwoman and wife Cesidia Hora.

EDCS-04201958.translation: This was made by a woman for herself and her family, and for her husband Lucius Caetronius Anderoudus, freedman of Lucius, and for her son Lucius Caetronius Firmus, son of Lucius, and for her daughter Caetronia Prima, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04201958.summary: This funerary epigram records a tomb commissioned by a woman for herself, her husband Lucius Caetronius Anderoudus, and their children Lucius Caetronius Firmus and Caetronia Prima.

EDCS-04201959.translation: Quintus Carminius Tertius ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Quintus Carminius, son of Quintus, and for his wife Clodia Festa, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-04201959.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb commissioned by will by Quintus Carminius Tertius for himself, his son Quintus Carminius, and his wife Clodia Festa.

EDCS-04201960.translation: Carminius Felicissimus made this while alive for his most chaste wife Bononiana Apices, in front 20 feet.
EDCS-04201960.summary: This funerary epigram records a tomb commissioned by Carminius Felicissimus for his wife Bononiana Apices, specifying a width of 20 feet.

EDCS-04201961.translation: Fulvia Tis, freedwoman of Quintus, made this while alive for Quintus Cartilius Optatus, freedman of Quintus, and for herself and her family.
EDCS-04201961.summary: This funerary epigram records a tomb commissioned by Fulvia Tis for herself, her family, and Quintus Cartilius Optatus.

EDCS-04201962.translation: Lucius Cartorius, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, is buried here; this plot extends 20 feet in front and 25 feet inwards from the middle ditch; I dedicate and bequeath this plot and monument to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04201962.summary: This is a property deed and funerary inscription recording the dimensions of a burial plot and its dedication to the Manes by Lucius Cartorius.

EDCS-04201963.translation: Cartorius made this while alive for himself and his family, for Tiberius Cartorius Anterus, freedman of Tiberius, and for Cartoria Aptae.
EDCS-04201963.summary: This funerary epigram records a tomb commissioned by Cartorius for himself, his family, Tiberius Cartorius Anterus, and Cartoria Aptae.

EDCS-04201964.translation: Titus Cassius and Lucius Domitius, freedmen of Lucius, placed this for Pamphilius.
EDCS-04201964.summary: This epitaph records the dedication of a monument by two freedmen for an individual named Pamphilius.

EDCS-04201965.translation: Caius Cassius Macula, son of Quintus, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04201965.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb commissioned by will by Caius Cassius Macula.

EDCS-04201966.translation: Cassia Cia, freedwoman of Titus, made this while alive for herself and for her patron Titus Cassius Faustus, son of Titus.
EDCS-04201966.summary: This funerary epigram records a tomb commissioned by Cassia Cia for herself and her patron Titus Cassius Faustus.

EDCS-04201967.translation: Titus Castrucius, son of Caius, and Opsidia, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-04201967.summary: This inscription names a married couple, Titus Castrucius and Opsidia.

EDCS-04201968.translation: Quintus Catius, son of Quintus, tribune(?) for himself [...]
EDCS-04201968.summary: This inscription begins the naming of Quintus Catius, likely a military officer, and indicates he is dedicating something for himself.

EDCS-04201970.translation: Catia Prima, daughter of Caius, made this for herself and for her husband Quintus Sicinius, son of Manius, while she was alive; this place and monument will not pass to an heir. In front 20 feet, behind 20 feet.
EDCS-04201970.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Catia Prima for herself and her husband, specifying its dimensions and indicating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-04201971.translation: Publius Causonius and Pupitimus made this while alive for themselves, and for Evionnterus, Vilona(?), and Publius Cano.
EDCS-04201971.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument made for several individuals, possibly a family group, by Publius Causonius and Pupitimus.

EDCS-04201972.translation: Of Quintus Cercenius Hermerotis. In front 20 feet, behind 70 feet.
EDCS-04201972.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot belonging to Quintus Cercenius Hermerotis.

EDCS-04201973.translation: Burial place of Fuscus, freedman of Gaius Cervenius, and a woman. In front 20 feet, behind 30 feet.
EDCS-04201973.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot for a freedman named Fuscus and a woman associated with Gaius Cervenius, detailing its dimensions.

EDCS-04201974.summary: This very fragmentary inscription names a person named Cervonius Pudnes.

EDCS-04201975.translation: Cipia Secunda, daughter of Publius, ordered this to be made; the plot in front 20 feet, into the ground 25 feet.
EDCS-04201975.summary: This funerary monument was ordered by Cipia Secunda, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04201976.translation: Quintus Clodius Maro, freedman of Quintus. Quintus Clodius, son of Quintus. His wife Trebia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, placed (this).
EDCS-04201976.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Quintus Clodius Maro and Quintus Clodius, and identifies Trebia Secunda as the wife of one of them.

EDCS-04201977.translation: Marcus Cocceius Ianuarius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04201977.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Cocceius Ianuarius, a freedman.

EDCS-04201978.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Claudia Toreuma, freedwoman of Tiberius Augustus, aged 19. 'I myself am buried in the earth before having reached twice ten years of age; Toreuma, known for her many jests, escaped the crime of a long old age with a short span of life happily lived.'
EDCS-04201978.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudia Toreuma, a 19-year-old freedwoman of Tiberius Augustus, including a poetic lament on her early death.

EDCS-04201979.translation: To Clodia Fortu, freedwoman of Caius, Restita.
EDCS-04201979.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Clodia Fortu, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04201980.translation: Claudia Prima, freedwoman of Manius, erected this for her patron Manius Clodius, freedman of Manius, and for her son Nero, son of Manius Clodius, freedman of Manius, during her lifetime.
EDCS-04201980.summary: A tombstone erected by a freedwoman for her patron and her son.

EDCS-04201981.translation: To the divine shades. Thaidis, wife of Clodius, lived 18 years and 16 days. Marcus Clodius Ianuarius erected this for himself and for his deserving freedmen while alive.
EDCS-04201981.summary: A tombstone for a deceased woman and a dedication by a man for himself and his freedmen.

EDCS-04201982.translation: Aulus Coelius, son of Caius, to the departed spirits, for himself forever, garden plot XV.
EDCS-04201982.summary: This inscription records a land purchase or dedication by Aulus Coelius for funerary purposes, specifying the size of the garden plot.

EDCS-04201983.translation: For Coelia Gemella, daughter of Gaius. Aulus Coelius Optatus, freedman of Aulus, erected this at his own expense. In the front 20 feet, in the back 20 feet.
EDCS-04201983.summary: A funerary dedication for Coelia Gemella, with dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04201984.translation: Lucius Cosius Donatus erected this while alive for himself and for Cosia Erotice, his dearest wife; for his friend Caius Clodius Metrodorus and his wife Clodiae Fortunata; for his friend Titus Varius Verecundus and his wife Varia Iusta; for his female friend Asconia Amabilis; for his female friend Asconia Flora; for Aulus Plotio P<hr=RH>onimus, Plotia Severa, and his freedman Diadumenus. In the front 44 feet, in the back 60 feet.
EDCS-04201984.summary: A large funerary monument erected by Lucius Cosius Donatus for multiple family members, friends, and freedmen, with plot dimensions.

EDCS-04201985.translation: Burial place for Crimilia Verecunda, freedwoman. 12.5 feet in the front, 22.5 feet in the back.
EDCS-04201985.summary: A marker for a burial plot belonging to Crimilia Verecunda, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-04201986.translation: Erected by [---] for Lucius Cusinius Quadratus, his fellow freedman.
EDCS-04201986.summary: A tombstone dedicated by a fellow freedman to Lucius Cusinius Quadratus.

EDCS-04201987.summary: A simple funerary inscription naming Gaius Domitius Firmus.

EDCS-04201988.translation: [...] Domitius / [...] Scaeva, of the Fabia tribe / [...]vonia, freedwoman of a woman / Pi[...] / [... Do]mitius
EDCS-04201988.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph mentioning several individuals, likely family members, with some names being of freedmen.

EDCS-04201989.translation: Gaius Domitius Severus, son of Marcus, [---]
EDCS-04201989.summary: A partial funerary inscription for Gaius Domitius Severus.

EDCS-04201990.translation: For the good memory of Domitia Atiliana, his dearest wife, who lived 47 years, 8 months, and 12 days. Flavius Laetus placed this [---] for himself, number 428.
EDCS-04201990.summary: A funerary inscription for a wife and a dedication by her husband, including a reference number.

EDCS-04201991.translation: Domitia Proba, freedwoman, erected this burial place, which will not follow an heir, for herself, for her sister Domitia Thallusa, a freedwoman, and for her sister's son Aethon, during her lifetime.
EDCS-04201991.summary: A tombstone erected by a freedwoman for herself, her sister, and her nephew, with a clause about inheritance.

EDCS-04201992.translation: Gaius Ennius Licinius, son of Gaius, made this while alive for himself, and for his father, his freedman Antiochus, and for his mother, Vettia Prisca, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04201992.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Ennius Licinius for himself and his parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201993.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Ennius Marcellinus, son of Titus. Titus Ennius Marcellinus [set this up].
EDCS-04201993.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ennius Marcellinus, set up by his father, Titus Ennius Marcellinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201994.translation: Manius Ennius Rufus, son of Publius, made this in honor of his freedmen Galenius Pisidas and Nysa.
EDCS-04201994.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Manius Ennius Rufus to honor his freedmen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201995.translation: Ettia Prima, daughter of Gaius, made this while alive for herself and for Gaius Sepullius Maturus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04201995.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Ettia Prima for herself and her companion, Gaius Sepullius Maturus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201996.translation: Fabia Quincta, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive for her father Lucius Fabius, son of Gaius, and for her mother Fabia Helena, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04201996.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fabia Quincta for her parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201997.translation: Fabia Quarta, freedwoman of Gaius, made this while alive for her patron and husband, Gaius Fabius Chrestus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-04201997.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fabia Quarta for her husband and patron, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201998.translation: For Gaius Fannius Felix, freedman of Gaius. Gaius Fannius Auctus, freedman of Gaius, and Fannia, freedwoman of Gaius, [set this up].
EDCS-04201998.summary: This is a funerary epitaph likely set up by Gaius Fannius Auctus and Fannia for their patron Gaius Fannius Felix, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04201999.translation: For himself and his family, and for his fellow freedmen Gidius and Fau[---].
EDCS-04201999.summary: This is a fragment of an epitaph for an individual and their fellow freedmen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202001.translation: To Marcus Firmicius, son of Marcus, Faus...
EDCS-04202001.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a funerary dedication, for Marcus Firmicius.

EDCS-04202002.translation: To Florus, of the Caecilia family.
EDCS-04202002.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Florus, a member of the Caecilia family.

EDCS-04202003.translation: Fortunatus and Priata set up this monument for their daughter and foster-child Velagia Ingenua, [asking] if they had not borne children by a better fate, they would not have suddenly buried the poor things in perpetual sorrow.
EDCS-04202003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph expressing grief over the death of a daughter, likely set up by her parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202004.translation: Burial place of Gaius Fulvius Dionysus. In front: 30 feet; in depth: 30 feet.
EDCS-04202004.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Gaius Fulvius Dionysus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202007.translation: To Gaius Gavius Iucundus, freedman of Gaius, his comrade, and to himself, Octavia Methe, while alive, made this. In front 12 feet, in the field 12 feet.
EDCS-04202007.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Octavia Methe for her comrade Gaius Gavius Iucundus, also for herself.

EDCS-04202008.summary: A very brief epitaph, likely for Gavia Maxima, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04202009.translation: To Hateria Felicitas, aged 33. Her mother Hateria Iustina and her husband Titus Flavius Hyginus placed this.
EDCS-04202009.summary: A funerary epitaph for Hateria Felicitas, set up by her mother and husband, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202010.translation: Helvia Prima, daughter of Gaius, ordered this to be made by her will for herself and for Gaius Helvius Communis, freedman of the woman, for Helvia Selenimia, freedwoman of the woman, for Coelia Clidis, freedwoman of the woman, for their descendants, freedmen and freedwomen. In front 20 feet, to the rear 20 feet.
EDCS-04202010.summary: A funerary epitaph ordered by will by Helvia Prima for herself and a number of relatives and freedpersons, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202011.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Herodiano, most beloved and most innocent son, who lived 4 years, 10 months, 24 days. Glycerius and Vera, parents, made this.
EDCS-04202011.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy named Herodiano, set up by his parents Glycerius and Vera.

EDCS-04202012.translation: To Horatia Donata: 20 feet in front and 46 feet behind.
EDCS-04202012.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a funerary plot dedicated to Horatia Donata.

EDCS-04202013.translation: Quintus Hostilius Eros, freedman of Quintus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and his family.
EDCS-04202013.summary: A funerary epitaph ordered by will by Quintus Hostilius Eros for himself and his family.

EDCS-04202014.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Sara dedicated this to Isellia Rena.
EDCS-04202014.summary: A funerary dedication by Sara to Isellia Rena.

EDCS-04202015.translation: [---] to Iucunda. Papus, freedman, [set this up] for his patron and fellow freedmen and for himself and for Culcia [---]reni.
EDCS-04202015.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iucunda, set up by Papus, possibly for himself, his patron, and other freedpersons.

EDCS-04202016.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Julia Valentine. Julius Valentius and Domitius Lupus set this up for their most dutiful mother.
EDCS-04202016.summary: A funerary epitaph for Julia Valentine, set up by her sons Julius Valentius and Domitius Lupus.

EDCS-04202017.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Titus Labienus Patavinus, his father. His daughter Eutychia set this up for him deserving well, for her freedmen and freedwomen and for her descendants.
EDCS-04202017.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Labienus Patavinus, set up by his daughter Eutychia for him, her freedpersons, and descendants.

EDCS-04202018.translation: For Manius Laelius, son of Quintus, of the Fabian tribe. The heirs willingly made this.
EDCS-04202018.summary: A funerary epitaph for Manius Laelius, set up by his heirs.

EDCS-04202019.translation: Manius Laeponius Surus, freedman of a woman, made this (monument) for himself and for Laeponia Attilla, freedwoman of Surus, and for his son Laeponius, while alive.
EDCS-04202019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely for a family tomb, set up by Manius Laeponius Surus for himself, his freedwoman wife, and their son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202020.translation: [---] Fabia Largus, one of the four chief magistrates, Severa, daughter of Lucius, daughter of Lucius, (dedicate this) to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04202020.summary: This fragmentary epitaph likely records the dedication of a tomb or monument to the 'Di Manes' (departed spirits) by officials, possibly relating to a magistrate and his family, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202021.translation: Gaius Lemonius Mollo, son of Gaius, and his wife Fremantio.
EDCS-04202021.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording Gaius Lemonius Mollo and his wife Fremantio, likely indicating a shared burial plot or monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202022.translation: Titus Livius Priscus, son of Titus, son of Gaius, and Titus Longus, son of Titus, son of Gaius, and his wife Prima, daughter of Sextus Cassius, (made this) for themselves and their family.
EDCS-04202022.summary: This funerary inscription records Titus Livius Priscus and Titus Livius Longus, likely brothers and sons of Titus Livius, and their mother Prima, establishing a family burial monument during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202023.translation: Titus Livius Optatus, freedman of Titus, aged 15.
EDCS-04202023.summary: An epitaph for Titus Livius Optatus, a 15-year-old freedman.

EDCS-04202024.translation: Lollianus set this up for his deserving wife, to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04202024.summary: This funerary epitaph records Lollianus dedicating a monument to his well-deserving wife, for the departed spirits, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202025.translation: Publius Lollius [---] set this up for himself and [---] while alive. In width, 15 feet; in depth.
EDCS-04202025.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Publius Lollius, indicating a tomb was constructed by him for himself and others while alive, specifying the dimensions of the plot (15 feet wide), from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202026.translation: Secundus and Homullus made this for their patron Quintus Lollius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, and for his wife Plotia, daughter of Publius, and for themselves and their families.
EDCS-04202026.summary: This funerary inscription records Secundus and Homullus commissioning a monument for their patron Quintus Lollius, his wife Plotia, and for themselves and their descendants, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202027.translation: Gaius Lucilius, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, (dedicated this) for his family and its descendants, 20 feet in width, across.
EDCS-04202027.summary: This inscription records Gaius Lucilius dedicating a plot of land or a monument of 20 feet width for his family and descendants, possibly a burial space, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202028.translation: Gaius Lucretius, son of Lucius, made this for himself and his family while alive. In width, 15 feet; in depth, 18 feet.
EDCS-04202028.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Gaius Lucretius, specifying that he constructed his family tomb for himself and his relatives while alive, with dimensions of 15 feet wide and 18 feet deep, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202029.translation: Gaius Luscius Quadratus made this for himself and for his wife Instesia Maxima and for his sons while alive. // Lucius Luscius Valens lies here, aged 19 years, 2 months, and 13 days. // Luscia Quadratilla lies here, aged 25 years, 9 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-04202029.summary: This inscription records Gaius Luscius Quadratus building a family tomb while alive, with subsequent burials of his son Lucius Luscius Valens and daughter Luscia Quadratilla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202030.translation: To the shades of the departed. Valgia Thallusa made this for her well-deserving husband, Lucius Maclo[---] Fortunatus.
EDCS-04202030.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife to her husband, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202031.translation: To the shades of the departed. Gaius Magius Ursinus made this for himself alive. Clodia Marcella granted this place for his most devoted daughter, Magia Valentina, who died at the age of seven years, two months, and four days.
EDCS-04202031.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl, set up by her father, with the plot granted by another individual, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202032.summary: A dedication to two individuals, possibly indicating a shared tomb or monument, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202033.translation: Gaius Manlius Priamus, freedman of Gibba, always sought [---] and did not cease to destroy [---].
EDCS-04202033.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly a curse or epitaph, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-04202034.translation: To Titus Manlius Quintus and Vetuliena Pelagia.
EDCS-04202034.summary: A dedication to Titus Manlius Quintus and Vetuliena Pelagia, likely on a tomb or public monument.

EDCS-04202035.translation: Burial place of Quintus Mantonius Mercator and Gaius Mantonius Gemellus. In front 30 feet, to the rear 29 feet.
EDCS-04202035.summary: A property marker for a burial plot belonging to two individuals, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202036.translation: Titus Ponenus Marcellus, son of Marcus, for his father S[---]dia and [---]VIII.
EDCS-04202036.summary: A funerary inscription fragment for a father, set up by his son, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202037.translation: Burial place of Marcia Festa. In front 32 feet, to the rear 30 feet.
EDCS-04202037.summary: A property marker for a burial plot belonging to Marcia Festa, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202038.summary: An ownership inscription or designation of property, possibly related to a tomb, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202039.translation: Burial place of Gaius Memmius Libanus and Publius Memmius Trophimus. In front 21 feet, to the rear 30 feet.
EDCS-04202039.summary: A property marker for a burial plot belonging to two individuals, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202041.translation: Minia Cila, freedwoman of the mulier [Minia], made this for herself and for her mother Epinice, freedwoman of Manius Quintus Laeponius. Burial place in front 30 feet.
EDCS-04202041.summary: A funerary monument set up by a freedwoman for herself and her mother, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202042.translation: To Manius Moenius, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04202042.summary: This is an epitaph for Manius Moenius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04202043.translation: To Gaius Mucius, son of Quintus, and Arruntia, daughter of Titus, and Muciae, daughter of Caius, and Muciae, daughter of Caius, Pro[...]; this monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-04202043.summary: This epitaph records the intended non-hereditary status of a monument for several individuals, including Gaius Mucius, Arruntia, and two Muciae.

EDCS-04202044.translation: To Quintus Murtius Aphrodisius. Lucius Domitius Hermes [erected it].
EDCS-04202044.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Murtius Aphrodisius, likely erected by Lucius Domitius Hermes.

EDCS-04202045.translation: Quintus Mustius Eusebes made this while alive for himself, for his wife Caetronia Procula, for his stepson Saufeius Nigrinus, and for their descendants, on private land, 30 feet in frontage and 30 feet in depth.
EDCS-04202045.summary: This is an epitaph for Quintus Mustius Eusebes, who established a burial plot for himself, his wife, stepson, and descendants on private land.

EDCS-04202046.translation: Muttiena Sige, freedwoman of Lucius Mu(lvius?) Titus and of the woman, ordered this to be made by will for herself and for Lucius Mulvius Urbanus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04202046.summary: This inscription states that Muttiena Sige, a freedwoman, established funerary arrangements for herself and Lucius Mulvius Urbanus by her will.

EDCS-04202047.translation: Quintus Octavius Athictus made this while alive. His wife Afronia Festa [dedicated it] to her husband. His sons Quintus Octavius Priscianus and Quintus Octavius Laberianus placed [it].
EDCS-04202047.summary: This epitaph records a tomb set up by Afronia Festa for her husband Quintus Octavius Athictus, and later additions by their sons.

EDCS-04202048.translation: Ofilia, daughter of Lucius, a married woman, made this for herself and for her excellent husband, Quintus Granius.
EDCS-04202048.summary: A funerary dedication by Ofilia for herself and her husband Quintus Granius, specifying her marital status.

EDCS-04202049.translation: Caius Oppius, son of Caius, [erected this] for his father Caius Oppius, his mother Rutilia Prima, and his wife Cassia Secunda, daughter of Lucius. Publius Oppius Pollio, son of Caius, brother, saw to its construction.
EDCS-04202049.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument established by will by Caius Oppius for his parents and wife, and overseen by his brother Publius Oppius Pollio.

EDCS-04202050.translation: Parcilia, daughter of Marcus Oxonius, made this while alive for herself and her family.
EDCS-04202050.summary: This is an epitaph for Parcilia, daughter of Marcus Oxonius, who established a burial space for herself and her family.

EDCS-04202051.translation: Perpernia Favor, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive for herself and for Lucius Perperna Philo and his family.
EDCS-04202051.summary: This inscription records that Perpernia Favor, a freedwoman, established a burial space for herself and Lucius Perperna Philo and his family.

EDCS-04202052.translation: Caius Petilius Anteros, freedman of Caius, ordered this to be made by will for himself and for Petilia Staphis, freedwoman of Caius, [and her] freedman.
EDCS-04202052.summary: This inscription indicates that Caius Petilius Anteros established a funerary monument by will for himself and Petilia Staphis.

EDCS-04202053.summary: A very brief inscription, likely an owner's name on a monument or property.

EDCS-04202054.translation: For Titus Petronius, son of Titus, and for himself, and for his son Publius Petronius; and for himself, and for his brother Quintus Curiatius Celer, son of Lucius, and for his sister Muccia Rufa, daughter of Lucius. Burial place in front 24 feet, to the rear 50 feet.
EDCS-04202054.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the burial plot allocated by Publius Petronius for himself and his family members, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-04202055.translation: To Petronia Grata, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-04202055.summary: A dedication to Petronia Grata, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04202056.translation: Musa, freedwoman of a woman, dedicated this while alive for herself, 28 feet in front, 46 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202056.summary: A funerary dedication by Musa for herself, specifying land dimensions.

EDCS-04202058.translation: To the departed spirits. Philumenus to his most loving wife Aemilia Marcianena, daughter of Celer.
EDCS-04202058.summary: A funerary dedication from Philumenus to his beloved wife, Aemilia Marcianena.

EDCS-04202060.summary: A very brief inscription, likely a self-dedication or ownership mark by Quintus Plo.

EDCS-04202061.translation: To the departed spirits. To Publius Pompeius Firmus, most unfortunate, whom the sea took with its waves. Julia Olympia placed this for her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-04202061.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Pompeius Firmus, who died at sea, dedicated by his wife Julia Olympia.

EDCS-04202062.translation: Gaius Pompeius Lepidus, son of Gaius, freedman, ordered this to be made for himself and for Pompeia Prima, freedwoman of Gaius, by his will.
EDCS-04202062.summary: A tomb inscription indicating that Gaius Pompeius Lepidus, a freedman, arranged for this monument to be built for himself and his freedwoman Pompeia Prima in his will.

EDCS-04202063.translation: Quintus Pomponius Severus, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, ordered this monument to be made for himself and for all his freedmen by his will. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04202063.summary: An inscription by Quintus Pomponius Severus stating that he commissioned this monument for himself and his freedmen in his will, and that it is not inheritable.

EDCS-04202064.translation: Pomponia Urbana, freedwoman of Quintus, made this for herself and for Quintus Pomponius Or[--], son of Quintus, freedman of Quintus, and for her own family while alive.
EDCS-04202064.summary: A tomb inscription by Pomponia Urbana, a freedwoman, who had this monument constructed for herself, her family, and Quintus Pomponius Or[--] during her lifetime.

EDCS-04202065.translation: For Popillia Prisca, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04202065.summary: A simple dedication to Popillia Prisca, daughter of Gaius, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-04202066.translation: Poppiaca Valeriana and Tiberius O[--] Marcellus, who is also Arsino[--], built from the ground, number 300.
EDCS-04202066.summary: This inscription records the construction of 300 units by Poppiaca Valeriana and Tiberius Marcellus (also known as Arsinoos?), built from the ground up.

EDCS-04202069.translation: Titus Publicius Phronimus, while alive, made this monument for himself and for his wife Cervonia Galena. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04202069.summary: An inscription by Titus Publicius Phronimus, who built this non-inheritable monument for himself and his wife Cervonia Galena during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202071.translation: Burial place of Titus Rubellius Pudentis, son of Lucius. In front 20 feet, to the rear 45 feet. For himself and his family.
EDCS-04202071.summary: A record of a burial plot designated for Titus Rubellius Pudentis and his family, specifying dimensions and location.

EDCS-04202072.translation: To Marcus Sagatius, son of Titus.
EDCS-04202072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Sagatius, son of Titus.

EDCS-04202073.translation: To Gaius Salvius Dion[---], freedman of Gaius; to Salvia Lesbia[---], freedwoman of Gaius; to Salvia Spons[---], freedwoman of Gaius; to Lemonia Prin[---]; to Salvia Grata, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-04202073.summary: This inscription lists several freedpersons of Gaius and their female relatives, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-04202074.translation: To Gaius Satrius Verus, son of Gaius; to Gaius Satrius Optat[us], son of Gaius; to Grania Morp[---]; to Gaius Satrius Hilarus; to Sarronia Tertia, daughter of Titus; to Deminconia Am[---]; to his wife Satria Helpid[---]. Front 10 feet, rear 12 feet.
EDCS-04202074.summary: This funerary epitaph records the deceased and provides dimensions for a plot, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04202075.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Lucius Varius Filetus, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, patron, aged 18 years, and for his dearest wife Satria Firmina, daughter of Gaius. [Lucius Varius Amerimnus] erected this.
EDCS-04202075.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a young man named Lucius Varius Filetus and his wife Satria Firmina, with a probable restoration of the dedicator's name.

EDCS-04202076.translation: To Gaius Sattius Clementus, son of Lucius, and to his wife Axsia Primula, freedwoman of Titus. Front 20 feet, rear 30 feet.
EDCS-04202076.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Sattius Clementus and his wife Axsia Primula, and specifies the dimensions of their burial plot.

EDCS-04202077.translation: To Gaius Saufeius Clemens for himself and for Valeria [---].
EDCS-04202077.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or tomb ownership for Gaius Saufeius Clemens and Valeria.

EDCS-04202078.translation: To Secundena Salvia, who lived 36 years and 8 months. Quintus Sertorius Leonic[---] erected this for his dearest deserving wife.
EDCS-04202078.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Secundena Salvia and is dedicated by her husband Quintus Sertorius Leonic[---].

EDCS-04202079.translation: To Tiberius Sempronius, son of Tiberius [---].
EDCS-04202079.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or epitaph, for Tiberius Sempronius.

EDCS-04202080.translation: To Titus Sempronius Auctus, patron; to Titus Sempronius Hermetus, a good freedman; to Lucius Thorio, friend; [
EDCS-04202080.summary: A dedication honoring Titus Sempronius Auctus, Titus Sempronius Hermetus, and Lucius Thorio, likely by a subordinate or beneficiary.

EDCS-04202081.translation: Gaius Sempronius Primus, son of Quintus, made this while alive for himself, his wife Claudia Secunda, and his brother Quintus Sempronius Tertius. Front 36 feet, rear 26 feet. May those gods be angry whom all worship, if anyone violates the tomb.
EDCS-04202081.summary: This is a funerary inscription where the dedicator, Gaius Sempronius Primus, provides plot dimensions and a curse against violators of the tomb.

EDCS-04202082.translation: To Sempronia Tryphena. To the spirits of the underworld. To Sempronia Tryphena.
EDCS-04202082.summary: This is a duplicate funerary inscription for Sempronia Tryphena, likely found on the same monument.

EDCS-04202083.translation: Living, Publius Sepullius Florentus, son of Publius, freedman, and Caecilia Crene, freedwoman, and Gaius Castricius Calvo, son of Gaius, freedman, and Castricia Euche, freedwoman, and Gaius Castricius Martialis, freedman, son of the freedman, made this (tomb) for themselves and their descendants; a burial plot, 20 feet in front and 25 feet in the rear, for Lucius Domitius Theophilus.
EDCS-04202083.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a burial plot for oneself and others, specifying dimensions, possibly indicating a commercial transaction or a family tomb arrangement.

EDCS-04202084.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Tacitus, son of Publius Sepullius, of the Fabian tribe.
EDCS-04202084.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the god Tacitus, identifying his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04202085.summary: A partial inscription indicating a dedication by Urius to Servilia.

EDCS-04202086.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Streceia, who died at the age of 22. Iusta lovingly placed this for her, who deserved it well.
EDCS-04202086.summary: A funerary epitaph for Streceia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202087.translation: Strabo, son of Mani, of the Arminian tribe, Clemens Sevius Clemens, Tiberinus, son of Quintus... (fragmentary names and tribal affiliations).
EDCS-04202087.summary: A fragmentary inscription listing several Roman citizens, possibly related to a tomb or public dedication, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202088.summary: This inscription simply records the name and parentage of Lucius Sulpicius, son of Gaius, possibly on a tombstone or ownership marker.

EDCS-04202089.translation: Living, Gaius Sulpicius Maturus made this for himself and his descendants, and for his brother Lucius Cavarius Maturus, and for his sister Cavaria Amaryllis, and for Manius Hostilius Maturus; 55 feet in front and 40 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04202089.summary: This inscription records a living person, Gaius Sulpicius Maturus, dedicating a burial plot for himself, his family, and another individual, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04202090.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tauria Tyche, freedwoman of Marcus, for Titus Annius Cerinthus, her husband, and for Annia Pieris, daughter of Titus, for herself and her descendants.
EDCS-04202090.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a wife for her deceased husband and for herself and her family.

EDCS-04202092.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, living for himself and the Spirits of the Departed. Centetra, his wife, Titus Terentius Lapidarius, son of Titus, and Terentia Prima, wife of Titus, daughter of Lucius, and Titus Terentius Severus, son of Titus.
EDCS-04202092.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a man, his wife, and son, also naming a deceased wife, likely for a family tomb.

EDCS-04202093.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Terentia Severa, daughter of Titus, likely on a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-04202094.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Tilonia Musica.
EDCS-04202094.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Spirits of the Departed for Tilonia Musica.

EDCS-04202095.translation: Gaius Titius, son of Statius, of the Lanuvian tribe...
EDCS-04202095.summary: A fragmentary inscription of a Roman citizen, likely part of a longer dedication or epitaph, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202096.translation: Lucius Minucius, father; Vinicia, mother, daughter of Publius; Lucius Minucius, brother, son of Lucius. Gaius Minucius, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04202096.summary: This inscription, a funerary dedication, records a son commissioning a tomb for his deceased parents and brother, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-04202097.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Vetulena Dorcas made this for Titia Tertylina, her beloved friend, who deserved it well.
EDCS-04202097.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titia Tertylina, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202099.translation: Living, Tullia Ursina made this for herself and for Baebius Gammicus, her deserving husband.
EDCS-04202099.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication made by a living woman for herself and her husband.

EDCS-04202102.translation: Gaius Valerius Silo, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-04202102.summary: This inscription is a simple name and tribal affiliation, likely from a tombstone or a funerary marker.

EDCS-04202103.translation: Valeria Matura and her freedman Valerius Aprion made this [monument] while alive. In front 20 feet, in the rear 55 feet.
EDCS-04202103.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Valeria Matura for herself and her freedman, indicating the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04202104.text_edition: \n Cai filio Fabia tribu Veio testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-04202104.translation: He ordered that it be made by will for his son, belonging to the Fabia tribe, from Veio.
EDCS-04202104.summary: This inscription records a posthumous commission for a monument, ordered by will for a son, identifying tribal affiliation and origin.

EDCS-04202105.translation: Quintus Veionius Suavis made this [monument] for Quintus Veionius Teuda, Quintus Veionius Faustus, and Veionia Cea. In front 30 feet, in the rear 55 feet.
EDCS-04202105.summary: This is a funerary monument with specific dimensions, indicating it was set up by Quintus Veionius Suavis for several individuals.

EDCS-04202107.translation: Sextus Vettius Fidelis and his freedwoman and partner in life, Amabilis, made this [monument] for themselves while alive.
