EDCS-04202107.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument created by Sextus Vettius Fidelis for himself and his freedwoman partner, Amabilis.

EDCS-04202108.translation: Titus Vettius Tertius, son of Titus, made this while alive for himself and for his wife Volumnia Festai, daughter of [unknown], and for Gaius Paccius [unknown], of the Fabia tribe.
EDCS-04202108.summary: This funerary inscription records a man setting up the monument for himself, his wife, and another individual, likely a relative.

EDCS-04202109.translation: Vettia Clara, freedwoman of Lucius Publius Gaius, ordered that this be made by will for herself and her family.
EDCS-04202109.summary: This inscription indicates a posthumous commission by Vettia Clara for a monument for herself and her relatives, made according to her will.

EDCS-04202110.translation: Veturia Primigenia, freedwoman of Tiberius Veturius Fuscus, aged twenty-four, is buried here with Gaius Synaecius Aprilis.
EDCS-04202110.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Veturia Primigenia, a freedwoman, and her age, along with Gaius Synaecius Aprilis.

EDCS-04202111.translation: Marcus Vibius Corintus, freedman of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and his freedwoman partner Hedia Philetini. In front 10 feet, in the rear 27 feet.
EDCS-04202111.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Vibius Corintus setting up a monument for himself and his freedwoman partner, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-04202112.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Vipsanius Longinus and Iulia Faustina, parents, [set this up] for their most unfortunate son, Vipsanius Firmus, who died at the age of 3.
EDCS-04202112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by parents to their young son, Vipsanius Firmus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202113.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Virio Stefano sic Veneria liberta patrono bene merenti\n
EDCS-04202113.translation: To the divine shades. Veneria, freedwoman, [erected this] for her well-deserving patron, Gaius Virius Stephanus.
EDCS-04202113.summary: A funerary dedication to a patron by his freedwoman, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04202114.translation: Burial place of Quintus Vittorius, son of Quintus. In front 5 feet, to the rear 4 feet. He set this up for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-04202114.summary: A funerary inscription specifying the dimensions of a burial plot and indicating it was set up by the deceased for his family.

EDCS-04202115.translation: To the divine shades. Gaius Julius Eutyches set this up for his well-deserving wife, Ulpia Pro//billa.
EDCS-04202115.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his wife, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202116.translation: Burial place of Caius Volumnius Privatus, son of Caius, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-04202116.summary: A funerary inscription marking the burial place of a freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202117.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary monument to Agraeca Vosinia, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202118.translation: For Vossinia, daughter of Caius, Qu//ieta; and for Caecilia, daughter of Caius, Postuma; [belonging to] Arminius.
EDCS-04202118.summary: A funerary inscription recording the names of two women, likely related and possibly belonging to an individual named Arminius.

EDCS-04202120.translation: Lucius I F pimus made this for himself and his wife, by his will.
EDCS-04202120.summary: An epitaph indicating a burial plot or monument dedicated by Lucius I F pimus for himself and his wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202122.translation: ...onius ces made this while alive for his freedwoman wife omeno, for his wife, 40 feet back.
EDCS-04202122.summary: A funerary inscription indicating the construction of a tomb or monument by a man for his freedwoman wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202124.translation: Fafifius (?), son of Quintus, Fereius, made [this] while alive for himself and his family. In front 30 feet, to the rear 5 feet.
EDCS-04202124.summary: An inscription marking a burial plot, set up by the deceased for his family, indicating dimensions.

EDCS-04202126.summary: A fragmentary inscription that likely contains names, possibly funerary or dedicatory, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202127.translation: The plot of Publius Acius: 15 feet in front, 20 feet inward.
EDCS-04202127.summary: A boundary inscription defining the dimensions of a plot belonging to Publius Acius, likely for a tomb or property, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202128.summary: A highly fragmentary inscription with illegible content, possibly part of a longer text, date uncertain.

EDCS-04202129.translation: [Burial place] of [...]nius, son of Lucius. [...] place. [...] Paterno. In front 23.5 feet, to the rear 20 feet, from the field 20 feet inwards, sixteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-04202129.summary: A funerary inscription detailing the precise dimensions of a burial plot, including its depth and extent from a field.

EDCS-04202147.translation: Opilio, most illustrious and notable man, prefect of the praetorium, and also patrician, with God's help, completed this basilica or oratory, begun from the foundations, in honor of Saint Justina the martyr.
EDCS-04202147.summary: A dedication for the completion of a basilica or oratory by Opilio, a high-ranking official, in honor of Saint Justina the martyr, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-04202148.translation: To the spirits of Aquae Apollinares, Lucius Saufeius, son of Caius, of the Scaptia tribe, made this offering in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04202148.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Lucius Saufeius to the deities of Aquae Apollinares, likely a bath or healing complex.

EDCS-04202149.text_edition: \n Dianae Salonius Secundinus IIIIvir iure dicundo aedilicia potestate votum solvit locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202149.translation: For Diana. Salonius Secundinus, one of the four magistrates responsible for dispensing justice, in his capacity as aedile, fulfilled his vow. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202149.summary: A dedication to the goddess Diana by an official named Salonius Secundinus, noting the land was granted by the local council.

EDCS-04202150.text_edition: \n Fortunai Satria Quinti filia Procula votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202150.translation: For Fortuna. Satria Procula, daughter of Quintus, fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202150.summary: A votive offering to the goddess Fortuna by Satria Procula, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202152.translation: Aulus Considius Capito, son of Marcius, grandson of Quintus, a soldier of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion, paid his vow to Nemesis.
EDCS-04202152.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Nemesis by Aulus Considius Capito, a soldier, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04202153.translation: To the august Nymphs and Waters, Publius Pomponius Cornelianus, a most distinguished youth, made this offering, as he vowed, upon the return of the waters.
EDCS-04202153.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Publius Pomponius Cornelianus to the Nymphs and Waters, likely in gratitude for the restoration of a water supply.

EDCS-04202154.translation: Sacred to Venus. Psechas, freedwoman of Cassia.
EDCS-04202154.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Venus by a freedwoman named Psechas.

EDCS-04202155.translation: Petronius Saturninus, one of the four magistrates with judicial authority, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04202155.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Petronius Saturninus, who held a magisterial office involving legal judgments.

EDCS-04202165.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Vaternius Calpurnius Lucretianus, procurator of the emperor, had this made for his father, Gaius Vaternius Calpurnius Lucretianus, who lived for one year and two months.
EDCS-04202165.summary: This funerary inscription records a son's memorial for his father, Vaternius Calpurnius Sabinus, and provides his age at death.

EDCS-04202167.translation: Marcus Abonius Acanthus, Sextaviral Augustalis, by the census of the consul, ordered this to be made in memory of his patron Abonis Mauricus by his will.
EDCS-04202167.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Marcus Abonius Acanthus in memory of his patron Abonis Mauricus.

EDCS-04202169.translation: Quintus Iulius Catullus, son of Quintus, of the Menenia tribe, a four-time magistrate, honored with honorable discharge from the 6th Praetorian cohort, made this monument for himself while alive and for his most holy wife Coelia Severa, and after death for his excellent mother-in-law Pompeia Mansueta and his dearest wife Hostilia Serena; this monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-04202169.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Iulius Catullus, a former praetorian officer, for himself and his family, stipulating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-04202170.translation: Laevius Praesens, son of Manius, of the Menenia tribe, a soldier of the 14th Urban cohort, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, and for his father Manius Laevius, son of Caius, and for his freedwoman mother Modesta; he lived 35 years and served 16 years; his freedmen arranged for it to be made.
EDCS-04202170.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by the will of Laevius Praesens, a soldier, for himself, his father, and his mother, and was executed by his freedmen.

EDCS-04202171.translation: Manius Vita[...], son of Quintus [...], a veteran.
EDCS-04202171.summary: This is a partial inscription identifying Manius Vita[...], son of Quintus, as a veteran.

EDCS-04202173.translation: Atilius Gallio N[...], one of the six Augustalis priests.
EDCS-04202173.summary: This is a partial inscription identifying Atilius Gallio N[...] as a member of the Augustalis priesthood.

EDCS-04202174.translation: Quintus Barbius Thallus, freedman of Quintus, one of the six priests, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04202174.summary: This inscription records that Quintus Barbius Thallus, a freedman and priest, commissioned a monument in his will.

EDCS-04202175.translation: Quintus Cal, freedman of Quintus, quinquennial official, for himself and his wife, the dearly beloved Miia Calvia.
EDCS-04202175.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Quintus Cal, a quinquennial official, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04202176.translation: Caius Camerius, son of Marcus, quinquennial official and pontifex, for himself and Terentia, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04202176.summary: This is a funerary monument established by Caius Camerius, a quinquennial official and pontifex, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04202177.translation: ssius Eutychus, a concordial Augustalis, who was honored for his industry, for himself and Quintus Cassius, freedman of Quintus, a concordial Augustalis, [honored] his patron by vow.
EDCS-04202177.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary monument or dedication, possibly related to a guild or association, honoring Eutychus and Cassius, who held the title of Augustalis.

EDCS-04202178.translation: Made during his lifetime. Lucius Cassius Proculus, freedman of Lucius, a freedman, a member of the Augustales college of six, and for his wife Cassia Theodora. In front 37.5 feet, behind 38 feet.
EDCS-04202178.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Cassius Proculus for himself and his wife, indicating the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04202179.translation: To Titus Dellius, son of Titus, a magistrate of the college of four, Titus Dellius Serenus, son of Titus, for his father and himself.
EDCS-04202179.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a son, Titus Dellius Serenus, to his father, Titus Dellius, who was a magistrate.

EDCS-04202180.translation: Lucius Fabius Lycaeus, son of Lucius, quinquennial official.
EDCS-04202180.summary: This is likely an epitaph or a record of office for Lucius Fabius Lycaeus, a quinquennial official.

EDCS-04202181.translation: Marcus Festus, son of Marcus, quinquennial official, [established this] by will for his son Festus, quinquennial official.
EDCS-04202181.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by will by Marcus Festus for his son, also named Marcus Festus, who was a quinquennial official.

EDCS-04202182.translation: [---] Severus, [---] of the Menenia tribe, quinquennial official with judicial powers, for [his] father [---].
EDCS-04202182.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Severus, a quinquennial official with judicial authority, dedicated to his father.

EDCS-04202183.translation: Tiberius Iulius Montanus, quinquennial official, ordered this to be made by will.
EDCS-04202183.summary: This inscription indicates that Tiberius Iulius Montanus, a quinquennial official, commissioned this monument in his will.

EDCS-04202184.text_edition: \n Lucius Lartius Maximus IIIIvir iure dicundo adlectus aerarii pontifex uxori statuam oblatam a collegio centonariorum municipii Vicetinorum de pecunia sua posuit\n
EDCS-04202184.translation: Lucius Lartius Maximus, a magistrate of the college of four with judicial authority, who was appointed to the treasury, erected this statue for his wife, which was offered by the college of cloth-makers of the municipality of Vicetini, using his own funds.
EDCS-04202184.summary: This inscription records Lucius Lartius Maximus, a prominent local official, dedicating a statue to his wife, funded by a guild.

EDCS-04202185.translation: Living, Publius Pescennius Optatus, freedman of a woman, a sexennial official, made this for himself and for Publius Pescennius Leon, son of Caecinia, freedwoman of a woman, Vitalis, his dearest wife, and for his own [family].
EDCS-04202185.summary: This is a funerary monument established by Publius Pescennius Optatus, a sexennial official, for himself, his son, his wife, and his family.

EDCS-04202186.translation: For Publius Poblicius Valens, freedman of the municipality of Vicetini, a member of the college of six. Matiena Suavis, freedwoman of Quintus Matiena, and freedwoman of Publius, for her patrons and herself, erected this during her lifetime.
EDCS-04202186.summary: This funerary inscription records Matiena Suavis dedicating a monument for her patrons, Publius Poblicius Valens and Matiena Rufa, and herself.

EDCS-04202187.translation: Lucius Putinius Vitalis, freedman of Lucius, sexennial official and Augustalis, ordered this to be made by will for Putinia Chion, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04202187.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Lucius Putinius Vitalis, a sexennial official and Augustalis, for Putinia Chion, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-04202188.translation: Caius Resius Patruus, son of Caius, quinquennial official with judicial powers.
EDCS-04202188.summary: This inscription records Caius Resius Patruus, son of Caius, who held the office of quinquennial official with judicial authority.

EDCS-04202189.translation: Gaius Resius Severus, son of Mani, served as a duovir (IIII vir) for dispensing justice.
EDCS-04202189.summary: This is an epitaph for Gaius Resius Severus, who held the office of duovir for dispensing justice.

EDCS-04202190.inscription_type: carmina, tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04202190.translation: Lucius Terentius Telephus, freedman of Terentianus. Telephus, a member of the college of six, for himself and his family. Here lie Telephus and Pothus; may this place not be ceded to an heir when the fated hour arrives for the three, and may the ashes that this grey ash covers be undisturbed.
EDCS-04202190.summary: This funerary inscription is a poetic epitaph set up by Lucius Terentius Telephus, a local official, for himself and his family.

EDCS-04202191.translation: Vettius Taur, son of Vettius, a six-man official (VI vir), to his most devoted parents who lived with him for 70 years.
EDCS-04202191.summary: This is a dedication by Vettius Taur, a VI vir, to his parents, likely on a tomb, noting their lifespan.

EDCS-04202192.translation: Lucius Scantius Veturianus, a six-man official (VI vir), ordered this to be made by will for Gaius Veturius Firmus, son of Gaius, and for Scantilla Secunda, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04202192.summary: This is a funerary dedication commissioned by Lucius Scantius Veturianus, a VI vir, for Gaius Veturius Firmus and Scantilla Secunda.

EDCS-04202193.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Vibius as a six-man official (IIIIII vir).

EDCS-04202194.translation: Lucius Virius Sabinus, a six-man official (IIIIII vir), purchased this for himself and for his wife, Furia Maxima, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-04202194.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Virius Sabinus, a IIIIII vir, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04202202.translation: To Publius Aelius Lygdamus, freedman of Publius, a measurer, and to his wife Lepidia Gemella, freedwoman of Lucius, and to their grandson Lygdamus, and to Lepidia Acime, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04202202.summary: This is a dedication honoring a measurer, his wife, their grandson, and another freedwoman, possibly a family group or patrons.

EDCS-04202203.translation: Quintus Clodius Niger, freedman of Quintus, an eye doctor, ordered this to be made by will for himself, for his patron Quintus Clodius Salvius, freedman of Quintus, for his fellow freedman Quintus Clodius Fronton, and for his freedman Hygino.
EDCS-04202203.summary: This is a funerary commission by Quintus Clodius Niger, an eye doctor, for himself and various relatives and fellow freedmen.

EDCS-04202204.translation: To Lucius Furius Lalo, freedman of Lucius, a pedagogue.
EDCS-04202204.summary: This is an inscription honoring Lucius Furius Lalo, a freedman who served as a pedagogue.

EDCS-04202205.translation: Marcus Terrentius Marcellus, a seller of caps [capsarius], for himself and his family.
EDCS-04202205.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Terrentius Marcellus, identified by his occupation, for himself and his family.

EDCS-04202207.translation: Lucius Aemilius Eupolis made this for himself, his mother Lollia, his sister Iunia, his sister Iunia, and his brother Sci Trophimus.
EDCS-04202207.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Aemilius Eupolis for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04202208.summary: This is a brief dedication by Satilius to Agrippa Menenia, possibly a funerary or commemorative marker.

EDCS-04202209.translation: Tiberius Allenius Florus made this while alive for himself, for his freedwoman wife Allenia Murra, for his freed children, and for Tiberius Allenius Tyrannus.
EDCS-04202209.summary: This funerary inscription records a man, Tiberius Allenius Florus, who dedicated a monument for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04202210.translation: For Aprusconius, son of Gaius, of the Menenia tribe.
EDCS-04202210.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription honoring a man named Aprusconius.

EDCS-04202211.translation: For 11 months and 7 days. For Caesonia, my beloved wife. In front 40 feet, in the back 19 feet.
EDCS-04202211.summary: This inscription likely marks a grave, specifying dimensions and dedicating the space to Caesonia.

EDCS-04202212.translation: Campilia Patronis made this while alive for the patrons.
EDCS-04202212.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Campilia Patronis for her patrons.

EDCS-04202213.translation: Lucius Cartorius Ras for his father and himself, from the funds of Nero.
EDCS-04202213.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lucius Cartorius Ras, funded by Nero, for his father and himself.

EDCS-04202215.translation: For Gaius Cornelius Rufus, son of Gaius. In front 20 feet, in the back 25 feet.
EDCS-04202215.summary: This inscription seems to mark a burial plot, specifying its dimensions and dedicating it to Gaius Cornelius Rufus.

EDCS-04202216.translation: For Gaius Dossenius Blandus, brother, and for Fonteia Egloge, daughter.
EDCS-04202216.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial for a brother named Gaius Dossenius Blandus and a daughter named Fonteia Egloge.

EDCS-04202217.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Fabia Marcella, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made by her will.
EDCS-04202217.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Fabia Marcella, daughter of Lucius, states that she has arranged for the monument to be built through her will.

EDCS-04202218.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Fortunius, dearest son, who lived 3 years, 7 months, and 6 days. The most dutiful parents made this while alive.
EDCS-04202218.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by devoted parents to their young son, Fortunius.

EDCS-04202219.summary: This fragment seems to be part of a funerary inscription honoring a son named Quintus Gallus.

EDCS-04202220.translation: Also for his deceased sisters Helpidius, aged 17, and Thaemis, aged 11, and Thais, aged 8. Herennia Proculina.
EDCS-04202220.summary: This inscription records Herennia Proculina dedicating a monument for her deceased sisters who died at young ages.

EDCS-04202222.translation: Labeo, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, Marcus.
EDCS-04202222.summary: This is likely a funerary epitaph for Labeo, identifying his name, father's name, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04202223.translation: Marcus Laberius Graecus, freedman of Manius, made this (monument) for himself and for Optata, a freedwoman.
EDCS-04202223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the self-dedication of Marcus Laberius Graecus and his freedwoman Optata.

EDCS-04202224.translation: To Julia Marcella, wife of Bo, a most pious woman, in good memory.
EDCS-04202224.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the memory of Julia Marcella, described as a pious woman and wife of Bo.

EDCS-04202225.translation: Manius Listinius, son of Manius, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04202225.summary: This inscription records a testamentary commission for a monument by Manius Listinius.

EDCS-04202226.translation: Maxuma Lucilia, mother; Lucius Sempronius Remus, son of Caius.
EDCS-04202226.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Maxuma Lucilia as a mother and Lucius Sempronius Remus as her son.

EDCS-04202227.translation: The daughter of Exorata, wife of Volsanalis, made this for Quintus Lusilius Siso, deserving well of her.
EDCS-04202227.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the dedication by the daughter of Exorata for her husband, Quintus Lusilius Siso.

EDCS-04202228.translation: Maria Frequens, freedwoman of Quintus, for herself and for Quintus Marius Ennychus, freedman of Quintus, her patron.
EDCS-04202228.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the self-dedication of Maria Frequens and her patron Quintus Marius Ennychus.

EDCS-04202229.translation: To Mundilla, daughter of Cursius P[--].
EDCS-04202229.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicating the monument to Mundilla, daughter of Cursius P[--].

EDCS-04202230.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicating something to the Nymphs.

EDCS-04202231.translation: Lucius Oppius Felix, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for Lucius Oppius Felix, his patron, freedman of Lucius, and for Callistus, a freedman.
EDCS-04202231.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the self-dedication of Lucius Oppius Felix and mentioning his patron and another freedman.

EDCS-04202232.translation: Lucius C. Severus Paconius to himself and to his son Lucius Paconius, son of Lucius; to his most dutiful father and mother Satria, this monument shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-04202232.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius C. Severus Paconius for himself, his son, and his parents, stipulating that it is not to pass to an heir.

EDCS-04202233.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Papiria Maxima [erected this] to her most beloved mother Laetilia Macrina.
EDCS-04202233.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deceased mother, Laetilia Macrina, by her daughter Papiria Maxima.

EDCS-04202234.translation: For Quintus Poblicius, son of LLG. Hippolytus [set this up] for himself.
EDCS-04202234.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Hippolytus for himself and possibly for Quintus Poblicius, son of LLG.

EDCS-04202235.translation: Lucius Poblicius Secundus, freedman of Lucius Poblicius, [erected this] from his own resources.
EDCS-04202235.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by Lucius Poblicius Secundus, a freedman, at his own expense.

EDCS-04202236.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Valerianus, a most honorable young man, son of Lucius Publicius, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, lived for 16 years and 33 days. His most unhappy parents, Publicius Paullus and Serena, [set this up].
EDCS-04202236.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valerianus, a young man who died at age 16, set up by his grieving parents, Publicius Paullus and Serena.

EDCS-04202237.translation: Who lived for 23 years and 8 months. His mother, Publicia Prima, [set this up].
EDCS-04202237.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely continuing from a previous inscription, recording the lifespan of an individual and dedicated by their mother, Publicia Prima.

EDCS-04202238.translation: To Gaius Proculus, son of Gaius, a soldier, and to his sister Aelia. While alive, his mother set up this monument, which shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-04202238.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a mother for her son Gaius Proculus, a soldier, and her daughter Aelia, with a clause that the monument is not to pass to heirs.

EDCS-04202239.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, possibly part of a larger text, identifying the deceased as the freedwoman Pusilla.

EDCS-04202240.translation: Amant, Femi, Quart, Apia, M. mi, M. mil. [erected this].
EDCS-04202240.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial possibly from multiple individuals, though the exact meaning and relationship between the names are unclear and the inscription is fragmentary.

EDCS-04202241.translation: Salonia Modesta, daughter of Gaius. Quintus Matidius lived for 18 years and months. Quintus Matidius Patruinus, son of Quintus, of the Menenia tribe, lived for 2 years and 4 months.
EDCS-04202241.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of two individuals, Salonia Modesta and Quintus Matidius Patruinus, likely a family memorial, with dates that suggest they were children.

EDCS-04202243.translation: To Quinto Sat, a most devoted father, from Italica.
EDCS-04202243.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quinto Sat by Italica, likely a family member, serving as a memorial.

EDCS-04202244.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sentia Amanda erected this for her husband, Lucius Sentius Superus, who deserved well.
EDCS-04202244.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sentia Amanda for her deserving husband, Lucius Sentius Superus.

EDCS-04202245.translation: Maxima, daughter of Sertorius Mani, made this while alive.
EDCS-04202245.summary: This inscription records that Maxima, daughter of Sertorius Mani, commissioned this monument during her lifetime.

EDCS-04202246.translation: The property of the freedwoman of Quintus Sincius Cleans: 27 feet in front, 35 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04202246.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a property belonging to the freedwoman of Quintus Sincius Cleans.

EDCS-04202248.translation: Gaius Terentius Sedatus ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his wife, Grasinia Helpis: 30 feet in front, 30 feet in the rear.
EDCS-04202248.summary: This funerary inscription, commissioned by will, records Gaius Terentius Sedatus dedicating a plot for himself and his wife Grasinia Helpis.

EDCS-04202249.translation: Lucius Turranius Valens, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and for his wife, Terentia Prisca, daughter of Quintus; this burial place will not follow an heir.
EDCS-04202249.summary: This inscription records Lucius Turranius Valens commissioning a burial plot for himself and his wife, specifying that it is not inheritable.

EDCS-04202250.translation: Burial place of Lucius Turranius Valens, son of Lucius: 30 feet in front, 60 feet in the rear, a wall 1.5 feet thick around it.
EDCS-04202250.summary: This inscription details the dimensions and construction of the burial plot belonging to Lucius Turranius Valens.

EDCS-04202251.translation: Lucius Vaternius, son of Lucius Oi s, made this for himself.
EDCS-04202251.summary: This is a self-commissioned funerary monument by Lucius Vaternius, son of Lucius Oi s.

EDCS-04202252.translation: Titus Ulius Collina Verecundus, son of Manius, ordered this to be made by his will for his father Manius Ulius, son of Manius Praesens, his mother Lucretia, daughter of Caius, his brothers Manius Ulius, son of Manius Clement, and Caius Ulius, son of Manius.
EDCS-04202252.summary: This inscription, commissioned by will, records Titus Ulius Collina Verecundus dedicating a monument for his family members.

EDCS-04202253.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caius Ulpius and Menenia, likely a couple or family members.

EDCS-04202254.translation: Lucius Volumnius, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, ordered this to be set up by his will for his wife, Sergiae Secundae, and for Manius Volumnius, son of Lucius, and for Lucius Volumnius, son of Manius.
EDCS-04202254.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Lucius Volumnius for his wife and other family members.

EDCS-04202256.translation: Navius, the patron, will not pursue his heir.
EDCS-04202256.summary: This inscription is a legal declaration by Navius, a patron, regarding his heir.

EDCS-04202264.translation: Lucius Postumius Facilis and Titus Kareius Valens, freedmen, gave lintels to Apollo from their own money, on land granted for public use.
EDCS-04202264.summary: This inscription records a dedication of lintels to Apollo by two freedmen using their own funds on public land.

EDCS-04202267.translation: To the Gods and Goddesses, Quintus Samicius Successus lived and willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04202267.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made to the gods by Quintus Samicius Successus.

EDCS-04202268.text_edition: \n Deo Augusto Tlapponi Domitia Cassia votum solvit libens merito locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202268.translation: To the god Augustus Tlapponus. Domitia Cassia fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202268.summary: This inscription records Domitia Cassia fulfilling a vow to the god Augustus Tlapponus, with the location granted by local officials.

EDCS-04202269.translation: To the eternal god Magna, Lucius Statius Diodorus, because he made himself prosperous through prayers, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202269.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown dedicator to the god Magna, dated by the script to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202270.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04202270.text_edition: \n Nomine Quinti Domitii Alpini Licinia mater signum Dianae et venationem et salientes testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-04202270.translation: In the name of Quintus Domitius Alpinus, his mother Licinia ordered a statue of Diana, a hunt, and dancers to be made by her will.
EDCS-04202270.summary: This inscription records a funerary commission by Licinia for her deceased relative Quintus Domitius Alpinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202271.text_edition: \n Dianae Conservatrici pro salute Gallicani nostri consulis flaminis Augustalis proconsulis pontificis sodalis Aureliani Antoniniani Hosius libertus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202271.translation: To Diana the Preserver, for the health of our consul Gallicanus, the Augustal flamen, proconsul, pontifex, and Aurelian Antoninian fellow-soldier, Hosius, his freedman, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202271.summary: This is a votive inscription from the freedman Hosius to Diana Conservatrix for the well-being of the high-ranking official Gallicanus, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202272.translation: Sextus Iuventius Suavis to Diana the Light-Bringer, to the Moon.
EDCS-04202272.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Sextus Iuventius Suavis to the goddesses Diana and Luna.

EDCS-04202273.translation: Sacred to Dis Pater, Gaius Julius Anteros paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202273.summary: This is a votive inscription from Gaius Julius Anteros to Dis Pater, dated by the script to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202274.text_edition: \n Fortunae Cassia Publi filia Marcella votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202274.translation: To Fortuna, Cassia Marcella, daughter of Publius, paid her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202274.summary: This is a votive inscription from Cassia Marcella to Fortuna, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202276.translation: Caius Vindius Priscus, freedman of Caius, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04202276.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made to Hercules by Caius Vindius Priscus.

EDCS-04202277.translation: Marcus Atilius Atilianus, a seviri Augustalis, to Augusta Isis.
EDCS-04202277.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Marcus Atilius Atilianus, a seviri Augustalis, to the goddess Isis.

EDCS-04202278.translation: Lucius Veronius Calais to Isis, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202278.summary: This is a votive inscription from Lucius Veronius Calais to the goddess Isis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202281.translation: Sacred to Juno Regina, from Publius Vitullius Philologus, a VI vir Augustalis, by order.
EDCS-04202281.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering to Juno Regina by Publius Vitullius Philologus, a member of the collegium of seviri Augustales.

EDCS-04202283.translation: Sacred to the Junones, from Ameryllus.
EDCS-04202283.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering to the Junones by Ameryllus.

EDCS-04202284.translation: To the Junones, Marcus Caesius and Caius Caesius, sons of Marcus, brothers, willingly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-04202284.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made to the Junones by two brothers, Marcus and Caius Caesius.

EDCS-04202287.text_edition: \n Iunonibus Augustis Lucius Licinius Hymnus VIvir votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202287.translation: To the August Iunones, Lucius Licinius Hymnus, VIvir, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202287.summary: This is a votive inscription from Lucius Licinius Hymnus, a member of the college of VIviri, to the Iunones Augustae, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202288.translation: Sacred to the August Iunones. Metella, in her own name and that of her husband Titus Flavius Hermes, gave this offering.
EDCS-04202288.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Iunones by Metella on behalf of herself and her husband, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202289.translation: Publius Percennius Sabinus, a veteran of the second Praetorian cohort, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter.
EDCS-04202289.summary: This is a votive inscription by a veteran of the Praetorian Guard, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202290.translation: To Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva, Lucius V. A. paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202290.summary: This is a votive inscription to the Capitoline Triad (Jupiter, Juno, Minerva) from an unknown dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202291.translation: To Jupiter the Preserver, for the health of Publius Pomponius Cornelianus and his wife Iulia Magia, and Julianus and...
EDCS-04202291.summary: This is a fragmentary votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Conservator for the well-being of several individuals, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202295.translation: Lucius Baetutius I[---] I[---] to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04202295.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Baetutius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202296.translation: Publius Falerius, son of Publius, consul, to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04202296.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Publius Falerius, identified as a consul, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04202297.translation: The pagani of Veratia, Caius Gavius, son of Caius, Valerianus, of the Poblilia tribe, with public equestrian rank, gave this offering to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04202297.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by the pagani of Veratia, including Caius Gavius Valerianus, who held equestrian rank, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202298.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo pro salute Cai Iuli Nobiliani |(centurionis) legionis XVI Flaviae firmae Caius Iulius Lucilianus frater votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202298.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, for the health of Caius Julius Nobilianus, centurion of the XVI Flavia Firma legion, Caius Julius Lucilianus, his brother, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202298.summary: This is a votive inscription from Caius Julius Lucilianus to Jupiter Best and Greatest for the health of his brother, a centurion in the XVI Flavia Firma legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202299.translation: Publius Octavius Patrobius and Attia Moschis and Publius Octavius Attianus, by command, to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-04202299.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Publius Octavius Patrobius, Attia Moschis, and Publius Octavius Attianus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202301.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Samucinnius Tertius for himself and his family paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202301.summary: This is a votive inscription from Gaius Samucinnius Tertius for himself and his family to Jupiter Best and Greatest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202302.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo conservatori Publius Pomponius Cornelianus consularis curator rerum publicarum\n
EDCS-04202302.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the preserver, Publius Pomponius Cornelianus, consular governor, curator of public affairs.
EDCS-04202302.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument to Jupiter by a consular governor.

EDCS-04202303.translation: Cassia Iusta, daughter of Caius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Jupiter the Holy.
EDCS-04202303.summary: This is a votive inscription by Cassia Iusta, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Sanctus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202304.translation: Titus Caecilius Sextus to Jupiter Summanus.
EDCS-04202304.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Summanus by Titus Caecilius Sextus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202305.translation: The magistrates, Marcus Licinius Pusillio, son of Marcus; Sextus Vipsanius Clemens, son of Marcus; Quintus Cassius Niger, son of Caius; the attendants, Blandus, slave of Caius Afinius Ascla; Murranus, slave of Publius Clodius Turpio; Auctus, slave of Marcus Fabricius Hilarus, repaired the sanctuary and its roof, raised the walls, and gave the doors as a gift from their own funds to the Lares, when Cosso Cornelius Lentulus and Lucius Piso Augur were consuls.
EDCS-04202305.summary: An inscription recording the repair of a sanctuary and its fittings by elected magistrates and their attendants, dedicated to the Lares, dated to the consulship of Lentulus and Piso.

EDCS-04202308.translation: Sacred to Liber. Marcus Lutarius Verus and Vera, a freedwoman of Novellia, having fulfilled their vow, [dedicated this].
EDCS-04202308.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Liber by Marcus Lutarius Verus and Vera, a freedwoman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202310.translation: Publius Firminus Martibus gladly erected this with a willing spirit; he fulfilled his vow gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202310.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Martibus by Publius Firminus.

EDCS-04202311.translation: Marcianus Severus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Augustus.
EDCS-04202311.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mars Augustus by Marcianus Severus.

EDCS-04202312.translation: Valeria Nempsis gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Matronae.
EDCS-04202312.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the Matronae by Valeria Nempsis.

EDCS-04202314.translation: Lucius Calvisius, son of Publius, from Oriculo, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04202314.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury by Lucius Calvisius from Oriculo.

EDCS-04202315.translation: Marcus Scaevilius Corneolus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04202315.summary: A votive inscription to Mercury by Marcus Scaevilius Corneolus.

EDCS-04202316.translation: Lucius Vitorius Festus, Quintus Vitorius Severus, and their mother Iuventia gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04202316.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury by Lucius Vitorius Festus, Quintus Vitorius Severus, and their mother Iuventia.

EDCS-04202318.translation: Publius Cassius, son of Publius, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04202318.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Minerva by Publius Cassius.

EDCS-04202319.translation: Sacred to Minerva: Caius Cassius Iustus, son of Lucius, a member of the VIvirate of Augustales, and Laelia Logas.
EDCS-04202319.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Minerva by Caius Cassius Iustus, a VIvir Augustalis, and Laelia Logas.

EDCS-04202321.translation: Hymnis, freedwoman of Titinius Decimus, to Minerva.
EDCS-04202321.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Minerva by Hymnis, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04202322.translation: Sextus Veronius Apelles gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04202322.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Minerva by Sextus Veronius Apelles.

EDCS-04202323.translation: Quintus Cassius Papiri and Clodius [dedicated this] to Minerva Augusta; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202323.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Minerva Augusta by Quintus Cassius Papiri and Clodius, with the land granted by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-04202324.translation: To Minerva Augusta, Gaius Seius Itharus gave this gift.
EDCS-04202324.summary: This is a votive dedication to Minerva Augusta, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04202325.translation: To Sol, Lucius Cassius Ianuarius, freedman of Lucius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow, a place granted by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-04202325.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the sun god Sol by a freedman, with the granting of space approved by local councillors, suggesting a public or semi-public dedication.

EDCS-04202326.translation: Sacred to the deified Pantheon, Quintus Salvius Verecundus.
EDCS-04202326.summary: This is a dedication to the deified Pantheon by Quintus Salvius Verecundus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04202327.translation: To the August Fates, Atilia Valeriana.
EDCS-04202327.summary: This is a dedication to the August Fates by Atilia Valeriana, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04202328.text_edition: \n Loco publico dato decreto decurionum Parcis Augustis sacrum Lucius Cassius Vervici filius Nigrinus VIvir Augustalis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202328.translation: On public ground granted by decree of the decurions, sacred to the August Parcae, Lucius Cassius Nigrinus, son of Vervicus, VIvir Augustalis, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04202328.summary: A votive inscription to the Parcae Augustae by Lucius Cassius Nigrinus, a VIvir Augustalis, on public land granted by decree.

EDCS-04202329.translation: To the August Fates, Publius Falerius Trophimus, [with] ducenarian honours...
EDCS-04202329.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the August Fates by Publius Falerius Trophimus, mentioning his senatorial rank or honours.

EDCS-04202332.translation: To the Underworld Gods, Lucius Antistius Vitulus with his family erected this by order.
EDCS-04202332.summary: This is a dedication to the gods of the underworld (Dis Parentibus) by Lucius Antistius Vitulus and his family, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202333.translation: To the Underworld Gods, Lucius Baebius Pri[...]
EDCS-04202333.summary: This is a partial inscription recording a dedication to the gods of the underworld (Dis Parentibus) by Lucius Baebius Pri[...], likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202334.translation: To the Underworld Gods, Marcus Sextius Primus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04202334.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the gods of the underworld (Dis Parentibus) by Marcus Sextius Primus, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202335.translation: To the Underworld Gods, Publius Tenatius.
EDCS-04202335.summary: This is a dedication to the gods of the underworld (Dis Parentibus) by Publius Tenatius, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202336.translation: Vinnia Modesta willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Deities, our Ancestors.
EDCS-04202336.summary: A votive inscription to the ancestral deities by Vinnia Modesta.

EDCS-04202337.translation: Lucius Iunius Pauper, son of Marcus, dedicated the portico to the August Ancestral Deities.
EDCS-04202337.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of a portico to the August Ancestral Deities by Lucius Iunius Pauper.

EDCS-04202338.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus, Marcus Cassius Firmus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04202338.summary: This is a votive dedication to Saturn Augustus by Marcus Cassius Firmus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04202339.translation: Publius Tossius Zosimus, VIvir Augustalis, and his wife Tossia Saturnina willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-04202339.summary: A joint votive inscription to Saturn Augustus by Publius Tossius Zosimus, a VIvir Augustalis, and his wife.

EDCS-04202341.translation: Licinius Gelasius, the cellarer, set up this altar to Serapis the Augustus and Isis the Queen.
EDCS-04202341.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to the gods Serapis and Isis by a cellarer named Licinius Gelasius.

EDCS-04202342.translation: Lucius Cassius Nigrinus, son of Vervicus, a six-man priest of the Augustals, to Silvanus.
EDCS-04202342.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Silvanus by Lucius Cassius Nigrinus, a member of the VI viri Augustales.

EDCS-04202343.translation: Isochrysus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Silvanus for Cornelia Magna.
EDCS-04202343.summary: A votive inscription to Silvanus by Isochrysus on behalf of Cornelia Magna.

EDCS-04202345.text_edition: \n Silvano Augusto sacrum Marcus Dubitatius Pervincus VIvir Augustalis et Festus filius votum solverunt libentes laeti merito locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202345.translation: Marcus Dubitatius Pervincus, VIvir Augustalis, and his son Festus, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Silvanus Augustus; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202345.summary: A joint votive inscription to Silvanus Augustus by a VIvir Augustalis and his son, on land granted by decree.

EDCS-04202346.translation: Publius Octavius Epaphroditus, freedman of Zmaragdus, willingly paid his vow to Silvanus Augustus, as was deserved.
EDCS-04202346.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Silvanus Augustus by Publius Octavius Epaphroditus, a freedman.

EDCS-04202347.translation: Caius Veronius Servilianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Silvanus Augustus.
EDCS-04202347.summary: A votive inscription to Silvanus Augustus by Caius Veronius Servilianus.

EDCS-04202348.translation: Publius Falerius Trophimus, the hunter, to Silvanus the Fortunate, with decurional honors.
EDCS-04202348.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Felicis by Publius Falerius Trophimus, a hunter, accompanied by decurional honors.

EDCS-04202349.translation: Flavia Donata willingly paid her vow to the Silvani, as was deserved.
EDCS-04202349.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the Silvani by Flavia Donata.

EDCS-04202352.translation: Sacred to the Augusti. Caius, son of Faber, F.
EDCS-04202352.summary: This fragmentary inscription dedicates something to the "Augusti" and includes the name Caius, son of Faber.

EDCS-04202353.translation: Sacred to the Mistress. Titus Titienius Florus, the butcher, [dedicated this] for the good fortune of the mistress and the entire populace.
EDCS-04202353.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a female deity, referred to as 'domina' (Mistress), by Titus Titienius Florus, a butcher.

EDCS-04202355.translation: [Dedicated to the] skilled artisan Marcus Visurus, [who carried out his duties] for the Emperor Augustus X times.
EDCS-04202355.summary: This damaged inscription seems to honor Marcus Visurus, a craftsman associated with the emperor.

EDCS-04202356.translation: Lucius Masurius Lacinia, Caius Masurius Optatus, Publius Cluvius Verus, Caius Cusonius Balbus, Lucius Lusius Proculus.
EDCS-04202356.summary: This inscription lists the names of five individuals, likely functioning as a dedication or record of office.

EDCS-04202357.translation: Caius Gavius Agrippa, Publius Cluvius Severus, Lucius Cluvius Senecio, Marcus Gavius Serenus, Lucius Valerius Firmus.
EDCS-04202357.summary: This inscription lists the names of five individuals, likely functioning as a dedication or record of office.

EDCS-04202358.text_edition: \n Cai Amurii Tacitinus et Hermes liberti VIviri Augustales signi abacum cum signis II Hercule et Amphale sic collegio dendroforum dono dederunt\n
EDCS-04202358.translation: Cai Amurii Tacitinus and Hermes, freedmen, members of the VIvirate Augustales, gave as a gift to the association of woodcutters a statue base with two statues, depicting Hercules and Omphale.
EDCS-04202358.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a statue base and statues by freedmen members of the VIvirate Augustales to the dendrophoroi (woodcutters' guild).

EDCS-04202359.translation: Betuia Philargyris, freedwoman of Caius, for her own health.
EDCS-04202359.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a freedwoman for her own health.

EDCS-04202360.translation: Marcus Clodius Firmus, son of Marcus, willingly paid his vow deservedly.
EDCS-04202360.summary: This inscription records a man fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04202361.text_edition: \n Signum basim Caius Cornelius Mar Valeria Firmina votum solverunt\n
EDCS-04202361.translation: Gaius Cornelius Mar and Valeria Firmina fulfilled their vow on the base of a statue.
EDCS-04202361.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Gaius Cornelius Mar and Valeria Firmina, likely dedicating a statue base.

EDCS-04202362.translation: Publius Iuventius to the Parental Gods.
EDCS-04202362.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Publius Iuventius to the Parental Gods.

EDCS-04202363.translation: Orcivia Nigela willingly paid her vow deservedly.
EDCS-04202363.summary: This inscription records a woman fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04202364.translation: Publius Pomponius Cornelianus and Iulia Magia, with their sons Iulianus and Magianus, built this from the ground up.
EDCS-04202364.summary: This inscription records a family constructing a building.

EDCS-04202365.translation: Prepon and Domitia Syrilla willingly paid their vow deservedly.
EDCS-04202365.summary: This inscription records a couple fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04202366.translation: Fausta, freedwoman of Tarquinia, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04202366.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Fausta, freedwoman of Tarquinia, likely in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04202367.translation: Lucius Valerius Ar[---] to the Eternal Great Sol, having been warned by a dream, dedicated what he vowed after its completion.
EDCS-04202367.summary: This is a dedication to the god Sol by Lucius Valerius, who was inspired by a dream.

EDCS-04202368.translation: I. Valerius Riqu, son of Pius, willingly gave this offering deservedly.
EDCS-04202368.summary: This inscription records a man making a voluntary offering.

EDCS-04202375.text_edition: \n Colonia Augusta Verona nova Gallieniana Valeriano II et Lucilio conssulibus muri Veronensium fabricati ex die III Nonarum Aprilium dedicati pridie Nonas Decembres iubente sanctissimo Gallieno Augusto nostro insistente Aurelio Marcellino viro perfectissimo duce ducenario curante Iulio Marcellino \n
EDCS-04202375.translation: The walls of Verona were built by the inhabitants of the Colonia Augusta Verona Nova Gallieniana, dedicated on the 3rd day before the Kalends of April, and consecrated on the day before the Nones of December, under the command of our most holy emperor Gallienus, with the supervision of Aurelius Marcellinus, a most perfect man and dux of the second cohort, and under the charge of Iulius Marcellinus.
EDCS-04202375.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of the walls of Verona during the consulship of Valeriano II and Lucilio, under the reign of Emperor Gallienus, likely in 260 CE.

EDCS-04202378.translation: Encouraged by the blessed times of our lords Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius, Augusti, Valerius Palladius, a most distinguished man, ex-consul of Venice and Istria, ordered a statue, long lying in the Capitol, to be set up in the busiest part of the forum.
EDCS-04202378.summary: This inscription records a high-ranking official, Valerius Palladius, commissioning the placement of a statue in Rome during the reign of late Roman emperors.

EDCS-04202380.text_edition: \n Publio Baebio Publi filio Poblilia Tuticano tribuno militum a populo praefecto equitum pro legato pontifici IIIIviro plebs urbana permissu decurionum\n
EDCS-04202380.translation: To Publius Baebius Tuticanus, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, military tribune of the legions, prefect of cavalry, propraetorian legate, and pontiff, by the urban plebs, with the permission of the decurions.
EDCS-04202380.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Publius Baebius Tuticanus, listing his military and civic offices, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202381.text_edition: \n Lucio Calpurnio Luci filio Publilia Squillio quaestori imperatorum tribuno plebis praetori decreto decurionum patrono\n
EDCS-04202381.translation: To Lucius Calpurnius Squillius, son of Lucius, of the Publilia tribe, quaestor of the emperors, tribune of the plebs, praetor, and patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202381.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Calpurnius Squillius, detailing his career as quaestor, tribune, praetor, and patron of the community, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202382.text_edition: \n Caio Calvisio Cai filio Poblilia Statiano populi advocato ab epistulis Latinis Augustorum Veronenses patrono\n
EDCS-04202382.translation: To Gaius Calvisius Statianus, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, advocate of the people, in charge of Latin correspondence for the emperors, and patron of the Veronese people.
EDCS-04202382.summary: This honorary inscription recognizes Gaius Calvisius Statianus for his services as an advocate and imperial secretary, and as a patron of Verona, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202383.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Tiberi filio Quirina Augustano patri Bellici Sollertis procuratori Augusti provinciae Britanniae Claudia Tiberi filia Marcellina socero optimo posuit\n
EDCS-04202383.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Augustanus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, father of Bellicus Sollertis, procurator of the emperor in the province of Britannia; erected by his very good father-in-law, Claudius Marcellinus, son of Tiberius.
EDCS-04202383.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Tiberius Claudius Augustanus, a procurator in Britannia, erected by his father-in-law, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202384.text_edition: \n Claudiae Tiberi filio Marcellinae Bellici Sollertis consulis Marcus et Caius Hortensi Paulinus et Firmus\n
EDCS-04202384.translation: Marcus and Gaius Hortensius Paulinus and Firmus [erected this] to Claudia Marcellina, daughter of Tiberius, wife of Bellicus Sollertis.
EDCS-04202384.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Marcus and Gaius Hortensius Paulinus and Firmus, likely to Claudia Marcellina, wife of Bellicus Sollertis, possibly funerary.

EDCS-04202385.translation: Marcus Fruticius, son of Quintus; Lucius, son of Quintus; Lucius, son of Lucius; Marcus Fruticius, son of Marcus, praetor, aedile, tribune of the plebs; Marcus, son of Marcus; Lucius, son of Marcus...
EDCS-04202385.summary: This inscription lists the names and offices of several members of the Fruticius family, likely part of a larger public monument or family record, dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04202386.text_edition: \n Publio Graecinio Publi filio Poblilia Laconi ornamentis consularibus\n
EDCS-04202386.translation: To Publius Graecinius Lacon, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, with consular rank.
EDCS-04202386.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Graecinius Lacon, who held consular rank.

EDCS-04202387.text_edition: \n Valerio Publi? filio Publilia Nasoni IIIIviro viarum curandarum flamini Augusti primo Veronensium creato plebs universa\n
EDCS-04202387.translation: To Valerius Nason, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, an aedile of roads and a flamen Augusti, created first among the Veronensians, the entire plebs.
EDCS-04202387.summary: This is a dedication by the plebs of Verona to Valerius Nason, honoring his roles as aedile and flamen.

EDCS-04202388.text_edition: \n Marco Nonio Marci filio Poblilia Arrio Muciano consuli praetori XVviro sacris faciundis curatori et patrono rei publicae Veronensium ob largitionem eius quod at thermas Iuventianas perficiendas HS CCCC (quadringenta milia) nummum rei publicae dederit ordo\n
EDCS-04202388.translation: To Marcus Nonius Mucianus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, consul, praetor, member of the Fifteen for Religious Matters, curator and patron of the Republic of the Veronensians, on account of his generosity, because he gave 400,000 sesterces to the Republic for the completion of the Baths of Juventius, the council.
EDCS-04202388.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Nonius Mucianus for his generous donation to the city of Verona for the construction of public baths.

EDCS-04202389.text_edition: \n Marco Nonio Marci filio Poblilia Muciano Publio Delphio Peregrino tribuno militum legionis X fretensis quaestori aedili praetori legato pro praetore provinciae Asiae patrono decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202389.translation: To Marcus Nonius Mucianus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, to Publius Delphius Peregrinus, military tribune of the Tenth Legion Fretensis, quaestor, aedile, praetor, legate pro praetore of the province of Asia, patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202389.summary: This inscription honors Publius Delphius Peregrinus, a military official and patron of Verona, by decree of the local council.

EDCS-04202390.translation: To Petronius Probus, a man of the highest distinction, a man worthy of all admiration, proconsul of Africa, praetorian prefect of Illyricum, praetorian prefect of Gaul (II), praetorian prefect of Italy and Africa (III), ordinary consul, a citizen of exceptional goodness, most eloquent and learned in all things, patron, grandson of Probianus, son of Probinus, of men most distinguished, urban prefects and consuls.
EDCS-04202390.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Petronius Probus, detailing his illustrious career and high offices in the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-04202391.text_edition: \n Aurelius Vincentius filius vir clarissimus et Tenagenonia Claudia clarissima femina nurus socrui karae\n
EDCS-04202391.translation: To Aurelius Vincentius, son of Vincentius, a most distinguished man, and Tenagenonia Claudia, a most distinguished woman, to their dear mother-in-law.
EDCS-04202391.summary: This is a familial dedication from Aurelius Vincentius and his wife Claudia to Vincentius's mother.

EDCS-04202393.text_edition: \n ------ quaestori] provinciae Siciliae aedili plebis praetori publice patrono decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202393.translation: To ---, quaestor of the province of Sicily, aedile of the plebs, praetor, publicly, patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202393.summary: This fragmentary inscription honors an unnamed individual who served as quaestor, aedile, and praetor and was recognized as a patron.

EDCS-04202394.translation: Four vexilla, a triumphal wall, and a theatre were erected by [---]rico in honor of the patron across the Atesis River.
EDCS-04202394.summary: This inscription likely records the construction of military standards, a defensive wall, and a theatre for a patron, possibly with a date indicated by the triumphal context.

EDCS-04202395.summary: This inscription is a fragment mentioning a consul, indicating a political or administrative context, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04202397.translation: Burial place for the family of Theopompus, the carrier, of the Twentieth Freedom, of the Transpadane region; also for Tryphonius and Quintus Sicinius(?), from his own funds.
EDCS-04202397.summary: This is a funerary inscription establishing a burial plot for several individuals, including a carrier named Theopompus.

EDCS-04202398.translation: Made by Lucius Appius Cinnamus, freedman of Sabinus, a painter, pontiff of Rome, Augustalis of the Seviri, for himself while alive.
EDCS-04202398.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument made by Lucius Appius Cinnamus, who held various religious and civic offices.

EDCS-04202399.summary: This inscription likely refers to a funerary monument or dedication to someone named Atticus, humorously comparing him to the herald of Priam.

EDCS-04202400.translation: To Lucius Calpurnius, a courier of the tribunes, summoned by a patron, and also appointed as a high priest of the Augustales. To his inseparable companion Vetere Fabrateria and Baibiai Procula.
EDCS-04202400.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Calpurnius, who held various administrative and religious offices, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202401.translation: Made by Sextus Varius Peregrinus while alive, to Marcus Adurius Expectatus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, a deserving veteran and friend.
EDCS-04202401.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Sextus Varius Peregrinus for his friend and a veteran, Marcus Adurius Expectatus.

EDCS-04202402.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Tiberi filio Quirina Alpino praefecto cohortis II praetoriae donis donato bello Germanico Claudia Tiberi filia Marcellina marito optimo\n
EDCS-04202402.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Alpinus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, prefect of the Second Praetorian Cohort, honored with gifts in the Germanic War, from Claudia Marcellina, daughter of Tiberius, to her most excellent husband.
EDCS-04202402.summary: This is a dedication from Claudia Marcellina to her husband, Tiberius Claudius Alpinus, a decorated prefect of the Praetorian Guard.

EDCS-04202403.translation: Publius Asinius Ballista, son of Lucius, a veteran of the Legio XV Apollinaris, for himself and [---]
EDCS-04202403.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a veteran of the Legio XV Apollinaris, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202404.text_edition: \n Caio Attio Cai filio Poblilia Alfiano Lucilio Rugae praefecto cohortis II Raetorum Lutonia Festa mater locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202404.translation: To Gaius Attius, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, Lucilius Rugas, prefect of the II Raetorum cohort; the site was granted by decree of the decurions to Lutonia Festa, mother.
EDCS-04202404.summary: This is a funerary inscription granting a burial plot to Lutonia Festa, mother of Gaius Attius, a prefect.

EDCS-04202406.translation: To Quintus Caelsius, son of Quintus, standard-bearer of the Pob(lilia) tribe, and to Marcus Caelsius, son of Quintus, veterans of the Legio XIIII Gemina. To Quintus Caelsius Primus, freedman of Quintus, [---]
EDCS-04202406.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication to two veterans of the Legio XIIII Gemina and a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202407.translation: Marcus Cintullus Severus, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe, soldier of the V Praetorian cohort, for himself and for his mother Colona, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04202407.summary: This funerary inscription records a soldier of the Praetorian Guard dedicating it to himself and his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202408.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus Coelius Homullus, son of Marcus, of the Flavia tribe, from Solva, a grain-duty soldier of the VI Legion Victrix, Tali[...].
EDCS-04202408.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Coelius Homullus, a soldier of the VI Legion Victrix, with his tribal affiliation and origin mentioned.

EDCS-04202409.translation: To Quintus Cornelius, son of Caius, of the IX cohort.
EDCS-04202409.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or mention of a soldier belonging to the IX cohort, possibly military or funerary in nature.

EDCS-04202411.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Dubitatus, who lived 28 years, of Astigi origin, for his deserving husband Serapius.
EDCS-04202411.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Dubitatus, specifying his age, origin, and his deserving husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202412.translation: Publius Fannius, son of Marcius, a centurion, prefect of cavalry, and a high-ranking official. His wife Annia Avillia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04202412.summary: This inscription records the honors and family of Publius Fannius, who held significant military and administrative positions, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202413.translation: Gavia, daughter of Gaius, of the Rullian tribe, made this for herself while alive, and for her son Marcus Valerius Crispinus, a centurion of the Seventh Legion.
EDCS-04202413.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gavia for herself and her son, a centurion, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202414.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Julius Maternus, an evocatus Augusti from the IX Praetorian cohort, to his well-deserving patron, erected by his freedman, Gaius Julius Aquila.
EDCS-04202414.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a freedman to his patron, Gaius Julius Maternus, who was an evocatus Augusti in the Praetorian guard.

EDCS-04202415.translation: Marcus Laelius Laelianus, a veteran of the Eighth Praetorian Cohort, made this for himself and Aia Procula while alive.
EDCS-04202415.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a Praetorian Guard veteran for himself and his wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202416.translation: [...] Mercator, veteran of the [...] Legion, for himself and [...]tio Iuvencatus, his [...] father, [...]sius Homullus, [...] soldiers of the [...] Legion, [...]uiend.
EDCS-04202416.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription likely commemorating several individuals, including veterans and soldiers, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04202417.translation: Lucius Octavius Marcellinus, son of Lucius, of the Poblilian tribe, a *beneficiarius* of the praetorian prefect and an *evocatus*, ordered this to be made by his will while alive.
EDCS-04202417.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Octavius Marcellinus, a high-ranking officer's aide and veteran, commissioned his funerary monument by his will, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202418.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Papirius Marcellinus, an incomparable father, deceived by the Dacisci in battle, for whom Papirius Marcellus made this for his well-deserving father.
EDCS-04202418.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a son to his father, who died in battle against the Dacisci, likely dating to the Roman expansion into Dacia in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04202419.translation: Sextus Salanius Mandatus, son of Publius, a soldier of the Fifteenth Legion.
EDCS-04202419.summary: This is a simple tombstone inscription for a soldier of the Fifteenth Legion, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202420.translation: Quintus Sertorius Festus, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe, centurion of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis Legion.
EDCS-04202420.summary: This inscription records Quintus Sertorius Festus, a centurion in the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis Legion.

EDCS-04202421.translation: Lucius Sertorius Firmus, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe, standard-bearer and aquilifer of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis Legion, discharged as curator of veterans of the same legion, to Domitia Prisca, wife of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-04202421.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Sertorius Firmus, a veteran standard-bearer and aquilifer, to his wife Domitia Prisca.

EDCS-04202425.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucius Aemilius Callippus, one of the six civic priests of the Augustan cult, for his most excellent and incomparable husband and for himself.
EDCS-04202425.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Aelia Merope for her husband, Lucius Aemilius Callippus, a prominent civic priest, and for herself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202426.translation: Lucius Annius Genitivos, decurion of Verona, for himself and for his parents Lucius Annius Harpatus and Annia Genesis, and for his brother Lucius Annius Marcellinus, and for his wife Valeria Phoebas, for whom she arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-04202426.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Annius Genitivos, a decurion of Verona, for himself and his family.

EDCS-04202427.translation: Manumissa, alumna, aged 4 years and 17 days, by Marcus Avenaeus Macro, most distinguished Roman equestrian, who had performed every honor. To Avenia Bassaris, her best daughter. Marcus Gavius Cornelius Agathemerus Avenianus, debilitated by all injury. She lived 25 years, 4 months, and 14 days, most perfect in all feeling, life, and piety.
EDCS-04202427.summary: This is a complex funerary monument with multiple dedications, commemorating a young woman named Manumissa and her daughter Avenia Bassaris, with inscriptions by Marcus Avenaeus Macro and Marcus Gavius Cornelius Agathemerus.

EDCS-04202428.translation: To Lucius Caesius Nicostratus, Augustal VIvir.
EDCS-04202428.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Caesius Nicostratus, an Augustal VIvir, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202429.translation: Publius Caecilius Epaphroditus, a civic priest of the Augustan cult and a calculator for Iostina Helena, made this for his wife and for himself while alive.
EDCS-04202429.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Publius Caecilius Epaphroditus, a priest and administrator, for himself and his wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202430.translation: For Gaius Cetronius Castalinus, son of Gaius, a member of the board of three Augustal priests; for himself; he lived 6 years, 8 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-04202430.summary: This inscription records the dedication to a young boy, Gaius Cetronius Castalinus, who was a member of a prestigious priesthood, and notes his lifespan, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202431.translation: Festa, daughter of Caius, of the Calpurnia tribe, made [this] while alive for herself and for her husband Caius Safinius Rufus, son of Lucius; for her son Lucius Safinius Rufus, a VIvir; and for Octavia, her mother-in-law.
EDCS-04202431.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Calpurnia Festa for herself and several family members, including her husband, son, and mother-in-law.

EDCS-04202432.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Gaius Calventius Firmus, curators of the equipment of Verona, from the guild of craftsmen.
EDCS-04202432.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Calventius Firmus, who managed equipment for the city of Verona as part of the craftsmen's guild, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202433.text_edition: \n Cassius filius Poblilia Calvio IIIIvir aedilicia potestate\n
EDCS-04202433.translation: Cassius, son of Cassius, of the Poblilia tribe, IIvir with aedilician power.
EDCS-04202433.summary: This inscription records Cassius, a IIvir with aedilician power, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-04202434.translation: To Claudia Firma, daughter of Lucius, Lucius Calpurnius Marcellus, son of Lucius, a Six-man official of the Augustals, [erected this] to his deserving wife [and] to himself.
EDCS-04202434.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, set up by her husband who also reserved a place for himself, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202435.translation: Sextus Clodius Festus, a Six-man official of the Augustals, and his wife Aggonia Marcella, and their freedwoman Clodia Amanda, made this while alive; Licinius, [their] father, [provided it].
EDCS-04202435.summary: A funerary monument for a family and their freedwoman, likely set up by the father, indicating a wealthy household. The text dates to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202436.translation: Lucius Coelius Valerius gave this place to Herennia Maxima by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-04202436.summary: A grant of burial space by a local magistrate to a woman, likely a private donation or favour, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202437.translation: Gaius Cornelius Hanno, freedman of Gaius, a Six-man official, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, and for Castus and Domestus, his freedmen.
EDCS-04202437.summary: A funerary epitaph for a freedman official and his freedmen, commissioned by will, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202438.text_edition: \n Cnaeus Cornelius Qurvini sic libertus Neritus VIvir Augustalis sibi et Clodiae Tonnianae libertae Chreste contubernali\n
EDCS-04202438.translation: Gnaeus Cornelius Neritus, freedman of Gnaeus Cornelius, a Six-member official of Augustus, for himself and for Chresta, freedwoman of Clodia, his partner.
EDCS-04202438.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a freedman for himself and his partner, identifying his patron and his status as a Six-member official.

EDCS-04202439.translation: Gaius Cornelius Sph, freedman of Gaius, a Six-man official.
EDCS-04202439.summary: An epitaph for a freedman who served as a Six-man official, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202440.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Curtius Agathemerus, a Six-man official, made these two plots for himself and for his dearest wife Loria Priscilla, and for his dear friends Quintus Cassius Valerianus and Toria Olympis, and for others belonging to me, while he was alive.
EDCS-04202440.summary: A funerary monument by a public official for himself, his wife, and friends, indicating the acquisition of multiple burial plots during his lifetime, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202441.translation: [---] Marcus Clodius [---], Lucius Domitius [---], Decimus Junius [---], Four-man officials.
EDCS-04202441.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning three individuals who served as Four-man officials, likely part of a larger monument or list, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202442.translation: Marcus Domitius, Six-man official, [for] Poblilia Mac.
EDCS-04202442.summary: An epitaph for Poblilia Mac, set up by Marcus Domitius, who held the position of Six-man official, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202443.translation: Lucius Fecinius Dasius, freedman of Lucius, of the Palatine tribe, a six-man official, made [this] while alive for himself and for Auge, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04202443.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman official for himself and his freedwoman, indicating their status and relationship, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202444.translation: Firmus, a Six-man official, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, and for his son Marcus Coelius Marcellinus, and for his wife Cipia Marcella, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04202444.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by will by a Six-man official for his son and wife, indicating family provisions and social standing, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202445.translation: Tiberius Flavius Noricus, son of Publius, served as a quaestor of the four-man board for dispensing justice.
EDCS-04202445.summary: This inscription records the public office held by Tiberius Flavius Noricus, who was a member of the IIII vir iure dicundo in Verona.

EDCS-04202446.translation: To Honor. By Marcus Gavi Squillianus, son of Marcus, of the Poblitian tribe, Roman eques, twice a magistrate with judicial power, twice a magistrate with aedilitian power, a good man, curator of the Vicetians. The apparitors and courthouse attendants of his tribunal dedicated this.
EDCS-04202446.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Gavi Squillianus, a prominent local official, and was dedicated by his subordinate staff, likely in the town of Vicetia.

EDCS-04202447.text_edition: \n Gavia Quinti filia Maxima in aquam HS |(sescenta milia) ex testamento dedit\n
EDCS-04202447.translation: Gavia Maxima, daughter of Quintus, gave 600,000 sesterces to the water supply in her will.
EDCS-04202447.summary: This is a testamentary dedication of funds for the water supply by a woman named Gavia Maxima.

EDCS-04202448.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Hostilius Tertinus, a decurion of Verona, and Abidia Maxima, parents, to their most dutiful son Campanus, venator, son of Publius Hostilius and of the Poblitian tribe, and to themselves, who lived 25 years and 25 days without fault in their flourishing life; death itself snatched him away. Live happily. I warn you, death awaits everyone; learn from our example, you who read. Live happily.
EDCS-04202448.summary: This funerary inscription is set up by parents for their son, a hunter, who died at a young age, and includes a philosophical reflection on mortality.

EDCS-04202449.translation: Gaius Julius Dosa, freedman of Caesar Augustus, a living sexvir, dedicated this for himself and for his wife, Numiasia, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04202449.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Gaius Julius Dosa, a living sexvir and freedman of Augustus, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04202450.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Julius Zelotis, a living Augustan sexvir, and his associates, Gaius Julius Medes, Gaius Julius Cus, Augustan sexvirs, and Gaius Julius Karicus, freedman, made this for a deserving patron, freedman, and for L. Iulia Ridi, freedwoman, and...
EDCS-04202450.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument established by Gaius Julius Zelotis and other Augustan sexvirs for a deceased patron and freedwoman.
