EDCS-04202451.translation: ... for Julia Venusta, freedwoman, and for Gaius Julius Anterotes, and for Julia Aphrodisia, freedwoman, and for Tiberius Claudius Peculiaris, an Augustan sexvir and friend, and for Atisia Aphrodisia.
EDCS-04202451.summary: This inscription, likely a continuation of the previous one, lists additional individuals for whom a monument was dedicated, including freedwomen, a freedman, an Augustan sexvir, and others.

EDCS-04202452.text_edition: \n Lucio Laetorio Luci filio Poblilia Anneio Rufo A--- IIIIvir(o)? viarum curandarum Narbonensis viro sexviri ob merita eius locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202452.translation: To Lucius Laetorius Anneus Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Poblitian tribe, a Four-member official for the maintenance of roads in Narbonensis, a Six-member official, for his merits, a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202452.summary: This inscription records a grant of public space to Lucius Laetorius Anneus Rufus, a local magistrate responsible for roads, by the town council.

EDCS-04202453.translation: [---]stinus, son of [---], of the Poblitian tribe, Lucilius Iustus, Roman eques, having held all municipal offices, also dedicated four columns with the upper floor and pavement, painted, in the portico that leads to the public gymnasium, by the will of the people.
EDCS-04202453.summary: This is a dedication of architectural elements and decoration for a public gymnasium by a local dignitary who had served in all municipal offices.

EDCS-04202454.translation: Magia Procula, daughter of Gaius, for herself, for Coelia, freedwoman of Octavia, her mother, and for Gaius Magius, son of Sextus, her father, a living Augustan sexvir, from her own resources.
EDCS-04202454.summary: This inscription records a monument established by Magia Procula for herself, her mother, and her father, who was an Augustan sexvir.

EDCS-04202455.translation: Gaius Marcius Callistus, freedman of Thermus, a living sexvir, and Aemilia Euche, freedwoman of Publius Lucius Gaius, made this monument while alive; it will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04202455.summary: This inscription records a monument built by Gaius Marcius Callistus and Aemilia Euche, both freedpersons and living sexvirs, with the condition that it would not be inherited.

EDCS-04202456.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Metellus Hadrianus, while alive, erected this, as magistrate of the guild of blanket makers, a candidate, by their decree; the plot was purchased.
EDCS-04202456.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Marcus Metellus Hadrianus, who was the magistrate of the guild of blanket makers, to be effective during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202457.translation: Marcus Mucius Maximus Pob[lilia], decurion of Verona, and Mucia, daughter of Publius, I[---] V Vi[---]
EDCS-04202457.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the names and positions of at least two individuals, including a decurion of Verona and a woman identified by her father and possibly her own name.

EDCS-04202458.translation: To Naeviola, daughter of Lucius Naevius, who lived 22 years, 4 months, and 5 days. Marcus Clodius Candidus, son of Marcus, a four-man officer for dispensing justice and quaestor of the treasury in Verona, and priest of the Laurentes Lavinates.
EDCS-04202458.summary: This inscription records the death of Naeviola and lists the offices held by Marcus Clodius Candidus, including IIII vir iure dicundo, quaestor, and priest of the Laurentes Lavinates in Verona.

EDCS-04202459.translation: To Quintus Octavius Anemo, an excellent friend, an Augustan sexvir. Marcus Gavius Ionicus.
EDCS-04202459.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Marcus Gavius Ionicus to his friend Quintus Octavius Anemo, an Augustan sexvir.

EDCS-04202460.translation: To Quintus Octavius Primus, freedman of Quintus, of the Poblitian tribe, Six-member official of Augustus, priest of the youth. Octavia Tigris, to her deserving patron and husband, and to herself, made this while alive. I always used to seek and never lose gifts; now I am free from both. From a small house, having moved, my bones rest in a composed tomb. And the labor that was always with me from boyhood is now gone, and troublesome cares. I know not what I am now, nor what I was. Yet small comforts remain from my deed; those who praise the living enjoy gifts while alive. Live happily, to whom Fortune has been left behind.
EDCS-04202460.summary: This funerary monument, erected by a woman for her patron and husband, contains a lengthy autobiographical poem reflecting on life, death, and contentment, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-04202461.translation: Gaius Julius Hymenaeus, his partner, made this while alive for Ofillia QusetInta, priestess of the Roman rites.
EDCS-04202461.summary: This funerary monument, erected by a man for his partner, identifies her role as a priestess of local Roman rites.

EDCS-04202462.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Julius Justus to his natural son Publius Pomponius Epipodius Laurentis of Lavinium, for his outstanding devotion to him.
EDCS-04202462.summary: A funerary dedication by a father to his son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04202463.translation: [To his wife] Primai, daughter of Quintus, [and to] Lucius F. Martial, of the IVvirate.
EDCS-04202463.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication to a wife and a member of the IVvirate, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202464.translation: Quartua lived here as a widow for 80 years. Marcellinus, her most beloved brother, made [this] for his most beloved and most dutiful sister, who was deservedly loved by the whole church.
EDCS-04202464.summary: A funerary inscription for a widow named Quartua, erected by her brother, suggesting a Christian context.

EDCS-04202465.text_edition: \n Sexto Rubrio Sexti filio Poblilia Festo flamini Romae et Augusti decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202465.translation: To Sextus Rubrius Festus, son of Sextus, of the Poblitian tribe, flamen of Rome and of Augustus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202465.summary: This inscription records a public honor, likely an honorific monument or statue, bestowed upon Sextus Rubrius Festus, a flamen, by the town council.

EDCS-04202467.translation: For Sextus Salanius Mandatus Virianus, son of Sextus, of the Poblilia tribe, VIvir, made [this] while alive. [To] his wife Paulla, daughter of Sextus, freedwoman of Paconia; and to his son Sextus Virius Mercator, son of Sextus; and to Placido, freedman of Virius, Sextus' freedwoman, guardian of our patrimony.
EDCS-04202467.summary: A funerary monument erected by a VIvir for his family, including his wife, son, and a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202468.translation: Xystus, a fellow slave, gives [this] to Salvia Sacraria, from his own funds.
EDCS-04202468.summary: A funerary dedication by a fellow slave to Salvia Sacraria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202470.translation: Publius Servilius Agatho, freedman of Publius, VIvir Augustalis, made [this] while alive for his fellow freedpersons Servilia Agathemero, Agathonice, and Venda, and for his friend Quintus Messius Restitutus, and for his freedwoman Tyche.
EDCS-04202470.summary: A funerary dedication made by a freedman and VIvir Augustalis for his freed fellow slaves, friend, and freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202471.summary: This is a simple dedication or identification of Gaius Sollonius Senecio, who held the office of Six-member official.

EDCS-04202473.translation: Soterichus, freedman of Lucius, VIvir, silversmith, maker of vessels.
EDCS-04202473.summary: An epitaph for Soterichus, a freedman and VIvir who was a silversmith, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202474.translation: Stlania Cytheris, freedwoman of Lucius, made [this] for Lucius Stlanius Homuncio, VIvir Augustalis and of Neronia, her patron, and for herself.
EDCS-04202474.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedwoman for her patron and VIvir Augustalis, also including herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202475.translation: [For] Stlanius Polyclitus, father, VIvir of Claudialis, [and for] his mother Iucunda, [and for] his brother Lucius Stlanius Crescens.
EDCS-04202475.summary: A funerary dedication for a father, mother, and brother, with the father identified as a VIvir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202476.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Tullius Ursio, one of the six priests. [---] Tullius.
EDCS-04202476.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Tullius Ursio, a member of the *quattuorviri*, set up by Tullius.

EDCS-04202477.translation: [To his grandfather] Turpilius Longus, son of Quintus, of the Poblilia tribe, who held the office of iuris dicendi; [to his brother] Quintus Turpilius Macro, son of Quintus, of the Poblilia tribe; [and to his sister] Turpilia Secunda, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-04202477.summary: A funerary dedication for a grandfather, brother, and sister, all from the same family and tribe, with the grandfather holding a legal office, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202478.translation: To the departed spirits. For Quintus Tuticanus Erotis, son of Quintus, a Latin teacher, honored with the decurional ornaments as a *viri* of the Claudian guild. For Varai, daughter of Quintus Tuticanus Feliciano, and for themselves.
EDCS-04202478.summary: This is a funerary monument for Quintus Tuticanus Erotis, a teacher and *viri* of the Claudian guild in Verona, set up by his daughter and for his family.

EDCS-04202479.text_edition: \n Publius Valerius Cai filius Quintus Caecilius Quinti filius Quintus Servilius Quinti filius Publius Cornelius Publi filius IIIIviri murum portam turreis cluacas de decurionum sententia faciundum coeraverunt Publius Valerius Cai filius Quintus Caecilius Quinti filius probaverunt\n
EDCS-04202479.translation: Publius Valerius, son of Caius, Quintus Caecilius, son of Quintus, Quintus Servilius, son of Quintus, Publius Cornelius, son of Publius, as *quattuorviri*, arranged for the wall, gate, and towers to be built and the sewers to be made, by decree of the decurions. Publius Valerius, son of Caius, Quintus Caecilius, son of Quintus, approved [the work].
EDCS-04202479.summary: This inscription records a public works project overseen by four magistrates (*quattuorviri*) and approved by two others, involving the construction of fortifications and sewers, likely in the 1st century AD given the names.

EDCS-04202480.translation: Quintus Valerius Actius, a six-man official, made this for himself and his wife, Hostilia Irene, and his most dutiful daughter, Hostilia Chrysidis.
EDCS-04202480.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Quintus Valerius Actius for himself and his family.

EDCS-04202481.summary: An inscription identifying Publius Vassidius as a six-man official.

EDCS-04202482.translation: Lucius Udicasius Silanus, son of Caius, a six-man official and Augustalis, made this for himself and Runcasia.
EDCS-04202482.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Udicasius Silanus for himself and Runcasia.

EDCS-04202483.translation: Caius Veronius Carpus, a Claudialis Major six-man official, priest of the Mother of the Gods, made this for the Most Holy Mother and for Veronia Profima and Veronius Primus.
EDCS-04202483.summary: An inscription from a priest of the Mother of the Gods, Caius Veronius Carpus, dedicating it to the goddess and to Veronia Profima and Veronius Primus.

EDCS-04202484.translation: Marcus Veronius Epaphroditus, a six-man official and Augustalis, president of the guild of carpet-makers, made this for himself and Veronia Calliste.
EDCS-04202484.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Veronius Epaphroditus, president of the carpet-makers' guild, for himself and Veronia Calliste.

EDCS-04202485.translation: Lucius Vitorius Festus, son of Lucius, and Quintus Vitorius Severus, son of Lucius, six-man officials and Augustales, made this for themselves and their wives Cassia Maxima, daughter of Sextus, and Cominia Festa, daughter of Lucius, and Catia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, and for their sons Lucius Vitorius Ferox, son of Lucius, Caius Vitorius Festus, son of Lucius, and Quintus Vitorius Festus, son of Quintus, six-man officials and Augustales.
EDCS-04202485.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Vitorius Festus and Quintus Vitorius Severus, six-man officials, for themselves, their wives, and their sons who also held the title of six-man official.

EDCS-04202516.translation: To the departed spirits of Aedon Secutor, a gladiator who fought eight times, and Arianilla, who lived for 26 years.
EDCS-04202516.summary: A funerary inscription for Aedon Secutor, a gladiator, and Arianilla.

EDCS-04202517.translation: For Quintus Catio Photinus, the clothier. Nicephorus, his freedman, made this for his excellent patron and for himself while alive.
EDCS-04202517.summary: This is a dedication made by a freedman, Nicephorus, for his patron, Quintus Catio Photinus, a clothier, and for himself.

EDCS-04202518.translation: Caius Cornelius Meliboeus for himself and his tent-mate Sentia Elidi, a physician, and Sentia Aste.
EDCS-04202518.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Caius Cornelius Meliboeus for himself, his tent-mate Sentia Elidi, and Sentia Aste.

EDCS-04202519.translation: Marcus Flavius Festus, son of Lucius, [made this for] Aesius Tiniatius Quasaunai, son of Marcus. F. F. [meaning] Mario.
EDCS-04202519.summary: A dedication, possibly funerary, from Marcus Flavius Festus to Aesius Tiniatius Quasaunai and Mario.

EDCS-04202520.translation: Lucius Vitruvius Cerdo, freedman of Lucius, architect. To Caius Gavius Strabo, son of Caius, to Marcus Gavius Macro, son of Caius, and to Gavia, daughter of Marcus. Lucius Vitruvius Cerdo, freedman of Lucius, architect.
EDCS-04202520.summary: An inscription by two architects named Lucius Vitruvius Cerdo, dedicating the work to members of the Gavius and Gavia families.

EDCS-04202521.translation: To the departed spirits. For Generosus, the retiarius, the unconquered, who fought 27 fights, a native of Alexandria, who fought with his own valor.
EDCS-04202521.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Generosus, a gladiator of the retiarius type from Alexandria, who fought 27 matches.

EDCS-04202522.translation: To the departed spirits. For Glaucus, a native of Mutina, who died after 8 fights, having lived 23 years and 5 days. Aurelia to her deserving and beloved husband. I advise you, players on this stage, not to trust in Nemesis; thus I was deceived. Farewell.
EDCS-04202522.summary: This is a funerary monument for Glaucus, a gladiator from Mutina, who died after 8 fights, set up by his wife Aurelia, who also warns others about the goddess Nemesis.

EDCS-04202523.translation: To Lucius Helvidius Thallus, born in Amastris on the Pontus, lived 70 years and 7 days. Lucius Helvidius Marcianus, his brother.
EDCS-04202523.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Helvidius Thallus, with his brother Lucius Helvidius Marcianus mentioned, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202524.translation: To the departed spirits. Pardon of Dertona, tricked in 10 and 11 battles, lived 27 years. To Arriana, dearest wife, who lived with me for [years].
EDCS-04202524.summary: A funerary dedication for Pardon of Dertona and his wife Arriana, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202525.translation: Lucius Sollius Secundio, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe from Ticinum, made this monument for himself and for his wife Pailonia Maxima, daughter of Lucius. In the field, 15 feet; in front, 12 feet. This monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-04202525.summary: A self-funded funerary monument for Lucius Sollius Secundio and his wife Pailonia Maxima, specifying dimensions and legal provisions, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202526.translation: For Veronia Caesiana. Heliodorus and Caesianus, sons, to their most dutiful mother. And Heliodorus of Verona, to his dearest wife and for himself.
EDCS-04202526.summary: This is a funerary dedication from sons for their mother Veronia Caesiana and from Heliodorus for his wife and himself.

EDCS-04202528.translation: A path by permission of Quintus Gasius Pharus.
EDCS-04202528.summary: This inscription records a right of way granted by Quintus Gasius Pharus.

EDCS-04202529.translation: A path, one and a half feet wide, of Titus Vibius Eronis, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-04202529.summary: This inscription defines the width of a path belonging to Titus Vibius Eronis, a freedman.

EDCS-04202530.translation: To Marcus Acilius Advena, freedman of Marcus; to Lucius Valerius Atimetus, freedman of Lucius; to Acilia Veneria, beloved, aged 26.
EDCS-04202530.summary: A dedication honoring Marcus Acilius Advena, Lucius Valerius Atimetus, and Acilia Veneria, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202531.translation: To the departed spirits. To Adiabescatia Quintina, dearest wife, who lived with me.
EDCS-04202531.summary: A funerary dedication for Adiabescatia Quintina, by her husband Nonius Neoc, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202533.translation: Lucius Afinius Celer, son of Publius.
EDCS-04202533.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Afinius Celer, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202534.translation: To Quintus Afinius Scitus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04202534.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Afinius Scitus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202535.translation: Africanus, son of Caius, freedman of Secundus; Iuventius, [son of] Titus.
EDCS-04202535.summary: An epitaph possibly recording the names and parentage/manumission of Africanus and Iuventius, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202536.translation: Maria Africana made this while alive for her parents, Gaius Africanus Abascanthus and Africana Elpis, and for her deserving brother, Gaius Africanus Iunianus.
EDCS-04202536.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Maria Africana for her parents and brother.

EDCS-04202537.translation: Lucius Albius Virdacus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04202537.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Albius Virdacus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04202538.translation: To Allia Secunda, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-04202538.summary: A funerary epitaph for Allia Secunda, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202539.translation: Lucius Annius, son of Caius, of the Poblilia tribe, ordered this to be made for himself and for his brother Marcus Annius, son of Caius, by his will. The freedmen Diomedes and Anthus approved.
EDCS-04202539.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Lucius Annius for himself and his brother Marcus Annius, as stipulated in their will and verified by their freedmen, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04202540.translation: Lucius Annius Anthus ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04202540.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Lucius Annius Anthus in his will.

EDCS-04202541.summary: This is a naming inscription, likely a funerary monument, for Quintus Annius Balbus.

EDCS-04202542.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Iavolenus Severus placed this for his most devoted foster-sister, Annia Aquilina, who lived 39 years, 11 months, and 16 days, as she deserved.
EDCS-04202542.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caius Iavolenus Severus for his foster-sister, Annia Aquilina, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-04202543.translation: Secunda Annia, daughter of Lucius, here.
EDCS-04202543.summary: This inscription identifies Secunda Annia, daughter of Lucius, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-04202544.translation: To the Divine Shades of Lucius Ansicius Iustinus, Lucius Ansicius Quintianus for his most devoted brother.
EDCS-04202544.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Lucius Ansicius Quintianus to his brother, Lucius Ansicius Iustinus.

EDCS-04202546.text_edition: \n Lucius Aquilius Secundus Lucio Aquilio Charitoni et Publiciae Veneriae parentibus pientissimis libertis libertabusque\n
EDCS-04202546.translation: Lucius Aquilius Secundus for his most devoted parents, Lucio Aquilio Charitono and Publiciae Veneriae, and for their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04202546.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Aquilius Secundus for his parents and their freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-04202547.translation: To the Divine Shades of Arruntia Felicitas, Gaius Valerius.
EDCS-04202547.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Gaius Valerius to Arruntia Felicitas.

EDCS-04202548.translation: To Gaius Atilius, son of Publius.
EDCS-04202548.summary: This is a naming inscription, likely funerary, for Gaius Atilius, son of Publius.

EDCS-04202549.translation: Made during his lifetime by Gaius Atilius Florentinus, freedman of Castalius, for himself and for the Divine Shades of Julia Fortunata, his most deserving wife.
EDCS-04202549.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Gaius Atilius Florentinus for himself and his wife, Julia Fortunata.

EDCS-04202550.translation: To the Divine Shades of Atilia Cornelia, she lived with me for 9 years. Crispinus for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-04202550.summary: This funerary inscription by Crispinus commemorates his wife, Atilia Cornelia, noting their shared life of 9 years.

EDCS-04202551.translation: To the Divine Shades of Atilia Maxima, most innocent soul. Caonius Vitalis for his incomparable wife who lived with me without any dispute for 19 years, 2 months, and 9 days, who carried with her 46 years, who took with her honor and glory, my eternal farewell solace.
EDCS-04202551.summary: This elaborate funerary inscription by Caonius Vitalis commemorates his wife, Atilia Maxima, detailing her life span and virtues.

EDCS-04202552.translation: Made during her lifetime by Atilia Proba, freedwoman of Caius, for her parents Lucius and Chiteris, and for her brothers Primio and Lycoris.
EDCS-04202552.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Atilia Proba for her parents and brothers.

EDCS-04202553.translation: Quintus Atinius Capito, son of Sextus, made this monument for himself and his wife Atinia Faustae while alive; it will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-04202553.summary: A funerary monument set up by Quintus Atinius Capito for himself and his wife, stating that the monument is not hereditary.

EDCS-04202554.translation: Caius Atisius Felix, freedman of Caius, and Caius Atisius Gamus, freedman of Caius, made [this] for themselves and their families.
EDCS-04202554.summary: A funerary monument established by two freedmen for themselves and their families.

EDCS-04202555.translation: Quintus Atisius Iucundus, freedman of a woman, and Caius Autus Narcissus, made [this] for themselves, and for Mollonia Lecta, freedwoman of a woman, their partner, 15 feet in front and 12 feet in depth, and for her brother Heracla.
EDCS-04202555.summary: A funerary monument established by Quintus Atisius Iucundus and Caius Autus Narcissus for themselves, their partner Mollonia Lecta, and her brother Heracla, with dimensions provided.

EDCS-04202556.summary: A very brief funerary epitaph for a person named Atticus.

EDCS-04202557.translation: He ordered by his will to be [made] for himself and for his son Gaius Attius Gallus, son of Publius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04202557.summary: A funerary inscription specifying that the monument was to be made by will for the deceased and his son, Gaius Attius Gallus.

EDCS-04202558.translation: Caius Audasius, son of Boduacus; Audasia Paulla, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-04202558.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying two individuals: Caius Audasius, son of Boduacus, and Audasia Paulla, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-04202559.translation: and for Marcus Audasius Suavius, his comrade.
EDCS-04202559.summary: A dedication or mention of Marcus Audasius Suavius as a comrade, possibly part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-04202560.translation: Marcus Audasius Titurus, freedman of Marcus, made [this] for himself while alive, and for Antistia Quintai, daughter of Spurius, his wife, and for Castrucia, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-04202560.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Audasius Titurus for himself, his wife Antistia Quintai, and Castrucia.

EDCS-04202561.translation: Crescens for himself and Aufillena Primigenia, his freedwoman.
EDCS-04202561.summary: A dedication by Crescens for himself and his freedwoman Aufillena Primigenia.

EDCS-04202562.translation: For his wife. The place was granted and made by Aufellina Tacita Communis and her freedwoman Fausta.
EDCS-04202562.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aufellina Tacita Communis and her freedwoman Fausta made a burial plot for the wife of an unnamed individual.

EDCS-04202563.translation: There, freedwoman of a woman, Avillia.
EDCS-04202563.summary: An epitaph for Avillia, identified as a freedwoman.

EDCS-04202564.translation: Aulogenes made this monument here for Urbana, his fellow slave.
EDCS-04202564.summary: This inscription records that Aulogenes dedicated a monument to his fellow slave, Urbana.

EDCS-04202565.translation: Marcus Aurelius Euporus, freedman of our Emperor, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-04202565.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Euporus, a freedman of the emperor, who provided for his own burial.

EDCS-04202566.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelius Novarius, sweetest infant, lived 1 year and 27 days. Lucius Statius Diodorus and Aurelia Cleopatra, most unhappy parents.
EDCS-04202566.summary: A tombstone for an infant named Aurelius Novarius, set up by his grieving parents, Lucius Statius Diodorus and Aurelia Cleopatra.

EDCS-04202567.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Vettia Aureliana had this monument made according to her will for her most dutiful mother, Aurelia Calpurniana.
EDCS-04202567.summary: This funerary epitaph records a daughter's dedication for her mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202568.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Whoever travels this road, look back, I pray. Here lies the holy and most chaste December, stolen by cruel Fates, who was a beautiful youth, and whose life was long, but not allowed to live. Valentinianus, his son, formed this tomb out of his piety and sorrow, and may he remember his Manes. Aurelia Ursula to her sweetest husband, with whom I lived for 26 years. Valentinianus, Decentius, and [---] made this monument for their dearest father. Bl
EDCS-04202568.summary: This is a poignant epitaph for a young man named December, dedicated by his son and wife, lamenting his early death and commemorating his life, possibly dating to the late Roman period given the name Valentinianus.

EDCS-04202569.translation: Made for herself while alive by Baebia Secunda, daughter of Quintus, and for Quintus Baebius, son of Marcus, her father; Servilia Prima, her mother; Epidia Severilla, daughter of Quintus; Quintus Baebius Celer, Marcus Baebius Rusticus, Curatio Primus, Sacidius Benignus, her brothers, in land 15 feet deep and 15 feet in front.
EDCS-04202569.summary: This is a large funerary epitaph where Baebia Secunda, while alive, provided for herself and her family including parents, siblings, and a sister, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-04202570.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Lucius Bellicius Anthus and Bellicia Myrtis, Primitiva Hygia Successa Eutychia, to their well-deserving patrons.
EDCS-04202570.summary: This is a dedication to deceased patrons by their freedmen or clients, typical of Roman funerary inscriptions.

EDCS-04202571.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Gaius Bersasius Philocyrus. Crispinia Amphale, mother.
EDCS-04202571.summary: A mother dedicates a tombstone to her deceased son, Gaius Bersasius Philocyrus.

EDCS-04202572.translation: Gaius C. Gamianus for himself and for Quintia Valeria, his deserving wife, and for Helvidius Primon and Augustia Quartilla. While alive, I relinquished these places.
EDCS-04202572.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Gaius C. Gamianus for himself, his wife Quintia Valeria, and two other individuals, indicating he relinquished the burial plots during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202574.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Caesia Romana, to her freedwoman and educator of her four sons, well-deserving.
EDCS-04202574.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication for a deserving freedwoman who served as an educator for her patron's children.

EDCS-04202575.translation: For Gaius Caecilius Anthus, son of Gaius, a freedman.
EDCS-04202575.summary: This is a simple dedication for a freedman named Gaius Caecilius Anthus.

EDCS-04202576.translation: Caius [?]irius Caecilius Fortis for himself and for Caecilia Festiva, his most beloved freedwoman, and for his family.
EDCS-04202576.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by Caius [?]irius Caecilius Fortis for himself, his freedwoman Caecilia Festiva, and his relatives.

EDCS-04202577.translation: To [---]. Quintus Caecilius. His wife, M[---]mma.
EDCS-04202577.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription mentioning Quintus Caecilius and his wife.

EDCS-04202578.translation: Gaius Caecilius Montanus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, ordered this monument to be made for himself by his will.
EDCS-04202578.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument commissioned by Gaius Caecilius Montanus through his will.

EDCS-04202579.translation: Quintus Caecilius Nymphius made this monument while alive for himself and for Maecia Gemella, his companion (contubernalis), and for Caecilia Maeciana, his daughter; he will not pass on the inheritance.
EDCS-04202579.summary: This is a funerary monument established by Quintus Caecilius Nymphius for himself, his partner, and his daughter, with a stipulation regarding inheritance.

EDCS-04202580.translation: For Publius Caecilius Secundus, son of Publius, and [---].
EDCS-04202580.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication, likely funerary, for Publius Caecilius Secundus and another individual.

EDCS-04202581.summary: This is a dedication to Caecilia Chrysis and Anicetus.

EDCS-04202582.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Caesius Crocus.

EDCS-04202583.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Publius Caecinius Mercurius [erected this] for his well-deserving parents, Caecinia Saturnina and Nigidius Agatho.
EDCS-04202583.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a son to his parents, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202584.translation: Publius Caesius Mantuanus for himself and for Viria Festa, and for Catia Priscilla, and for Caesius Servanda, and for Caesius Iuliana, and for his own [family].
EDCS-04202584.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Publius Caesius Mantuanus for himself and several female relatives.

EDCS-04202585.translation: Marcus Caetronius and his wife Valeria.
EDCS-04202585.summary: This inscription records Marcus Caetronius and his wife Valeria, likely as part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202586.translation: [For] three [people], and for his grandmother Prisca, his wife, and for his comrade Calidius Tyche, this monument will not follow the heir: in front 24 feet, in depth.
EDCS-04202586.summary: This inscription details the terms of a funerary monument, specifying it is not inheritable and giving its dimensions, dedicated by an unnamed person to his wife and comrade.

EDCS-04202588.summary: This inscription records that Calventia, daughter of Marcus, created this monument.

EDCS-04202589.summary: This inscription records the name Publius Cassius, likely as an owner or dedicant.

EDCS-04202590.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cassius Rosus, with partial names or titles remaining.

EDCS-04202591.translation: Marcus Cassius Didymus, freedman of Marcus, and his wife Cassia Graphis, freedwoman of Marcus, daughter of Marcus, and his daughter Pupa, being alive, made this monument for themselves, for their patron, and for their daughter; it shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-04202591.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman, his wife, daughter, and patron, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE, with a clause ensuring the monument is not subject to inheritance.

EDCS-04202592.translation: To Cassius Optatus, son of Quintus, [his] son.
EDCS-04202592.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Cassius Optatus, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04202593.translation: Cassius, son of Caius, of the Poblilia tribe, Pirata, [illegible] Vatian.
EDCS-04202593.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Cassius, son of Caius, with additional fragmented information.

EDCS-04202594.translation: Lucius Cassius Princeps, freedman of Manlianus, [dedicated this] for himself.
EDCS-04202594.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Cassius Princeps, a freedman, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202595.translation: To Gaius Cassius Pudentus, son of Publius.
EDCS-04202595.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Cassius Pudentus, son of Publius, likely a funerary monument from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202596.translation: Senecio Cassius, son of Cassius Eburus, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04202596.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that the deceased, Senecio Cassius, arranged for the monument in his will, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202597.translation: Marcus Cassius Trophimus, freedman of Marcus, made [this] while alive for himself and for Gaius Cassius Crescentus, his son.
EDCS-04202597.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Cassius Trophimus, a freedman, for himself and his son, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202598.translation: Lucius Cassius Verecundus, son of Lucius, Long [perhaps Longinus or a cognomen].
EDCS-04202598.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Cassius Verecundus, son of Lucius, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202599.translation: Cassius Verecundus, son of Marcus, made [this] while alive for himself and for Nasonia Maxima, daughter of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-04202599.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Cassius Verecundus for himself and his wife, Nasonia Maxima, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202600.translation: Gaius Cassius Vespa, son of Gaius, and his wife Manlia Repentina, daughter of Titus, aged 30 years.
EDCS-04202600.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a married couple, Gaius Cassius Vespa and Manlia Repentina, with the wife's age provided, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202602.translation: and to Cassia Apollonia, his wife, here.
EDCS-04202602.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Cassia Apollonia as a wife, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202603.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication, possibly funerary, to Cassia Dori, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202604.translation: Cassia Exorata, daughter of Caius, made [this] while alive for herself and for Cassia Prisca, daughter of Caius, and for Antonia Marcella, daughter of Lucius, and for Syntropus Publicus, in front 25 feet, in the land 31 feet.
EDCS-04202604.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Cassia Exorata, daughter of Caius, for herself and several others, including land measurements, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202605.translation: To Quintus Cassius Alcmus, son of Quintus, freedman of Quintus; to Cassia Pneuma, daughter of Quintus, freedwoman of Quintus; to Cassia Phoetis, daughter of Quintus, freedwoman of Quintus; to Quintus Cassius Lito, son of Quintus, freedman of Quintus; to Quintus Cassius Vitalis, son of Quintus, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-04202605.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing multiple individuals from the Cassii family, including freedmen and their children, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202606.translation: Poblilia Suaduttio, daughter of Caius, wife of Marcus Crassus, son of Publius Scorpio, and Crispus, son of Crassus, made [this].
EDCS-04202606.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Poblilia Suaduttio and Crispus, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202607.translation: Castricius, son of Caius, from Posilla.
EDCS-04202607.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary or ownership marker, possibly indicating a person named Castricius, son of Caius, possibly originating from Posilla.

EDCS-04202608.translation: Marcus Catius, son of Marcus, Tertius. Marcus Tullius, freedman of Marcus, Attius. Caius Cominius, freedman of Caius, Felix. Caius Clodius, freedman of Caius, Paratus. Quartus Manlius, son of Cnaeus, for a shared cremation pyre, in front, feet.
EDCS-04202608.summary: This fragmented inscription lists several individuals, likely related to a funerary context, possibly detailing plot dimensions or ownership for a cremation area (ustrina), with some individuals identified by their patron or father.

EDCS-04202609.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Parents Kattia Augustina and Valerius Mukianus, and brothers Kastianus Mukianus and Augusta, dedicated this for their well-deserving Valerius Markellinus, who lived 28 years, 2 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-04202609.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by parents and siblings to Valerius Markellinus, providing his age at death, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202610.translation: To Marcus, son of Fir, and his wife Pato Ceiono.
EDCS-04202610.summary: This is a dedication to a man named Marcus, son of Fir, and his wife Pato Ceiono, likely from a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202611.translation: Viva made this for Publius Cervonius Orientis, her husband, and for herself.
EDCS-04202611.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Viva commissioned this monument for her husband, Publius Cervonius Orienti, and for herself.

EDCS-04202613.summary: This is a dedication to Charito, a freedman.

EDCS-04202614.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Her parents Chius and Caenis, for their most dutiful daughter, who lived 9 years, 3 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-04202614.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by parents to their young daughter, providing her age at death, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202615.translation: Manius Cincius, son of Publius, ordered this to be made for himself, for his father Publius Cincius, and for his mother Calidia Secunda, by his will.
EDCS-04202615.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Manius Cincius, son of Publius, commissioned this monument for himself, his father Publius Cincius, and his mother Calidia Secunda, according to his will.

EDCS-04202616.translation: Lucius Clodius Actius, freedman of Lucius, being alive, made this for himself, for his companion Clodia Amphale, and for his daughter Clodia Liberalis; in front 6 feet, in depth 15 feet.
EDCS-04202616.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by a living freedman for himself, his companion, and his daughter, specifying the dimensions of the plot, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202617.translation: Vivus made this for Caius Clodius Firminus, for his well-deserving wife Faleria Veneria, for his most dutiful daughter Faleria Valeriana, and for himself.
EDCS-04202617.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Vivus commissioned this monument for his wife Faleria Veneria, his daughter Faleria Valeriana, and himself.

EDCS-04202618.translation: Marcus Clodius Firmus for himself and for his father Quintus Clodius Severus.
EDCS-04202618.summary: This funerary inscription records that Marcus Clodius Firmus dedicated this monument for himself and his father Quintus Clodius Severus.

EDCS-04202619.translation: To the Divine Shades. Helvidia Primula made this for her husband Clodius Publius Gemellus, who deserved well, and for herself, while alive.
EDCS-04202619.summary: This funerary epitaph indicates that Helvidia Primula commissioned this monument for her deserving husband Clodius Publius Gemellus and for herself.

EDCS-04202620.translation: Caius Clodius Marianus, son of Publius.
EDCS-04202620.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple naming convention, possibly for a tomb or a dedication, identifying Caius Clodius Marianus, son of Publius.

EDCS-04202621.translation: Gaius Clodius Priscinus [erected this] to Gaius Pallelius Severus, the deserving.
EDCS-04202621.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Clodius Priscinus to Gaius Pallelius Severus.

EDCS-04202622.translation: Titus Clodius, son of Gaius, [erected this] for himself.
EDCS-04202622.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Titus Clodius for himself.

EDCS-04202623.translation: Manius Cluentius, son of Marcus, [of the tribe] Romilia.
EDCS-04202623.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a Roman citizen, Manius Cluentius, by his name, filiation, and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04202624.translation: Marcus Cluttius Pob., son of Publius, of the tribe Pob(lilia), being alive, made this for himself and his family: for his wife Pacillia Vasilla, daughter of Marcus; for his father Publius Cluttius Virius; for his mother Caelia Maxima; for his sister Cluttia Tertia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04202624.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by a living Marcus Cluttius for himself and his family, including his wife, parents, and sister, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202625.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Cluvia Elpis.

EDCS-04202626.translation: Gaius Quintius Andrea [erected this] to Quinta Cornelia, daughter of Gaius, of the Rufiali tribe.
EDCS-04202626.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Quintius Andrea to Quinta Cornelia.

EDCS-04202627.translation: Of Lucius Cornelius Aquitanus; in front 11 feet, in the land 20 feet.
EDCS-04202627.summary: This inscription likely marks property belonging to Lucius Cornelius Aquitanus, specifying its dimensions, possibly related to a tomb or land ownership, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202628.translation: Publius Cornelius Balbus, son of Publius, [and] Cornelia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04202628.summary: This inscription records the names of Publius Cornelius Balbus and Cornelia, likely for a shared tomb or dedication.

EDCS-04202629.text_edition: \n Lucio Cornelio Luci filio Poblilia Balbo Norbano\n
EDCS-04202629.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Balbus Norbanus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04202629.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Cornelius Balbus Norbanus, son of Lucius, likely from an altar or dedication stone.

EDCS-04202630.translation: Hera, a freedwoman of the Palatine tribe, ordered this to be made by will.
EDCS-04202630.summary: This inscription records a posthumous commission for a monument ordered by Hera through her will.

EDCS-04202631.translation: To Gaius Cornelius Montanus, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-04202631.summary: This is a dedication of a monument to Gaius Cornelius Montanus, a freedman.

EDCS-04202632.translation: Lucius Cornelius Pauper, son of Lucius, made [this] while alive for himself, and for his wife Attia Secunda, and for his daughter Maxxima; 25 feet in front, 16 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04202632.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Cornelius Pauper for himself and his family, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-04202633.translation: Cornelius Priscus for himself and for his daughter Digna.
EDCS-04202633.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Cornelius Priscus for himself and his daughter Digna.

EDCS-04202634.translation: Gnaeus Semnus, freedman of Gnaeus Cornelius Victamulus, and Cornelia Tusca, daughter of Gnaeus, daughter of Semnus. Titus Orbius, son of Titus, a native of Tuscus, [erected this] for his mother Meleotini. To Titus Valerius [---]orius and Valeria [---]alia. This monument will not pass to the heir, [in front] 10 feet [---].
EDCS-04202634.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Orbius for his mother and possibly other relatives, indicating it is a tombstone that does not pass to heirs.

EDCS-04202635.translation: Lucius Cornelius Sulla, son of Lucius, alive, made this for himself, and for Amanda, and for Marcus Cominius Vindicus, and for his own family.
EDCS-04202635.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Lucius Cornelius Sulla for himself and his family and dependents during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202636.summary: This inscription records the name Cornelia, daughter of Publius, likely for a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-04202638.translation: Cornelia Festa, daughter of Publius, made this monument for herself and for her son Lucius Valerius Burrus, seven years old, son of Lucius Valerius. Lucius Valerius Festus shall not follow the heir; may he be separated.
EDCS-04202638.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Cornelia Festa for herself and her young son, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202639.translation: To Cornelia Iulia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04202639.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cornelia Iulia, daughter of Publius, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202640.translation: Cornelia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, aged four.
EDCS-04202640.summary: This is a tombstone or epitaph for Cornelia Marcella, aged four, daughter of Marcus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202641.translation: Cornelia Maxsuma, daughter of Marcus, made this for herself and for her son Valerius Aprilis.
EDCS-04202641.summary: This is a funerary monument created by Cornelia Maxsuma for herself and her son Valerius Aprilis, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202642.translation: To Cornelia Restituta, from Publius Pomponius Hermes, to his most beloved wife, and to Cornelia Fengusa, his most revered mother-in-law, and to himself.
EDCS-04202642.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Publius Pomponius Hermes to his wife Cornelia Restituta and his mother-in-law Cornelia Fengusa, and also includes himself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202643.translation: Set up by [her] alive. To the Divine Manes. For Curtia Procilla, daughter of Gaius, an excellent patroness. For Publius Alfienus Maximus, son of Publius, Curtio Valeriano, son of Procilla. Curtia Callipolis, [her] freedwoman, for herself and her freedmen and freedwomen of both sexes.
EDCS-04202643.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Curtia Procilla by her freedwoman Curtia Callipolis, who also sets it up for herself and her freedmen, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202645.translation: Lucius Decius Blastus, to his well-deserving sister Sempronia Leontis, here.
EDCS-04202645.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Lucius Decius Blastus to his sister Sempronia Leontis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202646.translation: Gaius Didius Phronimus made this for himself while alive, and for his most cherished wife Atisia Prumula, who lived 45 years, with her husband 28 years.
EDCS-04202646.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Didius Phronimus for himself and his wife Atisia Prumula, specifying their ages and years of marriage, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202648.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Euphrosynus made this for himself while alive, and for his excellent wife Flavia Maxima.
EDCS-04202648.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gnaeus Domitius Euphrosynus for himself and his wife Flavia Maxima, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202649.translation: Marcus Domitius Montanus, son of Gaius, lies here.
EDCS-04202649.summary: This is a simple epitaph indicating the burial place of Marcus Domitius Montanus.

EDCS-04202650.translation: Lucius Domitius Querra, son of Gaius, from the tribe Poblilia.
EDCS-04202650.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Domitius Querra, son of Gaius, identifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04202651.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Domitius Rufus, son of Publius, likely a funerary marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202652.translation: [---] Domitius Saturninus, son of [---], for himself and for [---] Domitius, [---], his father.
EDCS-04202652.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Domitius Saturninus for himself and his father.

EDCS-04202653.translation: Gaius Domitius Severus, son of Gaius, made this for himself while alive, and for his father Gaius Domitius Veranius, and for his mother Cluviena Severa, and for his sister Domitia Marcella.
EDCS-04202653.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Gaius Domitius Severus for himself, his parents Gaius Domitius Veranius and Cluviena Severa, and his sister Domitia Marcella, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202655.translation: who lived 10 years and 7 months, for his son H H C. Eustochius and Valeria, his parents, to the most innocent, who deserved well.
EDCS-04202655.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy, set up by his parents.

EDCS-04202657.translation: [---] This monument will not pass to the heir. Cornelius, son of Publius. Valeria Galla, daughter of Publius, the unfortunate, for herself and [---].
EDCS-04202657.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a monument that does not pass to heirs, set up by Cornelius and Valeria Galla.

EDCS-04202658.translation: For good memory. Gaius Fabius Corniolus for himself and for his mother Catia Secunda, his wife Sattava Sabina, and his son Cogitatus.
EDCS-04202658.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Gaius Fabius Corniolus and his family members, including his mother, wife, and son.

EDCS-04202659.summary: This is an epitaph for Fabricia Festa, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04202660.translation: For Bathyllus, freedman of Sextus Fadius, aged 15 years.
EDCS-04202660.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Bathyllus, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-04202661.translation: Gaius Ficarius: this monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-04202661.summary: This inscription records Gaius Ficarius's intention that his monument should not pass to his heir, likely indicating a desire for it to remain in its intended location.

EDCS-04202662.translation: Aulus Fidius Iustus and Aulus Fidius Verus for their father Aulus Fidio Potenti, for their mother Ducenia Macrini, daughter of Ursa, and for themselves.
EDCS-04202662.summary: This funerary epitaph is set up by Aulus Fidius Iustus and Aulus Fidius Verus for their parents and themselves.

EDCS-04202663.translation: Firmius Lucius Faustus, freedwoman of Allia Quinti, called Specu.
EDCS-04202663.summary: This inscription records the name and freed status of an individual named Specu, a freedwoman of Allia Quinti.

EDCS-04202664.translation: To the Divine Manes. Firmia Aste.
EDCS-04202664.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Manes for Firmia Aste.

EDCS-04202665.translation: Firmia Lucia, daughter of Serena, made [this] for herself and for Marcus Cassius, son of Marcus Firmus.
EDCS-04202665.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Firmia Lucia Serena for herself and her husband Marcus Cassius Firmus.

EDCS-04202666.translation: Ergennus, son of Titus Firmius. Burial place: 20 feet in front, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202666.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, specifying its dimensions (20 feet in front and 30 feet in the field) and identifying Ergennus, son of Titus Firmius, as the owner or deceased.

EDCS-04202667.translation: Marcus Flavius Rufus, son of Spurius, and Flavia Maxuma, daughter of Caius, made [this] for themselves while alive and for their son.
EDCS-04202667.summary: This funerary epitaph was created by Marcus Flavius Rufus and Flavia Maxuma for themselves and their son.

EDCS-04202669.translation: For Gaius Fonteius Paternus, son of Lucius, for Gaius Paconius, son of Caius.
EDCS-04202669.summary: This inscription records dedications or commemorations for two individuals, Gaius Fonteius Paternus and Gaius Paconius.

EDCS-04202670.translation: To the departed spirits. Furia Crispinus, daughter of Quintus, lived for 5 years, 6 months, and 28 days. Furii Aphrodisius and Tryphosa to their sweetest granddaughter.
EDCS-04202670.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Furia Crispinus, set up by her grandparents.

EDCS-04202671.translation: To Titus Lusius Verecundus, aged 23 years and 5 months. Lusia Tertulla to her most dutiful son.
EDCS-04202671.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Lusius Verecundus, set up by his mother.

EDCS-04202672.translation: Quintus Gaesius Secundus to Quintus Gaesius Lucanus, and to the members of the household.
EDCS-04202672.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Gaesius Secundus to Quintus Gaesius Lucanus and other members of his household, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-04202673.translation: Galeria Tertia made this for herself, for her husband Lucius Volusius Publius, son of Publius, and for her son Lucius Volusius Hillyricus.
EDCS-04202673.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Galeria Tertia for herself, her husband, and her son.

EDCS-04202674.translation: Gallius, son of Lucius, made this.
EDCS-04202674.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gallius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04202675.translation: Made by Sextus Gavius, son of Sextus, aged 90 years; his wife Tertia, aged 30 years; his brother Quintus, aged 40 years; his son Quintus, aged 20 years; his son Optatus, aged 20 years.
EDCS-04202675.summary: This is a funerary dedication listing multiple family members, likely made by Sextus Gavius for himself and his deceased relatives.

EDCS-04202676.translation: Titus Gavius Gallio, son of Caius, for himself and for his wife Petronia Grata.
EDCS-04202676.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Titus Gavius Gallio for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04202677.translation: Publius Gavius Hilarus, freedman of Publius, made this for himself while alive; this monument will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-04202677.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Publius Gavius Hilarus for himself, specifying that it is not inheritable.

EDCS-04202678.translation: Marcus Gavius Hilarus, freedman of Marcus, from the Collina tribe, made this while alive for Gavia Eleutheris, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Lucius Gavius, his son, and for Quarta, his daughter, and for Gavia Marcella, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04202678.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Marcus Gavius Hilarus for himself and members of his family, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04202679.translation: To Lucius Gavius Onesimus, for his well-deserved service. Trocceia Severa.
EDCS-04202679.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, from Trocceia Severa to Lucius Gavius Onesimus, recognizing his merit.

EDCS-04202680.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Gaius Gavius Quintianus, son of Gaius, aged 14 years and 10 months. His unhappy father, Gaius Gavius Menodorus, dedicated this to his most devoted son, for it would have been more just for you to have made this for me, and for yourselves.
EDCS-04202680.summary: This is a tombstone erected by a father for his young son, expressing grief and a poignant reflection on mortality, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202681.translation: Marcus Gavius Severus made this while alive for himself and for his excellent and deserving wife Cornelia Epimelia, and for his freedmen Marcus Gavius Serenus and Cornelia Restituta.
EDCS-04202681.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Marcus Gavius Severus for himself, his wife, and his freedmen, indicating a family burial plot, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202682.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely identifying a tomb or monument belonging to Gavia, daughter of Caius Baebius.

EDCS-04202683.translation: Prima, the freedwoman of Gavia, made this for herself, for my slave or freedman Polyclitus, and for Lucius Calpurnius Vegetus.
EDCS-04202683.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Prima, a freedwoman, for herself, Polyclitus, and Lucius Calpurnius Vegetus.

EDCS-04202684.translation: To Gavia Valeria, for her son Valerius Gavianus and for herself.
EDCS-04202684.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gavia Valeria for her son and herself.

EDCS-04202685.translation: She ordered by her will that ashes and bones be made for herself.
EDCS-04202685.summary: This inscription records a woman, C. Laucilia Philocupta, who arranged for her own funerary arrangements by will.

EDCS-04202686.translation: Grata made this while alive for her husband Cassius, her son Imo, and her freedmen Phaedimus and Primigenius.
EDCS-04202686.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by a woman named Grata for her family and freedmen.

EDCS-04202689.translation: For Helpidius, freedwoman, and Iphidus, freedwoman, and for Publius Servilius Placidus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-04202689.summary: This inscription is a dedication for several freedpersons, indicating their relationship to a patron named Publius Servilius.

EDCS-04202690.translation: Gaius Herennius Urtika, son of Gaius, [dedicated this] to his mother Herennia Prima, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04202690.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicating a monument to a mother, Herennia Prima, by her son Gaius Herennius Urtika.

EDCS-04202691.translation: Hirmius Octavius for Carattia and Festa Corollina, and for Gaius Valerius Surus and for himself, a space of 30 feet.
EDCS-04202691.summary: This inscription records the purchase or allocation of funerary space by Hirmius Octavius for named individuals and himself.

EDCS-04202692.translation: Lucius Hostilius, son of Caius, ordered by his will that this be made for himself and for Vicarius.
EDCS-04202692.summary: This inscription states that Lucius Hostilius arranged for his own funerary monument and one for Vicarius through his will.

EDCS-04202693.translation: Lucius Julius, son of Sextus, son of Cor[...].
EDCS-04202693.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name and parentage of an individual, possibly for a funerary monument.

EDCS-04202696.translation: Publius Julius Apollonius, while alive, prepared this for himself and for his most obedient wife Attia Valeria, and he placed her deceased body in the tomb and dedicated the place to himself while alive. Publius Julius Apollonius for himself and his most obedient wife Attia Valeria.
EDCS-04202696.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Publius Julius Apollonius prepared a tomb for himself and his wife, Attia Valeria, while alive.

EDCS-04202697.translation: Caius Julius Didymus, freedman and heir, for his master well-deserving.
EDCS-04202697.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Caius Julius Didymus, a freedman and heir, for his patron.

EDCS-04202698.translation: For Gaius Julius Valerianus, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, and for Octavia Festa, daughter of Marcus, parents well-deserving, by Gaius Julius Paternus and Verus.
EDCS-04202698.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to parents, Gaius Julius Valerianus and Octavia Festa, by their sons Gaius Julius Paternus and Verus.

EDCS-04202699.translation: By the will of Iulia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04202699.summary: This inscription likely records a testament or a bequest made by Iulia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-04202700.translation: To Iulia Dacia, who lived 23 years and 18 days.
EDCS-04202700.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Dacia, recording her age at death.

EDCS-04202701.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iulia Fortunata, daughter of Caius, and Satria Calliste, daughter of Lucius. Marcus Iunius Encolpus and Satria Calliste [dedicated this].
EDCS-04202701.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Iulia Fortunata and Satria Calliste by Marcus Iunius Encolpus and Satria Calliste.

EDCS-04202702.translation: [dedicated this] to his sister Iunia Tertia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04202702.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicating a monument to a sister, Iunia Tertia.

EDCS-04202703.translation: To Iusta, daughter of Caius, daughter [of...].
EDCS-04202703.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a woman named Iusta, daughter of Caius, and possibly another parent or relation.

EDCS-04202705.translation: Of Marcus Ladavonius, son of Publius, and Sempronia Prima, wife of Publius.
EDCS-04202705.summary: This inscription appears to name or commemorate Marcus Ladavonius and his wife Sempronia Prima.

EDCS-04202706.translation: Quintus Furius Secundus made this for his incomparable wife Laelia Clementina and for himself while alive. Having died, you lie here, but you will live again with your living Secundus; Laelia owes it to your good deeds that she will not die. I pray you, gentle underworld spirits, and you, Tellus, watch over my wife. Go, spirits, lightly covering her bones, may she rest in peace. She lived 27 years.
EDCS-04202706.summary: This is a tombstone for Laelia Clementina, erected by her husband Quintus Furius Secundus, who also included himself and added a poem about her life and his devotion, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202707.translation: Lucius Laetorius, son of Caius, [son of...] P.
EDCS-04202707.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Lucius Laetorius, son of Caius.

EDCS-04202708.translation: Made by Lucius Lannus, son of Primi, for himself, and for his brother Caius Lannus, and for his wife Tordina, daughter of Tertullus, and for his daughter Lanna Firma, and for his friend Caius Cornelius Successus.
EDCS-04202708.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Lannus for himself and several family members and a friend.

EDCS-04202709.translation: To his friend who deserved well.
EDCS-04202709.summary: This is a short dedication to a deserving friend, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-04202710.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Livia Venusta, freedwoman and wife, who lived 23 years, 7 months, and 17 days. Marcus Livius Fortunatus [dedicated this] to his deserving freedwoman and wife.
EDCS-04202710.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Livius Fortunatus for his freedwoman and wife, Livia Venusta, including her age at death.

EDCS-04202712.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that begins to name individuals, possibly Caius Marcianus.

EDCS-04202713.translation: Lucius Magius, son of Marcus, ordered in his will that a place of 40 feet and a path of 100 feet as close as possible to the public road be made for himself in any part.
EDCS-04202713.summary: This is a testamentary disposition concerning land and a path, likely from a boundary stone or a legal document inscribed on stone.

EDCS-04202714.translation: For himself and for his father Magius, for his mother Publia daughter of Verai, for his wife Sentia Modesta, for Titus Sentius Primigenius.
EDCS-04202714.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial, listing several individuals, possibly for a tomb or a shared monument.

EDCS-04202715.translation: Publius Manilius Strabo, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, and Marcus Manilius Silo Abidianus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, made [this] for Marcus Manilius Pansa, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-04202715.summary: This funerary inscription records three individuals from the Manilius family, indicating they jointly commissioned a monument for another family member, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202716.text_edition: \n Maniliae Luci filiae Sabinae Lucius Cassius Luci filius Tebulus\n
EDCS-04202716.translation: Lucius Cassius Tebulus, son of Lucius, [dedicated this] to his daughter Manilia Sabina, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04202716.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Lucius Cassius Tebulus to his daughter Manilia Sabina.

EDCS-04202717.translation: Adonclanus Laelius Maximus Adens and Valeria Marcellina to their brother [or husband?] Marcello Vaericondi and his wife Caesia Funanca, a well-deserving brother.
EDCS-04202717.summary: This text appears to be an epitaph or a dedication honoring Marcello Vaericondi and Caesia Funanca, possibly by their relatives Adonclanus Laelius Maximus Adens and Valeria Marcellina.

EDCS-04202718.summary: This fragmented inscription likely names individuals, possibly in an epitaph or a list, but is too incomplete to provide further details.

EDCS-04202719.translation: To Marcus Masio, son of Marcus, his brother.
EDCS-04202719.summary: This is a dedication, likely an epitaph, honoring Marcus Masio by his brother.

EDCS-04202720.summary: This is a simple identifying inscription, likely for a tomb or a property, stating the name and freedman status of Lucius Matius.

EDCS-04202721.translation: To the divine spirits of Matronia Maternina, his most sweet wife, who lived 23 years.
EDCS-04202721.summary: This is an epitaph for Matronia Maternina, a wife who died at age 23, dedicated by her husband.

EDCS-04202722.translation: For Maxsima, daughter, 25 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202722.summary: This inscription seems to record land measurements or plot boundaries, possibly for a funerary plot dedicated to Maxsima.

EDCS-04202724.translation: To Publius Minucius, son of Publius, [great-]grandfather of Gaius Minucius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04202724.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a great-grandfather, Publius Minucius, by his descendant Gaius Minucius.

EDCS-04202725.translation: To the divine spirits of Lucius Naevius Iustinus, from his most beloved husband Gabia Marcella.
EDCS-04202725.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Naevius Iustinus, dedicated by his wife Gabia Marcella.

EDCS-04202726.translation: Gaius Nasonius, son of Quintus, made this (monument) while alive for himself and for his fellow soldier (contubernalis) in the army, Gaius Nasonius Ianuarius, and for Minucia Maxima, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04202726.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Nasonius for himself, a fellow soldier, and Minucia Maxima.

EDCS-04202727.translation: who [dedicated this] to Nonia Firmina, her most beloved mother, and Lucius Pontius Favorinus.
EDCS-04202727.summary: This inscription appears to be part of a dedication or epitaph, honoring Nonia Firmina by her daughter and Lucius Pontius Favorinus.

EDCS-04202728.translation: Gellia, daughter of Lucius, made this for herself and her freedmen Publius Novellius Fidus and Lucius Faldus Pauper.
EDCS-04202728.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gellia for herself and her freedmen.

EDCS-04202729.translation: Lucius Novellius Pupus, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, for his mother Clodia Maxima, daughter of Caius, and for his wife Serena.
EDCS-04202729.summary: A funerary monument made by Lucius Novellius Pupus for his family, set up during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202730.translation: Lucius Novellius Rhodanus ordered this to be made by his will to the Divine Shades.
EDCS-04202730.summary: A funerary monument ordered by Lucius Novellius Rhodanus in his will.

EDCS-04202731.translation: Novellia Severa, daughter of Quintus, and Caius Laelius Optatus ordered this to be made by their will.
EDCS-04202731.summary: A funerary monument ordered by Novellia Severa and Caius Laelius Optatus in their will.

EDCS-04202732.translation: Novicius of the Rabutii made this (monument) while alive for himself and for Publius Rabutius Glagus, his comrade.
EDCS-04202732.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Novicius of the Rabutii for himself and his comrade Publius Rabutius Glagus.

EDCS-04202733.translation: A burial place for Marcus Octavius Aprinus, son of Marcus, for Valerius Firmus, son of Lucius, and for his freedman Quintus Melio Auctus.
EDCS-04202733.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot for several individuals, including Marcus Octavius Aprinus and Valerius Firmus.

EDCS-04202734.translation: For Quintus Octavius Callistus: 30 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202734.summary: This records a land measurement, likely for a property or tomb belonging to Quintus Octavius Callistus.

EDCS-04202735.summary: This is a simple tombstone or marker identifying Marcus Octavius Fronto.

EDCS-04202736.translation: For Trophime, his most devoted daughter, and for his grandsons Gaius Octavius Profuturus and Marcus Caesius Expeditus, this monument with access, use, and water rights from the well.
EDCS-04202736.summary: A monument for Trophime and her descendants, including water rights from a well, likely set up by a family member.

EDCS-04202737.translation: Octavius Secundus, son of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and for Marcus Octavius Celer and his children.
EDCS-04202737.summary: A funerary monument created during the lifetime of Octavius Secundus for his family.

EDCS-04202738.translation: For Publius Octavius Secundus, his father, and for Gaius Licinius Phronimus, his friend.
EDCS-04202738.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument or grave to Publius Octavius Secundus and his friend Gaius Licinius Phronimus.

EDCS-04202739.translation: Patruus, father, mother [and] Octavia Exsorata, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-04202739.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavia Exsorata, likely erected by her father and mother, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202739.

EDCS-04202740.translation: To the divine shades of Octavia Firmina, who lived with me for 30 years and 4 months. Gaius Sentius Secundus, to his incomparable wife, and Gaius Sentius Octavianus, to his most longed-for mother.
EDCS-04202740.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Octavia Firmina by her husband Gaius Sentius Secundus and their son Gaius Sentius Octavianus.

EDCS-04202741.translation: Octavia Hesperis made this for her parents, Lucius Trebius Cinnamus and Octavia Chreste.
EDCS-04202741.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Octavia Hesperis for her parents, Lucius Trebius Cinnamus and Octavia Chreste, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202741.

EDCS-04202742.translation: Octavia Hilara, freedwoman of the woman, made this while alive for herself, and for her husband Lucius Caelus Staturai, freedman of Lucius, and for her son Lucius Caelus Firmus; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04202742.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument built by Octavia Hilara for herself, her husband, and her son, specifying that it is not hereditary, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202742.

EDCS-04202743.translation: Marcus Octavius Zeno, freedman of Marcus, made this while alive for his fellow freedwoman Octavia Sabini and for himself.
EDCS-04202743.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument built by Marcus Octavius Zeno for himself and his fellow freedwoman Octavia Sabini, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202743.

EDCS-04202745.translation: To Opellius Secundus, son of Marcus, sister of Blandus (freedwoman of Blandus?), 35 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202745.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Opellius Secundus, possibly a relative of Blandus, with a measurement of land.

EDCS-04202748.translation: To the Divine Shades. Tertulla, daughter of Caius, aged 13.
EDCS-04202748.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tertulla, daughter of Caius, who died at the age of 13, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202748.

EDCS-04202749.translation: Petronianus, who lived 22 years and 42 days. Petronia Euchariste, most unhappy mother, [made this] for herself and [him].
EDCS-04202749.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Petronianus at the age of 22 years and 42 days, and was erected by his mother, Petronia Euchariste, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202749.

EDCS-04202750.translation: Quintus Plotius, son of Publius, Pubilia Destinata, (made this) while alive.
EDCS-04202750.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Quintus Plotius and Pubilia Destinata for themselves.

EDCS-04202751.translation: [This monument was made for] Essius, for himself, for his wife, and for Plotia.
EDCS-04202751.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument erected by Essius for himself, his wife, and Plotia, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202751.

EDCS-04202752.translation: Marcus Poblicius Linus made this while alive for himself and for his wife, Poblicia Attica.
EDCS-04202752.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Poblicius Linus for himself and his wife, Poblicia Attica.

EDCS-04202754.translation: For Gaius Poblicius Quartio, father. For Remmia, daughter of Caius, mother. For Gaius Poblicius Verus, son of Caius, brother. Poblicia Severa, daughter of Caius, ordered this monument to be made by will for them and for herself.
EDCS-04202754.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument ordered by Poblicia Severa in her will for her father, mother, brother, and herself, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202754.

EDCS-04202755.translation: Poblicia Festa, daughter of Quintus, [made this] for herself and for Gaius Bisios, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04202755.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument erected by Poblicia Festa for herself and Gaius Bisios, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202755.

EDCS-04202756.translation: [This monument was made] for Pollio, son of Gaius. Crispinus, brother, ordered this to be made by will.
EDCS-04202756.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument ordered by Crispinus in his will for his brother Pollio, identified by the EDCS ID EDCS-04202756.

EDCS-04202757.translation: Quintus Pompeius for Lucio and for his friend Gaius Novellius Crescent[---].
EDCS-04202757.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Quintus Pompeius for Lucio and his friend Gaius Novellius Crescent[---].

EDCS-04202758.translation: In memory of Pompeia Leidis, Pompeia Thois to her sister.
EDCS-04202758.summary: This inscription is a memorial dedication made by Pompeia Thois to her sister Pompeia Leidis.

EDCS-04202759.translation: To Pomponia Aristoclia, her foster child.
EDCS-04202759.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Pomponia Aristoclia by her foster child.

EDCS-04202760.translation: [The living] made (this). Publius Pontius Iucundus, freedman of Publius, for himself and for Publius Pontius Festus, son of Publius, patron, and for Gavia Lycnis, freedwoman of Quintus, his fellow soldier (contubernalis), and for Publius Pontius Agricola, his son.
EDCS-04202760.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Pontius Iucundus for himself, his patron, his fellow soldier, and his son.

EDCS-04202761.translation: Prima, daughter of Marcus Popillius, made this while alive.
EDCS-04202761.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Prima, daughter of Marcus Popillius, commissioned this monument during her lifetime.

EDCS-04202763.translation: Marcus Cavarasius Secundus made this for his incomparable wife Postumia Paulina, who lived with him for 37 years without any complaint, and for himself while alive, and for his mother Postumia Paulina, who deserved well, and for his grandmother Cavarasia Faustina, and for her who nursed him.
EDCS-04202763.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication and dedications to his wife, mother, grandmother, and nurse by Marcus Cavarasius Secundus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202765.translation: Primigenius for himself and for Elpis, his freedwoman, and for anyone who deserved well of me, and for Antonia Marcella Tutilia.
EDCS-04202765.summary: This is a self-dedication and dedication by Primigenius for his freedwoman Elpis, a benefactor, and Antonia Marcella Tutilia.

EDCS-04202767.translation: For himself and for Probanda, his concubine.
EDCS-04202767.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication and a dedication to Probanda, the dedicator's concubine.

EDCS-04202768.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for Publius Publius Aedultus Primus.

EDCS-04202769.translation: upius, son of Pupi, made this for himself.
EDCS-04202769.summary: This inscription records a self-commissioned monument by upius, son of Pupi.

EDCS-04202772.translation: Gaius Quintius Herma for himself and for Hedista Quintia, his fellow soldier (in barracks), 13 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202772.summary: This inscription is a self-dedication and a dedication to his contubernalis Hedista Quintia, specifying dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202773.translation: Marcus Quintius Moderatus, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, made this while alive for his father Publius Quintius Pollio and for Romaniai Moderatai.
EDCS-04202773.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Marcus Quintius Moderatus for his father and another individual, likely his mother.

EDCS-04202774.translation: Quintia Heuresis, daughter of Aelius Quinti's freedwoman Myrsine.
EDCS-04202774.summary: This is a funerary dedication naming Quintia Heuresis and her mother Myrsine, a freedwoman of Aelius Quinti.

EDCS-04202775.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintia Rufilla.

EDCS-04202776.translation: For the divine spirits. Epaphroditus made this while alive for his incomparable and deserving wife, Quintia Valeria.
EDCS-04202776.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Epaphroditus for his wife Quintia Valeria.

EDCS-04202777.translation: Rabutia Tertia, daughter of Marcus, ordered this monument to be made by her will for her father Cosmo, freedman of Marcus Rabutius, and for her mother Quartia, daughter of Publius, and for Maxuma, daughter of Cai.
EDCS-04202777.summary: This funerary dedication was erected by Rabutia Tertia by her will for her parents, Cosmo and Quartia, and another woman named Maxuma.

EDCS-04202778.translation: Publius Rantulanus Ianuarius, son of Publius, aged 5 years.
EDCS-04202778.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius Rantulanus Ianuarius, who died at the age of five.

EDCS-04202779.translation: Lucius Rhodius Festus made this while alive for his excellent companion Cassia Maxima, and for Publius Papirius Eutyches, and for himself.
EDCS-04202779.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Rhodius Festus for his companion Cassia Maxima, Publius Papirius Eutyches, and himself.

EDCS-04202781.translation: For his mother Exorata, daughter of Cai, and for his wife.
EDCS-04202781.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a mother named Exorata and the wife of the dedicator.

EDCS-04202782.translation: Aurelius Maiorinus for his parents and his wife Cletga Meria Rutilia, his dearest wife, and for Publius Rutilius Bregontius and his wife Quintia Marcella, and for Afrodisia, his daughter-in-law.
EDCS-04202782.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aurelius Maiorinus for his parents, his wife, and also includes inscriptions for Publius Rutilius Bregontius and his wife, and Afrodisia.

EDCS-04202783.translation: To the divine shades. To Caius Rutilius Callias. Magia Festa, to her well-deserving husband, and for herself.
EDCS-04202783.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Magia Festa for her husband, Caius Rutilius Callias, and herself.

EDCS-04202784.translation: For Gaius Rutilius Valerius, son of Gaius, who lived 24 years. Gavia Thamyrilla, his unhappy mother, will not follow this monument for an heir.
EDCS-04202784.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Rutilius Valerius, erected by his mother Gavia Thamyrilla, who states she will not be buried here.

EDCS-04202785.translation: Odianus Saturninus for himself and for his wife Ntia Padana.
EDCS-04202785.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely for a tombstone, recording the names of Odianus Saturninus and his wife Ntia Padana, with the former preparing for both.
