EDCS-04202787.translation: From the will of Publius Sacidius, son of Quintus, of the Poblilia tribe; [for] Publius Sacidius, son of Publius, aged 6 years; [and for] Marcus Sacidius, son of Publius, aged 4 years.
EDCS-04202787.summary: This inscription, likely from a tomb, records the beneficiaries of a will, including young children of the Sacidii family.

EDCS-04202788.translation: Paullus, a freedman, made [this] for Quintus Salasius, son of Quintus, and for Lucilia, his wife, and for himself.
EDCS-04202788.summary: This funerary epitaph records that a freedman named Paullus dedicated a monument for his patrons Quintus Salasius and Lucilia, and himself.

EDCS-04202789.translation: While alive, Lucius Scaevinus, son of Lucius, freedman Quadratus, made [this] for himself and for Aucta, his sister, to the Divine Spirits.
EDCS-04202789.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Lucius Scaevinus Quadratus, a freedman, dedicated a monument to the Divine Spirits for himself and his sister Aucta during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202790.translation: Secunda made [this] in the name of her daughter Julia Prisca. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-04202790.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Secunda commemorates her daughter Julia Prisca, likely a child, using a common epitaph formula.

EDCS-04202791.translation: To Seia Charite, who lived 17 years and 7 months. Quintus Catius Nicephorus, to his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-04202791.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Quintus Catius Nicephorus for his wife, Seia Charite.

EDCS-04202792.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Aguius Hypatus [made this] for his most devoted wife, Seia Synethia.
EDCS-04202792.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Marcus Aguius Hypatus dedicated a monument to the Divine Spirits for his wife Seia Synethia.

EDCS-04202794.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sem E, son of Publius, and C. ri Maius and [Valerius?], his(?) brothers, placed [this].
EDCS-04202794.summary: This funerary epitaph, dedicated to the Divine Spirits, records the names of Sem E and his brothers who erected the monument.

EDCS-04202795.translation: While alive, Gaius Sempronius Cassianus made [this] for himself, and for Quintus Macrius Severus, and for Sempronia Procula, his deserving wife, and for Quintus Macrius Lucius, and for Trau... Sabinus, and for Gaius Stacius Carpus, and for Lucius Ufruicius Tertius.
EDCS-04202795.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Gaius Sempronius Cassianus, during his lifetime, dedicated a monument to himself and a number of other individuals including his wife and friends.

EDCS-04202796.translation: Gaius Sempronius, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, Reita.
EDCS-04202796.summary: This inscription, likely from a tombstone, records the name and tribal affiliation of Gaius Sempronius Reita.

EDCS-04202797.translation: Senicio, son of Solitus, by his will ordered [this] to be made for himself and for Banilla, his wife.
EDCS-04202797.summary: This funerary epitaph indicates that Senicio, son of Solitus, arranged through his will for a monument to be erected for himself and his wife Banilla.

EDCS-04202798.translation: Sergia Propasis, freedwoman of Caius, made this while alive.
EDCS-04202798.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedwoman for herself.

EDCS-04202799.translation: To Sextus Sertorius Clemens, for his father and mother. Sextus Sertorius Volumnianus, son of Caius, and Tertulla, daughter of Lucius, wife, (made this) while alive.
EDCS-04202799.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Sextus Sertorius Clemens for his parents, Sextus Sertorius Volumnianus and Tertulla.

EDCS-04202800.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Lucius Sertorius, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe; for his father Sisenna; and for his mother Terentia Maxima, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04202800.summary: This funerary epitaph honors parents and a father.

EDCS-04202801.translation: Gnaeus Servilius Syrus, freedman of Gnaeus, made this while alive.
EDCS-04202801.summary: A funerary epitaph recording that Gnaeus Servilius Syrus, a freedman, commissioned his own tombstone during his lifetime.

EDCS-04202802.translation: Lucius Domitius Proculus, son of Lucius, for his mother Servilia Procula.
EDCS-04202802.summary: This funerary epitaph records a son's dedication to his mother.

EDCS-04202805.translation: Flavia Sabina made this for her well-deserving husband, Staberius Sympheronitus, to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-04202805.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her husband.

EDCS-04202806.translation: To Staedia Paulina, my incomparable wife. Hail, innocent soul, Staedia Paulina. Lucius Cantinius Hermippus.
EDCS-04202806.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an "incomparable wife," likely set up by her husband.

EDCS-04202807.translation: Made by Statia Severa, daughter of Publius, for her father Publius Statius Dentunus, son of Lucius, and for her mother Cassia Maxima, daughter of Quintus; and for her grandmother Maecana Secunda, daughter of Aulus.
EDCS-04202807.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by a daughter to her father, mother, and grandmother.

EDCS-04202808.translation: To Lucius Statius Eutychanus, aged 26 years and 11 months. Lucius Statius Eutychus and Statia Onesis for their most dutiful son.
EDCS-04202808.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their son who died at a young age.

EDCS-04202809.translation: Gaius Statius Mancinus, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe; 11 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202809.summary: An inscription indicating land dimensions, likely related to property ownership or a boundary marker, belonging to Gaius Statius Mancinus.

EDCS-04202810.translation: Statia Frequens, freedwoman of Statia, made this while alive for herself, and for her mother Statia Icone, freedwoman of Marcus; and for her brothers Marcus Statius Phelletus, freedman of Marcus, and Marcus Statius Modestus, freedman of the woman; and for her fellow freedman Marcus Statius Verecundus.
EDCS-04202810.summary: This funerary dedication, made by a freedwoman for herself, also includes family members and a fellow freedman.

EDCS-04202811.translation: To the departed spirits. Statia Severa, daughter of Publius, ordered this to be made by her will, with her freedman in charge.
EDCS-04202811.summary: A funerary epitaph where Statia Severa, through her will, arranged for her burial monument, managed by her freedman.

EDCS-04202812.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Suestidia Firmina, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-04202812.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Suestidia Firmina.

EDCS-04202813.translation: Publius Sulpicius Valens, son of Publius, for himself and for Lucius Sulpicius Po...
EDCS-04202813.summary: This funerary epitaph records a man making provisions for himself and another individual, possibly a family member.

EDCS-04202814.translation: Viva made this, Sulpicia Eutychis, for herself and for Gaius Sulpicius Philargyrus, her excellent freedman, and for Marcus Rutilius Restitutus, her associate, in front 23 feet, in the land 23 feet.
EDCS-04202814.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Sulpicia Eutychis for herself and her freedman and associate, likely indicating the dimensions of a burial plot.

EDCS-04202815.translation: Living, he made this for himself and for Sulpicia Galla, freedwoman of Publius, Publius Sulpicius Ac...
EDCS-04202815.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Publius Sulpicius Ac... made a monument for himself and his freedwoman Sulpicia Galla.

EDCS-04202817.translation: Marcus Tenatius, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04202817.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Tenatius, son of Lucius, stipulated the creation of a monument in his will.

EDCS-04202818.translation: Marcus Tenatius Labeo, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04202818.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Marcus Tenatius Labeo, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04202819.translation: Marcus Tenatius Niger, son of Gaius, son of Publius, by his will ordered this to be made for himself and for his father Gaius Tenatius Probus, son of Publius, and for his mother Domitia Secunda, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04202819.summary: This funerary inscription, set up by will, honors Marcus Tenatius Niger and his parents, Gaius Tenatius Probus and Domitia Secunda.

EDCS-04202820.translation: Blandia, daughter of Gaius, for her husband Lucius Tenatius, son of Publius.
EDCS-04202820.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Blandia, daughter of Gaius, for her husband Lucius Tenatius, son of Publius.

EDCS-04202821.translation: Lucius Tenatius Proclus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04202821.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Lucius Tenatius Proclus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04202822.translation: Lucius Tenatius Varianus for himself and for Macrina, his dearest sister, in front 50 feet, in the back 60 feet.
EDCS-04202822.summary: This funerary inscription by Lucius Tenatius Varianus for himself and his sister Macrina also specifies the dimensions of a burial plot.

EDCS-04202823.translation: For Lucius Firmus, of the Tenatii family, son of Maximus.
EDCS-04202823.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Firmus, son of Maximus, seemingly connected to the Tenatii family.

EDCS-04202824.translation: For Prisca, daughter of Quintus Terentius; this space is here, and for Quarta Terentia, 12 feet in front.
EDCS-04202824.summary: An epitaph allocating burial space to Prisca and Quarta Terentia, indicating specific dimensions for their graves.

EDCS-04202825.translation: For Lucius Terentius Sceptus and Severus, freedmen.
EDCS-04202825.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Terentius Sceptus and Severus, who are identified as freedmen.

EDCS-04202826.translation: Titus Thorius Rufus, son of Lucius, made this tomb for himself and for his freedwoman Gavia Prima, his wife.
EDCS-04202826.summary: This epitaph records a tomb built by Titus Thorius Rufus for himself and his wife, a freedwoman named Gavia Prima.

EDCS-04202827.translation: Severa, daughter of Lucius Thorius, made this while alive for herself, and for her husband Marcus Ennius Primus, son of Marcus, and for her daughter Collina, daughter of Lucius Baebius.
EDCS-04202827.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Thoria Severa for herself, her husband Marcus Ennius Primus, and her daughter Baebia Collina.

EDCS-04202828.translation: To Publius Trossius Primio, son of Publius, most dutiful, aged 20, and to his dearest wife Tossia Musica.
EDCS-04202828.summary: This epitaph commemorates Publius Trossius Primio, who died at the age of 20, and his wife Tossia Musica.

EDCS-04202830.translation: Marcus Travius Sabinus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04202830.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Marcus Travius Sabinus.

EDCS-04202831.translation: Marcus Travius Thallus made this monument for himself while alive; he will not be followed by an heir, and for Livia Psyche.
EDCS-04202831.summary: This inscription records a tomb built by Marcus Travius Thallus for himself and Livia Psyche, stipulating that no heir will inherit it.

EDCS-04202833.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Lucius Lucretius Epictetus for Trophimes, who deserved well.
EDCS-04202833.summary: This dedication is to the Divine Spirits and honors Trophimes, possibly a freedman or friend of Lucius Lucretius Epictetus.

EDCS-04202834.translation: Lucius Truttedius, son of Publius, and his wife Publilia, made this for themselves while alive, and for Baebia Secunda, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-04202834.summary: This epitaph records a tomb built by Lucius Truttedius and his wife Publilia for themselves and for Baebia Secunda.

EDCS-04202835.translation: To Publius Truttedius Philomusus, freedman of Publius, his father, and to Magia Maxima, daughter of Marcus, his mother.
EDCS-04202835.summary: This epitaph honors Publius Truttedius Philomusus and his mother Magia Maxima.

EDCS-04202836.translation: For Publius Truttedius Tertius, son of Publius, their brother, from Publilia.
EDCS-04202836.summary: This epitaph commemorates Publius Truttedius Tertius, son of Publius and brother of Publilia.

EDCS-04202837.translation: Fausta made this for her father Tullius.
EDCS-04202837.summary: This inscription records that Fausta erected a monument for her father, Tullius.

EDCS-04202838.translation: To Gaius Tullius Hermetus, patron, and to Verania Vera, his companion, for their well-deserved services.
EDCS-04202838.summary: This epitaph honors Gaius Tullius Hermetus, the patron, and his companion Verania Vera, for their merits.

EDCS-04202839.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Turpilius, son of Cassianus, [dedicated this] to his most dutiful father.
EDCS-04202839.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a father by his son.

EDCS-04202840.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vagidia, identified by her father's name.

EDCS-04202842.translation: Lucius Valentinus Eutychus made this while alive for himself and for his most esteemed patron Lucius Valentinus Senecio.
EDCS-04202842.summary: A tombstone erected by Lucius Valentinus Eutychus for himself and his highly respected patron, Lucius Valentinus Senecio.

EDCS-04202843.translation: Curfia Marcelina for her husband Titus Valentino Pisinioni, an excellent man deserving of kindness, and for his three brothers, and for her parents, made this while alive and for herself.
EDCS-04202843.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Curfia Marcelina for her husband Titus Valentino Pisinioni, his brothers, and her parents, also including herself.

EDCS-04202844.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Lucius Valerius.

EDCS-04202845.translation: Sextus Valerius, son of Sextus, for himself and for his wife Secunda Valeria, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04202845.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Valerius and his wife Secunda Valeria.

EDCS-04202846.translation: [Dedicated to] Gaius Valerius Antiochus, father, and Laevia, mother, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04202846.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring a father named Gaius Valerius Antiochus and a mother named Laevia.

EDCS-04202847.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Valerius Apollonius.
EDCS-04202847.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Valerius Apollonius.

EDCS-04202848.translation: Publius Valerius, son of Marcus Poblilia, and Capito, for himself and for Lucius Valerius, son of Publius, and Valeria, daughter of Publius, and Secunda, wife of Gaius Calpurnius, daughter of Secunda, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04202848.summary: This funerary epitaph records a will specifying the construction of a monument for several individuals, including the dedicator Publius Valerius and his family.

EDCS-04202850.translation: To Maxima, daughter of Lucius, and to Festus, son of Gaius Valerius, and to Lucius Valerius.
EDCS-04202850.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maxima and two individuals named Lucius Valerius, one of whom is identified as the son of Gaius Valerius Festus.

EDCS-04202851.translation: Gaius Valerius Gratus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-04202851.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Valerius Gratus as the freedman of a Gaius.

EDCS-04202852.translation: On these estates, a mesolaeum was built for Valerius Ianuarius of Ho [amount] silver.
EDCS-04202852.summary: This inscription records the construction of a mesolaeum on specific estates for Valerius Ianuarius, with a mention of a silver amount.

EDCS-04202853.translation: Gaius Valerius Ismarus, freedman of Gaius, made this while alive for himself, and for Valeria Aprilis, freedwoman of Gaius, and Valeria Prisca, freedwoman of Ismarus, and Gaius Valerius Imerus, freedman of Ismarus, and Ismyrine, freedwoman of Ismarus, and for his son-in-law Marcus Satrius Surus.
EDCS-04202853.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by the freedman Gaius Valerius Ismarus for himself, his family members (including freedmen and freedwomen), and his son-in-law.

EDCS-04202854.translation: Valeria Optata, freedwoman of Lucius Valerius Lucius son of Lucusta Valeria, made this.
EDCS-04202854.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Valeria Optata, a freedwoman, to her patrons Lucius Valerius and Lucusta Valeria.

EDCS-04202855.translation: Publius Valerius Montanus, son of Spurius, made this while alive for his mother Suria Dometia and father Ilarion, and for his own freedmen.
EDCS-04202855.summary: A tombstone erected by Publius Valerius Montanus during his lifetime for his parents, Suria Dometia and Ilarion, and his freedmen.

EDCS-04202856.translation: Quintus Valerius Macer, son of Quintus Valerius Poblilia and Poblicia Maxima, daughter of Marcus Oriclo, made this.
EDCS-04202856.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quintus Valerius Macer for himself and his family members, including his father and mother.

EDCS-04202857.translation: Gaius Valerius son of Gaius Pastorius, Quintus Valerius son of Gaius Lucusta, Gaius Valerius son of Gaius Secundus, and Clodia Paulla, daughter of Publius, [all children of] Gaius Valerius.
EDCS-04202857.summary: This inscription lists four individuals, likely siblings, all sons and daughters of a certain Gaius Valerius.

EDCS-04202858.translation: Gaius Valerius Planta, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, ordered this monument to be made by his will for himself, for Amphion, freedman of Gaius, and for Clara, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-04202858.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned in a will by Gaius Valerius Planta for himself and two freedpersons.

EDCS-04202859.translation: Marcus Valerius Valens made this for his most devoted wife, Iulia Muntana, aged 30.
EDCS-04202859.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Marcus Valerius Valens for his deceased wife, Iulia Muntana.

EDCS-04202860.translation: Caius Valerius Valerianus made this memorial while alive for himself, for my daughter Valeria Maxima, for my son Caius Valerius Firmus, for my wife Campullia Euthycia, for my freedman Valeria Secunda, and for my sister Valeria Secunda; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04202860.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument erected by Caius Valerius Valerianus for himself and several family members, explicitly stating it is not to be inherited.

EDCS-04202862.translation: Valeria Candida made this while alive and placed it for Gaius Marcius Cosmio, who deserved well.
EDCS-04202862.summary: A funerary epitaph where Valeria Candida erected a monument for Gaius Marcius Cosmio, indicating his worthiness.

EDCS-04202863.translation: Ordered to be made by will for Valeria Galla, freedwoman of Publius Lucius.
EDCS-04202863.summary: This inscription indicates that a monument was commissioned in a will for Valeria Galla, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04202864.translation: For Valeria Hecale, freedwoman of Gaius, her mother.
EDCS-04202864.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to Valeria Hecale, a freedwoman, by her mother.

EDCS-04202865.translation: Valeria Hecale, freedwoman of a woman, made this for herself and Ennychus while alive.
EDCS-04202865.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Valeria Hecale for herself and Ennychus, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202866.translation: For his most dutiful daughter Valeria Maxima, daughter of Gaius, and for himself; Herennia Augurina, daughter of Publius, [dedicates this].
EDCS-04202866.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Herennia Augurina for her daughter Valeria Maxima and for herself.

EDCS-04202867.translation: Valeria Secunda, daughter of Marcus, made this memorial while alive for herself.
EDCS-04202867.summary: This funerary monument was self-funded by Valeria Secunda, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-04202868.translation: To the divine spirits and the memory of Valerius Valerianus, Caius Maecius Atilianus [dedicated this] to his wife and to his mother Maecia Frontona and Atiliana.
EDCS-04202868.summary: A funerary dedication by Caius Maecius Atilianus to his wife and mother, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202869.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly referring to a person's parentage, date unknown.

EDCS-04202870.translation: To the divine spirits of Cetra, daughter of Marcus
EDCS-04202870.summary: A funerary dedication to Cetra, daughter of Marcus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202871.translation: To Marcus Varius, son of Lucius, patron, to Minicia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, and to himself. Marcus Varius Secundus, freedman of Marcus, Capria Secunda, daughter of Caius, Varia Maxima, daughter of Marcus, his daughter. This monument will not follow its heir.
EDCS-04202871.summary: A complex funerary monument set up by Marcus Varius Secundus and his wife Capria Secunda for themselves, their deceased family members including Marcus Varius (father or patron) and Minicia Tertia, with a clause specifying that the monument is not to pass to an heir, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202872.translation: Cornelius Favor ordered this to be made by will for his sister Varilla.
EDCS-04202872.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by will by Cornelius Favor for his sister Varilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202873.translation: Lucius Vassidius Mercator, son of Marcus, made this while alive for himself, and for Marcus Vassidius Fronton, son of Marcus, and for Gaius Vassidius Clement, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04202873.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Vassidius Mercator for himself and other family members, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202874.translation: He made [this] while alive for himself and for his fellow associate Lucius Vassidius Paederotes.
EDCS-04202874.summary: A funerary dedication made by an individual while alive for himself and a fellow colleague, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202875.summary: A fragmentary inscription continuing the previous one, referring to Vassidia Secunda, date unknown.

EDCS-04202876.translation: To the Divine Manes. Verecundus, the beloved pet, lived 18 years, 2 months, and 11 days. Gaius Vesius Martialis [erected this].
EDCS-04202876.summary: This epitaph commemorates the life of Verecundus, a beloved pet, and was likely erected by Gaius Vesius Martialis in the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202878.translation: To Marcus Vergilius Antiochus, only son of Marcus, for himself and Pamphilus.
EDCS-04202878.summary: A funerary dedication by an individual for himself and Pamphilus, potentially for his son Marcus Vergilius Antiochus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202879.translation: Vergilia Secunda, daughter of Quintus, ordered this to be made by will.
EDCS-04202879.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by will by Vergilia Secunda for herself or others, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202880.translation: Publius Veronius Amphion made [this] while alive for himself and for his deserving wife Magia Festa and for his family.
EDCS-04202880.summary: A funerary dedication made by Publius Veronius Amphion while alive for himself, his wife Magia Festa, and his family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04202881.translation: Veto, the relics. Publius Veronius Callistus, an excellent man, lies here.
EDCS-04202881.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Publius Veronius Callistus, described as an excellent man.

EDCS-04202882.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Veronius Pusittio, to his incomparable wife Veronia Charita, who lived 28 years, 4 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-04202882.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Veronius Pusittio to his wife Veronia Charita, who lived 28 years, 4 months, and 7 days.

EDCS-04202883.translation: Veronius Celsus, while alive, made this for his incomparable wife Veronia Chreste, and for his most devoted mother Chrestus Veronensium.
EDCS-04202883.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Veronius Celsus for his wife Veronia Chreste and his mother Chrestus Veronensium.

EDCS-04202885.translation: To Marcus Vettius Firmus, son of Cnaeus, his brother.
EDCS-04202885.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Vettius Firmus, son of Cnaeus, from his brother.

EDCS-04202886.translation: Cnaeus Vettius Sabellius, son of Cnaeus.
EDCS-04202886.summary: This inscription appears to be a name and filiation, possibly part of a larger monument.

EDCS-04202887.translation: To Gaius Vibius Eutyches, Vibiae Potentilla, to his parents, to his uncle Gaius Vibius Aphrodisius, to his grandmother Vibiae Aphrodisia, Gaius Vibius Callistio.
EDCS-04202887.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Vibius Callistio to his parents, uncle, and grandmother.

EDCS-04202888.translation: While alive, Publius Vibius Eutyches made this for his most devoted son Publius Vibius Proculus, who lived 23 years and 15 days, and for himself, and for his wife Vibiae Elena, and for his family spirits.
EDCS-04202888.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Publius Vibius Eutyches for his son, himself, his wife, and his family.

EDCS-04202890.translation: To Titus Vipsanius Cteson, to his son Marcus Vipsanius Clement, to his son Lucius Vipsanius Lucanus.
EDCS-04202890.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus Vipsanius Cteson and his sons Marcus and Lucius Vipsanius.

EDCS-04202891.translation: Gaius Virius Pulumo, son of Cai, while alive, made this for himself, and for his wife Brica, daughter of Marcus, with 12 feet in front and 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202891.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gaius Virius Pulumo for himself and his wife Brica, also specifying burial plot dimensions.

EDCS-04202892.translation: Tertia, sister of Cilo Viria, daughter of Publius, 12 feet in front and 45 feet in the field.
EDCS-04202892.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary marker for Tertia, sister of Cilo Viria, daughter of Publius, also specifying burial plot dimensions.

EDCS-04202893.translation: Marcus Viriatius Zosimus, his freedman, saw to its construction.
EDCS-04202893.summary: This is a funerary monument constructed by a freedman for his patron, Marcus Viriatius Zosimus.

EDCS-04202894.translation: Marcus Virraus, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, and for his wife Satellia Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, and for his son Marcus Virraus.
EDCS-04202894.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Virraus for himself, his wife, and his son, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04202895.translation: Lucius Voconius Severus, son of Lucius, made this for his son Quinto Voconio Festo, and for himself, and for his freedman Successeo.
EDCS-04202895.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Voconius Severus for his son, himself, and his freedman.

EDCS-04202896.translation: Gaius Volesius Luculus, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and for his wife, Barbilia Quarta, daughter of Gaius, and for his own people.
EDCS-04202896.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Gaius Volesius Luculus for himself, his wife, and his family, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202897.translation: Lucius Clodius, son of Marcus, made this while alive for his father-in-law Marcus Volumnius, and for his wife Volumnia Serena, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04202897.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Clodius for his father-in-law and wife.

EDCS-04202898.translation: Volusia Secunda for herself and for Prisca.
EDCS-04202898.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Volusia Secunda for herself and Prisca.

EDCS-04202899.translation: To the Divine Shades. Alcides made this while alive for his most rare wife, Zosime, daughter of Italus, a deserving woman.
EDCS-04202899.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Alcides to his wife Zosime, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-04202925.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Benenata, the wife of the dedicator.

EDCS-04202934.summary: This fragment seems to refer to Hicarethon, a freedman, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-04202940.summary: This fragment appears to be part of a name and filiation, possibly from a larger inscription.

EDCS-04202945.translation: Eusebia tiled with her people 120 feet.
EDCS-04202945.summary: This inscription records Eusebia tiling an area of 120 feet with her associates, likely a public or private building project.

EDCS-04202946.summary: This inscription appears to mark a plot of land of 120 feet belonging to Himeria.

EDCS-04202947.translation: Marinus the attendant with his people, 10 feet.
EDCS-04202947.summary: This inscription appears to mark a plot of land of 10 feet belonging to Marinus the attendant.

EDCS-04202948.translation: Here rests in peace the holy Valens, bishop, who lived about 85 years and held the episcopate for 8 years, 8 months, and 19 days, and departed on the 7th day before the Kalends of August, after the consulship of the most excellent Lampadius and Orestes, in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-04202948.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Bishop Valens, dating to after 535 AD based on the consuls.

EDCS-04202949.translation: Here rests in peace Placidia, a distinguished girl educated in letters, who lived 10 years and 18 days and 11 months, and was buried on the 5th day before the Ides of October, after the consulship of Lampadius and Orestes.
EDCS-04202949.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Placidia, a young girl, dating to after 535 AD.

EDCS-04202950.translation: Sacred to Cuslanus. Lucius Octavius Crassus, son of Gaius, and Lucius Gaius Octavius Martialis and Macer, sons of Lucius.
EDCS-04202950.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the deity Cuslanus by Lucius Octavius Crassus and his sons.

EDCS-04202952.translation: To Ihamnagalle and Sqnnagalle. Gaius Octavius Capito, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04202952.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Octavius Capito to the deities Ihamnagalle and Sqnnagalle.

EDCS-04202953.translation: Lucius Cassius Trophimus, freedman of Fulvus, paid his vow to the Iunones.
EDCS-04202953.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cassius Trophimus fulfilling a vow to the Iunones, likely in the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202954.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Minervae ceterisque dis deabusque pro salute Luci Servili Domiti Valeri Frontonis Luciani clarissimi iuvenis et Luci Servili Iuliani viri egregii patris et Valeriorum Valentis Caesoniani et Iuliani iunioris equo publico Servilius Callimorphus libertus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202954.translation: For Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno, Minerva, and all the other gods and goddesses, for the safety of Lucius Servilius Domitius Valerius Fronto Lucianus, most distinguished youth, and Lucius Servilius Iulianus, excellent man and father, and the Valerii Valentis Caesoniani and Iuliani the younger, of the equestrian order, Servilius Callimorphus, his freedman, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04202954.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Servilius Callimorphus for the safety of several prominent individuals, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202955.translation: Marcus I() M() gave this as a gift to Jupiter.
EDCS-04202955.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a gift to Jupiter by Marcus I() M().

EDCS-04202956.translation: Publius Calpurnius Mandatus ordered this to be made by will, from 800 sesterces, for Jupiter Felvennus.
EDCS-04202956.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a commission for a monument to Jupiter Felvennus funded by a will.

EDCS-04202957.translation: Flavius with his people to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-04202957.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Flavius and his group.

EDCS-04202958.text_edition: \n Minervae Augustae Papiri Threptus et Prepusa votum solverunt locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04202958.translation: Papiri Threptus and Prepusa paid their vow to Minerva Augusta. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202958.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Minerva Augusta, with the site granted by local authorities, likely in a provincial town in the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202960.translation: Lucius Iariovidius Cato, freedman of Gaius, paid his vow willingly and deservedly, and made this inscription with his own hand.
EDCS-04202960.summary: This inscription records Lucius Iariovidius Cato fulfilling a vow and personally creating the inscription, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202963.translation: To Minerva Augusta. Publius Cavaresius Proculus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04202963.summary: This votive inscription dedicates an offering to Minerva Augusta by Publius Cavaresius Proculus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202964.translation: For Gaius Aufustius Severus, son of Gaius. Rufria Secunda, daughter of Publius, his mother, paid her vow willingly and deservedly to Minerva.
EDCS-04202964.summary: This inscription records a mother, Rufria Secunda, fulfilling a vow to Minerva for her son, Gaius Aufustius Severus, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04202965.translation: To Minerva Augusta, Gaius Domitius Maximus gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04202965.summary: A dedication to Minerva Augusta by Gaius Domitius Maximus, likely a private individual making a votive offering.

EDCS-04202967.translation: To the August Nymphs and the Genius of the district of Arusnatium. Gaius Papirius Threptus.
EDCS-04202967.summary: This inscription records a dedication to local deities by Gaius Papirius Threptus.

EDCS-04202968.translation: To Saturn. Marcus Flavius Festus and Cusonia Maxima, priestess.
EDCS-04202968.summary: A dedication to the god Saturn by Marcus Flavius Festus and Cusonia Maxima, a priestess.

EDCS-04202969.translation: To Sol and Luna. Quintus Sertorius Festus, son of Quintus, priest.
EDCS-04202969.summary: A dedication to Sol and Luna by Quintus Sertorius Festus, son of Quintus, who served as a priest.

EDCS-04202971.text_edition: \n Vestae Quintus Cassius Marci filius Varus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04202971.translation: Quintus Cassius Varus, son of Marcus, gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Vesta.
EDCS-04202971.summary: A votive inscription dedicating a monument to Vesta by Quintus Cassius Varus.

EDCS-04202973.translation: Gaius Africanius Capito, son of Caius, priest.
EDCS-04202973.summary: An inscription recording Gaius Africanius Capito, son of Caius, as a priest.

EDCS-04202974.translation: Sextus Cariaus, son of Sextus, priest, and Pomponisia Severa, daughter of Pontus, priestess.
EDCS-04202974.summary: A dedication by Sextus Cariaus, son of Sextus, a priest, and Pomponisia Severa, daughter of Pontus, a priestess.

EDCS-04202975.translation: [?]us, son of Marcus, priest, and Cassia Iustina, daughter of Publius, priestess, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04202975.summary: An inscription recording [?]us, son of Marcus, as priest and Cassia Iustina, daughter of Publius, as priestess, likely made by decree of the local council.

EDCS-04202976.translation: Publius Fannius, son of Marcus, Gaius Masurius, son of Caius, Sabinus, Publius Cutius, son of Publius, Bibulus, Lucius Aemilius, son of Caius, Malo, overseers of the shrines, had this made from the shrine's funds and they also approved it.
EDCS-04202976.summary: Four individuals, Publius Fannius, Gaius Masurius Sabinus, Publius Cutius Bibulus, and Lucius Aemilius Malo, served as overseers of shrines and are recorded as having funded and approved this work.

EDCS-04202977.translation: [?] son of Marcus, to Gaius Domitius, son of Lucius, [?] son of Gaius, they had this made from the shrine's funds.
EDCS-04202977.summary: This inscription records the funding and construction of something by [?] son of Marcus, for Gaius Domitius, son of Lucius, [?] son of Gaius.

EDCS-04202978.translation: Gaius Octavius Capito, son of Marcus, dedicated to the memory of his relatives, in the name of Lucius Publius Octavius Clemens, sons of Marcus, and of the Staberi brothers, the best of men. He dedicated the Udisna Augusta on private land.
EDCS-04202978.summary: Gaius Octavius Capito dedicated the Udisna Augusta on private land in memory of his relatives, the Octavii and the Staberi brothers.

EDCS-04202979.translation: To Publius Octavius Verecundus, son of Publius, pontiff of the sacred rites of the temple, by his uncle Capito.
EDCS-04202979.summary: Capito dedicated this to his nephew, Publius Octavius Verecundus, son of Publius, who served as pontiff of the sacred rites of the temple.

EDCS-04202980.translation: To Octavia Magna, daughter of Marcus, priestess of the Arusnates district. Octavius Capito, Lucius Octavius Clemens.
EDCS-04202980.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Octavia Magna, daughter of Marcus, a priestess of the Arusnates district, and mentions Octavius Capito and Lucius Octavius Clemens.

EDCS-04202981.translation: Strabo, son of Publius, priest of Stibadia, made this at his own expense as a votive offering.
EDCS-04202981.summary: This is a dedication made by Strabo, a priest, likely for a religious purpose.

EDCS-04202982.text_edition: \n Cornel(ius) Cai filius Augustianus et Tullia Tulli filia Cardelia flaminica\n
EDCS-04202982.translation: Cornelius Augustianus, son of Caius, and Tullia Cardelia, daughter of Tullius, [priestess].
EDCS-04202982.summary: An inscription naming Cornelius Augustianus and Tullia Cardelia, who held priestly offices, possibly related to a funerary monument or public dedication.

EDCS-04202983.translation: Lucius Redonius Planta, son of Quintus, priest, [dedicated and] erected [this monument].
EDCS-04202983.summary: An inscription recording the dedication and erection of a monument by Lucius Redonius Planta, who held the office of flamen.

EDCS-04202984.text_edition: \n Publius Valerius Publi filius Montanus flamen mannisnavius dedit\n
EDCS-04202984.translation: Publius Valerius Montanus, son of Publius, priest, dedicated this.
EDCS-04202984.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of a monument by Publius Valerius Montanus, who held the office of flamen.

EDCS-04202985.summary: This inscription is a fragment that names Rufrius, a priest, but is otherwise incomplete.

EDCS-04202988.text_edition: \n Quinto Caicilio Cisiaco Septicio Picai sic Caiciliano sic procuratori Augustorum et pro legato provinciai sic Raitiai sic et Vindeliciai sic et Vallis Poeninai! auguri flamini divi Augusti et Romai sic Caius Ligurius Luci filius Voltinia Asper |(centurio) cohortis I civium Romanorum ingenuorum\n
EDCS-04202988.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Cisiacus Septicius Picai, Caicilianus, procurator of the Emperors and acting legate of Raetia, Vindelicia, and the Poenine Alps, augur, and priest of the deified Augustus and of Rome, Caius Ligurius Asper, son of Lucius, [a] centurion of the first cohort of Roman citizens of good birth, [dedicated this].
EDCS-04202988.summary: A complex dedication by Caius Ligurius Asper to Quintus Caecilius Cisiacus Septicius Picai, a high-ranking imperial official and priest, likely dating to the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04202989.translation: To Lucius Octavius Severianus, son of Lucius, governor, who lived 21 years and 29 days. Lucius Octavius Severus and Tratoria Severa, most unhappy parents, [erected this] to their most longed-for son.
EDCS-04202989.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Octavius Severianus, who died at the age of 21, erected by his grieving parents.

EDCS-04202990.translation: Gnaeus Arrius Caetronius, son of Gnaeus, duovir for judging, quaestor of the treasury, for himself and for his most holy wife Clodia Hedone, with whom he lived 38 years. By his own hand while living. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-04202990.summary: A funerary dedication made by Gnaeus Arrius Caetronius for himself and his wife Clodia Hedone, recording his public offices and their long marriage.

EDCS-04202991.translation: Calpurnia Prisca, daughter of Lucius, for herself and for Lucius Calpurnius Quadratus, her father, and Valeria Secunda, daughter of Caius, her mother, and Lucius Calpurnius Proculus, brother, a six-man official and Augustalis, [---]
EDCS-04202991.summary: This is a funerary inscription or a dedication listing several family members, including Calpurnia Prisca and her relatives, and mentioning her role as a six-man official and Augustalis.

EDCS-04202992.translation: Publius Numitorius Asclepiades, freedman of Publius, a six-man official and oculist doctor, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his wife, Sempronia Galla, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04202992.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Publius Numitorius Asclepiades, a freedman, oculist, and six-man official, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04202995.translation: Marcus Laeini and Celer, aediles, and a goddess.
EDCS-04202995.summary: This inscription records Marcus Laeini and Celer as aediles, possibly in relation to a cult of a goddess.

EDCS-04202996.translation: Gaius Sevius Valerianus Aesianus, son of Caius.
EDCS-04202996.summary: This is a simple funerary or commemorative inscription for Gaius Sevius Valerianus Aesianus.

EDCS-04202997.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Volumnius Proculus, son of Sextus.

EDCS-04202999.translation: To the departed spirits. Arria Protis, who lived 17 years, 5 months, 12 days. Parents.
EDCS-04202999.summary: A funerary epitaph for Arria Protis, who died at a young age, erected by her parents.

EDCS-04203000.translation: Aurelius Niceta for Aurelia Pieris, his most virtuous wife.
EDCS-04203000.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aurelius Niceta for his wife, Aurelia Pieris.

EDCS-04203001.translation: Gaius Caesius Agrippa, son of Caius.
EDCS-04203001.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Gaius Caesius Agrippa.

EDCS-04203002.summary: This is a dedication to Clodia, identified as a wet nurse.

EDCS-04203003.translation: Cosconia Vera, daughter of Gaius, ordered this to be made by her son Vero, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-04203003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her son Vero, naming his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04203004.translation: Lucius Cusonius Stutinus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203004.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Cusonius Stutinus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04203005.translation: Lucius Egnatius Niger, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203005.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Egnatius Niger, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04203006.translation: Egnatia Severa erected [this] for herself and for her most dutiful daughter Octavia Exorata.
EDCS-04203006.summary: A funerary dedication made by Egnatia Severa for herself and her daughter Octavia Exorata.

EDCS-04203008.translation: Gaius Magius Optatus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203008.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Gaius Magius Optatus, son of Gaius.

EDCS-04203009.translation: Quintus Nigidius Festus, son of Syri, and Atilia [unclear].
EDCS-04203009.summary: This inscription begins to identify Quintus Nigidius Festus, son of Syri, and Atilia, but is incomplete.

EDCS-04203010.translation: Quintus Nigidius Tertius, son of Festus.
EDCS-04203010.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Quintus Nigidius Tertius, son of Festus.

EDCS-04203013.translation: Marcus Octavius Campanus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04203013.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Marcus Octavius Campanus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04203014.text_edition: \n Lucio Octavio Luci filio Staberi nepoti Capitoni Caius Octavius Capito patruus posuit\n
EDCS-04203014.translation: Gaius Octavius Capito erected this for Lucius Octavius Capitolinus, son of Lucius, grandson of Staberius.
EDCS-04203014.summary: A tombstone erected by a paternal uncle for his nephew, indicating family relationships and possibly social standing through the mention of the grandfather.

EDCS-04203015.translation: Gaius Octavius Fronto, son of Lucius, made this (monument) while alive for himself and for Octavia Secunda, daughter of Publius, and for [Oc]tav[...].
EDCS-04203015.summary: A funerary monument set up by Gaius Octavius Fronto for himself and his wife Octavia Secunda, with a partial inscription for another individual.

EDCS-04203016.translation: Gaius Octavius Macer, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203016.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Gaius Octavius Macer, son of Gaius.

EDCS-04203017.summary: This incomplete funerary epitaph identifies Octavius Quadratus, son of an unnamed father.

EDCS-04203018.translation: Marcus Octavius Sto, son of Marcus, aged 35, grandson of Marcus, aged 14.
EDCS-04203018.summary: This funerary epitaph records the names and ages of Marcus Octavius Sto and his grandson, also named Marcus.

EDCS-04203019.translation: Domitia Clara, freedwoman of the woman, set this monument up for Quintus Pontius Capito, son of Quintus, while alive; it will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04203019.summary: A funerary monument set up by a freedwoman for her patron or associate, stipulating that the monument is not to be inherited.

EDCS-04203020.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Octavius Firminus (erected this) for his wife Pontia Justa, most innocent.
EDCS-04203020.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for an 'innocent' wife, set up by her husband.

EDCS-04203021.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Semus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04203022.translation: Lucius Tenatius Cato, son of Caius.
EDCS-04203022.summary: A simple inscription identifying an individual by name and parentage, likely on a tombstone or public marker.

EDCS-04203023.translation: Lucius Tenatius Varus, son of Marcus, [was buried here/erected this].
EDCS-04203023.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph for Lucius Tenatius Varus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04203026.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph possibly for Lucius Valerius.

EDCS-04203027.translation: Valerius, son of [---], [was buried here/erected this].
EDCS-04203027.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph for a man named Valerius, son of an unknown father.

EDCS-04203028.translation: Lucius Valerius, son of Marcus, for himself and for Cassia, freedwoman of the woman, and [...]
EDCS-04203028.summary: A funerary monument begun by Lucius Valerius for himself and his freedwoman Cassia, but the inscription is incomplete.

EDCS-04203029.translation: Gaius Valerius Clemens, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203029.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Valerius Clemens, son of Gaius.

EDCS-04203030.translation: Lucius Valerius Coxsinus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203030.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Coxsinus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04203031.translation: Marcus Varius Maximus, son of Varius.
EDCS-04203031.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Varius Maximus, son of Varius.

EDCS-04203032.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Valeria Festiva, daughter of Caius, (erected this) for her most dutiful mother, Valeria Primitiva, deserving well.
EDCS-04203032.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld, set up by a daughter for her highly esteemed mother.

EDCS-04203033.translation: Severus [erected this] for Quintus Vevus, son of Messi.
EDCS-04203033.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Severus for Quintus Vevus, son of Messi.

EDCS-04203043.translation: To Gaius Rabutius Campanus of Claudiens[is].
EDCS-04203043.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary or votive, to Gaius Rabutius Campanus, who was from the area of Claudiens[is].

EDCS-04203044.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Octavius Marcellianus Firmus and Viraia Paternus for their well-deserving father Octavius Firminus Marcellianus, and for Viraia Paternus for her most loving wife, deserving well.
EDCS-04203044.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for a father and his wife, set up by their son and daughter-in-law, indicating a multi-generational family memorial.

EDCS-04203045.translation: P. C. F. fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203045.summary: A votive inscription indicating the fulfillment of a promise or vow by an individual identified by initials.

EDCS-04203046.translation: Sabinus, son of [---], a good man.
EDCS-04203046.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sabinus, son of an unknown father, describing him as a good man.

EDCS-04203047.translation: Sextius Teudius' plot, 30 feet in front.
EDCS-04203047.summary: This is a boundary marker indicating the extent of Sextius Teudius' property, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203048.translation: Greetings, most innocent souls. Lucius Octavius(?) Trebiasius Maximus for his most beloved mother Valeriana, who lived 36 years and 8 days, and for Lucius Octavius(?) Lucilianus, most noble father, who lived 51 years, 3 months, and 22 days. Here lies the couple of most chaste fame, for whom it was not permitted to live even twenty years; whom fate too quickly snatched away. Vetor. To the Spirits of the Underworld. [It is not possible to read] my name other than this.
EDCS-04203048.summary: A funerary inscription to the spirits of the underworld, commemorating parents (Valeriana and Lucius Octavius Lucilianus) with detailed ages and a lament for their short lives, set up by their son, Vetor.

EDCS-04203049.translation: To Mincus and Benacus, Successus, son of Quintus Samicius Mirinus, has paid his vow willingly and deservedly. Quintus Samicius Successus again.
EDCS-04203049.summary: This is a dedication to Mincus and Benacus, with Successus paying a vow, possibly on behalf of himself and another, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203050.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Publius Velius Genialis, Publius Velius Hyginus, Velia Rufinia, Velia Hyginia. Alexander, a freedman, and for himself.
EDCS-04203050.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman named Alexander for his deceased family members, including Genialis, Hyginus, Rufinia, and Hyginia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203051.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelia Marciana placed this for her husband Gaius Julius Euhemerus, and Julius Maximus and Cornelius Marcianus for their deserving father.
EDCS-04203051.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Cornelia Marciana for her husband Euhemerus, and by two sons for their father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203052.translation: Marcus Turallasius and Satyrius Culicionis, his comrades, set this up for Scaevinus, son of Lucius, the veteran.
EDCS-04203052.summary: A funerary monument set up by friends for a veteran named Scaevinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203053.translation: Calliste lived 19 years. She made this for her daughter Dystris and for herself while alive.
EDCS-04203053.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calliste, who died at age 19, and for herself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203054.translation: Publius Calpurnius Mercator, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04203054.summary: A simple funerary epitaph for Publius Calpurnius Mercator, son of Marcus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203055.translation: To Hercules. Lucius Claudius Callistus [dedicated this].
EDCS-04203055.summary: A dedication to the god Hercules by Lucius Claudius Callistus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203057.translation: Pla, daughter of Sextus, Niger, to Lucius Aemilius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203057.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a funerary marker, possibly mentioning individuals named Niger, Lucius Aemilius, and possibly a freedwoman.

EDCS-04203059.translation: Gaius Menatius Severus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, rebuilt the temple to the Mother of the Gods and Isis and, at his own expense, built the portico in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04203059.summary: A religious dedication by Gaius Menatius Severus who rebuilt a temple and added a portico to the Mother of the Gods and Isis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203060.text_edition: \n Lucius Aufillenus Ascanius VIvir II Claudialis et Augustalis sibi et Catiae Titi filiae Rhodae uxori\n
EDCS-04203060.translation: Lucius Aufillenus Ascanius, VIvir of the Claudian and Augustan orders, for himself and for his wife Rhoda, daughter of Titus Catia.
EDCS-04203060.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Aufillenus Ascanius, a VIvir of the Claudian and Augustan orders, and his wife Rhoda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203061.text_edition: \n Titus Catius Titi libertus Docimus VIvir Augustalis sibi et Cluviae Marci libertae Petale uxori\n
EDCS-04203061.translation: Titus Catius Docimus, freedman of Titus, VIvir Augustalis, for himself and for his wife Petale, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-04203061.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titus Catius Docimus, a VIvir Augustalis and freedman, and his wife Petale, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203062.translation: Maxuma Aemilia, daughter of Gaius, 70 years old.
EDCS-04203062.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maxuma Aemilia, daughter of Gaius, who died at the age of 70, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203063.translation: Cusonia Marcella, daughter of Marcus; Clodia Severa, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-04203063.summary: A funerary epitaph recording two women, Cusonia Marcella and Clodia Severa, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203065.summary: Fragmentary inscription that appears to be a funerary monument, mentioning individuals such as Quintus Sertorius Pyramus and Valerius Hermodorus.

EDCS-04203066.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Augustus. Lucius Sammucino Justus, for himself and his family, has paid his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-04203066.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Augustus by Lucius Sammucino Justus for himself and his family, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203067.text_edition: \n Gai! Petroni sic Cai fili! Poblilia Marcellini sic inter primos colleciato sic in collegio naviculariorum Arelicensium cui collegio dedit legavitque SS nummum IIduo milia at sic sollemnia cibum et rosarum sibi et coniugi Petronia Pia patri pientissimo\n
EDCS-04203067.translation: He also gave to the college of ship-owners of Arelate, 2000 sesterces, so that from its income solemn meals and roses should be provided for himself and his spouse, and to his most dutiful father Petronia Pia.
EDCS-04203067.summary: This is a donation to the college of ship-owners of Arelate by Gaius Petronius, son of Titus, to fund annual meals and roses for himself and his family, as well as for his father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203068.translation: He also gave to the college of sailors of Arelate 1200 sesterces, so that from the income of this sum, funeral garlands and rites should be provided annually in perpetuity for Iustus, his son, for Iusta, his wife, and for himself. And Pontia Iusta added, in memory of Fortunata, her freedwoman, for the same reason, 600 sesterces, and so that the monument should be maintained.
EDCS-04203068.summary: This is a posthumous donation to the college of sailors of Arelate by the family of Iustus, funding perpetual funeral rites and monument maintenance, with an additional donation by Pontia Iusta for her freedwoman Fortunata, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203069.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Virucate Maximinus and Tertius have dedicated this to their well-deserving parents, Publius Virucate Maximus and Valeria Ursa, daughter of Publius, in whose memory they gave 4,000 sesterces to the guild of Veronese bargemen of Arilica, so that from its income roses and food may be provided for them annually, according to old custom. This monument shall not pass to the heir.
EDCS-04203069.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by sons to their parents and endowed a guild of bargemen for annual offerings, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203070.translation: To Septumia Severa, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius Poblicius Abascantus, because of her merits, though not fully, yet sufficiently according to his means.
EDCS-04203070.summary: This funerary inscription honors Septumia Severa and was erected by Lucius Poblicius Abascantus, likely in the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203072.translation: Marcus Congenetus Iustinus to his most dutiful father, Marcus Congenetus Marcellinus: If my paternal estate had been of greater value, I would have honored you with a more extensive inscription.
EDCS-04203072.summary: This epitaph is a posthumous dedication by a son to his father, expressing regret for the limited means to honor him more fully, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203073.translation: To Raedonia Protogenia, his incomparable and most rare wife. Pupus Plassa Marcellinus made this for himself and his wife while alive.
EDCS-04203073.summary: A "vivum sepulcrum" (tomb built by a living person) dedicated by Pupus Plassa Marcellinus to his wife Raedonia Protogenia, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203074.translation: To Jupiter. Gaius Aesius Urbanus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203074.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter by Gaius Aesius Urbanus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203075.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Ebussius Firminus and Cassianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-04203075.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Ebussius Firminus and Cassianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203076.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Epinia Trebis willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04203076.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Epinia Trebis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203077.translation: [...] Gaius Betutius Encolpus to Mercury the Restorer [dedicated this].
EDCS-04203077.summary: A votive inscription fragment dedicated to Mercury Redux by Gaius Betutius Encolpus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203078.translation: To Publius Clodius, freedman of Publius, [and...] [---].
EDCS-04203078.summary: A funerary inscription fragment for Publius Clodius, freedman of Publius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203081.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Quintia Horestilla, a woman of exceptional piety and singular modesty. Cornelius Iustus, to his most dutiful wife and most pious mother, and [her] sons. Cynegia. Here.
EDCS-04203081.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Cornelius Iustus to his wife Quintia Horestilla and their sons, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203083.translation: To the divine shades. To Atilia Urbica, daughter of Publius, from her sons Publius Abidius Tilicius Atilianus and Urbicus, to their most devoted mother. [She had] good health.
EDCS-04203083.summary: This is a tombstone for Atilia Urbica, set up by her sons.

EDCS-04203085.translation: Quintus Caecilius Aenbura, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-04203085.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Caecilius Aenbura, identified by his freedman status.

EDCS-04203086.translation: Orbia Servilla, freedwoman of Marcus, wife of Lucius Terentius Anterotis.
EDCS-04203086.summary: An epitaph for Orbia Servilla, a freedwoman and wife of Lucius Terentius Anterotis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203087.translation: To Mercury. Quintus Locceius Secundus, in fulfillment of a vow, under Antoninus III and Geta II as consuls.
EDCS-04203087.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury by Quintus Locceius Secundus, dated by the consulship of Antoninus and Geta.

EDCS-04203088.translation: To Lucius Betutius Sextus, son of Caius; to Prima, daughter of Sextia and Tiberius; Betutia Tertulla, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04203088.summary: This inscription appears to be a complex funerary monument or legal declaration of family relationships, listing multiple individuals and their parentage.

EDCS-04203089.translation: Marcus Servilius Macedo, son of Marcus of the Fabia tribe, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04203089.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Marcus Servilius Macedo in his will.

EDCS-04203090.translation: Caius Irucius Moderatus, freedman of Caius, for Hostilia Caianta.
EDCS-04203090.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Caius Irucius Moderatus for Hostilia Caianta.

EDCS-04203091.translation: Made by Caius Quinctius Primus, freedman of Caius, for himself and for Lycinini, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-04203091.summary: This is an epitaph for Caius Quinctius Primus and his wife Lycinini, who made the tomb while alive.

EDCS-04203092.translation: Marcus Cassius Capulus, son of Marcus of the Aniensi tribe, a centurion of the 5th praetorian cohort, made this temple to Isis with his own money.
EDCS-04203092.summary: This is a dedication of a temple to Isis by Marcus Cassius Capulus, a centurion in the Praetorian Guard, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203093.translation: For the Atiliae sisters, Maxima, Suava, and Quarta.
EDCS-04203093.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Atiliae sisters, Maxima, Suava, and Quarta.

EDCS-04203094.translation: To the Divine Manes of Aurelia Macriana, my incomparable wife.
EDCS-04203094.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Aurelia Macriana by her husband.

EDCS-04203095.translation: Quintus Egnatius, son of Publius, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his wife Philistia Paulla.
EDCS-04203095.summary: This funerary inscription was commissioned by Quintus Egnatius for himself and his wife, to be made after his death.

EDCS-04203096.translation: For a son-in-law, for a mother, for a father, for an uncle.
EDCS-04203096.summary: This inscription lists familial relationships, likely for a tomb or funerary monument.

EDCS-04203097.translation: Publius Magius Mani made this while alive for himself, for his wife Asselia Sabina, daughter of Marcus, and for his mother Satria Tertia, daughter of Marcus, and for Cassia Secunda, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04203097.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Publius Magius Mani during his lifetime for himself, his wife, and his mother.

EDCS-04203099.translation: To the Divine Manes, Lucius Valerius Ursio made this while alive for his most dutiful and deserving son Lucius Valerius Ansinio, and for himself, their immunities having been received in the guild of craftsmen.
EDCS-04203099.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Lucius Valerius Ursio for his son and himself, likely related to his membership in a trade guild.

EDCS-04203100.translation: For Publius Catius Callavius, son of Publius, and Satria Tertia, daughter of Marcus, and for Marcus Catius, son of Publius, and Loreia Congidia, daughter of Spurius.
EDCS-04203100.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication, possibly funerary, listing multiple individuals and their parentage.

EDCS-04203101.translation: To Publius Livius, son of Publius, of the tribe Poblilia.
EDCS-04203101.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Livius, son of Publius, identified by his tribe.

EDCS-04203102.summary: This is a dedication from Quintus Sertorius to Mevia Marcella.

EDCS-04203103.translation: Marcus Aemilius, son of Cnaeus, of the tribe Poblilia.
EDCS-04203103.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Aemilius, son of Cnaeus, by his tribe.

EDCS-04203104.translation: Publius Cal Severus to Cassia, daughter of Marcius.
EDCS-04203104.summary: This is a dedication from Publius Cal Severus to Cassia, daughter of Marcius.

EDCS-04203105.summary: This inscription identifies Postumia Brigia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-04203106.translation: Cornelius, son of Publius, for himself and for Secundus and Candidus.
EDCS-04203106.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Cornelius, son of Publius, for himself and two others, Secundus and Candidus.

EDCS-04203111.text_edition: \n Sexto Caecilio Sexti filio Sabatina Senecioni IIIIviro bis pontifici praefecto fabrum praefecto cohortis praefecto equitum ala Hispanorum praefecto posuit\n
EDCS-04203111.translation: He erected [this] for Sextus Caecilius Sabatinus Senecio, son of Sextus, twice quaestor, pontiff, prefect of the engineers, prefect of a cohort, prefect of cavalry of the ala Hispanorum.
EDCS-04203111.summary: This inscription records the career of Sextus Caecilius Sabatinus Senecio, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-04203112.translation: To the divine shades. To Marcus Fabius Praesens, son of Caius, of the Sabatina tribe, priest of the Caeninenses, a judge of the equestrian order, from five Augustan centuries, duovir with judicial authority. Here he bequeathed 400,000 sesterces to the state and 100,000 sesterces for the decoration of the school. Quintus Fabius [...] L[...].
EDCS-04203112.summary: This tombstone for Marcus Fabius Praesens details his public career and significant bequests to the community and a school.

EDCS-04203113.translation: Gaius Maecilius, son of Publius, of the tribe Sabatina, a VIvir, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his wife Novellia Prima.
EDCS-04203113.summary: This is a funerary inscription, ordered by testament, for Gaius Maecilius, a local magistrate (VIvir), and his wife Novellia Prima.

EDCS-04203114.translation: Marcus Messius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Sabatina, a magistrate with judicial powers (IIIIvir iure dicundo)...
EDCS-04203114.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Messius, a magistrate with judicial powers (IIIIvir iure dicundo) from the tribe Sabatina, with part of the text missing.

EDCS-04203115.translation: ... Rufus, a magistrate (IIIIvir), ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his wife Cassia Lepida, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04203115.summary: This is a funerary inscription, ordered by testament, for a magistrate (IIIIvir) named Rufus and his wife Cassia Lepida, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04203116.translation: To the divine shades. Hail, Cassia Sallustia Altinas. Here rests Lucius Aebutius Marianus, [in memory of] his wife.
EDCS-04203116.summary: This is a tombstone for Cassia Sallustia Altinas, placed by her husband Lucius Aebutius Marianus.

EDCS-04203117.translation: ... Agrippa, son of Caius, for himself and for his wife Prisca.
EDCS-04203117.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Agrippa, son of Caius, and his wife Prisca.

EDCS-04203118.translation: Made by Caius Alfenus, 20 feet in frontage, 16 feet in area.
EDCS-04203118.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property measured by Caius Alfenus.

EDCS-04203119.translation: To Lucius Annius Diphilus Maior, son of Lucius, freedman of Lucius; to Lucius Annius Diphilus Minor, son of Lucius, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Annius Diomedes [erected this] for his freedmen.
EDCS-04203119.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Lucius Annius Diomedes for his freedmen, Lucius Annius Diphilus Maior and Lucius Annius Diphilus Minor, likely set up in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203120.translation: Marcus Antonius [and] Valeria [his] mother, 10 feet in frontage, 10 feet in area.
EDCS-04203120.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property belonging to Marcus Antonius and his mother Valeria.

EDCS-04203121.translation: Caecilia, daughter of Marcus; Marcus Caecilius, son of Marcus, [dedicated this] to his paternal aunt.
EDCS-04203121.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Caecilius to his paternal aunt, Caecilia, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203122.translation: [---] of Caepio A[---]; [---] Caepio, son of Marcus, of the Sabatina tribe, [---]
EDCS-04203122.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a member of the Caepio family, possibly with a tribal affiliation, dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203123.translation: Lucius Cannius, son of Mani, made while alive for himself and for Marcella [---]a, the singer.
EDCS-04203123.summary: This is a tombstone made by Lucius Cannius for himself and his wife, Marcella Kantatrike.

EDCS-04203124.translation: [---] to his father Soccion; and to his mother Gallai, daughter of Gaius, wife of Cannutius; and to Procula, daughter of Marcus, daughter of Procula, aged four.
EDCS-04203124.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for a father, mother, and a young child named Procula, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203125.translation: To Cassia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, his mother.
EDCS-04203125.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cassia Tertia, mother of the dedicator, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203126.translation: Furia Prima, daughter of Sextus, made (this) while alive for herself and for Marcus Acilius Virum, son of Lucius, and for Publius Furius Virum, son of Publius, and for Quintus Caesius Virum, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04203126.summary: This funerary inscription records a woman, Furia Prima, making provision for herself and three men.

EDCS-04203127.translation: Marcus Herennius Philippus for himself, and for his son Marcus Herennius Petronianus, and for his wife Claudia Cosa, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04203127.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Herennius Philippus for himself, his son, and his wife, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203128.translation: Quintus Maesius, son of Lucius, for himself and for his daughter Quinta, wife of Titus Stabilion, he ordered [this] to be made by his will.
EDCS-04203128.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by Quintus Maesius by his will for himself, his daughter Quinta, and her husband Titus Stabilion, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203130.translation: Lucius Mestrius Cato, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203130.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely identifying an individual named Lucius Mestrius Cato, from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203131.translation: Publius Raius F. arranged for this to be made. Viator, by the law, now remember my name in this inscription. This house is mortal. Farewell, live in the upper world, I wish you the best life. I wanted it to be well.
EDCS-04203131.summary: This inscription, possibly from a tomb, urges the passerby to remember the deceased and expresses a wish for a good afterlife, arranged by Publius Raius F.

EDCS-04203132.translation: Lucius Sentius, son of Gaius, of the Aniensis tribe.
EDCS-04203132.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Sentius, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203133.translation: To Maxsuma, daughter of Gaius, wife of Sentius.
EDCS-04203133.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Maxsuma, wife of Sentius, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203134.translation: Quintus Sertorius Festus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04203134.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Quintus Sertorius Festus, son of Quintus.

EDCS-04203135.translation: The mother made (this) for her son Tatianus, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-04203135.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a mother to her deceased son, Tatianus.

EDCS-04203136.translation: Marcus Vettius Marcellus, son of Marcus, and Fulvia Marita, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-04203136.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Vettius Marcellus and Fulvia Marita, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203137.translation: Here rests in peace Thomas, an honest man, a penitential administrator, who lived approximately 25 years, interred on the eleventh day before the Kalends of March in the first indiction, six years after the consulship of Paolinus the Younger.
EDCS-04203137.summary: This is a Christian tomb inscription for Thomas, who died around 25 years old, dated to the 4th or 5th century CE based on the consular dating formula and Christian terminology.

EDCS-04203138.translation: Quintus Pompeius Primus and Pompeia Thymele, parents, made (this) for their incomparable daughter Pompeia Celerina, who lived 19 years, 11 months, and 5 days, and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-04203138.summary: This funerary inscription records parents dedicating a tomb to their deceased daughter, Pompeia Celerina, and also for themselves.

EDCS-04203139.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Stacia Ursa, most virtuous.
EDCS-04203139.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Stacia Ursa, described as 'most virtuous'.

EDCS-04203140.translation: To the present Lar gods, the following give this gift: Aphrodisius, slave of Plotus Caius; Apollonius, slave of Ofilius Numerius; Philemo, slave of Mescinia Numerius Lucius; Pothus, slave of Virrius Numerius Lucius; Philogenes, slave of Curtilius Publius; Dama, slave of Vettius Publius' freedman; Surus, slave of Iuventius Publius; Apollonius, slave of Arrius Cnaeus; Antiochus, slave of Plotus Caius; Thiasus, slave of Decius Publius; Diogenes, slave of Metilius Caius; Orpheus, slave of Afinnius Lucius Caius; Bacchus, slave of Afinius Lucius; Artemidorus, slave of Spedius Caelius; Sulla, slave of Flavius Publius; Pamphilus, slave of Nonius Publius; Eucaerus, slave of Flavius Publius; Antiochus, slave of Mescinius Quintus. In the consulship of Gaius Julius Marcus and Calpurnius.
EDCS-04203140.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the household gods (Laribus) by a group of slaves, likely from a large estate or household, during the consulship of Gaius Julius Marcus and Calpurnius in the late 1st century BCE or early 1st century CE.

EDCS-04203142.translation: Marcus Satrius Maior (dedicated this) to Victoriae Augustorum (Victory of the Emperors) Antoninus and Verus.
EDCS-04203142.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Marcus Satrius Maior to the imperial victory of Emperors Antoninus and Verus.

EDCS-04203144.translation: Of Gaius Varius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203144.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the top part of a tombstone, identifying Gaius Varius, son of Gaius, probably dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203145.translation: Lucius Lupavius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-04203145.summary: This is a personal identification of Lucius Lupavius, son of Quintus, noting his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04203148.translation: To Jupiter. Lucius Varius Barginus, son of Quintus, willingly and deservedly, from his own funds.
EDCS-04203148.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter, recording a dedication made by Lucius Varius Barginus at his own expense, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203150.translation: To Gaius Julius [---]anarius, prefect of the ala of the Pannonians, prefect of the ala of the Hispani Aurianae, prefect of the ala of the Aravacae. Postumia Casta, daughter of Quintus, to her dearest husband.
EDCS-04203150.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Julius [---]anarius, a military officer, and his wife Postumia Casta, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203151.translation: To Marcus Aemilius Primus, freedman of Marcus, and Aemilia Salvia, daughter of Spurius Aemilius, and Aemilia Acme, freedwoman of Marcus Aemilius. Primus and [---], a sexvir [---].
EDCS-04203151.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Aemilius Primus and Aemilia Salvia, and Aemilia Acme, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE, mentioning a 'sexvir' (a type of civic official).

EDCS-04203152.translation: Titus Praesentius, son of Quintus, and Publius Helvecius, son of Publius, as aediles, for the honor [of the office], on the road, 20,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04203152.summary: This is an inscription recording a public works dedication by two aediles, Titus Praesentius and Publius Helvecius, who funded road construction, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203153.translation: Lucius Statius Priscus, son of Spurius, decurion of Cremona, made (this) while alive for his mother, Fadia, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-04203153.summary: This inscription records Lucius Statius Priscus, a local official in Cremona, dedicating a monument to his mother while he was still alive.

EDCS-04203154.translation: Mitoius Salvius, freedman of Caius, made (this) for Fidelis, freedman of Salvius, a money changer (?), 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203154.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land and its dedication by a freedman, Mitonius Salvius, to another freedman, Fidelis, who was possibly a money changer.

EDCS-04203155.translation: To Aurelius Superus, a circitor under the care of Iustus, who lived 30 years, Aurelia Quintina made this memorial to her dearest husband, and expended 30,000 denarii for the funeral and memorial.
EDCS-04203155.summary: A funerary monument erected by a wife for her deceased husband, specifying the amount spent on his funeral and memorial, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203156.translation: Lucius Baburius Anthus, a barber, for himself and for Firmus, his freedman, and for his own [family].
EDCS-04203156.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Baburius Anthus, a barber, and his freedman Firmus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203157.translation: Gaius Caesius Silo, son of Gaius, and his relation Ennia Lesbia, freedwoman of Gaius, [bought this plot of land] 20 feet square.
EDCS-04203157.summary: A property boundary marker indicating the dimensions of a plot of land, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203158.translation: To the memory of Claudia Eutyche, his most dutiful wife, Tiberius Claudius Fortunatus, freedman of Tiberius, [dedicated this monument with] 10 feet in front and 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203158.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, erected by her husband, specifying the dimensions of the funerary plot, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203159.translation: To Barba, from Durrha, Nymphinus, [dedicated this] to his mother.
EDCS-04203159.summary: A dedication to a mother by her son, likely a funerary or honorary inscription, possibly from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203160.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a name and a cognomen, possibly from a tombstone or dedication, dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203161.translation: Verecundus Valerianus Gavianus Marcianus Minicianus Plotus and Plotina [dedicated this] to their most dutiful parents, Marcus Gavi Fortis and Baburia Trophime, and their son.
EDCS-04203161.summary: A dedication to parents by their children, likely a funerary or honorary monument, possibly from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203162.translation: Quintus Gavius Homullus, son of Quintus, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04203162.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Quintus Gavius Homullus via his will.

EDCS-04203163.translation: Lucius Lucilius, son of Quintus, grandson of Gnaeus, who was the freedman Statius, son of Gaius Lucilius, son of Gaius; the place is a square plot of land measuring six-and-a-half [duodecimal units], with a burial chest in the middle.
EDCS-04203163.summary: A description of a burial plot, possibly a property marker or funerary inscription, from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203164.translation: Quintus Rustius, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe, and Pusilla Clodia, daughter of Marcus, for themselves and their families.
