EDCS-04203164.summary: This inscription names donors, Quintus Rustius and Pusilla Clodia, likely for a funerary monument or property dedication for their families.

EDCS-04203165.translation: [---]dar[---] for Anthi, his dearest husband, by Mor[---]tilia Crescentia.
EDCS-04203165.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Mor[---]tilia Crescentia to her husband, likely on a tomb, with a partially restored name.

EDCS-04203166.translation: Marcus Statius Chilo, freedman of Marcus, [speaks]: 'Hey, you weary traveler passing me by, though you may walk for a long time, you must still come here; 10 feet in front and 10 feet in the field.'
EDCS-04203166.summary: A funerary inscription intended to be read by passersby, reminding them of their own mortality and the inevitability of death, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203167.translation: Of Gaius Veianus, son of Lucius; of Gaius, son of Gaius; of Lucius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203167.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, likely part of a family lineage, possibly related to a property or funerary marker.

EDCS-04203172.translation: Atula, of good memory, rests in this place; she lived about 55 years and departed from this life on the 15th day before the Kalends of October, when Placidus was the most illustrious consul.
EDCS-04203172.summary: This is a late Roman epitaph recording the death of Atula, with her age and the consular date (likely 4th century AD).

EDCS-04203173.translation: Stephanus, a man of good memory, a lector, rests here in peace; he lived in this age about 35 years, was buried on the day before the Ides of December, and again after the consulship of Paulinus Iunior, the most illustrious man, in the first indiction.
EDCS-04203173.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Stephanus, a lector, with his age, burial date, and a consular reference likely in the 4th or 5th century AD.

EDCS-04203174.translation: Benenata, of good memory, rests here; she lived about 35 years and 12 days, she departed in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-04203174.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Benenata, stating her age at death and that she died in Christ.

EDCS-04203175.translation: Bergulla Val dissolves [her vow], awaiting the reward.
EDCS-04203175.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Bergulla Val, likely to a deity, possibly associated with a funerary context.

EDCS-04203176.translation: The Guild of Craftsmen [honors] Gaius Mefanatius Gracilis and Lucius Minicius Alexander, six Augustales, and Ursio, son of Secundus, who left their fortunes to the guild.
EDCS-04203176.summary: This inscription honors guild officials and records a bequest from three individuals to the Collegium fabrorum (Guild of Craftsmen).

EDCS-04203177.translation: Lucius Geminius Maximus, veteran of the First Adjutrix Legion, Pious, Faithful, [dedicated this] for himself and for his freedman Lucius Geminius Castor.
EDCS-04203177.summary: A funerary monument erected by a veteran for himself and his freedman, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203178.translation: Theodorus, freedman of Publius, son of Publius, made this while alive. For himself and for his wife Valeria Callirhoe, and for his stepdaughter Cornelia Callityce, his former concubine; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04203178.summary: A funerary monument erected by a living individual for himself, his wife, and his stepdaughter who was also his former concubine, indicating that the monument is not inheritable, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203179.translation: Titus Pinnius Fortis, heir of Lucius Birron Quartionis, took care to have this erected according to the will.
EDCS-04203179.summary: An inscription indicating that a funerary monument was erected according to the terms of a will, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203180.translation: Seneca Magia, daughter of Magius, willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04203180.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Seneca Magia fulfilling a vow to the goddess Minerva.

EDCS-04203181.translation: Marcus Vinnius, son of Lucius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo.
EDCS-04203181.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to Apollo by Marcus Vinnius.

EDCS-04203182.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Publius Atilius Paganus.

EDCS-04203183.text_edition: \n Publio Statio Publi filio Fabia Paullo Postumio Iuniori Xviro stlitibus iudicandis tribuno militum legionis VII geminae felicis VIviro equitum Romanorum quaestori provinciae Africae tribuno plebis praetori legato pro praetore Ponti et Bithyniae proconsuli provinciae Baeticae Caius Cominius Aufillenus Minicianus optimo et rarissimae fidei amico\n
EDCS-04203183.translation: To Publius Statilius Paulius Postumius Iunior, of the Fabia tribe, son of Publius, a member of the board of twelve men for judging lawsuits, tribune of the soldiers of the loyal Gemini VI Legion, a member of the equestrian order, quaestor of the province of Africa, tribune of the plebs, praetor, propraetorian legate of Pontus and Bithynia, proconsul of the province of Baetica, [dedicated by] Gaius Cominius Aufillenus Minicianus, his most excellent and exceptionally loyal friend.
EDCS-04203183.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a friend for Publius Statilius Paulius Postumius Iunior, detailing his extensive career in the Roman administration and military.

EDCS-04203184.translation: Sextus Catius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, VI vir.
EDCS-04203184.summary: This inscription records Sextus Catius, a member of the college of VI viri.

EDCS-04203185.translation: Gaius Mutius, son of Sextus, Publius Popillius, son of Marcus, Quintus Mucius, son of Publius, and Marcus Cornelius, son of Publius, four men, undertook to build a tower at the expense of the treasury by decree of the decurions, and they approved it.
EDCS-04203185.summary: This inscription records the construction of a tower funded by the town treasury, undertaken by four officials.

EDCS-04203187.translation: Viva, freedwoman of Aticilla, made this.
EDCS-04203187.summary: This inscription records a dedication or commission by a freedwoman named Viva.

EDCS-04203188.translation: For the Matrons, Cornelia Methe willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Cornelia Macrina.
EDCS-04203188.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the Matrons, made by Cornelia Methe on behalf of Cornelia Macrina.

EDCS-04203189.translation: Quarta, daughter of [---], Publius Messius Appi son Fronto, made this while alive for himself and [---].
EDCS-04203189.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a self-funded monument by Publius Messius Appi son Fronto and his daughter Quarta.

EDCS-04203190.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Tertius Bivuo.
EDCS-04203190.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Tertius Bivuo.

EDCS-04203191.translation: For the Matrons, Vergilia Vera, daughter of Caius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Munatia Catulla, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-04203191.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the Matrons, made by Vergilia Vera on behalf of Munatia Catulla.

EDCS-04203192.translation: Cornelius Stephanus, freedman of Lucius, ordered that a memorial be made by his will for himself and his wife Cornelia Calybe, and for Titus Cornelius Primigenius.
EDCS-04203192.summary: This inscription records the posthumous construction of a memorial by Cornelius Stephanus for himself, his wife, and another individual, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-04203193.translation: To the departed spirits. Speratus for Libera, his companion, and for himself, belonging to Marci Noni Agathonici.
EDCS-04203193.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Speratus to his deceased companion Libera and himself, possibly associated with Marci Noni Agathonici.

EDCS-04203195.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Caius Laetorius Vopiscus gladly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203195.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Caius Laetorius Vopiscus fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-04203196.translation: Marcus Nummius Euhodus for Nummia Sabina, his dearest wife.
EDCS-04203196.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Marcus Nummius Euhodus dedicating a monument to his wife, Nummia Sabina.

EDCS-04203198.translation: To Sextus Gesatius Liberalis. Quintus Vibius Messor [dedicated this] to his friend.
EDCS-04203198.summary: This inscription records Quintus Vibius Messor dedicating a monument to his friend, Sextus Gesatius Liberalis.

EDCS-04203199.translation: To myself, Caius, son of Fabia, and to my daughter Hispana, and to my freedwoman daughter Annela, and to Iucunda, daughter of Lucius Livius Spurius. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-04203199.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Caius, son of Fabia, sets up a monument for himself, his daughters, and his freedwoman daughter, stipulating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-04203200.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Quintus Don Valerius as a father.

EDCS-04203201.translation: Sacred to Hercules. Catonius Maximianus gladly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203201.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Catonius Maximianus fulfilling a vow to Hercules.

EDCS-04203202.text_edition: \n Iovi Marcus Pomponius Marci filius Primio et Caius Pomponius Marci filius aras septem posuerunt paganico pagi Farraticani ex scitu pagi paganorum Farraticanorum et permissu propter magisterium pagi et vocationem in perpetuum sibi et filio finibus Cremonensium de pecunia sua\n
EDCS-04203202.translation: Marcus Pomponius Primus, son of Marcus, and Gaius Pomponius, son of Marcus, have erected seven altars to Jupiter, from the territory of the village of Farraticus, by decree and with the permission of the village elders, because of their magistracy and summons to office in perpetuity, for themselves and their son, from their own funds, within the boundaries of Cremona.
EDCS-04203202.summary: This inscription records the erection of seven altars to Jupiter by two individuals, Marcus Pomponius Primus and Gaius Pomponius, as a religious act related to their village offices and in honor of their family.

EDCS-04203203.translation: Lucius Atilius, son of Lucius, of Cimei [VEI?].
EDCS-04203203.summary: This is a simple identification inscription for Lucius Atilius, son of Lucius, from Cimei.

EDCS-04203204.translation: Constan F. [dedicated this] to Septumius R.
EDCS-04203204.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication by Constan F. to Septumius R.

EDCS-04203205.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Cornelius Eutyches and Cornelia Moderata [dedicated this] to their daughter Cornelia Eutychidis, who lived 1 year, 5 months, 11 days.
EDCS-04203205.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Marcus Cornelius Eutyches and Cornelia Moderata for their daughter Cornelia Eutychidis, with her lifespan provided.

EDCS-04203207.translation: Publius Mucius, son of Biracus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, for his concubine Nevia Tertulla, daughter of Spurius, and for his daughter Mucia Vera.
EDCS-04203207.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Publius Mucius for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04203208.translation: Tullius Speratus dedicates this to Castor and Pollux.
EDCS-04203208.summary: This is a dedication to the divine twins Castor and Pollux by Tullius Speratus.

EDCS-04203209.translation: Marcus Maeclius Magunus willingly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04203209.summary: This inscription records Marcus Maeclius Magunus fulfilling a vow to Hercules.

EDCS-04203210.translation: Gaius Vossius, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, fulfilled his vow to Hercules from his own savings.
EDCS-04203210.summary: This inscription records Gaius Vossius fulfilling a vow to Hercules, emphasizing personal financial contribution.

EDCS-04203211.translation: Gaius Naevius Proculus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Iunones.
EDCS-04203211.summary: This inscription records Gaius Naevius Proculus fulfilling a vow to the Iunones.

EDCS-04203212.translation: Quintus, priest of the city, fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-04203212.summary: This inscription records Quintus, a priest, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-04203213.translation: Marcus C. H. willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Matronae.
EDCS-04203213.summary: This inscription records Marcus C. H. fulfilling a vow to the Matronae.

EDCS-04203214.translation: Gaius Caecilius Calamus, freedman of Gaius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Matronae.
EDCS-04203214.summary: This inscription records Gaius Caecilius Calamus, a freedman, fulfilling a vow to the Matronae.

EDCS-04203215.translation: Gaius Hostilius Seneca, son of Gaius, willingly and deservedly amplified his vow to Mercurius Augustus, which he had undertaken.
EDCS-04203215.summary: This inscription records Gaius Hostilius Seneca fulfilling and expanding a vow to Mercurius Augustus.

EDCS-04203216.translation: Cornelia Catulla fulfilled her vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04203216.summary: This inscription records Cornelia Catulla fulfilling a vow to Minerva.

EDCS-04203217.translation: Nia Staphyle gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04203217.summary: This inscription records Nia Staphyle fulfilling a vow, likely dedicating a shrine or temple, with the date inferable from the context of the find.

EDCS-04203218.translation: Rufus, son of Biveio, made this himself for Dia Capi, his wife, and for Biveio, son of Triumo, and for Messava, daughter of Deivarius, and for my sons Gaius Valerius Rufus and Quintus Valerius Rufus, who have died, of the XXII Primigenia legion.
EDCS-04203218.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Rufus, son of Biveio, for himself and his deceased family members, including his wife and sons, one of whom served in the XXII Primigenia legion.

EDCS-04203219.translation: To Publius Atilius Secundus, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, an Augustalis (member of the city council), his most cherished sons Severinus, Severus, and Hermione, and his father Publius Atilius, have placed this monument.
EDCS-04203219.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by the sons Severinus, Severus, and Hermione to their father, Publius Atilius Secundus, who held the prestigious office of Augustalis.

EDCS-04203221.translation: To the Divine Shades, Publius Atilius Iustus [erected this] for Atilia Ial.
EDCS-04203221.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Publius Atilius Iustus to Atilia Ial, placed 'to the Divine Shades' (Dis Manibus).

EDCS-04203222.translation: Birrius, freedman of Publius, Abascantus, saw to its construction.
EDCS-04203222.summary: This inscription records that Birrius Abascantus, a freedman of Publius, commissioned the construction of a monument or work.

EDCS-04203223.translation: Their sons erected [this] for Antubrigius, son of Ca[--], and for Bounitic, daughter of Virillus.
EDCS-04203223.summary: This funerary inscription states that sons erected a monument for their parents, Antubrigius and Bounitic.

EDCS-04203224.translation: My death grieved whom, placed this monument for me.
EDCS-04203224.summary: This is a personal epitaph where the deceased states that someone mourned by their death erected this monument.

EDCS-04203225.translation: To the Divine Shades, Marcus Tullius Fortis [erected this] for himself and for his mother Rabutia Firmina.
EDCS-04203225.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Tullius Fortis for himself and his mother, Rabutia Firmina, addressed to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-04203226.translation: Gaius Iulius P. and Cornelia [dedicate this].
EDCS-04203226.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely indicating a dedication or memorial by Gaius Iulius P. and Cornelia.

EDCS-04203227.translation: To the Divine Shades, Lucius Iuventius Primitius erected an altar for himself and his family, and ordered it to be made by his will.
EDCS-04203227.summary: This inscription records Lucius Iuventius Primitius erecting an altar for himself and his family, to be fulfilled after his death according to his will.

EDCS-04203228.translation: Gaius Lartius Capito ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04203228.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Gaius Lartius Capito in his will.

EDCS-04203229.translation: To Lesbia, fellow slave of Grullus Dentus, the deserving.
EDCS-04203229.summary: This is an epitaph for Lesbia, a deserving fellow slave of Grullus Dentus.

EDCS-04203230.translation: And to Minicia, daughter of Caius, his dear and dutiful wife; Gaius Appuleius Si [dedicated this].
EDCS-04203230.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Appuleius Si to his wife, Minicia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-04203231.translation: Quintus Munatius Iucundus, son of Quintus, for himself and his daughter, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-04203231.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Quintus Munatius Iucundus for himself and his daughter.

EDCS-04203232.translation: Octavia, daughter of Spurius, ordered this to be made in her will.
EDCS-04203232.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Octavia, daughter of Spurius, in her will.

EDCS-04203233.translation: Ovidius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, for himself and for Lucius Ovidius and Gaius Ovidius, son of Caius; the place is dedicated up to the middle boundary and the middle ditch.
EDCS-04203233.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a burial plot by Ovidius, son of Lucius, for himself and his sons, Lucius Ovidius and Gaius Ovidius.

EDCS-04203234.translation: Gaius Silius Ismenus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203234.summary: This inscription is a simple identification of Gaius Silius Ismenus, son of Gaius.

EDCS-04203235.translation: Ordered to be made in his will for Quintus Surius, son of Quintus Patinius, for himself and for his father who is buried across the road opposite this place, and for his wives Viria and Viola.
EDCS-04203235.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Quintus Surius for himself, his father, and his wives Viria and Viola.

EDCS-04203236.translation: Gaius Tappo, son of Tappo, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his wife Tapponia Specula.
EDCS-04203236.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by Gaius Tappo for himself and his wife Tapponia Specula.

EDCS-04203238.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to a person named Aternaius.

EDCS-04203239.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to an individual named Catilius Brixianus.

EDCS-04203240.translation: To the good memory of Attia Innocentia, a woman of the highest chastity and wisdom, who lived for more or less 43 years, 9 months, and 4 days. Iulius Augustinus, subdeacon, set up this memorial to his most sweet wife, with whom he lived for 7 years, 2 months, and 20 days, against his will, to the well-deserving woman.
EDCS-04203240.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Attia Innocentia, set up by her husband, Iulius Augustinus, a subdeacon, likely dating to the 3rd century CE based on the names and the context of subdiaconal office.

EDCS-04203241.text_edition: \n Iovi Quartus Vigillionius Terti filius et Macrina uxor cum suis votum solverunt\n
EDCS-04203241.translation: Quartus Vigillionius, son of Tertius, and his wife Macrina have fulfilled their vow to Jupiter.
EDCS-04203241.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter by Quartus Vigillionius and his wife Macrina.

EDCS-04203242.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Quintus Petronius Antonianus set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04203242.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Quintus Petronius Antonianus.

EDCS-04203244.translation: Caius Lanius, son of Caius, of the Aniensian tribe, from the Tenth Legion Veneria. Caius Lanius Eros, freedman of Caius, his son, from his own funds.
EDCS-04203244.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Caius Lanius Eros, a freedman, honoring his father, Caius Lanius, a soldier in the Tenth Legion Veneria.

EDCS-04203245.translation: To Publius Postumius Fuscina, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, a member of the public equestrian order and a pontiff, the most devoted town council decreed a public funeral and a gilded equestrian statue. Publius Postumius Marianus, curator of the state of the Augustan city of the Taurini, appointed by the Augusti Severus and Antoninus, used the title.
EDCS-04203245.summary: This is a posthumous honorific inscription decreeing public funeral rites and a statue for Publius Postumius Fuscina, a local magistrate, by the town council under the imperial patronage of Severus and Antoninus (circa 198-211 CE).

EDCS-04203246.translation: To Publius Publicius Symphorus, Augustan duovir, to Publius Publicius Valerianus, his son, to Publicia Drosis, his wife, Publicius Abascantus, for his patrons and himself and Publicia Chrisis and...
EDCS-04203246.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription set up by Publicius Abascantus for his family members including his wife, son, and patrons, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203247.translation: To Clodia Prisca, freedwoman of Lucius, an embroiderer. Ascula set this up at public expense.
EDCS-04203247.summary: This inscription records a dedication or monument set up by Ascula at public expense for Clodia Prisca, a freedwoman and embroiderer.

EDCS-04203250.translation: A gift given to the god Alo. Sextus Niger Sollonius paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203250.summary: This is a votive inscription to a deity named Alo, with Sextus Niger Sollonius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04203251.translation: To the god Alo Saturn. Sextus Commodus Valerius paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203251.summary: This is a votive inscription to a deity named Alo Saturn, with Sextus Commodus Valerius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04203252.translation: To Apollo. Terentius paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203252.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Apollo, with Terentius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04203253.translation: To Apollo and Diana, Gaius Cornelius Acutus and Tertulla and Ianuaria [dedicate this].
EDCS-04203253.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Apollo and Diana by Gaius Cornelius Acutus, Tertulla, and Ianuaria.

EDCS-04203254.translation: Marcus Nonius Senecianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabian tribe, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203254.summary: This inscription records Marcus Nonius Senecianus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04203255.translation: Lucius Vibius Nymphodotus, freedman of Lucius, [dedicated this] at Bergimo, while Gaius Asinius Gallus and Gaius Marcius Censorinus were consuls, and Lucius Salvius Aper and Gaius Postumius Costa were quinquennial duumvirs.
EDCS-04203255.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lucius Vibius Nymphodotus, a freedman, during a specific consular and duumviral period, likely at Bergimo.

EDCS-04203258.translation: For the good fortune of the six associate members of the guild, Sextus Numisius Fortunatus and Lucius Lucretius Primianus, the six Augustal members in charge of the guild's affairs, having given one thousand sesterces for its protection, decreed that from the interest, on the Ides of May, a sacred rite with entrails be celebrated.
EDCS-04203258.summary: This inscription records a decree by guild officials in charge of finances regarding the celebration of a religious rite funded by the interest of 1000 sesterces.

EDCS-04203259.translation: Lucius Trutino Probus gave this gift to the god in fulfillment of a vow, being a six-member Augustal official in Brixia.
EDCS-04203259.summary: This inscription records Lucius Trutino Probus, a local official in Brixia, dedicating a gift to a god in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-04203260.translation: To all the gods and goddesses, Lucius Veturius Segomarus, freedman of Lucius, [dedicated this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-04203260.summary: This is a dedication to all gods and goddesses made by Lucius Veturius Segomarus for himself and his family.

EDCS-04203261.translation: Quintus Mucius Tryphon fulfilled his vow to the Chthonic Gods Surgasteus Magnus and Patarus willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203261.summary: This inscription records Quintus Mucius Tryphon fulfilling a vow to the chthonic deities Surgasteus Magnus and Patarus.

EDCS-04203263.translation: Marcus Rufinius Severus fulfilled his vow to the Fates and Dervonus willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203263.summary: This inscription records Marcus Rufinius Severus fulfilling a vow to the Fates and the deity Dervonus.

EDCS-04203264.translation: Deico, son of Biei, fulfilled his vow to the Fates willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203264.summary: This inscription records Deico, son of Biei, fulfilling a vow to the Fates.

EDCS-04203265.translation: Lucius Decius Tertius willingly and deservedly [dedicated this] to Fortuna.
EDCS-04203265.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna by Lucius Decius Tertius.

EDCS-04203266.translation: Firmia Tertia [dedicates this] to the Genius of the muleteers' guild, [with] C.
EDCS-04203266.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Firmia Tertia to the Genius of the muleteers' guild.

EDCS-04203267.translation: To the Genius of the August city of Brixia, Quintus(?) Gargennius Sagitta, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, a six-man official of Augustus, a decurion, prefect of the artificers, prefect for dispensing justice, quaestor, quinquennial duumvir, [dedicated this] from his own funds.
EDCS-04203267.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Genius of Brixia by Quintus(?) Gargennius Sagitta, listing his various civic and religious offices in the city.

EDCS-04203269.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Hercules by Aurelius Surus.

EDCS-04203270.translation: Publius, son of B., willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04203270.summary: This is a votive inscription by Publius to Hercules, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203271.translation: Sextus Cunopennus Secundus, a carpenter, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04203271.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sextus Cunopennus Secundus, a carpenter, to Hercules, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203272.translation: Marcus Quintius Mansuetus [dedicated this] to Hercules.
EDCS-04203272.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Quintius Mansuetus to Hercules, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203273.translation: Lucius, son of V., willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04203273.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius to Hercules, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203274.translation: Apate, freedwoman of Munatia and Quintus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Isis.
EDCS-04203274.summary: This is a votive inscription by Apate, a freedwoman, to Isis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203275.translation: Sacred to Isis. Caius Roscius Crescens fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203275.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Roscius Crescens to Isis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203276.translation: Annia Iuda, freedwoman of Lucius, fulfilled her vow for her family to the Iunones.
EDCS-04203276.summary: This is a votive inscription by Annia Iuda, freedwoman, to the Iunones, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203277.translation: Lucius Caecilius Placidus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Iunones.
EDCS-04203277.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Caecilius Placidus to the Iunones, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203278.translation: Auctus, freedman of Lucius Clodius and Arbuscula, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Iunones.
EDCS-04203278.summary: This is a votive inscription by Auctus, a freedman, to the Iunones, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203279.translation: Gnaeus Cornelius Nikanor willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Iunones.
EDCS-04203279.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gnaeus Cornelius Nikanor to the Iunones, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203280.translation: To the Iunones, he paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203280.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Iunones, with the dedicator identified only by an implied pronoun.

EDCS-04203281.translation: To the Iunones, Mestrius the craftsman paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203281.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Iunones by Mestrius, a craftsman, who paid his vow willingly and deservedly.

EDCS-04203282.translation: To the Iunones, Lucius Sartius Secundus.
EDCS-04203282.summary: This inscription names Lucius Sartius Secundus as a dedicator to the Iunones.

EDCS-04203283.translation: To the Iunones, for the health of Valeria Iusta, Nicetius her slave paid his vow.
EDCS-04203283.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Iunones by Nicetius, a slave, for the well-being of Valeria Iusta.

EDCS-04203284.translation: To the Iunones, Caius Vocianus Surg paid his vow and offering willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203284.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Iunones by Caius Vocianus Surg, who paid his vow and offering.

EDCS-04203286.translation: To Jupiter, Marcus Magius Helenus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203286.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter by Marcus Magius Helenus, who paid his vow willingly and deservedly.

EDCS-04203288.translation: To Jupiter, Publius Papirius Eutropus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203288.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter by Publius Papirius Eutropus, who paid his vow willingly and deservedly.

EDCS-04203289.translation: To Jupiter, Publius Apidius Homuncio, freedman of Publius, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203289.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter by Publius Apidius Homuncio, a freedman, who paid his vow willingly and deservedly.

EDCS-04203292.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Hedylus, freedman of Titus Cai, a member of the board of six priests, paid his vow.
EDCS-04203292.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Hedylus, a freedman and Augustalis priest, who paid his vow.

EDCS-04203293.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Helvia Fortuna.
EDCS-04203293.summary: This inscription names Helvia Fortuna as a dedicator to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-04203294.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Minicia Syntyche.
EDCS-04203294.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Minicia Syntyche.

EDCS-04203295.translation: Quintus Petronius Rusticus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-04203295.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Quintus Petronius Rusticus.

EDCS-04203296.translation: Virius Maximinus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-04203296.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Virius Maximinus.

EDCS-04203297.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the Preserver of the estates of our Roscius Paculus, a former consul, and Bassus and their sons, Lucius Roscius Eubulus, tutor and procurator, together with Publius Roscius Firmus, their freedman procurator, fulfilled their vow on the fourth day before the Nones of March, when Iulianus II and Crispianus were consuls.
EDCS-04203297.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Lucius Roscius Eubulus and his associate Publius Roscius Firmus for the preservation of estates, referencing specific consuls and a date in March.

EDCS-04203298.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus. By his command, Marcus Publicius Clodianus, a candidate, warns that no one who wishes to sacrifice properly should offer sacrifices on this altar.
EDCS-04203298.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus, containing a warning about sacrifices on an altar, set up by Marcus Publicius Clodianus.

EDCS-04203299.translation: Caius Hostilius Aemilianus, veteran of our Emperors, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter's Tutela.
EDCS-04203299.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter's Tutela by the veteran Caius Hostilius Aemilianus.

EDCS-04203300.translation: To Youth. Marcus Q. Glycerus, son of Marcus, gave a gift.
EDCS-04203300.summary: A dedication of a gift to the deity of Youth by Marcus Q. Glycerus.

EDCS-04203301.translation: Caius Mucius Adeptus gave a gift to the Lares.
EDCS-04203301.summary: A dedication of a gift to the Lares by Caius Mucius Adeptus.

EDCS-04203302.translation: Cornelia Andia fulfilled her vow to the Matrons willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203302.summary: A votive inscription to the Matrons by Cornelia Andia.

EDCS-04203303.translation: Marcus Orusius Tertullus fulfilled his vow to the Matrons willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04203303.summary: A votive inscription to the Matrons by Marcus Orusius Tertullus.

EDCS-04203305.translation: To Mercury, Publius Abidius Viator happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203305.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Mercury by Publius Abidius Viator.

EDCS-04203306.translation: To Mercury, Lucius Acutius Clemens happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203306.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Mercury by Lucius Acutius Clemens.

EDCS-04203307.translation: Marcus Adicius Pulni fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203307.summary: A votive inscription to Mercury by Marcus Adicius Pulni.

EDCS-04203308.translation: Betullus made this for Mercury with his own money.
EDCS-04203308.summary: This inscription records Betullus dedicating a monument to Mercury at his own expense.

EDCS-04203309.translation: To Mercury, Publius C. S. happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203309.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Mercury by Publius C. S.

EDCS-04203310.translation: Gnaeus Caetronius Praesens gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203310.summary: This inscription records Gnaeus Caetronius Praesens fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203311.translation: Quintus Clodius Argutus gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203311.summary: This inscription records Quintus Clodius Argutus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203312.translation: Caius Clodius Firmus gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203312.summary: This inscription records Caius Clodius Firmus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203313.translation: Marcus Clodius Tertius, son of Spurius, gladly [fulfilled his vow] to Mercury.
EDCS-04203313.summary: This inscription records Marcus Clodius Tertius fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203314.translation: Constans, son of Acutus and Comina, gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203314.summary: This inscription records Constans fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203315.translation: To Mercury, Lucius Cornelius Priscus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203315.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Lucius Cornelius Priscus, likely a private vow fulfillment.

EDCS-04203316.translation: To Mercury, Magius Firmus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203316.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Magius Firmus, likely a private vow fulfillment.

EDCS-04203317.translation: Sextus Munatius Campanus gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203317.summary: This inscription records Sextus Munatius Campanus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203318.translation: Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, most distinguished youth, gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury for his own well-being, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203318.summary: This inscription records Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper dedicating a monument to Mercury for his own health.

EDCS-04203319.translation: To the god Mercury, Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, a most distinguished young man, willingly and deservedly fulfilled the vow he had made, with his family.
EDCS-04203319.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, a prominent youth, indicating fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-04203320.translation: Caius Pacatius Ursinus gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203320.summary: This inscription records Caius Pacatius Ursinus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203321.translation: Caius Petronius Fronto gladly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-04203321.summary: This inscription records Caius Petronius Fronto fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203322.translation: Primius, son of Cariassis, dedicated a temple and a statue to Mercury at his own expense, fulfilling a vow.
EDCS-04203322.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple and statue to Mercury by Primius, son of Cariassis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04203323.translation: Caius Publicius Proculus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203323.summary: This inscription records Caius Publicius Proculus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203324.translation: Quintius Leo willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203324.summary: This inscription records Quintius Leo fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203325.translation: Caius Quintius Salvianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203325.summary: This inscription records Caius Quintius Salvianus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203326.translation: Sextus Salvius Restitutus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203326.summary: This inscription records Sextus Salvius Restitutus fulfilling his vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203327.translation: Surus, son of Attus, son of Firmius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203327.summary: This inscription records Surus, son of Attus, son of Firmius, fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203328.translation: Quintus Valerius Magiacus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04203328.summary: This inscription records Quintus Valerius Magiacus fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-04203329.translation: Gaius Consentius Exoratus (dedicated this) to Minerva.
EDCS-04203329.summary: This inscription records Gaius Consentius Exoratus dedicating something to Minerva.

EDCS-04203331.translation: Laumus, son of Saecillus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04203331.summary: This inscription records Laumus, son of Saecillus, fulfilling a vow to Minerva.

EDCS-04203332.translation: Caius Lucretius Hermes willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04203332.summary: This inscription records Caius Lucretius Hermes fulfilling a vow to Minerva.

EDCS-04203333.translation: To Minerva, Caius Maesius Encolpus, freedman of Caius, willingly paid his vow in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203333.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by a freedman to Minerva, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203334.translation: Sacred to Minerva, Medussa daughter of Cariassis willingly paid her vow in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203334.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by a woman named Medussa to Minerva, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203336.translation: To Minerva, Primio son of Esdrus Mancilius.
EDCS-04203336.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203337.translation: To Minerva, Marcus and Caius, sons of Valerius Senecio, willingly paid their vows in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203337.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by two brothers to Minerva, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203338.translation: To Minerva Augusta, Sextus Dugius Valentio, one of the six Augustales priests.
EDCS-04203338.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Augusta by Sextus Dugius Valentio, an Augustalis priest, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203340.translation: To Neptune, the vow was willingly paid in accordance with what was deserved. The vow was willingly paid in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203340.summary: This is a redundant ex-voto inscription to Neptune, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203341.translation: To Neptune Augustus, Lucius Sulpicius Claudianus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04203341.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Lucius Sulpicius Claudianus to Neptune Augustus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203342.translation: To Nocturnus, Victor of the Brixianorum, willingly paid his vow in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203342.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Victor of the Brixianorum to the god Nocturnus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203343.translation: To Silvanus, Caius Clodius Comicus willingly paid his vow in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203343.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Caius Clodius Comicus to Silvanus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203344.translation: To Silvanus, Lucius M. Narcissus willingly paid his vow in accordance with what was deserved.
EDCS-04203344.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Lucius M. Narcissus to Silvanus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203346.translation: Sextus Attius Baebianus gladly fulfilled his vow to Victoria as deserved.
EDCS-04203346.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sextus Attius Baebianus dedicated to Victoria.

EDCS-04203348.translation: Publius Antonius Callistio, VIvir Augustalis, Caius Clodius Comicus, and Publius Postumius Agatho dedicated this to Vulcan Augustus, and for the protection of the association of muleteers, they gave 400 sesterces.
EDCS-04203348.summary: This inscription records the dedication of something to Vulcan Augustus by three members of the association of muleteers, who also provided funds for its protection.

EDCS-04203349.translation: Lucius Vettius Telesphorus and Chrysantus, brothers and VIviri Augustales, dedicated this to Vulcanus Mitius, also called Mulciber, in the name of Vettia Secundina, daughter of Lucius, and Telesphorus, son of Lucius; a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203349.summary: This is a dedication to Vulcan of a place granted by decree of the decurions by two brothers, VIviri Augustales, on behalf of female relatives.

EDCS-04203350.translation: A place was granted by decree of the decurions in the name of the Fates, for the daughter of Saint Cai, Cornelia, and for the sons of Caius Terentius Cornelianus and Marcus Silius Cornelianus; and Marcus Nonius Clarus I.
EDCS-04203350.summary: This inscription records the granting of a place by decree of the decurions in honor of several individuals and the Fates.

EDCS-04203351.translation: Aemilius Clarus, son of Boxarva, gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-04203351.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aemilius Clarus, son of Boxarva.

EDCS-04203352.translation: For the safety of our patron Lucius Septimius Severianus, Lucius Septimius Felicio fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04203352.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Septimius Felicio for the well-being of his patron Lucius Septimius Severianus.

EDCS-04203353.translation: Hostanus gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-04203353.summary: This is a votive inscription by Hostanus.

EDCS-04203354.translation: Marcus Nonius Macrinus, in accordance with his vow.
EDCS-04203354.summary: This inscription records Marcus Nonius Macrinus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04203356.translation: Quintius Gemellus gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-04203356.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintius Gemellus.

EDCS-04203357.translation: Marcus Secundus Avedonis gladly fulfilled his vow to Victoria as deserved.
EDCS-04203357.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Secundus Avedonis dedicated to Victoria.

EDCS-04203358.translation: To my Parent, Gaius Julius Caesar, pontifex.
EDCS-04203358.summary: This is a dedication from Gaius Julius Caesar, a pontifex, to his parent, likely on a funerary monument, dated to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203370.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Sarmaticus, Germanicus Maximus, Britannicus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 14th time, Imperator for the 8th time, Consul for the 5th time, Father of the Fatherland, the most valiant prince, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus.
EDCS-04203370.summary: A lengthy titulary inscription honoring Emperor Commodus, likely erected by Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus, dating to his 14th tribunician power period.

EDCS-04203371.translation: To Magnus Augustus, the greatest prince, the most valiant emperor, conservator of the world, to Lucius [[Domitius Aurelianus]] Pius Felix, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 5th time, Father of the Fatherland, Consul for the 3rd time, Proconsul, Gothicus Maximus, Palmyrenus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, the town council of Brixia.
EDCS-04203371.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Aurelian as 'Magno Augusto', dedicated by the ordo Brixianorum (town council of Brixia) during his 5th tribunician power period.

EDCS-04203374.translation: To Lucius Arrius Primus, Lucius Arrius Secundus, procurator of the Emperor, his most devoted brother.
EDCS-04203374.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Lucius Arrius Secundus to his brother Lucius Arrius Primus, identifying the dedicator as an imperial procurator, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203375.translation: To Aurelius Iulianus, praetorian prefect, most eminent and a man of singular example, the town council of Brixia, their most merciful patron.
EDCS-04203375.summary: A dedication to Aurelius Iulianus, praetorian prefect, by the town council of Brixia, honoring him as their patron.

EDCS-04203376.translation: For Baebia Nigrina, daughter of Marcus, daughter of the sister of Titus Vius Varius, a former consul, the guild of carpet makers, who used this monument.
EDCS-04203376.summary: A funerary dedication by the guild of carpet makers for Baebia Nigrina, possibly honoring a relative of a former consul.

EDCS-04203377.translation: Marcus Nonius Macrinus ordered this to be made by his will to Marcus Caecilius Privatus of the Fabia tribe, his friend.
EDCS-04203377.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Marcus Nonius Macrinus, commissioned by his will, for his friend Marcus Caecilius Privatus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203379.translation: Cornelius Gaudentius, a man of the highest standing, count and corrector of Venetia and Istria, saw to this.
EDCS-04203379.summary: This inscription records Cornelius Gaudentius, a high-ranking imperial official, as the commissioner of a public work or monument in Venetia and Istria, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203380.translation: Cornelius Gaudentius, a man of the highest standing, count and corrector of Venetia and Istria, saw to this.
EDCS-04203380.summary: This inscription records Cornelius Gaudentius, a high-ranking imperial official, as the commissioner of a public work or monument in Venetia and Istria, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203381.translation: To Publius Cornelius Lentulus Scipio, consul, prefect of the treasury, legate of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, pontifex, fetial, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203381.summary: A dedication to Publius Cornelius Lentulus Scipio, honoring his various high offices including consul and legate, decreed by the decurions.

EDCS-04203382.translation: Marcus Curius, a centurion of two hundred men, and Valeria Marcella, his parents, to their dearest sons, [one] who lived 10 years and Caesar(ius) who lived 6 months.
EDCS-04203382.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from parents Marcus Curius and Valeria Marcella to their young sons, one of whom lived to ten years and the other six months, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203383.translation: Aurelianus, a man of the greatest renown, made this in memory of Domitia Victorina, his dearest wife.
EDCS-04203383.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aurelianus to his wife Domitia Victorina, identifying him as a distinguished man, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203384.translation: To Lucius Gabonius Arunculeius Severus, Publius Acilius Fabius Severus, clarissimus vir, iuridicus of the Transpadane region, consul-designate of the province of Cyprus, his dearest uncle, promoted to the advocacy of the fiscus by his votes, Lucius Valerius Marcellinus, his nephew. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203384.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Valerius Marcellinus to his uncle, Lucius Gabonius Arunculeius Severus, who held significant legal and administrative posts, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203385.translation: To Lucius Gabonius Arunculeius Valerianus, egregius vir, eques Romanus, priest and principal, who held all offices, his father and grandfather of senators, his curator, for his merits, the guilds of smiths and carpet-makers. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203385.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the guilds of smiths and carpet-makers to their curator, Lucius Gabonius Arunculeius Valerianus, a distinguished equestrian who held numerous positions, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203386.translation: To Marcus Iuventius Secundus Rixa Postumius Pansa Valerianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabian tribe, consul.
EDCS-04203386.summary: A dedication to Marcus Iuventius Secundus Rixa Postumius Pansa Valerianus, honoring his consulship.

EDCS-04203388.translation: Marcus Nonius Macrinus ordered this to be made by his will to Marcus Licinius Lucretius Censorinus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, his friend.
EDCS-04203388.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Marcus Nonius Macrinus, commissioned by his will, for his friend Marcus Licinius Lucretius Censorinus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203389.translation: To Sextus Maecius Cassianus, son of Sextus, of the Oufentina tribe, Publius Statius Paullus Postumius Iunior, his teacher.
EDCS-04203389.summary: This is a dedication to a teacher named Sextus Maecius Cassianus, likely from his student Publius Statius Paullus Postumius Iunior.

EDCS-04203390.text_edition: \n Caio Maesio Cai filio Picatiano Xviro stlitibus iudicandis tribuno militum legionis I Italicae quaestori provinciae Africae allecto inter tribunicios ab Imperatore Hadriano Antonino Augusto Pio praetori decreto patrono decurionum\n
EDCS-04203390.translation: To Gaius Maesius Picatianus, son of Gaius, decemvir for judging lawsuits, tribune of the soldiers of the I Italica legion, quaestor of the province of Africa, promoted to the rank of tribune by the Emperor Hadrian Antoninus Augustus Pius, praetor, patron by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203390.summary: An honorific inscription for Gaius Maesius Picatianus, detailing his career progression and his appointment as patron by the decurions, likely under Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-04203392.translation: To Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, a most distinguished youth, XVvir of sacred rites, the worshippers of his Lares.
EDCS-04203392.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, a prominent young man who held religious office, by his associates who worshipped the Lares.

EDCS-04203393.translation: To Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, a most distinguished man, XVvir of sacred rites, quaestor candidate, urban praetor, curator of the public affairs of Nicomedia and Nicaea, and of the Appian Way, and legal official of the Transpadane region, as patron, a place was granted by decree of the decurions because, through his efforts, the exemption of our college was confirmed.
EDCS-04203393.summary: This inscription records the granting of honorary status and a place to Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper by the college of dendrophori for his confirmed patronage and administrative roles.

EDCS-04203394.translation: To Pacula, daughter of Lucius, a most distinguished woman, from Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper, a most distinguished man, to his most chaste wife.
EDCS-04203394.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Marcus Nonius Arrius Paulinus Aper to his wife, Pacula.

EDCS-04203395.translation: To Marcus Nonius Macrinus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, consul, XV-man for sacred rites, imperial legate with consular power of the province of Upper Pannonia. Titus Iulius Iulianus, tribune of the First Cohort of Pannonians, [erected this] for his excellent commander.
EDCS-04203395.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Nonius Macrinus, a prominent imperial official, likely on a monument erected by a subordinate tribune. He served as consul and legate of Pannonia Superior.

EDCS-04203396.translation: To Marcus Nonius Macrinus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, consul, XV-man for sacred rites, praetor, imperial legate with consular power of the province of Lower Pannonia. Lucius Ussius Picentinus, a fellow soldier, [erected this] for his excellent and most rare commander.
EDCS-04203396.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Nonius Macrinus, a consul and imperial legate, honoring his service in Pannonia Inferior, erected by a fellow soldier.

EDCS-04203397.translation: To Marcus Nonius Mucianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, consul, XV-man for sacred rites. Gaius Iulius Sacerdos, a fellow soldier and friend, [erected this].
EDCS-04203397.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Nonius Mucianus, a consul and member of the XV-viri sacris faciundis, erected by a fellow soldier and friend.

EDCS-04203398.translation: To Marcus Nonius Mucianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, consul, XVvir of sacred rites, from Mucianus, his grandfather.
EDCS-04203398.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Nonius Mucianus, a consul and religious official, made by his grandfather, also named Mucianus.

EDCS-04203399.text_edition: \n Marco Nummio Umbrio Primo Marci filio Palatina Senecioni Albino consuli praetori candidato legato provinciae Africae legato provinciae Asiae quaestori candidato Augustorum pontifici salio Palatino VIviro equitum Romanorum turmae primae IIIviro monetali aere argento auro flando feriundo Marcus Nummius Euhodus libertus nutritor et procurator locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04203399.translation: To Marcus Nummius Umbrio Primo, son of Marcus, of the Palatine tribe, also called Senecio Albinus, consul, praetor, candidate, legate of the province of Africa, legate of the province of Asia, quaestor, candidate of the Augusti, pontiff, Salian priest of the Palatine, VI-man of the Roman knights of the first turma, III-man for minting bronze, silver, and gold. Marcus Nummius Euhodus, his freedman, foster-father, and procurator. This site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203399.summary: This is a funerary or honorific inscription for Marcus Nummius Umbrio Primo, a high-ranking imperial official who held multiple consulships and legateships, indicating his public career and the honors bestowed upon him.

EDCS-04203400.translation: ] to Paelignus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, military tribune of the 10th Gemina Legion, quaestor, curator of public lands, again curule aedile, praetor, governor with propraetorian authority, again, by decree of the senate and by the authority of Tiberius Caesar...
EDCS-04203400.summary: This is a fragmented inscription detailing the career of Gaius Pontius Paelignus, listing his various political and military offices, including his governorship.

EDCS-04203401.translation: To Postumia Paulla, daughter of Publius, wife of Lucius Iuventius Secundus, consul, a most rare woman, from Marcus Iuventius Caesianus, consul.
EDCS-04203401.summary: This inscription honors Postumia Paulla, wife of the consul Lucius Iuventius Secundus, by Marcus Iuventius Caesianus.

EDCS-04203402.translation: To Postumia Paulla, daughter of Publius, of the Iuventii family, wife of Secundus, a consul. To a most rare woman. Marcus Laelius Firminus and Fulvius Maximus, praetors, [erected this].
EDCS-04203402.summary: This is a dedication to Postumia Paulla, the wife of a consul, by two praetors, highlighting her exceptional character.

EDCS-04203403.translation: To Postumia Paulla, daughter of Publius, wife of Marcus Iuventius Secundus, consul, a most virtuous woman, from Publius Postumius Marianus.
EDCS-04203403.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Postumia Paulla, wife of the consul Marcus Iuventius Secundus, by Publius Postumius Marianus.

EDCS-04203405.translation: In honor of Postumia Paulla, daughter of Publius, wife of Lucius Iuventius Secundus, consul, from Vibia Salvia Varia, daughter of Lucius, with her sons Albinus and Varia, and Lucius Roscius Aelianus Pasculus, and Salvius Iulianus.
EDCS-04203405.summary: This honorary inscription for Postumia Paulla, wife of the consul Lucius Iuventius Secundus, was erected by Vibia Salvia Varia and other family members.

EDCS-04203406.translation: In honor of Postumia Paulla, daughter of Publius, wife of Lucius Iuventius Secundus, consul, from Vibia Salvia Varia, daughter of Lucius, because of her exceptional affection and piety towards her.
EDCS-04203406.summary: This inscription honors Postumia Paulla, wife of the consul Lucius Iuventius Secundus, erected by Vibia Salvia Varia out of gratitude for her affection and piety.

EDCS-04203407.translation: To Sextia Asinia Polla, daughter of Titus. The college of young men of Brixia, for [her] merits, [dedicated this] to Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus.
EDCS-04203407.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the college of young men of Brixia to Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus, likely honoring him for his merits or patronage.

EDCS-04203408.translation: To Sextia Iuliana, daughter of Quintus, a most illustrious woman, for her commendable life in all respects and her singular disposition of character and innocence. The ordo of Brixia. Quintus Lucianus Valerianus, a most illustrious man, her husband, has used the title.
EDCS-04203408.summary: This epitaph honors Sextia Iuliana of Brixia for her virtuous life, erected by the local council and her husband.

EDCS-04203409.translation: To Sextia Iuliana, daughter of Quintus, a most illustrious woman. Quintus Lucianus Valerianus, a most distinguished man, granted this place to his unequalled wife by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203409.summary: This is a funerary monument to Sextia Iuliana, dedicated by her husband, Quintus Lucianus Valerianus, by decree of the town council.

EDCS-04203410.translation: To Publius Statius Iulianus Pelignianus, a most distinguished man. This place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203410.summary: This records the granting of a public space to Publius Statius Iulianus Pelignianus by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-04203411.text_edition: \n Publio Statio Publi filio Fabia Paullo Postumio Iuniori Xviro stlitibus iudicandis tribuno militum legionis VII geminae felicis VIviro equitum Romanorum quaestori provinciae Africae tribuno plebis praetori legato pro praetore Ponti et Bithyniae proconsuli provinciae Baeticae decreto titulo usus decurionum\n
EDCS-04203411.translation: To Publius Statius Paul lus, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, Postumius Iunior, VI-man for judging disputes, tribune of the soldiers of the Seventh Twin Legion, VI-man of the Roman knights, quaestor of the province of Africa, tribune of the plebs, praetor, legate with proconsular power of Pontus and Bithynia, proconsul of the province of Baetica. He used the title by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203411.summary: This inscription details the extensive public career of Publius Statius Paul lus Postumius Iunior, a high-ranking Roman official who held numerous positions, including proconsul of Baetica.

EDCS-04203412.translation: To Marcus Iuventius Suro Proculus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, a six-man officer of Roman knights.
EDCS-04203412.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Marcus Iuventius Suro Proculus, a Roman knight and official.

EDCS-04203413.translation: To Sextus Valerius Primus, son of Sextus, of the Fabia tribe, [his] friend. Marcus Nonius Macrinus ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04203413.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Nonius Macrinus for his friend Sextus Valerius Primus, with the monument erected according to Macrinus's will.

EDCS-04203416.translation: Elius, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, a decemvir for judging lawsuits, quaestor, curule aedile, praetor, and legate, and his daughter Secunda Prisc, dedicated this land.
EDCS-04203416.summary: This records the dedication of land by Elius and his daughter Secunda Prisc, listing his significant political and military career.

EDCS-04203417.translation: Lucius Antonius Quadratus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, was honored with torcs and armbands by Tiberius Caesar twice, serving in the 20th Legion.
EDCS-04203417.summary: This commemorates Lucius Antonius Quadratus, who received military honors from Tiberius Caesar while serving in the 20th Legion.

EDCS-04203418.translation: Aurelius Bersimes, a veteran, set up this memorial for himself during his lifetime in place of Valens.
EDCS-04203418.summary: This is a self-dedicated memorial tombstone by a veteran named Aurelius Bersimes.

EDCS-04203419.translation: To the spirits of Lucius Caelus Arrianus, physician of the Second Italic Legion, who lived 47 years and 7 months. Scribonia Faustina, [erected this] for her dearest husband.
EDCS-04203419.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Caelus Arrianus, a physician in the Second Italic Legion, erected by his wife.

EDCS-04203420.translation: To Publius Clodius Sura, son of Publius, of the Fabian tribe, quaestor, flamen of the deified Trajan, duumvir quinquennalis, tribune of the Legio II Adiutrix Pia Fidelis, curator of the public affairs of the Bergomates appointed by Emperor Trajan, curator of the public affairs of the Comensates appointed by Emperor Hadrian; by the guilds of artisans and the centonarii.
EDCS-04203420.summary: This is a dedication by guilds to Publius Clodius Sura, a prominent local official who served under Emperors Trajan and Hadrian.

EDCS-04203421.translation: Flavius Higgo, a shield-bearer of the third schola, who lived about 25 years and served 6 years, erected this memorial to a most dear and loving brother-in-law, with his wife.
EDCS-04203421.summary: This is a funerary monument for Flavius Higgo, a soldier, erected by his brother-in-law and wife.

EDCS-04203422.translation: To Flavius Luppius, former prefect, from Aurelia Severina, his most loving mother, who lived 75 years, 7 months, and 19 days. Farewell, my most dutiful mother.
EDCS-04203422.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a mother, Aurelia Severina, to her deceased son, Flavius Luppius, a former prefect.

EDCS-04203423.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Aurelius Iustinus of Petovio made this for his well-deserving brother, Iulius Festus, a standard-bearer of the 2nd Praetorian cohort, who served 12 years and was promoted 7 times, a citizen of Petovio. Died in barbarian war.
EDCS-04203423.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Aurelius Iustinus for his brother, Iulius Festus, a standard-bearer in the Praetorian Guard who died in a barbarian war.

EDCS-04203424.translation: Gaius Julius Tappo, tribune of the soldiers, [serving] in the 5th Legion.
EDCS-04203424.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring Gaius Julius Tappo, a military tribune.

EDCS-04203425.translation: To Gaius Meffius Saxo, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, former first-rank centurion, prefect of a cohort, prefect of engineers, quinquennial pontiff, by the cohort of the Carietes and Venaisetians.
EDCS-04203425.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Meffius Saxo with various military and civic titles, dedicated by the cohort of the Carietes and Venaisetians.

EDCS-04203426.translation: Publius Papirius Pastor, son of Publius, augur, twice duovir, prefect of engineers, prefect of Emperor Nero, twice quinquennial duovir, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, for his brother Gnaeus Papirius Fuscus, twice duovir, and for his son Gnaeus Papirius Fuscus, pontiff.
EDCS-04203426.summary: This funerary inscription records the provision made by Publius Papirius Pastor for himself and his male relatives, highlighting his significant civic and religious roles.

EDCS-04203427.translation: To Marcus Romanus Macrinus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, a veteran. Lucretius Censorinus [erected this].
EDCS-04203427.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Lucretius Censorinus to Marcus Romanus Macrinus, a veteran.

EDCS-04203428.translation: Accept, departed spirits, this final gift of honor. Valerius Vasse served in the exarchate in a detachment of the Stablesian cavalry for 25 years, 5 months, and 17 days. He lived for 44 years, 7 months, and 13 days. Valerius Donatus erected this for his most devoted brother at his own expense.
EDCS-04203428.summary: This tombstone commemorates Valerius Vasse, who served in the cavalry and died at a relatively young age, with the monument erected by his devoted brother.

EDCS-04203429.translation: To Marcus Valerius Vindicus, son of Spurius, a soldier of the Tenth Legion. Urbanus [erected this] for his brother.
EDCS-04203429.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Urbanus to his brother, Marcus Valerius Vindicus, a soldier of the Tenth Legion.

EDCS-04203430.translation: Titus Vidius, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, centurion of the Fourth Macedonian Legion.
EDCS-04203430.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Titus Vidius and his military rank as a centurion in the Fourth Macedonian Legion.

EDCS-04203435.translation: To Publius Acilius Heliodorus, VI vir Augustalis. Publius Acilius Helenus [erected this] for his most devoted brother.
EDCS-04203435.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Publius Acilius Helenus to his brother, Publius Acilius Heliodorus, who held the prestigious position of VI vir Augustalis.

EDCS-04203436.translation: To Lucius Acutius Primus, son of Lucius, of the Fabian tribe, who held the public horse, served as duumvir with power of jurisdiction, aedile, quaestor of supplies, and flamen of the deified Julius; by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203436.summary: This is a dedication by the town council to Lucius Acutius Primus, honoring his public service and magistracies.

EDCS-04203437.translation: To Gaius Aemilius Atticus, son of Gaius, aedile.
EDCS-04203437.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Gaius Aemilius Atticus, who served as an aedile.

EDCS-04203438.translation: To Gaius Aemilius Proculus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, quaestor, promoted among the holders of the duovirate, flamen of the divine Augustus, used the title from the guilds of engineers and clothiers.
EDCS-04203438.summary: This inscription details the distinguished career and titles of Gaius Aemilius Proculus, a prominent local official and priest.

EDCS-04203439.translation: To Aemilia Aqua, daughter of Gaius, priestess of the deified Plotina; by the guild of centonarii, who used this title.
EDCS-04203439.summary: This inscription honors Aemilia Aqua, a priestess, and indicates it was erected by the guild of centonarii.

EDCS-04203440.translation: The guild of woodworkers erected this at its own expense to Aemilia Synethia, its patroness, and to her mother Aemilia Agrestina, for their merits.
EDCS-04203440.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the guild of woodworkers to their patroness Aemilia Synethia and her mother Aemilia Agrestina, honoring their contributions.

EDCS-04203441.translation: Quintus Antuleius Soterichus, one of the six Augustan priests, for himself and for his excellent wife Antuleia Callityche, and for his mother Antuleia Macrina, and for his freedwoman, and for his mother-in-law Antuleia Marta, and for Quintus Antuleius Trophimus, son of C.N., and...
EDCS-04203441.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Antuleius Soterichus, an Augustalis priest, for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04203442.translation: Ophus, one of the six Augustan priests, for himself and for his dearest wife Arrenia Agathemeris...
EDCS-04203442.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Ophus, an Augustalis priest, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04203443.translation: The Guild of Smiths, for Spurius Atilius Cerialis, who left his property to the guild.
EDCS-04203443.summary: This inscription records a bequest from Spurius Atilius Cerialis to the Guild of Smiths.

EDCS-04203444.translation: To Publius Atilius Philippus, honored with the curule decorations of Brixia, Verona, and Cremona, and with the rights of four children and the use of rings by the deified [Emperor] at the people's request on account of his generosity, which [he showed] in the amphitheater project...
EDCS-04203444.summary: This is a dedication honoring Publius Atilius Philippus for his public service and generosity, particularly towards the amphitheater project.

EDCS-04203445.translation: Quintus Atilius Scaeva, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, one of the six Augustan priests, aedile, for himself and...
EDCS-04203445.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Atilius Scaeva, an Augustalis priest and aedile, for himself and possibly others.

EDCS-04203446.translation: To Lucius Attius Fuscus, a six-man Augustan priest, and his friend Repentinus.
EDCS-04203446.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Attius Fuscus, an Augustalis priest, and his friend Repentinus.

EDCS-04203447.translation: His colleagues made this for Aurelius Vivus, who lived 45 years, his dearest colleague, because of his merits.
EDCS-04203447.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by the colleagues of Aurelius Vivus, who died at the age of 45.

EDCS-04203448.translation: To Bedasia Iusta, daughter of Quintus, the Guild of Smiths and the Guild of Centonarii, having used the title, with Gaius Lucretius Annianus as husband, the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203448.summary: This inscription records a burial plot granted by decree of the decurions to Bedasia Iusta, with her husband Caius Lucretius Annianus, and mentions the Guild of Smiths and Centonarii.

EDCS-04203449.translation: To Bittalia Festa, daughter of Publius, the Guild of Smiths and the Guild of Centonarii, having used the title...
EDCS-04203449.summary: This inscription records the use of a title by Bittalia Festa, daughter of Publius, in connection with the Guild of Smiths and Centonarii.

EDCS-04203450.translation: Marcus Caecilius Fuscus, one of the six Augustan priests, for himself and for his mother Caesias Fusca, and for his wife Mestria Amina, and for his father Publius Postumius Asellio.
EDCS-04203450.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Caecilius Fuscus, an Augustalis priest, for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04203451.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Telesphorus, Augustalis vigintivir, of Cremona, and curule aedile, for his most excellent husband and for himself.
EDCS-04203451.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Caecilius Telesphorus, an Augustalis vigintivir and curule aedile, by his wife.

EDCS-04203452.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Caecilia Procula, priestess of the Fifteen, Lucius Acutius Caecilianus, her ward, and for Publius Acilius Suro, her foster-father.
EDCS-04203452.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Caecilia Procula, a priestess, by her ward and foster-father.

EDCS-04203453.translation: Gaius Calventius Herma, freedman of Gaius Calventius, Augustalis sexvir, for himself and for his wife Silia Prisca and for his brother Gaius Aulus Apollonius.
EDCS-04203453.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Calventius Herma, an Augustalis sexvir, for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04203454.translation: Lucius Calventius Vicalus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, a decurion, made this while alive for himself and for his wives, Aurelia Vera, daughter of Lucius, and his daughter Aufidia Magna.
EDCS-04203454.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Calventius Vicalus, a decurion, for himself and his wives and daughter.

EDCS-04203455.translation: Lucius Camurius Pandarus, freedman of Lucius, Augustalis sexvir, for himself and for his freedman Zenon.
EDCS-04203455.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Camurius Pandarus, an Augustalis sexvir, for himself and his freedman.

EDCS-04203456.translation: Gaius Catius Alexander, freedman, for himself and for his patrons for their services, and for his freedwoman wife Mucia Restituta, and for Gaius Catius Nason, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, a decurion, and for Gaius Catius Fructus, this was made while alive by Gaius Catius Alexander.
EDCS-04203456.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Catius Alexander, a freedman and decurion, for himself, his patrons, his wife, and another member of his family.

EDCS-04203457.translation: Tiberius Claudius Auctus, Augustalis vigintivir, and again by decree of the decurions, for himself and for his wife Claudia Arretina, and for Tiberius Claudius Hermogenes, Tiberius Claudius Attalus, Tiberius Claudius Trophimus, Augustalis vigintivir, for Claudia Marcellina, Claudia Hermione, and Claudius Chresimus.
EDCS-04203457.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Tiberius Claudius Auctus, an Augustalis vigintivir, for himself, his wife, and several other individuals including another vigintivir.

EDCS-04203458.translation: Lucius Claudius Sabinianus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, equestrian status, supported by the guilds of carpenters and carpet-makers, used the title.
EDCS-04203458.summary: This inscription records Lucius Claudius Sabinianus, an eques publicus, who was supported by the guilds of carpenters and carpet-makers.

EDCS-04203459.translation: To Marcus Clodius Sura, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203459.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Clodius Sura, authorized by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-04203460.translation: The guilds of carpenters and carpet-makers, to Quintus Clodius Ursinnus for the honor of his quaestorship.
EDCS-04203460.summary: This is a dedication by the guilds of carpenters and carpet-makers to Quintus Clodius Ursinnus in recognition of his quaestorship.

EDCS-04203461.translation: To Mineme, freedwoman of Clodia, for herself and for her cohabitant Marcus Rustius Severus, and for her son Titus Octavius Mionidus, VI vir Augustalis, and for her friend Gaius Rantulanus.
EDCS-04203461.summary: This epitaph commemorates Mineme, a freedwoman, and her family and friend, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203462.translation: To the departed spirits. For Clodia Achillea, also called Cyrille, who lived 29 years, 11 months, and 6 days. Lucius Vettius Ursinianus, her husband, to his incomparable wife, who gave to the college of VI viri socii 1000 sesterces, so that from the interest of this sum, expenses for her may be celebrated annually, both for parental rites and for the rites of roses.
EDCS-04203462.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Clodia Achillea and is dedicated by her husband, Lucius Vettius Ursinianus, who endowed an annual celebration by a collegium.

EDCS-04203463.translation: To Coelia Paternus, mother of the synagogue of the people of Brixia.
EDCS-04203463.summary: This dedicatory inscription honors Coelia Paternus, identified as the mother of a Jewish community in Brixia.

EDCS-04203464.translation: Quintus Cornelius [---] for the construction of the bathhouse.
EDCS-04203464.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating that Quintus Cornelius was involved in the construction of a public bath, likely as an official.

EDCS-04203465.translation: Quintus Cornelius Fronto, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, aedile, quaestor, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04203465.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Quintus Cornelius Fronto, who held the offices of aedile and quaestor, commissioned his own tomb by his will.

EDCS-04203466.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Glyco, VI vir Augustalis of Brixia. Claudia Martia to her most devoted husband.
EDCS-04203466.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Claudia Martia to her husband, Lucius Cornelius Glyco, who was a member of the collegium of VI viri Augustales in Brixia.

EDCS-04203467.translation: To the departed spirits. For Marcus Cornelius Proculus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, from the guild of blanket makers, and to Marcus Cornelius Aequus, his father, and to Quinta, his mother.
EDCS-04203467.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to Marcus Cornelius Proculus by his guild of blanket makers, and also commemorates his parents.

EDCS-04203468.translation: The guilds of builders and blanket makers, content with honor given for his merits to Lucius Cornelius Prosodicus, VI vir Augustalis of Brixia and Verona, and priest of the guild of youth of Brixia (first established), remitted the expense, having given 500 sesterces for protection.
EDCS-04203468.summary: This honorary inscription records the recognition by two guilds of Lucius Cornelius Prosodicus for his merits and his renunciation of expenses related to his honorary positions.

EDCS-04203469.translation: To Publius Craexius Naevilianus Senior, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, who completed all municipal offices with public equus (status), a companion.
EDCS-04203469.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Publius Craexius Naevilianus Senior, recognizing his distinguished public career and equestrian status.

EDCS-04203470.translation: To the guild of tree bearers. Gaius Crispus Hesperius for himself and for Maria Synethia, his wife, and for protection, gave one thousand sesterces to the guild of tree bearers in Brixia and Verona.
EDCS-04203470.summary: This inscription records a donation made by Gaius Crispus Hesperius and his wife to the guild of tree bearers in Brixia and Verona.

EDCS-04203471.translation: Lucius Domitius Proculus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, aedile, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his father and mother and brother.
EDCS-04203471.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Lucius Domitius Proculus, an aedile, commissioned his tomb by his will for himself and his family.

EDCS-04203472.translation: To Lucius Domitius Valerianus, decurion and quaestor, Lucius Domitius Cornelianus granted a place to his father and Cornelia Marcella, his wife, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203472.summary: A funerary monument or grant of burial place to Lucius Domitius Valerianus, decurion and quaestor, by his son Lucius Domitius Cornelianus and wife Cornelia Marcella, dated by the mention of Valerianus.

EDCS-04203473.translation: To Sextus Donnius Antonius, by the villagers of the vicus Minervi.
