EDCS-04203473.summary: A dedication to Sextus Donnius Antonius by the villagers of the vicus Minervi, likely a local official or benefactor.

EDCS-04203474.translation: To Fabricia Centonia Arethusa, his most excellent wife, and to Chresime, his dearest daughter, by Fabricius Centonius, freedman of the collegia, Chresimus.
EDCS-04203474.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fabricia Centonia Arethusa and her daughter Chresime, set up by Fabricius Centonius, a freedman involved in collegia.

EDCS-04203476.translation: Lucius Fictorius Tertius, Augustalis VI vir, for himself and for his wife Firmia Firma and
EDCS-04203476.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Fictorius Tertius, an Augustalis VI vir, for himself and his wife, likely incomplete.

EDCS-04203478.translation: To the Collegium of the Centonarii, by Sextus Helvius Leo, for services rendered to them.
EDCS-04203478.summary: A dedication by Sextus Helvius Leo to the Collegium of the Centonarii in recognition of his services.

EDCS-04203479.translation: To Gaius Hostilius Carbo, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, IIII vir for administering justice.
EDCS-04203479.summary: An inscription honoring Gaius Hostilius Carbo, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, who held the office of IIII vir iure dicundo.

EDCS-04203480.translation: To Pietas Hostiliana, daughter of Hostilius, the Augustales VI viri, members, who by permission of the deified Pius were allowed to have a burial chest, used the inscription for the first deserving recipient.
EDCS-04203480.summary: A dedication to Pietas Hostiliana by the Augustales VI viri, noting her deserving status for the use of a burial chest granted by Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-04203481.translation: To Hostilia Tryphaena, by Publius Hostilius Comicus, freedman of Publius, son of Gaius, Augustalis VI vir, for himself and for his freedman Florentinus Encrinomenus.
EDCS-04203481.summary: A funerary dedication by Publius Hostilius Comicus, a freedman and Augustalis VI vir, for himself and his freedman Hostilia Tryphaena and Encrinomenus.

EDCS-04203482.translation: To Marcus Iulius Homuncio and Cornelia Tertulla, his most dutiful parents, and to Iulius Hominis and Iulia Marcellina, his most dutiful siblings, Marcus Iulius Marcellinus, decurion of Brixia, for himself and for his most excellent wife Mesia Pusinna.
EDCS-04203482.summary: A funerary monument by Marcus Iulius Marcellinus, a decurion of Brixia, for his parents, siblings, himself, and his wife Mesia Pusinna.

EDCS-04203483.translation: To Gaius Iulius Paulinus Andragathus, Augustalis VI vir, honorary, Gaius Iulius Aquilinus, to his father.
EDCS-04203483.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Iulius Aquilinus to his father, Gaius Iulius Paulinus Andragathus, who was an honorary Augustalis VI vir.

EDCS-04203484.translation: Iunius Evira and the members of the college of the Lares to their well-deserving patroness.
EDCS-04203484.summary: This is a dedication by members of a college to their patroness, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203485.translation: The college of craftsmen to Marcus Iuventius Magius, who left his possessions to the college.
EDCS-04203485.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a college of craftsmen to a benefactor, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203486.translation: To Sextus Laetilius Firminus, son of Sextus, of the Fabia tribe, a VI vir Augustalis, from Laetilia Vera and Secunda, to their most dutiful brother.
EDCS-04203486.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a VI vir Augustalis, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203487.translation: Sextus Laetilius, VI vir Augustalis, had this made in his lifetime for himself, for his parents Sextus Laetilius Valens and Rufa Raucula, and for his daughter Festa Ianuaria, his wife, and for his sons Sextus Laetilius Secundus and Laetilia Primula, and for his daughter-in-law Laetilia Firmina.
EDCS-04203487.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a VI vir Augustalis for himself and his family members, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203488.translation: Lucius Laudonius Hermes, a VI vir Augustalis of Brixia, had this made in his lifetime for himself and his wife Laudonia Firma, for his freedmen Laudonia Firmula and Laudonius Primitivus Quartio, and donated the plot to Lucius N. Diogenes.
EDCS-04203488.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by a VI vir Augustalis for himself and his family, including the donation of a plot, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203489.translation: Lucius Lepidius Philemo, freedman of Lucius, a sexvir Augustalis, had this made in his lifetime for himself, for his wife Melia Maxima, daughter of Lucius, and for his son Marcus Lepidius Primus.
EDCS-04203489.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman who held the office of sexvir Augustalis, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203490.translation: Iuventius Eros erected this altar for his dearest friend, Lucius Lucretius Ephorus, a VI vir Augustalis, and for his most holy mistress and dearest friend, Statia Vera.
EDCS-04203490.summary: This inscription records an altar erected by Iuventius Eros for his friend and his friend's wife, who was also his friend, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203491.translation: Gaius Lucretius Erasmus, freedman of Gaius, a sexvir Augustalis of Brixia and Tridentum, [dedicated this] for himself and for his dearest wife Comminia Onesime, for his most dutiful freedman Gaius Lucretius Hermes, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, [also] free of charge.
EDCS-04203491.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman who held the office of sexvir Augustalis, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203492.translation: Marcellina to the college of the Lares, I have given 500 denarii so that for us (there may be) rose wreaths and funeral rites.
EDCS-04203492.summary: This inscription records a donation of money by Marcellina to a college for the provision of funeral rites, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203493.translation: The ordo of the Brixians decreed a public funeral and a gilded equestrian statue to Publius Matienus Proculus, son of Publius, of the Fabian tribe, Romanicus Maximus, aged six years, two months, and five days; his unhappy father, Matienus Exoratus, used this monument.
EDCS-04203493.summary: This inscription records a posthumous honor granted by the town council of Brixia to a young boy, Publius Matienus Proculus, with his father dedicating the monument.

EDCS-04203494.translation: Po[...], son of S., Latro, priest of the divine Augustus at Cremona, and Ir. Merkator of Cremona, and Viator of Cremona.
EDCS-04203494.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning priests and individuals from Cremona, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203495.translation: To Quintus Minicius Macro, son of Quintus, of the Poblilia tribe, duovir of Verona, quaestor of Verona and Brixia. Minicia Fortunata, his mother, lovingly gave this place to her most dutiful son by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203495.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a mother for her deceased son, Quintus Minicius Macro, who held magistracies in Verona and Brixia, with the space granted by local officials.

EDCS-04203496.translation: Marcus Minicius Quintianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, decurion of Brixia, quaestor of the treasury. Marcus Minicius Minicianus, his uncle, had this made according to his will.
EDCS-04203496.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Minicius Quintianus, a local official, paid for by his uncle as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-04203497.translation: Lucius Naevidius, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe, VI vir Augustalis, ordered this to be made for himself, Vitalis, Faustus, Cnomius, Fidus, and his freedmen by his will. Then, weary of a long life full of many inconveniences, I rested at this time.
EDCS-04203497.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Naevidius, a member of the VI viri Augustales, who provided for himself, his family, and freedmen in his will, and reflects on the burdens of a long life.

EDCS-04203498.translation: Nymphodotus, VI vir Augustalis, for himself and his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04203498.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Nymphodotus, a member of the VI viri Augustales, for himself and his freed dependents.

EDCS-04203499.translation: To Paccia Verina, daughter of Caius, of the Verina tribe. Titus Maesius Licinianus gave this place to his wife by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203499.summary: This funerary monument records the allocation of space by the decurions for Paccia Verina, granted by her husband Titus Maesius Licinianus.

EDCS-04203500.translation: To Pamn, who lived 6 years, 9 months, 15 days, dearest son, and to Cornelia Servanda, sweetest wife. Iulius Bittici, his son, who gave this to the guild of artisans, so that from the interest they may make expenditures annually and place roses.
EDCS-04203500.summary: This is a funerary monument for a young boy, Pamn, and his mother Cornelia Servanda, funded by his father Iulius Bittici, who endowed a fund for the artisans' guild to maintain the grave and provide roses.

EDCS-04203501.translation: To the Genius and Honor of Primi Pampili Secundi and Lucius Atilius Exoratus, sextum viri Augustales, and to Marcus Vettidius Aquileiensis, sextum vir Augustalis, quinquennalis, and having served as master in all guilds; by Artemisius who is also [---]asco Ortensius Firmianus, Valerius Surianus, Publilius Vitalis, and Adiacius Primianus, who served in their office as masters of the aforementioned; erected as a memorial, having granted 1000 sesterces for tutelage, so that on the Kalends of February a sacrifice is made, and for distribution 300 sesterces; the aforementioned masters, having performed their office, used this title of honor, having granted 1000 sesterces for tutelage, so that from their usury, annually on the 3rd Ides of April, a sacrifice is made through officials, with oil and drink offering, they dedicated [this].
EDCS-04203501.summary: This inscription details a funerary endowment by several members of the collegium of Augustales and other guilds, establishing annual sacrifices and distributions funded by their donations.

EDCS-04203502.translation: To Publius Papirius Onesiphorus, by the villagers of the Minervius vicus.
EDCS-04203502.summary: This is a dedication by the villagers of the Minervius vicus to Publius Papirius Onesiphorus.

EDCS-04203503.translation: To Papiria Patrobi, freedwoman, by the villagers of the Minervius vicus, Trophimus.
EDCS-04203503.summary: This is a dedication by the villagers of the Minervius vicus and Trophimus to Papiria Patrobi, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04203504.translation: To Petronia Baebiana, daughter of Quintus, of the Baebiana tribe, the guild of blanket makers used this inscription.
EDCS-04203504.summary: This inscription records that the guild of blanket makers used this monument for Petronia Baebiana, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-04203505.translation: To Caius Picatius Trophimus, her father, and to her husband, the best VI vir Augustalis. Placidia Tertiola and Picatius Eleuther.
EDCS-04203505.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Placidia Tertiola and Picatius Eleuther to commemorate her father, Caius Picatius Trophimus, and her husband, a VI vir Augustalis.

EDCS-04203506.translation: A place was granted to Picatia, daughter of Lucius, by decree of the decurions, for the associations of fullers and fabric workers.
EDCS-04203506.summary: This inscription records a grant of space to an association by decree of local councillors.

EDCS-04203507.translation: To Gaius Pladicius Clodianus, son of Gaius, of the Palatine tribe, a decurion of Brixia with public equestrian rank, Gaius Pladicius Hermadion and Lucretia Persis granted a place to their most dutiful son by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203507.summary: This inscription records the granting of a plot of land to a decurion of Brixia by his parents.

EDCS-04203508.translation: Gaius Postumius Costa, son of Gaius; Gaius Postumius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04203508.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple naming of two individuals, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-04203509.translation: Gaius Postumius Varus, son of Quintus, a Sextumvir Augustalis and aedile, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Ratumedia Severa, daughter of Lucius, his wife, and for his father Quintus Postumius, son of Gaius, and for Naevia Mogetilla, daughter of Gnaeus, his mother, and for his brother Quintus Postumius Pusion, son of Quintus, and for his brother Lucius Postumius Ferox, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04203509.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the bequests and relationships of Quintus Postumius Varus, a Sextumvir Augustalis and aedile.

EDCS-04203510.translation: To Postumia Paula, daughter of Publius; and to Avidia Procula; and to Rutilia Proba, priestess of the divine Augusta, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203510.summary: This inscription honours several women, including a priestess of the deified Augusta, and was erected by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-04203511.translation: To Marcus Publicius Sextius Calpurnianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabian tribe, flamen of the deified Julius with public equestrian rank, prefect with aedilician power, quaestor of the treasury, priest of the youth of Brixia, defender of the republic of Brixia, a place was granted by decree of the decurions for the associations of fullers and fabric workers.
EDCS-04203511.summary: This inscription records a grant of space for guilds to Marcus Publicius Sextius Calpurnianus, a prominent local magistrate and priest.

EDCS-04203512.translation: Gaius Quintius Catullus, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, a decurion of Brixia, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Cornelia Magna, daughter of Marcus, his wife, and for his brother Quintus Quintius, son of Gaius, and for his father Gaius Quintius Secundus, and for his mother Antonia Catulla.
EDCS-04203512.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the bequests and family members of Gaius Quintius Catullus, a decurion of Brixia.

EDCS-04203513.translation: Titus Quinctius Daphnus, freedman of Titus, a Sextumvir Augustalis, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04203513.summary: This inscription records a funerary commission by Titus Quinctius Daphnus, a freedman and Sextumvir Augustalis.

EDCS-04203514.translation: Lucius Quinctius Grullus, son of Publius, of the Fabian tribe, a duumvir and pontifex, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his son Labeo Scipio, and for his son Quinctia, and for Publius Cornelius Scipio, son of Publius, and for Lucius Quinctius Ursulus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203514.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Quinctius Grullus, a duumvir and pontifex, detailing his bequests and family members.

EDCS-04203515.translation: To Quintia Restituta, for Gaius Petronius Fronton, of the Fabian tribe, a Sextumvir Augustalis of Brixia, for her most dutiful husband.
EDCS-04203515.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Quintia Restituta to her husband, Gaius Petronius Fronton, a Sextumvir Augustalis of Brixia.

EDCS-04203517.translation: Marcus Romanius Suavis, freedman of Marcus, an Augustalis priest, ordered by his will to be made for himself, his son Marcus Romanus Probus, and his partner Cincia Modesta.
EDCS-04203517.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Romanius Suavis, commissioned by himself and intended for his family, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203518.translation: Publius Rufrius Balbinus, son of Publius, a decurion in the colony, ordered by his will to be made for himself, his brother Gaius Rufrius Pedon, son of Publius, his freedwoman Rufria Amona, daughter of Publius, and his own family.
EDCS-04203518.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Rufrius Balbinus, a local official, commissioned by himself and intended for his family, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203519.translation: Marcus Rustius Gamus, an Augustalis priest, for himself and his partner Quintia Sebaste.
EDCS-04203519.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Rustius Gamus, an Augustalis priest, and his partner Quintia Sebaste, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203520.translation: Marcus Salvidienus Vettianus, prefect with aedilician power, olive measures and a statue with his own money.
EDCS-04203520.summary: This inscription records Marcus Salvidienus Vettianus, a magistrate, donating olive measures and a statue, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203522.translation: Publius Senecius Garrulus ordered to be made by the heirs according to the will for Caecilia Macrina, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-04203522.summary: This funerary inscription records the posthumous commission by heirs for Caecilia Macrina, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203523.translation: To Publius Senecio Garrulus, son of Publius, of the Fabian tribe, who held the public horse, and served as praefect of the artisans and quaestor; by his heirs, according to his will.
EDCS-04203523.summary: This inscription is a posthumous dedication by the heirs to Publius Senecio Garrulus, honoring his public offices.

EDCS-04203524.translation: By decree of the decurions, Gaius Sentius Valerianus, father of Caius Sentius Mariano, who had used the public horse and was a decurion, bequeathed 12,000 sesterces in his will for its construction; Eutychus and Nicephorus, freedmen, placed it, adding 8,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04203524.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument, funded by a bequest and additional contributions from freedmen, by order of the local council, likely dating from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203525.translation: Gaius Sentius Onesimus, an Augustalis priest, for his excellent wife Sentia Alexandria, and for himself.
EDCS-04203525.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Sentius Onesimus, an Augustalis priest, and his wife Sentia Alexandria, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203526.translation: Lucius Septimius Agatianus, an Augustalis priest, for himself and Lucius Septimius, a decurion of Brixia, Lucius Septimius Frugio Proculus Camo Calventius, Lucius Septimius Frugio Calventius, a freedman.
EDCS-04203526.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Septimius Agatianus, an Augustalis priest, and several family members, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203527.translation: A place was granted by decree of the decurions for Gallinianus, son of Lucius Septimius, a Fabia, aedile, decurion, quaestor, to his excellent husband.
EDCS-04203527.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by decree of the local council for Gallinianus, a local official, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203528.translation: Servilius Verus, the father, requested that a place be made for Servilius Popilianus, a decurion who had used the public horse; a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04203528.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by decree of the local council for Servilius Popilianus, a decurion, at the request of his father, likely dating from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04203529.translation: To Sextus Sextius Onesigenus, for the decurional honors and as VI vir Augustalis, patron of the guilds of builders, fullers, and wood-carriers.
EDCS-04203529.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a patron of several guilds, recognizing his civic and religious offices.

EDCS-04203530.translation: Gaius Sillenus Serenianus, son of Gaius, of Aniensis, after having held all municipal offices, and to his incomparable wife, Vera, daughter of Gaius, with whom I lived for 27 years, 11 months, and 27 days, erected this tomb while alive.
EDCS-04203530.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a man for his deceased wife, detailing his own municipal career and their shared life, likely dating from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203531.translation: Erected this while alive by Publius Sta Hori, IIII vir Augustalis.
EDCS-04203531.summary: A brief funerary dedication for himself by a local magistrate (IIII vir Augustalis), likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203532.translation: To Marcus Terentius Pyramus, VI vir Augustalis, for his free friend Lucius Appius Aphrobetus, VI vir Augustalis, and to his wife Terentia Pista, and to Publius Postumius Primus, and to Postumia Quarta, and to his well-deserving friends.
EDCS-04203532.summary: This inscription commemorates multiple individuals, including Marcus Terentius Pyramus who held the high office of VI vir Augustalis, likely a tomb inscription from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203534.translation: To Anteros Asiaticus, freedman of Marcus Valerius, son of Lucius Publius, and of the freedwoman Valeria Tryphera, his wife, and to his freedman Philetus.
EDCS-04203534.summary: This inscription records a tomb erected by Anteros Asiaticus, a freedman who held the position of VI vir, for himself, his wife, and another freedman, probably dating from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203535.translation: To Primo Valerius Magirra, of the guilds of builders and fullers, who lived 33 years, 2 months, and 24 days, full of integrity, whom his grieving friends mourned upon his death. Marcus Publilius Valentinus, a friend, gave the burial place. Magius Valerius Surius erected the altar to his most pious and unfortunate grandson.
EDCS-04203535.summary: This inscription records a burial plot granted by a friend and an altar erected by a grandfather for his deceased grandson, who was a member of the guilds of builders and fullers.

EDCS-04203536.translation: To Sextus Valerius Poblicola, son of Sextus, of the Fabia tribe, Vettilliani, Roman knight with public horse, perpetual priest of the eternal city of Rome, curator and patron of the communities of Vardagates and Dripsinates, patron of all guilds, who had fulfilled all offices, a good man who lived without complaint for 45 years with his wife below named, and to Arria Hermionilla, daughter of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, with the greatest piety, beloved by them, his very rare grandparents, Marcus Annius Valerius Catullus, his grandson.
EDCS-04203536.summary: This extensive epitaph honors Sextus Valerius Poblicola, a man of equestrian rank, priest, and patron, and his wife Arria Hermionilla, highlighting his extensive public career and virtues, likely from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203537.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-04203537.translation: To Sextus Valerius Poblicola, son of Sextus, of the Fabian tribe, Roman knight, who held the public horse, decurion of Brixia, Verona, and Trident, and Nicomedia, for whom the ordo of the Brixians decreed a gilded equestrian statue and a public funeral; and to Clodia Procilla, daughter of Quintus, priestess of the deified Plotina; by Sextus Valerius Poblicola Priscillianus, his son.
EDCS-04203537.summary: This inscription honors Sextus Valerius Poblicola and his wife Clodia Procilla, detailing public honors granted to him by the town council of Brixia and erected by their son.

EDCS-04203539.translation: To Sextus Valerius Rufus, son of Sextus, of the Fabian tribe, praefect with power of jurisdiction, quaestor, and to Bivonia Priscilla, daughter of Publius; honored with a public funeral; by Sextus Valerius Primus, son of Sextus, of the Fabian tribe, their most excellent parents.
EDCS-04203539.summary: This inscription records a public funeral granted to Sextus Valerius Rufus and Bivonia Priscilla, erected by their son.

EDCS-04203540.translation: To the spirits of Mannulus and Valeria Aprilis, his deserving parents, and to himself and his wife Acutia Ursa. Caius Valerius Primitius bequeathed 20,000 sesterces and in addition the shops with upper floors in the Street of Hercules to the guild of fullers in perpetuity, to be administered by the officials of the guild of fullers. What did not bring me enough pleasure, I decree that it shall have the Ingenani, which yields 200 denarii, so that 100 denarii from this may be used for my pleasure and 100 denarii for the guardianship of the aforementioned shops.
EDCS-04203540.summary: This inscription is a will detailing a bequest of property and money to the guild of fullers by Caius Valerius Primitius for the benefit of his parents, himself, and his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203541.translation: To Valeria Ursa, who lived with me for 30 years, 3 months, and 8 days, who while alive transferred her field in Aeseianum to the guild of builders from her half portion, so that from the income of this field every year 50 denarii should be celebrated annually for Silia, her husband, on her birthday, the day before the Kalends of March, and on her own birthday, the day before the Kalends of March, through the magistrates. Likewise, on the days of the Parentalia and Rosalia, 25 denarii for each should be expended in perpetuity. She also transferred her field IVE Janus to the guild of public pharmacists while alive, so that from the income of this field every year 50 denarii should be celebrated annually for Silia, her husband, on his birthday, the 8th day before the Kalends of November, and on her own birthday, the day before the Kalends of March, through the magistrates. Likewise, on the days of the Parentalia and Rosalia, 25 denarii for each should be expended in perpetuity. Marcus Ulpius Fortunius to his most chaste wife.
EDCS-04203541.summary: This inscription records the property bequests of Valeria Ursa, made while alive to the guilds of builders and public pharmacists, with specific instructions for expenditures on festivals and for her husband, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203542.translation: To Quinto Vibio, VI vir Augustalis, to Quinto Vibio Ac, VI vir Augustalis, to Vibia Preti, to Quinto Vibio Vibianus, to Epula Vibia, to his granddaughter Vibia.
EDCS-04203542.summary: This inscription is a dedication or list of honorees, all seemingly connected to the office of VI vir Augustalis, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04203543.translation: To Gaius Vibius Justus and Gaius Vibius Burdo, the guild of cloth-makers [dedicated this] to the Six, Augustals.
EDCS-04203543.summary: This is a dedication by the guild of cloth-makers to two individuals honored as Six, Augustals.

EDCS-04203544.translation: Caius Viracius Quintinus [dedicated this] to Gaius Viracius Longinus, Six, priest of Salii, and to Quintia Quinta, daughter of Publius, in Verona.
EDCS-04203544.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Caius Viracius Quintinus to Gaius Viracius Longinus and Quintia Quinta, likely family members, in Verona.

EDCS-04203545.translation: To Lucius Virius Secundus, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-04203545.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Virius Secundus, authorized by a decree of the local councillors.

EDCS-04203548.translation: To the Divine Shades of Dicaeus, a Six, Augustal. M.
EDCS-04203548.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Dicaeus, honored as a Six, Augustal.

EDCS-04203552.translation: Wash well. Salvus, having been washed, Peripsuma...
EDCS-04203552.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly related to bathing or hygiene, mentioning individuals named Salvus and Peripsuma.

EDCS-04203553.translation: The members of the association of wool-combers placed [this] to Acceptus, a slave of Chia.
EDCS-04203553.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the association of wool-combers to Acceptus, a slave.

EDCS-04203554.translation: To the Divine Shades of Antigonus, the provokator. Verus, the trainer, erected [this].
EDCS-04203554.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Antigonus, identified as a provokator, erected by Verus, who was a trainer.

EDCS-04203556.translation: To Claudia Varilla, his excellent companion, from Quartio, the bailiff and treasurer of the people of Brixia.
EDCS-04203556.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Quartio to his 'companion' Claudia Varilla, identifying his roles as treasurer and bailiff in Brixia.

EDCS-04203557.translation: To Gaius Cominius Successor, the wool-pressers, from their own funds.
EDCS-04203557.summary: This is a dedication by wool-pressers to Gaius Cominius Successor, funded by themselves.

EDCS-04203558.translation: To the Divine Shades of Lucius Cornelius Ianuarius, who lived 17 years, the wool-pressers and Lucius Cornelius Primio, his father.
EDCS-04203558.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Lucius Cornelius Ianuarius, who died at 17, erected by wool-pressers and his father.

EDCS-04203559.translation: To the Divine Shades. Ingenua placed this for her dear husband Iantinus, a net-fighter, who lived 24 years, 4 months, of Fryx origin, and had won 5 fights, with whom she lived 5 years, 2 months.
EDCS-04203559.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iantinus, a net-fighter, set up by his wife Ingenua.

EDCS-04203560.translation: Cosmus, the steward of the Brixian farmers, in his capacity as deputy.
EDCS-04203560.summary: An inscription identifying Cosmus as a deputy steward of farmers, likely from Brixia.

EDCS-04203561.translation: Of Quintus Postumius Rufus, son of Lucius, a ticket-seller.
EDCS-04203561.summary: An inscription identifying Quintus Postumius Rufus, son of Lucius, who worked as a tesserarius (ticket-seller or official messenger).

EDCS-04203562.translation: Marcus Pupius Urbanus, freedman of Marcus, a cobbler, ordered this to be made in his will for himself, for his fellow freedwoman Clarae, and for his daughter Laurentina.
EDCS-04203562.summary: A funerary monument commissioned in a will by Marcus Pupius Urbanus, a cobbler, for himself and his family.

EDCS-04203563.translation: To the Divine Shades. Secura for her dearest husband Thiophilus, the doctor.
EDCS-04203563.summary: A funerary epitaph for Thiophilus, a doctor, dedicated by his wife Secura.

EDCS-04203564.translation: Friends erected this for Volusenus, a Thracian freedman. [---]
EDCS-04203564.summary: A funerary inscription erected by friends for Volusenus, a Thracian freedman, with an illegible portion.

EDCS-04203566.summary: A dedication or ownership inscription for Acceptus, belonging to Caius Julius Tappo.

EDCS-04203568.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aelia Crispina and Ulpia Aelia for their most dutiful brother Aelius Crispinianus and for their wife Victorina. DE ENONO SE ANIS T XXX
EDCS-04203568.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by sisters Aelia Crispina and Ulpia Aelia to their brother Aelius Crispinianus and his wife Victorina, with an unclear final phrase.

EDCS-04203569.translation: Marcus Aemilius Tellus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04203569.summary: An inscription identifying Marcus Aemilius Tellus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04203570.translation: Tertius Aemilius Surus made this while alive for himself and for his wife Messia Fortunata.
EDCS-04203570.summary: A funerary monument self-funded by Tertius Aemilius Surus for himself and his wife Messia Fortunata.

EDCS-04203571.translation: To Marcus Aemilius Valens, her dearest husband, with whom she lived 21 years and 14 days, and to her most dutiful son, Aemilius Sabinus, this monument was erected by Aemilia Sabina, his most loving wife, for his well-deserved merits.
EDCS-04203571.summary: A funerary monument set up by a wife and son for a deceased husband and father.

EDCS-04203572.translation: To Callero and Marcus Aemilius Valerianus, his dearest mother, and [---]
EDCS-04203572.summary: A funerary inscription likely set up by children for their mother.

EDCS-04203573.summary: A dedication to Publius Aeteius Frequens.

EDCS-04203574.translation: To Afrania Paeloris, by her grandson Papirianus.
EDCS-04203574.summary: A dedication to Afrania Paeloris by her grandson.

EDCS-04203575.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Viridia Tertulla, her most worthy mother, by Albucia Tertulla.
EDCS-04203575.summary: A funerary dedication to a mother by her daughter.

EDCS-04203576.translation: To Alpinus, son of Fronto, and to Dugiava, daughter of Bimus, six [---] and [---]
EDCS-04203576.summary: A funerary inscription likely for two individuals, possibly children, with incomplete information.

EDCS-04203577.translation: To Caius Ancharius Trophimus, his dearest tent-mate, and to himself.
EDCS-04203577.summary: A funerary dedication likely by a soldier or fellow soldier to a tent-mate and for the dedicator's own memory.

EDCS-04203578.translation: To [---], 18 years of age. Anteros and Chia, to their fellow slave.
EDCS-04203578.summary: A funerary inscription by fellow slaves for a deceased slave of 18 years.

EDCS-04203579.translation: To Antiochus the Younger, his dearest son. Antiochus, his father, erected this against his vow.
EDCS-04203579.summary: A funerary monument set up by a father for his son, erected against his wishes (implying the son died prematurely).

EDCS-04203580.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Antonia Procla, who lived 33 years, 6 months, and 5 days. [---]
EDCS-04203580.summary: A funerary inscription for Antonia Procla, detailing her lifespan.

EDCS-04203581.translation: To Antuleia Campana for herself and for Antuleia Agapomene, and Antuleia Agatetyche, and her son Amoenus, [daughter] of Antuleia Amanda.
EDCS-04203581.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Antuleia Campana for herself and other family members.

EDCS-04203582.translation: Burial place of Cai Appius Threptus and Messia Lucilla; seven feet in front, sixteen feet in the ground.
EDCS-04203582.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Cai Appius Threptus and Messia Lucilla.

EDCS-04203583.translation: Argus, son of Avilia Prima, aged seventeen years.
EDCS-04203583.summary: This inscription records the age and parentage of a person named Argus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04203584.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Aristenetes, a simple soul. [Erected by] Marcus Nonius Severinus, husband, and his daughters Nonia Severa and Severina.
EDCS-04203584.summary: This funerary inscription honors Aristenetes, a 'simple soul,' and was set up by her husband and daughters.

EDCS-04203585.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Lucius Arrius Primus, who lived 20 years, 2 months, and 30 days. [Erected by] Arria Maxima.
EDCS-04203585.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Arrius Primus and was likely erected by Arria Maxima.

EDCS-04203586.translation: Arr, son of Cai, by his will.
EDCS-04203586.summary: This inscription indicates that the burial plot or monument was designated by Arr, son of Cai, according to his will.

EDCS-04203587.translation: To Arruntia, daughter of Marcus. A square plot, 20 feet.
EDCS-04203587.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot of 20 square feet for Arruntia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-04203588.translation: To Artilius Gregorius, for his wife Saturnina.
EDCS-04203588.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Artilius Gregorius to his wife Saturnina.

EDCS-04203589.translation: Arugus, son of Iovincillus, ordered this to be made for himself and for his wife Adlucca, daughter of Messilius, by his will.
EDCS-04203589.summary: This inscription records Arugus, son of Iovincillus, ordering a funerary monument for himself and his wife through his will.

EDCS-04203590.translation: Iucunda, the freedwoman of Caius Arrius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04203590.summary: This inscription identifies Iucunda as the freedwoman of Caius Arrius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04203591.translation: Benigna, freedwoman, erected this for Quintus Aulius Uradius, son of Aulus.
EDCS-04203591.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a freedwoman for her patron.

EDCS-04203594.translation: For Marcus Aurelius Piso; Vitullia Suavia for her parents.
EDCS-04203594.summary: This inscription records a dedication for Marcus Aurelius Piso and also mentions Vitullia Suavia dedicating something for her parents.

EDCS-04203595.translation: For Etion and Aurelius Sabassus, most beloved.
EDCS-04203595.summary: A dedication for two individuals, Etion and Aurelius Sabassus.

EDCS-04203596.translation: Paulus, his son, and Secundina, his daughter, erected this memorial for their most pious father Aurelius Secundinus, who lived 102 years, and for their most sweet mother Mercuria, who deserved well.
EDCS-04203596.summary: A funerary monument erected by children for their parents, noting the father's exceptional age.

EDCS-04203597.translation: To the divine shades: Marcus Aurelius Filentius, freedman, made this for Aurelia Victoria, Aurelius Victorinus, Secundus Callistus.
EDCS-04203597.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a freedman for Aurelia Victoria and two other individuals, likely family members.

EDCS-04203598.translation: For Aurelia Victoria, dearest wife, who lived 37 years and with her husband 4 years; Aurelius Homuncio erected this memorial for her, who deserved well.
EDCS-04203598.summary: A funerary monument erected by a husband for his deceased wife, specifying her age and duration of their marriage.

EDCS-04203599.translation: Caius Barbius Senecio made this while alive: 20 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203599.summary: A property marker indicating dimensions, erected by the owner Caius Barbius Senecio during his lifetime.

EDCS-04203600.translation: Boduisso Coipillonis, and Bena Criponis, and Pontus Boduissonis, and Ersea daughter of Vorvodisius, wife of Crera Boduissonis, are located here.
EDCS-04203600.summary: An inscription identifying several individuals and their familial relationships, likely marking a shared burial place.

EDCS-04203601.translation: For Lucius Caius Tertullianus: 10 feet in front.
EDCS-04203601.summary: A property marker indicating a frontage dimension for Lucius Caius Tertullianus.

EDCS-04203602.translation: Sextus, freedman of Sextus As, and Pupa.
EDCS-04203602.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to name two individuals, Sextus and Pupa, one identified as a freedman.

EDCS-04203603.translation: To Lucius Cabalacius Pudens, son of Sextus, of the Fabia tribe. Sextus Cabalacius Pudens and Cornelia Melite, parents, for themselves.
EDCS-04203603.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by parents for their son, Lucius Cabalacius Pudens, and for themselves.

EDCS-04203604.translation: Caecilius for himself and for his patron Caecilius Onesimus, for his patron's wife Primigenia, and for my freedman Firma.
EDCS-04203604.summary: This funerary inscription records Caecilius' dedication for himself, his patron, his patron's wife, and his freedman.

EDCS-04203605.translation: Lucius Caecilius Diogenes for himself and for his freedwoman wife Caecilia Artemisia.
EDCS-04203605.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Caecilius Diogenes for himself and his freedwoman wife, Caecilia Artemisia.

EDCS-04203606.translation: She ordered by will to be made for Basilia, his freedwoman and partner, and for his son Caecilius Firmo, son of Caius, and for Caecilia Cleobule.
EDCS-04203606.summary: This inscription states that a monument was ordered by will for Basilia (freedwoman and partner), Caecilius Firmo (son), and Caecilia Cleobule.

EDCS-04203607.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus Caecilius Gemellus and Laetilia Rufina, daughter of Tiberius. Caecilius Rufinus and Memor, for their most dutiful parents, and...
EDCS-04203607.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits of Quintus Caecilius Gemellus and Laetilia Rufina by their sons, Caecilius Rufinus and Memor.

EDCS-04203608.translation: Caecilia Severa for herself and for her sons Quintus Caecilius Calvisius and Quintus Caecilius Quintio.
EDCS-04203608.summary: This funerary inscription records Caecilia Severa's dedication for herself and her sons, Quintus Caecilius Calvisius and Quintus Caecilius Quintio.

EDCS-04203609.translation: To the memory of Caius Caletius Victor.
EDCS-04203609.summary: This is a memorial inscription for Caius Caletius Victor.

EDCS-04203610.summary: This is a tombstone for Sextus Calinnus, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-04203611.translation: To Lucius Calventius, legate. Calventia T.
EDCS-04203611.summary: This inscription likely dedicates a monument to Lucius Calventius, a legate, with Calventia T. as the dedicator.

EDCS-04203612.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Camillus as the son of Iacius.

EDCS-04203613.translation: Marcus Aemilius [son] of Canuleia, of the voting tribe Sempronia.
EDCS-04203613.summary: This inscription records the tribal affiliation of Marcus Aemilius, likely part of a longer dedication or epitaph from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203614.translation: Philotea, daughter of Sextus, of the Capinian tribe.
EDCS-04203614.summary: This inscription identifies Philotea, daughter of Sextus, and her tribal affiliation, likely part of a funerary or dedication marker.

EDCS-04203615.translation: Cartilia, daughter of Plecus, [wife] of Cartilius Priscus.
EDCS-04203615.summary: This inscription names Cartilia, daughter of Plecus, and her husband Cartilius Priscus, likely from a funerary monument.

EDCS-04203616.translation: To Lucius Cassius, son of Spurius.
EDCS-04203616.summary: This inscription is a dedication or epitaph to Lucius Cassius, son of Spurius, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203619.summary: This inscription is a dedication or epitaph to Claudia Tertiola, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203620.translation: Lucius Clodius, son of Lucius, called Publilia Niger.
EDCS-04203620.summary: This inscription names Lucius Clodius, son of Lucius, with the cognomen Niger, likely part of a longer inscription identifying an individual.

EDCS-04203621.translation: Marcus Clodius Rusticus, freedman of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and for his faithful partner in life, Clodia Faustae, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-04203621.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up during the lifetime of Marcus Clodius Rusticus for himself and his partner Clodia Faustae, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203622.translation: To their dearest son Clodius Sulpicius, his most devoted parents Sulpicius Alexius and Clodia Brixiana established this memorial; he lived 11 days.
EDCS-04203622.summary: This is a touching epitaph set up by devoted parents for their son Clodius Sulpicius, who died at the age of 11 days, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203623.translation: To the departed spirits: for Cluentia Restita, for Samicius, son of Sextus, for Quintiano, grandson of Quintia, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-04203623.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes (departed spirits) for multiple individuals, including Cluentia Restita, Samicius, and Quintiano, likely from a family tomb of the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203624.translation: Publius Coelius, freedman of Publius, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04203624.summary: This inscription records that Publius Coelius, a freedman, directed the construction of this monument in his will, likely a funerary marker from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203626.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a son named Constans.

EDCS-04203627.translation: To Rapta, immature, dearest to her mother, by Gaius Cornelius Candidas, son of Gaius, aged six years.
EDCS-04203627.summary: This is a tombstone for a young child, Rapta, erected by her father, Gaius Cornelius Candidas.

EDCS-04203629.translation: Made by the living: Macrio Cornelius Attusa, and to her freedman Cornelius Cornelius, and to her freedwoman Cornelia Matrona, and to her grandson Cornelius Iunius, in the field, 10 feet.
EDCS-04203629.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by Macrio Cornelius Attusa for herself and her freedmen and grandson, specifying a land area.

EDCS-04203630.translation: Gaius Cornelius Callistus for himself, and for his dearest wife Cornelia Agatha, and for his daughter Cornelia Calliste, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04203630.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument dedicated by Gaius Cornelius Callistus for himself and his family members, including freed slaves.

EDCS-04203631.translation: To Cornelius, son of Caius, a friend.
EDCS-04203631.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a friend named Cornelius.

EDCS-04203632.translation: Of Sextus Cornelius Felicio, 30 feet in front.
EDCS-04203632.summary: This inscription likely marks the extent of a property belonging to Sextus Cornelius Felicio.

EDCS-04203633.translation: Gaius Cornelius Firminus, son of Gaius, ordered by his will to be made for himself and for his father Gaius Cornelius Firminus.
EDCS-04203633.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument that Gaius Cornelius Firminus ordered to be erected for himself and his father.

EDCS-04203634.translation: To Gaius Cornelius Habendus, my most dutiful son, who lived 25 years. Picatia Thaeotema, his mother, and for herself, to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04203634.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument set up by a mother for her son who died at 25, and also for herself.

EDCS-04203635.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Secundus, who lived 10 years, 5 months, 20 days. Lucius Cornelius Glycon, unhappy father, to his most sweet son: if only your fate had allowed you, you ought to have buried us.
EDCS-04203635.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument from a father to his son who died young, lamenting the reversal of their expected fates.

EDCS-04203636.translation: To Cornelius Severus, son of Caius.
EDCS-04203636.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cornelius Severus.

EDCS-04203637.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Cornelia Cacterra.

EDCS-04203638.translation: Moderata, freedwoman of Caius, made this for herself, for her partner Quintius Exsoratus, and for her mother Quintia Clara.
EDCS-04203638.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Moderata, a freedwoman, for herself and her family.

EDCS-04203639.translation: For Cornelia Modesta, freedwoman of Ituo and Theorus, and for her mother Cornelia Parhalis and her brothers.
EDCS-04203639.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Cornelia Modesta, a freedwoman, and her relatives.

EDCS-04203640.translation: For Cornelia Quarta, daughter of Cnaeus, and for Quintia Tertia, daughter of Publius. Grullus made this for his mother and sister.
EDCS-04203640.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Grullus for his mother and sister.

EDCS-04203642.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Crispia Magnecia, Threpte, freedwoman of Caius, her mother.
EDCS-04203642.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Crispia Magnecia by her mother, Threpte, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04203645.translation: For Dugiavissa and for her daughter Dugia, his wife E.
EDCS-04203645.summary: This appears to be a funerary inscription for Dugiavissa and her daughter, possibly set up by a husband named E.

EDCS-04203646.translation: Quintus Egnatius Blandus, freedman of Quintus, made this for himself and his wife Minucia Urbana. "Poor as I am, in my greatest need, wife, I gave you these humble gifts as best I could. She lived an innocent life for 28 years."
EDCS-04203646.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, records a husband's dedication to his deceased wife, lamenting her early death.

EDCS-04203647.translation: Endubrus, son of Rigius, made this for himself, for his wife Virico, daughter of Pladus, and for Mansu.
EDCS-04203647.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Endubrus for himself, his wife, and another individual named Mansu.

EDCS-04203648.translation: STAV, son, for himself and Ennissa, daughter of Enis.
EDCS-04203648.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by STAV for himself and Ennissa.

EDCS-04203649.translation: Priscus and Terpusa made this for their son Epaphra, slave of Postumus the Younger, aged 3, and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-04203649.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by parents for their young son and themselves.

EDCS-04203650.translation: Secundus and Albanus, sons of Quartio, made this for Eppupa, daughter of Albicco.
EDCS-04203650.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument dedicated by two sons for their mother.

EDCS-04203651.translation: Augustianus, son of Mucianus, for his well-deserving wife Erasina.
EDCS-04203651.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Augustianus for his deserving wife Erasina.

EDCS-04203653.translation: Esdric, son of Carassus, made this while alive for himself and for his wife Esdrus, daughter of Mang, and for his son Manlius, and for his son Carassus, and for Pontilus.
EDCS-04203653.summary: A funerary monument made by Esdric, son of Carassus, for himself and his family members.

EDCS-04203654.translation: Marcus Fannius, son of Titus, made this while alive for his parents Titus Fannius Atecus and Maxuma, daughter of Cornelia and Contesilo; the monument space is 12 feet in every direction.
EDCS-04203654.summary: A funerary monument made by Marcus Fannius, son of Titus, for his parents, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04203655.translation: Faustus, son of Madicon, made this while alive for himself and for his father Madicon and for his mother Vescassona and for Primo and...
EDCS-04203655.summary: A funerary monument made by Faustus, son of Madicon, for himself and his parents.

EDCS-04203656.summary: An epitaph for Felix, a freedman of Servilia Prima.

EDCS-04203657.translation: To Festus, for his wife Labonia M., and for his wife Paccia Firma.
EDCS-04203657.summary: An epitaph commemorating Festus and his two wives, Labonia M. and Paccia Firma.

EDCS-04203658.translation: Firmus Valerius Saturninus made this while alive for himself and for his wife Caecilia Macrina and for their daughter Valeria Saturnina, who lived 16 years, 10 months.
EDCS-04203658.summary: A funerary monument made by Firmus Valerius Saturninus for himself, his wife, and their daughter, including the daughter's age at death.

EDCS-04203659.translation: To Titus Flavius Aristocritus of the Quirina tribe, for his excellent wife Flavia Lacaena, and for himself.
EDCS-04203659.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Titus Flavius Aristocritus to his wife Flavia Lacaena and himself.

EDCS-04203660.translation: To Fortunatus, a worthy comrade, and Helpidephorus.
EDCS-04203660.summary: An epitaph honoring Fortunatus and Helpidephorus.

EDCS-04203661.translation: To Fulonia, freedwoman of Publius, and to Publius Quintius, freedman of Publius, and to Urbigena, a household slave of Thiasus.
EDCS-04203661.summary: An epitaph for Fulonia, a freedwoman, Publius Quintius, a freedman, and Urbigena, a slave.

EDCS-04203662.translation: Marcus Fulvius Marcellus, son of Mago, of the Fabia tribe, made this while alive for himself and for his most loving, most chaste, most dutiful wife and preserver, Clodia Tertulla.
EDCS-04203662.summary: A funerary monument made by Marcus Fulvius Marcellus for himself and his wife Clodia Tertulla, praising her virtues.

EDCS-04203663.translation: Burial place for Lucius G and his son D, his own and his son's property, 40 feet square.
EDCS-04203663.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a burial plot allocated to Lucius G and his son.

EDCS-04203664.translation: To Gemellus, his brother, by Caius Lucius, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04203664.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a plot to Gemellus by his brother Caius Lucius.

EDCS-04203665.translation: To Helvia Leonis, her most beloved mistress and wife, deceived by both divine powers, Caius Petranius Asclepiades [erected this].
EDCS-04203665.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Caius Petranius Asclepiades to his beloved mistress and wife, Helvia Leonis, suggesting a tragic end.

EDCS-04203666.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription mentioning Hilara, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04203667.translation: Hostilia Thalia for herself, her comrade Piero, and Veiania.
EDCS-04203667.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Hostilia Thalia for herself and two other individuals, Piero and Veiania.

EDCS-04203668.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Hyacinthus.
EDCS-04203668.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes (spirits of the underworld) for Hyacinthus.

EDCS-04203669.translation: His most devoted parents set up this memorial for Hyacinthus here.
EDCS-04203669.summary: This funerary inscription records parents setting up a memorial for their son, Hyacinthus.

EDCS-04203671.translation: Lucius I T, 60 feet square in his land; Lucius C M, 60 feet square in his land.
EDCS-04203671.summary: This inscription records land dimensions for two individuals, Lucius I T and Lucius C M, likely for funerary plots.

EDCS-04203673.translation: To Caius Julius Amantius, Nonia Heliodora for her well-deserving husband, of most innocent soul.
EDCS-04203673.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Nonia Heliodora to her deserving husband, Caius Julius Amantius.

EDCS-04203674.translation: To Caius Julius Veranus and Sempronia Rhodis, his wife, lived...
EDCS-04203674.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription dedicated to Caius Julius Veranus and his wife Sempronia Rhodis.

EDCS-04203675.translation: To Iulia, unwillingly, by L. P. M. in this tomb.
EDCS-04203675.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Iulia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203676.translation: To Iulia, daughter of Publius, wife of Titullus.
EDCS-04203676.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Iulia, daughter of Publius and wife of Titullus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203677.translation: Sextus Iunius, son of Valentinus, husband of Iunia.
EDCS-04203677.summary: This inscription identifies Sextus Iunius, son of Valentinus, as the husband of Iunia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203678.translation: Ingenuus Iuventius, son of xtus I, born.
EDCS-04203678.summary: This inscription records the birth and parentage of Ingenuus Iuventius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203679.translation: Marcus Iuventius Rhodon made this for himself and for his dearest wife Metilia Hedone and for his son Publius Metilius Valerianus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04203679.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus Iuventius Rhodon for himself, his wife, his son, and his freedmen and freedwomen, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203680.translation: Iuventia Longina for her dearest friend, and for herself; she will not be followed by an heir.
EDCS-04203680.summary: This inscription records Iuventia Longina dedicating a monument to a friend and herself, specifying that no heir will inherit it, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203681.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Iuventia Prima. Quintus Quintius Brixianus for his dearest wife and for himself. Beware of Nasavia.
EDCS-04203681.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Quintius Brixianus to his wife Iuventia Prima and himself, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203682.translation: To Marcus Laelius, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe.
EDCS-04203682.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Laelius, son of Marcus, belonging to the Fabia tribe, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203683.translation: Lucius for his most dutiful mother, Laelia.
EDCS-04203683.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius to his mother, Laelia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203684.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Licinius as the freedman of Lucius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203685.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a meaningful summary.

EDCS-04203686.translation: Marcus Licinius Receptus, son of Marcus, ordered by his will that this be made for himself, for his father Marcus Licinius, for his mother Maxima Seia, for his brother Saturio, and for his sister Marciae filia Severa.
EDCS-04203686.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Marcus Licinius Receptus for himself and his family, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-04203688.translation: Marcus Livius Artemidorus for himself, for his son Marcus Livius Aemilianus, and for his wife Livia Athenaïs.
EDCS-04203688.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Marcus Livius Artemidorus for himself, his son, and his wife.

EDCS-04203689.translation: To Tertia, daughter of Clussimus Lubamus, his wife. Sex. Madiae f. [made this].
EDCS-04203689.summary: This epitaph from the 1st-2nd century CE is a dedication by Sex. Madiae f. to his wife Tertia.

EDCS-04203690.translation: To the Divine Shades, for Lucretia Epictesis, the most dutiful mother, and for Quintus Cai Valerius, her incomparable husband.
EDCS-04203690.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucretia Epictesis by her husband, Quintus Cai Valerius.

EDCS-04203692.summary: This is likely a funerary dedication to Maesia Antenora.

EDCS-04203693.summary: This inscription names Magius, son of Numerius, possibly indicating a person's identity on a monument, though the end is cut off.

EDCS-04203694.translation: Lucius Magius Primus made this for himself, for his most dutiful wife Messia Atticilla, and for his daughter Procula.
EDCS-04203694.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Lucius Magius Primus for himself, his wife, and his daughter.

EDCS-04203695.translation: Magia ordered by her will that this be made for herself, for her father, for Hilara her mother, for Prisca, for Secundio, and for Ublatus.
EDCS-04203695.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Magia for herself and several family members, as stipulated in her will.

EDCS-04203696.translation: To Magna, wife: 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203696.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot measuring 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field, dedicated to Magna.

EDCS-04203698.translation: Gaius Marius, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, ordered by his will that this be made for himself and for his mother Tatia.
EDCS-04203698.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Gaius Marius for himself and his mother Tatia, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-04203699.translation: Priscus son of Maro to his parents and brother: to Esdriccus son of Maro, and to Vesgasa daughter of Bittio, and to Arruntius son of Maro.
EDCS-04203699.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Priscus son of Maro to his parents and brother.

EDCS-04203700.translation: To Publius Matienus Sextus Secundus, from Publius Matienus Exoratus Valerianus, his most beloved pupil.
EDCS-04203700.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication from a pupil, Publius Matienus Exoratus Valerianus, to his deceased teacher, Publius Matienus Sextus Secundus.

EDCS-04203702.translation: Burial place of Mefanatis Ianuari, 20 feet in front, 20 feet on the front.
EDCS-04203702.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Mefanatis Ianuari, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04203703.translation: To Caio Mefanati, freedman of Caius, from Mefanatia Nymphe, freedwoman of Caius, to her father; and to Auge, freedwoman of Caius, to his mother; and to Arion and Serotinus, brothers, freedmen of Caius.
EDCS-04203703.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by Mefanatia Nymphe to her deceased father, mother, and brothers, who were all freedmen of Caius.

EDCS-04203704.translation: Of Caius Messius Firmus, 13 feet in front.
EDCS-04203704.summary: This inscription marks a property line or burial plot belonging to Caius Messius Firmus, specifying its width.

EDCS-04203705.translation: Metellia Prima made this while alive for herself and for her children: for her husband Publius Valerius Ingenuus, son of Publius Valerius; for her daughter Valeria Firma, daughter of Publius Valerius; for her son Publius Valerius Vitalis, son of Publius Valerius; for her son Lucius Valerius Celatus, son of Publius Valerius.
EDCS-04203705.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Metellia Prima for herself and her children, naming her husband and identifying her children as sons and daughters of Publius Valerius.

EDCS-04203706.translation: Greetings, Pudens. Farewell, Gaius Minicius Chrhestus, freedman of Gaius. There is nothing further: neither death nor the useful.
EDCS-04203706.summary: This inscription is a farewell message from Gaius Minicius Chrhestus, freedman of Gaius, to Pudens.

EDCS-04203707.translation: Marcus Minicius Servantius to Quintia Maxima, his wife, and to Marcus Minicius Secundus, his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-04203707.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Marcus Minicius Servantius to his wife Quintia Maxima and his brother Marcus Minicius Secundus.

EDCS-04203708.translation: Minicia Fortunata made this while alive for herself and for Minicia Tryphaena, her freedwoman. I have never stopped searching nor ceased to lose; death intervened. Now I am free from both. Live happily, you who read.
EDCS-04203708.summary: This is a funerary epitaph inscribed by Minicia Fortunata for herself and her freedwoman Minicia Tryphaena, reflecting on life, death, and the futility of pursuing worldly goods.

EDCS-04203709.translation: To Monime, dearest to Crescenti. Aelius, son.
EDCS-04203709.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication from Aelius to Monime, who was dear to Crescenti.

EDCS-04203710.translation: Musicius and Victorina, husband and wife, for themselves [a memorial].
EDCS-04203710.summary: This inscription is a dedication for a memorial, set up by a married couple.

EDCS-04203711.translation: Marcus Valerius Phronimus to his wife Mutia, freedwoman of Caius, [and] Chiai.
EDCS-04203711.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a husband to his wife, with another person named Chiai included.

EDCS-04203712.translation: To Nasidia, wife of Marcus Salluvius Syra, and to Call, freedwoman of Call [or to her freedpersons].
EDCS-04203712.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a wife and potentially her freedwoman or freedpersons.

EDCS-04203713.translation: For Mutia, wife of Noni Genialis, 17 feet in front, 28 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203713.summary: This inscription records land dimensions associated with Mutia, wife of Noni Genialis.

EDCS-04203714.translation: Nonia Theano [erected this] for her husband Marcus Nonius Telesinus and her son Nonius Theanus, and her daughter Nonia Telesilla.
EDCS-04203714.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Nonia Theano for her husband, son, and daughter.

EDCS-04203715.translation: Euxenus and Euphemus [erected this] for Stor and Marcus Nonius Abascantus.
EDCS-04203715.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Euxenus and Euphemus for Stor and Marcus Nonius Abascantus.

EDCS-04203716.translation: The sons [made this] to the Divine Spirits for their mother Nonia Hermaida, dearest, well-deserving.
EDCS-04203716.summary: This is a funerary inscription from sons to their beloved and deserving mother, Nonia Hermaida.

EDCS-04203717.translation: Epaphra and Basilaeus [made this] to the Divine Spirits for their mother Nonia Sabina, dearest.
EDCS-04203717.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Epaphra and Basilaeus to their beloved mother, Nonia Sabina.

EDCS-04203718.translation: Maxima for herself, and for her husband Gaius Oclatius Epitectus, and for Marcus Cornelius Eutycus, and for her granddaughter Valeria Firmina.
EDCS-04203718.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Maxima for herself, her husband, and two other individuals, likely family members.

EDCS-04203719.translation: Papiria, freedwoman of a woman, Cytheris, for herself and for her husband Marcus Tilius, son of Marcus, of the tribe Voltinia.
EDCS-04203719.summary: This inscription is a self-dedication by Cytheris, a freedwoman, for herself and her husband Marcus Tilius.

EDCS-04203720.translation: Regilla, freedwoman of Papiria Cytheris, [dedicated this] to Sextus Clodius Broccus, son of Sextus.
EDCS-04203720.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedwoman to her patron Sextus Clodius Broccus, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203721.translation: To Lucius Petreius Felix, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04203721.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Petreius Felix, a freedman, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203722.translation: Lucius Petronius Tai ordered this to be made by his will, and for his wife Secunda.
EDCS-04203722.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Lucius Petronius Tai commissioned a monument for himself and his wife Secunda in his will, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203723.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Petronius Iunior.
EDCS-04203723.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Petronius Iunior, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203724.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Laelia Venustina, a most dear mother, [erected this] for her son, Quintus Petronius Messianus, who lived 9 years, 5 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-04203724.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy, Quintus Petronius Messianus, dedicated by his mother Laelia Venustina, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203725.summary: This appears to be the end of a funerary inscription, possibly a dedication by a father, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203726.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Philetus made this for himself and for his descendants.
EDCS-04203726.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Philetus for himself and his family, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203727.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Plinia Hermione. Helvia Atiliana, a most loving mother, [dedicated this].
EDCS-04203727.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Helvia Atiliana to her daughter Plinia Hermione, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203728.translation: Lucius Poblicius Hebenus [dedicated this] for himself, and for Optata Mulvia, his partner, and for Velllae Firmae Pisainae.
EDCS-04203728.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Poblicius Hebenus for himself, his partner, and another individual, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203730.translation: [Dedicated] to Gaius Popilius Iucundus and Fulvia Apstinentia, his partner, and [their] friends.
EDCS-04203730.summary: This appears to be a funerary dedication or a dedication of a public benefit by Gaius Popilius Iucundus and his partner Fulvia Apstinentia, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203731.translation: For the memory of Lucius Popillius Senex, son of Lucius, and Travia, daughter of Publius Seccus.
EDCS-04203731.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lucius Popillius Senex and Travia, daughter of Publius Seccus.

EDCS-04203732.translation: By the decision of Publius Popillius Valens.
EDCS-04203732.summary: This inscription records a decision made by Publius Popillius Valens, likely related to a legal or administrative matter.

EDCS-04203733.translation: Publius Postumius Hermes for himself and for his wife Postumia Politice, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-04203733.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Publius Postumius Hermes for himself and his wife, Postumia Politice.

EDCS-04203734.translation: Lucius Postumius Ingenuus, son of Lucius, for himself and for his brother Lucius Postumius Stabili, son of Publius, and their sisters Quintia Satulla and Exorata, and their sisters' sons, and for his slaves and freedwomen, all deceased, 29 in number.
EDCS-04203734.summary: This funerary dedication by Lucius Postumius Ingenuus includes himself, his brother, sisters, nephews, and enslaved people, numbering 29 individuals.

EDCS-04203735.translation: To Postumia Secunda, for her most beloved and deserving husband Quinto Clodio Pardioni.
EDCS-04203735.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Postumia Secunda to her beloved husband, Quinto Clodio Pardioni.

EDCS-04203736.translation: To the Divine Manes. Arria placed this for the deserving Primitivus.
EDCS-04203736.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Arria to the Divine Manes for Primitivus.

EDCS-04203737.translation: Publius Publicius Brixianus for himself and for his wife Publicia, and for Publius Publicius Dorus, Publius Publicius Magius, Publicia Artemidis, and Onesimus, the Doryphoros, and the sixth-order Augustalis priest.
EDCS-04203737.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Publius Publicius Brixianus for his family and associates, including an Augustalis priest.

EDCS-04203738.translation: To Quinto Publicio Fausto and Publiciae Quintae, his parents, and to Tia Pal and his brothers.
EDCS-04203738.summary: This inscription is a dedication to parents Quinto Publicio Fausto and Publiciae Quintae, and to siblings Tia Pal and others.

EDCS-04203739.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Publicius Gaius for his most devoted brother Lucius Publicius Octobris.
EDCS-04203739.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Publicius Gaius to the Divine Manes for his brother, Lucius Publicius Octobris.

EDCS-04203740.translation: Lucius Publicius Primus for himself, and for his wife Secunda, daughter of Turius, and for Lucius Septimius Crescentes.
EDCS-04203740.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Lucius Publicius Primus for himself, his wife Secunda, and Lucius Septimius Crescentes.

EDCS-04203741.translation: Caecilius Saturus set up this memorial to his dearest and incomparable wife, Publicia Florentia.
EDCS-04203741.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a husband to his wife.

EDCS-04203742.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Publius Laronius [set this up for] Publicia Lucinia.
EDCS-04203742.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Publicia Lucinia.

EDCS-04203743.translation: The length from the boundary to the public road for Lucius Quintus Primus and Caius Marcius Terentianus is 26 feet.
EDCS-04203743.summary: A boundary marker defining a length of 26 feet for a public road, likely during the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04203744.translation: To Quintae, daughter of Marcellus, and to Secunda, daughter of Balbus.
EDCS-04203744.summary: A funerary inscription honoring two individuals, Quintae and Secunda.

EDCS-04203745.translation: Marcus Quintius Glycerus made this for himself and his incomparable wife Quintia Priscula. 20 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203745.summary: This epitaph from the 1st-2nd century CE records the purchase of a burial plot by Marcus Quintius Glycerus for himself and his wife, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04203746.translation: The bones of Lucius Quinctius Grullus.
EDCS-04203746.summary: A simple epitaph marking the burial place of Lucius Quinctius Grullus.

EDCS-04203748.translation: Publius Quintius Primigenius made this for himself and Successa during his lifetime.
EDCS-04203748.summary: A funerary monument made by Publius Quintius Primigenius for himself and Successa, indicating he was still alive when it was erected.

EDCS-04203749.translation: He ordered this to be made by will for Lucius Quintius Quartio.
EDCS-04203749.summary: An inscription stating that a monument was to be erected in accordance with the will of Lucius Quintius Quartio.

EDCS-04203750.translation: Quintus Quintius Terentianus for himself and for his wife Esdrila Clua, daughter of [---].
EDCS-04203750.summary: A funerary monument set up by Quintus Quintius Terentianus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04203751.translation: [Property of Quintia, daughter of Caius?], 30 feet in front and 8 feet in the field.
EDCS-04203751.summary: A boundary marker detailing land measurements associated with Quintia.

EDCS-04203752.translation: To his incomparable wife, Quintia Prima, Publius Crexius Naevilianus Senior, her husband.
EDCS-04203752.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by a husband to his beloved wife.

EDCS-04203753.translation: Quinctia Prisca, daughter of Sextus, [dedicated this] for herself and for her father Sextus Quinctius, her mother Aemilia Paulla, and Quinctia Procula.
EDCS-04203753.summary: This epitaph records a dedication made by Quinctia Prisca for herself and other family members.

EDCS-04203754.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilius Marcianus and Nigellius Firmus, heirs of Quintia Valeria and her husband Caecilius Secundus, had this made according to her will.
EDCS-04203754.summary: This epitaph records a funerary monument commissioned by the heirs for Quintia Valeria and her husband Caecilius Secundus.

EDCS-04203757.translation: Romania Optata, daughter of Spurius, ordered this to be made by her will for herself and for her husband Cripponius, son of Casticus.
EDCS-04203757.summary: This epitaph records a funerary monument commissioned by Romania Optata for herself and her husband.

EDCS-04203758.translation: To Insequens and Tertia, daughters of Marcus, and to Publius Romanus, brother, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04203758.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Insequens, Tertia, and Publius Romanus.

EDCS-04203759.translation: To Rotalus, for his most beloved wife Quintia Macrina, who lived with me for 40 years, 3 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-04203759.summary: This epitaph records a dedication from Rotalus to his wife Quintia Macrina, specifying their years of cohabitation.

EDCS-04203760.translation: On the front, as far as the monument of Caius Rufinius Senecio, in field 299.
EDCS-04203760.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker indicating land ownership related to Caius Rufinius Senecio.

EDCS-04203761.translation: To Publius Rufrius Atticus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-04203761.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Publius Rufrius Atticus, a freedman.

EDCS-04203762.translation: Sextus Veirius Iunius, son of Rufus Brigovicis.
EDCS-04203762.summary: This inscription records the name of Sextus Veirius Iunius, son of Rufus Brigovicis.

EDCS-04203763.summary: This inscription contains the name Gaius Salustius followed by illegible or abbreviated characters.

EDCS-04203764.translation: For himself and for his incomparable wife Salvia Firmina, and for his daughter Philumene, Salvia, daughter of Caius, dearest innocent little soul, who lived for 11 years and 8 days.
EDCS-04203764.summary: This epitaph records a dedication by a man for himself, his wife Salvia Firmina, and his young daughter Philumene, specifying the daughter's age at death.

EDCS-04203765.translation: Marcus Salvienus Cinnamus, freedman of Marcus, made this in his lifetime for himself and for Doridis Conchidonis, a freedwoman, his daughter.
EDCS-04203765.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman for himself and his daughter.

EDCS-04203766.translation: 20 feet in the land of the Satrii.
EDCS-04203766.summary: This inscription records a land measurement, likely a boundary marker.

EDCS-04203767.translation: Restuta, her mother, placed this for her daughter Secundina, who lived 10 years, her dearest daughter.
EDCS-04203767.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her young daughter.

EDCS-04203768.translation: Secundus Spuri Strabo made this in his lifetime for himself, for his excellent wife Minacia Tertia, and for his most dutiful son Gaius Minacius Vegetus Primus.
EDCS-04203768.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a man for himself, his wife, and his son.

EDCS-04203769.translation: Balbinus for his parents, Sega Triumi's son, and Lea, Sextus's daughter, his wife, and for his son Clevius and his daughter Segessa.
EDCS-04203769.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Balbinus for his parents and siblings or children.

EDCS-04203770.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Marcus Sempronius Placidus.

EDCS-04203772.translation: Aurelius Thallus made this place for his wife Sentia Bittalia, of good memory, sincere in loyalty and simplicity, and beside her, his sister Sentia Cornelia also made a place for herself while alive.
EDCS-04203772.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a wife, also mentioning a sister who procured a neighboring plot.

EDCS-04203773.translation: For Gaius Septimius, son of Gaius, his father.
EDCS-04203773.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a father, dedicated by his son.

EDCS-04203774.translation: For Septimia Chrysarion, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius Septimius Amaranthus, freedman of Lucius, for his sister and himself. LA BO
EDCS-04203774.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman for his sister and himself.

EDCS-04203775.translation: For Gaius Sertorius Pollio, son of Quintus, his brother.
EDCS-04203775.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a brother, dedicated by his sibling.

EDCS-04203776.translation: Severa Ispanus set up this memorial to his most beloved wife, who lived with me for 26 years, well-deserving. His most beloved son, N. Senator, lived for 6 years after his parents, [setting this up] for his most beloved parents.
EDCS-04203776.summary: A son set up this memorial for his parents, Severa and Ispanus, and his mother Severa, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203777.translation: Sextus, son of Primi, for himself and Vitalia, daughter of Iunius, his wife.
EDCS-04203777.summary: A funerary dedication for Sextus and his wife Vitalia, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203778.translation: To the departed spirits of Sidonia, wife of P. Tatias; a memorial to a well-deserving woman.
EDCS-04203778.summary: A funerary dedication to Sidonia, wife of P. Tatias, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203779.translation: Nonius Liberalis set this up to his wife Silvania Flora, who lived with me for 10 years, well-deserving.
EDCS-04203779.summary: A funerary dedication by Nonius Liberalis to his wife Silvania Flora, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203780.translation: Gaius Soius Severus for himself and his excellent wife Claudia Prisca, and for Petronius Ianuarius, Mettaius Secundus, Vinillius Tertius, Marcella, his relatives, and for Sura, well-deserving.
EDCS-04203780.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Soius Severus for himself, his wife, relatives, and a deserving woman named Sura, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203781.translation: Solia set up this memorial for Proseria, her foster-daughter.
EDCS-04203781.summary: A memorial set up by Solia for her foster-daughter Proseria, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203783.translation: Publius Vettius Cupitus for his friends Spurius Homuncio and Secunda, daughter of Aulon.
EDCS-04203783.summary: A dedication by Publius Vettius Cupitus for his friends Spurius Homuncio and Secunda Aulonis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04203785.translation: To the departed spirits of Statia Faustina, most innocent soul.
EDCS-04203785.summary: A funerary dedication to Statia Faustina, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203786.translation: To the departed spirits of Leda, wife of Gaius Stlaccius Plocamus, well-deserving.
EDCS-04203786.summary: A funerary dedication to Leda, wife of Gaius Stlaccius Plocamus, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04203787.translation: Burial place of Quintus Sulpicius Marcellinus, 12 feet in front.
EDCS-04203787.summary: A funerary boundary marker indicating the burial plot of Quintus Sulpicius Marcellinus, likely from the Imperial period.
