EDCS-04203789.translation: Lucius Terentius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, called Varro.
EDCS-04203789.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a tombstone or other dedication, of Lucius Terentius Varro.

EDCS-04203791.translation: To the Divine Manes of Trophimus, a public slave, and Severa, his wife/companion.
EDCS-04203791.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Trophimus, a public slave, and Severa, likely his wife or fellow member of a contubernium.

EDCS-04203792.translation: To the Divine Manes of Trophimus, most deserving...
EDCS-04203792.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Trophimus, honoring him for his deserving qualities.

EDCS-04203793.translation: Of Marcus. On the front, 14 feet.
EDCS-04203793.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or a tombstone, indicating a measurement of 14 feet belonging to Marcus.

EDCS-04203797.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a tombstone or other dedication.

EDCS-04203798.translation: Of Marcus Valerius Iucundus. On the front, 30 feet; in the field, 30 feet.
EDCS-04203798.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or a tombstone, indicating measurements of 30 feet on the front and 30 feet in the field belonging to Marcus Valerius Iucundus.

EDCS-04203799.translation: To Lucius Valerius, son of Solibodus, of the Lafarda tribe; Caius Calvasius and Caius Terentius, his uncle.
EDCS-04203799.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or tombstone for Lucius Valerius, mentioning his father, tribe, and possibly patrons or family members Caius Calvasius and Caius Terentius.

EDCS-04203800.translation: Lucius Valerius, of the Fabia tribe, Mont-...
EDCS-04203800.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a tombstone or other dedication, of Lucius Valerius.

EDCS-04203801.translation: To the Divine Manes of Valerius Nicephorianus, who lived 23 years, 6 months, and 28 days; Valeria Nicotyche, to her dearest brother.
EDCS-04203801.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Valeria Nicotyche to her brother Valerius Nicephorianus, including his lifespan.

EDCS-04203802.translation: To Lucius Valerius Niger, son of Spurius; Poblicia, daughter of Marcus, to Lucius Valerius Firmus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04203802.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or tombstone, possibly honoring Lucius Valerius Niger and including references to Poblicia and Lucius Valerius Firmus.

EDCS-04203803.summary: A funerary dedication by Publius Valerius Princeps, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203804.translation: To his dearest son, and to Valerius Restutus, his former husband, and to himself, and to Sextus Petilius Titianus, deserving well, and [to others].
EDCS-04203804.summary: A funerary dedication to multiple individuals, including a son, former husband, and Sextus Petilius Titianus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203805.translation: To the divine shades. For Valeria Crispinia, most innocent soul, who lived 24 years, 5 months, 7 days, 5 hours. Lucius Postumius Ursianus [erected this] for his most frugal wife. Oh, Simplecius, alas, that death snatches away such flourishing years!
EDCS-04203805.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Crispinia, detailing her lifespan and lamenting her early death, erected by her husband Lucius Postumius Ursianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203806.translation: Valeria, daughter of Lucius, Fabia, made this while alive for herself and for Bittalius Epagathus, her most excellent husband, and for Maesia Prima, [her] parents.
EDCS-04203806.summary: A funerary dedication made by Valeria Fabia for herself, her husband Bittalius Epagathus, and her parents Maesia Prima and Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203807.translation: Hilara, wife of Quintus Quintius, and Valeria Samila.
EDCS-04203807.summary: An inscription mentioning Hilara, wife of Quintus Quintius, and Valeria Samila, possibly a dedication or a record of family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203808.translation: And he ordered [this] to be made by his will for Valeria Secunda, and Statidia Proba, and Lucius Lubicius Secundus, and Vettia Pyrallis.
EDCS-04203808.summary: A testament commissioning funerary monuments for several individuals, including Valeria Secunda and Statidia Proba, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203809.translation: For Valeria Trophime, daughter of Lucius. Publius Valerius Euphemus and Valeria, [his] most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-04203809.summary: A funerary dedication for Valeria Trophime, daughter of Lucius, by Publius Valerius Euphemus and his daughter Valeria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203810.translation: [daughter] and Lucius M. Cornelius, who lived 24 years. Valeria Valentina for her husband and son, dearest [to her], and for herself.
EDCS-04203810.summary: A funerary dedication by Valeria Valentina for her deceased husband, son, and herself, mentioning Lucius M. Cornelius who died at 24, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203811.translation: Aurelius Primitius placed this memorial for Valeria Variana, his sweetest wife, [and] his most rare wife.
EDCS-04203811.summary: A funerary monument erected by Aurelius Primitius for his cherished wife Valeria Variana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203812.summary: A fragment possibly continuing a list of names or a dedication, mentioning Valeria Vitalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04203813.translation: Vassidius Cae, son of Cattavus, made this for himself while alive, and for Caecilia Pile, freedwoman, and for Secundus, freedman, and for Alpina Vera, his heir, and for his natural sons Pilius Largo.
EDCS-04203813.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Vassidius Cae for himself and his family members, including freedpersons and heirs.

EDCS-04203815.translation: To Cai, son of Vetus, and Publia, daughter of Marcius Viator, and to his brother Marcius, and to his sister Maxima.
EDCS-04203815.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cai, Publia, Marcius, and Maxima, possibly family members of the dedicator.

EDCS-04203817.translation: To Victor, his brother, well-deserving, who lived fifty years and four months and days.
EDCS-04203817.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Victor, commemorating his life and likely erected by a sibling.

EDCS-04203818.translation: In memory of Victorina, who lived 90 years and 3 months. Ursus, her son, erected this memorial to his most beloved and well-deserving mother.
EDCS-04203818.summary: This is a funerary memorial erected by Ursus for his mother Victorina, including her age at death.

EDCS-04203819.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Marcus Ulpius Diadumenus, likely the deceased.

EDCS-04203820.translation: To the divine shades. Gaius Prastina Agathangelus and Volusia Calliope, to their most dutiful son Cai Volusius Rufinianus, and to themselves.
EDCS-04203820.summary: This funerary dedication is by Gaius Prastina Agathangelus and Volusia Calliope for their son Cai Volusius Rufinianus and for themselves.

EDCS-04203821.translation: For himself and for Zosime, his dearest wife, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and.
EDCS-04203821.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication for the dedicator, his wife Zosime, and his freedpersons.

EDCS-04203839.translation: To Cai, son of Maximus, burnt.
EDCS-04203839.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, possibly referring to a cremation burial for Cai, son of Maximus.

EDCS-04203843.translation: R TENARI lived 20 years INOVIM Aticia who while alive made the memorial.
EDCS-04203843.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an individual who lived 20 years, with a memorial erected by Aticia while still alive.

EDCS-04203850.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication or ownership mark, mentioning Cnaeus.

EDCS-04203853.translation: To the departed spirits of Iulianus.
EDCS-04203853.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring a person named Iulianus.

EDCS-04203860.translation: Trophimus, the freedman of Ius, for himself.
EDCS-04203860.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by a freedman named Trophimus for himself.

EDCS-04203861.translation: Valerius anus to his freedman Valerius Onesimus.
EDCS-04203861.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Valerius anus to his freedman Valerius Onesimus.

EDCS-04203864.translation: In his own name for his patroness Por[---].
EDCS-04203864.summary: This inscription records a dedication made in the dedicator's name for a patroness.

EDCS-04203865.translation: [---] to Marci, son of Cla[---], a nonanus, of [---] years.
EDCS-04203865.summary: This inscription records details about a person named Marci, son of Cla[---], possibly related to age.

EDCS-04203867.translation: Marci, son of [---], of the Fabia tribe.
EDCS-04203867.summary: This inscription identifies a person named Marci and mentions his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04203870.translation: To his friend Murnus, companion of Aurunculeius.
EDCS-04203870.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a friend named Murnus, who was a companion of Aurunculeius.

EDCS-04203877.translation: Irda, the mother, to her most dutiful son and to herself.
EDCS-04203877.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a mother, Irda, to her son and for herself.

EDCS-04203879.translation: to the best [---] and to Rino, to his sons [---] and [---].
EDCS-04203879.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a person referred to as 'best' and to Rino and his sons.

EDCS-04203884.summary: This inscription identifies a freedman named Quinti and notes his position as a VI vir Augustalis.

EDCS-04203887.translation: Irrius made this for his incomparable wife and for himself during his lifetime.
EDCS-04203887.summary: This is a dedication by Irrius for his wife and himself, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-04203890.translation: I, Sirus, was a superior and for my family.
EDCS-04203890.summary: A brief personal statement or epitaph by someone named Sirus, possibly indicating status or ownership.

EDCS-04203891.translation: Maximianus and Leontius with their people, 100 foot soldiers.
EDCS-04203891.summary: This inscription records Maximianus and Leontius, possibly military figures, and mentions 100 foot soldiers.

EDCS-04203892.translation: Sirus the deacon paved this place with his people.
EDCS-04203892.summary: This inscription records that Sirus, a deacon, paved a location, possibly a church or public space.

EDCS-04203893.translation: To good memory, Leontius rests here in peace, who lived about 40 years, laid to rest on the 5th day before the Kalends of February, in the 3rd indiction, under Consul Probus.
EDCS-04203893.summary: This is an epitaph for Leontius, recording his lifespan, burial date, and the consul.

EDCS-04203894.translation: Publius P. Vincom rests here in peace, who lived 60 years, laid to rest on the 5th day before the Nones of August, in the 4th indiction. And Presbyter Iustinus, who lived 56 years, laid to rest on the August Nones, in the 4th indiction, in the 5th year after the consulship of Emperor and Consul Justinus Augustus.
EDCS-04203894.summary: This epitaph records the burial of two individuals, Vincom and Presbyter Iustinus, including their lifespans, burial dates, and the imperial consulship.

EDCS-04203895.translation: Thus my powers are given, O mighty and powerful minister of learning, laid to rest on the 5th day before the Nones of the Emperor and Consul Maurice, in his 12th year.
EDCS-04203895.summary: This inscription seems to be a funerary text for a minister of learning, referencing Emperor Maurice and a specific year.

EDCS-04203896.translation: Flavia Paulina, granddaughter, set up this memorial to the well-deserving Flavio Latino, bishop, aged 2 years, 7 months; to the presbyter, aged 15 years; to the exorcist, aged 12 years; and to Latinilla and Flavia Macrino, the lector.
EDCS-04203896.summary: This is a memorial erected by Flavia Paulina for several deceased family members who held ecclesiastical offices, detailing their ages and roles.

EDCS-04203897.translation: Fabia Secunda set up this tombstone against her vow to her sweetest son, Attius Proculus, the lector, who lived 18 years, 8 months, and 7 days, to one well-deserving.
EDCS-04203897.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Fabia Secunda for her son, Attius Proculus, a lector, mentioning his age and her vow.

EDCS-04203898.translation: To good memory, in peace. The sweetest wife set up this memorial against her vow to Aurelius Valerinus, her most loving husband, who lived about 65 years, and with whom she lived about 35 years.
EDCS-04203898.summary: This is a memorial erected by a wife for her husband, Aurelius Valerinus, recording their lifespans and her vow.

EDCS-04203899.translation: To Aurelia Firmina, dearest daughter, who lived 14 years and 6 months. Aurelius and Valeria Augusta, parents [dedicated this]. Deposited on the day of Mars.
EDCS-04203899.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Aurelia Firmina, dedicated by her parents.

EDCS-04300004.translation: Eugonos fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-04300004.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the goddess Minerva.

EDCS-04300005.translation: Sacred to Nemesis Augusta. Titus For...
EDCS-04300005.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Nemesis Augusta, begun by Titus.

EDCS-04300006.translation: Gellia Nicostrate willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Nemesis Augusta.
EDCS-04300006.summary: This dedicatory inscription, likely from the 2nd century CE, records Gellia Nicostrate fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nemesis.

EDCS-04300007.translation: To Sol, Numerius Placentius Atticus [dedicates this].
EDCS-04300007.summary: This dedicatory inscription, likely from the 2nd century CE, records Numerius Placentius Atticus dedicating something to the sun god Sol.

EDCS-04300009.translation: Klaudia Kallikrateia and Cornelius Diadumenos dedicated the altar by the command of the god.
EDCS-04300009.summary: This bilingual (Greek text) dedication from the 2nd-3rd century CE records a couple dedicating an altar in response to a divine command.

EDCS-04300014.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow and a dedication, likely a continuation of another inscription.

EDCS-04300016.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Coelia Felicissima, who lived 13 years, 4 months, and 2 days. Felix, his parents, and Coelia Quartilla, most dutiful parents [dedicated this].
EDCS-04300016.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Coelia Felicissima, dedicated by her parents, Felix and Coelia Quartilla.

EDCS-04300017.summary: This inscription names Helops, an official (dispensator) in the service of the emperor.

EDCS-04300018.translation: ...and Secundina, parents of Augustus, made this while alive.
EDCS-04300018.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that parents named ... and Secundina commissioned their tomb while alive.

EDCS-04300021.text_edition: \n Caio Settidio Cai filio Pupinia Firmo praefecto cohortis IIII Thracum Syriacae tribuno militum legionis V Macedonicae quaestori urbano Palpellia Sexti filia Antonilla cliens\n
EDCS-04300021.translation: To Gaius Settidius Firmus, son of Gaius, of the Pupinia tribe, prefect of the 4th Cohort of Thracians of Syrian origin, military tribune of the 5th Macedonian Legion, urban quaestor. Palpellia Antonilla, daughter of Sextus, his client.
EDCS-04300021.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE, honors Gaius Settidius Firmus, detailing his military and political career, and also mentions his patroness Palpellia Antonilla.

EDCS-04300023.translation: Gaius Caulinius Maximus, son of Sextus, a veteran of the 9th praetorian cohort, ordered this to be made in his will for himself, his wife Palpellius Loebe, his father Sextus Caulinus Syros, his mother Voltidia Processa, his sister Caulinia, his brother Lucius Caulinus Histro, and all his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-04300023.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by a veteran, Gaius Caulinius Maximus, who detailed in his will who the monument was for.

EDCS-04300024.translation: To Lartius (?) Vindicius, soldier of the 4th Flavian Felix Legion. His mother, Aemilia Thalamis, [dedicated this].
EDCS-04300024.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a soldier, Lartius (?) Vindicius, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-04300026.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Claudia Eugenia, daughter of Quintus, who by her chastity and obedience made life pleasant for her husband, and when she herself was ailing, she passed away for her husband. Quintus Mursius Celer, public haruspex, decurion of Pola, made this for his wife, for himself, and for his descendants.
EDCS-04300026.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the mid-2nd century CE, is a dedication by Quintus Mursius Celer to his deceased wife Claudia Eugenia, praising her virtues and stating his intention to be buried with her and their descendants.

EDCS-04300027.translation: Lucius Treblanus Cilo, son of Caius, twice holder of a high office, and four times a member of the decurions, holding judicial power, formerly aedile, ordered this to be made in his will for his father Lucius Treblanus, son of Sextus; his mother Carvilia Maxima, daughter of Lucius; his brother Titus Treblanus; his sister's son Bassus, son of Sextus Flavonius; his wife Treblana, daughter of Pomponius; and his daughter Paulla.
EDCS-04300027.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Lucius Treblanus Cilo, detailing family members included in his will for the monument.

EDCS-04300034.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Claudia Pusilla, dearest wife. Sabinus of the coloni of Pola made this, alive.
EDCS-04300034.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the mid-2nd century CE, is a dedication by Sabinus to his wife Claudia Pusilla.

EDCS-04300036.translation: Publius Cannutius Optatus, an Augustalis IIIIvir, made this for himself and his wife Cannutia Vitalis, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, while alive. This monument will not pass to an heir. Place and burial plot: of Publius Cannutius Optatus and Lucius Aratrius Primus, 33.5 feet in front, 28 feet in the field.
EDCS-04300036.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the mid-2nd century CE, is a dedication by Publius Cannutius Optatus for his family and freedmen, specifying burial plot dimensions and stating it is not to be inherited.

EDCS-04300037.translation: Lucius Annius Falernus, freedman of Lucius Annius, and Annia Rustica, freedwoman of the woman, as *vivi* (living) members of the *Vigintiviri Augustales), made this for themselves.
EDCS-04300037.summary: An inscription recording a funerary monument made by a freedman and his wife, who were members of the *Vigintiviri Augustales*.

EDCS-04300039.translation: For Gnaeus Minucius Agathopus, freedman of Gnaeus, *Vigintivir Augustalis*; Minucia Thallusa, freedwoman of Gnaeus, wife, made this while alive.
EDCS-04300039.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a wife for her deceased husband, who was a freedman and a *Vigintivir Augustalis*.

EDCS-04300041.translation: The Augustalis freedman dedicated this while alive for himself, for Octavia Iucunda, and for his family.
EDCS-04300041.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman to himself and his family, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04300046.summary: This is a name inscription, possibly a tombstone or a dedication, for Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300047.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription bearing probable personal names, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300048.translation: Selicia Postuma, daughter of Gaius, paved the slope in her own name and that of Gaius Octavius Attus.
EDCS-04300048.summary: This inscription records the paving of a slope by Selicia Postuma on behalf of herself and Gaius Octavius Attus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300063.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that seems to record a name, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300072.translation: To Quintus Catusius Severianus, a merchant citizen of Gaul, Flavia Fortunata, his incomparable wife, and to Quintus Catusius Flavianus, his deserving father.
EDCS-04300072.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Flavia Fortunata to her husband Quintus Catusius Severianus and her father Quintus Catusius Flavianus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300073.summary: This is a dedication to Diocles, a procurator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300074.summary: This is an inscription identifying Sabinus as a steward, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300075.translation: Gaius Turpilius Chilo, son of Gaius, the cucumber seller, Cucumer the runner, and...
EDCS-04300075.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording names and occupations, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300076.translation: The plot, of Lucius Aebutius Claros, freedman of Lucius, 12 feet in every direction, he made while alive.
EDCS-04300076.summary: An inscription marking a burial plot measuring 12x12 feet, set up by its owner, Lucius Aebutius Claros.

EDCS-04300077.translation: Aelius, son of Gaius, dedicated this while alive for himself and his family.
EDCS-04300077.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aelius for himself and his family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300078.translation: A plot belonging to Agria, freedwoman of Laina, for herself and her family, 12 feet in frontage and 23 feet in depth.
EDCS-04300078.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking a burial plot of specified dimensions for Agria and her family.

EDCS-04300079.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or name, possibly for Marcus Albius.

EDCS-04300082.translation: Antistia Tyce made this while alive for herself and for Titus Valerius Amentus and Memorius; here he lies.
EDCS-04300082.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a woman for herself and two other individuals, likely a family member and a slave or freedman.

EDCS-04300083.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Gaius Antonius Zosimianus, called Dalmatius, for the incomparable youth who lived 18 years, 4 months, and 16 days, without any flaw. Gaius Antonius Eucarpus, for his most rare and dutiful son.
EDCS-04300083.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicated by Gaius Antonius Eucarpus to his son, detailing the son's youth and virtuous life.

EDCS-04300084.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Aquilius Eumenus; Julius Sabinus and Epagathus [set this up] for their friend.
EDCS-04300084.summary: A funerary dedication by two friends, Julius Sabinus and Epagathus, for their deceased friend, Quintus Aquilius Eumenus.

EDCS-04300086.translation: A plot belonging to Fausta, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and Attius Rufio, also called Arminius, 12 feet in frontage.
EDCS-04300086.summary: This funerary inscription marks a burial plot of specified frontage for Fausta and Attius Rufio.

EDCS-04300088.translation: Of Caius Atullius, son of Lucius; of Titus Atullius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04300088.summary: This inscription records the names and patronymics of two individuals, Caius Atullius and Titus Atullius, both sons of Lucius.

EDCS-04300089.translation: Aurelius Proclus, son of Leoitus, having lived sixty-five years.
EDCS-04300089.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and lifespan of Aurelius Proclus.

EDCS-04300090.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelius H[---] erected this while alive for himself.
EDCS-04300090.summary: A funerary inscription recording an individual named Aurelius who set up a monument for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04300091.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or name identification for Aurunceius Epaphroditus.

EDCS-04300092.translation: Oppia Aurunceia, freedwoman of Philotis, wife of Marcus, made this for her patron while alive, and for her family, and for Titus Seius Hilarion, freedman of Titus; 15 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-04300092.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a freedwoman for her patron and family, also including space for another individual, with dimensions of the plot provided.

EDCS-04300093.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Baria Argia.
EDCS-04300093.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Baria Argia.

EDCS-04300094.translation: A plot belonging to Cnaeus Cacurius Tertius, son of Cnaeus, and Publius Cacurius Moderatus, 20 feet in frontage and 10 feet in depth.
EDCS-04300094.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of specified dimensions for Cnaeus Cacurius Tertius and Publius Cacurius Moderatus.

EDCS-04300095.translation: [---] he made while alive for himself and for Caecilia Calliopa, freedwoman of Quintus, and for Lucius Cassius Maximus, and for Gaius Cassius Rufus, and for Cassia Tertia, his children.
EDCS-04300095.summary: An inscription by a man who prepared his tomb while alive, dedicating it to his wife and children.

EDCS-04300096.translation: To Caesennia Prima, patroness; to Lucius Octavius Fronton, father; to Caesennia Felicia, mother.
EDCS-04300096.summary: This funerary inscription honors a patroness, father, and mother, indicating familial and social relationships.

EDCS-04300097.translation: Publius Caesius Cilo, freedman of Publius, made this while alive.
EDCS-04300097.summary: A simple funerary inscription by a freedman, Publius Caesius Cilo, who prepared his own tomb.

EDCS-04300099.translation: Calania Pulixinia, freedwoman of Marcus, and Marcus Calanius Philao, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-04300099.summary: This is a funerary epitaph naming two freedpersons, Calania Pulixinia and Marcus Calanius Philao.

EDCS-04300100.translation: Belonging to Celer, freedman of Titus. 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-04300100.summary: This inscription seems to record land boundaries, possibly for a funerary plot, indicating dimensions of 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field, belonging to Celer, a freedman.

EDCS-04300101.translation: Cincia Aphrodisia erected this for herself while alive.
EDCS-04300101.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Cincia Aphrodisia set up a monument for herself during her lifetime.

EDCS-04300102.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or gift to a woman named Clara and her freedman.

EDCS-04300104.translation: To the departed spirits. Oppia Laeta made this while alive for Marcus Crassicius Verecundus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04300104.summary: A funerary inscription by Oppia Laeta for her deceased husband, Marcus Crassicius Verecundus.

EDCS-04300105.translation: To Quintus Culcinius (?). For his daughter. In front, 10 feet; in the field, [X] feet.
EDCS-04300105.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a funerary plot or land, mentioning a daughter and a possible dedicator named Quintus Culcinius.

EDCS-04300106.translation: Belonging to Decimina, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-04300106.summary: This inscription likely refers to property or a funerary dedication belonging to Decimina, a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-04300107.translation: Lucius Decius Maximus is buried here.
EDCS-04300107.summary: This is a simple tomb inscription for Lucius Decius Maximus.

EDCS-04300109.translation: To Eucharistos, beloved of Titus Terentius Bassus, aged 2 years.
EDCS-04300109.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eucharistos, the beloved child of Titus Terentius Bassus, who died at the age of two.

EDCS-04300110.translation: Eros Squ/rix [erected this]. Fulvius Sarvus(?) [erected this] for himself and his freedwoman Aia/[dia(?)]...
EDCS-04300110.summary: This funerary epitaph records Fulvius Sarvus setting up a monument for himself and his freedwoman Aiadia, with Eros also potentially involved.

EDCS-04300112.translation: For [her husband]. She lived 35 years, 6 months, and 25 days. Favia Severina, his wife, erected this.
EDCS-04300112.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of a deceased woman and states that her wife, Favia Severina, set up the monument.

EDCS-04300113.translation: To the Divine Shades, for Festianus, slave of Oc-
EDCS-04300113.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' (Divine Shades), likely a funerary epitaph for Festianus, a slave.

EDCS-04300114.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Floridus, aged 10 years, 11 months. Vaccia Hygia, his most devoted sister, made this for her brother while alive.
EDCS-04300114.summary: This epitaph, set up by a devoted sister for her young brother Floridus, is a dedication to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-04300115.translation: For Iulius (?) Frontonius, son of Quintus, and Septimia (?), daughter of Lucius, his wife. [She] ordered [it] to be made by her will.
EDCS-04300115.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband and wife, with the wife having ordered the monument to be erected in her will.

EDCS-04300118.summary: This inscription records Homilus, identified as a student, possibly on a tombstone or educational marker.

EDCS-04300120.translation: To Quintus Kanuleius Priscus, son of Quintus, of the Pupinia tribe, aged 1 year.
EDCS-04300120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Kanuleius Priscus, a one-year-old boy from the Pupinia tribe.

EDCS-04300122.translation: Iulius, freedman of a woman, for himself and for Quintus Iulius, son of Spurius, and for Iulia, daughter of Spurius, [restored name].
EDCS-04300122.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by Iulius, a freedman, for himself and other relatives.

EDCS-04300123.translation: Lucius Laberius Commodus, son of Marcus, made this tomb for himself and for Laecania Tertia, daughter of Spurius, while alive; 16 feet in front, 15 feet in area.
EDCS-04300123.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Laberius Commodus for himself and Laecania Tertia, indicating the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-04300124.translation: Laberia Perssis, freedwoman of a woman, for herself and her family; 14 feet in front, 26 feet in area.
EDCS-04300124.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Laberia Perssis, a freedwoman, for herself and her family, specifying the plot's dimensions.

EDCS-04300125.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Gaius Lepidus.

EDCS-04300126.translation: Licinia Primigenia, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive for herself and for Tetius Crescens, in memory of Venustus, her patron, Primigenia.
EDCS-04300126.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Licinia Primigenia, a freedwoman, for herself, her freedman Tetius Crescens, and in memory of her patron Venustus.

EDCS-04300127.translation: Lucia, freedwoman of a woman, ordered this to be made by her will for herself and for her.
EDCS-04300127.summary: This funerary inscription states that Lucia, a freedwoman, arranged for her burial through her will.

EDCS-04300129.translation: To the departed spirits of Marcella Pollentia Clymene.
EDCS-04300129.summary: This is a dedication to the Manes (departed spirits) for Marcella Pollentia Clymene.

EDCS-04300130.translation: To Gaius Marius Hermogenes, freedman of Caius, [from] Karitti.
EDCS-04300130.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Marius Hermogenes, a freedman.

EDCS-04300131.translation: Maximinae Eutychia, a most devoted mother, lived for 11 years.
EDCS-04300131.summary: This epitaph records the life of Maximinae Eutychia, a devoted mother who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-04300132.translation: Maximus for himself. [Restored text possibly indicating an offering or dedication].
EDCS-04300132.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Maximus for himself.

EDCS-04300133.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Sextus Munatius Secundus.

EDCS-04300135.translation: Quintus Nonius Athenio, son of Quintus.
EDCS-04300135.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary inscription, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-04300136.translation: For himself and for Gaius Oppius Archias, freedman of Lucius, and Sapphia Felix.
EDCS-04300136.summary: This is a funerary dedication for several individuals, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300139.translation: The plot of Lucius Ovinius Auctus, 24 feet in front and 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-04300139.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Ovinius Auctus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300141.translation: To the departed spirits. Cap from Palpellius, aged 100.
EDCS-04300141.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for Cap, a woman aged 100, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300144.translation: Publius Papius Liberalis. In front, 12 feet; in the field, 16 feet.
EDCS-04300144.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Publius Papius Liberalis.

EDCS-04300149.translation: To the departed spirits. For Pollentia Clymene and Pollentia.
EDCS-04300149.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for two individuals named Pollentia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300151.translation: Procula, his daughter, made this while alive for her son Velinus Paullus.
EDCS-04300151.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Procula for her son Velinus Paullus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300154.translation: Quinctilia made this for her mother Quinctilia and her sister Tertia Quinctilia.
EDCS-04300154.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Quinctilia for her mother and sister, both also named Quinctilia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300155.translation: Publius Remius Ruga, son of Quintus, for himself and his family, 25 feet in front and [..] feet in the field.
EDCS-04300155.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot dedicated by Publius Remius Ruga for himself and his family, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300156.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Secundus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300157.translation: To the departed spirits. From the plot of Marcus' freedman Secundus, 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field, and for Flaminia Secunda.
EDCS-04300157.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to a freedman of Marcus and includes a dedication for Flaminia Secunda, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300161.translation: Daughter of Marcus [?], son of Marcus Sempronius Fuscus [?].
EDCS-04300161.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the name of a Roman man, Marcus Sempronius Fuscus, and possibly his daughter, from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04300162.summary: This is a very brief inscription naming a Roman individual, Gaius Settidius.

EDCS-04300164.translation: Storge, freedwoman of [?], made this for herself and for Synistor, freedman of Arescusa, and for Eurema, freedman, while alive, in a plot of land 20 feet deep and 16 feet wide.
EDCS-04300164.summary: This inscription records the self-funded construction of a burial plot by a freedwoman named Storge, specifying dimensions and beneficiaries, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300166.translation: Suavis, freedwoman, made this plot 12 feet in every direction.
EDCS-04300166.summary: This inscription records a burial plot of 12 square feet made by Suavis, a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300168.translation: Titacia made this for Titacus Firmus.
EDCS-04300168.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Titacia for Titacus Firmus, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-04300169.translation: For myself, and for Gaius Travius, freedman brother of a woman, and for Gentilis, freedman, and for Felicla.
EDCS-04300169.summary: This inscription lists beneficiaries of a dedication or will, including family members or freedmen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300170.translation: By will, according to the law of Treblanus, son of Caius, to his father.
EDCS-04300170.summary: This inscription indicates a provision made by will, likely concerning a road or public work, in honor of a father named Treblanus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300171.translation: Gaius Vallius Maximus, son of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and his mother.
EDCS-04300171.summary: This inscription records a self-funded funerary dedication made by Gaius Vallius Maximus for himself and his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300173.translation: Vibia Arbuscula, freedwoman of Gaius, made this while alive for herself and for Gaius Vibius Felix, her freedman.
EDCS-04300173.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Vibia Arbuscula, a freedwoman, for herself and for her freedman Gaius Vibius Felix.

EDCS-04300174.translation: Lucius Volusius, son of Lucius, son of Ca[...].
EDCS-04300174.summary: This incomplete inscription records the name and parentage of a Roman individual, Lucius Volusius, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04300175.translation: To the Manes, for Urbana, his sister.
EDCS-04300175.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Manes (spirits of the dead) for Urbana, the sister of the dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04300236.summary: This is a dedication to Acens, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04300255.translation: Damianus and Laurentia made 200 feet with their children.
EDCS-04300255.summary: This inscription records the construction of 200 feet by Damianus and Laurentia, likely a funerary or building context, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300256.translation: Donatianus made 200 feet for the commemoration of Zebida.
EDCS-04300256.summary: This inscription records Donatianus creating 200 feet in memory of Zebida, likely a funerary monument or a dedication for remembrance, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300264.translation: Silius Candidianus built this temple/shrine here.
EDCS-04300264.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple or shrine by Silius Candidianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300265.translation: Diogenes gladly and deservedly to Silvanus.
EDCS-04300265.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Diogenes to the deity Silvanus, indicating personal devotion, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300269.summary: This fragmented inscription likely refers to a child and a person named Fausta, the context of which is unclear but possibly funerary, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04300272.translation: Maecenas, son of Spurius Rufus, while alive made this for himself and for Titus Maecenas, freedman of Titus, and for Onia, mother of Maecenas, freedwoman of Caius, and for Simai, sister of Maecenas.
EDCS-04300272.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Maecenas Rufus for himself and several family members and freedpeople, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300274.summary: This inscription records Valens and Nymphe as parents who made a dedication, possibly funerary or votive, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300276.translation: The bones and ashes of Caius Octavius Silon.
EDCS-04300276.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the remains of Caius Octavius Silon, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300277.translation: Marcus Iulius Eunus and Iulia Zosime, parents, made [this] for Iulia Hora, aged 18 years, months, and days.
EDCS-04300277.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Iulius Eunus and Iulia Zosime as parents dedicating a monument to their daughter Iulia Hora, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04300278.translation: Titacia Dionysia, freedwoman of Caius, made this while alive for her daughter Aspasia.
EDCS-04300278.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother for her daughter, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04300280.translation: To the Divine Shades of Laecania Amoena. Selicius Geminus, a VI vir Augustalis.
EDCS-04300280.summary: A funerary dedication to Laecania Amoena by Selicius Geminus, an Augustan priest, probably from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04300281.translation: Sacred to Liber Augustus. Octavianus [repaired/rebuilt] the temple, which had collapsed from age.
EDCS-04300281.summary: An inscription recording the repair of a temple dedicated to Liber Augustus, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04300282.summary: A very fragmentary funerary dedication to Caia, daughter of Caius, date uncertain.

EDCS-04300285.translation: Galgestia Suavis, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and her family. In front, 13 feet; in the field, 18 feet.
EDCS-04300285.summary: A funerary dedication specifying burial plot dimensions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04300286.translation: Virtia Tertia, daughter of Spurius, made this while alive for her husband and son, Publius Athenius Erotus, freedman of Publius, a VI vir, and Publius Athenius Bassus, son of Publius, an aedile.
EDCS-04300286.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife for her husband and son, who held civic and religious offices, likely from the mid-Imperial period.

EDCS-04300287.text_edition: \n Mindius Narcissus Mindius Maleus Decidius Hister Decidia Certa Minervius Epaphroditus Menander Lucifer dispensator Lucifer alius Amandus dispensator Vitalis dispensator Trophimus qui dispensavit Anconius qui vilicavit Viator colonus Septimius Sabinianus Flavius Hedistus Annius Calvo Annius Civilis\n
EDCS-04300287.translation: Mindius Narcissus, Mindius Maleus, Decidius Hister, Decidia Certa, Minervius Epaphroditus, Menander Lucifer, steward; Lucifer, another; Amandus, steward; Vitalis, steward; Trophimus, who administered; Anconius, who managed the farm; Viator, a colonist; Septimius Sabinianus, Flavius Hedistus, Annius Calvo, Annius Civilis.
EDCS-04300287.summary: This inscription lists numerous individuals, including stewards and farm managers, likely related to an estate or a collective funerary monument.

EDCS-04300288.translation: Iulia Prophasis, freedwoman of Augustus, made this while alive for herself and for Gaius Iulius Aplus, quinquennial duovir and son; Gaius Iulius Cupitus, son; Iulia Phyllis, daughter; Iulia Apula, daughter; Caristus, beloved.
EDCS-04300288.summary: This extensive funerary inscription was erected by Iulia Prophasis, a freedwoman of Augustus, for herself and her children and beloved companion.

EDCS-04300289.translation: To Titus Flavius Heliades, freedman of Augustus. Dionysius, friend of Spurius Ennius Rufus.
EDCS-04300289.summary: An inscription honoring Titus Flavius Heliades, a freedman of Augustus, by his friend Dionysius, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-04300290.translation: To the Divine Shades of Caius Coelius Restitutus, freedman of Caius. Caius Coelius Halys, to his fellow freedman, well deserving.
EDCS-04300290.summary: A funerary dedication from one freedman to another, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04300291.translation: to [name], freedman of Orcivius, [made this] while alive for his deserving fellow slave and companion.
EDCS-04300291.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman for his deceased partner, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04300292.translation: To the Divine Shades of Felix.
EDCS-04300292.summary: A very brief funerary dedication to Felix, date uncertain.

EDCS-04300293.translation: Horatia Festa, freedwoman of Marcus, made this while alive.
EDCS-04300293.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Horatia Festa for herself, indicating she made it during her lifetime.

EDCS-04300294.translation: For Sextus Palpellius Alpa and himself, from VIIc Palpelliae Hedone, to his grandmother.
EDCS-04300294.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Sextus Palpellius Alpa for his grandmother and himself.

EDCS-04300298.translation: To the Divine Shades. Laevia Hedone, while alive, made this for her husband Lucius Laevius Elpidephorus, the best.
EDCS-04300298.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Laevia Hedone to her husband, Lucius Laevius Elpidephorus, likely set up during her lifetime.

EDCS-04300299.translation: The place of the monument of Lucius Modius Speratus, freedman of a woman, a member of the IVviratus.
EDCS-04300299.summary: This inscription identifies a burial plot belonging to Lucius Modius Speratus, a freedman who held a specific priesthood role.

EDCS-04300303.translation: Modestus made this for Primio and for his mother Fausta, his son.
EDCS-04300303.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Modestus, the son, for Primio and his mother Fausta.

EDCS-04300305.translation: Lucius Modius Donatus made this while alive: 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04300305.summary: Lucius Modius Donatus records the dimensions of a plot he purchased or prepared for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-04300306.translation: For Lucius Menacius, son of Publius. Menacia Quarta, daughter of Lucius, made this for her father while alive.
EDCS-04300306.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Menacia Quarta for her father, Lucius Menacius, during her own lifetime.

EDCS-04300309.translation: Caius Sal made this for himself and...
EDCS-04300309.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Sal for himself and at least one other person, but the inscription is incomplete.

EDCS-04300310.translation: ...to Amaranthus, freedman of Maro, freedman of Maro, for his father.
EDCS-04300310.summary: This incomplete inscription seems to be a funerary dedication for a father, mentioning a freedman named Amaranthus.

EDCS-04300312.translation: Publius Fufidius Optatus, freedman of a woman, a member of the IIIIviratus, for himself and Ussua...
EDCS-04300312.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Publius Fufidius Optatus, a freedman and IIIIvir, for himself and at least one other individual, but it is incomplete.

EDCS-04300313.translation: Cinio placed this as a votive offering to Silvanus Augustus.
EDCS-04300313.summary: This inscription records a votive offering dedicated to Silvanus Augustus by Cinio.

EDCS-04300314.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Maxuma Umbria.

EDCS-04300315.translation: Lucius Iulius Besidianus and Servilia Secunda give this gift to Jupiter Victor.
EDCS-04300315.summary: This inscription records a gift dedicated to Jupiter Victor by Lucius Iulius Besidianus and Servilia Secunda.

EDCS-04300316.translation: By order of Sextus Tettius, a gift to Mother Earth.
EDCS-04300316.summary: This inscription records a gift to Mother Earth, commissioned by Sextus Tettius.

EDCS-04300318.translation: Brissinius IER willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the August Dea.
EDCS-04300318.summary: This inscription records the willing fulfillment of a vow to the August Dea by Brissinius IER.

EDCS-04300319.translation: Lucius Torius Stephanus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the August Dea.
EDCS-04300319.summary: This inscription records the willing fulfillment of a vow to the August Dea by Lucius Torius Stephanus.

EDCS-04300321.translation: Settidi Euhemerus and Eutychus willingly fulfilled their vow to Silvanus Augustus.
EDCS-04300321.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Silvanus Augustus by Settidi Euhemerus and Eutychus.

EDCS-04300322.translation: Thalassa Deciorum willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Terra Histria.
EDCS-04300322.summary: This inscription records the willing fulfillment of a vow to Terra Histria by Thalassa Deciorum.

EDCS-04300324.translation: Titus Annius Lyrassus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04300324.summary: This inscription records the willing fulfillment of a vow by Titus Annius Lyrassus.

EDCS-04300325.translation: Caecilia Barbara willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04300325.summary: This inscription records the willing fulfillment of a vow by Caecilia Barbara.

EDCS-04300326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying a woman named Fabia Prisca.

EDCS-04300327.translation: Mecenatia, freedwoman of Titus, paid her vow.
EDCS-04300327.summary: This inscription records a freedwoman named Mecenatia fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04300329.text_edition: \n Faustinae Augustae Aeli Antonini Augusti Pii filiae Aureli Caesaris uxori decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04300329.translation: To Faustina Augusta, daughter of Emperor Caesar Antoninus Pius, wife of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-04300329.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Empress Faustina the Elder, wife of Antoninus Pius and mother of Marcus Aurelius, likely honoring her memory or divine status by a local council.

EDCS-04300330.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Antonio Gordiano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo patri patriae res publica Nesactiensium\n
EDCS-04300330.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, by the republic of the Nesactians.
EDCS-04300330.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Emperor Gordian III by the community of Nesactium.

EDCS-04300331.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus.
EDCS-04300331.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Philip I, likely honoring him by a local community.

EDCS-04300336.translation: Caius Iulius Fuscus, a Sextumvir Augustalis, made this for his wife, Hostilia Maximilla, freedwoman of Marcius. Fabia Natalis, freedwoman of Lucius, also contributed. [---]
EDCS-04300336.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by a prominent local official, Caius Iulius Fuscus, for his wife Hostilia Maximilla, with a contribution from Fabia Natalis.

EDCS-04300337.translation: Maxima, daughter of Marcius, dedicated the temple and the colonnades from her own land.
EDCS-04300337.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a temple and porticoes by Maxima, daughter of Marcius, using her own land.

EDCS-04300339.translation: Florus and Ampliata, most devoted parents, made this for their son Sextus Palpellius Maximus, aged 11 years.
EDCS-04300339.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by parents, Florus and Ampliata, to their son Sextus Palpellius Maximus.

EDCS-04300340.translation: Maxima Vibia made this while alive.
EDCS-04300340.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, indicating that Maxima Vibia commissioned her own tomb during her lifetime.

EDCS-04300342.translation: Gaius Rufellius Rufus, son of Gaius, made this while alive for himself and his family, and for Seia Maxuma, daughter of Publius, and Rufellia Secunda, daughter of Gaius. Lucius Vallius, grandson of Lucius, [reserved?] space in front 20 feet and in the field 10 feet.
EDCS-04300342.summary: This is a funerary or property inscription by Gaius Rufellius Rufus, dedicating a plot of land for his family and mentioning measurement specifications.

EDCS-04300343.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Plautia Maximilla, a most unhappy mother, made this for Aulus Septimius Maximianus, who lived 13 years, 5 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-04300343.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Septimius Maximianus, dedicated by his grieving mother Plautia Maximilla.

EDCS-04300349.translation: For the freedman of Farna Hostilia.
EDCS-04300349.summary: This is a funerary marker for a freedman of Farna Hostilia.

EDCS-04300358.summary: This incomplete inscription likely refers to Transitus, a deacon, and possibly a sacred dedication.

EDCS-04300359.translation: To the Genius of Barbulanus. Publius Flavius Diomedes.
EDCS-04300359.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Genius of Barbulanus by Publius Flavius Diomedes.

EDCS-04400001.summary: This inscription records Calpurnius Proculus fulfilling a vow, likely on a votive monument.

EDCS-04400002.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pertinaci Augusto Parthico Arabico propagatori imperii Publius Gavius Secundinus ob honorem decurionatus oblatum sibi a splendidissimo ordine Parentinorum locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04400002.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Arabia, enlarger of the empire, Lucius Gavius Secundinus was granted a place by decree of the town councillors by the most splendid order of the Parentini, on account of the honor of the decurionate offered to him.
EDCS-04400002.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot to Publius Gavius Secundinus by the town council of Parentium in recognition of his appointment as a decurion.

EDCS-04400003.translation: Lucius Arius Proculus, son of Lucius, served as a speculator in the Praetorian Guard for 10 years and lived for 28 years. Titus Arius Proculus, son of Lucius, made this for his brother while he was alive.
EDCS-04400003.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Lucius Arius Proculus, a Praetorian Guard soldier, and records his brother Titus Arius Proculus as the dedicator.

EDCS-04400005.translation: To Quintus, centurion of the Second Legion, from a friend.
EDCS-04400005.summary: This is a dedication from a friend to Quintus, a centurion of Legio II.

EDCS-04400006.translation: To the divine shades. The bones of Coelia Marcia, daughter of Marcus, wife of Cantius Septimianus, are placed here; her respected remains were granted a public funeral.
EDCS-04400006.summary: This funerary inscription honors Coelia Marcia, detailing her burial and a public funeral decreed for her.

EDCS-04400007.translation: Caius Peppienus Macer, son of Caius, who died at the age of 10, is buried here. Caius Andricus, freedman of Caius, and Firmia Salvia, daughter of Marcus, while alive.
EDCS-04400007.summary: This inscription records the burial of young Caius Peppienus Macer and also mentions Caius Andricus and Firmia Salvia who set it up while alive.

EDCS-04400009.translation: Alexander made this while alive for himself, his concubine Annia Asia, and his family.
EDCS-04400009.summary: This is a tomb inscription made by Alexander for himself, his concubine, and his family.

EDCS-04400010.translation: Aurelius Albanus and Castor, guardians of the children and heirs of Aurelia Rufina, wife of Aurelius Zabba, placed this.
EDCS-04400010.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by guardians to Aurelia Rufina, wife of Aurelius Zabba.

EDCS-04400011.translation: Lucius Caesius Maximus, son of Lucius, and Maxuma Caesia, daughter of Caius, daughter of Lucius, snatched from her parents at the age of 12.
EDCS-04400011.summary: This inscription laments the death of young Maxuma Caesia, daughter of Lucius and Maxuma, who died at 12 years old.

EDCS-04400012.translation: To the divine shades. Claudia Callityche. Marcus Claudius.
EDCS-04400012.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription for Claudia Callityche, set up by Marcus Claudius.

EDCS-04400014.translation: To the divine shades. Hedylus, who was deserved, I made this for you, Severa.
EDCS-04400014.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Severa to Hedylus, acknowledging his merits.

EDCS-04400016.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Eusebes, freedman of Salvia Lesbia, made this for his wife while he was alive.
EDCS-04400016.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salvia Lesbia, dedicated by her freedman and husband.

EDCS-04400023.translation: Lupicinus and Pascasia made [a tomb?] of 400 feet. Clamosus, master of the boys, and Successa, [made?] 100 feet. Felicissimus with his family [made?] 100 feet.
EDCS-04400023.summary: This inscription appears to record contributions or specifications for a burial area, possibly a columbarium or a shared tomb, with different individuals or families allocating specific amounts of space.

EDCS-04400024.translation: Memorius and Valeria, [a tomb?] of 50 feet.
EDCS-04400024.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating a burial plot of 50 feet, attributed to Memorius and Valeria.

EDCS-04400025.translation: Castus and Ursa made one hundred feet.
EDCS-04400025.summary: This records the construction of a length of 100 feet, likely a pavement or wall, by Castus and Ursa.

EDCS-04400027.translation: Lupicinus and Pascasia, slaves, made C [feet].
EDCS-04400027.summary: This inscription records the construction of 100 feet of something by the slaves Lupicinus and Pascasia.

EDCS-04400028.summary: This inscription records the construction of 100 feet of something by the slave Spectata, likely continuing from a previous inscription.

EDCS-04400029.translation: This sacred resting place contains the snowy body of the confessor Maurus; this primitive church was restored by his prayers; here he was fittingly translated, where he was made bishop and confessor; therefore the place was doubled in honor.
EDCS-04400029.summary: This inscription is a dedication for a church or shrine built/restored in honor of Bishop and Confessor Maurus, commemorating his translation and veneration.

EDCS-04400030.translation: Iohannis Romeus made 20 feet for himself, according to his vow.
EDCS-04400030.summary: This inscription records Iohannis Romeus fulfilling a vow by constructing 20 feet of something.

EDCS-04400033.translation: Theofrastus and Ianuarius, deacons, made 300 feet.
EDCS-04400033.summary: This inscription records the construction of 300 feet by the deacons Theofrastus and Ianuarius.

EDCS-04400034.translation: By the gifts of God and Holy Church, Bassinus the deacon made 90 feet for himself, according to his vow.
EDCS-04400034.summary: This inscription records Bassinus, a deacon, fulfilling a vow by constructing 90 feet of something, attributing it to divine gifts.

EDCS-04400036.translation: By the gifts of God and Holy Church, Innocentius the deacon made 90 feet for himself, according to his vow.
EDCS-04400036.summary: This inscription records Innocentius, a deacon, fulfilling a vow by constructing 90 feet of something, attributing it to divine gifts.

EDCS-04400037.translation: Mucianus and Deciana, with their household, made 130 feet.
EDCS-04400037.summary: This inscription records Mucianus and Deciana, along with their household, constructing 130 feet of something.

EDCS-04400039.translation: Clamosus, the teacher of boys, and Victorina made 111 feet.
EDCS-04400039.summary: This inscription records the construction of 111 feet by Clamosus, a teacher of boys, and Victorina.

EDCS-04400042.translation: Ulpus and Maxima made this with their people, 50 feet.
EDCS-04400042.summary: This inscription records a construction project measuring 50 feet, likely by two individuals named Ulpus and Maxima.

EDCS-04400045.translation: Claudius the archdeacon, Eufrasius the bishop, Eufrasius the son of the archdeacon, Saint Maurus.
EDCS-04400045.summary: This inscription lists several ecclesiastical figures, including two named Eufrasius and a Claudius, indicating their presence or association with a site.

EDCS-04400046.translation: This temple, before a terrible landslide from a shaking ruin and not firm with certain strength, was small and lacking great metal, but only perishable roofs depended on merits; then the priest Eufrasius, prudent and fervent with zeal of faith, foresaw the sliding seat of its weight and the ruin; with a holy mind, he pulled down the decaying buildings that they might be better established, laying the foundations and raising the peaks of the temple, which you see recently shining with varied metal, completing the begun work and adorning it with a great gift, calling the church, he signed it with the name of Christ; rejoicing, the fortunate one thus completed the work.
EDCS-04400046.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Bishop Eufrasius detailing the rebuilding and beautification of a church, likely in the 5th or 6th century, emphasizing his foresight and piety.

EDCS-04400048.translation: Saint Felicitas, Saint Basilissa, Saint Eugenia, Saint Cecilia, Saint Agnes, Saint Agatha, Saint Euphemia, Saint Thecla, Saint Valeria, Saint Perpetua, Saint Susanna, Saint Justina.
EDCS-04400048.summary: This inscription lists the names of several female saints, likely commemorating their veneration or relics at a church.

EDCS-04400049.translation: Saint Simon, Saint Thomas, Saint Bartholomew, Saint James, Saint Andrew, Saint Peter, I am the true light, Saint Paul, Saint John, Saint Philip, Saint Matthew, Saint James son of Alphaeus, Saint Jude son of Jacob.
EDCS-04400049.summary: This inscription lists the names of several apostles and includes a quote from Christ, likely from a church dedicated to or associated with these figures.

EDCS-04400052.summary: This inscription identifies Dominicus as an archdeacon, likely marking a position or dedication.

EDCS-04400053.summary: This inscription identifies Iohannes by his noble status ('vir clarissimus'), likely a dedication or memorial.

EDCS-04400054.summary: This inscription identifies Eufrasius as a bishop, likely marking a building or dedication associated with his office.

EDCS-04400055.translation: From the gifts of God and of Saint Mary, Stefanus the custos of the church.
EDCS-04400055.summary: This inscription records a donation by Stefanus, custos of the church, dedicated to God and Saint Mary.

EDCS-04400056.translation: Eufrasius, a servant of God and bishop, in his time, in his 11th year, with God's help, founded this place for the holy Catholic Church from its foundations.
EDCS-04400056.summary: This inscription records Bishop Eufrasius founding a site for the Catholic Church in his 11th year of office, likely in the late 5th or early 6th century.

EDCS-04400057.translation: Directing prayers and pious duties to Christ, seeking the blessed Theodorus with a merciful heart and glory of the flock among all.
EDCS-04400057.summary: This fragmentary inscription invokes Christ and mentions Theodorus, possibly relating to a religious dedication or prayer.

EDCS-04400059.translation: On the second day before the Ides of October, the death of Iusta.
EDCS-04400059.summary: This is a brief funerary notice recording the death date of Iusta.

EDCS-04400060.translation: On the Ides of March, Leo died.
EDCS-04400060.summary: This is a brief funerary notice recording the death date of Leo.

EDCS-04400061.translation: On the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, the death of Macara.
EDCS-04400061.summary: This is a brief funerary notice recording the death date of Macara.

EDCS-04400062.translation: On the eighth day before the Kalends of February, Theodorus the priest.

EDCS-04400064.translation: On the Kalends of June, the death of Iohannes Polensis, the bishop.
EDCS-04400064.summary: This is a brief funerary notice recording the death date of Bishop Iohannes Polensis.

EDCS-04400065.translation: On the Kalends of September, the death of Ma...

EDCS-04400077.translation: On the day before the Ides of August, the death of Marinus, priest of the invincible holy bishop Maurus.
EDCS-04400077.summary: This inscription records the death of the priest Marinus, associated with the cult of bishop Maurus, on August 12th, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-04400081.translation: On the third day of January, Iacobus.

EDCS-04400106.translation: On the Ides of September, the death of Tiso.

EDCS-04400117.translation: On the fifth Ides of March, the death of Andreas Bonagratia.
EDCS-04400117.summary: This inscription records the death of Andreas Bonagratia on March 11th.

EDCS-04400118.translation: On the thirteenth day before the Kalends of August, the death of Francha.
EDCS-04400118.summary: This inscription records the death of Francha on July 20th.

EDCS-04400119.translation: On the seventh Ides of July, the death of Amara.
EDCS-04400119.summary: This inscription records the death of Amara on July 9th.

EDCS-04400121.translation: On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of May, Iuliano died.
EDCS-04400121.summary: This inscription records the death of Iuliano on April 14th.

EDCS-04400122.translation: On the seventeenth day before the Kalends of June, Venerus died.
EDCS-04400122.summary: This inscription records the death of Venerus on May 16th.

EDCS-04400123.translation: On the ninth day before the Kalends of December, Iohannes.
EDCS-04400123.summary: This inscription records the name Iohannes with a date of November 23rd, likely commemorating a death.

EDCS-04400124.translation: most venerable Bishop Domienicus, what terrible scourges I suffer, not because of my miseries but because of the judge to come, read from it what pain I suffer from every crime.
EDCS-04400124.summary: This inscription is a personal reflection or plea addressed to Bishop Domienicus, expressing suffering due to sin and fear of future judgment.

EDCS-04400125.summary: This is a personal epitaph or inscription identifying Mauricius as an acolyte.

EDCS-04400126.summary: This is likely a tombstone inscription for Andreas, a cleric, expressing his faith.

EDCS-04400128.translation: On the first day before the Kalends of March, the death of Vendema.
EDCS-04400128.summary: This inscription records the date of death for Vendema, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04400130.translation: On the third day before the Ides of April, Xemo died.
EDCS-04400130.summary: This inscription marks the death of Xemo on a specific date, probably on a tombstone.

EDCS-04400131.translation: On the sixth day before the Kalends of June, the death of Marinus, priest.
EDCS-04400131.summary: This inscription records the death of Marinus, a priest, on a specific date, likely on his tombstone.

EDCS-04400132.translation: On the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May, the death of Martinus.
EDCS-04400132.summary: This inscription records the death of Martinus on a specific date, probably on a tombstone.

EDCS-04400133.translation: Nuno, on the day of the Kalends of February, the death of Germanus.
EDCS-04400133.summary: This inscription records the death of Germanus on the Kalends of February, likely on his tombstone.

EDCS-04400134.translation: On the tenth day before the Kalends of January, the death of Ioannes Campari.
EDCS-04400134.summary: This inscription records the death of Ioannes Campari on a specific date, likely on his tombstone.

EDCS-04400135.translation: On the twelfth day of the month of May, the death of Maria.
EDCS-04400135.summary: This inscription records the death of Maria on the twelfth day of May, likely on her tombstone.

EDCS-04400138.summary: This is a personal epitaph or inscription identifying Basilius as an acolyte.

EDCS-04400140.translation: On the sixth day before the Nones of March, the death of Anastasia.
EDCS-04400140.summary: This inscription records the death of Anastasia on March 2nd.

EDCS-04400141.translation: On the third day before the Nones of June, the death of Johannes the deacon.
EDCS-04400141.summary: This inscription records the death of Johannes the deacon on June 3rd.

EDCS-04400142.translation: On the fourth day before the Kalends of July, the death of Mutulinus.
EDCS-04400142.summary: This inscription records the death of Mutulinus on June 28th.

EDCS-04400143.summary: This inscription is a pious statement by Philippus.

EDCS-04400144.translation: In honour of Saint Valentine, Petrus died.
EDCS-04400144.summary: This inscription records the death of Petrus, associated with Saint Valentine.

EDCS-04400146.translation: The fourteenth day before the Kalends of January. Domniga.
EDCS-04400146.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a tombstone or a date marker, mentioning the name Domniga.

EDCS-04400147.translation: Ianuarius with his family, 250 feet; Rusticianus, a religious man, with his mother Clarissima, 250 feet; Gaianus and Renata, 250 feet.
EDCS-04400147.summary: This funerary inscription records the measurement of burial plots for several individuals and families, possibly dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-04400148.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription recording Archelaus and his family, with an incomplete measurement.

EDCS-04400149.translation: Eraclius the lector with his wife Laurentia.
EDCS-04400149.summary: This inscription records Eraclius, a lector, and his wife Laurentia.

EDCS-04400152.summary: This is a prayer for mercy addressed to Epagathus.

EDCS-04400153.translation: Gunna lived for [some number of] years.
EDCS-04400153.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating the lifespan of Gunna, with the length of life missing.

EDCS-04400157.translation: Dercilis, slave of Cnaeus Magurus, aged VI years, and [his sister?] aged III years. Their father set up this monument.
EDCS-04400157.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a father for his two young daughters, Dercilis and another whose name is not fully preserved.

EDCS-04400158.translation: Sacred to Minerva Flanatica. Bassus, having received what he asked from the goddess, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04400158.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Flanatica by Bassus, fulfilling a vow made after receiving what he petitioned for.

EDCS-04400159.summary: This inscription likely records the names of a father and son, possibly related to a tomb or family monument, though much of the text is missing.

EDCS-04400160.translation: To the Divine Shades. Mename, aged 1 year and 10 months. Agathemerianus and Digna, parents, for their dearest daughter.
EDCS-04400160.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young child named Mename, set up by her parents.

EDCS-04400163.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating the burial place of a person named Fia.

EDCS-04400165.translation: To the Unconquered Holy God Mithras, for the safety and victory of our most holy lords, the Augusti, the Philippi, and of Otacilia Severa Augusta, Charitinus, freedman, sub-procurator, and Sabinianus, freedman, assistant of the scribes, devoted to their divine power and majesty.
EDCS-04400165.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mithras, made by two freedmen officials for the well-being and success of the emperors Philip I and II and Empress Otacilia Severa.

EDCS-04400167.translation: Venusta, the slave of Sisenna, made this for Atticus, the ironworker.
EDCS-04400167.summary: A funerary dedication by a slave for her deceased master.

EDCS-04400168.translation: Celadus and Prima set [this up] for their fellow slave and for themselves.
EDCS-04400168.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Celadus and Prima for a fellow slave and for themselves.

EDCS-04400170.translation: Lucius Marcius Tertius, freedman of Lucius Marcius, made this while alive for himself and his family, for Marcia Stactine, freedwoman of Lucius. The monument occupies 20 feet in front and 20 feet in width in every direction.
EDCS-04400170.summary: A funerary monument established by a freedman for himself, his family, and a freedwoman, with specific dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-04400172.translation: Sacred to Liber Augustus. Sextus Appuleius Hermias built this from the ground up, during the consulship of Pollio and Apro.
EDCS-04400172.summary: This is a building inscription recording the construction of a sacred structure dedicated to Liber Augustus by Sextus Appuleius Hermias during the consulship of Pollio and Apro.

EDCS-04400173.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Florentinus, aged 9 years. His parents, Euryches and Successa, made this.
EDCS-04400173.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Florentinus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-04400174.translation: Axius Gratus, his great-uncle, made [this] for Prisca.
EDCS-04400174.summary: This funerary inscription records that Axius Gratus erected a monument for Prisca.

EDCS-04400176.translation: Lucius Pontius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, a veteran soldier of the 7th Praetorian cohort for 18 years, an haruspex, erected this monument during his lifetime for himself and his family, and for his wife Paecilia Paula, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04400176.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Pontius Rufus, a veteran of the Praetorian Guard and haruspex, for himself, his family, and his wife.

EDCS-04400177.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Optatus Iunior, while his father was still alive, made this in dutiful devotion for his parents, Cornelia Secundina, aged 40, and Cominius Optatus.
EDCS-04400177.summary: This funerary epitaph records Optatus Iunior's dedication to his parents, Cornelia Secundina and Cominius Optatus.

EDCS-04400178.summary: This inscription is a simple naming of an individual, Lucius Iunius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04400179.summary: This inscription simply names Voltilia Maxuma.

EDCS-04400180.translation: Calvia Marcella, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive for herself and her own, for her father Calvius, son of Titus, and for her mother Gnavinia Maxuma, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-04400180.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Calvia Marcella for herself, her husband, and her parents.

EDCS-04400182.translation: Publius Tedius Valens, son of Spurius, of the Pupinia tribe, standard-bearer of the Fourth Flavian Felix legion, honored with gifts of torcs, armbands, and phalerae, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04400182.summary: This inscription honors Publius Tedius Valens, a standard-bearer of a Roman legion, detailing military decorations he received and his posthumous wishes for a monument.

EDCS-04400183.translation: Hilara, freedwoman of Egnatius Marcus, rests here.
EDCS-04400183.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hilara, the freedwoman of Egnatius Marcus.

EDCS-04400184.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Marcellus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04400186.translation: Veidius Saturninus, son of Titus, aged 25.
EDCS-04400186.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Veidius Saturninus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04500005.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Dignitas for her well-deserving sister, Lucida.
EDCS-04500005.summary: A funerary dedication to a deceased sister.

EDCS-04500008.summary: This inscription names Sextus Pedanius Seneca, son of an unnamed father.

EDCS-04500009.translation: Sacred to Nemesis Augusta. Protoctetus, slave of Lucius [---]nicus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04500009.summary: A dedication of a vow fulfilled to the goddess Nemesis, likely by a slave.

EDCS-04500010.summary: This fragmentary inscription names Ofillia Bu[---].

EDCS-04500013.translation: Calpurnia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, made this for Gaius Calpurnius Proculus and her mother Ionia, freedwoman of Lucius Callamus, for herself and her family.
EDCS-04500013.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a daughter for her parents and herself.

EDCS-04500016.translation: Lucius Barbius Cer[---], freedman of Lucius, for himself, a quinquennial duovir.
EDCS-04500016.summary: A funerary epitaph recording an individual and his position as a quinquennial duovir.

EDCS-04500017.translation: For you, well; Marcelus. Itali Caero, a fellow slave, lived 18 years, 8 months.
EDCS-04500017.summary: A funerary inscription for a young slave named Marcelus, likely set up by a fellow slave.

EDCS-04500020.translation: Marcus Ceppuleius Pudens, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made by his will for his father Marcus Ceppuleius Bito, freedman of Marcus, and his mother Hilara, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-04500020.summary: A funerary epitaph set up according to a will for parents.

EDCS-04500022.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment mentioning a female individual and her 'tent-mate' (contubernalis).

EDCS-04500025.translation: [---] to Aelia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, his wife.
EDCS-04500025.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment dedicated to a wife.

EDCS-04500026.translation: For Vinullia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, of Lauricum, aged 21. Lauricius Certus, with utmost piety, made this while alive; 20 feet on the front and 25 feet in the plot.
EDCS-04500026.summary: A funerary monument erected by a father for his deceased daughter, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-04500027.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of an individual.

EDCS-04500028.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name of an individual.

EDCS-04500029.translation: Sextilia Procula, daughter of Titus, aged 75 years.
EDCS-04500029.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of an individual.

EDCS-04500030.translation: Gaius Tullius Tertius, son of Quintus, aged 43 years.
EDCS-04500030.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of an individual.

EDCS-04500031.translation: Lucius Volumnius Orfo, son of Lucius, lies in this place.
EDCS-04500031.summary: A funerary epitaph stating that an individual is buried in this location.

EDCS-04500032.translation: To Calpurnius, son of Lucius, a very rare infant.
EDCS-04500032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Calpurnius.

EDCS-04500033.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph for Cantenia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-04500034.translation: To Marius, son of Turus (?), grandfather; to Sextus Mariarius, son of Sextus, father; to Volumnia, daughter of Publius [---].
EDCS-04500034.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph likely commemorating multiple family members, including a grandfather, father, and daughter.

EDCS-04500035.translation: Gaius Commius, son of Lucius; Commia Maxima; Acutia Tertia.
EDCS-04500035.summary: This inscription lists several names, possibly belonging to a family or individuals associated with a monument.

EDCS-04500036.translation: Titus Statilius Cladus, freedman of Taurus, and Statilia Quarta, freedwoman of Taurus, made this while alive for their faithful freedman.
EDCS-04500036.summary: A funerary monument established by two freedpersons for their faithful freedman.

EDCS-04500037.translation: Maximus, son of Gavi, Volsso, aged 75.
EDCS-04500037.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maximus Volsso, aged 75.

EDCS-04500039.translation: Apiaria Sabina for Martae, daughter of [---], aged 56.
EDCS-04500039.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age of the deceased Apiaria Sabina.

EDCS-04500040.translation: Publius Patalicus, son of Secundus, is buried here.
EDCS-04500040.summary: A simple burial inscription for Publius Patalicus.

EDCS-04500041.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name and age of the deceased Voltiomnus Taesallocus.

EDCS-04500042.translation: To his mother, Linai, Severa, his daughter.
EDCS-04500042.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Severa to her mother, Linai.

EDCS-04500043.summary: This inscription is the beginning of a funerary dedication for Calpurnius, son of Caius.

EDCS-04500044.translation: Gaius Dommicus, son of Marcus, aged seventy.
EDCS-04500044.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name and age of Gaius Dommicus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04500064.summary: This inscription is a partial dedication, likely funerary, for Publius Domitius Constans.

EDCS-04500066.translation: Remia Secunda, daughter of Maximu, aged forty, lies here.
EDCS-04500066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Remia Secunda, daughter of Maximu, stating her age and burial.

EDCS-04500067.translation: Ennia Sexta, daughter of Rufi, aged 80, is buried here.
EDCS-04500067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ennia Sexta, who died at the age of 80.

EDCS-04500070.translation: Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, Septonia (?), aged [---].
EDCS-04500070.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph, likely for a woman named Maxuma, possibly also Septonia, with her age incomplete.

EDCS-04500072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Agrsa, aged 70.
