EDCS-04500073.translation: Quintus Labienus, son of Quintus Mollio, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Aquilia Tertia, wife of Spurius, son of Lucius; L. M. C. Aquillis arranged for it to be constructed.
EDCS-04500073.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned in a will by Quintus Labienus for himself and his wife Aquilia Tertia, with construction overseen by others.

EDCS-04500075.translation: To his sister Pia Julia, Tertullinus, her brother, made this; she lived for 22 years.
EDCS-04500075.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Tertullinus to his sister Pia Julia, including her lifespan.

EDCS-04600001.translation: Barbia Stadium, freedwoman of Lucius, (dedicated this) to Bona Dea, as deserved.
EDCS-04600001.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Bona Dea by Barbia Stadium, a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-04600003.translation: Lucius Apisius, son of Titus, and Titus Arruntius, son of Lucius, duovirs, had this constructed at public expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04600003.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work by two duovirs, Lucius Apisius and Titus Arruntius, funded by the state.

EDCS-04600004.translation: Iulia Severa paid her vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-04600004.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a dedication made by Iulia Severa to the god Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.

EDCS-04600005.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Livia Heorte votum solvit\n
EDCS-04600005.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus, Livia Heorte fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04600005.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Livia Heorte to the god Jupiter Dolichenus.

EDCS-04600016.translation: To Sextus Vibius Cordus, soldier of the third praetorian cohort, Quintus Clodius Sestius made this while alive for his freedmen and freedwomen; this monument will not pass to an heir, 12 feet in front, 50 feet in the ground.
EDCS-04600016.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Clodius Sestius for himself and his freedpeople, specifying dimensions and stipulating it is not heritable.

EDCS-04600025.translation: Sextus Caesius Felix, freedman of Sextus, Auguistalis VIvir, [erected this] for his wife, Caesia, freedwoman of Sextus, [3]ca.
EDCS-04600025.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a freedman and his wife, both of whom held the Augustalis VIvir office, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04600026.translation: Gaius Vibius Valens ordered this to be made by his will, at a cost of 20,000 sesterces. Felix, freedman and Augustalis VIvir, made it.
EDCS-04600026.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Gaius Vibius Valens in his will and constructed by his freedman, Felix, who was also an Augustalis VIvir, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04600028.translation: Lucius Alfius Isochrysus, freedman of Lucius, a doctor, and Lucius Alfius Eudemus, freedman of Isochrysus, made [this] for themselves and for their patroness and for Alfia Attica, freedwoman of Lucius, their wife, and for their own good people and you.
EDCS-04600028.summary: This funerary monument was jointly erected by two freedmen doctors for themselves, their patroness, and family, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04600029.translation: To Hermes, freedman of Marivus Paullus, superintendent of the Tergestines, ...
EDCS-04600029.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Hermes, a freedman and superintendent, likely from Tergeste.

EDCS-04600030.translation: Publius M. Pollio, decurio of Pola.
EDCS-04600030.summary: This inscription records Publius M. Pollio, a local council member in the Roman town of Pola, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04600032.translation: Of Quintus Albius Secundus and Manius Titus Albinus: in the front 50 feet, in the field 30 feet.
EDCS-04600032.summary: This text records the dimensions of a property owned by Quintus Albius Secundus and Manius Titus Albinus.

EDCS-04600034.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Antistia Helia, for her most dutiful mother Antistia Tertia.
EDCS-04600034.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Antistia Helia to her mother Antistia Tertia.

EDCS-04600038.translation: Publius Gallonius Secundus, son of Publius, made this while alive for himself and for his wife Fortunata and for his son Publius Gallonius Rufus.
EDCS-04600038.summary: This funerary inscription records a man, Publius Gallonius Secundus, who built his own tomb along with those for his wife and son.

EDCS-04600039.translation: Iulius Severus, son of Lucius, for himself and for his incomparable wife Sempronia Sabina and for his most dutiful sister Demetria Severina.
EDCS-04600039.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulius Severus for himself, his wife Sempronia Sabina, and his sister Demetria Severina.

EDCS-04600041.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Marcius Trophimio. Quintus Manlius Aper, for his son-in-law Marcius Trophimus; Marcia Trophime, daughter, Marcius Trophimus, Papirius Trophimas, Manlia Trophime, his grandchildren; Commia Euodia, his wife; to one who deserved well of himself.
EDCS-04600041.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Commia Euodia to her husband Marcius Trophimio, and also mentions their children and grandchildren.

EDCS-04600042.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely identifying a tomb or owner, possibly dating from the Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-04600043.translation: Quintus Nonius Favor, while alive, made this monument for himself and for his wife Commia Ursa; it will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-04600043.summary: This is a tomb inscription by Quintus Nonius Favor for himself and his wife Commia Ursa, stating the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-04600044.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that begins with the name Marcus Postumius (restored).

EDCS-04600046.translation: To Aulus Tullius Philargyrus, freedman of Aulus. Tullia Hilara, freedwoman, made this while alive for herself and for her patron.
EDCS-04600046.summary: This funerary inscription records Tullia Hilara, a freedwoman, dedicating the monument to herself and her patron Aulus Tullius Philargyrus.

EDCS-04600049.translation: To Aulus Tullius, son of Lucius, from P[...].
EDCS-04600049.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely a dedication to Aulus Tullius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04600053.translation: He ordered that it be made by his will for himself and for Veturia, freedwoman of Caius. Monumental space in front: 12 feet; in the field: 3 feet.
EDCS-04600053.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered by will for the deceased and his freedwoman, specifying dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04600054.translation: Lucius Virdius Chius made this while alive for himself and for Virdia Chiae.
EDCS-04600054.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Lucius Virdius Chius for himself and Virdia Chiae.

EDCS-04600057.summary: This inscription likely records the name of a freedwoman, possibly as part of a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-04600058.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Potamilla, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04600059.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records names, possibly including Prima and a son of Lucius.

EDCS-04600069.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its content, but it appears to contain personal names and possibly titles, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04600137.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication to the Bona Dea, possibly by a woman named Ursa, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04600140.summary: This funerary inscription records Sabina dedicating a monument to Marcus Secundinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04600142.translation: Sacred to Fontus. Poblicius Statutus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04600142.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Fontus by Poblicius Statutus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04600144.text_edition: \n Herculi Augusto sacrum Caius Curius Quintianus Opiterginus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-04600144.translation: Caius Curius Quintianus Opiterginus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Augustus Hercules.
EDCS-04600144.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Hercules Augustus by Caius Curius Quintianus Opiterginus.

EDCS-04600146.translation: Gaius Sacconius Varro, tribune of the first cohort of Dalmatians, fulfilled his vow to Imperial Hope.
EDCS-04600146.summary: This votive inscription records Gaius Sacconius Varro, a military officer, fulfilling a vow to the personified deity of Imperial Hope, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04600148.translation: Caius Magius Secundus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04600148.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Magius Secundus.

EDCS-04600149.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Plinius Faustinus, likely on a monument.

EDCS-04600152.translation: To Antonius Valentinus, princeps of the XIII Gemina legion, killed by brigands in the Julian Alps in a place called Scelerata, his son Antonius Valentinus, to his father.
EDCS-04600152.summary: This is a dedication by a son to his father, Antonius Valentinus, a centurion of the XIII Gemina legion, who was killed by brigands.

EDCS-04600153.translation: Titus Asinius, son of Lucius, father; Sessidena Maxuma, daughter of Caius, mother; Grata, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-04600153.summary: This inscription lists the parents of an individual, Titus Asinius, and his mother Sessidena Maxuma, and grandmother Grata.

EDCS-04600154.translation: Taroco Briscinius, son of Tropius, ordered this title to be placed for himself and commanded, by the decision of Rufa, daughter of Lucius Lucius, his daughter-in-law, at his own expense.
EDCS-04600154.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Taroco Briscinius for himself, indicating his wishes for his monument and its cost, with instructions given through his daughter-in-law Rufa.

EDCS-04600155.summary: This is a label identifying Gaius Mutilius Varus as a father, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04600157.translation: Caius Petedius Moderatus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04600157.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Petedius Moderatus.

EDCS-04600158.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Cohortali Lucius No miles legionis II adiutricis laetus libens merito votum solvit\n
EDCS-04600158.translation: Lucius, a soldier of the II Adiutrix legion, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Cohortalis.
EDCS-04600158.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius, a soldier of the II Adiutrix legion, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Cohortalis.

EDCS-04600160.translation: Valens, son of Tertius, here, aged 3 years.
EDCS-04600160.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valens, son of Tertius, stating his age at death.

EDCS-04600161.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Septimius, incomplete.

EDCS-04600162.translation: Voluminia Cerula, daughter of Lucius, aged 60 years.
EDCS-04600162.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Voluminia Cerula, stating her age at death.

EDCS-04600175.translation: Gaius Ninnius Alexander dedicated this gift to Jupiter Sabazius.
EDCS-04600175.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Jupiter Sabazius by Gaius Ninnius Alexander.

EDCS-04600178.translation: Dio, freedman of a woman named Arius, made this in his lifetime for himself and for Ammias, wife of Dio, freedwoman of a woman named Arius.
EDCS-04600178.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman for himself and his wife.

EDCS-04600181.translation: Marcus Caecilius Felix, freedman of Clymenus, and
EDCS-04600181.summary: This inscription begins a dedication or funerary notice for Marcus Caecilius Felix, freedman of Clymenus, but it is incomplete.

EDCS-04700001.translation: Publius Acilius Florus, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, prefect with the power of an aedile for administering justice, erected a statue of Equity.
EDCS-04700001.summary: This is a dedication by Publius Acilius Florus, a magistrate, of a statue of Equity, likely in a public space.

EDCS-04700003.translation: Gaius Popilius Cultor willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Father Dis.
EDCS-04700003.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Father Dis by Gaius Popilius Cultor.

EDCS-04700004.translation: Marcus Rustius Theomnestus, in fulfillment of his vow, to Father Dis.
EDCS-04700004.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Father Dis by Marcus Rustius Theomnestus.

EDCS-04700005.translation: Marcus Cornelius Alexander, quinquennial magistrate, to the genius of the college of dendrophoroi (tree-bearers).
EDCS-04700005.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Marcus Cornelius Alexander, a quinquennial magistrate, to the genius of the dendrophoroi college.

EDCS-04700006.translation: Plasidienus Primigenius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Juno.
EDCS-04700006.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Juno by Plasidienus Primigenius.

EDCS-04700008.translation: Sextus Magius Primus [dedicates this] to Jupiter.
EDCS-04700008.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Sextus Magius Primus.

EDCS-04700010.translation: Marcus Quinctius, son of Fabia Runcus, formerly prefect of the engineers, as duovir, saw to the restoration of the entrance and the temple of Mercury at a cost of 150,000 sesterces.
EDCS-04700010.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the entrance and temple of Mercury by Marcus Quinctius, a former prefect of the engineers and duovir, funded by 150,000 sesterces.

EDCS-04700011.translation: Cingenus Sabellus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-04700011.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Cingenus Sabellus.

EDCS-04700013.translation: Sacred to Minerva. Quintus Romanius, son of Camburo, adorned the altar and temple with plasterwork, in fulfillment of his undertaken vow.
EDCS-04700013.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating an altar and temple to Minerva, adorned with plasterwork by Quintus Romanius.

EDCS-04700014.translation: Sacred to Augusta Nemesis. Iuventia Stephane, in fulfillment of her vow.
EDCS-04700014.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Augusta Nemesis by Iuventia Stephane.

EDCS-04700015.translation: Valerius Hermes willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Priapus.
EDCS-04700015.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Priapus by Valerius Hermes.

EDCS-04700016.translation: To Sol Invictus, from a vow, Sextus Dugius Valentio, one of the six public priests of the Augustan cult.
EDCS-04700016.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Sol Invictus by Sextus Dugius Valentio, a member of the VI viri Augustales.

EDCS-04700017.translation: Marcus Ulpius Valens Vagada willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Vergusta.
EDCS-04700017.summary: This inscription records Marcus Ulpius Valens Vagada fulfilling a vow to Vergusta.

EDCS-04700018.translation: To the Augustan Victory, Publicius Eutychius, the temple attendant, from a vow.
EDCS-04700018.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Victoria Augusta by the temple attendant Publicius Eutychius.

EDCS-04700019.translation: Caius A Callistianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04700019.summary: This inscription records Caius A Callistianus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04700021.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Vespasiano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate -- imperatori XIII patri patriae consuli V designato VI censori Quintus Cornelius Quinti filius Fabia Placidus aedilis quaestor testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-04700021.translation: Quintus Cornelius Placidus, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, as aedile and quaestor, ordered this to be made by his will for Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, chief priest, in his thirteenth tribunician power, father of his country, consul elect for the sixth time, censor.
EDCS-04700021.summary: This inscription records a testamentary dedication by a magistrate to Emperor Vespasian.

EDCS-04700028.translation: Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus [dedicated this to] the most excellent prince, Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius, conqueror of the Germans and Sarmatians, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, [and to] Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of the Sarmatians and Germans, greatest conqueror of the Britons, chief priest, in his fourteenth tribunician power, emperor for the eighth time, consul for the fifth time, father of his country.
EDCS-04700028.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus to Emperor Commodus, listing his extensive titles and honors.

EDCS-04700030.text_edition: \n Caio Hostilio Maximo Ro quaestori privinciae aedili Ceriali provincia[e ------\n
EDCS-04700030.translation: To Gaius Hostilius Maximus, quaestor of the province, aedile, [and] Cerialis, of the province [---].
EDCS-04700030.summary: This is a fragmented inscription possibly related to provincial administration and dedication.

EDCS-04700031.translation: Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus and Manlius Carbo to their father Marcus Nonius Macrinus, son of Marcus, of the Fabian tribe, consul.
EDCS-04700031.summary: This is a dedication from sons to their deceased father, Marcus Nonius Macrinus, who held the consulship.

EDCS-04700035.text_edition: \n Titus Marcius Omuncio veteranus legionis IIII Flaviae felicis testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-04700035.translation: Titus Marcius Omuncio, a veteran of the IV Flavia Felix legion, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-04700035.summary: This inscription records a testamentary dedication by a veteran of the IV Flavia Felix legion.

EDCS-04700036.text_edition: \n Lucius Nutrius Cai filius Gallus sibi et Cominiae Secundae nutrici suae et Caio Nutrio Cai filio Gallo militi legionis VII Hispanae et Secundo liberto et Primigenio liberto et Tertio et Venustae testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-04700036.translation: Lucius Nutrius Gallus, son of Caius, ordered this to be made by his will for himself, for Cominia Secunda, his nurse, for Caius Nutrius Gallus, son of Caius, a soldier of the VII Hispana legion, for Secundus, his freedman, for Primigenius, his freedman, and for Tertius and Venusta.
EDCS-04700036.summary: This inscription records a testamentary dedication by Lucius Nutrius Gallus for himself and several family members, including his nurse, a soldier, freedmen, and others.

EDCS-04700037.translation: Marcus Valerius Crassus, son of Marcus, pontifex, duovir, military tribune.
EDCS-04700037.summary: This inscription lists the offices held by Marcus Valerius Crassus, including pontifex, duovir, and military tribune.

EDCS-04700038.translation: [---] to Caius Valens, son of I-, brother, military tribune of the same legion, prefect of a cohort, [---] to Tius, son of Caius, [---] to Fusculus, son [---] I I.
EDCS-04700038.summary: This inscription is fragmented and appears to list familial relationships and military titles of several individuals, possibly as part of a larger dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-04700039.translation: Vinnaius Silvinus, a veteran, formerly a centurion of the Legio XIIII Gemina, who served for 32 years.
EDCS-04700039.summary: This inscription records the service of Vinnaius Silvinus, a veteran centurion of Legio XIIII Gemina, detailing his 32 years of service.

EDCS-04700040.translation: Caius, son of Tius, son of Lucius, of the Maecia tribe; Caius, son of Pollia; Publius Tarquitius, son of Titius, of the Pollia tribe; Caius Lepidius, son of Marcus, of the Claudia tribe; Lucius, son of Marcus, of the Falerna tribe.
EDCS-04700040.summary: This is a list of names with their patronymics and tribal affiliations, likely related to citizenship or senatorial rolls, or possibly a collegium.

EDCS-04700041.translation: Living, Caius Antonius Agilis, freedman of Caius, a member of the VI viri Augustales, made this for himself and for Cornelia Tertia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-04700041.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription made by Caius Antonius Agilis, a freedman and Augustalis, for himself and his wife Cornelia Tertia.

EDCS-04700042.translation: For Publius Balbillius, son of Lucius, of the Publilia tribe, Poblicola, one of the six Augustales priests, and for himself, and for Pompeia Aucta, his companion, and for Marcus Nonius Tertius, a dyer, and for Balbillia, daughter of Publius, and for Meroe, a domestic slave.
EDCS-04700042.summary: This inscription records funerary dedications made by Pompeia Aucta for her husband Publius Balbillius and other individuals, likely on a tomb or altar.

EDCS-04700043.translation: To Honor: Lucius Falto Primus, to the best of young men, from Marcus Calpurnius Acilianus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, praefect with aedilic power.
EDCS-04700043.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Honor by Lucius Falto Primus for Marcus Calpurnius Acilianus, a magistrate, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-04700045.translation: For Lucius Cornelius Glyco, one of the six Augustales priests of Brixia, Claudia Martia [dedicates this] to her most devoted husband.
EDCS-04700045.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Claudia Martia for her husband Lucius Cornelius Glyco, an Augustalis priest in Brixia.

EDCS-04700046.translation: Sextus Epidius Senecio, son of Marcus, one of the six Augustales priests, for himself and for Cassia Calibe, his companion, and for Marcus Epidius, son of Publius, his father, and for Lucilia Maxima, his mother, and for Congonnetia Urbana, his companion.
EDCS-04700046.summary: This inscription is a self-dedication and funerary dedication by Sextus Epidius Senecio, an Augustalis priest, for himself and his family members, including parents and companions.

EDCS-04700048.translation: Sextus Helvius Anthimus, one of the six Augustales priests, made [this] while alive for himself and for Helvia Helpidi, his dearest wife, and for his most dutiful children, Sextus Helvius Classicus, Sextus Helvius Classiciano, and Helvia Rufina.
EDCS-04700048.summary: This is a living funerary dedication by Sextus Helvius Anthimus, an Augustalis priest, for himself and his family, including his wife and children.

EDCS-04700049.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Asiaticus: Caius Pladicius Zoticus, one of the six Augustales priests, a grieving father, [dedicates this] to his dearest son, and for himself, and for Caius Pladicius Augendus, his son, and for Cornelia Brixiana, his wife, and [others...].
EDCS-04700049.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Caius Pladicius Zoticus, an Augustalis priest and grieving father, for his son Lucius Cornelius Asiaticus and other family members.

EDCS-04700050.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed: Postumia Delphis [dedicates this] to her most beloved husband, Publius Postumius Trophimus, one of the six Augustales priests of Brixia.
EDCS-04700050.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Postumia Delphis to her husband Publius Postumius Trophimus, an Augustalis priest in Brixia.

EDCS-04700051.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed: Flavia Afrodisia [dedicates this] to her deserving husband, Quintus Publicius Priscianus, one of the six Augustales priests.
EDCS-04700051.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Flavia Afrodisia to her husband Quintus Publicius Priscianus, an Augustalis priest.

EDCS-04700052.translation: For Lucius Quinctius Ursus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, twice a priest and pontiff.
EDCS-04700052.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Quinctius Ursus, a local magistrate and priest, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04700053.translation: Marcus Suricius Epagathus, one of the six Augustales priests, [dedicated this] for himself and for Acutia Accepta, and for the beloved freedmen and freedwomen of Heros Ingenuus.
EDCS-04700053.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Suricius Epagathus, an Augustalis priest, for himself, Acutia Accepta, and freedpersons.

EDCS-04700054.translation: To Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus, maternal grandfather.
EDCS-04700054.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Valerius, identified by his patronymic and his role as maternal grandfather, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-04700055.translation: To Lucius Valerius Catullus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04700055.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Valerius Catullus, honored by the town council (decurions), probably in a provincial context.

EDCS-04700056.translation: Optatus, freedman of Publius Vettius Benignus, a Six-time (IIIIII) official, [erected this].
EDCS-04700056.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription set up by a freedman, Optatus, for his former master, Publius Vettius Benignus, who held a high office.

EDCS-04700057.translation: The guild of public criers, by decree of the decurions, [granted this] honorific title to Lucius Vettius Pinna, Six-time (VI) Augustal official, free of charge; Pinna used the title.
EDCS-04700057.summary: This inscription records an honor granted by the guild of public criers and the town council to Lucius Vettius Pinna, an Augustal official, recognizing his service.

EDCS-04700061.translation: Lucius Cornelius Labeo, son of Lucius, a comb-maker, made this while alive for himself, and for his wife Antistia Tertia, daughter of Publius, and for his mother Clienta.
EDCS-04700061.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Cornelius Labeo, a comb-maker, for himself and his wife and mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700062.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Marinus, the painter, and [dedicated to] the rose for eternity, by the guild of blanket-makers.
EDCS-04700062.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the guild of blanket-makers to Lucius Cornelius Marinus, a painter, possibly associated with a cult or a funerary context.

EDCS-04700063.translation: I, Marcus Hostilius Dicaeus, came into this citizenship when I was 14 years old, in which household I came; I changed neither household nor master except this eternal one. I lived 70 years. No one summoned me to court, no one summoned me to judgment. You who stand and read, if this is not the best [life], teach me what is better. Clodia Paullina gave the place.
EDCS-04700063.summary: This is a self-written epitaph of Marcus Hostilius Dicaeus, who reflects on his life, citizenship, and peaceful death, with the burial place provided by Clodia Paullina.

EDCS-04700064.translation: To Smaragdus, the Murmillo gladiator, a free man, and to Tiche, his wife.
EDCS-04700064.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Smaragdus, a Murmillo gladiator, and his wife Tiche.

EDCS-04700065.translation: Quintus [set this up] for Varia, his comrade-in-arms (contubernalis).
EDCS-04700065.summary: This is a dedication by Quintus to Varia, his contubernalis, likely indicating a military or domestic partnership.

EDCS-04700066.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Magnus Valerius [set this up] for Aemilia Eutychia, his dearest wife, and for himself.
EDCS-04700066.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Magnus Valerius for his wife Aemilia Eutychia and himself, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-04700067.translation: Gaius... Gaius Aequus Marcus Gavius Va[lentinus?]
EDCS-04700067.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly for a member of the Gavius family, with the name Marcus Gavius Va[lentinus?].

EDCS-04700069.translation: Antonius, son of Lucius, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his daughter I(?) ES, and for the freedman Titus.
EDCS-04700069.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing that Antonius, son of Lucius, commissioned this monument for himself, his daughter, and a freedman in his will.

EDCS-04700070.translation: ...ni and for himself and for Antoninus the true...
EDCS-04700070.summary: This fragment of an inscription likely records a dedication for two individuals, one possibly named Antoninus.

EDCS-04700071.translation: ...us, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for Arria Laodicia E TO[nus?]
EDCS-04700071.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a freedman of Lucius for himself and for Arria Laodicia.

EDCS-04700072.translation: Attia Augusta set up this memorial for Aurelius Victorinus, her most beloved husband, who lived about 40 years and with me 13 years, 9 months, 15 days.
EDCS-04700072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Attia Augusta for her husband Aurelius Victorinus, providing details of his age and the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-04700073.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Publius Atilius Eutyches set this up for Bittia Valeria, his most devoted wife, and for himself, with whom I lived 22 years.
EDCS-04700073.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Publius Atilius Eutyches for his wife Bittia Valeria and himself, mentioning the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-04700074.translation: Biveia Prima made this for herself and for Biveius Bassinus, her most devoted brother, and for Titus Biveius Severianus, her brother, who lived 24 years, 3 months, 17 days.
EDCS-04700074.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Biveia Prima dedicates a monument for herself and her brothers Biveius Bassinus and Titus Biveius Severianus.

EDCS-04700075.translation: Gaius Caesius Faustus, freedman of Gaius, ordered this to be made in his will for himself, and for his son Gaius Caesius Nothus, and for his patron Gaius Caesius, son of Gaius, and for Valeria Galla, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Lucius Cornelius Eleutherus.
EDCS-04700075.summary: This inscription details a posthumous commission for a funerary monument by Gaius Caesius Faustus for himself and several family members and associates.

EDCS-04700076.translation: Calventia Nobilis, freedwoman of Lucius Calventius Firmus, [dedicated this] for herself, and for her son Lucius Calventius Legativus, and for Publius Papirius Optatus, father [of?], freedman of Publius, and for Papiria Prima, freedwoman of Publius, mother [of?], and for Papiria Satulla, sister, and for Publius Papirius Aequalis, [and for?] her brothers.
EDCS-04700076.summary: This funerary inscription lists dedications by Calventia Nobilis for herself, her son, her freedman father, her freedman father's wife, her sister, and her brothers.

EDCS-04700077.translation: Calventia Verecunda made this tomb forever for her daughter Maximilla, previously of tiles but now of everlasting stone; we acknowledge that she lived 27 years, 3 months, 12 days; for her worthy husband, for whom she wrote this, with whom she lived 5 years, 4 months, 9 days; and her daughter lived 2 years, 5 months, 16 days. What she endured for the love of her husband she built as a memorial of her name for her daughter, who suffered a similar fate.
EDCS-04700077.summary: This epitaph by Calventia Verecunda commemorates her daughter Maximilla and husband, detailing their lifespans and the circumstances of their deaths, emphasizing love and shared grief.

EDCS-04700078.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Publius Cervonius Chryseros [dedicated this] for himself and...
EDCS-04700078.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Publius Cervonius Chryseros, likely for himself and at least one other person.

EDCS-04700080.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of Cleopatra, specifying its frontal dimensions.

EDCS-04700081.translation: Quintus Cornelius Sanuacus, freedman of Quintus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his fellow freedman Quintus Cornelius Secundus.
EDCS-04700081.summary: This is a funerary commission by Quintus Cornelius Sanuacus for himself and his fellow freedman, Quintus Cornelius Secundus.

EDCS-04700082.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Cornelia Laodice. Cnaeus Cornelius Heracleon and Cornelia Galene, parents, and likewise to the spirits of the underworld, for Cornelia Galene, [his] mother.
EDCS-04700082.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Cornelia Laodice and her mother Cornelia Galene, dedicated by Cnaeus Cornelius Heracleon and Cornelia Galene.

EDCS-04700084.summary: This fragmented inscription refers to a person named uricio, son of Credo, likely in a funerary context.

EDCS-04700085.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription recording the age of death for Crispinus.

EDCS-04700088.translation: For Favilla, 15 feet in front, in the field 30 feet.
EDCS-04700088.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Favilla.

EDCS-04700089.translation: Burial place of Publius G T, 35 feet in front, 40 feet in the field.
EDCS-04700089.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot of Publius G T, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-04700090.translation: To Gesatia Trophime, dearest wife, and to Gesatia Chresime, her most dutiful sister, and for himself.
EDCS-04700090.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a man for his wife Gesatia Trophime, her sister Gesatia Chresime, and himself.

EDCS-04700093.translation: Caius Iulius Merkator made [this] while alive for himself, and for his father Proclus, and for his wife Allia Biblidis.
EDCS-04700093.summary: This is a funerary commission by Caius Iulius Merkator for himself, his father Proclus, and his wife Allia Biblidis.

EDCS-04700095.translation: To Iunius Quietus, son of Titus Publicius Pardalus.
EDCS-04700095.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Iunius Quietus, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04700096.translation: Laevia Prima, daughter of Spurius, made this for herself and for Flavia Severa, daughter of Titus, and for Publius Herennius Botryo, and.
EDCS-04700096.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by Laevia Prima for herself and other named individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700097.translation: Marcus Licinius Iucundus, freedman of Marcus, made this for himself and his parents, and you in the field, 10 feet.
EDCS-04700097.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman for himself and his parents, specifying dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700098.translation: Lucilia Polla, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made by her will for herself and for Marcus Murrius Saturio, son of Murrius. In front 5 feet, in the field 8 feet.
EDCS-04700098.summary: This funerary epitaph records a testamentary dedication with dimensions of the plot, likely for Lucilia Polla and Marcus Murrius Saturio.

EDCS-04700099.translation: Marcus Lusius Scaeva, freedman of Marcus, made this for himself and his wife Cornelia Secunda, and for his son Rufus, and for his daughter Proba, in front 25 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-04700099.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument with specified dimensions, set up by Marcus Lusius Scaeva for his family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700102.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Augustina to her dearest husband Maesius Vericundus.
EDCS-04700102.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Maesius Vericundus by his wife Augustina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700103.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Marcellinus.
EDCS-04700103.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Marcellinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700104.summary: This is a personal inscription, likely a tombstone or memorial, identifying Aemilius Marcellus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-04700105.translation: Marcellus, son of Spurius, to his sister Bitulla.
EDCS-04700105.summary: This inscription records a dedication from Marcellus, son of Spurius, to his sister Bitulla, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04700109.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Caius Mefanas Crispinianus to his dearest sister Mefanatia Cornificia and.
EDCS-04700109.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Mefanas Crispinianus to his sister Mefanatia Cornificia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700111.translation: To Panthaga tus, [son of] Caius Terentius Bassus, [and freedman] of Mefanas Etruscus.
EDCS-04700111.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Panthaga tus, identifying his father and patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700112.translation: and to Publius Papirius Vicarius, son of Publius, his brother.
EDCS-04700112.summary: This is an epitaph recording a familial relationship and possibly a bequest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700113.translation: To the divine shades. Quintianus placed this for Parthenope, his dearest fellow freedwoman, who deserved well.
EDCS-04700113.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a freedman for his fellow freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700115.translation: Lucius Petronius Secundus made this while alive for himself, and for his dearest wife Vigilia Nigrina, and for his father Lucius Petronius Primus, and for his mother Petronia Primula.
EDCS-04700115.summary: This is a funerary monument intended for the dedicator, his wife, and his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700116.translation: Pisti Quinti, 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-04700116.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a plot of land or a grave, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700117.translation: Pisti Quinti, 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-04700117.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a plot of land or a grave, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700118.translation: Lucius Plautius Princeps, son of Lucius, his freedman, ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for Caesiae Fusca, daughter of Titus, his fellow slave.
EDCS-04700118.summary: This is a funerary inscription mandated by will, for the deceased and his partner, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700120.translation: under the supervision of Publius Popillius Valens.
EDCS-04700120.summary: This phrase likely refers to the person who oversaw the construction or dedication of a monument, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700121.translation: Gaius Postumius Thrasulus, son of Gaius, his freedman, and Postumia Sponsa, daughter of Gaius, his fellow slave.
EDCS-04700121.summary: This is an epitaph naming two individuals, likely a couple who were freedmen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700126.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04700126.text_edition: \n Publiciae Afrodite Publicia Valeriana matri carissimae mensam de suo fecit\n
EDCS-04700126.translation: Publicia Valeriana made this table from her own means for her most beloved mother, Publicia Aphrodite.
EDCS-04700126.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Publicia Valeriana for her mother, Publicia Aphrodite, likely a funerary or votive offering.

EDCS-04700129.translation: To the divine shades. Quintus Samillus Valerianus and Valeria Magia for their most dutiful son, Quintus Samillus, son of Quintus, [buried here?] who lived 22 years, 4 days. And Primus.
EDCS-04700129.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a young man by his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700131.translation: Syncleticus who lived 4 years, 11 months, 15 days, [and?] Syncletice.
EDCS-04700131.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Syncleticus and another individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04700133.summary: This inscription records the name Tapponia Synois, likely a person's name or a dedication.

EDCS-04700134.translation: Amphio, freedman of Lucius Terentius, and Rustica, freedwoman of Terentia.
EDCS-04700134.summary: This inscription records the names of two freedmen, Amphio and Rustica, possibly indicating a familial or social connection.

EDCS-04700135.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of an individual named Tertiae, son of Chilo, identified as Artanius.

EDCS-04700136.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Thallusae, referring to her freedmen.

EDCS-04700137.summary: This inscription records the name Titia Saturnina, identified as the wife of Iuventus.

EDCS-04700141.translation: To the divine spirits of Valerius Aprilis Maximus. Valerius Aprilis Maximus and Valeria Senecia to their dearest father.
EDCS-04700141.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Valerius Aprilis Maximus and Valeria Senecia for their father, Valerius Aprilis Maximus.

EDCS-04700142.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Valerius Blandus, likely identifying an individual.

EDCS-04700143.translation: To the divine spirits. Valeria Maxima and Severus Omo set this up for their most beloved daughter, Valerius Felicianus.
EDCS-04700143.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Valeria Maxima and Severus Omo for their dearly loved daughter, Valerius Felicianus.

EDCS-04700144.translation: Lucius Valerius Rusticio made this tomb for himself and his excellent wife Birria Secunda, 10 feet in front and 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-04700144.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Lucius Valerius Rusticio for himself and his wife Birria Secunda, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-04700145.translation: Aulus Vetilius Symphoniacus, son of Publius, made this memorial for his wife Fullonia, freedwoman of a woman, while he was alive.
EDCS-04700145.summary: This is a memorial erected by Aulus Vetilius Symphoniacus for his wife Fullonia, a freedwoman, during his lifetime.

EDCS-04700213.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Cinna as the son of Marcus.

EDCS-04700220.translation: Theodorus and Marta with their family made 17 feet. Liberius and Pientia with their family made 17 feet with their family made 17 feet.
EDCS-04700220.summary: This inscription records the construction of 17 feet by two groups of people, Theodorus and Marta, and Liberius and Pientia.

EDCS-04700222.translation: Brothers, contrary to their vows, erected this memorial to Aurelius Primillion, their dearest father, who lived X years, VII months, and [some days], and to their son Aurelius Cemoni, who lived XXII years, III months, XXV days.
EDCS-04700222.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by brothers in memory of their father Aurelius Primillion and their son Aurelius Cemoni, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04700223.translation: Aurelius Macrinus and Irene, his freedwoman, erected this memorial to Plenia Storacia, their most beloved virgin, who lived with me XXV years, her most worthy patroness, who deserved well. She died on Wednesday, the day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-04700223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Plenia Storacia, dedicated by Aurelius Macrinus and Irene, possibly dating to the 3rd century CE based on naming conventions.

EDCS-04700227.translation: In the land [belonging to] Iusta Vera, 40 feet.
EDCS-04700227.summary: This inscription likely records a land boundary or measurement in the name of Iusta Vera.

EDCS-04700228.translation: Marcus Clodius, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, having held the aedilician power, prefect of the cohort of Cantabrians, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Scythica legion, prefect of a detachment of the V Macedonica legion, prefect of the engineers, duovir with judicial authority, pontiff, duovir for quinquennial review.
EDCS-04700228.summary: This is a comprehensive cursus honorum for Marcus Clodius, detailing his extensive career in military and civic roles, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04700229.translation: Gaius Postumius Marcellus and Lucius Fictorius.
EDCS-04700229.summary: This is a simple inscription naming two individuals, Gaius Postumius Marcellus and Lucius Fictorius.

EDCS-04700231.translation: A plot of land by permission from Titus Octavius Allifanus [and] Marcus Cornelius Placidus.
EDCS-04700231.summary: This inscription records a precarium, a form of land tenure granted by Titus Octavius Allifanus and Marcus Cornelius Placidus.

EDCS-04700232.translation: In the land [belonging to] Lucius V. Severus, 40 feet.
EDCS-04700232.summary: This inscription likely records a land boundary or measurement in the name of Lucius V. Severus.

EDCS-04700233.translation: Marcus Voconius, son of Marcus, Rufus, for himself and for Gaius Voconius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-04700233.summary: This is a dedication for a tomb or monument made by Marcus Voconius Rufus for himself and his relative Gaius Voconius.

EDCS-04700236.translation: To Severus, a Six-Man official of the Augustals, for himself and for his wife Mesavoni Cariassis, and for his son Secundus, and for his daughter Severa.
EDCS-04700236.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Severus for himself and his family, mentioning his role as a Six-Man official of the Augustals.

EDCS-04700237.translation: To Gaius Vibius Verdavus and Gaius Vibius, son of Caius, Gaius Vibius Secundus, to his father and grandfather and to his wife Prima.
EDCS-04700237.summary: This funerary inscription honors multiple family members, including a father, grandfather, and wife, erected by Gaius Vibius Secundus.

EDCS-04700239.translation: To the Divine Shades of Victorinus and of Gaius Gargilius Festus, the forest warden.
EDCS-04700239.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Victorinus and Gaius Gargilius Festus, who served as a forest warden.

EDCS-04700240.translation: To Quintus Petronius Veteranus, Six-Man official of the Augustals, and to Publius Valerius Alpinus, Six-Man official of the Augustals, by the guild of builders.
EDCS-04700240.summary: This inscription honors two Six-Man officials of the Augustals, Quintus Petronius Veteranus and Publius Valerius Alpinus, by the guild of builders.

EDCS-04700242.translation: To the Divine Shades, Claudia Corneliana, who, to honor her memory perpetually, granted to the villagers of Ariciacus the valley from the colony of Augusta Brixia, tax-free, so that on the days of roses, of the vintage, and of the parentalia, solemn observances are celebrated by all.
EDCS-04700242.summary: This funerary inscription records Claudia Corneliana's grant of tax-free land to the villagers of Ariciacus for perpetual remembrance and celebration of festivals.

EDCS-04700243.translation: Quintus Hortensius Dorus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04700243.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Hortensius Dorus, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-04700245.translation: Rufus, son of Acutius Comincilus, made this for the Iunones by order, willingly and deservedly paid.
EDCS-04700245.summary: This votive inscription, likely honoring the Iunones (goddesses), was made by Rufus, son of Acutius Comincilus, following an order.

EDCS-04700246.translation: To the August Iunones, Euelpistus, son of Marcus (I), paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04700246.summary: This votive inscription records Euelpistus, son of Marcus, fulfilling a vow to the August Iunones.

EDCS-04700247.translation: To the god Castor, from a vision, Sextus Sextius Epagathus.
EDCS-04700247.summary: This votive inscription records Sextus Sextius Epagathus dedicating a gift to the god Castor after a divine vision.

EDCS-04700249.summary: This is a dedication to Atilia Stastia.

EDCS-04700252.translation: Gaius Sulpicius, son of Gaius, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04700252.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Gaius Sulpicius ordered the monument to be erected via his will.

EDCS-04700253.translation: Gaius Acutius Iulius, son of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-04700253.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Gaius Acutius Iulius during his lifetime.

EDCS-04700254.translation: Acutia Egloge, freedwoman of Gaius, gladly paid her vow to the Junones as deserved.
EDCS-04700254.summary: This is a dedication to the Junones by a freedwoman named Egloge, likely a thank-offering.

EDCS-04700256.translation: Cornelius Firmus, quaestor of the river.
EDCS-04700256.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name and title of Cornelius Firmus, possibly related to a water or river official.

EDCS-04700261.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Petronia Achillia, referred to as 'mother'.

EDCS-04700262.translation: [He/She/It] ordered this to be made in [his/her/its] will for himself/herself/itself and Prima.
EDCS-04700262.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment indicating that a monument was ordered to be made in a will for the deceased and another person named Prima.

EDCS-04700264.translation: To Victor, freedman of [Name starting with IVI?], ASCA.
EDCS-04700264.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary marker, mentioning a freedman named Victor and a possible abbreviation 'ASCA'.

EDCS-04700266.translation: [He/She] made this for Atia, [his/her] wife, and [---].
EDCS-04700266.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment indicating that the monument was made by someone for his wife Atia and possibly others.

EDCS-04700270.translation: Of Quintus Rufus Fronto: 13 feet in front, 25 feet in the land.
EDCS-04700270.summary: This inscription records land measurements belonging to Quintus Rufus Fronto, likely defining property boundaries.

EDCS-04700272.translation: To Mercury, Germanus the freedman, with his family.
EDCS-04700272.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by a freedman named Germanus for himself and his family.

EDCS-04700273.translation: Of Marcus Romanus, twelve feet in front and twelve feet into the field.
EDCS-04700273.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker defining property limits.

EDCS-04700274.translation: To the Divine Shades. Nymphe and Trophime, freedwomen, made this for Marcus Numerius, son of Lucius, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-04700274.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Numerius, dedicated by his freedwomen Nymphe and Trophime.

EDCS-04700277.translation: Lucia Frontonia, daughter of Lucius, of the Voturia tribe, by her will ordered this to be made for Lucius Statius, son of Lucius, a former member of the six-man board and a former four-man official.
EDCS-04700277.summary: This epitaph records the posthumous commission of a monument by Lucia Frontonia for Lucius Statius, noting his civic roles.

EDCS-04700278.translation: To Nigiloni, mother; to Ateciana Severa, wife of Publius, daughter of Severus; to their son Severus, whom I buried at the age of 8.
EDCS-04700278.summary: This inscription is a fragmented epitaph for Nigiloni, Ateciana Severa, and their son Severus.

EDCS-04700279.summary: This inscription is a fragment likely naming a father and son, possibly part of a larger genealogical record.

EDCS-04700286.translation: Sacred to the Daemon. Lucius Tenainus gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04700286.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Lucius Tenainus to a household deity or spirit.

EDCS-04700288.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. Lucius Calpelc, son of Lucius.
EDCS-04700288.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Lucius Calpelc, son of Lucius.

EDCS-04700289.translation: To Medilavinus. Secundus, son of Enduibatasius, gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04700289.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Secundus, son of Enduibatasius, to the deity Medilavinus.

EDCS-04700290.translation: To Saturn. Gnaeus Domitius Saturninus gladly, happily, and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-04700290.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Gnaeus Domitius Saturninus to the god Saturn.

EDCS-04700291.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Crispinus, dearest husband, and for myself.
EDCS-04700291.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Crispinus, with the inscription also intended for the person who commissioned it.

EDCS-04700292.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a mother by Caius Luculenus.

EDCS-04700293.translation: Marcus Nonius Cornelianus, a man of the highest standing, gave 150,000 denarii to the college of boatmen of Brixia, so that from the interest, for the current year and for 18 years, 20 denarii each year should be provided by Publicia Pusinna and her daughter for annual distributions.
EDCS-04700293.summary: This inscription records a significant donation by Marcus Nonius Cornelianus to the boatmen's college in Brixia for annual distributions, with conditions set by Publicia Pusinna and her daughter.

EDCS-04700294.translation: Lucius Pontius Virianus made this for his most dutiful mother Viria Ursae, for himself and his family.
EDCS-04700294.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Pontius Virianus for his mother Viria Ursae and for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-04700296.translation: That they perform and attend the individual solemnities, and that three of our heirs attend the solemnities themselves; but if our aforesaid colleagues deem it necessary to do something less, then they shall repay the aforementioned entheca and interest to my heirs without delay. The members of the Pacatienses, we have spoken, we give thanks and willingly accept the condition offered by Ravius Mallucianus and Flavia Fausta his wife, from whom we received the aforementioned entheca. Let the aforementioned ria res be given in perpetuity, otherwise as stated above by all.
EDCS-04700296.summary: This inscription details the conditions for solemn rituals and the acceptance of an offer from Ravius Mallucianus and Flavia Fausta by a college, likely related to religious or civic duties.

EDCS-04700298.translation: Lucius Tinnavius Quartus and Lubiamus, his sons, arranged for this to be made for Lucius Tinnavius Robiae, a man of the highest standing in Brixia.
EDCS-04700298.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Lucius Tinnavius Quartus and his son for Lucius Tinnavius Robiae in Brixia.

EDCS-04700299.translation: To the divine spirits, in memory of Tychetus, Nonius Chresimus for his most beloved wife, well-deserving.
EDCS-04700299.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Nonius Chresimus to the memory of his wife Tychetus.

EDCS-04700300.translation: In memory of Ulpia Prima Ganicianae, Caius L P ex p for his most beloved wife and for himself, to the divine spirits.
EDCS-04700300.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Caius L P ex p to the memory of his wife Ulpia Prima Ganicianae and for himself.

EDCS-04700306.translation: Lucius Trebius Primus and Bitumus Sexti, son of Luppisi Mainialis, made this.
EDCS-04700306.summary: This inscription records the makers, Lucius Trebius Primus and Bitumus Sexti, son of Luppisi Mainialis, likely of a monument or structure.

EDCS-04700308.summary: This is a dedication to the god Saturn.

EDCS-04700309.translation: Cassius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, a veteran discharged from the VIII Augusta legion, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-04700309.summary: This inscription states that Cassius, a veteran of the VIII Augusta legion, ordered this monument to be erected in his will.

EDCS-04700311.translation: Valucius gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-04700311.summary: This is a dedication recording a vow paid to the god Hercules by Valucius.

EDCS-04700312.translation: Cullonius Nianus gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Augustus.
EDCS-04700312.summary: This is a dedication recording a vow paid to the emperor Augustus by Cullonius Nianus.

EDCS-04700313.translation: Sextus Blegina, tax-exempt soldier of Caesar...
EDCS-04700313.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records Sextus Blegina, a tax-exempt soldier serving under Caesar.

EDCS-04700314.translation: Marcus Ulpius Bellicus, a veteran of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion, made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-04700314.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a veteran of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion for himself and his family.

EDCS-04700316.translation: For Marcus Virius Receptus, a veteran of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion...
EDCS-04700316.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication or funerary text for Marcus Virius Receptus, a veteran of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion.

EDCS-04700317.translation: Festa, daughter of Dugiavissa Capito, and Lucius, son of Sextus, to his wife...
EDCS-04700317.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or funerary text for a wife, set up by Festa and Lucius.

EDCS-04700318.translation: Publius P. Firmus gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Brassenus.
EDCS-04700318.summary: This is a dedication recording a vow paid to Brassenus by Publius P. Firmus.

EDCS-04700319.translation: Lucretia Anapauma gladly and deservedly paid her vow to Aburnus and Aburna.
EDCS-04700319.summary: This is a dedication recording a vow paid to the deities Aburnus and Aburna by Lucretia Anapauma.

EDCS-04700320.translation: Lucius Lucretius Maior, freedman of Lucius, gladly and deservedly to Fortuna.
EDCS-04700320.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna by Lucius Lucretius Maior, a freedman.

EDCS-04700321.translation: Appia Prima, daughter of Titus, gladly and deservedly to Queen Isis.
EDCS-04700321.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Isis Regina by Appia Prima, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-04700323.summary: An altar dedicated to Isis by Lucius Cusonius.

EDCS-04700324.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Lucius G S, a jurar(ius), [dedicated this].
EDCS-04700324.summary: An altar dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius G S, possibly a jurar(ius) (a type of official or priest).

EDCS-04700325.translation: To Minerva, Vesbaedus son of Ambicius.
EDCS-04700325.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Minerva by Vesbaedus, son of Ambicius.

EDCS-04700327.text_edition: \n Votum libentes merito Diis Penatibus Publius Secundus et Valentina Albani\n
EDCS-04700327.translation: With willing heart and deservedly, Publius Secundus and Valentina Albani [dedicate this] to the Household Gods.
EDCS-04700327.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the Di Penates by Publius Secundus and Valentina Albani.

EDCS-04700329.translation: To Silvanus, Lucius Saeconius Zosimus and Lucius Saeconius Po[...], [dedicated this].
EDCS-04700329.summary: An inscription honoring Silvanus, with dedicants named Lucius Saeconius Zosimus and Lucius Saeconius Po[...].

EDCS-04700330.translation: Lucius Sextius Florentius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Silvanus for the well-being of the Silvanensian worshippers.
EDCS-04700330.summary: A votive inscription by Lucius Sextius Florentius to Silvanus, dedicated for the welfare of his worshippers.

EDCS-04700334.translation: Trophimus, his freedman, [dedicated this] to Lucius Teudicius Fronton, son of Lucius, II vir iure dicundo.
EDCS-04700334.summary: A dedication to Lucius Teudicius Fronton, who held the office of II vir iure dicundo, by his freedman Trophimus.

EDCS-04700335.translation: For the memory of Medi Crescens, the guilds of the 'fabri' and 'centonarii' [offer this] 10 feet.
EDCS-04700335.summary: A funerary inscription for Medi Crescens, commemorating a dedication of 10 feet by the guilds of artisans ('fabri') and 'centonarii' (possibly firemen or a similar guild).

EDCS-04700337.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the name of Munatius, son of Tiberius, likely a dedication.

EDCS-04700338.translation: To Munatius Fronton, husband of Frontonis Ponticia, [dedicated this].
EDCS-04700338.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Munatius Fronton, husband of Frontonis Ponticia.

EDCS-04700340.translation: For the memory of Marcus Numisius Primus and Numisia, his wife, the fab[...], [dedicated this].
EDCS-04700340.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Numisius Primus and his wife Numisia, possibly dedicated by a guild of 'fabri'.

EDCS-04700344.summary: A simple dedication by Lucius Saeconius Reburrus.

EDCS-04700366.translation: Secundus, son of Con, piously erected [this monument].
EDCS-04700366.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Secundus, son of Con, likely to a deity or for a public purpose.

EDCS-04700367.translation: Secundus, in fulfillment of his vow to Victor.
EDCS-04700367.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Secundus to a figure named Victor.

EDCS-04700375.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Valerio Maxentio Invicto et aeterno [Augusto ------\n
EDCS-04700375.translation: To our Lord Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Unconquered and Eternal Augustus.
EDCS-04700375.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument to Emperor Maxentius, likely dating to his reign (306-312 CE).

EDCS-04700377.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Bunnerus, identified as a potter, possibly on a tombstone or as a dedication of his work.

EDCS-04700381.translation: Quintus Sulgius Pollio, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe.
EDCS-04700381.summary: This inscription appears to be an official or personal designation, likely on a tombstone or a public record, for Quintus Sulgius Pollio.

EDCS-04700383.translation: Licinius, son of Quintus, gave [this] for himself and his guardianship.
EDCS-04700383.summary: This inscription records Licinius, son of Quintus, making a dedication or endowment related to his guardianship.

EDCS-04900328.translation: To the departed spirits. To [---]nco and Acerretina Thymele, parents, Lucius Acerretinus Verus, his son, made this.
EDCS-04900328.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Acerretinus Verus to his parents, Acerretina Thymele and another individual whose name is partially lost, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900329.translation: Fabia Serena, freedwoman of Aulus, made this while alive for Fabia Nymphe, her daughter, freedwoman of Aulus, aged 25.
EDCS-04900329.summary: A funerary dedication set up by Fabia Serena for her deceased daughter Fabia Nymphe, who died at age 25, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900330.summary: This inscription is likely a tombstone epitaph for Lucius Paulus, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-04900332.translation: The place of the monument of Lucius Minicius Fuscus, son of Lucius. In front, 18 feet; in the field, 32 feet.
EDCS-04900332.summary: A property marker defining the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Minicius Fuscus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900333.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-04900333.translation: To the departed spirits. For Martina, well-deserving, who lived 25 years, and Maurio her brother, who lived 35 years, [she] departed the day before the Ides of October, in faithful peace. Her grieving mother made this against her vow.
EDCS-04900333.summary: A funerary epitaph for Martina and her brother Maurio, set up by their mother, dating to before 312 CE (indicated by the mention of Maxentius in another inscription from the same find context).

EDCS-04900335.translation: To the goddesses of the crossroads (Triviis?). Caius Vardius, craftsman, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-04900335.summary: A dedication to a deity, likely a local or rural goddess, by Caius Vardius, a craftsman, who is fulfilling a vow, probably from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900336.translation: [...] Amandus, freedman of Augustus(?), fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly. To Belenos Aeternus.
EDCS-04900336.summary: A votive inscription to the Celtic god Belenos Aeternus, made by Amandus, possibly an imperial freedman, dating from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900339.summary: A very brief inscription simply listing the names of two physicians, Hagi and Ai.

EDCS-04900340.translation: For Publius Trosius Sextio, freedman of Salinator. Romanus, freedman, made this while alive for himself and his kin, his freedmen and freedwomen. The place of the monument: in front, 16 feet; in the field, 32 feet.
EDCS-04900340.summary: A funerary monument inscription set up by the freedman Romanus for himself and his household, also marking the plot size, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900345.translation: The place of the monument of Lucius V() M(). In front, 20 feet; in the field, [---] feet.
EDCS-04900345.summary: A property marker defining the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius V() M(), with the depth of the plot lost.

EDCS-04900346.translation: Publius Vaccius Malchio, freedman of Publius, a freedman, and Troia Aufidia, freedwoman, and Primus, freedman, and Hilara, freedwoman, made this [tomb] for their freedmen and freedwomen. It is 16 feet wide in front and 15 feet long inside. They made it while alive.
EDCS-04900346.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for freedmen and freedwomen, specifying the dimensions of the tomb, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04900347.translation: Flavius Amantius, a veteran of the third Italian legion, formerly an optio, made this while alive for himself and his dearest wife Sirica, who lived with me for 21 years and 20 days, and [for himself] 85 years without complaint.
EDCS-04900347.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a veteran soldier, Flavius Amantius, and his wife, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04900348.translation: To the Unconquered god Mithras, Gaius Iulius Saturninus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-04900348.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mithras by Gaius Iulius Saturninus on behalf of himself and his family, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04900349.translation: Marcus Petronius, son of Marcus, a quinquennial magistrate with judicial authority, first centurion, [died...]
EDCS-04900349.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph or dedication for Marcus Petronius, who held significant civic and military positions, dating possibly to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05000273.translation: Laetus and his freedwoman Clara, and their children Gratus and Grata.
EDCS-05000273.summary: This inscription lists family members, possibly on a tombstone, including Laetus, his freedwoman Clara, and their children.

EDCS-05000282.translation: Sacred to the gods and goddesses. Lucius Aebutius...
EDCS-05000282.summary: This inscription begins a dedication to the gods and goddesses, initiated by Lucius Aebutius.

EDCS-05000285.translation: To Barbia Syntychinus, a freedwoman. Marcus Tettius Felix, her companion, erected [this] and [for] Facili.
EDCS-05000285.summary: This inscription is a tombstone erected by Marcus Tettius Felix for his companion Barbia Syntychinus and another person, Facili.

EDCS-05000287.translation: ...for himself and his family. For his son Primigenius. For his son [...]rius. For [...] freedman of Titus?
EDCS-05000287.summary: This inscription appears to be a tombstone listing family members, including sons and possibly a freedman.

EDCS-05000289.translation: Sweet [daughter/wife?] departed on the day before in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-05000289.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman who died in Christian peace.

EDCS-05000292.translation: Titus Sulcanius Vitulus, freedman of Titus, a market official.
EDCS-05000292.summary: This is a short inscription identifying Titus Sulcanius Vitulus, a freedman and market official, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05000293.translation: Optata Fadia, daughter of Titus; Statia; Lucius Vallius Rufus, son of Lucius; Lucius Vallius Nam[---], freedman of Lucius; Marcus Vallius Mar[---], son of Lucius. [A plot of] 10 square feet.
EDCS-05000293.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to record a land division or property allocation, possibly for burial plots, involving members of the Vallius family, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05000300.translation: Silia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, made this for her father Gaius Silus, son of Gaius, her mother Titia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, and her brother Marcus Silus, son of Gaius. Lucius Sempronius, son of Lucius, donated the place.
EDCS-05000300.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Silia Secunda and her family, with the burial plot donated by Lucius Sempronius, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05000302.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that appears to be a dedication or funerary epitaph to someone named Tiberius Claudius Cotu[---].

EDCS-05000303.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning a Lucretia and her father-in-law, possibly a funerary or dedicatory text.

EDCS-05000304.translation: To the Genti Pescenniae, also to Petro[ni]ae Caetroniae [---]
EDCS-05000304.summary: This is a fragmented inscription dedicating something to members of the Pescennia and Petronia Caetronia families, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05000307.translation: Lucius Ticco, son of Marcus, and Repentinus Ticco, and Lucius Festus Ticco, and Novia Tertulla, daughter of Lucius, made this for Marcus Ticconius Marcellus, son of Marcus, and his sister Severa, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-05000307.summary: A family monument created by brothers and a sister for their brother and his sister-in-law.

EDCS-05000308.translation: Lucius Valerius Iucundus, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for his wife Corisia Secunda, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-05000308.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05000309.translation: Twenty-five feet in the field of Quintus Deci Felix and Lucius Minicius Alexsandrus: this place will not follow its heir.
EDCS-05000309.summary: This inscription records a property boundary marker, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period, indicating that the land does not pass to the heirs of the owners.

EDCS-05000322.translation: Firmus, ten feet in the field.
EDCS-05000322.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a boundary marker from the Roman period, identifying a plot of land of ten feet belonging to someone named Firmus.

EDCS-05000323.summary: A simple funerary dedication for Antuleia Campana.

EDCS-05000328.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Annia Basilissa made this for her son, Marcus Iuventius Annianus, who lived 25 years, 6 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-05000328.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased son.

EDCS-05000335.translation: To Minerva. Lucius Naevius Secundus [dedicated this].
EDCS-05000335.summary: A dedication to the goddess Minerva by Lucius Naevius Secundus.

EDCS-05000338.translation: To the departed spirits. To Rutumannus, a retiarius who fought twenty-three victorious battles, from his wife, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-05000338.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period for Rutumannus, a gladiator (retiarius), commemorating his undefeated record and acknowledging his wife's devotion.

EDCS-05000339.translation: Iustus lived 60 years, devoted always to Christ. Sentius lived. Iustus lived 8 years.
EDCS-05000339.summary: A Christian epitaph with confusing age notations, possibly for two individuals named Iustus.

EDCS-05000340.translation: Ponticus [bought this?] from the sons of Maccius. Vanius [is present/involved?].
EDCS-05000340.summary: An inscription possibly recording a property transaction involving Ponticus and Vanius related to the sons of Maccius.

EDCS-05100002.translation: Festus Titus and Valeria Tertulla, daughter of Publius, [dedicated this] to their most devoted fellow members of a society.
EDCS-05100002.summary: A dedication by Festus Titus and Valeria Tertulla to their fellow society members.

EDCS-05100003.translation: To the Holy Gods, to Hercules and the Junos. Lucius Valerius Severus and Clodia Corneliana gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow for Lucius Valerius Cornelianus.
EDCS-05100003.summary: A votive inscription by Lucius Valerius Severus and Clodia Corneliana for Lucius Valerius Cornelianus, dedicated to Hercules and the Junos.

EDCS-05100004.translation: Publius P. Dionysius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter.
EDCS-05100004.summary: This is a votive inscription from Publius P. Dionysius dedicated to Jupiter, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100005.translation: Quintus, son of Suricius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-05100005.summary: This is a votive inscription from Quintus, son of Suricius, dedicated to Minerva, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100006.translation: Publius Eppius Rufus, son of Publius, of the Fabia tribe, a soldier of the II Praetorian Cohort, ordered this to be made by his will, under the arbitration of [---].
EDCS-05100006.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription ordered by a soldier, Publius Eppius Rufus, of the II Praetorian Cohort, to be made after his death, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100007.translation: Suavius and his four sons, living, made this for their deceased kinsmen: Iamunus, son of Rufus, and Tertulla Stacassus, wife of Basius, and their sons Quartio and Sextus, soldiers of the XXI Rapax Legion.
EDCS-05100007.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription commissioned by Suavius and his sons for their deceased family members, including soldiers of the XXI Rapax Legion, likely from the late 1st century CE.

EDCS-05100008.translation: Sextus Calvisius Saturninus, while alive, made this for himself and for his deceased wife Calvisia Saturnina, and for his sons Calvisius Firmio and Valention, and their wives and grandchildren and great-grandchildren and [---].
EDCS-05100008.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription commissioned by Sextus Calvisius Saturninus for himself and his extended family, indicating his status and provisions for descendants, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100009.translation: Clodia Restituta gave this burial place to her most beloved daughter, Cassia Festa, who lived 34 years and 41 days, and to her most beloved husband Quintus Minucius Macer.
EDCS-05100009.summary: This is an epitaph and burial plot inscription from Clodia Restituta for her daughter Cassia Festa and husband Quintus Minucius Macer, detailing the daughter's lifespan, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100010.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lorenia Mercatilla, who lived 32 years and 2 months, and for her incomparable and well-deserving husband, Lorenius Nasiabius.
EDCS-05100010.summary: This is an epitaph for Lorenia Mercatilla and her husband Lorenius Nasiabius, mentioning their lifespans and marital devotion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100011.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lorenia Venusta, his most holy and incomparable wife, who lived 24 years and 9 months; her husband Gaudentius, for her well-deserving.
EDCS-05100011.summary: This is an epitaph for Lorenia Venusta, commissioned by her husband Gaudentius, detailing her lifespan and their marital devotion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100012.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Publius Aelius Philetus and Aelia Chresta; Publius Aelius Parthenopaeus and Publius Aelius Heracles [made this] for their most dutiful parents.
EDCS-05100012.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Publius Aelius Parthenopaeus and Publius Aelius Heracles for their parents, Publius Aelius Philetus and Aelia Chresta, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100013.translation: Marcus Nonius Macrinus consecrated this to the Preserving Gods for the safety of his Arria.
EDCS-05100013.summary: This is a dedication to the 'Conserving Gods' by Marcus Nonius Macrinus for the well-being of Arria, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100019.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Dubitatus, most distinguished, honored by many military offices, for his worthy and benevolent merit, and to his most distinguished and beloved son, Gaius Centullius Fortunatus, Marcus Aurelius Dubitatus, most distinguished, ordered this to be made.
EDCS-05100019.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Aurelius Dubitatus to his father and son, both named Marcus Aurelius Dubitatus, and his son Gaius Centullius Fortunatus.

EDCS-05100020.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Profuturus erected this for Severa, his deserving wife, and gave in her name to the Argenian family 600 sesterces, so that from its income, wreaths and funeral rites might be provided every year in perpetuity.
EDCS-05100020.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a bequest, where Profuturus dedicates a monument to his wife Severa and provides funds for her perpetual care.

EDCS-05100021.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, possibly naming the deceased Titus Caecias.

EDCS-05100024.translation: Revino, sacred. Publius P I fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05100024.summary: This is a votive inscription where Publius P I fulfills a vow to the deity Revino.

EDCS-05100025.translation: Titus Atestas Priscus, one of the six Augustan priests of Brixia, for himself and for Vera Primula, his dearest wife, and for his parents, Gaius Atestas Servandus and Gaius Atestas Securus, deserving of all honor.
EDCS-05100025.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Atestas Priscus, his wife, and his parents, with Titus serving as an Augustalis priest in Brixia.

EDCS-05100026.translation: Marcus Helvius Primus made this while alive for Marcus Helvius Ursio, his deserving father, an Augustan priest in Brixia, and for himself, and for Pontia Iusta, his dearest wife, and for his own departed family.
EDCS-05100026.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Marcus Helvius Primus for his father, himself, his wife, and deceased family members, identifying his father as an Augustalis priest in Brixia.

EDCS-05100027.translation: Titus Aurelius Carcenius for himself and for Necidia Severa, his sweetest wife, and for his parents, Titus Aurelius Severus and Laetilia Rufina, and for his departed family.
EDCS-05100027.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Titus Aurelius Carcenius for himself, his wife, parents, and deceased family.

EDCS-05100028.translation: Mango Clugasis, his son, for himself and for Cluidea Vosionis, his wife, and for Clugasion, his son. Farewell, all.
EDCS-05100028.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Mango Clugasis for himself, his wife, and his son.

EDCS-05100029.translation: Sasius Vesgasionis, his son, for himself and for Deica, daughter of Sextus, his wife, and for his sons Esdrio and Vesgasion.
EDCS-05100029.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Sasius Vesgasionis for himself, his wife, and his sons.

EDCS-05100030.translation: Triumus Celeris, his son, made this while alive for himself and for Duciava, daughter of Turi, his wife.
EDCS-05100030.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Triumus Celeris for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05100031.translation: Celer, son of Mando, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-05100031.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Celer, son of Mando, indicating he commissioned his own monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-05100032.translation: Tetumus, son of Sextus, and Dugiava, daughter of Sasadis.
EDCS-05100032.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple dedication or ownership marker, possibly from the Roman period, identifying two individuals, Tetumus and Dugiava, and their paternal lineage.

EDCS-05100033.translation: Messava, daughter of Sextus, made [this] while alive for herself and for her husband Staio, son of Secus, and for Secus, son of Staio.
EDCS-05100033.summary: This funerary inscription is for Messava, daughter of Sextus, dedicating the monument to herself, her husband, and her son.
