EDCS-05100034.translation: Iuricus, freedman of Triumo, by order of his patron.
EDCS-05100034.summary: This inscription records Iuricus, a freedman, acting on the instructions of his patron.

EDCS-05100036.translation: To Primio, son of Staius Arruntius, for himself and for his mother Dugiava, daughter of Sextus, and for his wife Atestatia, daughter of Arruntius, Atestatia Secunda, and for his daughter Atestatia Primula, and for Gaius Atestatius Quartio, VIvir of Brixia, and for his sons Gaius Atestatius Quintus and his own, and for his wife Dugiava. Viator, farewell, and you too.
EDCS-05100036.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Primio, son of Staius Arruntius, for himself and multiple family members, including his wife, mother, daughter, and sons, and mentioning a civic official.

EDCS-05100037.translation: To the divine shades. Petronia Primigenia placed [this] for her parents, Lucius Petronius Primio and Mennica Ciustica, daughter of Ciustus, his wife. And you.
EDCS-05100037.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Petronia Primigenia to her deceased parents, Lucius Petronius Primio and his wife Mennica Ciustica.

EDCS-05100038.translation: Esdricus Ambisasius gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05100038.summary: This inscription records Esdricus Ambisasius fulfilling a vow, likely a dedication at a shrine.

EDCS-05100039.translation: Tiberius Claudius, son of Caius, for himself and for his wife Tertulla, daughter of Sextus, and his own.
EDCS-05100039.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Tiberius Claudius, son of Caius, for himself and his wife and family.

EDCS-05100040.translation: [V]osis, son of Pontis, and [E]dassus(?) and his wife Cussae, daughter of Gassumi, and [Cl]uidia, daughter of Vosis, daughter of Edranus.
EDCS-05100040.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary dedication for multiple individuals, including Vosis, his wife, and his daughter.

EDCS-05100041.translation: To the shades. For Hviae, wife of Benacus, and for Marcus Cornelius Secundus, soldier of the legion XXI Rapax, deceased.
EDCS-05100041.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to a woman named Hviae and a soldier, Marcus Cornelius Secundus, of the legion XXI Rapax.

EDCS-05100042.translation: Firmus, son of Ingenuus, chief of the Sabini, for himself and for his wife Cornelia Rustica and for his son Marcus Cornelius Priscus, aged 13.
EDCS-05100042.summary: This funerary inscription is by Firmus, chief of the Sabini, for himself, his wife Cornelia Rustica, and their son Marcus Cornelius Priscus.

EDCS-05100043.translation: Mesa Manilia Severa for herself and her son, husband Maior, and her son, the soldier Aurelius Ursioni of the VIII Legion, her daughter Ursula, and her son Sextilius.
EDCS-05100043.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Mesa Manilia Severa for herself and various family members, including her husband, son, and daughter.

EDCS-05100045.translation: Marcus Mestrius Primus and Caecilia Valentina for Marcus Mestrius Severus, his father, VIvir Augustalis of Brixia, and his grandfather Primillonis Secundus, for himself and his mother.
EDCS-05100045.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Marcus Mestrius Primus and Caecilia Valentina for their father and grandfather, a prominent citizen of Brixia.

EDCS-05100048.translation: Ponticus, son of Caius Gemellus, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-05100048.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating something to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Ponticus.

EDCS-05100049.translation: To the Divine Manes of Voconia Ursula, Quintus Caecilius Secundinus for his wife.
EDCS-05100049.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Caecilius Secundinus dedicating a monument to his wife, Voconia Ursula.

EDCS-05100050.translation: Marcus Vetinius Assianus willingly fulfilled his vow to Mars.
EDCS-05100050.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Marcus Vetinius Assianus fulfilling a vow to Mars.

EDCS-05100051.translation: ...inium to Publius Aemilius Vocus, to Mars and Minerva.
EDCS-05100051.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mars and Minerva, likely part of a longer dedication.

EDCS-05100052.translation: Lucio Leuconio, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, veteran of the XXI Legion, lives on; Lucio Leuconio, son of Lucius, Firmus, lives on; Leuconia, daughter of Lucius, Procula, lives on; Allia, daughter of Lucius, Suavis, for her husband, children, and herself.
EDCS-05100052.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating multiple members of the Leuconia family, including a veteran, and dedicated by Allia.

EDCS-05100053.translation: Lucius Salvius, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe, standard-bearer of the veterans of the IIII Legion, for himself and Popilia Hispana, freedwoman of Titus, and for his son Capitoni, and his daughter Prisca, and his son Firmo.
EDCS-05100053.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Lucius Salvius, a veteran standard-bearer, for himself and his family members.

EDCS-05100054.translation: Marcus Laetilius Cassianus, of the Fabia tribe, prefect with aedilician power in Brixia, for himself and his mother Laetilia Primula, his wife Ratinia Ingenua, and his sons Marcus Laetilius Quintianus, Laetilii Firmina, and Severa.
EDCS-05100054.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Marcus Laetilius Cassianus, a local magistrate in Brixia, for himself and his family.

EDCS-05100055.translation: Publius Atinius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, rests here. If thirst delays you here, traveler, or if the arid land lessens your journey, read on, and when fate brings you back to your homeland, you may often say to your people that you saw in the lands of Italy the monument in which the body of Atinius is buried.
EDCS-05100055.summary: This funerary inscription is a poetic epitaph for Publius Atinius, encouraging travelers to read it and remember him, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05100056.translation: To Marcus Aemilius Naevianus, who lived 28 years, 7 months, and 10 days, Marcus Aemilius Valentinus [dedicates this] to his most obedient son and to himself.
EDCS-05100056.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a father to his deceased son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05100057.translation: To Lucius Clodius Strato and Clodia Secunda, Lucius Clodius Crescens [dedicates this] to his parents and to Laetilia Secunda, his wife, and...
EDCS-05100057.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Lucius Clodius Crescens to his parents and wife, suggesting a family monument.

EDCS-05100058.translation: To Quintus Clodius Festianus [dedicates this] to his parents-in-law, Spurii Primi Minci and Scutriniae Paternae, and to his brothers Valentio and Spurius Primus Paternus.
EDCS-05100058.summary: This epitaph records dedications made by Quintus Clodius Festianus to his in-laws and brothers, likely part of a family burial plot.

EDCS-05100059.translation: To the Genius of the Livian district.
EDCS-05100059.summary: This is a dedication to the local protective spirit (Genius) of a district named Livius.

EDCS-05100060.translation: To Staia Esdragassi, daughter of Vobenatus, prince of the Trumplini, prefect of the Trumplini cohort, under Gaius Vibius Pansa, legate pro praetore in the Vindolices, exempt from Caesar's taxes and for himself, Messava Veci, daughter of Vesi, his wife.
EDCS-05100060.summary: This inscription honors a Trumplinian leader and military official, likely dating to the early Roman Empire, with his wife also mentioned.

EDCS-05100061.translation: To the well-deserving Genius of the people of the Julian district, Quintus Publicius Abascantus [dedicates this].
EDCS-05100061.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of the Julian district by Quintus Publicius Abascantus, likely a freedman or local benefactor.

EDCS-05100062.translation: Strenuus, son of Brisia, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-05100062.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a payment of a vow to the god Mercury by Strenuus, son of Brisia.

EDCS-05100063.translation: Postumia Prisca willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Minerva.
EDCS-05100063.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a payment of a vow to the goddess Minerva by Postumia Prisca.

EDCS-05100065.translation: Philete, freedwoman of Publius, willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Victory.
EDCS-05100065.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a payment of a vow to the goddess Victory by Philete, a freedwoman.

EDCS-05100066.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Acutia Caesia [dedicates this] to her most excellent husband, L. Aprius, freedman of Marcus, and to herself.
EDCS-05100066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband and herself, dedicated to the Dis Manibus (spirits of the dead).

EDCS-05100067.translation: Crescentius and Paterna with their families made 100 feet. Crescentius and Crescentina with their families made 100 feet.
EDCS-05100067.summary: This inscription appears to record the construction of 100 feet (likely of a road or wall) by two family groups, with the names Crescentius and Paterna being prominent.

EDCS-05100068.translation: Melanalia Severa willingly and deservedly paid her vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-05100068.summary: This is a votive inscription by Melanalia Severa dedicated to the Nymphs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05100069.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Crassus Frugi and Lucius Calpurnius Piso, on the third day before the Nones of February. The citizenship of Themetra from Africa made a guest-friendship with Gaius Silius Aviola, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, and adopted him, his children, and their descendants as their patron for themselves, their children, and their descendants. Gaius Silius Aviola, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, received the citizenship of Themetra, their children, and their descendants into his protection and patronage, for himself, his children, and their descendants. The following acted as legates: Banno, son of Himilis, sufes; Azdrubal, son of Baisillecis; Iddibal, son of Bosiharis, legate.
EDCS-05100069.summary: This inscription, dated to 45 BCE, records the establishment of a guest-friendship and patronage relationship between the citizens of Themetra in Africa and Gaius Silius Aviola, with local officials acting as intermediaries.

EDCS-05100070.text_edition: \n Marco Crasso Frugi Lucio Pisone consulibus senatus populusque Thimiligensis hospitium fecerunt cum Caio Silio Cai filio Fabro Aviola praefecto fabrum eumque liberos posterosque eorum sibi liberis posterisque suis patronum cooptaverunt Caius Silius Aviola praefectus fabrum Thimiligenses universos sibi liberis posterisque suis suorumque in fidem clientelamque suam suorumque recepit egerunt legati Azrubal sufes Annobalis filius Agdibil Boncarth Iddibalis filius Risuil Anno Azrubalis filius Aucfiarzo Ammicaris filius Agdibil l Balithonis filius Sirni\n
EDCS-05100070.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Crassus Frugi and Lucius Piso, the senate and people of Thimiliges made a guest-friendship with Gaius Silius Fabrus Aviola, prefect of the engineers, and adopted him, his children, and their descendants as their patron for themselves, their children, and their descendants. Gaius Silius Aviola, prefect of the engineers, received all the people of Thimiliges into his protection and patronage, for himself, his children, his descendants, and his own people. The following acted as legates: Azrubal, son of Annobalis, sufes; Agdibil, son of Boncarth Iddibalis; Risuil, son of Anno Azrubalis; Aucfiarzo, son of Ammicaris; Agdibil, son of Balithonis; Sirni.
EDCS-05100070.summary: This inscription, likely from 45 BCE, documents a mutual agreement of guest-friendship and patronage between the people of Thimiliges and Gaius Silius Aviola, a Roman official, with local leaders acting as representatives.

EDCS-05100071.translation: Under the consulship of Lucius Silanus, the priest of Mars, and Gaius Vellaeus Tutor, on the day before the Nones of December, the community of Apisa Maius established a guest-friendship with Gaius Silicius, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, Aviola, military tribune of the Third Augustan Legion, prefect of the armorers, and they chose him, his children and descendants as their patron, for themselves, their children and descendants. Gaius Silicius, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, Aviola, military tribune of the Third Augustan Legion, prefect of the armorers, received Apisa Maius, their children and their descendants, for themselves, their children and descendants, into his protection and patronage. The delegates Hasdrubal, son of Iummo, Iader, son of Iummo, Hasdrubal, son of Hanno, Banno, Gabali, Chinisdo, the sufes, Aristo, son of Apo, Saepo, son of Chanaebo, acted.
EDCS-05100071.summary: This inscription records the establishment of a patron-client relationship between the community of Apisa Maius and Gaius Silicius Aviola, a Roman official, during the consulship of Silanus and Vellaeus Tutor, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05100072.translation: Under the consulship of Lucius Silanus, the priest of Mars, and Gaius Vellaeus Tutor, on the Nones of December, the senate and people of Siagita established a guest-friendship with Gaius Silicius, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, Aviola, military tribune of the Third Augustan Legion, prefect of the armorers, and they chose him and his descendants as their patron, for themselves and their descendants. Gaius Silicius, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, Aviola, received them and their descendants into his protection and patronage, with Celere, son of Imilcho, of Gulalsa, the sufes, acting.
EDCS-05100072.summary: This inscription documents a grant of hospitality and patronage from the community of Siagita to the Roman official Gaius Silicius Aviola, during the consulship of Silanus and Vellaeus Tutor, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05100073.translation: Gaius Mestrius, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, a veteran of the Twentieth Legion, ordered this to be made by his will. He also requested that it be made for Esdron Cangina, whom he had as a wife, while he was alive and she was alive.
EDCS-05100073.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, was commissioned by Gaius Mestrius, a veteran, in his will, to honor his wife Esdron Cangina, indicating a desire for a joint monument erected during their lifetimes.

EDCS-05100074.translation: Velia, daughter of Clado, made this for herself and for her husband Cariassus Bitionis, of the Gennanates, and Clado, son of Cariassus, and Bitio, son of Cariassus, placed this for their father.
EDCS-05100074.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Velia for herself and her husband Cariassus, and further dedicated by their sons Clado and Bitio for their father.

EDCS-05100075.translation: Niger, son of Salvius, ordered this to be made for himself and for his wife Esdron, daughter of Teudus.
EDCS-05100075.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Niger for himself and his wife Esdron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05100076.translation: Publius Valerius Myrinus to his friend Gaius Valerius Secundinus and Valeria Festa.
EDCS-05100076.summary: This is a dedication of friendship or memorial from Publius Valerius Myrinus to his friends Gaius Valerius Secundinus and Valeria Festa.

EDCS-05100077.translation: Sugassis, son of Cnaninus, made this while alive for himself, and for his wife Ierdia, daughter of Staius, and for his sons Sugasus and Staius, soldiers of the XXI Rapax Legion, deceased; I placed this tombstone for my sons, which my sons should have provided.
EDCS-05100077.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Sugassis for himself, his wife, and his two deceased sons who were soldiers in the XXI Rapax Legion, indicating he fulfilled their obligation.

EDCS-05100078.translation: Marcus Cornelius Sextus for himself and for his wife Marcia Firmina and for Quinto Lucius and Cornelia Secunda and for Tertius, son of Sextus, his father and for Cornelia Priscilla, his mother.
EDCS-05100078.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Marcus Cornelius Sextus for his immediate family, including his parents and wife, and possibly other relatives.

EDCS-05100079.translation: Huimenus, son of Lubiam, made this while alive for himself and for his brother Bitumus, son of Lubiam, and for his son Peino and for his wife Messava, daughter of Peino.
EDCS-05100079.summary: This funerary inscription was created by Huimenus for himself, his brother, his son, and his wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05100080.translation: Marcus Publicius Aphrodisius for himself and for his most excellent patron Marcus Publicius Onesimus.
EDCS-05100080.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Marcus Publicius Aphrodisius for himself and his patron, likely on a tomb or a dedicatory monument.

EDCS-05100081.translation: son for himself and for his sister Pono, and for his son Puvius, and for M...sae, 105 years old.
EDCS-05100081.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial, listing individuals and possibly an age, though incomplete.

EDCS-05100082.translation: Sextus Valerius Primus for Brasenno, willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-05100082.summary: This inscription records Sextus Valerius Primus making a willing dedication or fulfilling a vow to Brasenno.

EDCS-05100083.translation: Priscus, son of Sextus, for himself and for Pontia Tertulla, his wife.
EDCS-05100083.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, made by Priscus for himself and his wife, Pontia Tertulla.

EDCS-05100084.translation: Sextus Cornelius Primus willingly fulfilled his vow to Alantedoba, as deserved.
EDCS-05100084.summary: This inscription records Sextus Cornelius Primus fulfilling a vow to Alantedoba, possibly a deity or local spirit.

EDCS-05100085.translation: Caius Munatius Quirina Tiro, as chief magistrate exercising judicial power, and Caius Munatius Fronto, his son, gave this gift.
EDCS-05100085.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Caius Munatius Tiro, a local magistrate, and his son Caius Munatius Fronto, likely to a deity or public building.

EDCS-05100086.translation: Willingly to the gods and goddesses, as deserved, Caius Pladicius Reburrus, son of Celsus.
EDCS-05100086.summary: This inscription is a dedication to deities by Caius Pladicius Reburrus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-05100088.translation: Sacred to the Divine Springs. Marcus Antonius Stephon, son of Spurius, fulfilled his vow willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-05100088.summary: This inscription records Marcus Antonius Stephon fulfilling a vow to the Divine Springs, likely a sacred natural site.

EDCS-05100089.translation: To Isis Regina, Tiberius Claudius Hilarinus and his wife Valeria Prima willingly and joyfully fulfilled their vow, as deserved.
EDCS-05100089.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Claudius Hilarinus and his wife Valeria Prima fulfilling a vow to the goddess Isis Regina.

EDCS-05100092.translation: To Mercury, Lucius Saeconius Zosimus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05100092.summary: This inscription records Lucius Saeconius Zosimus fulfilling a vow to the god Mercury.

EDCS-05100093.translation: Lucius Sasius Rufus, son of Lucius, and his sons Sasi Valerianus and Rufinus, dedicated this to Mercury from their own money.
EDCS-05100093.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury made by Lucius Sasius Rufus and his sons.

EDCS-05100094.translation: Vinicia Tertia willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Mercury.
EDCS-05100094.summary: This inscription records Vinicia Tertia fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-05100095.translation: Sextus Evaristus, son of Seccius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Minerva for himself and his family.
EDCS-05100095.summary: This inscription records Sextus Evaristus fulfilling a vow to Minerva for his family.

EDCS-05100096.translation: Munatia Secunda willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Minerva.
EDCS-05100096.summary: This inscription records Munatia Secunda fulfilling a vow to Minerva.

EDCS-05100099.translation: Lucius Decius Tertius fulfilled his vow to Victoria.
EDCS-05100099.summary: This inscription records Lucius Decius Tertius fulfilling a vow to Victoria.

EDCS-05100100.translation: Aevius Martialis, priest of the deified Augustus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05100100.summary: This inscription records Aevius Martialis, priest of the deified Augustus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-05100101.translation: Cerialis, son of Plada, centurion of the Alpine cohort, restored the altar willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05100101.summary: This inscription records the restoration of an altar by Cerialis, a centurion.

EDCS-05100102.translation: Gaius Domitius Docilis and his brother Lucius Statius Secundus, a soldier of the VI Legion, willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vows.
EDCS-05100102.summary: This inscription records two soldiers, Gaius Domitius Docilis and Lucius Statius Secundus, fulfilling vows.

EDCS-05100107.translation: Gaius Pladicius Casdianus, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, who left money to the public of the Camunni in his will, ordered this to be placed. He served as duovir with judicial authority, aedile, quaestor, and prefect with judicial authority in Brixia, a judge from five decuries by public horse, prefect of the first cohort of Thracians, cavalry, and military tribune of the Tenth Legion Gemina Pia Felix.
EDCS-05100107.summary: This epitaph, from the Roman Imperial period, commemorates Gaius Pladicius Casdianus, detailing his extensive career in local magistracies and military service, and noting a testamentary bequest to the community of the Camunni.

EDCS-05100108.translation: Tresus, son of Endubronis, a recruit, ordered this to be made by testament, with the approval of his father Endubronis and his brothers Silon and Secundus.
EDCS-05100108.summary: This inscription records a testament by Tresus, son of Endubronis, instructing the construction of something.

EDCS-05100109.translation: Quintus Antistius Valens, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, duumvir for judging legal cases, and Gaius Antistius Fronto, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, [dedicated this] to Gaius Antistius Primus, son of Domitia and Quintus.
EDCS-05100109.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Antistius Valens and Gaius Antistius Fronto to Gaius Antistius Primus.

EDCS-05100110.translation: Gaius Claudius, son of Sasius, priest of Augustus, out of his own money, built the public tribunal and repaired the column.
EDCS-05100110.summary: This is a public building inscription from an unknown individual, Gaius Claudius, who funded the construction of a tribunal and the repair of a column.

EDCS-05100112.translation: To Gaius Clodius Valentus, son of Gaius, from the villagers of Grebiae.
EDCS-05100112.summary: This is a dedication from the villagers of Grebiae to Gaius Clodius Valentus.

EDCS-05100113.translation: Lucius Decius Quirina Primus, the aedile, made (this) for himself while alive, and for his sons, the decurions Lucius Decius Reburrus and Sextus Decius Primus, and for his wife Lessae Chloe.
EDCS-05100113.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription set up by Lucius Decius Quirina Primus for himself, his sons, and his wife.

EDCS-05100116.translation: To Rhea, daughter of Triumus, priestess of Caesar, and to Enna, daughter of Tresi, his wife.
EDCS-05100116.summary: This is a dedication from the Roman Imperial period honoring two individuals, Rhea, a priestess of Caesar, and her wife Enna, indicating a familial or religious connection.

EDCS-05100117.translation: Lucius Sasius Quirina Secundus, IIvir with jurisdiction, made (this) for his wife Rufia Tertia, incomparable, and for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-05100117.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Sasius Quirina Secundus, a magistrate, for his wife and himself and his family.

EDCS-05100118.translation: Publius Valerius Crispinus, a Flavial priest, (made this) for himself, and for his wife Sextia Secunda, daughter of Sextus, and for his son Publius Valerius Numisius.
EDCS-05100118.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription by Publius Valerius Crispinus, a priest, for himself, his wife, and his son.

EDCS-05100119.translation: to Quintus, son of [---], Quirina, IIvir with jurisdiction, friend.
EDCS-05100119.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to a man named Quintus, who held the office of IIvir with jurisdiction.

EDCS-05100123.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary marker, to Elipidus Frontosus.

EDCS-05100124.translation: Gaius Gavius Quirina Primus and Lucius Gavius Quirina Fronto (dedicated this) to their most dutiful parents, Secundus and Frontasia, daughter of Fronto.
EDCS-05100124.summary: This is a dedication by two sons, Gaius Gavius Primus and Lucius Gavius Fronto, to their parents, Secundus and Frontasia.

EDCS-05100125.translation: Sasius Quirina Quartus gave (this) from his own funds.
EDCS-05100125.summary: This is a dedication recording a gift made by Sasius Quirina Quartus from his own resources.

EDCS-05100126.translation: Lucius Statius Quirina Valens, son of Lucius, made (this) for himself and for his dearest son Lucius Statius Capito while alive.
EDCS-05100126.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription by Lucius Statius Quirina Valens for himself and his son, Lucius Statius Capito.

EDCS-05100127.translation: Ennus son of Iennius, and Vesgassis son of Gassis Biumi, and his son, [made this for] all their parents.
EDCS-05100127.summary: This inscription is a dedication to parents by their sons.

EDCS-05100131.translation: Sabinus, [made this for] the goddess One.
EDCS-05100131.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a goddess named One by Sabinus.

EDCS-05100133.translation: Sextus Nigidius Primus of the Fabia tribe, aedile and decurion of Brixia, restored the altar of Bergimus at his own expense, by decree of the decurions, upon the petition of the people.
EDCS-05100133.summary: This inscription records the restoration of an altar by Sextus Nigidius Primus, aedile and decurion of Brixia, likely in the early Imperial period.

EDCS-05100134.translation: Sextus Nigidius Primus Iunior of the Fabia tribe, decurion of Brixia, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Augustan Tutela.
EDCS-05100134.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Sextus Nigidius Primus Iunior, a decurion of Brixia, to the goddess Tutela.

EDCS-05100135.translation: Luculena Tatias gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Juno Regina.
EDCS-05100135.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Juno Regina by Luculena Tatias.

EDCS-05100136.translation: Tiberius Claudius Primus of the Lucusta tribe gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-05100136.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Tiberius Claudius Primus.

EDCS-05100137.translation: Numisius Hermes enlarged the sanctuary of the Mother of the Gods Magnae for his daughters Numisia Tyches and Numisia Primi.
EDCS-05100137.summary: This inscription records the enlargement of a sanctuary by Numisius Hermes for his daughters, dedicated to the Mother of the Gods Magnae.

EDCS-05100138.translation: Sacred to the Augustan Victory. Lucius Aemilius Faustus, son of Lucius Aemilius Spurius and freedman of Lucius Aemilius Primus.
EDCS-05100138.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Augustan Victory, mentioning a father-son relationship and a freedman.

EDCS-05100139.translation: Marcus Mutellius, son of Marcus of the Fabia tribe, a veteran of the Tenth Legion, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-05100139.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Marcus Mutellius in his will.

EDCS-05100140.translation: Staius Primus, a veteran of the Twenty-second Legion, [dedicated this].
EDCS-05100140.summary: This inscription identifies Staius Primus as a veteran of the Twenty-second Legion.

EDCS-05100141.translation: To Sextus Laelius Primigenius, one of the six Augustal priests, and to Laelia Restituta, their most devoted daughter Laelia Priscilla [erected this] to her most devoted parents.
EDCS-05100141.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a daughter to her parents.

EDCS-05100142.translation: To Lucius Magius Magianus, Claudia Severa [erected this] to her most beloved husband, and to their most dutiful son, Cornelius Valerius, and to Magius Priscinianus, their deserving father-in-law; and to herself, and in memory of them, she gave 60,000 sesterces to the guild of boatmen of Brixia for the purpose of yearly offerings and upkeep, to the departed spirits.
EDCS-05100142.summary: A funerary monument with a substantial endowment for religious services by a woman to her husband, son, and father-in-law, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05100143.translation: To the good memory of Claudia.

EDCS-05100144.translation: Lubiamus Triumi, son of Ebusus, of the Palarian tribe, made [this] while alive, and iud[icavit?].
EDCS-05100144.summary: A funerary epitaph indicating the monument was constructed by the deceased himself.

EDCS-05100145.translation: To Publicia Pusinna, Marcus Nonius Cornelianus [erected this] to his most beloved wife. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-05100145.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife.

EDCS-05100146.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintia Maxima, Servilia Festa [erected this] to her most devoted mother.
EDCS-05100146.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a daughter to her mother.

EDCS-05100147.translation: To Valeria Quarta, wife, and Homulla, daughter. B(onae) N(e) A(nimæ)?
EDCS-05100147.summary: A fragmented funerary dedication to Valeria Quarta by her wife and daughter.

EDCS-05100148.translation: To Pontius, son of Dacus, my tent-mate.
EDCS-05100148.summary: A funerary dedication to a companion, likely a soldier or fellow slave.

EDCS-05100150.translation: To Nonia Euthymia, his excellent wife, Marcus Nonius Syntrophus [erected this] to her deserving self. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-05100150.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife.

EDCS-05100151.translation: To my excellent wife Nonia Euthymia, deserving of all good things. To the divine shades.
EDCS-05100151.summary: A funerary dedication to a wife by her husband, Marcus Nonius Syntrophus.

EDCS-05100152.translation: To the Divine Shades. Pliamnus, son of Terti Mandilonis, for himself and Prima, his freedwoman wife.
EDCS-05100152.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Pliamnus for himself and his freedwoman wife, Prima.

EDCS-05100153.translation: Sacred to the Masculine Fates. Staumus Vesumi Britti and Cornelia Sexti filia Prisca set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05100153.summary: This dedication to the Masculine Fates was set up by Staumus Vesumi Britti and Cornelia Prisca in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-05100154.translation: In his lifetime, Quintus Medenasius, son of Cai, made this for himself, his wife Lubama, and --.
EDCS-05100154.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Quintus Medenasius for himself and his wife, Lubama, with space for additional individuals.

EDCS-05100156.translation: Druinus, acting supervisor of the Tublinatium estates for the most distinguished man Marci Noni Arri Muciani, built a hut from the ground up at his own expense for the Feminine Fates and also dedicated 200 HS in coin for the Vettian farm's census, while under its guardianship.
EDCS-05100156.summary: This inscription records Druinus's construction of a hut for the Feminine Fates and a dedication of money for the Vettian farm, commissioned by a prominent official.

EDCS-05100157.translation: Lucius Cullonius, son of Lei, of the Fabia tribe, Primus, a decurion of the 1st Wing of Cannanefates, ordered by his will that this be made in his name and that of his sons Primi and Paternus, decurion of Brixia; Lucius Ebusius took care of its construction.
EDCS-05100157.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, ordered in the will of Lucius Cullonius Primus, a decurion of the ala I Cannanefatium, and carried out by Lucius Ebusius.

EDCS-05100158.translation: To Silvanus Augustus. Lucius Septimius Macrinus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, a prefect with public equestrian rank, quinquennalis in Brixia, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05100158.summary: This is a votive dedication to Silvanus Augustus by Lucius Septimius Macrinus, a quinquennalis official in Brixia.

EDCS-05100159.translation: Claudius Tertius Palariacus and Cornelius Tertius Trigalianus, supervisors of the people, restored this with public money.
EDCS-05100159.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a public monument by two supervisors, Claudius Tertius Palariacus and Cornelius Tertius Trigalianus.

EDCS-05100160.translation: To Fortuna Redux. Lucius Valerius Iustus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05100160.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Fortuna Redux by Lucius Valerius Iustus.

EDCS-05100161.translation: In his lifetime, Marcus Ulpius Bellicus, a veteran of the 30th Ulpia Victrix legion, made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-05100161.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Marcus Ulpius Bellicus, a veteran of the 30th legion, for himself and his family.

EDCS-05100162.translation: Sacred to Diana the Holy. Logetus Maximus and Probus gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-05100162.summary: This is a votive inscription from the Roman period where Logetus Maximus and Probus dedicate a sacred object or structure to the goddess Diana, having successfully fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-05100164.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, Lubiamus son of Endrubius Quintallus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05100164.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Hercules Saxanus.

EDCS-05100165.translation: To Mercury, sacred. Furii Claudianus and Severus paid their vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-05100165.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Mercury by two dedicants.

EDCS-05100166.translation: To Mercury, Quintus Julius Africanus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05100166.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Mercury by Quintus Julius Africanus.

EDCS-05100167.translation: Lucius Calventius Firmus paid his vow willingly and deservedly to Minerva.
EDCS-05100167.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Minerva by Lucius Calventius Firmus.

EDCS-05100168.translation: --tius, son of Cai / -- and pavement / -- he made.
EDCS-05100168.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the construction of a pavement by a person identified only by their praenomen and nomen.

EDCS-05100169.translation: [---]us, son of Gaius, of the Crep[---] tribe, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05100169.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow, likely to a deity, with the name of the dedicator partially preserved.

EDCS-05100170.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras, Lucius Claudius Iustus with his sons Iustus and Iustinus gave this gift.
EDCS-05100170.summary: An inscription recording a gift to the god Mithras by Lucius Claudius Iustus and his sons.

EDCS-05100171.translation: To the Genius of the Birthplace, Quintus Muielius Iustus with his family.
EDCS-05100171.summary: An inscription dedicated to the Genius of the Birthplace by Quintus Muielius Iustus and his family.

EDCS-05100172.text_edition: \n Deo sancto Saturno ex voto Claudius Victorinus signum cum base pro salute sua suorumque omnium libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-05100172.translation: To the holy god Saturn, Claudius Victorinus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly gave a statue with a base for his own health and that of all his family.
EDCS-05100172.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of a statue and base to the god Saturn by Claudius Victorinus for the health of himself and his family.

EDCS-05100173.translation: To Saturn, Iulius Iustinianus paid his vow willingly with good spirit.
EDCS-05100173.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Saturn by Iulius Iustinianus.

EDCS-05100174.translation: To the god Saturn, Lucius Lavisno Paternus paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-05100174.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the god Saturn by Lucius Lavisno Paternus.

EDCS-05100175.translation: To Saturn, August, sacred. Lucius Nonius Sabinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05100175.summary: This is a dedication to the god Saturn, offered by Lucius Nonius Sabinus, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-05100177.translation: To the mistresses Cassia Marcella, Iuventia Maxsuma, Firmidia Modesta, and Numonia Secunda, from the assistants Iuventia Secunda, Manneia Pupa, Loreia Prima, and Vettia Secunda.
EDCS-05100177.summary: This inscription lists the names of mistresses and their assistants, likely related to a religious or collegial group.

EDCS-05100178.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Divi filius Augustus consul XI tribunicia potestate dedit Marcus Appuleius Sexti filius legatus iussu eius faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-05100178.translation: The emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the divine, consul for the eleventh time, holder of tribunician power, gave this; Marcus Appuleius, son of Sextus, as legate, had it carried out by his order.
EDCS-05100178.summary: This inscription records a public work commissioned by Emperor Augustus and executed under the supervision of his legate, Marcus Appuleius.

EDCS-05100181.text_edition: \n Magno et Invicto Imperatori Caesari P(ublio)? Licinio Gallieno \n
EDCS-05100181.translation: To the Great and Unconquered Emperor Caesar, Publius Licinius Gallienus.
EDCS-05100181.summary: This is an acclamation or dedication to the emperor Gallienus.

EDCS-05100183.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Ingenuo clarissimo iuveni tribuno legionis III Italicae Tiberius Claudius Victor vir egregius infanti benigno plura de se merenti\n
EDCS-05100183.translation: To Gaius Julius Ingenuus, most distinguished young man, tribune of the III Italica legion. Tiberius Claudius Victor, an outstanding man, to his beloved infant, who deserved more from him.
EDCS-05100183.summary: This is a dedication from Tiberius Claudius Victor to the young tribune Gaius Julius Ingenuus, likely commemorating a deceased individual.

EDCS-05100184.translation: Living, he made [this] for Sassius Remus, son of Lubia Esdra, daughter of Turi, to his wife Pladia, daughter of Sassi Curisi, and to Verecunda Fundania, wife of Marcus Curisius Sabinus, a soldier of the XXI Rapax legion, and for his own family.
EDCS-05100184.summary: This is a tombstone inscription made by Marcus Curisius Sabinus, a soldier of the XXI Rapax legion, for his wife and family.

EDCS-05100186.translation: Living, he made [this] for himself and for Secunda, his excellent wife, and [---].
EDCS-05100186.summary: This is a tombstone inscription begun by Lucius Octavius Trophimus, a VIvir, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05100187.text_edition: \n Caio Valerio Cai filio Papiria Mariano honores omnes adepto Tridenti flamini Romae et Augusti praefecto quinquennali auguri adlecto nnae legionis III Italicae sodali sacrorum Tusculanorum iudici selecto decuriis tribus decurioni Brixiae curatori rei publicae Mantuanorum equo publico praefecto fabrum patrono coloniae publice\n
EDCS-05100187.translation: To Gaius Valerius Marianus, son of Gaius Valerius, of the Papiria tribe, who attained all honors, as flamen of Tridentum, prefect of the Augustal cult at Rome, quinquennial official, augur, admitted to the III Italica legion, member of the sodality of sacred rites of Tusculum, selected judge of three decuries, decurion at Brixia, curator of the public affairs of the Mantua, with public horse, prefect of the fabrum, patron of the colony, publicly [honored].
EDCS-05100187.summary: This inscription lists the numerous prestigious civic and religious offices held by Gaius Valerius Marianus, a prominent citizen from Tridentum.

EDCS-05100188.translation: Living, she made [this] for herself and Quintus Man[---].
EDCS-05100188.summary: This is the beginning of a tombstone inscription by Cassidia for herself and Quintus Man[---].

EDCS-05100189.translation: To Marcus Cornelius Favos, son of Marcus Cornelius, and to his brother Quintus Cornelius Constantius, from his father Marcus Cornelius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-05100189.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a father and son, Marcus Cornelius Favos and Quintus Cornelius Constantius, by the father.

EDCS-05100190.translation: Leus made this while alive for himself and for his wife Ambia Saubia, daughter of Galerius Pladius.
EDCS-05100190.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Leus for himself and his wife Ambia Saubia during his lifetime.

EDCS-05100192.translation: Living, he made [this] for himself and for Ulpia Secunda, daughter of Ulpius Gaeticus, his dearest wife, and for his most dutiful daughter Ulpia Prisca, and for his excellent son-in-law Marcus Vibuleius Primus, 11.5 feet in the field, 11.5 feet in the front, in possession.
EDCS-05100192.summary: This is a tombstone inscription by Priscus, son of Bilo, for himself, his wife, his daughter, and his son-in-law, also specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-05100193.translation: Titia, daughter of Buculus, lies here.
EDCS-05100193.summary: This is a simple epitaph identifying Titia, daughter of Buculus, as deceased.

EDCS-05100194.translation: Caius Cassius Optatus to his mother Tertia, daughter of Metellus Tullius, who lived 100 years and more.
EDCS-05100194.summary: This inscription is a tombstone erected by Caius Cassius Optatus for his mother Tertia, providing her lineage and age.

EDCS-05100195.translation: To Tullia Victorina, his dearest wife, from Lucius S. Hermes.
EDCS-05100195.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Tullia Victorina by her husband Lucius S. Hermes.

EDCS-05100198.summary: This is a simple dedication made by Leius during his lifetime, likely for a monument or tomb.

EDCS-05100199.translation: To Diana. Anthius, son of Cosurus, the actor, paid his vow.
EDCS-05100199.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana by an actor named Anthius.

EDCS-05100201.translation: Under the consulship of Marcus Junius Silanus and Quintus Sulpicius Camerinus, on the Ides of March at Baiae, in the Praetorium, the edict of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus was posted, which is written below. Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 6th time, acclaimed imperator for the 11th time, father of the country, consul designate for the 4th time, says: Since among long-standing disputes which have been pending for some time, even during the reign of Tiberius Caesar, my uncle, for whose resolution he had sent Pinarius Apollinaris, and which concerned only the people of Comum and Bergaleos, he himself rightly neglected to report them, first due to the persistent absence of my uncle, and then even during the principate of Gaius, since it was not demanded of him; and afterwards Camurius Statutus brought it to my attention that many fields and pastures were under my jurisdiction, I sent my friend and companion, Lucius Plantus Iulius, to the spot. He, having summoned my procurators, both those in that region and those nearby, with the utmost care inquired and investigated. I permit him to decide and pronounce upon the other matters, just as they have been demonstrated to me in a report made by himself. As regards the condition of the Anauni, Tulliassii, and Sinduni, a part of whom the informant claims was attributed to the Tridentines and a part not attributed, I observe that this people does not have a very firm basis in Roman citizenship. However, since they claim to have been in possession for a long time, and are so mixed with the Tridentines that they cannot be separated from them without serious injury to the splendid municipality, I allow them to remain in the status they believe they hold, by my favor, all the more willingly because many of this group are said to have served in my praetorian guard, some have even led cohorts, and some have judged cases in Rome in decuries. I grant them this favor in such a way that I decree that whatever they have done and undertaken as Roman citizens, either among themselves or with the Tridentines or others, should be valid, and I permit them to continue to hold the names they previously had as if they were Roman citizens.
EDCS-05100201.summary: This is an imperial edict by Emperor Claudius from AD 46 concerning the legal status of several indigenous tribes in the northern Italian Alps, granting them local autonomy and recognition of their rights within the Roman legal system.

EDCS-05100208.translation: To the Lord God Cavavius, Gaius C. E. erected (this) willingly and with pleasure, as a deserved offering.
EDCS-05100208.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to a local deity named Cavavius, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-05100209.translation: Raedonius Victorinus and Tertius and Ingenuus, brothers, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly set up this altar with its figure to the august Concord, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05100209.summary: This inscription records the vow and erection of an altar to the goddess Concord by two brothers, Raedonius Victorinus and Ingenuus, likely in gratitude for a blessing.

EDCS-05100210.translation: Gaius V. Quadratus, for the safety of the inhabitants of Verassus, dedicated this altar to all the gods and goddesses, willingly, joyfully, and publicly.
EDCS-05100210.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to all gods and goddesses by Caius V. Quadratus for the well-being of the community of Verassus.

EDCS-05100211.translation: Sacred to all the gods and goddesses. Lucius C. Quartus fulfilled his vow willingly, with pleasure, and deservedly.
EDCS-05100211.summary: This is a dedication to all gods and goddesses, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD, by a private individual fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-05100213.translation: His father Iustinus dedicated this; placed by Justinus, son of Iulius Edurinus, freed from the danger of death while serving in the cohort of Iulius Edurinus, veteran of the first cohort of Pannonians.
EDCS-05100213.summary: This inscription is a dedication of an altar to Jupiter and the guardian gods by Iulius Edurinus, commemorating his deliverance from danger while serving in the military.

EDCS-05100214.translation: To Jupiter Victor. Lucius Visaeus Cerius fulfilled his vow willingly, with pleasure, and deservedly.
EDCS-05100214.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Victor, likely from the 2nd century AD, by Lucius Visaeus Cerius.

EDCS-05100215.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars by Lucius Viseus Crescens, likely an altar or monument.

EDCS-05100216.translation: Lucius Nemla Iustinus with his family willingly paid his vow to the Augustan Minerva, as was deserved.
EDCS-05100216.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Lucius Nemla Iustinus and his family to the goddess Minerva.

EDCS-05100219.translation: To the god Saturn Augustus. Lumennones Arvetius and Maximus and Rufus and Quadratinus and Firmianus and Clemens and Iustus and Iustinus and Asprius and Glabistus Quintus and Ris Rufinus and Lad Optatus and Quartus and Lucius and Severus and Maximinus Aurelius Firminus and Paternus and Iustinianus (dedicated this) with their own money, willingly, with pleasure, and deservedly.
EDCS-05100219.summary: This is a large communal dedication to the god Saturn Augustus by a group of men named Lumennones, likely dating to the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-05100220.translation: Sacred to Saturn. Lucius Papirius Syntropus (?), freedman of Lucius, [---]
EDCS-05100220.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn, likely from the early imperial period, mentioning a freedman but with a damaged text.

EDCS-05100221.translation: Marcus Propertius Tertius and Marcus Publius Quintus, his sons, set up this gift to Saturn and paid their vow.
EDCS-05100221.summary: This is a dedication to the god Saturn by Marcus Propertius Tertius and his sons.

EDCS-05100222.translation: To Augustan Victoria, Publius Tula Max, Publius Tula Quin, Publius Tula Ter, Publius Tula Vem.
EDCS-05100222.summary: This inscription lists individuals, possibly brothers named Publius Tula, dedicating something to the goddess Victoria.

EDCS-05100223.translation: Lucius Scantius Crescens, veteran of the Praetorian Guard, century of Iustus, (dedicated this) to himself and to Pontia Guseda, his wife.
EDCS-05100223.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a retired Praetorian Guardsman and his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-05100224.translation: Caius V. Quintinus, son of Gaius V. Firmus, veteran of the IV Praetorian Cohort, (and) Quartus, daughter of Kaninia Teda, while alive, made (this) for themselves.
EDCS-05100224.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a veteran of the Praetorian Guard and his wife, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-05100225.translation: [---] to Nonia, [his most beloved?] wife, and to his own (family), while alive, made (this) for the well-deserving.
EDCS-05100225.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man dedicating a tomb for his wife and family, with a damaged text, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-05100227.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius R. Severus (dedicated this) to Serania Procella, his most beloved wife.
EDCS-05100227.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a wife by her husband, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-05100230.translation: For good and perpetual memory and security, may the remains of Maximinus rest in peace.
EDCS-05100230.summary: This is an epitaph intended to ensure the peaceful repose of the remains of someone named Maximinus.

EDCS-05100231.translation: Festinus, servant and treasurer ('arcarius') of Titus Iulius Saturninus, collector of public taxes ('portorii publici'), willingly paid his vow to the Augustan Isis, as was deserved.
EDCS-05100231.summary: This is a votive inscription to the goddess Isis, dedicated by Festinus, a freedman and treasurer for a tax collector.

EDCS-05100232.translation: Sacred to Isis Myrionymos. Festinus, slave of T. Iulius Saturninus, a publican tax collector, placed this. Fortunatus, his fellow slave and accountant, saw to its construction.
EDCS-05100232.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to the goddess Isis by two slaves of a publican tax collector.

EDCS-05100233.text_edition: \n Marti Augusto conservatori corporis sui Mercurialis Augusti nostri vilicus ex iussu numinis ipsius sigillum marmoreum posuit\n
EDCS-05100233.translation: To Mars Augustus, preserver of his body, Mercurialis, steward of our Augustus, placed this marble figurine by order of the god himself.
EDCS-05100233.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a marble figurine to Mars Augustus by his steward, Mercurialis, following divine command.

EDCS-05100234.translation: Sacred to the Unconquered God Mithras and the Sun. Valentinus Secundionis, in memory of his father, from the guild, willingly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-05100234.summary: This inscription records a joint dedication to Mithras and the Sun, made by Valentinus Secundionis in memory of his father and on behalf of a guild.

EDCS-05100237.translation: Marcus Betulius Firminus, freedman of Marcus, a member of the VI viri Augustales, ordered it to be made in his will.
EDCS-05100237.summary: This inscription indicates that a monument or object was commissioned in the will of Marcus Betulius Firminus, who was a member of the collegium of VI viri Augustales.

EDCS-05100238.translation: Lucius T Sininus ordered it to be made in his will.
EDCS-05100238.summary: This inscription states that Lucius T Sininus commissioned something to be made via his will.

EDCS-05200247.translation: Manius Tivalicus gave this gift to Temavus willingly, as was deserved.
EDCS-05200247.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Temavus by Manius Tivalicus.

EDCS-05200255.text_edition: \n tus in memoriam aeroniae Maximae coniugi dulcissimae quae liberos adultos defuncta est annorum XXXV\n
EDCS-05200255.translation: ... to the memory of his most beloved wife Aeronia Maxima, who died after her children, at the age of 35.
EDCS-05200255.summary: This inscription is a memorial to Aeronia Maxima, a woman who died at the age of 35 after her children.

EDCS-05200262.text_edition: \n Murranius Maxsimus sic sibi fecit et coniugi sui sic ViSeverinae\n
EDCS-05200262.translation: Murranius Maximus made this for himself and for his wife ViSeverina.
EDCS-05200262.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Murranius Maximus commissioned his own tomb and that of his wife Severina.

EDCS-05200264.text_edition: \n Nomine Quinti Domitii Alpini Licinia mater signum Dianae et venationem salientes testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-05200264.translation: In the name of Quintus Domitius Alpinus, his mother Licinia ordered a statue of Diana and a hunt to be made by his will.
EDCS-05200264.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Licinia in memory of her son Quintus Domitius Alpinus, depicting Diana and a hunt.

EDCS-05200266.text_edition: \n Quinto Latinio Publi filio Quinti nepoti Poblilia Musculo praefecto fabrum Gyas libertus\n
EDCS-05200266.translation: To Quintus Latinus, son of Publius, grandson of Quintus. Gyas, his freedman, (dedicated this).
EDCS-05200266.summary: This is a dedication by Gyas, a freedman, to his former master Quintus Latinus, son of Publius and grandson of Quintus.

EDCS-05200267.text_edition: \n Publio Octavio Cai filio Publilia Pudenti vestiario\n
EDCS-05200267.translation: To Publius Octavius, son of Caius, (by) Publilia Pudenti, a cloth merchant.
EDCS-05200267.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Publius Octavius, son of Caius, by Publilia Pudenti, identified as a cloth merchant.

EDCS-05200268.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Marcus Antistius Marci libertus Poblilia Dignus sibi et Apponiae Luci filiae Maximae uxori\n
EDCS-05200268.translation: Marcus Antistius, freedman of Marcus, made this while alive for himself and for Apponia Maxima, daughter of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-05200268.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Marcus Antistius, a freedman, dedicating his tomb for himself and his wife Apponia Maxima.

EDCS-05200269.text_edition: \n Publio Atilio Publi liberto Philippo o \n
EDCS-05200269.translation: To Publius Atilius Philippus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-05200269.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Publius Atilius Philippus, a freedman.

EDCS-05200270.text_edition: \n Titus Vassidius Exomni filius Namulla Tedua Lastae Appia Quinti filia Maxima in fronte pedes XXVSsemis in agro pedes XXIII\n
EDCS-05200270.translation: Titus Vassidius, son of Exomnius, (and) Namulla, (and) Appia Maxima, daughter of Quintus, (and) Tedua Lasta: 25 and a half feet in front, 23 feet in the land.
EDCS-05200270.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property belonging to Titus Vassidius, Namulla, Appia Maxima, and Tedua Lasta.

EDCS-05200272.translation: Burial place of Marcus Albucius Vitalis.
EDCS-05200272.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial place of Marcus Albucius Vitalis.

EDCS-05200277.text_edition: \n Ad innocentes fratres Amaros et Matrona puer defunctus anno I et mensibus X et diebus XII puella defuncta annoro sic IIII et diebus II et in die sic obiti sunt frater et soror\n
EDCS-05200277.translation: To the innocent siblings Amaros and Matrona, a boy died at the age of 1 year, 10 months, and 12 days; a girl died at the age of 4 years and 2 days, and on the same day the brother and sister died.
EDCS-05200277.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for two young siblings, Amaros and Matrona, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-05200279.translation: Here rests the distinguished man Censorius, who lived for 64 years and 7 days and passed away on the day before the Ides of March in the second indiction.
EDCS-05200279.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and lifespan of a man named Censorius, dated by indiction.

EDCS-05200281.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Raedo Firmus pro salute sua\n
EDCS-05200281.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius Raedo Firmus for his own safety.
EDCS-05200281.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Lucius Raedo Firmus for his well-being.

EDCS-05401247.translation: Diocletian, Valerius Maximian, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, and Flavius Constantius. [Venetia]
EDCS-05401247.summary: This inscription records the consuls Diocletian and Maximian, and possibly Flavius Constantius, likely from the period of their joint rule.

EDCS-05401253.translation: To our lord the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus. [Year] I.
EDCS-05401253.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Maxentius, likely indicating the start of his reign or a specific milestone.

EDCS-05401255.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 4th time, imperator for the 11th time, father of the country, censor, maintained the road the Via Claudia Augusta, which his father Drusus had constructed after opening the Alps in war, from Altinum all the way to the river Danube, 350 miles.
EDCS-05401255.summary: This is a monumental inscription by Emperor Claudius detailing the construction and maintenance of the Via Claudia Augusta, a major Roman road.

EDCS-05401260.translation: Publius Popillius, son of Caius, consul, 81.
EDCS-05401260.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name and consular dating of Publius Popillius.

EDCS-05401263.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, and Flavius Valerius Constantius, and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars, [number] miles.
EDCS-05401263.summary: This inscription lists the joint emperors Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius, likely commemorating a public work or military achievement.

EDCS-05401264.translation: To our lord the Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantine the Great, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 23rd time, hailed as emperor for the 22nd time, consul for the 7th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, excellent prince, son of the deified Constantius, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-05401264.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription in honor of Emperor Constantine the Great, listing his titles and honors.

EDCS-05401268.translation: To our lord Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, 11 miles. Our lords Julius Crispus and [Licinius] and Claudius Constantinus, most noble Caesars, 11 miles.
EDCS-05401268.summary: This inscription dedicates a distance of 11 miles to Emperors Maxentius and the Caesars Crispus, Licinius, and Constantine, possibly related to a road or aqueduct.

EDCS-05401276.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Trajanus Decius, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country. [Year] XIX.
EDCS-05401276.summary: This inscription records the titles and powers of Emperor Trajan Decius, likely from the period of his rule around his second consulship.

EDCS-05401277.translation: To our lord the Emperor Caesar Flavius Claudius Julianus, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious, and Triumphant, always Augustus, chief priest, hailed as emperor for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, born for the good of the state, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-05401277.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Emperor Julian, listing his titles and honors.

EDCS-05401278.translation: To our lord Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantinus Maximus, Pious, Fortunate, Victor Augustus. [Year]
EDCS-05401278.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, likely marking a victory or a period of his reign.

EDCS-05401279.translation: To our lords Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor, unconquered and eternal Augusti, born for the good of the state, 20 miles.
EDCS-05401279.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to the Augusti Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor, indicating a distance of 20 miles.

EDCS-05401280.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantinus Maximus, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, 24 miles.
EDCS-05401280.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, likely marking a distance of 24 miles related to a public work.

EDCS-05401293.translation: to the son of the deified Constantius, born for the good of the state
EDCS-05401293.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the son of the deified Constantius, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-05401294.translation: To our Lord the Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantius Maximus, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious Augustus, supreme pontiff, holder of tribunician power for the 23rd time, hailed as emperor for the 22nd time, consul for the 7th time, father of the country, proconsul, to the perfect princeps, son of the deified Constantius, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-05401294.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantius II, listing his numerous titles and honors, likely part of an honorific monument.

EDCS-05401295.translation: To the Emperors Caesars Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletian and Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian and Marcus Aurelius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximian, most noble Caesars, for the 17th time. To our Lord Flavius Jovian, triumphant forever Augustus, for the 17th time.
EDCS-05401295.summary: This inscription records honors granted to multiple emperors, including Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, Galerius, and Jovian, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-05401297.translation: Devotedly, Venice placed this in honor of our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Valens, divine brothers and always Augusti.
EDCS-05401297.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Venice honoring the co-emperors Valentinian and Valens.

EDCS-05401298.translation: Spurius Postumius Albinus, son of Spurius, grandson of Spurius, consul, 122 [miles] from Genoa to Cremona.
EDCS-05401298.summary: This is likely a milestone inscription indicating a distance of 122 miles from Genoa to Cremona, and it records the name and consular dating of Spurius Postumius Albinus.

EDCS-05401299.translation: To our lord Flavius Iovianus, triumphant, always Augustus.
EDCS-05401299.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Emperor Flavius Iovianus.

EDCS-05401305.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered, for the 29th time.
EDCS-05401305.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Maxentius, likely part of an honorific monument, possibly a milestone given the repetition of 'XXIX'.

EDCS-05401306.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered, 29.
EDCS-05401306.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Emperor Maxentius, possibly indicating a number of years or a legion.

EDCS-05401308.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-05401308.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Maxentius, likely part of an honorific monument.

EDCS-05401365.translation: Sacred to the divine spirit of Augustus, Gnaeus Papirius Eumelus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05401365.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the divine spirit of Augustus by Gnaeus Papirius Eumelus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401366.translation: Anusia Phoebas made this for her husband Marcus Mutilius Processus, son of Marcus, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-05401366.summary: A funerary dedication made by Anusia Phoebas for her husband and herself, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05401367.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Scribonia Maxima, daughter of Publius, probably Roman Republican or early Imperial.

EDCS-05401368.translation: Gaius Tecusenus Tertius made this for himself and his family while alive, for 21 feet in length and 10 feet in frontage.
EDCS-05401368.summary: A funerary monument set up by Gaius Tecusenus Tertius for his family, indicating property boundaries, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401369.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Papirius Andronicus, with his family, willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-05401369.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Papirius Andronicus and his family.

EDCS-05401371.translation: For the Nebri, Tertia, servant of Augustus, for Barbar[a?].
EDCS-05401371.summary: A dedication or memorial possibly by Tertia, a freedwoman of Augustus, for the Nebri family or an individual named Barbara, likely Imperial period.

EDCS-05401373.translation: Sacred to Nemesis Augusta, Gaius Julius Chrysogonus made this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05401373.summary: A votive dedication to Nemesis Augusta by Gaius Julius Chrysogonus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401374.translation: Sacred to the holy god Silvanus, Gaius Julius Chrysogonus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05401374.summary: A votive dedication to the god Silvanus by Gaius Julius Chrysogonus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401375.summary: An incomplete dedication to the goddess Venus Caelestis, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401376.translation: Acutinus set this up with his family for Venus Caelestis.
EDCS-05401376.summary: A dedication to Venus Caelestis by Acutinus and his family, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401377.translation: In the colonia Iulia Pola Pollentia Herculanea, upon the report of the duovirs Publius Mutienus Priscus and Gaius Marcius Histro on the Nones of September, concerning the words spoken by Settidius Abascantus, that beyond the probity of his life, with such solicitude and industry he carried out the office delegated to him in the island of Minerva, so that he was not only content with care and diligence to satisfy public religious duties but also devised and expended his own funds for the beautification of the place, and therefore, because of the merits of such a disposition, he should be rewarded by public decree [...], for the public gr[atefulness...]
EDCS-05401377.summary: A public decree from the colony of Pola Pollentia Herculanea, dating to September (likely Imperial period), honouring Settidius Abascantus for his diligent service and personal investment in public works and religious duties on the island of Minerva.

EDCS-05401379.translation: To Titus Galgestius Syntrophus, Augustalis of Pola. Galgestia Pergamis made this for her deserving husband, most devoted.
EDCS-05401379.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her devoted husband, who held the office of Augustalis in Pola.

EDCS-05401380.translation: Gaius Laecanius Menander, duovir of the Augustales, an accensus of the patrons, [erected this] for himself and for his mother Laecania Thalia and for his freedman Polybius.
EDCS-05401380.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Laecanius Menander's dedication for himself and his family members.

EDCS-05401381.translation: Setidius Ossatus and Setidia Frontonila, brother and sister, have placed this chest while alive, by judgment of Aquilius Rufus and Tacitus Secularis, from the guild of craftsmen, during the tribunate, near the place of death.
EDCS-05401381.summary: This inscription details the placement of a funerary chest by a brother and sister, likely for themselves, referencing guild membership and a judicial decision.

EDCS-05401385.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caeparia Aphrodisia made this for her daughter Caeparia Chresima, aged 13 years, 10 months, and 11 days, her dearest daughter, while she herself was alive.
EDCS-05401385.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Caeparia Chresima, dedicated by her mother Caeparia Aphrodisia.

EDCS-05401386.translation: The plot of Gaius Caetranus Clemens, 12.5 feet in front and 22 feet in the field, for himself, Licinia Primigenia, and their family.
EDCS-05401386.summary: This is a boundary or property inscription defining the dimensions of a plot of land for Gaius Caetranus Clemens and his family.

EDCS-05401387.translation: To Valentino, from Laecania Staphyle, his partner in the barracks.
EDCS-05401387.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Valentino by his military companion Laecania Staphyle.

EDCS-05401388.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Minicius Tetrico, son of Gaius, his sons and wife made this for their most excellent father, while alive.
EDCS-05401388.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by the children and wife for their father, Gaius Minicius Tetrico.

EDCS-05401389.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Orbius Phronimus and Caius Orbius Asellio [erected this] for their well-deserving patron, Gaius Orbius Cosmo.
EDCS-05401389.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to a patron, Gaius Orbius Cosmo, by his freedmen.

EDCS-05401390.translation: Publius Orcivius Fronto, son of Gaius, placed this while alive for his wife Orcivia Quarta, daughter of Publius, and for his daughter.
EDCS-05401390.summary: This funerary epitaph records Publius Orcivius Fronto dedicating a monument for his wife and daughter during his lifetime.

EDCS-05401391.translation: Postumius Primogenes [dedicated this] for himself and for Munatia Vitalis, freedwoman of Lucius, 12 feet in front, and in the field [feet...].
EDCS-05401391.summary: This inscription records Postumius Primogenes dedicating a plot of land for himself and Munatia Vitalis, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-05401392.translation: To Sextia Procope, from Gaius Apuleius Vitalis, her husband.
EDCS-05401392.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextia Procope, dedicated by her husband Gaius Apuleius Vitalis.

EDCS-05401394.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Bona, daughter of Quintus Titacius.

EDCS-05401395.translation: To the Divine Shades, for Lucius Tutilius Glycerus, who deserved well.
EDCS-05401395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Lucius Tutilius Glycerus for his good service.

EDCS-05401422.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to Seixomnia Leucitica by Polates.

EDCS-05401423.translation: Lucius Campanius Verecundus, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, a veteran of the Fourth Scythian Legion, a standard-bearer (signifer) and centurion of the cohort of the Cispadanes, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-05401423.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Campanius Verecundus, a veteran of the Fourth Scythian Legion, who specified its erection in his will.

EDCS-05401425.translation: Minicius made this for his dearest wife, Minicia, with whom he lived for 22 years, and for Pompeius, his father, while alive.
EDCS-05401425.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Minicius for his wife Minicia and his father Pompeius.

EDCS-05401426.translation: Pomponius arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-05401426.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Pomponius arranged for the monument's construction.

EDCS-05401428.translation: To the departed spirits. Leontiscus the colonus made this for Aquilinus, aged seven, his most unfortunate son.
EDCS-05401428.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father for his young son, Aquilinus.

EDCS-05401429.translation: Fausta Hostilia Quarta, daughter of Caius, to her sister Fausta Hostilia, daughter of Caius, set this up while alive.
EDCS-05401429.summary: A private funerary monument set up by Fausta Quarta to her sister Fausta, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05401434.translation: To the departed spirits. Parents made this for their son Florentinus, aged 6, and for Successus.
EDCS-05401434.summary: This is a funerary inscription by parents for their young son Florentinus and another individual named Successus.

EDCS-05401437.translation: Gaius Hostilius Florus, son of Titus, aged 70.
EDCS-05401437.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Hostilius Florus, son of Titus, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-05401438.translation: Lucius Magplinus, son of Lucius, aged 70.
EDCS-05401438.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Magplinus, son of Lucius, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-05401439.translation: Sextilia Propontis, willingly paid her vow for the health and safe return of her sons to her lady Haera.
EDCS-05401439.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to a goddess named Haera by Sextilia Propontis for the well-being of her sons, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401446.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription with names and filiations, likely from a family tomb.

EDCS-05401450.translation: [---]dius, son of Lucius, [---]lens, soldier [---] who is [---] years old, [---] years, [---] was [---].
EDCS-05401450.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a soldier with ages and names that are partially lost.

EDCS-05401451.translation: Nonius, son of Titus, [---], Nonia, daughter of Titus, [---], sister.
EDCS-05401451.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning siblings Nonius and Nonia, children of Titus.

EDCS-05401452.translation: Lucius Canthenius Iugalio, son of Lucius; Vettia daughter of Marcus, his wife (?); Lucius Canthenius Balbus (?), son of Lucius; Titus Canthenius Uccis (?), son of Lucius, made this while alive for themselves and their family.
EDCS-05401452.summary: A funerary monument for the Canthenius family, likely erected in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05401456.translation: Aulus Aurelius Paetus, son of Aulus, ordered this to be made, as a duovir.
EDCS-05401456.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Aulus Aurelius Paetus, indicating he commissioned the monument in his role as a duovir.

EDCS-05401458.translation: For his outstanding and unique support for the state, our lord Julian, the invincible emperor, ordered that the fiscal administration of the provinces be expedited, shortening the periods of change, under the supervision of Claudius Mamertinus, a most distinguished man and praetorian prefect, with Vetulenius Praenestius, a most accomplished man and corrector of Venetia and Istria, in charge.
EDCS-05401458.summary: This inscription records an imperial rescript from Emperor Julian, concerning fiscal reforms and provincial administration, supervised by Claudius Mamertinus and Vetulenius Praenestius, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-05401459.text_edition: \n Publio Cominio Publi filio Claudia Clementi praefecto classium praetoriarum Misenensis et nnatis praeposito a censibus procuratori Augusti XX hereditatium procuratori Augusti provinciae Lusitaniae procuratori Augusti provinciae Daciae Apolensis sic subpraefecto nnonae procuratori Augusti ad familiam gladiatoriam Transpadanam procuratori Augusti XX hereditatium per Hispaniam citeriorem omnibus equestribus militiis functo pontifici patrono coloniarum Concordiensium Aquileiensium Parmensium Venafranorum ordo Concordiensium\n
EDCS-05401459.translation: To Publius Cominius Clement, son of Publius Claudia, prefect of the Praetorian fleets at Misenum and [annonae?], overseer of the census, procurator of Augustus for inheritances (XX hereditatium), procurator of Augustus for the province of Lusitania, procurator of Augustus for the province of Dacia Apulensis, sub-prefect of the annona (?), procurator of Augustus for the Transpadane gladiatorial families, procurator of Augustus for inheritances (XX hereditatium) in Hither Spain, having completed all equestrian military services, pontifex, patron of the colonies of Concordia, Aquileia, Parma, and Venafrum, the council of Concordia gave [this place].
EDCS-05401459.summary: A dedication of a place by the town council of Concordia to Publius Cominius Clement, honoring his extensive career in Roman administration and religious roles, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05401460.text_edition: \n Tito Desticio Titifilio Claudia Severo primo pilo legionis X geminae subpraefecto vigilum procuratori Augusti provinciae Daciae superioris procuratori provinciae Cappadociae item Ponti mediterranei et Armeniae minoris et Lycaoniae Antiochianae procuratori provineiae Raetiae flamini divi Hadriani pontifici patrono coloniae alae II Flaviae Germanus Martialius Titianus Frontiniusanus alae I Flaviae Iulius Memorinus Iulius Ds Flavius Speratus alae I singularium Aelius Severus Petronius Iulianus decuriones exercitus Raetici praesidi optimo et sanctissimo locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-05401460.translation: To Titus Desticius Severus, son of Titus Claudia, primipilaris of the tenth legion Gemina, sub-prefect of the vigiles, procurator of Augustus for the province of Dacia Superioris, procurator for the province of Cappadocia, also of Pontus Polemoniacus and Lesser Armenia and Antiochian Lycaonia, procurator for the province of Raetia, flamen of the deified Hadrian, pontifex, patron of the colony of Ala II Flavia, Germanus Martialius Ticianus Frontinianus of Ala I Flavia, Iulius Memorinus, Iulius Ds, Flavius Speratus of Ala I Singularium, Aelius Severus, Petronius Iulianus, decurions of the Raetian army, gave [this place] to their best and most sacred governor.
EDCS-05401460.summary: A dedication of a place by the decurions of the Raetian army to their governor Titus Desticius Severus, recognizing his military and administrative career, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05401462.translation: Flavius Romulianus, formerly prefect, purchased a tomb for his most beloved wife, Aurelia Domnula, at his own expense.
EDCS-05401462.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Flavius Romulianus purchased a tomb for his wife Aurelia Domnula.

EDCS-05401465.text_edition: \n Quinto Decio Quinti filio Claudia Mettio Sabiniano equo publico Laurenti Lavinati quaestori aedili IIviro iterum patrono collegiorum fabrum et centonariorum praefecto collegii fabrum curatori rei publicae Polensium ordo Polensium iustissimo nnue locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-05401465.translation: To Quintus Decius Sabinianus, son of Quintus Claudia Mettia, on the public horse of Laurentum Lavinum, quaestor, aedile, duovir for the second time, patron of the guilds of fabric workers and centonarii, prefect of the guild of fabric workers, curator of public affairs of Pola, the council of Pola gave [this place] to their most just [?-nnue?] by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05401465.summary: A dedication of a place by the town council of Pola to Quintus Decius Sabinianus, honoring his local political and guild leadership roles, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401466.translation: Publius Rotenius Faustus, as a duovir, paved the road with his own money.
EDCS-05401466.summary: This is a public works inscription by Publius Rotenius Faustus, recording that he paved a road at his own expense in his capacity as a duovir.

EDCS-05401467.translation: Titus Valerius Romulus, son of Titus, of the Claudia tribe, duovir, 20 feet in every direction.
