EDCS-05401467.summary: This inscription likely marks the dimensions of a funerary plot or structure, commissioned by Titus Valerius Romulus in his role as duovir.

EDCS-05401470.translation: To Salionus, and Terentia [---]ca, most distinguished woman, and to Salutaris and Britannica, children, and to the archivist.
EDCS-05401470.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to be a dedication or funerary text for several individuals, possibly including children and an archivist.

EDCS-05401471.translation: Here lies Leonitos, son-in-law of Gaianos of Constantinople, and if anyone dares to open another tomb, may he give 20 pounds of silver to the most holy treasury.
EDCS-05401471.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a curse against desecration, likely from Constantinople, warning against disturbing the tomb of Leonitos.

EDCS-05401472.translation: To Caius Aemilius Zosimus, son, who lived 6 years, 11 months, 14 days. Caius Aemilius Zosimus and Vettia Charite, parents [set this up].
EDCS-05401472.summary: A tombstone for a young boy, Caius Aemilius Zosimus, erected by his parents, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401474.translation: To Asco[---]rina, daughter of Lucius Pontius [---]anus, for her most loving mother.
EDCS-05401474.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Pontius [---]anus to his most loving mother, Asco[---]rina.

EDCS-05401475.translation: Marcus Aterus Florentus and Iulia Valeria made [this] while alive, from the gift of the god.
EDCS-05401475.summary: A dedication by Marcus Aterus Florentus and Iulia Valeria, possibly for a tomb or a religious offering, indicating a benefaction from a deity, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401476.translation: Place of Lucius Sertorius Cinnamus, Marcus Aufidius Gratus, in front 30 feet, behind 50 feet.
EDCS-05401476.summary: A plot of land designated for burial, owned or allocated to Lucius Sertorius Cinnamus and Marcus Aufidius Gratus, with dimensions specified, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401477.translation: Place of Marcus Aufidius Gratus, Lucius Sertorius Cinnamus, in front 30 feet, behind 50 feet.
EDCS-05401477.summary: A plot of land designated for burial, owned or allocated to Marcus Aufidius Gratus and Lucius Sertorius Cinnamus, with dimensions specified, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401478.translation: Lucius Caelius, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Caelius, freedman of Lucius, and Caelia, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for themselves, their descendants, while alive. 15 feet in front, in the field [illegible].
EDCS-05401478.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caelius, his freedman namesake, and Caelia, freedwoman of Lucius, who built their tomb while alive, with a measurement of the front and possibly the land area.

EDCS-05401479.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary marker, with illegible names and remnants of a prohibition against disturbing the grave.

EDCS-05401480.translation: Burial place for Lucius Calventius Atticus and Silicia Viola, 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-05401480.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of 16 feet in each direction, designated for Lucius Calventius Atticus and Silicia Viola.

EDCS-05401481.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, possibly a funerary dedication or a mention of a living person named Cassia.

EDCS-05401482.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Cassia Didymes, a most dutiful daughter, from Publius Cassius Ursio.
EDCS-05401482.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a grave to Cassia Didymes by her father, Publius Cassius Ursio.

EDCS-05401483.translation: Coceius Ursus bought this chest for himself and for his incomparable wife; whoever wishes to open it will give ten pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401483.summary: This is an epitaph inscribed on a chest, possibly a funerary monument, with a penalty for unauthorized opening, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401484.translation: To Cicria Eutychiane, Iulius Hyperanthes [dedicated this] to his most beloved and chaste wife. Cicrius Eutyches and Circia Mansueta, parents, [dedicated this] to their sweetest daughter.
EDCS-05401484.summary: This epitaph records the dedication of a tomb by parents to their daughter and by a husband to his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401485.translation: To Cicria Eutychis, Cicrius Heracleon [dedicated this] to his sweetest wife.
EDCS-05401485.summary: This epitaph records a husband's dedication to his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401486.translation: To Cicria Mansueta, his incomparable wife, Publius Atilius Cicrius Eutyches [dedicated this].
EDCS-05401486.summary: This epitaph records a husband's dedication to his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401487.translation: To Cominia Gratilla, Oppius Sabinus [dedicated this] to his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-05401487.summary: This epitaph records a son's dedication to his mother, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401488.translation: Titus Desticius made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-05401488.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Titus Desticius, who built a tomb for himself and his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-05401490.translation: To Quintus Fabius Fabianus, son of Quintus, Quintus Fabius and Turrania Sestia [dedicated this] to their most dutiful son.
EDCS-05401490.summary: This epitaph records parents dedicating a monument to their son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401491.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, possibly for an individual named Fabius, of indeterminate date.

EDCS-05401492.summary: This is a very short epitaph, likely for an individual named Fabia Paulina, of indeterminate date.

EDCS-05401494.translation: Firmina made this for herself while alive.
EDCS-05401494.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Firmina, who built her tomb while alive.

EDCS-05401495.translation: Flavius Romulianus, prefect of the sagittary workshop, made this memorial at his own expense for his wife Taheta and himself; if anyone in the future wishes to place a body in this place, he will pay one thousand money-bags to the state.
EDCS-05401495.summary: This is an epitaph for a wife and husband, commissioned by the husband who held a military administrative position, and includes a penalty for unauthorized burial, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-05401496.summary: This inscription marks a burial place belonging to Quintus Granius Phosphoros, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401497.translation: Greetings! Servius Iulius Pardalus and his daughter Iulia Serena, and you, whoever you are, farewell! They made this for their freedmen and freedwomen, and for Iulia Carphima, freedwoman, while alive.
EDCS-05401497.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Servius Iulius Pardalus and his daughter Iulia Serena, dedicating a tomb to their freedpeople, including Iulia Carphima, while they were alive.

EDCS-05401498.translation: To Gaius Iunius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina.
EDCS-05401498.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Gaius Iunius, son of Lucius, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05401499.translation: [...] Marcian[us?], son of Publius, Metr[---] to his brother [---]dui[---].
EDCS-05401499.summary: This is a highly fragmented inscription likely commemorating a familial relationship, possibly funerary, with names like Marcianus and Metr[---] mentioned.

EDCS-05401500.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription mentioning Lucius Minicius, with the context of the inscription largely lost.

EDCS-05401501.translation: Minicia, his wife, set this up.
EDCS-05401501.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Minicia, the wife of an unnamed individual, is the dedicator.

EDCS-05401502.translation: Pontia, who lived 14 days, Lucius Pontius [erected this?].
EDCS-05401502.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Pontia, who lived only 14 days, likely set up by Lucius Pontius.

EDCS-05401503.translation: Selia Iucunda, freedwoman of Quintus, ordered this to be made.
EDCS-05401503.summary: This inscription records that Selia Iucunda, a freedwoman of Quintus, commissioned a monument or object.

EDCS-05401504.translation: [illegible] to mother, [illegible] to father, [illegible] to brother's son, [illegible] to Severus, brother, [illegible] to Ep(h)agathus, freedman, [illegible] daughter Galla ordered this to be made in her will.
EDCS-05401504.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Galla, daughter of [illegible], in accordance with her will, commemorating her mother, father, brother, another brother named Severus, and a freedman.

EDCS-05401505.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the age of a deceased person (5 years) and may include the name Severus, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-05401507.translation: Vettia Anthis, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for herself and for Eutychia, freedwoman of Caius, while alive.
EDCS-05401507.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Vettia Anthis, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and Eutychia, freedwoman of Caius, made during their lifetimes.

EDCS-05401508.translation: To Vitaliano. To the spirits of the departed. Titus Laelius Crispinianus, to his father.
EDCS-05401508.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Titus Laelius Crispinianus to his deceased father, Vitaliano.

EDCS-05401509.translation: Ulpia Zen[---], while alive, for herself [---] Aeliae [---].
EDCS-05401509.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication made by Ulpia Zen[---] for herself and possibly for Aeliae, indicating a self-funded funerary monument.

EDCS-05401512.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning freedwomen and possibly personal names, with its precise purpose unclear due to damage.

EDCS-05401516.summary: This is a very damaged inscription that possibly refers to a freedman, but its context and purpose are largely lost.

EDCS-05401520.translation: To Alexander, my most dutiful son, of wonderful modesty, singular innocence, and unblemished chastity, learned in letters of note, who lived 17 years. Sabbatia, his mother, mourning the final end of her son, made this for herself and him.
EDCS-05401520.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased son, Alexander, who died at the age of 17.

EDCS-05401521.translation: Aurelius Alexander of Mezianai, village of the Apameans, lies here. If anyone dares to open this tomb apart from his own kin, he shall give one pound of gold to the temple treasury.
EDCS-05401521.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a penalty clause, warning against desecration of the tomb of Aurelius Alexander from Mezianai.

EDCS-05401522.translation: Aurelius Aurelianus, veteran, acquired this chest from his own funds while alive. If anyone wishes to place [someone] here violently, let him pay one denarius to the treasury.
EDCS-05401522.summary: This is an epitaph purchased by a veteran, Aurelius Aurelianus, with a penalty for unauthorized burial.

EDCS-05401523.translation: Aurelius Bassus, a new convert from Zophai, village of the Apameans, lies here. If anyone dares to open this chest apart from his own kin, he shall give one pound of gold to the high priest's treasury.
EDCS-05401523.summary: This funerary inscription from the village of Zophai includes a fine for unauthorized opening of the tomb of Aurelius Bassus.

EDCS-05401524.translation: Aurilius Gaudentius and Martina acquired [this] for themselves while alive. If anyone does them an injury, [he shall pay] one pound of gold.
EDCS-05401524.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurilius Gaudentius and Martina, who purchased their burial plot while alive, with a penalty for those who disturb it.

EDCS-05401525.translation: Aurelius Gennadius, a new convert from Alanon, village of the Apameans, lies here. If anyone dares to open this chest, he shall give one pound of gold to the temple treasury. However, it is permitted for his kin.
EDCS-05401525.summary: This funerary inscription from the village of Alanon stipulates a penalty for unauthorized burial in the tomb of Aurelius Gennadius, a convert.

EDCS-05401526.translation: Aurelius Makedonios, son of Abbivas, from the settlement of Genneos, of the Apameans, lies here. If anyone dares to open this chest apart from his own kin, he shall give one pound of gold to the temple treasury.
EDCS-05401526.summary: This funerary inscription from the settlement of Genneos warns against unauthorized opening of the tomb of Aurelius Makedonios.

EDCS-05401527.translation: Aurelius Malchos, a new convert from Medianon, village of the Apameans, lies here. If anyone dares to open this chest apart from his brothers, he shall give one pound of gold to the supreme temple treasury.
EDCS-05401527.summary: This funerary inscription for Aurelius Malchos, a convert from Medianon, imposes a penalty for opening his tomb except by his brothers.

EDCS-05401528.translation: Aurelius Marianos, son of Maros, from the settlement of Sekla, of the Apameans, in the region of Syria, lies here. If anyone dares to open this tomb apart from his own kin, he shall give three ounces of gold to the temple treasury.
EDCS-05401528.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Marianos from the settlement of Sekla, specifying a penalty for unauthorized disturbance of his tomb.

EDCS-05401529.translation: Aurelius Olbanos, son of Alexandros, from the settlement of Sekla, of the Apameans, in Coele Syria, lies here. He was a young man of 30 years. If anyone dares to open this tomb apart from his own kin, he shall give one pound of gold to the temple treasury. Year 170.
EDCS-05401529.summary: This funerary inscription for Aurelius Olbanos, a 30-year-old man from Sekla, includes a penalty for unauthorized opening and is dated to the year 170.

EDCS-05401530.translation: Aurelius Sammos and Firmīnos the newly baptized, Syrians from the village of Magaratarichoi, borders of Apoma, where he is laid to rest. If anyone dares to move this boundary stone without the consent of his family, he shall give 2 pounds of gold to the treasurer of the sacred treasury.
EDCS-05401530.summary: This Greek inscription from Apoma sets a penalty in gold for disturbing a boundary stone, likely related to a burial.

EDCS-05401531.translation: Here is laid to rest Aurelius Ouranis, son of Heraskonaon, from the village of Sascha, borders of Epiphaneis, of the valley of Syria. If anyone dares to move this sarcophagus, he shall give 1 pound of gold to the temple treasury. Year 328.
EDCS-05401531.summary: This Greek inscription from Syria records the burial of Aurelius Ouranis and sets a penalty in gold for disturbing his sarcophagus, dated to 328.

EDCS-05401532.translation: To the spirits (of the dead). Aurelia Alexandria bought this chest for myself and for my sweetest husband Flavius Sopatus, who lived with me for 19 years. Thus, after our death, let no one believe they can violate the same chest. Whoever does so shall give 20 solidi to the treasury or 50 ounces in silver.
EDCS-05401532.summary: This Latin inscription records Aurelia Alexandria purchasing a burial chest for herself and her husband Flavius Sopatus, with a penalty for violation.

EDCS-05401533.translation: Aurelia Diunisia lived 9 years, 7 months, 7 days with her grandmother Ap. If anyone wishes to open her (tomb), he shall give 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401533.summary: This Latin inscription records the short life of Aurelia Diunisia and sets a penalty in silver for opening her burial.

EDCS-05401534.translation: Aurelia Dionisia, who lived for 9 years, 7 months, and [illegible] days. If anyone wishes to break into her tomb, they owe the treasury 5 pounds of silver.
EDCS-05401534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelia Dionisia, recording her age and imposing a penalty in silver for desecrating her tomb.

EDCS-05401535.translation: Cocceius Ursus bought this chest for his incomparable wife Decentia, who lived with me for 11 years, 10 months, 25 days, so that I also might be placed with her after my death.
EDCS-05401535.summary: This Latin inscription records Cocceius Ursus purchasing a burial chest for his wife Decentia, intending to be buried with her.

EDCS-05401536.translation: Flavius Augustus, from the senior Mattiacorum, bought this chest for himself from his own property. Whoever wishes to open it shall give 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401536.summary: This Latin inscription records Flavius Augustus, a member of the Mattiacorum, purchasing a burial chest with a penalty for violation.

EDCS-05401537.translation: Flavius Alatancus, a domestic official, and his wife Bitorta bought this chest for themselves from their own property. We ask all the clergy and the entire brotherhood that no one from our family or anyone else be placed in this sepulcher. It is written, 'What you do not wish to be done to you, do not do to another.'
EDCS-05401537.summary: This Latin inscription records Flavius Alatancus and his wife Bitorta purchasing a burial chest and forbidding others from being buried there, citing the Golden Rule.

EDCS-05401538.translation: Flavius Ampius, a semissalis from the senior Mattiacorum, placed this chest for himself from his own property. Whoever wishes to open it shall give 10 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401538.summary: This Latin inscription records Flavius Ampius, a member of the Mattiacorum, acquiring a burial chest with a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401539.translation: Flavius Servilius Otraustaguta and Ilateuta Felicitas bought this chest from their labor for Flavius Andius, a centenarian of the bracchiatorum, their excellent colleague. We entrust this chest to the holy church of the city of Concord. Whoever wishes to open it shall give 2 pounds of gold to the treasury without delay.
EDCS-05401539.summary: This Latin inscription records colleagues purchasing a burial chest for Flavius Andius and entrusting it to the church, with a penalty in gold for disturbance.

EDCS-05401540.translation: Flavius Aristo, the faithful chief physician, and Aurelia Veneria, the faithful wife, dearest spouses, bought this bodily chest for themselves while alive from their own property. Whoever wishes to open it after their death shall give 80 solidi to the public treasury, and also whatever is permitted above concerning our people.
EDCS-05401540.summary: This Latin inscription records a physician and his wife purchasing a burial chest for themselves and setting a penalty in solidi for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401541.translation: Flavius Calladinus, a veteran, served in the arrow-making factory. He lived about 80 years. He purchased this tomb for himself from his own property. Whoever opens it shall pay one pound of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401541.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavius Calladinus, a veteran, detailing his service and the penalty for unauthorized burial.

EDCS-05401542.translation: Flavius Carpilio, a domestic officer from the senior Batavian contingent, who lived 30 years, purchased this tomb for himself from his own property. Whoever wishes to open it shall pay 5 pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401542.summary: This tomb inscription is for Flavius Carpilio, a domestic officer, specifying the cost for unauthorized burial.

EDCS-05401543.translation: Flavius Dassiolus, a veteran from the junior Mattiacan contingent, purchased this tomb for himself, and also for his son Variosus. Whoever wishes to open it after their death shall pay 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401543.summary: This tomb inscription is for Flavius Dassiolus, a veteran, and his son Variosus, stipulating a penalty for unauthorized burial in silver.

EDCS-05401544.translation: I commend my tomb to the most revered clergy of the city of Concord. Flavius Diocles, a centurion of the auxiliary Palatine unit, placed in this tomb. Whoever wishes to place themselves here shall pay three pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401544.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavius Diocles, a centurion, dedicating his tomb to the clergy and setting a fee for future burials.

EDCS-05401545.translation: Flavius Exsuperantius and Constantia dedicated this memorial to their dearest son, Marinus, who lived 18 years, 10 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-05401545.summary: This is a memorial dedication by Flavius Exsuperantius and Constantia for their son, Marinus.

EDCS-05401546.translation: Flavius Fandigildus, a protector from the shield-bearer contingent, purchased this tomb for himself while alive. Whoever wishes to open it shall pay six ounces of gold to the treasury, and shall also commend the tomb itself to the church.
EDCS-05401546.summary: This tomb inscription is for Flavius Fandigildus, a protector, with a penalty for unauthorized burial and a stipulation for the tomb's commendation to the church.

EDCS-05401547.translation: Flavius Felix and Lucia, his wife, made this for themselves from their own property while alive, so that no one may be placed in this burial after our death. Whoever does so shall pay two pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401547.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavius Felix and his wife Lucia, reserving the burial space and setting a penalty for unauthorized use.

EDCS-05401548.translation: Flavius Gidnadius, a deserving veteran, and Emilia Apra, purchased this tomb for themselves from their own labor on Concordian soil. After our death, whoever wishes to open it shall pay 10 solidi to the treasury.
EDCS-05401548.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavius Gidnadius, a veteran, and Emilia Apra, purchased from their labor and stipulating a payment for unauthorized burial.

EDCS-05401549.translation: Flavius Hariso, first master of the senior Herulian contingent, purchased this tomb from his own property. Whoever wishes to open it shall pay two pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401549.summary: This tomb inscription is for Flavius Hariso, a leader of the Herulian contingent, with a penalty for unauthorized burial.

EDCS-05401550.translation: Flavius Ianuarinus, a veteran from the junior Mattiacan contingent, is buried here. Whoever wishes to open his tomb shall pay 10 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401550.summary: This tomb inscription is for Flavius Ianuarinus, a veteran, and states the penalty for disturbing his burial.

EDCS-05401551.translation: To Flavius Launio, senator, from the unit of Batavian seniors, who lived 40 years. If anyone wishes to open this tomb, he will owe two pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401551.summary: A tomb inscription from a Batavian senior who lived 40 years, with a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401552.translation: Flavius Marcaridus, military tribune of the Iovii Iuniores, who lived 45 years. If anyone bothers her, he will owe one pound of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401552.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Marcaridus, a military tribune, who lived 45 years, with a penalty for disturbance.

EDCS-05401553.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavius Martinianus, biarchus of the fabricensis, made this for himself and Aurelia Severiana his wife, during his lifetime. After death, if anyone wishes to [open it], he will give three ounces of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401553.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Martinianus and his wife Aurelia Severiana, a biarchus of the fabricensis, with a penalty for opening.

EDCS-05401554.translation: Flavius Mansuetus, a biarchus who served in the unit of the senior Lions, placed this tomb for himself from his own property. If anyone wishes to open it, he will give ten pounds of silver to the treasury, a tomb which he commended to the veterans.
EDCS-05401554.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Mansuetus, a biarchus of the senior Lions, who set up his own tomb and commended it to veterans.

EDCS-05401555.translation: To Flavius Maximianus, dearest loyal son. Flavius Maximianus the loyal father bought this tomb for himself during his lifetime from his own property.
EDCS-05401555.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Maximianus, a son, purchased by his father Flavius Maximianus.

EDCS-05401556.translation: Flavius Mercurius, biarchus fabricensis, and Flavia Ursa his wife, bought this during their lifetime from their own property. If anyone wishes to open it after their death, he will owe two pounds of gold.
EDCS-05401556.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Mercurius, a biarchus fabricensis, and his wife Flavia Ursa, purchased from their own property.

EDCS-05401557.translation: Flavius Roveos, centenarius from the unit of senior horse archers, placed this tomb for himself from his own property. If anyone wishes to open it, he will owe five pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401557.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Roveos, a centenarius of senior horse archers, with a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401558.translation: Flavius Savinus, ducenarius from the unit of Batavian seniors, lived approximately fifty years. He bought this tomb for himself from his own property. If anyone wishes to open it, let him bring two pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401558.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Savinus, a ducenarius of Batavian seniors, who lived around 50 years and purchased his own tomb.

EDCS-05401559.translation: They bought this tomb for Flavius Sauma, a biarchus from the unit of armed horsemen. His brother Viax and senator Alacildus, a biarchus, purchased it. If anyone wishes to open it, he will owe one pound of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401559.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Sauma, a biarchus of armed horsemen, purchased by his brother and another biarchus.

EDCS-05401560.translation: Flavius Victurinus, from the unit of Batavian seniors, who lived approximately 35 years. This tomb was bought for him with the fruits of his own labor. Whoever wishes to open this tomb will have his hands cut off by law, or else he will owe one pound of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401560.summary: A tomb inscription for Flavius Victurinus, a Batavian senior who lived about 35 years, purchased with his own earnings, with severe penalties for opening.

EDCS-05401561.translation: Flavius Victurus, from the unit of Nervian archers, who lived approximately 27 years. A burial chest was bought for him from his own earnings, and whoever wishes to open it will have their hands cut off by law or pay 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401561.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Victurus, an archer, recording the purchase of his burial chest and the penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401562.translation: Flavia Concordia set up a burial chest for herself from her own property. Whoever wishes to open it will pay ten pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401562.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Concordia, detailing the provision of her burial chest and a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401563.translation: Flavia Optata, wife of a soldier from the Regian unit, bought a burial chest for herself from her husband's property. Whoever wishes to open it after my death will pay one pound of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401563.summary: This funerary inscription records Flavia Optata, wife of a soldier, acquiring her burial chest and stipulating a penalty for unauthorized access.

EDCS-05401564.translation: I, Gerontia, purchased a burial chest for myself from my own property. Whoever wishes to open it will pay 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401564.summary: This is a personal funerary inscription by Gerontia, who purchased her own burial chest and set a penalty for its unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401567.translation: Burial chest for Manio, a soldier from the Bructerian unit. If anyone opens it, his hands will be cut off or he will pay two pounds of gold to the treasury, under our consuls Arcadius and Honorius Augusti.
EDCS-05401567.summary: This funerary inscription, dated to the consulship of Arcadius and Honorius, records a burial chest for the soldier Manio and the penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401568.translation: Oppius Marinus bought a burial chest for himself from his own labor and ordered it to be inscribed thus: after his death, if any outsider wishes to be buried in it, they will pay six pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401568.summary: This funerary inscription by Oppius Marinus records the purchase of his burial chest and specifies conditions and a penalty for an outsider to be buried with him.

EDCS-05401569.translation: Burial chest for Numerianus, a principalis from the city of Mursa, aged 30. If anyone wishes to open this chest, they will pay six ounces of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-05401569.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial chest of Numerianus, a principalis from Mursa, and stipulates a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401570.translation: Saturninus, a centenarian from the office of the prefect of Illyricum Dacia Ripensis, buried by his friends.
EDCS-05401570.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription for Saturninus, a centenarian official, indicating he was buried by friends.

EDCS-05401571.translation: Turranius Honoratus to Aurelia Iovina, his dearest wife, who lived with me for 10 years and 2 months. Whoever wishes to open it will pay five pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401571.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication from Turranius Honoratus to his wife Aurelia Iovina, noting their time together and a penalty for unauthorized opening of her burial chest.

EDCS-05401572.translation: A burial chest for Vassio, a campidoctor from the unit of Batavorum seniorum, whom his wife Andacca buried. She lived with him for 22 years, he served for 35 years, she will live sixty years. Whoever wishes to move this chest will pay 25 solidi to the treasury.
EDCS-05401572.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial chest for Vassio, a campidoctor, with details about his wife Andacca and their lifespan, and a penalty for disturbing the chest.

EDCS-05401573.translation: Valeria Peregrina bought a sarcophagus at her own expense, into which she ordered herself to be placed and her name to be inscribed.
EDCS-05401573.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the purchase and arrangement for burial of a sarcophagus by Valeria Peregrina.

EDCS-05401574.translation: Flavius Vitalinianus and Flavius Severus bought a sarcophagus at their own expense and acquired it for themselves; whoever wishes to open it will pay ten pounds of silver to the public treasury.
EDCS-05401574.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Flavius Vitalinianus and Flavius Severus purchased a sarcophagus for themselves and stipulated a fine for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401575.translation: In this sarcophagus lies Ursacius, a biarch from the senior Batavian cohort, who lived for 30 years; whoever wishes to open it must pay two pounds of gold to the public treasury.
EDCS-05401575.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ursacius, a biarch of Batavian origin, specifying a penalty for opening his sarcophagus.

EDCS-05401576.translation: Terco, a centurion (ducenario), who served in the 8th Dalmatian cavalry, bought a sarcophagus for himself at his own expense; whoever wishes to open it will pay ten pounds of silver to the public treasury for my god ECI Vera.
EDCS-05401576.summary: This funerary inscription records the purchase of a sarcophagus by Terco, a centurion in the Dalmatian cavalry, and sets a fine for its opening, dedicated to a deity.

EDCS-05401583.translation: Gaius Attius Apro made this for Gaius Attius Maximi, his well-deserving son, during his lifetime.
EDCS-05401583.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription where Gaius Attius Apro dedicated a tomb for his deserving son, Gaius Attius Maximi, during his own lifetime.

EDCS-05401584.translation: For Quintus Cassius Crescens: 25 feet in front, 13 feet in the rear.
EDCS-05401584.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a plot of land or tomb belonging to Quintus Cassius Crescens.

EDCS-05401586.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication naming Lucius Valerius Megabocchus.

EDCS-05401587.translation: Publius Veneteius Philostratus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-05401587.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Publius Veneteius Philostratus, a freedman, and his patron.

EDCS-05401595.translation: Quintus Carminius Optatus, to the Lares.
EDCS-05401595.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Quintus Carminius Optatus to the household gods (Lares).

EDCS-05401596.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Safinia Festa and her father, Quintus.

EDCS-05401597.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Maximus for himself and his dearest wife Cassia Marcelli. He dedicated this. (3 letters).
EDCS-05401597.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavius Maximus for himself and his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401598.summary: A dedication to a wife named Jan Rufi, possibly a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-05401599.translation: Lucius Saufeius Clemens, son of Lucius, of the Claudian tribe, gave a covered portico and a sun-dial.
EDCS-05401599.summary: A dedication recording the gift of a portico and sun-dial by Lucius Saufeius Clemens, likely a public benefactor from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-05401600.translation: To the Fateful, Conserving Gods. Vettius Secundus, mindful.
EDCS-05401600.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the Fates by Vettius Secundus, possibly related to a vow for preservation.

EDCS-05401601.translation: Tiberius Poblicius Felix willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05401601.summary: This is a votive inscription by Tiberius Poblicius Felix, likely a private individual, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-05401602.translation: Igonius Faber gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Luccianus.
EDCS-05401602.summary: A votive inscription where Igonius Faber fulfills a vow to Luccianus, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401604.translation: V. Saitina gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-05401604.summary: A votive inscription where V. Saitina fulfills a vow, possibly marking the completion of a promise.

EDCS-05401605.translation: The bathhouse, destroyed by fire [---]. Under the supervision of Publius Acilius, son of Publius, from Rome, [---] curator of the republic [---].
EDCS-05401605.summary: An inscription concerning the reconstruction of a public bathhouse destroyed by fire, mentioning a curator of the republic and a local dignitary, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05401607.translation: Manius Naevidius Phainus Augustalis made this living for his patroness, Occ Naevidia Melae, daughter of Mela.
EDCS-05401607.summary: A dedication made by a freedman, Manius Naevidius Phainus Augustalis, for his patroness, Occ Naevidia Melae.

EDCS-05401616.translation: To the Divine Manes. Quintus Spedius Mercator, heir from the same place, erected this for the well-deserving Quintus Turellius Rufus, trierarch of the ship *Venera*, a Sardinian by birth, who lived 45 years and served 25 years.
EDCS-05401616.summary: This funerary inscription honors Quintus Turellius Rufus, a trierarch from Sardinia, and was erected by his heir Quintus Spedius Mercator.

EDCS-05401617.translation: Atilius Mus, freedman of Lucius, a member of the college of six, [left money] in his will for the freedmen of Nigra Theris.
EDCS-05401617.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that Atilius Mus, a freedman and member of the college of six, left provisions in his will for the freedmen of Nigra Theris.

EDCS-05401618.translation: Quintus Veronius Silvester [dedicated this] to Lucius Antonius Verus, the best.
EDCS-05401618.summary: A dedication by Quintus Veronius Silvester to Lucius Antonius Verus, likely a dedication of a monument or statue.

EDCS-05401619.translation: Caius Aperi Suavis made this for himself and for Gaius Cassius Primus, son of Quintus, during his lifetime.
EDCS-05401619.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Caius Aperi Suavis for himself and another individual, likely indicating a personal memorial.

EDCS-05401620.translation: Didius Philetianus erected this for his most sweet wife, Cassia Secundina, while he was alive.
EDCS-05401620.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a husband, Didius Philetianus, for his wife Cassia Secundina during his lifetime.

EDCS-05401621.translation: To the divine spirits of Iulia Primitiva, deceased, aged 8, daughter of Flavia Soteris, most unhappy, most beloved.
EDCS-05401621.summary: This is a tombstone set up for a young girl, Iulia Primitiva, highlighting her age and the grief of her mother.

EDCS-05401622.translation: To Lucrio, son of Canius, and to Lucius Turillius Caesoni, son of Lucius, father.
EDCS-05401622.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to two individuals, one named Lucrio and the other Lucius Turillius Caesoni, who is identified as a father.

EDCS-05401623.translation: Siarius Gemus made this during his lifetime.
EDCS-05401623.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Siarius Gemus for himself while he was still alive.

EDCS-05401624.translation: Lucius Tatius Socrus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-05401624.summary: This is an epitaph or identification of Lucius Tatius Socrus, indicating his status as a freedman and his former patron.

EDCS-05401625.translation: To the divine spirits of Manilia Elpis, to Vero, her most beloved husband.
EDCS-05401625.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Manilia Elpis, intended for her most beloved husband, Vero.

EDCS-05401626.translation: Marcus Iulius, son of Marcus, a veteran.
EDCS-05401626.summary: This is an identification of Marcus Iulius, son of Marcus, who served as a military veteran.

EDCS-05401627.translation: Publicius Peregrinus, son of Gaius, VI vir C V.
EDCS-05401627.summary: This identifies Publicius Peregrinus, son of Gaius, and notes his membership in the college of VI viri, with the abbreviation C V likely referring to his status or role.

EDCS-05401629.translation: To Publius Iuventius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, father; to Lucretia; [daughter?]
EDCS-05401629.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication for a father, Publius Iuventius, and potentially his daughter Lucretia, indicating familial relationships.

EDCS-05401630.summary: This inscription likely records a person named Nymphius in relation to Rutilia Celido, possibly as a slave or freedman.

EDCS-05401631.translation: Phryxus, freedman of Lucius [vius], goldsmith, erected this for himself while alive.
EDCS-05401631.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Phryxus, a goldsmith and freedman, for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-05401632.translation: To Lotteia Primigenia and to her most dutiful son Lotteius Primigenius, from Lotteia Lucifera, their mother, for their well-deserving.
EDCS-05401632.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a mother to her daughter and grandson, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401635.summary: This very brief inscription identifies a person, likely a gravestone or boundary marker, dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-05401636.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the goddess Fortuna, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401637.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Firmius Cogitatus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05401637.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter, made by Gaius Firmius Cogitatus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401639.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Epidius Adiutor willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05401639.summary: This is a votive inscription to Saturn Augustus, made by Lucius Epidius Adiutor, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401642.translation: Marcus Caecilius Ascanius, freedman of Marcus Caecilius, a college priest of the Six, for himself and for Marcus Caecilius Deuteros, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-05401642.summary: This funerary inscription is for Marcus Caecilius Ascanius, a priest of a college, and his freedman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401643.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication or honorific text for an official named Porcius iralis, the aedile, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05401645.translation: Of Festus, the clerk from Verona.
EDCS-05401645.summary: This inscription identifies Festus, a clerk from Verona, likely a funerary or property marker from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401646.translation: Lucius Aemilius Niger, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and for Octavia Nota, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-05401646.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Aemilius Niger for himself and his freedwoman partner, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401648.translation: Manius Clodius Candidus made this while alive for himself and for his deserving wife Maesia Helpidi, who lived with me for 15 years without any complaint. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-05401648.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Manius Clodius Candidus for himself and his wife, recording their years of marriage and invoking the departed spirits, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05401649.translation: Marcus Cornelius Crescens and Valeria Tertia, daughter of Sextus, made this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-05401649.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus Cornelius Crescens and his wife Valeria Tertia for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-05401650.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Eros, slave of our two Emperors, set up this monument for Attia Restuta, his respected mother-in-law and mistress, who deserved well; I set up the inscription and wrote the letters.
EDCS-05401650.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a slave named Eros to his deceased mother-in-law and mistress, Attia Restuta, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-05401651.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or names individuals, possibly Lucius Herennius Saturninus and another person named Sur.

EDCS-05401652.summary: This inscription lists the names of three freedmen: Hermetis, Eutyches, and Syntyche, possibly indicating a group memorial or dedication.

EDCS-05401654.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Titus Matius as a freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-05401655.translation: Caius Nar, son of Lucius, of the Livia tribe.
EDCS-05401655.summary: This inscription identifies Caius Nar by his name, father, and tribal affiliation (Livia).

EDCS-05401656.translation: Caius Papirius, son of Sextus, of the Romilia tribe, father; Lucilia Titia, daughter of Titus; Lucius Papirius Vitulus, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-05401656.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, Caius Papirius, Lucilia Titia, and Lucius Papirius Vitulus, including their filiations and tribal affiliations (Romilia).

EDCS-05401657.translation: Secundinus Uxxoalli son, Mansueta Modesti daughter, Primigenius Secundini son, Tertia Ploti daughter, Martialis Secundini son, Quinta Senec.
EDCS-05401657.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names with filiations, possibly related to a family or group.

EDCS-05401658.translation: To Ortii N, mother Sulpiciae, daughter of Caius Lai, sister Caio Sulpicio Senic, brother Sulpicio, brother AI.
EDCS-05401658.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Ortii N, likely a mother, and lists other family members including a sister and brothers.

EDCS-05401660.translation: Publius Sertorius Optatus, freedman of Publius, and Calventia Mansueta made this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-05401660.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Publius Sertorius Optatus and Calventia Mansueta for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-05401662.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Tertia.

EDCS-05401663.translation: To Tullia, daughter of Caius, Secunda.
EDCS-05401663.summary: A funerary dedication to Tullia Secunda.

EDCS-05401664.translation: To Valeria, daughter of Publius, Maxima.
EDCS-05401664.summary: A funerary dedication to Valeria Maxima.

EDCS-05401666.translation: Quarta, daughter of Cia and Caius, made this monument; it shall not bind her heir.
EDCS-05401666.summary: A funerary monument set up by Quarta, specifying that it does not bind her heir.

EDCS-05401667.translation: [---]cila erected this for herself and for her sons, Quintus Clodius Licinus, son of Quintus, and C. Clodius [---]inus, son of Quintus M[---], while alive.
EDCS-05401667.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by [---]cila for herself and her sons, indicating family burial arrangements.

EDCS-05401668.translation: Valeria Maxima, daughter of Publius, erected this for her husband [---]ius Plos[---]o, her son Lucius Opsidius Severus, and her son Caius Opsidius Geminus, while alive.
EDCS-05401668.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Valeria Maxima for her deceased husband and sons.

EDCS-05401669.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning the name Carina.

EDCS-05401670.translation: While alive, Caius Tenatius [---] erected this for Secunda Octavia, daughter of Caius, wife of Caius Tenatius, aged 23, and for Lucius Tenatius, son of Lucius, aged 22.
EDCS-05401670.summary: This is a family funerary monument erected by Caius Tenatius for his wife Secunda Octavia and his son Lucius Tenatius.

EDCS-05401671.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Martialis lived 4 years, 5 months, 5 days. Eutychus [made this dedication].
EDCS-05401671.summary: A funerary dedication recording the lifespan of Martialis, likely set up by Eutychus.

EDCS-05401672.translation: Clara, freedwoman of a woman, to herself and to Lucius Ofatorius, freedman of Lucius, her partner, and to her own family. She made this while alive; no future event ever separated us.
EDCS-05401672.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Clara for herself, her partner Lucius Ofatorius, and their family, emphasizing their inseparable bond.

EDCS-05401676.translation: To Orina, daughter of Caius, Aure... the most distinguished man... me.
EDCS-05401676.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning Orina and a distinguished man, possibly a dedication or a funerary text.

EDCS-05401677.translation: To Ioni, praefect of Germania, Marcus Caecilius.
EDCS-05401677.summary: A dedication to Ioni, a prefect of Germania, by Marcus Caecilius.

EDCS-05401678.translation: Lucius Livius, one of the IIII viri, Lucius Li...
EDCS-05401678.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning Lucius Livius, a member of the IIII viri, likely a public or religious office.

EDCS-05401680.translation: To Ximinus, most excellent, from Eustrius and Loria, his very dear wife.
EDCS-05401680.summary: This is an epitaph for Ximinus, set up by his wife Loria and Eustrius, likely an inscription from a tomb.

EDCS-05401683.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Primius son of Enstalipon fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05401683.summary: A dedication to Jupiter, fulfilling a vow by Primius, son of Enstalipon, possibly from an altar or shrine.

EDCS-05401684.translation: For himself and for Titus Laronius, his son, of the Quirina tribe, his most excellent husband; and for Laronius, son of Titus Laronius, of the Quirina tribe, a member of the equestrian order; and for Laronius, son of Titus Laronius, of the Quirina tribe, his most dutiful sons; and for Laronius Hilario and Octavia Secunda, daughter of Titus, his parents-in-law.
EDCS-05401684.summary: A funerary inscription detailing a family, possibly set up by a wife for her husband and sons, and mentioning parents-in-law.

EDCS-05401685.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ulda Marius.

EDCS-05401761.text_edition: \n Quinto Axilio Urbico viro perfectissimo magistro sacrarum cognitionum a studiis et a consiliis Auggustorum Aquileienses publice patrono praestantissimo decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-05401761.translation: The people of Aquileia publicly honored Quintus Axilius Urbicus, most excellent husband, master of sacred legal proceedings, from the studies and councils of the Augusti, and their most outstanding patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05401761.summary: This is a public honorific inscription from the city of Aquileia dedicated to Quintus Axilius Urbicus, recognizing his service as a legal advisor to the emperors.

EDCS-05401762.translation: Lucius Petronius Fuscus, duovir. Titus Heius Speratus. Publius Gavius Clemens. Titus Novanius Passer. Marcus Petronius Pamphilus. Marcus Petronius Primus. Publius Trosius Gamus. Lucius Annavos Speratus. Caius Minicius Montanus. Lucius Petronius Severus. Lucius Petronius Doctus. Quintus Albius Pudens. Lucius Fullonius Iucundus. Quintus Licovius Optatus. Lucius Petronius Licco. Caius Egnatius Priscus. Caelia Ingenua. Petronia Sperata. Monument location: 10 feet in front, [---] feet in the field.
EDCS-05401762.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including a duovir and other prominent citizens, along with burial plot dimensions, suggesting it relates to a communal burial space or a dedication of land for burials.

EDCS-05401763.translation: Whoever knew Alexandria, I ask you to read a few words, and go away grieving, or feel no grief, for there is no pain where there is nothing. You killed as you perished.
EDCS-05401763.summary: An epitaph for Alexandria, found in Alexandria, reflecting on death and oblivion.

EDCS-05401764.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. [Son/daughter?] of Caeus, son/daughter? of Caeus. [Name?] Fucapus.
EDCS-05401764.summary: A fragmented epitaph for members of the Caena family, dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed.

EDCS-05401765.translation: Chrestus, his freedwoman, set this up.
EDCS-05401765.summary: A funerary inscription indicating a freedwoman named Chrestus set up a monument for someone.

EDCS-05401766.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Her heirs set this up for Flavia Icone, who deserved well.
EDCS-05401766.summary: An epitaph for Flavia Icone, set up by her deserving heirs and dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed.

EDCS-05401769.translation: To Pris and his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05401769.summary: An inscription dedicating a space or monument to Pris and his descendants, including freed slaves.

EDCS-05401770.translation: Lucius Safinius Sabellius, son of Lucius. His father [...]
EDCS-05401770.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription, likely recording the name of Lucius Safinius Sabellius and his father.

EDCS-05401771.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely identifying ownership or a dedication by Caius Vettius Aeschinus.

EDCS-05401776.translation: For Bona, Pascentius sought rest in the house before she completed her innocent age, in peace she rests; in the tomb, in the place of Cerbonia, his most sweet wife, who did not enjoy riches and completed the eternal light, who lived 35 years, 6 months, 12 days, and for his most innocent son Pascentius, who lived 3 years, 5 months, 7 days. And grieving, his husband Fugantius set this up against his will, laid in peace, the faithful one, the day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-05401776.summary: A funerary epitaph for Bona, her son Pascentius, and wife Cerbonia, set up by Fugantius, providing detailed ages and dates.

EDCS-05401777.translation: Claudia Artimisia, while alive, set this up for herself.
EDCS-05401777.summary: A self-dedicated funerary monument set up by Claudia Artimisia during her lifetime.

EDCS-05401778.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Cusica Sabina set this up while alive for herself and for her dearest husband, Ennius Paccius.
EDCS-05401778.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed, set up by Cusica Sabina for herself and her husband Ennius Paccius.

EDCS-05401779.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead: Flavius Ligurius and Cricia Victorina, while alive, set this up for themselves.
EDCS-05401779.summary: A funerary inscription where Flavius Ligurius and Cricia Victorina set up a monument for themselves.

EDCS-05401780.translation: I, Baicca the magister, purchased a chest for myself from my own funds. If anyone wishes to open it, they will owe 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401780.summary: A self-purchased chest inscription by Baicca, a magister, with a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-05401781.translation: Flavius Constantius, bereft by the loss and sorrow of his most dutiful son Eutherius, erected this memorial for his body, whose sight I trust will bring some solace. He lived 28 years.
EDCS-05401781.summary: A memorial stone erected by Flavius Constantius for his deceased son Eutherius, who lived 28 years, expressing grief and hope for solace.

EDCS-05401782.translation: Ennia Asteria, daughter of Ennius Asterius, from the lineage of her grandfather Ennius Cerealis, renewed the chest in her own name. After her death, if anyone breaks into it, they will owe 200,000 sesterces to the treasury accounts; her children, however, will have leave.
EDCS-05401782.summary: A funerary inscription by Ennia Asteria, renewing a chest and stipulating a penalty for unauthorized access after her death, with an exemption for her children.

EDCS-05401783.translation: Here lies Lexes. Reader, [name?] of Piterma, who sailed small for thirty-five years. If anyone excavates, let them give twenty-five litres of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-05401783.summary: A bilingual (Greek/Latin) epitaph for Lexes, a sailor who died at 35, with a penalty for disturbing the grave.

EDCS-05401784.translation: Quintus Fabius Nicephor, at Aquae Apollinares.
EDCS-05401784.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Quintus Fabius Nicephor, possibly related to the spa town of Aquae Apollinares.

EDCS-05801459.translation: Caius Servilius Septidianus Firmus, Marcus Martius Torquatus, Quintus Pinnius Valerianus, Saxius Marius Calestrius Maximus, and Horatius Macer, the Seven Commissioners for Feasts, made this for the Mother Goddess of Idaea.
EDCS-05801459.summary: A dedication to the Mother Goddess of Idaea by a group of seven high-ranking priests (quindecimviri epulonum).

EDCS-06100239.translation: The place of Caius Numisius Nepos and Mamia.
EDCS-06100239.summary: This is a property boundary marker, likely from the Imperial period, indicating ownership of Caius Numisius Nepos and Mamia.

EDCS-07000484.text_edition: \n Locus Marci Miledi Marcelli quoquov(ersus) pedes XVI\n
EDCS-07000484.translation: To Marcus Miledius Marcellus, 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-07000484.summary: This inscription records a boundary marker for Marcus Miledius Marcellus, indicating a plot of land measuring 16 feet in each direction.

EDCS-07000488.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae Primitibo sic qui vixit annus sic XXII mensis IIII dies XV depositus XI Kalendas Octobres in pace fidelis\n
EDCS-07000488.translation: To good memory, Primitivus, who lived 22 years, 4 months, and 15 days, was placed in peace on the 11th day before the Kalends of October, a faithful one.
EDCS-07000488.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Primitivus, a faithful person who died at the age of 22 years, 4 months, and 15 days, and was buried on September 21st.

EDCS-07000490.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-07000490.text_edition: \n Hic requiescit Albucio in pace qui vixit annos XIIII et menses V dies X parentes carissimo d titulum posuer(unt)\n
EDCS-07000490.translation: Here rests Albucio, in peace, who lived 14 years and 5 months and 10 days; his parents placed this monument to their dearest son.
EDCS-07000490.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Albucio, who lived 14 years, 5 months, and 10 days, and was commemorated by his parents.

EDCS-07000492.text_edition: \n Immeritae filiae Augurinae innocenti parentes contra votum fecerunt quae vixit annis X diebus sic in pacae sic posita tertium Kalendas Martias\n
EDCS-07000492.translation: To their undeserving daughter Augurina, the innocent one, her parents made this against their will, who lived 10 years and some days; placed in peace on the third day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-07000492.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Augurina, who died at the age of 10 years, and was placed in peace on February 27th, with her parents noting the hardship of her early death.

EDCS-07000498.text_edition: \n Grata anicula Castus trimus frater et soror\n
EDCS-07000498.translation: To Grata, the dear old woman, her three-year-old brother and sister.
EDCS-07000498.summary: This is a dedication from a brother and sister to their dear old woman, Grata, with the brother specified as three years old.

EDCS-07400319.translation: Florentius made it with his people, 200 feet.
EDCS-07400319.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 200 feet by Florentius and his associates, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-07400320.translation: Aquilinus and Urania made it with their people, 300 feet.
EDCS-07400320.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 300 feet by Aquilinus and Urania and their associates, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-07400321.translation: Dalmatius the presbyter made it, 300 feet.
EDCS-07400321.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 300 feet by Dalmatia, a presbyter, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-07400322.translation: In honor of the blessed saints, Felicianus and Ingenua, sinners, made this.
EDCS-07400322.summary: This is a dedication to the saints Felicianus and Ingenua by Felicianus and Ingenua, who identify themselves as sinners, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-07400324.translation: To Publius Valerius Maron, his father Vergilius.
EDCS-07400324.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Publius Valerius Maro from his father, Vergilius.

EDCS-07400326.text_edition: \n Victorinus et virginia sua Verissima annos VIIII et mensis X posita est Verissima Verissimus cum filios sic suos sic vixsit sic Verissima annos XXII menses IV\n
EDCS-07400326.translation: Victorinus and his wife Verissima, 9 years and 10 months; Verissima was placed with her sons; Verissima lived 22 years, 4 months.
EDCS-07400326.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Verissima, who lived 22 years and 4 months, and was buried with her sons, with her husband Victorinus also mentioned.

EDCS-07400329.text_edition: \n Bene meretus sic Iovinus qui vixit annus sic plus meaus sic XXX mensis V et dies III recessit in pace fedelis sic deposetus sic III Nonas Septemiris sic\n
EDCS-07400329.translation: Well-deserving Iovinus, who lived more than 30 years, 5 months, and 3 days, departed in faithful peace, placed on the 3rd day before the Nones of September.
EDCS-07400329.summary: This epitaph honors Iovinus, who lived over 30 years, 5 months, and 3 days, and was buried on September 2nd.

EDCS-07400331.translation: To the Liberator of the Roman world, restorer of liberty and the republic, preserver of soldiers and provincials, our lord Magnentius, unconquered prince, victor and triumphant, always Augustus.
EDCS-07400331.summary: This is a lengthy acclamation of the emperor Magnentius, highlighting his titles and perceived achievements, likely dating to his reign (350-353 AD).

EDCS-07400333.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that names Marcus Paconius Lucius Trebius and possibly the beginning of a cognomen or cognomen like 'Hermes' or 'Herculanus'.

EDCS-07400334.translation: Paulus made it with his people, from the gift of God, 27 feet.
EDCS-07400334.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 27 feet by Paulus and his associates, attributing the work to divine inspiration, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-07400339.translation: Georgius and Olosericus made [it] with their people, feet.
EDCS-07400339.summary: This inscription records a construction project by Georgius and Olosericus, although the exact measurement is lost, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-07400341.text_edition: \n Publius Paetinius Publi libertus Aptus sibi et Attiae Peregrinae uxori et collegiatis gentilibus lanariorum purgatorum in fronte pedes XXXXV retro pedes XVIII vivus fecit\n
EDCS-07400341.translation: Publius Paetinius Aptus, freedman of Publius, made this for himself and for his wife Attia Peregrina and for the collegiates, kinsmen of the wool-cleaners, with 45 feet in front and 18 feet in the rear, while alive.
EDCS-07400341.summary: This is a funerary monument built by Publius Paetinius Aptus, a freedman, for himself, his wife Attia Peregrina, and fellow members of the wool-cleaners' guild, specifying dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-07400342.text_edition: \n Lucius Varius Marci filius Pudens vivus fecit sibi et Iuniae Mani filiae Maximae matri in fronte pedes XIV retro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-07400342.translation: Lucius Varius Pudens, son of Marcus, made this for himself and his mother, Iunia Maxima, daughter of Manus, with a frontage of 14 feet and a depth of 30 feet.
EDCS-07400342.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Varius Pudens and his mother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400343.text_edition: \n Titus Terentius Cai filius Pompeius Fabia et Lucania Mani liberta Fausta uxsor sic vivi sibi fecerunt locus sepulturae in fronte pedes retro pedes XXXX\n
EDCS-07400343.translation: Titus Terentius Pompeius, son of Caius, and his freedwoman wife, Fausta, daughter of Manus, and Lucania, made this tomb for themselves while alive, with a frontage of [unknown] feet and a depth of 40 feet.
EDCS-07400343.summary: This funerary epitaph records the tomb purchased by Titus Terentius Pompeius and his wife Fausta, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400344.text_edition: \n Luci Lemoni Titi filii Pittiacae Luci filiae Primullae in fronte pedes retro pedes \n
EDCS-07400344.translation: For Lucius Lemon, son of Titus, and his daughter, Primulla, daughter of Lucius, with a frontage of [unknown] feet and a depth of [unknown] feet.
EDCS-07400344.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Lucius Lemon and his daughter Primulla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400345.translation: In the consulship of Gaius Caesar and Marcus Lepidus.
EDCS-07400345.summary: This inscription records a date by mentioning the consuls Gaius Caesar (likely Julius Caesar) and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, placing it in 46 BC.

EDCS-07400346.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Quintus Spurius Senecio sibi et Quinto Spurio Secundo filio et Spuriae Augustinae filiae ex permissu collegii iumentariorum portae Ioviae\n
EDCS-07400346.translation: Quintus Spurius Senecio made this for himself and his son Quintus Spurius Secundus and his daughter Spuria Augustina while alive, with the permission of the association of beast-drivers of the Iovian Gate.
EDCS-07400346.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-made tomb by Quintus Spurius Senecio for himself and his children, approved by a collegium, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400347.text_edition: \n Laribus Augustis Licinius Mysticus tinctor tenuarius magisterio suo posuit Pro Campano\n
EDCS-07400347.translation: Licinius Mysticus, a wool-dyer, dedicated this to the Augustan Lares in his magistracy, for Pro Campus.
EDCS-07400347.summary: This is a dedication to the Lares Augusti by a fuller named Licinius Mysticus, likely during his term as a magistrate, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07600187.text_edition: \n Theodore felix adiuvante Deo omnipotente et poemnio caelitus tibi traditum sic omnia baeate sic fecisti et gloriose dicasti\n
EDCS-07600187.translation: Theodore, fortunate, with the all-powerful God assisting, and the mission divinely handed down to you, you have thus done all things blessedly and gloriously dedicated.
EDCS-07600187.summary: This is a commendatory inscription praising Theodore for divinely inspired success and dedication, likely Christian, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-07600191.summary: This is a very short funerary dedication for Edio, son of Arusnates, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07600192.text_edition: \n Lualdae Caius Poblicius Marci filius Capito flamen vovit MANISNAVIVS\n
EDCS-07600192.translation: Caius Poblicius Capito, son of Marcus, a priest, vowed to Lualda, the Manisnavius.
EDCS-07600192.summary: This inscription records a vow made by the priest Caius Poblicius Capito to Lualda, identified as a Manisnavius (possibly a guardian spirit or deity), dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07600194.text_edition: \n Pergemus Primus Tavanus deo Invicto sacrum\n
EDCS-07600194.translation: Pergemus Primus Tavanus, sacred to the unconquered god.
EDCS-07600194.summary: This is a dedication of something sacred to the unconquered god by Pergemus Primus Tavanus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07600195.summary: This is a very brief dedication to the unconquered god, likely by a group or individual named Genituri, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07600196.text_edition: \n rima Pittino Publi filio Reidavius aedilis coeravit de suo\n
EDCS-07600196.translation: Reidavius, son of Publius Pittinus, as aedile, saw to this at his own expense.
EDCS-07600196.summary: This is a building inscription from an aedile who funded the construction, likely a public work, at his own expense.

EDCS-08000002.translation: Apiaria Sabina, to her daughter, aged 56 years.
EDCS-08000002.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Apiaria Sabina, recording her name, relationship (daughter), and age at death, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08000003.translation: Primigenius fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08000003.summary: A freedman named Primigenius dedicates an offering, likely on a religious monument, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08000029.translation: To the divine shades. For Macia PII[...]. Titus Aelius [...]rus, freedman of Augustus, from the cognitions [case-related official duties? ...].
EDCS-08000029.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Macia, set up by Titus Aelius, a freedman of the emperor who held an administrative position, possibly from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-08000040.translation: [...] on the sixth pile from the front of the second Parthian legion, with eleven army stipends, as guardian of the arms.
EDCS-08000040.summary: This inscription likely refers to a soldier in the Legio II Parthica, possibly detailing his rank or duties and service duration.

EDCS-08000048.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording the name of a slave, Priscus, connected to the colonists of Aquileia.

EDCS-08000051.translation: To Marcus Tossius Rufus, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, a IIIIvir iure dicundo, from his brother Quintus Tossius, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, also a IIIIvir iure dicundo.
EDCS-08000051.summary: A funerary or honorary inscription from Aquileia dedicated by a brother to a deceased magistrate (IIIIvir iure dicundo).

EDCS-08000087.text_edition: \n Cai Dindi Familiaris sibi et suis Caio Dindio Cai liberto Claro locus monumenti quoquo versus pedes XVI\n
EDCS-08000087.translation: Caius Dindius Familialis [dedicates this] for himself and his family, and for Gaius Dindius Clarus, son of Caius Dindius. Monumental plot, sixteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-08000087.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking a burial plot, dedicated by Caius Dindius Familialis for himself, his family, and his freedman, Caius Dindius Clarus.

EDCS-08000091.translation: Place of the monument of F. (Freedman) of Quintus, of Orientis.
EDCS-08000091.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Orientis, a freedman of someone named Quintus.

EDCS-08000096.translation: Fulvius Faustinus, aged nineteen. Tedia Crispina [erected this] to her son-in-law.
EDCS-08000096.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fulvius Faustinus, aged 19, erected by Tedia Crispina, likely his mother-in-law.

EDCS-08000098.translation: Herennia lived ten years. Iulius Chryso [erected this].
EDCS-08000098.summary: A funerary epitaph for Herennia, who died at the age of ten, set up by Iulius Chryso.

EDCS-08000105.summary: An inscription indicating a dedication to Iulianus by Secundina.

EDCS-08000110.translation: Monumental plot of Marcus Metellus Agathon, twenty feet in front.
EDCS-08000110.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Marcus Metellus Agathon, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-08000111.summary: A simple epitaph indicating the burial place of Mevia Abascanti.

EDCS-08000113.translation: Gnaeus Octavius Cladus, freedman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-08000113.summary: An inscription identifying Gnaeus Octavius Cladus, who was a freedman of a man named Gnaeus.

EDCS-08000117.translation: To Publius Artisci Augustalis, a well-deserving spouse, from Sentia Semne and for herself.
EDCS-08000117.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a wife, Sentia Semne, to her deserving husband, Publius Artisci Augustalis, and also for herself.

EDCS-08000138.translation: Gaius Statius, son of Gaius. Gaius, son of Gaius. Publius, son of Gaius. Publius, son of Publius, quaestor. Licinius.
EDCS-08000138.summary: This inscription appears to be a complex family record listing multiple individuals with their patronymic and one holding the quaestorian office, possibly related to property or inheritance.

EDCS-08000142.translation: Tertia, daughter of Caius, Secunda, while alive, made this for herself and for her daughter Bia Prisca.
EDCS-08000142.summary: A funerary monument erected by Tertia Secunda for herself and her daughter Bia Prisca, indicating she was still alive when it was made.

EDCS-08000145.translation: Marcus Turpilius Omacius, freedman of Marcus, and Tertia Attia, daughter of Caius. A plot of twelve feet in every direction.
EDCS-08000145.summary: This is a boundary inscription defining a burial plot allocated to Marcus Turpilius Omacius and Tertia Attia.

EDCS-08000152.translation: Place of the monument [---] / Of Caius A[
EDCS-08000152.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely marking a burial location or a monument belonging to Caius A[---].

EDCS-08000153.translation: Lucius Ti[beri!] B() Ab(). Forty feet in front, twenty feet of land.
EDCS-08000153.summary: This inscription likely marks land boundaries or a plot of land, measuring 40 feet in front and 20 feet in depth, owned by Lucius Ti[beri!] B() Ab().

EDCS-08000190.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-08000190.translation: To the divine shades. For a deserving son, Covoidonius, who lived 9 years, 2 months, 7 days, buried on the 5th day before the Kalends of January, departed in peace. Sorrowful parents, against their vows, made this.
EDCS-08000190.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy named Covoidonius, set up by his grieving parents, dating to the early Roman Empire.

EDCS-08000191.translation: In the name of God the Father, and of the [Son, and of the Holy] Spirit. In peace Emelia, who lived approximately 50 years and after a year in peace [...]. Victorinus the innocent [...].
EDCS-08000191.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph with Christian elements, commemorating Emelia who lived about 50 years and mentioning Victorinus, possibly from the late Roman period.

EDCS-08000192.translation: ---six [---] she lived more or less [---] and for her merits, when she had received her name, they placed this contrary to their vow.
EDCS-08000192.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly a dedication made against a vow, for an individual whose name is not fully preserved, who lived a certain number of years and possessed merits.

EDCS-08000193.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-08000193.translation: To eternal memory. Exsuperantia, who lived 25 years and lived with her husband for three years, nine months, and ten days, her grieving parents erected [this monument] against their vow. She departed in peace, laid to rest the eighteenth day before the Kalends of [---].
EDCS-08000193.summary: A funerary epitaph for Exsuperantia, who died at a young age, erected by her grieving parents.

EDCS-08000198.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-08000198.translation: To the hands of the gods for Gorgonius, aged 60, well-deserved. To Iustus, who lived more or less 30 years, 2 months, his mistress grieving, they made [this] against [their] vow.
EDCS-08000198.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gorgonius and Iustus, erected by Iustus's mistress.

EDCS-08000199.translation: [To good memory.] Maximius, son of [---]atrinianus, [---]XII, a guardsman, lived 22 years.
EDCS-08000199.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maximius, a guardsman, whose parentage and further details are lost.

EDCS-08000202.translation: To good memory. In this place rests the sweetest Petronia, who lived more or less 5 years, 6 months, 8 days. Laid to rest the nineteenth day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-08000202.summary: A funerary epitaph for Petronia, a young child, buried on March 14th.

EDCS-08000205.text_edition: \n Septimino cum quo fecit o XV annos suII depositus III Nonass virginia contra votum fecit filiis suis Septiminina annos III praedolis fecit\n
EDCS-08000205.translation: Septiminius, with whom she lived for 15 years. Virginia, his daughter, died after 3 years, made [this] against [her] vow for her sons.
EDCS-08000205.summary: A funerary epitaph for Virginia, who died young, erected by her parents, likely for her children.

EDCS-08000206.translation: For the good memory. Simplicius and Venantianus, while alive, bought for themselves in common from Venantiana, their sister.
EDCS-08000206.summary: This inscription records a purchase of property, likely for burial, made by Simplicius and Venantianus from their sister Venantiana.

EDCS-08000207.translation: Sudis placed this for his partner Iovena, who lived with me for 15 years and departed from this life at the age of fifty.
EDCS-08000207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sudis for his partner Iovena, recording her age at death and the duration of their companionship.

EDCS-08000211.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription that begins to record the lifespan of a person named Victor.

EDCS-08000215.translation: ---twenty-two years with his partner [---] XXIII DAE [---] Antra and Saturi gave.
EDCS-08000215.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to record the age of a deceased person and is a dedication made by Antra and Saturi.

EDCS-08000217.translation: To the deserving one who lived with his Virginia for 20 years and months; he placed this contrary to a vow.
EDCS-08000217.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a deserving individual who lived with Virginia for 20 years, with the dedication made contrary to a vow.

EDCS-08000223.translation: We, VV, by the work of Theodore, order this title to be made with my seal.
EDCS-08000223.summary: This inscription concerns the commissioning of a monument or title, with specific instructions regarding its creation and the involvement of Theodore and the speaker.

EDCS-08000224.text_edition: \n Deo Herculi Lucius Vitius Severus votum solvit\n
EDCS-08000224.translation: Lucius Vitius Severus fulfilled his vow to the god Hercules.
EDCS-08000224.summary: A votive inscription dedicating the fulfillment of a vow to Hercules by Lucius Vitius Severus.

EDCS-08000225.text_edition: \n Caius Ennius Cai filius Colonus Herculi votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08000225.translation: Gaius Ennius, son of Gaius, from Colonus, fulfilled his vow to Hercules willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08000225.summary: A votive inscription dedicating the fulfillment of a vow to Hercules by Gaius Ennius.

EDCS-08000226.translation: Tiberius Poppaius, son of Tiberius, from Temavo, gave this gift willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08000226.summary: This is an inscription recording a voluntary and deserved dedication made by Tiberius Poppaius, son of Tiberius, originating from Temavo.

EDCS-08000227.translation: The bones of Lucius Flaminius Rufinus, aged four years.
EDCS-08000227.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the death of a young child, Lucius Flaminius Rufinus.

EDCS-08000228.translation: To Laetilius Gallus, son of Gaius, a decurion, who wished to see the city while still eager in his youth; returning from there, I was struck by severe fevers and was greatly oppressed. I lost my youth in its bloom, since indeed the unequal fates called me. And I bore my beard crudely, and met a cruel death; unhappy, I could not fulfill the vows of my people. I lie in this tomb, and my wretched mother has pain in her heart every day, sheds tears and beats her palms on her chest. He lived 20 years, 7 months, 7 days. Laetilia Custa, daughter of Titus, to her dearest and most devoted son, an unhappy mother.
EDCS-08000228.summary: A funerary epitaph for Laetilius Gallus, a young decurion who died of fever, written by his grieving mother.

EDCS-08000234.translation: To Hope, Augusta: 2 pounds of silver.
EDCS-08000234.summary: This is a dedication to the deified empress 'Hope Augusta', likely for a private shrine, recording a silver offering.

EDCS-08000236.translation: [---]izo, a soldier of the XI Claudia legion, VI cohort, I century, served for 5 years, lived 25 years.
EDCS-08000236.summary: A funerary epitaph for a soldier of the XI Claudia legion.

EDCS-08000239.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly related to a funerary monument or a dedication, with several names and titles missing.

EDCS-08000242.translation: S. Cai's freedman ordered this to be made for himself and his wife Secunda by his will.
EDCS-08000242.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by a freedman for himself and his wife.

EDCS-08000244.translation: Ennius the gladiator made this while alive.
EDCS-08000244.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by a gladiator named Ennius.

EDCS-08000246.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely for a monument commissioned by Valentinus for himself.

EDCS-08000248.translation: Aulus Vibe[---] / Lucius Cassiu[s ---] / Titus Tibur[---]
EDCS-08000248.summary: This inscription appears to list the names of three individuals, possibly associated with a shared monument or legal document, with significant portions missing.

EDCS-08000254.translation: Secunda Fulvia, daughter of R. Lopponis.
EDCS-08000254.summary: This inscription records the name of Secunda Fulvia, identified by her father's name, with a partially illegible patronymic.

EDCS-08000255.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists parts of three names, likely representing individuals associated with a monument or legal context.

EDCS-08000256.summary: This inscription contains the name Publius Vett followed by possibly abbreviated words or names, the meaning of which is unclear due to missing context.

EDCS-08000257.translation: He made this while alive for himself and for Prima, his freedwoman wife.
EDCS-08000257.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by a man for himself and his wife, Prima, who was his freedwoman.

EDCS-08000258.translation: To Iaia, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-08000258.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Iaia, wife of Caius.

EDCS-08000261.translation: Publius Firmius and Cap Secundeus, who gladly paid their vow as was deserved.
EDCS-08000261.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Publius Firmius and Cap Secundeus.
