EDCS-08000262.translation: To Braetia Maxima, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-08000262.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Braetia Maxima, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-08000265.translation: To Annia Grata, Caupius Albicius Primus made this monument for his most virtuous wife, having lived, by his will.
EDCS-08000265.summary: This funerary epitaph records a husband dedicating a monument to his deceased wife, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-08000274.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, mentioning CGE, son of Caius.

EDCS-08000277.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a name on a tomb or a marker, the 'X' might indicate a quantity or be a separate mark.

EDCS-08000278.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a personal name or a dedication.

EDCS-08000279.summary: This inscription records a personal name, Frema, and her patronymic, suggesting a tombstone or personal marker.

EDCS-08000280.translation: Secunda, daughter of Titus, wife of Futiacus.
EDCS-08000280.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Secunda, daughter of Titus and wife of Futiacus.

EDCS-08000282.translation: Publius Cervonius Licinus, son of Publius, for himself and [...]
EDCS-08000282.summary: This epitaph begins the dedication of a tomb by Publius Cervonius Licinus for himself and at least one other person, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08000283.translation: The site of the monument of Quintus Cornelius Chryseros: in length 21 feet, in width 70 feet.
EDCS-08000283.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Quintus Cornelius Chryseros, indicating the sale or allocation of land for a tomb.

EDCS-08000284.translation: The site of the monument of Publius, son of Publius, son of [?], Firmus: in length 20 feet, in width 32 feet.
EDCS-08000284.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Publius (son of Publius) Firmus, similar to EDCS-08000283.

EDCS-08000290.translation: To the Social Genius, Quintus Titius Quintulus, son of Lucius, gladly paid his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-08000290.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Social Genius by Quintus Titius Quintulus.

EDCS-08000291.translation: Sacred to a god. Teidius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-08000291.summary: This is a dedication to a deity by Teidius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-08000293.translation: Quintus Accius Aco, son of Publius, grandson of Quintus, Auditus.
EDCS-08000293.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription providing the full names and lineage of Quintus Accius Aco.

EDCS-08000294.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription or a dedication to Gnaeus Bilvenus Narcissus.

EDCS-08000296.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Moderatus, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-08000297.translation: Lucius Numisius, son of Lucius, from the tribe Trebia.
EDCS-08000297.summary: This names Lucius Numisius, son of Lucius, and indicates his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08000298.summary: This identifies Rufa as the freedwoman of Sinia.

EDCS-08000299.summary: This identifies Quintus Teidius as the freedman of Manius.

EDCS-08000301.summary: This names Quintus Accius and identifies his father, Fus.

EDCS-08000302.summary: This identifies Flora as the freedwoman of an unnamed woman.

EDCS-08000304.translation: Lucius Lupavius, son of Lucius, from the tribe Romilia, sacred to Jupiter.
EDCS-08000304.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Lucius Lupavius, son of Lucius, who belonged to the tribe Romilia.

EDCS-08000306.translation: Manius Caesius, son of Lucius, from the tribe Romilia, aquilifer of the Fourth Macedonian Legion, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-08000306.summary: This funerary inscription records that Manius Caesius, an aquilifer in the Fourth Macedonian Legion, instructed that this monument be erected in his will.

EDCS-08000307.translation: To Lucius Saufeius, freedman of a woman, named Paratus, a palearius, in the place of Tiberius Cassius Probus.
EDCS-08000307.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Lucius Saufeius, a freedman identified as Paratus and a palearius, associated with Tiberius Cassius Probus.

EDCS-08000308.translation: Quintus Acutius, freedman of Quintus, set up [this for] his freedwoman Agilia.
EDCS-08000308.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quintus Acutius, freedman of Quintus, for his freedwoman Agilia.

EDCS-08000310.translation: The bones of Adiutor. Annius So...
EDCS-08000310.summary: This text appears to be the beginning of a funerary inscription, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period, identifying the deceased as Adiutor and the one who began the inscription as Annius So.

EDCS-08000311.translation: Publius Alfius Serenus made this while alive for himself and for his good friend Titus Calventius Firmus.
EDCS-08000311.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period where Publius Alfius Serenus dedicated a tomb for himself and his friend Titus Calventius Firmus.

EDCS-08000314.translation: Manio Antonio, son of Titus, and Romilia Antoniae, daughter of Manius, Maxima are buried here. Caius Antonius Vitalis, son of Manius, made this while alive. 23 feet in front, 23 feet in the field.
EDCS-08000314.summary: This is a Roman Imperial funerary inscription that records the burial of Manio Antonio and Romilia Antoniae, with Caius Antonius Vitalis as the dedicator, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-08000315.translation: For Caius Apicius, son of Caius, tribe Romilia. 20 feet in front, ... feet in the field.
EDCS-08000315.summary: This incomplete Roman Imperial funerary inscription records a plot of land allocated for Caius Apicius, son of Caius, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-08000316.translation: Quintus Asconius Euthetus made this while alive for himself and...
EDCS-08000316.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period indicates that Quintus Asconius Euthetus erected it for himself and potentially others.

EDCS-08000317.translation: Caius Atius, son of Titus, a decurion of Ateste, for himself, and for Lucius Atius and Nonia and Martia, his parents. Aurelius and Flavius, his sons, oversaw the work.
EDCS-08000317.summary: This Roman Imperial funerary epitaph from Ateste records Caius Atius, a decurion, dedicating the tomb for himself and his parents, with his sons overseeing the construction.

EDCS-08000318.translation: Lucius Cassius, son of Quintus, tribe Romilia.
EDCS-08000318.summary: This inscription likely marks a tomb or property belonging to Lucius Cassius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000323.translation: For Quintus Coelius Hilarus, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-08000323.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, honoring Quintus Coelius Hilarus, who was the freedman of a Quintus.

EDCS-08000324.translation: For Quintus Cotis, son of Manius.
EDCS-08000324.summary: This dedication or funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period is for Quintus Cotis, son of Manius.

EDCS-08000325.translation: The place of Caius Domitius Anti, freedman of Caius. 16 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-08000325.summary: This Roman Imperial funerary inscription marks a burial plot allocated to Caius Domitius Anti, freedman of Caius, specifying the dimensions of the land.

EDCS-08000326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Edona, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-08000327.translation: Lucius Ennius Rufio, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-08000327.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Ennius Rufio, identifying his former master.

EDCS-08000328.translation: Caius Gestilius, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08000328.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Gestilius, indicating his filiation and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08000330.translation: Caius Herennius, son of Caius, of the Voturia tribe.
EDCS-08000330.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Herennius, indicating his filiation and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08000331.translation: To Erennia Secunda, daughter of Caius. Lucius Iunius Claudius [erected this].
EDCS-08000331.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Erennia Secunda, erected by Lucius Iunius Claudius.

EDCS-08000332.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hilarius, son of Titus.

EDCS-08000334.translation: And to Licinia Blända, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-08000334.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinia Blända, identifying her former master.

EDCS-08000335.translation: Aulus Lucanus, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08000335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Lucanus, indicating his filiation and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08000336.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cnaeus Lucilius, indicating his filiation.

EDCS-08000337.translation: Caius Planius Balbus, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08000337.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Planius Balbus, indicating his filiation and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08000338.translation: Lucius Renestus had this made for his brother Flavius Alforisius and his patron Flavius Acharius, who deserved well, and for his dearest son Atestius Attius.
EDCS-08000338.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Renestus for his relatives.

EDCS-08000340.translation: Burial place for Tilia Secunda, daughter of Caius, 20 feet in front, in the field.
EDCS-08000340.summary: A funerary plot designation for Tilia Secunda.

EDCS-08000341.summary: A dedication or epitaph for Sicinia Maxsuma.

EDCS-08000342.translation: Burial place for Lucius Syric Bathyllus, 11 feet in front, in the field.
EDCS-08000342.summary: A funerary plot designation for Lucius Syric Bathyllus.

EDCS-08000343.translation: 14 feet. Publius Truttedius Philomusus, freedman of Publius Truttedius, gives from his own property to Publius Truttedius, son of Publius, freedman of Amphionis.
EDCS-08000343.summary: A funerary plot boundary marker, possibly indicating a donation of land for burial.

EDCS-08000344.translation: Firmus, son of Titus, from the Romilia tribe, for himself and for his wife Varia, daughter of Secundus, and for his son Titus Calventius, son of Titus.
EDCS-08000344.summary: A funerary epitaph for Firmus and his family members.

EDCS-08000345.translation: Marcus Vettius, son of Publius, from the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08000345.summary: An indication of tribal affiliation, likely related to citizenship or property, for Marcus Vettius.

EDCS-08000346.summary: A dedication or epitaph for Vicellia Anchari.

EDCS-08000348.translation: Publius Volumnius, son of Caius, from the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08000348.summary: An indication of tribal affiliation, likely related to citizenship or property, for Publius Volumnius.

EDCS-08000349.translation: Quintus Volumnius, son of Caius, from the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08000349.summary: An indication of tribal affiliation, likely related to citizenship or property, for Quintus Volumnius.

EDCS-08000351.translation: Volumnia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, and Publius Lucius, sons of Gaius Volumnius, made this monument for themselves and their family while alive; its front is 33 feet, its depth 25 feet; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-08000351.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by Volumnia Secunda and Publius Lucius Volumnius for themselves and their family, specifying dimensions and stipulating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-08000356.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Volumnia Laurens as the freedwoman of a certain Gaius.

EDCS-08000376.translation: Cassia Secunda, daughter of Annius; Cassia Secunda, daughter of Annius.
EDCS-08000376.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph, possibly recording the name of Cassia Secunda, daughter of Annius, twice.

EDCS-08000377.translation: To Lucius Tintinius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-08000377.summary: This inscription is a dedication or epitaph for Lucius Tintinius, son of Gaius.

EDCS-08000378.translation: To Lucius Titinius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-08000378.summary: This inscription is a dedication or epitaph for Lucius Titinius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-08000380.summary: This inscription identifies the subject as the mother of Manius Titinius.

EDCS-08000381.translation: Curon made the place for Manius Tintenus.
EDCS-08000381.summary: This inscription records that Curon constructed a burial place for Manius Tintenus.

EDCS-08000382.translation: The wife made the mother of Manius Titinius.
EDCS-08000382.summary: This inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, states that a wife erected it for the mother of Manius Titinius.

EDCS-08000383.translation: The wife of Manius Titinius, Ivana.
EDCS-08000383.summary: This funerary epitaph identifies the wife of Manius Titinius as Ivana.

EDCS-08000384.translation: Claudius Rogatus(?) threw down with his own hand 300 in the theatre.
EDCS-08000384.summary: This inscription records the demolition of 300 items (possibly seats or statues) in the theatre by Claudius Rogatus, likely during a renovation or clearance, possibly from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-08000386.translation: Lucius Camerius Philostratus, freedman of Lucius, son of Manius.
EDCS-08000386.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Camerius Philostratus, identifying him as the freedman of Lucius, son of Manius.

EDCS-08000387.translation: Lucius Camerius Rusticus, son of Lucius, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-08000387.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Camerius Rusticus, who commissioned his own tomb during his lifetime.

EDCS-08000390.translation: Set up while living: Manius Cartorius Eronis, son of Manius, freedman; his wife Cartoria Ampelia, freedwoman, daughter of Manius; their son Manius Cartorius Runco, living; [son] Cartorius Firmo, living; [daughter] ia Cartoria, living; [son] Manius Cartorius Quadratus; in front 28 feet, in the field 35 feet.
EDCS-08000390.summary: This is a complex family epitaph recording multiple members, including freedmen and their descendants, along with the dimensions of their burial plot, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-08000393.translation: He paid his vow willingly and deservedly for the health of Publius Terentius Lastulus, son of Publius, and his wife Caerelia.
EDCS-08000393.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow for the health of Publius Terentius Lastulus and his wife Caerelia.

EDCS-08000394.translation: To the divine shades. Marcus Valerius Ingenuinus, soldier of the III Praetorian Cohort, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Claudia Celeia, served for 9 years and lived for 35 years. Lucius Valerius, his brother, set this up for the well-deserving.
EDCS-08000394.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius Ingenuinus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, set up by his brother.

EDCS-08000395.translation: To the divine shades. To Viridomarus, son of Batto, a soldier of the III Praetorian Cohort, century of Specius, our comrade, from Tens, served for 20 years and lived for 62 years.
EDCS-08000395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Viridomarus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, likely set up by his family or comrades.

EDCS-08000396.translation: For Aelia Sperata, who lived for 1 year and 4 days. Julia Firmina, her most unhappy mother, set this up for her well-deserving daughter.
EDCS-08000396.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Aelia Sperata, set up by her grieving mother.

EDCS-08000397.translation: Allenius Hedyle made this while alive for Tiberius Allenius Chrysanthus, her patron, and for Allenia Synerosa, her sister, and for Allenius Hecaton, her son, and for herself and her family.
EDCS-08000397.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned during life by Allenia Hedyle for her patron, sister, son, and herself and her household.

EDCS-08000398.text_edition: \n Isidi donum Caius Papirius Luci filius Poblilia Macer Calventianus IIIIvir aedilicia potestate quaestor aerari flamen Romae et Augusti locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-08000398.translation: A gift to Isis: Gaius Papirius Macer Calventianus, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe, duovir with aedilic power, quaestor of the treasury, flamen of Rome and Augustus, was granted the site by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08000398.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a site to the goddess Isis by a prominent local magistrate, Gaius Papirius Macer Calventianus, who held several important civic and religious offices, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08000400.translation: Publius Numitorius Asclepiades paid his vow willingly and deservedly to Silvanus.
EDCS-08000400.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the deity Silvanus by Publius Numitorius Asclepiades.

EDCS-08000403.translation: Aquila, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, four times official for dispensing justice.
EDCS-08000403.summary: This inscription records the name and official position (IIIIvir iure dicundo) of Marcus Aquila.

EDCS-08000404.translation: Lucius Fabius, son of Quintus, ordered this to be made in his will for his father Quintus Fabius Celer, his mother Baebia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, and his sister Fabia.
EDCS-08000404.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by Lucius Fabius in his will for his parents and sister.

EDCS-08000405.translation: To the departed spirits: of Publius Vitullius Symphorus, one of the six Augustal priests, and of Herennia Aphrodisia; Lucius Valerius [...]
EDCS-08000405.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Publius Vitullius Symphorus, an Augustalis, and Herennia Aphrodisia, with Lucius Valerius also mentioned, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-08000410.translation: Lucius Domitius, son of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-08000410.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned during his lifetime by Lucius Domitius.

EDCS-08000412.translation: Fronto, son of Fronto, made this.
EDCS-08000412.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Fronto, son of Fronto, commissioned the monument.

EDCS-08000414.translation: To Modesta, freedwoman of Marcus, his wife.
EDCS-08000414.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Modesta, freedwoman and wife of an unnamed man.

EDCS-08000415.translation: Pieris, freedwoman of the woman Saufeia Itaoca, made this.
EDCS-08000415.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Pieris, freedwoman of Saufeia Itaoca, commissioned the monument.

EDCS-08000416.translation: Carvilius Refectus, freedman of Caius, most unfortunate father, [made this] for himself and for his daughter Carvilia Maxima and...
EDCS-08000416.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Carvilius Refectus, a freedman, made this for himself and his daughter, indicating a very sorrowful sentiment.

EDCS-08000417.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Hilara, a freedwoman of Caius.

EDCS-08000420.translation: To Caius Stlaccius Eros, for Stlaccia Trophima, his freedwoman and wife, most deserving, and his most innocent little soul, and for himself.
EDCS-08000420.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Caius Stlaccius Eros to his freedwoman and wife, Trophima, and also for himself, expressing deep affection.

EDCS-08000421.translation: Marcus Tussasius, freedman of the woman Primus, made this.
EDCS-08000421.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Marcus Tussasius, freedman of Primus, commissioned the monument.

EDCS-08000422.translation: Claudia [---] to Vettia, freedwoman of Caius, Aucta, in front 13 feet, in the field 25 feet.
EDCS-08000422.summary: This inscription seems to be a boundary marker or land division record, specifying measurements for a plot of land belonging to Vettia, freedwoman of Caius.

EDCS-08000423.translation: To his grandmother Mania, daughter of [---] Cana, his cousin, the most excellent, Bonius Fidus, son of [---]us, his procurator.
EDCS-08000423.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Bonius Fidus, acting as procurator, to his excellent grandmother Mania and cousin Cana.

EDCS-08000432.translation: Gaius Octavius, son of Marcus, Turpilius.
EDCS-08000432.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely identifying Gaius Octavius Turpilius, son of Marcus, possibly a name and filiation for an individual.

EDCS-08000433.summary: A dedication to the goddess Diana by Bedasius Primus.

EDCS-08000435.translation: To Gaius Marius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-08000435.summary: A dedication to Gaius Marius, son of Gaius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-08000436.translation: To my dearest wife, Quintus Sertorius Callistus.
EDCS-08000436.summary: A funerary dedication to a wife by her husband, Quintus Sertorius Callistus.

EDCS-08000437.text_edition: \n Herculi Augusto Lucius Sentius Bantius Marcus Baebius Rusticus Marcus Octavius Onomastus VIviri ex summis honorariis quas collegio nautarum debuerant adiectis HS |(duobus milibus) CC posuerunt\n
EDCS-08000437.translation: Lucius Sentius Bantius, Marcus Baebius Rusticus, and Marcus Octavius Onomastus, six men of the highest honorary rank, set this up, having added 2,200 sesterces to the amount they owed to the college of shipmen.
EDCS-08000437.summary: A dedication to Hercules Augustus by three prominent members of the collegium nautarum, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE, recording a financial contribution.

EDCS-08000438.translation: Gaius Artorius Eum Rufius Favius dedicated this while lying on his back.
EDCS-08000438.summary: An unusual personal dedication by Gaius Artorius Eum Rufius Favius, possibly related to a sporting event or ritual.

EDCS-08000443.translation: To Aelius Firmus, by Quintina, his freedwoman.
EDCS-08000443.summary: A dedication to Aelius Firmus by his freedwoman Quintina.

EDCS-08000447.translation: Lucius, son of Lucius, son of Gaius, Tertius, has fulfilled his vow to the Lares, deservedly.
EDCS-08000447.summary: A votive offering to the household gods (Lares) by Lucius Tertius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08000448.translation: Sacred to the Holy God Saturn Augustus. Quintus Tenagino Maximus [dedicated this] for his own health and that of his family.
EDCS-08000448.summary: A dedication to the god Saturn Augustus by Quintus Tenagino Maximus for his well-being and that of his household.

EDCS-08000684.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Valerio Liciniano Licinio Pio Faelici sic Invicto Augusto\n
EDCS-08000684.translation: To our lord Valerius Licinianus Licinius, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-08000684.summary: A formal imperial acclamation or dedication to Emperor Valerius Licinianus Licinius.

EDCS-08000697.translation: Burial place of Titus Calpurnius Flaccus, decurion. Frontage 16 feet, depth in the field 24 feet.
EDCS-08000697.summary: A funerary boundary marker for Titus Calpurnius Flaccus, a decurion, specifying the dimensions of his plot.

EDCS-08000698.translation: To Gaius Pomponius Modestus, six-time decurio. Gaius Pomponius Chresimus (dedicated this).
EDCS-08000698.summary: A dedication by Gaius Pomponius Chresimus to Gaius Pomponius Modestus, who held the office of decurio six times, possibly a tomb inscription.

EDCS-08000703.translation: [To...] Secundus, freedman of Titus Annius, and his wife Secunda, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-08000703.summary: Part of a tomb inscription mentioning Secundus, freedman of Titus Annius, and his wife Secunda.

EDCS-08000705.translation: Aurelius Laetus made this while alive for his daughter Olydiana, daughter of Annus. Aurelia Flacca (made this) for her most beloved daughter.
EDCS-08000705.summary: A funerary monument made by Aurelius Laetus for his daughter Olydiana, and also by Aurelia Flacca for her daughter.

EDCS-08000706.translation: To the departed spirits. For Daphnis, freedwoman of Salvius, and Hyginus, freedman of Lucia Aurelia. 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the land.
EDCS-08000706.summary: A funerary inscription dedicating a plot of land to the spirits of Daphnis and Hyginus, with dimensions provided.

EDCS-08000714.translation: The remains of Marcella, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-08000714.summary: A funerary inscription identifying the remains of Marcella, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-08000718.translation: Favonia Nigella, freedwoman, for herself and her kin. Monument site: 16 feet in front, 16 feet in the land.
EDCS-08000718.summary: A funerary inscription by Favonia Nigella, a freedwoman, reserving a plot of land for herself and her family.

EDCS-08000719.translation: For Primo, and his freedmen and freedwomen. Ponicia, daughter of Lucius, (made this) for Marcus Flavius Fideius, for herself and her kin.
EDCS-08000719.summary: A funerary inscription by Ponicia for Marcus Flavius Fideius, and for herself and her freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-08000720.translation: Fellenius, son of Publius, Colonus, made this while alive for himself and his family, freedmen and freedwomen. 16 feet every way.
EDCS-08000720.summary: A tomb inscription by Fellenius Colonus, intended for himself, his family, and his freedpersons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08000721.translation: To Lucius Lastorius, son of Anneus, and Marcius Rufus.
EDCS-08000721.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Lastorius to Anneus and Marcius Rufus, likely a funerary or honorary inscription.

EDCS-08000722.translation: Gaius Icius Epaphroditus and Lucretia Marcellina, most unhappy parents.
EDCS-08000722.summary: This inscription is a parent's memorial to their child, expressing profound grief.

EDCS-08000729.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to two individuals, Gaius Popilius and Claudius, likely honorific.

EDCS-08000730.translation: Lucius Sallustius Sophilus, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Aster, freedman of Lucius, while alive. Place of 16 square feet.
EDCS-08000730.summary: An inscription marking a burial plot of 16 square feet, set up by two freedmen, Lucius Sophilus and Lucius Aster.

EDCS-08000731.translation: Gaius Tonnius Valens made this himself while alive, for himself and for Tonnia Primigenia, his wife.
EDCS-08000731.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Tonnius Valens and his wife, erected by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-08000740.translation: Tyce, freedwoman of Quintus Flavius, aged 25, is buried here.
EDCS-08000740.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tyce, a freedwoman, providing her age and patron.

EDCS-08000753.translation: To the most blessed martyr Proto.
EDCS-08000753.summary: A dedication to the Christian martyr Proto.

EDCS-08000754.translation: To the most blessed martyr Chrysogonus.
EDCS-08000754.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the martyr Chrysogonus.

EDCS-08000756.text_edition: \n Tito Desticio Titi filio Claudia Iubae Marcus Claudius Moderatus amico optimo locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-08000756.translation: To Titus Desticius, son of Titus, of the Claudia tribe. Marcus Claudius Moderatus gave this place to his excellent friend by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08000756.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by Marcus Claudius Moderatus to his friend Titus Desticius, by decision of the local council.

EDCS-08000757.translation: Her husband Ando erected this monument for his wife Valentina.
EDCS-08000757.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valentina, erected by her husband Ando.

EDCS-08000758.translation: Vettia, daughter of Gaius, ordered this to be made by her will.
EDCS-08000758.summary: This is an epitaph for Vettia, daughter of Gaius, indicating the monument was commissioned through her will.

EDCS-08000760.summary: This inscription possibly records a lineage or succession within the Valerius family.

EDCS-08000761.translation: Sacred to Diana from the household of the Rubenii.
EDCS-08000761.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Diana by the family of the Rubenii.

EDCS-08000763.translation: Lucius Caxssaeus, freedman of Lucius Pai, [---] Pho[---].
EDCS-08000763.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for Lucius Caxssaeus, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-08000764.translation: To Aelius Quintus, son of Palm(us?).
EDCS-08000764.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aelius Quintus, son of Palm(us?).

EDCS-08000769.translation: Alive, Allenia Hedyle made this for her patron Tiberius Allenius Chrysanthus, and for her sister Allenia Synerosa, and for Allenius Hecaton, her son, and for their own family.
EDCS-08000769.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Allenia Hedyle for her patron, sister, son, and family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000771.translation: Publius Cleusius Proculus, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, a centurion (primus pilus) of the VII Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, formerly a deputy officer (cornicularius) to a praetorian prefect, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-08000771.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Cleusius Proculus, a high-ranking soldier who served in the VII Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, with the monument commissioned by his will.

EDCS-08000772.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Publius Vitullius Hermias, one of the six officials (VIvir Augustalis), by his will.
EDCS-08000772.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Publius Vitullius Hermias, a member of the college of VIviri Augustales, commissioned by his will, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000773.translation: To the Great Goddess Cybele, Tiberius Priamius, a member of the IIIviri, paid his vow with his own money.
EDCS-08000773.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Great Goddess Cybele by Tiberius Priamius, a magistrate, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000774.translation: To Lucius Vibius, son of Cnaeus.
EDCS-08000774.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Lucius Vibius, son of Cnaeus.

EDCS-08000776.translation: Stercorius and Vespula made (this) with their own (property), two hundred feet.
EDCS-08000776.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument or structure of two hundred feet by Stercorius and Vespula, possibly a property boundary or funerary area.

EDCS-08000778.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication to Augusta, but lacks sufficient context for a precise summary.

EDCS-08000782.translation: Publius Eppius Urbanus, freedman of Publius, made this for himself and for Stertinia Prima, daughter of Marcus, by her husband.
EDCS-08000782.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Publius Eppius Urbanus for himself and Stertinia Prima, likely his wife.

EDCS-08100065.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate II consuli proconsuli Voltinius Saloninus vir perfectissimus praefectus classis praetoriae nnatis devotus numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-08100065.translation: Voltinius Saloninus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the praetorian fleet, devoted to the divinity and majesty of our lords, the Emperor Caesar, the Pious, the Fortunate, the Unconquered Augustus, twice holder of tribunician power, consul, proconsul.
EDCS-08100065.summary: This is a dedication by Voltinius Saloninus, a high-ranking naval officer, to the emperor.

EDCS-08100070.translation: To the divine shades. Laetilia Maxima and Camuria Primitiva and Camuria Priscilla set up this monument to their well-deserving patron, Titus Camurius Priscus, a veteran of the 14th urban cohort.
EDCS-08100070.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by family members to Titus Camurius Priscus, a veteran, and his wife.

EDCS-08100072.translation: Titus Atilius, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe, decurion. Atilia Maxima, daughter of Titus. Pinnia Phoebe, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-08100072.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including a decurion and his family members, possibly related to a funerary monument.

EDCS-08100074.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Domitius Modestus and Iulia Secunda made this for their daughter Domitia Paulina, daughter of Caius, who lived for 4 years.
EDCS-08100074.summary: This funerary inscription records parents dedicating a monument to their deceased young daughter.

EDCS-08100079.translation: To the divine shades. Marcus Marcius Seberinus and Marcus Marcius Agricola, his sons, set up this monument for their dearest father, Marcus Marcius Nepos, who deserved well.
EDCS-08100079.summary: A funerary dedication by two sons to their father, Marcus Marcius Nepos.

EDCS-08100081.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Octavius Prudens and Provincialis set up this monument for their parents, Gaius Octavius Vindex and Marcellina Carfena, who deserved well.
EDCS-08100081.summary: A funerary dedication by two sons to their parents, Caius Octavius Vindex and Marcellina Carfena.

EDCS-08100083.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Publicio Dionysio qui vixit annis L mense uno diebus X et Cobia Paulina coniugi bene merenti posuit cum quo vixit annos XXXVIIII\n
EDCS-08100083.translation: To the divine shades. Cobia Paulina dedicated this to her husband, Caius Publicius Dionysius, who lived for 50 years and one month and 10 days, with whom she lived for 39 years.
EDCS-08100083.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a wife to her deceased husband, detailing his lifespan and their years of marriage.

EDCS-08100086.translation: To Gaius Trebius Anterus, freedman of Gaius, and to Gellius Urbana, freedwoman of Quintus, his wife. Lucius Scaptius Primus [erected this] while alive.
EDCS-08100086.summary: A funerary monument set up by Lucius Scaptius Primus for his freedman Anterus and his wife Urbana.

EDCS-08100090.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Valerius Gracilis. Aucilia [his wife] [and mother?], [his] wife.
EDCS-08100090.summary: A funerary dedication to Lucius Valerius Gracilis and his wife Aucilia.

EDCS-08300313.text_edition: \n Gemeli O iae sibi Publi filia Secunda \n
EDCS-08300313.translation: Gemellia Secunda, daughter of Publius, [dedicated this] to herself.
EDCS-08300313.summary: An epitaph for Gemellia Secunda, daughter of Publius, likely self-dedicated.

EDCS-08300315.text_edition: \n sus Titi filius Luci filio Prisco Salvius \n
EDCS-08300315.translation: Salvius to his son Priscus, son of Lucius, son of Titus.
EDCS-08300315.summary: A dedication from Salvius to his son Priscus, recording three generations of male lineage.

EDCS-08300316.translation: To the gods, to Theodorus, Pola, T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?), T(itus?).
EDCS-08300316.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the gods and to a person named Theodorus, with multiple individuals named Titus, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300317.translation: Sacred to Ica Augusta. Vesiducus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-08300317.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Ica Augusta by Vesiducus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300318.translation: Titus Annius and Lucius Mu [from this place].
EDCS-08300318.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely marking a property boundary, mentioning Titus Annius and Lucius Mu.

EDCS-08300319.text_edition: \n Locus memoriae Marci Futi Flacci Futia Marci liberta Chora viva fecit patrono in fronte pedes XX in agro pedes \n
EDCS-08300319.translation: A place for the memory of Marcus Futtius Flaccus. Futia Chora, freedwoman of Marcus, made [this] for her patron, 20 feet in front and [---] feet in area.
EDCS-08300319.summary: A funerary marker established by Futia Chora for her patron Marcus Futtius Flaccus, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-08300320.text_edition: \n Sextus Palpellius Sexti filius Velina Mancia IIvir\n
EDCS-08300320.translation: Sextus Palpellius, son of Sextus, of the Velina tribe, a duovir.
EDCS-08300320.summary: An inscription identifying Sextus Palpellius, a local magistrate (duovir) from the Velina tribe.

EDCS-08300321.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Quinti Petrusi Hylli in fronte pedes XII in agro pedes XXX sibi et suis\n
EDCS-08300321.translation: A place of burial for Quintus Petrussius Hyllus, 12 feet in front and 30 feet in area, for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300321.summary: A burial plot designated for Quintus Petrussius Hyllus and his family, with specified dimensions.

EDCS-08300322.translation: Sextus Vettius Repentinus, freedman of Sextus, for himself and his freedwoman Vettia NI I and his mother Flania, [in the] front 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-08300322.summary: This inscription, likely a boundary marker, records Sextus Vettius Repentinus dedicating a plot of land for himself, his freedwoman, and his mother.

EDCS-08300323.translation: [Dedicated] to [his] devoted sister. Iulius Tertullinus, [her] brother, made [this]. She lived 22 years.
EDCS-08300323.summary: A funerary monument erected by Iulius Tertullinus for his sister, who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-08300324.translation: Donata, his own wife, who lived 5 years and 5 months, passed away. A mother, widowed by excessive love, made [this] above the aforementioned Basil, most distinguished man, as consul.
EDCS-08300324.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a grieving wife to her deceased husband, Basil, referencing his consulship.

EDCS-08300327.text_edition: \n Iovi Augusto sagrum sic Aurelius Iulianus posuit\n
EDCS-08300327.translation: A sacred precinct for Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Aurelius Iulianus set [this] up.
EDCS-08300327.summary: A dedication of a sacred area to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Aurelius Iulianus.

EDCS-08300339.summary: An inscription simply recording the name Quintus Cornelius Threptus, possibly an epitaph or ownership mark.

EDCS-08300340.translation: Publius Cal Salinator [son of] Publius Calv[ius].
EDCS-08300340.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or epitaph for Publius Cal Salinator, son of Publius Calvius.

EDCS-08300341.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a father named Thessalus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08300342.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely an epitaph or dedication, referring to Titi Regi Diadumeni.

EDCS-08300345.text_edition: \n Neptuno Augusto sacrum Publius Sicinius Coelinus Quintus Paccius Maturus IIIIviri iure dicundo quinquennales ex stilaris\n
EDCS-08300345.translation: Sacred to Augustus Neptune. Publius Sicinius Coelinus and Quintus Paccius Maturus, the IIIIviri (four magistrates) exercising judicial power, quinquennales (officials serving a five-year term), from the fund.
EDCS-08300345.summary: This is a dedication to the god Neptune Augustus, made by two magistrates (IIIIviri iure dicundo quinquennales) of a city, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08400175.text_edition: \n Marcus Cespius Marci filius Optatus vivus fecit aviae sorori patri\n
EDCS-08400175.translation: Marcus Cespius Optatus, son of Marcus, made this while alive for his grandmother, his sister, and his father.
EDCS-08400175.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus Cespius Optatus for his female relatives and father, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08400260.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Damae Nebris coniux cum filio et Fortunatus frater \n
EDCS-08400260.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Nebris, wife of Dama, with her son and brother Fortunatus.
EDCS-08400260.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Manes (spirits of the underworld) for Dama, set up by his wife Nebris and brother Fortunatus, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08500299.translation: To Augusta Eia. Gnaeus Pollentius... [partially illegible]
EDCS-08500299.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Augusta Eia, made by Gnaeus Pollentius, with the remainder of the inscription lost, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08500300.text_edition: \n ntius Symmachus et Antistia Libas s uniter \n
EDCS-08500300.summary: This inscription records Symmachus and Antistia Libas, with the context suggesting a joint dedication or commemoration, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08500301.text_edition: \n Florae Augustae Marcus Aurelius Iustus vivus libens solvit votum laetus fecit\n
EDCS-08500301.translation: Marcus Aurelius Iustus, while alive, gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow to Augusta Flora.
EDCS-08500301.summary: This is a votive inscription where Marcus Aurelius Iustus dedicates a fulfillment of a vow to Augusta Flora, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08500309.summary: This is an inscription honoring the martyrs Felix and Fortunatus.

EDCS-08500310.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Lucius Arrenius Maurus from the region of Anaunia, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08600251.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus - Mummius Valerianus QV coniugi posuit memoriam in re sua bene merenti posuit\n
EDCS-08600251.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Mummius Valerianus placed this memorial for his well-deserving wife in his own property.
EDCS-08600251.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Mummius Valerianus set up a memorial for his wife, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08600259.text_edition: \n Marcus Flavidius |(mulieris) libertus Philogenes Egnatia |(mulieris) liberta Amoena Lucius Tudicius Cai filius Baebia Quinti filia Frema Secunda Luci filia Lucius Tudicius Luci filius Cervolius\n
EDCS-08600259.translation: Marcus Flavidius Philogenes, freedman of a woman. Egnatia Amoena, freedwoman of a woman. Lucius Tudicius, son of Caius. Baebia Frema Secunda, daughter of Quinti. Lucius Tudicius Cervolius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-08600259.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including freedmen and members of a family, possibly related to a funerary monument or property record, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08600260.text_edition: \n Publius Carfulenus Publi libertus Modestus negotiator Corneliensis Publius Carfulenus Princeps libertus locus monumenti quoquo versus pedes XVI\n
EDCS-08600260.translation: Publius Carfulenus Modestus, freedman of Publius, a merchant from Cornelium, [and] Publius Carfulenus Princeps, freedman, [set this monument] 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-08600260.summary: This inscription records the setting of a monument by two freedmen, possibly merchants, defining its dimensions.

EDCS-08600263.translation: I lie here, Manes, born in Dardania, with my wife who lived with me for twice four years, without any complaint. I departed in peace. I served in the army among the Moesians for thirty-five years, released from the protectors, buried. I died on the fifth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Decentius Caesar and Paulus.
EDCS-08600263.summary: This epitaph records the life and military service of Manes, a soldier from Dardania, who died in the consulship of Decentius and Paulus.

EDCS-08600266.translation: Here lies Secundinus, who lived 45 years, 8 months, and 3 days. Buried in peace on the 3rd Ides of July, in the consulship of the most distinguished men Tatianus and Summacus.
EDCS-08600266.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of Secundinus, who died in the consulship of Tatianus and Summacus.

EDCS-08600273.text_edition: \n Minucio Titi filio Lorario centurioni in legione Martia Terti fecit idemque r\n
EDCS-08600273.translation: He made [this] for Minucius, son of Titus, a lorarius centurion in the Martian legion, the third legion; and he himself...
EDCS-08600273.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription recording the maker of a monument for Minucius, a centurion in the Martian legion.

EDCS-08600275.text_edition: \n Arruntio Prisco Arruntiai sic Maximai sic\n
EDCS-08600275.translation: To Arruntius Priscus, of Arruntia Maxima, his son/daughter [by adoption?].
EDCS-08600275.summary: This is a dedication to Arruntius Priscus, with his parentage indicated.

EDCS-08900383.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Quintus Sirtius Fidiclanus Apronianus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, former aedile, former duovir, former quinquennial duovir, former prefect of engineers, [son of] his freedman.
EDCS-08900383.summary: This epitaph honors Quintus Sirtius Fidiclanus Apronianus, detailing his civic and military offices.

EDCS-08900384.text_edition: \n us Titi filius Velina aedilicia potestate \n
EDCS-08900384.translation: ...son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, in aedilician power.
EDCS-08900384.summary: This fragment mentions a man of the Velina tribe who held aedilician power, likely related to a political office.

EDCS-08900385.summary: This is a simple mention of a personal name, Lucius Ceius Pavo, possibly the subject of a lost inscription.

EDCS-08900387.translation: Salonius Mauricus, a praiseworthy man, former count, lived for fifty-two years. He departed on the 7th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-08900387.summary: This epitaph records the death of Salonius Mauricus, a man of distinction who lived to be fifty-two years old.

EDCS-08900388.text_edition: \n Titia Marci liberta Ariste viva sibi fecit quem locum sepolturae sic cum suis terminis Attio Abascanto vel heredi eius viva dedit cum itu ambitu et si quis eos hortos possiderit itum ambitum praestare debebit in fronte pedes LV in agro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-08900388.translation: Titia Ariste, freedwoman of Marcus, made [this] for herself while alive. She also gave this place for burial, with its boundaries, to Attius Abascantus or his heir while she was alive, with its surrounding area; and whoever possesses these gardens must guarantee the surrounding area, 55 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-08900388.summary: This inscription records a woman, Titia Ariste, who purchased a burial plot for herself and an heir, specifying the dimensions and terms of its use.

EDCS-08900940.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Caius Iulius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus Aquileiensium restitutor et conditor viam quoque Anniam a porta usque ad miliarium septimum per tirones iuventutis novae Italicae suae dilectus posterioris longi temporis labe conruptam munivit ac restituit\n
EDCS-08900940.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, restorer and founder of Aquileia, also paved and restored the Via Annia from the gate up to the seventh milestone through the recruits of his new Italian levy of the later draft, which had been ruined by the decay of a long time.
EDCS-08900940.summary: This inscription records Emperor Maximinus Thrax's restoration of the Via Annia near Aquileia, completed by new army recruits.

EDCS-08900943.text_edition: \n miles legionis XIIII geminae centuria Luci Aciri stipendiorum XVIIII vixit annos XXXXIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-08900943.translation: A soldier of the XIV Gemina legion, from the century of Lucius Acirius, [served for] 19 years of service; he lived 43 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900943.summary: This tombstone records the details of a soldier from the XIV Gemina legion, including his service length, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-08900944.text_edition: \n Marco Laevio Felici Calventiae Quinti filiae Marcellae Marcus Laevius Marcellus parentibus optimis vivus fecit in fronte pedes XXII retro pedes XLIII\n
EDCS-08900944.translation: Marcus Laevius Marcellus made [this] for his most excellent parents, Marcus Laevius Felix and Marcella, daughter of Quintus Calventius, while alive, [with a plot] 22 feet in front and 43 feet in the rear.
EDCS-08900944.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Marcus Laevius Marcellus for his parents, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-08900945.text_edition: \n cus Mani filius no decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-08900945.translation: ...son of Manius, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08900945.summary: This fragment indicates an honor or action taken concerning an individual, son of Manius, decided by the local council (decurions).

EDCS-08900946.text_edition: \n Manius Acilius Mani filius sibi et suis\n
EDCS-08900946.translation: Manius Acilius, son of Manius, for himself and his family.
EDCS-08900946.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Manius Acilius for himself and his family.

EDCS-08900948.translation: Quintus Coelius Niticus, son of Volusius.
EDCS-08900948.summary: This inscription records the name Quintus Coelius Niticus, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-08900949.summary: This inscription records the name Cornelia Tertia, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-08900950.text_edition: \n Caio Firmio et Caio Firmio Aniceto Quintus Persa\n
EDCS-08900950.translation: Quintus Persa [dedicates this] to Gaius Firmis and Gaius Firmis Anicetus.
EDCS-08900950.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Persa to Gaius Firmis and Gaius Firmis Anicetus.

EDCS-08900951.summary: This inscription records the name Manius Laelius, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-08900952.summary: This inscription records the name Oppius, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-08900953.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Publi Oppi Aprilis in fronte pedes XXXII retro pedes LX\n
EDCS-08900953.translation: Burial plot of Publius Oppius Aprilis, 32 feet in front and 60 feet in the rear.
EDCS-08900953.summary: This inscription records the dimensions and ownership of a burial plot belonging to Publius Oppius Aprilis.

EDCS-08900954.text_edition: \n Publius Peticius Publi libertus Hannibal Peticia Publi liberta Surisca\n
EDCS-08900954.translation: Publius Peticius Hannibal, freedman of Publius, and Surisca, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-08900954.summary: This inscription records the names of two freedmen, Publius Peticius Hannibal and Surisca, likely associated with a funerary monument.

EDCS-08900955.summary: This fragmentary inscription refers to Gaius Petridius, likely in the context of a dedication or ownership.

EDCS-08900956.translation: To Publius Pontius Rufio, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-08900956.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Publius Pontius Rufio, a freedman of a woman.

EDCS-08900958.summary: A dedication to Lucius Valerius, likely on a monument whose full text is lost.

EDCS-08900959.text_edition: \n Caius Vettius Cai libertus Chrestus vivo sibi fecit et Arutiae Tiberi filiae Maximae \n
EDCS-08900959.translation: Caius Vettius Chrestus, freedman of Caius, made this for himself and for Arutia Maxima, daughter of Tiberius, while alive.
EDCS-08900959.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Caius Vettius Chrestus for himself and his wife Arutia Maxima.

EDCS-08900963.text_edition: \n Volcenia Luci filia Marcellina ariam sic lapide stravit et podio circumdedit\n
EDCS-08900963.translation: Volcenia Marcellina, daughter of Lucius, paved the threshing floor with stone and enclosed it with a platform.
EDCS-08900963.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a threshing floor by Volcenia Marcellina.

EDCS-08900964.text_edition: \n Oliola Quinti Vincii ave cus posuit\n
EDCS-08900964.translation: Oliola placed this on behalf of her grandfather Quintus Vincius.
EDCS-08900964.summary: A dedication by Oliola for her grandfather Quintus Vincius.

EDCS-08900965.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Caerelliae Primigeniae in fronte pedes XXVIII retro pedes XX\n
EDCS-08900965.translation: Burial place of Caerellia Primigenia, 28 feet in front, 20 feet in the rear.
EDCS-08900965.summary: A burial plot designated for Caerellia Primigenia, with specific dimensions recorded.

EDCS-08900966.translation: To Manius Carm Statius, for his daughter Coelia.
EDCS-08900966.summary: An inscription possibly dedicating a monument to Coelia, daughter of Manius Carm Statius.

EDCS-08900967.text_edition: \n Caio Aio Cai f(ilio) Optato in fronte pedes XX retro pedes \n
EDCS-08900967.translation: To Caius Aius Optatus, son of Caius, 20 feet in front, [ ] feet in the rear.
EDCS-08900967.summary: A funerary inscription for Caius Aius Optatus, specifying dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-08900968.text_edition: \n Caius lius Cai filius Maximus sibi et Marcellae uxori optimae vivus fecit in fronte pedes in agro pedes \n
EDCS-08900968.translation: Caius Ilius Maximus, son of Caius, made this for himself and his excellent wife Marcella, while alive, [ ] feet in front, [ ] feet in the field.
EDCS-08900968.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Caius Ilius Maximus for himself and his wife Marcella, with incomplete dimensions.

EDCS-08900970.translation: To Abellia Gemella, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-08900970.summary: An inscription likely dedicating a monument to Abellia Gemella.

EDCS-08900971.text_edition: \n in fronte pedes XX retro pedes XXXX Pobliicia Phoebe\n
EDCS-08900971.translation: 20 feet in front, 40 feet in the rear, Pobliicia Phoebe.
EDCS-08900971.summary: A funerary inscription for Pobliicia Phoebe, specifying the dimensions of her burial plot.

EDCS-09001338.summary: This inscription seems to record the name of Max, freedman of Sextus, with some incomplete information about him.

EDCS-09001341.translation: To C. S. Theodorus of Pola, 4 [units/pounds].
EDCS-09001341.summary: This is a dedication to C. S. Theodorus of Pola, likely related to a measurement or quantity.

EDCS-09001343.text_edition: \n Caius Sevius Quinti filius veteranus lecione sic quartae Scuthicae testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-09001343.translation: Gaius Sevius, son of Quintus, a veteran of the fourth Scythian legion, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-09001343.summary: This inscription records a veteran of the fourth Scythian legion, Gaius Sevius, who arranged for a monument or construction by his will.

EDCS-09001344.text_edition: \n Quinto Sempronio Damati coniugi optimo Sempronia Veneria viva fecit IIIIIIviro Concordiae\n
EDCS-09001344.translation: Sempronia Veneria made this while alive for her most excellent husband Quintus Sempronius Damas, a member of the Concordiae college of six priests.
EDCS-09001344.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Sempronia Veneria for her husband Quintus Sempronius Damas, who was a high-ranking priest.

EDCS-09001345.text_edition: \n Luci Abei Narcissi in fronte pedes XIX semis retro pedes XVII\n
EDCS-09001345.translation: Lucius Abeius Narcissus: front 19 feet, rear 17 feet.
EDCS-09001345.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or land division for property owned by Lucius Abeius Narcissus.

EDCS-09001346.translation: Lucius Acutius Quadratus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-09001346.summary: This inscription simply records the name and freedman status of Lucius Acutius Quadratus.

EDCS-09001347.text_edition: \n Publius Aetriacus Cai filius fieri iussit\n
EDCS-09001347.translation: Gaius Aetrius, son of Caius, ordered this to be made.
EDCS-09001347.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Aetrius, son of Caius, commissioned a monument or construction.

EDCS-09001348.text_edition: \n Caius A vivus sibi et Ulpiae Publi filiae Terti\n
EDCS-09001348.translation: Gaius [---], alive, for himself and for Ulpia Tertia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-09001348.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication made by Gaius for himself and his wife, Ulpia Tertia.

EDCS-09001349.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Titi Ammini Hermetis in fronte pedes XXXVII retro pedes XVIII testamento\n
EDCS-09001349.translation: Burial place of Titus Amminus Hermetis: front 37 feet, rear 18 feet, by will.
EDCS-09001349.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot designated by will for Titus Amminus Hermetis, with dimensions provided.

EDCS-09001350.text_edition: \n Lucio Attio Luci filio Anniae Cai <f=E>(iliae) \n
EDCS-09001350.translation: To Lucius Attius, son of Lucius, and Annia, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-09001350.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or memorial to Lucius Attius and Annia.

EDCS-09001351.text_edition: \n Attia Marci filia sibi et Marco Attio Publi filio Marcello viro et Caio Attio Marci filio Severo et Tito Attio Marci filio filiis viva fecit\n
EDCS-09001351.translation: Attia, daughter of Marcus, made this while alive for herself, and for her husband Marcellus, son of Publius, and for her sons Gaius Attius Severus, son of Marcus, and Titus Attius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-09001351.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Attia for herself, her husband Marcellus, and her two sons, Gaius Attius Severus and Titus Attius.

EDCS-09001352.text_edition: \n Caius Aurelius Titi filius Scaptia Salvius\n
EDCS-09001352.translation: Gaius Aurelius Salvius, son of Titus, of the Scaptia tribe.
EDCS-09001352.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Gaius Aurelius Salvius.

EDCS-09001353.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Axius.

EDCS-09001354.text_edition: \n rae pedes LVI semis frontibus Marci Barbi Marci liberti\n
EDCS-09001354.translation: Fifty-six and a half feet in the front by the properties of Marcus Barbus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-09001354.summary: This inscription records land measurements and ownership, likely for property boundaries.

EDCS-09001355.text_edition: \n Caius Caelius Luci filius in fronte pedes XIII retro pedes XXXII\n
EDCS-09001355.translation: Gaius Coelius, son of Lucius, thirteen feet in the front and thirty-two feet in the rear.
EDCS-09001355.summary: This inscription records land dimensions, likely for property boundaries or a funerary plot.

EDCS-09001356.text_edition: \n Marcus Calventius Marci filius Marcellus vivus sibe sic et suis in fronte pedes V retro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-09001356.translation: Marcus Calventius Marcellus, son of Marcus, made this for himself and his family while alive, five feet in the front and thirty feet in the rear.
EDCS-09001356.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot and states that Marcus Calventius Marcellus commissioned it for his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-09001357.text_edition: \n Publius Carminius Titi filius vivus sibi et <i=O>n fronte pedes IIII retro pedes VIII \n
EDCS-09001357.translation: Publius Carminius, son of Titus, while alive, for himself and his wife, four feet in the front and eight feet in the rear.
EDCS-09001357.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot commissioned by Publius Carminius for himself and his wife during his lifetime.

EDCS-09001358.text_edition: \n Caius Cassius Cai libertus Moderatus sibi et Caio Cassio Cai liberto Mnemoni conliberto vivus fecit\n
EDCS-09001358.translation: Gaius Cassius Moderatus, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself and for his fellow freedman Gaius Cassius Mnemone, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-09001358.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Cassius Moderatus commissioned a monument for himself and his fellow freedman, Gaius Cassius Mnemone.

EDCS-09001359.text_edition: \n Marcus Cassius Cai filius patri posuit\n
EDCS-09001359.translation: Marcus Cassius, son of Gaius, erected this for his father.
EDCS-09001359.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Cassius erected a monument for his father.

EDCS-09001361.text_edition: \n Caio Catio Cai filio patri filius fecit\n
EDCS-09001361.translation: His son erected this for Gaius Catins, son of Gaius, his father.
EDCS-09001361.summary: This inscription records that a son erected a monument for his father, Gaius Catins.

EDCS-09001362.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Centius, with the dedicant and context missing.

EDCS-09001363.text_edition: \n Cinnamus in fronte pedes XX retro pedes XXXX\n
EDCS-09001363.translation: Cinnamus: 20 feet in front, 40 feet behind.
EDCS-09001363.summary: This inscription likely records land measurements for a property belonging to Cinnamus.

EDCS-09001364.text_edition: \n Cleppia |(mulieris) liberta Urbana Cilae sorori viva fecit\n
EDCS-09001364.translation: Urbana, freedwoman of Cleppia, made this for her sister Cila while alive.
EDCS-09001364.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Urbana for her sister Cila.

EDCS-09001365.translation: He ordered by will that it be made.
EDCS-09001365.summary: This inscription is a fragment from a will or funerary monument indicating a posthumous construction.

EDCS-09001366.summary: This inscription identifies Mulus Diogenes as a freedman.

EDCS-09001367.text_edition: \n Luci Firmi Lepidi in fronte pedes XX retro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-09001367.translation: Lucius Firmius Lepidus: 20 feet in front, 30 feet behind.
EDCS-09001367.summary: This inscription likely records land measurements for a property belonging to Lucius Firmius Lepidus.

EDCS-09001368.text_edition: \n Lucio Iulio Luci liberto Iuliae Luci libertae Iuliae Luci libertae? Annia Pon\n
EDCS-09001368.translation: To Lucius Iulius, freedman of Lucius; for Iulia, freedwoman of Lucius; for Iulia, freedwoman of Lucius? Annia Pon...
EDCS-09001368.summary: This inscription is a dedication to several individuals, possibly related by patronage and freedom, with Annia Pon potentially being the dedicant or a recipient.

EDCS-09001369.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Quintus Iulius.

EDCS-09001370.text_edition: \n Lucanae Quinti libertae Atticae Marcus Pupius Primigenius\n
EDCS-09001370.translation: To Lucana, freedwoman of Quintus; Marcus Pupius Primigenius.
EDCS-09001370.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucana, a freedwoman, and identifies Marcus Pupius Primigenius, possibly as a patron or dedicant.

EDCS-09001371.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Macioriae Ariadine im sic agro (pedes) XX retro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-09001371.translation: Burial place for Macoria Ariadne, in this land: 20 feet in front, 30 feet behind.
EDCS-09001371.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot for Macoria Ariadne and specifies the dimensions of the land.

EDCS-09001372.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae M Macioriae Ariadine im sic pagro pedes XX retro (pedes) XXX\n
EDCS-09001372.translation: Burial place for M. Macoria Ariadine, in this land: 20 feet in front, 30 feet behind.
EDCS-09001372.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot for M. Macoria Ariadine and specifies the dimensions of the land.

EDCS-09001373.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Publi Manni Septimini in fronte pedes XXXV retro pedes VL\n
EDCS-09001373.translation: The burial place of Publius Mannius Septiminus, 35 feet in front and 40 feet in depth.
EDCS-09001373.summary: This is a funerary boundary marker specifying the dimensions of a burial plot for Publius Mannius Septiminus.

EDCS-09001374.text_edition: \n ae Publi libertae et Primigenio viro eius Caius Messius Strenuus\n
EDCS-09001374.translation: To the freedwoman of Publius, and to Primigenius, her husband, Gaius Messius Strenuus [erected this].
EDCS-09001374.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication or funerary dedication by Gaius Messius Strenuus to a freedwoman of Publius and her husband.

EDCS-09001376.text_edition: \n Marcus Papirius Publi filius vivus fecit Tito Papirio Publi filio fratri\n
EDCS-09001376.translation: Marcus Papirius, son of Publius, made this while alive for his brother Titus Papirius, son of Publius.
EDCS-09001376.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that Marcus Papirius, son of Publius, erected this monument during his lifetime for his brother, Titus Papirius, son of Publius.

EDCS-09001377.text_edition: \n Publius Papirius Luci filius vivus fecit sibi et Maximae \n
EDCS-09001377.translation: Publius Papirius, son of Lucius, made this while alive for himself and for Maxima.
EDCS-09001377.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Publius Papirius, son of Lucius, erected this monument during his lifetime for himself and for Maxima.

EDCS-09001378.text_edition: \n Marcus Pontius Mani filius vivus sibi et Coeliae Titi filiae Fuctienae uxori et \n
EDCS-09001378.translation: Marcus Pontius, son of Mannius, [made this] while alive for himself and for Coelia Fuctiena, daughter of Titus, his wife, and...
EDCS-09001378.summary: This funerary epitaph indicates that Marcus Pontius, son of Mannius, erected this monument during his lifetime for himself, his wife Coelia Fuctiena, and possibly others.

EDCS-09001379.text_edition: \n Popillia Publi liberta Amoena sibi et Popilliae Publi libertae Musae sorori viva fecit\n
EDCS-09001379.translation: Popillia Amoena, freedwoman of Publius, made this while alive for herself and for Popillia Musa, freedwoman of Publius, her sister.
EDCS-09001379.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Popillia Amoena, a freedwoman, erected this monument during her lifetime for herself and her sister, Popillia Musa.

EDCS-09001381.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Auli Quinctili Rhodini in fronte pedes XXII retro pedes IX\n
EDCS-09001381.translation: To the Divine Shades of Aulus Quinctilius Rhodinus, 22 feet in front and 9 feet in depth.
EDCS-09001381.summary: This is a funerary boundary marker dedicating a plot to Aulus Quinctilius Rhodinus and specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-09001382.translation: Seia, daughter of Publius, and Chia, his freedwoman.
EDCS-09001382.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a tombstone or a funerary marker, naming Seia, daughter of Publius, and Chia, his freedwoman.

EDCS-09001383.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely a tombstone or funerary marker, identifying Lucius Sicinius as the freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-09001384.text_edition: \n Locus monumenti Publi Staumi Primigeni in fronte pedes XXVIII in agro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-09001384.translation: The site of the monument of Publius Staumius Primigenius, 28 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-09001384.summary: This is a funerary boundary marker detailing the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Publius Staumius Primigenius.

EDCS-09001386.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Terentius, likely the recipient of a monument or offering.

EDCS-09001387.text_edition: \n Terentiae Clementi in fronte pedes XX retro pedes XXV\n
EDCS-09001387.translation: For Terentia Clementa, 20 feet in front, 25 feet behind.
EDCS-09001387.summary: This inscription indicates dimensions related to a property belonging to Terentia Clementa, possibly marking land boundaries.

EDCS-09001388.summary: This is a simple personal identification of Terentia Gavina, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-09001389.text_edition: \n Vettia Publi liberta Bucca viva sibi et Caio Puti Vettia Publi liberta Bucca\n
EDCS-09001389.translation: Bucca, freedwoman of Vettia and Publius, while alive, for herself and for Gaius Puti.
EDCS-09001389.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Bucca, a freedwoman, for herself and for Gaius Puti, possibly indicating a shared tomb or plot.

EDCS-09001390.text_edition: \n lea Viceria viva sibi et Lucio Tarutio\n
EDCS-09001390.translation: Ilea Viceria, while alive, for herself and for Lucius Tarutius.
EDCS-09001390.summary: This inscription records a self-dedicated funerary monument by Ilea Viceria for herself and Lucius Tarutius.

EDCS-09001391.text_edition: \n Vilonia Mani liberta Dica sibi et Publio Terentio Titi filio viro suo fecit\n
EDCS-09001391.translation: Dica, freedwoman of Mani, made this for herself and for her husband Publius Terentius, son of Titus.
EDCS-09001391.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Dica, freedwoman of Mani, for herself and her husband Publius Terentius.

EDCS-09001392.text_edition: \n Volusia Publi liberta Glaphyra Publio Volusio |(mulieris) liberto Commodo patri Volusiae Publi et |(mulieris) libertae Lamyrae matri viva fecit\n
EDCS-09001392.translation: Glaphyra, freedwoman of Publius, made this while alive for her father Commodus, freedman of a woman, and for her mother Lamyra, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-09001392.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Glaphyra, freedwoman of Publius, for her parents Commodus and Lamyra.

EDCS-09001393.text_edition: \n Precilia |(mulieris) liberta Primigenia sibi et Firmae sorori suae nnorum XX viva fecit\n
EDCS-09001393.translation: Primigenia, freedwoman of a woman, made this while alive for herself and for her sister Firma, aged 20.
EDCS-09001393.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Primigenia, a freedwoman, for herself and her deceased sister Firma.

EDCS-09001394.text_edition: \n Connonia Luci filia Maxima sibi et Lucio Domitio Polemoni marito testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-09001394.translation: Maxima, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made in her will for herself and for her husband Lucius Domitius Polemon.
EDCS-09001394.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument commissioned by Maxima, daughter of Lucius, in her will for herself and her husband Lucius Domitius Polemon.

EDCS-09200295.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mithras by Aurelius Commodus.

EDCS-09200299.translation: To Nymphinus, freedman of Decidia Prota.
EDCS-09200299.summary: This funerary inscription records an offering to Nymphinus, a freedman.

EDCS-09200301.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Saturn.

EDCS-09200303.translation: To Marcus Patolcius, freedman of Arruntius, 8 pounds.
EDCS-09200303.summary: This is a dedication or record of weight for Marcus Patolcius, freedman of Arruntius.

EDCS-09300001.translation: To the Divine Sun, Lucius Apisocius Successus for himself and for his patrons Marcus, Gaius, Lucius, Quintus, [through?] these gods.
EDCS-09300001.summary: This is a dedication to the Sun by Lucius Apisocius Successus for himself and his patrons, possibly referencing deities.

EDCS-09300235.text_edition: \n liqui cuius natos infantes in fide patres quos ego suo patri opto superst<it>es futuros nam mihi duas filias ante paravi duces valete Lucius Avidius Cai filius Maritimus annorum VII hic situs est hic locus monumenti quoquov(ersus) pedes XVI\n
EDCS-09300235.translation: I, Lucius Avidius Maritimus, son of Caius, who lived 7 years, am buried here. My father had two daughters before me, whom I wish to be older than me, my own children. Farewell. This plot of ground for a monument extends 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09300235.summary: This epitaph records the burial of a 7-year-old boy, Lucius Avidius Maritimus, and dedicates a funerary plot.

EDCS-09300239.text_edition: \n Dianae Augustae sacrum Titus Flavius Helius frumentarius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09300239.translation: Sacred to the August Goddess Diana. Titus Flavius Helius, a corn-supply official, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09300239.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to Diana Augusta by Titus Flavius Helius, a corn-supply official.

EDCS-09300243.translation: Here lies in his own burial, before the thresholds of the lords apostles, Saint Maurentius the presbyter.
EDCS-09300243.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Saint Maurentius, a presbyter, buried near the thresholds of the apostles.

EDCS-09300244.text_edition: \n Infans bima iacet bis denis aucta diebus quam nova lux animae servat et alma fides imprudens corpusque decens dulcissima verba condet hic tumulus cetera sancta Deus novit praecipuo vernans fringylla canore garrulitas pia culis sic sub meliore polo heu Tarsilla tuum numen pro nomine ferres attamen sanctis sidus habenda tuis deposita III Nonas Iulias\n
EDCS-09300244.translation: Here lies an infant girl, two years old, increased by twenty days. A new light guards her soul, and fostering faith. And although her body is beautiful and her innocent speech sweet, this tomb will hold her. May God know her sacredness. You, Tarsilla, shining with exceptional birdsong and pious chatter, would carry your divine spirit under a better sky. Deposited on the 3rd day before the Nones of July.
EDCS-09300244.summary: This epitaph commemorates an infant girl named Tarsilla who died at the age of two years and twenty days, buried on July 5th.

EDCS-09300248.translation: Cham, a man of consular rank, a count, of wondrous goodness.
EDCS-09300248.summary: This is an epitaph or commendation for Cham, a high-ranking official known for his kindness.

EDCS-09300249.translation: Flavia Fesa and her husband Bonosus bought this tomb for themselves from their own property; whoever attempts to open it will pay 15 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-09300249.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the purchase of a tomb by Flavia Fesa and her husband Bonosus, with a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-09300250.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cavarasiae Iustae quae vixit annos XXIII menses VII dies XXVIII Lucius Coelius Quintianus coniugi karissimae et incomparabili vixit mecum nnum I menses II dies XXIII sine ulla quaerella sic animae innocentissimae\n
EDCS-09300250.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cavarasia Iusta, who lived 23 years, 7 months, and 28 days. Lucius Coelius Quintianus to his dearest and incomparable wife, with whom he lived 1 year, 2 months, and 23 days, without any complaint, thus to the most innocent soul.
EDCS-09300250.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Cavarasia Iusta after 23 years, 7 months, and 28 days, dedicated by her husband Lucius Coelius Quintianus.

EDCS-09300251.text_edition: \n Vivus Publius Coelius Publi libertus Princeps Liburnia Sexti liberta Flora\n
EDCS-09300251.translation: Living: Publius Coelius Princeps, freedman of Publius. Flora, freedwoman of Sextus Liburnus.
EDCS-09300251.summary: This inscription records two living individuals, Publius Coelius Princeps and Flora.

EDCS-09300254.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Aurelius Tullius Paumnianus pro salute sua et fratrerum sic suorum Tulli Secundi et Tulli Severini\n
EDCS-09300254.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras. Aurelius Tullius Paumnianus for the health of himself and his brothers, Tulli Secundus and Tulli Severinus.
EDCS-09300254.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mithras by Aurelius Tullius Paumnianus for the health of himself and his brothers.

EDCS-09300255.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras. Aelius s
EDCS-09300255.summary: This inscription is a partial dedication to the god Mithras by Aelius.

EDCS-09300256.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Aurelius Hermes Protemus et suis votum solvit libens\n
EDCS-09300256.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras. Aurelius Hermes Protemus and his [family/household] gladly fulfilled [their] vow.
EDCS-09300256.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the god Mithras by Aurelius Hermes Protemus and his household.

EDCS-09300909.text_edition: \n Rutilius Regillus quaestor Lucius Porcius Germanus magister i ex voluntate collegii fabrum constitutione facta nni primi Kalendis Ianuariis Imperatore Nerva Caesare Augusto III Lucio Verginio Rufo III consulibus I XI Kalendas Apriles secundum eor(um?) decretumlocum sepu[lturae ------\n
EDCS-09300909.translation: Rutilius Regillus, quaestor, and Lucius Porcius Germanus, magistrate, by the will of the college of artisans, by a decree made on the Kalends of January, when the Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus was consul for the third time and Lucius Verginius Rufus was consul for the third time, on the 11th day before the Kalends of April, according to their decree, a place of burial [---].
EDCS-09300909.summary: This inscription records a decree made by officials and the college of artisans concerning a burial place, dated to the consulship of Nerva and Verginius Rufus (AD 97).

EDCS-09300911.translation: Publius Sacirius, son of Saciro, of the tribe Matia.
EDCS-09300911.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying an individual named Publius Sacirius.

EDCS-09300914.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a dedication or erection by Serius and Lucia Seran.

EDCS-09300922.text_edition: \n Clodius Licini libertus os vivus fecit sibi et Clodiai sic Licini libertae Septumai sic\n
EDCS-09300922.translation: Clodius, freedman of Licinus, made this while alive for himself and for Clodia, freedwoman of Licinus, and Septumia.
EDCS-09300922.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedman for himself and other named individuals, indicating a private tomb.

EDCS-09300923.summary: This inscription likely records Secundula as responsible for removing something, possibly a grave marker.

EDCS-09300924.translation: Aelia Decimana, daughter of Decimus, Julius [Isina?] [will perish?].
EDCS-09300924.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning Aelia Decimana and potentially Julius Isina, with a curse or threat.

EDCS-09300926.translation: Of Tigris, the bull colony, of swine, 13 fleeces [in weight?].
EDCS-09300926.summary: This inscription records quantities or weights of livestock (bulls, swine) and fleeces, possibly related to trade or tribute.

EDCS-09300927.translation: Aebutius: 47 pounds of wool from Myrina, 25 and three-quarters pounds.
EDCS-09300927.summary: This inscription records a transaction involving weights of wool by Aebutius, likely a merchant.

EDCS-09300928.translation: Hostilius Asiaticus: 40 pounds of wool, 27 pounds.
EDCS-09300928.summary: This inscription records a transaction involving weights of wool by Hostilius Asiaticus, likely a merchant.

EDCS-09300929.translation: Menander: 8 and a half pounds of allicium, 15 pounds of wool.
EDCS-09300929.summary: This inscription records a transaction involving weights of allicium and wool by Menander, likely a merchant.

EDCS-09300930.translation: Cincia Tuches: 9 pounds of wool from Myrrinus, 4 pounds.
EDCS-09300930.summary: This inscription records a transaction involving weights of wool by Cincia Tuches, likely a merchant.

EDCS-09300932.text_edition: \n Caio Flaminio Cai filio Velina Marcello tribuno cohortis VI praetoriae primo pilo bis donis donato a divis Vespasiano et Tito Tiberius Claudius Atticus amico optimo\n
EDCS-09300932.translation: To Gaius Flaminius, son of Gaius, of the tribe Velina, tribune of the VI Praetorian cohort, twice awarded military decorations, from Tiberius Claudius Atticus, his very best friend.
EDCS-09300932.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a friend to Tiberius Claudius Atticus honoring Gaius Flaminius, a decorated military officer.

EDCS-09300933.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Securae coniugi dulcissimae Aurelius Crescens fecit\n
EDCS-09300933.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aurelius Crescens made this for Secura, his dearest wife.
EDCS-09300933.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a husband, Aurelius Crescens, for his wife, Secura.

EDCS-09400346.translation: Splendonius and Hilara with their family made 200 feet.
EDCS-09400346.summary: This inscription records the completion of a construction project, possibly a pavement or floor, by Splendonius and Hilara.

EDCS-09400348.translation: Ursa with her family made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400348.summary: This inscription records the completion of a construction project, possibly a pavement or floor, by Ursa.

EDCS-09400349.summary: This inscription records the completion of a construction project, possibly a pavement or floor, by Anatolius.

EDCS-09400350.translation: Primenius and Leontia with their family made 300 feet.
EDCS-09400350.summary: This inscription records the completion of a construction project, possibly a pavement or floor, by Primenius and Leontia.

EDCS-09400351.translation: Constantius and Agrippina with their family made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400351.summary: This inscription records the completion of a construction project, possibly a pavement or floor, by Constantius and Agrippina.

EDCS-09400352.translation: Euticius with his family made 33 feet.
EDCS-09400352.summary: This inscription records the completion of a construction project, possibly a pavement or floor, by Euticius.

EDCS-09400354.translation: Leo and his household made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400354.summary: This inscription records a construction of 100 feet made by Leo and his household.

EDCS-09400356.translation: Anicitus and his household made feet. Basilius and his household made 70 feet.
EDCS-09400356.summary: This inscription records two constructions, one by Anicitus and his household, and another of 70 feet by Basilius and his household.
