EDCS-09400358.translation: Atelia Pascentius and Severa and their households made 300 feet.
EDCS-09400358.summary: This inscription records a construction of 300 feet made by Atelia Pascentius, Severa, and their households.

EDCS-09400359.translation: Constantius and Maximella and their households made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400359.summary: This inscription records a construction of 100 feet made by Constantius, Maximella, and their households.

EDCS-09400360.translation: Eusebius and his household made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400360.summary: This inscription records a construction of 100 feet made by Eusebius and his household.

EDCS-09400361.translation: Eusebius and Niaru and their households made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400361.summary: This inscription records a construction of 100 feet made by Eusebius, Niaru, and their households.

EDCS-09400363.translation: Festus and Ursacia and their households made 200 feet.
EDCS-09400363.summary: This inscription records a construction of 200 feet made by Festus, Ursacia, and their households.

EDCS-09400364.translation: Gaudentius and Sora and their households made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400364.summary: This inscription records a construction of 100 feet made by Gaudentius, Sora, and their households.

EDCS-09400368.translation: Iulianus and Acricia and their households made 500 feet.
EDCS-09400368.summary: This inscription records a construction of 500 feet made by Iulianus, Acricia, and their households.

EDCS-09400370.translation: Lucianus and Romulus made 100 feet. Sorillio and Nonnosa made 35 feet.
EDCS-09400370.summary: This inscription records two constructions, one of 100 feet by Lucianus and Romulus, and another of 35 feet by Sorillio and Nonnosa.

EDCS-09400371.translation: Martyris and Felicitas with their household made 200 feet.
EDCS-09400371.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 200 feet by Martyris and Felicitas, likely a husband and wife or business partners, with their dependents.

EDCS-09400372.translation: Maxentius with his household made [something of] feet.
EDCS-09400372.summary: This inscription records a dedication of an unspecified length of feet by Maxentius and his dependents.

EDCS-09400374.translation: Primenius and Leontia with their household made 200 feet.
EDCS-09400374.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 200 feet by Primenius and Leontia, likely a married couple, with their household.

EDCS-09400375.translation: Victor and Theosebes with their children made 200 feet.
EDCS-09400375.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 200 feet by Victor and Theosebes and their children.

EDCS-09400376.translation: Victorinus and Anes with their household made 200 feet.
EDCS-09400376.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 200 feet by Victorinus and Anes, likely a couple, with their dependents.

EDCS-09400377.translation: O and [others] with their household made 50 feet for the Lord Sabaoth.
EDCS-09400377.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 50 feet to the Lord Sabaoth by O and unspecified individuals with their dependents.

EDCS-09400380.translation: From the lands of the church, Nonnosus with his household made 100 feet.
EDCS-09400380.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 100 feet by Nonnosus, possibly a steward or manager, from church property, along with his dependents.

EDCS-09400384.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 25 feet by a woman named Iohanna.

EDCS-09400385.translation: Vigilius with his household made 25 feet.
EDCS-09400385.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 25 feet by Vigilius and his dependents.

EDCS-09400386.translation: Honoratus with his household made 25 feet.
EDCS-09400386.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 25 feet by Honoratus and his dependents.

EDCS-09400387.translation: Martinianus and Simplicia with their children made this, 100 feet.
EDCS-09400387.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 100 feet made by Martinianus and Simplicia with their children, likely for a building project.

EDCS-09400389.translation: Domninus, your most distinguished servant, fulfilling his vow, paid his debt.
EDCS-09400389.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Domninus, described as a distinguished servant, likely to a deity.

EDCS-09400390.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Elias as a bishop, possibly on a tomb or a dedicatory monument.

EDCS-09400394.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by a person named Honoratus, likely to a deity.

EDCS-09400395.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by a person named Probus, likely to a deity.

EDCS-09400405.translation: Serges and Thecla and their son Theodorus and Anastasia with their families made this, 45 feet.
EDCS-09400405.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 45 feet made by Serges, Thecla, their son Theodorus, and Anastasia with their families, likely for a building project.

EDCS-09400407.translation: Malchus and Eufimia with their families fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-09400407.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Malchus and Eufimia with their families, likely to a deity.

EDCS-09400408.translation: Amara and Valentinianus made this, 25 feet.
EDCS-09400408.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 25 feet made by Amara and Valentinianus, likely for a building project.

EDCS-09400409.translation: Iohannes and Afrodites fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-09400409.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Iohannes and Afrodites, likely to a deity.

EDCS-09400410.translation: Felix with his family made this, 20 feet.
EDCS-09400410.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 20 feet made by Felix with his family, likely for a building project.

EDCS-09400415.text_edition: \n Publio Cassio Florenti IIIIIIviro et sibi Sempronia Decimi liberta Iucunda viva fecit in fronte pedes retro pedes \n
EDCS-09400415.translation: Sempronia Iucunda, freedwoman of Decimus, made this while alive for Publius Cassius Florentus, a duovir, and for herself, measuring 6 feet in front and 6 feet in depth.
EDCS-09400415.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a woman for herself and a local magistrate, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-09400426.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Iulius Aequanus Lauto.

EDCS-09400427.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary or ownership inscription.

EDCS-09400428.text_edition: \n Lucius Stetilius Blandi filius Repentinus testamento fieri iussit longum in agro pedes XX in fronte pedes XX\n
EDCS-09400428.translation: Lucius Stetilius Repentinus, son of Blandus, ordered this to be made in his will, measuring 20 feet long and 20 feet wide.
EDCS-09400428.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument ordered in a will by Lucius Stetilius Repentinus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-09400429.translation: Ius Naevius, son of Tertius, of the XV Apollinaris legion.
EDCS-09400429.summary: This identifies Ius Naevius as a soldier of the XV Apollinaris legion.

EDCS-09400432.translation: I, Aulus Vergilius Acutus, freedman of Aulus, was here. The place...
EDCS-09400432.summary: This inscription begins with a funerary dedication by Aulus Vergilius Acutus.

EDCS-09400433.text_edition: \n Titus Aponius Publi filius Aniensis signifer legionis IX Hispaniensis veteranus donatus torquibus armillis phaleris Lucius Aponius Publi filius fratri fecit\n
EDCS-09400433.translation: To Titus Aponius, son of Publius, of the tribe Aniensis, standard-bearer of the IX Hispana legion, a veteran awarded with neck-rings, armlets, and phalerae. Lucius Aponius, son of Publius, made this for his brother.
EDCS-09400433.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Aponius to his brother, Titus Aponius, a decorated veteran standard-bearer of a Roman legion.

EDCS-09400434.text_edition: \n Viva fecit Sextilia Marci liberta Pamphila sibi et Marco Sextilio Marci liberto Hilarioni filio et Sextiliae Spuri filiae Secundae filiae in fronte pedes XV in agro pedes XV\n
EDCS-09400434.translation: Sextilia Pamphila, freedwoman of Marcus, made this while alive for herself, and for Marcus Sextilius Hilarion, son of Marcus, her son, and for Sextilia Secunda, daughter of Spurius, daughter, measuring 15 feet in front and 15 feet in depth.
EDCS-09400434.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedwoman for herself and her children, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-09400435.translation: In the name of Herennia Amanda, wife, Etruscus.
EDCS-09400435.summary: This inscription names Herennia Amanda and likely refers to a property or ownership matter.

EDCS-09400436.text_edition: \n Quintus Domatius Cai filius bonum tempus mihi meaeque aetati id ego mando remandata quo iis apud Deos Inferos ut pereant et defigantur quo ego heres sim pupillus Cai Grani Cai filii Caius Poblicius populi libertus Aphrodisius Lucius Cornelius meo sumptu defigo illos quo pereant\n
EDCS-09400436.translation: Quintus Domatius, son of Gaius, 'good times' for me and my lifetime. I order that they perish and be fixed down among the Gods Below, so that I may be heir. Caius Poblicius Aphrodisius, freedman of Lucius Cornelius, of the people, fixes them at my expense so that they may perish.
EDCS-09400436.summary: This is a curse inscription by Caius Poblicius Aphrodisius, acting as heir, intended to ensure the destruction of certain property or records, possibly related to an inheritance dispute.

EDCS-09401069.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sept<i=E>mo abietario homini studiosissimo musicae bene merenti Phaedimus praepositus posuit retro quae legis \n
EDCS-09401069.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Phaedimus, the prefect, set this up for Septimus, a most dedicated lover of music, who deserved well; read what is behind.
EDCS-09401069.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Phaedimus for Septimus, a musician.

EDCS-09401070.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Aug. Anthis, his wife.
EDCS-09401070.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Aug. Anthis, his wife.

EDCS-09401071.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Victor pater Victoriae filiae bene merenti vivus posuit\n
EDCS-09401071.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Victor set this up during his lifetime for his well-deserving daughter Victoria.
EDCS-09401071.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Victor for his daughter Victoria.

EDCS-09401424.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai libertus Philippus vivus fecit sibi et Iuliae Melissae\n
EDCS-09401424.translation: Gaius Julius Philippus, freedman of Gaius, made this during his lifetime for himself and Julia Melissa.
EDCS-09401424.summary: A private dedication made by Gaius Julius Philippus for himself and his wife Julia Melissa.

EDCS-09700137.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gemella, an incomparable wife, who lived nineteen years, nine months, and ten days.
EDCS-09700137.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gemella, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-09700145.translation: Here rest Antoninus the tribune and Agnella his wife.
EDCS-09700145.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Antoninus, a tribune, and his wife Agnella.

EDCS-09700147.translation: Valentius Baebianus the Younger built the bathhouse from the ground up, in the consulship of Nepotianus and Facundus.
EDCS-09700147.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a bathhouse built by Valentius Baebianus the Younger, dated by consuls to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09700961.translation: Eudicus gave this gift to Temavus, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09700961.summary: This is a votive or dedicatory inscription by Eudicus to Temavus.

EDCS-09800091.text_edition: \n Titus Cassius Neptuno votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09800091.translation: Titus Cassius willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Neptune.
EDCS-09800091.summary: A votive inscription recording Titus Cassius paying a vow to Neptune.

EDCS-10000446.translation: Publius Clodius. Publius Clodius. Eleven feet in front and in the field...
EDCS-10000446.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary, specifying dimensions related to Publius Clodius.

EDCS-10000449.translation: Antiocus ordered by his will to have this made in the field, 12 feet.
EDCS-10000449.summary: This inscription records a posthumous building instruction from a will, specifying dimensions in a field, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10000450.translation: to the daughter of Aelius Frontinus, to Titius Quinti, son of Sexta, from his mother.
EDCS-10000450.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial, possibly for a family member, with names and filiation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10000457.translation: To the Genius of Barbulanus, Philaedemon.
EDCS-10000457.summary: An inscription dedicating a gift to the Genius of Barbulanus.

EDCS-10000458.translation: To the departed spirits of Titus Galgestius Proculus.
EDCS-10000458.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a deceased individual named Titus Galgestius Proculus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10000459.summary: This is a simple naming inscription, likely identifying a person and their father (filiation), possibly from a tombstone or other monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10000460.text_edition: \n Marcus Claudius Marci filius Acerrentinus IIIIvir aedilicia potestate IIIIvir iure dicundo sibi et Pomlinae coniugi suae castissimae\n
EDCS-10000460.translation: Marcus Claudius Acerrentinus, son of Marcus, as a four-man official with aedilician power and a four-man official for administering justice, for himself and his most chaste wife Pomlinae.
EDCS-10000460.summary: An inscription recording the public offices held by Marcus Claudius Acerrentinus and his dedication for himself and his wife.

EDCS-10000461.translation: Tiberius Volusius Hermes, freedman of Tiberius, the Augustalis, made this while alive for himself and for Volusia Clymene, his freedwoman and wife, and for my sons Tiberius Volusius Severus and Tiberius Volusius Maximus, and for my freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-10000461.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman, Tiberius Volusius Hermes, for himself and his family including his wife, children, and freedmen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10000462.translation: To the departed spirits. Valeria Saturnina made this while alive for herself and for Zoticus, her deserving husband.
EDCS-10000462.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a woman, Valeria Saturnina, for herself and her husband, Zoticus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10000467.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flavia Ii filio suo dulcissimo vixit annis XII et sibi et coniugi suo et libertis libertabusque posterisque eorum\n
EDCS-10000467.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Flavia, his sweetest son, who lived 12 years, and for himself, and for his wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-10000467.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a parent for a son, and also for the dedicator, spouse, and descendants.

EDCS-10000471.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly part of a larger dedication or funerary text.

EDCS-10001204.translation: Servilia Scione, his wife, made this while alive for herself.
EDCS-10001204.summary: This inscription records a woman, Servilia Scione, setting up a monument for herself during her lifetime, likely a funerary marker, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10001207.summary: This inscription is a memorial dedicated to a person named Honoratus, possibly marking a tomb or a monument in his honor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10001208.translation: Marcus Aurelius Iustus gladly fulfilled a vow undertaken for Flora Augusta.
EDCS-10001208.summary: This inscription records a private individual, Marcus Aurelius Iustus, fulfilling a vow made to a deity or personified entity named Flora Augusta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10001210.summary: This inscription records an individual named Petrus fulfilling a vow, likely a personal religious offering or dedication, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10001213.translation: Publius Virtius Mogetius, son of Publius, freedman, a sexvir, made this monument for himself and for Virtia Athenis, freedwoman of Publius, while alive; in front 20 feet, in depth 11 feet. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-10001213.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Virtius Mogetius for himself and his freedwoman partner, specifying its dimensions and non-hereditary status.

EDCS-10001214.summary: This is a brief dedication to Gaius Virdius, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-10001220.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Gemella, an incomparable wife, who lived 19 years, 9 months, 10 days.
EDCS-10001220.summary: This epitaph records the death of Gemella, a devoted wife, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-10001223.translation: [...ertius...onia, daughter of Cai... Secunda, made this while alive for herself and for [Bi]a Prisca.
EDCS-10001223.summary: This funerary inscription records that Secunda made a monument for herself and Bia Prisca.

EDCS-10001226.translation: Gaius Julius Anymphus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10001226.summary: A votive inscription recording Gaius Julius Anymphus paying a vow.

EDCS-10700030.translation: To Fortuna Felix. Built by the Augusti many years ago.
EDCS-10700030.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Felix, noting it was erected by emperors in the past.

EDCS-10700033.text_edition: \n Silvano Silvestri Auctor vectigalis Illyrici stationis Plorucensis votum posuit libens merito\n
EDCS-10700033.translation: To Silvanus of the Forest, Auctor, collector of taxes for the Illyrian customs post at Plorucensis, willingly and deservedly placed this vow.
EDCS-10700033.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Silvanus by a tax collector, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700034.translation: Lucius Oppius Peregrinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10700034.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Lucius Oppius Peregrinus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700036.translation: Getacius Vincentius, a most distinguished man, and Turrania Iusta, a most distinguished lady, erected [this monument] for themselves.
EDCS-10700036.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument for Getacius Vincentius and Turrania Iusta, both of high status, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700037.translation: Lucius Voltigonius, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, named Celer. He served in the 10th Praetorian Cohort for 12 years, and was transferred and served as a speculator for 14 years. He lived 44 years. For himself and for his mother, Capenia Maxima, daughter of Gaius, and for his brother, [---] Voltigonius [---].
EDCS-10700037.summary: This funerary inscription records the military service and lifespan of Lucius Voltigonius, who served in the Praetorian Guard and as a speculator, and also commemorates his mother and brother, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700040.summary: This is a dedication or memorial to Lucius, son of Balbus.

EDCS-10700047.translation: Titus Ammonius Clemens, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, lived and made this for himself and his family, and for his grandmother Petronia Secunda, daughter of Venetus; for his father Lucius Ammontius Volti(a)vus; for his mother Petronia Quarta, daughter of Sextus; and for his brother Lucius Ammontius Maximus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-10700047.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Titus Ammonius Clemens for himself and his family, including his parents, grandmother, and brother, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700048.translation: Pomponia Procula, daughter of Lucius, of the Pomponia tribe, lived and made this for her father Lucius Pomponius Sampsaron, freedman.
EDCS-10700048.summary: This funerary inscription records Pomponia Procula setting up a monument for her father, Lucius Pomponius Sampsaron, a freedman, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700049.text_edition: \n Caius Servius Iunia Titi filia vivi fecerunt sibi suisque \n
EDCS-10700049.translation: Gaius Servius and Iunia, daughter of Titus, lived and made this for themselves and their family.
EDCS-10700049.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording Gaius Servius and Iunia setting up a monument for themselves and their family, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700051.summary: This inscription identifies Philo as a freedman and son of Ci.

EDCS-10700052.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription indicating that Ursos and others were responsible for its creation.

EDCS-10700053.translation: Bones / Of Volta, daughter of Veroparis.
EDCS-10700053.summary: This inscription records the burial of Volta, daughter of Veroparis.

EDCS-10700076.translation: Vigilius and Dominica with their family made 300 feet. Profuturus and Matura with their family made 300 feet.
EDCS-10700076.summary: This inscription seems to record the creation of funerary plots or structures, each measuring 300 feet, by two separate family groups.

EDCS-10700092.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Ammon. Marcus Aemilius, consul, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly for the restored CIL (or Cenomani?).
EDCS-10700092.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Ammon by Marcus Aemilius, a consul, likely from the CIL or Cenomani region.

EDCS-10700093.translation: Sacred to Isis. Antenor gave this gift at her admonition.
EDCS-10700093.summary: A dedication to Isis by Antenor, who claims divine inspiration.

EDCS-10700094.translation: For Quintus Lentulus, proconsul, who died during the Italian War.
EDCS-10700094.summary: An inscription commemorating Quintus Lentulus, a proconsul who perished in the Italian War.

EDCS-10700095.translation: To Luxonia, daughter of Caius Atius.
EDCS-10700095.summary: A dedication or memorial for Luxonia, daughter of Caius Atius.

EDCS-10700096.summary: The name of Publius Julius Marcellus, possibly as a dedication or a memorial.

EDCS-10700097.translation: Calventia Ren and Calventius Ditus willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to the Saving Fates.
EDCS-10700097.summary: A vow fulfilled by Calventia Ren and Calventius Ditus to the Saving Fates.

EDCS-10700099.translation: To the Genius of Augustus of the college. For Caius Rubenius, son of Caius Romilius. With public money. Caius Rubenius, son of Caius.
EDCS-10700099.summary: A dedication to the Genius of Augustus by a college, funded by public money, possibly commemorating Caius Rubenius.

EDCS-10700102.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus. Caius Virius Pollio, by vision and command.
EDCS-10700102.summary: A dedication to Neptune Augustus by Caius Virius Pollio, who claims divine instruction.

EDCS-10700103.translation: For the private man Camidius. Quintus Praesentius Albus, Secunda his wife, Titus Praesentius Maxsuma, wife of Titus Praesentius, Caius Arilius, Caius Arenus, Polla, Fabricia, Lucius Allius, Lucius Vassidius Clemens, Prisca his wife, Vassidi Monimus, Acutius Erotis, Acutia, Caius Pro Damio, his freedman: If any enemy, female enemy, adversary, foe, to you, Father Orcus, with your Proserpina, with your Pluto, I hand him over, so that you may cast him down and oppress him, and your two-headed and three-headed dogs may seize his head and thoughts, and receive him into your underworld.
EDCS-10700103.summary: A powerful curse inscription invoking the underworld deities Orcus, Proserpina, and Pluto against enemies, dedicated by a group including Quintus Praesentius Albus and his family, and freedmen.

EDCS-10700105.translation: Marcus Crimilius fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10700105.summary: A vow fulfilled by Marcus Crimilius.

EDCS-10700112.translation: Gavis Raupatnis, a soldier, from the Ostobii, to his father Frivus.
EDCS-10700112.summary: This funerary inscription records a soldier's dedication to his father.

EDCS-10700113.translation: Lucius Blattius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, a centurion of the Fourth Macedonian Legion, was chosen as a decurion.
EDCS-10700113.summary: This inscription records the career advancement of Lucius Blattius, a centurion, to the position of decurion.

EDCS-10700115.translation: Marcus Antius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, serving in the Fifth Urban Legion.
EDCS-10700115.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Antius and his military service in the Fifth Urban Legion.

EDCS-10700116.translation: To Lucius Helvius Fronton, serving in the Fifth Urban Legion.
EDCS-10700116.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Helvius Fronton, a soldier in the Fifth Urban Legion.

EDCS-10700117.translation: The remains of Publius Lucilius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, from the 5th Urban Legion.
EDCS-10700117.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating the burial place of Publius Lucilius, a soldier from the 5th Urban Legion, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700118.translation: Caius Vinnius, son of Salvius, of the Romilia tribe, serving in the Fifth Urban Legion; his wife Maxima, daughter of Marcus, of the Mucia tribe; and their daughter Paulla, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-10700118.summary: This inscription lists a family, including Caius Vinnius, his wife Maxima, and their daughter Paulla, with mention of military service for Caius Vinnius.

EDCS-10700119.translation: Lucius Villius, son of Publius, of the Romilia tribe, serving in the Eleventh Legion.
EDCS-10700119.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Villius and his military service in the Eleventh Legion.

EDCS-10700120.translation: Caius Aelius Tertius, son of Tertius, of the Romilia tribe, serving in the first Praetorian cohort, aged 27.
EDCS-10700120.summary: This inscription records the identity, military service, and age of Caius Aelius Tertius.

EDCS-10700121.translation: To Quintus Magius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe, a scout from the praetorian guard, aged 27; his wife Prisca, daughter of Lucius, alive.
EDCS-10700121.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quintus Magius, a scout, and his wife Prisca, indicating he was alive at the time of its creation.

EDCS-10700124.translation: Caius Coelius Laetus, freedman of Caius, a priest of the college of Six (IIIIII vir); Coelia, freedwoman of a woman, his concubine Chia.
EDCS-10700124.summary: This inscription lists Caius Coelius Laetus, a priest, and his concubine Chia, indicating their social status.

EDCS-10700126.translation: To Marcus Vassidius Severus, son of Marcus, priest of the college of Six (IIIIII vir); and to his son Marcus Vassidius Proculus, priest of the college of Six; and to his son; Sabina, daughter of Lucius, alive, made this for herself and her family, and for Marcus Vassidius Memorialis, freedman of Marcus, this place of burial; the heir shall not inherit.
EDCS-10700126.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial plot and monument established by Sabina for her family, including her husband and son, both priests, and a freedman, explicitly forbidding inheritance by a future heir.

EDCS-10700129.translation: The decuria of Quintus Arruntius Surus, with Quintus Arruntius Callo Sabellus as guarantor and Titus Arrius as financier, 98 people in total, 42 feet per person, for a total of 214,000 feet of work.
EDCS-10700129.summary: This inscription records the construction of a work by a decuria, likely a work gang, detailing the number of people, their contribution per person, and the total work accomplished, overseen by specific officials.

EDCS-10700130.translation: Caius Plotius Lemonia, son of Marcius, and Publius Opsius Calvio, freedman of Publius, gave the remaining money.
EDCS-10700130.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Caius Plotius Lemonia and Publius Opsius Calvio, handing over remaining funds, possibly in an administrative or financial context.

EDCS-10700133.translation: Burial place of Publius Acutius, son of Publius, 17 feet on one side and 17 feet on the other.
EDCS-10700133.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Publius Acutius, son of Publius, and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-10700134.summary: This is a simple funerary or ownership marker for Quintus Acutius Rufio.

EDCS-10700135.translation: Clemens placed this for Acutia Lyris, freedwoman, his fellow soldier.
EDCS-10700135.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Clemens for his fellow soldier (contubernalis), Acutia Lyris, who was a freedwoman.

EDCS-10700137.summary: This is a fragment, likely part of a larger inscription, identifying Aemilia as the daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-10700138.summary: This is a fragment, likely part of a larger inscription, identifying Secunda Aemilia as the daughter of Cnaeus.

EDCS-10700142.translation: For Alfena Matrona, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-10700142.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or memorial for Alfena Matrona, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-10700143.summary: This is a simple name inscription, possibly a tombstone or dedication by Publius Alfidius Princeps.

EDCS-10700145.translation: Cnaeus Annius Romilia, son of Surus, placed this, a most dutiful son.
EDCS-10700145.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Cnaeus Annius Romilia, son of Surus, who is identified as a very dutiful son.

EDCS-10700147.translation: Lucius Antonius Philoxenes, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-10700147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Antonius Philoxenes, a freedman.

EDCS-10700150.translation: Caius Aupicius made this, 15 feet across the front, during his lifetime.
EDCS-10700150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the dimensions of a burial plot made by Caius Aupicius.

EDCS-10700151.translation: Manius Baebius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, and Marcus Baebius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, Celer, aged 25, 15 feet in all directions; this place.
EDCS-10700151.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Manius Baebius and Marcus Baebius Celer, possibly indicating a family burial plot and its dimensions.

EDCS-10700152.translation: Manius Baebius, son of Manius, 12 feet across the front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-10700152.summary: This inscription, likely part of a funerary monument, specifies the dimensions of a plot belonging to Manius Baebius.

EDCS-10700153.translation: Lucius Betilienus Eron, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-10700153.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Betilienus Eron, a freedman.

EDCS-10700154.translation: Paeta, mother of Blattia, freedwoman of Lucius, set this up.
EDCS-10700154.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Paeta set up a monument for her daughter Blattia.

EDCS-10700155.translation: Gaius Caerellius, son of Gaius; Quintus Caerellius, son of Gaius; Lucius Caerellius, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-10700155.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, likely brothers, of the Caerellius family and the Romilia tribe.

EDCS-10700156.translation: Gaius Calventius, son of Cai [---]marius / [---]ia C[---]
EDCS-10700156.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly related to a family or an individual named Calventius.

EDCS-10700157.translation: To Cassius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, Mac[---]
EDCS-10700157.summary: This is a dedication to Cassius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, likely a funerary or honorific inscription.

EDCS-10700158.text_edition: \n Lucio Cassio Luci liberto Paullo et Marco Spintio Marci filio Marcello et Marco Spintio Marci liberto Secundo\n
EDCS-10700158.translation: To Lucius Cassius Paulus, freedman of Lucius; and to Marcus Spintius Marcellus, son of Marcus; and to Marcus Spintius Secundus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-10700158.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Lucius Cassius Paulus, Marcus Spintius Marcellus, and Marcus Spintius Secundus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700159.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iucunda, a freedwoman.

EDCS-10700160.translation: Titus Sextus, son of Catus, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, gives the wall of Casconius around the entire tomb of the Catius, Calidius, and Helvius families.
EDCS-10700160.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a wall around a family tomb by Titus Sextus.

EDCS-10700161.translation: Gaius Cisonius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-10700161.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Gaius Cisonius.

EDCS-10700162.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Gaius Claudius.

EDCS-10700163.translation: Konia, daughter of Gnaeus, Libona, daughter of Gaius, Quarta, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-10700163.summary: This inscription lists the names of three women, Konia, Libona, and Quarta, along with their parentage.

EDCS-10700164.translation: For Gaius Coponius Scirpa, son of Gaius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-10700164.summary: This inscription is a dedication or mention of Gaius Coponius Scirpa.

EDCS-10700165.translation: Gaius Corellius Synistor, freedman of Gaius, ordered by his will to be made for himself and for his wife Corellia Athenis, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-10700165.summary: This inscription records a posthumous funerary commission by Gaius Corellius Synistor for himself and his wife.

EDCS-10700166.translation: Titus Corelius Tertius, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-10700166.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Titus Corelius Tertius.

EDCS-10700167.summary: This inscription is a dedication or mention of Cornelia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-10700169.translation: Curilia Secunda, daughter of Mani, of the Curilia tribe, lived and made this for herself, and for her husband Gaius Arruntius Stabilis, son of Gaius, most deserving; and for her son Lucius Arruntius Crescent, son of Gaius, most dutiful, who lived 19 years, 11 months, and 5 days; and for [her] freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-10700169.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Curilia Secunda for herself, her husband, her son (recording his age at death), and her freedpersons, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700170.translation: Lucius Decius, son, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-10700170.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Decius.

EDCS-10700171.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Valerius Diodorus, identifying him as Greek.

EDCS-10700173.translation: To Egusia Severa, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-10700173.summary: This is a dedication to Egusia Severa, a freedwoman, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700174.translation: Mestria Fortunata, freedwoman of Sextus, and her daughters, placed [this] for Manius Ennius Criton.
EDCS-10700174.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Mestria Fortunata and her daughters for Manius Ennius Criton, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700176.summary: This is a dedication by Arria Prima for Eronis, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700179.translation: Quintus ... from the Romilia tribe, son of Lo...
EDCS-10700179.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription providing only a name and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-10700180.translation: Publius Tudicius, son of Lucius, husband, made [this] for Geminia Secunda, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-10700180.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a husband for his wife, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700181.summary: This is a dedication to Gentei Ivantios, likely an Italic personal name, possibly from the 1st century BCE - 1st century CE.

EDCS-10700184.translation: Epidia Donata placed [this] for Marcus Herennius Chrestus.
EDCS-10700184.summary: This is a dedication by Epidia Donata for Marcus Herennius Chrestus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700185.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription for Hipparchus, son of Marcus Arrius Maximus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700186.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription for Lais, daughter of Marcus Arrius, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700187.translation: On the front, 15 feet. Of Titus Livius, freedman of Aulus, Leuga.
EDCS-10700187.summary: This inscription records a measurement of 15 feet and names Titus Livius, freedman of Aulus, and possibly another person or descriptor 'Leuga', likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700189.summary: This is a simple grave marker identifying the burial place of Caius Lusius.

EDCS-10700190.translation: For Lucius Luxonius, son of Lucius, twenty feet in front.
EDCS-10700190.summary: This inscription records the funerary space for Lucius Luxonius, son of Lucius, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-10700193.translation: To the shades of the underworld, for Marsia Eucharis, his wife.
EDCS-10700193.summary: This is a funerary dedication (dis manibus) for a woman named Marsia Eucharis, likely set up by her husband, implied by the missing word 'coniu[gi]' (wife).

EDCS-10700195.translation: To Titus Minucius, son of Titus, for his father.
EDCS-10700195.summary: This dedicates a monument to Titus Minucius, son of Titus, for his father.

EDCS-10700197.translation: Titus Sallonius Pollio and Aenius, sons of Gaius, made this for Modesta.
EDCS-10700197.summary: This funerary monument was created by Titus Sallonius Pollio and Aenius, sons of Gaius, for Modesta.

EDCS-10700198.translation: Burial place of Caius Naevius Fructus, twenty feet in front and twenty feet in depth.
EDCS-10700198.summary: This grave marker specifies the burial plot dimensions for Caius Naevius Fructus.

EDCS-10700199.translation: Narantus, son of Marcus Arrius, aged three.
EDCS-10700199.summary: This inscription records the name and age of a child, Narantus, son of Marcus Arrius.

EDCS-10700201.translation: The bones of Caia Pacatia, aged forty, who earned her freedom, were placed here; Lucius Barbius Mansuetus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive.
EDCS-10700201.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Lucius Barbius Mansuetus for his freedwoman Caia Pacatia, specifying her age and the fact that she earned her freedom.

EDCS-10700202.translation: Publius Papirius Serenus, son of Publius, aged ten.
EDCS-10700202.summary: This inscription records the name and age of a child, Publius Papirius Serenus.

EDCS-10700204.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Petronius Vitulus and his age, though it is incomplete.

EDCS-10700205.translation: To the freedman of Gaius, Philargyrus, and to the freedwoman of Lucius, Fausta.
EDCS-10700205.summary: This monument is dedicated to Philargyrus, a freedman of Gaius, and Fausta, a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-10700206.translation: Vitalis, freedwoman of Postumulena, the daughter of Postumulenus Lucius, Sabina, her freedwoman, made this while alive.
EDCS-10700206.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a freedwoman for her patroness, likely in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-10700211.translation: Prima, the maidservant, and her daughter.
EDCS-10700211.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription for a maidservant named Prima and her daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700212.translation: Calybe, freedwoman, set this up for Primigenius, aged 17, son of Publius Atidius Peregrinus, and for herself and her sons.
EDCS-10700212.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a tomb by a freedwoman for her son and herself, with the son being the son of a known man, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700213.translation: Daughter Prisca, 60 feet in front, 46 feet behind.
EDCS-10700213.summary: This inscription likely marks the dimensions of a burial plot allocated to a daughter named Prisca, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700216.translation: Pullia Secunda, daughter of Sextus Pullius, for herself and for her father Sexitus Pullius Bassus, son of Titus, and for her mother Procula, daughter of Quintus, and for her husband Lucius Turranius Firmus, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-10700216.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by Pullia Secunda for herself, her parents, and her husband, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700217.translation: Lucius Terentius Asti, father, set this up for his son Phyramis.
EDCS-10700217.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a father for his son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700218.translation: Lucius Raecius Actiacus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-10700218.summary: This is a simple epitaph identifying an individual by name and filiation, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700220.translation: For Fuxsia Rutilia, wife of Soccius.
EDCS-10700220.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to Fuxsia Rutilia, the wife of Soccius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700222.translation: Burial place for Rutilia Firma, daughter of Quintus. In front 22 feet. In front 22 feet.
EDCS-10700222.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot and its dimensions for Rutilia Firma, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700224.summary: This is a brief epitaph stating the name and age of the deceased, Samus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700225.translation: Quintus Satrius, son of Annius, made this while alive; 30 feet in front, 20 feet in his land.
EDCS-10700225.summary: An epitaph recording the dimensions of a burial plot donated by Quintus Satrius.

EDCS-10700226.translation: Quintus Satrius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-10700226.summary: A tribal affiliation and name, likely related to a funerary context.

EDCS-10700228.translation: 20 feet in front; buried in April.
EDCS-10700228.summary: A brief funerary inscription indicating the dimensions of the burial space and the month of interment.

EDCS-10700229.translation: Titus Sicinius Ursio made this while alive; 16 feet in front, 20 feet deep.
EDCS-10700229.summary: A funerary inscription detailing the dimensions of a plot prepared by Titus Sicinius Ursio.

EDCS-10700232.translation: To Gaius Strabunius, freedman of Gaius, Trimixsus.
EDCS-10700232.summary: A dedication to Gaius Strabunius, a freedman, likely for a funerary monument or cult.

EDCS-10700233.translation: 8 feet for the path from the embankment to the burial of Lucius Suillius Tiro, son of Gaius. 8 feet for the path to the embankment.
EDCS-10700233.summary: An inscription defining a pathway to a burial, specifying its dimensions and its connection to a road or embankment.

EDCS-10700234.translation: The caretakers of the house set up (this monument) for the ashes of Suetonia Logadis, freedwoman of Lucius, and of Lucius Suetonius Crescentis, his wife, in the plot of Lucius Sicius Florus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-10700234.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Suetonia Logadis and her husband Lucius Suetonius Crescentis, placed in the plot of Lucius Sicius Florus.

EDCS-10700235.translation: Quintus Tasatinus Atimetus made this while alive for himself and for his most dutiful son Quintus Tasatinus Simplicius; this plot and monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-10700235.summary: A self-dedicated funerary monument for Quintus Tasatinus Atimetus and his son, specifying that the plot is not inheritable.

EDCS-10700237.translation: Maxsuma Titia, daughter of Titus, daughter's daughter of Marcus, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-10700237.summary: An abbreviated funerary inscription providing the name and patronymic of a woman, likely Maxsuma Titia.

EDCS-10700238.translation: To the Divine Shades of Gaius Trosius Hermetes, son of Gaius, aged [---].
EDCS-10700238.summary: A dedication to the Divine Shades (Dis Manibus) for Gaius Trosius Hermetes, specifying his parentage and age.

EDCS-10700239.translation: His sister placed this for Publius Trottidius Malliolus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-10700239.summary: A funerary monument set up by a sister for her freedman brother.

EDCS-10700242.translation: Marcus Vassidius Adiutor, freedman of Marcus, made this in his lifetime for his fellow slave and freedman son, Epimelus, freedman of Vassidia Prisca.
EDCS-10700242.summary: A funerary monument made by a freedman for his deceased slave partner and son.

EDCS-10700243.translation: Venusta, aged 3. Her father Caius Cotius Buculus.
EDCS-10700243.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child, set up by her father.

EDCS-10700245.translation: Titus Vetius Valens, son of Titus, aged 5.
EDCS-10700245.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child.

EDCS-10700246.summary: A funerary inscription identifying Vettia as a freedwoman.

EDCS-10700325.summary: An inscription recording the creation of a monument by Decimus Arrius Felix.

EDCS-10700326.translation: Epagathus' diasmyrnes, after an attack of eye inflammation, Epagathus' diamisus, to remove roughness, Epagathus' horaeon crocodes, for roughness, Epagathus' theoctiston, to remove diathesis.
EDCS-10700326.summary: A list of medicinal preparations, likely for eye treatment, associated with someone named Epagathus.

EDCS-10700327.summary: A label for a substance, likely medicinal, for improving clarity.

EDCS-10700328.summary: A label for a substance, likely medicinal, for improving clarity.

EDCS-10701342.text_edition: \n Iovi Lucius Caius Titus Mettai Cai filii votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-10701342.translation: Lucius Caius Titus and Titus, sons of Caius, freely and deservedly paid their vow to Jupiter.
EDCS-10701342.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter by Lucius Caius Titus and Titus, sons of Caius.

EDCS-10701344.text_edition: \n Libertati Augustae sacrum Titus Publicius Ianuarius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10701344.translation: Titus Publicius Ianuarius freely and deservedly dedicated this sacred offering to August Liberty.
EDCS-10701344.summary: This is a dedication to the deified Liberty (Libertas Augusta) by Titus Publicius Ianuarius, likely commemorating an imperial grant or freedom.

EDCS-10701345.text_edition: \n Cornaeliae sic Saloninae Augustae coniugi domini nostri Gallieni Augusti decurionum decreto\n
EDCS-10701345.translation: For Cornelia Salonina, wife of our lord Gallienus Augustus, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-10701345.summary: This is a dedication to Cornelia Salonina, wife of Emperor Gallienus, commissioned by a decree of the decurions (local councillors).

EDCS-10701346.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Flavio Valerio Constantio nobilissimo Caesari decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-10701346.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-10701346.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantius, honoring him by decree of the local councillors.

EDCS-10701347.text_edition: \n Ithaci Marco Carminio Marci filio Papiria Pudenti equo publico sacerdoti Laurentium Lavinatium electo ad causas fisci tuendas in provincia Alpium Maritimarum patrono rei publicae Tergestinorum patrono plebis urbanae patrono collegiorum dendrophororum et fabrum curatori rei publicae Mantuanorum curatori rei publicae Vicetinorum patrono Catubrinorum Iunia Valeriana marito rarissimo locus datus decreto decurionum Ithaci\n
EDCS-10701347.translation: To Ithacus, son of Marcus Carminius, of the Papiria tribe, Pudentus, a publically-funded equestrian priest of the Laurentes Lavinates, elected to protect the interests of the treasury in the province of the Maritime Alps, patron of the state of Tergestinum, patron of the urban plebs, patron of the collegia of dendrophori and fabrorum, curator of the state of Mantua, curator of the state of Vicetia, patron of the Catubrini; Iunia Valeriana gave this place to her most wonderful husband, by decree of the decurions, for Ithacus.
EDCS-10701347.summary: This extensive dedication honors Marcus Carminius Pudentus, detailing his many public and religious offices and his patronage of various groups, likely marking a funerary monument or public space dedicated by his wife Iunia Valeriana.

EDCS-10701348.text_edition: \n Marco Carminio Marci filio Papiria Pudenti equo publico sacerdoti Laurentium Lavinatium electo ad causas fisci tuendas in provincia Alpium Maritimarum patrono rei publicae Tergestinorum patrono plebis urbanae patrono collegiorum dendrophororum et fabrorum curatori rei publicae Mantuanorum curatori rei publicae Vicetinorum patrono Catubrinorum plebs urbana patrono ob merita statuam a plebe oblatam Iunia Valeriana remissa plebei sic inpensa pecunia sua posuit\n
EDCS-10701348.translation: To Marcus Carminius, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, Pudentus, a publically-funded equestrian priest of the Laurentes Lavinates, elected to protect the interests of the treasury in the province of the Maritime Alps, patron of the state of Tergestinum, patron of the urban plebs, patron of the collegia of dendrophori and fabrorum, curator of the state of Mantua, curator of the state of Vicetia, patron of the Catubrini; the urban plebs, as patron, having offered a statue to him for his merits, Iunia Valeriana, having remitted the expenses to the plebs, erected it with her own money.
EDCS-10701348.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Marcus Carminius Pudentus by the urban plebs, honoring his patronage, with the expenses being covered by his wife Iunia Valeriana.

EDCS-10701349.text_edition: \n Capertiae Maximi filiae Valerianae plebs urbana patronae\n
EDCS-10701349.translation: To Capertia, daughter of Maximi, Valeriana, patroness, by the urban plebs.
EDCS-10701349.summary: This inscription records the urban plebs honoring Capertia Valeriana, daughter of Maximi, as their patroness.

EDCS-10701350.text_edition: \n Tito Aemilio Papiria Casto ex testamento Turraniae Placidae Publius Turranius Severus Titus Turranius Iustus posuerunt\n
EDCS-10701350.translation: To Titus Aemilius Castus, according to the will of Turrania Placidus, Publius Turranius Severus and Titus Turranius Iustus erected this.
EDCS-10701350.summary: This is a funerary dedication erected by Publius Turranius Severus and Titus Turranius Iustus, in accordance with the will of Turrania Placidus, for Titus Aemilius Castus.

EDCS-10701352.translation: Mettaia Severa, daughter of Lucius, aged 25.
EDCS-10701352.summary: A funerary epitaph for Mettaia Severa.

EDCS-10701353.text_edition: \n Titus S Secundus vivus fecit sibi et coniugi carissimae\n
EDCS-10701353.translation: Titus S. Secundus made this for himself and his dearest wife while alive.
EDCS-10701353.summary: This is a funerary monument (vivus fecit) erected by Titus S. Secundus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-10701355.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Tuton[---]
EDCS-10701355.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for someone named Tuton[---].

EDCS-10701540.summary: This is the name of the Roman poet Aulus Persius Flaccus, likely the subject or author of an inscription.

EDCS-10701544.text_edition: \n Decurionum decreto publice Lucio Hostilio Luci filio Menenia Statuto IIIIviro iure dicundo adlecto aerario Hostilius et Caerulea parentes inpensa remissa fecerunt\n
EDCS-10701544.translation: By decree of the decurions, the parents, Hostilius and Caerulea, in remission of expenses, made this for Lucius Hostilius Statutus, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, who was appointed as a IIIIvir iure dicundo and to the aerarium.
EDCS-10701544.summary: A public dedication made by parents for their son, Lucius Hostilius Statutus, who held significant local magistracies, likely dating to the early Empire.

EDCS-10701545.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Maximiae Victoriae Arpagius et I\n
EDCS-10701545.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Arpagius and I[---] for Maximia Victoria.
EDCS-10701545.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for Maximia Victoria, made by Arpagius and I[---].

EDCS-10701546.translation: in memory of Aeronia Maxima, dearest wife, who died having raised adult children, aged 35.
EDCS-10701546.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating Aeronia Maxima, a woman who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-10701721.text_edition: \n Lucio Domitio Marci filio Poblilia Severo praefecto cohortis Campanae praefecto alae Aureanae Hispanorum I tribuno militum legionis XX IIIIviro iure dicundo flamini designato ala Aureana Hispanorum I\n
EDCS-10701721.translation: To Lucius Domitius Severus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, prefect of the Campana cohort, prefect of the Aureana I Spanish ala, tribune of the soldiers of the XX legion, IIIIvir iure dicundo, designated flamen; [dedicated by?] the Aureana I Spanish ala.
EDCS-10701721.summary: An epitaph or dedication commemorating Lucius Domitius Severus, detailing his extensive military and civil career, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10701722.text_edition: \n Cornelio Publi filio Poblilia Balbo tribuno militum IIIIviro iure dicundo auguri Caecilia Luci filia uxor\n
EDCS-10701722.translation: To Cornelius Balbus, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, tribune of the soldiers, IIIIvir iure dicundo, augur; and Caecilia, daughter of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-10701722.summary: A funerary dedication for Cornelius Balbus and his wife Caecilia, listing his cursus honorum which included military and religious offices.

EDCS-10701723.text_edition: \n Numerio Caesio Luci filio Senecioni tribuno militum Lucius Annius Iucundus\n
EDCS-10701723.translation: To Numerius Caesius Senecio, son of Lucius, tribune of the soldiers; Lucius Annius Iucundus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10701723.summary: A dedication made by Lucius Annius Iucundus for Numerius Caesius Senecio, a military tribune.

EDCS-10701729.translation: Marcus Mammius Mucro, freedman of Marcus, his husband, and Herennia Rufilla, freedwoman of Lucius, her mother, and Marcus Mammius Repentinus, freedman of Marcus, and Eunya, freedwoman of Lucius, made this while alive, for themselves.
EDCS-10701729.summary: A funerary monument set up by Eunya for her husband Marcus Mammius Mucro, his mother Herennia Rufilla, and others, including herself.

EDCS-10701739.translation: Gaius Vaxonius Mercator, son of Gaius, a member of the board of four officials, holding the power of an aedile.
EDCS-10701739.summary: An inscription recording the name and civic offices of Gaius Vaxonius Mercator.

EDCS-10701742.translation: Marcus Virtius Proculus, father, made this for his soldier son of the II Traiana legion, aged 21.
EDCS-10701742.summary: A funerary dedication by a father for his deceased son, a soldier in the Legio II Traiana.

EDCS-10800095.translation: Publici Festius and Festiva, husband and wife, set up [this] votive offering to Fortuna and Victoria.
EDCS-10800095.summary: A votive offering to the goddesses Fortuna and Victoria by a married couple, Publici Festius and Festiva.

EDCS-10800096.translation: Marcus Minicius Minicianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled [his] vow to the Iunones.
EDCS-10800096.summary: A vow fulfilled by Marcus Minicius Minicianus to the Iunones (a group of goddesses).

EDCS-10800097.translation: [---] son of Lucius, Celer / to the Matronae, willingly and deservedly fulfilled [his] vow.
EDCS-10800097.summary: A vow fulfilled by Celer, son of Lucius, to the Matronae, likely local mother goddesses.

EDCS-10800099.text_edition: \n Ruca Maximi filius Veneri Augustae sacrum votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800099.translation: Ruca, son of Maximu, willingly and deservedly fulfilled [his] vow to Venera Augusta.
EDCS-10800099.summary: A vow fulfilled by Ruca, son of Maximu, to the divine Venera Augusta.

EDCS-10800100.text_edition: \n Saturno Augusto sacrum Claudius Parrus solvit votum merito\n
EDCS-10800100.translation: Claudius Parrus dutifully fulfilled his vow to the divine Saturn.
EDCS-10800100.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Saturn by Claudius Parrus.

EDCS-10800101.translation: For Marcus Tussanius Saturninus, son of Marcus, decurion of Verona, and for V[---]iasia Pura, daughter of Sextus, and for his parents.
EDCS-10800101.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcus Tussanius Saturninus, a decurion of Verona, and his family members.

EDCS-10800102.translation: Quintus Gavius Felix, son of Marcus, member of the college of six priests...
EDCS-10800102.summary: An incomplete inscription that appears to record the name and religious office of Quintus Gavius Felix.

EDCS-10800105.translation: ...for his sister, and for Marcus Minicius Proculus, son of Marcus, his brother, and for Cassia Secunda, daughter of Spurius, his wife, he ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-10800105.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that a monument was erected by will for a brother, sister, and wife.

EDCS-10800106.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Caius Domitius Luci filius Clemens sibi et Domitiae Publi filiae Secundae uxori et suis\n
EDCS-10800106.translation: Gaius Domitius Clemens, son of Lucius, made this for himself, his wife Domitia Secunda, daughter of Publius, and his family, while alive.
EDCS-10800106.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Gaius Domitius Clemens for himself and his family.

EDCS-10800107.translation: Marcus Tecesalus Constans ordered this to be made by his will for himself and his family.
EDCS-10800107.summary: A funerary dedication ordered by will by Marcus Tecesalus Constans for himself and his household.

EDCS-10800360.text_edition: \n Flavio Valerio Constantio fortissimo ac nobilissimo Caesari Iulius Asclepiodotus vir clarissimus et Aurelius Hermogenianus vir eminentissimus praefecti praetorio devoti numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-10800360.translation: For Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the most courageous and noble Caesar, Iulius Asclepiodotus, a man of the highest rank, and Aurelius Hermogenianus, a man of eminent status, prefects of the praetorium, devoted to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-10800360.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus by two high-ranking officials, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-10800361.translation: For Marcus Nonius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-10800361.summary: A simple dedication, likely funerary, for Marcus Nonius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-10800362.translation: To Gaius Bellicius Primus, son of Gaius, of the Claudian tribe, a distinguished man, tribune of the 2nd Cohort of Gauls, procurator of the sacred grain supply, of the citizenship of Verona, in memory of his outstanding loyalty in friendship and everlasting praise of concord, and for the memory of so good a name, Lucius Germanus Cassianus and Gaius Masculinius Reginus, to their patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10800362.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by two friends to their patron, a former military tribune and imperial official, with the location granted by a decree of the town council.

EDCS-10800363.translation: For Clodia Secunda, daughter of Publius, priestess of the divine Matidia, the guilds of craftsmen and the cloth merchants.
EDCS-10800363.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Clodia Secunda, a priestess, by two guilds.

EDCS-10800364.translation: To Publius Antonius Callistio, VIvir Augustalis, for his services, his freedwoman Thallusa dedicated and gave in trust 1000 sesterces, from the interest of which, on the Ides of February each year, a sacrifice shall be made. The quaestor, whoever he may be.
EDCS-10800364.summary: A dedication by a freedwoman to her patron, a member of the VIvir Augustalis college, endowing an annual sacrifice with 1000 sesterces.

EDCS-10800365.translation: To Publius Bodius Iuventius, VIvir of Milan and Brixia, Quintus Sentius Clemens and Sextus Sextius Secundus, to their best friend.
EDCS-10800365.summary: A dedication by two friends, Quintus Sentius Clemens and Sextus Sextius Secundus, to their friend Publius Bodius Iuventius, a VIvir of Milan and Brixia.

EDCS-10800367.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Verina placed this for Aether, the net-fighter.
EDCS-10800367.summary: This is a tombstone inscription set up by Verina for Aether, a retiarius gladiator.

EDCS-10800368.translation: For Sextus Cornelius Firmus, of the vicus of Minerva.
EDCS-10800368.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Cornelius Firmus, likely associated with the district (vicus) of Minerva.

EDCS-10800369.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly recording a name and an associated office or title, with significant lacunae.

EDCS-10800370.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely dedicated to a freedwoman named Placidia, with missing context.

EDCS-10800371.summary: A fragmentary inscription dedicating something to Lucius Sextius Capito, with missing context.

EDCS-10800374.summary: An extremely fragmentary inscription, possibly containing parts of names or titles, with no discernible meaning.

EDCS-10800380.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Valerius Hymnus.
EDCS-10800380.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Gaius Valerius Hymnus, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-10800384.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus, Marcus Coelius Fabia Catullus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10800384.summary: A votive inscription to Neptune Augustus by Marcus Coelius Fabia Catullus.

EDCS-10800388.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, of Quintus Gargennius Primigenius.
EDCS-10800388.summary: A funerary inscription dedicating a tomb or memorial to Quintus Gargennius Primigenius.

EDCS-10800391.translation: Lucius Decius Primus gladly paid his vow to Minerva, as was deserved.
EDCS-10800391.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a payment to Minerva by Lucius Decius Primus.

EDCS-10800392.translation: Quintus P S paid his vow to Minerva.
EDCS-10800392.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a payment to Minerva by Quintus P S.

EDCS-10800393.translation: Marcus Statius Valens gladly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10800393.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Statius Valens.

EDCS-10800394.summary: This is a funerary or identification marker for Axil, a freedman of Sextus.

EDCS-10900075.text_edition: \n Libero A(ugusto)? s(acrum) Lucius Va Turro et Claudia A port om\n
EDCS-10900075.translation: Sacred to Liber Augustus (?). Lucius Va Turro and Claudia Aportom.
EDCS-10900075.summary: This is a dedication to Liber Augustus by Lucius Va Turro and Claudia Aportom.

EDCS-10900076.translation: Silicius Rufus gave this as a gift to Sentona.
EDCS-10900076.summary: This is a dedication inscription by Silicius Rufus to Sentona.

EDCS-10900078.text_edition: \n Quinto Baieno Publi filio [Pupinia Blassiano] [] [] [] [] c [ Imperatori Caesari Flavio Constantino Maximo Pio Felici Augusto res publica Tergestinorum devota numini potestatique eius\n
EDCS-10900078.translation: For Quintus Baienus, son of Publius, [Pupinius Blassiannus]... the state of the Tergestines, devoted to the divine will and power of the Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantinus Maximus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-10900078.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the state of Tergeste to Emperor Constantinus, possibly relating to a monument or a grant.

EDCS-10900079.text_edition: \n Caius Velitius Marci filius Lemonia Bononia miles legionis XX stipendiorum XXIV locus monumenti pedes quadratos XII\n
EDCS-10900079.translation: Gaius Velitius, son of Marcus, from the Lemonian tribe, of Bononia, a soldier of the 20th legion, with 24 years of service; the monument's area is 12 square feet.
EDCS-10900079.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Velitius, a soldier of the 20th legion, indicating his military service and burial plot size.

EDCS-10900081.text_edition: \n Sextus Palpellius Sexti libertus Fructus Augustalis sibi et suis et Aeliae Priscae uxori et Laecaniae Acri coniugi testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-10900081.translation: Sextus Palpellius Fructus, freedman of Sextus, Augustalis, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and his family, and for his wife Aelia Prisca, and for his wife Laecania Acta.
EDCS-10900081.summary: This is a funerary dedication ordered by Sextus Palpellius Fructus for himself, his family, and his wives.

EDCS-10900082.text_edition: \n Synhodo Titaciae Tertiae dispensatori Solo frater\n
EDCS-10900082.translation: Synhodus to Titacia Tertia, his sister, the steward Solo.
EDCS-10900082.summary: This is an inscription honoring Titacia Tertia, the steward Solo, and his sister Synhodus.

EDCS-10900086.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Acerretinus Verus made this for his parents, [---] and Thymele, freedwoman of Acerretinus.
EDCS-10900086.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Acerretinus Verus for his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900088.translation: Gaius Carconius Myrtilus made this while alive for himself, and for his wife Marcella Moliavisa, and for his son Marcellus, buried here.
EDCS-10900088.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Carconius Myrtilus for himself, his wife, and his son.

EDCS-10900089.translation: Fabia Serena, freedwoman, made this while alive for her daughter Nymphe, daughter of the freedwoman of Aulus Fabius, aged 25.
EDCS-10900089.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fabia Serena for her daughter Nymphe, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900090.text_edition: \n et Flaviae Paezusae filiabus et viv-- sibi in fronte pedes XXX in agro pedes XX\n
EDCS-10900090.translation: and for his daughters Flavia Paezusa and ... while alive for himself, 30 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-10900090.summary: This inscription seems to record land dimensions and is possibly part of a larger funerary or property dedication.

EDCS-10900091.translation: Laetus [made this] for Aphrodisias, daughter of Petronius Aper.
EDCS-10900091.summary: This is a dedication or funerary marker, likely from the Roman Imperial period, by Laetus for Aphrodisias.

EDCS-10900092.text_edition: \n Caio Liburnio Cai filio Valenti Achaicus libertus vivus fecit sibi et suisque sic omnibus\n
EDCS-10900092.translation: Achaicus, freedman, while alive, made this for Gaius Liburnius Valentus, son of Gaius, and for his family, all thus.
EDCS-10900092.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Achaicus, a freedman, for himself, his family, and Gaius Liburnius Valentus.

EDCS-10900093.text_edition: \n Glyconi Titi Sextili Se patris et Rosci Omuncionis viri \n
EDCS-10900093.translation: to Glyco, son of Titus Sextilius Sex. [---] and husband of Roscia Omuncionis.
EDCS-10900093.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to Glyco, mentioning his father Titus Sextilius Sex. and his husband Roscius Omuncionis.

EDCS-10900094.translation: Quintus Teidius Donatus and Teidia Zosima made this while alive for their son Teidius Eulimenus.
EDCS-10900094.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Quintus Teidius Donatus and Teidia Zosima for their son Teidius Eulimenus.

EDCS-10900095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Vi Paulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900103.translation: Uranius Maior made this with his family, 90 feet.
EDCS-10900103.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication measuring 90 feet, made by Uranius Maior and his family, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900107.translation: Apronianus, an illustrious man, made this in fulfillment of his vow.
EDCS-10900107.summary: This is a votive inscription by Apronianus, a man of high status, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900108.translation: Johannes and Dominica, together with their sons Maximus, notary and defender of the holy church of Aquileia, and Agnello, a most illustrious man, made 200 feet for their vow.
EDCS-10900108.summary: This is a votive inscription from Aquileia, likely dating to the 5th or 6th century CE, recording a dedication of 200 feet by a family including church officials.

EDCS-10900109.translation: Eufemia, together with her son Chrysogonus, defender of the holy church of Aquileia, made 100 feet.
EDCS-10900109.summary: This inscription from Aquileia, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE, records a dedication of 100 feet by a mother and son who were associated with the church.

EDCS-10900110.translation: Bonosus, defender of the holy church of Tergeste, made 100 feet.
EDCS-10900110.summary: This inscription from Tergeste, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE, records a dedication of 100 feet by a church official.

EDCS-10900113.translation: Your servant Constantinos, a priest, made 100 feet.
EDCS-10900113.summary: This is a dedication of 100 feet by Constantinos, a priest, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE.

EDCS-10900114.translation: Ianuarius, priest of the holy church of Tergeste, made 100 feet.
EDCS-10900114.summary: This inscription from Tergeste, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE, records a dedication of 100 feet by a priest of the local church.

EDCS-10900115.summary: This is a dedication of 100 feet by Augustinus, a deacon, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE.

EDCS-10900116.translation: Barsaina, primicerius of the pensorum, made 16 feet.
EDCS-10900116.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 16 feet by Barsaina, an official in charge of the 'pensorum', likely from the 5th or 6th century CE.

EDCS-10900117.translation: Iubianus, a sarsor, and Secunda, together with their family, made 50 feet.
EDCS-10900117.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 50 feet by Iubianus, identified as a 'sarsor', and Secunda and their family, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE.

EDCS-10900118.translation: Iustinianus, together with his family, made 15 feet.
EDCS-10900118.summary: This inscription records a dedication of 15 feet by Iustinianus and his family, likely from the 5th or 6th century CE.

EDCS-10900186.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Minervae Veneri Lucius C Firmianus votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900186.translation: Lucius C. Firmianus joyfully, willingly, and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Minerva, and Venus.
EDCS-10900186.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius C. Firmianus to Jupiter, Minerva, and Venus.

EDCS-10900187.text_edition: \n Laribus Augustis Marcus Arinius Epagathus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900187.translation: Marcus Arinius Epagathus joyfully, willingly, and deservedly paid his vow to the Household Gods.
EDCS-10900187.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Arinius Epagathus to the Lares Augusti (Household Gods).

EDCS-10900188.text_edition: \n Silvano Augusto Publius Camerius Euangelus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900188.translation: Publius Camerius Euangelus joyfully, willingly, and deservedly paid his vow to Silvanus Augustus.
EDCS-10900188.summary: This is a votive inscription by Publius Camerius Euangelus to Silvanus Augustus.

EDCS-10900190.translation: Gaius Gavius Gratus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900190.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Gavius Gratus, indicating the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10900193.text_edition: \n Caius Atilius Publi filius Papiria Attianus miles sibi et Fafilinoni uxori et Atiliae Ampliae filiae\n
EDCS-10900193.translation: Caius Atilius Attianus, son of Publius, of the Papiria tribe, a soldier, [dedicated this] for himself, his wife Fafilinona, and his daughter Atilia Ampla.
EDCS-10900193.summary: This is a dedication by a soldier, Caius Atilius Attianus, for himself and his family.

EDCS-10900194.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Aurelio Sexti filio VIviro Tridenti Acutia Ursula coniugi carissimo bene merenti\n
EDCS-10900194.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Marcus Aurelius, son of Sextus, a VIvir of Tridenti, and for his dearest and most deserving wife, Acutia Ursula.
EDCS-10900194.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius and his wife Acutia Ursula, possibly dating to the late Roman Republic or early Empire given the VIvir title.

EDCS-10900195.text_edition: \n Marco Publicio Tridentinorum liberto Metrodoro VIviro Augustali Amphion Tridentinorum bene merenti\n
EDCS-10900195.translation: For Metrodorus, freedman of the people of Tridenti, a VIvir and Augustalis, to Amphion of Tridenti, most deserving.
EDCS-10900195.summary: This inscription honors Metrodorus, a freedman and local official, likely from Tridentum.

EDCS-10900196.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Dis Manibus Aphrodisiae alumnae Titus Munatius Charito VIvir Augusta<l=I>(is) \n
EDCS-10900196.translation: Made while alive. To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Aphrodisia, his foster-daughter. Titus Munatius Charito, a VIvir of Augusta.
EDCS-10900196.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Titus Munatius Charito for his foster-daughter Aphrodisia, likely from Augusta Treverorum.

EDCS-10900199.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Luci Cossoni Sabiniani fistulatoris Lucius Cossonius Florus patrono et Axia Saturnina et Axius Bubalus \n
EDCS-10900199.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Lucius Cossonius Sabinianus, the fistulator. Lucius Cossonius Florus, and Axia Saturnina and Axius Bubalus [dedicated this] to their patron.
EDCS-10900199.summary: This funerary inscription honors Lucius Cossonius Sabinianus, a fistulator (pipe player), by his patron and family members.

EDCS-10900201.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caeciliae Firminae Lucius Valerius Valerianus hunc locum curavit coniugi bene merenti\n
EDCS-10900201.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Valerius Valerianus arranged for this place for Caecilia Firmina, his most deserving wife.
EDCS-10900201.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Valerius Valerianus for his wife Caecilia Firmina.

EDCS-10900202.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus C Leandri fili Marcus Valerius vius pater \n
EDCS-10900202.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For C. Leander, son of [---]. Marcus Valerius [Vi]us, his father.
EDCS-10900202.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for C. Leander, dedicated by his father, Marcus Valerius Vius.

EDCS-10900203.text_edition: \n Call coniugi et Caio Iulio Ti filio \n
EDCS-10900203.translation: For Calli, his wife, and for Gaius Julius, son of Titus.
EDCS-10900203.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a wife named Calli and a son named Gaius Julius.

EDCS-10900205.text_edition: \n Lucio Romanio Salvio Lucius Romanius Peregrinus patri merenti\n
EDCS-10900205.translation: Lucius Romanius Peregrinus [dedicated this] to his deserving father, Lucius Romanus Salvius.
EDCS-10900205.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Romanius Peregrinus to his father, Lucius Romanius Salvius.

EDCS-10900206.text_edition: \n ------] Pistauci filius sibi et Luppae Biumi Bursaci filiae uxori carissimae huic monumento Turus filius meus exheres esto\n
EDCS-10900206.translation: To Pistaucus, his son, for himself and for his dearest wife Luppa Biumi, daughter of Bursacus; may my son Turus be disinherited from this monument.
EDCS-10900206.summary: This funerary inscription records a disinheritance decree related to the monument for Pistaucus and his wife.

EDCS-10900207.summary: This is a very brief inscription naming Valerius Valentinus as a freedman, likely of the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10900213.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly recording names or dedications.

EDCS-10900214.translation: From the gifts of God and Saints Cosmas and Damian, in the time of our lord Eugypius the bishop, Laurentius the cantor founded [this].
EDCS-10900214.summary: This inscription records the foundation of something by the cantor Laurentius during the episcopacy of Eugypius, likely in honor of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

EDCS-10900216.translation: Here lies the distinguished man Censorius, who lived 62 years and 7 days, and passed away on the day before the Ides of March, in the second indiction.
EDCS-10900216.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life span and death date of a distinguished man named Censorius.

EDCS-10900220.text_edition: \n Deo Herculi Lucius K Silvinus cum suis ex voto posuit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900220.translation: Lucius K Silvinus, with his family, set this up to the god Hercules in fulfillment of a vow, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-10900220.summary: This votive inscription records the dedication of a monument to Hercules by Lucius K Silvinus and his family.

EDCS-10900221.translation: Valerius Probus fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-10900221.summary: This votive inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Hercules by Valerius Probus.

EDCS-10900224.text_edition: \n D(eo) Soli Invicto M(ithrae) sacrum Caius Cus Iunianus votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900224.translation: Sacred to the Unconquered Sun God Mithras. Gaius Cus Iunianus fulfilled his vow, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-10900224.summary: This votive inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Sol Invictus Mithras by Gaius Cus Iunianus.

EDCS-10900225.text_edition: \n Saturno Patri Servano Macrinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900225.translation: Macrinus fulfilled his vow to Father Saturnus Servanus, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-10900225.summary: This votive inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Saturnus Servanus by Macrinus.

EDCS-10900226.text_edition: \n Caius Cassius Valens votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900226.translation: Caius Cassius Valens fulfilled his vow, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-10900226.summary: This votive inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Caius Cassius Valens.

EDCS-10900228.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Titus Aurelius Moravesus Servano veteranus legionis XXX Ulpiae victricis ex beneficiario tribuni sibi et suis\n
EDCS-10900228.translation: Titus Aurelius Moravesus, a veteran of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion, serving as beneficiarius of a tribune, made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-10900228.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made for himself and his family by Titus Aurelius Moravesus, a veteran and former beneficiarius of a tribune.

EDCS-10900229.text_edition: \n Cusoniae Pittae matri pientissimae et Proculo fratri carissimo et Raedoniae Firminae coniugi eius et Uldanoniae Maximae coniugi Victorini carissimae Raedonii Victorinus Tertius et Ingenuus et sibi et suis\n
EDCS-10900229.translation: Raedonius Victorinus Tertius and Ingenuus and for themselves and their families, to Cusonia Pitta, their most dutiful mother, and Proculus, their dearest brother, and Raedonia Firmina, his wife, and Uldanonia Maxima, the dearest wife of Victorinus.
EDCS-10900229.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument dedicated by Raedonius Victorinus Tertius and Ingenuus to various family members, including their mother, brother, and wives.

EDCS-10900230.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lumennones su pater et Firmina Lumennoni Maximo filio carissimo annorum XVIII vivi fecerunt et sibi\n
EDCS-10900230.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Father Lumennones and Firmina made this for their dearest son Lumennonius Maximus, aged 18, while they were alive, and also for themselves.
EDCS-10900230.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made by Lumennones and Firmina for their deceased son Lumennonius Maximus and for themselves.

EDCS-11600110.translation: Gaius Clodius Iucundus fulfilled his vow to the Spring.
EDCS-11600110.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Clodius Iucundus to a Spring deity.

EDCS-11600113.translation: To Eunomus(?), most faithful slave, of Publius Salvius Nepotis, lived 20 years.
EDCS-11600113.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Eunomus, a loyal slave of Publius Salvius Nepotis.
