EDCS-11600114.translation: To the shades of the underworld. To Julia Valentin(a), wife of Marcus [---], most beloved. Titus Aureli[us] Apron[ianus(?)] (a veteran of the Emperor) made this (monument) for himself and (his wife) while alive.
EDCS-11600114.summary: This is a tombstone for Julia Valentin(a), set up by her husband, a veteran, who also provided for himself.

EDCS-11600117.translation: Fortunatus [dedicated this] for himself and for his patron Heracles, the ephai, Amandus and Verus.
EDCS-11600117.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Fortunatus for himself and possibly for patrons or officials named Heracles, Amandus, and Verus.

EDCS-11600119.translation: To Titia Maximilla, a respectable woman. Valerius Maximinus, a recalled soldier, [---]
EDCS-11600119.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Titia Maximilla by Valerius Maximinus, a recalled soldier.

EDCS-11600120.translation: Sacred to the shades of the underworld. To Lucius [Licinius?] Lucullus, son of Caius, who held the office of quaestor for aedileship, served four times as aedile, and four times as a judge, and was prefect of justice, [---]
EDCS-11600120.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Lucullus, who held several important municipal offices, set up by an unknown person.

EDCS-11600122.translation: [---] Tertius, [---]ronia Secunda, daughter of Caius, made this (monument) for herself and for Barba Prisca, daughter of Titus, [---] while alive.
EDCS-11600122.summary: This is a tombstone for Tertius and Secunda, who made it for themselves and for Barba Prisca.

EDCS-11600123.translation: Faustus and Communis made this (monument) for their brother Primus and for themselves while alive, slaves of Tiberius Caesar.
EDCS-11600123.summary: This is a tombstone for Primus, set up by his brothers Faustus and Communis, who were slaves of Tiberius Caesar.

EDCS-11600128.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Onesimus, slave and steward of the revenues of Severilla, made this (monument) for his most dutiful wife, aged 35, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-11600128.summary: This is a tombstone for Onesimus' wife, set up by himself, who was a slave and steward.

EDCS-11600129.translation: To the shades of the underworld. To Claudia Marcellina, his most beloved friend, with whom he lived for 18 years. Publius Aelius [---]
EDCS-11600129.summary: This is a tombstone for Claudia Marcellina, set up by Publius Aelius, who records her age at death and their relationship.

EDCS-11600130.translation: [---] daughter of Quintus, [---]a, [---]verus, [---] made this (monument) for his wife while alive.
EDCS-11600130.summary: This is a tombstone for an unnamed wife, set up by her husband.

EDCS-11600131.translation: By the office of Publius Favonius, freedman of Publius, and Quintus Braetius, freedman of Quintus and Publius, Erotis, and Caius Tullius, freedman of Caius, Priamus, and Publius Favonius, freedman of Publius, Elpidica, and Caius Tullius, freedman of Caius, Philoxenus, and Quintus Braetius, freedman of Quintus, G[---], and Caius Tullius, freedman of Caius, Das[---], and Quintus Braetius Secun[---], and Publius Favonius, son of Auctus. A burial place for himself and his family, 22 feet in front, 26 feet deep.
EDCS-11600131.summary: This inscription records the sale of a burial plot measuring 22 by 26 feet to a group of freedmen, for their use and that of their families.

EDCS-11600132.translation: Quintus Dellius Myro, freedman of Quintus, a statue-maker.
EDCS-11600132.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Dellius Myro, a statue-maker and freedman.

EDCS-11600133.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly indicating ownership or a name.

EDCS-11600135.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly indicating ownership or a name.

EDCS-11600139.translation: Lucius Gnatius Germanus, of the Pob(ilia) tribe, a duovir, made this while alive.
EDCS-11600139.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Gnatius Germanus, a duovir, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11800657.text_edition: \n Quinto Poblicio Quinti filio legato pro praetore\n
EDCS-11800657.translation: To Quintus Poblicius, son of Quintus, legate pro praetor.
EDCS-11800657.summary: This is an inscription honoring Quintus Poblicius, son of Quintus, who held the office of legate pro praetor, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000876.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Titus Aurelius Seleucus dono dedit\n
EDCS-12000876.translation: Titus Aurelius Seleucus gave this to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-12000876.summary: This is a dedication to the god Jupiter Dolichenus by Titus Aurelius Seleucus, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000879.translation: To the August Hope, Gaius Cartorius Acereus [dedicated this] in memory of Cartoria Acte.
EDCS-12000879.summary: This inscription is a memorial dedication by Gaius Cartorius Acereus to the 'August Hope' and Cartoria Acte.

EDCS-12000880.text_edition: \n OSIIII Andetius Crassi filius avo @(obito) Marcus Pileius filius tribunus plebis\n
EDCS-12000880.translation: Andetius, son of Crassus, [having been appointed] tribune of the plebs after his grandfather Marcus Pileius, son of Andetius, died.
EDCS-12000880.summary: This inscription records the career progression of Andetius, son of Crassus, who became tribune of the plebs, likely dating to the Roman Republic.

EDCS-12000881.text_edition: \n Tito Trebelleno Luci filio Claudia Rufo quaestori urbano legato Imperatoris Caesaris Augusti tribuno plebis Publius Octavius Titi filius\n
EDCS-12000881.translation: To Titus Trebellius, son of Lucius, Rufus, urban quaestor, legate of Emperor Caesar Augustus, tribune of the plebs; Publius Octavius, son of Titus.
EDCS-12000881.summary: This inscription lists the career of Titus Trebellius, who held multiple important offices including urban quaestor and tribune of the plebs, likely during the early imperial period.

EDCS-12000884.text_edition: \n Tito Desticio Titi filio Claudia Severo primo pilo legionis X geminae subpraefecto vigilum procuratori Augusti provinciae Daciae superioris procuratori provinciae Cappadociae item Ponti mediterranei et Armeniae minoris et Lycaoniae procuratori Augustorum provinciae Raetiae procuratori provinciae Belgicae flamini divi Hadriani pontifici patrono coloniae Marcus Claudius Paternus amico optimo locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-12000884.translation: To Titus Desticius Severus, son of Titus, of the Claudia tribe, primus pilus of the Tenth Gemina legion, subprefect of the vigiles, procurator of Emperor Augustus of the province of Dacia superioris, procurator of the province of Cappadocia, likewise Pontus mediterraneus, Armenia minor, and Lycaonia, procurator of the Augusti of the province of Raetia, procurator of the province of Belgica, flamen of the deified Hadrian, pontiff, patron of the colony; Marcus Claudius Paternus, an excellent friend, was granted this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-12000884.summary: This lengthy inscription details the extensive career of Titus Desticius Severus and records a land grant to his friend Marcus Claudius Paternus by the local decurions, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-12000888.translation: [... by] will and [filled] the imperial [ditch] with trees and [mud(?)] and rubble. [...] Cicr[ius Severus] [made necessary(?)] [...] Sempronius Syrius [...] first concurring, with Cicrius Sev[erus ...] his homeland [...] his own [...]
EDCS-12000888.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription detailing the filling of an imperial ditch with materials and mentioning individuals likely involved in its creation or maintenance.

EDCS-12000891.translation: Manius Acilius, freedman of Manius, Eudamus, one of the VI viri, ordered this to be made by his will. Manius Acilius, freedman of Manius, Eudamus, one of the VI viri, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-12000891.summary: This inscription records that Manius Acilius Eudamus, a freedman and member of the college of VI viri, commissioned something in his will, with the text repeated for emphasis.

EDCS-12000892.translation: Lucius Seius Quadratus, one of the six imperial priests.
EDCS-12000892.summary: This is a funerary or official inscription identifying Lucius Seius Quadratus by name and his membership in the sexvirate, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100253.text_edition: \n Caio Cornelio Publi filio Claudia patri Cassiae matri Marco Cornelio Cai filio Claudia fratri Lucius Cornelius Cai filius Claudia Aquilinus |(centurio) legionis II testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-12100253.translation: To Gaius Cornelius, son of Publius, father Cassia, mother Marcus Cornelius, son of Gaius, brother Lucius Cornelius, son of Gaius Aquilinus, centurion of the Second legion, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-12100253.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Lucius Cornelius Aquilinus, a centurion of the Second legion, in his will for his family members, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12100255.translation: Gaius Aurelius Liccaeus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-12100255.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Gaius Aurelius Liccaeus, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100256.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Baiania Secunda by her praenomen, gentile name, and filiation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100257.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Titus Cervonius by his praenomen, gentile name, and filiation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100259.translation: Gaius Cornelius Anthus, son of Gaius, his freedman, made this while alive, and Galatini.
EDCS-12100259.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman, Gaius Cornelius Anthus, and possibly his wife or associate Galatini, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12100261.translation: Quintus Lemonius, son of Sextus, of the tribe Claudia.
EDCS-12100261.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Quintus Lemonius by his praenomen, gentile name, filiation, and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100263.translation: To Titus Petronius, son of Caius.
EDCS-12100263.summary: This is a dedicatory or funerary inscription identifying Titus Petronius, son of Caius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100264.summary: This is an ownership inscription, likely for a slave or freedman named Phoebus, belonging to Quintus Masenius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100265.translation: [...]ius, son of Marcus, from the Putinia tribe; [his] wife [Se]cunda; [his daughter]la, daughter of Quintus, Procula.
EDCS-12100265.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription naming three individuals, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12100266.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying an individual named Terentius, son of Publius, with some illegible preceding text, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100267.translation: Gaius Terentius Erasistratus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-12100267.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Gaius Terentius Erasistratus, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100269.translation: Area: 25 feet in front, 50 feet in depth, belonging to Lucius Regontius Rufus.
EDCS-12100269.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Lucius Regontius Rufus, likely for funerary or property purposes, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12100270.translation: The monument occupies 19 feet in front of the property of Venetia Maxima, and 50 feet in the field.
EDCS-12100270.summary: This is a boundary or property inscription defining the dimensions of a monument or land belonging to Venetia Maxima, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12100273.translation: To Titus Aetrius, son of Titus [---].
EDCS-12100273.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring Titus Aetrius, son of Titus, likely part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-12100274.translation: Marcus Armonius, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-12100274.summary: This inscription records a freedman, Marcus Armonius, who was manumitted by a woman.

EDCS-12100275.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Apate, a freedwoman, with Pontia as her former patron, probably on a tomb.

EDCS-12100276.translation: Marcus Porcius Auctus, freedman of Marcus. 50 feet in front, 75 feet in the rear.
EDCS-12100276.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a plot of land owned by Marcus Porcius Auctus, a freedman, possibly for burial purposes.

EDCS-12100277.translation: To Manius Barbius Severus, son of Tiberius, of the Claudia tribe.
EDCS-12100277.summary: This is a dedication to Manius Barbius Severus, son of Tiberius, a member of the Claudia tribe, likely for a public monument or grave.

EDCS-12100278.translation: Argentilla, freedwoman of a woman, made this while alive.
EDCS-12100278.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Argentilla, a freedwoman, who commissioned her own tomb during her lifetime.

EDCS-12100279.translation: Sextus Trebius, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe. Trebia Galla, freedwoman of Sextus, his wife. Trebia Primogenia. Sextus Trebius Gratus(?), freedman of Sextus.
EDCS-12100279.summary: This inscription lists members of a family, including a father, his wife, and children, with indications of their tribal affiliation and freed status.

EDCS-12100280.translation: The father [---]ttius, son of Titus, and Quarta, daughter of Marcus, his wife, and Philargurus [---]ttius, son of Publius, and Titullius, son of Titus, made [this].
EDCS-12100280.summary: This inscription records the makers of a monument, likely a tomb, including parents and possibly other relatives.

EDCS-12100281.translation: [...] for his most holy and most dutiful wife. Caius Porcius Felicissimus, her husband, made this while alive, and for himself, as much as from the will [of the wife?], he placed [this] for his most loving wife, and for himself, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-12100281.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Caius Porcius Felicissimus for his wife and himself, referencing her will and specifying dimensions.

EDCS-12100282.text_edition: \n Marcus Varienus filius Sabatina Dotus vivus fecit sibi et Gaio Varieno Iucundo filio et Erboniae uxori Spuri libertae Iucundae in fronte pedes XI retro pedes\n
EDCS-12100282.translation: Marcus Varienus Dotus, son of Sabatina, made this while alive for himself and for his son Gaius Varienus Iucundus and for his wife Erbonia, freedwoman of Spurius, and for Iucunda. 11 feet in front, [...] feet in the rear.
EDCS-12100282.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by Marcus Varienus Dotus for himself, his son, and his wife, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-12100283.summary: This inscription records Statia as the mother of Cytherinus Ennius, likely part of a funerary dedication.

EDCS-12100284.translation: To Titus Domitius Zosimus; to Titus Domitius Acilanus; to Acilia Threpte; Publius Caemius Paezo [dedicated this] to [his] friends.
EDCS-12100284.summary: This is a dedication by Publius Caemius Paezo to his friends Titus Domitius Zosimus, Titus Domitius Acilanus, and Acilia Threpte, likely on a tomb or a memorial.

EDCS-12100285.translation: To the departed spirits. Mestria Lais for her well-deserving patron, Titius Diogenes, made this while alive.
EDCS-12100285.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Mestria Lais to her deceased patron, Titius Diogenes.

EDCS-12200226.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Vibius Secundinus for his most dutiful wife, Porcia Ursa, who deserved well.
EDCS-12200226.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Vibius Secundinus to his deceased wife, Porcia Ursa.

EDCS-12200228.translation: To the most dutiful father, from the brothers Ulpius Avitianus and [---] Avitus, sons of Ulpius.
EDCS-12200228.summary: This is a dedication by sons to their most dutiful father, likely on a tomb, identifying them as brothers and sons of Ulpius.

EDCS-12200229.translation: To the departed spirits. For Vetia Chrysida, who lived 23 years and 6 months. Ostilius [---]
EDCS-12200229.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vetia Chrysida, detailing her age at death and mentioning Ostilius, likely a relative or commissioner.

EDCS-12200230.translation: Aged 10 years, 2 months, and 7 days. Iulius Iulianus, most unhappy father [dedicated this].
EDCS-12200230.summary: This inscription records the age of a deceased child and is a dedication by their unhappy father, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-12200231.translation: For Cattia Hermaida, who lived 2 years and 8 months. Her parents.
EDCS-12200231.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cattia Hermaida, indicating her young age and that her parents commissioned the monument.

EDCS-12200232.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Titus Desticius Sallustius, freedman.
EDCS-12200232.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedman named Titus Desticius Sallustius.

EDCS-12200233.translation: To Concordia, from Laelius Saturninus, to his most dutiful wife, well-deserving.
EDCS-12200233.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Laelius Saturninus to his wife Concordia, praising her virtues.

EDCS-12200234.translation: To the most dutiful mother [---]neratia Memmia Verecunda; from her son Antonius [---] Macer(?).
EDCS-12200234.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a most dutiful mother, Memmia Verecunda, by her son Antonius [---] Macer(?), likely on a tomb.

EDCS-12200235.text_edition: \n Publio Saepio Eufratae Saepia Leontis patri\n
EDCS-12200235.translation: To Publius Saepius Eufratas, father of Saepia Leontis.
EDCS-12200235.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Publius Saepius Eufratas, identified as the father of Saepia Leontis.

EDCS-12200236.text_edition: \n Irenaeae libertae dulcis quae fuisti in saeculo nnum XVIII Iulia Ravenna patrona\n
EDCS-12200236.translation: To Irenaea, sweetest freedwoman, who lived to be 18 years of age. From Julia Ravenna, patroness.
EDCS-12200236.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Irenaea, a freedwoman who died at age 18, dedicated by her patroness Julia Ravenna.

EDCS-12200237.translation: To Gaius Satelius Valentinus, from Oppia Cale, his excellent wife.
EDCS-12200237.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a wife to her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200239.translation: In this place lies the puppy, after his fate was restored. His sweet honey-like body is remembered. His name was Fuscus; he endured twelve years and his old limbs could scarcely bear him. [---]
EDCS-12200239.summary: This is a humorous epitaph for a dog named Fuscus who lived for twelve years.

EDCS-12300278.inscription_type: diplomata militaria, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12300278.translation: Emperor Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 12th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Country, to those who served in the praetorian fleet of Misenum which is under Iulius Fronto, having completed twenty-six years of service and been honorably discharged, has granted citizenship and the right of legal marriage to them and their children and descendants; and to those who were unmarried at the time citizenship was granted, they may have legal marriage with those they subsequently marry, provided each man has only one wife. Dated the 12th day before the Kalends of March, with Publius Iuventius Celsus II and Quintus Iulius Balbus as consuls. From a private soldier, Marcus Numisius Nomasius Corusus Vinacenus, son of Saionis. Transcribed and verified from the bronze tablet which is fixed in Rome on the wall behind the Temple of the deified Augustus near the Minervam. Officials: Tiberius Iulius Urbanus, Gaius Caelius Romanus, Tiberius Claudius Menander, Gaius Vettienus Modestus, Lucius Atteius Atteianus, Lucius Pullius Verecundus, Gaius Vettienus Hermetis.
EDCS-12300278.summary: This is an imperial rescript issued by Emperor Hadrian in 117 AD granting citizenship and the right of legal marriage to retired sailors of the praetorian fleet at Misenum, with officials listed.

EDCS-12300357.inscription_type: diplomata militaria, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12300357.translation: [---] whom [---] Bassus commands / [---]M / [---]S / [---]laudic[---] / [---]GI[---]laudic[---]L / [---] Besso / [---]GINO Alaband[---] / [---] Pann[---] / [---]L / [---]oni Philadel[---] / [---]O Alaband[---]C / [---] Nicom[---] / Emperor Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 5th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Country, Proconsul. Emperor Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 2nd time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Country. The names of the soldiers who served in the ten praetorian cohorts, Philippianae, Piis Vindicibus, who served faithfully and bravely, we grant the right of marriage, but only with single and first wives, so that even if they have joined women of foreign law in marriage, they may have children as if born of two Roman citizens. Dated the 7th day before the Ides of January, with Emperor Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus III and Emperor Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus II as consuls. Cohort VIII Praetoria Philippiana Pia Vindex. Marcus Braetius Iustinus, son of Marcus, from Sabatina, Mantua. Transcribed and verified from the bronze tablet which is fixed in Rome on the wall behind the Temple of the deified Augustus near the Minervam.
EDCS-12300357.summary: This is an imperial rescript issued by Emperors Philip I and II in 247 AD granting the right of legal marriage to soldiers of the Philippian praetorian cohorts, specifying it is for the first wives and listing a soldier from Cohort VIII.

EDCS-12800393.summary: This is a property mark or ownership inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12800395.summary: This is likely an ownership inscription or funerary marker, possibly indicating a property or tomb belonging to Commodus and Aelia Crispinus.

EDCS-13302536.text_edition: \n Hilari libertus Carpus Martialis libertus Alypus Hermae libertus Trophimus Sinon Marci Trosi Primi Onesimus Luci Stati Narcissi Primigenius Cai Iuli Verecundi magistri dederunt\n
EDCS-13302536.translation: Hilarius, freedman; Carpus Martialis, freedman; Alypus, freedman; Trophimus; Sinon; Onesimus, freedman; Primigenius, freedman. They were given by the freedman Lucius Statius Narcissus and the master Caius Iulius Verecundus.
EDCS-13302536.summary: This inscription records a dedication by several freedmen and a master, possibly in a religious or civic context.

EDCS-13302655.text_edition: \n Aulo Pisidio Auli liberto Phileroti IIIIIIviro Aulus Pisidius Alexander Aulus Pisidius Felix libertus Aulus Pisidius Faustus libertus Aulus Pisidius Adiutor libertus vota fecerunt\n
EDCS-13302655.translation: To Aulus Pisidius Philerotus, freedman of Aulus Pisidius, duovir, [four times?] vows were made by Aulus Pisidius Alexander, Aulus Pisidius Felix, freedman, Aulus Pisidius Faustus, freedman, Aulus Pisidius Adiutor, freedman.
EDCS-13302655.summary: This inscription records vows made by several freedmen, likely related to Aulus Pisidius Philerotus, who held a position of authority.

EDCS-13302730.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Arista, slave of our Caesar, an accountant and steward of the 20th tax collection. Herennia Heliodora, wife, and Heliodorus and Felix, sons.
EDCS-13302730.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Arista, a slave of the emperor who worked as an accountant and steward, with a dedication from her family.

EDCS-13302736.summary: This inscription likely refers to Lucius Minicius Mancus and his association with a stage, possibly in a theater or amphitheater.

EDCS-13400077.translation: The living Publius Coelius Princeps, freedman of Publius, and Flora, freedwoman of Liburnia Sextus.
EDCS-13400077.summary: This inscription records the names of two freedpersons, likely indicating their ownership of property or a burial plot, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500284.translation: The Thirteenth Legion Gemina, the Loyal.
EDCS-13500284.summary: This inscription names the Legio XIII Gemina, highlighting its loyalty, likely serving as a military standard or unit designation.

EDCS-13500286.translation: Claudia Priscus made [this] for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13500286.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600371.text_edition: \n Honori Cai Saeni Cai filii Scaptia Veri equo publico IIIIviri iure dicundo II Laurentium Lavinatium curatoris rerum publicarum Vicetinorum Atrianorum Opiterginorum Lucius Acutius Marc<e=I>llus cliens \n
EDCS-13600371.translation: To Honor, Gaius Saenius Verus, son of Gaius, of the Scaptia tribe, aedile with the power of jurisdiction, curator of public affairs for the Vicetinians, Atrians, and Opiterginians, Lucius Acutius Marcellus, his client.
EDCS-13600371.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Honor by Lucius Acutius Marcellus, client of Gaius Saenius Verus, who held several magistracies in various communities, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-13600393.text_edition: \n Cassia Titi filia hic sita est S<e=I>xtius Quinti filius speculator legionis IIII Macedonicae \n
EDCS-13600393.translation: Cassia, daughter of Titus, is buried here. Sextius, son of Quintus, a scout of the Fourth Macedonian Legion.
EDCS-13600393.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cassia, daughter of Titus, with a mention of Sextius, a scout in the Fourth Macedonian Legion, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13700342.text_edition: \n Lucius Lucilius Luci libertus Primus vivus fecit et coniugi suae et Lucilio Archelao conliberto suo sibe sic suis libertis libertabusque in frontem sic pedes XVI in agrum sic pedes XXXII pro indivisso sic\n
EDCS-13700342.translation: Lucius Lucilius Primus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive for himself, his wife, and his fellow freedman Lucius Archelaus, and his own freedmen and freedwomen, 16 feet in front, 32 feet in depth, undivided.
EDCS-13700342.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Lucilius Primus, a freedman, for himself and his family, including his wife and fellow freedman, detailing the dimensions of the plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13700414.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Iulia Severa votum solvit\n
EDCS-13700414.translation: Iulia Severa fulfilled her vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-13700414.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Iulia Severa fulfilling a vow to the god Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13700432.text_edition: \n Caius Atisius Cai filius Poblilia Pollio praefectus Drusi Caesaris iure dicundo fratri\n
EDCS-13700432.translation: Gaius Atisius Pollio, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, prefect of Drusus Caesar with the power of jurisdiction, to his brother.
EDCS-13700432.summary: This inscription records Gaius Atisius Pollio, who served as prefect under Drusus Caesar with judicial authority, and is addressed to his brother, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-13800144.text_edition: \n Titus Aelius Maternus veteranus ex beneficiario legionis II Italicae vivus emit filius testamento posuit \n
EDCS-13800144.translation: Titus Aelius Maternus, a veteran, formerly a beneficiary of the Second Italian Legion, bought this while alive; his son placed it according to his will.
EDCS-13800144.summary: This inscription records a veteran, Titus Aelius Maternus, who purchased a plot during his lifetime, and his son erected the monument according to his will, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13800145.text_edition: \n Marco Gargilio Quinti filio Claudia Secundo militi legionis XX qui sub vexsillo sic decessit Marcus Gargilius Quinti filius frater\n
EDCS-13800145.translation: To Marcus Gargilius, soldier of the Twentieth Legion, son of Marcus, who died under the standard. Marcus Gargilius, his brother, son of Marcus.
EDCS-13800145.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Gargilius for his brother, Marcus Gargilius, a soldier of the Twentieth Legion who died in service, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900036.text_edition: \n Lucius Petronius Auli Lusci filius Calvio testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-13900036.translation: Lucius Petronius, son of Aulus Luscius, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-13900036.summary: This inscription indicates that Lucius Petronius, son of Aulus Luscius, commissioned the erection of a monument or building through his will, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900037.text_edition: \n Allenius Cai filius Strabo praefectus iure dicundo tribunus militum populi suffragio curator aerari pluteum dedit\n
EDCS-13900037.translation: Allenius Strabo, son of Gaius, prefect with the power of jurisdiction, military tribune, and curator of the treasury by popular vote, dedicated the pluteum.
EDCS-13900037.summary: This inscription records Allenius Strabo, who held several significant civic and military offices including prefect, tribune, and curator of the treasury, dedicating a 'pluteum' (likely a bench or barrier), probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900074.translation: To Cerdon, a communal kitchen in the triangular area.
EDCS-13900074.summary: This inscription records a communal kitchen dedicated to Cerdon in a triangular space, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900502.translation: Faustiniana, most noble lady, servant of Christ, entrusted herself and her burial alive to the tabernacle of Christ and the memory of the saints.
EDCS-13900502.summary: This is a late antique or early Christian inscription recording a vow or dedication of property for religious purposes by a noblewoman.

EDCS-13900503.translation: Here rests the eternal [rest] of Daniel, the infant levite.
EDCS-13900503.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant levite, indicating a Christian burial from late antiquity.

EDCS-13900504.translation: Zimarcus, primicerius of the Tarvisian cohort, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13900504.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by a military officer, Zimarcus, of the Tarvisian cohort, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-13900505.translation: Stefanus, a soldier of the Tarvisian cohort, troop of Justinus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13900505.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by a soldier, Stefanus, serving in the Tarvisian cohort under the troop of Justinus, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-13900562.translation: Here rests Peter, son of Paparius, alone of the Jews from the family of Olympius, who deserved to reach the grace of Christ and was worthily buried in this holy court on the day before the Ides of July, in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-13900562.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Peter, a Jew who converted to Christianity, with the date specified by the Ides of July and the fourth indiction.

EDCS-14100315.translation: His fellow soldier in the tent made (this) while alive.
EDCS-14100315.summary: A tombstone erected by a contubernalis (fellow soldier) for a deceased comrade.

EDCS-14100316.text_edition: \n liena Cai liberta Sa testamento fieri i(ussit)\n
EDCS-14100316.translation: Liena, freedwoman of Caius, ordered this to be made in her will.
EDCS-14100316.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that the deceased, Liena, a freedwoman, mandated the construction of her tomb in her will.

EDCS-14100319.translation: Claudius Maximus gave (this) to Liber Pater, his patron, when Sura and Senecio were consuls for the third and second time respectively.
EDCS-14100319.summary: A dedication by Claudius Maximus to the god Liber Pater, honoring his patron, dated by the consuls Sura and Senecio.

EDCS-14100322.text_edition: \n Septimius Theodulus vir clarissimus turres ornavit\n
EDCS-14100322.translation: Septimius Theodulus, most distinguished man, adorned the towers.
EDCS-14100322.summary: An inscription recording that Septimius Theodulus, a high-ranking individual, decorated some towers.

EDCS-14100326.translation: To the departed spirits. Laetilia Maxima, and Camuria Primitiva, and Camuria Priscilla, set this up for their well-deserving husband and patron, Titus Camurius Priscus, a veteran of the 12th urban cohort.
EDCS-14100326.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife and daughters to their husband and father, Titus Camurius Priscus, a veteran, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-14100328.translation: To Domitia Paulina, daughter of Caius. She lived 4 years. Gaius Domitius Modestus and Iulia Secunda, her parents, made this.
EDCS-14100328.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child, Domitia Paulina, erected by her parents, Gaius Domitius Modestus and Iulia Secunda.

EDCS-14100336.translation: To Dica Praesens, who set this up for a well-deserving person.
EDCS-14100336.summary: A dedication to Dica Praesens, possibly for services rendered, set up by an unnamed person.

EDCS-14100339.translation: Sextus Pontius Diocaris, son of Isauricus.
EDCS-14100339.summary: A simple funerary epitaph naming Sextus Pontius Diocaris, son of Isauricus.

EDCS-14100343.summary: A funerary epitaph for a 3-year-old named Secundio, identified as a mother, likely a child bride or a pet with a human name.

EDCS-14100344.translation: To the departed spirits. This poor tomb here covers [my wife?], dear to me, and faithful, who lived twenty volumes of years. Behold, I, Basilides, shed tears for you, together with Paulinus, our little son.
EDCS-14100344.summary: A lament for a deceased wife and young son, erected by Basilides, lamenting the loss of his wife and their son, possibly referencing years lived in a metaphorical way.

EDCS-14100345.translation: Marovehus of the gentile school lies here, who lived more or less 50 years.
EDCS-14100345.summary: A tombstone for Marovehus, a member of a gentile school, who died around the age of 50.

EDCS-14100347.translation: [Epitaph for] Exuperius, former prefect [---], lived 75 years [---], served 46 years. Flavia Vict[orina] together with [her] son [---] to her husband.
EDCS-14100347.summary: A funerary inscription for Exuperius, a former prefect, detailing his lifespan and military service, erected by his wife Flavia Victorina and son.

EDCS-14100348.translation: Gaius Valerius Priscus, with his patron, willingly and deservedly fulfilled (his) vow.
EDCS-14100348.summary: A votive inscription by Gaius Valerius Priscus, dedicated with his patron, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-14100349.summary: An inscription indicating that the monument was created by the person named Hermes during his lifetime.

EDCS-14100351.summary: A fragmentary epitaph possibly for a woman named Calupa.

EDCS-14100352.translation: To the shades of the departed. Lucius Publicius Valentinus and Publicia Valentina dedicated this to their sister Publicia Melitina.
EDCS-14100352.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a deceased sister by her siblings, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14100353.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Samo Tertius and Quartus fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-14100353.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Silvanus by Samo Tertius and Quartus, indicating a vow fulfilled.

EDCS-14600002.text_edition: \n Mogiancus Ingenui filius et Tulliu Ingenua uxor et Covnertus et Secundinus filii fecerunt\n
EDCS-14600002.translation: Mogiancus, son of Ingenuus, and his wife Tullia Ingenua, and his sons Covnertus and Secundinus, made this.
EDCS-14600002.summary: This is a dedication of a monument by a family, Mogiancus, his wife, and sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800219.translation: Lucius Caecilius, son of Quintus, as proconsul, ordered boundary stones and markers to be set up, by decree of the Senate, between the people of Padua and Atesta.
EDCS-14800219.summary: An inscription recording the establishment of boundaries between two communities by Lucius Caecilius, son of Quintus, acting as proconsul.

EDCS-15000164.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Imperatori Caesari Flavio Constantino Maximo Pio Felici Victori Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XXIII imperatori XXII consuli VII patri patriae proconsuli humanarum rerum optimo principi divi Constanti filio bono rei publicae nato \n
EDCS-15000164.translation: To our lord, the Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantinus Maximus, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 23rd time, hailed as emperor for the 22nd time, consul for the 7th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, concerning human affairs, the best prince, son of the divine Constantius, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-15000164.summary: This is a lengthy honorific inscription praising Emperor Constantine the Great, dating to his later reign based on the consulships and tribunician power.

EDCS-15300240.text_edition: \n Tenatio Luci filio Primioni militi praetoriano cohortis IIII chorographiario item caelatori filio piissimo mater\n
EDCS-15300240.translation: To Tenatius Primus, son of Lucius, a soldier of the Praetorian Guard, cohort IV, a chorographer, also an engraver, a most dutiful son, his mother [dedicated this].
EDCS-15300240.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tenatius Primus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard with artistic professions, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-15300242.text_edition: \n Caius Valerius Cai filius Clemens sibi et Manio Sulpicio Luci filio Acuto fratri Petroniae Hecatei Quinto Sincio Ianuario testamento fieri iussit vitor hic fuit\n
EDCS-15300242.translation: Gaius Valerius Clemens, son of Caius, dedicated this for himself and for his brother Manius Sulpicius Acutus, son of Lucius, and for Petronia Hecatei and Quintus Sincianus Ianuarius by his will; he was the victor here.
EDCS-15300242.summary: This is a funerary dedication commissioned by will, commemorating the dedicator himself, his brother, and two other individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300600.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aurelius Sabinus miles cohortis praetoriae primae militavit nnos XII centuria Dionysi posuit Amplius fratri\n
EDCS-15300600.translation: To the shades of the departed. Aurelius Sabinus, a soldier of the first Praetorian cohort, served for 12 years. Amplius placed this for his brother.
EDCS-15300600.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Sabinus, a Praetorian soldier, dedicated by his brother Amplius after his service.

EDCS-15300601.translation: To the Iunones. Gaius Vibius Philippus [dedicated this].
EDCS-15300601.summary: This is a dedication to the Iunones (female guardian spirits) by Gaius Vibius Philippus, likely a private religious offering.

EDCS-15300602.text_edition: \n Exspectata domnabus sic Iunonibus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-15300602.translation: Exspectata fulfilled her vow to the domnae and the Iunones willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-15300602.summary: This is a votive inscription where Exspectata fulfilled a vow to female deities (domnae and Iunones) out of gratitude.

EDCS-15300603.text_edition: \n Iovi Lustra<l=R>i Quintus Madavasius Festus libens merito \n
EDCS-15300603.translation: To Jupiter Lustralis. Quintus Madavasius Festus [dedicated this] willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-15300603.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating an offering to Jupiter Lustralis by Quintus Madavasius Festus, signifying a fulfilled vow.

EDCS-15300604.text_edition: \n Iovi Lustrali Phoebus Veronensis vilicus plombariorum votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-15300604.translation: Phoebus of Verona, supervisor of the plumbers, gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Lustralis.
EDCS-15300604.summary: This inscription records a plumber's votive offering to Jupiter Lustralis.

EDCS-15300605.text_edition: \n Lucius Virius Achillaeus Isidi Augustae signum Harpocra<t=I>(is) voto dedit libens merito locus datus decreto decurionum \n
EDCS-15300605.translation: Lucius Virius Achillaeus dedicated a statue of Harpocrates to Isis Augusta, his vow gladly and deservedly paid; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-15300605.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue to Isis Augusta by Lucius Virius Achillaeus, with the land granted by local officials.

EDCS-15700197.translation: Lucius Heius, son of Lucius, of the Collina tribe, as aedile, and Gellia Secunda, daughter of Quintus, his wife.
EDCS-15700197.summary: An inscription identifying Lucius Heius, an aedile, and his wife Gellia Secunda, indicating their social standing and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-15800458.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Imperatori Caesari Flavio Constantino Maximo Pio Felici victori Augusto pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis XXV imperatori XXIIII consuli VIII proconsuli humanarum rerum optimo principi divi Constanti filio bono rei publicae nato a Patavio XVII\n
EDCS-15800458.translation: To our lord, Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantinus, most great, pious, fortunate, victorious Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 25th time, acclaimed imperator for the 24th time, consul for the 8th time, proconsul, best prince of human affairs, born of the divine Constantius, born for the good of the state, from Padua, 17 miles.
EDCS-15800458.summary: This lengthy inscription is a dedicatory text for Emperor Constantine the Great, listing his titles and acknowledging his lineage and benefactions, likely from a milestone.

EDCS-16000595.text_edition: \n Caio Bassio Spuri filio Collino IIIIviro aedilicia potestate\n
EDCS-16000595.translation: To Gaius Bassius Collīnus, son of Spurius, four times duovir with aedilician power.
EDCS-16000595.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Bassius Collīnus, identifying his civic positions.

EDCS-16100347.translation: Sacred to Minerva Flanatica. Deus Bassus, having received what he asked from the goddess, dedicated this in fulfillment of his vow.
EDCS-16100347.summary: A votive inscription to Minerva Flanatica by Deus Bassus, indicating a prayer answered and a vow fulfilled.

EDCS-16100348.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Eutychus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-16100348.translation: Eutychus gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-16100348.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Best and Greatest by Eutychus.

EDCS-16200828.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Caius Arrius Cai filius Optatus sibi et suis et Caio Arrio Cai filio Clementi filio suo et Tito Saufeio Marci filio et amicis et sodalibus carpentaris vir devotus in fronte pedes XXXXI retro pedes XXXXX\n
EDCS-16200828.translation: Caius Arrius Optatus, son of Caius, made this in his lifetime for himself and his family, and for his son Caius Arrius Clemens, son of Caius, and for Titus Saufeius, son of Marcius, and for his friends and fellow cart-makers, a devoted man. In front 41 feet, behind 50 feet.
EDCS-16200828.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Arrius Optatus dedicating a tomb for himself, his family, friends, and colleagues in the cart-making trade, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-16400073.translation: Laekanius Viator, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Amethystus, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Crescens, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Pierus, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Barbus, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus [---], son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Cominus, son of Laekanius Di, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Datia, son of Laekanius Heri, son of Caius Laekanius Amycus, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Eucharus, son of Caius Laekanius Bassus Felix, a slave.
EDCS-16400073.summary: An extensive funerary inscription detailing a complex lineage of freeborn individuals and a slave named Felix, likely associated with the Laekani family.

EDCS-16500108.text_edition: \n Lucio Tullio Luci filio Maxumo militi legionis V\n
EDCS-16500108.translation: To Lucius Tullius Maximus, son of Lucius, a soldier of the Fifth Legion.
EDCS-16500108.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Tullius Maximus, a soldier of the Legio V.

EDCS-16500160.summary: This inscription records the name and former rank of Baebius Eusebius, likely from an epitaph or official record.

EDCS-16600294.translation: To the gods Manes. His freedmen and heirs erected this.
EDCS-16600294.summary: This is a dedication to the Manes gods by freedmen and heirs, likely for a tomb.

EDCS-16800194.translation: Rufius Sertorius saw [this] on the Ides of Sextilis [in the year of the consulship] of Lucius Afranius and Quintus Metellus.
EDCS-16800194.summary: This inscription records a sighting or event occurring during the consulship of Lucius Afranius and Quintus Metellus.

EDCS-17500068.translation: Vettius Serenianus, a guest and his heir, by his will, purchased a fitting tomb for Flavius Fortunatus, an Augustalis from the number of the Jovian soldiers, from his own property.
EDCS-17500068.summary: This inscription records the funerary arrangements made by Vettius Serenianus for Flavius Fortunatus, a former soldier and Augustalis, as per his will.

EDCS-17800051.summary: This inscription records the name and ownership of a slave named Pilota.

EDCS-18300747.translation: Flavius Abruna, from the senior Batavian contingent, who lived 25 years, bought a tomb for himself from his own property; whoever wishes to open it shall pay three ounces of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-18300747.summary: This epitaph for Flavius Abruna, a senior soldier from the Batavian contingent, records his age at death and the penalty for unauthorized opening of his tomb.

EDCS-18300748.translation: Flavius Ziper, a captain from the first contingent of Victrix, lived 20 years and served 8 years in the ranks. Flavius Vitalis, quaestor, and Maximianus, from the armatura of the Vicenarii, made this [tomb] from their own property. Whoever wishes to deface the tomb shall pay eight pounds of gold to the treasury, in accordance with the penalty for the offense.
EDCS-18300748.summary: This inscription records the details of Flavius Ziper, a soldier who died young, and the penalties for defacing his tomb, erected by his colleagues.

EDCS-18300749.translation: Flavius Exuperantius, his son, purchased this tomb for his most beloved father, Flavius Martidius, prefect of the Jovian auxiliary troops, who served 38 years, and arranged it for himself [his own burial]. Whoever touches it shall suffer danger to his head.
EDCS-18300749.summary: This inscription records the funerary arrangements made by Flavius Exuperantius for his father, Flavius Martidius, a former prefect of auxiliary troops, and includes a curse against those who disturb the tomb.

EDCS-18300750.translation: His colleagues purchased this tomb for Flavius Cascinivus, a ducenarius from the armatura, who lived 43 years and served 23 years, from his own property, where he is laid. Whoever wishes to open it shall pay six pounds of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-18300750.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a tomb for Flavius Cascinivus, a high-ranking soldier, by his colleagues, and specifies a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-18300751.translation: Florus erected this memorial for his most dutiful father. Whoever attempts to move this burial shall owe six pounds of gold to the treasury. Iovinus, a biarch and draconarius from the eighth Dalmatian cohort, who served 20 years and lived 40 years, [his] protector and father, placed the memorial.
EDCS-18300751.summary: This inscription records a memorial erected by Iovinus for his father Florus, including a penalty for disturbing the tomb, and provides details about Iovinus's military service.

EDCS-18300752.translation: Flavius Severianus, a centenarius from the unit of cataphract cavalry, served for 22 years, having parents from milecastle XI in the village of Suriliacis. If anyone wishes to open this tomb, they will pay a penalty to the treasury of two pounds of gold.
EDCS-18300752.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavius Severianus, a centenarius, specifying a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-18400020.translation: Flavius Ursacius, a ducenarius from the senior Lion unit, lived for more or less 40 years and served for 20 years. He purchased this tomb for himself from his own funds. If anyone opens it, they will pay 10 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-18400020.summary: This tomb inscription records Flavius Ursacius, a ducenarius, who purchased his own tomb and set a penalty for opening it.

EDCS-18400021.translation: Flavius Sindila, a senator from the senior Heruli unit, lies in this tomb, which he purchased with his own money. If anyone wishes to open it, they will pay 12 pounds of silver to the treasury. He lived for 60 years.
EDCS-18400021.summary: This tomb inscription for Flavius Sindila, a senator, details his purchase of the tomb and sets a penalty for unauthorized access.

EDCS-18400022.translation: Flavius Odiscus, a biarchus from the senior spearmen unit, purchased this tomb for himself with his own funds. If anyone wishes to open it, they will pay three pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-18400022.summary: This tomb inscription records Flavius Odiscus, a biarchus, who purchased his own tomb and stipulated a penalty for opening it.

EDCS-18400023.translation: I, Gunthia, and Flavius Silvimarus from the Heruli unit purchased this tomb with our own money. If anyone considers opening this tomb, they will pay 5 pounds.
EDCS-18400023.summary: This tomb inscription records the purchase of a tomb by Gunthia and Flavius Silvimarus from the Heruli unit, with a penalty for unauthorized opening.

EDCS-18400024.translation: Flavius Fasta, a ducenarius from the senior Batavian knights, purchased this tomb. If anyone wishes to open it, they will pay 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-18400024.summary: This tomb inscription records Flavius Fasta, a ducenarius of Batavian knights, purchasing his tomb and setting a penalty for opening.

EDCS-18400025.translation: Flavius Batemodus, a ducenarius from the senior Heruli unit, purchased this tomb. If anyone wishes to open it, they will pay 5 pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-18400025.summary: This tomb inscription records Flavius Batemodus, a ducenarius of the Heruli, purchasing his tomb and stipulating a penalty for its opening.

EDCS-18400026.translation: Flavius Florentius, from the workshop, purchased this tomb during his lifetime with his own funds.
EDCS-18400026.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavius Florentius, a craftsman, recording his purchase of the tomb while alive.

EDCS-18400027.translation: Flavius Messius, a centenarius from the archer's workshop, ordered this tomb to be made from his own funds. If anyone wishes to place it in this location, they will pay five pounds of silver to the school.
EDCS-18400027.summary: This inscription records Flavius Messius, a centenarius, commissioning a tomb and specifying a payment to the 'school' for its placement.

EDCS-18500150.translation: I, Flavius Nunnus, son of Isatus, a merchant from the Opitergine civitas, purchased this for myself. If anyone wishes to open it, they will pay two ounces of gold to the treasury.
EDCS-18500150.summary: This tomb inscription records Flavius Nunnus, a merchant, purchasing his tomb and setting a penalty of gold for its unauthorized opening.

EDCS-19800434.translation: Sextus Veronius Apelles gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Diana.
EDCS-19800434.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Diana by Sextus Veronius Apelles, likely a freedman, in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-19900646.translation: Arnouphis, sacred scribe of Egypt, and Terentius Preiscos [dedicated this] to the manifest goddess.
EDCS-19900646.summary: This is a dedication to an epiphany goddess, presented by Arnouphis, a high-ranking Egyptian priest, and Terentius Preiscos.

EDCS-19900647.translation: To Zeus Thalles / Tiberius Iulius / Mamertinus / dedicated.
EDCS-19900647.summary: This bilingual inscription records a dedication to Zeus Thalles by Tiberius Iulius Mamertinus.

EDCS-19900648.translation: [Ak]ilius Hierax, also called Ptolemaeus, prefect of the artisans, dedicated [this] in fulfillment of a vow for good fortune.
EDCS-19900648.summary: This is a votive dedication by Akilius Hierax, also known as Ptolemaeus, who held the position of prefect of artisans.

EDCS-19900649.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Vibianius Hostilia made [this] for Sergius Hestiaeus, friend and physician of the consular Servilius Fabianus.
EDCS-19900649.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Chthonic Gods, made by Vibianius Hostilia for her friend and physician, Sergius Hestiaeus.

EDCS-19900650.translation: The Muse of many cities, who received resounding fame in theatrical performances, displaying all kinds of virtue in mimicry and often in choral dances, but not so much when she died on the tenth day, the wise Heracleides set up this monument for the eloquent Bassilla, the tenth muse; though dead, she obtained an equal honor of life, resting her body on the stage; these your fellow actors say: 'Be of good cheer, Bassilla, no one is immortal.'
EDCS-19900650.summary: This is a funerary epigram for the actress Bassilla, commemorating her fame and talent in theatrical performances and setting her as a 'tenth muse'.

EDCS-19900651.translation: Titus Flavius Euporus of Corinth, shipowner of the ship 'Aphrodite', [lived for] ... years.
EDCS-19900651.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Flavius Euporus, a Corinthian shipowner, possibly indicating the age of his ship or his own age.

EDCS-19900653.translation: Decimus Lailius Bassus of Adramyttium lies here.
EDCS-19900653.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Decimus Lailius Bassus, who was from Adramyttium.

EDCS-19900654.translation: To Aurelius Epictetus, soldier of the eleventh Claudian legion, Aurelius Artemidorus, soldier, in memory.
EDCS-19900654.summary: This is a funerary memorial set up by Aurelius Artemidorus for his fellow soldier Aurelius Epictetus of the eleventh Claudian legion.

EDCS-19900655.translation: Eutyches lies here, having lived 24 years; my homeland was Tacheira, but now Aquileia.
EDCS-19900655.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Eutyches, who died at age 24, stating his original homeland was Tacheira and he died in Aquileia.

EDCS-19900656.translation: Here lies Procopius the Galatian, who practiced ascetically and lived 50 years, from the village of Glodorok.
EDCS-19900656.summary: This Greek funerary inscription records the burial of Procopius, a Galatian ascetic, indicating his lifespan and village of origin.

EDCS-20401529.translation: Mastalio, deceased infant, [died at] 4 years, 5 months, 18 days, 9 hours.
EDCS-20401529.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant named Mastalio, detailing the exact duration of their life.

EDCS-20401532.translation: Ursulius Peregrinus [dedicated this to] Marcellinia, his dearest wife Ammula, who lived 43 years and 10 months.
EDCS-20401532.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating a wife named Marcellinia, whose husband dedicated the monument.

EDCS-20401533.translation: Lucius Catibulus [dedicated this to] his own Tertia, freedman of Cerbonia, son of P. Catius, [a plot of land] of Tertia Locus, of 25 square feet.
EDCS-20401533.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely dedicating a burial plot to Tertia, with a complex set of familial and freedman relationships mentioned.

EDCS-20401535.translation: Titus Poblicius, freedman of Publius, [dedicated a plot] 15 feet deep, 30 feet back.
EDCS-20401535.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot dedicated by Titus Poblicius, a freedman.

EDCS-20401537.translation: To the Divine Manes. Maenia, daughter of Lucius, Marcella, aged 43 years. Titus Petricasius, son of Lucius, [dedicated this] to his wife.
EDCS-20401537.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Titus Petricasius to his wife Maenia Marcella.

EDCS-20401538.translation: To Sextus Ennius Frontō, son of Gnaeus, of the Arnensi tribe, centurion of the Fourth Macedonian Legion.
EDCS-20401538.summary: This inscription honors Sextus Ennius Frontō, a centurion of the Legio IV Macedonica.

EDCS-20401542.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely marking a tomb or grave belonging to Sepullius.

EDCS-20401543.translation: Trophimus, Zosimus, Charis, vengeance from them...
EDCS-20401543.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly relating to a legal dispute or accusation, with names of individuals and a reference to justice or revenge.

EDCS-20401544.translation: To Tullia Valeriana, daughter of Quintus, an incomparable wife, who lived 21 years, 6 months, 23 days. Gaius Atilius Doryphorus, her husband, and Quintus Tullius Paulus and Tullia Valeria, her daughters, to their most dutiful wife and daughters and to themselves.
EDCS-20401544.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tullia Valeriana, set up by her husband and children, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401545.translation: To the right of the decumanus [road] III beyond the kardo [road] III: 173 jugera, 1/6, 1/12, 1/24... To the right of the decumanus II beyond the kardo III: 139 jugera, 1/6... of Marcus Clodius Pulcher: 31 jugera, 1/12, 1/24... To the right of the decumanus III beyond the kardo III: 112 jugera, 1/12, 1/24, 1/36... of Publius Valerius: 52 jugera, 2/3, 1/24... [To the right of the decumanus] III [beyond the kardo] II...
EDCS-20401545.summary: This inscription appears to be a land survey record, detailing land measurements (in jugera and fractions) assigned to various individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401546.translation: Sacred to Minerva. Marcus, Lucius, Publius Viri.
EDCS-20401546.summary: A dedication to the goddess Minerva by three individuals named Marcus, Lucius, and Publius Viri.

EDCS-20402395.translation: Made by a living person. Lucius Lucretius Chresimus, freedman of Lucius, to himself and to Lucretia Primigenia, his freedwoman and most excellent wife, and to Lucretius Italicus and Lucretius...
EDCS-20402395.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Lucius Lucretius Chresimus for himself, his wife, and others, indicating a desire for perpetual remembrance, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20402726.translation: To the Divine Manes. Caius Sulpicius Amandus, alive, dedicated [this] to himself and to Rosidia Verissima, his wife, who deserved well of him, 25 feet in front, 25 feet in the rear.
EDCS-20402726.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Caius Sulpicius Amandus dedicated a plot for himself and his deserving wife, Rosidia Verissima.

EDCS-21700007.translation: To Caius Clausius Dexter, son of Caius, of the Pupinia tribe, twice aedile, twice duovir. Clausia Marcella, daughter of Caius, sister [---].
EDCS-21700007.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Caius Clausius Dexter, who held prominent local magistracies, dedicated by his sister.

EDCS-22700299.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely identifying ownership of a tomb or property.

EDCS-23702135.translation: ...Rufus, veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion. Cosconia Galatea(?), freedwoman of Aulus Lucius, to [her] patron.
EDCS-23702135.summary: A funerary inscription mentioning a veteran of a Roman legion and his freedwoman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23800840.translation: Publius Catius Murranus, freedman, alive, dedicated [this] to his patron Publius Catius, son of Lucius, and to himself and to Cincia Viola.
EDCS-23800840.summary: This is a funerary inscription where a freedman, Publius Catius Murranus, dedicates a burial space for his patron and himself and Cincia Viola.

EDCS-23800841.translation: Gaius Laecanius Amycus [dedicated this to] Phorbe, his cohabitant.
EDCS-23800841.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Gaius Laecanius Amycus to his partner, Phorbe.

EDCS-23800851.translation: Sacred to Fortuna by Nonia Provincia, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-23800851.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna.

EDCS-23900862.summary: A fragmentary inscription consisting of a personal name, Manius Acilius, possibly indicating ownership or a very brief dedication.

EDCS-23900863.summary: An inscription with a personal name and filiation (son of Lucius), likely indicating ownership or a personal marker.

EDCS-23900864.translation: ...Cleppia, daughter of Manius, in front 5 feet, behind 20 feet
EDCS-23900864.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly related to property boundaries or burial plots, mentioning a woman named Cleppia and dimensions in feet.

EDCS-23900865.summary: A very fragmentary inscription that seems to denote a location or property belonging to Manius Cleppius.

EDCS-23900866.translation: To Publius Clepius Primus, son of Mani, freedman of Lucius Domitius, 3 feet in front.
EDCS-23900866.summary: This inscription records a funerary boundary, indicating a space of 3 feet in front of a tomb.

EDCS-23900867.translation: Ossuary of Manius Porcius, son of Mani, 7 feet in front, 9 [feet deep/wide].
EDCS-23900867.summary: This inscription describes the dimensions of an ossuary belonging to Manius Porcius.

EDCS-23900868.translation: To Lucius Cosutius, son of Marcus, in front 10 feet, behind 30 feet.
EDCS-23900868.summary: This inscription records land boundaries, specifying dimensions in front and behind for a plot belonging to Lucius Cosutius.

EDCS-23900869.translation: For Lucius Cosutius, son of Marcus, 10 feet in front, 30 feet behind.
EDCS-23900869.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to Lucius Cosutius.

EDCS-23900870.translation: Gaius Barbius Hilarus, freedman of Caius, and Philaenes, freedwoman of Magia.
EDCS-23900870.summary: This inscription lists the names of two freedmen, Gaius Barbius Hilarus and Philaenes, likely associated with a funerary monument.

EDCS-23900871.translation: To Marcus Arcius Glandro, son of Caius.
EDCS-23900871.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Marcus Arcius Glandro, son of Caius.

EDCS-23900872.translation: To Publius Firmus Malaudicanus, son of Publius.
EDCS-23900872.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Publius Firmus Malaudicanus, son of Publius.

EDCS-23900874.translation: Burial place of Lucius Saufeius, in front 20 feet, behind 25 feet.
EDCS-23900874.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot for Lucius Saufeius, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-23900875.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Hostilia, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-23900876.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription, providing only the nomen and filiation of the deceased.

EDCS-23900877.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Asellia Quarta.

EDCS-23900883.translation: To Augusta Venus, Publicia Amabilis and Virilis, servant and steward of the treasury of the freemen of Altinum, have willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-23900883.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augusta Venus made by Publicia Amabilis and Virilis, officials of the Altinum municipality, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-23900884.translation: Iulia willingly and deservedly fulfilled [her vow].
EDCS-23900884.summary: This inscription records Iulia fulfilling a vow, likely a votive dedication.

EDCS-23900889.translation: Cornelius Proculus gave [this] to Ettia Quarta.
EDCS-23900889.summary: This inscription records a gift from Cornelius Proculus to Ettia Quarta, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-23900890.translation: To Quintus Pompeius Helioprepes, most beloved husband, Caesidia Heorte set this up for herself and him, with whom she lived for 23 years and 5 months, while alive.
EDCS-23900890.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband, detailing their married life together.

EDCS-23900898.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Numai, priest of the deified Augustus, granted immunity by the same [Augustus], and to Claudias Secundus.
EDCS-23900898.summary: This inscription honors a priest of the deified Augustus and another individual, likely related to imperial administration and status.

EDCS-23900899.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide specific details about its content or purpose, but appears to name individuals.

EDCS-23900901.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with very little legible text, likely part of a name or funerary dedication.

EDCS-23900902.translation: Augustianus, priest, rests in his own [tomb] on the sixth day before the Ides of March, a religious man, priest of Februaria.
EDCS-23900902.summary: This inscription records the death and burial of Augustianus, a priest, on a specific date.

EDCS-23900906.translation: Here lies Metronius, priest, son of Eliodorus, of good memory, custos of this basilica, buried on the day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-23900906.summary: This inscription records the burial of Metronius, a priest and custos of a basilica, with his date of death.

EDCS-23900907.translation: Here Paternus, deacon, rests in peace, aged 54.
EDCS-23900907.summary: This inscription records the death and age of Paternus, a deacon.

EDCS-23900908.summary: This inscription likely records the ownership or dedication of a tomb or funerary monument.

EDCS-23900910.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Entina Ersicus, a bishop.

EDCS-23900911.translation: Here rests Tricia of good memory.
EDCS-23900911.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Tricia, noted for her good memory.

EDCS-24300046.translation: Quintus Passienus of Aquileia willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Isis Invicta.
EDCS-24300046.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Isis Invicta by Quintus Passienus.

EDCS-24300265.translation: To Gaius Julius Nicostratus, dearest son, 18 years, 9 months, and 12 days old. Gaius Julius Nicostratus and Julia Nymphe, his most unhappy parents, set this up while alive.
EDCS-24300265.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by grieving parents for their young son, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-24300267.summary: This is a dedication to the god Saturn.

EDCS-24400490.summary: This inscription records the name of Caius Oppius Agathopus, likely as owner or recipient.

EDCS-24400491.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Minicius Pudentis, likely as owner or recipient.

EDCS-24400492.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Minicius Pudentis, likely as owner or recipient.

EDCS-24400498.translation: Of Epiborus, son of Caius Marcius.

EDCS-25800612.translation: Herakleides, the wise speaker, set up this tombstone for Bassilla, who gained a reputation among many peoples and many cities through her acting in the theater and her performances in choruses, often on stage. Though she received the highest honors for her diverse virtues, she did not receive them as much in life as after death. Even as a corpse, she attained equal honor in life, resting her body on the musical stage. 'Your fellow actors speak these words: Be of good cheer, Bassilla, no one is immortal.'
EDCS-25800612.summary: A funerary epigram for the actress Bassilla, praising her artistic achievements and lamenting her death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25800613.translation: Here lies Eutropis, the well-born, from the city of Constantinople.
EDCS-25800613.summary: A funerary inscription for Eutropis, who hailed from Constantinople, dating to the Late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-25800616.translation: Here lies Kainos Maiumius, aged 15 years, in the 10th indiction, 6 days before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-25800616.summary: A funerary inscription for Kainos Maiumius, providing his age, the indiction year (likely 5th or 6th century AD), and date of death.

EDCS-25800617.summary: This inscription records the short life and peaceful death of a child named Laurentis.

EDCS-25800619.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Quirace, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900209.translation: For Victoria, for the health of Quintus Minicius Macrinus, Sextus Gabinasius Primus, according to his vow.
EDCS-25900209.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating something to Victoria for the health of Quintus Minicius Macrinus.

EDCS-25900234.translation: To Fougontai, daughter of Ostinus; to Fougontai, daughter of Totius.
EDCS-25900234.summary: This inscription seems to record dedications or ownership for two individuals named Fougontai, possibly within a family context.

EDCS-25900235.summary: This inscription is a very brief record, likely identifying Gaius Papirius and Romilia, possibly in a funerary or ownership context.

EDCS-26001119.translation: He made this for himself and his family while alive for Sextus Campanus, freedman of Sextus, named Adiutor.
EDCS-26001119.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a freedman named Adiutor for his patron Sextus Campanus and his own family.

EDCS-26001121.translation: Gavillia Maxima, freedwoman of Cale, daughter of Quintus, placed this.
EDCS-26001121.summary: This inscription records that Gavillia Maxima, daughter of Quintus and freedwoman of Cale, erected this monument.

EDCS-26200382.summary: This inscription likely refers to a group of Gallic colonists, possibly indicating their settlement or status.

EDCS-26201106.translation: Pacenia Frema, daughter of Gaius, a freedwoman, willingly fulfilled her vow to Fortuna, as deserved.

EDCS-26300077.translation: Onocles, slave of Dindus, [son of] Tiberius.

EDCS-26601026.translation: [---]ni, son of Manius Ostialaus Gallena, cavalryman.

EDCS-26601027.text_edition: \n ECVMME Caius Calpurnius Cai filius Calavo\n
EDCS-26601027.translation: Gaius Calpurnius, son of Gaius, from Calavo.
EDCS-26601027.summary: An inscription mentioning Gaius Calpurnius from Calavo, likely part of a larger record or funerary monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26601028.translation: Lucius Cervonius, son of Titus, made this for his wife, Secundae Terentiae, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-26601028.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Cervonius for his wife Secundae Terentiae.

EDCS-26700104.summary: This inscription records a maker's signature, likely on a statue or other artwork.

EDCS-26700425.text_edition: \n centuria Caesidieni Caius Tomius centuria Postumi Marci Valeri Bacini\n
EDCS-26700425.translation: In the century of Caesidienus, Gaius Tomius; in the century of Postumus, son of Marcus, Valerius Bacinus.
EDCS-26700425.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Gaius Tomius and Valerius Bacinus, each associated with a specific centuria, likely related to military organization or land division in the Roman period.

EDCS-26801390.summary: This inscription is a genitive ownership or dedication by Publius Quinctius Scapula.

EDCS-28000106.translation: To the good man born for the Republic.
EDCS-28000106.summary: A dedicatory inscription praising an individual for his service to the Republic, likely from the Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-28000535.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication to a person named I/turi[o] for his wife.

EDCS-28000536.translation: To Lucius Titus Threptus, husband, one of the six priests.
EDCS-28000536.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Titus Threptus, who served as a husband and a priest.

EDCS-28000957.translation: ] Fortunatus, who lived [some years]. Aurelius gave [this] as a gift, and Aurelia [...].
EDCS-28000957.summary: This inscription is a dedication for Fortunatus, with gifts from Aurelius and Aurelia, likely indicating a funerary monument.

EDCS-28000958.translation: Publius Popaedius Onesimus Augustalis, while alive, made this for himself and for Gavilia Saturnina, his excellent wife, and for Peregrina, his freedwoman, and for their descendants.
EDCS-28000958.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Popaedius Onesimus Augustalis, his wife, and his freedwoman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000959.translation: To Flavius Lito, Eugen[ius?] of the Jovian soldiers, aged 40 years, with [some] years of service, for his well-deserved [...].
EDCS-28000959.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Flavius Lito, a soldier of the Jovian unit, who died at age 40 after some years of service.

EDCS-28000962.summary: This inscription is likely a name inscription, possibly on a property or possession belonging to Decimus Titus Secundus Firmus.

EDCS-28000964.translation: Covos Sabinaius. Tiberius Volusius Firmus, son of Tiberius, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Apollo.
EDCS-28000964.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo by Tiberius Volusius Firmus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100380.translation: Tiberius Barbius Tertius. Willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Apollo.
EDCS-28100380.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo by Tiberius Barbius Tertius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100381.summary: This is a dedication possibly related to a tomb or monument, made by Memmius for Ecetia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100382.translation: Maturus for Turio. Blood. To the gods. (or To the gods, from the blood)
EDCS-28100382.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning Maturus and Turio, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100383.translation: Lucius Firmecus topazissius. To the gods.
EDCS-28100383.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly mentioning a name and dedicated to the gods, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100384.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly mentioning a name and a dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100385.translation: I, Antiochus the pederast, do not deny that I made [it].
EDCS-28100385.summary: This inscription is a self-referential statement by Antiochus, identifying himself and his work.

EDCS-28100387.translation: Marcus Atinius Lucanus, son of Lucius, for himself and for his wife Pontia Secunda, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-28100387.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Atinius Lucanus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-28100388.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Acculeia Zosime made this for Publius Acculeius Apollastus, her deserving husband, and for herself.
EDCS-28100388.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits by Acculeia Zosime for her husband and herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100390.translation: Titus Firmius, son of Sextus, a six-time magistrate and decurion, for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen, in the front 22 feet, in the rear 19 feet.
EDCS-28100390.summary: This is a funerary inscription specifying plot dimensions for Titus Firmius, his freedmen and freedwomen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100395.translation: So that she may do no harm or injury, Lentillia Ursa, daughter of Lentilius Lupus, and Ovidies Secundes, be of assistance.
EDCS-28100395.summary: This inscription is a plea for divine assistance, possibly in a legal or personal dispute, invoking Lentillia Ursa and Ovidies Secundes.

EDCS-28200052.translation: By decree of the town councillors, Marcus Teudicius Verus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, Roman knight, eligible for the public horse, has been honoured by this title by his father, Marcus Teudicius Mercator.
EDCS-28200052.summary: This inscription records a posthumous honour granted by decree of the town councillors to Marcus Teudicius Verus, a Roman knight, as a result of his father's request.

EDCS-28200053.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Martialis, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe.
EDCS-28200053.summary: This is a dedication to Tiberius Claudius Martialis, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe.

EDCS-28200054.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Restitutus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe.
EDCS-28200054.summary: This is a dedication to Tiberius Claudius Restitutus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe.

EDCS-28200056.translation: For himself and for his mother Cluvia, daughter of Laecius, and for his wife Mennica, daughter of Faustus, and for his own family.
EDCS-28200056.summary: This inscription records a dedication made for the dedicator, his mother, his wife, and his family.

EDCS-28200057.translation: To Hercules. Lucius Cusonius Secundus erected (this) in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-28200057.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Hercules by Lucius Cusonius Secundus.

EDCS-28200059.translation: To Molieri(?) / Imenae, while alive(?), wife of Sextinius Rufinus.
EDCS-28200059.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Imenae, wife of Sextinius Rufinus.

EDCS-28300275.text_edition: \n Manius Acilius Mani libertus Eudamus IIIIIIvir testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-28300275.translation: Manius Eudamus, freedman of Manius, a priest, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-28300275.summary: This inscription states that Manius Eudamus, a freedman and priest, commissioned the monument in his will.

EDCS-28600154.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Sestia Ursina erected (this) for Ianuarius, her deserving husband, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-28600154.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Sestia Ursina for her husband Ianuarius and for herself.

EDCS-29100257.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, Pious, Fortunate, Victor, and Triumphant, ever Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, Imperator for the 7th time, Consul for the 4th time, born for the good of the state, Proconsul.
EDCS-29100257.summary: This inscription is a lengthy honorific titulature for the Emperor Julian.

EDCS-29200075.translation: For Crispina Augusta, wife of Emperor Commodus Augustus, the Sarmatic, the Germanicus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-29200075.summary: This is a dedication to Crispina, wife of Emperor Commodus, passed by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-29200076.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, by decree [of the decurions].
EDCS-29200076.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), son of Septimius Severus, likely by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-29200080.translation: To Severa Celia, wife of Maximus, who lived 52 years, [and to] Secundus Piuonus.
EDCS-29200080.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Severa Celia, wife of Maximus, and to Secundus Piuonus.

EDCS-29600343.translation: By the authority of Quintus Iunius Rusticus, Prefect of the City.
EDCS-29600343.summary: This inscription records an act or decree made under the authority of Quintus Iunius Rusticus, the Prefect of the City.

EDCS-29600344.translation: To our lords Leone and Iulius Maiorianus, perpetual Augusti. Caecina Decius Basilius, Praetorian Prefect, made (this).
EDCS-29600344.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the Praetorian Prefect Caecina Decius Basilius to the Emperors Leo and Julius Maiorianus.

EDCS-29600345.translation: Completed at the Temple of Castor
EDCS-29600345.summary: This inscription likely marks the completion of a work or a boundary near the Temple of Castor, possibly in Rome.
