EDCS-29601034.translation: By order of the Senate concerning Titus Augustus
EDCS-29601034.summary: This inscription refers to a senatorial decree concerning a person named Titus Augustus, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-29601042.translation: From Marcus (son of Marcus) stacte, from Marcus (son of Marcus) myrrh, from Marcus (son of Marcus) ointment, from Marcus (son of Marcus) incense
EDCS-29601042.summary: This inscription lists various fragrant resins or perfumes, likely associated with trade or funerary offerings, attributed to a Marcus.

EDCS-29601043.text_edition: \n Chresimus Viri spectavit Idibus Iuniis Sexto Aelio Caio Sentio consulibus\n
EDCS-29601043.translation: Chresimus, son of Virius, saw [this] on the Ides of June, when Sextus Aelius Gais and Sentius were consuls.

EDCS-29601044.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Secundus Pudens, likely the deceased.

EDCS-29601045.translation: Gnaeus Piso, son of Gnaeus, triumvir of the mint
EDCS-29601045.summary: This records the name and official position (triumvir monetalis) of Gnaeus Piso, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-29601046.translation: Of the son of Marcus Kaeson, Barbos, son of Marcus Kaeson, the chair
EDCS-29601046.summary: This inscription appears to record ownership or patronage related to a person named Barbos, son of Marcus Kaeson, and possibly a piece of furniture or office.

EDCS-29601057.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal dedication or memorial, possibly noting a relationship between individuals named Sodales.

EDCS-29601063.translation: Quintus Lo, sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus

EDCS-29601124.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary personal name, possibly for a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-29900232.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Quintus Sossius Albus, the retiarius. Sossia Iusta, his freedwoman, [erected this] for her well-deserving patron.
EDCS-29900232.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for her deceased patron, a gladiator of the myrmillo type, in Roman Egypt.

EDCS-29900233.translation: Pontia Posilla, daughter of Lucius, made [this] for herself and her family while alive; also for Annia Paulla, daughter of Lucius, daughter of daughter of daughter, while alive; for Titus Accius Firmus, son of Titus, son of son, while alive; and for Lucius Accius Secundus, son of Titus, son of son.

EDCS-29900234.translation: For Postuma, daughter of Trosia, by decree of the town council.
EDCS-29900234.summary: This dedicates a monument or honors Postuma, daughter of Trosia, based on a decree by the local council.

EDCS-29900235.translation: Lucius Annaeus Zosimus, alive, made this for himself and for Annaea Secundina, daughter of Lucius; and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. Lucius Helvius Eutycius, one of the VI viri of Aquileia, alive, made this for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-29900235.summary: This is a funerary碑 inscription recording self-dedication and dedication for family members and freedmen by two individuals, Lucius Annaeus Zosimus and Lucius Helvius Eutycius, a VI vir in Aquileia.

EDCS-29900236.translation: For Pudentius, freedman, one of the VIIIIvir, with deceased servants(?); [died at] 20 years; Pudentius, 20 years; [died at] 25 years.

EDCS-29900238.translation: Manius Servius Marcellus, son of Manius, for himself and his family, and for his father and mother Servia Eunia, freedwoman of Manius, and for his sister, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-29900238.summary: This is a funerary碑 inscription recording self-dedication and dedication for family members including parents and a sister, and for freedmen and freedwomen by Manius Servius Marcellus.

EDCS-29900239.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Aurelius Plutas, soldier of the Legion XII Fulminata, lived 25 years, served 6 years. Aurelius Plutas made [this] for his deserving brother.
EDCS-29900239.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier of the Legio XII Fulminata, erected by his brother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-29900240.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Restutus, aged 20.
EDCS-29900240.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph for Restutus, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-29900242.translation: For Marcus Cornelius Cerdon and Annaea Secundina, daughter of Lucius, parents, and for Epidia Fortunata, wife. Marcus Cornelius Secundinus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-29900242.summary: This is a funerary碑 inscription dedicated by Marcus Cornelius Secundinus to his parents, Marcus Cornelius Cerdon and Annaea Secundina, and to his wife Epidia Fortunata.

EDCS-29900243.translation: Publius Barbius Marcellinus, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, made [this] for himself while alive, and for Publius Barbus Verus, son of Publius, aged 24, and for his wife Baria Tyche, freedwoman of Publius, and for his father Publius Barbius Vedianus Firmus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-29900243.summary: This is a large family funerary monument erected by Publius Barbius Marcellinus for himself, his son, wife, father, and freedmen, indicating a significant burial plot.

EDCS-29900245.translation: Aulus Oppius Cassius, who lived 22 years and 51 days. Cassia Ursa, his mother, [erected this] for her most beloved son.
EDCS-29900245.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her young son, Aulus Oppius Cassius, who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-29900246.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Calopus, slave of Carminus Veteris. For his son Tychio, aged 9 years, and for his companion Aura. In front 20 feet, behind 28 feet.
EDCS-29900246.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a slave named Calopus and his family, also specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-29900250.summary: This funerary碑 inscription names Publius Salonio Stabilioni and Salonia Galla as parents, and Marcus Salonio as their son, likely dedicating the monument.

EDCS-29900251.summary: This names Smypronius Scitus, identifying him as a freedman of someone named Marcus.

EDCS-29900253.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, nine miles. Devota Venetia dedicated nine [miles] to our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Valens, divine brothers, always Augusti.
EDCS-29900253.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a milestone or marker by 'Devota Venetia' to Emperor Maxentius and later to the Augusti Valentinian I and Valens, indicating a period of transition or dual authority.

EDCS-29900254.translation: To our lord Flavius Iovianus, victorious and triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the republic.

EDCS-30200003.translation: The first (?) won. The second (?) won. Caecrops perished.

EDCS-31200130.translation: Under the consulship of Marcus Vinicius and Tauro Statilius Corvinus, Gaius Vibius Rufus, legatus, and Gaius Horatius [---], princeps praetorius, [honoured ---] of the Fourth Macedonian Legion.
EDCS-31200130.summary: This inscription records an honour granted to an officer of the Fourth Macedonian Legion during the consulship of Marcus Vinicius and Tauro Statilius Corvinus.

EDCS-31300131.translation: In fulfillment of a vow by Stephanos, a senator of the chariot-racing faction.

EDCS-31400277.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Appeus Augurinus and his wife for his father, Quintus Appeus Eutychianus.

EDCS-36700001.text_edition: \n Caio Baebio Publi filio Claudia Attico IIviro iure dicundo primo pilo legionis V Macedonicae praefecto civitatium Moesiae et Treballiae praefecto civitatium in Alpibus maritumis tribuno militum cohortis VIII praetoriae primo pilo iterum procuratori Tiberi Claudi Caesaris Augusti Germanici in Norico civitas Saevatum et Laiancorum\n

EDCS-36700001.summary: A dedication to Gaius Baebius Atticus, listing his extensive military and administrative career, likely for his grant of citizenship to the Saevates and Laianci.

The monument plot, sixteen feet in front and twenty-five feet in depth, is held in common. Lucius Sarius Philinus, freedman of Lucius, made this while alive. The monument plot [---].
EDCS-36700055.summary: A large family funerary monument inscription by Marcus Curius Marcellus, recording himself, his wife, parents, grandparents, children, brother, sister, niece, and freedmen, along with plot dimensions.

EDCS-37400034.translation: He made this for his daughter Vera, aged 32.

EDCS-37400035.translation: [---] Octavius, freedman of [---]ae. [---]o. [---] Octavius, freedman of [---]nis. [---] He made this while alive as a IIIIVir, for [---]ustus, his fellow freedman.
EDCS-37400035.summary: An epitaph by a freedman, likely a member of the IIIIViri, for himself and a deceased fellow freedman.

EDCS-37400036.translation: [Restored name], freedman of Gaius Eros, [restored name] Augustalis, for himself and [restored name] his son Augurinus, [restored name] and Primus [restored name].
EDCS-37400036.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the dedication of a monument by a freedman of Gaius Eros, possibly for himself, his son, and others.

EDCS-37400038.translation: Marcus Metelius Felix, IIIIvir, made this while alive for himself and for Arria [---], his concubine, and for his mother-in-law Arria Ianu[---].
EDCS-37400038.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Metelius Felix, a IIIIvir, for himself, his concubine, and his mother-in-law.

EDCS-37400039.translation: For Lucius Naevius Felix the Elder, IIIIvir, who lived for 74 years. Lucius Naevius Felix the Younger, for his adoptive father, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-37400039.summary: An epitaph for Lucius Naevius Felix the Elder, a IIIIvir, set up by his adoptive son, Lucius Naevius Felix the Younger.

EDCS-37400040.translation: In front, Mani Murtranus, freedman of Mani Aemilius, [measured] 11 feet, behind [measured] feet.
EDCS-37400040.summary: This inscription appears to record land measurements or boundaries related to Mani Murtranus, a freedman of Mani Aemilius.

EDCS-37400045.translation: Burial place of Amarantus, freedman of Manius Muttienus; to the rear on the left side, in the garden, 65 feet long; in the rear part, 45 feet wide.

EDCS-37400047.translation: Of Marcus Septicius Cynthus, 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the rear.
EDCS-37400047.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property, likely a burial plot, belonging to Marcus Septicius Cynthus.

EDCS-37400048.translation: Place for a monument of Caius Vettius, son of [---]; in front 10 feet; [to the rear --- feet].

EDCS-37400053.translation: Gaius Lusius Florus, son of Gaius, 10 feet in front and 31 feet in the rear.
EDCS-37400053.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land, possibly for burial, belonging to Gaius Lusius Florus.

EDCS-37400054.translation: Plot (?) of burial place (?) of Valeria Laidis, daughter of Lucius; in front 25 feet; to the rear [---] feet.
EDCS-37400054.summary: This is a funerary boundary marker for Valeria Laidis, with partial dimensions recorded.

EDCS-37400055.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property, likely a burial plot, belonging to Lucius Accius Calvio.

EDCS-37500005.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot for Licinna, freedwoman of Quintus, with specified dimensions.

EDCS-37500007.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Pe() Epi() while alive marked out this tomb.
EDCS-37500007.summary: This tomb inscription records Titus Pe() Epi() reserving a burial plot for himself while alive.

EDCS-37500017.translation: Burial place of Titus Cassius Eupco(); in front 30 feet; to the rear 30 feet.
EDCS-37500017.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot of Titus Cassius Eupco(), with dimensions of 30 feet in both front and rear.

EDCS-37500018.translation: Burial place in front 30 feet, to the rear 30 feet. Titus Cassius Eupco.

EDCS-37500019.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to begin with the name of Titus Cassius Eupco, likely a dedication or owner's name.

EDCS-37500020.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot owned by Antias, a freedman.

EDCS-37500022.translation: For Titus Terentius, son of Publius, and for Terentius Lepidus, in front [unknown measurement] feet.
EDCS-37500022.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a plot to Titus Terentius and Terentius Lepidus, with an incomplete measurement.

EDCS-37500024.summary: This inscription records a plot of land for Lucius Pinnius with specific dimensions, though the measurement is partially uncertain.

EDCS-37500025.translation: Burial place, [for Baetia?], [for Pyrrhidus], in front 15 feet, to the rear 10 feet [unknown measurement].
EDCS-37500025.summary: This is a funerary inscription that, despite damage, indicates a burial plot with dimensions and possibly names the intended recipients.

EDCS-37500027.translation: Burial place. L(uci) I() S(), in front 20 feet, to the rear 30 feet.
EDCS-37500027.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot with its dimensions and an abbreviated name or designation.

EDCS-37500028.translation: Burial place. Quintus Sabinius Secundio for himself and for his wife Cannusia Felicula, in front 12.5 feet, to the rear 16.5 feet.
EDCS-37500028.summary: This inscription records the purchase or allocation of a burial plot by Quintus Sabinius Secundio for himself and his wife, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-37500030.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Petelius, son of Publius, established this sepulchre for himself while alive, 60 feet in front and 80 feet in the rear.
EDCS-37500030.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a tomb by Titus Petelius, son of Publius, who established it for himself during his lifetime and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-37500032.translation: For Annia, in front 12 feet, to the rear 36 feet.
EDCS-37500032.summary: This funerary inscription specifies the dimensions of a plot designated for Annia.

EDCS-37500036.summary: This is a simple dedication or identification of Ciceria, daughter of Caius, likely associated with a tomb or monument.

EDCS-37500040.translation: Publius Domitius Philippus, freedman of Publius, made this for himself and for Pollia, freedwoman of Caius, Dic[---] and for his own [family] while alive, in front 20 feet, to the rear 30 feet.
EDCS-37500040.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Publius Domitius Philippus for himself, his wife Pollia, and other family members, specifying the plot dimensions and indicating it was built during his lifetime.

EDCS-37500041.translation: Of Publius Terentius Nereus. In front 60 feet, to the back [3] feet.
EDCS-37500041.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Terentius Nereus, specifying the dimensions of his plot.

EDCS-37601027.translation: Arria Cinnamys, freedwoman of Gaius, for herself and for Lucius Antonius Maturus, freedman of Lucius, son of Ianuarius, aged 4, for Gaius Arrius, son of Gaius, Arria Clara, Arria Terpne, and Carpus, freedman of a woman named Gaius. In front 19 and a half feet, to the back 36 feet.

EDCS-37601029.translation: Marcus Servilius, son of Marcus, for himself and for Papiria Quinta, daughter of Quintus, and for his sons Firminus and Proculus.
EDCS-37601029.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Marcus Servilius and his family, including his wife and sons.

EDCS-37601030.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription, likely for Quintus Allenius, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-37601031.translation: Quintus Pompeius Longus, son of Publius, for himself and for his brother Gaius Pompeius Longus, son of Publius, for his mother Gavia Visauni, daughter of Marcus, for his brother Publius Pompeius Labeo, son of Publius, for his brother Marcus Pompeius, son of Publius.
EDCS-37601031.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Pompeius Longus, dedicating the plot for himself and several male relatives, including his mother.

EDCS-37601032.translation: To Valeria Secunda. Marcus Carullius Verecundus and [---] made this.
EDCS-37601032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Secunda, erected by Marcus Carullius Verecundus.

EDCS-37601033.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Gaius L. H.
EDCS-37601033.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Gaius L. H.

EDCS-37601034.translation: Lucius Sentius Inacebilus, Lucius Sentius, son of Lucius. Gaius Sentius, son of Gaius, made [this] while alive. In a square 25 feet.
EDCS-37601034.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Gaius Sentius for his father Lucius Sentius Inacebilus and grandfather Lucius Sentius, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-38500006.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph, likely for someone named Passenius Augurinus.

EDCS-39200628.translation: Rejoicing in the feasts of the blessed, called suddenly on the second day from heaven, Satria Fabia to her sweetest husband, eternal [---].
EDCS-39200628.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed husband, dedicated by his wife Satria Fabia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period given the Greek text.

EDCS-39200629.translation: Valeria Sophrosyne and Emilianē to Valerius Elianus, their father, in memory and gratitude.
EDCS-39200629.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valerius Elianus, dedicated by his daughters Valeria Sophrosyne and Emilianē.

EDCS-39200630.translation: Here lies Aurelius Aesopus of the village of Addana in Syria, having lived 50 years, a little more.
EDCS-39200630.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Aesopus, who lived in Syria and died at the age of 50.

EDCS-39200631.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Cosmoss and Theodote made this for their sweetest child, Cosmia, who lived for 6 years, 19 days, and 2 hours, for remembrance.
EDCS-39200631.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to a young girl named Cosmia by her parents, Cosmoss and Theodote, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39200634.translation: Suddenly we were extinguished, what is the cause? Kari, it is right to do so. I am a slave, Phylogios raised me, Hyle [---].
EDCS-39200634.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed person, possibly a slave, expressing grief and questioning the cause of death.

EDCS-39200635.translation: Here lies Ioannes, who served during the time of TSY N Kernes, in most blessed memory, at Beroea, of Alan H and Salomes, having died at the age of twenty-eight.
EDCS-39200635.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ioannes, who died at the age of 28 while serving under TSY N Kernes in Beroea.

EDCS-39200638.translation: Here, Ida made a beautiful tomb for you, my sweet Telesilla, his wife, who deserved the greatest of all faith, goodwill, virtue, and especially love, so that your glory might be unfading for those to come.
EDCS-39200638.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Telesilla, erected by her husband Ida, praising her virtues.

EDCS-39200642.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or identification, possibly for Epianax, son of Proclus.

EDCS-39200644.translation: In the 287th year, Aurelius Marcianus of the village of Fisoura, belonging to the territory of Antioch, aged 19, lies here. If anyone dares to open this sarcophagus without his own people, he shall give one pound of gold to the treasurer.
EDCS-39200644.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the territory of Antioch, dated to the 287th year, which includes a curse against those who disturb the tomb.

EDCS-39200645.translation: To Jupiter Highest, Tiberius Iulius Mamertinus dedicated this.
EDCS-39200645.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Highest by Tiberius Iulius Mamertinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39200646.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Vibania Hostilia made this for Sergius Hestiaius, son of Servilius Fabianus, consular, her friend and physician.
EDCS-39200646.summary: A dedication to the Chthonic Gods by Vibania Hostilia for her friend and physician Sergius Hestiaius, who held consular rank, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39200647.translation: Aurelia Maxeimiane for her most sweet child Asclepiodotus, who believed in God and lived for 7 years.
EDCS-39200647.summary: A funerary epitaph for Asclepiodotus, son of Aurelia Maxeimiane, who died after 7 years, possibly in the late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-39200650.translation: Eutyches lies here, having lived 21 years. My homeland was Taucheira, but now it is Aquileia.
EDCS-39200650.summary: This is a Greek funerary epigram for Eutyches, who lived 21 years and moved from Taucheira to Aquileia.

EDCS-39200667.translation: The hero Duinus, renowned, who surpassed all wisdom and glory, lies here, from the village of Dienkauna, the most blessed in all of Galatia.
EDCS-39200667.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Duinus, a local hero from the village of Dienkauna in Galatia, celebrated for his wisdom and glory.

EDCS-39200668.translation: Tertia Tertinia, daughter of Sporius, from Alexandra, greetings.
EDCS-39200668.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tertia Tertinia, likely from a Greek-speaking context.

EDCS-39200669.translation: Aurelius Proclus, son of Leuitus, lived sixty-five years.
EDCS-39200669.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Aurelius Proclus, son of Leuitus.

EDCS-39200670.translation: Claudia Callicrateia and Cornelius Diadumenus, by divine command, dedicated the altar.
EDCS-39200670.summary: A dedication of an altar by Claudia Callicrateia and Cornelius Diadumenus, who claim divine inspiration, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39200671.translation: Ruffia Chrysopolis, the beautiful and modest.
EDCS-39200671.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ruffia Chrysopolis, describing her as beautiful and modest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39501602.translation: Ennion made this. May the buyer remember.
EDCS-39501602.summary: An inscription by Ennion, likely on a piece of property or an object, asking the buyer to remember him.

EDCS-40000332.translation: To Ionis, daughter of Domitia Lucilla.
EDCS-40000332.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Ionis, daughter of Domitia Lucilla, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-40200160.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Valeria Valeria Prisca, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-40200161.translation: To Lucius Caelus Severus, son of Lucius Caelus Severus.
EDCS-40200161.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Caelus Severus, likely on a funerary monument, indicating a familial connection.

EDCS-40200162.translation: To Gaius Gavius, son of Gavius Capito.
EDCS-40200162.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Gavius, son of Gavius Capito, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-40200163.translation: To Comisia Ariadne, daughter of Pompeius Comisius.
EDCS-40200163.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Comisia Ariadne, daughter of Pompeius Comisius, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-40200165.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Gavius Phoebus, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-40200166.translation: To Fabulla Valeria, daughter of Titus, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-40200166.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Fabulla Valeria, daughter of Titus and granddaughter of Gaius, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-40200189.summary: This inscription likely marks a tomb or possession belonging to Quintus Clodius Ambrosus.

EDCS-40300016.translation: Under the consulship of Pontianus and Attilanus, from the estates of the heirs of Junius Sulpicianus. Pilagyrus?
EDCS-40300016.summary: This text records a legal or administrative matter concerning estates during the consulship of Pontianus and Attilanus.

EDCS-40300020.translation: From the potteries of Gaius Julius Dioscorus, when Antoninus was consul for the third time and Verus for the second.
EDCS-40300020.summary: This inscription marks products from the pottery workshops of Gaius Julius Dioscorus and is dated by the consulship of Antoninus (III) and Verus (II), likely to 161 AD.

EDCS-41500039.translation: Sirramnis the tribune purchased a chest for himself from his own funds; whoever wishes to open it will give five pounds of silver to the treasury.
EDCS-41500039.summary: This inscription details the purchase of a chest by Sirramnis, a tribune, and sets a penalty for unauthorized opening, likely related to funerary or public property.

EDCS-41500040.translation: Flavius Olus, from the contingent of the Fortenses, bought a tomb for himself with his own money. Whoever wishes to open it...
EDCS-41500040.summary: This inscription likely records the purchase or designation of a tomb by Flavius Olus, a soldier from the Fortenses unit.

EDCS-41500041.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Ursicinus, a stone-cutter.

EDCS-41700021.translation: From the workshops of Plaetorius Nepos. Earthenware pottery made by Aulus Aristius Thallus, when Servianus and Varus were consuls.
EDCS-41700021.summary: This inscription records the production of pottery from the workshops of Plaetorius Nepos, identifying the maker and the consuls for dating purposes.

EDCS-41700178.translation: Gaius Veratius, son of Gaius, an Italian from Aquileia, a military tribune of the fifth cohort, praefect of the fleet, praefect of the first cohort of Dalmatians, curator of roads, praefect of the grain supply in the province of Africa, curator of Illyricum and Istria, patron of the communities of Concordia and Altinum, of the college of mechanics, of the centonarii, of the dendrophori, and of the shipowners, and the urban plebs, to him for his merits, from a public collection, decreed by public authority.
EDCS-41700178.summary: This is a lengthy dedication honoring Gaius Veratius for his many distinguished military and administrative posts, presented by various professional and civic bodies.

EDCS-41700179.translation: In this holy place rests in peace Anicia Ulfina, venerable lady, devoted to God, who lived 18 full years, 5 months, and 7 days. Anicius Probus and Adeleta, her most devoted parents, placed [this] on the third day before the Kalends of September, in the consulship of Flavius Ricimer the honored.
EDCS-41700179.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Anicia Ulfina, detailing her age at death and stating that it was erected by her parents.

EDCS-41700180.translation: Tiberius Claudius Syntrophus, freedman of Tiberius, a dealer in cloaks, rests here.
EDCS-41700180.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Syntrophus, a cloak dealer.

EDCS-41700184.translation: Lucius Titius Severus, son of Gaius, for himself and for his wife Lartia Secunda, daughter of Publius, and for his sons Publius and Lucius Titius, has willingly made this vow.
EDCS-41700184.summary: This is a dedication of a tomb or monument, made by Lucius Titius Severus for himself, his wife, and his sons.

EDCS-41700186.translation: To Venus, the unconquered, victorious, beloved, celestial mother of gods, and mother of the gods. Gaius Caes Tinus has willingly dedicated this.
EDCS-41700186.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Venus, patronized by Gaius Caes Tinus.

EDCS-41700250.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Publius Manlius Surus, son of Publius, IIIvir capitalis, and Pomponia, daughter of Cnaeus, with incomparable marital harmony, having made this agreement under penalty, that the survivor will honor the tomb of the deceased each year on the Kalends of June with roses, and will feast here with all the Suri whom the dying man condemns, and that any descendant who survives will accompany the deceased, unchanged, to the tomb, since all must die by the unchangeable law of fate, will not follow the heir. But as their souls stood in harmony while alive, so may their ashes lie in harmony. The monument will not follow the heir, but as their souls stood in harmony while alive, so may their ashes lie in harmony. What is hidden here do I wish to bring forth and speak? Sercius Polensis, your most festive actor and parasite, lies here. This one thing at least is spoken of my own free will, but if anyone doubts, let him smell this earth: it smells of wine and the flower of old wine, with which, being satisfied, I lived. But if I have lived a life so pleasing and well-known to you, to the city, and to the world, it is no less fitting that I obtain a gift from you. Come to my aid and favor me, and subscribe to and seal this decree. If anyone feels his bladder full, let him carry this burden home to the sewer; but if he has been in too much haste, let him relieve himself here for the sake of religion. He who does not obey, may he be cursed, let him have no witness, let him be beaten by dogs with sticks. Let the dogs also understand this decree. You have been present, you have favored, and you have sealed. I see that you wish to give laughter to this place. I feel that he wanted this said. What is this that proceeds so easily? Truth itself, surely, is thirsty and has become my parasite, which has come uninvited to drink. Now, if you wish to be considered urbane, and to the truth which is my parasite, and to my dry ashes, hasten with a cup of wine as atonement. Farewell, go about your business, excellent travelers. Forgive my posthumous trifles, tricks, and circumlocutions.
EDCS-41700250.summary: This is a highly unusual and verbose funerary inscription by Sercius Polensis, a parasite and actor, who dictates the terms of his burial and imposes bizarre conditions and curses on visitors, while also making pronouncements about truth and wine.

EDCS-41700257.translation: Excellent travelers, whether arriving or visitors, whether walking in pairs or singly, or in groups, whatever will be more pleasing, brace your steps and do not wonder if you tarry a little. I was indeed a prompt speaker, and a concise discourse cannot be given to you. As it pleases me to be with you and to hold you captive, hanging on my words, as it always pleased me, this stone calls you. What, I ask, did I, who when alive could, want now that I am dead? Now you are called here. This was once my will, and my will wanted you to read this. Ah, what am I saying? Rather, carved! How unwillingly does truth still reconcile itself with me. For not here with ink, or papyrus, or any parchment, but with a chisel and a mallet, a lettered silicious stone, silent. What lies hidden here that I wish to bring forth and utter? Sercius Polensis, your most festive actor and parasite, lies here. This one thing, at least, is spoken of my own free will. But if anyone doubts, let him smell this earth: it smells of wine and the flower of old wine, with which, being satisfied, I lived. But if I have lived a life so pleasing and well-known to you, to the city, and to the world, it is no less fitting that I obtain a gift from you. Come to my aid and favor me, and subscribe to and seal this decree. If anyone feels his bladder full, let him carry this burden home to the sewer; but if he has been in too much haste, let him relieve himself here for the sake of religion. He who does not obey, may he be cursed, let him have no witness, let him be beaten by dogs with sticks. Let the dogs also understand this decree. You have been present, you have favored, and you have sealed. I see that you wish to give laughter to this place. I feel that he wanted this said. What is this that proceeds so easily? Truth itself, surely, is thirsty and has become my parasite, which has come uninvited to drink. Now, if you wish to be considered urbane, and to the truth which is my parasite, and to my dry ashes, hasten with a cup of wine as atonement. Farewell, go about your business, excellent travelers. Forgive my posthumous trifles, tricks, and circumlocutions.
EDCS-41700257.summary: This is an extremely verbose and self-aware epitaph by Sercius Polensis, an actor and parasite, who addresses travelers, discusses truth and wine, and issues a series of humorous and bizarre instructions and curses, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-41901175.translation: Marcus Magius, son of Lucius, built the crypt and restored(?) the porticoes.
EDCS-41901175.summary: This is a building inscription recording a public work, likely funded by Marcus Magius.

EDCS-41901184.translation: Gaius Satrius Communis, freedman of Gaius, in front 23 feet, in depth 13 feet.
EDCS-41901184.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land owned or designated by Gaius Satrius Communis, likely for a tomb or building.

EDCS-41901230.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Seia [dedicated this].
EDCS-41901230.summary: An altar dedicated to Jupiter by Seia.

EDCS-42100228.translation: Flavius Germanus and Flavius Lupicinus made this in memory of their mother, Flavia Ienuaria, while they were alive.
EDCS-42100228.summary: A memorial inscription for Flavia Ienuaria, set up by her sons Flavius Germanus and Flavius Lupicinus.

EDCS-42100230.translation: To the divine shades. P. lived 16 years, 6 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-42100230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of P. Inpostor.

EDCS-42600170.translation: Saint Cantius, Saint Cantianus, Saint Cantianilla, Saint Quirinus, Saint Latinus.
EDCS-42600170.summary: A list of names of saints, likely commemorating martyrs or holy figures.

EDCS-42600171.translation: Laurentius, a man of standing, and Niceforus, a man of standing, fulfilled their vow to the holy ones.
EDCS-42600171.summary: A vow fulfilled by two men of standing, Laurentius and Niceforus, to unspecified holy figures.

EDCS-42600183.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Saint Sebastian.

EDCS-42600515.translation: Quiddila, may you live in God
EDCS-42600515.summary: This is a funerary inscription wishing the deceased, Quiddila, eternal life in God.

EDCS-43600068.translation: Gordian, for the state of the Nesasentines
EDCS-43600068.summary: This inscription records an action or dedication by Gordian for the benefit of the community of Nesasentes.

EDCS-44100313.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely an epitaph, naming Caius Lindius.

EDCS-44100315.translation: To Publius Sariolenus Rufus, my brother
EDCS-44100315.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a sibling to Publius Sariolenus Rufus.

EDCS-44100316.translation: To the divine shades. Sex. Saccidius Valentis lived 19 years and 2 days. His parents, Saccidia Zosima and Aelius Hermes, erected this monument during their lifetime.
EDCS-44100316.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sex. Saccidius Valentis, erected by his parents.

EDCS-44100317.translation: To the divine shades. To Publius Atilius Iustus, [---] his [con]cubine [---]
EDCS-44100317.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Publius Atilius Iustus and his concubine.

EDCS-44100318.translation: Caius Caeparius Ursio gave this gift to Venus
EDCS-44100318.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Caius Caeparius Ursio to the goddess Venus.

EDCS-44100320.translation: Gaius Tarvisius Secundus, son of Aulus, four-time magistrate with curule authority, gave this gift to Juno Regina.
EDCS-44100320.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Tarvisius Secundus, an elected official, dedicating a gift to Juno Regina.

EDCS-44100321.translation: Ambulasia, daughter of Marcus, gives this to her son Gaius Fadienus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-44100321.summary: A familial dedication by a mother to her son, likely from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-44100322.translation: Lucius Pompennius Placidus, son of Caius; Fadiena Tertia, daughter of Caius. Marcus Pompennius Valens, son of Lucius, aged 23 years. Cruel shades snatched away the harsh youth in his twenty-third year; a mournful hour brought him to the darkness.
EDCS-44100322.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with a poetic elegy for Marcus Pompennius Valens, who died at age 23.

EDCS-44100323.translation: Caius Fadienus Repentinus, son of Caius; Cursoria Secunda, daughter of Lucius. Caius Fadienus Vegetus, son of Caius, aged 21 years. Death, which the son should have inflicted upon the father, the father performed due to premature death, exposed to griefs; observe, traveler, the monument composed for the son whom the father himself gave.
EDCS-44100323.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Fadienus Vegetus, erected by his father, with a poignant verse about parental grief.

EDCS-44100324.translation: To Marcus Fadienus Camillus, son of Caius, father; to Valeria Secunda, daughter of Quintus, mother. Marcus, Caius, Lucius, sons, erected this. Greetings, Marcus, traveler, you have read my name on this inscription; remember that this is a mortal home. Farewell, may you live an excellent life in the upper world; I lived as I could and as I wished; I gave to whom I wanted, I did not give to whom I did not want; if anyone accuses me, let him come and argue with me. Farewell, Marcus.
EDCS-44100324.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Fadienus Camillus and his wife Valeria Secunda, erected by their sons, with a lengthy epitaph and a personal message to the reader.

EDCS-44100325.translation: Father, alive, erected [this] to Lucius Fadienus Actor, son of Lucius. You who pass by and look at my tomb, behold how unjustly life was taken from me; I lived twenty years minus three years; I laid down my sweet soul, aged eighteen. Do not grieve, traveler, it was necessary to die; fate willed this. Lucius Fadienus Agilis, son of Marcus; Atilia Felicia, freedwoman of Caius. Stone, I implore you, rest lightly on the bones and remain for the underworld; do not be heavy. What the son owed to the parent, death prematurely caused the parent to do.
EDCS-44100325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with two parts: one for Lucius Fadienus Actor, erected by his father, and another for Lucius Fadienus Agilis and Atilia Felicia, likely his parents, with a verse lamenting premature death.

EDCS-44100329.translation: To Mars, Ianuaria Maior dedicated this as a gift.
EDCS-44100329.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the god Mars by Ianuaria Maior.

EDCS-44100332.translation: To Bitutia Paterna, her well-deserving son-in-law.
EDCS-44100332.summary: A dedication to a son-in-law, possibly on a tombstone or funerary monument, date uncertain.

EDCS-44100333.translation: Sius, son of Caius, [dedicates this] to M. Poblilia.
EDCS-44100333.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning a dedicator and a recipient, likely a funerary or votive dedication.

EDCS-44100334.translation: To the Good Goddess, Attius Priscus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-44100334.summary: An inscription recording a votive offering to the Bona Dea, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-44100335.translation: Flavius Valerianus set this up to his incomparable and deserving fellow soldier and comrade, whose many benefits in my times of need I experienced during his lifetime.
EDCS-44100335.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavius Valerianus to his deceased fellow soldier and comrade, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-44100336.translation: From Balbanus, in the twelfth indiction, through Romulus the legate.
EDCS-44100336.summary: A reference to a transaction or administrative record involving Balbanus and a legate named Romulus, likely from the late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-44100344.translation: Felix, the public servant of the people of Tergeste, made this.
EDCS-44100344.summary: A dedication or commission by a public official from Tergeste, possibly of an architectural or civic nature, date uncertain.

EDCS-44500110.translation: Publius Saufeius Meridianus, son of Publius, made this monument while alive for himself and his freedmen Dasio, Primo, and for his freedwomen Quinctia and Venusta, and for his other freedmen and freedwomen. Saufeia Festa, daughter of Publius. The monument's location is 20 feet in front and 32 feet in the ground.
EDCS-44500110.summary: A funerary monument set up by a freedman for himself and his freed slaves, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE, with measurements for the plot.

EDCS-44500111.translation: Gaius Arpi[---], freedman of Marcus, Sta[---]
EDCS-44500111.summary: A fragmentary inscription identifying an individual with Roman names and freedman status, possibly funerary or dedicatory.

EDCS-44500112.translation: Publius Pe[---], son of Publius, a centurion of the le[gion?]
EDCS-44500112.summary: A fragmentary inscription identifying a centurion, likely military, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-44600086.summary: A votive dedication to the goddess Juno Regina, a common practice throughout the Roman world.

EDCS-44600087.summary: A votive dedication to the god Saturn, often associated with agriculture and time, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-44700046.translation: Place of the monument of Manlius Zosimus and Livia Pude[---].
EDCS-44700046.summary: This inscription marks the location of a monument belonging to Manlius Zosimus and Livia Pude[---].

EDCS-44700050.translation: [---] Marcus Ai[---], freedman of Marcus Pris[---].
EDCS-44700050.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a freedman named Pris[---], belonging to Marcus Ai[---].

EDCS-44700051.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly the beginning of a name and another letter or abbreviation.

EDCS-44700059.summary: This inscription records Maxsuma, the daughter of Secunda, with a possible misspelling of 'maxima'.

EDCS-44900001.translation: Gaius Calidius Priscianus, to his parents Gaius Calidius Hermetus and Annaea Priscilla, and to his freedwoman Calidia Ursula.
EDCS-44900001.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to parents and a freedwoman by Gaius Calidius Priscianus.

EDCS-45600018.translation: Lucius V I gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-45600018.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius V I to the god Mercury.

EDCS-45600044.translation: Titus Annius, son of Titus, consul.
EDCS-45600044.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Titus Annius, who held the office of consul.

EDCS-45800003.translation: To the gods, to the parents, Marcus Censor willingly and deservedly [dedicated].
EDCS-45800003.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Censor to the gods and his parents.

EDCS-45900104.text_edition: \n Caio Herennio Cai filio Poblilia Caeciliano adlecto in senatum ab Imperatore Hadriano Augusto quaestori provinciae Narbonensis tribuno plebis IIIIviro iure dicundo Veronae patrono decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-45900104.translation: To Gaius Herennius, son of Gaius, from the Poblilia tribe, Caecilianus, who was appointed to the Senate by the Emperor Hadrian Augustus, quaestor of the province of Narbonensis, tribune of the plebs, and duovir for judging cases in Verona, and patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-45900104.summary: An inscription honoring Gaius Herennius Caecilianus for his distinguished career and public service, likely dating to the reign of Hadrian (117-138 CE).

EDCS-46600143.translation: [---]ssius by his will ordered a market building to be made with twenty thousand sesterces; the heirs gave the money by decree of the decurions. Valeria [---], his wife, gave fifteen thousand sesterces for the crypt.
EDCS-46600143.summary: This inscription records the execution of a will for a market building and a crypt, funded by the deceased and his heirs, with a specific contribution for the crypt by his wife Valeria.

EDCS-46600144.translation: Caesernius Severus vows to give you a goose for 30,000 sesterces, so that you may not be harmed; and I also vow a chick.
EDCS-46600144.summary: A magical or ritualistic inscription where the dedicator vows offerings to a deity or spirit, possibly for protection, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-46600148.translation: Saufeia [dedicated this to] Rhodinus. 20 feet in front, 20 feet behind.
EDCS-46600148.summary: A funerary inscription marking a grave plot measuring 20 feet in front and 20 feet behind, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-46600149.translation: Publici's pot [---] 116 pounds, good [---] 247 pounds, pot [---] 120 pounds, pot [---] 115 pounds. Marci's pot [---] 256 pounds, pot [---] 117 pounds, good [---] 253 pounds, pot [---] 120 [---] 4. Trosi's good [---] 211. Sari [---] 370.
EDCS-46600149.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of weights or quantities, possibly of goods like pottery, belonging to different individuals such as Publici, Marci, Trosi, and Sari.

EDCS-46600150.summary: This inscription identifies Saint Prosdocimus as a bishop and confessor.

EDCS-46600151.summary: This inscription names Gaius [---] Marsus, likely a person's name.

EDCS-46600152.translation: To Publius Cassius Nepos, son of Publius, freedman, VIvir (member of a college of six).
EDCS-46600152.summary: An epitaph for Publius Cassius Nepos, a freedman and member of a college of six, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-46600153.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Lucius Cercinius Attalus, VIvir (member of a college of six), and his wife Myranthis, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-46600153.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Cercinius Attalus and his wife, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-46600154.translation: Sextus Popillius Macer, son of Sextus, from the Poblilia tribe, made this while alive for himself and his brother.
EDCS-46600154.summary: A funerary monument erected by Sextus Popillius Macer for himself and his brother, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-46600875.summary: This inscription records the name Publius Romilius Amarantus, possibly related to a property or monument.

EDCS-46600902.translation: To my sweetest daughter, Severiana, who lived 3 years, [some months], and 11 days, departed in faith. Faithful Juliana, mother, and Severianus, father.
EDCS-46600902.summary: A poignant epitaph for a young daughter named Severiana, set up by her grieving parents, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-46600918.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-46600918.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for the well-deserving Iulianetis, who lived 18 years, and with her husband Virginio for about one year and 2 months and [some days], died. Grieving, the husband placed this against his vow. Departed in faith. Faithful. The 11th day before the Ides of March.
EDCS-46600918.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulianetis, who died young after a year of marriage, set up by her grieving husband, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-46600919.translation: To Marcellinus(?), his well-deserving brother, Exsuperius(!) placed this for his most deserving brother, who lived 30 years and 6 months.
EDCS-46600919.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to a brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46600920.translation: Agorinus, well-deserving, who lived for one year and two months.
EDCS-46600920.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Agorinus, recording his short lifespan.

EDCS-46600921.summary: This inscription provides the full name and filiation of Sextus Laelius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-46600922.translation: Burial place of Praecellia Primigenia, freedwoman of Umulier, 16 feet in front, 25 feet in the rear
EDCS-46600922.summary: This funerary inscription specifies the burial plot dimensions for Praecellia Primigenia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-46600923.translation: The remains of Prima, freedwoman of Pinaria, 3 feet in front, 3 feet in the rear.
EDCS-46600923.summary: A funerary inscription marking the burial plot of Prima, freedwoman of Pinaria, indicating the dimensions of her property.

EDCS-47001231.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Perennius Crescens, likely related to a monument or ownership.

EDCS-47300002.summary: This inscription mentions Quinctus Appolinaris, identified as a member of a group or association.

EDCS-47400326.translation: Of Titus Aelius Victor, a soldier of the cohort
EDCS-47400326.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Aelius Victor as a soldier of a cohort.

EDCS-47400337.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Marcus Aurelius Sossius, veteran of the IIII Flavia legion, made this for himself and for Julia Valentina(?), while alive.
EDCS-47400337.summary: A funerary monument set up by a veteran of the IIII Flavia legion for himself and his wife.

EDCS-47400413.translation: [He/She] made it for Quinctus, son of Eos
EDCS-47400413.summary: This inscription records that someone made a dedication for Quinctus, son of Eos.

EDCS-47501074.translation: Titus Ennius Passer, son of Lucius
EDCS-47501074.summary: This inscription provides the full name and filiation of Titus Ennius Passer, son of Lucius.

EDCS-47800711.translation: Saint Philip the apostle, from Scythia.
EDCS-47800711.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Saint Philip the Apostle as being from Scythia.

EDCS-48000983.translation: Flavia Telesphoris made this for Secundus, who deserved well.
EDCS-48000983.summary: This is a dedication by Flavia Telesphoris to Secundus, honoring his merits.

EDCS-48500154.translation: Acume, freedwoman of Philositus, alive, made this for herself and for Marcus Poblicius Secundus.
EDCS-48500154.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a freedwoman for herself and another individual, likely her partner or benefactor.

EDCS-48500155.translation: Publius Braetius [---] for himself and Braetia [---] Ter[---], ordered this to be made by his will for Publius Braetius [---] Ver[---] and Munatia, daughter of Caius, his wife, and Petronia, daughter of Caius. 40 feet in front, 45 feet in the rear.
EDCS-48500155.summary: A funerary monument established by testament by Publius Braetius, indicating dimensions and beneficiaries of the plot.

EDCS-48500156.translation: Capellius Gerens; Lucius Capellius Frequens, son of Lucius, [made this].
EDCS-48500156.summary: This inscription records the names of Capellius Gerens and Lucius Capellius Frequens, son of Lucius, possibly related to a funerary monument.

EDCS-48500157.translation: [Dedicated to] Titus Cassius Aescina, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-48500157.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication to Titus Cassius Aescina, a freedman.

EDCS-48500158.translation: Gaius Catius Quers, freedman of Gaius, [made this] for himself and for his wife Catia, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-48500158.summary: This funerary inscription records that Gaius Catius Quers, a freedman, dedicated a monument for himself and his wife Catia, also a freedwoman.

EDCS-48500159.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Publius Coccilius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-48500160.translation: Flavia Telesphoris made this for Secundus, who deserved well.
EDCS-48500160.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavia Telesphoris to Secundus.

EDCS-48500161.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Floridus and his father, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory monument.

EDCS-48500162.summary: This fragmentary inscription names Fremicinia, daughter of Fremaestus.

EDCS-48500163.translation: Fulvia Lepida, freedwoman of Mulieris, alive, made this for herself, for Gaius Cassius Peregrinus, freedman of Priscus, and for Clidia, daughter.
EDCS-48500163.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by Fulvia Lepida, a freedwoman, for herself and others, including a freedman and a daughter.

EDCS-48500164.translation: Inacho [---] 20 feet in front, 30 feet in the rear, [he] made [this] while alive.
EDCS-48500164.summary: A funerary inscription marking a burial plot, likely set up by Inacho for himself, with specified dimensions.

EDCS-48500165.translation: Burial place for Magia, daughter of Gaius, [...]
EDCS-48500165.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot for Magia, daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-48500166.translation: Sem[---], son of Manius(?), and Marcia, daughter of Marcus, [erected this] while alive.
EDCS-48500166.summary: This inscription, likely from a tomb, records the names of two individuals, Sem[---] and Marcia, who set up the monument during their lifetime.

EDCS-48500167.translation: Marcia Salvia, freedwoman of Lucius, [and] Marcia Erotis, freedwoman of Lucius, [erected this].
EDCS-48500167.summary: This inscription records two women, both freedwomen of Lucius, named Marcia Salvia and Marcia Erotis, who likely dedicated this monument.

EDCS-48500168.translation: Manius Sescinius Licinus dedicated [this]. 32 feet in front, 72 feet in the rear.
EDCS-48500168.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of land or a property by Manius Sescinius Licinus, with dimensions.

EDCS-48500169.translation: Gaius Trebius, son of Quintus, [dedicated this] to himself and [---] while alive.
EDCS-48500169.summary: This inscription records Gaius Trebius, son of Quintus, dedicating a monument to himself and possibly others during his lifetime.

EDCS-48500170.translation: To Trosius, son of Publius, [and] Claudia [---].
EDCS-48500170.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Trosius, son of Publius, and Claudia.

EDCS-48500171.summary: This inscription records the name Valeria and possibly the place name Eleusis, perhaps as a dedication or memorial.

EDCS-48500180.translation: Decidia daughter of Iucundus, 20 feet in front, 35 feet in the field.
EDCS-48500180.summary: A boundary marker or funerary inscription indicating property dimensions belonging to Decidia, daughter of Iucundus.

EDCS-48500186.summary: This fragment records the name Titus Virius, likely part of a larger dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-48500222.translation: According to the will of Marcus Caepio, son of Marcus, Lucius Caepio [---].
EDCS-48500222.summary: This inscription records Lucius Caepio, son of Marcus Caepio, acting according to a will, likely related to inheritance or a funerary monument.

EDCS-48500223.translation: [---] to his son Lucius, to Maximai, daughter of Marcus Acutius, his mother [---].
EDCS-48500223.summary: This inscription appears to be an epitaph honoring a mother, Maximai, and a son, Lucius.

EDCS-48600002.translation: Marcus Maeclius Magnus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-48600002.summary: This inscription records Marcus Maeclius Magnus fulfilling a vow to the god Hercules, likely in thanks for a favor received.

EDCS-48700069.translation: To Atius, son of Pupil(l)ius, from Coelius Festus.
EDCS-48700069.summary: This is a dedication to Atius, son of Pupil(l)ius, by Coelius Festus.

EDCS-48700122.translation: To the Youth: Tiberius Publicius Primitivos, the runner, dedicated this gift to the precinct of Venus.
EDCS-48700122.summary: This is a dedication by Tiberius Publicius Primitivos, identified as a runner for the precinct of Venus, likely an athletic or youth group.

EDCS-48700144.summary: This inscription is a dedication or epitaph addressed to Laetilia Rufina.

EDCS-48700146.translation: To Quintus Homonius, son of Quintus.
EDCS-48700146.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Homonius, son of Quintus, likely on a public monument or tombstone.

EDCS-48700153.summary: This inscription indicates a dedication or remembrance from Quartilla to someone named Augurinus, possibly on a funerary context.

EDCS-48700155.translation: To Severa; and C. ... M. ... Au. ... Ei. ...
EDCS-48700155.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication or a memorial, possibly funerary, with multiple names or abbreviations.

EDCS-48700156.translation: To the Iunones: Lucius Licinius Firmus willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-48700156.summary: This is a votive offering to the Iunones by Lucius Licinius Firmus.

EDCS-48700158.translation: Holy First-Born, I, Tertius, whom Sira dedicated, entreat you: keep me, Tertius, whom Sira dedicated, from this day and this hour, safe in all time, from all danger, fear, demonic possession, apparition, and every disease, and every destructive spirit; whether the disease comes from the gods, or men, or demons, or from the self-delusions of dreams, phantoms, or darkness.
EDCS-48700158.summary: This is a magical invocation or amulet inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, seeking protection for Tertius, dedicated by Sira, against various spiritual and physical ailments.

EDCS-48700859.translation: Caecilius Ocratius Sertius, son of V. Crispius Pa Varius, son of Ap. Publicius Tertius Sertorius Aemilius Valerius Blandius.
EDCS-48700859.summary: This inscription lists the names of several individuals, likely for a funerary monument or a record of patronage, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-48700861.translation: [... by] the vote of the people / [to] Brixia for himself / [... to] Viator / [... of] years
EDCS-48700861.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to record a grant or dedication made by a community ('populi suffragio') to Brixia and Viator, possibly related to land or a public work.

EDCS-48700862.translation: Made during his lifetime: Lucius Atilius Philargyrus, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for Nonia Salvia, freedwoman of Sextus, and for their adopted child (vernaculus) Primigenius, aged 8.
EDCS-48700862.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Atilius Philargyrus for himself, his freedwoman wife Nonia Salvia, and their young adopted son Primigenius.

EDCS-48700863.translation: Gaius Julius Syneros, son of Sedata.
EDCS-48700863.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Julius Syneros, son of Sedata, likely appearing on a tombstone or a dedicatory monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48700867.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary monument, mentioning individuals named Domitius and Postumius.

EDCS-48700874.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that seems to record measurements and names, possibly related to a boundary or property marker.

EDCS-49900001.translation: Attia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, wife of Manius Cutius Philargyrus, freedman of Manius.
EDCS-49900001.summary: This inscription identifies Attia Secunda as the wife of Manius Cutius Philargyrus.

EDCS-51200037.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Sextus Julius Severus, likely from a tombstone or a personal dedication.

EDCS-51200038.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Aurarius Blaesus, likely for a funerary monument or a public dedication.

EDCS-51200039.summary: This is a personal name, likely appearing on a monument or as a dedicant.

EDCS-51400878.translation: To Calediae Procula, freedwoman Tertulla, aged 5[---] years.
EDCS-51400878.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tertulla, freedwoman of Caledius Proculus, indicating her age.

EDCS-51400879.translation: Potens, son of Aufidius, in the Mato [district/area].
EDCS-51400879.summary: This inscription appears to be a name with a patronymic and a possible location identifier.

EDCS-51400917.translation: Gaius Cornelius Leucus, freedman of a woman, made [this] for himself while alive.
EDCS-51400917.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Cornelius Leucus, who dedicated the monument to himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-51400918.translation: For the Republic of the Veronesi, through Clodius Rufinus and Valerius Crescens.
EDCS-51400918.summary: This inscription likely records a public work or donation made to the city of Verona by Clodius Rufinus and Valerius Crescens.

EDCS-51400925.translation: Quintus Luci[---] Supstin[us] and Lucius Lucius Cupitus gave this offering sacred to the Great Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-51400925.summary: This is a dedication of a religious offering to the Great Mother of the Gods by Quintus Luci[---] Supstin[us] and Lucius Lucius Cupitus.

EDCS-51400927.translation: Aquillia Ide [dedicated this] to Bellona, in accordance with a vow.
EDCS-51400927.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Bellona by Aquillia Ide, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-51400928.translation: [---]: Polla willingly paid her vow as deserved.
EDCS-51400928.summary: This is a votive offering by Polla, who willingly paid her vow.

EDCS-51701017.summary: This is a milestone inscription marking a distance of 12 miles for Emperor Maxentius, dated to his reign (306-312 AD).

EDCS-51800167.translation: To our Lords, Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, perpetual and fortunate.
EDCS-51800167.summary: This is an inscription dedicating something to the emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-51800225.summary: This is a religious dedication to Hercules by a veteran, seeking divine favour for himself and his companion.

EDCS-51800228.summary: This is a dedication by Titus Barbius to the god Apollo, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-51800229.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titus Volusius Firmus to Apollo, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-52100139.translation: Celadus, freedman of Titus Arius Soterichus, a physician, [lived] for 60 years.
EDCS-52100139.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Celadus, a freedman and physician, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-52302279.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld: Aucilia, wife of Lucius Valerius Gracilis.
EDCS-52302279.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Aucilia, the wife of Lucius Valerius Gracilis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-52600147.translation: To Aelius Marcellus, for his well-deserving service, by his heirs named above.
EDCS-52600147.summary: This is an epitaph honoring Aelius Marcellus, likely erected by his heirs.

EDCS-52600148.translation: Publius Herennius Faustus, son of Sextus, of the Macedo family, freedman; a plot of 10 feet in front and 10 feet behind.
EDCS-52600148.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot, indicating ownership or purchase.

EDCS-52600149.translation: Burial plot. Maria Thala, Pollia Marinus, freedman of Lucius, 20 feet in front and 22 feet behind. This monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-52600149.summary: This inscription defines a burial plot, specifying its dimensions and stating that it is not inheritable.

EDCS-52600150.translation: Burial place of Gaius Q. Hermes: 24 feet in front, 36 feet in depth.
EDCS-52600150.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot allocated to Gaius Q. Hermes.

EDCS-52600151.translation: Gaius Trebius, freedman of a woman, [for] himself and Trebia Secunda, daughter of Caius, 20 feet in front.
EDCS-52600151.summary: This epitaph records the allocation of a burial space for Gaius Trebius and Trebia Secunda, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-52600181.translation: Lucius Pitiavius Sutor, son of Lucius, of the Pob(lilia) tribe, 14 feet in front.
EDCS-52600181.summary: This inscription records the front dimensions of a plot of land, likely for burial purposes.

EDCS-52600182.translation: Made by the living. [---]nius, son of Quintus, [---]is, [---] for himself and [---] Sabina, daughter of Quintus? [---]
EDCS-52600182.summary: This incomplete inscription appears to be a dedication for a tomb made by a living person for themselves and others.

EDCS-52600183.translation: Lucius Caesius Eros, freedman of Lucius, for himself and Caesias, freedwoman of Lucius, and Cornelia [and] Calpurnia.
EDCS-52600183.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caesius Eros and several other individuals, likely freedmen and members of their families.

EDCS-52600184.translation: Made by the living. Gaius Marius [---
EDCS-52600184.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating that the monument was made by a living person, Gaius Marius.

EDCS-52600185.translation: Gaius Cornelius Longus of the Pob(lilia) tribe, [and] Cassia Galla.
EDCS-52600185.summary: This inscription records the names of Gaius Cornelius Longus and Cassia Galla, possibly related to a burial.

EDCS-52600186.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Cassia Primigenia, identified as a freedwoman.

EDCS-52600187.translation: By his will, Gaius Capitius Gallus, son of Gaius, veteran of the 20th Legion, a standard-bearer for the tribunes, ordered this to be made for himself and for his freedwoman Capitias Lesbia, and for his Lucius Valerius Calvus.
EDCS-52600187.summary: This funerary inscription, ordered by will, commemorates Gaius Capitius Gallus, a veteran and standard-bearer, and his freedwoman and another individual named Lucius Valerius Calvus.

EDCS-52600190.summary: This is an incomplete epitaph for Marcia, wife of Marcus.

EDCS-52600192.translation: Place granted by Gaius Iuventius Agathopus.
EDCS-52600192.summary: This inscription records the granting of a place, likely for burial, by Gaius Iuventius Agathopus.

EDCS-52600193.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Memmius Geminianus for Minervalis, a deserving slave.
EDCS-52600193.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a master to a deserving slave.

EDCS-52600194.translation: To the Deities of the Departed. Coelius Fronto willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-52600194.summary: This is a funerary dedication with a vow fulfilled, likely for deceased relatives.

EDCS-52600196.translation: Marcus Brabuttius Arrianus for himself and for Julia Quarta.
EDCS-52600196.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates a burial space for Marcus Brabuttius Arrianus and Julia Quarta.

EDCS-52600198.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Larcius Peregrinus, Clodia Vitalina to her husband, and Lucius Larcius Myrinus and Larcia Myrine to their father, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-52600198.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by children for their parents, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-52600200.translation: Son of Caius, [---]. Marcus Varrhenius, son of Caius, [---]. Frontage [3] feet, recess [3] feet.
EDCS-52600200.summary: A funerary inscription possibly recording dimensions of a tomb or plot, with names partially lost.

EDCS-52600201.translation: Gaius Attius Ruga, son of Gaius, of the Pob(lilia) tribe, made (this) for himself and for his father Gaius Attius Mancia, son of Publius, of the Pob(lilia) tribe, and for his mother Apernicia Maxima, daughter of Publius, while alive.
EDCS-52600201.summary: A funerary epitaph where a son dedicates a monument to himself and his deceased parents, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-52900054.translation: Barbes and Martana made [this] with their people, 120 feet.

EDCS-52900055.translation: Rufinus, a most distinguished man, made [this] with his people, 300 feet.
EDCS-52900055.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 300 feet by the distinguished man Rufinus and his dependents.

EDCS-52900056.translation: Stercorius and Decentia made [this] with their people, 300 feet.

EDCS-52900057.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 300 feet, possibly dedicated to Valeria by Maurilio.

EDCS-52900058.translation: To Carpil(i?) and Penetia with their family, in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-52900059.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sacri

EDCS-52900061.translation: Felix, a most distinguished man, and Toribius and Immola, his most distinguished sons, in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-52900062.translation: Mauricus and Macriana, in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-52900069.translation: May God Eutherius preserve you and yours here; live long.
EDCS-52900069.summary: A short devotional or funerary inscription asking for divine protection for Eutherius and his family.

EDCS-52900072.translation: Theodore, you have grown up here, be happy here.
EDCS-52900072.summary: A funerary or commemorative inscription wishing happiness to Theodore, who lived or grew up in this place.

EDCS-52900085.translation: Probus and Severa made [this] with their people, one thousand feet.
EDCS-52900085.summary: This inscription records a construction project of 1000 feet by Probus and Severa and their dependents.

EDCS-53501128.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Caecilia Melite for her son, herself, and her freedmen and freedwomen, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-55200071.summary: This inscription records a granted right-of-way, possibly for travel or access.

EDCS-55702086.translation: For the vow and salvation of the most glorious Anastasia.

EDCS-56000352.translation: Marcus Arnius Severus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, a freedman.

EDCS-56500136.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a gift by Lucius V. Pr. to someone named Sedatus.

EDCS-57000056.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a freedman, Lucius Valerius Primigenius, and his freedwoman wife, Valeria Tertulla.

EDCS-57000057.translation: Lucius Vassidius Viator, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe, soldier of the VII Praetorian cohort, for himself and for Lucius Vassidius, his son, and for Cassia Secunda, daughter of Caius, his mother.
EDCS-57000057.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a Praetorian Guard soldier, Lucius Vassidius Viator, dedicating the monument for himself, his son, and his mother.

EDCS-57100031.summary: A simple funerary or commemorative inscription bearing the name Titus Duronius Niger.

EDCS-57100032.translation: To Publius Calpurnius Saturninus, from Gaius Calpurnius Maximus, son of Lucius, freedman of Caesernia, and Calpurnia Maxima, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-57100032.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Publius Calpurnius Saturninus by members of his family.

EDCS-57100060.text_edition: \n Tiberius Tablinius Tiberi libertus Epaphra testamento \n
EDCS-57100060.translation: Tiberius Tablinius Epaphra, freedman of Tiberius, [made this] by his will.

EDCS-57200210.translation: Tampia, daughter of Lucius, of Diovei.
EDCS-57200210.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tampia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-57200217.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Sextus Hirrius Pudens, soldier of the 9th Praetorian cohort, of the century of Petronius, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-57200217.summary: A military dedication by Sextus Hirrius Pudens, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter.

EDCS-57400142.summary: A fragmentary inscription that likely records the name and filiation of an individual.

EDCS-57400143.translation: To Petrius Primus, for his daughter Primigenia, [restored text].
EDCS-57400143.summary: This inscription likely records a funerary dedication for Primigenia, possibly by her father Petrius Primus.

EDCS-58000056.summary: This inscription identifies Pilotas as the slave of Arrius Quintus.

EDCS-58800038.translation: Sextus Cloatius Gracchus, son of Gaius, of the Maecia tribe, primipilaris (chief centurion) of the 18th legion.
EDCS-58800038.summary: A military inscription honoring Sextus Cloatius Gracchus, a distinguished officer (primipilaris) of the 18th Legion.

EDCS-58800040.translation: The burial place of Pilio, freedman of Gaius Cornelius.
EDCS-58800040.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Pilio, a freedman.

EDCS-58800043.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Caecilia Severa Philumenus.

EDCS-58800045.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Coelia Verecunda, the wife of the dedicator.

EDCS-58800046.translation: The monumental plot of Gaius Tettidius Primus and Quintus Lucilius "Florus"; in front sixteen feet, in the field thirty-two feet.

EDCS-58800047.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the dimensions of a burial plot made by Tiberius Vibius Spendon for his family.

EDCS-58800048.translation: Cassia Ianuaria, daughter of Publius, made this while she was alive, for herself, and for her husband Lucius Valerius Bithus, and for her brothers Cassis, measuring 30 feet in front and 30 feet of land.
EDCS-58800048.summary: This funerary epitaph records a woman, Cassia Ianuaria, dedicating a burial plot for herself, her husband, and brothers.

EDCS-59200008.translation: Quintus Lepidius Niger, son of Lucius.
EDCS-59200008.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely for a tombstone, identifying Quintus Lepidius Niger and his father Lucius.

EDCS-59200010.translation: Lucius Baebius Pladomenus, a sailor from the fleet, aged 29.
EDCS-59200010.summary: This is a military epitaph for Lucius Baebius Pladomenus, a sailor, specifying his age and service branch.

EDCS-59400051.translation: He ordered by will that this be made for himself and for his wife Perelia Grata, having served as aedile, duovir, and quinquennial magistrate, and prefect of the engineers.
EDCS-59400051.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the offices held by the deceased, who commissioned his tomb and that of his wife.

EDCS-59400052.translation: Silvanus, of the colonists of Aquileia.
EDCS-59400052.summary: This inscription identifies Silvanus in relation to the colonists of Aquileia, possibly as a member or representative.

EDCS-59400053.translation: Egleptus, a freedman of the colonists of Aquileia.
EDCS-59400053.summary: This is a dedication by Egleptus, a freedman associated with the colonists of Aquileia.

EDCS-59400054.translation: Of Lucius Avilius T. O., a freedman: six cloaks, 5 denarii.
EDCS-59400054.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of goods or a debt settlement, listing items and a monetary amount associated with Lucius Avilius T. O.

EDCS-59500320.translation: Eutyches, a freedman of the colonists of Concordia, makes this.
EDCS-59500320.summary: This is a dedication by Eutyches, a freedman associated with the colonists of Concordia.

EDCS-59500321.translation: Gaius Poblicius Germanus, freedman of the municipality of Opitergium, made this while he was alive, for himself and Secunda.
EDCS-59500321.summary: This funerary epitaph records Gaius Poblicius Germanus dedicating a tomb for himself and Secunda.

EDCS-59500324.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Pilota as the slave of Arrius Quintus.

EDCS-59500326.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership marker, simply stating the name Caius Laekanius Bassus.

EDCS-59500328.summary: This inscription identifies Clymenus as belonging to or being associated with the Emperor.

EDCS-59500332.translation: Of Caius Lesbius, of Emperor Domitian.
EDCS-59500332.summary: This inscription likely marks an object dedicated by Caius Lesbius in honor of or during the time of Emperor Domitian.

EDCS-59500337.translation: To Aelia Fortunata, most dutiful companion, by Pothinus of the people of Verona.
EDCS-59500337.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Pothinus to his devoted partner Aelia Fortunata.

EDCS-59500338.translation: To the divine shades, Iulius Pa[...]

EDCS-59800028.translation: To the Father Dis and the goddess Lua, in the name of Lucius.
EDCS-59800028.summary: This is a religious dedication to the deities Dis Pater and Lua, made in the name of Lucius.

EDCS-60000057.translation: Axia Prima and Lartidia Urbana, freedwoman of Marcus, and Mulvia Prisca, freedwoman of the woman (Urbanus?), made this while alive, for memory and friendship, measuring 12 feet in front and 40 feet in the rear.
EDCS-60000057.summary: This funerary epitaph records Axia Prima, Lartidia Urbana, and Mulvia Prisca dedicating a monument for memory and friendship.

EDCS-60000058.translation: Melete, freedwoman of the woman (Calaecinius?), made this while she was alive, for herself, measuring 22 feet in front and 30 feet in the rear.

EDCS-60000059.translation: To Efolia Saturnina, freedwoman of Aulus.
EDCS-60000059.summary: This is a dedication to Efolia Saturnina, a freedwoman, likely on a tombstone or a similar monument.

EDCS-60000060.translation: Gaius Helvius Iucundus, freedman of Gaius, his fellow freedman Iucunda, placed this while alive.
EDCS-60000060.summary: This funerary epitaph records Gaius Helvius Iucundus dedicating a monument for his fellow freedwoman Iucunda.

EDCS-60000061.translation: Quintus Licinius Acceptus, son of Quintus, his freedman, for himself.

EDCS-60000062.translation: Marcus Remmius, son of Marcus, from the tribe Andreas.

EDCS-60000063.translation: torenti Claro, son of Prisca Su[---]
EDCS-60000063.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a dedication or funerary text mentioningarentus Claro, son of Prisca.

EDCS-60000064.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name of a freedman, Chresimus, of his patron Titus.

EDCS-60000067.translation: To Tattia Procula, daughter of Spurius, and to Servolus, freedman of Publius Valerius, her son-in-law.
EDCS-60000067.summary: This inscription dedicates the monument to Tattia Procula and her son-in-law Servolus, a freedman.

EDCS-60300076.translation: By decree of the decurions, he gave 16,000 sesterces to the republic of Altinum, in such a way that the baths of Sergius and Putinus, repaired with 800,000 sesterces, would be in use by the municipals, and another 400,000 sesterces, so that from their income they would be heated, and 200,000 sesterces for the perpetual protection of the same, and likewise 200,000 sesterces, so that from their interest, on the 10th day of July, on his birthday, and on the 10th day of July, on the birthday of Petronia Magna, his mother, and on the 16th day of December, on the birthday of Lucius Fabius Stellatina Amminianus, his father, the decurions and Augustales and seviri would receive sportulas.
EDCS-60300076.summary: This inscription records a substantial endowment by an unnamed individual for the upkeep of public baths and the provision of gifts to local officials in Altinum, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-60500001.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a dedication or funerary text mentioning Faustina, daughter of Pau[---].

EDCS-60600013.translation: Quintus Varius Naeulus, freedman of Aebutius, made this while alive for his grandfather Sextus Varius Valens, son of Lucius; and for his father Manius Aebutius Valerianus Valens, formerly prefect with judicial authority; and for his mother Numeria, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-60600013.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Quintus Varius Naeulus for his deceased relatives, including his grandfather, father, and mother.

EDCS-60600014.text_edition: \n Natali CCXXV Aulus Publicius Felix votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-60600014.translation: On his 225th birthday, Aulus Publicius Felix willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-60600014.summary: This is a dedication recording the fulfillment of a vow by Aulus Publicius Felix on his birthday.

EDCS-60600015.translation: Quintus Satrius Severus made this while alive for his patron Quintus Satrius Laetus, freedman of Lucius Quintus, and for himself.
EDCS-60600015.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Quintus Satrius Severus for his patron and himself.

EDCS-60600016.translation: Verania Severa, Livia Iesatria. The cup made for her. Daughter with the permission of Severa Tur Veraniae.
EDCS-60600016.summary: This inscription indicates a cup was made for Verania Severa, possibly by her daughter, with permission from Severa Tur Veraniae.

EDCS-60600017.translation: Burial place of Mani Cl[---]nicus, procurator, 22 feet in front, 41 feet behind.
EDCS-60600017.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Mani Cl[---]nicus, a procurator, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-60600046.summary: This is a dedication to Chreste Laecania, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-60800043.translation: Quintus Tita Maxsim willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Fontus.
EDCS-60800043.summary: This inscription records a votive offering fulfilled by Quintus Tita Maxsim to the deity Fontus.

EDCS-60800044.translation: Poblicius Statutus willingly fulfilled his vow to Fontus.
