EDCS-60800044.summary: This inscription records a votive offering fulfilled by Poblicius Statutus to the deity Fontus.

EDCS-61200065.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or an ownership mark, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61200094.summary: This inscription identifies Maurus as a deacon, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-61300089.summary: This inscription records the name of Caius Corelius Celer, likely a freedman or resident of Frontiniana, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61600001.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Petronia Successa for her most beloved husband Gaius Messius Felix.
EDCS-61600001.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Petronia Successa dedicated to her husband.

EDCS-61600087.summary: This inscription is an ownership mark or a dedication belonging to Quintus Granius Priscus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61600089.translation: Lucius, son of Lucius, [son of] Marcus.
EDCS-61600089.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary or commemorative inscription providing a Roman-style patronymic, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61600090.summary: This inscription is an ownership mark or a dedication belonging to Titus Regius Diadumenus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61600091.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary marker for Marcus Laetorius.

EDCS-61600092.translation: Gaius Poblicius, freedman of the municipium of Opitergium, Germanus, made this while alive for himself and for Secunda.
EDCS-61600092.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by Gaius Poblicius, a freedman of the municipium of Opitergium, for himself and his wife Secunda, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61600093.translation: Lucius Terentius [---] and [---] Terentius, son of Marcus, and Marcus Terentius [---] and Gaius Terentius, son of Lucius, set up [---] Tua and the son (?) Terentia (?).
EDCS-61600093.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription possibly recording the erection of a monument by multiple members of the Terentia family.

EDCS-61600094.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary marker, mentioning at least one individual named Gaius.

EDCS-61600095.translation: Lucius Sinconius, son of Publius, by his will.
EDCS-61600095.summary: An inscription indicating that Lucius Sinconius, son of Publius, made a disposition by his will.

EDCS-61600096.translation: [Gaius] Valerius, freedman of Gaius, [---] alive for himself [---].
EDCS-61600096.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, indicating that Gaius Valerius, a freedman, set it up for himself while alive.

EDCS-61600099.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Titus Messius, possibly with a cognomen.

EDCS-61600100.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Titus Messius, possibly with a cognomen.

EDCS-61600102.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Laekanius Felix, possibly a dedication or ownership mark, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61600105.summary: This inscription likely records the name of a person, Lucius Pomponius, possibly as a dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-61600108.summary: This inscription records the name of Titus Helvius Basila, likely a funerary or dedicatory epigraph.

EDCS-61600109.summary: This inscription fragment names Publius Aufidius, suggesting a dedication or ownership.

EDCS-61600115.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Titus Messius, possibly with a cognomen.

EDCS-61600129.translation: Balenti lived for 3 years, buried on the Nones (?).
EDCS-61600129.summary: This inscription fragment records the lifespan and burial date of a person named Balenti.

EDCS-61600131.summary: This inscription records the full name and filiation of Lucius Neppiacus.

EDCS-61600132.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Neppiacus, possibly as a funerary or dedicatory epigraph.

EDCS-61600133.translation: Lucius Neppiacus, son of Lucius; Titus Neppiacus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-61600133.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Lucius Neppiacus and Titus Neppiacus, identified by their patronymic, likely from a tomb or a shared monument.

EDCS-61600134.summary: This inscription records the name Gaius Fulvius Scorpio.

EDCS-61600135.summary: This inscription records the name of Quintus Clodius Ambrosius, possibly as a dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-61600137.summary: This inscription records Potens Aufidius in a place called the Mattonianum, possibly a funerary context or a property designation.

EDCS-61600138.summary: This inscription records the name of Satria Didyme, possibly as a dedication or ownership marker, likely from a tomb.

EDCS-61600317.text_edition: \n Aurelio Marco viro perfectissimo Marcus Nonius Mercusenus vir p(erfectissimus) amico incomparabili\n
EDCS-61600317.translation: To Aurelius Marcus, most perfect man. Marcus Nonius Mercusenus, a most perfect man, to his incomparable friend.
EDCS-61600317.summary: A dedication from Marcus Nonius Mercusenus to his friend Aurelius Marcus, likely a high-ranking official.

EDCS-61700634.summary: This inscription records the full name and filiation of Arria Fusca, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-61700641.translation: Satrius, son of Satrius; Satrius, son of Satrius; Satrius, son of Satrius; Satrius, son of Satrius
EDCS-61700641.summary: This inscription lists multiple individuals named Satrius, all identified by their patronymic, suggesting a family tomb or monument.

EDCS-61700642.summary: This inscription records the name of Titus Dellius Serenus, possibly as a dedication or ownership marker, likely from a tomb.

EDCS-61700645.translation: Caecilia Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius, her living husband, made this for herself and for Caecilia Musa, freedwoman, and Caecilia Thyche, freedwoman, and Lucius Veronius Sentinus.
EDCS-61700645.summary: This funerary inscription records Caecilia Secunda, a freedwoman, dedicating a monument for herself, other freedwomen, and Lucius Veronius Sentinus, likely her husband or patron.

EDCS-61700646.translation: Nae Valerius Egialus [erected this] for his incomparable and most faithful wife, who lived 32 years, 5 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-61700646.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman, likely from the Roman Imperial period, commemorating her life span.

EDCS-61900008.translation: I, Timelis, by precarious tenure from Lucius Caius Metius, son of Aulus Brixelius, son of Manius Cassius, and Lucius Caius Ollius, son of Titus.
EDCS-61900008.summary: This inscription pertains to a precarium grant, detailing the names of the grantor (Timelis) and the beneficiaries or intermediate parties, possibly related to land tenure.

EDCS-62000079.summary: This is a short dedication by a reader, likely marking a contribution to a building or project, possibly of early Christian origin.

EDCS-62000086.translation: Honoratus made 60 feet [of this] with his people.
EDCS-62000086.summary: This inscription records the contribution of 60 feet of work or material by Honoratus and his group, possibly for a public work or building.

EDCS-62000087.translation: Syrus the deacon tessellated this place with his people and Iul with his people, 50 feet.
EDCS-62000087.summary: This inscription indicates that Syrus, a deacon, along with Iul and their respective groups, completed 50 feet of mosaic work, likely in a church or public building, probably from the later Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-62000088.summary: This is a simple dedication by Faustinina, potentially for a building or offering, dating likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-62000113.translation: Malchus made 33 feet for [the fulfillment of] a vow.
EDCS-62000113.summary: This inscription, in Greek, records Malchus fulfilling a vow by completing 33 feet of work, likely a dedication of a section of a building or structure.

EDCS-62300962.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gnostus, sweetest parent, who lived 3 years [---].
EDCS-62300962.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Gnostus, honoring him as a very dear parent figure, possibly indicating an adoption or a term of endearment, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-62300964.translation: To the divine shades. The heir [dedicated this] to Marcus Stardius Sextianus and Stardius Sabinianus, [his sons, well-deserving.]
EDCS-62300964.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by an heir for two men, Marcus Stardius Sextianus and Stardius Sabinianus, suggesting a family tomb.

EDCS-62300968.translation: Burial place of Sevia Tyrannis. In front 20 feet, behind 20 feet.
EDCS-62300968.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Sevia Tyrannis, specifying its dimensions in feet.

EDCS-62501255.translation: Titus Vettius, son of Titus, 5 years old. Farewell.
EDCS-62501255.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Titus Vettius, who died at the age of five, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-62501256.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph or dedication, possibly for a woman named Valgia, daughter of Caius V, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-62501262.translation: From Cytirinus / From Ennius / Statia, mother [erected this].
EDCS-62501262.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, possibly indicating that Statia, the mother, erected monuments or memorials for Cytirinus and Ennius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-62501265.translation: Potens, son of Aufidius, in the territory of Mato.
EDCS-62501265.summary: This is a boundary stone marking the territory of Mato with the name of Potens, son of Aufidius.

EDCS-62800043.summary: This inscription records the name Publius Cornelius Rufus and a weight of 157 pounds, possibly related to a funerary monument or a record of goods.

EDCS-62800044.translation: Sacred to the goddess Diana. By Valerius Severus.
EDCS-62800044.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Diana made by Valerius Severus.

EDCS-62900325.translation: Lucius Terentius, son of Titus, a member of the duoviri iure dicundo, ordered this monument to be made. With that money, by decree of the decurions, the roads were paved from Annia to the wall and beyond the crypt to the theater.
EDCS-62900325.summary: This inscription records the paving of roads by order of Lucius Terentius, a local magistrate, funded by a decree of the town council.

EDCS-64100225.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantinus, the Greatest, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, and the invincible Augusti.
EDCS-64100225.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine I and other Augusti, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-64100226.translation: To our lords Flavius Claudius Constantinus and Flavius Iulius Constantius, most noble Caesars, sons of our lord Constantine the Greatest, the Victorious Augustus, grandsons of the divine Constantius, princes of youth.
EDCS-64100226.summary: This inscription dedicates honors to the Caesars Constantinus and Constantius, sons and grandsons of emperors, from the Constantinian dynasty.

EDCS-64100228.translation: To our lord Flavius Iovianus, the Victorious and Triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the republic. To our lord Flavius Iovianus, the Triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the republic. To our lords Valentinianus, Theodosius, and Arcadius, perpetual [emperors], born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-64100228.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Iovianus, Valentinianus, Theodosius, and Arcadius, highlighting their roles as protectors of the republic, likely from the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-64100232.translation: To the Emperor Caesar N.T. always Augustus and Valerius Valerius, most noble Caesar. To our lords Flavius Iulius Crispus and Valerius Licinianus Licinius and Flavius Claudius Constantinus, most noble Caesars. To our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Valens, divine brothers and always Augusti, devoted Venetia erected [this].
EDCS-64100232.summary: This extensive dedication from Venetia honors multiple emperors and caesars, including Crispus, Licinius, Constantine, Valentinianus, and Valens, likely from the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-64100234.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to be a dedication or mention of Aelia Faustina, possibly funerary.

EDCS-64100237.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying 'Felix the bishop', possibly found on a tomb or a dedicatory object.

EDCS-64100239.translation: To Quintus Carminius Asicianus, son of Quintus, of the Scaptia tribe, for his merits, because [he donated?] of the college of fullers [of Altinum] with a base [he restored?] 13,000 sesterces and gave 6,000 sesterces. [---] has made [---] for [---] a certain [---] to [---] them. [---]. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-64100239.summary: This inscription records a donation and restoration project by Quintus Carminius Asicianus, likely for a collegium, with a plot of land granted by the decurions.

EDCS-64100240.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, 12 miles.
EDCS-64100240.summary: This inscription records a distance of 12 miles to Emperor Maxentius, likely a milestone from the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-64100243.translation: This oratory to blessed Mary, mother of the Lord, Gregory, a distinguished official, built and dedicated it in the name of Christ from the foundations.
EDCS-64100243.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of an oratory to the Virgin Mary by a high-ranking official named Gregory, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-64100244.translation: In the name of the Lord, here rests in peace Iohannes the lector.
EDCS-64100244.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Iohannes, a lector, and placing him at rest in the Lord.

EDCS-64100245.translation: Here lies in peace Ansult the innocent.
EDCS-64100245.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Ansult.

EDCS-64100246.translation: To the divine shades. For Furia Bassilla, daughter of Quintus. Quintus Furius Eumenes [dedicated this].
EDCS-64100246.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Furia Bassilla, daughter of Quintus, set up by Quintus Furius Eumenes.

EDCS-64100248.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely mentioning two individuals, Primi[us?] and Clodia Utilis, possibly in a funerary or dedicatory context.

EDCS-64100249.translation: For the health of Lucius Claudius Ennianus, Publius Claudius Secundinus, his father, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-64100249.summary: This is a votive inscription where Publius Claudius Secundinus fulfilled a vow for the well-being of Lucius Claudius Ennianus.

EDCS-64300087.translation: To the underworld father, to the divine shades. Urbanus, of the twentieth liberty (i.e., freedman of the twentieth lictor's cohort).
EDCS-64300087.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Urbanus, identifying him as a freedman associated with the twentieth cohort.

EDCS-64400001.translation: Burial place of Caius Helvius Parrion and Asinia Ides. In front 24 feet, behind 28 feet.
EDCS-64400001.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot for Caius Helvius Parrion and Asinia Ides, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-64400007.translation: Aelia Tertia(?), daughter of Publius, in front 30 feet, to the rear [perhaps behind?] 58 feet.
EDCS-64400007.summary: This inscription, likely from a tomb, records the dimensions of a plot belonging to Aelia Tertia. It dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400008.translation: Burial place of Titus V[---] Justus. In front 26 feet, to the rear 27 feet.
EDCS-64400008.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, specifying its dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400010.translation: Sextilius Clemens for himself and his family, for Axia Procula, his wife, and for his freedmen and freedwomen. In front 35 feet, in the rear 45 feet.
EDCS-64400010.summary: This is an funerary epitaph for Sextilius Clemens, his wife Axia Procula, and their freedpersons, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-64400011.translation: Gaius Remmius Festus made this, while alive, as a burial place for himself and his family. In front 24 feet, to the rear 45 feet.
EDCS-64400011.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot made by Gaius Remmius Festus for himself and his family, with dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400012.translation: Burial place of Aulus P. C. In front 20 feet, to the rear 20 feet.
EDCS-64400012.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, specifying its dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400015.translation: Gaius Laberius Iucundus, freedman of Gaius, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Laberia Melissa, a freedwoman.
EDCS-64400015.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Laberius Iucundus's posthumous arrangement for his burial plot and that of his freedwoman, specifying dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400017.translation: Publius Fabius(?), freedman of Publius, in front 15 feet, to the rear 28 feet.
EDCS-64400017.summary: This inscription, likely from a tomb, records the dimensions of a plot belonging to Publius Fabius(?). It dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400019.translation: [---] and to Gaius Blo[---] Campanius. In front 25[1?] feet, in the field 40 feet.
EDCS-64400019.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records land division or property boundaries, possibly related to a burial plot, with dimensions, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400020.translation: For Cornelia Prima, freedwoman of Gaius. In front 20 feet, to the rear 40 feet.
EDCS-64400020.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot dedicated to Cornelia Prima, specifying its dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400108.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Gaius Viccius, son of Marcus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400268.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription providing a name and filiation.

EDCS-64400271.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication to Augustus.

EDCS-64400355.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription providing a name and filiation.

EDCS-64400357.translation: ...given by himself, Lucius V. Pr. gave and placed this gift.
EDCS-64400357.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a dedication or offering by Lucius V. Pr., with the land presumably donated by himself.

EDCS-64400360.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, 7 miles. Our Lords Julius Crispus and Licinianus Licinius the younger and Claudius Constantinus, most noble Caesars, 7 miles.
EDCS-64400360.summary: This inscription records a dedication and milestone, likely commemorating a road or construction project associated with Emperor Maxentius and the Caesars of the Tetrarchy, dating to the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-64400387.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Constantius, most noble Caesar. Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor, Augusti, (born) for the good of the state.
EDCS-64400387.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Constantius, Magnus Maximus, and Victor, likely erected by the latter two as a joint declaration of their imperial status and duty, dating to the period when Magnus Maximus and Victor were co-emperors, possibly in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-64400420.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription containing possible personal names.

EDCS-64400422.translation: To Gaius Attius(?), ... duovir, and Lu...
EDCS-64400422.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning a dedication to Gaius Attius(?), who held the office of duovir.

EDCS-64400424.translation: ...to Attia Festa, his sister, Gaius Attius Priscinianus, son of Gaius, of the Pob(lilia) tribe.
EDCS-64400424.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a tomb to Attia Festa by her brother Gaius Attius Priscinianus.

EDCS-64400425.translation: Lucius Decimius Policarpus made this while alive for his excellent wife Superata.
EDCS-64400425.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Decimius Policarpus for his wife Superata.

EDCS-64400426.translation: Atia Cinna made (this) for herself and for Marcus Coelius Cinna while alive. In front 20 feet, behind 30 feet.
EDCS-64400426.summary: This is an epitaph for Atia Cinna, who set it up for herself and Marcus Coelius Cinna, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400436.translation: In memory of Iunia Varilla, daughter of Publius, and of her parents, and of her brother Publius Iunius Severianus; Abudius Verus made (this) at the request in the will of Varilla, his wife, daughter of Lucius, and of Publius Iunius Novatus.
EDCS-64400436.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Abudius Verus in memory of his wife Varilla, her parents, and her brother.

EDCS-64400439.translation: The remains of Sextus Lollius Numeri son, of the Romilia tribe, standard-bearer of the 11th legion.
EDCS-64400439.summary: This inscription identifies the remains of Sextus Lollius Numeri, a standard-bearer in the 11th legion, indicating his tribal affiliation and military service, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400440.translation: [...]dus, slave of [...] of Tergestinum, lies here.
EDCS-64400440.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for a slave named Dus, possibly from Tergestinum, indicating burial and including illegible text, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400462.text_edition: \n Locus sepulturae Quinti D L in fronte pedes XXIX retro pedes XXX\n
EDCS-64400462.translation: Burial place of Quintus D L, in front 29 feet, behind 30 feet.
EDCS-64400462.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Quintus D L, specifying the dimensions of the land, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400471.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription possibly starting with the name Titus, with the rest illegible, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400472.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription possibly starting with the name Gaius, with the rest illegible, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400473.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a person, possibly named Pra Coelia Gratia, who made something while alive, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400474.summary: This inscription refers to Copio, a freedman of Cnaeus, with the rest of the text missing, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400477.text_edition: \n Luci G F in fronte pedes XXI semis retro pedes IX\n
EDCS-64400477.translation: Lucius G F, in front 21 and a half feet, behind 9 feet.
EDCS-64400477.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot belonging to Lucius G F, specifying its dimensions, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400480.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a personal name, possibly Gaius.

EDCS-64400500.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription possibly containing a name and an initial.

EDCS-64500123.summary: This inscription likely marks a territorial boundary or administrative division within the territory of Caere.

EDCS-64500195.translation: Satria Quarta, daughter of Publius Sempronius, dedicated this gift to Apollo and Victoria.
EDCS-64500195.summary: This is a dedication of a gift by Satria Quarta to the gods Apollo and Victoria.

EDCS-64500421.translation: Place of Hilary, freedman of Publius Postumius, in front 14 feet, in the field 32 feet.
EDCS-64500421.summary: This funerary boundary stone marks a plot of land measuring 14 feet in the front and 32 feet in the field, belonging to Hilary, freedman of Publius Postumius.

EDCS-64500480.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Diomedes impendio suo posuit\n
EDCS-64500480.translation: Gaius Julius Diomedes erected this at his own expense.
EDCS-64500480.summary: This inscription records Gaius Julius Diomedes erecting a monument at his own expense.

EDCS-64500481.translation: Maximinus, son of Aurelianus, who lived 22 years and 10 months, rests here in peace.
EDCS-64500481.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Maximinus, son of Aurelianus, at the age of 22 years and 10 months.

EDCS-64500504.text_edition: \n Caio Attio Cai filio Poblilia Pollioni IIIIviro iure dicundo\n
EDCS-64500504.translation: To Gaius Attius, son of Gaius, of the Poblilia tribe, aedile with judicial power.
EDCS-64500504.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Attius, a local magistrate (quattuorvir iure dicundo) from the Poblilia tribe.

EDCS-64500505.translation: To Claudia Secunda, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-64500505.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Claudia Secunda, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-64500506.translation: To Marcus Laetorius, son of Marcus, his brother.
EDCS-64500506.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Laetorius, son of Marcus, by his brother.

EDCS-64500507.translation: To Marcus Magius Urbanus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-64500507.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Magius Urbanus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-64500508.text_edition: \n Publio Valerio Publi filio Publilia Nasoni IIIIviro iure dicundo IIIIviro aedilicia potestate publice decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-64500508.translation: To Publius Valerius, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, aedile with judicial power, aedile with aedilic power, by public decree of the decurions.
EDCS-64500508.summary: This inscription honors Publius Valerius, son of Publius, a local magistrate (quattuorvir iure dicundo and aedile) from the Poblilia tribe, recognized by a decree of the town council.

EDCS-64500509.translation: Sextus Clodius, son of Quintus, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-64500509.summary: This inscription records the name Sextus Clodius, son of Quintus, belonging to the Poblilia tribe.

EDCS-64500510.text_edition: \n Quinto Clodio Quinti filio Postumo Cornelia Luci filia Polla mater\n
EDCS-64500510.translation: To Quinto Postumo, son of Quinto, from his mother Polla, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-64500510.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her son.

EDCS-64500511.text_edition: \n Fabiae Quinti filiae Marcia Luci filiae Quarta testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-64500511.translation: Marcia Quarta, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made in her will for Fabia, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-64500511.summary: This funerary epitaph, set up by will, commemorates Fabia.

EDCS-64500512.text_edition: \n Titus Iuventius Quinti filius Milo testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-64500512.translation: Titus Iuventius Milo, son of Quintus, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-64500512.summary: This funerary epitaph, set up by will, commemorates Titus Iuventius Milo.

EDCS-64500513.translation: Caius Laetorius Tiro, son of Caius.
EDCS-64500513.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Laetorius Tiro.

EDCS-64500514.text_edition: \n Marco Valerio Marci filio Poblilia Ciloni Publius Valerius Marci filius Publilia Naso fratri\n
EDCS-64500514.translation: To Marco Valerio Naso, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, from his brother Publius Valerius Fronto, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-64500514.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Marcus Valerius Naso and was erected by his brother.

EDCS-64500515.text_edition: \n Marci filiae Anui o Publi Fanni\n
EDCS-64500515.translation: To Anuia, daughter of Marcus, from Publius Fannius.
EDCS-64500515.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to Anuia by Publius Fannius.

EDCS-64500516.text_edition: \n Volesiae Cai filiae uxori Publius Cutius Bibulus\n
EDCS-64500516.translation: To Volesia, wife of Caius, from Publius Cutius Bibulus.
EDCS-64500516.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to Volesia by her husband.

EDCS-64500565.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly part of a funerary epitaph, with an incomplete name and patronymic.

EDCS-64600119.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph stating that Carisius Tertius is buried in this location.

EDCS-64600120.translation: The place of the monument for Quintus Vassidius Primus and his descendants, 18 feet in front and 21 feet in the field.
EDCS-64600120.summary: This is a boundary marker for a family burial plot, indicating its dimensions.

EDCS-64600125.translation: Herennia Citunya placed (this) for her husband, who was called Marcus Mammius Mucro, and for her mother Herennia Rufilia, and for Mammius Repentinus.
EDCS-64600125.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Herennia Citunya for her husband Marcus Mammius Mucro, her mother Herennia Rufilia, and Mammius Repentinus.

EDCS-64600201.translation: Caius Hostilius Hilario, freedman of Caius, made this for Hostilia Lepida, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-64600201.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hostilia Lepida, set up by her husband.

EDCS-64600217.translation: [---]dents, son of Quintus, of the Publilia tribe, ordered (this) to be made by his will for himself and for Quintus Tossius, son of Quintus, his father, and for Catia, daughter of Catius, his mother, and for [---]Tossius, son of Quintus, his brother.
EDCS-64600217.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by will by Pudens for himself, his parents, and his brother.

EDCS-64600218.translation: To our lord Flavius Iovianus, victorious and triumphant, always Augustus.
EDCS-64600218.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Jovian, acknowledging his military victories and imperial title.

EDCS-64600222.translation: Licinia Maximilla willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-64600222.summary: This is a votive inscription by Licinia Maximilla.

EDCS-64600233.translation: To Aulus Gavillius Gallio, freedman of Aulus, a member of the college of six, and to Aulus Gavillius Antiochus, freedman of Aulus, a member of the college of six.
EDCS-64600233.summary: This is a dedication to two men, Aulus Gavillius Gallio and Aulus Gavillius Antiochus, both freedmen and members of a college of six, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-64600264.translation: To Soteris, my best husband, and to Fortunata (?), my darling (?).
EDCS-64600264.summary: This is a dedication to a husband and possibly a beloved woman, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-64600265.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Putinia Maxuma, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-64600266.translation: To Curtia Lupa, by Curtius Hylianus, her patron, a soldier of the Legio X Fretensis.
EDCS-64600266.summary: This is a dedication to Curtia Lupa by her patron, Curtius Hylianus, a soldier of the Legio X Fretensis, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-64600267.translation: [---] Manilius [---] to [---] Manilius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-64600267.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to be a dedication or memorial, mentioning two individuals named Manilius, possibly father and son.

EDCS-64700382.translation: To our lord Flavius Jovian, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus.
EDCS-64700382.summary: This is an acclamation or dedication to the Roman Emperor Flavius Jovian, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-64700391.translation: To our lord Emperor Caesar Flavius Gratianus, pious and fortunate, ever Augustus, son of the deified Valentinian Augustus. The city [made this] 8 miles.
EDCS-64700391.summary: This inscription dedicates a road of 8 miles to Emperor Gratian, son of Valentinian I, likely from the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-64700394.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars, three times.
EDCS-64700394.summary: This inscription records the joint rule of the Tetrarchs, including Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius, likely marking a public building or monument.

EDCS-64700396.translation: To our lord Flavius Jovian, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-64700396.summary: This is an acclamation or dedication to the Roman Emperor Flavius Jovian, likely from the 4th century CE, emphasizing his suitability to rule.

EDCS-64800308.translation: To Duronia, freedwoman of Titus Certus, for 11 feet in front and 15 feet in back; for herself and her family.
EDCS-64800308.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Duronia, specifying the dimensions of her burial plot.

EDCS-64800309.translation: From Lucius, son of G., 21 feet in front, a dextans [one-tenth less than a full measure] behind.
EDCS-64800309.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker, recording measurements of land belonging to Lucius, son of G., likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-64800310.translation: The site of the monument of Publius Staumius Primigenius, for 28 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-64800310.summary: This inscription marks the boundaries of a burial plot belonging to Publius Staumius Primigenius.

EDCS-64800326.translation: Burial plot of Lucius Porcius, son of Caius, 35 feet in front and [width in] the rear.
EDCS-64800326.summary: This is a funerary boundary marker specifying the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Porcius.

EDCS-64800327.translation: Burial plot of Marcus Ce[---], 24 feet in front and [width in] the rear.
EDCS-64800327.summary: This is a funerary boundary marker indicating the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Marcus Ce[---].

EDCS-64800347.translation: From the house of the 11th Claudian Legion, Lucius Varius and Beniviva [recorded dimensions of a plot?].
EDCS-64800347.summary: This inscription likely records dimensions related to property or a burial plot, possibly associated with the 11th Claudian Legion.

EDCS-64800394.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Depius Irenicus made this while alive for his well-deserving wife, Depia Melibe, and for himself.
EDCS-64800394.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Depius Irenicus for his wife and himself.

EDCS-64800395.translation: Marcus Cassius Licinus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-64800395.summary: This is a tombstone or epitaph identifying Marcus Cassius Licinus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-64800400.translation: [---] to Nigrus, son of Lucius, son of [---]; his sons Valeria [and? ---].
EDCS-64800400.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph fragment, possibly for Nigrus, son of Lucius, with a mention of his sons and Valeria.

EDCS-64800401.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucretia Ianuaria, who lived 34 years, 3 months, and 18 days. Senecius Rabutius Maximus to his well-deserving wife, who lived with me 21 years, 4 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-64800401.summary: This epitaph records the death and life spans of Lucretia Ianuaria and her husband, Senecius Rabutius Maximus, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800402.translation: Here lies Inn(e)ofytus Victornianus, who lived 2 years and 11 months.
EDCS-64800402.summary: This is a tombstone for a child named Inn(e)ofytus Victornianus, indicating his age at death.

EDCS-64800403.translation: Gaius Metellus Ianuarius made this while alive.
EDCS-64800403.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Gaius Metellus Ianuarius for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-64800484.translation: To the departed spirits. Saturia Pezusa [sets this up] for her parents, Saturus, son of Valerius, and Antonia Aelianae.
EDCS-64800484.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Saturia Pezusa to her parents.

EDCS-64800505.translation: Gaius Gellius, son of Quintus, of the Papiria tribe, as aedile, for his father Quintus Gellius Antiochus, freedman of Quintus, and for his wife Caesiana Secunda, daughter of Tiberius.
EDCS-64800505.summary: This is an epitaph for a father and his wife, set up by their son Gaius Gellius who held the office of aedile.

EDCS-64900337.translation: Titus Vessonius, son of Publius, a veteran, set this up for his father, Publius Vessonius Sulla, and for his mother, Romniacae Maxima, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-64900337.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Titus Vessonius for his parents.

EDCS-64900358.translation: Turrania Stratonis for herself and for her excellent husband Gaius Samicius Firmus, six-man official of the Claudiali maiores college of dendrophores and of the college of cento-makers, and for her foster-father and [daughter?] Samicia Viria[---].
EDCS-64900358.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Turrania Stratonis for her husband Gaius Samicius Firmus, mentioning his official roles in several collegia, and also for other family members.

EDCS-64900381.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to contain personal names, possibly part of an epitaph or dedication.

EDCS-64900525.translation: Quintus Teidius Sodala, freedman of Quintus, and Teidia Hilara, freedwoman, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-64900525.summary: This is an epitaph for Quintus Teidius Sodala and Teidia Hilara, set up by them during their lifetime.

EDCS-64900526.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, with partially preserved names.

EDCS-64900538.translation: To the god Melisokos, Silvester having offered sacrifice.
EDCS-64900538.summary: This is a dedication to the god Melisokos by Silvester, likely a pagan inscription.

EDCS-64900853.translation: Gaius Calvisius Catullus, son of Gaius, made this for himself and for Theminis, his freedwoman.
EDCS-64900853.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Gaius Calvisius Catullus for himself and his freedwoman.

EDCS-64900854.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription containing a Roman praenomen and nomen, likely part of a name or dedication.

EDCS-64900879.translation: Lucius Volcacius Stephanus, freedman of Lucius, [for] himself and Saga[...]
EDCS-64900879.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication or dedication to family by Lucius Volcacius Stephanus, a freedman.

EDCS-64900880.translation: Traveler, stop and greet Phoebe, the servant of Manilius, son of Titus; she brought worthy rewards for services rendered.
EDCS-64900880.summary: This is a tombstone that describes the virtues of a servant named Phoebe.

EDCS-64900882.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Lucretius Agamemnon, friend and heir, [placed this] for Titus Sacidius Iustus.
EDCS-64900882.summary: A funerary dedication by a friend and heir to the deceased, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-64900883.translation: To Hermes, freedman, and a member of the college of Augustales.
EDCS-64900883.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Hermes, a freedman and a member of the prominent college of Augustales.

EDCS-64900884.translation: To the ancestral spirits. Ecinia Maxima, daughter of Marcus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-64900884.summary: A votive dedication by a woman named Ecinia Maxima to the ancestral spirits, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-64900885.translation: Murranus made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-64900885.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Murranus made the monument for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-64900888.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name of Gaius Marsus.

EDCS-64901117.translation: Lucius Gra[---] Quintianus [---] of the [---] cohort lived for 35 years, served for 7 years, [---]
EDCS-64901117.summary: A fragmented military funerary inscription recording the name, service, and lifespan of a soldier, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65000033.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a parent's dedication to their son, Lucius.

EDCS-65200049.translation: Site of the monument of Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200049.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200050.translation: Site of the monument of Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200050.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200051.translation: Site of the monument of Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200051.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for Marcus Papinius Rhetoricus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200052.summary: This inscription records a measurement of 16 square feet attributed to Mettius Cirrus, possibly related to land or building.

EDCS-65200053.translation: The plot of the freedmen and freedwomen of Gnaeus Albius Murranus.
EDCS-65200053.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot designated for the freedmen and freedwomen of Gnaeus Albius Murranus.

EDCS-65200054.translation: Site of the Apponii, Primi and Blandi: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200054.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for the Apponii family, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200055.translation: Site of the monument of Quintus Aristus: 16 feet in front, 32 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200055.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for Quintus Aristus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200059.translation: Site of the monument of Carfenius Fortunatus: 15 feet in front, 32 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200059.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for Carfenius Fortunatus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200060.translation: Site of the monument of Aulus Livius Euhodus: 20 feet in front, 40 feet in the rear.
EDCS-65200060.summary: A property marker indicating the burial plot size for Aulus Livius Euhodus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65200064.translation: The place of the monument of Caius Titius Primus, son of Caius, and of Titia Ampliata, freedwoman of Caius; 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the ground.
EDCS-65200064.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Caius Titius Primus and Titia Ampliata.

EDCS-65200126.summary: This is a dedication to Fortunatus, identified as the protector of a woman named Secundina.

EDCS-65300211.translation: Publius Volumnius, son of Caius, and Iemiaria Maxima, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-65300211.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, likely a couple.

EDCS-65300234.summary: This is a dedication to a person named Lucius, son of [---].

EDCS-65800132.summary: This inscription seems to record a dedication or a note about goods for someone named Marion.

EDCS-65900036.translation: Publius Caetronius Verecundus, of the II viri iure dicundo, erected this for himself and for his wife Tutinia Rufa, daughter of Rufus; and for his son Publius Caetronius Exoratus, son of Caius; and for his wife Dellia Secunda, daughter of Dellius; and for his wife Ducellia Sabina, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-65900036.summary: This funerary inscription was erected by Publius Caetronius Verecundus for himself and several family members, including his wives and sons.

EDCS-66200015.translation: To Publius Terentius, son of Caius, and Lucius Terentius, son of Caius, and their mother, and to Caius Moenius Cilo, freedman of Caius; Secunda Terentia, daughter of Caius, made (this) for herself, her brothers, and her husband.
EDCS-66200015.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Secunda Terentia for her family members, including her parents and husband.

EDCS-67400245.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ituria Tigris, mother, to her most dutiful son Lucius Iturius Corinthus, who served as II vir iure dicundo in Tergeste.
EDCS-67400245.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a mother for her son, a magistrate in Tergeste.

EDCS-67400256.summary: This inscription simply records the name Lucius Tarquitius.

EDCS-67400260.translation: Gaius Plinius Secundus of Verona, to Rhodius, for good services rendered to the mill of the municipality, by the authority of the most holy lord.
EDCS-67400260.summary: This inscription records a commendation or award given to Rhodius for his service related to a mill, possibly by Gaius Plinius Secundus.

EDCS-67500096.translation: C. Plinius Veronensis of his histories, dedicates this for the memory of all, and also T. C. XXXV, a macer.
EDCS-67500096.summary: This inscription records the dedication of something related to the histories of Plinius of Verona, possibly a monument or collection.

EDCS-67500097.translation: To his most beloved parents, he willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-67500097.summary: This inscription is a votive offering or dedication made by a person to their parents.

EDCS-67600011.summary: This inscription simply records the name Titus Ulgeus Cherinthus.

EDCS-67600012.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Domitius Celeris, possibly as a dedicant or the owner of the monument.

EDCS-67600021.summary: This inscription records the name of Caius Hosidius Demetrius, likely as a dedicant or the subject of the monument.

EDCS-67900804.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of a dedicatee.

EDCS-67900814.translation: To Lucius Horatius Longus, tribune of the II cohort of vigiles, a duovir with judicial power; Caius Publicius Anteros and Lucius Publicius Perennis made (this) for their patron.
EDCS-67900814.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Caius Publicius Anteros and Lucius Publicius Perennis to their patron, Lucius Horatius Longus, who held military and administrative positions.

EDCS-68100001.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Clodius Quirinalis, possibly as a dedicant or the recipient of the monument.

EDCS-68100004.summary: This inscription records the name of Calvia Vrispinilla, likely as a dedicant or the subject of the monument.

EDCS-68100005.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Iturius Sabinus, possibly as a dedicant or the owner of the monument.

EDCS-68100009.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Clodius Quirinalis, possibly as a dedicant or the recipient of the monument.

EDCS-68100012.summary: This inscription records the name of Calvia Crispinilla, likely as a dedicant or the subject of the monument.

EDCS-68100013.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Iturius Sabinus, possibly as a dedicant or the owner of the monument.

EDCS-68100015.translation: Of Marcus Poblicius, son of Decimus
EDCS-68100015.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Poblicius, son of Decimus, likely as a dedicant or the subject of the monument.

EDCS-68100016.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Stasius Justus, possibly as a dedicant or the owner of the monument.

EDCS-68100017.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Luci Stati Iustus.

EDCS-68800013.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal statement or epitaph, possibly identifying the deceased as 'Paris'.

EDCS-69000082.translation: Augustum Carsadium Secundum Caupunum I fix.
EDCS-69000082.summary: This inscription likely records the setting up of a boundary marker or a sign, possibly related to a property or business.

EDCS-69200226.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription that records the name of Caius Catronius.

EDCS-69200227.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely indicates ownership or a dedication related to Tiberius Veturius.

EDCS-69200228.translation: To Secundus, son of Marcus Horatius.
EDCS-69200228.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication to Secundus.

EDCS-69200229.summary: This inscription likely refers to a place or person, possibly related to Ostia and a Samnite individual or group.

EDCS-69200230.translation: To the spirit of Publius Pulius Lucretis.
EDCS-69200230.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Pulius Lucretis, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-69200231.translation: Ostruo, son of Titus, of the Luccatici tribe.
EDCS-69200231.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying an individual, Ostruo, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-69200232.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying the deceased, Decimus Messius Timo.

EDCS-69200234.text_edition: \n Publice Lucio Anchario Cai filio Romilia tribuno militum bis praefecto fabrum IIviro auguri honoris caussa locus sepulturae datus ipsi posterisque eius sepulturam Vicellia Titi fi[lia ------\n
EDCS-69200234.translation: In accordance with the law, a place for burial was granted to Lucius Ancharius, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe, tribune of the soldiers, twice prefect of the engineers, and a duovir, and to his descendants, for the sake of honor; the burial of Vicellia, daughter of Titus...
EDCS-69200234.summary: This is a funerary inscription granting burial rights to Lucius Ancharius and his descendants, detailing his various civic and military offices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69500009.summary: This inscription records a historical event concerning King Anthenor and the Euganei people.

EDCS-69500010.translation: To Bassanus, called Bassus, constructed by Anthenor of Troy.
EDCS-69500010.summary: This is a dedication of a monument constructed by Anthenor of Troy to Bassanus.

EDCS-69500012.translation: Nestor Germanicianus, freedman of Caesar, lived 40 years from the household goods.
EDCS-69500012.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Nestor Germanicianus, who lived 40 years and was a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-69500014.translation: Boundary stone of Albinus, 30 feet to the rear. This will be the boundary.
EDCS-69500014.summary: This inscription marks a property boundary established by Albinus.

EDCS-69500015.translation: Lucius Pactumeius Ferox, soldier of the XIV Legion, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-69500015.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Pactumeius Ferox, a veteran of the XIV Legion, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-69500016.translation: To Fortuna Domestica (?). Publius Opsidius Rufus, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Scythica Legion, [prefect of the engineers(?)]...
EDCS-69500016.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna Domestica by Publius Opsidius Rufus, who held military and engineering positions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69500017.translation: To Isis, Decumia Vitalis gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-69500017.summary: This is a votive inscription by Decumia Vitalis to the goddess Isis.

EDCS-69500018.translation: ...lia Procula dedicated an altar to Silvanus...
EDCS-69500018.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to the god Silvanus by a woman named Procula, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-69500021.translation: Gaius Valerius Cicereius, freedman of Gaius, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-69500021.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Valerius Cicereius, a freedman, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-69500032.translation: ...NA[---] Marcus Epidius Proculus, prefect, [adjudicating]... Marcus Epidius Lybicus...
EDCS-69500032.summary: This inscription mentions Marcus Epidius Proculus, who held a judicial office, and Marcus Epidius Lybicus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69500033.translation: Of Quintus Minius Faustus, scribe of the library.
EDCS-69500033.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Minius Faustus as a scribe of the library, likely found on a monument related to his office.

EDCS-69500036.translation: [...]ius / [belonging to the] state / [and...] Quintus Ven/[...] gave.
EDCS-69500036.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication by Quintus Ven[...], with some mention of the state.

EDCS-69500037.translation: Boundary // Of Lucius Sempronius, son of Titus // Of Gaius Caesius, son of Publius.
EDCS-69500037.summary: This inscription marks a boundary, with ownership attributed to Lucius Sempronius and Gaius Caesius.

EDCS-69500039.translation: Gaius Albinus, son of Lucius, on the front 36 feet, at the back 22 feet.
EDCS-69500039.summary: This inscription records land dimensions, measuring 36 feet in front and 22 feet at the rear, belonging to Gaius Albinus.

EDCS-69500040.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Lucius Arrius, son of Lucius, from his most devoted mother.
EDCS-69500040.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Arrius, set up by his mother.

EDCS-69500041.translation: For Aurelia Gemella. Marcus Aurelius Severus / [...] Vilius Lacer / [...]
EDCS-69500041.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aurelia Gemella, with Marcus Aurelius Severus and Vilius Lacer possibly involved as dedicators or subjects.

EDCS-69500042.translation: Burial place. In front 20 feet, at the rear 40 feet. Titus C. C.
EDCS-69500042.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot with specific dimensions (20 feet front, 40 feet rear) and mentions Titus C. C.

EDCS-69500043.translation: Gaius Can[...]/ on the front [..] feet, / at the rear [..] feet.
EDCS-69500043.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records land dimensions for Gaius Can[...], specifying front and rear measurements.

EDCS-69500044.translation: [...] / Fabia / to [her] father / Capria Sabina, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-69500044.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Capria Sabina to her father, possibly set up by Fabia.

EDCS-69500045.translation: Of the gens Cascica and Betucia.
EDCS-69500045.summary: This inscription possibly refers to the Gens Cascica and Betucia, perhaps marking a family property or tomb.

EDCS-69500046.translation: To the Gens Cascica, Betutia, Seppia, Salonia.
EDCS-69500046.summary: This is a funerary dedication to multiple women from the Gens Cascica.

EDCS-69500047.translation: To Gaius Catitus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, and to Suavia, freedwoman of a freedman, wife of the same, Gaius Catius Priscus, freedman of Gaius, erected this.
EDCS-69500047.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Gaius Catius Priscus for his wife Suavia and himself.

EDCS-69500048.translation: Burial place of Manius Cipius Nicephorus. In front 23 feet, behind 43 feet.
EDCS-69500048.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot of Manius Cipius Nicephorus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-69500050.translation: Of Sextus Coelius, of Publius Ettius, of Titus Coelius, of Quintus Coelius.
EDCS-69500050.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription listing several individuals, likely owners of burial plots.

EDCS-69500051.translation: To Lucius Combullius Faustus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-69500051.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Combullius Faustus, a freedman.

EDCS-69500052.translation: Cornelia Quintilla for herself and her family. Publicia, daughter of Lucius, and [...ITIA]...
EDCS-69500052.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription indicating that Cornelia Quintilla dedicated the plot for herself and her family, with a partial dedication from Publicia.

EDCS-69500053.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Cornelius Clementis, likely in a funerary context.

EDCS-69500054.translation: To Gaius Crimilius Donatus, freedman of Gaius. // Of Titus Terentius, of Gaius Postumius, freedman...
EDCS-69500054.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record multiple individuals, possibly in a funerary or ownership context.

EDCS-69500055.translation: To Gaius Curtius Scyrus, to Curtia Daphne, to Gaius Curtius Hermerotes, to Curtia Cypris, to Quanta Curtia.
EDCS-69500055.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely family members, possibly related to a funerary monument or property.

EDCS-69500056.translation: To Lucius Cylius Iustinus, who lived 22 years, 11 months. Of good memory.
EDCS-69500056.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, lifespan, and a commendation for Lucius Cylius Iustinus.

EDCS-69500057.translation: Gaius Delius Phoebus, free of all debt, made this (monument) while alive: "I lie here." He made it for himself and for his wife Vibius Quieta.
EDCS-69500057.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Delius Phoebus for himself and his wife, specifying that he was debt-free when he commissioned it.

EDCS-69500058.translation: for himself and his slave Eron.
EDCS-69500058.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a burial plot intended for the owner and their slave.

EDCS-69500059.translation: Manius Fulvius Maturus made this while alive.
EDCS-69500059.summary: This funerary epitaph records Manius Fulvius Maturus commissioning his monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-69500060.translation: [to] Laelius, son of Publius, (her) husband, and Lucius Laelius, son of Lucius, [---]
EDCS-69500060.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be part of a funerary monument commemorating two individuals named Laelius.

EDCS-69500061.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely identifying Octavia, daughter of Caius, possibly on a tomb or a dedication.

EDCS-69500062.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely identifying Octavia, daughter of Caius, possibly on a tomb or a dedication.

EDCS-69500063.translation: Octavia Prima, daughter of Lucius, made this while alive for herself and her son Antatius, who completed his first year, with a frontage of 13 feet and a depth of 13 feet.
EDCS-69500063.summary: This funerary inscription records Octavia Prima setting up a burial plot for herself and her infant son, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-69500064.translation: Lucius Octavius Hilario, freedman of Lucius, [---]
EDCS-69500064.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to identify Lucius Octavius Hilario, a freedman.

EDCS-69500065.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. The burial place of Lucius Pacatus, with a frontage of 16.5 feet and a depth of 19.5 feet.
EDCS-69500065.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking a burial plot belonging to Lucius Pacatus, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-69500066.translation: Burial place of Petronia, [daughter] of Marcus Crispina, with a frontage of 91.5 feet and a depth of 23 feet.
EDCS-69500066.summary: This inscription records a burial plot belonging to Petronia Crispina, daughter of Marcus, detailing the dimensions of the property.

EDCS-69500067.translation: Of Lucius Plotus Firmus, of Marcus Plotus Optatus, of Gaius Plotus Severus. In front 21 feet, at the back 35 feet. Of Quintus Domitius Commodus. In front 43 feet, at the back 35 feet.
EDCS-69500067.summary: This is a boundary marker for a burial plot, specifying the dimensions and possibly indicating multiple owners or divisions of the space.

EDCS-69500068.translation: Lucius Poblicius Argius for himself and for Clodia Modesta, Clodia Pudica. Place of burial. In front 32 feet, at the back 28 feet.
EDCS-69500068.summary: This inscription records a burial plot purchased or allocated by Lucius Poblicius Argius for himself and several women, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-69500069.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription identifying a person named Sextus Pompeius.

EDCS-69500070.translation: To the departed spirits. Menophilus, son of the freedwoman Publicia (daughter) of Titus, set this up for his mother.
EDCS-69500070.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Menophilus for his mother Euterpe.

EDCS-69500071.translation: [...] F[---]I, Quintus Q[---], son of Quintus, for his father [...].
EDCS-69500071.summary: A highly fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication or funerary monument, mentioning a father and son.

EDCS-69500072.translation: To Lucius Remmius, brother, son of Marcus. To Remmia Festa, sister, daughter of Marcus. [...]
EDCS-69500072.summary: A funerary inscription dedicating a space or monument to a brother and sister, Lucius Remmius and Remmia Festa.

EDCS-69500074.translation: Gaius Sulpicius Serenus, freedman of Gaius. In front 30 feet, at the back 30 feet.
EDCS-69500074.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot with its dimensions, belonging to Gaius Sulpicius Serenus.

EDCS-69500075.translation: [...] for himself and for Turrania Severa Livia Festa, [---]ori. In front 15 feet, at the back 30 feet. With permission of Severa Turrania, for Satria Cuparina.
EDCS-69500075.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription detailing a burial plot, its dimensions, and indicating permission was granted by Severa Turrania for Satria Cuparina.

EDCS-69500076.translation: Place of burial. Of Lucius Valerius, son of Lucius. In front 14 feet, at the back 2[--].
EDCS-69500076.summary: An inscription marking a burial plot, specifying the owner Lucius Valerius and the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-69500077.translation: [...] freedman of Marcus C[---]. [...]nnius, son of Marcus Se[---]. [...] Lucius Valerius Severus, son of Lucius. [...] Quintus Cornelius, freedman of Quintus Api[---]. [...]s Turrania, daughter of Gaius Ter[---]. [...] Gaius [...] Nedymus [...]. [...]cept[--- Lucius] Terentius Oct[---], freedman of Lucius. [...] Dorcas [...] Munatia Am[---], daughter of Publius. [...] Munatia R[---], daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-69500077.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly listing multiple individuals and their familial or social relationships, potentially related to burials or property.

EDCS-69500078.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. Publius Varius Niger, son of Caius, by his father Caius Varius Niger, while alive, for himself.
EDCS-69500078.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a son for his deceased father, and also for himself, dedicated to the gods of the underworld.

EDCS-69500080.translation: Quintus Vit[---] Sal[---]. 27 feet in front, 40 feet in the rear.
EDCS-69500080.summary: This inscription records boundary measurements for a plot of land, likely for a tomb or property, with incomplete names of the owner(s).

EDCS-70200006.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaburia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-70200016.summary: This inscription records that Celintius was the maker of the object.

EDCS-70200178.translation: To Lucius Clodius, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, as a tresvir.
EDCS-70200178.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Clodius, son of Marcus, a member of the Fabia tribe, who held the office of tresvir.

EDCS-70700047.translation: The brothers from the village of Chason made it, 6 feet.
EDCS-70700047.summary: This inscription records that brothers from the village of Chason made an object measuring 6 feet.

EDCS-70700048.translation: Mareas Julianus, Palladis, and Joseph from the village of Kaproturis, 25 feet.
EDCS-70700048.summary: This inscription records the contribution of 25 feet by Mareas Julianus, Palladis, and Joseph from the village of Kaproturis.

EDCS-70700049.translation: Eusebes and the 6 [sons?] of Zenobius from the village of Hemias made it, 100 feet.
EDCS-70700049.summary: This inscription records that Eusebes and the 6 [sons?] of Zenobius from the village of Hemias made an object measuring 100 feet.

EDCS-70700051.translation: Barbeusos, son of Drakontios, of the village of Ravona, together with his wife Mathbi and his children Ioanna and Malchos, made feet.
EDCS-70700051.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription from a village, listing the dedicator, his wife, and children.

EDCS-70700166.translation: Helvia Mansueta and [her husband?] placed this for themselves.
EDCS-70700166.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Helvia Mansueta, likely with her husband, set up a monument for themselves.

EDCS-70800171.translation: Publius Mercusenus, son of Publius, son of Publius Mercusenus Rufus, aedile, [his] father made [this].
EDCS-70800171.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely commissioned by a father for his son, Publius Mercusenus Rufus, who was an aedile and an Augustalis decurion.

EDCS-70900525.translation: Petronia Nymphe, freedwoman of Publius, for her husband Cerdon, freedman of Publius, a freedman of the Augustales, and for herself.
EDCS-70900525.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a freedwoman for her husband and herself, mentioning his status as a freedman of the Augustales.

EDCS-70900526.translation: Publius Fabius Helle be lives, and Lucius Cassius Heraclidas.
EDCS-70900526.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating the survival of two individuals, Publius Fabius Helle be and Lucius Cassius Heraclidas.

EDCS-70900527.translation: Minidius for Minidia, and also for his wife Minidia, and for his son Lucius Minidius Proculus.
EDCS-70900527.summary: This funerary inscription records dedications for Minidia, her wife (also named Minidia), and their son Lucius Minidius Proculus.

EDCS-70900528.translation: For his mother Firma and for Gaius Dorcatius Secundus Concordialis.
EDCS-70900528.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the mother of the dedicator, Firma, and to Gaius Dorcatius Secundus Concordialis.

EDCS-70900529.translation: To the good memory of Julia Marcella, his wife, a most pious woman.
EDCS-70900529.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Julia Marcella, described as the wife of the dedicator and a pious woman.

EDCS-70900530.translation: Titus Herennius Tertius, son of Secundus, ordered this to be made for himself in his will.
EDCS-70900530.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Titus Herennius Tertius arranged for his own monument through his will.

EDCS-70900532.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Siniscia Festa as the daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-70900536.translation: [---], daughter of Marcus Firma, 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the rear.
EDCS-70900536.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land, likely for a tomb, dedicated to the daughter of Marcus Firma.

EDCS-70900539.translation: Caius Cartorius Menophilus, freedman of Caius; Cornelia Tertia, freedwoman of the woman.
EDCS-70900539.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Caius Cartorius Menophilus and Cornelia Tertia, identifying their former owners.

EDCS-70900560.translation: To Delphidis the beloved, aged 6 years. Lucius Safinius Fuscus, son of Lucius, for himself and for Maria Prima, daughter of Lucius, his wife, he began...
EDCS-70900560.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young girl named Delphidis, and also for Lucius Safinius Fuscus and his wife Maria Prima.

EDCS-70900561.translation: Manius Braetius Secundus Maior, Caius Antonius Cresp[us].
EDCS-70900561.summary: This inscription appears to list two names, possibly indicating joint ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-70900562.translation: Baebia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, ordered [this] to be made for Quintus Antonius Clemens, son of Quintus, son of Quintus; and for Lucius Faustus, freedman of Lucius; and for Salvius, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-70900562.summary: This funerary inscription records that Baebia Secunda commissioned the monument for three individuals: Quintus Antonius Clemens, Lucius Faustus, and Salvius.

EDCS-70900599.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantinus Maximus Pius Felix Invictus semper Augustus.
EDCS-70900599.summary: This is a titulary inscription for the emperor Constantine the Great, likely found on a public monument, dating to his reign.

EDCS-70900656.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus, by Publius Sertorius Lotus.
EDCS-70900656.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred object or monument to the god Aesculapius Augustus by Publius Sertorius Lotus.

EDCS-70900871.translation: To Decimus Fabius Maximus, from Titus Cassius.
EDCS-70900871.summary: This is a dedication from Titus Cassius to Decimus Fabius Maximus, possibly indicating a funerary or honorific context, and is likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-70900873.translation: Marcus Viccius, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe, from the will of Marcus Viccius, son of Lucius, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-70900873.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a will for Marcus Viccius, likely related to funerary arrangements or property inheritance, and dates to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-70900885.translation: To Aquilia, daughter of Lucius Oclatinus.
EDCS-70900885.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to Aquilia, daughter of Lucius Oclatinus.

EDCS-70900990.translation: Gaius Petronius, son of Marcus, son of Acutus(?), ordered it to be made.
EDCS-70900990.summary: This is a building or dedication inscription by Gaius Petronius, son of Marcus, indicating he commissioned the work, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-70900991.translation: To Septicia, freedwoman of Lucius, from her mother and to Sottica, freedwoman of Marcus, her fellow freedwoman.
EDCS-70900991.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to two women, Septicia and Sottica, one being the mother of the other or a close associate, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-71000539.translation: To the Divine Shades. Julius Maximus, soldier of the VI Praetorian cohort, Antoninianae, aged 14.
EDCS-71000539.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julius Maximus, a soldier of the Praetorian Guard, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-71000540.translation: To the Unconquered Invictus Mithras. Tullius.
EDCS-71000540.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mithras by Tullius, likely from a Mithraeum or a private shrine, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-71000541.translation: The plot of Aebutius Titus Firmus, 30 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-71000541.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Aebutius Titus Firmus, likely for boundary marking.

EDCS-71000542.translation: Publius Terentius Velox, son of Publius; Cerdo Suber; Marcellina; Fidelis; made these while alive.
EDCS-71000542.summary: This is an epitaph for several individuals, including Publius Terentius Velox, who commissioned their own funerary monuments during their lifetime, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-71000627.translation: To the Divine Shades. Publius Firmiteius Redempto, father to his most sweet son, lived 18 years.
EDCS-71000627.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a father, Publius Firmiteius Redempto, to his son who died at the age of 18, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-71000723.translation: For the health, safe return, and victory of Gaius Caesar Augustus, best princeps, chief pontiff, great-grandson of divine Augustus, with tribunician power IV, consul designate V, Imperator VII, father of the fatherland, father of the armies. Prima, daughter of Publius, priestess of the divine(?) Drusilla.
EDCS-71000723.summary: This inscription honors the emperor Gaius Caesar (Caligula) and records Prima as a priestess of Drusilla, likely from the period of Caligula's reign (37-41 AD).

EDCS-71100097.translation: Location of the monument of Salvia Gavia: 16 feet in front, 36 feet in the field.
EDCS-71100097.summary: This is a boundary inscription marking the location of a monument belonging to Salvia Gavia.

EDCS-71100098.translation: Location of the monument of Salvia Gavia: 36 feet in the field.
EDCS-71100098.summary: This is a boundary inscription marking the location of a monument belonging to Salvia Gavia.

EDCS-71200021.summary: This is a fragment of a personal name, Lucius, son of Lucius, likely from a tombstone or other monument.

EDCS-71200022.summary: This is a fragment of a personal name, Lucius, son of Lucius, likely from a tombstone or other monument.

EDCS-71200025.summary: This is a genitive case of a personal name, Lucius Minicius Pudentis, likely the owner or dedicatee of a monument.

EDCS-71200137.translation: To Concordia. Septimius Theodulus, a most distinguished man and corrector, adorned [this monument]. For the people of Aquileia and the Concordians...
EDCS-71200137.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Concordia by Septimius Theodulus, a high-ranking official, for the citizens of Aquileia.

EDCS-71200302.translation: To Lucius Cossutius, son of Marcus, 10 feet in front and 30 feet in the rear.
EDCS-71200302.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land dedicated to Lucius Cossutius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-71200303.translation: To Lucius Cossutius, son of Marcus, 10 feet in front and 30 feet in the rear.
EDCS-71200303.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land dedicated to Lucius Cossutius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-71200325.translation: To Lucius Aulenius: 55 denarii for a silversmith, 15 denarii for a goldsmith. To Armonius the magistrate: the 6th day before the Kalends of September, the 3rd day before the Nones of December.
EDCS-71200325.summary: This inscription records payments made to a silversmith and a goldsmith, and lists two dates related to a magistrate named Armonius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71200326.translation: To Aufidius, magistrate, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of April; to Aufidius, magistrate, on the Ides of June; on the 3rd day before the Nones of January [---].
EDCS-71200326.summary: This inscription lists magistracies and specific dates, likely related to official duties or dedications by Aufidius.

EDCS-71200693.translation: Aulus Secundus for himself and for his wife Antistia Firman, for his son Quintus Cavarus, son of Quintus Saturninus, 12 feet in front and 25 feet in the recess.
EDCS-71200693.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial plot dimensions and dedicants for Aulus Secundus, his wife, and son.

EDCS-72200164.translation: Aureliana Nunna placed this for Aurelius Mucapor, from the fifth Macedonian region, her husband, with whom she lived for 25 years, without any complaint, and for herself.
EDCS-72200164.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Aureliana Nunna for her husband Aurelius Mucapor, indicating their marital duration and mutual affection.

EDCS-72300189.translation: Location of the monument of Maesia Optata, freedwoman of Gaius, from Sentino: 12 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-72300189.summary: This is a boundary inscription marking the location of a monument belonging to Maesia Optata, a freedwoman originally from Sentino.

EDCS-72300209.translation: Gaius Canius: [3] feet in front, [3] feet in the rear.
EDCS-72300209.summary: This is a boundary inscription indicating the dimensions related to a monument of Gaius Canius.

EDCS-72300238.translation: Here lies Nenofytus Victorinianus, who lived 2 years and 11 months.
EDCS-72300238.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and lifespan of Nenofytus Victorinianus.

EDCS-72400138.translation: 8 1/2 iugera | 1/2 1/3 iugera / 19 1/2 1/6 iugera / 5 1/4 1/12 iugera / Argen [---] 5 1/4 1/8 iugera // [---] 1/2 iugera / [---] / [---] 10 1/2 1/3 iugera / // Bituci 4 1/3 1/12 iugera / Vindilli 23 iugera / Segomari 3 1/4 iugera / Dusti 19 iugera / Cac[---]ri Meteli 35 1/6 iugera / Surus Talusacr() 26 1/2 iugera / Samoiali 47 1/6 1/12 iugera // [---] 6 1/2 [---] / [---] 10 [---]
EDCS-72400138.summary: This inscription is a detailed record of landholdings, listing various individuals and the amount of land (in iugera) they possessed, possibly for tax or administrative purposes.

EDCS-72500249.translation: ...for Pupinia, most beloved mother. Paulinus placed [this] while alive.
EDCS-72500249.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Paulinus for his mother Pupinia, placed during his own lifetime.

EDCS-72700001.translation: Location of the monument of Lucius Titovius Eutychus: 40 feet in front, 60 feet in the field.
EDCS-72700001.summary: This is a boundary inscription marking the location of a monument belonging to Lucius Titovius Eutychus.

EDCS-72800051.summary: This inscription likely records a weight of 10 pounds belonging to Titus Macr, possibly related to a transaction or inventory.

EDCS-72800053.translation: Ancharius, son of Lucius Tarus Rufus.
EDCS-72800053.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Ancharius, son of Lucius Tarus Rufus.

EDCS-72800055.translation: Sacred to Fortuna. Vitullia Procula, daughter of Publius, has willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow. The site was granted publicly.
EDCS-72800055.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Fortuna by Vitullia Procula, indicating a public grant of land for the monument.

EDCS-72800062.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Marcus Licinius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-72800063.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Marcus Licinius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-72800064.summary: This inscription records the incomplete name and parentage of Publius Romilius.

EDCS-72800177.translation: Plotia made this for herself and for Primigenius.
EDCS-72800177.summary: A funerary inscription recording Plotia's self-dedicated monument for herself and Primigenius.

EDCS-72900112.translation: To Anatolius and Gero, a man of good and excellent memory.
EDCS-72900112.summary: A dedication honouring Anatolius and Gero, described as men of excellent memory.

EDCS-72900114.translation: To the Divine Manes. Aemilius Iovinus, who lived 66 years. Let no one wish to disturb his rest after the death of his parents.
EDCS-72900114.summary: A funerary inscription for Aemilius Iovinus, who lived 66 years, with a prohibition against disturbing his peace.

EDCS-72900116.translation: Ennius, a decurion of the colony.
EDCS-72900116.summary: An inscription identifying Ennius as a decurion (a local official) in the colony.

EDCS-72900119.summary: A fragmentary inscription identifying an individual as the son of Sextus, named Ter.

EDCS-73900002.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Orystienis(?) Photini, my very rare wife, and mother, and most holy daughter, erected this while alive, well deserving.
EDCS-73900002.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a living person for their deceased wife and daughter, praising their virtues.

EDCS-73900003.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Caius Laevonicus Stephanephoros, my most devoted father, [he erected this]...
EDCS-73900003.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Caius Laevonicus Stephanephoros, described as a devoted father.

EDCS-73900004.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Fructuosa, my dearest daughter, who lived 37 years and 20 days. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-73900004.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Fructuosa, a daughter, specifying her age and including a common epitaph formula.

EDCS-73900005.summary: A simple dedication or monument erected by Titus Fabricius.

EDCS-73900006.summary: A simple dedication or monument erected by Titus Fabricius.

EDCS-73900008.translation: To Antonia Maxuma, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-73900008.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of Antonia Maxuma.

EDCS-74100189.translation: Caesernius L. Celer, while alive, [dedicated] to...?
EDCS-74100189.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication by Caesernius L. Celer during his lifetime.

EDCS-74100229.translation: To Valeria, daughter of Publius, Apicharis.
EDCS-74100229.summary: An inscription dedicating something to Valeria, daughter of Publius, and Apicharis.

EDCS-74300116.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a name and filiation, possibly from a funerary context.
