EDCS-74300139.summary: This is a personal name, likely an owner or subject of a monument, with no further context provided.

EDCS-74300143.summary: This inscription records ownership or a dedication by Sextus Julius Severus.

EDCS-74300145.summary: This inscription records ownership or a dedication by Publius Quinctius Scapula.

EDCS-74300146.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Sepullius, son of Publius, likely for a monument.

EDCS-74300147.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Sepullius, son of Publius, likely for a monument.

EDCS-74300167.translation: Quintus's earthenware pot weighing 170 pounds, 107 pounds weight.
EDCS-74300167.summary: This inscription records the weight of a pot belonging to Quintus, likely a measure of goods or a trade record.

EDCS-74300172.translation: Sextus Magius Serenus, son of Sextus, decurion, erected this while alive for himself and for Hermerotis, his beloved.
EDCS-74300172.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Sextus Magius Serenus, a decurion, for himself and his beloved Hermerotis.

EDCS-74300173.translation: Lucius Sescinius, son of Titus, and Ennia, daughter of Appius, Tertia, his wife, to Lucius Sescinius, son of Lucius, Titus Sescinius, son of Lucius, Daedalus Sescinius, son of Lucius, and Munita Sescinius, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-74900036.text_edition: \n Caecilius Honoratus Mindius Donatus Mindius Charmides Mindius Zoticus Mindius Hermes Mindius Maleus Mindius Narcissus Mindius Eititeus sic Marcius Soter Decidius Hister Decidia Certa Minervius Epaphroditus Lucifer dispensator Lucifer adiutor coloni Vitalis dispensator Trophimus Trophimus alius Anconius qui vilicavit Tertius Amandus Viator\n
EDCS-74900036.translation: Caecilius Honoratus, Mindius Donatus, Mindius Charmides, Mindius Zoticus, Mindius Hermes, Mindius Maleus, Mindius Narcissus, Mindius Eititeus, as well as Marcius Soter, Decidius Hister, Decidia Certa, Minervius Epaphroditus, Lucifer the steward, Lucifer the assistant of the tenants, Vitalis the steward, Trophimus, another Trophimus, Anconius who was the farm manager, Tertius, Amandus, Viator.
EDCS-74900036.summary: This inscription lists numerous individuals, likely freedmen and household staff, possibly associated with a large estate or family, given the presence of stewards and farm managers. The date is uncertain without further context.

EDCS-75000360.translation: Maxentius, may you conquer, may you live!
EDCS-75000360.summary: This is a short acclamatory inscription wishing victory and life to Maxentius, possibly related to games or a political context.

EDCS-75100009.translation: Quintus Sertorius Firminus, a centurion of the IV Flavia Felix legion, erected this for his most dutiful father, Quintus Sertorius Apolaustus, who was one of the six officials of the Augustales.
EDCS-75100009.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a son for his father, a freedman honored with a priesthood, and who himself served as a military officer. The approximate date can be inferred from the legion mentioned.

EDCS-75100010.translation: [...], brother, he ordered this to be made by will for Cornelius Favor, prefect of the III(?) cohort of the Breucori, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Flavia Felix legion, and duovir with judicial authority.
EDCS-75100010.summary: This inscription records the posthumous honors or funerary monument for Cornelius Favor, who held several military and administrative positions, erected by his brother. The approximate date can be inferred from the legion mentioned.

EDCS-75400001.translation: To Prima, daughter of Lucius; and to Festae, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-75400002.translation: To the departed spirits. To Publius Requintilius Crescentius, my well-deserving husband.

EDCS-76100158.translation: Titus Atilius Gelenius, freedman of Titus, made this tomb while alive for himself and for Valeria Primigenia, daughter of Lucius; monument plot in front 8 feet, in the land 15 feet.

EDCS-76400069.translation: [...] due to a vow, he placed this, and for the sake of appeasing all his own people, he fulfilled the vow.

EDCS-76600238.translation: Sacred to Melisoco. Gaius Septidius Philumenus gladly paid his vow.

EDCS-76600323.translation: Gaius Cornelius, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, [...]

EDCS-76600325.summary: This inscription names Publius Tufidius Sedulus and Tufidia Urbana, both freedpersons of Publius, and indicates they erected the monument while alive.

EDCS-76600327.translation: To the departed spirits. Of Gaius Sippius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the Scaptia tribe.
EDCS-76600327.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Sippius Priscus, son of Gaius, specifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-76900106.translation: Lucius Vibius Lepidus. Veia Clara, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-76900106.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Lucius Vibius Lepidus and Veia Clara, likely a funerary monument from the early imperial period.

EDCS-77600009.translation: To the most blessed martyr Proto.

EDCS-77700066.translation: He served for 13 years, lived for 40 years.
EDCS-77700066.summary: This funerary inscription records the military service and lifespan of an unnamed individual, likely from the Roman army, possibly dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-77700070.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Claudius, the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus. From the people of Benacus.
EDCS-77700070.summary: This is an imperial dedication to Emperor Claudius Gothicus by the people of Benacus, likely from the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-77700087.translation: To Lucius Licinius Niger, son of Lucius, from Bacchis, freedwoman. Frontage 15 feet, plot [in the] field.
EDCS-77700087.summary: This inscription records a property boundary or sale for Lucius Licinius Niger and his freedwoman Bacchis, specifying dimensions of a plot of land.

EDCS-77700088.translation: From the workshop of Fortissimus and Ursa.

EDCS-77700131.translation: This workshop was built in the consulship of Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus and Marcus Licinius Crassus, the workshop of Barnaeus, Quintus' slave.
EDCS-77700131.summary: This inscription records the construction of a workshop during the consulship of Pompey and Crassus, attributing its building to a slave named Barnaeus.

EDCS-78200055.translation: Cleaned by Saufeius Livianus. 8 weights, 19 fleeces.
EDCS-78200055.summary: This inscription records a quantity of goods, possibly wool fleeces and weights, processed or accounted for by Saufeius Livianus.

EDCS-78400176.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Marcus Veronius Pudens and another person, indicating it was erected during their lifetime.

EDCS-78400190.translation: Gaius Fabius, son of Gaius, from the Publilia tribe, from Verona, a soldier of the Ninth Spanish Legion, is buried here.
EDCS-78400190.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Fabius, a soldier of the Ninth Spanish Legion, originating from Verona.

EDCS-78700051.translation: Built by [---]. Lucius Petronius, son of Decimus, [---]t[---]. Publius F[---]

EDCS-78700054.translation: Quintus Longu[--]us, son of Quintus, from the Aniensis tribe, shoemaker.
EDCS-78700054.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Longu[--]us, a shoemaker from the Aniensis tribe, likely a funerary marker from the Imperial period.

EDCS-78700055.translation: Marcus Iuventius, son of Lucius, patron of Aniensis, made this while alive for himself and for Aninia Rufa, freedwoman of Lucius, his wife. [...] Marcus? Iuventius [...] the same [...]
EDCS-78700055.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Iuventius for himself and his wife Aninia Rufa, with a possible further mention of Marcus Iuventius, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-78700059.translation: For Gaius Cornelius Calvus. Senex, patron, 30 feet in front, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-78700059.summary: This inscription dedicates a plot of land for Gaius Cornelius Calvus, indicating its dimensions and possibly a public role of Senex, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-78700060.translation: To Marcus Licinius Postuminus, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, who holds public equestrian rank. His mother Beronice, daughter of Marcus, of the Ulpia tribe, [dedicated this] to her most dutiful son. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-78700060.summary: This funerary inscription honors Marcus Licinius Postuminus, a man of equestrian rank, dedicated by his mother, and the plot of land was approved by the town council, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-78800142.translation: Bolgolio Tertius, son of Donnedo Tertullus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-78800142.summary: An epitaph recording a vow paid by Bolgolio Tertius.

EDCS-79000074.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Publius Caesius Archigenes willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-79000074.summary: This is a votive inscription by Publius Caesius Archigenes dedicating a promise fulfilled to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-79000075.translation: To Mercury, Gaius Poblicius Proculus willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-79000075.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Poblicius Proculus dedicating a promise fulfilled to Mercury.

EDCS-80200120.summary: A dedication to Arria Fadilla, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-80200122.translation: Lucius Fabius, son of Lucius, while alive, for himself and Fabia I[...]

EDCS-80200189.translation: To our lord Flavius Jovianus, triumphant, always Augustus, born a good man for the republic.
EDCS-80200189.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Flavius Jovianus, praising him as a triumphant ruler and a virtuous leader.

EDCS-80300124.summary: A record of fleeces, likely commercial, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80300129.summary: A record of wool, likely commercial, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80300131.translation: Primus [provided?] 6 fleeces, 3 pounds [of hemp?], 3.5 pounds [of hemp?].
EDCS-80300131.summary: A record of fleeces and hemp, likely commercial, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80300132.translation: Lucius Varius Pilocus, a purple (cloak?) weaver.
EDCS-80300132.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Varius Pilocus, who was likely a weaver of purple cloth, possibly dated to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-80300133.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of goods or services, possibly related to trade or accounting, mentioning a person named Fronto and quantities of items, dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-80300135.translation: From Tarentum, Priscus, provided with a tunic. Four rolls, thirty-and-a-half pounds.
EDCS-80300135.summary: This inscription records goods, possibly for sale or trade, from Tarentum, mentioning Priscus and specifying quantities and weights, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-80300136.summary: This inscription seems to be a record of weights and quantities, possibly related to trade or inventory, mentioning Terentia Urbana and dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-80300137.translation: Purgata, Saufi, Liviani. Eight pounds, nineteen rolls.

EDCS-80700115.translation: The place of the monument of Gnaeus Moenius Priscus: in the front twenty-four feet, in the field sixteen feet.
EDCS-80700115.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Gnaeus Moenius Priscus, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-81200002.translation: Mother Af Prisca, the daughter, ordered this to be made for herself and her family, in the tomb of Geres.
EDCS-81200002.summary: This funerary inscription records a commission by Af Prisca for her family's tomb, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-81200007.translation: To Gaius Ennius Opilio, son of Gaius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-81200007.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Gaius Ennius Opilio, son of Gaius, son of Gaius, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-81200011.translation: To Lucius Ancharius Secundus, son of Lucius, father and patron. To Ancharia Accepta, daughter of Lucius, mother and freedwoman. To Mulvia Serena, wife of Lucius Ancharius Crescens, son of Lucius, daughter of Mulvia, freedwoman of Marcus. Notellia Cinnama, freedwoman of Marcus. "I hurried too much." Lucius Ancharius Crescens, freedman of Lucius, made this for himself and his family while alive. And you, and for yourself.
EDCS-81200011.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Ancharius Secundus, his freedwoman/daughter-in-law Ancharia Accepta, and his wife Mulvia Serena, set up by Lucius Ancharius Crescens, also his freedman, who expresses regret with the phrase 'nimium festinavi' and dedicates the monument to himself and his family.

EDCS-81200012.translation: To Gaius Coelius Priscus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-81200012.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Gaius Coelius Priscus, son of Gaius.

EDCS-81200015.translation: Homuncio, son of Almus, placed this. Aged 16.

EDCS-81200017.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Manius Cornelius, identified as 'father'.

EDCS-81200019.translation: Donatus, aged 20. Proculus, to his comrade.

EDCS-81200108.summary: This is a simple owner's name, likely from a tomb or property marker, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-81200109.translation: The freedman Laevonicus fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-81200110.translation: Secundus to his deserving wife Iustea.

EDCS-81700297.translation: Quintia Lupa, to her dearest husband.

EDCS-81700299.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest. Lucius Attius Agapomenus, a VIvir Augustalis, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-81700301.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication or funerary notice to Decimus Attulius.

EDCS-82000087.translation: Born for the good of the republic.

EDCS-82000088.translation: Of Sextus Ganius, son of Sextus, from Collis, for himself and his freedmen; in front 18 feet, in the field 26 feet.

EDCS-82000089.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Aufidia Secunda.

EDCS-82400124.translation: Septimius Theodulus, a most distinguished man, adorned [it].

EDCS-82600024.translation: To the Divine Shades. Of Acius Martialis.

EDCS-82600025.translation: Scaevinus, son of Marcus, to his father Marcus Scaevinus, to his mother Cai filia, and to his brother Scaevinus, son of Marcus, made this while alive.
EDCS-82600025.summary: This funerary inscription records the creation of a monument by Scaevinus, son of Marcus, for his deceased family members, dating to the Roman period.
